issues.title: Leverage model's bash affinity via Zero-Dependency OS Sandboxing & Post-Execution Intent Routing

labels.name: priority/p2
labels.description: Important but can be addressed in a future release.

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Issues related to Core Agent, Tools, Memory, Sub-Agents, Hooks, Agent Quality

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.name: workstream-rollup
labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

labels.name: effort/large
labels.description: 3+ days: platform-specific, architecture, memory leaks

type.name: Epic
type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
## Description
Gemini 3 models are fundamentally trained to operate as native bash users, chaining standard POSIX tools (`grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`) to explore codebases and edit files. To make full use of the model's native and preferred capabilities without compromising user security or UX, we need to allow the model to use these tools directly to interact and make changes.

## Prior Art
Historically, we have attempted to force models to use custom tools (such as `replace`, `grep_search`, `write_file`, etc.). However, these methods fight the model's core training. Malicious prompts or complex scripts are inherently hard to control and catch via parsing, and forcing custom tools creates significant downstream UX and security issues.

## The Challenge & Value Proposition
Because the model strongly favors raw bash calls even when nudged towards custom tools, it frequently outputs large, complex bash scripts to accomplish tasks. Under our current security model, these scripts require explicit user confirmation. 

This creates a critical point of failure: users are frequently presented with dense, hard-to-read bash messages to evaluate. This leads to severe prompt fatigue, causing users to either blindly confirm the execution or enter "yolo mode" (auto-approving all actions). This behavior is highly detrimental to security and degrades the overall user experience. 

**Value Proposition:** By safely embracing the model's native bash tendencies, we can eliminate confirmation fatigue, prevent unsafe "yolo mode" habits, and drastically improve both the UX and our underlying security posture. 

## Proposed Solution
A highly viable solution is to utilize a secure sandbox. ALL standard shell commands will execute within a zero-dependency, kernel-enforced sandbox. Instead of trying to predict intent before execution (which led to the parsing challenges described above), we can safely observe and handle the results *after* execution.

### Method
By running commands in a sandboxed replica of the workspace, we achieve three distinct UX lanes:
1. **Reads:** Commands that do not mutate the filesystem (e.g., `ls`, `grep`) are auto-approved. We must ensure this does not read from protected spaces or outside our trusted workspaces.
2. **Edits:** Commands that mutate the sandboxed filesystem (e.g., `sed -i`, `>`) trigger a post-execution Diff UI before the changes are synced back to the host, allowing for a seamless "Edit" tool experience using the model's preferred mechanisms. 
3. **Side-Effects:** A dynamic command router will handle commands requiring host credentials or network access (e.g., `git`, `gh`), completely bypassing the sandbox but requiring strict upfront user confirmation (i.e., stays the same as today, utilizing the policy engine to execute or ask for user confirmation).

## Architectural Mandates
In order to support this properly, we must explore, investigate, and implement the proper sandboxing for all major platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Epic
This is an epic that tracks this investigation and implementation. It will contain subtasks used to track progress towards its overall completion. After initial investigation, if this is not a feasible route, the epic can be marked as closed.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Current context baseline is approximately 36.6k tokens per turn. Large file reads often 'firehose' the context, leading to bloat (previously observed at +15k tokens/turn). 

The goal of 'Tactful Extraction' is to establish a surgical code-discovery hierarchy:
1. **grep_search**: Primary scout for locating symbols.
2. **shell/sed**: scalpel for semantic block extraction (preferred for specific line ranges).
3. **read_file**: surgical range-reading (migrated to 1-based start/end lines).

Telemetry indicates that making ~2.1% more targeted tool calls results in a ~6.9% reduction in total input tokens.

## Changes

- **read_file migration**: Switched from 0-based 'offset'/'limit' to 1-based 'start_line'/'end_line' for better model alignment.
- **Surgical Guidance**: Updated tool descriptions and system prompts to mandate 'token-frugal' behavior.
- **Tool Hierarchy**: Emphasized the use of 'grep_search' and 'sed' via 'run_shell_command' for efficient context management.

## Status

This work is temporarily sidelined in favor of other priorities but remains a key architectural goal for efficiency.

Linked Draft PR: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/18924

labels.name: priority/p3

type.name: Epic
type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve selected worktree across authentication restarts (#30078)
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserves the Git worktree selected by `--worktree` across authentication restarts (`RELAUNCH_EXIT_CODE = 199`) in both the bootstrap supervisor (`packages/cli/index.ts`) and the legacy child-process supervisor (`packages/cli/src/utils/relaunch.ts`).

Previously, `setupWorktree()` created/entered the worktree and set `GEMINI_CLI_WORKTREE_HANDLED='1'` only inside the initial child process. When an authentication change or re-authentication triggered a restart (`exit(199)`), the supervisor spawned the replacement child process from the original repository root without `GEMINI_CLI_WORKTREE_HANDLED='1'`, causing `--worktree` to either create a new timestamped worktree on every restart or fail with a git branch collision for named worktrees.

## Details

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/worktreeSetup.ts`**:
  - Added `notifyWorktreeSelected(worktreePath)` which sends `{ type: 'worktree-selected', path: worktreePath }` over `process.send` and awaits the IPC delivery callback with a bounded `500ms` fallback timeout (`WORKTREE_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`) and `try/catch` safety.
  - Called `await notifyWorktreeSelected(worktreeInfo.path)` in `setupWorktree()` immediately after switching `cwd` and setting `GEMINI_CLI_WORKTREE_HANDLED = '1'`.
- **`packages/cli/index.ts` & `packages/cli/src/utils/relaunch.ts`**:
  - Track `selectedWorktreePath` across relaunch iterations and pass `cwd: selectedWorktreePath` to `spawn(...)` when set.
  - On receiving `{ type: 'worktree-selected', path }`, validate `path`, switch the supervisor `cwd` via `process.chdir(msg.path)` inside a `try/catch` block first, and then persist `selectedWorktreePath = msg.path`, `process.env['GEMINI_CLI_WORKTREE_HANDLED'] = '1'`, and `newEnv['GEMINI_CLI_WORKTREE_HANDLED'] = '1'` across subsequent restarts while keeping `GEMINI_CLI_AUTH_OVERRIDE` one-time and `admin-settings` persistent.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/processUtils.ts`**:
  - Preserved `initialProcessSend = process.send` at module load so child processes spawned with `GEMINI_CLI_NO_RELAUNCH='true'` or tests supplying custom `process.send` handlers still send IPC messages when `VITEST` is set in the environment.
- **Tests**:
  - Added unit tests in `packages/cli/src/utils/worktreeSetup.test.ts` for IPC handoff completion, bounded `500ms` timeout fallback, and synchronous `process.send` error handling.
  - Added unit tests in `packages/cli/src/utils/relaunch.test.ts` verifying worktree retention across multiple consecutive authentication restarts alongside one-time `GEMINI_CLI_AUTH_OVERRIDE` and persistent `admin-settings`, plus graceful recovery when `process.chdir` fails.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30078

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests:
   ```bash
   npx vitest run --root packages/cli src/utils/worktreeSetup.test.ts src/utils/relaunch.test.ts src/utils/processUtils.test.ts
   ```
2. Manual reproduction check:
   - Start Gemini CLI in a Git repository with `--worktree` (or `--worktree keep-this-worktree`).
   - Trigger an authentication restart (e.g., `/auth` or auth method switch that exits with `RELAUNCH_EXIT_CODE = 199`) across 2+ restarts.
   - Verify `process.cwd()` remains inside the initial worktree and `git worktree list` shows only the single expected worktree.

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

prs.title: fix(cli): keep pasted @ text and fuzzy @ matches from attaching secrets
prs.body:
Fixes #26730

## Summary

A pasted shell transcript could make Gemini CLI attach an SSH private key to the model request without asking. This PR closes both halves of that path:

- **Pasted text is inert by default.** `ui.escapePastedAtSymbols` now defaults to `true`, so `@` in pasted text is stored as `\@` and is not treated as a file reference. The escape is removed before the text reaches the model or a `!` shell command.
- **The fuzzy fallback never picks secrets.** When an `@name` reference does not resolve, the recursive glob fallback skips matches that look like credentials and uses the next match instead.

This builds on #29458 by @MartinCajiao, which flipped the default but was closed by the bot before review. The default change, its description text, and the paste and schema tests are adapted from that PR.

## Root cause

1. `ui.escapePastedAtSymbols` (#21239) was opt-in, so pasted text such as `[dave@webserver ~]$ ssh-add -l` kept a bare `@webserver`.
2. `webserver` is not in the workspace root, so `resolveFilePaths` ran `**/*webserver*` in every workspace directory (dotfiles included) and attached the first match. Started from `$HOME`, that match can be `~/.ssh/webserver`.

The existing escape feature also had a gap: when no `@` reference resolved, the escaped text reached the model with the backslashes still in it (`dave\@webserver`), and shell commands received them too. That had to be fixed before the setting could default to on.

## Changes

- `settingsSchema.ts`: `ui.escapePastedAtSymbols` defaults to `true` (docs and JSON schema regenerated).
- `atCommandProcessor.ts`: glob-fallback matches are skipped when they are inside `.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.aws`, `.azure` or `.kube`; when the name looks like a private key (`id_rsa`, `id_dsa`, `id_ecdsa`, `id_ed25519` and variants, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.ppk`) or an env file (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`); when the file is owner-only (for example 0600); or when it cannot be stat'ed. The early return for queries without resolvable references now unescapes `\@`.
- `useGeminiStream.ts`: plain prompts and `!` shell commands receive the unescaped text.
- `docs/reference/commands.md`: documents paste escaping and the fuzzy-match exclusions.

Explicit paths are unchanged: `@.ssh/webserver` still attaches the file, because typing the exact path is a deliberate request.

## Trade-offs

- **Skip instead of confirm.** The issue suggests a confirmation prompt. A dialog inside `@` processing needs new async UI plumbing. Skipping is smaller, fails closed, and leaves a clear way to include the file on purpose: type its exact path.
- **Filter instead of exact-match-only.** Accepting only exact basename matches would not have stopped this leak (the key was named after the host) and would break lookups like `@README` → `README.md`.
- **Heuristics can over-match**, but only in the fuzzy fallback: Keynote `.key` files, `.env.example`, repositories with an `.aws/` folder, or every file of a user with umask 077. An exact `@path` still works for all of them. The permission check has no effect on Windows.
- **Visible `\@`.** Pasted `@` now shows as `\@` in the input box, as it already did for users who enabled the setting.

## Not in this PR

- Ignoring `user@host` in the parser (issue item 3).
- Pasted text in slash-command arguments and model-steering hints still keeps `\@`, as it does today with the setting on.
- Terminals without bracketed paste cannot be detected; the secret filter still applies there.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/cli
npx vitest run src/ui/hooks/atCommandProcessor.test.ts src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx src/ui/components/InputPrompt.test.tsx src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts
```

- `atCommandProcessor.test.ts`: the pasted-transcript repro; `.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.aws`, `id_ed25519_*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `.env.*` and `*.env` matches; an owner-only (0600) match (skipped on Windows); picking the next non-sensitive match; an exact `@.ssh/...` path still attaching. All but the last fail on `main`.
- `useGeminiStream.test.tsx`: `\@` is unescaped for the model and for shell commands.
- `InputPrompt.test.tsx`, `settingsSchema.test.ts`: escaping is on by default for Ctrl+V and bracketed paste.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run

prs.title: fix(core): stop local subagents from waiting out their deadline on a stalled model call
prs.body:
Fixes #29257

## Summary

When a single model call stalled, `cli_help` waited out its whole 3-minute `maxTimeMinutes`, then up to 60 s more on a recovery turn, before reporting `Agent timed out after 3 minutes.` This PR adds an optional per-turn limit on the model response to the local agent executor and enables it for `cli_help` (1 minute), so a stalled call fails fast with a clear error.

## Root cause

- `LocalAgentExecutor` bounds a model call only by the agent's overall deadline. Inside one call, `GeminiChat` can retry for minutes without yielding a stream event (connection retries with 5–30 s backoff on 429/503/timeouts, retries of empty or thought-only responses). When the deadline fires, the executor sends a recovery turn to the same model and waits up to `GRACE_PERIOD_MS` (60 s) again.
- The `thinkingBudget: -1` called out in the issue is not what the API receives. `callModel` sends the bare model name (`flash`) to `GeminiChat`, which resolves that model's default chat config. `AgentRegistry.registerModelConfigs` only registers the agent's `generateContentConfig` as a scope override for `auto` models. With a mocked content generator, the request goes to `gemini-3.5-flash` with `temperature: 1` and `thinkingLevel: HIGH`, so capping the budget alone does not change the request. This affects every local agent with a non-`auto` model; I left it for a separate issue because fixing it changes generation settings for those agents.

## Changes

- `RunConfig.maxTurnTimeMinutes` (optional): the maximum time to wait for the model's response in a single turn. Tool execution is not counted. On expiry the turn stops with `ERROR` and `Agent stopped: the model did not respond within N seconds.` The recovery turn is skipped because it would wait on the same model. Agents that don't set the field are unchanged.
- `cli_help`: sets `maxTurnTimeMinutes: 1` and replaces `thinkingBudget: -1` with `DEFAULT_THINKING_MODE` (8192), the cap other configs use.

@saikat709 proposed a capped budget and a per-turn timeout earlier in the issue. This PR implements the timeout in the shared executor and explains why the cap by itself would not change the request.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/agents
```

- `local-executor.test.ts`, new `run (Turn Timeout)` suite (mocked streams, fake timers): a stalled stream that ends, or throws `AbortError`, stops with `ERROR` after the limit, with one model call and no recovery turn; tool execution time is not counted, and the timer is cleared; after an empty model turn, the recovery turn is bounded by the turn limit instead of the 60 s grace period; the real `cli_help` definition fails after 60 s instead of waiting out 3 minutes. Against the previous executor, the four stall tests hang until the vitest timeout.
- `cli-help-agent.test.ts`: the budget is capped and `maxTurnTimeMinutes` is below `maxTimeMinutes`.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS

prs.title: fix(core): flag recursive and forced rm regardless of flag position
prs.body:
Part of #26767

## Summary

On POSIX, `isDangerousCommand` only compared `args[1]` of an `rm` call with `-f`, `-rf` and `-fr`. Equivalent forms such as `rm -r -f x`, `rm -Rf x`, `rm -vrf x`, `rm --recursive --force x` and `rm x -rf` were classified as not dangerous, so `PolicyEngine.applyShellHeuristics` did not force a confirmation for them when the shell tool is allowed without an argument pattern (for example `tools.allowed: ["run_shell_command"]`). This PR parses the `rm` options instead.

## Details

- New helper `isRecursiveOrForcedRm()` in `packages/core/src/sandbox/utils/commandSafety.ts`. It scans every argument up to `--` and returns true for a short-option cluster that contains `r`, `R` or `f`, or for `--recursive` / `--force`, including the unambiguous prefixes GNU `getopt_long` accepts (such as `--rec`).
- Options after operands count (`rm x -rf`), because GNU rm permutes its arguments. `--` still ends option parsing, so `rm -- -rf` (removing a file named `-rf`) stays non-dangerous.
- `rm -r` without `-f` is now dangerous as well, as suggested in the issue.
- Long options are matched by name or prefix, not by letter, so `--verbose`, `--interactive=always` and `--one-file-system` are not flagged.
- Like the existing `ln` and `find` checks, the scan looks at every parsed argument, so a compound command that starts with `rm` can be flagged because of a later segment (for example `rm a.txt && ls -R`). This errs on the side of asking.
- Function signatures are unchanged. Windows (`packages/core/src/sandbox/windows/commandSafety.ts`) is not touched.
- Not covered, to keep this small: path-qualified calls such as `/bin/rm`, and `sudo` options that shift the wrapped command (`sudo -u root rm -rf x`).

Thanks to @mahirhir for tracing the root cause in the issue. The new test table covers every row of their expected-results table.

## How to Validate

```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/sandbox/utils/commandSafety.test.ts
```

The new `rm command safety in isDangerousCommand` table has 29 cases. Without the `commandSafety.ts` change, 12 of them fail: the 7 rows from the issue, plus `rm -R x`, `rm --recursive x`, `rm --force x`, `rm --rec x` and `sudo rm -r -f x`.

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

prs.title: fix(core): keep one result per tool call ID in session records and live history
prs.body:
Fixes #28004

## Summary

Each tool-call ID now has exactly one result in saved sessions and in the requests sent to the model. The `--resume` duplication from #28004 was fixed when reading sessions by #29618. This PR removes the two places that still produced extra results per call ID.

## Details

- **Session records** (`chatRecordingService.ts`): the masking sync in `updateMessagesFromHistory` copied the whole tool-response turn into every matching `toolCalls[].result`, so with parallel calls each record held every sibling's response (the second half of #29365). It now stores only the call's own parts: its `functionResponse` plus the sibling parts that follow it, such as `inlineData`. Parts before the first response stay with the first call, so behavior for single calls does not change. Sessions written by earlier versions are repaired the next time they are resumed.
- **Live tool loop** (`turn.ts`): when the provider omits `functionCall.id`, `Turn` builds `${name}_${Date.now()}_${counter}`. A new `Turn` is created for every model request and the counter belonged to the instance, so two rounds in the same millisecond produced the same ID. The counter is now shared by all turns. The ID format is unchanged.
- There is no new dedupe at send time, and `convertSessionToClientHistory` is unchanged.

Thanks to @N0zoM1z0 for the deterministic reproducer, and to @xanister for the version bisection (0.42.0 to 0.45.0), which pointed to #26939 as the origin.

## Related Issues

Fixes #28004. Related to #29365 and #29618.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts
```

These new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change:
- `turn.test.ts`: should not reuse a synthesized call ID across turns in the same millisecond
- `chatRecordingService.test.ts`: should store only each call's own parts when parallel calls share a response turn
- `chatRecordingService.test.ts`: should repair sibling results stored on parallel calls and send each response once after resume

prs.title: fix(cli): load ~/.gemini/.env in untrusted folders
prs.body:
Fixes #27114

## Summary

In an untrusted folder, the CLI never read the user's own `~/.gemini/.env`. Workspace-account users who keep `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` there got an endless login loop outside trusted folders. This PR lets untrusted folders read `~/.gemini/.env` again, with the same allowlist and sanitization that untrusted folders already apply to other `.env` files.

## Details

- `findEnvFile()` (`packages/cli/src/config/settings.ts`): #25814 gated both `.gemini/.env` checks on workspace trust. That also skipped the user's `~/.gemini/.env`, both when the upward walk reaches the home directory and in the home fallback. The walk now also checks `.gemini/.env` when the current directory is the home directory, and the home fallback is no longer gated.
- Nothing else changes. A project's `.gemini/.env` is still skipped in untrusted folders. The plain `.env` lookup, `advanced.ignoreLocalEnv` / `--ignore-env`, and `loadEnvironment()` (allowlist plus `sanitizeEnvVar()` for untrusted folders) are untouched. Trusted folders behave exactly as before.
- Precedence is unchanged: a project `.env` found while walking up still beats `~/.gemini/.env` ("first file found, not merged"). Users who want their home file instead can use `advanced.ignoreLocalEnv` / `--ignore-env` (#26445), which with this fix also works in untrusted folders.
- `docs/cli/trusted-folders.md` now says which variables an untrusted folder loads and from where. The old sentence said no project `.env` file is loaded, which hasn't been accurate since #17806/#25814.

## How to Validate

```bash
npm run build
cd packages/cli
npx vitest run src/config/settings-env-isolation.test.ts src/config/settings.test.ts src/config/trustedFolders.test.ts
```

New cases cover an untrusted folder with only `~/.gemini/.env` (cwd under home and outside home), `~/.gemini/.env` winning over `~/.env`, a project `.env` still winning when untrusted, a project `.gemini/.env` never being loaded when untrusted, and trusted folders unchanged. On `main`, the four untrusted cases that read `~/.gemini/.env` fail.

prs.title: fix(core): stop body timeouts from killing and replaying long model turns
prs.body:
Fixes #29747

## Summary

With API-key, Vertex AI or gateway auth, a streamed turn that sends nothing for 5 minutes (for example while the model writes one large `write_file` argument at high thinking) is aborted by undici's body timeout. `GeminiChat` then replays the whole request up to 3 more times, and each replay is billed again.

This PR gives the global dispatcher a 15-minute body timeout and stops `GeminiChat` from replaying a request after a body timeout.

## Details

Root cause:
- `defaultBodyTimeout` in `packages/core/src/utils/fetch.ts` is a `const` (300 000 ms), and `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()` only changes the headers timeout.
- The only input to that function is the `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` experiment flag, which comes from the Code Assist server. For API-key, Vertex AI and gateway auth `getCodeAssistServer()` is `undefined`, so the flag never arrives. Those are exactly the auth types whose requests go through the dispatcher: `@google/genai` calls Node's built-in `fetch`, while Code Assist streams through gaxios and node-fetch.
- `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` is in `RETRYABLE_NETWORK_CODES` (#26191), so the mid-stream retry in `GeminiChat.sendMessageStream()` replays the request up to `MID_STREAM_RETRY_OPTIONS.maxAttempts` (4) times.

Changes:
- `fetch.ts`: the global dispatcher and the global proxy dispatcher use `bodyTimeout: 900000` (15 minutes). Google's Gemini 4 guide says to "set HTTP client timeouts to at least 15 minutes" (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/latest-model). undici's body timeout is an idle timeout, so it is never stricter than that. `@google/genai` has no per-request dispatcher option, so the global dispatcher is where its stream timeout lives. The safe agent used by `web_fetch` and the extension registry keeps 5 minutes, and the 60 s headers timeout is unchanged (#29693, #30082).
- `geminiChat.ts`: a mid-stream `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` is no longer retried. The model already sent nothing for the whole window, so a replay restarts the generation and is billed again. Everything else is retried as before: resets before any data, 429 and 503 in `retryWithBackoff`, and 503, SSL errors and premature close mid-stream. The code stays in `RETRYABLE_NETWORK_CODES`, so other callers and `getRetryErrorType()` are unchanged, and telemetry still reports `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`.

No new setting: the default itself was the problem, and a body-timeout setting is best decided together with the headers one proposed in #30082. If you want it configurable, I can add it on top, building on #29756 by @1sakshm.

Note: on Node 26, built-in `fetch` (undici 8) does not use the global dispatcher set through the pinned `undici@7.10.0`, so none of the CLI's dispatcher settings reach `@google/genai` there. Node 20, 22 and 24 (the CI matrix) are unaffected. That is a separate issue, related to #30077.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29747
Related to #29693

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core
```

prs.title: fix(core): apply local subagents' generateContentConfig for every model
prs.body:
Fixes #30168

## Summary

Local subagents now send the generation settings they declare in `modelConfig.generateContentConfig` (temperature, topP, topK, thinkingConfig) for every model value: `auto`, aliases such as `flash` and `pro`, and concrete model names. Before this change, only `auto` agents got them, and they lost them after `refreshAuth()` or `/clear`, which in `gemini -p` means before the first prompt.

## Details

- **Root cause.** Since #16043, `LocalAgentExecutor.callModel` sends GeminiChat the model name rather than the agent's model config alias, and GeminiChat looks the config up again by the concrete model id. The agent's settings only travelled through an override scoped to the agent, and #16043 registered that override for `auto` models only. #27315 later added `clearRuntimeOverrides()`, which deletes those overrides along with the quota-fallback ones.
- **Fix.** A new `ModelConfigService.registerRuntimeScopeOverride(scope, modelConfig)`, which `AgentRegistry` now uses for every local agent. It is stored per scope, so re-registering on a model change replaces the previous entry. `clearRuntimeOverrides()` does not remove it. It is applied before configured overrides, so `modelConfigs.overrides` and `customOverrides` that target the agent's scope (as `docs/core/subagents.md` describes) still win.
- **Thinking settings.** The API rejects a request that sets both `thinkingLevel` and `thinkingBudget`. `ModelConfigService.merge` now lets the one an override sets replace the inherited one. Without this, `cli_help`'s `thinkingBudget` would be merged with Gemini 3's default `thinkingLevel: HIGH` and every request would fail. No default model config sets both, so the main chat is unchanged.
- **Behaviour changes.** `codebase_investigator`, `cli_help`, `browser_agent`, and markdown agents with a non-`auto` model now send their declared temperature and thinking settings. `generalist`, the skill extraction agent and the main chat are unchanged. For `auto` agents, user overrides that target the agent's scope now beat the agent's defaults; before, the defaults silently won.
- **Interplay with #29257.** `cli_help` declares `thinkingBudget: -1` (dynamic thinking, no cap), which is never sent today. With this PR, the −1 takes effect. The #29257 fix (a separate PR) caps it at `DEFAULT_THINKING_MODE` and adds a per-turn timeout; that cap only reaches the API once this PR lands. The two PRs touch different files and can merge in either order.

## Related Issues

Related to #29257.

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/agents/registry.test.ts src/services/modelConfigService.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

The "generation config sent by the agent" tests fail on `main` for `flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `cli_help` and the cleared-overrides case, and pass with this change.

prs.title: feat(acp): let clients steer a running turn with _session/steering
prs.body:
## Summary

Lets ACP clients (Zed, JetBrains, VS Code extensions, and others that run `gemini --acp`) add a user message to a running `session/prompt` turn without cancelling it, the same way `experimental.modelSteering` works in the terminal.
Today an ACP client can only send `session/cancel` or a new prompt, and both throw away the work in progress.

This implements the `_session/steering` extension that Claude Code's ACP adapter (`claude-agent-acp`), `codex-acp` and Oh My Pi already ship, as proposed in #30048, so clients can use one code path for all of these agents. A client that doesn't call the method sees one extra `_meta` key in the `initialize` response and nothing else.

## Details

**Protocol** (constants in `acpUtils.ts`)

- `initialize` advertises the extension at the top-level `_meta.steering = { supported: true }`, beside `agentCapabilities`. No client opt-in or setting is needed; calling the method is the opt-in.
- New request `_session/steering` with `{ sessionId, prompt: ContentBlock[], _meta?: { steering?: { idleBehavior?: "promptRequired" } } }`. It answers with an `outcome`:
  - `injected`: a turn is running and the message was queued for it. Gemini CLI adds `_meta["geminicli.com"] = { steerId, pending }`.
  - `startedNewTurn`: no turn was running, so the message started a new one. If the previous turn was still finishing, the new turn starts after it ends.
  - `promptRequired` with `reason: "noRunningTurn"`: no turn was running and the client asked for this instead of a new turn. Nothing is stored.
- Additive Gemini CLI fields, under `_meta["geminicli.com"]` so they don't clash with the shared contract:
  - When a message reaches the model, the client gets a `user_message_chunk` with the user's text and `steering = { steerId, state: "delivered" }`.
  - Messages still queued when the turn ends (cancel, replacement prompt, or turn limit) come back in the `session/prompt` response as `undeliveredSteering`. If the turn throws, each one is sent as a `user_message_chunk` with `state: "undelivered"` before the error.

**Behavior in `Session.prompt()`**

- A turn accepts steering from the moment `session/prompt` arrives, including while the prompt is still being resolved, so a steer at that point can't start a second turn.
- Queued messages are added at the start of each loop iteration, after the turn-limit and cancel checks, in front of the tool results.
- They're joined and wrapped with `buildUserSteeringHintPrompt`, the same as the terminal UI does for hints sent after tool calls (`useGeminiStream.ts`). Each message still gets its own `delivered` update on the client.
- If the model finishes without tool calls while a message is queued, the loop sends one more request in the same turn, like the terminal UI auto-submits leftover hints.
- Running tools and open permission requests are not interrupted. While a turn runs, text starting with `/` or `$`, text over 8,000 characters, and more than 20 queued messages are rejected with `-32602`. A second `session/prompt` still cancels the first, and the replaced turn reports its queue as undelivered.
- Messages are also passed to `InjectionService` with source `user_steering`, so running local subagents see them, as in the terminal. This is a no-op unless `experimental.modelSteering` is on.
- Loading a session replays stored steering as the user's own text, not the wrapped prompt.

**Dispatcher**

- `GeminiAgent.extMethod` validates and routes `_session/steering` (`-32602` for bad params or an unknown session) and returns `-32601` for unknown methods. `GeminiAgent.extNotification` ignores unknown notifications, as the ACP spec advises.

No core changes. Terminal behavior and the `experimental.modelSteering` default are unchanged. No breaking changes.

**Open question for maintainers:** the longer-term ACP proposal (agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol#1261) puts this on `session/prompt` itself in protocol v2. This PR follows the extension that agents ship today, and can move to the v2 form once it lands.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29900
Fixes #30048

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:

   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/
   ```

   For the full suite, run `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true npm run preflight`, as CI does. Without that variable, 9 tests in `gemini.test.tsx` fail on `main` too.

   New cases in `acpSession.test.ts` cover delivery, ordering, continuation when the model ends, `startedNewTurn`, `promptRequired`, cancel, open permission requests, turn limits, replacement prompts, errors, validation, injection, and history replay. `acpRpcDispatcher.test.ts` covers the capability, routing and parameter validation.

2. Protocol smoke test against the built CLI (no model call needed): send `initialize` and check `_meta.steering.supported`; steer an unknown session and expect `-32602`; call an unknown `_` method and expect `-32601`.
3. End to end with an ACP client: start a prompt that runs a tool, send `_session/steering` while it runs, then check that the result is `injected`, the next model request contains the hint, the client gets a `delivered` chunk, and the turn finishes without being cancelled.

I ran 14 scenarios like this over stdio against the built CLI and a real model (Code Assist), covering each outcome, cancel, replacement prompts, open permission requests, turn limits, validation, the setting turned off, and session replay. All passed. A released CLI (0.67.0) answers `-32601` and advertises nothing, so clients can detect support.

prs.title: fix(core): prevent path traversal in legacy checkpoint fallback
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the path-traversal vulnerability in `Logger._getCheckpointPath()` and `Logger.deleteCheckpoint()` when falling back to the legacy unencoded checkpoint filename (`checkpoint-${tag}.json`).

While `_checkpointPath(tag)` safely percent-encodes special characters (including `/` and `\`) via `encodeTagName(tag)`, both `_getCheckpointPath(tag)` and `deleteCheckpoint(tag)` previously fell back to constructing `path.join(this.geminiDir, `checkpoint-${tag}.json`)` directly from the raw `tag`. A tag containing `../` segments (for example, `x/../../target`) caused `path.join` to normalize the `checkpoint-x` prefix away and resolve to `../target.json` outside `this.geminiDir`, allowing `loadCheckpoint`, `checkpointExists`, and `deleteCheckpoint` to read, probe, or delete arbitrary `*.json` files outside the checkpoints directory.

### Key Changes
- **Legacy Path Guard (`packages/core/src/core/logger.ts`)**: Added `_legacyCheckpointPath(tag)` to validate that the legacy candidate filename is a flat basename within `this.geminiDir` with no path separators before `_getCheckpointPath` or `deleteCheckpoint` touches the filesystem.
- **Unit Tests (`packages/core/src/core/logger.test.ts`)**: Added regression coverage verifying that `checkpointExists`, `loadCheckpoint`, and `deleteCheckpoint` reject `../` traversal tags on the legacy fallback path while preserving backward compatibility for flat legacy tags with special characters.

## Related Issues

Closes #29191

## How to Validate

```bash
npx vitest run --root packages/core src/core/logger.test.ts
npx eslint --max-warnings 0 packages/core/src/core/logger.ts packages/core/src/core/logger.test.ts
npm run typecheck --workspace=@google/gemini-cli-core
```

prs.title: fix(core,cli): emit ACP retry progress updates and enforce retry delay cap and model fallback
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29805.

In ACP (`--acp`) mode, when a model request hits a 429 quota or capacity exhaustion error, the CLI previously failed to emit any ACP progress signals while retrying, could treat multi-hour quota reset messages (`Your quota will reset after 14h31m12s`) as transient capacity exhaustion and sleep for hours, and did not persist model fallback transitions for non-interactive/ACP sessions or background utility models (`flash-lite`).

This PR addresses all three root causes:
1. **ACP Retry Progress Notifications**: Adds session attribution (`sessionId`) to `RetryAttemptPayload` and subscribes `acpSession.ts` to `CoreEvent.RetryAttempt`, forwarding retry progress as `agent_thought_chunk` updates with structured `_meta.retry` metadata (`attempt`, `maxAttempts`, `delayMs`, `error`, `model`) so ACP clients have visibility during retries.
2. **Retry Delay Budget Enforcement**: Excludes explicit quota-reset messages (`quota will reset after`) from transient capacity retry promotion and enforces `maxDelayMs` (and `MAX_RETRYABLE_DELAY_SECONDS`) in `retryWithBackoff`, promoting excessive retry delays to `TerminalQuotaError` so fallback is triggered immediately instead of sleeping for hours.
3. **Persistent Non-Interactive & Utility Model Fallback**: Resolves the failed model's own policy chain in `handleFallback` when a utility model (such as `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) fails, enables `onPersistent429` fallback in `BaseLlmClient` and automatic fallback in `handleFallback` for non-interactive/ACP sessions, and preserves `ModelAvailabilityService` terminal states in `activateFallbackMode` so subsequent calls in the session skip exhausted models immediately.

## Details

- `packages/core/src/utils/events.ts`: Add optional `sessionId` to `RetryAttemptPayload`.
- `packages/core/src/core/baseLlmClient.ts`, `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts`, `packages/core/src/core/client.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts`: Include `sessionId` when emitting `CoreEvent.RetryAttempt`, enable `onPersistent429` in `BaseLlmClient`, and respect `getFallbackOverride` during retries.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts`: Subscribe to `CoreEvent.RetryAttempt` for the active session and emit `agent_thought_chunk` updates with `_meta.retry`; unsubscribe on `dispose()`.
- `packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts` & `packages/core/src/utils/googleQuotaErrors.ts`: Export `MAX_RETRYABLE_DELAY_SECONDS` and enforce `maxDelayMs` budget for both silent capacity retries and `RetryableQuotaError` backoff delays.
- `packages/core/src/fallback/handler.ts` & `packages/core/src/config/config.ts`: Resolve failed utility model policy chains, enable automatic fallback in non-interactive sessions when no UI handler is registered, and avoid resetting `ModelAvailabilityService` or overwriting the active chat model when a non-active utility model falls back.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29805

## How to Validate

- Run unit and integration tests:
  - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/retry.test.ts src/fallback/handler.test.ts src/availability/autoRoutingFallback.integration.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts src/config/flashFallback.test.ts`
  - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/acpSession.test.ts`

prs.title: fix(core): keep the unsent request when loop recovery starts before a turn
prs.body:
## Summary

When the loop check at the start of a turn reports a loop, `_recoverFromLoop` sends only the loop feedback and drops the pending request. That request is usually the `functionResponse` of a tool that already ran, so the call is closed as `"Response was lost or interrupted."` and the model loses the record of what the tool did.

## Details

`processTurn` now passes the unsent request to `_recoverFromLoop`, which sends the request parts first and the feedback text after them, in one user turn. `isFunctionResponse` matches a turn with any `functionResponse` part, so `closeUnansweredToolCallsTurn` no longer replaces the real result.

The loop check during streaming is not changed, because there the request was already sent. I did not postpone the check while a tool response is pending: late in a prompt a response is almost always pending, so the check would almost never run.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29815

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/core/client.test.ts`. The new test `should keep an unsent tool response when the loop is found before the request is sent` fails on `main`, because the recovery request contains only the feedback text.
- The `--fake-responses` script in #29815: `step-29.txt` is answered with its real `functionResponse`, followed by the loop feedback.

prs.title: fix(core,cli,sdk): discard buffered tool calls on mid-stream error or retry
prs.body:
## Summary

When a model stream emits one or more `ToolCallRequest` events and then fails mid-stream (`Error` / `InvalidStream`), retries mid-stream (`Retry`), or terminates abnormally (`UserCancelled`, `AgentExecutionStopped`, `ContextWindowWillOverflow`, `LoopDetected`, `MaxSessionTurns`), `GeminiChat` rolls back the incomplete model turn from `agentHistory`. Previously, several stream consumers retained the buffered `toolCallRequests` (and `Turn.pendingToolCalls`) and still scheduled them after the stream loop exited, producing an orphaned `functionResponse` turn with no preceding `functionCall` in `agentHistory`.

This change:
- Clears `this.pendingToolCalls` (and resets per-attempt state on `Retry`) in `Turn.run()` when a stream retries, aborts, stops, or throws.
- Clears buffered `toolCallRequests` and tracks `StreamProcessingStatus` in `useGeminiStream.ts` when `Retry`, `Error`, `InvalidStream`, `UserCancelled`, `AgentExecutionStopped`, `ContextWindowWillOverflow`, `MaxSessionTurns`, or `LoopDetected` occurs, preventing orphaned tool execution and suppressing empty-response auto-nudges on non-completed streams.
- Clears buffered `toolCallRequests` / `toolCallsToSchedule` on mid-stream `Retry` and terminal stream events across `nonInteractiveCli.ts`, `acpSession.ts`, `legacy-agent-session.ts`, `sdk/src/session.ts`, and `a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts`.

## Related Issues

prs.title: fix(core): preserve file search results across query changes
prs.body:
## Summary

File searches can silently omit valid results after an earlier query populates the result cache. For example, searching `Src` and then `Src*` hides lowercase paths that a fresh `Src*` search finds. Reuse cached results only for identical queries so a new query always starts from the complete candidate list.

## Details

- Remove the assumption that a longer query must match a subset of its string prefix's results. Fuzzy search uses smart case, while glob filtering is case-insensitive.
- Cover the same failure within glob matching: `!*.ts` followed by `!*.tsx` must recover `.ts` files excluded by the first query. Separating caches by matcher alone would not fix this case.
- Preserve exact-query cache hits, filtering, ordering, cancellation, file-watcher invalidation, and result limits. Rename the existing broad-to-narrow integration test to describe the behavior it checks.
- Each new glob query now filters the full candidate list rather than a cached prefix subset. Repeated queries remain cached; fuzzy matching already searches the full list. No settings, dependencies, or matching rules change.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29055.

## How to Validate

```bash
npm exec -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- vitest run src/utils/filesearch --coverage.enabled=false --reporter=dot
npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli-core
npm run preflight
```

Before the implementation change, all four new integration cases failed: a nonempty fuzzy result, an empty fuzzy result, and negated-glob extension with fuzzy search enabled and disabled. The cache unit test also failed. With the fix, all 84 file-search tests pass, including existing file-watcher tests, and core type checking and targeted lint pass on macOS arm64 with Node.js 24.16.0.

Full preflight completed installation, formatting, all package builds, repository-wide lint, and type checking. Its workspace test run passed all 8,518 core tests, 182 A2A-server tests, 29 SDK tests, and 68 VS Code companion tests. The CLI run passed 7,431 tests and failed nine existing startup/workspace-trust cases in `src/gemini.test.tsx`.

Those same nine failures reproduce with the original cache source and built implementation restored. After restoring this fix, running that startup suite with `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` (also set by `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) passes all 45 enabled tests (one skipped):

```bash
GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true npm exec -w @google/gemini-cli -- vitest run src/gemini.test.tsx --coverage.enabled=false --reporter=dot
```

The setting was scoped to that test process; no persistent trust settings were changed.

The separate script suite initially passed 183 tests and failed 19 in `patch-create-comment.test.js`, whose helper invokes a script with an unquoted checkout path containing `Open Source`. All 202 script tests pass from an isolated copy of unchanged upstream sources at a path without spaces. All 17 SEA launcher tests also pass. The file-search suite was rerun after the baseline comparison and again passed all 84 tests.

The default `npm run preflight` invocation is therefore **not green** in this local environment; the failing cases pass with the environment/path corrections above. This is a draft while maintainers triage contribution eligibility and review the validation notes.

prs.title: fix(core): drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry
prs.body:
## Summary

On a mid-stream retry, `GeminiChat` has already yielded the failed attempt's chunks, while only the successful attempt's model turn is written to history. Every front end collected `ToolCallRequest` events from both attempts, executed both calls and answered both. A side-effecting command therefore ran twice, and the extra `functionResponse` no longer matched the model turn, so the next request failed with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` and every later request in the session was rejected too.

This implements the existing `RETRY` contract ("The UI should discard any partial content from the attempt that just failed") for tool calls in every consumer.

## Details

- `core/Turn`: reset `pendingToolCalls` when a retry is signalled, so calls that never entered history are not reported as pending.
- ACP (`acpSession`), interactive UI (`useGeminiStream`, including `pendingToolCallRequestsRef`), headless (`nonInteractiveCli`), a2a-server (`executor`) and the subagent `LocalAgentExecutor`: drop the collected tool call requests on `Retry`.
- No behavior change when a turn is not retried; clearing only happens when the backend signals a retry.
- Out of scope (unchanged): partial text from a failed attempt is still displayed, and headless stream-json may still emit a `tool_use` event for a call that is dropped.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30014

## How to Validate

Each new test streams a tool call, then `Retry`, then a second call, and asserts that exactly one call is executed and answered. All of them fail without the source change.

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts src/agents/local-executor.test.ts
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp/acpSession.test.ts src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
cd packages/a2a-server && npx vitest run src/agent/executor.test.ts
```

Additional checks:

- `tsc --noEmit` (core/cli/a2a), `eslint --max-warnings 0` and `prettier --check` pass.
- Full `@google/gemini-cli-core` suite: 8555 passed. The single failure is the pre-existing macOS-only `/dev/ttys001` test from #30008.
- Full a2a-server suite: 183 passed.
- Affected suites also pass in a Linux Docker container (`node:22-bookworm`, linux/arm64) after a clean `npm ci` + `npm run build`.

## 中文说明

修复 #30014。流式中途重试时，失败 attempt 的 tool call 已经发给前端但不会进入 history，导致同一命令被执行两次，且多余的 functionResponse 与 history 不匹配，后续请求持续 400。现在各前端在收到 `Retry` 时丢弃失败 attempt 收集到的调用，并清空 `Turn.pendingToolCalls`；无重试时行为不变。

prs.title: fix(core): tolerate dev 0 from Windows path stat in secure file reads
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29898.

On Windows with libuv 1.49.x–1.50.x (Node 22.12–22.16, 23.x), `fs.promises.stat(path)` returns `dev: 0` while `fileHandle.stat()` on the same file returns the real volume serial. `readSecureFileBuffer` compared the two, so every read failed with "File device or inode changed during read".

## Change

- The identity comparison moves into `fileIdentityChanged()`, used by both the open-handle check and the post-read check.
- On win32, a `dev` of 0 on either side is treated as unknown and only `ino` is compared.
- Unchanged: an `ino` mismatch is still rejected on every platform, and a `dev` mismatch is still rejected on non-Windows platforms. Missing dev/ino values (mocked fs) are handled as before.

## Tests

Three new cases in `fileUtils.test.ts` → `readSecureFileBuffer`:
- win32, path `dev: 0`, handle real `dev`, same `ino` → reads
- win32, path `dev: 0`, different `ino` → still rejected
- linux, path `dev: 0`, handle real `dev` → still rejected

Results on Windows 11, same machine:

| Suite | Node 22.14.0 before | Node 22.14.0 after | Node 22.23.3 after | Node 20.20.2 after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core: fileUtils, read-file, read-many-files, skillLoader, skillManager, memory, at-reference-resolution | 77 failed | 319 passed | 319 passed | 319 passed |
| cli: atCommandProcessor | 42 failed | 81 passed | — | — |

`prettier --check`, `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` (core) are clean.

## Notes

Not covered here: the Windows CI jobs pin `node-version: '20.x'`, so they can't catch this class of bug. Adding a Node 22 Windows leg seemed out of scope for this PR; happy to do it separately if useful.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve session history during tool output masking
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve the user's first prompt when resuming sessions whose tool outputs were masked.

## Details

`getHistory()` is prepared for API requests: for modern Gemini models it coalesces adjacent user turns and removes durable IDs. Writing this view back after masking merges the first prompt into the `<session_context>` message, which is skipped on resume.

Mask the stored history contents and reattach each original turn ID before updating the recording. This preserves turn boundaries and thought parts while allowing the recording service to update the masked tool response.

The masking service replaces contents at their original indices without filtering or reordering turns.

The regression test exercises `sendMessageStream`, real masking and recording, and `convertSessionToClientHistory`, with masking enabled and disabled. Existing chat mocks now include their durable history.

prs.title: fix(core): treat project temp paths as local in untrusted flag checks
prs.body:
## Summary

The agent's own helper scripts under Gemini CLI's session project temp directory
(`~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/...`) were reported as untrusted shell arguments. Once
shell output such as a Python traceback mentioned the script path, the next
`python3 <path>` invocation requested confirmation even in YOLO mode.

This change treats the project temp directory as local for untrusted-flag
detection, alongside the workspace.

## Details

`findUntrustedFlags()` exempts path arguments that resolve inside the workspace
(`isPathWithinWorkspace`). The project temp directory lives outside the
workspace, so a local script written there and later named in its own traceback
was flagged as untrusted — the false positive reported in #30004.

- `packages/core/src/utils/untrustedContextTracker.ts`: `UntrustedFlagOptions`
  gains `projectTempDir`; `isWorkspaceLocalPath()` now also accepts paths below
  it via `isSubpath()`, and `isPathWithinWorkspace` is optional so the temp-dir
  exemption works without a workspace callback.
- `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`: passes
  `config.storage?.getProjectTempDir()` when finding untrusted flags.

This mirrors the project temp directory trust that `Config.isPathAllowed()`
already applies for file access.

The remaining issue items are intentionally unchanged here: executable scripts,
URLs, and paths with shell expansions (`~`, `$VAR`) stay out of the
workspace-local exemption, and output from remote-retrieval commands keeps
external provenance, per #29833. The settings toggle is a separate design
decision.

## Related Issues

Related to #30004

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/untrustedContextTracker.test.ts src/tools/shell.test.ts`
  - New tests: `should not flag project temp paths that appeared in local shell output`
    and `should not flag project temp paths printed by earlier shell output`.
    Both fail before the change and pass after it.
- Manual check: in a session, run a command whose output names a file under the
  project temp directory (for example a traceback), then run `python3 <path>`.
  No confirmation should appear in YOLO mode. Paths outside both the workspace
  and the project temp directory are still reported.
- `npm run preflight` passed locally (Linux, Node 20.19.0) on the initial

## Summary

Fixes an issue where mid-stream retries (`StreamEventType.RETRY` -> `GeminiEventType.Retry`) resulted in partial text and tool calls from abandoned attempts being concatenated and executed, particularly in ACP mode.

## Details

1. **Turn State Cleanup (`packages/core/src/core/turn.ts`)**:
   - Upon receiving `StreamEventType.RETRY`, `Turn` now resets its accumulators (`this.debugResponses = []`, `this.cachedResponseText = undefined`, `this.pendingToolCalls.length = 0`, `this.pendingCitations.clear()`, `this.finishReason = undefined`, `this.hasLoggedRagTrace = false`).
   - This guarantees that `turn.getResponseText()` isolates only the successful attempt and prevents phantom tool call requests from abandoned attempts from leaking.

2. **ACP Retry Event Handling (`packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts`)**:
   - In `Session.prompt()`, added a handler for `GeminiEventType.Retry`:
     - Clears any pending tool call requests accumulated during the aborted attempt.
     - Logs a warning via `debugLogger.warn`.
     - Emits an `agent_thought_chunk` with human-readable notification and `_meta: { retry: true }`.
     - Marks the next `agent_message_chunk` with `_meta: { retry: true, reset: true }` so ACP clients can discard partial message buffers.

3. **Testing**:
   - Added unit test in `packages/core/src/core/turn.test.ts` verifying that `debugResponses`, `pendingToolCalls`, and `getResponseText()` reset on retry.
   - Added unit test in `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts` verifying that mid-stream retry events emit thought notifications, set reset metadata, and discard abandoned tool calls.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29897

## How to Validate

Run unit tests for both modified workspaces:
```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/core/turn.test.ts
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/acpSession.test.ts
```

All tests should pass.

prs.title: feat(cli): support standalone theme.json configuration for custom themes
prs.body:
Decouples custom color theme definitions from behavioral preferences in `settings.json` by automatically discovering standalone `theme.json` files from `~/.gemini/theme.json` and XDG fallback paths (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gemini/theme.json` and `~/.config/gemini/theme.json`). This allows dynamic palette generators (such as `wallust`, `pywal`, and `matugen`) to regenerate color palettes independently without overwriting user preferences like `vimMode`, model configuration, or authentication settings in `settings.json`.

## Details

- **Standalone `theme.json` Discovery (`packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.ts`)**:
  - Added `getUserThemePaths()` and `loadUserThemes()` to `ThemeManager` to discover standalone theme definitions from `~/.gemini/theme.json` (respecting `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` via `homedir()`) with fallback to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gemini/theme.json` and `~/.config/gemini/theme.json`.
  - Supports single theme objects, named theme catalog maps (`Record<string, CustomTheme>`), and `customThemes`-wrapped objects, with JSON comment support via `stripJsonComments`.
  - Enforces directory boundary checks on resolved canonical paths (`realpathSync`) so symlinks resolving outside trusted user configuration directories are skipped with a warning.
  - Gives `~/.gemini/theme.json` precedence over XDG paths and inline `settings.json` `customThemes`, deduplicating entries in `getAvailableThemes()` while keeping `settings.json` persistence completely untouched when behavioral settings or `ui.theme` are saved.
- **Startup & Interactive Refresh (`packages/cli/src/utils/terminalTheme.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useThemeCommand.ts`)**:
  - Calls `themeManager.loadUserThemes()` during `setupTerminalAndTheme` and refreshes standalone user themes when opening `/theme` or selecting a theme so external palette updates can be picked up during an active session.
- **Storage & macOS Seatbelt Configuration (`packages/core/src/config/storage.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxBuiltinProfiles.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-macos-*.sb`)**:
  - Added `Storage.getUserThemePath()` alongside `Storage.getUserKeybindingsPath()`.
  - Permitted read-only access to `~/.gemini/theme.json` in restrictive and strict macOS Seatbelt profiles (matching `settings.json` and `keybindings.json`).
- **Documentation & Tests**:
  - Documented standalone `theme.json` usage and XDG fallback paths in `docs/cli/themes.md`.
  - Added unit tests in `packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-macos-profiles.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts`, and `packages/cli/src/utils/terminalTheme.test.ts`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29997

## How to Validate

### Automated Tests

1. Run targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/themes/theme-manager.test.ts src/utils/terminalTheme.test.ts src/utils/sandbox-macos-profiles.test.ts src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts
   ```
2. Run full preflight checks:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```

### Manual Validation (Interactive Mode)

1. Create a standalone `~/.gemini/theme.json` (or `~/.config/gemini/theme.json`) containing a custom theme palette:
   ```json
   {
     "custom-wallust": {
       "name": "custom-wallust",
       "type": "custom",
       "background": {
         "primary": "#1d2021"
       },
       "text": {
         "primary": "#ebdbb2",
         "secondary": "#a89984",
         "accent": "#d3869b"
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Set `"ui": { "theme": "custom-wallust" }` alongside a behavioral setting (e.g. `"general": { "vimMode": true }`) in `~/.gemini/settings.json` without any `customThemes` block.
3. Launch Gemini CLI in interactive mode from the worktree:
   ```bash
   cd /usr/local/google/home/jesussamuel/ughcl/gemini-cli/.gemini/
   npm start
   ```
4. Verify the CLI launches directly with the `custom-wallust` palette applied and no theme-not-found dialog.
5. Run `/theme` in interactive mode:
   - Verify `custom-wallust` appears in the theme list.
   - Modify a color in `~/.gemini/theme.json` externally, run `/theme` again, and confirm the updated palette is reflected while `~/.gemini/settings.json` retains `"general": { "vimMode": true }` without any `customThemes` written into `settings.json`.

prs.title: fix(cli): resolve folder trust before entering the macOS Seatbelt sandbox
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the folder trust failure that remains under the macOS Seatbelt sandbox
once the startup crash from #28598 is fixed (#30143):

- Since #29214, the Seatbelt profiles deny the sandboxed process access to
  `~/.gemini/trustedFolders.json`. Inside the sandbox, the folder trust dialog
  could neither see existing trust decisions nor save new ones, so every launch
  showed the dialog and any choice exited with "Failed to save trust settings"
  (exit code 52).
- Folder trust is now resolved in the parent process before relaunching into
  the sandbox. An existing decision is reused. Otherwise, a terminal prompt asks
  once and saves the choice. The decision is passed to the sandboxed process
  through `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE`, which `checkPathTrust` already honors.

## Details

- New `packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxFolderTrust.ts`, called from `gemini.tsx`
  right before `start_sandbox()`. It only applies to `sandbox-exec`.
- The Seatbelt profiles are unchanged; the sandboxed process still cannot read
  or write trust settings.
- The terminal prompt mirrors the in-app dialog (same explanation, options, and
  discovery results, with ANSI escapes stripped). The in-app dialog can't be
  used before the Ink UI starts. The prompt writes through `writeToStdout`,
  because `process.stdout` is patched during startup.
- Behavior matches the in-app dialog: ending the input without an answer exits
  with code 130, and a failure to save exits with code 52.
- Non-interactive sessions without a trust decision keep the current behavior.
- Decisions set through environment variables (`--skip-trust`,
  `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE`, restricted mode) are left as they are.
- Docker and Podman are unchanged. They mount a sanitized, ephemeral
  `~/.gemini`, so they may need a similar change in a follow-up.
- Documented the behavior in `docs/cli/trusted-folders.md`.
- Based on the analysis by @luiacuaniello in #28598.

## Related Issues

Fixes #28598

Related to #30143 and #29214

## How to Validate

- Run the unit tests:

  ```bash
  npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/sandboxFolderTrust.test.ts src/gemini.test.tsx
  ```

  Expected result: all tests pass. They cover reusing existing decisions,
  prompting and saving each choice, cancellation, save failures,
  non-interactive sessions, environment overrides, other sandbox commands, and
  the prompt output.
- With `"tools": { "sandbox": true }` on macOS, a folder without a trust
  decision shows the trust prompt in the terminal before the sandbox starts.
  The choice is saved to `~/.gemini/trustedFolders.json`, and later launches
  in that folder start without prompting.
- Ran `npm run preflight`.

prs.title: fix(cli): validate model names and support direct arguments in /model command
prs.body:
In `packages/cli/src/ui/commands/modelCommand.ts`, two issues affected model selection via the `/model` slash command:

1. `/model set <model-name>` accepted any arbitrary string (such as nonexistent model names or bare flags like `--persist`) without validating whether the requested model or alias exists, updating `Config.setModel()` and only failing on the subsequent API request with a raw 400/404 error.
2. Invoking `/model <model-name>` directly with arguments unconditionally delegated to `manageModelCommand.action`, ignoring the arguments and opening the interactive selection dialog instead of applying the requested model.

This change validates model names in `setModelCommand` against built-in Gemini/Gemma models (`VALID_GEMINI_MODELS` and `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelDefinitions`), model aliases (`auto`, `pro`, `flash`, `flash-lite`, `auto-gemini-3`, `auto-gemini-2.5`), and custom user-configured model definitions/aliases, adds tab-completion for valid model names on `/model set`, and forwards non-empty arguments passed to `/model <model-name>` to `setModelCommand`.

## Details

- **`getValidModelNames` & `setModelCommand` (`packages/cli/src/ui/commands/modelCommand.ts`)**:
  - Parses `--persist` separately from positional arguments so `/model set --persist` without a model name reports a usage error instead of setting the model to `'--persist'`.
  - Validates the requested model name against `VALID_GEMINI_MODELS`, `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelDefinitions`, model aliases, `ModelConfigService.getModelDefinitions()`, and user-configured `modelConfigs.customAliases` / `modelConfigs.modelDefinitions`.
  - Emits an actionable `MessageType.ERROR` (`Invalid model "<modelName>". Run /model to view and select from available models.`) when an unrecognized model name is supplied.
  - Adds a `completion` handler to `setModelCommand` so tab-completing `/model set <partial>` suggests matching valid model names.
- **`modelCommand.action` (`packages/cli/src/ui/commands/modelCommand.ts`)**:
  - Forwards non-empty `args` to `setModelCommand.action(context, args)` while continuing to open the interactive model selection dialog when invoked without arguments (`/model` or `/model manage`).
- **Unit Test Coverage (`packages/cli/src/ui/commands/modelCommand.test.ts`)**:
  - Verifies setting valid models, persistence via `--persist`, custom model aliases from settings, usage errors when only `--persist` is passed, rejection of invalid model names, direct `/model <model-name>` invocation, and tab-completion suggestions.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29754

## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/commands/modelCommand.test.ts
   ```
2. **Full Preflight**:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. **Interactive CLI Validation**:
   1. Build the CLI package:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      ```
   2. Launch the interactive CLI:
      ```bash
      node packages/cli/dist/index.js
      ```
   3. Test rejecting an invalid model name:
      ```text
      /model set nonexistent-model
      ```
      **Expected**: Displays an error (`Invalid model "nonexistent-model". Run /model to view and select from available models.`) without changing the active model.
   4. Test setting a valid model via `/model set` or `/model <model-name>`:
      ```text
      /model set gemini-2.5-flash
      /model auto
      ```
      **Expected**: Displays `Model set to gemini-2.5-flash` and `Model set to auto`, updating the active session model.
   5. Test opening the interactive model dialog with no arguments:
      ```text
      /model
      ```
      **Expected**: Opens the interactive model configuration dialog.

prs.title: fix(cli): handle file watcher errors and permit FSEvents in macOS permissive sandbox
prs.body:
## Summary

Resolves an unhandled error during startup when initializing directory watchers
on macOS under restrictive sandbox policies:

- Adds an asynchronous `error` listener to the `fs.watch` instance in
  `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGitBranchName.ts`. If directory watching is
  restricted by the OS or kernel sandbox, the watcher gracefully closes and logs
  debug details without raising an unhandled exception.
- Adds `(allow mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.FSEvents"))` to
  `sandbox-macos-permissive-open.sb`, `sandbox-macos-permissive-proxied.sb`, and
  `sandboxBuiltinProfiles.ts` to allow filesystem event observation under
  permissive sandbox profiles.

## Details

**Type of Change**

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality
      to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update

**Notes**

- `fs.watch` reports some failures through the watcher's `error` event instead
  of throwing, so the existing `try`/`catch` around the watcher setup does not
  cover them. The new listener logs via `debugLogger.debug` and closes the
  watcher; the last known branch name stays displayed and live updates stop.
- The FSEvents rule is added as a separate, commented block, leaving the
  existing `mach-lookup` allow-list (which mirrors `baseProfile.ts`) unchanged.
  The builtin profile definitions in `sandboxBuiltinProfiles.ts` are kept in
  sync with the `.sb` files.
- The restrictive and strict profiles are unchanged. With the new listener,
  branch-name live updates are disabled there instead of raising an error.
- No documentation changes are needed.

## Related Issues

Related to #28598

## How to Validate

- Added a regression test in
  `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGitBranchName.test.tsx` verifying that
  asynchronous `EMFILE` watcher errors are intercepted and handled cleanly
  without process exit.
- Added tests in the sandbox profile validation suite
  (`packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-macos-profiles.test.ts`) verifying the
  FSEvents permission in the permissive profiles and their builtin definitions.

Run the targeted tests:

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve pending tool confirmation when escaping editor selection
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->

When a file-edit tool (`replace` / `write_file`) is awaiting user confirmation in `ToolConfirmationMessage` and the user selects **"Modify with external editor"** without a `preferredEditor` configured in settings, `EditorSettingsDialog` opens while `ToolConfirmationQueue` remains mounted. Previously, keyboard input routing and focus conflicts between `ToolConfirmationMessage`, `EditorSettingsDialog`, and the active stream-cancellation `Escape` handler caused `Escape` and directional keys inside `EditorSettingsDialog` to fail to close the dialog cleanly or to cancel/disable the pending tool approval.

This PR resolves both the primary issue reported in #30076 and the underlying modal focus and keypress priority issues that manifested during interactive testing.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->

### Main Issue (#30076)
- **Escape from Editor Selection Cancels or Disables Pending Tool Approval**:
  - While a file-edit tool is waiting for approval (`CoreToolCallStatus.AwaitingApproval`), selecting **"Modify with external editor"** calls `resolveEditorAsync`, which emits `CoreEvent.RequestEditorSelection` and awaits `CoreEvent.EditorSelected` before transitioning the tool into `isModifying: true`. As a result, `ToolConfirmationQueue` (`ToolConfirmationMessage`) and `EditorSettingsDialog` remain mounted simultaneously.
  - Pressing `Escape` while `EditorSettingsDialog` is open did not reliably dismiss only the editor selector and return to usable `Allow` / `Reject` controls:
    1. When a competing stream-cancellation `Escape` handler (`useGeminiStream` / `useAgentStream` or a parent `useKeypress` listener) ran ahead of `EditorSettingsDialog`, pressing `Escape` cancelled the ongoing turn and aborted the pending tool approval.
    2. When `ToolConfirmationMessage` intercepted `Escape`, it set `isCancelling = true` (which was never reset to `false`). Once `EditorSettingsDialog` exited and `resolveConfirmation` updated the tool call with a new `correlationId` (recreating `confirm` in `ToolActionsContext` and `handleConfirm` in `ToolConfirmationMessage`), `useEffect([isCancelling, handleConfirm])` immediately fired `handleConfirm(ToolConfirmationOutcome.Cancel)` against the new `correlationId`—or left `isCancelling` stuck at `true` so subsequent `Escape` presses were ignored.

### Secondary Issues (Identified During Interactive Testing)
1. **Persistent Cursor Lock on `ToolConfirmationMessage` (Menu 1)**:
   - `ToolConfirmationQueue` passed a hardcoded `isFocused={true}` to `ToolConfirmationMessage`, keeping its `priority: true` (`KeypressPriority.High`) `<RadioButtonSelect />` active while `EditorSettingsDialog` registered its `<RadioButtonSelect />` lists at default `KeypressPriority.Normal`. Pressing `Up` or `Down` arrows moved the selection cursor in `ToolConfirmationMessage` instead of `EditorSettingsDialog`.
2. **Focus Desynchronization on `Tab` & Modal Input Starvation**:
   - Pressing `Tab` updated `focusedSection` visually inside `EditorSettingsDialog`, but directional arrow keys and `Enter` continued to be consumed by `ToolConfirmationMessage` at `KeypressPriority.High`.
3. **`Escape` Key No-Op / Deadlock in `EditorSettingsDialog` (Menu 2)**:
   - Because `ToolConfirmationMessage`'s `useKeypress` listener ran at `KeypressPriority.High` (`priority: true`) and returned `true` on `Escape` (firing `confirm(Cancel)` against the already-consumed first `correlationId` while `resolveEditorAsync` was still awaiting `CoreEvent.EditorSelected`), `EditorSettingsDialog`'s `KeypressPriority.Normal` `onExit` listener never received `Escape`, leaving `EditorSettingsDialog` stuck open.
4. **Parent-Child LIFO Stack Inversion in `useKeypress`**:
   - `useKeypress` included `onKeypress` in its subscription `useEffect` dependency array (`[isActive, onKeypress, subscribe, unsubscribe, priority]`). Because React executes `useEffect` hooks bottom-up (children before parents), any parent component passing an inline `onKeypress` callback unsubscribed and re-subscribed *after* child modal dialogs (`EditorSettingsDialog`) mounted, jumping to the top of `KeypressContext`'s LIFO dispatch stack.

### How It Is Fixed
1. **Suspend `ToolConfirmationMessage` Focus When `EditorSettingsDialog` Is Open (`packages/cli/src/ui/components/ToolConfirmationQueue.tsx`)**:
   - Read `isEditorDialogOpen` from `useUIState()` and pass `isFocused={!isEditorDialogOpen}` to `ToolConfirmationMessage` so its high-priority `useKeypress` and `<RadioButtonSelect />` hooks deactivate while `EditorSettingsDialog` is open and automatically regain focus when `EditorSettingsDialog` closes.
2. **Reset `isCancelling` State on Dispatch (`packages/cli/src/ui/components/messages/ToolConfirmationMessage.tsx`)**:
   - Call `setIsCancelling(false)` inside the `useEffect` before invoking `handleConfirm(ToolConfirmationOutcome.Cancel)` so cancellation state is a clean one-shot transition and cannot re-fire when `handleConfirm` updates or leave `Escape` disabled.
3. **Prioritize `EditorSettingsDialog` Listeners (`packages/cli/src/ui/components/EditorSettingsDialog.tsx`)**:
   - Register `EditorSettingsDialog`'s `useKeypress` hook (`Tab` / `Escape`) and both `<RadioButtonSelect />` components (`editor` and `scope` sections) with `priority: true` (`KeypressPriority.High`).
4. **Preserve LIFO Subscription Order Across Re-renders (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useKeypress.ts`)**:
   - Store `onKeypress` in a `useRef` updated via `useEffect` and remove `onKeypress` from the subscription `useEffect` dependency array (`[isActive, subscribe, unsubscribe, priority]`), ensuring parent re-renders do not re-subscribe above newly mounted child modals.
5. **Gate Stream-Cancellation `Escape` Handler (`packages/cli/src/ui/AppContainer.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useAgentStream.ts`)**:
   - Pass `isEditorDialogOpen` from `AppContainer` to `useGeminiStream` and `useAgentStream` and gate their `Escape` stream-cancellation `useKeypress` hooks with `!isEditorDialogOpen`.

## Related Issues

<!-- Use keywords to auto-close issues (Closes #123, Fixes #456). If this PR is
only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

fixes: [#30076](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/30076)

## How to Validate
