prs.title: fix(cli): wait for piped stdin EOF and avoid destroying process.stdin
prs.body:
## Summary

    Fixes two piped-input bugs in `readStdin()` (`packages/cli/src/utils/readStdin.ts`):

    1. **Silent data loss on slow pipes (`> 500ms`):** Removes the unconditional `500ms` timeout that resolved `readStdin()` to `''` before slow upstream commands emitted their first byte, causing `gemini -p "..."` to silently drop all piped context (or fail with exit code `42` when invoked without `-p`).
    2. **Broken `process.stdin` reuse on `> 8MB` truncation:** Replaces `process.stdin.destroy()` with listener cleanup plus `process.stdin.unpipe()` and `process.stdin.pause()`, keeping the global `process.stdin` stream intact (`destroyed === false`) for any subsequent reads or stream operations.

## Details

    - **Early TTY and closed-stream guards (`readStdin.ts`):** Returns `''` immediately when `process.stdin.isTTY`, `process.stdin.destroyed`, or `process.stdin.readableEnded` is truthy so interactive terminals and closed streams never block.
    - **EOF-driven piped reading (`readStdin.ts`):** Waits for `'end'` (or `'error'`, or `MAX_STDIN_SIZE` truncation) on non-TTY piped streams instead of cutting off after `500ms`, with a `settled` guard and safe `Buffer` / `string` chunk handling.
    - **Non-destructive truncation (`readStdin.ts`):** When piped input exceeds `MAX_STDIN_SIZE` (`8MB`), truncates cleanly on a valid UTF-8 character boundary (including `maxBytes <= 0` when an earlier chunk landed on the exact `8MB` boundary), detaches `readStdin`'s listeners while preserving the no-op `'error'` guard, and calls `unpipe()` + `pause()` instead of `destroy()`.
    - **Unit test coverage (`readStdin.test.ts`, `gemini.test.tsx`):** Added unit tests covering slow pipes (`> 500ms` initial delay and multi-chunk delays), TTY / ended / destroyed guards, `Buffer` chunks, exact `8MB` boundary overflow, and `PassThrough` stream reuse after oversize truncation; ensured non-piped `main()` test suites in `gemini.test.tsx` explicitly stub `process.stdin.isTTY = true` in non-TTY test runners.

## Related Issues

 Fixes #29312

## How to Validate

    1. **Run unit tests, typecheck, and linter:**
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/readStdin.test.ts src/utils/readStdin_safety.test.ts src/gemini.test.tsx src/gemini_cleanup.test.tsx
       npm run typecheck
       npm run lint
       ```
    2. **Validate slow piped input in the terminal CLI (previously dropped stdin and returned `NONE`):**
       ```bash
       npm run build
       (sleep 0.8; echo "SECRET_WORD_BANANA_42") | GEMINI_CLI_NO_RELAUNCH=true node packages/cli/dist/index.js -p "Reply ONLY with the exact secret word from the piped input, or NONE if no piped input was provided."
       ```
       Expected output: `SECRET_WORD_BANANA_42`.

prs.title: fix(core): prevent thoughtSignature-only turns and preserve multimodal tool responses
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes `400 Bad Request ("Requests ending with a model turn are not supported")` and empty-response retry loops when using `read_file` on images (or receiving `thoughtSignature`-only model responses after tool execution).
When Gemini 2.5 / 3 models return a post-tool response containing only `thoughtSignature` (or empty text alongside `thoughtSignature`), the history validation and sanitization pipeline previously treated `thoughtSignature` as an active content key. This allowed empty/signature-only model turns into `agentHistory`, bypassed `closeUnansweredToolResponseTurn`, and caused `stripToolCallIdPrefixes` to drop the model turn *after* `ensureTerminalUserTurn` had already run—leaving the outgoing API payload ending on a `model` turn or triggering an invalid-stream retry loop. Additionally, multimodal tool response parts (such as sibling `inlineData` image parts) were dropped in subagent execution (`LocalAgentExecutor`) and when dynamic model configuration lacked an explicit `multimodalToolUse` feature flag.

## Details

1. **Exclude `thoughtSignature` from active content-key checks (`packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts`):**
   - Updated [`isValidContent`](file:///usr/local/google/home/tadipavan/pavan/gemini-cli-b-30074-readFile_Image/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L190-L204), [`isEmptyTextPart`](file:///usr/local/google/home/tadipavan/pavan/gemini-cli-b-30074-readFile_Image/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L1930-L1941), and [`stripToolCallIdPrefixes`](file:///usr/local/google/home/tadipavan/pavan/gemini-cli-b-30074-readFile_Image/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L2026-L2038) to ignore `'thoughtSignature'` when checking whether a `Part` carries active payload keys (`functionCall`, `functionResponse`, `inlineData`, `fileData`, etc.).
   - Updated [`closeUnansweredToolResponseTurn`](file:///usr/local/google/home/tadipavan/pavan/gemini-cli-b-30074-readFile_Image/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L909-L950) to check `!hasNonEmptyParts(targetTurn.content)` and use immutable `this.agentHistory.set(...)` when inserting `INTERRUPTED_RESPONSE_PLACEHOLDER`.
   - Reordered [`makeApiCallAndProcessStream`](file:///usr/local/google/home/tadipavan/pavan/gemini-cli-b-30074-readFile_Image/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L1221-L1232) so `stripToolCallIdPrefixes` executes *before* `ensureTerminalUserTurn`, and preserved `model` turns that immediately follow a `user` `functionResponse` turn by falling back to `INTERRUPTED_RESPONSE_PLACEHOLDER` instead of dropping the turn.
2. **Preserve multimodal tool support in dynamic model configs (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`):**
   - Updated [`supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse`](file:///usr/local/google/home/tadipavan/pavan/gemini-cli-b-30074-readFile_Image/packages/core/src/config/models.ts#L679-L698) to pass `config?.getHasAccessToPreviewModel?.() ?? true` to `resolveModel` and fall back to `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/.test(resolved)` when `definition?.features?.multimodalToolUse` is `undefined`.
3. **Preserve sibling multimodal `Part[]` in `LocalAgentExecutor` (`packages/core/src/agents/local-executor.ts`):**
   - Changed `syncResults` in [`processFunctionCalls`](file:///usr/local/google/home/tadipavan/pavan/gemini-cli-b-30074-readFile_Image/packages/core/src/agents/local-executor.ts#L1164-L1396) from `Map<string, Part>` to `Map<string, Part[]>` so all `call.response.responseParts` (including sibling `inlineData` image parts when `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` is `false`) are forwarded instead of only `responseParts[0]`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30074

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted unit test suites covering `GeminiChat`, model feature resolution, and `LocalAgentExecutor`:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- \
     src/core/geminiChat.test.ts \
     src/config/models.test.ts \
     src/agents/local-executor.test.ts
   ```
2. Run the full `read_file` and history hardening test suites:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- \
     src/tools/read-file.test.ts \
     src/utils/generateContentResponseUtilities.test.ts \
     src/utils/historyHardening.test.ts
   ```

prs.title: fix(cli): forward IDE auth token and accept container host header for sandboxed IDE connections
prs.body:
## Summary

IDE integration (`/ide status`, `/ide enable`, open-file context, native diffs)
does not work when Gemini CLI runs inside a container sandbox
(`GEMINI_SANDBOX=docker|podman|runsc|lxc`). Users see a generic
"Failed to connect to IDE companion extension" message. This PR fixes the two
application-level breaks in the sandbox → VS Code connection path:

- The sandbox launcher never forwarded `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN`, so every
  MCP request from the container was rejected with **401**.
- The companion extension's Host allow-list rejected the
  `host.docker.internal:<port>` header the CLI sends from containers with
  **403 Invalid Host header**.

Both changes are minimal, additive, and preserve the existing security model.

## Details

**Root cause.** The IDE ↔ CLI link is HTTP over host loopback, authenticated
with a bearer token that the extension publishes two ways: a connection file in
the host tmpdir (`/tmp/gemini/ide/gemini-ide-server-<pid>-<port>.json`) and the
`GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN` env var in the integrated terminal. Inside a
sandbox:

1. `TMPDIR` is a fresh, empty `gemini-sandbox-*` directory, so
   `getConnectionConfigFromFile()` finds nothing and the CLI falls back to env
   vars.
2. `sandbox.ts` forwarded `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT`,
   `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_WORKSPACE_PATH` and `TERM_PROGRAM`, but **not** the token →
   `establishHttpConnection(port, undefined)` → 401.
3. `getIdeServerHost()` returns `host.docker.internal` when `/.dockerenv` is
   present (#7464). Eight days later #8512 added a Host allow-list containing
   only `localhost:<port>` / `127.0.0.1:<port>`. The two changes never worked
   together; #13627 has a `curl` repro of the resulting 403.
4. `establishHttpConnection` swallows the underlying error, so users only ever
   saw the generic connection failure — which is why this went unnoticed.

**Changes.**

- `packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox.ts`
  - Add `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN` to the IDE env passthrough loop used for
    docker/podman/runsc.
  - Add the same key to the LXC `envVarsToForward` map so both backends stay in
    lockstep.
- `packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts`
  - Add `host.docker.internal:${this.port}` to `allowedHosts`.

**Design decisions.**

- Kept the Host allow-list exact-match (no wildcard, no regex). The port is
  random per server instance and bearer auth is still enforced after the Host
  check, so the DNS-rebinding hardening from #8512 is intact.
- Did not mount the host connection-file directory into the sandbox; the env
  var path already exists and mounting would interact with the uid check in
  `verifyAndReadFile` (sandbox runs as `node`).
- Did not change `establishHttpConnection`'s error handling to keep the diff
  surgical; a follow-up to log the real failure reason is worthwhile.

**Why previous tests missed this.** `sandbox.test.ts` asserted the docker argv
contained `run`/`--rm`/`--name`/`SANDBOX=` but never asserted on the IDE env
vars, and `ide-server.test.ts` tested `localhost:<port>` (allow) and `evil.com`
(deny) but never the container hostname. Neither suite exercises the two
packages together, and the integration tests don't run with a sandbox and a
live companion extension. The new tests close both gaps at the unit level.

**Known limitation (gVisor).** This PR is necessary but may not be sufficient
for `GEMINI_SANDBOX=runsc`. The extension still binds `127.0.0.1` on the host,
so reachability from gVisor's user-space netstack depends on the runsc network
mode and whether `host.docker.internal` is proxied to host loopback (Docker
Desktop) or resolves to the bridge gateway (native Linux). A transport that
avoids host TCP entirely (e.g. a Unix socket) is the proper follow-up for full
gVisor support; this PR therefore uses `Related to` rather than `Fixes` for
#21331.

## Related Issues

- Fixes #13627
- Related to #21331 (resolves the auth/Host-header breaks reported there;
  gVisor network reachability tracked separately)
- Context: #7464 (introduced `host.docker.internal` fallback), #8512
  (introduced the Host allow-list)

## How to Validate

**Automated**

```bash
npm run build
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/sandbox.test.ts
npm test -w gemini-cli-vscode-ide-companion -- src/ide-server.test.ts
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/
```

New tests:

- `sandbox.test.ts` › `should forward IDE connection environment variables into
  the container` — asserts `--env GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN=…` is present
  alongside port and workspace path in the `docker run` argv.
- `ide-server.test.ts` › `should allow requests from a container sandbox via
  host.docker.internal` — Host `host.docker.internal:<port>` passes the host
  check (reaches MCP handler → 400, not 403).
- `ide-server.test.ts` › `should deny host.docker.internal with a mismatched
  port` — still 403.

**Manual (Linux, Docker, VS Code with the companion extension)**

1. Open a workspace folder in VS Code, open the integrated terminal and confirm
   `echo $GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT $GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN` prints both.
2. Before this change: `GEMINI_SANDBOX=docker gemini` → `/ide status` →
   🔴 `Failed to connect to IDE companion extension in VS Code…`
3. After this change (CLI rebuilt, extension reloaded):
   `GEMINI_SANDBOX=docker gemini` → `/ide status` → 🟢 Connected;
   `/ide enable`, open-file context and `openDiff` work.
4. Isolate each break with curl from inside the sandbox image:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm -it --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
     -e PORT=$GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT -e TOK=$GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN \
     <sandbox-image> bash
   # Old extension:            → {"error":"Invalid Host header"} (403)
   # New extension, no token:  → Unauthorized (401)
   # New extension + token:    → MCP 400/200 (past auth)
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://host.docker.internal:$PORT/mcp
   ```
5. Edge cases: `GEMINI_SANDBOX=lxc` (token forwarded via `envVarsToForward`);
   running outside any sandbox (unchanged — connection file path still used);
   `Host: evil.com` and `Host: host.docker.internal:<other-port>` still 403.

**Results on this branch**

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `sandbox.test.ts` | 45 passed |
| `ide-server.test.ts` | 14 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing) |
| `core/src/ide/**` (regression) | 158 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing) |
| `npm run preflight` | ✅ exit 0 — build, lint, typecheck, all workspace suites (~16k tests) |
| ESLint / Prettier on changed files | clean, no new `eslint-disable` |

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — suggest a
      follow-up note in `docs/ide-integration/index.md` › "Using with
      sandboxing" clarifying the gVisor limitation
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [ ] Linux
    - [x] npm run (preflight + unit tests)
    - [ ] npx
    - [x] Docker (end-to-end with live VS Code — see verification comment)

## Summary

Preserve meaningful leading and trailing whitespace in `@file` references across both the interactive CLI (`atCommandProcessor.ts`) and ACP sessions (`acpSession.ts`).

## Details

- `ReadManyFilesTool` (`packages/core/src/tools/read-many-files.ts`) formats each read file's content as `--- ${filePath} ---\n\n${fileContentForLlm}\n\n`.

- Removed `.trim()` when assigning `fileActualContent = match[2]` in both `atCommandProcessor.ts` and `acpSession.ts`, and added parameterized unit tests in `atCommandProcessor.test.ts` and `acpSession.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(core): fix Windows PowerShell substitution false positives and policy handling
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes severe Windows PowerShell shell-command regressions introduced in v0.63.0 where routine developer commands containing parentheses in arguments, method/static calls, control-flow headers, or `-NonInteractive` shell wrappers were falsely blocked as command substitutions, and where explicitly user-confirmed or policy-allowed (`--yolo` / `allowCommandSubstitution = true`) substitutions were still unconditionally blocked in `ShellToolInvocation.execute()`.

## Details

- **Linear-time (`O(N)`) PowerShell substitution scanner (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`)**:
  - Rewrote `detectPowerShellSubstitution` as a stateful character/token scanner that tracks PowerShell quoting rules (ASCII + Unicode single/double quotes, backtick escapes inside double quotes, `@'...'@` and `@"..."@` here-strings, `#` line comments, `<# ... #>` block comments, and `${...}` braced variables).
  - Properly distinguishes safe PowerShell parentheses (command string/path arguments like `dir C:\Program Files (x86)\Git` or `git log --grep="\"(feat|fix)\""`, instance/static calls like `$str.Trim()` and `[System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath('foo')`, control-flow headers like `if (...)` / `switch -regex ($x)`, and pure parenthesized expressions) from actual command substitutions (`$(...)`, `@(...)`, bare `(whoami)` subexpressions, and scriptblock `.Invoke()`).
  - Rejects comment-spoofed closing parentheses (`echo ($a <# ) #> ; whoami)`), redirections, assignments, pipelines, and nested here-strings inside parenthesized expressions, and enforces monotonic lookahead watermarks to guarantee `O(N)` runtime without ReDoS risk.
- **Shell wrapper unwrapping & `pwsh.exe` flags (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`)**:
  - Rewrote `stripShellWrapper` with token-level scanners supporting full executable paths, `.exe` suffixes, `-NonInteractive` / PowerShell parameter prefixes, and `powershell.exe` / `pwsh.exe` / `cmd.exe` / POSIX shells while refusing to unwrap double-quoted wrappers when outer-shell `$()` substitution would become hidden inside inner single quotes.
  - Updated `getShellConfiguration` so `pwsh.exe` also receives `-NonInteractive` alongside `-NoProfile` and `-Command`.
  - Updated `extractPowerShellDetails` to extract static and scriptblock `.Invoke()` calls and propagate `hasCommandSubstitution` without falling back to the Bash parser on PowerShell substitution syntax.
- **Policy-aware & confirmation-aware substitution handling (`packages/core/src/policy/*`, `packages/core/src/scheduler/*`, `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`)**:
  - Added `allowCommandSubstitution` support to policy rules (`yolo.toml`, `toml-loader.ts`, `policy-engine.ts`, `config.ts`, `docs/reference/policy-engine.md`).
  - Propagated `confirmedByUser` / `isUserConfirmed` through `resolveConfirmation`, `Scheduler`, and `ToolExecutor` strictly when a user interactively approves a confirmation prompt (resetting across `ModifyWithEditor` edits).
  - Updated `ShellToolInvocation` so commands with command substitution are permitted only when explicitly confirmed by the user or explicitly allowed by policy (`allowCommandSubstitution = true`), while unconfirmed or untrusted/tainted substitutions continue to be denied.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29738

## How to Validate

1. Run unit and policy safety test suites:
   ```bash
   npx vitest run \
     packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/policy/shell-safety.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/policy/policy-updater.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts \
     packages/core/src/scheduler/confirmation.test.ts
   ```
2. Verify PowerShell false positives from #29738 are no longer flagged as command substitution while real substitutions remain detected:
   - Allowed (`false`): `node -e "console.log(\"hello (world)\")"`, `git log --grep="\"(feat|fix)\""`, `$str.Trim()`, `[System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath('foo')`, `Get-ChildItem | Where-Object { $_.Name.EndsWith('.ts') }`, `dir C:\Program Files (x86)\Git`, `if (($a -eq 1) -and ($b -eq 2)) { Write-Host ok }`
   - Flagged (`true`): `echo $(whoami)`, `echo "$(whoami)"`, `echo @(whoami)`, `echo (whoami)`, `{ whoami }.Invoke()`
3. Verify policy enforcement with the bundled CLI:
   - With `allowCommandSubstitution` omitted (`false`), `run_shell_command` with `echo $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` prompts (`ASK_USER`) in interactive mode and is denied in non-interactive `--approval-mode default`.
   - With `--yolo` or a policy rule setting `allowCommandSubstitution = true` for all inner and outer commands, `echo $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` executes as configured.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx

prs.title: Fix zizmor template-injection findings in eval-pr workflow
prs.body:
Summary

This PR fixes the mandatory zizmor findings in .github/workflows/eval-pr.yml caused by injecting GitHub Actions expressions directly into bash scripts.

The problem was that values such as ${{ github.base_ref }}, ${{ github.actor }}, ${{ github.repository }}, and ${{ steps.analysis.outputs.* }} were being interpolated directly inside shell commands. zizmor flags this as template-injection, which is treated as a blocking security issue.

What changed

Moved workflow values into env: variables before shell execution
Replaced direct ${{ ... }} interpolation inside run: blocks with safe shell variables
Used quoted variable references to avoid unsafe expansion
Kept the PR guidance/comment behavior unchanged while making the workflow compliant with the repo’s mandatory security checks
Why this matters

These findings were reported by zizmor as:

template-injection
code injection via template expansion: may expand into attacker-controllable code
This was causing the workflow to fail with exit code 14 and block the job due to mandatory security checks.

Validation

Re-run the GitHub Actions security scan / zizmor check
Confirm .github/workflows/eval-pr.yml passes the mandatory checks without regressing the PR eval workflow behavior

prs.title: fix(cli): use isSubpath for theme file home-directory check
prs.body:
## Summary

Replaces the naive string prefix check (`canonicalPath.startsWith(homeDir)`) in `ThemeManager.loadThemeFromFile` with `isSubpath(homeDir, canonicalPath)` from `@google/gemini-cli-core` so that:
1. Theme files in sibling directories that share the home directory string prefix (e.g. `/home/albert/theme.json` when home is `/home/al`) are properly rejected.
2. Valid theme files inside the home directory with differing path or drive-letter casing on Windows and macOS (e.g. `c:/users/me/theme.json` when `os.homedir()` is `C:\Users\me`) are accepted.

## Details

- `ThemeManager.loadThemeFromFile` (`packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.ts`) previously checked `!canonicalPath.startsWith(homeDir)` to verify that a custom theme file resides within the user's home directory.
- Because `startsWith` performs a raw string comparison without checking path-segment boundaries or platform case sensitivity:
  - Sibling directories sharing the home directory prefix bypassed the check.
  - On Windows and macOS, valid paths inside the home directory whose resolved casing differed from `homedir()` were falsely rejected as outside the home directory.
- `@google/gemini-cli-core` already provides `isSubpath(parentPath, childPath)` (`packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts`), which compares by path segments via `path.relative` and handles case-insensitivity on `win32` and `darwin` (used for the same purpose in `extension-manager.ts` and `ideBridge.ts`).
- Added unit tests in `packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.test.ts` covering sibling-prefix rejection and case-insensitive home path acceptance on `win32` and `darwin`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29955

## How to Validate

1. Run the `theme-manager` unit test suite:
   ```bash
   npm --prefix packages/cli test -- src/ui/themes/theme-manager.test.ts
   ```
2. Manual verification (sibling directory prefix rejection):
   - Create `/tmp/theme-test/al` (as `HOME`) and `/tmp/theme-test/albert/sibling-theme.json`.
   - Configure `"ui": { "theme": "/tmp/theme-test/albert/sibling-theme.json" }` in `/tmp/theme-test/al/.gemini/settings.json`.
   - Launch Gemini CLI with `HOME=/tmp/theme-test/al` and verify that the sibling theme is rejected with `Theme file at "/tmp/theme-test/albert/sibling-theme.json" is outside your home directory. Only load themes from trusted sources.`

## Summary

Agent definitions in `~/.gemini/agents/` (or a project's `.gemini/agents/`) are skipped when the `.md` file is a symlink. `loadAgentsFromDirectory()` filters directory entries with `Dirent.isFile()`, which returns `false` for symlinks, so linked agent files never get read.

prs.title: ci(chained_e2e): don't expose GEMINI_API_KEY to fork-controlled code
prs.body:
## What
`chained_e2e.yml` runs on `workflow_run` (base-repo context, with secrets) and checks out the fork PR's code (via the artifact from `trigger_e2e.yml`), then runs `npm ci` / build / integration tests with `secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY` in scope. This means fork-controlled code (npm lifecycle scripts, build, tests) executes in the trusted context with the production Gemini API key readable.

This PR gates the key so it is only passed when the checked-out repository is the base repo; fork-originated runs still build and run non-secret tests, but the production key is never exposed to untrusted code.

## Why
Defense-in-depth for the classic `workflow_run` + fork-checkout ("pwn request") pattern. Today the only control is the repo's fork-PR-approval setting, and the pinned `actions/checkout` (v4.3.0) predates GitHub's built-in `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout` guard, so GitHub's native mitigation does not apply here. Scoping the secret out of the fork-controlled path removes the highest-value target without disabling fork E2E.

## Note
If full fork E2E with the key is required, the recommended alternative is the trusted-base pattern (run untrusted PR code in a secret-less job; run secret-requiring steps only on trusted code) or an `environment:` approval on the secret-bearing jobs. Happy to adjust to whichever you prefer.

prs.title: fix(core): only replace true cycles with [Circular] in safeJsonStringify
prs.body:
## Summary

`safeJsonStringify` replaced any object it saw a second time with `"[Circular]"`, even when there was no cycle. The telemetry file exporters use it, and the OpenTelemetry SDK shares one `endTime` array across all data points in a collection and one `boundaries` array per histogram. As a result, every metric data point after the first in the telemetry outfile lost its `endTime` and `boundaries`. Other callers (`RecordingContentGenerator`, `LoggingContentGenerator`, the message bus) lose data in the same way whenever an object is shared.

## Details

- **Root cause** (`packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.ts`): the replacer added every visited object to a `WeakSet` and never removed it, so "seen before" was treated as "circular".
- **Fix:** keep only the ancestors of the value currently being visited (the path from the root). An object is replaced with `"[Circular]"` only if it is one of its own ancestors, which is the definition of a cycle. Shared, non-cyclic references are now serialized in full each time. Output for inputs without shared references is unchanged.
- **Tests** (`packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts`): four new cases that fail on the old implementation and pass now:
  - the same object referenced from two keys, and twice in an array;
  - a shared array referenced at several different depths;
  - a true cycle mixed with shared references (the cycle is still replaced, the sharing is not);
  - OpenTelemetry-style data points that share `endTime` and `boundaries`.

  All existing circular-reference tests pass unchanged.
- No user-facing documentation changes.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29406

## How to Validate

1. Run the unit tests for the utility:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: 12 tests pass.

2. To confirm the new tests guard the fix, revert only `safeJsonStringify.ts` and re-run the same command.

   Expected: the four shared-reference tests fail (the second occurrence is returned as `"[Circular]"`).

3. Run the suites of the modules that use the function:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/telemetry src/core src/utils src/confirmation-bus src/tools/mcp-tool.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: all pass. (On Windows without symlink privileges, `fileUtils` and `planUtils` have two `EPERM` symlink failures that also occur on `main`.)

4. Lint, formatting and types:

   ```bash
   npx eslint packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.ts packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts
   npx prettier --check packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.ts packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts
   npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli-core
   ```

prs.title: fix(telemetry): buffer chat compression events until the OTel SDK is ready
prs.body:
## Summary

`logChatCompression` was the only logger in `packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.ts` that emitted its OTel log record and metrics directly instead of going through `bufferTelemetryEvent`. If chat compression fired before the OTel SDK finished initializing, the `gemini_cli.chat_compression` log event and its metrics data point were emitted against a no-op provider and silently dropped.

## Details

- **Fix** (`packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.ts`): wrap the OTel `logger.emit` and `recordChatCompressionMetrics` calls in `bufferTelemetryEvent`, the same pattern every other logger in the file uses. The Clearcut call stays outside the wrapper, as in the sibling functions.
- **Test** (`packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts`): added `defers OTEL emission until the SDK is initialized`, which stubs `bufferTelemetryEvent` as a no-op and asserts that Clearcut is still called while the OTel emit and `recordChatCompressionMetrics` are not. This mirrors the existing `logModelRouting` buffering test. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- No user-facing behavior or documentation changes.

## Related Issues

Fixes #23445

## How to Validate

1. Run the telemetry test suite:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/telemetry
   ```

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts -t logChatCompression
   ```

issues.title: Sandbox enforcement probe fails with CreateProcessW error 2 on Windows when `failIfUnavailable: true` (managed settings)

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
**Environment**
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 (stable). Also reproduced on 1.0.106-9 and 1.0.106-10 (pre-release).
- Windows 11 Pro, build 26200.9711, x64. Administrator account with UAC enabled; the Copilot session runs with a standard token.
- Managed settings file: `%ProgramFiles%\GitHubCopilot\managed-settings.json`.

**Managed settings that reproduce it**
```json
{
  "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "failIfUnavailable": true, "allowBypass": false },
  "permissions": { "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable" }
}
```

**Steps**
1. Save the file above as the managed settings file.
2. Run from an interactive desktop session: `copilot --sandbox --allow-all-tools -s -p "Run exactly this command with cmd /c and report only the output line: echo sandbox-probe"`
3. Repeat.

**Expected:** `sandbox-probe`.

**Actual (every run):**
```
Error executing prompt: Error: Request session.send failed with message: This session is blocked because your organization's sandbox policy requires enforcement, but the sandbox is unavailable: backend_error: CreateProcessW failed with error code 2 (0x00000002). (CreateProcessW(PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_SECURITY_ENVIRONMENT) failed: WIN32_ERROR(2) ...)
```
Earlier variant of the same error: `sandbox enforcement probe exited with status -1073741502`.

**Observations**
- Removing `failIfUnavailable` makes the sandbox start, so the failure is specific to the enforcement probe.
- Removing any one of `allowBypass`, `addCurrentWorkingDirectory`, `auth`, or `permissions` does not fix it (3 runs each).
- With no managed file, sandboxed `cmd /c` works in the same session.
- The MXC runner (`wxc-exec.exe`) with the same filesystem policy, UI disabled, passed 10/10, so the backend itself works.
- The same probe passes 3/3 when run from an interactive PowerShell window, and 5/5 when run from a scheduled task in the logged-on session. It fails in non-interactive SSH sessions.

**Question:** Is the enforcement probe expected to pass on this configuration? If not, what does it need (UI access, a particular path, a helper binary)?

issues.title: Sandbox: report the extra temp-storage read-write rule in sandbox.decision, and allow opting out

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
When a host passes a sandbox config with exactly one read-write path, the resolved policy reports two read-write rules (`sandbox.decision` / `policy_resolved` shows `readwrite: 2`). The second one is the temporary-storage grant, which follows `$TMPDIR`. It is not named in the event, and the schema's `readwritePaths` does not mention it either; the schema only says temporary storage "follows its own rules and stays granted".

Repro (Linux, bubblewrap, Copilot CLI 1.0.105; also seen with the SDK 1.0.24 runtime):
1. Start a session with a sandbox config whose only read-write path is the project folder, `addCurrentWorkingDirectory: false`, `allowDevToolAccess: false`.
2. Approve `touch "$TMPDIR/x"`: it succeeds. A sibling folder outside the project is refused, as expected.
3. The `sandbox.decision` event lists `readwrite: 2` without saying what the second rule is.

Requests:
1. Include the resolved rule paths (or at least the temp-storage path) in `sandbox.decision`, so a host can show the user exactly what is writable.
2. Offer an opt-out for the temp-storage grant (for example `allowTempStorage: false`), for hosts that want a strict policy and can give the session its own scratch folder.

issues.title: ACP `session/new` reports a `model` that the session is not running

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Over ACP (`copilot --acp`), the `session/new` response lists a `model` config option with `currentValue: "claude-sonnet-5.5"`, but the session doesn't use that model until the client sets it explicitly with `session/set_config_option`. Until then:

- the session runs a different model, and
- `session/set_config_option` for `reasoning_effort` fails with `-32603 "Request session.model.setReasoningEffort failed with message: This model does not support reasoning_effort configuration."`, although the reported model offers `reasoning_effort` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`) and the response already reports `reasoning_effort: "medium"`.

Setting `model` to the value `session/new` already reports makes the `reasoning_effort` change succeed. The `configOptions` array returned by that `set_config_option` is identical to the one from `session/new`, so a client can't tell from the protocol that anything changed.

The reproduction below needs no prompt and shows the `reasoning_effort` rejection. The wrong model was observed separately, in real use: in one T3 Code setup, sessions that showed `claude-sonnet-5.5` recorded `session.model_change` events to `gpt-6.1-sol` in `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`. ACP clients reasonably skip setting a config option that already has the value they want (T3 Code does), so they hit both whenever the user picks the model Copilot reports as current.

## Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 (Homebrew, macOS arm64). Reproduced with a fresh `COPILOT_HOME` containing only a copied `config.json`, which has no `model` setting.

## Steps to reproduce

No prompt is needed. Send these ACP frames to `copilot --acp --no-custom-instructions --disable-builtin-mcps`, which a short Node script can do:

1. `initialize {protocolVersion: 1, clientCapabilities: {}}`
2. `session/new {cwd, mcpServers: []}`
3. `session/set_config_option {sessionId, configId: "reasoning_effort", value: "low"}`
4. `session/set_config_option {sessionId, configId: "model", value: <model currentValue from step 2>}`
5. `session/set_config_option {sessionId, configId: "reasoning_effort", value: "low"}`

Output (`model` and `reasoning_effort` current values from each response):

```
session/new ok [["model","claude-sonnet-5.5"],["reasoning_effort","medium"]]
effort=low (no model set) ERROR {"code":-32603,"message":"Request session.model.setReasoningEffort failed with message: This model does not support reasoning_effort configuration."}
model=<reported> explicitly ok [["model","claude-sonnet-5.5"],["reasoning_effort","medium"]]
effort=low (after model set) ok [["model","claude-sonnet-5.5"],["reasoning_effort","low"]]
```

## Expected behavior

The model `session/new` reports as `currentValue` is the model the session runs. Setting `reasoning_effort` right after `session/new` succeeds for that model, just as it does after the same model is set explicitly.

## Additional context

- The `session/new` response also reports `models.currentModelId: "claude-sonnet-5.5"`. I assume it is just as inaccurate, but I didn't test it separately.
- I only checked `session/new`. I couldn't check `session/load`, because a session that never received a prompt isn't saved (`session/load` returns `-32002 Session ... not found`), and I didn't send prompts.
- Workaround for ACP clients: after `session/new`, send `session/set_config_option` for `model` even when the value already matches.

— Opus 5.5 with Claude Code, reviewed by GPT 6.1 Sol

issues.title: Let the model replace a junk tool result with a one-line summary (model-judged context pruning)

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

**TL;DR:** When a tool call returns junk the model didn't intend, let the model **swap that output for a one-line summary** before the turn ends.
Pay for it once; keep the context clean for the rest of the session.

![Human vs AI: the human looks away from junk output, the AI re-reads it every turn](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/nicezic/69f13fde6fa080a571825b56fd76392d/raw/pruning-demo.gif)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Why prevention can't fix this**
> You open a file or run a command *because* you don't know what's in it, so its output size can't be predicted in advance.
> A human glances at junk and looks away. A model re-reads it on every turn.
> **This gives the model the ability to look away.** 🙈

### Proposed solution

#### Sequence

```
TODAY
  turn N        grep -r ...   ──►  ~40 KB of target/ build fingerprints
                model         ──►  "oops, irrelevant"   (but can't drop it)
  turn N+1..50  every request ──►  re-sends the same ~40 KB   ❌ cost + diluted attention

PROPOSED
  turn N        grep -r ...   ──►  ~40 KB
                model         ──►  prune_tool_result(call_id, "grep hit target/ fingerprints, irrelevant")
                context now   ──►  [pruned] grep hit target/ fingerprints, irrelevant   (1 line)
  turn N+1..50  every request ──►  1 line   ✅
```

#### Why it's cheap: only the tail changes

```
[ instructions | turns 1 .. N-1 | junk output | rest of turn N ]
 └───── cached prefix: kept ──────┘ └── re-cached once (small) ──┘
```

Prompt caching is prefix-based, so pruning a result from the *current* turn leaves everything before it cached.

#### Design

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| **Model-judged** | "This is junk" is a semantic call; no size cap or rule can make it. |
| **Tail-only** (current turn) | The cached prefix survives; nothing old is rewritten. |
| **Visible** | Original stays in the user-facing transcript with a one-line notice. Nothing disappears silently. |

#### Bonus: a bigger effective window

Removing junk grows the *useful* space by more than the junk's share, because the denominator shrinks:

| Junk share of context | Useful space | Effective window gain |
|---|---|---|
| 10% | 90% → 100% | **+11%** |
| 20% | 80% → 100% | **+25%** |
| 30% | 70% → 100% | **+43%** |
| 50% | 50% → 100% | **+100%** |

Same hardware, same model: compaction comes later, and what remains is signal. *(Junk shares are illustrative.)*

### Example prompts or workflows

- `grep -r` that unexpectedly walks a build/output directory (`target/`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`)
- `cat` of a file that turns out to be generated or minified
- a full `pytest` / `npm install` / `pip` log when only the last error line mattered

In each case the model knows within one glance that the output is noise, but it is carried in every later request.

### Additional context

| Mechanism | Gap |
|---|---|
| Automatic compaction (with checkpoints) | Periodic and lossy; junk rides along until it fires, and the summary can drop what was needed. |
| Output size limits | Cut by size: wanted long output is cut, short-enough junk passes. A `grep` can be essential one call and junk the next. |

"This output is junk" is a semantic judgment only the model can make, at the moment the output arrives.

#### Everyone wins 🌱

| Who | What they get |
|---|---|
| **Users** | Fewer tokens burned per task |
| **The model** | A clean context, better answers |
| **Providers** | Less KV cache per session, more sessions per GPU |
| **The planet** | Less power, fewer GPUs to build |

Junk is pure overhead: no answer improves because a build-fingerprint dump was re-read many times. Drop it in every harness, and the whole industry does the same work with less. The cheapest watt is the one you never spend.

Filed across 17 agent harnesses; full list: https://gist.github.com/nicezic/69f13fde6fa080a571825b56fd76392d

issues.title: BYOK Azure OpenAI: `429` throttling exhausts all retries in ~0.15s with no effective backoff; retry count/wait not configurable

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Using a BYOK **Azure OpenAI** provider (`COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=azure`), transient throttling (`429 Too Many Requests`) causes Copilot CLI to burn all 5 retries near-instantly and abort, instead of backing off. This is especially impactful for self-hosted / air-gapped Azure OpenAI deployments with low quota ceilings (e.g. small TPM/PTU allocations), where brief, fully recoverable throttle windows are common.

I hit this **quickly and often** with an Azure-hosted **GPT 5.4** deployment on a **270K token/min** quota — even routine sessions trip the limit and then fail hard instead of waiting out the short throttle window.

Observed output:

```text
Request failed due to a transient API error. Retrying....
Request failed due to a transient API error. Retrying....
Request failed due to a transient API error. Retrying....
Request failed due to a transient API error. Retrying....
Request failed due to a transient API error. Retrying....

Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times (total retry wait time: 0.15 seconds).
```

All 5 retries are consumed in ~0.15s total (as low as ~0.02s each), so a recoverable throttle is treated as a hard failure.

### Affected version

**Copilot CLI version:** 1.0.51

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a BYOK Azure OpenAI deployment with a low rate-limit ceiling (e.g. GPT 5.4 at 270K token/min).
2. Run Copilot CLI with that provider/model and issue requests that exceed the ceiling.
3. Observe 5 immediate retries and abort with a sub-second total wait time.

### Expected behavior

- On `429`/`503` from a BYOK provider, apply effective backoff:
  - Respect `Retry-After` when present (Azure OpenAI typically returns it) — confirm this path is wired for the `azure`/BYOK provider, not only GitHub-hosted CAPI.
  - When no `Retry-After` is present, fall back to a **default exponential backoff with jitter** (capped at a few minutes) rather than ~0.
- Make retry behavior **user-configurable**, e.g. environment variables such as `COPILOT_RETRY_MAX` and `COPILOT_RETRY_WAIT_MS` for headless/CI use.
- Don't reinterpret a long server-side wait as a transport failure (the ~30–60s client-timeout interaction noted in #2661 

### Additional context

- #2760 (closed, v1.0.32) added `Retry-After`-based bounded exponential backoff, but on BYOK **Azure OpenAI** with 1.0.51 the retries still exhaust in ~0.15s — suggesting the backoff isn't applied on the BYOK/`azure` path, or the throttle response is reaching the client without a usable `Retry-After`.
- Docs confirm no retry settings exist today

issues.title: Allow users to configure submit key (e.g., Ctrl+Enter) to prevent accidental submission with IME input

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Accidental prompt submission when using IME (Input Method Editor) for CJK languages, because the Enter key is used both for IME conversion confirmation and prompt submission.

### Proposed solution

When using languages that require an IME — such as Japanese, Chinese, and Korean — the Enter key serves double duty: it confirms character conversion in the IME **and** submits the prompt in Copilot CLI. This leads to frequent accidental submissions and wasted tokens.

Allow users to configure which key submits the prompt and which key inserts a newline. For example:

| Setting | Submit | Newline |
|---------|--------|---------|
| Default (current) | Enter | Shift+Enter / Ctrl+Enter |
| IME-friendly | Ctrl+Enter | Enter |

This could be a configuration option (e.g., in `~/.config/github-copilot/config.json`) or a `/settings` toggle in the TUI.

The key point is that users should be able to **swap** the roles of Enter and Ctrl+Enter (or Shift+Enter), not just add alternative newline keys.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. A Japanese user types: "このファイルをリファクタリングして". They press Enter to confirm the IME conversion of "して" → the incomplete prompt is accidentally submitted.
2. A user sets submit key to Ctrl+Enter in config → Enter now inserts a newline, Ctrl+Enter submits — matching muscle memory from Slack/Discord.
3. A Korean user composing Hangul hits Enter to finalize syllable blocks → with configurable submit key, they avoid wasting tokens on partial prompts.

### Additional context

- Related: #786 (`--confirm-send` flag) — addresses accidental submission via double-Enter confirmation. This proposal is complementary.
- Related: #1481, #1437, #660, #1871 — existing issues around Enter/Shift+Enter/Ctrl+Enter behavior, all of which assume Enter=submit is fixed.
- This is a common feature in chat applications (Slack, Discord, Telegram all offer this toggle).
- IME-based input affects a large user base: Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and other CJK language users.

issues.title: Option for 1-hour prompt cache TTL for Claude models (5-minute cache expires during normal interactive use)

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Claude prompt caching in Copilot CLI appears to use Anthropic's default **5-minute** cache TTL. In normal interactive use (read the answer, think, write the next prompt) gaps of more than 5 minutes are common, so the full conversation gets re-written to cache on almost every turn instead of being read from cache.

I measured this with `copilot -p` / `--resume` in fresh sessions (~35k-token context), sending a follow-up after different idle gaps, and reading `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` from the local session usage data. Two independent runs gave identical results:

| Idle gap | Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6.1-sol / GPT-6-sol / GPT-5.6-sol |
|---|---|---|
| 2 min | ~95% cache read | ~95% cache read |
| 11 min | **0% cache read** (~100% cache write) | ~95% cache read |
| ~85 min | 0% | 0% |

My broader session history (Claude 5.x, CLI) shows the same pattern: 98% cache read for gaps < 4 min vs ~1% for gaps of 6–60 min.

Anthropic supports a 1-hour TTL (`cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}`). VS Code Copilot Chat already has experimental settings for this (`github.copilot.chat.anthropic.promptCaching.extendedTtl` / `extendedTtlMessages`), though they currently miss Claude 5.x models (microsoft/vscode#340830, fix in microsoft/vscode#340831). Copilot CLI has no equivalent option.

### Proposed solution

Add an option in Copilot CLI (config setting and/or env var) to use the 1-hour cache TTL for Claude models, covering the Claude 5.x family. Consider making it the default for interactive sessions, since the higher write cost (2x vs 1.25x) is usually recovered after one or two follow-up turns with a pause longer than 5 minutes.

### Example prompts or workflows

Any interactive session with a large context where the user pauses longer than 5 minutes between prompts (reviewing diffs, testing changes, meetings).

### Additional context

- Related: #3808 (prompt caching for Claude), #4724 (auto-compact on idle aligned to cache TTL)
- Triggered by this discussion: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1xauf3s/anthropic_caching_is_this_a_bad_joke/
- Tested with Copilot CLI 1.0.102-1 on Windows.

issues.title: [Feature request] Authoritative foreground-session change hook for terminal integrations, including warm resume

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Problem

Terminal integrations need to associate a pane with the **currently foreground**
root conversation, rather than the last conversation that submitted a prompt.
Command `sessionStart` hooks do not appear to provide a complete foreground-change
stream when switching between already-loaded sessions.

### Isolated observation

Tested Copilot CLI **1.0.105 on Linux**, using an empty disposable project, separate
`HOME`/`COPILOT_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, user-level command hooks for `sessionStart`,
`sessionEnd` and `userPromptSubmitted`, normal folder consent and Manual Approval.
No auto-approval, production hooks or existing conversations were used.

1. Start the interactive CLI and submit a synthetic prompt in session A.
   Observe `sessionStart(A, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(A)`.
2. Run `/new` and submit another synthetic prompt in B.
   Observe `sessionStart(B, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(B)`.
3. Run `/resume <A-id>`, then `/session id` to independently confirm A is foreground.
4. Repeat `/resume <B-id>`, `/session id`, then `/resume <A-id>`, `/session id`.

Across these warm A-B-A switches, there were **no additional Start, End or
Prompt hook invocations** within the bounded 5-8 second observation windows.
A file written only by Start hooks would still identify B while A is displayed.
New idle conversations likewise produced no Start until the first submitted
prompt in this run.

A same-version `/restart` changed the observed CLI owner PID/start identity.
After restart, the first submitted prompt emitted Start with `source=resume`.
This was not a cross-version handoff test.

**Limitation:** model requests were rejected by account billing-entity
configuration, so this observation does not establish successful-completion,
subagent, background-model or all-platform behavior. The foreground switches,
session IDs and hook events were nevertheless observed independently. Please
confirm whether this limitation affects the intended lifecycle contract.

### Requested capability

Please provide or document one supported identity-only integration surface:

- A complete, causally serialized **foreground-session-changed** event covering
  warm switches, startup, new/clear/no-current transitions, with ordering and
  failure/supersession semantics; or
- A read-only authenticated accessor for current root identity (or no-current),
  resolved session-store location and an activation revision/conditional-current
  operation suitable for safely publishing asynchronous identity records.

An equivalent supported in-process integration would also work. Explicit revision
fields are not essential if the API guarantees complete serialized publication.
Session-only snapshots or hook-arrival counters alone do not establish that
delayed work still belongs to the current activation, particularly A-B-A.

This is not a request for tool approval, busy/idle authority, a heartbeat service,
or access to transcript contents. The goal is to stop relying on diagnostic log
registration lines to identify the displayed conversation.

Related but different: #4365 discusses prompt-hook/new/clear behavior; this request
concerns **command-hook coverage of warm foreground switches**.

issues.title: Android/Termux support broken in v1.0.48+ (runtime.node requires glibc)

labels.name: area:platform-linux
labels.description: Linux-specific: Wayland, X11, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, ARM, terminal emulators

labels.name: area:installation
labels.description: Installing, updating, versioning, PATH setup, and binary distribution

issues.body:
## Summary

Copilot CLI v1.0.48 introduced a native Rust addon (`runtime.node`) that is compiled against glibc, making it impossible to run on Android/Termux where Node.js uses Bionic libc.

## Environment

- **Platform**: Android (Termux)
- **`process.platform`**: `"android"`
- **`process.arch`**: `"arm64"`
- **Node.js**: v24.x (Termux package)
- **Last working version**: 1.0.45

## Issues by version

### v1.0.45 (workable with patches)

Three fixable issues:
1. **ripgrep**: Looks for `ripgrep/bin/android-arm64/rg` — fixed by copying from `linux-arm64/rg` (statically linked, runs fine)
2. **pty.node**: Looks for `prebuilds/android-arm64/pty.node` — fixed by building `node-pty` from source on Termux
3. **Platform switch**: The native module loader in `app.js`/`index.js`/`sdk/index.js` doesn't handle `case "android"` — fixed by patching the JS

### v1.0.48+ (BROKEN — no workaround)

A new `runtime.node` Rust addon was introduced that handles token counting (tiktoken), MCP config parsing, shell analysis, hooks, and session filesystem. It is linked against glibc:

```
NEEDED: libgcc_s.so.1, libpthread.so.0, libm.so.6, libdl.so.2, libc.so.6
```

This **cannot** run on Android because:
- Android uses Bionic libc, not glibc
- The glibc TLS (Thread-Local Storage) model is incompatible with Android's linker
- You cannot mix glibc and Bionic libraries in the same process
- The binary is closed-source Rust, so we cannot rebuild it

## Request

1. **Ship an Android-compatible `runtime.node`** — Rust supports the `aarch64-linux-android` target natively. Cross-compiling with `cargo build --target aarch64-linux-android` would produce a Bionic-compatible binary.

2. **Add `android-arm64` to the platform matrix** — The optional dependencies (`@github/copilot-linux-arm64`, etc.) should include an `@github/copilot-android-arm64` variant.

3. **Handle `"android"` in the platform switch** — The JS code in `app.js`, `index.js`, and `sdk/index.js` should map `process.platform === "android"` to the appropriate prebuild path.

## Workaround

We are pinned to v1.0.45. Users who accidentally upgrade are stuck.

## Additional context

Termux is a widely-used terminal emulator for Android that provides a Linux-like environment. Node.js runs natively on it. Before v1.0.48, Copilot CLI worked with minor patches. The introduction of the glibc-only native addon broke this entirely.
