prs.title: perf(site): cut each page's JavaScript by about 40%
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Part of the opencode.ai launch speed work.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Every page of opencode.ai now sends about 40% less JavaScript, with no visible change. Visitors download less before a page is usable, and much less in total while a page sits idle.

What changed:

- **The browser bundles are minified.** They never were: `minify: "esbuild"` on the client environment is ignored by Vite 8 unless the top-level `build.minify` asks for it, and that is off so the Worker keeps readable stack traces. The client now uses Oxc, Vite's own minifier.
- **No zod in production pages.** Production only ever renders the default settings, so it reads them from `settings-defaults.json` instead of building the zod schema. A test keeps the file equal to the schema's defaults (`bun script/settings-defaults.ts` regenerates it), and the dev server still parses live. The 404 arcade's three tuning modules skip their zod parsing in production the same way.
- **Server-only changelog code stays on the server.** Loading releases moved to `lib/changelog-releases.ts`; `lib/changelog.ts` keeps the types and queries. Before, the edge cache, the GitHub calls and the 178 kB build snapshot chunk reached the browser.
- **Search no longer loads the legal documents.** The ⌘K index reads a generated `legal-search.json` (headings and snippets) instead of the full privacy policy and terms. A test keeps it in sync (`bun script/legal-search.ts`).
- **rolling-number loads only for the home variants that use it.** The default page doesn't.
- **The dev-only pre-paint script is empty in production**, so its bundle doesn't carry it or the functions it inlines.
- **`/docs` and `/download` are full page loads.** Neither is a page of this app. Before, the idle preload of `/docs` pulled the 404 route onto every page, and a `/docs` link rendered the 404 arcade client-side. This fits the speculation rules from #62256.
- **`check-client-bundle.ts` guards it.** It fails the build when server-only code reaches the browser, and when a page's initial JavaScript passes its budget (each route's current size plus 1 kB; a new route needs a budget).

#### Initial JavaScript (what the HTML loads and modulepreloads), bytes

| Route | Before: files, gzip / brotli | After: files, gzip / brotli |
|---|---|---|
| / | 24, 300,140 / 252,740 | 24, **181,220 / 157,426** |
| /desktop (and ide, mini, mobile, sdk, terminal) | 27, 285,235 / 241,051 | 27, 176,977 / 154,228 |
| /product | 27, 269,128 / 227,691 | 27, 166,107 / 144,660 |
| /brand | 20, 252,140 / 213,263 | 19, 151,467 / 132,406 |
| /press | 22, 253,727 / 214,109 | 21, 153,268 / 133,251 |
| /font | 17, 279,159 / 233,857 | 16, 172,466 / 149,526 |
| /changelog | 23, 268,298 / 226,716 | 23, 165,032 / 143,807 |
| /legal/privacy-policy | 22, 297,622 / 250,921 | 20, 191,407 / 165,231 |
| 404 | 14, 229,622 / 194,142 | 13, **142,081 / 122,160** |
| /ja (same HTML as /, plus the ja dictionary and content loaded before hydration) | 328,081 / 276,949 | 208,248 / 181,016 |

#### Everything a page downloads with no interaction (load, then idle), desktop

| Route | JS files | gzip | brotli |
|---|---|---|---|
| / (same for /product, /desktop, /changelog) | 44 → 41 | 435,980 → 237,594 (−45%) | 363,584 → 205,606 |
| /brand | 46 → 43 | 458,683 → 253,496 | 382,163 → 219,574 |
| /font | 45 → 42 | 480,510 → 269,254 | 399,027 → 232,790 |
| /legal/privacy-policy | 46 → 43 | 474,032 → 290,234 | 396,169 → 249,632 |
| /ja | 38 → 37 | 444,309 → 290,528 | 371,262 → 249,674 |
| 404 | 23 → 22 | 456,161 → 315,413 | 374,886 → 264,843 |

Each page's CSS also drops by one file (about 9 kB brotli), because the 404 route's stylesheet is no longer preloaded.

#### Top modules in `/`'s initial JavaScript (minified bytes)

- Before: `site.tsx` 68.6k, `routes/index.tsx` 53.5k, seroval 51.3k, `products.tsx` 51.0k, zod 90k+ across modules, `en.ts` 39.7k, `settings.ts` 38.2k, solid 33.7k, rolling-number 28.8k.
- After: `en.ts` 38.4k, `site.tsx` 35.4k, `products.tsx` 28.8k, `routes/index.tsx` 28.2k, seroval 25.7k, solid 16.5k, `nav-order.tsx` 14.3k, `brand-content.ts` 13.4k.

#### What's left, with estimated savings (not in this PR; each changes timing or behavior)

- **Preload on intent instead of idle.** Every page fetches the code for six other pages and the search palette while idle (about 56 kB gzip). Loading them on hover, focus or the first ⌘K would remove that, but the first click on a link nobody hovered, and a very fast ⌘K, would wait for the download.
- **Compile the settings away in production.** Design mode's variants and editing code (nav ordering, history, versions) still ship because components read the settings store. Treating settings as build-time constants would save an estimated 15–25 kB gzip per page.
- **No hydration for static sections.** The framework alone (solid, seroval, router) is about 33 kB gzip and the English dictionary 12 kB, so pages under 50 kB need static sections that don't hydrate. SolidStart has no islands mode; it would mean full page loads instead of client-side navigation, which loses the card-grow transition.
- **Lazy Markdown view.** About 7 kB gzip; the first toggle and a restored Markdown view would wait for the chunk.
- **Split the legal pages.** Each legal page ships both documents and the print layout. Per-document chunks save about 8–25 kB, loading print code before printing about 15 kB gzip.
- **Hydration layouts.** The banner, the menu watcher and the surface watcher force layouts while hydrating (about 50–100 ms of main thread at 4× CPU slowdown). Fixing it shifts when those states settle.
- **i18n.** `en.ts` is 12 kB gzip on every page and the English page content 18 kB gzip in the shared entry. Japanese pages add 27 kB gzip before hydration.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun test` (131 pass) in `services/site`, and `bun run check` at the root.
- `bun script/build.ts --mode dev` through the QA harness: both bundle guards, the new budgets and the Worker startup check pass. The server output is a single `ssr.mjs`, and every build was served locally in workerd and loaded.
- **Pixel and style parity** against a baseline built from the same origin/dev commit (82229fb7d4): `/`, `/ja`, `/ar/press`, `/desktop`, `/legal/privacy-policy` and the 404 at desktop, laptop and mobile, with forced hover, focus-visible and active on every interactive element. 18 of 18 captures identical.
- Before the rebase, a full run over 43 routes (en, ja, ar, 404) × 3 viewports with every menu opened. Every capture without a menu open was identical. The 30 menu captures that differed show the same differences as a baseline-against-baseline run with menus open, so they're harness noise in that mode.
- **Using it:**
  - ⌘K search returns the same results for six queries, and choosing a legal result lands on the same page.
  - Client-side navigation and changelog paging and filters work.
  - The Markdown view toggles, survives a reload and toggles back in en, ja and ar.
  - The 404 arcade renders, with no console errors.
  - The only differences from the baseline are the intended ones: no 404 chunk preload, and `/docs` takes a full page load.

**Not verified:**
- Safari and Firefox.
- Real video playback (media isn't served locally).
- LCP and TBT after the rebase. Before it, home measured TBT 638 → 452 ms at 4× CPU slowdown.
- Locales other than en, ja and ar, beyond bundle sizes.
- Design mode flows on the dev server. The rolling-number variants now load lazily there behind their own Suspense fallback.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="currentColor">
  <style>
    .b{animation:s 3.2s cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) infinite}
    .b2{animation-delay:.15s}.b3{animation-delay:.3s}

    <rect x="24" y="48" width="192" height="10" rx="2"/>
  </g>
  <rect class="b" x="24" y="14" width="116" height="10" rx="2" style="transform-origin:24px 0"/>
  <rect class="b b2" x="24" y="31" width="110" height="10" rx="2" opacity=".8" style="transform-origin:24px 0"/>
  <rect class="b b3" x="24" y="48" width="91" height="10" rx="2" opacity=".6" style="transform-origin:24px 0"/>
</svg>
```

No visual change; see the parity results above.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. The site's Text.js console apps were pinned to 1.5.0, and 1.6.0 is mostly bundle-size work.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Updates `services/site` from `@textjs/app`, `@textjs/core`, `@textjs/opencode` and `@textjs/react` 1.5.0 to 1.6.0, and adapts the small Bun build that writes `/textjs/` for the new loaders.

Only the two DevTools console apps are affected: `opencode.install.pick()` (the install picker) and `opencode.try()` (OpenCode Lite). No page loads Text.js at page load. The site's pages, styles and client chunks are unchanged, and `/textjs/` is fetched only when a visitor runs one of those two commands in the console.

1.6.0 loads Yoga's WebAssembly from a `.wasm` file instead of a base64 copy inside the JavaScript, and loads the bidi engine from its own chunk. Both happen under the `@textjs/client` resolve condition, which is what `text build` sets. What that took here:

- `services/site/textjs/script/build.ts` builds with `conditions: ["@textjs/client"]`, copies `@textjs/core/yoga.wasm` to `public/textjs/yoga-<sha256:8>.wasm`, and defines that name into the entries.
- Bun's bundler doesn't resolve the loader's default `new URL("@textjs/core/yoga.wasm", import.meta.url)`. It leaves it in the output, where it would request `/textjs/@textjs/core/yoga.wasm` and 404. So `src/lite.tsx` and `src/picker.tsx` call `initYoga({ wasm })` with the hashed file before rendering.
- `public/_headers` caches `/textjs/yoga-*` as immutable next to the chunks. It is served as `application/wasm`, so it compiles while it streams.
- The build's size report now prints each app's eager closure, its on-demand chunks and Yoga's wasm.

Everything one console open downloads, before and after (raw / gzip / brotli):

| app | 1.5.0 | 1.6.0 | change (gzip) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opencode.install.pick()` | 450,253 / 159,563 / 136,602 B | 393,790 / 134,990 / 117,062 B | -15.4% |
| `opencode.try()` (Lite) | 820,082 / 267,743 / 225,643 B | 754,222 / 239,877 / 203,265 B | -10.4% |

The bidi engine (15.4 KB gzip) loads only when the app shows right-to-left text, and Lite's session dialogs (29.3 KB gzip) only when a dialog opens. Opening either app costs one extra request for `yoga.wasm` (28.6 KB gzip), cached as immutable.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Parity with `site-qa/parity.ts` on `/` and `/terminal` at desktop, laptop and mobile: no pixel or style differences, both against a build of the same commit on 1.5.0 and against the harness baseline. The site's 107 client chunks keep their names and sizes, apart from build-stamp hashes.
- Console frames: drove `opencode.install.pick()` (arrow keys, Enter) and `opencode.try()` (typing a prompt, Enter) in headless Chromium on both versions and compared every `console.log` call the driver paints, with its `%c` styles. Boot frames and the final frame are identical for both apps, and the picker returns the same command. The only frame that ever differs is an in-flight digit in the scripted reply's progress counter, and two runs of the same build differ there in the same way.
- The site build's own checks pass, including the workerd startup check.

Checks run: `bun run check` at the repo root, and in `services/site`: `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun test` (129 pass).

prs.title: fix(opencode): cap images re-sent from history (backport #39929)
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Backport of #39929 (and the follow-up #56983) to the 1.x release line. No separate issue.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

1.x keeps every image in a session's history and re-sends all of them as base64 on every request. Auto-compaction only counts tokens, and images cost almost none, so on 1M-context models (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) request bodies reach 100–200 MB before compaction kicks in. On 2026-11-05, 1.x clients sent 23.4k of the 29.4k requests over 64 MB that reached the OpenCode gateway; 2.x sent 232. Those bodies run gateway isolates out of memory and get 413/400s from providers.

**Image cap (ported from 2.x `boundImages`).** At the end of `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect`, once inline images in the converted history pass 25 MiB, the oldest are replaced with the same placeholder text 2.x uses until 15 MiB remain. It uses the stable-cut version from #56983: the cut only moves each time another 10 MiB of images arrives, so the replaced prefix and the provider prompt cache stay the same between cuts. It counts user image/file parts, tool-result `media`/`image-data`/`file-data` items, and the synthetic user message that carries tool-result images for providers that can't take them in tool results (OpenAI-compatible and others). Remote URLs don't count.

Differences from 2.x:
- It runs on AI SDK `ModelMessage[]`, since 1.x has no `LLMRequest`. It's applied in `toModelMessagesEffect`, which feeds both the AI SDK and native runtimes, title generation and the compaction size estimate, rather than in `ProviderTransform.message` (which receives the AI SDK's provider-level prompt shape on one path and `ModelMessage` on the other).
- There's no `unsupportedParts` composition. 1.x handles unsupported media separately in `ProviderTransform.message`, which runs after this.

**Overflow classification.** `Request body too large` and `multimodal data size is too large` now count as context overflow in `@opencode-ai/llm`'s `isContextOverflow`, so 1.x compacts and retries instead of failing the turn, the same way it already handles HTTP 413 and `context_length_exceeded`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Ported the four `boundImages` tests from 2.x (below the trigger, oldest-first replacement with identity kept for untouched messages, stable cut across new images, images nested in tool results), plus one end-to-end `toModelMessages` test for the OpenAI-compatible synthetic user message path. Added both new error strings to the existing overflow tests in `packages/llm` and `message-v2.test.ts`.
- Red proof: with the cut disabled and the two patterns removed, every cap test except the below-trigger one (4 of 5) fails, and both overflow tests fail. With the change, they pass.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/opencode` and `packages/llm`. `bun test test/session test/provider` in `packages/opencode` (1166 pass, 0 fail). `bun test` in `packages/llm` (298 pass, 0 fail).

@rekram1-node: this is your #39929 on the v1 branch. Could you take a look?

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Reopening a closed file tab from the file browser showed old content. A closed tab stops watching its file, and `open()` reused the cached copy. The read starts before the tab opens: selecting the tab loads the file too, and since #61818 a forced load during a read asks for one more read, so forcing afterwards read a newly opened file twice. prs.title: fix(core): leave commentary text out of generated titles
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51997

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

With OpenAI Responses models that send commentary-phase text before the answer (e.g. gpt-6-luna), the generated session title includes the commentary:

```text
before  We need title only. Need capture investigation. Title concise.Read-only performance investigation
after   Read-only performance investigation
```

`SessionTitle.attempt` in `packages/core/src/session/title.ts` collected every `text-delta` regardless of phase and joined them. The two messages run together with no newline, so taking the first line doesn't help.

**Change**

The title stream now records which text blocks carry `phase: "commentary"` in their provider metadata (read with the same `route.providerMetadataKey ?? provider` key the runner uses) and leaves those blocks out of the title. It checks both `text-start` and `text-end`, because a Responses message can arrive without a phase and only get it on `response.output_item.done`. Text without a phase, or with `final_answer`, is used as before.

Same approach and test as #52006 by @shanebishop1, which was closed by the stale-PR cleanup. This doesn't touch inline reasoning blocks in titles, which #57071 covers.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/session-title.test.ts` (packages/core): 22 pass. The two new cases (phase on the added item, and phase only on the done item) fail without the fix with the commentary in the title.
- Ran `opencode run --standalone` from source against a local fake Responses server that streams a commentary message and then the title, with the same model as the title model. `opencode session list` showed the joined commentary title on dev and `Read-only performance investigation` with the fix.
- `bun typecheck` (packages/core) and `bun run check`: pass.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(ui): use nouns for ukrainian tool titles
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #50651

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

In Ukrainian, the edit and write tool steps in the session timeline say "Редагувати" and "Написати". Those are infinitives ("to edit", "to write"), so they read like commands. The other tool titles in the same list are nouns: "Читання", "Оболонка", "Патч".

**Change**

`packages/ui/src/i18n/uk.ts` now uses nouns for these titles, the same way the other tool titles are written:

```diff
-  "ui.messagePart.title.edit": "Редагувати",
-  "ui.messagePart.title.write": "Написати",
+  "ui.messagePart.title.edit": "Редагування",
+  "ui.messagePart.title.write": "Запис",
...
-  "ui.tool.execute": "Виконати",
+  "ui.tool.execute": "Виконання",
```

`ui.tool.execute` comes from the same `switch` in `packages/session-ui/src/tools/tool-renderer.tsx` and the same map in `tool-error-card.tsx`, and it had the same problem, so I changed it here too. "Редагування" is the word the app's Ukrainian strings already use for edit permissions. I picked "Запис" for write because it is the usual Ukrainian word for writing a file, and the same file already says "Записування команди...".

The verb strings in `packages/app/src/runtime/i18n/uk.ts` (`common.edit`, `dialog.server.menu.edit` and others) label buttons and menu items, so they stay verbs.

Same idea as #50646 by @seesmof, which the template bot closed. That PR used "Написання" for write.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Rendered the session-ui stories `current-session-research-agents--agent-research` (scenario `failures`) and `current-session-terminal-work--execute-grouped` with `globals=locale:uk` in Playwright, on dev and then with this change. The tool group summary changes from "Оболонка, Редагувати, Написати, Патч…" to "Оболонка, Редагування, Запис, Патч…", and "Виконати" changes to "Виконання".

prs.title: fix(core): keep MCP prompts when a refresh fails
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #50918

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

If an MCP server sends `notifications/prompts/list_changed` and the follow-up `prompts/list` fails, all of that server's prompts vanish from the command list. The server still shows as connected, so nothing tells the user why their commands are gone.

**Cause**

`refreshPrompts` in `packages/core/src/mcp/connection.ts` turned any listing error into an empty list and stored it:

```diff
   const refreshPrompts = (client: McpClient.Connection) =>
     client.prompts().pipe(
-      Effect.orElseSucceed(() => []),
       Effect.map((prompts) => {
         state.prompts = prompts
       }),
```

**Change**

Drop the `orElseSucceed`, so prompts work like `refreshTools` right above it: a failed refresh never reaches the `Effect.map` and the previous prompts stay. The error is dropped by `whenLive` (`Effect.ignore`), the same as for tools. On the first listing after connect, `state.prompts` is already `[]`, so a failure there still leaves no prompts.

Same approach as #50920 by @feiiiiii5, which was closed by the stale-PR cleanup.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Ran `opencode serve` on a throwaway XDG dir with a local stdio MCP server that lists a `greet` prompt, then sends `prompts/list_changed` and fails the next `prompts/list`. Checked `GET /api/command` and `GET /api/mcp`:

prs.title: fix(util): show git's error when a plugin install fails
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54483

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

Installing a plugin from a `github:` spec that is missing or private gave no useful reason. `opencode plugin add` printed an empty `NpmInstallFailedError:` with a `[cause]` of "An unknown git error occurred", and the TUI's plugin error dialog showed just `NpmInstallFailedError`.

**Cause**

`reify` in `packages/util/src/npm.ts` wraps the Arborist failure as `InstallFailedError({ add, dir, cause })`, which has no message, so the TUI's `errorMessage` falls back to the tag name. For Git specs, `@npmcli/git` replaces any error it doesn't recognize with "An unknown git error occurred" and keeps git's real output on `cause.stderr`, which nothing printed.

**Change**

`InstallFailedError` now builds its `message` from the requested packages (or the directory), the cause's message, and the cause's trimmed `stderr` when there is one. Both the CLI and the TUI already show `error.message`, so no caller changes. The original `cause` object is still kept.

```text
before: NpmInstallFailedError
after:  Failed to install github:nonexistent-user-xyz/nonexistent-repo: An unknown git error occurred
        ERROR: Repository not found.
        fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
        ...
```

Server plugins that fail to install still show "Plugin failed to load" with a ref in the plugin list. The full error goes to the log, which now includes git's output too.

The message part uses the same approach as #50252 by @andreivince, which was closed by the stale-PR cleanup. This adds git's `stderr` on top. @liudongyan13701205717-source offered in the issue to take this but hasn't opened a PR.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `opencode plugin add "github:nonexistent-user-xyz/nonexistent-repo"` from source, with throwaway `HOME`/XDG dirs: on dev it prints `NpmInstallFailedError: ` with `[cause]: Error: An unknown git error occurred`. With the fix it prints `NpmInstallFailedError: Failed to install github:nonexistent-user-xyz/nonexistent-repo: An unknown git error occurred` followed by git's `ERROR: Repository not found.` / `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.`
- `bun dev --standalone` with that spec in `cli.json` `plugins`, then `/plugins` and opening the failed entry: on dev the dialog shows `NpmInstallFailedError`. With the fix it shows the same message as the CLI.
- New test in `packages/core/test/npm.test.ts` installs a `git+file://` spec for a missing repo and checks the message includes git's "does not appear to be a git repository". It fails on dev (empty message) and passes with the fix.
- `bun test test/npm.test.ts test/plugin/supervisor.test.ts test/plugin/module.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 36 pass. `bun typecheck` in `packages/util` and `packages/core`, and `bun run check` from the root.

prs.title: fix(core): normalize webfetch permission rules like requested URLs
prs.body:
### Problem

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60505 started checking webfetch permissions against the parsed URL (`new URL(input).href`), which lowercases the host, punycodes it, drops a default port and adds a `/` path. Rules from config are still matched as written, so some rules that used to match stopped matching:

| Rule | Request | Before 60505 | Since 60505 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `https://example.com` | `https://example.com` | deny | allow |
| `https://Internal.Corp/*` | `https://Internal.Corp/docs` | deny | allow |
| `https://пример.срб/*` | `https://пример.срб/docs` | deny | allow |
| `https://port.test:443/*` | `https://port.test/docs` | deny | allow |

A deny rule silently stops blocking, and an allow rule starts prompting.

### Change

Rewrite the scheme and host of each `webfetch` rule the same way when agent permissions are loaded, next to the existing `~` expansion for path rules. The path and everything after it stays as written, so wildcards keep working.

```text
https://example.com       → https://example.com/
HTTPS://Internal.Corp/*   → https://internal.corp/*
https://пример.срб/*      → https://xn--e1afmkfd.xn--90a3ac/*
https://port.test:443/*   → https://port.test/*
https://prefix.test*      → unchanged (trailing wildcard, no `/` added)
https://query.test?q=*    → unchanged (`?` is also a wildcard, so ambiguous)
*                         → unchanged
```

Image downloads in `image_generate` also check `webfetch`, but with the raw URL, so they now use the parsed URL too to match the same rules.

### Out of scope

- Paths are not re-encoded, so a rule with a literal space in its path still won't match `%20`.
- A trailing-dot host (`evil.com.`) still differs from `evil.com`, same as before.

### Verification

- `bun test test/config/agent.test.ts`: 38 pass. The new test fails without the change.
- `bun test test/permission.test.ts test/tool-webfetch.test.ts test/codemode test/tool-image-generate.test.ts test/config`: 531 pass.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`: clean.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" font-family="ui-monospace,monospace" font-size="9">
```

prs.title: perf(site): fetch each page's CSS once and prefetch pages on hover
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None. Part of the opencode.ai speed work (make the site faster with no visual change).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Visitors download 37–47 KB less CSS on every page, make 6–9 fewer requests, and pages that open with a full page load start loading on hover. Nothing looks or behaves differently.

**1. Each page's CSS is downloaded once.** `lib/one-stylesheet.ts` combines a page's stylesheets into one file. It also kept each original link in the head as `<link rel="stylesheet" disabled>`, so Vite's chunk loader wouldn't add that CSS again on a client-side navigation. Chrome's preload scanner downloads disabled links anyway, so every first visit in Chrome fetched the page's CSS twice: 29–36 KB of extra compressed CSS competing with the stylesheet that blocks rendering. A small script in front of the combined link now creates the same disabled links. Chrome doesn't fetch disabled links that a script adds (checked in Chromium and WebKit). The script's text is the same on every page; the file names are in its `data-css` attribute, so a hash-based CSP can still allow it.

**2. IBM Plex Mono's font rules leave production CSS.** IBM Plex Mono is only a choice in the development-only Settings › Mono font, but its 120 `@font-face` rules (about 22 KB uncompressed) were in every page's main stylesheet. Stylesheets named `*.dev.css` now build empty in production (`devOnlyCss` in `vite.config.ts`), and the file is renamed `style/ibm-plex-mono.dev.css`. Development is unchanged. The build no longer emits the 69 IBM Plex font files either.

**3. Full page loads are prefetched on hover.** A Speculation Rules script (`eagerness: moderate`) prefetches a link's page once the pointer rests on it, for the pages that open with a full page load: `/product`, `/ide`, `/mini`, `/font`, `/extensions/*` (in any language), the docs at `/v2/*` and Stats at `/data`. It never prefetches the Console, downloads, or language links (`[hreflang]`), because a language page sets the `oc_locale` cookie. Pages the router opens client-side don't need it. Browsers without Speculation Rules ignore it.

#### Before → after

Local production build in workerd (site-qa `serve.ts`), `mobile` profile (390×844, 4× CPU slowdown, Fast 4G), median of 5 runs. Byte and request counts are exact. Timings moved 20–50% between runs on a busy machine, so they're left out.

| Route | CSS | Requests | Transferred |
|---|---|---|---|
| / | 116.0 → 69.2 KB (−40%) | 98 → 92 | 1000 → 954 KB |
| /product | 106.4 → 67.4 KB (−37%) | 74 → 65 | 949 → 911 KB |
| /desktop | 110.3 → 66.9 KB (−39%) | 74 → 66 | 831 → 788 KB |
| /brand | 113.6 → 75.9 KB (−33%) | 84 → 77 | 775 → 737 KB |
| /press | 112.4 → 74.8 KB (−33%) | 73 → 65 | 751 → 714 KB |
| /font | 117.4 → 80.2 KB (−32%) | 69 → 65 | 1181 → 1144 KB |
| /changelog | 106.1 → 68.9 KB (−35%) | 64 → 58 | 743 → 706 KB |
| /legal/privacy-policy | 115.6 → 76.8 KB (−34%) | 68 → 61 | 861 → 823 KB |
| /ja | 107.8 → 61.1 KB (−43%) | 96 → 90 | 893 → 847 KB |
| /ar/desktop | 94.5 → 51.1 KB (−46%) | 71 → 63 | 799 → 757 KB |

The CSS saving is the same on desktop. HTML and JS each grow by 0.2 KB (the script and the rules). Fonts, images and CLS (0) are unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

- **Parity:** site-qa `parity.ts` against a build of fe1e3e35fe, all 53 routes in `routes.txt` (English, Japanese, German, Arabic and 404), at 1440×900, 1024×768 and 390×844. That's 159 captures comparing pixels, about 170 computed-style properties per element, forced `:hover`, `:focus-visible` and `:active` on every interactive element, and loaded fonts. Result: **no differences**. Five captures matched only on a retry, which the harness counts as timing noise. After rebasing, `/`, `/ja` and `/ar/desktop` at all three viewports again showed no differences.
- **Cascade order:** the active stylesheets are in the same order after loading `/` and navigating client-side to `/desktop`, `/press`, `/brand` and back. CSS requests over that path went from 20 to 14, with no duplicates.
- **Prefetching:** hovering `/product`, `/v2/docs` or `/data` sends a `Sec-Purpose: prefetch` request. Hovering `/desktop` (client-side), `/console/go` or a language link sends none.
- **Checks:** `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun test` (124 pass, including the new `test/one-stylesheet.test.ts`), oxlint, and the full build with both bundle guards.
- **Worker startup:** the server build is still one `_ssr/ssr.mjs`, with no `ssr2.mjs`, and every page loads under workerd.

**Not verified:**
- Firefox.
- That a click actually uses the prefetched response; only the prefetch request was checked.
- The change on Cloudflare's edge rather than local workerd.
- Restoring a page from the back/forward cache. Nothing in the code blocks it, but headless Chrome reports `BrowsingInstanceNotSwapped` for the test navigations.

**Considered and skipped (could change visuals or behavior):**
- **Tracking parameters in the HTML cache key:** dropping `utm_*` and `gclid` would hand one visitor's parameters to another in the server-rendered language links.
- **Nitro's built-in list of static files:** removing it saves about 1–3 ms per cold start but means overriding Nitro internals.
- **Preloading OpenTUI Mono Bold:** it changes what visitors see while the page loads.
- **AV1/HEVC video copies:** re-encoded video isn't pixel-identical to the H.264 originals.
- **Minifying the server bundle:** the bundle stays readable for stack traces.

**Outside this PR, owner Adam/Dax (opencode.ai zone settings, read-only check):**
- **HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 are off for the zone.** dev.opencode.ai only negotiates HTTP/1.1, so a page's 60–170 requests share at most 6 connections. This is the biggest single speed win left.
- **Email Obfuscation is on**, and Cloudflare strips the `ETag` from every HTML response while it scans. Repeat visits re-download the whole page instead of getting a 304. A Configuration Rule turning it off for the site's hostnames fixes it.
- **Early Hints is off.** If it's turned on, the site should hint the combined stylesheet and the fonts itself. SolidStart's built-in hints would point at the individual CSS files and bring the double download back.
- **`/files` media is cached for only 4 hours** (`max-age=14400`), even though its paths are versioned (`site/2026-11`). It could be cached for a year as immutable. This lives in `services/files`.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52069

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem.** Pasting a subagent (child) session ID into the open menu (ctrl+o) showed "No matches", so there was no way to jump to a child session by its ID.

**Cause.** In `DialogOpen` (`packages/tui/src/component/dialog-open.tsx`), the `matched` resource fetches the session for an exact typed ID, but the `sessions` memo then drops every session with a `parentID`, including the one it just looked up.

**Change.** The `parentID` filter now spares the exact-ID match, the same way the `archived` filter on the next line already does:

```diff
-      if (session.parentID || seen.has(session.id)) return false
+      if ((session.parentID && session.id !== match?.id) || seen.has(session.id)) return false
```

Child sessions still don't appear in the ordinary list. Same filter condition as #52086 by @kernel-oops, which was closed by the stale-PR cleanup; this keeps it inline instead of adding a helper.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Extended the existing exact-ID test in `packages/tui/test/cli/tui/dialog-open.test.tsx` so the looked-up session has a `parentID`. `bun test --timeout 30000 test/cli/tui/dialog-open.test.tsx`: fails on dev ("Timed out waiting for frame predicate"), 22 pass with the fix.
- Real TUI with `bun run dev:live`, ctrl+o, pasted the ID of an existing subagent session: dev shows "No matches · search all sessions with ctrl+x l"; with the fix the session is listed under Sessions.

prs.title: chore(site): fail the build when the Worker can't start
prs.body:
The site build now starts the Worker it just built and loads a few pages. If the Worker can't start, or a page answers wrongly, the build fails, so a broken Worker can't reach `cf deploy`.

## The failure this prevents
On 5 Nov, a small change to one release page (using `HttpHeader` from `@solidjs/start`) made the bundler split the Worker's server code into two files, `_ssr/ssr.mjs` and `_ssr/ssr2.mjs`. workerd refused to load the result: "Export 'ssr_exports' is not defined". The Worker would have crashed on every request. Every other check still passed: the build, both bundle checks and `cf deploy --prebuilt --dry-run`.

## How it works
`services/site/script/check-worker-start.ts` runs at the end of `script/build.ts`, after the Build Output is written:

- It reads the Build Output (`readBuildOutput` from `@cloudflare/build-output-utils`) and starts that Worker, with its real bundle, assets and bindings, in workerd through Miniflare, the runtime `cf` itself uses.
- It requests `/`, `/ja` and `/desktop` (each must answer 200), a made-up URL (must answer 404) and `/v2/docs/` (anything but a 5xx for now).
- It needs no secrets and no network. Every outbound call from the Worker gets a 503, which looks like a GitHub or status outage, so the site falls back to its build snapshot as it does in production. Miniflare's `cf: false` keeps it from downloading request metadata.
- It adds one devDependency, `miniflare`, pinned to `5.20260930.0-alpha`, the version `cf` already installs, so nothing new is downloaded. The `bun.lock` diff is bun re-sorting packages that were already there.

## Proof
I temporarily added the `HttpHeader` change back, which reproduced the split, and ran `bun script/build.ts --mode dev`. It exited 1:

```
check-worker-start: FAILED
  the Worker did not start: The Workers runtime failed to start. …
  "Uncaught SyntaxError: Export 'ssr_exports' is not defined in module … _ssr/ssr2.mjs"
```

On a normal build, in both modes:

```
check-worker-start: opencode-site-dev starts in workerd; / 200, /ja 200, /desktop 200, /check-worker-start-404 404, /v2/docs/ 404; 2 outbound calls answered offline (614 ms)
check-worker-start: opencode-site-production starts in workerd; / 200, /ja 200, /desktop 200, /check-worker-start-404 404, /v2/docs/ 404; 2 outbound calls answered offline (600 ms)
```

## Time added
About 1.8 seconds per build, including Bun's startup. The check itself takes 0.4 to 1.3 seconds, and a full site build takes about 85 seconds.

## Gap and follow-ups
- PR CI doesn't build `services/site` yet, so today the guard runs in `deploy-site.yml`, before `cf deploy`. It blocks the deploy, but a broken build is only caught after it merges to `dev`. #62229 adds a check-docs workflow; once it merges, it becomes a full site build on PRs that also runs this guard.
- `/v2/docs/` should become a strict 200 once #62229 merges and the docs are part of this build. It's a 404 today.

## Checks
- `bun run check` from the repo root: 35/35 tasks.
- `services/site`: `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun test` (121 pass).
- `bun script/build.ts` in both modes, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`.

prs.title: fix(site): security headers, Workers Logs and launch fixes
prs.body:
Launch fixes for the opencode.ai site (`services/site`) from the pre-launch audit. Nothing visitors can see changes: no pixels, timings or interactions. Pixel parity is below.

## What changes

**For visitors**
- Browsers get the standard protections on every page: HTTPS only (HSTS, the same one-year value the Console already sends on this host), no content sniffing, a strict referrer policy, no framing by other sites (the site can still frame itself, which the device preview needs), and camera, geolocation, payment and USB turned off. The microphone stays allowed for voice mode.
- Switching language through a redirect (for example `/ja/changelog`) sends the language cookie once instead of twice.
- A release page such as `/changelog/v1.1.6` used to answer 404 when GitHub was slow and the build snapshot didn't have that release, so search engines could drop real release pages. It now answers 503 with `Retry-After: 60` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. A tag GitHub really doesn't have still gets a 404. `/changelog/<tag>.json` uses the same rule: a tag missing from a stand-in list was a 404 and is now a 503.

**For operators**
- Workers Logs are on for the site Worker (`observability: { enabled: true }` in `cloudflare.config.ts`, both modes). Requests, errors and `console` output can now be searched in the Cloudflare dashboard. **The alert for 5xx on page routes still needs setting up in Cloudflare (owner: Dax/Adam).**
- `/oauth/opencode/client.json`, the Apple app association file and the static files (`/config.json`, `/tui.json`, `/openapi.json`, images, fonts) keep their exact current headers.

## Commits
- `fix(site): send security headers with the site's responses`. Adds `src/lib/security-headers.ts`, applied in `middleware.ts` right after the meta-file check, and a test that fails if code starts using a feature the policy blocks.
- `docs(site): fix stale sitemap, docs and deploy notes`. AGENTS.md names `/v2/sitemap.xml`; comments in `lib/docs.ts` and `public/_headers` are corrected.
- `fix(site): send the locale cookie once on redirects`. h3 already merges the pending `Set-Cookie` into a returned redirect, so the manual copy doubled it.
- `chore(site): turn on Workers Logs for the site Worker`.
- `fix(site): answer 503, not 404, for releases GitHub couldn't list`. Adds `entryStatus` in `lib/changelog-notes.ts`, used by the page and the JSON, and makes `html-cache.ts` send server errors with `no-store` and `Retry-After`. Includes a test.

## Checks
- `bun run check` from the repo root: 35/35 tasks.
- `services/site`: `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun test` (126 pass).
- `bun script/build.ts --mode dev` and `--mode production`, each followed by `cf deploy --prebuilt --dry-run`, pass. Both write `"observability":{"enabled":true}` into `worker.config.json`.
- Served the build in workerd (the site-qa harness) and checked with curl:
  - Pages, 404s, redirects and text files carry the headers; the meta files don't.
  - Redirects send one cookie.
  - `/changelog/v2.2.5` is 200 and `/changelog/v0.0.1` is 404 when GitHub answered.
- With GitHub unreachable (`vite dev` behind a dead proxy), `/changelog/v0.0.1` and its `.json` return 503 with `Retry-After: 60` and `no-store`, while `/changelog/v2.2.5` still serves from the stand-in.

## Parity
I compared against the baseline build of `origin/dev` using the site-qa harness (`parity.ts`): all 54 routes in `routes.txt`, at desktop 1440, laptop 1024 and mobile 390, first interaction state.
- **For the first three commits:** 162/162 captures match.
  - The only differences were harness noise: the server port inside absolute `mask-image` URLs on `/`, now normalized by the harness.
  - A 42-pixel flicker in the footer graphic, and one-off differences on `/ide`, `/ar` and `/de/terminal` laptop, all matched on rerun. The harness's own baseline-against-baseline run shows the same signatures.
- **For the last two commits:** 24/24 captures match on `/`, `/product`, `/changelog`, `/changelog/v2.2.5`, `/changelog/v2.2.0`, `/legal`, `/ar` and the 404 page. `/product` desktop showed the 42-pixel footer flicker and matched on rerun.

## Conflicts
This will conflict trivially with the docs move into `services/site` (`src/middleware.ts`, `src/lib/docs.ts`). The orchestrator will resolve it.

## Launch checklist (dev.opencode.ai and a local production build, 5 Nov 2026)
✅ pass · 🔧 fixed in this PR · ⚠️ needs owner

### Meta and sharing
- ✅ Every page has its own title, description, canonical and full Open Graph and X cards in the server HTML, in en, ja and ar. og:url matches the canonical and nothing is duplicated.
- ✅ All 17 link-preview cards load: PNG, 1200×630, 24–95 KB. Their URLs are `https://opencode.ai/og/…`, so in production they work only after cutover.
- ✅ theme-color, viewport, favicons, apple-touch-icon and the web manifest are in place.
- ✅ Structured data parses and the facts look right: Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication, FAQ, release articles and breadcrumbs.

### Crawling and links
- ✅ robots.txt, the sitemap index, the pages sitemap (403 URLs, all 200), llms.txt, llms-full.txt, the `.md` versions of pages, humans.txt, security.txt (expires 2027-11-04) and the feeds.
- ✅ The 404 page returns 404 in every language. Trailing slashes and `/en/…` redirect with a 301. `/legal` loads, so the footer and search links work.
- 🔧 Release pages answer 503, not 404, when GitHub's list isn't available (see above).
- ⚠️ Docs links in 17 languages point to `/<locale>/v2/docs…` and 404 (i18n agent, assigned).
- ⚠️ `/docs/zen` and `/docs/go` are 302s from the V1 docs app (`packages/web/src/pages/go.ts` and `zen.ts`). Permanent moves fit a 301 better (docs owner).
- ⚠️ The terms of service and llms-full.txt link to `/auth`, a legacy URL that AGENTS.md says nothing may link to (David).

### Headers, errors and exposure
- 🔧 Security headers and the single locale cookie, as above.
- ✅ The video editor, its API and the voice API return 404 in production. `/devices` is noindex. No stack traces leak.
- ⚠️ An unknown server function (`GET /_server?id=x`) answers 500 instead of 400 or 404 (low; David).
- ⚠️ **A build can produce a Worker that fails at startup, and nothing catches it** (Dax).
  - While writing the 503 fix, I first used `HttpHeader` from `@solidjs/start` in the release page.
  - That split the SSR chunk in two (`_ssr/ssr.mjs` and `_ssr/ssr2.mjs`), and workerd rejected the Worker: "Export 'ssr_exports' is not defined".
  - `script/build.ts`, both bundle guards and `cf deploy --dry-run` all passed. I switched to setting the header in `html-cache.ts`, and the split went away.
  - Proposal: a build guard, such as a smoke start in workerd or a check that `_ssr/ssr.mjs` defines `ssr_exports`, plus a note to avoid `HttpHeader`.

### Accessibility
- ✅ Keyboard: the skip link comes first, the order is logical (RTL too) and focus is visible. Menus, the language picker and the mobile menu open from the keyboard, report their open state and close on Escape with focus returned.
- ✅ Lighthouse on dev.opencode.ai (SEO / Best Practices / Accessibility):

  | Page | SEO | Best Practices | Accessibility |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `/` | 92 | 100 | 97 |
  | `/product` | 92 | 100 | 100 |
  | `/desktop` | 100 | 100 | 100 |
  | `/press` | 100 | 100 | 100 |
  | `/changelog` | 100 | 100 | 96 |
  | `/legal/privacy-policy` | 100 | 100 | 100 |
  | `/ar` | 100 | 100 | 97 |

- ⚠️ Proposals for David (visual or copy):
  - "Trusted by 16M+ developers" has a contrast ratio of 1.95, and the legal "Contents" label 3.24.
  - "Learn more" link text costs the SEO point on `/` and `/product`; a better accessible name needs a translated string in every language.
  - The changelog's pull request links are small touch targets.
  - The corner GitHub link sits outside any page landmark.
  - axe flags a label mismatch on the brand page's copy buttons and the press page's project rows (low).

### Media and integrations
- ⚠️ **The media upload is incomplete** (owner: David; the list is with David and Dax in Slack). Of the 517 files in `media-manifest.txt`, 120 are in `opencode.ai/files/site/2026-11/` and 397 are missing:
  - 334 sounds for the 404 arcade
  - 22 brand badge zips
  - 41 product videos

  Pages and llms-full.txt link 23 of the missing videos directly.
- ⚠️ Media is served with a one-hour cache. The files are versioned by folder, so a one-year `immutable` cache would save revalidations (files Worker owner).
- ✅ CORS on `/files` allows any origin and Range requests, which covers the arcade's 3D model and sound fetches.
- ⚠️ Dev only: the desktop page's download links go to `/update/api/…`, which 404s on dev.opencode.ai. Production redirects them to the file correctly.
- ⚠️ The newsletter form needs `EMAILOCTOPUS_API_KEY` on the site Worker. Without it, the form shows its error message rather than crashing. Set it on `opencode-site-dev` too if dev should work.
- ✅ The site makes no `/api/enterprise` calls.

### Legal
- ✅ The new legal pages (the content from #62164, already in `services/site`) are approved by legal and ship with the site.

### Go-live plan review (Dax's plan; nothing here changes infra)
- 🔧 Workers Logs are on. ⚠️ The 5xx alert still needs setting up in Cloudflare for `opencode-site-production`: a Workers Observability alert on status ≥ 500, or an uptime check on `/`, `/product` and `/changelog.json` (Dax/Adam).
- ⚠️ What the site Worker needs at runtime:
  - `EMAILOCTOPUS_API_KEY`: only the newsletter form uses it, and it degrades to an error message without it.
  - `STAGE`: already set.
  - Voice-mode keys: unused while voice mode is off.
  - No GitHub token, by decision: stars come from the build snapshot, and releases from tokenless GitHub calls (hence the 503 fix).
- ✅ The cutover order, rollback, and the note about the `AAAA 100::` record look right.

## Not verified
- These changes on a real deploy: they ran on a local workerd build of the dev-mode output and in `vite dev`. The production-mode output passed `cf deploy --dry-run` but I didn't serve it.
- Parity of open menus and every interaction state.
- Which secrets are set on the dev and production Workers, and a real newsletter signup.
- Whether the media files that did upload match the manifest's SHA-256 hashes; I checked presence and size only.

Closes #48581

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

**Problem**

The TUI docs list a `/details` command that "toggles tool execution details", and the translated pages add a `ctrl+x d` keybind for it. Neither exists. Typing `/details` in the TUI shows "No matching commands", and it has been missing since the OpenTUI rewrite (#3792).

On `dev`, no slash command or alias in `packages/tui/src` is named `details`, and nothing toggles tool details under another name or keybind. So there is no real command to rename the section to.

**Out of scope**

prs.title: fix(tui,app): only apply extended 5min retry to ServiceUnavailableError location sync
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61359

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When a workspace plugin starts slowly (for example a cold UNC location), the agent/model/provider endpoints return 503 `ServiceUnavailableError` while plugins are still activating. The sync gave up after three attempts, so the composer stayed stuck with no catalog metadata and the prompt could not be sent.

Changes:

- `retry()` in `@opencode/util` gets an optional `timeout` option: when set, retries continue past `attempts` until the elapsed budget expires. It defaults to off, so existing callers are unchanged.
- Both the TUI and web app location sync pass a 5-minute timeout, but it only extends `ServiceUnavailableError` retries. `LocationNotFoundError` is never retried, and every other failure keeps the original three attempts, so transient failures such as a dropped connection still recover without hammering a persistently failing server for five minutes.
- `@opencode/client` solid data: when a cold location's first full sync failed, the `provider.updated` / `model.updated` / `agent.updated` events the server publishes after boot were ignored because nothing had been stored. They now trigger a full sync of that location, so it recovers without a manual reload.
- The TUI shows a toast when the catalog never loads (using a new `useToastOptional`, since this provider mounts above the ToastProvider) instead of failing silently. The web app still fails silently after its 5 minutes; surfacing that is out of scope.

Public API: the only addition is the optional `timeout` option on `retry()` in `@opencode/util`. The SDK, server HTTP API, events, and config are unchanged.


### How did you verify your code works?

- New `packages/tui/test/context/location.test.tsx` drives the real provider against a mocked server with fake timers: a persistent 500 is retried exactly three times, a 404 is tried once and surfaces as the missing location, and a 503 retries past three attempts and stops at the 5-minute timeout. This test fails on the previous commit, where non-503 errors were only attempted once.
- Added `retry()` timeout tests in `packages/util` and a client solid-data test covering the 503 bootstrap.
- `tsc -b` is clean for `util`, `client`, `app`, and `tui`.
- Manually reproduced #61359 with a plugin whose `setup()` takes ~40s: the TUI keeps retrying, then shows the model and sends the prompt once the location warms up.

Not a user-facing UI change.

Not a UI change.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51912

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**: if any matching line is not valid UTF-8 (a Latin-1 or GBK file, for example), the grep tool fails with `Invalid ripgrep match output` and returns no matches at all, including the ones from normal UTF-8 files.

**Cause**: ripgrep's `--json` output uses `{ "bytes": "<base64>" }` instead of `{ "text": "..." }` for any path, line or submatch that isn't valid UTF-8. `RawMatch` in `packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts` only accepted `text`, so decoding that one row failed and the failure ended the whole search.

**Change**: `path`, `lines` and each submatch now accept either form. `bytes` are decoded from base64 as UTF-8, so invalid sequences become U+FFFD and the match is still reported. Offsets are unchanged, since ripgrep already reports them in bytes. The existing line truncation and submatch limit now run on the decoded text.

```text
before: Invalid ripgrep match output
after:  Found 2 matches ... latin1.txt: Line 1: needle caf�
```

Same approach as #51913 by @nkootstra, which was closed by the stale-PR cleanup, adapted to the current line truncation code.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52457

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

If you ever used the `system` theme on a dark terminal, opencode cached that dark palette in `system-theme.json`. After that, any theme opened dark on a light terminal, even though the terminal reported light. Deleting the cache file fixed it.

**Cause**

When `ThemeProvider` in `packages/tui/src/context/theme.tsx` starts up, it takes the mode from the cached palette, even when the renderer already knows the terminal's mode. The cache only refreshes while the `system` theme is active (`refreshPalette()` returns early otherwise). So with any other theme, the stale dark palette won every startup. The terminal answers before the first render (`app.tsx` waits for `waitForThemeMode`), so no later `THEME_MODE` event arrived to fix it.

**Change**

The terminal's reported mode now wins over the cached palette. The cache is only used when the terminal hasn't answered.

```diff
-      const mode = store.lock ?? terminalMode(palette) ?? store.mode
+      const mode = store.lock ?? renderer.themeMode ?? terminalMode(palette) ?? store.mode
```

A pinned `mode: "dark" | "light"` still wins. The `system` theme still repaints from a fresh palette after the first frame, as before.

Same approach as #52459 by @x0c, which was closed by the stale-PR cleanup. I also added a smaller version of its test to `packages/tui/test/context/theme.test.tsx`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Ran the dev TUI (`bun dev --standalone`, throwaway `HOME`) in a pty that answers OSC 10/11/4 and `?996n` like a real terminal, using the repro script from the issue. Steps: run `system` on a dark terminal (writes a dark cache), then run `github` on a light terminal. On dev, the second run painted `rgb(13,17,23)` (github dark). With the fix, it painted `rgb(255,255,255)` (github light).

- `bun test --timeout 30000 test/context/theme.test.tsx --rerun-each 10` in `packages/tui`: 20 pass. The new test fails on dev with `Expected: "light"`, `Received: "dark"`.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #50393

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem.** When a line comment or note in the composer context contains a bare `@word` like `@here` or `@team`, `parseCommentMentions` in `packages/app/src/composer/request.ts` treats it as a workspace path. The prompt then goes out with an extra `file://<project>/here` attachment that doesn't exist.

**Change.** `parseCommentMentions` now keeps a mention only if it looks like a path: it starts with `~` or contains `/`, `\`, `.` or `#`. Session mentions are still skipped as before. This is the heuristic proposed in the issue, and the same one @rafaetri used in #52877 (and #50526 before it); both were closed without merging.

```diff
 "or should I use @here?"
-files: [src/app.ts?start=1&end=1, here]
+files: [src/app.ts?start=1&end=1]
```

I looked for a structured signal instead of guessing from text. The comment editor is a plain textarea, and picking a file from its `@` autocomplete just inserts `@path ` as text, so there is nothing else to go on without a larger change.

**Out of scope.** The trade-off is that a dotless file at the project root, such as `@Makefile` or `@LICENSE`, written inside a comment is no longer attached. `@./Makefile` still works. File mentions in the main prompt are pills and are not affected.

- Extended the existing `request.test.ts` case "deduplicates context files and adds files for @mentions inside comment text" with `@here` in the comment. ### Issue for this PR

Closes #50969

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature

### What does this PR do?

**Problem:** when models come from somewhere other than a saved integration connection (a provider declared in config, or an add-on), `/models` shows no favorite hint and `ctrl+f` does nothing. Remapping `model.dialog.favorite` doesn't help either.

**Cause:** `DialogConnectedModels` in `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-model.tsx` hides the `model.dialog.favorite` action with `hidden: !connected()`, and `connected()` is only true when some integration has a connection. `DialogSelect` only binds keys for shown actions, so a hidden action has no binding at all. The gate predates v2, when `useConnected()` meant "has a non-free provider". It now also catches config-defined providers.

**Change:** favorites no longer depend on `connected()` in this picker:

- the favorite action is always shown, which brings back the hint and the `ctrl+f` binding
- favorited rows are marked (`(Favorite)`, or the marker under new designs)

Nothing changes when an integration is connected. The flat list still has no Favorites/Recent sections when nothing is connected, because the rows below them would have no provider headers and would look like part of the section. The integration action keeps its `connected()` wording.

#51760 by @argszero went after the same gate and was closed because of a PR limit. This PR also removes the hidden gate but keeps the flat list instead of adding sections.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): render partial diffs when review expand mode is on
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52263

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

With the review pane in "show all lines" (expand) mode, opening a modified file with a hunk-only patch leaves the diff blank and throws `FileDiff: loadDiffFiles is required to load full files for a partial diff`. Switching to collapse mode renders the same file fine.

**Cause**

`SessionReviewFilePreviewV2` passes `expandUnchanged` to the diff viewer for every diff. Since `@pierre/diffs` 1.5, `FileDiff` tries to load the full files when `expandUnchanged` is set on a partial diff, and throws because nothing in the app provides `loadDiffFiles`. A partial diff has no unchanged lines to expand anyway, and the same component already treats partial diffs differently for `hunkSeparators`.

**Change**

```diff
-      expandUnchanged={expandUnchanged()}
+      expandUnchanged={expandUnchanged() && !view().fileDiff.isPartial}
```

Partial diffs now render their hunks in expand mode, the same as in collapse mode. Full diffs (with before and after contents) still expand as before.

#52213 is the same crash (closed by the template bot). #57441 and #58881 look like the same blank pane, but they have a different cause (a broken patch from the server on Windows) and are not fixed here.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Mounted `SessionReviewFilePreviewV2` with a two-hunk patch-only diff and `expandMode="expand"` in a throwaway story on the stories server, and loaded it with Playwright in a fresh browser context.
  - On dev: page error `FileDiff: loadDiffFiles is required to load full files for a partial diff`, 0 diff rows rendered.

prs.title: fix(core): keep custom providers whose model sets only part of limit
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53005

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

A custom provider in the legacy `provider` / `npm` / `options` format disappears with no error if any of its models sets only part of `limit`, for example `"limit": { "context": 1000000 }`. It's missing from `opencode models` and from the normalized config.

**Cause**

The V1 model schema in `packages/core/src/v1/config/provider.ts` requires both `limit.context` and `limit.output`. A provider is decoded as a whole, so one partial limit fails the decode and the whole provider is skipped. The V2 schema (`packages/schema/src/config/provider.ts`) already makes every limit field optional.

**Change**

`context` and `output` are now optional in the V1 schema, and `migrateModel` in `packages/core/src/v1/config/migrate.ts` only calls `int()` on the ones that are set, the same way it already handles `input`:

```diff
-      context: int(info.limit.context),
+      context: info.limit.context === undefined ? undefined : int(info.limit.context),
```

Malformed values (strings, `NaN`, `Infinity`) are still rejected. Same approach as #53129 by @Sinfony8838 and #60291 by @craigalbrecht, both closed by the stale-PR cleanup.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Throwaway config dir with two legacy providers: `e-infra`, whose model sets only `limit.context`, and `no-limit`, which has no limit. `bun dev --standalone models` on dev lists only `no-limit/plain`. With the fix it lists `e-infra/thinker` too. `opencode debug config` shows the same difference.
- Added a "context-only limits" case to the existing legacy-vs-native table in `packages/core/test/config/provider.test.ts`. It fails without the source change and passes with it.
- `bun test test/config/provider.test.ts test/config/normalization.test.ts` and `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, and `bun run check` from the root.

prs.title: feat(core): agent tunnel messaging between sessions
prs.body:
## What

Agent-to-agent messaging between sessions in the same family, plus report-to-parent, as the backend for the agent graph view.

A running session can use the new built-in `tunnel` tool to send a directed message to another session in its family:

- `kind: "message"` targets any family member (sibling, ancestor, or descendant) via `to`.
- Omitting `to` (or passing `kind: "report"`) reports back to the parent session; `report` requires a strict ancestor.

Every send is **permission-gated**: `permission.assert({ action: "tunnel", resources: [<target's agent ?? session id>], ...Permission.invocation(context) })`, so per-agent allow/ask/deny rules control who may message whom. The tool's context hook only advertises family members the caller is permitted to reach.

Delivery reuses the existing synthetic inbox admission: the message id doubles as the synthetic inbox item id, so resends are idempotent and cross-recipient id reuse fails. Running targets receive it as a steer; idle targets are woken (`session.inbox.enqueued` / `session.inbox.delivered` record delivery — no new execution path). The send itself is recorded as one minimal durable event, `session.tunnel.sent`, on the **recipient** aggregate, projected into a new `session_tunnel` table that serves family queries.

## Feature flag

Gated by `agent_tunnel` (in `packages/schema/src/config/flag.ts`). On in local and dev builds, **off in releases**; override with `experimental.agent_tunnel: true` in config or `OPENCODE_FLAGS=agent_tunnel`. While the flag is off the `tunnel` tool is absent from the registry (reloaded on config change) and the experimental endpoints return 503.

## Endpoints / identifiers

| Path | Identifier | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/experimental/agent-tunnel?sessionID=<family member>&after=<seq>` | `experimental.agentTunnel.list` | Family messages ordered by `(time.created, sequence)` with an exclusive `after` cursor; `404 SessionNotFoundError` for unknown sessions |
| `GET /api/experimental/agent-tunnel/log?sessionID=<member>&after=<seq>&follow=true\|false` | `experimental.agentTunnel.log` | SSE: replay → one `agent-tunnel.synced` marker → live messages when `follow=true`; replay-and-close otherwise |

Both are experimental (may change without compatibility guarantees). The subscription is acquired before the replay read, so nothing is missed or duplicated across the sync boundary. The generated client exposes them as `client.experimental.agentTunnel.list(...)` / `client.experimental.agentTunnel.log(...)` (promise, Effect, and solid flavors).

## Pieces

- `packages/schema` — `AgentTunnel.Message` wire/storage contract (`agent-tunnel.ts`), `SessionEvent.TunnelSent` (`session.tunnel.sent`), the `agent_tunnel` flag.
- `packages/core` — `SessionTunnel` service (family validation, event publish, delivery), `session_tunnel` table + migration, projector fold, the `tunnel` tool plugin, 8 test cases.
- `packages/protocol` + `packages/server` — experimental endpoints, handler wiring, SSE follow stream, flag gate, smoke tests.
- `packages/client` — regenerated for the new event and endpoints, plus the group-coverage test.

prs.title: fix(core): serialize prompt settlement
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #34853

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Claim each Form or Permission request before publishing its settlement event. Concurrent replies, cancels and permission cascades fail or skip immediately, including inline listener re-entry. `always` saves approvals before publishing; failed storage keeps requests retryable while the service is open.

The owner retains cleanup responsibility when `close()` skips an active reply. Shutdown-driven cancellation makes one publication attempt, including when a form is created after shutdown.

Follow-up to #52550. Thanks @535628443 (#52550) and @sahiljagtap08 (#44340) for the per-request settlement approach. No feature flag is needed for this bug fix.

### How did you verify your code works?

issues.title: High CPU usage on Mac OS with long session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Mac OS, when running Pi, I can experience very high cpu usage, 100% and more; it appears to swing between 50-110%, while memory usage is at 600-800MB.

Anecdotally this appears linked to the context size (or perhaps rather the length of the session; I haven't tested with a large context but only a few turns). When I run multiple sessions, it is clearly the larger one that hits 100% cpu and not the others; cpu usage does seem to grow with the size of the session. 

But the weird thing is that the cpu usage is in the hot rendering path, so not in the actual processing of requests or responses from the llm (where I assume a longer context would take more time to process). So the problem is that the tui appears to use more cpu as the session gets longer, and I would expect this to be stable since at any time only a given portion of the session is on screen. 

An overview of sampling findings from the AI is available [here](https://gist.github.com/gterzian/3473a87df286d9c22c0872e61a2d1255)

I had the AI itself try to patch it, with some limited success, overview of what was tried and what the results were is [here](https://gist.github.com/gterzian/dbead50582b6f3bab546a23ef4bb76da )

### Steps to reproduce

Run Pi on Mac OS, and notice how the longer the session gets, the more CPU and memory is used. I get 100% on a long session with a 700k context. 

Here is the breakdown of the session in which the problem was noticed:
                                                                                                                                                                                                    
 - Session file: 3,831,794 bytes (~3.8 MB), 2,172 lines                                                                                                                                                        
 - User turns: 38                                                                                                                                                                                              
 - Assistant messages: 1,077                                                                                                                                                                                   
 - Tool calls: 1,072                                                                                                                                                                                           
 - Tool breakdown: bash 725, browser_evaluate 179, edit 102, read 12, write 12, browser_navigate 12, spec tools 12, misc browser tools ~17, readme_chain 1                                                     
 - Total context read: 430.4M tokens                                                                                                                                                                           
 - Uncached input: 1.57M tokens                                                                                                                                                                                
 - Cache hits: 428.9M tokens (99.6%)                                                                                                                                                                           
 - Total output: 464.7K tokens                                                                                                                                                                                 
 - Peak context (single message): 733,345 tokens

Just to say, this was a large session.

### Expected behavior

Stable CPU usage on the rendering path.

### Version

0.84.0

issues.title: subagent example: on Windows, Bun's virtual entry path (`B:/~BUN/root/pi.exe`) leaks into the subagent's first user message

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Windows, when pi runs as the compiled (Bun SEA) binary, the `subagent` example
extension (`packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts`) prepends
`B:/~BUN/root/pi.exe` — Bun's virtual filesystem entry path, i.e. `process.argv[1]` —
to the child `pi` argv. Because `pi --print` runs **each positional argument as a
separate prompt**, the child agent's **first user message** is the literal string
`B:/~BUN/root/pi.exe`. The child burns several assistant turns investigating that
nonexistent path (it reads the path, runs `ls B:/~BUN`, checks the scoop manifest…)
before the real `Task: ...` prompt arrives as the second user message. In one real
run, 13 of 35 child messages were wasted; the parent only sees the final text, so
the waste is invisible (exit code 0).

Root cause: `getPiInvocation()` guards with
`isBunVirtualScript = currentScript?.startsWith("/$bunfs/root/")` — Bun's **POSIX**
virtual prefix only. On Windows the prefix is `<drive>:/~BUN/root/`, and
`fs.existsSync()` returns **true** for bunfs virtual paths inside a Bun process, so
neither the guard nor the `existsSync` fallback filters it. The guard came from
#3002, which fixed the leak for POSIX only. Still present in v1.5.0 and
`main@d57c2d21916e`.

### Steps to reproduce

Prerequisites: Windows 10/11, pi installed as the compiled binary
(`scoop install pi-coding-agent`), subagent example extension enabled.

1. `pi --version` → 1.4.0 (Bun runtime 1.3.14).
2. Enable the example: copy `examples/extensions/subagent/` to
   `~/.pi/agent/extensions/subagent/`, and add any agent definition, e.g.
   `~/.pi/agent/agents/researcher.md` with `name`/`description` frontmatter.
3. Start `pi` in a terminal (TUI, default session saving) and dispatch any task:
   `Use the subagent tool: agent "researcher", task: run \`echo hi\` with bash and report its output.`
4. Let it finish. In the newest session file under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, find the
   subagent `toolResult` record and look at `details.results[0].messages[1]`:

   ```json
   {"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"B:/~BUN/root/pi.exe"}]}
   ```

   The actual prompt (`Task: ...`) only appears as the **second** user message,
   after several assistant turns spent investigating the phantom path. A quick scan:
   `rg --glob '*.jsonl' -l 'B:/~BUN/root/pi.exe' ~/.pi/agent/sessions`
5. Optional, zero-LLM proof of the argv layout — drop this temp extension, then run
   `pi -p --no-session probe`:

   ```ts
   // ~/.pi/agent/extensions/probe-argv/index.ts
   import { existsSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
   export default function () {
     writeFileSync("argv.json", JSON.stringify({
       argv: process.argv,
       argv1_exists: existsSync(process.argv[1]),
     }, null, 2));
     process.exit(0);
   }
   ```

   Output: `{"argv":["bun","B:/~BUN/root/pi.exe","-p","--no-session","probe"],"argv1_exists":true}`
   — `process.argv[1]` is Bun's virtual entry path and `fs.existsSync()` resolves it,
   so both the prefix guard and the existence check miss it.


### Expected behavior

The child process receives exactly one prompt — the task text — as its first (and
only) user message; no Bun virtual paths leak into the child argv; no extra LLM
turns.

### Version

pi 1.4.0 (scoop, Bun-compiled binary, Bun runtime 1.3.14), Windows 11 24H2. Code paths verified unchanged in v1.5.0 and `main@d57c2d21916e`.

issues.title: Send the session name as the OSC 7501 `title`
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Follow-up to #10607. Pi already puts the session name in `msg` while working and done. I'd like it to also send the session name as the `title` key, in every report, when the session has a name. `msg` and the states stay as they are.

### Why?

Agent dashboards (e.g. Herdr) want a stable label per session. Today the only place to get it is `msg`. But `msg` is only the session name while working or done: it is empty when idle, the dialog title when blocked, the error when failed, and "Compacting context" during compaction. So the label changes or disappears depending on state. The alternative is parsing the window title (`π - <name> - <folder>`), which #10607 was meant to avoid.

The spec has a key for this: `title` is the record's "short human-readable label", while `msg` says what it is doing right now. herdr-core already stores it (`status.title`).

### How? (optional)

- `packages/tui/src/program-status.ts`: add `title?: string` to `ProgramStatus`. Encode it in `formatProgramStatus` like `msg`, with the spec's 192-byte decoded limit.
- `program-status-reporter.ts`: set `title` to the session name on every report.
- Add a test and a line in `docs/terminal-setup.md`.

Happy to send the PR.

We fixed it on the extension side by adding `invalidate`, but every new extension will trip over the same opaque diagnostic.
