prs.title: Superseded by #11828: feat(ai): add native LongCat-2.5 provider
prs.body:
Adds native `longcat` provider support for LongCat-2.5 in pi-ai. Users can select it from the built-in provider directory and authenticate with `LONGCAT_API_KEY`, including in consumers such as DeepSeek Harness.

Reuses the OpenAI completions transport with binary thinking, text/image input, and tool-call reasoning replay. The existing OpenAI transport handles tool-only assistant messages unchanged; no shared API implementation or compatibility schema is modified. Catalog metadata follows the current official LongCat documentation because models.dev still lists older model IDs.

Supersedes #11776 using `feat/longcat-2.5-provider`, with upstream `main` merged through `b317575fd`. Related contribution proposal: #9308. This targets LongCat-2.5 and the current catalog layout, replacing the earlier LongCat-2.0 implementation. Maintainer contributor approval is still pending; this PR is a draft for review.

Validation:
- On 2026-11-05, real LongCat-2.5 tool-history replay accepted `content: null` with thinking both enabled and disabled (HTTP 200). The unnecessary string-content compatibility option and its related changes were removed, reducing the diff from 30 to 23 files. Repacked pi (off/high) and DSH UI tool-call smoke tests passed after removal.
- `npm run check` passes; focused provider/compatibility tests after simplification: 65 passed.
- After upstream synchronization, `npm run check` passed again and the newly merged terminal regression suite passed all 83 tests. Installed-package smoke tests below preceded the final upstream-only terminal/Azure/Windows/llama merges.
- `npm run build` passed. The pi-ai section of the isolated offline suite passed: 1,786 tests passed, 888 skipped.
- Packed and installed the changed packages locally. Real user flows passed in pi 1.5.0 interactive CLI and DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 UI: native model selection, thinking off/on, CSV read/write tools, image understanding, and follow-up recall using the real LongCat API.
- Rechecked on 2026-11-04 with a separate real validation API key: LongCat-2.5 model lookup returned HTTP 200, and the installed pi package read a CSV and wrote the correct total (`70`) using tools.

issues.title: Workflow agent permission approval never renders — the run hangs indefinitely while the status bar shows it needs approval (observed 0.26.6; reproduced 0.26.8)

labels.name: priority/P1
labels.description: High priority issue

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/interactive
labels.description: Interactive CLI features

labels.name: roadmap/multi-agent
labels.description: Roadmap: Multi-agent collaboration

issues.body:
## Summary

The core defect: a **workflow-runner agent** reaches a permission approval that
needs a human. The harness raises the request — `PermissionRequest` and
`Notification(permission_prompt)` both fire — and the status bar even shows a
pending-approval badge ("1 workflow ⚠ requires approval"). But **no approval
dialog ever renders**, and the run hangs indefinitely: no error, no timeout, no
recovery except a manual `Esc`.

- Production occurrence: 0.26.6 (a review-workflow agent's shell cleanup).
- Reproduced under control: **0.26.8** (one-agent workflow; deterministic
  steps in Reproduction below).

One additional verified shape of the same class — a non-main executor left
waiting on a permission decision, without reliable delivery, notification, or
honest status — plus two historical single observations kept for the record:

| Mode | Version(s) | Executor | `Notification(permission_prompt)` | Approval dialog | What wedges |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B — this issue** | 0.26.6 / **0.26.8 (reproduced)** | workflow agent | fires + `PermissionRequest` | **never rendered**; the badge shows "needs approval" | run stays `running`, `agentsDispatched: 1, agentsCompleted: 0`; agent transcript frozen on `functionCall` |
| **C — same class** | 0.24.4 / 0.24.5 (deterministic repro) | foreground subagent (parallel batch, one call matches `permissions.ask`) | **does not fire** | rendered in repros; silent in one production capture | whole batch parks `awaiting_approval`: `calls=3, responses=0`; task list keeps showing "running" |

Invariants shared by every verified mode:

- transcript frozen on `functionCall`(s) with no `functionResponse`;
- registry meta stays `status: "running"`, `lastUpdatedAt === createdAt`;
- no timeout, no error; the only observed exit is a manual `Esc` (confirmed
  for B in the 0.26.8 run: `Esc` cancelled the run and cleared the badge);
- the visible status stays "running" (or the badge) instead of "awaiting
  approval".

Localization, from the 0.26.8 control run (same session, same ask rule): a
foreground subagent making the identical call **got a rendered dialog, and
after the answer the call executed** (`PostToolUse` observed). The dialog loss
is specific to the workflow-agent executor. The badge proves the pending state
reaches at least the status-bar UI model — this narrows localization, but does
not distinguish dialog routing from rendering.

## Mode B — workflow agent: dialog never renders, the UI knows

Production (0.26.6): a review workflow run (`qwen review emit-workflow`, one
`verify` agent) worked normally for 7 minutes. At 13:06:44 UTC the agent
issued a shell cleanup (`rm -rf` of temp files) which correctly required
approval: hooks observed `PreToolUse` → `PermissionRequest` →
`Notification(permission_prompt)`. Then nothing:

- the agent transcript ends with a `functionCall` and no `functionResponse`;
- the main conversation was **idle** (no turn in flight; input field active,
  `Enter to steer`) — so this is not the "queued behind an active turn" case;
- the status bar carried the badge («1 workflow ⚠ требует подтверждения»)
  for the whole 24+ min stall — the approval state was present in the UI
  model, yet no dialog was routed to the surface;
- the TUI process was alive and rendering (debug log: continuous reflow
  lines, memory monitor every 30 s).

Reproduced under control on 0.26.8 (steps in Reproduction): identical
signature — `PreToolUse` → `PermissionRequest` →
`Notification(permission_prompt)` at the same second, badge shown, no dialog
for 3+ verified minutes, transcript frozen on the `functionCall`; `Esc`
cancelled the run and cleared the badge. Evidence captured for both runs
(hook logs, transcript tails, run checkpoints, pane captures); available on
request.

## Mode C — `permissions.ask` batch parks `awaiting_approval`, no notification (0.24.4/0.24.5)

A subagent's **parallel tool batch** where one call matches a
`permissions.ask` rule parks the whole batch in `awaiting_approval`:
`calls=3, responses=0` (including calls that match no rule). No
`Notification` event fires (desktop-notify hooks never trigger); the task
list keeps showing "running". Deterministic repro (ask rule on a protected
config path + a three-call batch); 4 production occurrences, worst 3 h 18 m.
Headless (`qwen -p`) degrades correctly to deny —
"non-interactive mode cannot prompt for confirmation" — so the fallback
logic exists; the interactive+subagent context is the one that parks. Not
re-verified on 0.26.8; please confirm whether still live. Full case write-up
with the deterministic repro available on request.

## Reproduction

**Mode B — reproduced under control on 0.26.8** (first occurrence 0.26.6
in production):

1. Project `.qwen/settings.json` contains an ask rule, e.g.
   `"ask": ["Read(~/.qwen/settings*.json)"]`.
2. Interactive session (auto approval mode). Run a one-agent **workflow**
   (Dynamic Workflow; invoking the bundled review skill also enables the
   Workflow tool) whose only agent must call `grep_search` with
   `path ~/.qwen/settings.json` (matches the ask rule).
3. Observe: `PreToolUse` → `PermissionRequest` →
   `Notification(permission_prompt)` all fire; the status bar shows
   "1 workflow ⚠ needs approval"; **no approval dialog renders** (verified
   3+ minutes); the workflow-agent transcript freezes on that
   `functionCall` with no `functionResponse`; `Esc` cancels the run and
   clears the badge.
4. **Contrast control in the same session, same ask rule:** a foreground
   subagent making the identical call got a rendered dialog, and after the
   answer the call executed (`PostToolUse` observed). The dialog loss is
   specific to the workflow-agent executor.

**Mode C — deterministic** (tested on 0.24.4/0.24.5):

1. In `settings.json`, add an ask rule matching a protected file, e.g.
   `"ask": ["Read(~/.qwen/settings*.json)"]`.
2. In an **interactive** session (auto approval mode), dispatch a foreground
   subagent (Agent tool) whose task is to make exactly three tool calls in
   one parallel turn: a `grep_search` on `~/.qwen/settings.json` (matches
   the ask rule) plus two `grep_search` calls on a plain file.
3. Observe: the whole batch parks in `awaiting_approval` —
   `calls=3, responses=0`; the task list keeps showing "running"; no
   `Notification` event fires. In our repros the dialog rendered in the
   parent TUI; in one production capture the wait surfaced silently (no
   dialog anywhere in the UI).
4. Control: the same dispatch headless (`qwen -p`) degrades correctly to
   deny ("non-interactive mode cannot prompt for confirmation").

## Expected behavior

The invariant we ask for: **no silent indefinite wait on a permission
decision.**

1. **In an interactive session, deliver the decision to the user** — render
   the approval dialog for foreground subagents and workflow agents (mode B
   shows the UI model already knows it is pending — the badge exists).
2. **Where delivery is impossible** (background or headless executors),
   fail closed: an explicit denial or error instead of parking forever. The
   codebase already documents this reasoning for background agents
   (`canPromptForAskBounce()`: "background agents cannot prompt, so an 'ask'
   there must fall back to deny rather than hang forever in
   `awaiting_approval`") — an analogous precedent for the subagent/workflow
   cases, not a prescribed implementation.
3. **Independently, honest status + signal**: task/workflow status should
   read "awaiting approval", not "running", and a `Notification`-class
   event should fire so monitoring hooks can alert the user. This makes the
   wait visible but does not substitute for (1)–(2).

## Historical observations (single occurrences, 0.25.0, not reproduced)

The generic foreground-subagent prompt/answer/resume path worked in one
0.26.8 control run; the original A and D scenarios were not re-run. Recorded
for the class history, not as demands of this issue.

**Mode A — subagent dialog never rendered (0.25.0).** Subagent `edit` on a
directory the session had not been granted. Hooks saw
`Notification(permission_prompt)` ("needs your permission to use edit"); no
dialog was ever drawn (1063-line scrollback: no Allow/Deny, no footer);
`PreToolUse` never fired; the transcript froze on `functionCall`. Stall
≈2–3 h across a machine sleep; a manual `Esc` the next morning ended it.
Same session, same tool, granted approval 30 minutes earlier: dialog
rendered and resolved in 11 s.

**Mode D — dialog rendered and answered, calls never resumed (0.25.0).**
Two parallel `run_shell_command` calls: `PreToolUse` ×2 →
`Notification(permission_prompt)` ×2 + `PermissionRequest` ×2. The dialog
**was shown and answered by the user** — and the calls never resumed:
transcripts frozen at that timestamp, 12 calls / 10 responses, hook silence
for ~1 h 20 m until `Esc`.

## Ask for maintainers

The modes likely live in different code paths (pre-UI gating, dialog
rendering, post-answer resume). Per-mode checklist:

- [ ] Mode B — a workflow agent's approval dialog renders (or the call fails closed) — observed 0.26.6; reproduced 0.26.8
- [ ] Mode C — an ask-rule match in a parallel batch either prompts (notification + dialog) or denies; the batch is not parked — deterministic repro, 0.24.4/0.24.5, please verify still live

We suggest keeping this issue open until B and C are resolved (or split).
Historical modes A and D carry no acceptance criteria — not re-tested, and
the generic foreground-subagent control was healthy on 0.26.8 (see
Historical observations).

## Environment

- 0.26.6 + 0.26.8 (mode B), 0.24.4 / 0.24.5 (mode C), 0.25.0 (modes A, D —
  historical); WSL2 and native Linux; interactive TUI; auto approval mode
  in all incidents.
- Executors: workflow-runner agents (Dynamic Workflow) and foreground
  subagents (Agent tool).
- Hooks registered: `Notification`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`,
  `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`,
  `UserPromptSubmit`.

issues.body:
## Proposal

We maintain bzmem, a general-purpose long-term memory service for AI applications, with APIs, SDKs, and client integrations. We would like to discuss adding an optional bzmem integration to Qwen Code.

bzmem separates original evidence, user facts, and assistant-derived knowledge. It evaluates whether information is worth retaining across sessions, tracks fact revisions and their sources, and returns relevant memory context within the configured user and project scope.

## About bzmem

bzmem (百智云长期记忆服务) turns interactions into durable, source-linked memory for AI applications. Its service-side responsibilities include memory extraction, fact revision, retrieval, and governance; clients consume it through APIs, SDKs, or MCP integrations.

- Public service: https://dolphinmem.app.baizhi.cloud/
- Evidence-backed memory: inspect the original material supporting retained facts.
- Source separation: distinguish user facts from assistant-derived knowledge.
- Context delivery: retrieve relevant information within the authorized user/project scope.
- Memory lifecycle: distinguish accepted input from retained facts, and support corrections and forgetting.

We maintain bzmem and are proposing this integration as its maintainers, rather than as an independent endorsement.

## Current integration

We have implemented an external integration using Qwen Code's existing Hooks and MCP capabilities:

- Session binding and context retrieval before model execution.
- Background capture of user input and final assistant replies, excluding reasoning and tool output.
- MCP tools for memory lookup, explicit submission, evidence inspection, processing receipts, and forgetting.
- Session title synchronization and an installer supporting installation, upgrades, and removal.

We have exercised this integration with Qwen Code 0.26.5, including real CLI requests, input/final-reply capture, and retrieval of existing cloud memories in fresh sessions with local automatic memory disabled. Web usage has also been user-verified. Installer checks cover repeat installation, credential reuse, upgrades, and preservation of unrelated configuration during removal.

These checks do not establish compatibility with every Qwen runtime or platform. In one new-memory test, the service filtered the test-only facts below its retention threshold; that case is not claimed as a successful write-and-recall test. Submission acceptance and completed memory retention are distinct states.

## Suggested integration

We propose an optional user-level connection setting, tentatively `memory.bzmem`, which would register the service tools and bind the configured credentials and scope. The service would continue to handle storage, extraction, revision management, and retrieval; Qwen would contain only the client-side integration.

Automatic context retrieval and conversation capture should be separately and explicitly enabled. Documentation would describe which content is sent, how it is scoped, how to disable the integration, and how it interacts with Qwen's native memory. Enabling an ordinary connection should not silently enable conversation uploads.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Would an optional built-in connection be an acceptable contribution, or would you prefer a native Qwen extension?
2. Would explicitly enabled automatic retrieval and background capture be appropriate within the existing Hook lifecycle?
3. What configuration, packaging, and runtime acceptance requirements should an initial PR follow?

We would follow the agreed scope with a focused PR, documentation, a reproducible demo, and tests. Our current adapter implementation is in our internal repository; publicly accessible integration artifacts would need to be prepared for review. We are responsible for bzmem and would maintain the adapter as Qwen evolves.

issues.body:
## Latest PR verification — 2026-10-07

Formal, open [PR #13599](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13599) is now at `1e92feee82ed7ad297cac5e65829eeb1761f859c`. It preserves the tested production tree and includes the parallel patrol fixes additively. Latest targeted-file receipts cover 1,509 distinct executed passing cases; affected core/CLI builds and typechecks passed. [High-pressure native CLI/tmux report](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13599#issuecomment-6039023549) and [actual JSON MCP discovery/invocation/tmux report](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13599#issuecomment-6039068913) verify next-request sizes, complete-output recovery and digests. The reports pin their individual executed commits and controlled-provider boundaries.

MCP deliberately inherits both global character and line limits (defaults 80,000 / 2,000), and explicit values remain independent. This is a proposed default/observability improvement with local verification, not a claim of production billing savings. **The PR is unmerged and unreleased; keep this issue open until merge.**

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

正式 PR #13599 已推送到 `1e92feee82ed`，增量纳入并行修正，保留实际验收的 production tree。最新定向文件回执去重后共 1,509 个实际执行通过的用例，相关 core/CLI 构建与类型检查通过；两份真实 tmux 报告分别核验高压力 CLI 与 MCP JSON 的实际请求大小、完整恢复文件及摘要，并明确各自测试 commit 和受控 provider 边界。MCP 同时跟随全局字符/行数预算，默认 80,000 / 2,000，显式值分别有效。PR 未合入、未发布，issue 继续开放，不宣称生产账单收益。

</details>

---

## Current main verification — 2026-10-07

Verified at [`1aba19c87889`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/commit/1aba19c87889e8bd55f5249b81e21d8de3f056dd) using freshly built core/CLI artifacts.

This issue is partially implemented, not complete. PR #11727 has merged and improves producer-side budget ordering. In the freshly built core, a successful `read_file` `ToolCallEvent` still exposes `content_length` but no `raw_content_length` or `injected_content_length` fields. Source inspection also confirms that the scheduler recomputes model-facing length after truncation. This is a telemetry-type/configuration check, not an end-to-end metrics-backend run. Current finalizer diagnostics are useful prior work, but they do not prove the requested per-call raw-versus-injected reporting and consistent handling across tools. The issue remains open.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

已有预算相关修复合并，但每次调用的原始大小与注入大小统计仍未完整提供，继续保持开放。此次证据是实际类型/配置和源码检查，不是指标后端验收。

</details>

---

### What would you like to be added?

Two coupled changes: make oversized tool-result handling consistent and observable across tools, and report raw-vs-injected result size for **every** tool call.

#### A. Oversized-result handling

`origin/main` already has an extensive pipeline, so this is not a greenfield request. Four ordered layers run in `coreToolScheduler` before a result reaches history:

1. **Persistence gate** — `maybePersistLargeToolResult()` (L6353, called at L5423/L5831). Fires above `getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() + GATE_HEADROOM` (3000, so 28k by default) and replaces the result with a `<persisted-output>` stub pointing at `tool-results/<callId>.txt`. Exempt: `GATE_EXEMPT_TOOLS` = `read_file`, `read_mcp_resource`, `enter_plan_mode`.
2. **Per-tool / global truncation** — `truncateLlmContent()` (L5567) → `truncateAndSaveToFile()`, budget from `maxOutputChars`, preview `PREVIEW_SIZE_CHARS = 2000` (head/tail), sha256 digest (`FULL_OUTPUT_DIGEST_LABEL`), idempotency sentinel (`TOOL_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED_PREFIX`).
3. **Combined second pass** — L5603, re-bounds at `COMBINED_PASS_TOLERANCE_FACTOR` (2x) after hook/skill `<system-reminder>` metadata is appended.
4. **Per-message batch budget** — `applyBatchOutputBudget()` (L6403) → `finalizeToolResponses()` (`tools/tool-response-finalizer.ts`), reducing the aggregate of parallel calls to `DEFAULT_TOOL_OUTPUT_BATCH_BUDGET = 200_000`.

Global defaults: `DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_TOOL_OUTPUT_THRESHOLD = 25_000`, `DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_TOOL_OUTPUT_LINES = 1000` (`config/config.ts` L773-780). Per-tool budgets vary by more than an order of magnitude:

| tool | `maxOutputChars` |
| --- | --- |
| `shell` | 30,000 default (`getShellOutputThreshold`, config-overridable); also truncates in-`execute()` |
| `grep` / `ripGrep` | 20,000 |
| `agent` | 32,000 (`truncateKeep = tail`) |
| `web_search` | 100,000 + 2,000 envelope headroom |
| MCP tool (`mcp-tool.ts`) | 500,000; also truncates in-`execute()` via `truncateTextParts()` |
| `read_file`, `read_mcp_resource`, `enter_plan_mode` | `Infinity` (self-managed, and gate-exempt) |
| everything else | `undefined` → global 25,000 |

Requests:

1. Re-examine the 500k MCP budget. An MCP result under 500k chars is injected verbatim: no spill, no preview, no event — in practice the largest uncontrolled contributor to injected context, and it is 20x the global default.
2. `web_fetch` (`MAX_CONTENT_CHARS = 100_000`, head-only `truncateText()`) and `web_search` self-truncate inside `execute()` with their own wording and **no** spill-to-file, while `shell` and MCP self-truncate *and* spill. The recovery story therefore differs per tool for no stated reason; worth consolidating or at least documenting which mechanism wins.
3. Improve the recovery path when a result does spill. The model sees head+tail only and loses the middle; the ask from the field is to make the stub self-sufficient (total chars/lines, digest, and an explicit "page in with `read_file` offset/limit" hint) so the model reads the spilled file instead of re-running the tool. `truncateKeep` is already the per-tool hook.
4. Consider a middle tier between "inject verbatim" and "character-window slice" for structured results (notably MCP JSON): keys/shape + row counts + a sample. A char window can cut JSON mid-token, which is the accuracy complaint behind this request.

#### B. Telemetry: raw vs injected size, on all four layers

Current state:

- **`tool_output_truncated` covers exactly one of the four layers.** `logToolOutputTruncated()` is emitted only from `truncateToolOutput()` (`tools/truncation.ts`), and only inside `if (result.outputFile)`. The persistence gate (`persistAndTruncateToolResult`) and the batch budget (`tool-response-finalizer.ts`, `tool-result-retention.ts`) contain **no telemetry calls at all** — verified by grep. So the two layers that offload the most content are unobservable, and even layer 2 silently skips the fallback path where the wrapped form is not smaller than the original.
- **`ToolCallEvent.content_length` is post-truncation only.** The scheduler captures the raw length first, then deliberately overwrites it (`// Recompute AFTER truncation so it reflects the model-facing length`, L5659) and again after the batch pass (L6440). The raw number is lost for every call that did not spill.
- **`contentLength` stays `undefined` for non-string (`Part[]`) results**, so a whole class of MCP results reports no size at all on `tool_call`.
- **No metric carries a size dimension.** `recordToolCallMetrics` attributes are `function_name`, `status`, `success`, `decision`, `tool_type` only; `TOOL_CALL_COUNT` / `TOOL_CALL_LATENCY` / `TOOL_EXECUTION_*` have nothing size-related, and `endToolExecutionSpan()` sets no content-length attribute. Nothing is aggregatable in the metrics backend.
- **`content_length` does not reach the RUM path either** — `QwenLogger.logToolCallEvent` has no size field (it does mirror `original_content_length` / `truncated_content_length` for the truncation event).
- **`ToolResultPersistedEvent` is dead code.** Declared in `telemetry/types.ts` L977 with `tool_name` / `bytes_written` / `output_file` / `prompt_id`, listed in the event union, but never constructed and never logged — there is no `logToolResultPersisted` and no call site. This is the obvious ready-made hook for layer-1 telemetry.
- Everything is measured in characters; the governance target is tokens.

Requests:

1. On every completed tool call, report `raw_content_length` and `injected_content_length`, plus a `truncated` flag and the applied budget with its source (per-tool vs global fallback vs batch). Compute it for `Part[]` results too.
2. Emit size telemetry from all four layers — wiring up the existing `ToolResultPersistedEvent` for the persistence gate is the cheapest first step — so offload rate is measurable per layer, not just for layer 2.
3. Add an estimated token count next to the character count, reusing the estimator the compression pipeline already uses (`estimatePartChars`, `services/compactionInputSlimming.ts`) so both agree about the same history.
4. Add a size histogram metric (e.g. `qwen_code.tool.result.chars` / `.tokens`) with `function_name`, `tool_type` and `truncated` attributes, so per-tool consumption can be charted and alerted on rather than sampled from logs. Respect the existing metric-cardinality controls.

Already done, do not re-request: `analyzeToolResultRetention()` diagnostics (`toolResultCount`, `totalChars`, `largestResultChars`, `oversizedResultCount`) are surfaced by `/doctor memory` (`packages/cli/src/ui/commands/doctorCommand.ts` L496/L569). Extending that same view with the layer-1/4 blind spots would be a natural follow-on.

### Why is this needed?

Tool results are the dominant *controllable* contributor to injected context, and the two problems reinforce each other:

- **Accuracy.** When a result is oversized the model gets a head/tail preview and loses the middle. Reported internally as degrading answer quality; the workaround people fall back to is rewriting the underlying script or skill to emit less, which does not generalise.
- **Blindness.** We cannot rank tools by injected cost. The raw size is discarded for every call that fits under budget, `content_length` is post-truncation, and the only size-bearing event fires on one of four layers. Without per-tool raw-vs-injected numbers there is no data to tune the budgets in section A, and no way to tell whether a change helped.

Fixing only one side is not enough: tightening budgets without measurement risks silently degrading accuracy, and adding measurement without a consistent spill path leaves the largest results unbounded.

### Additional context

- **Read the prior art first.** `docs/design/2026-08-10-tool-output-offload-preview.md` is the authoritative description of the offload/preview state transition and privacy model (required by [#4184](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/4184), mitigation implemented in #4880). Also `docs/design/final-tool-response-budget.md` — which notes the layers do not share structured state, the root cause of the observability gap in section B — plus `docs/plans/final-tool-response-budget-implementation.md` and `docs/design/tool-use-summary/unified-tool-output.md`. `FULL_OUTPUT_DIGEST_LABEL` came out of [#9450](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/9450) (loop guards fingerprinting persisted output); any new stub format must keep `loopDetectionService` recognising the sentinels.
- Origin: feedback on tool-result context costs. The request combines spill-to-file and read-on-demand handling with per-tool raw-versus-injected character/token reporting. Extra read round trips and precision loss from partial reads are the concerns addressed by A.3/A.4.
- Related but distinct: [PR #10410](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/10410) preserves the prompt cache for deferred tools. That addresses tool-*declaration* context cost (deferred loading currently only kicks in above ~10% of model context because loading invalidates the cache), not tool-*result* size. Not a substitute for this issue.
- All paths, constants and line numbers above were read from `origin/main` (`b1ac3e2970`). No existing open issue covers this (searched tool-result truncation / oversized output / result-size telemetry).

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

One implementation of the agent loop in `packages/core`, used by every surface. The agent loop is the cycle that sends a prompt, streams the reply, runs the requested tools, sends their results back, and repeats until the model stops calling tools.

The shared loop is introduced behind one experimental setting and adopted one surface at a time:

- `experimental.unifiedAgentLoop` is a boolean, `false` by default, and takes effect after a restart. `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=1` overrides it for CI and scripted runs. Both follow the pattern of `experimental.agentTeam` / `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_AGENT_TEAM`.
- At each surface's entry point the setting chooses between the shared loop and that surface's current loop. The current loop stays untouched as the `else` branch, so with the setting off a surface behaves exactly as it does today. Surfaces that have not moved yet ignore the setting.
- A surface moves only after a parity suite shows that, with the setting on, its model requests and its output match the current loop. Any difference must be listed and linked to an issue.
- Each surface changes its default on its own once it has moved, starting with headless, and drops its current loop one release later. A surface does not wait for the others. Send options that tell the client to skip part of its work for one host are transition steps. Each is listed in the design with the step that removes it, and a surface keeps its old default while it has one open.

This issue tracks that work. Each step is its own PR.

#### Today's loops (upstream `56733c35aa`)

| Surface | Loop | Model call | Tool execution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ink TUI | `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/use-llm-stream.ts` | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` | scheduler completion callback → `submitQuery(ToolResult)` |
| OpenTUI | `packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/live-session.ts` | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` | a new scheduler per batch |
| Headless `-p` and the stream-json SDK transport | `packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.ts`, with a second copy of the loop in the drain turn (`:2888-3066`) | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` | `executeToolCall` per call, which builds a `CoreToolScheduler` per call (`nonInteractiveToolExecutor.ts:75-96`), plus its own partitioning, in-flight cap and ordered finalize |
| ACP: Zed, VS Code companion, `qwen serve` / Web Shell, channels | `packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/Session.ts`, four loop bodies: main `:7534`, Stop continuation `:8420`, cron `:11463`, notifications `:12792` | `LlmChat.sendMessageStream` directly (`:9744-9751`) | its own executor, `runToolCalls` / `runTool` (`:13799-17842`) |
| Hosted Harness | `packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-harness-model.ts:828-1143` | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream`, but fires 13 hook events itself (`:67-81`) | journaled sequential dispatch (`hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts`) |
| Subagents, background and forked agents, workflows, in-process teams | `packages/core/src/agents/runtime/agent-core.ts`: `_runReasoningLoopInner` (`:1016`) and `processFunctionCalls` (`:2023`) | `LlmChat.sendMessageStream` directly, parsing chunks itself | one `CoreToolScheduler` per round |
| Speculation | `packages/core/src/followup/speculation.ts` | `LlmChat.sendMessageStream` directly | runs tools directly, without the scheduler |

`LlmClient.sendMessageStream` runs one model request plus the continuations it owns: the Stop hook, steering at a model boundary and the next-speaker check. It never runs tools. So every surface writes its own "run the tools, send the results, repeat" part, and three loops skip `LlmClient` altogether.

#### Target

```text
Surfaces: Ink · OpenTUI · headless/SDK · ACP · AgentCore · speculation (Hosted evaluated last)
   │  input, event sink, approval responder, mid-turn input, surface policies
   ▼
Shared agent loop (packages/core)
   model round : LlmClient.sendMessageStream for a main session,
                 Turn over the agent's own LlmChat for subagents and speculation
   tool batch  : one whole-batch CoreToolScheduler per round
   after batch : duplicate handling → finalizeToolResponses → recording
                 → loop guards and reminders → mid-turn input → ToolResult continuation
   outcome     : a typed terminal reason, mapped by each surface
   ▼
LlmClient → Turn → LlmChat (unchanged)
```

- Approvals go through a responder the surface supplies: a dialog in the TUI, `session/request_permission` in ACP, `can_use_tool` for SDK clients, and auto-deny in plain headless.
- Each surface maps the terminal reason to its own result: an exit code, an ACP `stopReason`, an agent `terminateMode`, or UI state.
- Surface-specific behavior is a policy passed to the loop, not a fork of it. Examples: the `--max-tool-calls` pre-launch ticker, structured output, idle-time continuations (Goal, teammates, drain turns), model overrides, and the daemon tool-loop guards.
- An interface with a second implementation, such as the `Turn`-backed model round, is added in the PR that needs it, not up front.

#### Plan

- [x] Design document, English and Chinese: #15343
- [x] PR1: the shared loop, the setting, headless (`-p` and stream-json) on the shared loop, and the parity suite: #15369
  - [x] scheduled signal: a nightly E2E Linux leg with the setting on, which headless and ACP wait on for two weeks on main before their defaults change: #16192
  - [ ] headless default on
  - [ ] remove the current headless loop
- [ ] PR2: ACP sessions
  - [x] PR 2a: the model round of fresh user prompts on the shared round; ACP keeps its tool step: #15509
  - [x] PR 2b: the tool batch of those turns on the whole-batch scheduler; the daemon tool-loop guards become the client's guards plus a surface policy: #15627
  - [x] PR 2c-1: the stop point of those turns on the client's chain, with the Todo Stop Guard as an ordered stop policy; background results and queued input no longer continue a turn at its stop point; `stopHookRunByHost` removed: #15695
  - [x] PR 2c-2: channel, Goal-proposal, retry, continue and restore turns: #15902
  - [x] PR 2c-3: Goal turns: #16131
  - [x] PR 2c-4: cron and background-notification turns: #16190
  - [ ] ACP default on, then remove its current loop
- [ ] PR3: Ink TUI, then default on and removal
  - [x] PR 3a: every model round on the loop's round; the TUI keeps its tool step; the Ink parity suite: #16206
  - [x] PR 3b-1: a round's tool calls as one shared batch; the TUI's completion step continues the turn: #16304
  - [x] PR 3b-2a: the TUI's stops end the shared batch; a tool that ends the turn ends it: #16365
  - [x] PR 3b-2b: the batch awaited by the turn; the TUI's steps before the next round: #16385
  - [ ] PR 3c-1: input at a tool boundary through the loop's next round; a retry: #16428
  - [ ] PR 3c-2: cron, background-notification, teammate and Goal turns
  - [ ] Ink TUI default on, then remove its current loop
- [ ] PR4: OpenTUI, then default on and removal
- [ ] PR5: AgentCore (subagents, background and forked agents, workflows), then default on and removal
- [ ] PR6: speculation, then default on and removal
- [ ] Hosted Harness: evaluated separately, after the other surfaces
- [ ] Remove the setting

Out of scope for this round:

- session-level scheduling, i.e. when notifications, cron jobs, Goal turns and teammate messages start a loop;
- the Hosted Harness until its separate evaluation;
- the provider layer and `LlmChat`;
- `CoreToolScheduler` internals beyond the hooks the loop needs;
- UI rendering and wire protocols.

### Why is this needed?

Every behavior that belongs to the loop has to be written once per surface, and the copies have drifted apart.

In the code (upstream `56733c35aa`):

- **The session turn cap has three formulas.**
  - `LlmClient` stops at `max > 0 && count > max` (`client.ts:4529-4531`).
  - Headless stops at `max >= 0 && count > max` (`nonInteractiveCli.ts:663`).
  - The Hosted Harness stops at `max > 0 && round >= max` (`hosted-harness-model.ts:841`).

  With `model.maxSessionTurns: 0`, headless stops at the first turn while the other two never stop.
- **Duplicate provider tool-call suppression is assembled four times**: `nonInteractiveCli.ts:1962`, `use-llm-stream.ts:3236`, `Session.ts:14086` and `agent-core.ts:2085`. The key falls back three different ways.
- **The tool concurrency cap is implemented four times**: `coreToolScheduler.ts:5465`, `nonInteractiveCli.ts:2264`, `Session.ts:14365` and `:17031`. ACP runs only consecutive Agent calls concurrently (`Session.ts:14234`), while the scheduler runs every concurrency-safe call concurrently.
- **`finalizeToolResponses` is called separately by six loops, and once more inside the scheduler.**
- **Mod tool checks reach only some surfaces.** `modToolCheck` is wired per surface and reaches Ink, OpenTUI and headless. ACP sessions have none, so Zed, VS Code and Web Shell don't get them either.
- **ACP bypasses `LlmClient.sendMessageStream`.**
  - It re-implements UserPromptSubmit, the Stop hook and its cap, MessageDisplay, file snapshots, plan/arena reminders, workflow intent, the session token gate and Goal permits.
  - It has no next-speaker check, no `maxSessionTurns`, and none of the content loop heuristics or late MCP/skill reminders.
  - Its comments say so: "duplicated from coreToolScheduler.ts" (`Session.ts:15721`), "Mirrors the core send path" (`:9547`), "Mirror of core's checkGlobalDuplicate" (`:1364`). Some of its cross-references already point at code that has moved (`:7375`, `:14600`).
- **The Hosted Harness fires 13 hook events itself** (`hosted-harness-model.ts:67-81`). It sends a blocking Stop hook's continuation as `ToolResult`; `LlmClient` sends it as `Hook`.

Defects found while comparing the loops are filed separately: #15324 (ACP writes an edit cut off by max_tokens), #15325 (a stream-json message past `--max-session-turns` returns success), #15326 (OpenTUI runs tool calls from a retried attempt and skips recording native results). Writing the parity suite also turned up #15365 (in stream-json, a message sent during startup runs before the first message), which is outside the loop.

Open issues that come from this split: #14114, #12209, #12020, #8542, #13851, #12113.

Every new loop-level behavior pays the same price. For example, the loop-protection reminders (#15016) had to be injected separately in `client.ts`, `agent-core.ts` and `Session.ts`.

### Additional context

**Related issues.**

- #8775 proposed unifying the session loops on a `Turn`-based runtime. Its inventory still holds on current main. This issue tracks a staged, opt-in way to carry that direction out.
- #10219 and #10078 make agent backends pluggable.
- #11695 separates where tools execute.

This issue changes neither of those. It only makes sure there is one loop for them to plug into.

**Verification.**

- `integration-tests/fake-openai-server.ts` already records every request body. The parity suite runs each scripted scenario on a surface twice, with the setting off and on.
- It compares two things: the normalized request sequence (what the model saw), and the surface's output (stream-json frames or ACP `session/update` notifications).
- First scenarios:
  - plain text, a single tool, and a parallel read-only batch;
  - mixed safe and unsafe calls;
  - approval allowed and denied;
  - cancel during a tool;
  - retry mid-stream and model fallback;
  - an output-truncated edit;
  - loop detection;
  - a blocking Stop hook;
  - `--max-tool-calls`, `maxSessionTurns` and structured output.

**Acceptance for the end state.**

| Measure | Today | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent loop implementations | 7, plus the extra copies inside headless and ACP | 1 |
| Loops that call `LlmChat.sendMessageStream` directly | 3 | 0 |
| Loops that parse stream chunks outside `turn.ts` | 3 | 0 |
| Loops that call `finalizeToolResponses` | 6 | 1 |
| Session turn-cap formulas | 3 | 1 |

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

### 希望新增什么？

在 `packages/core` 中只保留一份 agent loop 实现，供所有入口共用。agent loop 指这样一个循环：发送提示、流式接收回复、执行模型请求的工具、把工具结果发回模型，直到模型不再调用工具为止。

共享 loop 通过一个实验性设置引入，并按入口逐个迁移：

- `experimental.unifiedAgentLoop` 是布尔值，默认 `false`，重启后生效。`QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=1` 可以覆盖它，供 CI 和脚本化运行使用。两者沿用 `experimental.agentTeam` / `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_AGENT_TEAM` 的写法。
- 每个入口在启动处根据该设置，选择共享 loop 或自己现有的 loop。现有 loop 原样保留为 `else` 分支，所以设置关闭时，入口的行为与现在完全一致。尚未迁移的入口忽略该设置。
- 只有当对拍测试证明设置开启时，该入口的模型请求和输出都与现有 loop 一致，这个入口才算完成迁移。任何差异都必须列出，并关联到对应 issue。
- 每个入口完成迁移后各自修改默认值，从 headless 开始，一个版本之后再删除它的现有 loop，不必等其他入口。为某个宿主让 client 跳过部分工作的发送选项只是过渡手段：设计文档会逐项列出它们，并写明由哪一步移除；入口还有未关闭的选项时，保持原默认值。

本 issue 跟踪这项工作，每一步都是单独的 PR。

#### 现有的 loop（upstream `56733c35aa`）

| 入口 | loop 位置 | 模型调用 | 工具执行 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ink TUI | `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/use-llm-stream.ts` | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` | scheduler 完成回调 → `submitQuery(ToolResult)` |
| OpenTUI | `packages/cli/src/ui/opentui/live-session.ts` | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` | 每批新建一个 scheduler |
| Headless `-p` 与 stream-json SDK 传输 | `packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.ts`，drain turn 中还有一份 loop 副本（`:2888-3066`） | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` | 每个调用走一次 `executeToolCall`，每次都新建一个 `CoreToolScheduler`（`nonInteractiveToolExecutor.ts:75-96`），另外自行实现分批、并发上限和按序收尾 |
| ACP：Zed、VS Code companion、`qwen serve` / Web Shell、channels | `packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/Session.ts`，内含四份 loop：主循环 `:7534`、Stop 续发 `:8420`、cron `:11463`、通知 `:12792` | 直接调用 `LlmChat.sendMessageStream`（`:9744-9751`） | 自带执行器 `runToolCalls` / `runTool`（`:13799-17842`） |
| Hosted Harness | `packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-harness-model.ts:828-1143` | `LlmClient.sendMessageStream`，但 13 种 hook 事件由它自己触发（`:67-81`） | 写日志的串行调度（`hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts`） |
| Subagent、后台与 fork agent、workflow、进程内 team | `packages/core/src/agents/runtime/agent-core.ts`：`_runReasoningLoopInner`（`:1016`）与 `processFunctionCalls`（`:2023`） | 直接调用 `LlmChat.sendMessageStream`，并自行解析 chunk | 每轮一个 `CoreToolScheduler` |
| Speculation | `packages/core/src/followup/speculation.ts` | 直接调用 `LlmChat.sendMessageStream` | 直接执行工具，不经过 scheduler |

`LlmClient.sendMessageStream` 只负责一次模型请求，外加它自己处理的几种续发：Stop hook、模型边界处的 steering，以及 next-speaker 检查。它从不执行工具。因此“执行工具、发回结果、继续下一轮”这部分由每个入口各写一份，其中三个 loop 完全绕过了 `LlmClient`。

#### 目标结构

```text
入口：Ink · OpenTUI · headless/SDK · ACP · AgentCore · speculation（Hosted 最后单独评估）
   │  输入、事件出口、审批应答、中途输入、入口策略
   ▼
共享 agent loop（packages/core）
   模型轮：主会话用 LlmClient.sendMessageStream，
           subagent 与 speculation 在各自的 LlmChat 上使用 Turn
   工具批：每轮一个整批调度的 CoreToolScheduler
   批次后：重复调用处理 → finalizeToolResponses → 记录
           → 循环守卫与提醒 → 中途输入 → ToolResult 续发
   结束：返回带类型的终止原因，由各入口映射
   ▼
LlmClient → Turn → LlmChat（不改）
```

- 审批通过入口提供的应答器完成：TUI 弹对话框，ACP 发 `session/request_permission`，SDK 客户端走 `can_use_tool`，普通 headless 自动拒绝。
- 各入口把终止原因映射成自己的结果：退出码、ACP `stopReason`、agent 的 `terminateMode` 或 UI 状态。
- 入口特有的行为作为策略传给 loop，而不是复制一份 loop。例如：`--max-tool-calls` 的启动前计数、structured output、空闲时的续发（Goal、teammate、drain turn）、模型覆盖，以及 daemon 的工具循环守卫。
- 只有在需要第二种实现的 PR 里，才引入对应的接口（例如基于 `Turn` 的模型轮），不预先抽象。

#### 计划

- [x] 设计文档（中英文）：#15343
- [x] PR1：共享 loop、设置项、headless（`-p` 与 stream-json）切到共享 loop，以及对拍测试：#15369
  - [x] 定时信号：每晚的 E2E 增加一个开启设置的 Linux 分支，headless 和 ACP 修改默认值前要等它在 main 上连续通过两周：#16192
  - [ ] headless 默认开启
  - [ ] 删除 headless 现有的 loop
- [ ] PR2：ACP 会话
  - [x] PR 2a：全新用户 prompt 的模型轮切到共享模型轮，ACP 保留自己的工具步骤：#15509
  - [x] PR 2b：这些轮次的工具批切到整批 scheduler；daemon 工具循环守卫改为 client 的守卫加一项入口策略：#15627
  - [x] PR 2c-1：这些轮次的 stop 点迁到 client 的链上，Todo Stop Guard 作为有序的 stop 策略；后台结果和排队的输入不再在 stop 点让这一轮继续；删除 `stopHookRunByHost`：#15695
  - [x] PR 2c-2：channel、Goal 提案、retry、continue 和 restore 轮次：#15902
  - [x] PR 2c-3：Goal 轮次：#16131
  - [x] PR 2c-4：cron 和后台通知轮次：#16190
  - [ ] ACP 默认开启，随后删除它现有的 loop
- [ ] PR3：Ink TUI，随后默认开启并删除旧 loop
  - [x] PR 3a：每个模型轮改用 loop 的模型轮；TUI 保留自己的工具步骤；Ink 对拍测试：#16206
  - [x] PR 3b-1：一个模型轮的工具调用作为一个共享工具批运行；由 TUI 的完成步骤续发轮次：#16304
  - [x] PR 3b-2a：TUI 自己的停止条件结束共享工具批；结束轮次的工具会结束轮次：#16365
  - [x] PR 3b-2b：工具批由轮次等待完成；TUI 的步骤改为在下一轮之前运行：#16385
  - [ ] PR 3c-1：工具边界的输入改走 loop 的下一轮；retry：#16428
  - [ ] PR 3c-2：cron、后台通知、teammate 和 Goal 轮次
  - [ ] Ink TUI 默认开启，随后删除旧 loop
- [ ] PR4：OpenTUI，随后默认开启并删除旧 loop
- [ ] PR5：AgentCore（subagent、后台与 fork agent、workflow），随后默认开启并删除旧 loop
- [ ] PR6：speculation，随后默认开启并删除旧 loop
- [ ] Hosted Harness：在其他入口之后单独评估
- [ ] 删除该设置项

本轮不包括：

- 会话层调度，即通知、cron、Goal 轮次、teammate 消息何时启动一轮 loop；
- Hosted Harness（等单独评估）；
- provider 层与 `LlmChat`；
- loop 所需钩子之外的 `CoreToolScheduler` 内部逻辑；
- UI 渲染与通信协议。

### 为什么需要？

所有属于 loop 的行为都要在每个入口各实现一次，而这些副本已经各自走样。

代码中的例子（upstream `56733c35aa`）：

- **会话轮数上限有三种算法。**
  - `LlmClient`：`max > 0 && count > max`（`client.ts:4529-4531`）。
  - headless：`max >= 0 && count > max`（`nonInteractiveCli.ts:663`）。
  - Hosted Harness：`max > 0 && round >= max`（`hosted-harness-model.ts:841`）。

  设置 `model.maxSessionTurns: 0` 时，headless 在第一轮就停止，另外两处则永远不停。
- **重复的 provider 工具调用过滤被组装了四次**：`nonInteractiveCli.ts:1962`、`use-llm-stream.ts:3236`、`Session.ts:14086`、`agent-core.ts:2085`。键的回退规则有三种。
- **工具并发上限实现了四次**：`coreToolScheduler.ts:5465`、`nonInteractiveCli.ts:2264`、`Session.ts:14365` 和 `:17031`。ACP 只让连续的 Agent 调用并发（`Session.ts:14234`），而 scheduler 会让所有并发安全的调用并发。
- **六个 loop 各自调用 `finalizeToolResponses`，scheduler 内部还另有一次调用。**
- **Mod 工具检查只覆盖部分入口。** `modToolCheck` 按入口分别接线，只接到了 Ink、OpenTUI 和 headless。ACP 会话没有接，因此 Zed、VS Code、Web Shell 也都没有。
- **ACP 绕过了 `LlmClient.sendMessageStream`。**
  - 它自己重新实现了 UserPromptSubmit、Stop hook 及其次数上限、MessageDisplay、文件快照、plan/arena 提醒、workflow intent、会话 token 门限和 Goal 许可。
  - 它没有 next-speaker 检查，没有 `maxSessionTurns`，也没有内容循环启发式和会话中途的 MCP/skill 提醒。
  - 它的注释也写明了这一点：“duplicated from coreToolScheduler.ts”（`Session.ts:15721`）、“Mirrors the core send path”（`:9547`）、“Mirror of core's checkGlobalDuplicate”（`:1364`）。部分交叉引用指向的代码已经挪走（`:7375`、`:14600`）。
- **Hosted Harness 自己触发 13 种 hook 事件**（`hosted-harness-model.ts:67-81`）。Stop hook 阻断后的续发，它以 `ToolResult` 类型发送，而 `LlmClient` 用的是 `Hook`。

对比各 loop 时发现的缺陷已另行提交：#15324（ACP 会写入被 max_tokens 截断的编辑）、#15325（stream-json 中超过 `--max-session-turns` 的消息仍返回成功）、#15326（OpenTUI 会执行重试前的工具调用，且不记录原生工具结果）。编写对拍测试时还发现了 #15365（在 stream-json 中，启动期间发来的消息会先于第一条消息执行），它不属于 loop 本身。

由这种分裂导致的未关闭 issue：#14114、#12209、#12020、#8542、#13851、#12113。

每加一项 loop 层的新行为，都要付出同样的代价。例如 loop-protection 的提醒（#15016）就不得不分别注入到 `client.ts`、`agent-core.ts` 和 `Session.ts` 三处。

### 补充信息

**相关 issue。**

- #8775 提出以基于 `Turn` 的运行时统一各会话 loop，它的盘点在当前 main 上依然成立。本 issue 跟踪的是落实这一方向的一种分阶段、可选择开启的做法。
- #10219 与 #10078 让 agent 后端可插拔。
- #11695 把工具的执行位置独立出来。

本 issue 不改变上述两类工作，只确保它们可以接入的 loop 只有一份。

**验证方式。**

- `integration-tests/fake-openai-server.ts` 已经会记录每个请求体。对拍测试把每个脚本化场景在同一入口上跑两次：一次关闭设置，一次开启设置。
- 比较两样东西：规范化后的请求序列（模型实际看到的内容），以及入口的输出（stream-json 帧或 ACP `session/update` 通知）。
- 首批场景：
  - 纯文本、单个工具、并行只读批次；
  - 安全与不安全调用混合；
  - 审批通过与拒绝；
  - 工具执行中取消；
  - 流中途重试与模型回退；
  - 输出被截断的编辑；
  - 循环检测；
  - 阻断型 Stop hook；
  - `--max-tool-calls`、`maxSessionTurns` 与 structured output。

**最终状态的验收指标。**

| 指标 | 现在 | 目标 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| agent loop 实现数 | 7 份，另加 headless 与 ACP 内部的额外副本 | 1 |
| 直接调用 `LlmChat.sendMessageStream` 的 loop | 3 | 0 |
| 在 `turn.ts` 之外解析流式 chunk 的 loop | 3 | 0 |
| 调用 `finalizeToolResponses` 的 loop | 6 | 1 |
| 会话轮数上限的算法 | 3 | 1 |

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): upload Skill archives and reconcile results (4/4)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Completes the browser-facing fourth layer of #15862. A user can upload a real 20 MiB Skill ZIP from the Skills page when the daemon supports native archives. The browser sends the selected File directly, displays the daemon's advertised limits, and reports installation success only after a confirmed commit. If runtime activation fails afterwards, the installation stays successful and the UI shows a separate activation warning.

Cancellation, timeout or a lost response can leave the outcome uncertain. The UI queries the original installation attempt once, then offers **Check result** while the result is running or unknown. It never automatically uploads the archive again. Closing and reopening the still-mounted dialog retains that attempt and its original owner; switching workspaces does not make an old completion start a new refresh or display its success/warning on the new workspace.

Older daemons retain small-ZIP base64 installation. A ZIP above their existing 7,864,071-byte limit is rejected before reading or sending it, with an upgrade hint. GitHub and local-folder sources retain their existing path and limits.

#16421 (kernel), #16422 (daemon) and #16423 (SDK) are merged. This PR now targets `main`, includes their merged baseline through `1bac51b7d9e28d5c0f7d9a0a6fcd3add14443ebb`, and contains only seven Web Shell files. The follow-up adds two reproduced lifecycle fixes; it does not reintroduce the preceding implementation layers.

## Why it's needed

The old browser path converts the whole ZIP into base64 inside JSON. Its request-size budget prevents a 20 MiB archive from reaching installation even though the new daemon and SDK can accept it. This PR exposes those capabilities to browser users while preserving compatibility with older daemons.

A lost response does not establish whether installation committed. Treating it as failure and resending could duplicate an operation; treating it as success could hide a failed installation or retained recovery paths. Looking up the original receipt lets the UI distinguish committed, not committed, recovery required, running and unknown outcomes. Keeping installation and runtime activation separate also avoids telling a user that an already-installed Skill failed to install.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Upload a valid 20 MiB ZIP on a capable daemon. Expect one binary upload, advertised ZIP limits, installed content, and a success message after confirmation.
- Cancel an upload or lose its response. Expect an independent receipt lookup. If still pending, close and reopen the dialog, then choose **Check result**: it must query the same owner and attempt, without another upload. A confirmed cancellation should show that the archive was not installed.
- Start an upload in A, then switch to B, replace the client, or switch A→B→A before completion. Expect no stale installation notice and no new refresh started by the invalidated callback. A subsequent installation in the current workspace must still work.
- Confirm that a committed installation with an activation error shows success plus a separate warning. On an old daemon, confirm small-ZIP installation still works and a large ZIP shows upgrade guidance before any install request.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before the lifecycle repair, independent component tests reproduced stale notices and lost close/reopen receipts; a real-Hook test also reproduced A's late completion replacing B's catalog. After the repair, all three independent reproductions pass. The permanent suites contain 75 passing tests, including nine owner/phase combinations and two close/reopen paths; the combined run passed 78/78. These race tests use real React components with controlled SDK responses, not a real browser race simulation.

At `aa84fc85aa904b9f4f8239d06127e4e4bfe359d0`, root build, typecheck, bundle, changed-file ESLint and formatting passed. The final real-daemon acceptance run passed 12 HTTP cases and four Chromium flows, including a real pending Close → Reopen → Check result path with one upload and the same receipt URL. Served assets matched the local build. The [separate E2E report](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16424#issuecomment-6677825705) records identity, terminal outcomes and limitations.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Build, typecheck, 75 permanent + 3 independent tests, real HTTP and Chromium |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not run locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not run locally; main-target CI is tracked separately |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js 26.7.0, pnpm 11.24.0, isolated worktree. Current bundle SHA-256: `b0a2a1f01e9b97b29c9b86c82b43040b619035c47b73abec8c07ccb886e7f4c1`. The legacy compatibility target is global qwen 0.22.0; it is not evidence about current main.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: an unknown receipt remains unknown and blocks a new submission in that dialog until a terminal result is known. Pending retention covers close/reopen while mounted, not page reload or unmount. Cancelling the request is not a guarantee of undoing a server commit.
- Not validated / out of scope: cross-restart receipt persistence, resumable uploads, automatic retries, full limit/concurrency stress, Linux/Windows local execution, and cancellation of generic Hook requests already in flight before a workspace switch. Optional coverage and cleanup suggestions are explicitly deferred in their review threads.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none in this Web Shell layer. Native upload is capability-gated; old-daemon and non-ZIP limits remain unchanged.

Existing full-stack design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1bac51b7d9e28d5c0f7d9a0a6fcd3add14443ebb/docs/design/2026-10-29-skill-archive-installation.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1bac51b7d9e28d5c0f7d9a0a6fcd3add14443ebb/docs/design/2026-10-29-skill-archive-installation.zh-CN.md). No design files change in this layer.

## Linked Issues

Split from #15862; follows #15030 and the merged #16421, #16422 and #16423.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

完成 #15862 拆分后的第四层浏览器界面。在 daemon 支持原生归档时，用户可以从 Skills 页面上传真实的 20 MiB Skill ZIP。浏览器直接发送所选 File，展示服务端宣告的限额，并且只有确认安装提交后才显示安装成功。如果之后的运行时激活失败，安装仍保持成功，界面另行展示激活警告。

取消、超时或响应丢失可能使安装结果不确定。界面先查询一次原安装尝试；若结果仍在运行或未知，就提供“检查结果”。归档不会被自动重新上传。同一弹窗未卸载时，关闭再打开仍保留该尝试及原 owner；切换工作区后，旧安装完成不会再启动新的刷新，也不会向新工作区写入成功或警告提示。

旧 daemon 继续通过 base64 安装小 ZIP。超过其原有 7,864,071 字节上限的 ZIP 会在读取和发送前被拦截，并提示升级。GitHub 和本地文件夹来源保持现有路径与限额。

#16421（内核）、#16422（daemon）和 #16423（SDK）均已合入。本 PR 已改为面向 `main`，同步了截至 `1bac51b7d9e28d5c0f7d9a0a6fcd3add14443ebb` 的合入基线，差异仅包含 7 个 Web Shell 文件。本次跟进增加两处已复现的生命周期修复，没有重新包含前面三层实现。

## 为什么需要

旧浏览器路径将整个 ZIP 转为 base64 后放入 JSON。请求大小上限使 20 MiB 归档无法进入安装流程，即使新的 daemon 和 SDK 已能接收它。本 PR 将这些能力接入浏览器，同时保留旧 daemon 兼容性。

丢失响应不能证明安装是否已经提交。直接当成失败并重传可能重复执行；直接当成成功又可能掩盖失败或需要保留的恢复路径。查询原回执才能区分已提交、未提交、需要恢复、仍在运行和结果未知。将安装与运行时激活分开，也避免把已经安装的 Skill 错报为安装失败。

## 审查验证计划

### 如何验证

- 在支持能力的 daemon 上上传有效的 20 MiB ZIP。应只有一次二进制上传，显示宣告的 ZIP 限额，内容完成安装，并在确认后显示成功。
- 取消上传或使响应丢失。应独立查询回执；若仍待确认，关闭再打开弹窗后点击“检查结果”，应查询同一个 owner 和 attempt，不再上传。确认取消后应提示本次归档未安装。
- 在 A 开始上传，完成前切换到 B、更换客户端或 A→B→A。应没有旧安装提示，失效回调也不应再启动新的刷新；当前工作区的后续安装仍应正常成功。
- 确认安装已提交但激活失败时，显示成功及单独警告。在旧 daemon 上，小 ZIP 仍能安装，大 ZIP 在任何安装请求发出前提示升级。

### 改动前后证据

修复前，独立组件测试复现了旧提示串台和关闭重开后丢失回执；真实 Hook 测试还复现了 A 延迟完成后将 B 目录替换成 A。修复后，三项独立复现全部通过。永久测试共 75 项通过，包含九种 owner/异步阶段组合及两条关闭重开路径；合并执行共 78/78 通过。这些竞争场景使用真实 React 组件及受控 SDK 响应，不宣称是真实浏览器竞争复现。

在 `aa84fc85aa904b9f4f8239d06127e4e4bfe359d0` 上，根目录 build、typecheck、bundle、改动文件 ESLint 和格式检查均通过。最终真实 daemon 验收通过 12 个 HTTP 用例及 4 个 Chromium 流程，其中实际到达待确认状态下的“关闭 → 重开 → 检查结果”，上传只有一次，回执 URL 保持一致。服务端提供的静态资源与本地构建一致。[单独 E2E 报告](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16424#issuecomment-6677825705)记录了身份、终态和验证限制。

### 测试平台

| 系统 | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 构建、类型检查、75 项永久 + 3 项独立测试、真实 HTTP 和 Chromium |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地执行 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地执行；面向 main 的 CI 单独跟踪 |

### 环境

macOS arm64、Node.js 26.7.0、pnpm 11.24.0，独立 worktree。当前 bundle SHA-256：`b0a2a1f01e9b97b29c9b86c82b43040b619035c47b73abec8c07ccb886e7f4c1`。旧版兼容目标为全局 qwen 0.22.0，不作为当前 main 的行为证据。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：未知回执仍保持未知，在终态明确前阻止该弹窗发起新提交。待查状态仅在弹窗未卸载时关闭重开保留，不跨页面刷新或卸载。取消请求不保证撤销服务端已经提交的安装。
- 未验证或不在范围内：跨重启回执持久化、断点续传、自动重试、完整限额与并发压力测试、Linux/Windows 本地执行，以及切换工作区前已经发出的通用 Hook 请求取消。可选覆盖与清理建议已在对应审查讨论中明确延期。
- 兼容与迁移：本 Web Shell 层没有破坏性变更。原生上传受能力开关控制，旧 daemon 及非 ZIP 来源限额保持不变。

已有完整设计：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1bac51b7d9e28d5c0f7d9a0a6fcd3add14443ebb/docs/design/2026-10-29-skill-archive-installation.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1bac51b7d9e28d5c0f7d9a0a6fcd3add14443ebb/docs/design/2026-10-29-skill-archive-installation.zh-CN.md)。本层不修改设计文档。

## 关联

从 #15862 拆分；基于 #15030 及已合入的 #16421、#16422、#16423。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): surface workflow agent approvals in the interactive TUI (#16425)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A workflow agent that runs in the background and hits a tool-approval gate deadlocked in the interactive TUI: the approval was parked with nothing able to answer it, so the run never progressed. This PR makes the registry require a real responder before it parks an approval, wires the TUI's background-task view-model up as that responder, and opens the background-tasks detail view on a parked workflow approval so the user actually gets a prompt.

## Why it's needed

`WorkflowRunRegistry.parkApproval` accepted a park whenever *either* the display-only `approvalChangeCallback` or the responder `approvalRequestCallback` was registered. The TUI only ever registered the former — it repaints the "needs approval" footer badge but cannot answer anything. The result was the worst shape of failure: a visible badge that says something needs approval, and no surface anywhere in the dialog from which to approve it.

Two independent defects, both fixed here:

1. **`packages/core/src/agents/workflow-run-registry.ts:1152-1167`** — the park gate was `(!approvalChangeCallback && !approvalRequestCallback)`. A badge-only host satisfied it and then had no way to respond. It is now `!approvalRequestCallback`, so a badge-only host fails closed: the request is cancelled and the caller sees `ToolConfirmationOutcome.Cancel` instead of waiting forever.
2. **`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useBackgroundTaskView.ts:322-329`** — the view-model never registered a responder at all. It now registers its snapshot refresh as the approval-request responder (and clears it in the same cleanup that clears the other callbacks), which puts the parked approval into `entries` — the surface the dialog renders and settles through `resolvePendingApproval`.
3. **`packages/cli/src/ui/contexts/BackgroundTaskViewContext.tsx:178-196`** — even with the approval in `entries`, it was only reachable by opening the dialog and walking to the row. The provider now promotes a parked workflow approval to the detail view once per `approvalId`. Keying on the id matters: without it, closing the dialog would be undone by the next refresh and the user would be trapped in a re-opening dialog.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The regression is pinned at two levels.

`packages/core/src/agents/workflow-run-registry.test.ts` adds "fails closed when only a badge (approval-change) callback is registered": a host that registers only `setApprovalChangeCallback` emits a `TOOL_WAITING_APPROVAL` event, and the test asserts the request's `respond` is called with `ToolConfirmationOutcome.Cancel` and that `pendingApprovals` stays empty.

`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useBackgroundTaskView.test.ts` adds "registers a workflow approval-request responder that re-reads the snapshot", which asserts (a) mount registers a function, (b) firing the request actually re-reads the registry — a list-call counter increases and the parked approval shows up in `entries`, so this is a behaviour assertion rather than a call-count one — and (c) unmount releases it with `undefined`.

`packages/cli/src/ui/contexts/BackgroundTaskViewContext.test.tsx` drives the provider: a parked approval moves `dialogMode` to `'detail'` with the workflow row selected; after `closeDialog()` a same-`approvalId` refresh leaves the dialog closed; a new `approvalId` surfaces again.

Expected vs observed: on `main`, commenting out the single `setApprovalRequestCallback(refreshFromRegistry)` line makes the new hook test fail with `expected "spy" to be called with arguments: [ Any<Function> ]` (`1 failed | 19 passed`). With the fix in place both suites are green:

```
packages/core  → 163 passed (163)   src/agents/workflow-run-registry.test.ts
packages/cli   →  22 passed (22)    src/ui/hooks/useBackgroundTaskView.test.ts
                                     src/ui/contexts/BackgroundTaskViewContext.test.tsx
```

`packages/cli` vitest cannot be launched through its own config in this working copy: the repo's `scripts/vitest-global-setup.js` guard refuses to start because `packages/channels/*` and `packages/acp-bridge` have no `dist/` in a fresh worktree, and this machine's symlinked `node_modules` additionally fails to resolve `@qwen-code/channel-email`. The suite above was run with the same `vitest.config.ts` minus `globalSetup` (`vitest run --config <temp config with globalSetup: []>`), which is the closest honest run available here; the temp config was deleted before committing.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible rendering change beyond which dialog mode opens; the behaviour is covered by the tests above rather than by screenshots.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Linux dev box, `vitest` from the repo root `node_modules`, run inside the worktree.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the registry gate is now strictly narrower — a host that previously relied on the badge callback to park an approval will now get a cancellation. Grepping the tree, the only hosts that call `setApprovalChangeCallback` on the workflow registry are `useBackgroundTaskView` (fixed here to also register a responder) and the test fixtures; headless and ACP paths never register the badge callback in the first place, so they are unaffected.
- Not validated / out of scope: the CLI suite was run with `globalSetup` disabled as described above, not through the repo's default `npm test` path; the auto-expand was not verified interactively in a real terminal (no tmux capture in this round), only through the provider-level component test.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for `main`'s behaviour; the only semantic change is fail-closed instead of fail-silent for badge-only hosts.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16425

prs.title: feat: add hybrid code mode
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a Codex-aligned `tools.mode` enum with `direct`, `code_mode`, and `code_mode_only`. `code_mode` keeps ordinary tools directly callable while also exposing the isolated `exec` JavaScript tool; each visible ordinary tool carries its nested JavaScript declaration, while `exec` retains compact `ALL_TOOLS` metadata. `code_mode_only` preserves the strict exec-only ordinary-tool surface, and `direct` remains the default.

Updates filtered subagent tool surfaces so direct declarations and nested exec bindings honor the same allowlists, exposes the enum in Settings as Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only, regenerates the settings JSON schema, and removes the former `tools.codeModeOnly` boolean setting entirely.

Adds synchronized [English](docs/design/code-mode.md) and [Chinese](docs/design/code-mode.zh-CN.md) design documents, and brings the existing CodeModeOnly design up to the repository's bilingual documentation standard ([English](docs/design/code-mode-only.md), [Chinese](docs/design/code-mode-only.zh-CN.md)).

## Why it's needed

Qwen Code previously offered only the default direct tool surface or the strict CodeModeOnly surface. Models could not combine direct calls for simple operations with `exec` orchestration for multi-tool workflows. A three-value enum matches Codex's `ToolMode` naming and gives users one explicit setting for all supported exposure modes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Leave `tools.mode` unset or set it to `direct`, restart Qwen Code, and confirm ordinary tools remain available while `exec` is absent.
2. Set `tools.mode` to `code_mode`, restart, and confirm both ordinary tools and `exec` are available. Confirm ordinary tool descriptions include their `tools.<name>(args)` declaration and deferred tools remain discoverable through `tool_search`.
3. Set `tools.mode` to `code_mode_only`, restart, and confirm ordinary tools are available through `exec` rather than as top-level calls, while direct control tools remain available.
4. Open Settings and confirm Tool Mode cycles among Default, Code Mode, and Code Mode Only. Confirm `tools.codeModeOnly` is no longer present in the settings schema.
5. Start with `--safe-mode` or `--bare` while either code mode is configured and confirm the effective mode is `direct`.

Automated verification completed: focused Core tests (121 tests), focused CLI tests (585 tests), a repeated settings-schema regression run (60 tests), full build, full typecheck, full lint, and both installed and branch-built CLI version smoke checks.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: Settings exposed `Code Mode Only (Experimental)` as a boolean with `false` / `true`.

After: Settings exposes `Tool Mode (Experimental)` as an enum displaying Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only. Updated TUI snapshots cover the default display.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

macOS, Node.js v24.18.0; local source build and package-level Vitest suites.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Hybrid mode adds a short nested-call declaration to each ordinary tool description, increasing prompt size slightly; complete schemas are not duplicated in the `exec` description.
- Not validated / out of scope: Live-provider interactive runs and Windows/Linux local execution were not tested; CI covers supported platforms.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: `tools.codeModeOnly` is removed. Replace `{ "tools": { "codeModeOnly": true } }` with `{ "tools": { "mode": "code_mode_only" } }`.

## Linked Issues

Related to #10377.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

新增与 Codex 对齐的 `tools.mode` 枚举，支持 `direct`、`code_mode` 和 `code_mode_only`。`code_mode` 在保留普通工具直接调用能力的同时提供隔离的 `exec` JavaScript 工具；每个可见普通工具会携带自己的嵌套 JavaScript 声明，而 `exec` 保留精简的 `ALL_TOOLS` 元数据。`code_mode_only` 保持严格的普通工具仅经 `exec` 调用模式，`direct` 仍为默认值。

更新经过过滤的子智能体工具面，使直接声明和 `exec` 嵌套 binding 遵守同一组 allowlist；在设置界面中将该枚举显示为 Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only；重新生成 settings JSON schema；并彻底移除原来的 `tools.codeModeOnly` 布尔设置。

新增同步的[英文](docs/design/code-mode.md)和[中文](docs/design/code-mode.zh-CN.md)设计文档，并将现有 CodeModeOnly 设计补齐为仓库要求的双语文档（[英文](docs/design/code-mode-only.md)、[中文](docs/design/code-mode-only.zh-CN.md)）。

## 为什么需要

Qwen Code 此前只提供默认的直接工具面或严格的 CodeModeOnly 工具面。模型无法在简单操作中使用直接调用，同时在多工具工作流中使用 `exec` 编排。三值枚举与 Codex 的 `ToolMode` 命名一致，并为所有支持的暴露模式提供一个明确的统一设置项。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 不设置 `tools.mode` 或将其设为 `direct`，重启 Qwen Code，确认普通工具仍可用且不存在 `exec`。
2. 将 `tools.mode` 设为 `code_mode` 并重启，确认普通工具和 `exec` 同时可用；确认普通工具描述包含各自的 `tools.<name>(args)` 声明，延迟工具仍可通过 `tool_search` 发现。
3. 将 `tools.mode` 设为 `code_mode_only` 并重启，确认普通工具通过 `exec` 而不是顶层调用使用，同时直接控制工具仍然可用。
4. 打开设置界面，确认 Tool Mode 可在 Default、Code Mode 和 Code Mode Only 之间切换，并确认 settings schema 中不再存在 `tools.codeModeOnly`。
5. 配置任一 code mode 后用 `--safe-mode` 或 `--bare` 启动，确认有效模式为 `direct`。

已完成自动化验证：Core 相关测试（121 个）、CLI 相关测试（585 个）、再次运行的 settings schema 回归测试（60 个）、完整 build、完整 typecheck、完整 lint，以及已安装版本和分支构建版本的 CLI 版本 smoke 检查。

### 前后对比证据

之前：设置界面以 `false` / `true` 布尔值展示 `Code Mode Only (Experimental)`。

之后：设置界面以枚举展示 `Tool Mode (Experimental)`，可选 Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only。更新后的 TUI snapshot 覆盖默认显示。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

macOS、Node.js v24.18.0；本地源码构建和 package 级 Vitest 测试套件。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：混合模式会在每个普通工具描述中增加一段简短的嵌套调用声明，使 prompt 略微增大；完整 schema 不会在 `exec` 描述中重复。
- 未验证 / 范围外：未进行真实 provider 的交互式运行，也未在 Windows/Linux 本地执行；支持平台由 CI 覆盖。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：`tools.codeModeOnly` 已移除。请将 `{ "tools": { "codeModeOnly": true } }` 替换为 `{ "tools": { "mode": "code_mode_only" } }`。

## 关联 Issue

关联 #10377。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): show the resolved global directory in the permissions dialogs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The permissions dialog's "User settings" row now names the settings file the running process actually uses. The resolved global settings path is rendered through the existing `Saved in {{path}}` message and shortened to `~` for display, so a default install still reads `~/.qwen/settings.json` while a `QWEN_HOME` install reads its own path; long relocated paths are middle-compressed so the file name stays visible in the row at an 80-column terminal.

Both renderers are updated: the ink dialog and its OpenTUI parity copy. The hardcoded `Saved in at ~/.qwen/settings.json` message is retired, and `Saved in {{path}}` — which had no entry in any bundled locale, so the memory manager was silently falling back to English for that row — now exists in all nine locales and is listed in `MUST_TRANSLATE_KEYS`, so a future locale sync cannot drop it again without a failing test.

## Why it's needed

Addresses the dialog half of #15628. `Storage.getGlobalSettingsPath()` already honours `QWEN_HOME`, and the permissions dialog was the one place that ignored it: with `QWEN_HOME=/tmp/custom-qwen` the process reads `/tmp/custom-qwen/settings.json` while the User-settings row points at `~/.qwen/settings.json`. Because the row reads the resolved directory rather than a fixed string, it also follows the config-directory move planned in #15458 without another edit.

This is deliberately only the dialog half of the issue. The setting descriptions and the published VS Code schema are untouched: `scripts/generate-settings-schema.ts` copies `setting.description` verbatim into the shipped schema, so interpolating a resolved path there would freeze the build machine's home directory into the artifact, and that half is coupled to #15458 anyway.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `QWEN_HOME=/tmp/custom-qwen npm run dev`, run `/permissions`, open the User settings scope → the row names `/tmp/custom-qwen/settings.json`.
2. Unset `QWEN_HOME`, repeat → the row names `~/.qwen/settings.json`.
3. `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialogs-permissions.test.ts src/ui/components/PermissionsDialog.test.tsx src/ui/components/MemoryDialog.test.tsx` → all pass.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, on the parent commit, with the new assertions in place: `expected 'Saved in at ~/.qwen/settings.json' to be 'Saved in /var/folders/…/settings.json'` — both scope-item tests failed.

After: 13 tests in the OpenTUI permissions suite, 2 in the ink scope-item suite, and 17 in the memory dialog suite pass.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Windows was not run; the only platform-sensitive part is the separator, and both tests build their expectations from `path.sep`. The Linux run used a clean `node:22-bookworm` checkout of this branch.

### Environment (optional)

`packages/cli` unit tests on the host, plus the same suite in a `node:22-bookworm` container for the Linux check.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: nine locale entries change, because the old key is retired and the placeholder key is added. Rendering in every bundled language is unchanged for a default install — only the path itself now varies.
- Not validated / out of scope: no interactive TUI screenshot; the rendered description is covered through the exported scope-item helpers rather than through a full dialog render.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: a custom locale pack that translated `Saved in at ~/.qwen/settings.json` will no longer be consulted for this row; the bundled locales carry the new key.

## Linked Issues

Related to #15628 — this ships the dialog half only. The setting descriptions and the published VS Code schema stay open on the issue until that half lands.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

权限对话框里"用户设置"这一行，现在显示的是进程实际使用的设置文件。解析后的全局设置路径通过已有的 `Saved in {{path}}` 消息渲染，并做 `~` 缩写，因此默认安装仍显示 `~/.qwen/settings.json`，而设置了 `QWEN_HOME` 的安装会显示它自己的路径；被重定向到别处的长路径会做中间段压缩，保证在 80 列终端下文件名仍然可见。

两个渲染器都改了：ink 对话框和它的 OpenTUI 对等实现。硬编码的 `Saved in at ~/.qwen/settings.json` 消息被退役；而 `Saved in {{path}}` 原本在所有内置语言包里都没有条目，导致记忆管理器的那一行一直在悄悄回落成英文，现在九个语言包都补齐了，并已加入 `MUST_TRANSLATE_KEYS`，将来语言包同步若丢掉它，测试会直接变红。

## 为什么需要

处理 #15628 的对话框这一半。`Storage.getGlobalSettingsPath()` 本来就认 `QWEN_HOME`，权限对话框是唯一忽略它的地方：`QWEN_HOME=/tmp/custom-qwen` 时进程读的是 `/tmp/custom-qwen/settings.json`，而"用户设置"那一行却指向 `~/.qwen/settings.json`。由于这一行改为读取解析后的目录，它也会自动跟随 #15458 计划中的配置目录迁移，不需要再改一次。

这个 PR 刻意只做 issue 的对话框这一半。设置项描述和对外发布的 VS Code schema 没有动：`scripts/generate-settings-schema.ts` 会把 `setting.description` 原样写进发布的 schema，在那里插值会把构建机的 home 目录固化进产物；而且那一半本来就依赖 #15458。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. `QWEN_HOME=/tmp/custom-qwen npm run dev`，执行 `/permissions`，打开"用户设置"作用域 → 该行显示 `/tmp/custom-qwen/settings.json`。
2. 取消 `QWEN_HOME`，重复上述步骤 → 该行显示 `~/.qwen/settings.json`。
3. `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialogs-permissions.test.ts src/ui/components/PermissionsDialog.test.tsx src/ui/components/MemoryDialog.test.tsx` → 全部通过。

### 证据（修复前 / 修复后）

修复前（父提交，已带新断言）：`expected 'Saved in at ~/.qwen/settings.json' to be 'Saved in /var/folders/…/settings.json'` —— 两个作用域断言均失败。

修复后：OpenTUI 权限套件 13 个、ink 作用域套件 2 个、记忆对话框套件 17 个用例全部通过。

### 测试平台

|    系统    | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

Windows 未运行；唯一与平台相关的部分是路径分隔符，两个测试的期望值都由 `path.sep` 拼出。Linux 侧用的是本分支的干净 `node:22-bookworm` 检出。

### 环境（可选）

宿主上跑 `packages/cli` 单测，另在 `node:22-bookworm` 容器里跑同一套用例作为 Linux 验证。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：九个语言包条目发生变化，因为旧 key 退役、占位符 key 新增。默认安装下各语言的渲染结果不变，变化的只是路径本身。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：没有交互式 TUI 截图；渲染结果通过导出的作用域条目辅助函数覆盖，而非完整对话框渲染。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：自定义语言包（用户 locales 目录）里翻译过 `Saved in at ~/.qwen/settings.json` 的条目对这一行不再生效，内置语言包已带新 key。

## 关联 issue

关联 #15628（不自动关闭）——本 PR 只做对话框这一半。设置项描述与对外发布的 VS Code schema 仍需在该 issue 上继续跟进，待那一半落地后再关闭。

</details>
