prs.title: fix(web-shell): leave current standalone session before deletion
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Allows an idle current no-workspace session to be deleted from the sidebar. After confirmation, the tab leaves the session, waits for its attachment to be released, and then deletes the original session. The confirmation stays open and cannot be dismissed while this operation is in flight. If detach fails, the current attachment and transcript remain available for a safe retry; if deletion fails after leaving, the session stays listed and an error is shown.

## Why it's needed

The current row's Delete action is disabled today, requiring users to open another chat before deleting it. This implements the leave-first follow-up to #12636 while preserving the daemon's protection of sessions with active work or attached clients. The row's work summary and App's streaming state guard the current session, with another check on confirmation. Delete stays disabled until the current attachment is ready, and navigation changes cannot redirect deletion to another session.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open an idle no-workspace session and choose Delete from its sidebar row. Cancel the confirmation and verify that the session stays open.
2. Choose Delete again and confirm. Expect a fresh no-workspace draft and the original row to disappear only after deletion succeeds.
3. Open the same session in two tabs. Confirm Delete in the first tab: it should leave, retain the original row, and report that the session is busy. Leave through New task in the second tab, then retry Delete in the first tab's existing confirmation; the original row should disappear.
4. Check that running work disables deletion of the current row and that deleting a different no-workspace session does not leave the current chat. While the current session is loading, its Delete action should be disabled with a readiness hint and become available after attachment completes.
5. While leave or deletion is pending, try Cancel, Escape, the backdrop, and the dialog close button. The confirmation must remain open, with a disabled “Deleting...” button, until the operation settles; an unrelated row mutation must disable its Delete confirmation button while that mutation is pending.
6. If detach fails, expect a localized failure notice, the current attachment, transcript, original row, and confirmation to remain, with no delete request. Retry the same confirmation after detach can succeed; it must attempt detach again before deleting. Cancel instead and continue the chat to confirm its event stream resumes.
7. If the event stream disconnects while reconnecting, confirm Delete during the retry delay. Reconnection must wait while detach is pending; after successful detach the old session must stay cleared, while failed detach must preserve the session and allow its stream to resume.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before: the baseline component test confirmed that the current no-workspace row's Delete action was disabled (1 passed, 141 skipped).
- After: isolated real-daemon browser testing observed detach HTTP 204 before delete HTTP 200 with the original ID in `removed`, followed by the row disappearing. Cancelling confirmation sent neither request.
- Two tabs: attachment count changed from 2 to 1, deletion returned HTTP 200 with per-session `session_busy`, and the row and error remained visible. After the second tab left, the count became 0 and retrying the first tab's confirmation deleted the original session successfully.
- Review also identified that a failed strict detach cleared the local attachment before the daemon released it. Regression tests failed on the preceding head and passed after the fix, including retry, timeout, replacement attachment, and continued chat after an event-stream end or error. A further review exposed a reconnect-backoff race: tests reproduced re-subscription while detach was pending and the old session being republished after detach succeeded. The current head passes all three backoff ordering and recovery cases; six related Web Shell suites passed 2013/2013 tests, and the full build and typecheck, changed-file lint/format, diff whitespace checks, and commit hook passed.
- Earlier isolated real-daemon Chrome checks observed “Deleting...” and `aria-busy` throughout held detach and delete requests, a disabled current-row Delete during loading that became enabled after attachment, and an injected detach 503 browser response that showed the localized failure, retained the row, and sent no delete request. Those browser runs predate the strict-detach retry fix.

The [confirmation screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-confirm.png) shows the dialog opened from the current row. The two screenshots below show the busy result and a successful retry; the earlier busy toast is still fading in the second image, while the list already says “No sessions.”

| Busy result: original row retained | Retry after the second tab leaves: row removed |
| --- | --- |
| ![The original standalone row remains after session_busy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-busy.png) | ![The standalone list is empty after retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-after.png) |

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Unit tests, build/typecheck, isolated real-daemon Chrome checks |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js 26.8.2, built local Web Shell, and an embedded daemon with temporary Conversations, project, runtime, and discovery directories for the earlier browser runs. The global `qwen` command was unavailable. No model request was made. Unit tests used `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`; the build used a temporary Corepack shim around installed pnpm 11.19.0 because Corepack was unavailable (repository pin: 11.24.0).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: another client can keep the original session busy after this tab has already left. The daemon's per-session result remains authoritative, and the row stays visible on failure. Listed client counts are not used to disable Delete because the sidebar does not continuously refresh them.
- Not validated / out of scope: the latest strict-detach and reconnect fix was not rerun in a real-daemon browser; its failure and recovery paths have focused action, provider, and component tests. The earlier detach 503 was an injected browser response, not a real daemon transport failure. Active prompts were not exercised in the browser. Windows, Linux, and full preflight were not run locally. A fresh frozen dependency install was attempted after the main merge but could not fetch package metadata on this machine's restricted network; build and tests passed with the existing dependencies. The `/delete` picker excludes standalone sessions and is outside this change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; no daemon routes, persistence formats, or dependency changes.

Design: [English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.zh-CN.md). Both versions contain the same decisions, constraints, verification results, and acceptance criteria.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12669

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## What this PR does

允许从侧栏删除空闲的当前无工作区会话。确认后，标签页先离开会话，等待其附着解除，再删除原会话。操作进行中确认框保持打开且无法关闭。detach 失败时保留当前附着与对话记录以便安全重试；离开后删除失败时，原会话继续显示在列表中，并显示错误。

## Why it's needed

当前行的 Delete 目前被禁用，用户必须先打开其他聊天才能删除。本改动实现 #12636 后续的“先离开再删除”流程，同时保留 daemon 对活动工作和已附着客户端的保护。行摘要与 App 的流式输出状态共同保护当前会话，用户确认时再次检查。当前附着就绪前 Delete 保持禁用；导航变化也不会把删除目标改成其他会话。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. 打开空闲的无工作区会话，从侧栏行选择 Delete。取消确认，检查原会话仍然打开。
2. 再次选择 Delete 并确认。应进入新的无工作区草稿，且只有删除成功后原行才消失。
3. 在两个标签页打开同一会话。在第一个标签页确认 Delete：它应离开会话，保留原行并提示会话忙碌。第二个标签页通过 New task 离开后，在第一个标签页保留的确认框中重试 Delete，原行应消失。
4. 检查当前会话有运行中的工作时删除被禁用，以及删除其他无工作区会话不会离开当前聊天。当前会话加载期间，Delete 应禁用并显示未就绪提示；附着完成后恢复可用。
5. 离开或删除待完成时尝试 Cancel、Esc、遮罩和对话框关闭按钮。确认框应保持打开，按钮禁用并显示“Deleting...”，直至操作结束；其他行的变更操作待完成时，其删除确认按钮也应禁用。
6. 若 detach 失败，应显示本地化失败提示，保留当前附着、对话记录、原行和确认框，且不发删除请求。待 detach 可以成功后在同一确认框重试，必须再次 detach 成功才可删除；也可取消并继续聊天，检查事件流恢复。
7. 若事件流断开并等待重连，在退避期间确认 Delete。detach 未完成时不得重新订阅；成功后旧会话应保持清空，失败后应保留会话并允许事件流恢复。

### Evidence (Before & After)

- 修复前：基线组件测试确认当前无工作区行的 Delete 被禁用（1 项通过、141 项跳过）。
- 修复后：隔离真实 daemon 的浏览器测试观察到 detach HTTP 204 先于删除 HTTP 200，结果的 `removed` 包含原 ID，随后原行消失。取消确认不发送这两个请求。
- 双标签：附着数从 2 降至 1，删除返回 HTTP 200，逐项结果为 `session_busy`，原行和错误仍可见。第二个标签页离开后，计数变为 0；在第一个标签页原确认框重试，成功删除原会话。
- 审查还发现严格 detach 失败时，在 daemon 释放附着前清空本地状态。定向回归测试在上一 head 失败、修复后通过，覆盖重试、超时、附着替换，以及事件流结束或出错后继续聊天。后续审查又发现重连退避竞态：测试复现了 detach 未完成时重新订阅，以及 detach 成功后旧会话被重新发布。当前 head 的三种退避顺序与恢复用例全部通过；六个相关 Web Shell 套件共 2013/2013 项通过，全仓构建和类型检查、改动文件 lint/format、差异空白检查和提交钩子也通过。
- 此前隔离真实 daemon 的 Chrome 测试在暂停 detach 与 delete 请求期间观察到“Deleting...”和 `aria-busy`；加载期间当前行 Delete 禁用，附着完成后恢复；浏览器注入 detach 503 响应后显示本地化失败提示、保留原行，且没有删除请求。这些浏览器测试早于最新的严格 detach 重试修复。

[确认框截图](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-confirm.png)显示从当前行打开的对话框。上方两张截图依次展示忙碌时保留原行，以及第二标签离开后重试成功；后一张中旧的 busy 提示尚在消退，但列表已显示“No sessions”。

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 单测、构建/类型检查、隔离真实 daemon 的 Chrome 验证 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地验证 |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64、Node.js 26.8.2、构建后的本地 Web Shell；此前浏览器测试使用临时 Conversations、项目、runtime 和 discovery 目录的内嵌 daemon。本机没有全局 `qwen` 命令，未发送模型请求。单测使用 `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`；由于 Corepack 不可用，构建通过临时 Corepack 包装调用已安装的 pnpm 11.19.0（仓库固定版本为 11.24.0）。

## Risk & Scope

- 主要风险或取舍：此标签页离开后，其他客户端仍可能使原会话保持忙碌。最终以 daemon 的逐项结果为准，失败时原行保留。侧栏不会持续刷新客户端计数，因此不使用列表中的计数禁用 Delete。
- 未验证或范围外：最新严格 detach 与重连修复未在真实 daemon 浏览器重跑；失败与恢复由会话动作、Provider 和组件定向测试覆盖。此前 detach 503 是浏览器注入的响应，不是真实 daemon 传输故障；浏览器也未运行活动提示。本机未运行 Windows、Linux 或完整 preflight。合入主线后曾尝试冻结依赖安装，但受限网络无法获取包元数据；构建与测试在现有依赖下通过。`/delete` 选择器不包含 standalone 会话，不在本次范围内。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无；未改变 daemon 路由、持久化格式或依赖。

设计：[English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.zh-CN.md)。两版的决策、约束、验证结果和验收标准一致。

prs.title: feat(cli): have an Ink TUI turn await its shared tool batch
prs.body:
## What this PR does

With `experimental.unifiedAgentLoop` on, an Ink TUI turn now awaits its shared tool batch and the round that batch continues with. This is PR 3b-2b of #15327, after #16365.

Until now a round returned once its stream ended, and the batch, launched on the side, sent the next round from its completion step. The stream processor now hands the batch to the round's `submitQuery`, which awaits it once its own stream and activity ended. The completion step still stops the turn or sends the next round, so the history repair, the split by interaction owner and the tool-use summary now run in the turn, right before the next round.

| The TUI today | With the setting on |
| --- | --- |
| a round returns once its stream ended, and its batch's completion step sends the next round | the round's turn awaits the batch, its completion step and the round that step sends |
| the scheduler starts no queued batch until the completion step returned, after the next round's stream | until the completion step stopped the turn or is about to send the next round, whose calls need the scheduler |
| a batch whose executed calls history all answered sends nothing | the same: the batch's replay answers do not go out alone |

The last two rows are the two items #16304's review left for this step. The scheduler hold restores what the current path does, up to the next round: holding it through that round would deadlock now that the round awaits its own calls. Before this PR, the shared batch's scheduler callback returned at once, and a batch whose executed calls history had all answered still sent its replay answers as a continuation.

When the round's stream ends while another stream is active, the turn does not wait. That other stream may be the one that sent the round and waits for it: a response of provider replays alone sends its answers before its stream closes. Its batch then waits for the streams to end and completes on its own, as before. Batches that wait for the streams still go out in one continuation, as the user chose for this step.

The pieces:

- `createInkToolExecutor` takes an optional `schedulerHold`. The scheduler's completion callback returns once it settles; the batch does not wait for it.
- In `use-llm-stream.ts`, `processLlmStreamEvents` returns the shared batch, and `submitQuery` awaits it after the round's submission settled when no other stream is active. `runSharedToolBatch` holds the scheduler and passes `releaseScheduler` to the completion step, which calls it right before it sends the next round; the batch releases it once the step returned. The completion step sends the batch's replay answers only with one of its executed calls.

No shared code in core changes, and with the setting off the TUI is unchanged.

The design doc describes 3b-2b.

## Why it's needed

In #15327 the Ink TUI moves onto the shared loop in steps. With the turn awaiting its batch, input at a tool boundary can go through the loop's next round (3c-1), and the loop can run the TUI's rounds (3d).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Unit tests:
  - `packages/cli` `use-llm-stream.test.tsx`, "shared agent loop round": a turn awaits its batch and the round it continues with; the scheduler is released before the next round is sent, and its second batch runs; replay answers are not sent alone when history answered every executed call; a round sent by a response of replays alone runs its batch while that response is handled. The tests with batches that settle during another stream now leave the earlier turns awaiting, and the scheduler's callback is held while a batch's results are persisted.
  - `packages/cli` `ink-tool-executor.test.ts`: the scheduler's callback returns once the hold settles, and the batch settles without it.
- Run `npm run bundle`, then `cd integration-tests && QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=ink npx vitest run interactive/ink-agent-loop-parity.test.ts`. All scenarios must still pass.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A: the change is behind an off-by-default setting.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local results on Linux:

- the Ink parity suite: 14/14, from a fresh `npm run bundle`;
- `use-llm-stream.test.tsx`, `ink-tool-executor.test.ts` and `useToolScheduler.test.ts`: 458 passed;
- root `npm run typecheck` passes; eslint and prettier are clean on the changed files.

Mutation checks:

- When the turn no longer awaits its batch, the test that the turn awaits its batch fails, with five others.
- Without the scheduler hold, the test that holds the scheduler's callback while the results are persisted fails.
- When the completion step no longer releases the scheduler before the next round, the turn deadlocks: the release test times out.
- When the replay answers go out alone, the test for a batch whose executed calls history answered fails.
- When the turn also awaits its batch while another stream is active, the round sent by a response of replays alone deadlocks.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a turn now resolves after all its rounds, so callers of `submitQuery` that await it (the queued-input drain) wait for the whole turn instead of its first round. They act once the TUI is idle, which the turn reaches at the same point.
- Not validated / out of scope: input at a tool boundary through the loop's next round, a retry, and other turn kinds (3c); removing the queue that merges batches that wait for the streams.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Design: [docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.md](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.md) and [docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.zh-CN.md](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Part of #15327.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

开启 `experimental.unifiedAgentLoop` 后，Ink TUI 的轮次会等待自己的共享工具批，以及工具批接着发出的那一轮。这是 #15327 的 PR 3b-2b，接在 #16365 之后。

此前一轮在它的流结束后就返回，工具批在旁边启动，由它的完成步骤发出下一轮。现在流处理把工具批交给这一轮的 `submitQuery`，后者在自己的流和活动结束后等待它。完成步骤仍然结束轮次或发出下一轮，因此历史修复、按交互 owner 拆分和工具使用摘要现在在轮次中、在下一轮之前运行。

| TUI 现在 | 开启设置后 |
| --- | --- |
| 一轮在它的流结束后就返回，由工具批的完成步骤发出下一轮 | 这一轮所在的轮次等待工具批、它的完成步骤，以及这个步骤发出的那一轮 |
| 完成步骤返回之前（在下一轮的流结束之后），scheduler 不启动排队的工具批 | 直到完成步骤结束了轮次，或即将发出下一轮为止，因为下一轮的调用需要 scheduler |
| 已执行的调用全部被历史应答过的工具批不发送任何内容 | 相同：这一批的重放应答不会单独发出 |

后两行是 #16304 的 review 留给这一步的两项。scheduler 的占用恢复了现有路径的行为，但只到下一轮为止：现在下一轮要等待自己的调用，如果占用到那一轮结束就会死锁。此前共享工具批的 scheduler 回调会立即返回，已执行调用全被历史应答过的工具批仍会把重放应答作为一次续发发出。

如果这一轮的流结束时还有另一个流在进行，轮次不等待。那个流可能就是发出这一轮并在等它的流：只由 provider 重放组成的响应会在自己的流关闭之前发出应答。这时工具批和以前一样等各个流结束后自行完成。按这一步的选择，等待模型流的各个工具批仍在一次续发中发出。

具体改动：

- `createInkToolExecutor` 接受可选的 `schedulerHold`。scheduler 的完成回调在它完成后才返回；工具批不等待它。
- `use-llm-stream.ts` 中，`processLlmStreamEvents` 返回共享工具批，`submitQuery` 在这一轮的提交结束后、且没有其他流进行时等待它。`runSharedToolBatch` 占住 scheduler，并把 `releaseScheduler` 交给完成步骤，完成步骤在发出下一轮之前调用它；完成步骤返回后，工具批也会释放。完成步骤只在这一批至少有一个已执行调用发出时，才发送它的重放应答。

core 的共享代码没有改动；设置关闭时 TUI 不变。

设计文档描述了 3b-2b。

## 为什么需要

在 #15327 中，Ink TUI 分步迁到共享 loop。轮次等待工具批之后，工具边界的输入才能通过 loop 的下一轮（3c-1），loop 才能运行 TUI 的各轮（3d）。

## 验证方法

- 单元测试：
  - `packages/cli` 的 `use-llm-stream.test.tsx`，"shared agent loop round"：轮次等待工具批和它接着发出的那一轮；scheduler 在下一轮发出之前释放，第二个工具批能运行；历史应答了全部已执行调用时，不单独发送重放应答；只由重放组成的响应发出的那一轮，在该响应处理期间能运行自己的工具批。在另一个流期间完成的工具批相关测试，现在让前面的轮次保持等待；工具批结果持久化期间，scheduler 回调被占住。
  - `packages/cli` 的 `ink-tool-executor.test.ts`：scheduler 回调在占用结束后才返回，工具批不等待它。
- 运行 `npm run bundle`，然后 `cd integration-tests && QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=ink npx vitest run interactive/ink-agent-loop-parity.test.ts`，所有场景仍须通过。
- 本地（Linux）：Ink 对拍 14/14（重新 `npm run bundle` 后）；相关单测 458 个通过；根目录 `npm run typecheck` 通过；改动文件的 eslint 和 prettier 都干净。五组变异（轮次不等待工具批、不占用 scheduler、下一轮之前不释放 scheduler、单独发出重放应答、有其他流时仍等待）都会让对应测试失败，其中第三、五组表现为死锁超时。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：轮次现在在所有轮结束后才完成，因此等待 `submitQuery` 的调用方（排队输入的排空）会等待整个轮次，而不是只等第一轮。它们在 TUI 空闲后才动作，而轮次在同一时刻到达空闲。
- 未验证/不在范围内：工具边界的输入通过 loop 的下一轮、重试和其他轮次类型（3c）；去掉合并等待模型流的工具批的队列。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。

</details>

releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

_See the complete change list below._

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- feat(mods): run prompt.submit hooks in the OpenTUI terminal ([#16195](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16195)) by @qqqys
- feat(cli): run the Ink TUI's model rounds on the shared loop's round ([#16206](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16206)) by @qqqys
- feat(web-shell): collapse channel editor tuning behind advanced settings ([#16239](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16239)) by @wenshao
- feat(web-shell): link GitHub PR/Issue targets in channel events ([#16226](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16226)) by @wenshao
- feat(channels): role-aware action templates for GitHub bound-session delivery ([#16258](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16258)) by @wenshao
- feat(cli): run the Ink TUI's tool batches on the shared loop's batch ([#16304](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16304)) by @qqqys
- feat(mods): let a Mod submit a prompt of its own in headless runs ([#16302](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16302)) by @qqqys
- feat(managed-agent): allow concurrent workspace rewinds ([#16369](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16369)) by @doudouOUC
- feat(channels): edit bound-session action templates on demand ([#16349](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16349)) by @wenshao
- feat(serve): allow configuring the Conversations working-directory root ([#16105](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16105)) by @jkxiao
- feat(cli): end the Ink TUI's shared tool batch on the TUI's own stops ([#16365](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16365)) by @qqqys
- feat(web-shell): link channel event rows to their sessions ([#16375](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16375)) by @wenshao
- feat(mods): run the prompts a Mod submits in the Ink terminal ([#16373](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16373)) by @qqqys
- feat: add Qwen subscription support across CLI, VS Code, and Desktop ([#16378](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16378)) by @liuxuely0626

### Bug Fixes

- Makes linter archive downloads resume after stalls so CI lint installs fail less often on slow or throttled releases. ([#16067](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16067)) by @yiliang114
- Repins the RHEL 10 rpm build root to a current CentOS stream10 digest so CI containers start instead of failing on manifest lookup. ([#16261](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16261)) by @yiliang114
- Waits for the RocketMQ port listener to clear after stop, reducing flaky script test failures on shared CI hosts. ([#16252](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16252)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- fix(core): preserve Gemini thought signatures for tool replay ([#16270](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16270)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(core): recognize Hugging Face TGI context overflow errors so reactive compaction runs ([#16245](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16245)) by @Shizoqua
- fix(core): accept images for Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL and QVQ models the catalog does not list ([#16247](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16247)) by @Shizoqua
- fix(daemon): automatically discover config Skills changes ([#16262](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16262)) by @callmeYe
- fix(mods): skip hooks on ui.backdrop instead of failing ([#16289](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16289)) by @qqqys
- fix(cli): derive context tool details from declared schemas ([#16292](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16292)) by @callmeYe
- fix(managed-agent): enforce strict SQL mode per embedded connection ([#16288](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16288)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(ci): widen the built-tree download window for eight shards ([#16285](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16285)) by @yiliang114
- fix(ci): fail Java lanes before disk exhaustion ([#16068](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16068)) by @yiliang114
- fix(managed-agent): use current state for approval changes ([#16296](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16296)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(managed): Reap Git descendants before terminating parents ([#16298](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16298)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(cli): gate project hooks behind an approval dialog ([#14748](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14748)) by @TianYuan1024
- fix(managed-agent): reject dangling Hosted cleanup references ([#16275](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16275)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(web-shell): express the PR watch events dependency in the channel editor ([#16236](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16236)) by @wenshao
- fix(serve): read PR sidecars directly for the bindings snapshot ([#16241](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16241)) by @wenshao
- fix(managed-agent): restore JournalCommit under its class-size ratchet ([#16323](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16323)) by @wenshao
- fix(ci): pin COREPACK_HOME for Linux test shards on cold-HOME runs ([#16328](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16328)) by @yiliang114
- fix(managed-agent): bound runtime thread pools ([#16330](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16330)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(managed-agent): refuse every URL fetch refuses and say why a health probe failed ([#16110](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16110)) by @wenshao
- fix(cli): keep project hook approval env inside the workspace ([#16316](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16316)) by @yiliang114
- fix(verify-pr): post flaky demotions on closed PRs and pin the blank class ([#16135](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16135)) by @wenshao
- fix(managed-agent): find the Flyway scripts in the module jar the server ships them in ([#16175](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16175)) by @wenshao
- fix(managed-agent): harden capacity recovery and clean up Java conventions ([#16318](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16318)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(ci): clear the pinned corepack cache before every install ([#16351](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16351)) by @wenshao
- fix(core): headless project-hook trust requires the folder-trust feature ([#16264](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16264)) by @yiliang114
- fix(web-shell): align welcome models and make UI language sessionless ([#16297](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16297)) by @liuxuely0626
- fix(channels): keep GitHub notifications unread on transient thread errors ([#16333](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16333)) by @wenshao
- fix(cli): stop Agent Host disconnects being undone and report unsaved joins ([#16156](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16156)) by @wenshao
- fix(core): tell the model the date once, from the history ([#16362](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16362)) by @qqqys
- fix(cli): preserve raw context usage estimates ([#16360](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16360)) by @callmeYe
- fix(serve): serve qualified hooks status for untrusted workspaces ([#16388](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16388)) by @yiliang114
- fix(cli): land a Web Shell update on the current latest release ([#16374](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16374)) by @wenshao
- fix(channels): keep GitHub replies hit by a secondary rate limit ([#16334](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16334)) by @wenshao
- fix(cli): forward the folder-trust store into the container sandbox ([#16390](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16390)) by @yiliang114

### Performance

- Improves managed-agent performance and stability by queueing ordinary journal commits on the Session row instead of a tenant-wide lock. ([#16256](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16256)) by @doudouOUC
- Narrows managed-agent lock scopes for output, lifecycle, and storage updates to reduce contention and improve throughput. ([#16268](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16268)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(managed-agent): separate workspace reads from durable admission ([#16283](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16283)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(managed-agent): avoid storage locks in read preflight ([#16312](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16312)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(managed-agent): index the Runtime slot lookup by isolation key ([#16325](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16325)) by @wenshao
- perf(managed-agent): share the storage fence in session command admissions ([#16329](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16329)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(managed-agent): take ordinary tool publication and read leases off the tenant lock ([#16335](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16335)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(core): defer workflow tool schemas by default ([#16310](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16310)) by @callmeYe
- perf(managed-agent): narrow queue dispatch and workspace session creation locks ([#16327](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16327)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(managed-agent): take ordinary publication lanes off the placement guard ([#16354](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16354)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(memory): move the main session's auto-memory guidance into a bundled skill ([#16303](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16303)) by @qqqys
- perf(managed-agent): remove ordinary journal and publication storage locks ([#16370](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16370)) by @doudouOUC
- perf(serve): keep the ACP spawn channel out of Managed Runtime workers ([#16235](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16235)) by @wenshao

### Documentation

- docs: configure Qwen3.x served under a custom model name ([#16342](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16342)) by @spped2000

### Internal Changes

- Keeps ACP parity test runtime state outside the workspace so integration tests compare only intended files and run more reliably. ([#16254](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16254)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Makes the ACP parity workspace guard compare the home directory against its pre-run listing, improving test reliability. ([#16266](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16266)) by @wenshao
- Speeds up CI by sharding Linux unit tests and web-shell smoke tests and reusing cached builds instead of rebuilding each workspace. ([#16133](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16133)) by @sorrycc
- test(web-shell): wait for the restored card before clicking continue ([#16286](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16286)) by @yiliang114
- test(interactive): share one CI-scaled wait policy across the TUI suites ([#16276](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16276)) by @yiliang114
- test(e2e): accept both plan-mode wordings in the ACP case ([#16273](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16273)) by @yiliang114
- test(managed-agent): ratchet persistence and runtime-broker class sizes ([#16284](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16284)) by @wenshao
- test(acp): expect the scheduler's plan-mode notice on the shared loop ([#16305](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16305)) by @qqqys
- test(sdk): read before an approved write in the tool-control E2E tests ([#16366](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16366)) by @qqqys
- test(managed-agent): declare v2 reader in the cleanup-conflict MySql IT ([#16372](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16372)) by @yiliang114
- test(managed-agent): fix busy-storage assertion broken by #16369 ([#16382](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16382)) by @yiliang114
- test(ci): pin the zero-skip timeout shape in awaitTwoSkipLines ([#16384](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16384)) by @yiliang114
- test(web-shell): pin the rewind capacity-latch re-open ([#16358](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16358)) by @yiliang114
- test(managed-agent): gate lifecycle-v2 close with a stopped worker ([#16123](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16123)) by @wenshao
- test(review): pin the carried-ledger carrier order and fail-open arms (#10464) ([#16395](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16395)) by @yiliang114

## New Contributors

## Highlights

The bundled CLI 0.23.0 includes two fixes requested in #11022:

- Managed memory availability now respects the `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` setting (#6941). Hosts that disable managed auto memory no longer see remember/dream requests admitted or managed-memory instructions in the system prompt; local patches can be removed.
- Size-triggered microcompaction now clears old tool results toward a low watermark (#8464), so it no longer rewrites another part of the conversation prefix on every subsequent turn. Provider prompt-cache reuse is preserved across long tool-heavy sessions, reducing cached-input cost.

milestone.title: v0.11
milestone.description:
Planned architecture release. Reuse this existing milestone rather than creating a competing v0.11.0 bucket.

Scope approved November 5, 2026: gix read-path adoption, coarse host/crate decomposition, completion of the command-contract frontier, typed Responses profiles and tool projection, embedder capability contracts, incremental context-folding/model-invoked compaction, and optional independent goal verification.

Complete every admitted consumer of a migration, retain a single turn loop/request authority, and qualify platform, cancellation and recovery behavior. Existing PRs and historical completed work stay attached. No due date or publication commitment.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against v0.9.3 (filed 2026-08-02 for the v0.9.4 milestone).
>
> **What remains**
> - Introduce one typed Responses dialect policy (as data, per the 2026-08-07 overlay) covering store/include, instructions vs system item, sampling fields, max_output_tokens, reasoning shape and replay for the three live dialects: OpenAI Codex, DeepSeek, Concentrate
> - Refactor crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs (`build_responses_body_for_provider` and the input-replay builder near :815) to read that policy instead of ProviderKind checks
> - Add JSON-in / expected-wire-out golden fixtures for request bodies and SSE (split function-call args, usage, malformed/out-of-order events) runnable offline
> - Document how to add a new profile and its fixtures
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - No `ResponsesDialectProfile` or equivalent type at the tag: `git grep -il 'ResponsesDialect\|responses_dialect' v0.10.1` matches only crates/tui/src/integrations/dsh/tests.rs
> - `build_responses_body_for_provider` still takes a ProviderKind and branches on it: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:45-58 (signature, `is_deepseek`, `is_concentrate`), :64, :72, :75, :109, :118, :127
> - Input replay also branches on provider identity: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:815, :903, :913, :930, :987
> - A third hard-coded Responses dialect (Concentrate) was added since filing, so the branch count grew: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:51-58
> - No language-neutral fixture harness for Responses: the tag has only Rust unit tests in crates/tui/src/client/responses/tests.rs; crates/tui/src/conformance/ holds events/golden/hooks/mcp/prompt/sse/stream_json and nothing for the Responses dialect
> - No commit in v0.9.3..v0.10.1 references #5093 (`git log --grep '#5093'` empty)

---

## Problem

The Responses bridge already covers substantial request construction, streaming, tool calls, and usage handling, but provider-specific branches are embedded in the adapter and exercised as individual cases. Adding custom Responses routes without a table-driven dialect contract would make regressions likely in tool loops, reasoning, caching, and normalized usage.

v0.9.4 needs a typed dialect-policy seam backed by deterministic conformance fixtures. Both built-in and custom Responses routes should share one normalized runtime contract while declaring their wire differences explicitly.

## Current evidence

- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs` owns Responses request construction, SSE event parsing, function-call assembly, and usage extraction.
- `build_responses_body_for_provider` currently receives an `ApiProvider` and contains provider-specific request branches.
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs::prepare_outbound_request` is the shared no-I/O preparation seam used by execution and request preview.
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs` provides a typed prepared-request boundary suitable for snapshot and contract tests.
- #3019 and #3084 established the reliability and provider-adapter baselines that this work should preserve.

## Scope

1. Introduce an internal typed `ResponsesDialectProfile` (name may vary) that owns declared differences in:
   - endpoint and header policy
   - stateful versus stateless turns
   - reasoning field shape
   - supported sampling and output-token fields
   - `store` and `include` behavior
   - input replay requirements
   - supported server-side capabilities
2. Refactor request preparation to consume the profile instead of scattering provider identity checks through body construction. Provider identity may select a profile; it must not implicitly grant unrelated capabilities.
3. Add a table-driven conformance harness covering at least the standard and stateless/plain-reasoning profiles.
4. Cover outbound request fixtures for:
   - instructions/system input and exact model identity
   - function tools and schema sanitation
   - parallel tool-call policy
   - function-call outputs and multi-turn replay
   - reasoning configuration and reasoning summaries
   - stateful/stateless `store` and `include` behavior
5. Cover SSE fixtures for:
   - text and reasoning deltas
   - split function-call arguments
   - completion and usage events
   - unknown, malformed, duplicated, and out-of-order events
   - UTF-8 boundaries, idle timeout, retry, and terminal errors
6. Verify normalized usage and cache accounting for input, output, reasoning, cache hits, cache misses, and cache writes. Do not fabricate cost when a route has no known SKU.
7. Add a deterministic error matrix:
   - invalid profile/configuration fails before network
   - 400/401/403 errors fail fast with sanitized diagnostics
   - 429/5xx behavior follows the declared retry policy
8. Document how to add a new typed profile and its fixtures.

Tests must use loopback or in-process fixtures only; no live provider traffic.

## Key files

- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/models.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/cost_status.rs`
- Existing cache-guard and provider-native-search tests where capability gating intersects the profile

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Standard and stateless/plain-reasoning profiles pass the same normalized transcript and tool-loop contract wherever the capability is supported.
- [ ] Unsupported features fail before network access with an error naming the selected profile and capability.
- [ ] Production execution and request preview use the same profile-derived prepared request.
- [ ] Function-call argument fragments assemble correctly across event boundaries and never emit a partial tool call.
- [ ] Unknown or malformed events produce deterministic, sanitized behavior without hiding terminal provider errors.
- [ ] Reasoning, token, and cache usage survive normalization without double counting.
- [ ] Cost remains unknown unless the exact route/model SKU is registered.
- [ ] Fixture snapshots contain no credentials or account identifiers.
- [ ] The full harness runs offline and documents how another profile is added.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui client::responses`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui client::prepared`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui cache_guard`
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- Confirm all fixtures are deterministic and require no provider credentials.

## Out of scope

- Live provider certification
- A user-programmable adapter language
- New provider authentication flows
- Default enablement of server-side tools
- Pricing additions without a verified SKU

## Related

- Parent architecture issue: #5092
- Responses reliability baseline: #3019
- Provider descriptor and adapter baseline: #3084

## Triage note

Milestone: **v0.9.4**. This is the adapter-extraction and offline proof slice for the parent architecture issue.

issues.body:
## Summary

I need a way to run CodeWhale **without any sandbox at all** on my own development machine. The kernel-level Seatbelt sandbox is breaking basic shell commands daily, and I've exhausted every workaround.

## Two Sandbox Layers

CodeWhale has two layers:

1. **Internal sandbox** (`--sandbox-mode`) — controllable via config, I have it set to `danger-full-access`
2. **macOS Seatbelt** — kernel-level, compiled into the binary, **not controllable by any config flag**

Layer 2 is the problem. `danger-full-access` bypasses `sandbox-exec` for child processes, but the main TUI process retains Seatbelt restrictions.

## What's Broken (even with danger-full-access)

| Operation | Blocked by |
|-----------|-----------|
| `open -a TextMate file.md` | Seatbelt |
| `ps aux` | Seatbelt |
| `osascript` | Seatbelt |
| `which rsvg-convert` | PATH stripped |
| `git push` | Intermittent |
| `python3.12 script.py` | Intermittent |
| `echo test > ~/Desktop/file` | Seatbelt |
| `find /opt/homebrew` | PATH/Seatbelt |

## Workarounds Tried (all insufficient)

1. `--sandbox-mode danger-full-access` — only affects internal sandbox, not Seatbelt
2. Per-project `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in config.toml — same
3. Rebuilding from source — sandbox baked into build, same behavior
4. Custom `lbl exec` relay (launchd plist → watcher → relay) — works but requires TCC grants, exact bash paths, single-quoting hacks, and breaks on brew upgrades. A Rube Goldberg machine just to run `which convert`.
5. `tasks gate_run` — inconsistent, works for some commands but not general shell
6. `open.txt` trigger + launchd polling — unreliable

## Request

A true zero-sandbox mode. Options, in order of preference:

1. **`--no-sandbox` CLI flag** that strips Seatbelt at runtime
2. **Separate "dev" build** without the Seatbelt entitlement — I'll sign it myself
3. **Entitlements file I can edit** before building from source, with docs
4. **Sanctioned escape hatch** — e.g., `cw exec --unsandboxed` that spawns outside Seatbelt

I'm on my own machine doing local dev. I'll accept any warning, waiver, or "here be dragons" banner. I just need the assistant to stop fighting me at the kernel level.

## Environment

- macOS 15.x, Apple Silicon (M4 Max)
- CodeWhale 0.9.1
- Config: `danger-full-access`, project trusted
- Homebrew tools at `/opt/homebrew/bin`

issues.body:
Hey! o/

Quick intro — I use Claude Code backed by DeepSeek and I've been eyeing DeepSeek-TUI for a bit. I'm on FreeBSD and I finally gave `npm install -g deepseek-tui` a shot today. Here's what I got:

```
root@worker:/home/user # npm install -g deepseek-tui
npm error deepseek-tui install failed: Unsupported platform: freebsd.
Supported platforms: 'linux', 'darwin', 'win32'.
npm error No prebuilt binary is available for this platform/architecture combo.
```

Fair enough — I knew it was a long shot :]

So here's my humble request: would you consider adding FreeBSD to the supported platforms? Two possible paths (not mutually exclusive, one can come way later than the other):

- **Ship a FreeBSD prebuilt binary on GitHub Releases** — The npm package already does the heavy lifting (downloads + installs binaries). It just needs a `freebsd` binary to pick up. This would unblock `npm install -g deepseek-tui` for us BSD folks right away.
- **`pkg install deepseek-tui`** — A proper FreeBSD port/package down the line. That's the long game, and I'm not expecting anyone to drop everything for it. But if it could land on the roadmap somewhere, that'd be amazing.

I know maintaining packages and build matrices isn't free. If you have no time for it right now, no worries — could you maybe plan it and add it to the roadmap? That way I know it's on the radar and I can keep an eye out. Totally fair if it's a "someday maybe" thing.

And hey, if you ever want someone to test the BSD side of things, I'm around and happy to help. Break my system, I don't mind :]

Cheers for the work you put into this — looking forward to trying it one way or another!

issues.body:
## Background

Codewhale's agent memory is currently a hardwired, single-implementation native feature with no pluggable third-party backend entry:

- The `MemoryBackend` enum has only `Native` / `Off` variants (`crates/tui/src/config.rs:1985`) — no `Custom`/`External`/`MCP`.
- `NativeMemoryStore` (`crates/tui/src/native_memory.rs:51`) is a concrete struct (Markdown source + SQLite FTS5 index) with no trait, so a third party cannot supply their own store.
- The plugin activation capability list `PluginActivationCapability` (`crates/tui/src/plugins/activation.rs:26`) has no `Memory` category, so a plugin cannot declare "I provide a memory backend".
- `docs/MEMORY.md` states that native is the only memory system, the planned Moraine MCP backend was removed, and `backend` accepts only `native` / `off`.

Today a third-party memory system can only be side-mounted through the generic MCP channel (most external memory systems expose an MCP server). It can be wired in, but it is not a first-class backend recognized by `[memory]` — `# quick-add`, the `remember` tool, and the `/memory` command all remain pinned to native.

## Goal

Upgrade memory from "single, hardwired implementation" to a **generic, pluggable, optional** seam:

- Keep native as the default, zero-dependency local backend.
- Define a stable backend seam that **any** third-party memory system can implement — not one tailored to a particular vendor.
- Make `[memory] backend` a first-class config choice, with the existing `remember` / recall / `/memory` lifecycle routing to whichever backend is selected; a backend only implements "store" and "retrieve".
- Ship causal-memory and mem0 as the **first two reference implementations** to prove the seam is generic across very different backend shapes — not as the endpoint of the work.

## The seam is open to any memory system

The abstraction is deliberately transport- and vendor-agnostic, so the following (and others) can all be implemented behind the same interface:

- **causal-memory** — causal/decision memory (local, MCP stdio/HTTP).
- **mem0** — fact/preference recall (remote service, API/SDK + MCP).
- **Zep, Letta (MemGPT), LangMem, MemOS, Mem0** — any agent-memory platform exposing a service API or MCP.
- A custom in-house store — implement the trait directly.

The only requirement is that a backend can answer "store an entry" and "retrieve relevant entries for a query".

## Reference implementation #1 (focus): causal-memory (developed in-house)

causal-memory is our open-source agent memory system (Rust, Apache-2.0, `JingxuanC/causal-memory`). Its core differentiator is a **causal core + inhibition modeling**: facts, temporal state, and `decision → outcome` causal edges live on a single SQLite store, driven by a hippocampus-style engine (typed spreading activation with excitatory *and* inhibitory edges, Hebbian co-occurrence reinforcement, Q-value dynamics, immutable SWR consolidation). Agents recall not only *what* happened and *when* it was true, but *why* it worked and *what would happen if* they acted differently.

Why it is the first backend we build:

1. **Causal information is the most fragile type under text compaction.** The causal table lives outside the agent's context window, so compaction cannot touch it — in a real-LLM compaction benchmark causal-memory retains 100% causal-table recall while mem0 drops to 45%. This directly patches the "re-hits the same bug the same wrong way" hole after long-session compaction.
2. **Clearly ahead of mem0 on causal capabilities** (CausalEval): C7 belief update 100% vs 80%, C2 intervention prediction 75% vs 40%, C4 inhibition distinction 80% vs 50%.
3. **Integration surface is ready**: 14 MCP tools (stdio + HTTP transports), a Python `Memory` facade, and an existing DSH plugin shape — wiring into Codewhale's MCP/plugin channel is nearly zero new code.
4. The honest caveat: pure fact recall (LoCoMo 79.1% vs mem0 91.6%) is not its strong suit — that is exactly mem0's strength. The two are complementary, which is why a generic seam beats "pick one".

## Reference implementation #2: mem0

mem0 is the fact-recall specialist (LoCoMo 91.6%) and is chosen as the second reference implementation precisely because its shape is the opposite of causal-memory's: a **remote hosted service** with an API/SDK, rather than a local store. If the seam can absorb both, it is general enough for the rest of the ecosystem.

## Plan (phased)

- **Phase 0 — baseline (already landed)**: native as the only backend, `[memory]` opt-in, `#` quick-add, `remember`/recall tools. Landed in v0.9.x.
- **Phase 1 — define the generic backend seam (core change)**: introduce a `MemoryBackend` trait with a minimal, transport-agnostic method set (`store` / `search` / `prompt_block`, plus a health/`status` probe); add an `External`/`Custom` variant to the `MemoryBackend` enum; make `[memory] backend` resolve a backend by **kind + connection parameters** (process/stdio command, HTTP service URL, or MCP server name) rather than hardcoding vendor names. Native becomes a default impl of the trait; `Off` stays as-is. Add a `Memory` capability to `PluginActivationCapability` so a backend can ship as a plugin bundle.
- **Phase 2 — two reference implementations to prove genericity**: land **causal-memory** first (MCP stdio + HTTP), then **mem0** (remote API/SDK). Success criterion: the trait needed no vendor-specific escape hatches to absorb two very different backend shapes.
- **Phase 3 — bring-your-own-backend**: document the driver/adaptor contract so any third party (Zep, Letta, LangMem, a custom store, …) can add a backend — ideally as an external plugin bundle, without a core change.
- **Phase 4 — wrap-up**: update `docs/MEMORY.md`, `config.example.toml`, and the `[memory]` config contract; add backend selection + fallback (degrade to off or native when a backend is unavailable); document the KV-cache effect (the boundary of memory injected into the system-prompt prefix is unchanged).

## Integration surface

- **Reuse the existing MCP/plugin channel**: causal-memory is already an MCP server and can land first as a plugin bundle (`McpStdio`/`McpRemote`) as the Phase 2 bootstrap — no need to wait for the trait abstraction before trying it out. Any MCP-speaking memory system gets the same path for free.
- **Add a native trait backend**: make `[memory] backend = "causal-memory"` (or any registered backend) a first-class config option, with the `remember` tool, `/memory` command, and `#` quick-add all routing to the selected backend.
- **Open the plugin capability**: a `Memory` activation capability lets a third party ship a backend as a reviewed plugin, exactly like they ship skills, MCP servers, or hooks today.

## References

- Current memory implementation: `crates/tui/src/native_memory.rs`, `crates/tui/src/config.rs` (`MemoryBackend` / `MemoryConfig`)
- Memory docs: `docs/MEMORY.md`
- Plugin activation capabilities: `crates/tui/src/plugins/activation.rs`
- causal-memory: https://github.com/JingxuanC/causal-memory (README includes the CausalEval / compaction-survival benchmarks)
- Original memory EPIC: #489

issues.body:
<!-- cw-release-routing-current -->
## Release routing - November 5, 2026

Target: **v1.0** (planned, undated).

Automatic skill learning/evolution is long-term product design requiring approval, privacy and version-history controls; manual skill creation does not complete it.

This is the approved November 5 release-scope decision. Earlier 0.10.3 acceptance entries below are retained as historical implementation/evidence records, not the current release assignment. Unfinished criteria remain open; this move does not claim resolution or waive a confirmed release-critical defect.
<!-- /cw-release-routing-current -->

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

Manual skill creation is present; the proposed continuous learning feature is not built.

This is a criterion-by-criterion source reconciliation against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). “Source complete” credits the owning implementation; it does not claim an unrun native, provider, deployment or final-distribution check. The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

- **manual-existing — source complete existing workflow:** skills command maps new to bundled skill-creator; this remains an explicit user-directed skill-authoring workflow.
- **pattern-detection — implementation missing:** No production occurrence threshold, pattern detection or correction-to-skill pipeline exists in the searched owners.
- **generation-approval — implementation missing:** Manual skill-creator is not automatic generation with confidence/occurrence policy and ratification. No suggest/approve/reject learning command flow exists.
- **evolution — implementation missing:** No learned-skill evolution/version history/merge or confidence pruning authority is present.
- **cross-session-controls — implementation missing:** Proposed learning config fields/learning history controls are absent. Existing session/skill discovery is not cross-session learning.

**Next action:** Root confirms current release admission and assigns the existing Backlog issue. If retained, implement the explicit suggest+preview+approve first phase over existing Skills owner; preserve all later evolution/privacy scope as unfinished.

Current owner: [CW-6300](https://linear.app/shannonlabs/issue/CW-6300).

Whole issue remains open. 0.10.3 is unpublished; earlier dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Problem
CodeWhale has a powerful Skills System where users can manually create `SKILL.md` files that the agent can reference. However, the knowledge remains static:

1. **No automatic pattern extraction** - The agent doesn't recognize when it's solving the same type of problem repeatedly
2. **No skill evolution** - When a user provides corrections or better approaches, the agent doesn't update existing skills
3. **No cross-session learning** - Lessons learned in one session don't automatically improve future sessions
4. **Manual overhead** - Users must proactively identify patterns and write skills themselves, which breaks flow

**Example**: A developer builds 3 FastAPI endpoints with MongoDB over a week. Each time, they go through similar steps (configure connection, create models, implement CRUD, add error handling, write tests). The agent executes these steps each time but never "learns" that this is a repeatable pattern worth codifying as a skill.

## Proposed Solution
Implement a **self-learning loop** that automatically observes, extracts, and codifies patterns from successful interactions:

#### Core Components:

**1. Pattern Detection Engine**
- Monitor dialog history for repeated solution patterns
- Identify multi-step workflows that occur 3+ times
- Detect corrections and incorporate them into skills
- Track successful outcomes vs. failures

**2. Automated Skill Generation**
- Create `SKILL.md` files based on detected patterns
- Generate structured YAML frontmatter with:
  - Name, description, version
  - Step-by-step instructions
  - Common pitfalls (learned from corrections)
  - Usage examples from real dialog
  - Confidence scores based on success rate

**3. Skill Evolution System**
- Update existing skills when better approaches are discovered
- Merge related skills into more comprehensive ones
- Archive unused or low-confidence skills
- Version tracking with change history

**4. Learning Triggers**

```toml
# Example configuration
[learning]
auto_create_skills = true          # Default: false (requires confirmation)
confidence_threshold = 0.8          # Only auto-create if pattern confidence > 80%
pattern_occurrence_threshold = 3    # Pattern must appear 3+ times
enable_cross_session_learning = true
skill_review_frequency = "weekly"   # Suggest reviewing skills periodically
```

**5. User Control & Transparency**

- Preview suggested skills before creation (/suggest-skills)
- Approve/deny skill creation (/approve-skill fastapi-crud)
- Review learning history (/learning-history)
- Manual override and pruning (/delete-skill old-pattern, /merge-skills)

## Use Case

Scenario: A development team building a FastAPI + React + MCP application over 6 months:

Month 1: Manual Mode

- Developers work with CodeWhale, solving problems

- Agent silently observes patterns but doesn't act

- Team reviews /suggest-skills weekly and creates the most useful ones manually

Month 2-3: Semi-Automated Mode

- Agent automatically creates skills for patterns with 90%+ confidence

- Team reviews and approves skills weekly

- Skills begin covering 40% of repetitive tasks

Month 4-6: Fully Automated Mode

- Agent creates, updates, and merges skills autonomously

- Skills cover 80% of repetitive patterns

- Development speed increases 2-3x for common tasks

Specific Example:

```text
Session 1: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth"
Session 2: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth and role-based permissions"
Session 3: "Build FastAPI endpoint with JWT auth, roles, and rate limiting"

→ Agent detects the pattern and creates skill "fastapi-jwt-crud"
→ Future request: "Build user management API" 
→ Agent uses the skill, saving 30 minutes of work
→ User adds "also needs email verification" 
→ Agent updates the skill with email verification step
→ Next team member gets the improved skill automatically
```

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Pros | Cons |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Manual Skills** | Full control, simple to implement | High overhead, knowledge loss between sessions |
| **Third-party Learning Tools** | Could use external ML | Integration complexity, additional dependencies |
| **Prompt-based Learning** | Simple to implement | Temporary, lost between sessions |
| **MCP-based Learning** | Extensible, modular | Requires separate MCP server, not built-in |


This proposal leverages CodeWhale's existing infrastructure (skills, hooks, MCP) while adding intelligence on top, keeping everything integrated and user-friendly.

## Impact 

This feature would transform CodeWhale from a static assistant into an adaptive pair programmer that grows with its users. It's technically feasible using CodeWhale's existing infrastructure (skills, hooks, MCP) and would provide immense value to both individual developers and teams.

For Individual Developers:

- ⚡ 2-3x faster for repetitive coding tasks

- 🧠 Preserves knowledge - don't need to remember every best practice

- 🔄 Continuous improvement - your assistant gets smarter every day

For Teams:

- 📚 Shared knowledge base - skills become team documentation

- 🎯 Consistent code quality - best practices automatically enforced

- 🚀 Faster onboarding - new members learn patterns through skills

For the CodeWhale Project:

- 🏆 Unique competitive advantage - no other open-source agent has this

- 🌟 Stronger community - users will share their learned skills

- 📈 Increased adoption - teams will choose CodeWhale for the learning capability

Metrics to Track:

- Number of skills created automatically vs. manually

- Time saved per task (before/after learning)

- Skill usage rates and success rates

- User satisfaction scores



## Additional context

### Why Now?

- The skills system is already built - this adds the "learning" layer

- MCP provides the perfect hook for pattern detection

- Users are already asking for smarter assistants

#### Potential Challenges & Mitigations:

- False positives → Confidence thresholds and human approval (especially initially)

- Skill bloat → Automatic archiving and merging of similar skills

- Security → Version control and rollback for skills, opt-in feature with clear controls

### Implementation Phases (Suggestion)

#### Phase 1: Pattern Detection (MVP)

- Add /suggest-skills command that analyzes current session

- Show proposed skill template for user approval

- Implement via MCP server (external)

#### Phase 2: Automated Creation

- Detect patterns without prompting

- Auto-create skills with configurable confidence threshold

- Add /approve-skill and /reject-skill commands

#### Phase 3: Evolution

- Update skills when corrections are detected

- Merge related skills automatically

- Track skill usage and confidence scores

#### Phase 4: Cross-Session Learning

- Share learned skills across all projects

- Aggregate best practices from multiple sessions

- Privacy controls for sensitive code

### Example

```bash
$ codewhale

> Build a FastAPI endpoint for user registration with email validation

[Agent builds the feature through 8 steps]

> Now build a product listing endpoint

[Agent notices pattern...]

🧠 I've noticed you're building FastAPI CRUD endpoints with validation.
   I've seen this pattern 3 times this week.

   Would you like me to create a skill called "fastapi-crud-with-validation"? [y/n] y

✅ Skill created! It includes:
   - MongoDB connection setup
   - Pydantic model generation
   - CRUD endpoint implementation
   - Email validation pattern
   - Error handling best practices

   Type `/skill fastapi-crud-with-validation` to use it next time.

[Next week...]

> Build a blog post API

💡 I see you're building FastAPI CRUD again. Using skill: fastapi-crud-with-validation
   [Executes in 3 steps instead of 8, with best practices applied]

> Also add category filtering

🔄 I've added category filtering to the skill. This will be available for future tasks.
```

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against v0.9.3 (filed 2026-08-02 for the v0.9.4 milestone).
>
> **What remains**
> - Replace the `is_deepseek` / `is_concentrate` / `OpenaiCodex` branches in crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs with one typed profile selected at route resolution (this is #5093's work)
> - Per the 2026-08-07 overlay, express the profile as a data table (JSON/TOML) rather than Rust branches
> - Add the optional `responses_profile` key for named custom providers that already accept `wire = "responses"` (left open when #5094 closed)
> - Fail unsupported profile/feature combinations before network I/O with a provider-named error
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Child #5094 is CLOSED/COMPLETED (2026-09-02): custom providers can select the Responses wire explicitly - crates/tui/src/client.rs:2513-2525 (`provider_wire_format_for_config`, `wire = "openai" | "anthropic" | "responses"`), crates/config/src/lib.rs:1042 (aliases wire/api_style/protocol/wire_format/dialect), crates/config/src/provider.rs:89
> - No typed Responses dialect/profile exists: `git grep -il 'ResponsesDialect\|responses_dialect' v0.10.1` matches only crates/tui/src/integrations/dsh/tests.rs
> - Loose provider booleans still drive the Responses body: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:50 (`is_deepseek`), :58 (`is_concentrate`), :64, :75, :133, :145, :815, :930, :1051
> - Further ProviderKind::OpenaiCodex branches in the same builder: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:72, :109, :118, :127, :161 (`is_chatgpt`), :903, :913, :987
> - The shared prepared-request seam the issue asks to preserve is in place: crates/tui/src/client.rs:2826-2855 (WireDialect chosen before body build) and :4218-4221, :4318-4321 (dispatch on prepared.dialect)
> - No commit in v0.9.3..v0.10.1 references #5092 or #5093 (`git log --grep` empty)

---

## Problem

Codewhale can resolve `WireFormat::Responses` from a provider/model offering, but the Responses serializer still chooses important wire behavior from provider-enum branches. That makes a new Responses-compatible route more than a base-URL change: request fields, endpoint shape, reasoning representation, replay/state behavior, tool events, headers, and usage normalization can drift independently.

For v0.9.4, Responses behavior should be selected through a typed provider/dialect profile attached to the resolved route. The route resolver still chooses the provider and model; the profile only describes how that exact Responses endpoint speaks.

## Current evidence

- `crates/config/src/provider.rs::WireFormat` and `WirePolicy` already separate Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages at the route layer.
- `crates/config/src/provider.rs::Deepseek::wire_policy` is model-aware, while `Custom::wire_policy` is fixed to Chat Completions.
- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs::build_responses_body_for_provider` derives an `is_deepseek` boolean and branches on request fields, reasoning, and replay behavior.
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs::prepare_outbound_request` selects Responses body construction, endpoint URL, and route shape using `ApiProvider` checks.
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs` already provides the typed prepared-request seam that production dispatch and request preview share.
- Closed #185 established that wire format comes from the exact route offering, not a model slug. Closed #3084 established the provider-descriptor/wire-adapter ownership boundary.

## Architecture contract

1. A resolved route carries both `WireFormat::Responses` and a typed Responses dialect/profile.
2. The dialect owns endpoint-path policy, supported request fields, reasoning encoding/replay, tool item/event variants, statefulness, provider-only headers, and usage/cache extraction.
3. `prepare_outbound_request` remains the single no-I/O seam used by production and `/preview-request`.
4. Provider/model selection remains in route resolution. The Responses adapter must not infer a dialect from a model slug or rewrite the selected provider.
5. Profiles are typed and allowlisted. Do not add arbitrary JSON body patches, arbitrary event remapping, or a prompt hook.
6. Existing OpenAI API, ChatGPT OAuth/Codex, DeepSeek, and model-aware gateway behavior must remain byte/fixture compatible unless a fixture demonstrates an existing bug.

## Implementation issues

- [ ] #5093 — extract the typed Responses dialect policy and prove it with an offline conformance harness.
- [ ] #5094 — let named custom providers explicitly select Responses plus an allowlisted dialect profile while preserving the Chat Completions default.

Together these two issues implement the architecture contract above; neither should add model-name or base-URL inference.

## Key files

- `crates/config/src/provider.rs`
- `crates/config/src/provider_kind.rs`
- `crates/config/src/route/resolver.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs`
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No Responses request-body or endpoint decision depends on a loose `is_deepseek`/`is_codex` boolean when the same fact can come from the typed dialect profile.
- [ ] Exact route resolution selects wire format and dialect before request serialization.
- [ ] Current OpenAI API, ChatGPT OAuth/Codex, DeepSeek, and model-aware gateway fixtures still pass.
- [ ] One named custom provider can select Responses explicitly without model-name inference.
- [ ] Request preview and production dispatch produce the same normalized prepared request.
- [ ] Unsupported profile/feature combinations fail before network I/O with a provider-named corrective error.
- [ ] All verification is provider-free and uses redacted loopback fixtures; no live credential is required.

## Verification

    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo test -p codewhale-config --locked
    cargo test -p codewhale-tui --bin codewhale-tui --locked client::responses
    cargo test -p codewhale-tui --bin codewhale-tui --locked prepared
    python3 scripts/check-provider-registry.py
    git diff --check

## Out of scope

- Adding or privileging a new built-in provider or model.
- A hosted API proxy or Codewhale-operated inference service.
- Arbitrary user-authored request/response transformation code.
- Pricing claims without an exact provider/model SKU source.
- Live-provider, OAuth, billing, publishing, or release actions.

## Related

- #185 — exact route offerings choose Responses versus Chat Completions; this issue begins after that selection.
- #3019 — existing Responses reliability and tool-result behavior that must not regress.
- #3084 — provider descriptors and wire-adapter ownership contract.
- #5084 — current named-custom-provider compatibility spike; it remains Chat Completions unless this work explicitly enables Responses.

_Triage note: filed for the v0.9.4 milestone on 2026-08-02 from verified current source anchors._

<!-- cw-release-routing-current -->
## Release routing - November 5, 2026

Target: **v0.11** (planned, undated).

Move gix adoption to the architecture release so operation-family, hostile-repository, MSRV and target qualification are not rushed into a patch release.

This is the approved November 5 release-scope decision. Earlier 0.10.3 acceptance entries below are retained as historical implementation/evidence records, not the current release assignment. Unfinished criteria remain open; this move does not claim resolution or waive a confirmed release-critical defect.
<!-- /cw-release-routing-current -->

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**not adopted: no gix dependency in canonical Cargo graph.**

Source reconciled against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c).

Credited source:

- **CLI lock avoidance predecessor**: [f704e0c9c0](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/f704e0c9c05e0e82917d6d57b3d5f6131660a934)
- **hardened Git read/source prerequisites**: existing shared real-Git facade remains; does not implement gix or zero-spawn acceptance

Remaining:

- Exact pinned minimal dependency/MSRV/advisory/target closure and compatible upstream backport must be reviewed/adopted
- Migrate every admitted internal discovery/HEAD/status/diff/aheadbehind/worktree/config consumer; keep writes and agent shell on realGit
- Observe actual zero internal read subprocesses, no hooks/filters/fsmonitor/lazyfetch/optionalwrites, hostile repository failclosed behavior, cancellation, Windows and maintained targets. Later log/show/blame phase remains explicitly labeled by existing maintainer scope

**Next action:** Review frozen gix artifact/backport packet against the full required operation-family ledger, resolve real gaps, then one coordinated native batch and actual normal/hostile/no-spawn/no-write controls.

Whole issue remains open. Uncommitted Pager corrections and uncompiled gix/host-band artifacts are excluded from delivered source. Current routing: CW-7763. 0.10.3 remains unpublished; previous dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Problem

codewhale shells out to the real `git` CLI for all internal read operations — repository badge probes, workspace context, `@status`/`@diff` mentions, and the model-callable Git tools. After #5617, two costs remain:

1. **Process spawn overhead**: the internal probes still spawn roughly **48 git processes per minute** while the TUI is idle in a git repo (≈190/min before the lock-reduction issue). Each spawn pays process creation + CLI startup for a computation that is a few milliseconds in-process.
2. **Unnecessary dependency on the git binary**: internal badge and context reads could work purely from the repository's on-disk format, without requiring git to be installed at all.

## Proposed solution

Migrate codewhale's **internal read-only** git operations from the `git` CLI to **gix** (gitoxide, pure Rust). Requirement-level scope (implementation follows the project's own conventions; no specific files are prescribed). This issue only makes sense after the lock-reduction issue is merged: the migration replaces the lock-free CLI reads with in-process reads and removes the event-driven refresh path's remaining process spawns.

- Add `gix` as a workspace dependency, pinned to an exact version, with the minimal feature set covering the read paths.
- Replace the following internal operations with gix in-process equivalents:
  - repository discovery / work-tree root resolution
  - HEAD / branch resolution (including detached-HEAD short hash)
  - working-tree status computation (staged / modified / untracked / conflicts)
  - ahead/behind counts vs upstream
  - worktree listing
  - remote origin URL and git config reads
  - commit log / show / blame (model-facing Git tool — may be a later phase)
- **Keep the `git` CLI for real write operations** (side-repo snapshot commits, worktree create/remove, branch deletion) and for agent-executed shell commands (`exec_shell` remains the model's surface and must stay a real CLI).

## Expected gains

- **Zero subprocess spawns for internal reads**: the idle ~48 processes/min (baseline after the lock-reduction issue) drop to **~0** — badge and context data become pure in-process computation.
- **No lock files, permanently**: gix reads never touch `.git/index.lock`, eliminating the commit-collision problem at the root, without environment-variable mitigations.
- **Faster refresh**: in-process status computation (~5-30ms) vs. process spawn + CLI startup per probe.
- **Works without the git binary**: badge and context reads succeed from the on-disk format even where `git` is not installed; write paths still report cleanly when git is missing.
- **Consistent with the event-driven direction**: when combined with `.git` metadata watching (lock-reduction issue, point 3), the refresh path becomes event-triggered in-process computation with near-zero idle cost.

---

## Combined Core execution: C09

[Core execution plan](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/document/codewhale-core-execution-plan-a11e2e1c601d>) owns order and scope. This issue contributes to C09; the linked plan owns the complete packet and any outstanding candidate acceptance. Record this issue's path claims and implementation evidence here.

**Issue mapping:** [SHA-6291 / GitHub #5586](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6291/decompose-the-mega-files-librs-187k-configrs-123k-clientrs-111k>)
  covers cohesive large-file decomposition across C03–C09; move whole behaviors
  and owning tests, with checked dependency boundaries rather than line-count
  targets. [SHA-6286 / GitHub #5580](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6286/streamline-tui-monoliths-split-event-looprs-match-into-per-domain>) moves remaining
  event handling into domain reducers and leaves dispatch in `event_loop.rs`;
  preserve the existing reducer pattern and migrate touched arms completely.
  [SHA-6287 / GitHub #5581](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6287/event-granularity-audit-surfaces-that-stall-at-turn-boundaries-despite>) supplies the per-call
  telemetry consumer requirements implemented in C11 with #6011: live token/time
  display, cache visibility and durable mid-turn accounting, with authoritative
  completion reconciliation and no double counting. Credit already-live cost,
  background cost, timing and context surfaces.

[SHA-5509 / GitHub #3957](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-5509/refactor-split-shared-modal-infrastructure-and-owned-views>) separates shared modal
  infrastructure from owned Config/SubAgents views and makes all provider
  credential entry use the same masking, validation and geometry primitive.
  Prove paste/delete/Enter/Esc/failure/retry and 80x24/120x32 wrapping; secrets
  must never reach screenshots, logs or errors.
  [SHA-5506 / GitHub #3954](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-5506/refactor-split-setup-wizard-constitution-runtime-provider-and>) splits setup by
  constitution, runtime, provider, persistence/report and navigation ownership
  where warranted; preserve constitution checkpoints and onboarding handoff.
  These client refactors keep behavior and private-test visibility intact.

[SHA-6251 / GitHub #5528](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6251/workflow-runs-fail-silently-dispatchschema-errors-never-surface-in-the>) requires visible
  workflow dispatch/schema failures even before a child starts, with preserved
  error/status receipts over the shared event authority.
  [SHA-6156 / GitHub #5268](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/issue/SHA-6156/mid-turn-control-queue-send-now-esc-keep-draft-named-waits>) requires visible queue,
  send-now, cancel/keep-draft and named waits over existing runtime channels;
  qualify those states with C12 and C08's submitted-steer consume/ack contract.
  C01's #5479 register and controls must use this same runtime projection.

**Owner: client-adapter owner. Dependencies: C08.** Fold the embedded HTTP
  API into the existing app-server HTTP/SSE/stdio surface over the shared
  runtime, preserving routes and authentication. Move argument parsing and
  headless presentation from TUI `lib.rs` into CLI; preserve binary names and
  public commands. TUI owns terminal lifecycle, rendering, input, pickers and
  slash-command presentation, calling the same runtime operations. Use existing
  in-process `EngineHandle`/`Op`/`Event` seams; local terminal use need not hop
  through HTTP. Separate wire DTOs from internal reply channels/capabilities.

**Completion evidence required:** all three clients reach the same lifecycle/execution owner,
  transport/auth/protocol parity and reconnect/recovery pass, no UI-owned
  provider I/O/policy/store/loop remains, and obsolete dependencies and temporary
  internal shims are removed. Adopt `core/protocol_parity.rs` in real consumers
  or retire it; unused parity code is not convergence. Resize UI files only by
  remaining responsibility. Apps product work is not part of this packet.

---

## Original issue and contributor history

User ask for the 0.9.12 cleanup lane: the 10k+-line files keep causing pain. Measured today (prod code, excluding the 20k-line test files which should split alongside their subjects):

* `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` — 18,747
* `crates/tui/src/config.rs` — 12,346
* `crates/tui/src/client.rs` — 11,122

Approach (same discipline as #5580): mechanical module extraction, one cohesive region per commit, no behavior change, moves verified by `cargo check` + the file's existing test slice. Suggested first cuts: [client.rs](<http://client.rs>) wire-parsing (parse_usage/SSE chunk parsing + their tests) into `client/wire.rs`; [config.rs](<http://config.rs>) merge/persistence into `config/merge.rs`; [lib.rs](<http://lib.rs>) engine-config assembly into its own module. Declared one-way per AGENTS.md once started: new code lands in the extracted modules, touched regions migrate.

Tracker: #5573. Related: #5580, #5581.

## Developer fast loop

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (\~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

* `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
* `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
* The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
* Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.
