```text
│Output                                            23.8M │
│Cache Read                                      8402.2M │
│Cache Write                                           0 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      MODEL USAGE                       │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash                 │
│  Messages                                       25,371 │
│  Input Tokens                                   110.1M │
│  Output Tokens                                   14.7M │
│  Cache Read                                    3473.7M │   → hit ≈ 96.9%
│  Cache Write                                         0 │
│  Cost                                          $0.0000 │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ opencode/x-preview-f-free                              │
│  Messages                                       17,109 │

│  Output Tokens                                   10.1M │
│  Cache Read                                    1941.9M │   → hit ≈ 92.3%
│  Cache Write                                         0 │

├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash                          │

```

(Hand-computed hit rates annotated inline with `→`; opencode prints no such column.)

**Precedent: rtk hook (real output)**

Users already track token leakage manually with shell-wrapper hooks. This real report shows where tokens actually go across 89k commands (hook-side savings, i.e. what the wrapper trimmed before the agent saw it):

```text
RTK Token Savings (Global Scope)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Total commands:    89010
Input tokens:      2006.2M
Output tokens:     576.9M
Tokens saved:      1429.3M (71.2%)
Efficiency meter: █████████████████░░░░░░░ 71.2%

By Command
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  #  Command                   Count    Saved    Avg%    Time  Impact
 1.  rtk read                   2343  1030.7M   23.2%    45ms  ██████████
 2.  rtk grep                  12298   158.4M   23.9%   197ms  ██░░░░░░░░
 3.  rtk git diff output/p...      3   105.2M  100.0%    1.2s  █░░░░░░░░░
 4.  rtk git diff -- outpu...      1    36.5M  100.0%    1.2s  ░░░░░░░░░░
 5.  rtk diff                     27    35.2M   64.3%   153ms  ░░░░░░░░░░
 6.  rtk find                    535    24.3M   12.7%   789ms  ░░░░░░░░░░

```

Key insight: **read** is the single biggest sink (1030.7M = 72% of all savings), then grep (158M), then git diff (105M) — the same tools dominate both hook-side savings and (we should verify) in-context cost. CW can measure the *actual* in-context footprint of its own built-in tools without any external hook.

**Code refs (data already exists)**

* Persisted session stats: `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs` — `SavedSession` (`total_tokens`, `cost: SessionCostSnapshot` incl. session/subagent USD+CNY, high-water), sessions dir + journal (`#5262`).
* In-session surfaces: `/tokens`/`/cost` (`crates/tui/src/commands/groups/debug/tokens.rs`), `/cache` (`.../debug/cache.rs`), TUI Context panel (`crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:1826` `context_panel`, `work_surface/views.rs`).
* Tool-result sizes/truncation: `crates/tui/src/tools/truncate.rs` (spillover + bounded preview), `crates/tui/src/tools/web/extract.rs` (`format=markdown|text|raw`).
* Compaction ownership: `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs` (`runtime_cost_owner`), `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`.
* Thinking replay tokens: `crates/tui/src/client.rs` ("multi-turn thinking-mode conversation should report replay tokens").

**Related work**

* Shipped: [#5624](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/5624>) (live session token totals), [#5623](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/5623>) (post-compaction input tokens)
* Open, related: #5977 (tok/s audit), #5620 (agent doesn't react to context pressure), #5581 (event-granularity audit — feeds error analytics), #5479 (fleet/agents TUI view)
* Outbox/events (can feed error analytics): lifecycle outbox `[lifecycle_outbox]` in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`
* Fleet ledger / status: `codewhale fleet status|inspect|logs|artifacts`, durable ledger `.codewhale/fleet.jsonl`, Runtime API `/v1/fleet/runs`, `/v1/fleet/runs/{id}/workers` (docs/FLEET.md "Status Surfaces"); `SessionCostSnapshot.subagent_cost_usd/cny` in `session_manager.rs`; `/fleet workers` = session sub-agents view (`/subagents` compat).

## Open questions (decide during implementation)

* **TUI surface**: `/tokens` (and subcommands like `/tokens models`, `/tokens tools`, `/tokens errors`) as in-TUI commands are an **open question** — the TUI Context panel already covers live session view, and the confirmed deliverable here is the **global** `codewhale stats` **CLI**. Whether the same reports should also be reachable from inside the TUI can be decided separately.
* **Duplicate / re-send waste ("token survival")** — how many tokens re-enter history verbatim (same file read twice, `git diff` + `read` of same files)? Measurable via content hashing (VTCode drops duplicate reads during compaction). Worth the complexity? Measure first, optionally dedupe later.
* **Tokenizer-estimate accuracy (unique)** — Codewhale uses \~4 chars/token and marks windows `(unverified)`. Accumulate estimate-vs-provider-actual bias per request. Nobody ships this; great for budget debugging. How much is derivable from TurnUsage receipts?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `codewhale stats --days N` prints: sessions, messages, total cost, tokens (input/output/cache read/write), per-session average/median tokens
- [ ] `codewhale stats --models N` prints per-model rows: input/output, cache read/write, cost, **cache hit %**, **reasoning split**
- [ ] `codewhale stats --tools N` prints per-tool rows: calls, tokens added to history, truncated/spooled share, **failure rate + top error**
- [ ] `codewhale stats --project <id>` filters by project
- [ ] compaction ledger (count, trigger, summarizer tokens/cost, history dropped) visible in stats or a dedicated subcommand
- [ ] `--days`/`--models`/`--tools`/`--project` behave like opencode's flags
- [ ] sub-agent/fleet stats: per-role (incl. custom) and per-worker calls, tokens, cost, status counts, failure sources — in `stats --roles N` or `codewhale fleet stats`

issues.body:
## Problem

While a foreground shell command runs and is not waiting for interaction, the tool card shows the detach hint instead of the command. In `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1031-1039` the header is chosen as:

```rust
let command_summary = command_header_summary(&self.command);
let compact_foreground_wait = self.is_foreground_shell_wait();
let header_summary = if compact_foreground_wait {
    Some(FOREGROUND_SHELL_WAIT_HINT)          // "Ctrl+B → /jobs"
} else {
    self.interaction.as_deref().or(Some(command_summary.as_str()))
};
```

`is_foreground_shell_wait()` (`crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1006-1011`) is true for exactly the state the user watches while work happens — `Running`, assistant-issued, no interaction. So the command is invisible precisely while it runs, and the row reads `run running (81s) · Ctrl+B → /jobs`.

With the default `tool_collapse_mode = "compact"` this is total for the live view: a collapsed cell is the header line alone ("the tool-name + arg/command summary as the single intent line", `crates/tui/src/tui/app/types.rs:140-146`), and the hint has taken that line. The command still exists one level down — the card body renders it through `render_command_mode` (`crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1140`, `:2160-2176`: capped at `TOOL_COMMAND_LINE_LIMIT` = 6 wrapped lines with a details affordance in live mode, unwrapped in the transcript) — but that means expanding the card or leaving the transcript for `/jobs`.

A second, related truncation applies in every other state: `command_header_summary` (`crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:2187-2195`) keeps only the **first line** of the command, so a multi-line invocation (heredoc, `&&` chain, `for` loop) shows one line and hides the rest.

Nothing here is configurable: no key for either behaviour exists in `settings.toml`, `crates/tui/src/settings.rs`, `crates/tui/src/config.rs` or `crates/config/src/lib.rs`. The full command is available in `/jobs` — `cmd: <full command>` with cwd and output tail (`crates/tui/src/tui/shell_job_routing.rs:21-56`) — but answering "what is it running?" then means leaving the transcript.

## Proposed solution

One display setting whose absent/off value is exactly today's behaviour:

```toml
# settings.toml, alongside the other display knobs and editable from /config
running_shell_command = "off"        # off | first_line | full   (default: off)
```

- **`off` (default, and what an absent key means)** — no change at all: the header stays the detach hint. Existing installs and every user who never sets the key see precisely what they see today.
- `first_line` — the hint stays and the command's first line is appended: `cmd: cargo test -p codewhale-tui · Ctrl+B → /jobs`.
- `full` — the whole command is rendered, wrapped to the card width and bounded by the existing line budget (`TOOL_COMMAND_LINE_LIMIT = 6`, `crates/tui/src/tui/history/constants.rs:27`), with the detach hint kept on the last line so the affordance is never lost.

Why this shape is cheap and safe:

- It is pure presentation: the command is already in the transcript and in the job snapshot, so nothing new has to be captured.
- The default preserves the reason the current design exists — the row must advertise `Ctrl+B` → `/jobs` — so the change is strictly opt-in and reversible by config.
- `full` must wrap, not overflow, and must respect narrow card widths, the same bounded-line discipline the body already uses.
- If an enum is unwanted, the equivalent is a boolean `show_running_command` (default `false`) plus `running_shell_command_detail = "first_line" | "full"`.

## Use case

Long builds, test suites and installs in a multi-repository workspace: the operator glances at the screen and needs to know which command is running, in which of several concurrent lanes, without expanding a card or looking an id up in `/jobs`. It matters most for multi-line commands, where today even a non-running card shows only the first line — a `for` loop or heredoc is indistinguishable from its first statement.

## Alternatives considered

- `/jobs` — prints the full command with cwd, status, exit code and output tail, but it is a separate view while the question is asked *inside* the transcript.
- Expanding the tool card — the body does render the command (live: up to 6 wrapped lines; transcript: full), so this is the closest workaround today; it costs an interaction per glance, and in the default `compact` collapse mode the live cell shows nothing but the header anyway.
- Putting the command in the footer or status strip — crowded; it already carries mode, model, context and tokens.
- Unconditionally showing the command — rejected: it would remove the detach affordance from the one row that carries it.

## Impact

Every session with a long-running shell call, and every multi-line command in every session (the first-line truncation). The cost is one settings key and a rendering branch; with the default unchanged, the risk is confined to users who opt in.

## Additional context

- Live reproduction on 0.10.0 (dev) @ `384439634` with `show_tool_details = true`, `tool_collapse_mode = "compact"`, `calm_mode = true`: the cell read `run running (81s) · Ctrl+B → /jobs` while the command ran.
- Relevant code: `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1006-1011` (`is_foreground_shell_wait`), `:1031-1039` (header choice), `:1140` and `:2160-2176` (body command rendering), `:2187-2195` (`command_header_summary`); `crates/tui/src/tui/history/constants.rs:27` (`TOOL_COMMAND_LINE_LIMIT`) and `:112` (`FOREGROUND_SHELL_WAIT_HINT`); `crates/tui/src/tui/app/types.rs:140-151` (`ToolCollapseMode`).
- `/jobs` output shape: `crates/tui/src/tui/shell_job_routing.rs:21-56`.

## Environment

- OS: Arch Linux
- codewhale: 0.10.0 (dev), built from `Hmbown/CodeWhale@384439634`
- Settings: `show_tool_details = true`, `tool_collapse_mode = "compact"`, `calm_mode = true`, `show_thinking = true`
- Shell/terminal: bash tool shell, tmux

issues.body:
> Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Cursor/sequence commits before the side effect, missing generation/session fencing, and check-then-use (TOCTOU) windows let stale events, restarted sequences, or concurrent writers clobber newer state. An event from an old turn, a restarted generator, or a second process is applied without a session/turn generation check, and a cursor is sometimes advanced before the effect it describes. The result is newer state silently overwritten by an older event, or a duplicated effect from a re-run sequence. Fence mutations by generation, commit cursors after the side effect, and close TOCTOU windows with atomic create/open.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **22** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Fence mutations by session/turn generation; commit cursors/checkpoints after the side effect; close TOCTOU with atomic create/open.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

## Key files
- `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs`
- `crates/core/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/src/backends/harmonyos.mjs`
- `crates/tui/src/mcp/oauth.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_setup.rs`
- `crates/state/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/delivery.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/compaction.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/mod.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/live.rs`
- `crates/config/src/lib.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every listed candidate is either fixed with a test, or downgraded with a written reason in the PR.
- [ ] No new instance of this class is introduced (guarded by the test/budget).
- [ ] Existing behavior for unrelated paths is unchanged.

## Verification
```sh
cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-core -p codewhale-state -p codewhale-config
cargo test  -p codewhale-tui --lib
cargo test  -p codewhale-state -p codewhale-config
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
( cd pet && npm run check )
( cd web && npm run check )
```

## Out of scope
- Findings that belong to another systemic class or to the localized backlog.
- Re-architecture beyond the listed sites.

## Related existing work (do not duplicate)
#6184 (engine freeze mid-run), #6207 (session picker), #6224, #5151, #5929, #5735

## Candidate findings (22)
- [ ] **CU01-10** · CU01 — Computer-use · `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/src/backends/harmonyos.mjs:107` — stale element index after tree reorder clicks a different control.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **T06-08** · T06 — Remote control, MCP, OAuth, cloud dispatch · `crates/tui/src/mcp/oauth.rs:829` — rejected refresh can delete a newer concurrent login due to a load→delete race.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **U09-03** · U09 — Dashboards, Fleet/settings/status/help · `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_setup.rs:1227` — late async draft without request generation is applied to changed wizard state.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **R03-07** · R03 — Agent, app-server, models, protocol, state, shared tools · `crates/state/src/lib.rs:368` — two-process fresh DB migrations race after pre-transaction schema checks.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **C02-08** · C02 — TUI engine and turn loop · `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:2253` — session replacement does not cancel in-flight MCP boot; generation/in-flight stay stale.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **D02-11** · D02 — `agent`/subagent runtime · `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/delivery.rs:297` — checkpoint >1000 paths switches to `git add -A`, capturing foreign edits.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **T03-07** · T03 — Models, providers, routing, pricing · `crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs:230` — cache fingerprint is not checked, a future timestamp becomes age=0 and suppresses refresh.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **T07-05** · T07 — Sessions, context, compaction, prompts, memory · `crates/tui/src/compaction.rs:324` — legacy restore deletes a user message merely containing a checkpoint marker.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **U02-07** · U02 — Event loop, dispatch/apply · `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:2503` — TurnComplete without session/turn generation can close a new turn.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **U02-09** · U02 — Event loop, dispatch/apply · `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:123` — shutdown after local cancel considers the session settled before the authoritative terminal event.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_

- [ ] **R05-05** · R05 — Core, memory, telemetry client/ingest · `crates/core/src/lib.rs:584` — thread/message/checkpoint mutations are not atomic; partial history possible.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **D03-m3** · D03 — Git/GitHub/review/web tools · `crates/tui/src/tools/finance.rs:68` — `f64` without finite/decimal policy, stale market time, and doubled full timeout.  
  _audit severity: medium; reassessed: medium_

> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Timed-out or dropped children are not killed or reaped (`kill_on_drop`/process-group), descendants survive shutdown, and a restart can overlap a surviving worker. A dropped future, an early error return, or a stop request can leave the child and its grandchildren running; the replacement then races the survivor over the same state. ## Goal / Why
Fan-out/cardinality, task counts, login attempts, ingest rate, and request-body limits are not bounded or are keyed on attacker-controlled values. Limits keyed on a caller-supplied value (random IDs, request headers, chunked bodies) can be bypassed entirely, letting a malicious or buggy client exhaust memory/CPU, flood the public ingest, or lock the sole maintainer out of the admin surface. The fix is global quotas keyed on trustworthy identity and hard caps independent of caller-supplied length. Every site below either lacks a cap or trusts a value the caller controls.

> Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Errors are swallowed or logged at debug while execution proceeds, defaults turn malformed or absent input into success, and review/verifier/goal gates can report a clean PASS on a malformed result. Fail-open defaults and swallowed errors let a broken or unparseable result look like success, so a human, a gate, or an automated review proceeds on a false signal. In the worst case a safety, verification, or goal gate reports PASS without having actually passed. Fail closed: propagate the error, record a durable failure, and never classify an unparseable gate result as success.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **25** (reassessed severity noted per line).

issues.body:
<!-- cw-release-routing-current -->
## Release routing - November 5, 2026

Target: **v0.10.4** (planned, undated).

The remaining evidence concerns native FreeBSD approval-wait/background CPU, distinct from the retained macOS/Linux fixes.

This is the approved November 5 release-scope decision. Earlier 0.10.3 acceptance entries below are retained as historical implementation/evidence records, not the current release assignment. Unfinished criteria remain open; this move does not claim resolution or waive a confirmed release-critical defect.
<!-- /cw-release-routing-current -->

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**scoped CPU improvements; reported platform open.**

Verified: Existing macOS release wake/CPU repair and three-version Ubuntu idle measurements are retained; orphaned companion stops periodic work after leases expire.

Remaining: No FreeBSD15 reported approval-wait/background-workload measurement on current release bytes. Ubuntu idle is a different surface.

Next action: Measure native FreeBSD release idle, approval wait and background-job CPU/wakeups with the reported workload; reuse unchanged macOS/Ubuntu receipts.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

**Platform**: FreeBSD 15.0 (x86-64)
**Binaries analyzed**:

* `cw00912` — Codewhale v0.9.12 (82 MB ELF, dynamically linked)
* `cw00913` — Codewhale v0.9.13 (89 MB ELF, dynamically linked)
* `cw01000` — Codewhale v0.10.0 (90 MB ELF, dynamically linked)

All three binaries are Rust executables (ELF 64-bit LSB pie, compiled for FreeBSD).

## Observed Behavior

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200,200 -->
| Version | Idle CPU (top) | Threads | event_loop.rs size |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| v0.9.12 | \~1% (uwait) | 17 | \~4264 lines |
| v0.9.13 | \~5-8% | \~25-30 | \~7323 lines |
| v0.10.0 | \~8-15% | \~30+ | \~7323 + dispatch |

`uwait` state = waiting on user event (interrupt-driven). Later versions show active polling.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Between v0.9.12 and v0.9.13 (+7 MB, major CPU increase)

The event loop grew from \~4264 to \~7323 lines (+70%). Multiple **background polling workers** were added:

1. **@-mention discovery worker** (`crates/tui/src/tui/mention_completion.rs`)
   * Background thread `codewhale-mention-discovery` that continuously scans the workspace for @-mention candidates
   * Polls filesystem even when user is idle
2. **LSP (Language Server Protocol) integration**
   * New modules: `crates/tui/src/lsp/mod.rs`, `lsp/client.rs`, `core/engine/lsp_hooks.rs`, `tools/lsp.rs`
   * Spawns `lsp-writer`, `lsp-reader`, `lsp-dispatcher` threads
   * Supports rust-analyzer, gopls, typescript-language-server, clangd, etc.
   * Background language analysis runs continuously, even with no files open
3. **Runtime event tap / store monitoring**
   * `runtime event tap lagged; a store-failure notice may have been missed`
   * Polls runtime store state periodically
4. **Thread goal stall monitoring**
   * `failed to initialize durable goal stall schema`
   * Tracks `stalled_ms`, `pause_reason`, `repeated_gap_count`, `last_gap_fingerprint`
   * Continuously checks if threads are stalled
5. **Engine tick & telemetry bucket aggregation**
   * `engineTick` increments every iteration, bucket aggregation every 12 ticks
   * Telemetry events with timestamps, agent IDs, tool tracking
6. **Session persistence polling**
   * Polls `session_index.jsonl` for job status changes
   * Periodic SQLite queries for thread status (`SELECT id, rollout_path, preview...`)
7. **File frecency tracking** (`crates/tui/src/tui/file_frecency.rs`)
   * Background tracking of file access frequency
8. **[Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>) live fetch** (`crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs`)
   * Periodic HTTP fetch of model catalog

### Between v0.9.13 and v0.10.0 (+1 MB, additional CPU)

1. **Fleet manager** (`crates/tui/src/fleet/manager.rs:1338`)
   * Fleet worker coordination with active polling
   * `Fleet worker coordination is not currently admissible`
2. **Background hooks**
   * `background hooks cannot deny tool calls because they exit immediately with no result`
   * Hooks run for every tool call/event
3. **Dispatch completion mailbox**
   * `dispatch completion mailbox is unavailable/full/closed`
   * Polls mailbox for dispatch results
4. **VM thread management**
   * `VM thread exited without reporting a result`
   * `VM admission gate closed`
5. **Agent profile permissions** (`AgentProfilePermissionsToml`)

## Architectural Shift

**v0.9.12** uses an **interrupt-driven** event loop: it sleeps on `kevent`/`kqueue` and wakes only on user input. The TUI event loop had \~4264 lines.

**v0.9.13+** switches to a **polling-driven** architecture: background workers wake periodically regardless of user activity. The event loop grew to \~7323 lines with runtime tap lag detection, persistence health checks, and session validation — all running on every iteration.

## Impact

* Significant battery drain on laptops
* Unnecessary CPU contention on shared/small VPS
* Background LSP scanning may be redundant with external editor LSP

2026-10-08 Codex continuation: [owner.rs](<http://owner.rs>) now stops world advancement and periodic saves after viewer/producer/audio leases expire, with authenticated /v1/frame wake messages on its existing bounded queue and a frame-deadline wait replacing 2 ms polling. Existing archives and active producer/audio semantics are retained. Exact checkout: engine-0102, local 80e1d2a9be plus owned changes. Focused native validation is starting at one build job and lower CPU priority. This addresses an orphaned-companion cause seen on macOS; it does not yet establish the reported FreeBSD idle/focus behavior or installed acceptance. No new tests or code comments, no new branch.

```sh
cargo check -p codewhale-tui
```

issues.title: Deferred-toolbox eviction is economically net-negative under provider prompt caching: full-prefix re-prefill + write premiums, permanent stale recovery notes, wire-byte-blind budget

milestone.title: v0.10.4
milestone.description:
Planned follow-up: reliability hardening, replay/archive retention, cache-economics evidence, native CPU/IME investigation and bounded dead-code cleanup.

Undated planning target approved November 5, 2026, not a published release or a completion claim. Revalidate historical audit candidates against current source before implementing. Any confirmed defect that blocks the agreed 0.10.3 release must be promoted back immediately; this milestone is not a security or data-integrity waiver. Preserve recovery before applying retention limits, and obtain approval for paid-provider experiments.

issues.body:
<!-- cw-release-routing-current -->
## Release routing - November 5, 2026

Target: **v0.10.4** (planned, undated).

Schedule eviction/re-admission economic qualification after the landed wire controls. Paid-provider runs still require separate approval.

This is the approved November 5 release-scope decision. Earlier 0.10.3 acceptance entries below are retained as historical implementation/evidence records, not the current release assignment. Unfinished criteria remain open; this move does not claim resolution or waive a confirmed release-critical defect.
<!-- /cw-release-routing-current -->

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**wire controls landed; economic acceptance open.**

Verified: Wire-budget/supersession repair9633c9fafa is landed.13actual DeepSeek request captures retained stable provider headers.

Remaining: Captured runs contained no eviction, so they cannot establish eviction/re-admission cost or net savings.

Next action: Perform matched eviction/re-admission intervention and reconcile authoritative provider usage/cost per call; retain unknown price/cache fields as unknown. New provider spending requires applicable approval.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

### What happened? 发生了什么？

The bounded deferred-tool toolbox (`ToolActivationCache`, 8 names / 16 KiB, `crates/tui/src/core/session.rs:17-19` at HEAD `008d21d69`) is **cost-blind**, and under current provider prompt-cache pricing its eviction path is economically net-negative. Concretely:

**1. Eviction invalidates the entire downstream prefix — the one toolbox operation with no offsetting benefit.**
The prefix fingerprint is `SHA256(system) + SHA256(tools wire array)` with order load-bearing (`crates/tui/src/prefix_cache.rs`), and tools sit at the front of the rendered prompt on every provider. Any admission/eviction mutates the tools array, so system + tools + the **entire conversation history** re-prefills at miss price. `docs/CACHE.md` calls this "an expected, one-request miss" (lines 39-40) — wording written when cache writes were free:

| Provider/API | Cached-input read | Write premium | Tool-change invalidation |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OpenAI Chat/Responses | 0.1x | 1.25x (GPT-5.6+) | prefix from that point (tools are first) |
| Anthropic Messages | 0.1x | 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h) | **any tool change invalidates the entire cache** (tools are block 1) |
| DeepSeek | 1/30 – 1/50 | none | prefix-based |
| Moonshot Kimi k3 | 0.1x | 1x (5m) / 2x (1h) | prefix from that point |

Break-even for evicting one \~400-token schema from a session with H tokens of history: pay ≈ 0.9–2.25 × H once, save ≈ 0.9 × 400 per later request → needs \~75 further tool-free requests at H = 30K. Real conversations run 6–40 requests. Admission at least unlocks a needed capability; **eviction only pays when the session is about to end anyway**. LRU position alone is the eviction trigger today — no hysteresis, no cost term, and two alternating overflowing searches would re-prefill the full prefix every round.

**2. The eviction→recovery cycle multiplies the loss (relevant to the in-flight reporting work).**
Reporting evictions (as the Pinvou fork's open PR [#101](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/101>) does) is necessary for correctness — silent eviction caused a live incident where a model fabricated tool results for tools that had vanished from its `<functions>`. But the recovery contract ("re-search to re-activate") completes a cycle whose full cost stack, for one eviction of 4 browser tools (\~460 tokens of schema) in a 30K-token history with 20 requests remaining (0.1x reads, 1.25x writes):

| \# | Cost item | Tok-eq |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Eviction invalidation (re-prefill + write premium) | \~34,500 |
| 2 | Eviction note in history (≈72–147 tokens/event; rides the result forever; 1 + 19×0.1x) | \~427 |
| 3 | Recovery re-search round trip | \~3,050 |
| 4 | Search-result payload becomes history | \~1,160 |
| 5 | Re-activation invalidation (tools array changes again — second re-prefill + write) | \~34,500 |
|  | **Total vs never evicting** | **≈ 73,600 (\~2.5× the entire history)** |

Two structural gaps in the reporting design: (a) **notes are never retracted** — ride-time netting (`render_toolbox_eviction_notes`) only trims the note at the moment it attaches to a result; once in history it is permanent, and the only "compaction" that removes it is generic conversation compaction; (b) **re-activation carries no supersession marker** — the re-admitting search result is byte-identical to a first-time hit (`tool_references` list only), so after recovery the model's history permanently contains "these tools are no longer callable" next to a tools array that has them again. (Compare: the direct-call hydration path does emit an explicit "was deferred and has now been loaded" receipt.)

**3. The headline saving is first-turn-only, and the budget does not measure wire bytes.**
The historical justification ("reduce catalog tokens 73%") measures a first-request, native-tools-only, `bytes/4`-estimated ratio — no provider, no tokenizer, no MCP, caching never modeled. Under caching, both an eager stable header and the deferred header are hit-priced after request 1; the durable steady-state saving is \~0.1x-scale. Separately, the 16 KiB toolbox budget is measured in engine-side serde bytes (`ToolActivationCache::serialized_bytes`), while the same tool serializes differently per wire family (Chat Completions wrapper \~69 B/tool, Anthropic \~40 B, Responses \~71 B) and per-provider sanitizers (Moonshot MFJS, root-level `oneOf/anyOf` flattening) change schemas further — so the budget is a proxy that matches no provider's actual token accounting.

**4. In practice the mechanism survives by accident.**
Across five real sessions on k3/DeepSeek (93–94% hit ratios with heavy `tool_search` churn vs 92.5% baseline without), activation happened at request 1 (short history) and the surface then stayed stable within turns. The measured re-prefill drivers were skill loading and engine restarts — not tool_search. The one live failure (mid-task silent eviction) is exactly the case with no offsetting saving.

### Expected 期望

Surface-change decisions — especially LRU eviction — should be cost-aware or at least cost-attributed, and the eviction-recovery loop should not leave permanent stale statements in history:

1. **Hysteresis / eviction economics**: a minimum activation lifetime, or an eviction cost term once current re-prefill size exceeds a few multiples of the evicted schema. Pure LRU position makes mid-task eviction the default worst case.
2. **Update** `docs/CACHE.md`'s "expected, one-request miss" for the write-premium era, and reconcile observed `cache_hit_tokens`/`cache_miss_tokens` against declared `change:<what>` re-pins — today telemetry and decisions never meet (`calculate_cache_savings` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only).
3. **Supersession semantics for recovery**: when a reported-evicted tool is re-activated, emit an explicit restored/re-admitted marker (hydration-receipt style) so the history's "no longer callable" note is not left as the last word; consider bounding note persistence (e.g. drop after the next successful activation of the named tools, or fold into compaction).
4. **Evaluate append-in-context injection** for dynamic tools (Moonshot's documented pattern: keep the top-level `tools` array stable, append dynamic declarations as a trailing system message inside `messages`) — zero prefix invalidation by construction, which sidesteps items 1 and 5 of the cost stack entirely.
5. **Measure the toolbox budget in wire-shaped bytes** (or tokenizer tokens) per active wire format rather than engine serde bytes.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Economic issue rather than a crash; the observable sequence:

1. Start a conversation that activates ≥8 deferred tools (e.g. a browser task: `tool_search` for browser tools, then a second search for page-management tools).
2. Observe the second search silently evicting earlier activations from the request tools array (no model-visible signal at HEAD `008d21d69` — `delta.evicted` is consumed by `remove_evicted_cache_activations` in `execute_tool_search_inner`, `tool_catalog.rs:1546-1551`).
3. Watch `/cache stats` + provider usage: the next request reports a miss covering the full history; on Anthropic routes the write premium applies; re-searching to recover triggers a second full miss + write.
4. Cross-check the arithmetic against `calculate_turn_cost_from_usage_with_prision`-billed totals for the session.

### Codewhale version 版本

`008d21d69` (workspace 0.10.2; latest tag v0.10.1) — verified at this HEAD on 2026-10-13; the mechanism is unchanged from v0.9.12 through HEAD. Observed live via the Pinvou downstream (fork pinned at v0.9.12 + maintenance), engine-level, platform-independent.

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

Engine — affects all surfaces (TUI / CLI / Desktop / Web) and all providers with prefix caching, which in 2026 is all of them.

### Before you start 前置确认

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。（recent 100 issues swept for tool/cache/deferred/eviction — no overlap）

Verified prepared-schema hashes, prefix observations and provider-reported cache usage for 13 previously captured real DeepSeek requests. The five source-default requests kept one 6,768-byte tool header, and the eight host-eager requests kept one 12,352-byte header. All observed prefix checks were stable. These receipts contain no eviction intervention, so they cannot establish eviction costs or a net saving. Source 9633c9fafa already measures provider-wire admission and supersedes stale eviction notices. Evidence: toolbox-6969-recorded-wire.json in the October 31 continuation artifacts.

issues.body:
<!-- cw-release-routing-current -->
## Release routing - November 5, 2026

Target: **v0.10.4** (planned, undated).

Finish replay-index bounds and living-session archive retention as a coherent accounting/recovery follow-up. This does not authorize deleting retained history.

This is the approved November 5 release-scope decision. Earlier 0.10.3 acceptance entries below are retained as historical implementation/evidence records, not the current release assignment. Unfinished criteria remain open; this move does not claim resolution or waive a confirmed release-critical defect.
<!-- /cw-release-routing-current -->

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

Partial source work is landed; both named remaining mechanisms are still open.

This is a criterion-by-criterion source reconciliation against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). “Source complete” credits the owning implementation; it does not claim an unrun native, provider, deployment or final-distribution check. The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

- **landed-journal — source complete:** SessionManager archives off-branch entries durably before pruning; body sharing is Arc-based; failure retains full journal. Existing deletion removes archive only together with its session. Carrying source: [d9ccf8f3e4](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/d9ccf8f3e4017aba8e9595a706b50961b78277bb), [e20aaedf19](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/e20aaedf199afd0b8166cd09c2d2825c5eeb62f4), [1e66ad3837](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/1e66ad3837c81afe879c3d69c7a966d331c7c8ec).
- **replay-index — implementation missing:** SessionCostSnapshot.usage_source_fingerprints remains a BTreeSet; restore collects the full supplied set into seen_usage_source_fingerprints. No safe ordered expiry/tombstone reconciliation bound is present.
- **archive-retention — policy and implementation missing:** append_journal_archive appends fsynced JSONL. remove_journal_archive is tied to deleting the session; there is no age/size/explicit retention policy for a living session.
- **current-performance — evidence missing:** Old synthetic clone measurements and the reporter six-day RSS sample are historical. This audit does not establish current long-session latency/RSS.

**Next action:** Resolve current admission/owner without changing the canceled packet, then finish ordered replay accounting and archive retention together with their actual recovery checks.

The former Linear packet CW-7034 stays Canceled. The October 31 founder instruction replans Engine work against App Server v2; cancellation is neither proof of implementation nor an implicit removal of this public requirement. Current release routing must be recorded in the Core plan. No canceled packet was reopened.

Whole issue remains open. 0.10.3 is unpublished; earlier dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Current remaining work — verified 2026-10-29

This issue remains open for **usage replay identifiers and retained journal archive growth**. The original0.10.1-dev report below is historical; its claims that no pruning exists and resume always reads twice no longer describe canonical Engine main2231d73df5d6d4538653a54920695a389d575451.

Already implemented:
* Off-branch journal entries are durably archived before pruning, normally at4096dead/1024retained; oversized documents archive all off-branch entries. Failed archive writes prune nothing. Active branches and recoverable ancestor chains remain intact, and live memory consumes the archived-ID result.
* Ended, non-durable, unpinned Work Graph operations are pruned to256 by the live registration path, as well as by oversized-session projection. This is not merely a serialization bound.
* Session entry bodies are shared through Arc, so the UI snapshot no longer deep-copies every body. Snapshot assembly still occurs on the UI task; no new latency/RSS benchmark is claimed here.
* Metadata reads grow geometrically from64KiB to16MiB before a full-file fallback. Fingerprints no longer force a whole transcript read as soon as metadata exceeds64KiB.
* Normal attach/resume parses the saved document once. A newer crash checkpoint still requires reading and validating the document before replacement, preserving the unreadable-document guard. Stale checkpoint cleanup happens after successful attach.

Carrying commits verified as ancestors of current main: d9ccf8f3e4017aba8e9595a706b50961b78277bb; e20aaedf199afd0b8166cd09c2d2825c5eeb62f4; 1e66ad3837c81afe879c3d69c7a966d331c7c8ec. Current owners are runtime/session_tree.rs, TUI session_manager.rs, work_graph/runtime.rs/reducer.rs, tui/ui/frame.rs and persistence_actor.rs.

Remaining acceptance, in order:
1. Bound the in-memory/persisted usage replay index through the existing late-usage authority while preserving exact spend deduplication after restart and late delivery. Do not truncate the current unordered fingerprint set: forgetting a still-replayable identifier can double-count money. Read/migrate every producer and restore consumer together.
2. Define and implement the retained journal archive's storage/retention behavior through the existing archive owner. Preserve branch restoration and receipts; no silent deletion of historical branches or user files. A memory bound is not a disk-retention policy.
3. Reuse/extend existing archive-failure, failed-document-write, archived-branch restore, large-metadata and late-usage dedupe checks. Measure long-session save/attach cost on current source before making performance claims; the reporter's six-day Linux RSS record is historical evidence, not a new qualification result.

The read-only source audit is recorded under artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029. No source, live session or billing state was changed for this reconciliation. The separate lock-contention issue remains separate. This is unreleased source status, not a shipped0.10.3 claim.

## Original report —0.10.1-dev historical measurements

# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

Searched open and closed for: session journal grows, compaction memory,
memory grows in session, rebranch, metadata too large. Closest matches, and why
each is a different store or mechanism:

- **#4217** (`subagents.v1.json` grows unbounded) — same class of defect, but the
  sub-agent ledger rather than the session journal.
- **#5262** (session tree design) — introduced the append-only entry journal; that
  is the design issue, not a report that the journal is unbounded.
- **#5472** (TUI memory retention of Bash stdout/stderr) — shell-output
  retainers, a different structure with a different growth mechanism.

# What happened?

A long session grows without bound, and RSS grows with it. On one 6-day session:

- process: **872 MB RSS**, reaching **1694 MB** high-water since start
- session file: **98.7 MB**, of which **99.6% is dead weight**

(MB = 10⁶ bytes throughout; `kB` in the log excerpts below is KiB from
`/proc`.)

The active branch holds **181 entries**. The rest of the file is history that
nothing reads. A high dead share is expected of an append-only journal; the
problem is the absolute size, which keeps growing.

The transcript is the main grower. `SessionJournal.entries` is a plain `Vec`
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:131`) with **no trimming path at all** —
`grep -n "trim_front\|clear\|retain"` over that file returns zero matches for
`entries`; the only mutation is `self.entries.push(entry)` at `:168`.

Every compaction rewrites the active tail via `rebranch_active_messages_stamped`
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:343`), and the superseded versions stay
behind forever. Four samples of that session:

| sample | `entries` | active branch | dead share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 15:43 | 45 793 | 4 072 | 91.1% |
| 00:15 | 48 653 | 2 861 | 94.1% |
| 01:00 | 49 232 | 155 | 99.7% |
| 01:42 | **49 258** | **181** | **99.6%** |

Across the 9 h 59 m the samples span, the live branch shrank **22×**
(4 072 → 181, not monotonically — it rose from 155 to 181 in the last interval)
while the journal grew by 3 465 entries. Compaction is doing its job; it just
trades live history for retained history rather than releasing it.

## The same pattern in `WorkGraphSnapshot.nodes`

`crates/tui/src/work_graph/model.rs:889` — also a plain `Vec`. The neighbouring
fields are bounded: `history` is a `BoundedVec<_, HISTORY_CAP>` with cap 256
(`:891`, constant at `:34`) and `seen_keys` is capped at 1024 (`:897`).

That session's graph had **16 838** nodes at the first sample and **18 004** by
the last, **16 696** of them `operation` rows — one per shell call — each keeping the full command text in `title` and the output
reference in `binding.last_observation`. Removal happens only through
`proposal.removed_nodes` (`crates/tui/src/work_graph/reducer.rs:420`); there is no
age- or count-based eviction.

## The 64 KB metadata fast path is defeated

`load_session_metadata` (`crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3175`) deliberately
reads only a 64 KB prefix, carrying the comment *"One bounded metadata-prefix
read, not a transcript scan"* (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs:1172-1175`).

But `usage_source_fingerprints` lives inside `SessionMetadata.cost`
(`crates/tui/src/cost_status.rs:86`) and has no bound of its own. Each entry is a
64-character hex string plus JSON quoting, so 8 919 of them add roughly
0.59 MB to `metadata` — already past the 64 KB prefix, which is truncated
mid-object. `extract_top_level_metadata` then cannot find the object's end, and
the fallback at `session_manager.rs:3193-3195` reads the remainder of the file
and re-concatenates it. The 64 KB read becomes pure overhead on top of a full
~98.7 MB read.

This fires on two paths: `merge_persisted_lifecycle`
(`frame.rs:1176` → `session_manager.rs:3124`), and `list_session_records`
(`session_manager.rs:3062`), which calls it for every `.json` in `sessions/`
on each save.

## Each snapshot costs ~659 ms on the UI task

`build_session_snapshot` (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:82` →
`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs:1129`) deep-clones the whole journal at
`frame.rs:1147` (`app.session_journal.clone()`).

The comment at `crates/tui/src/tui/persistence_actor.rs:1-13` records that disk
I/O was moved off the event loop, but the snapshot construction was not — and the
comment at `event_loop.rs:3256` ("Offloaded to the persistence actor so the UI
stays responsive") sits above a block that still builds it inline.

Reproduced per operation against the same data:

| operation | size | cost |
|---|---|---:|
| journal deep clone | 48 964 entries (benchmark snapshot) | ~484 ms |
| graph deep clone | 18 004 nodes (last sample) | ~166 ms |
| `root_to_leaf` | HashMap over all entries | ~9 ms |

Each figure is a standalone replay of that one operation against the same
on-disk session, not an in-process measurement of the code path.

≈ **659 ms** in total. It runs on every `EngineEvent::SessionUpdated`, i.e. on every message added to
the session — once per assistant response and once per tool result.

## `resume` reads the whole session file, twice

`crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:2829-2830` reads the session file in full with
`fs::read_to_string` + `serde_json::from_str`, with no size limit and no prefix
fast path — unlike `load_session_metadata`. `resume` reaches it through
`attach_session` (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:917`), and
`promote_interrupted_checkpoint` (`session_manager.rs:2929`) calls it a second
time via `load_session`, which is the same `recover_session_for_resume`
(`:3003-3005`). A resumed 100 MB session therefore reads the file at least twice
before the first frame.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session in a project and work for several hours (the measured run was
   ~6 days with regular tool use and several compactions). Reopening it later
   with `codewhale resume` takes noticeably longer as the journal grows.
2. Watch the file and the process:
   ```
   watch -n 60 'ls -l ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json; ps -o rss= -p $(pgrep -n codewhale)'
   ```
3. Compare the journal's active branch against its total entries:
   ```python
   import json, os
   d = json.load(open(os.path.expanduser("~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json")))
   e = d["journal"]["entries"]; by_id = {x["id"]: x for x in e}
   on, cur = set(), d["journal"]["leaf_id"]
   while cur in by_id: on.add(cur); cur = by_id[cur].get("parent_id")
   print(len(e), len(on), f"{(len(e)-len(on))/len(e):.1%} dead")
   ```
4. Observed end state matches the figures quoted above and the log section
   below.

To see the metadata-prefix effect (finding 3) rather than just the file size,
check where the `metadata` object ends in the serialized document:

```python
import json, os
raw = open(os.path.expanduser("~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json"), "rb").read(2_000_000)
end = raw.find(b'"messages"')
print("metadata block ends at byte", end,
      "-> prefix path works" if end <= 64*1024 else "-> falls back to full read")
```

At 8 919 fingerprints this prints an offset above 65 536, which is what forces
`load_session_metadata` off its fast path. To see the UI cost (finding 4), run a
turn that uses several tools and watch for input latency while a session with a
large journal is open.

# Codewhale version 版本

`0.10.1 (dev)`, source build from git.

# Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

# Operating system 操作系统

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model 提供商和模型

Not observed to be provider-specific.

# Terminal and shell 终端

any

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not captured.

# Logs

```
on active branch : 181 entries
journal entries  : 49 258
dead share       : 99.6%
session file     : 98.7 MB
process RSS      : 872 MB
VmHWM            : 1694 MB (peak since process start)
```

`VmHWM` is the peak since launch and never decreases; RSS returns to its
baseline between writes, so the current figure is well below it.

RSS tracks checkpoint writes rather than idle time. Selected rows from a 3 s
sampling of `/proc/<pid>/status`, aligned with the checkpoint's mtime
(`kB` = KiB):

```
23:59:56  rss= 887104 kB   mtime=23:59:13
23:59:59  rss= 981216 kB   mtime=23:59:57   <- +94 MB at the checkpoint write
00:00:05  rss= 882012 kB   mtime=23:59:57   <- back to baseline
00:00:44  rss= 981736 kB   mtime=00:00:42   <- +99.7 MB, repeats, ~45 s apart
```

The amplitude matches the per-snapshot cost above: the transient copies exist only
while the write is in flight.

A quieter leak appears in the same logs: `work-graph registration skipped;
running without a bound operation` occurs **1 351 times** over ~25 h, always with
`error=To-do state is busy` — `retry_lock`
(`crates/tui/src/work_graph/runtime.rs:1462-1473`, loop at `:1466`,
`yield_now` at `:1470`), called with `retries = 100` from
`runtime.rs:134`, doing 100 `std::thread::yield_now()` per attempt and then
failing, so `ShellSpawnIntentGuard`
(`crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs:1191`) discards the registration. Reported
separately in #6435 (open).



# References

- #6435 — the `retry_lock` / To-do lock contention visible in the same logs
- #5262 — introduced the append-only entry journal reported on above
- #6193 — no runtime performance gate exists

<!-- cw-release-routing-current -->
## Release routing - November 5, 2026

Target: **v0.10.4** (planned, undated).

Schedule matched token-savings research after the corrective release; 0.10.3 must not advertise an unqualified savings claim.

This is the approved November 5 release-scope decision. Earlier 0.10.3 acceptance entries below are retained as historical implementation/evidence records, not the current release assignment. Unfinished criteria remain open; this move does not claim resolution or waive a confirmed release-critical defect.
<!-- /cw-release-routing-current -->

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**existing functionality measured; savings claim unqualified.**

Verified: Existing bounded read/execute_tools paths retrieved the same three independently seeded values. Controlled serial/composed comparison used4vs2 requests and52202vs22160 wire bytes. Ordinary local Ollama completed both allowed-tool arms in2 requests and never invoked execute_tools.

Remaining: Ordinary planning did not demonstrate a default savings improvement. Arms shared a cache and differed in declared tools; usage/latency cannot establish causation.

Next action: Reconcile the six requested principles to existing consumers and retain the negative ordinary result. Any benefit claim needs matched task/provider/cache intervention; do not build a duplicate reader merely to close the issue.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

### Before you start

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What problem does this solve? 要解决什么问题？

Significantly reduce context overhead

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

[https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx](<https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx>)

A significant reduction in token consumption through FastCtx, rather than through model compression or conversation summarization. The actual amount of token savings depends on how the Agent is used and the type of tasks.

Core principles:

**1. Batch reading:** Read multiple files or code ranges in a single call, reducing the number of tool invocations and repeated reads.
**2. Limit output length:** Set output budgets for file reading, searching, and command execution to avoid irrelevant content consuming context.
**3. Reduce redundant operations:** Simplify command execution through structured tools, minimizing syntax errors, failed retries, and redundant work.
**4. Optimize truncation handling:** Clearly indicate omitted content and allow on-demand log retrieval, avoiding repeated execution of already completed commands.
**5. Simplify tool descriptions:** Shorten MCP tool descriptions to reduce token consumption from the tool definition itself.
**6. Background task execution:** Run time-consuming tasks such as building and testing in the background, and retrieve results only when needed, reducing repeated polling and output.

### Where? 在哪里？

*No response*

### Workarounds or other tools (optional)

*No response*

### Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this. 我愿意提交 PR。

Measured the public issue’s multi-range request using the existing read tool and execute_tools VM on Ubuntu ARM64 CLI a20bd7fb9b09. A scripted local provider requested lines 10–19 of three real files. Both approaches recovered the same three independently seeded values with the same read-only sandbox. Serial reads used four requests, 52,202 total request-body bytes and 4,455 final tool-content bytes. The composed read used two requests, 22,160 total bytes and 501 final tool-content bytes, with three nested calls. No new read tool was required. Model token/cache usage was unreported by the fixture. These are controlled wire measurements and do not qualify ordinary model planning. Evidence: linux-package/reads-6991-q4.json in the October 31 continuation artifacts.

November 1 local qualification. Using the installed Ollama qwen3:4b and the source-built Ubuntu CLI to check ordinary planning on the three-file natural-language request. The read-only sandbox, file bytes and prompt are fixed. The serial arm exposes read alone and the composition arm also exposes execute_tools. Capture the actual tools, independently compare the three returned values and record provider-reported input/output usage when available. No source or provider policy change in this run.

November 1 result. The actual Ubuntu ARM64 CLI binary `5996280091ef` returned all three seeded values in order on both ordinary runs. Installed Ollama qwen3:4b requested the three reads together on the first provider request and answered on the second, with or without the VM in its allowed tools. Read-only alone used 4,981 input, 3,431 output and 2,061 cached-input tokens across 23,225 request bytes. Offering execute_tools as well used 6,191 input, 2,437 output and 4,122 cached-input tokens across 29,317 bytes. The model never invoked execute_tools. The runs shared a cache and the read-only arm ran first. The controlled four-versus-two serial comparison does not establish an ordinary planning or latency improvement. Evidence is recorded in `linux-package/ordinary-reads-summary.json` in the October 31 Engine continuation artifacts.

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Corrective release and exact-candidate qualification. Release scope approved November 5, 2026.

Keep history/undo and compaction continuity, login/model selection, worker durability and safe retries, bounded input/output, runtime responsiveness, and supported installation/client qualification here. Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. Use status:awaiting-release for source fixes that are landed but still need final verification and shipment; do not close them merely because main contains the fix.

Broad refactors, optional features, full historical audit sweeps and unqualified optimization claims move to the later planning milestones. This replaces the previous all-refactors-for-0.10.3 umbrella scope; unfinished requirements are deferred, not completed or discarded. Confirmed release-critical defects must not be hidden by a future umbrella target.

Freeze the final source and binaries, finish the required platform/client evidence, then run final validation. Provider spend, signing and publication retain their separate approvals. No due date or published release is created by this milestone.

<!-- cw-0103-status-20261025 -->
## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

## Goal / Why
Filesystem, subprocess, git, secret-store, and tempfile work is executed synchronously inside `async` call chains (engine tasks, tool handlers, UI event loop, runtime API). Repository convention #6149 requires `tokio::fs`/`tokio::process` or `spawn_blocking`, and `scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py` ratchets the unprotected-site count precisely to stop this class from creeping back. Each site below must move to async IO, `spawn_blocking`, or a dedicated thread without raising that budget.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **9** (reassessed severity noted per line).

1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Move each listed site to `tokio` async IO, `spawn_blocking`, or a dedicated thread; do not raise the blocking-calls budget.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**stall guards implemented; original long-run incident open.**

Verified: Phase watchdog/timeouts/durable diagnostics and queued-message recovery are landed. A controlled reasoning stall produced a visible record in2.303s and preserved queued follow-up. Settlement uses event_sent instead of claiming user-visible delivery.

Remaining: Original hours-long ZAI/tool-heavy silent freeze was never reproduced; scoped fixture does not prove that incident resolved.

Next action: Capture the original-condition phase/request/thread trace and queued-message outcome on an authorized real-provider long task, or an independent reproducible counterexample.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Body

```markdown
### Environment

- codewhale 0.9.13 (Rust TUI), linux x86_64
- provider: zai, model: GLM-5.3-Flash
- posture: Ask / workspace-write

### Summary

During long, tool-heavy runs the engine stops producing model output mid-turn.
Everything the user types afterwards is persisted into the session journal but
never answered. The stall is completely silent: no ERROR/WARN in the TUI log,
no crash entry, the spinner just keeps absorbing input.

This happened twice in two independent sessions on consecutive days.

### Steps to reproduce (observed, not deterministic)

1. Run an interactive session with a long skill-driven task that issues many
   bash tool calls (session A), or a multi-turn task with tool approval
   round-trips (session B).
2. Mid-run, the model stops emitting output (session B stalled right after an
   assistant thinking block, before any text/tool output).
3. Send follow-up user messages. They are accepted and persisted.
4. No reply ever arrives; force-quit is the only way out.

### Observed evidence (timestamps UTC)

Session A `a69916b2…` (2026-09-14):

- TUI log `tui-2026-09-14-2784622.log` ends at `10:51:38` with
  `engine.turn completion settled status=Completed delivered=true`.
- The session demonstrably continued for hours after that line and stalled
  later. The entire stall window produced **zero** additional log lines —
  the freeze is invisible to the log.
- Journal tail contains three consecutive `user` entries with no assistant
  response after them (a Chinese follow-up question, `"hello?"`, and a
  `/feedback bug` draft request).
- On-disk session JSON is structurally intact: 95 journal entries, valid
  `leaf_id` pointing at an existing entry, undamaged parent chain.

Session B `53b16822…` (2026-09-15):

- Assistant emitted a thinking block, then stalled before any text or tool
  output. A later `"继续"` (continue) user message also got no response.
- On force-quit, the TUI logged **two** pending turns at the same moment:

  ```
  2026-09-15T03:27:48.318072Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted delivered=true
  2026-09-15T03:27:48.548725Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted delivered=true
  ```

  Note `delivered=true` even though the user received no model output for
  either turn — the flag does not mean the user saw anything.

- `~/.codewhale/crashes/` is empty in both cases.

### Expected

- A stalled provider stream should be subject to a read/response timeout and
  surface a visible error in the UI.
- Queued user messages during a stalled turn should be rejected or reported,
  not silently absorbed.
- `delivered=true` on an Interrupted turn should not be recorded when nothing
  was ever rendered to the user.

### Impact

Long tasks can absorb follow-up messages indefinitely with zero feedback. The
user cannot distinguish "still working" from "dead" and must force-quit, which
then triggers the separate resume bug (filed separately).

### Hypothesis (unconfirmed)

No network-layer logs are available, so the transport-side root cause is
unknown. Suspected: a zai streaming hang with no read timeout in the harness.
Regardless of the transport cause, the missing stall detection and the silent
absorption of user messages are harness-side gaps.

---
Sanitized log excerpts: see `attachment-issue-1-logs.en.md`.
```

## Goal / Why
Network responses, files, child pipes, and artifact reads are consumed with `.text()`/`read_to_string`/`read_to_end` (or a growing buffer) before any size bound. A single oversized response, artifact, or pipe can OOM the process or wedge a worker, and several paths buffer the whole body before they even consult the configured cap. The sources differ (HTTP, filesystem, child stdin/stdout, artifact store) but the failure mode is the same and the fix is one bounded reader. Apply a byte cap with a truncation note at ingest, not after materialising content.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **23** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Apply a bounded reader (byte cap + truncation note) at every listed site before materialising content; add a regression test per reader.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

milestone.description:
Corrective release and exact-candidate qualification. Release scope approved November 5, 2026.

Keep history/undo and compaction continuity, login/model selection, worker durability and safe retries, bounded input/output, runtime responsiveness, and supported installation/client qualification here. Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. Use status:awaiting-release for source fixes that are landed but still need final verification and shipment; do not close them merely because main contains the fix.

Broad refactors, optional features, full historical audit sweeps and unqualified optimization claims move to the later planning milestones. This replaces the previous all-refactors-for-0.10.3 umbrella scope; unfinished requirements are deferred, not completed or discarded. Confirmed release-critical defects must not be hidden by a future umbrella target.

Freeze the final source and binaries, finish the required platform/client evidence, then run final validation. Provider spend, signing and publication retain their separate approvals. No due date or published release is created by this milestone.

> Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Tool calls, MCP calls, HTTP turns, bridge messages, and forge actions are retried or replayed on ambiguous failure without an `operation_key`/CAS. When a request times out or the connection drops the operation may already have been applied, so the retry applies it a second time. Duplicate side effects range from noisy (a double comment) to costly (double billing, divergent remote state, a duplicate PR). The fix is an operation key (or compare-and-swap) on every side-effecting call on the retry path, so replay can detect an already-applied operation.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **20** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Introduce an operation key (or CAS) for every side-effecting call on the retry path; make replay detect an already-applied operation.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

> Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
State, session, ledger, goal, and job records are written with non-unique temp names, without fsync, or as multi-step commits. A crash, power loss, or a second writer can then leave a truncated file or a half-applied batch that later code reads as valid — losing claims, decisions, or session history, or reviving deleted records. The fix is one atomic durable-write contract per record set: unique temp name, fsync, rename, and batch/transaction semantics for multi-file commits. Non-atomic Windows replacement and mirror-write ordering belong to the same contract.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **8** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. One owner for atomic durable writes: unique temp file, fsync, rename, and batch/transaction semantics per record set.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

- `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/views/fleet_detail.rs`

- [ ] Every listed candidate is either fixed with a test, or downgraded with a written reason in the PR.
- [ ] No new instance of this class is introduced (guarded by the test/budget).
- [ ] Existing behavior for unrelated paths is unchanged.

```sh
cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-cli
```

# ACP regression in 0.10.1: `sandbox_mode` / `ask` from config ignored again — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

## Summary

The ACP posture bug from [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) (fixed in the 0.10.0 nightlies and verified in Paseo) is back in stable **0.10.1**: sessions launched via `codewhale serve --acp` ignore `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `ask = "never"` from `~/.codewhale/config.toml`, and run with the OS sandbox on, network off, and approval gates firing on every shell call.

## Environment

* codewhale **0.10.1** (build `fead51eeea0f`), macOS (Apple Silicon)
* Launched as an ACP provider for the Paseo app (verified: multiple `codewhale serve --acp` processes owned by Paseo)
* `~/.codewhale/config.toml`:

  ```toml
  approval_policy = "suggest"
  sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"
  ask = "never"
  ```

## Observed (live session, 2026-10-15)

* `CODEWHALE_SANDBOX=seatbelt` is set in the session environment → the OS sandbox is applied despite `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.
* `python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind("/tmp/x.sock")'` → `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` — the exact [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) signature; this breaks Node test runners and Playwright webServer.
* `ps` → `operation not permitted` (can't even list processes).
* Network is blocked: `curl -sI https://example.com` returns nothing (`000`).
* Every shell call still hits the typed-ask gate and requires a manual approval in the client UI, even though `ask = "never"`. (`gh` could not even read its own config at `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` — EPERM — until the shell was escalated.)
* The policy engine itself agrees these should be skipped: `codewhale sandbox check --ask never 'ls -la /tmp'` → `{"allow": true, "requires_approval": false}`. So the disconnect is between the policy engine and the posture actually applied to live ACP sessions.

## Difference vs the original [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) report

* Writes to `/tmp` now succeed (in 0.9.13 they were EPERM), but AF_UNIX socket creation is still blocked — the one thing Playwright/Node runners need.
* Approval prompts now reach the Paseo UI and can be approved manually (in 0.9.13 they were auto-denied). Still: `ask = "never"` should not gate at all.

## Suspected relation

[#6473](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6473>) (Full Access now requires per-session confirmation) combined with [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>)'s fix ("makes Full Access discoverable **without letting a client select it**") leaves the ACP path with no way to enter Full Access at all. `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` is effectively dead config for Paseo users, and every real workflow — network, sockets, process listing, CLI tools like `gh` — breaks. If per-session confirmation is the intended mechanism, the ACP client needs a way to request/confirm it. Until then this is a regression from the verified-working 0.10.0 nightly.

## Ask

1. Restore config-derived posture for ACP sessions when the client does not pin one, or
2. Expose a Full Access selection/confirmation path to ACP clients (Paseo), or
3. At minimum, honor `ask = "never"` so gated commands skip instead of prompting.

Happy to provide full transcripts or run a nightly/repro build. Greetings from Colombia 🇨🇴

Current 0.10.3 qualification is exercising the shipping ACP stdio entry, the reporter's exact approval settings, CLI opt-in forms, a stricter read-only floor, and local-only socket effects on macOS. No Paseo or Windows result is inferred. Source ownership remains in crates/tui/src/acp_server.rs, its runtime adapter, and the Engine's existing approval/sandbox authority.

Seven macOS source-candidate ACP stdio scenarios passed (binary codewhale-hq/codewhale-app#334 03fcb66028f5aefc7252f99c0357638deb39b008bb8cc421e2c0645299a71e27). The reported suggest/danger-full-access/ask-never config advertised Ask and rejected client-side escalation. A terminal-capable client saw one permission request, denied it and produced no effect. Explicit post-serve --full-access bound a Unix socket and reached a loopback HTTP server with no prompt. Global/post-serve --yolo, config yolo=true, a stricter Plan floor and rejection of approval_policy=never behaved as specified. Ports, provider responses, workspace and account state were local fixtures. Published macOS 0.10.2 independently passed the Ask vs Full Access socket comparison. Paseo and native Windows acceptance remain open.
