issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**continuity boundary qualified; canceled plan needs routing.**

Verified: Three actual translated-Linux CLI scenarios passed independent ordered raw-history/instruction/reasoning oracles: automatic compaction, provider overflow, summary refusal. Separate-process list/resume continuation passed in every scenario, without automatic calls. Nine owning source files matched entry main.

Remaining: This does not execute the user personalized save-session skill or prove summary quality. Original first emergency listing failed and remains recorded. CW-6990 was canceled for replanning; it must not be silently reopened.

Next action: Attach retained proof through the current release/Core plan and reconcile the personalized task acceptance; reuse the bounded transaction rather than adding another compaction authority.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

@Hmbown 
More of an FYI background information than a bug - but it does impact reliability and prompted an idea

I use a 'save session' command to a personalised context transfer as an adjunct to codewhale does.  The agent was cut off while executing that command and it was impacted.

Details follow - from the new agents view on the other side of an Emergency Compaction

It has also prompted a though that I will expand on later. Perhaps we can avoid (by design) the need for emergency context compaction.

In essence, the agent is most effective when the context buffer is nearly full - lots of relevant recent experience to call on.  /new destroys that and the agent only has its training to rely on. Emergency compact does much better by transferring context to the new agent.

But perhaps instead of codewhale directly doing the compaction (keep that for true emergencies) ...the agent could be given a tool to allow it to selectively prune its context..
. 
As long as the agent is given the state of the context buffer and the config parameters at each turn,  it could  then prune some of its older context by calling that tools if the parameters require it - but let the agent choose the scope of the context to prune

That should leave an agent with a ongoing mildly varying (almost full) context buffer and not suffer the  drastic interruption that /compact implies. Continuity rather than disruption





# Emergency compaction — the impact on the `save session` task

**Recorded:** 2026-09-29, by the session that resumed after the compaction.
**Subject:** the emergency context compaction that interrupted the `save session` command, and what it
cost the agent's ability to complete that task accurately.
**Evidence class:** every number and path below was measured with a tool after the compaction, from the
live filesystem and the runtime's own stores. Statements that come from the compaction's summary rather
than from a measurement are marked **[reported]**. Statements that could not be explained are marked
**[unresolved]** rather than given a cause.

---

## 1. What happened, in short

The user issued `save session`. That turn began, produced **3,908 characters of reasoning and nothing
else**, and was cut off by an emergency compaction before it called a single tool. The compaction took a
2.5 MB snapshot of the transcript, wrote an 8,608-byte relay summary, and handed that summary to a resumed
turn — the one that wrote this file.

The consequence for accuracy is not that facts were lost. It is that **the only continuity between the
two turns was a model-written summary of a transcript that no longer exists**. Everything inherited from
it had to be re-measured before it could be written down; and of the four claims that failed that
re-measurement, none was a small detail. What cost the agent its accuracy was not the gap in the
transcript but the confidence of the summary that filled it.

Cost, measured: roughly ten gathering calls across three full-state probes, plus the re-measurement that
the four failures forced. The delivered file is `workbench-development/context-transfer-2026-09-29-11:36:26.md`
(24,229 bytes, 339 lines), written between 11:36:26 and 11:36:55, about three minutes after the resume.

---

## 2. The event, as far as it is observable

No tool records the compaction itself. What follows is the trace it left, and the timestamps agree to
within half a minute.

- **Snapshot** — `~/.codewhale/sessions/cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9/artifacts/context-transfer-4cf0b914-6eba-41da-b993-987d1e769a4a.json`,
  2,540,963 bytes, written **11:33:08**.
- **Relay summary** — the `.md` beside it, 8,608 bytes, written **11:33:38**. Its first line is
  *"Another language model started to solve this problem and produced a summary of its thinking process…"*
  — and that is the text that appears in the resumed session's transcript as a user-role message.
- **Resumed turn** — its first tool call ran at **11:33:08**, its second at **11:33:41**. The compaction's
  two writes therefore straddle the resume: the resolver handover and the disk write overlap by seconds.
- **The interrupted turn** — one assistant message, index `msg[57]` in both stores, 3,908 characters of
  reasoning, **no tool calls**. Its closing lines are *"Let me gather facts first."*, then a blank line,
  then *"Let me run."* — so it died in the act of starting, not in the act of writing.
- **Nothing partial was left behind** — verified, not assumed: the project root's newest transfer before
  the resumed one is `context-transfer-2026-09-29-04:40:48.md` (14,845 bytes), and nothing in the project
  root has a modification time between 11:25 and 11:36 except the file the resumed turn wrote.

**This was not the session's first compaction.** The session `cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9` was
created **2026-08-30**, and its `artifacts/` directory holds **46** compaction relays dated from
2026-09-15 onward — including **two today** (04:47 and 11:33). The transfer files at the project root are
a separate, user-facing series written on request; the relays are the runtime's own. So the content of
the delivered transfer file inherits from a chain of summaries, even though the *file* has exactly one
compaction hop behind it.

---

## 3. What was lost, and what was not

**Lost:** the agent's side of the transcript for every turn before the compaction boundary. The live log
and the checkpoint both retain assistant reasoning only from `msg[57]` onward — the interrupted turn's
block and the resumed turn's segments. Everything the agent reasoned in the earlier turns of this session
was replaced by summary text.

**Not lost — the user's own words.** All **57** of this session's user turns survive verbatim in the
stores — `msg[0]` through `msg[56]`, every one of them. (The 58th user-role message is the compaction
relay itself, at `msg[59]`.) Every instruction, every correction — "No point
referencing line numbers", "try to avoid using invented shorthand", "Option B", "deploy this to a514" —
is checkable word for word. The asymmetry is exact and worth stating plainly: **the compaction destroyed
the agent's reasoning and preserved the user's instructions.**

**Recoverable, and where:** the interrupted turn's own 3,908 characters survive in both stores, and the
resumed turn's reasoning survives in the checkpoint. The fuller record is the checkpoint beside the log —
`~/.codewhale/sessions/checkpoints/cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9.json` (22.7 MB, rewritten as the
session turns) — which carries more messages and more reasoning segments than the live log at any moment:

- live log, first sampled early in the resumed turn: **61 messages, 1 assistant block, 3,908 chars**.
- live log, sampled at the end of the resumed turn: **118 messages, 30 assistant blocks**.
- checkpoint, sampled at the end of the resumed turn: **125 messages, 33 assistant blocks**.

So the stores do retain reasoning — progressively, and only from the last boundary. The live log simply
lags within a turn, which is what made the first sample look like an empty store.

---

## 4. Impacts on the ability to complete the task accurately

### 4.1 Continuity arrived as a summary, and the summary was the only record

The resumed turn began with no transcript of the interrupted turn — no tool results, no partial
deliverable, no working memory. The provenance chain for the file it produced is: **full transcript
(dropped) → relay summary → delivered transfer file.** Each hop is lossy, neither is checkable against
its source, and the second hop was written by an agent that had itself only the summary. The practical
effect: the deliverable could be made *true* only by re-measuring the world, never by trusting its input.

### 4.2 The reasoning behind every decision was unavailable — only its conclusion survived

The summary states outcomes: decision 3 is Option B; the composer is PHP; the headline figures are read
from each site's rendered report; the report links were dropped. It does not carry the argument for any of
them. For conclusions that rest on a chain — *why* the five headline figures cannot come from the data
file, for instance — the resumed turn could restate the conclusion with the summary's own one-line
justification and nothing more. It could not re-derive it, and could not tell whether the justification was
the real one. **Errors of fact were catchable; errors of reasoning were not.**

### 4.3 Four claims failed on contact with live state

All four were completion claims — the class of statement a summary compresses hardest and asserts most
confidently. Each was found by measuring, not by reading:

1. **"The `debian/changelog` quirk is now recorded in `docs/code-quirks.md`."** Measured false. That file's
   newest entries are dated **2026-09-27**; it contains **no** 2026-09-28 or 2026-09-29 entry at all — so
   neither the build quirk nor any of the four composer defects reached the quirks backlog, though the
   project rule requires the append in the turn each is found. The summary reported a diligence that had
   not happened. **[Reported, then refuted by measurement.]**
2. **The `.buildinfo.new`.** The summary and the user's own screenshot disagreed with each other; live
   state resolves neither: the file is absent from `~/Documents`, from `/tmp`, and from a full-depth search
   beneath `~/Documents`, and no command in the resumed turn removed it. **[Unresolved — recorded as
   observed.]**
3. **The reasoning-retention measurement.** The summary's figure — 599 messages, 225 thinking blocks,
   845,169 characters — matches **neither** store. Measured: the live log began the resumed turn with 61
   messages and one 3,908-character block, and the checkpoint with 109 messages and 25 blocks. **[Reported,
   then refuted.]**
4. **Where the `.deb` goes.** The summary's "published" implied the parent directory; the build script
   publishes it with `mv` to `workbench-linux/website/workbench-linux.sentuny.com/dl/`, where it verifies
   at 31,402,694 bytes dated 11:28. This one the resumed turn could settle by reading the code. **[Reported,
   then corrected.]**

Three of the four were caught only because the resumed turn re-measured the world rather than describing
it. Had it written the file first and verified afterwards, all four would have been written down as fact.

### 4.4 A measurement that could not be reconciled at all

The 599/225/845,169 figure cannot be reproduced from either store now, and no third store was found. The
resumed turn recorded the divergence as a divergence, inside the outstanding-questions section of the
delivered file, rather than choosing a number. That is the honest handling — but it leaves the record
with a figure that is known to be wrong and is not known to be replaced by a right one.

### 4.5 The boundary between the two turns was destroyed — including my ability to audit the loss

The resumed turn could not tell, from the stores alone, whose reasoning the one retained block was. It
reasoned about it, concluded it was the resumed turn's own (streamed live), and **wrote that conclusion
into the delivered transfer file** — where it is wrong. The block at `msg[57]` is the *interrupted* turn's;
its closing lines ("Let me gather facts first.", then "Let me run.") show it died before its first tool call.
The live log was simply lagging in persisting the resumed turn's own segments.

So the compaction did not merely remove information; it removed the *marker* by which the loss could be
measured. Reconstructing the boundary took several probes of two stores and their timestamps. One
reconstruction was committed to paper before it was checked, and it was false. This is the sharpest form
of the impact: **a summary that does not date itself makes its own errors unattributable.**

### 4.6 No partial artefact existed to inspect or salvage

A real hazard for a task whose deliverable *is* a file is a half-written file that reads as complete. It
did not materialise here: the interrupted turn made no tool calls, wrote nothing, and the project root's
previous transfer file is untouched at 04:40:48. The resumed turn verified that instead of assuming it.

### 4.7 The session's own subject was demonstrated by its own ending

The session opened with the user noticing that the previous turn's reasoning cannot be reviewed after the
fact, and it closed with the agent's reasoning being destroyed mid-task by the machinery that keeps the
context window. Both are the same mechanism seen from two sides. The delivered transfer file records the
first; this document records the second.

---

## 5. What the resumed turn had to re-establish before it could write anything

Every one of these was measured after the resume; none was inherited as fact.

- The three deployed files' **md5 sums against the box** — `acd494130580eba918449a48badd706d`
  (`/etc/draff.yaml`), `a0f074b5128f2d36d61ef142297ecbcc` (`/opt/draff/compose-daily-report.php`),
  `1a9333e314a47bfe2545fb628498b548` (`/opt/draff/run-daily.sh`) — all three matching the repos.
- The **cron line** (`35 1 * * * /opt/draff/run-daily.sh >> /var/log/draff.log 2>&1`) and the last line in
  `/var/log/draff.log` (04:25:34, the old `draff` job), which is what proves the composer has never run in
  production.
- **PHP 8.3.6** on the box.
- The **test suite, re-run live**: 14 passed, 0 failed; message 119,836 bytes; longest line 657 bytes;
  195 bar rows; 11 plain tables; three download detail blocks.
- **Seven repositories' branch and dirty state**, and the one commit since the previous transfer
  (`779354c`).
- The **plan document**: 882 lines, decision 3 settled as Option B, the nineteen categories listed, the
  Revisions section present.
- `~/Documents` **free of build artefacts at any depth**, and the `.deb` present in the website's `dl/`.
- The **session stores' own shape** — which is what turned a hidden risk into a recorded one.

**What could not be re-measured, and is therefore inherited in the delivered file:** that the four
composer defects were each "fixed and proved" (only their *consequences* were re-measured — the clean test
suite, the line-length distribution, the `-f` sender in the source, the Postfix log line); the user's own
in-conversation confirmation that the email "looks good"; the account of the earlier over-broad cleanup
that deleted three `/tmp` artefacts; and every statement about *why* a decision was taken. These are
written in the delivered file as they were reported, and they carry the summary's authority rather than a
measurement's.

---

## 6. Defects this event exposed in the delivered file

Both are corrections the resumed turn found *after* writing the transfer file. Neither has been applied —
an edit needs the user's word.

1. **A mis-attribution in the `### Session Log` section.** It says the live log's single retained
   `thinking` block is *"the current turn's reasoning, streamed as it is produced."* Measured after the
   fact, that block is `msg[57]`, the **interrupted** turn's reasoning — and the claim's second half is
   wrong too: the live log does retain assistant reasoning, from the compaction boundary onward, and now
   holds 30 such blocks.
2. **A pointer that understates the record.** The section directs a future reader to the live log, which
   at any moment is the *thinner* of the two stores. A fresh session following the delivered pointer would
   conclude that reasoning is barely retained and stop looking — the opposite of the truth. The checkpoint
   beside it, and the 46 relays in the session's `artifacts/` directory, are the fuller record.

---

## 7. Structural risks for future `save session` turns, and proposed mitigations

Recorded as proposals; none is implemented.

1. **A summary's completion claims are its least trustworthy content.** They are the most compressed and
   the most confidently asserted. A relay should mark each claim as *verified by tool* or *reported*, and
   the resumed turn must treat everything unmarked as a hypothesis to test. Here the four failures were
   all of this class.
2. **A summary must date and delimit itself.** Without a statement of which turns it covers and when it
   was taken, the boundary is unreconstructable and its own errors become unattributable (§4.5). The
   compaction's own artifacts do carry timestamps; the relay text does not.
3. **Write the deliverable early, then verify.** The interrupted turn gathered facts in no particular
   order and died with nothing on disk. Even a first-pass skeleton on disk would have made the resume
   cheap and the loss small. This is compatible with authoring the document in full — it changes the
   order, not the authorship.
4. **Layer the pointers.** A transfer file's research section should name the live log, the checkpoint and
   the compaction relays, and say which is fuller — otherwise the next session reads the thinnest one and
   believes it.
5. **Record the provenance depth in the file itself.** The delivered transfer file has one compaction hop
   behind it, but its content inherits a chain of 46 relays. A reader cannot tell the difference, and
   should be able to.
6. **State the boundary index.** `msg[57]` is where retained reasoning begins. One line in the research
   section would tell the next session exactly which turns' reasoning is gone and need not be hunted for.

---

## Appendix A — measurements cited

```
session id                 cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9
session created            2026-08-30
compaction relays in store 46, dated 2026-09-15 .. 2026-09-29 (two today: 04:47, 11:33)
snapshot (11:33 compaction)  artifacts/context-transfer-4cf0b914-….json  2,540,963 bytes  11:33:08
relay summary (same event)   artifacts/context-transfer-4cf0b914-….md       8,608 bytes  11:33:38
interrupted turn             msg[57], assistant, 3,908 chars of reasoning, no tool calls
resumed turn first tool call 11:33:08      second tool call 11:33:41
live log, early in resume    61 messages (60 user, 1 assistant), 1 thinking block (3,908)
live log, end of resume     118 messages (88 user, 30 assistant), 30 thinking blocks
checkpoint, end of resume   125 messages (92 user, 33 assistant), 33 thinking blocks
delivered transfer file      workbench-development/context-transfer-2026-09-29-11:36:26.md
                             24,229 bytes, 339 lines, written 11:36:26–11:36:55
previous transfer file       context-transfer-2026-09-29-04:40:48.md  14,845 bytes (untouched)
user turns retained         57 verbatim (msg[0] .. msg[56]); the 58th user-role message is the relay
```

## Appendix B — the interrupted turn's surviving reasoning

Recoverable in full from both stores at `msg[57]`. Opening, verbatim:

> The user says "save session". Per AGENTS.md, that means: generate a context-transfer file at the pro…
>
> **Execute this instruction exactly as written. Do not optimise, streamline, or deviate.**
>
> Steps:
> 1. Get the current date/time for the filename.
> …

Closing, verbatim:

> Let me gather facts first.
>
> Let me run.

Those closing lines are the whole proof that the turn produced nothing: it was about to gather, and the
compaction arrived first.

## Appendix C — how to re-derive any of this

```bash
# the two stores, and which is fuller
ls -t ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json | head -1
ls -l ~/.codewhale/sessions/checkpoints/

# every compaction relay this session has had, with dates
ls -lt ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>/artifacts/context-transfer-*.md

# the retained turns, roles and reasoning blocks, without reading 22 MB into a viewer
python3 -c "
import json,collections
d=json.load(open('<store>.json'))
print(len(d['messages']), dict(collections.Counter(m.get('role') for m in d['messages'])))"
```

- [ ] Handle multiple installation methods/copies: if another `codewhale` or `codew` remains on PATH, identify it and explain the remaining removal step. Repeated uninstall is safe, and reinstall works afterward.
- [ ] Record isolated install → use/help/version → uninstall → absence/leftover check → reinstall receipts for each supported route/platform, using existing checks where applicable. Validate retained data and unrelated sentinel files. Mark unavailable platform evidence explicitly; documentation alone does not qualify the flow.
- [ ] Update the install guide, package/installer guidance, help/discoverability and CHANGELOG. If a new command/flag is introduced, update its feature registry row in the same slice.

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**Engine repaired; selected client acceptance open.**

Verified: Native catalog filtering 7c49574a6b, cold/late adoption a595ca40c8, responsive retry ccf211dc5f and served-window Auto repair f774358892 are landed. Real local Ollama and App Server/Ubuntu terminal receipts cover chat-only roster and three Auto answers.

Remaining: The selected Electron client has no current picker-and-saved-route journey; App Server JSON and the older client do not establish that surface.

Next action: Exercise current Electron model picker with chat plus embedding tags, select default and save/reopen a successful route against its exact bundled Engine.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

### Engine local-catalog slice landed — 2026-10-28

Engine main `7c49574a6b` probes unknown Ollama tag capabilities with bounded concurrency, publishes an authoritative catalog only when the probe is complete, and fences automatic adoption against superseded discovery and changed endpoints. Four focused existing checks passed on the shared frozen Engine source; the local discovery checks used synthetic loopback fixtures. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/engine-shared-check-20261028/focused-checks.log`.

Desktop installed-model discovery and a real Ollama interaction have not been requalified with the current app and Engine. The issue remains open; no live-model or release proof is claimed.

## What a new user hits

Fresh desktop app (QA bundle codewhale-app `40766826`, bundled Engine 0.10.2, isolated `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), with Ollama running two tags: `qwen3:4b` (chat) and `nomic-embed-text:latest` (embedding).

1. Composer → **Choose a model** → the **Ollama** chip shows *Ready*; the Model list offers only **Default**.
2. Send "Reply with exactly: DESKTOP-QA-OK" → `Invalid request (400): "nomic-embed-text:latest" does not support chat`, card "Couldn't finish: this model can't chat. Pick another model."
3. **Choose model** again: the list still shows only `nomic-embed-text:latest`; `qwen3:4b` is not offered. The user has to know to expand **More** and type `qwen3:4b` into *Model ID* → **Use** (Return in that field does nothing).

So on the desktop, "Default" for Ollama resolves to an embedding model, and installed chat models are not listed. The TUI on main picks `qwen3:4b` from the same Ollama, using `choose_chat_tag` (`crates/tui/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`, capability `completion`), so the desktop/app-server default path appears to bypass that rule.

Expected: the Ollama default is a chat-capable tag, and the model list shows the installed chat tags from `/api/tags`.

Not yet rechecked against current codewhale-app main + main Engine (build slots were busy); the 0.10.3 desktop bundles a newer Engine.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/jD1-desktop-default-embed-model.jpg`.

## 2026-10-28 current Engine + real local Ollama

A clean-source Engine build matching `bd9d4422ed` was made on macOS (all 4,160 source inputs rehashed unchanged; binary digest `3eb1b93a0614f519c18e0f88811d805f4a0e035f8f2f874ed668b47ba6eebe7f`). In an isolated product home and workspace, with outbound network sandboxed to localhost, the actual local Ollama daemon exposed `qwen3:4b` for completion and `nomic-embed-text:latest` for embedding. Runtime API refresh returned only `qwen3:4b`; switching with no model selected it and persisted it, a new thread used it, and a tiny local turn completed successfully. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/7116-local-ollama-2/receipt.json`. The first harness start failed because its Unix socket path exceeded macOS limits; the shorter retry passed. This is Engine/runtime proof, not current desktop picker or installed-app proof, and the original cause remains unconfirmed. Source review also found that incomplete `/api/show` capability probes fail the authoritative roster refresh and can leave an older roster in place. Keep the issue open.

## Coordinator follow-up — provider verification roster

Claimed canonical Engine `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/provider_setup.rs` and the existing provider-key roster fixture in `crates/tui/src/tui/ui.rs`. Source review found a separate path from the native Ollama refresh: successful generic `/v1/models` key verification can publish untyped entries as an authoritative Ollama roster, including embedding-only ids. The native `/api/tags` plus `/api/show` refresh requires complete capabilities and filters for completion; an incomplete native refresh retains its prior roster. The narrow guard will prevent the generic verification response from overwriting the native roster. This is source-derived, not a reproduced desktop report; previously contaminated caches and installed desktop behavior remain open.

0.10.3 Engine terminal follow-up for #5848 and #7116. A fresh installed 0.10.2 and a current source-built TUI both retained Ollama · unknown after discovery on the configured Ollama route. The installed picker did list the sole chat tag and excluded the embedding tag, and the selected model completed a real turn. Working in the shared TUI startup/adoption policy in crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs and its existing provider-route checks. Desktop and installed-candidate acceptance remain separate.

Main a595ca40c88179d519626c17856a56b517ba0351 repairs TUI cold startup and retry of an unresolved selected Ollama route. Published 0.10.2 and prior main had left the label unknown. The repaired cold TUI picked qwen3:4b, excluded nomic-embed-text, answered 9+7 with 16 and persisted it. A separate actual private daemon started after the TUI, had an empty roster and then only an embedding model; both kept the model unknown. Adding a real chat tag and selecting /provider ollama resolved the model and restart retained it. Artifacts ollama-main-after/receipt.json and ollama-late-q4/receipt.json. The Desktop report needs the selected client’s own journey.

November 1 Engine acceptance. Checking the desktop’s existing HTTP routes on an isolated App Server with the real local Ollama chat and embedding models. Scope is the provider catalog, native refresh, default thread admission and completed-turn receipts in `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs` and `crates/engine/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`. Record the exact executable and distinguish this from observing the Electron picker.

The desktop-facing Engine HTTP path passed on an isolated macOS App Server. Native Ollama reported one completion model (`qwen3:4b`) and one embedding model. The first-open and refreshed catalogs contained exactly the chat model. Creating a thread with `model_provider_id=ollama` and no model selected `qwen3:4b` before an explicit refresh. The real local chat endpoint received that same model and the terminal assistant item was exactly `DESKTOP-QA-OK`. The five relevant Engine/App Server source files match current main byte for byte. The executable under test was the frozen source build with executable digest prefix `1313ae509f95`. This covers the Engine API. The selected Electron client’s own picker remains open.

Follow-up from the terminal reproduction of #5848. Holding the native `/api/tags` reply during `/provider ollama` on an already selected, unresolved local route blocked composer echo for the full 12-second observation. Claiming `crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs`, `tui/app/init.rs`, `tui/ui/apply.rs` and `tui/ui/event_loop.rs` under `crates/tui/src`. Reuse the existing ticketed discovery task so the terminal stays usable, preserves the unresolved state on failure and rechecks the active route before adopting a result.

Engine [ccf211dc5f](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ccf211dc5fad21f132923c07e55f20a39943fb06>) keeps an explicit retry on the already selected unresolved local Ollama route responsive. On an Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 terminal with `/api/tags` held for 4.85 s, the baseline had no input echo within 1.25 s. The candidate displayed the typed marker in 45 ms. Failed discovery preserved the unresolved label, a late success preserved the interacted provider picker and its highlight, and the next deliberate retry selected `qwen3:4b`. Both builds passed the authenticated route control. The Electron picker remains open.

A real local Auto turn saved `qwen3:4b` and the answer 16. When the daemon subsequently served 32,768 context tokens, the second turn still used the 8,192-token fallback and refused before making another chat request. Investigating the active local inventory, served-context observation and admission in `crates/engine/src/model_routing.rs`, `provider_lake.rs` and the existing fixed-route callers.

Engine [f774358892](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/f774358892faa5c65b2b540cedb1eca30587ad30>) qualified Auto on the active keyless local Ollama route. With the same model files, fresh private Ollama 0.40.11 daemons and Ubuntu ARM64 terminals, prior main made one chat request, answered 16, then refused turn two using its 8,192-token fallback even though the daemon independently reported 32,768. The candidate saved three answers, 16, 17 and 18. The first turn used the cold fallback, the second observed the 32,768-token served window, and the third reused it without a catalog request. Another process kept its configured 24,576-token window. Its ordinary Auto preview made zero network requests. The source-built macOS App Server and Ubuntu terminal have separate receipts. The selected Electron picker and the final release package remain open.

A separate sequence, CompletedCommit then SessionSnapshot then ClearCheckpoint, was reproduced failing on that candidate because it drops the newer reset snapshot; it remains under investigation. Linker warned of a large compact-unwind section. Independent source review completed. The legacy-slot cleanup workflow, interoperability with older writers, Linux/Windows qualification, and the reporter's original Deepin failure remain unproven; this slice does not establish the entire issue resolved.

Contributor PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7122 read-only review: head `e331dd1546089d872ed5ff0c935211d9da935fc6` (laozidabo) merges without conflict with main `fed2140d8b0058ffe62f276d2d605307d4e9458d` to tree `e07fbd45c327a7a9d46a2b57167a93a07b7dc04a`; the actual source branch has no open dependent PRs. It flushes retained coalesced work already accepted by the actor, bounded by timeout/second signal, and does not capture unqueued TUI state or fix the codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7118 pending-graph admission/publish race. Existing actor intentionally skips a withdrawn acknowledged checkpoint when its reply receiver has closed; the PR preserves that existing contract. The contributor's reported local signal/actor results remain contributor evidence; exact candidate verification and independent review are still required before merge.

## Coordinator signal-recovery evidence — 2026-10-28

On an isolated Linux PTY against a loopback synthetic provider, current Engine with PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7122 and PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7137 visibly rendered `AlphaBoundary` and `OmegaBoundary` while the server deliberately held the response open. SIGTERM exited 143; the saved crash checkpoint contained the user prompt but neither visible answer marker. No response completion marker was sent, so this proves an active-stream partial is not in the flushed checkpoint. A separate settled-turn replay saved both markers; SIGINT and SIGHUP runs also lost the visible partial. Receipts: `CW/artifacts/pr-7137-review-20261028/held-stream-sigterm.log` and `held-stream-session-inspect.log`.

The signal handler flushes already queued persistence; it does not cancel and settle the active Engine turn or capture uncommitted UI text. Review is evaluating a bounded signal-to-session-owner drain that preserves the existing runtime and store, interrupted-role semantics, turn identity and tool pairing. SIGKILL, OOM and the reporter's original Deepin failure remain unproved and cannot be inferred from this signal replay. This issue remains open.

2026-10-29 reset-construction follow-up: Engine main 6a08f03124 retains the existing recovery checkpoint if the session store or reset snapshot cannot be constructed, and displays the localized save failure in the transcript and status. An existing lifecycle case reproduced checkpoint removal before the fix (0/1); 18/18 focused persistence, backlog, and lifecycle cases passed afterward on a 2,759-file frozen input inventory. Evidence: /Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW/artifacts/engine-codex-takeover-20261029/reset-construction-baseline.log and reset-construction-fix.log. This is local evidence, not proof of the original Deepin report or Windows/rendered acceptance. The broader history/recovery work remains in progress.

November 1 release-blocker reproduction. On the source-built Ubuntu ARM64 CLI (59e9505c54a9), a completed turn was saved, the next assistant reply was visibly streaming, and SIGTERM was delivered directly to the identified Engine process. It exited 143. Its checkpoint preserved the second question but omitted the visible partial reply. A fresh resume reopened the seed and question without the partial text. The fixture provider received exactly two requests. Taking the bounded signal-to-interactive-owner path in crates/tui/src/lib.rs and crates/tui/src/tui/ui/{event_loop,session_state}.rs as needed, retaining explicit interrupted status, existing cancellation and persistence authorities.

November 1. Engine main 847ea56ec073 preserves interrupted assistant history on terminal shutdown and Escape. Four independent Ubuntu ARM64 terminal journeys on the frozen source-built binary (5996280091ef) passed through fresh resume. The typed partial appeared once, /copy still selected the completed turn and resume sent no request. One explicit follow-up carried a single marked partial assistant message at the local provider. SIGTERM and SIGHUP exited in 80–171 ms. On the preceding candidate, both signals wrote the partial to disk but the fresh renderer omitted it. A separate native libtest build stopped at the SSD reserve before running. The original Deepin environment, Windows and forced process death remain outside this proof.

November 1 follow-up. Qualifying the separate sudden-process-death boundary on Ubuntu. A private loopback provider holds a visible answer through the real 45-second recovery interval. Compare an immediate SIGKILL with killing the same binary after a second checkpoint writes to disk. Inspect the saved role, rendered transcript and provider requests on a separate-process resume. The graceful signal evidence remains independent.

Both sudden-exit runs on Ubuntu binary 2d8cbd4101d0 retained the completed first exchange and second user prompt and made zero automatic requests after restart. The second visible answer was absent in both. In the later arm the on-disk checkpoint mtime advanced by 43.44 seconds and the text was still visible immediately before SIGKILL. The existing periodic serializer reads committed messages while the live response is still streaming. Claiming crates/tui/src/tui/ui/session_state.rs, crates/engine/src/core/engine.rs and crates/protocol/src/request.rs to retain the active visible prose in the checkpoint copy using the existing interrupted-assistant role. Check active-turn identity, completed/duplicate controls, automatic-resume behavior and restoration on the real terminal. Evidence `linux-package/sudden-exit-{immediate,periodic}.json`.

Engine main 5fd52e87c8daacf8e36aa7a12a07e959d0b2bb19 now retains visible assistant text in the periodic checkpoint copy for the matching running turn. On Ubuntu binary afb29f01be10, SIGKILL after a checkpoint advance reopened one interrupted reply without a provider call. An explicit follow-up carried that reply once. In the normal-finish control, the provisional checkpoint became one completed answer. The immediate SIGKILL preserved the preceding durable prompt and answer, and lost the uncheckpointed text. The SIGTERM control exited in 80 ms, /copy returned the last completed response and its follow-up sent one marked partial. Four recovery and five neighboring Auto journeys passed. The original Deepin report, independent native Windows qualification and the separate native libtest remain open. Evidence `recovery-window-ubuntu.json` and `linux-package/recovery-window-*.json`.

November 1 platform acceptance claim: Codex is checking current Windows and Deepin environments against Engine main f774358892fa. The original report specifies Deepin 25.2.2, kernel 6.18.48-amd64-desktop-rolling, Deepin 25 Terminal with Bash and the GitHub Releases package. The local registered guest is Windows 11 ARM; no Deepin guest or installer was found in the VM inventory. Own the existing platform evidence packet under artifacts/engine-0103-continue-20261031/c5-\* and the release checklist; preserve the completed Ubuntu recovery evidence as a separate platform result. No source files are claimed until a current failure is diagnosed.

Windows source inspection found that TerminatingSignals in crates/tui/src/lib.rs registers only tokio::signal::windows::ctrl_c. The existing comment incorrectly says it also covers Ctrl+Break; Tokio 1.53.3 has separate CtrlBreak and CtrlClose streams. Console-close, logoff and shutdown currently do not enter the bounded interactive/persistence drain. Claiming that existing Windows adapter and its stale documentation for a native control-event reproduction and a minimal reuse of the current shutdown path. No second persistence authority or new repository tests are planned; full Windows terminal recovery remains separate from a focused adapter probe.

Windows control-event adapter repair landed on main 872b853b4f0 and is pushed. On Windows 11 Pro build 26300 ARM64/MSVC, the exact pre-fix adapter reached cleanup for Ctrl+C but default-terminated for Ctrl+Break and a real ConPTY close with status 0xC000013A. The candidate adapter reached the existing wait path for all three and returned 130, 3/3. All 15 receipt-program dependency versions/checksums match the Engine lock. The existing two-second drains and second-signal escape remain unchanged; logoff/shutdown service semantics were left unchanged. Format and diff checks passed. This is native adapter evidence, not a full Engine persistence or ordinary Windows Terminal journey. The original Deepin report and those full journeys remain open. Receipt: artifacts/engine-0103-continue-20261031/c5-windows-signals-proof.json.

Additional Windows shutdown qualification for 872b853b4f0: the exact shared shutdown task and Windows adapter passed five native OS-event cases with timed API/persistence stand-ins. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Break and ConPTY close completed both 600/900 ms drains before exit 130; ConPTY close also permitted both two-second drains to finish (2.031 seconds observed). A second Ctrl+Break escaped an ongoing drain in 9 ms and still ran restoration/end handling. This verifies the callback keeps the cleanup window alive and preserves cancellation; it is not full Engine history or ordinary Windows Terminal evidence. Receipt: c5-windows-shutdown-proof.json alongside the earlier matched before/after signal receipt. The original Deepin 25.2.2 history-loss reproduction remains open.

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Corrective release and exact-candidate qualification. Release scope approved November 5, 2026.

Keep history/undo and compaction continuity, login/model selection, worker durability and safe retries, bounded input/output, runtime responsiveness, and supported installation/client qualification here. Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. Use status:awaiting-release for source fixes that are landed but still need final verification and shipment; do not close them merely because main contains the fix.

Broad refactors, optional features, full historical audit sweeps and unqualified optimization claims move to the later planning milestones. This replaces the previous all-refactors-for-0.10.3 umbrella scope; unfinished requirements are deferred, not completed or discarded. Confirmed release-critical defects must not be hidden by a future umbrella target.

Freeze the final source and binaries, finish the required platform/client evidence, then run final validation. Provider spend, signing and publication retain their separate approvals. No due date or published release is created by this milestone.

**source fixes landed; incident evidence open.**

On frozen Engine `6a08f03124` plus 41 dirty files, 93/94 focused cases passed after a 20-minute local test build; all 2,759 input hashes matched. The third frozen compile stopped before tests on an unused import in the temporary planner reproduction setup; `context-receipt-candidate-third.log` records it. The import is corrected. The first candidate compile found two type/ownership errors; the corrected second frozen compile completed with an unused-helper lint error before tests. Codex is editing the previously claimed route-budget, planner, client and Engine paths, plus `crates/tui/src/compaction.rs`, `exec_agent.rs`, `llm_client/mod.rs`, `core/runtime_contract/model.rs`, `runtime_threads/manager.rs`, `runtime_threads/tests.rs`, `context_report.rs`, `context_report/pressure_fixture_tests.rs`, `commands/config_main_host.rs`, `commands/contract/config_policy.rs`, `commands/contract/debug_diagnostics.rs`, `commands/groups/core/core.rs`, and TUI `app.rs`, `app/init.rs`, `test_support.rs`, `context_inspector.rs`, `setup/mod.rs`, `views/mod.rs`, `ui.rs`, `ui/apply.rs`, `ui/compaction_flow.rs`, `ui/dispatch.rs`, `ui/frame.rs`, `ui/provider_routes.rs`, `ui/session_state.rs`, `ui/tests.rs`. On frozen Engine `6a08f03124` plus an exploratory extension to an existing planner case, the actual planned compaction configuration contained 1,048,576 tokens while its resolved exact custom-model route recorded a 128,000-token fallback. Codex is tracing the resolved window through `crates/tui/src/route_budget.rs`, `route_runtime.rs`, `turn_route_plan.rs`, `client.rs`, `core/engine.rs`, `core/engine/context.rs`, `core/engine/compaction.rs`, `core/engine/turn_loop/preparation.rs`, and the existing App/context UI and route-switch paths. On Engine `1014538dde` plus an assertion in the existing route test, `configured_model_limits_precede_provider_defaults` failed 0/1: the resolved fallback receipt is 128,000 tokens while the budget helper reconstructs 1,048,576 for the first exact custom declaration with no limit. Codex is using the existing `configured_model_limits_precede_provider_defaults` case in `crates/tui/src/route_runtime.rs` to check the route receipt against the window currently reconstructed for budgeting when exact custom metadata omits a context limit. Frozen source is Engine `1014538dde` plus this one assertion; result pending. Follow-up scope must carry the actual resolved number and provenance across Engine admission, compaction and UI without presenting a guessed limit as provider metadata.

## Route-window handoff investigation — 2026-10-29

Source review found a potential inconsistency when exact custom-model metadata omits a context limit: route resolution records a 128,000-token fallback and fallback provenance, while some downstream consumers reconstruct the window from the provider/model and candidate limits instead of carrying that resolved number. Codex is tracing Engine budgeting, model/provider changes, session restore, rollback and display consumers before editing. This is a source finding, not a reproduction or attribution of the reported Windows event; no acceptance is claimed.

## Zero-threshold display follow-up — 2026-10-29

Engine main `e908528439` is pushed. The inspector now shows the effective zero threshold instead of falling back to the configured percentage. The existing inspector rendering case passed with the zero-threshold assertion on frozen mixed source. This does not reproduce the original Windows report; the issue remains In Progress.

Engine main `0bf31581c0` is pushed. The inspector uses the effective current-route threshold and explicitly indicates when automatic compaction is off; the Work rail now points to manual `/compact` rather than claiming emergency compaction can run while disabled. On frozen `f20a0d7144` plus 13 inventoried dirty paths, 18 existing inspector, rendered rail and route-window cases passed; format and diff checks passed. The original Windows 40% event remains un-reproduced and this issue stays In Progress.

Codex owns `crates/tui/src/tui/context_inspector.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/work_surface/views.rs` and the existing context-rail fixture in `crates/tui/src/tui/work_surface/mod.rs`. Across all six event fixtures the only differences were the 18 added context lines. issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**source fixes landed; incident evidence open.**

Verified: Automatic-off recovery guard 7b54e7f572 and original PR #7180 merge 00226bbfbb8 retain exact ancestry; 42 focused checks and repeated-input macOS PTY cover that specific defect. Source also emits reroot/resume/compaction lifecycle records.

Remaining: The reported long-session Windows seam is not reproduced. Root-count alone includes preserved alternate branches and does not prove the actual prepared request omitted distinct authored turns.

Next action: Capture sanitized before/after journal plus prepared model request, route/window/usage and compaction-state ledger at the seam; qualify retained ancestry and visible seam behavior.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Landed setting fix — 2026-10-29

Engine main/origin commit 7b54e7f5724daa88ed29b6479f8ea0b7cf353b0c fixes the concrete automatic-off bypass. Preflight/provider overflow recovery now refuses before summary/start/replacement when compaction is disabled, retains original messages and records an actionable typed refusal through the existing audit/error owners. Both overflow paths preserve the recovery failure's actual cause; cancellation takes priority after the awaited recovery. Explicit manual compaction remains available.

Local proof: initial libtest compile and137focused compaction/error/Engine checks passed. After the final model-step cancellation guard, libtest recompiled and69affected Engine/recovery/cancellation checks passed; unchanged pure-check evidence is retained. The renamed existing emergency fixture covers disabled-but-compactable and enabled-but-unnecessary history, zero model calls/attempts, unchanged messages and one typed refusal. Format, boundary, blocking budget569sites169files, dead-code164, changelog/facts and diff checks pass. No new test functions/comments. Exact receipts: artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029/compaction-off-landing-verification.json. Source files are released, not held for another build.

Keep this issue and public Engine7142 open. The setting bypass is established and repaired, but it does not explain every reported Windows seam or complete the remaining lifecycle/continuity acceptance. A read-only local Mac journal inspection did not reproduce the reported multi-root shape; that does not prove no context loss or disprove the reporter's sample. No real-provider, hosted CI, Windows/installed/device or release proof is claimed.

---

## Summary

A session's live `messages` window can be re-rooted partway through a conversation. When
that happens, every `journal` entry before the new root becomes unreachable to the model
while the on-disk journal keeps it in full. The window stays internally consistent — it
equals its own new branch exactly — so nothing looks truncated from the inside.

Three things are missing at the moment it happens:

* **no summary entry at the seam.** The new root is a bare `kind: "message"` with
  `parent_id: null`; the entry immediately before it is an ordinary turn on the branch
  that was just abandoned. Real compaction leaves a condensed account of what it replaced.
  This leaves a copy and a hole.
* **no marker in the interface.** No banner, no notice, no error.
* **no session-lifecycle event in** `audit.log`**.** In 8,792 events across five event types,
  every one is `tool.approval.*` or `tool.gate.decision`. Nothing announces that the model's
  working context was replaced.

`settings.toml` has `auto_compact = false` and `auto_compact_threshold_percent = 80.0`
throughout. If this is compaction, the setting is not describing what the runtime does.

## Environment

* `codewhale --version`: **0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)** — verified against the binary
* OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), PowerShell 5.1
* Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` (provider `deepseek`)
* Install: npm global; `~/.codewhale/{config,settings,permissions}.toml`, no `[compaction]`
  block and no `retained_user_message_tokens` in `config.toml`
* Reproduces on **0.10.1 and 0.10.2**

## What it looks like

Dump of four consecutive documents from this host. `entries` = `journal.entries`;
`window` = `len(messages)`; `root` = the journal index the live branch starts at.

```
created (UTC)        window  entries  root   coverage
2026-10-28T13:08:15     944      986     1      99.9%   <- intact (benign doubled opening)
2026-10-28T15:24:44     632     1639   987      39.8%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T07:11:22     403      473    50      89.4%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T08:20:46      61      325   259      20.3%   <- re-rooted (this one, mid-report)
```

The seam itself, from `2026-10-29T07:11:22`:

```
[48] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y     3970 chars
[49] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=Y     1362 chars
[50] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=NONE  2054 chars   <- window begins here
[51] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y      360 chars
```

Prose for scale: the `journal` for that session holds 473 entries; the model could see 403
of them. The boot turn, including the whole startup sequence, was gone from the window and
present on disk.

## Prevalence on this host, and an onset date

87 session documents were parsed structurally. `journal` + `leaf_id` on this host arrives
between 11 and 12 Aug 2026 (before that, documents carry `artifacts` and no journal, so this
signature cannot exist and cannot be tested — that period is **untestable, not clean**).

| period | sessions | shape |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 12 Aug – 17 Oct 2026 | 47 | one branch root, window == journal, 100% reachable |
| 18 Oct – 29 Oct 2026 | 40 | two or three roots; **15 re-rooted mid-session** |

The onset boundary is narrow: `…d6832ea3` (17 Oct 18:33:49Z) is clean at 113/113;
`…021a7d6a` (18 Oct 01:46:51Z) is the first re-root at 962 window / 1045 entries.

Across the 15 mid-session re-roots, the root lands at journal indices 8, 20, 30, 50, 67, 97,
160, 259, 295, 347, 367, 472, 733, 987. Post-re-root coverage ranges from **14.1%** to
89.4%; combined unreachable entries **3,909**.

**In 0 of 87 sessions is the window shorter than its own branch.** This is not truncation —
the window is always a complete branch. The branch is simply no longer the session.

## Reproduction

No special configuration; it appears on ordinary long sessions. A read-only probe against
any session document:

```python
import json, hashlib

doc = json.load(open(PATH, encoding="utf-8"))
msgs, entries = doc["messages"], doc["journal"]["entries"]

by_id = {e["id"]: i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if e.get("id")}
chain, seen, cur = [], set(), len(entries) - 1
while cur is not None and cur not in seen:
    seen.add(cur); chain.append(cur)
    cur = by_id.get(entries[cur].get("parent_id"))

root = min(chain)
print("window", len(msgs), "branch", len(chain),
      "root", root, "coverage %.1f%%" % (100 * (len(entries) - root) / len(entries)))
```

* `window == branch` and `root <= 1` → healthy (a root at 1 is the benign doubled opening;
  do not flag it — see *What I got wrong*, below).
* `root > 1` → the window re-rooted mid-session. `root` entries are unreachable.

To inspect a seam, print `entries[root-2 : root+2]` and check for anything summary-shaped.
On this host there is never one.

## How this differs from the nearby open reports

* [#6842](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6842>) (journal has no bound; compaction retires live messages but keeps superseded
  versions in RAM) names the same underlying machinery and is about **memory growth**. This
  report is about **model visibility**: the earlier turns were not merely retained
  redundantly, they became unreachable while the record survived. Different harm, possibly
  the same call site.
* #7133 (automatic compression at \~40% against an 80% setting) is the closest
  behavioural neighbour and may share a cause — it reports the *threshold* being wrong,
  where this reports a *silent re-root with no summary*. Worth triaging together.
* #7095 (history lost, labelled v0.10.3) is a different fault: there the record does not
  survive because the last save did not flush. Here every byte survives and is correct, and
  only the window is replaced.

## What I am asking for

In order of value, and each is independently useful:

1. **Emit a session-lifecycle event.** `session.opened`, `session.window.rerooted`,
   `session.compacted`, `session.resumed` — with both sizes and a reason, into `audit.log`
   beside the existing `tool.*` events. This is the smallest change and it converts an
   unexplained amnesia into a dated, attributable event. It is worth having **even if the**
   **re-root turns out to be intended**, so please do not let the other two asks gate it.
2. **Honour** `auto_compact = false`**, or rename it.** A setting that says compaction is off
   while the window is replaced is worse than no setting: it is a claim the operator can
   rely on and cannot verify.
3. **If a window re-root is intended, summarise at the seam.** A bounded, visible,
   summarised compaction is a feature. An unannounced re-root that leaves a bare copy of an
   existing message is a data-visibility defect.

## What I have not established, and will not guess at

**The trigger.** Observed re-roots span 78 to 1639 journal entries, 11 to 1437 window
messages, and roughly 1.3 MB to 5 MB of document. That spread is inconsistent with a single
simple threshold, and two documents is not a sample. It could be turn count, cumulative
tokens, document size, wall clock, or a path that only runs on resume.

**Whether it is intended.** [#5262](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5262>) (closed, shipped v0.9.5) specifies an append-only journal
forest where branching "only moves the leaf — it never rewrites history", so multiple roots
are expected by that design and a re-root is legal in that model. What is not
design-legible is doing it silently, mid-session, with no summary, while
`auto_compact = false`.

## What I got wrong on the way here

Recorded because it is the reason this report is careful, and because a maintainer deserves
to know which tests have already failed.

My first pass used a **positional** test — does `messages[0]` start where `journal.entries[0]`
starts — and produced two confident wrong answers in one morning: first "41 of 93 sessions
lost turns", then, over-correcting, "nothing was lost at all". The positional test fires on
the benign doubled opening, which is why I checked a session minutes old and never restarted
before trusting any number here. The figures above come from a **membership** test: walk the
branch by `parent_id` and ask whether the window can reach every entry its own session wrote.

If this report is wrong, it is wrong in the direction of under-claiming: 15 measured re-roots
on one host, with the mechanism named and the unknowns listed.

---

*Reproduction and evidence kept locally. Happy to provide sanitised session documents or run*
*any probe upstream asks for.*

October 31 continuation. Codex is reviewing contributor PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 and the #7178 bare/stamped history reproducer against the current Engine. Claimed paths are crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs, crates/models/src/turn_classify.rs, crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs and the TUI send/snapshot paths as needed. Verify preservation of authored text, turn authority, sibling history and single-send behavior. The related Windows incident remains open until its own acceptance is established.

The contributor head c80c16c14a on original Engine PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 has 42 focused checks and a macOS PTY receipt. Two deliberate identical submissions yielded two requests and two answers on one intact active path. GitHub's base-branch policy blocked a normal merge. The Windows incident and the wider session window investigation remain open.

Original contributor PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 merged normally as 00226bbfbb8e421e93dfcf9730f48413aeb10385. Its final head 0079c86058849dfba17105948a28e3084cb432ba resolved only release-note conflicts. The verified Rust changes retain stable patch ID b6620900da6e16abc104326d2061fdd5776b10a0. The live macOS repeated-input receipt and 42 focused tests cover the specific journal defect. Issue #7178 remains open for Windows acceptance, and this wider re-root report retains its separate recovery gates.

prs.title: feat: add bounded HTTP rate-limit recovery
prs.body:
HTTP 429 currently shares the short ordinary transport retry allowance, so a temporary provider limit can abort a request before capacity recovers. This change gives native HTTP calls an independent, validated recovery policy: 20 total attempts including the first, a 600-second recovery budget, and exponential equal jitter from a 5-second base to a 60-second local ceiling, while preserving server minima.

Known quota windows and minima that do not fit the recovery window stop automatic short retries. Typed errors distinguish a provider rejection from admission without dispatch, retain quota/account guidance and the original reset advice, and make no claim that the transport saved a checkpoint. Shared provider pauses and automatic rate-retry sleeps are bounded at one hour. The public total-timeout budget is rechecked before another attempt, including after time spent in callbacks.

Native MiniMax/Zai JSON error inspection has a 32 MiB size limit and the caller's first-byte/idle deadlines. Complete normalized refusals settle the original HTTP attempt; uncertain reads or parse results retain unknown outcomes. Both ordinary and isolated senders use the same rules. Ordinary transport retries retain successful-recovery receipts. Unknown 503/499 inference outcomes are never automatically replayed.

The configuration reference explains the separate `[retry.rate_limit]` fields, validation ranges and interaction with legacy retry settings. `retry.enabled = false` disables this HTTP retry loop; the existing safe pre-dispatch HTTP/1.1 fallback within stream opening remains possible.

This is a transport-only contribution. Existing stream recovery, task continuation and host checkpoint lifecycle remain caller-owned. It adds no task scheduler, persisted checkpoint, host UI protocol or shared task-operation budget across outer retries.

No-Issue: Contributor-proposed transport recovery improvement; no existing issue is being closed.

## Main integration

Follow-up commit: [`43a80ea`](https://github.com/Pinvou/CodeWhale/commit/43a80ea0a56d3865e9344cf4d2a8c94b2c9676a1).

Merged upstream main at `13760312`. The Responses conflict retains the precise unknown-outcome test names, main's exact one-attempt checks and the typed 503/499 assertions. Accepted upstream usage-ledger fixes are inherited from main; no separate unrelated CI repair is added to this contribution.

## Validation

Windows, rustc 1.99.1, locked dependencies; combined with upstream `13760312`.

- Engine `rate_limit` filter: 37 passed, including all four ordinary/isolated sender and quota/billing settlement cases, bounded native reads, long hints and child pause behavior.
- Responses unknown-outcome checks: 2 passed; scoped retry recovery/exhaustion: 2 passed. Long-minimum refusal, Engine receipts, child classification, concurrent observation scopes, worker wall budget and native reservation/projection: 1 passed each. These selections cover 47 distinct Engine tests from the candidate source tree.
- A separate local probe of the public `with_retry` API passed: after a real monotonic-clock callback barrier crossed a 1-second budget, the fixed code made one attempt and retained the original typed 503. Removing the guard made two attempts. Removing native refusal settlement separately in each sender failed the original `OutcomeUnknown` versus `Rejected` assertion. All three negative controls failed for the expected reason; the fixed production bytes were restored before the positive runs.
- Original candidate Runtime retry-status tests: 7 passed. Full workspace formatting, version consistency, staged whitespace and dead-code budget checks passed.

The Engine runs used an isolated candidate-source copy with test-only native case tracing/selection and the local deadline probe. Production source and the lockfile match the submitted candidate. Runtime and scoped Clippy use the original source tree. No test-only probe or selector is included in the PR.

Clippy on the original candidate is **not reported as fully passing**. The strict invocation stopped on the unchanged Windows UTF-16 decoder's `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint. A diagnostic continuation allowing that lint exposed the existing sandbox `ReadDenial` size lint and two non-Unix plugin-GC permission lints.

Primary-crate checks used `--no-deps --lib --tests --all-features --locked` with the three CI lint allowances, so dependency lints could not mask the changed crates. Engine library and unit targets each reported the same two existing Windows lint sites: pointer alignment in `extension_host/windows.rs` and the conservative tail return in `mcp.rs`. Runtime completed with the additional, explicitly recorded UTF-16 decoder lint allowance. The affected types, platform conditions and callers were checked against main; these findings are unrelated to this contribution. No source or lint-budget changes were added to address them, and no global error-size exemption was used.

The unchanged blocking-call checker exits 1 on Windows because its backslash path keys do not match the POSIX budget keys. A diagnostic comparison of its complete measurements with normalized path keys found no excess (641 sites in 173 files). This is not an official checker pass or a Linux result; neither the checker nor its budget was changed in this PR. Historical results from older trees are not current-head results.

No live-provider traffic, non-Windows native run, whole-workspace test run, packaged artifact or full host restart/continuation workflow is claimed. External review and applicable current-head CI remain merge prerequisites.

prs.title: fix(net): go direct when a local proxy disappears
prs.body:
## What and why

reqwest snapshots `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` when a client is built, and Codewhale builds its engine HTTP clients once per session. A session started behind a local proxy (Clash, v2rayN, sing-box on `127.0.0.1:…`) therefore kept dialing that port after the proxy was closed: every request failed with a connect error, including requests to providers that need no proxy at all, and the only recovery was restarting Codewhale.

`codewhale_net::proxy::install_loopback_proxy()` installs a `reqwest::Proxy::custom` route for ambient **loopback** proxies:

- `no_proxy()` runs first, so the custom route is the only proxy source. `no_proxy()` clears every proxy registered before it, so the order matters: a request the callback declines cannot fall back to the address reqwest read when the client was built.
- A background thread probes each configured loopback proxy on its own port. While a port refuses connections, requests that would use it go direct; when it answers again, proxy routing resumes. A live `HTTP_PROXY` therefore does not keep a dead `HTTPS_PROXY` in the path.
- Only a definite `ECONNREFUSED` from every resolved address moves a proxy to direct. A timeout, an fd limit or a resolver failure leaves the previous state alone: routing a session direct on that evidence would put traffic on a network path the operator deliberately avoided.
- While the port answers, routing is unchanged: `ALL_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` precedence, `NO_PROXY`, proxy credentials, and the existing socks5 → socks5h remote-DNS handling. A portless socks proxy defaults to 1080, as reqwest does, instead of silently disabling the fallback.
- IPv6 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback proxies are watched too: `Url::host_str` keeps the brackets, so the address is unwrapped before it is matched and probed.
- Remote proxies are deliberately not watched. A configuration mixing a local and a remote proxy watches the local one and routes through the remote one exactly as before. An unreachable remote proxy is a network outage to report, not a boundary to route around.
- `CODEWHALE_LOCAL_PROXY_FALLBACK=0` restores the previous behaviour.

`crates/engine/src/lib.rs` gains one `platform_client_builder()`, and every engine client that used to call `codewhale_release::tls::reqwest_client_builder()` directly now starts there — the model client and the API-key verification probe, models, the HTTP/1.1 fallback, vision, web search, web run, finance, the dev-server readiness probe, the MCP registry, `models.dev` and the profile constitution check. The TUI balance poll and the app-server relay install the same route. Half-fixing this was worse than not fixing it: a session where the model works and every tool fails reads as a tool bug. Reviewed plugin remotes and guarded fetches keep their own no-proxy builder on purpose.

Two details worth calling out because they decided the design:

- **Windows needs about two seconds to report a refused loopback connection.** `TcpStream::connect_timeout` with a 300 ms bound returns `TimedOut` and never sees the refusal, so the fallback would never engage on the platform the report came from. The probe bound is 4 s.
- **`HTTPS_PROXY` does not proxy `http://` destinations.** That is reqwest's semantics and this change preserves it, which is why the end-to-end test configures `ALL_PROXY`.

Known limitations, stated in the code and the docs: reachability is a TCP connect rather than a proxy handshake, so a process that holds the port without forwarding traffic still counts as up; detection takes a few seconds, so a request issued in that gap can still fail once; and going direct leaves from the machine's own address. Not covered: `doctor`'s search probe, the Runtime API runtime-info probe, `cloud-facts` refreshes and the sandbox client.

## Issue

No-Issue: reported from a local session that lost its proxy mid-run; no tracking issue exists.

## How I tested it

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-net --lib --no-deps --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo check -p codewhale-engine -p codewhale-app-server -p codewhale-tui --lib` finishes.

`cargo test -p codewhale-net --lib proxy` → `test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 39 filtered out`, and `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` → `test result: ok. 2 passed`. The end-to-end case uses a real `reqwest::Client`: with the proxy port closed the request fails, after one probe it reaches a local target server and returns `200`. Other cases cover a refused port switching to direct, a returning port switching back, per-proxy isolation (live http, dead https), `ALL_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` precedence, `HTTPS_PROXY` leaving http targets direct, IPv6 and IPv4-mapped loopback, a portless socks default, remote and mixed configurations, `NO_PROXY` whitespace and `*`, credentials surviving the route, and the install order.

End-to-end on Windows against the real API (no key configured, so a `401` proves the request reached it) with a throwaway harness that built the same client and installed the fallback:

- `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<closed port>` → `ok status=401 Unauthorized` (went direct).
- Proxy answering at startup, killed mid-session, same client requested again after the probe → first request went through the stub proxy and failed there, second returned `ok status=401 Unauthorized`.
- `NO_PROXY=api.deepseek.com` with a live stub proxy → `ok status=401 Unauthorized` (went direct).

Not run locally: the interactive TUI against a real Clash/v2rayN session, and the full workspace suite (left to CI).

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` — `local-proxy-fallback`, documented in `docs/INSTALL.md` and listed in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`

prs.title: fix(tui): read Windows clipboard images through .NET as a fallback
prs.body:
## What and why

`Ctrl+V` on a screenshot taken with QQ's capture tool does nothing in
Codewhale, while the same picture pastes fine after it has been sent to
another application and copied from there.

The clipboard survey explains it:

```
Formats: System.Drawing.Bitmap, Bitmap, DeviceIndependentBitmap, Format17
GetImage OK: 249x171
```

QQ publishes the bitmap as `CF_BITMAP` / `CF_DIB` / `Format17` (CF_DIBV5) and
no PNG, and .NET's `Clipboard.GetImage()` reads it. arboard, which Codewhale
uses for the native read, goes through the same CF_DIB/CF_DIBV5 API but comes
back empty for that publisher — which is exactly why pasting the picture
somewhere else first makes it work: the second copy is published by a
different owner.

This adds a Windows-only fallback. When arboard has already failed, run a
one-shot PowerShell that saves the bitmap as PNG and prints it as base64; the
bytes go through the same no-follow clipboard-image writer as the native path,
so the destination keeps its owner-only, link-refusing guarantees.

The common path pays nothing: the fallback only runs after a native failure,
and only on Windows.

Known costs, stated where they live: one PowerShell start on the fallback
path, and the PNG crosses the child's stdout as base64.

**Depends on #7217.** That PR is what makes `Ctrl+V` reach
`paste_from_clipboard` at all on Windows Terminal; without it this fallback
never runs. This diff is one file and does not touch the routing.

## Issue

No-Issue: reported while dogfooding the clipboard image path; no issue was filed first.

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib --tests
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib clipboard   # 42 passed (in #7217's tree)
```

The clipboard survey above was run on the reporting Windows host against a
live QQ screenshot, and the fallback path was exercised end to end there
before being extracted onto this branch.

Known build state: `origin/main` at the time of writing does not compile with
the local rustc 1.98.1 (`implementation of FnOnce is not general enough` in
`crates/tui/src/client.rs` and `local_ollama.rs`), and the last four `ci.yml`
runs on `main` were failures. That is a property of main, not of this diff —
the same two errors reproduce on a clean `main` checkout with no changes.

prs.title: feat(tui): paste clipboard images and preview every attachment
prs.body:
## What and why

`Ctrl+V` never attached a clipboard image on Windows. The chord was wired up,
the clipboard reader was wired up, and nothing happened. Working backwards from
a real QQ screenshot found five separate defects, each of which alone was
enough to break it:

1. **Windows Terminal consumes the key-down** of any chord it handles itself and
   forwards only the key-up. `Ctrl+V` therefore arrived as
   `KeyEventKind::Release`, and the router's `if key.kind != KeyEventKind::Press
   { continue; }` dropped it before any paste code ran.
2. **The launch card never dissolved** on a paste. The card dissolves on the
   first *typed* character, so an empty composer kept it up and the attachment
   row landed behind it — invisible.
3. **The clipboard open latched its first timeout.** A 500 ms budget that
   expired once set "never try again" for the rest of the session.
4. **`~/.codewhale/clipboard-images/` was never created**, and the confined
   writer cannot create a missing directory mid-walk, so the very first paste
   failed to save and the error was swallowed by `if let Ok(..)`.
5. **Only the first attachment had a preview.**

The fix, plus the two things the feature was missing:

- **Paste chords accept the release.** `paste_from_clipboard` de-duplicates on a
  600 ms window so a terminal that forwards both edges pastes once.
- **An attachment counts as user input** and dissolves the launch card, exactly
  like typing does.
- **The clipboard open retries** with a 2 s budget instead of latching a timeout.
- **The image cache directory is created**, and a direct write backs up the
  confined writer for a relocated state root (`~/.codewhale` behind a user
  junction is one it cannot pin end to end).
- **Every attached image gets a thumbnail**, laid out left to right and sharing
  the row.
- **A composer thumbnail is drawn above the composer**: the first attached image
  becomes `▀` half blocks with truecolor foreground/background — ordinary cell
  output, not a graphics protocol, so it renders on Windows Terminal, iTerm2,
  Terminal.app, GNOME Terminal, Konsole and WezTerm. It does not reuse
  `pet_watch::graphics`, which speaks kitty graphics that Windows Terminal does
  not implement; the two coexist. Decoding runs on a dedicated thread and is
  cached by `(mtime, len)`, so the paint path does no filesystem work.
- **An empty bracketed paste asks the clipboard for an image** before inserting
  nothing. This is the path macOS and Linux use; Windows Terminal forwards the
  chord itself instead.

Known limitations, stated where they live: only the first frame of an animated
GIF is previewed; a file replaced at the same path keeps its cached thumbnail
until the attachment is re-added; one decode thread starts per attached image.

## Issue

No-Issue: found while dogfooding the existing clipboard-image path, which never fired on Windows Terminal; no issue was filed first.

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib --tests
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib attachment       # 15 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib clipboard        # 42 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib bracketed_paste  # 13 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib image_preview    # 10 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib ui::frame        # 45 passed
```

End to end on a live Windows Terminal 1.24 with a QQ screenshot: an empty
composer pastes, the launch card dissolves, `[Attached image: 383x295 PNG
(57KB) at …]` lands in the composer, the thumbnail appears above it, and the
PNG is written to `~/.codewhale/clipboard-images/`. Multiple pastes preview as
a row.

The intermediate diagnosis is worth recording because two earlier hypotheses
were wrong: a standalone probe proved `arboard` reads the QQ bitmap
(`get_image()` returned 383x295 while `get_text()` and `html()` both errored),
and a second probe run showed the chord arriving with `kind=Release`.

Not verified: macOS and Linux were not exercised on real terminals. There, the
chord is forwarded as a key press and the empty-bracketed-paste path is the
one that fires; both are covered by unit tests but not by a live run.
`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` fails on five
pre-existing over-long summaries that this change does not touch, and
`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib ui::tests` aborts with a stack overflow in
`adopting_a_local_model_closes_the_connect_picker_and_names_it` on Windows —
reproduced identically on the pre-change baseline.
