prs.title: fix(subagent): report follow-up delivery truthfully and follow the answering successor
prs.body:
## What and why

Two halves of one fix: report follow-up delivery truthfully, and follow the agent that will actually answer.

**Engine.** `continue_child_from_user`'s Interrupted/Completed arm hardcoded `delivered: true, resumed: true` for every outcome — so a follow-up landed on an already-running successor via the successor-reuse path claimed that a new agent loop was re-dispatched. `resume_from_checkpoint_with_policy` now returns the receipt with truthful flags per the fields' own documented meanings: `resumed` = a new loop was re-dispatched from a checkpoint (only the fresh-resume path); `delivered` = the message actually went out (`woke && post-drain queue empty`, the same criterion `followup_child` uses internally — applied in both the direct-Running arm and the Interrupted arm). Settled successors answer from their existing result: a settled **Completed** successor reports `delivered=true` (result-carried); a settled **Failed/Cancelled/BudgetExhausted** successor reports `delivered=false` with a note naming its status — a follow-up that sits in no transcript and that nothing will ever answer is never presented as delivered. The public `resume_from_checkpoint` keeps its `SubAgentResult` contract (wrapped via `get_result`), so the coord tool path and existing callers are unchanged.

**TUI.** Focus following gated on `resumed` only, so a follow-up delivered to an existing successor left focus on the original (often finished) agent and named the wrong recipient. The guard now follows the successor on a new continuation **or** a successful delivery to an existing continuation; failure keeps focus unchanged and surfaces the note.

Disclosed: delivery to a settled Completed successor still reuses the pre-existing "Queued for {agent} — it reads it next round" toast message id; the wording doesn't describe a result-carried delivery, and a dedicated message means i18n churn across all packs — left as follow-up polish, not claimed fixed here.

## Issue

No-Issue: live multi-agent sessions left focus on a finished agent after retrying a follow-up onto its successor.

## How I tested it

- Red on base: the new engine test `user_follow_up_to_running_existing_successor_reports_delivery_without_resume` panics on base (base hardcodes `resumed: true`); green after — it asserts the running successor receives the text on its live channel and the outcome is `delivered=true, resumed=false, target=successor`.
- Second new test: a settled **Failed** successor yields `delivered=false` with the status-naming note (red on base, which claimed delivery).
- `dev-cargo.sh test -p codewhale-engine --lib user_follow_up` → 5 passed, 0 failed; `dev-cargo.sh test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- agent_focus follow_up` → 23 passed, 0 failed.
- Full engine lib suite on this machine: 88 failures on both the fix run and pristine main (environmental; 85 common). No test weakened; the failure accounting is in the commit body.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] N/A — behavior fix; docs/design/SUBAGENT_FOCUS.md runtime contract updated for the two existing-successor shapes

prs.title: fix(vision): accept absolute image paths that resolve inside the workspace
prs.body:
## What and why

The same asymmetry, on the read-only `image_analyze` lane: an absolute spelling of an image inside the workspace was refused by `resolve_image_path` before its containment check ever ran, while the relative form of the same file succeeded. `resolve_image_path` now admits absolute spellings through the same canonical containment the relative path already passes through (both sides canonicalized, component-aware `starts_with`).

Still refused, pinned by unchanged tests: absolute paths outside the workspace, `..` traversal in both spellings (including a non-existent escaping target, which gets the boundary message instead of a resolve error), and symlinks that resolve outside the workspace. The `image_path` schema itself spells no path form ("Path to the image file to analyze") — unlike the write/edit tools, which say "(relative or absolute)"; this aligns behavior across the tools that take workspace file paths.

Test-comment alignment: the trust-boundary pin on `execute_rejects_absolute_path` now states the precise invariant — an absolute path outside the workspace must be rejected, while an absolute path resolving inside is admitted through the same canonical containment as the relative spelling of the same file.

## Issue

prs.title: fix(bridges): rotate WeCom stream replies before the 10-minute expiry
prs.body:
## Problem

WeCom stream messages stop accepting updates after ~10 minutes:

```
{ errcode: 846608, errmsg: 'stream message update expired (>10 minutes), cannot update' }
```

`streamTurnEvents` keeps one `streamId` for the whole turn. A turn that runs longer (a report pipeline, a multi-step agent task) fails its next `replyStream`, the error surfaces as `Failed to handle WeCom message`, and the user never receives the final result even though the turn completed.

## Change

- `createStreamReply(client, frame, {rotateMs, now, genId})` in `wecom-bridge/src/lib.mjs`: finalizes the current stream ("…(continued)") and opens a fresh one when it is older than `rotateMs` (default 8 min), and reopens once when an update is rejected. Clock and id generation are injectable for tests.
- `streamTurnEvents` routes its three `replyStream` call sites through the helper.
- Unit tests for rotation and for the reopen-on-rejection path.

Verified live: a 12-minute turn now delivers its result as two messages instead of failing after minute 10.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: fix(bridges): surface WeCom API error details in bridge replies
prs.body:
## Problem

When the WeCom SDK rejects a call it throws a plain object, e.g.

```
{ errcode: 846608, errmsg: 'stream message update expired (>10 minutes), cannot update' }
```

The bridge's error formatter did `String(error?.message || error)`, which renders an object as `[object Object]`. Phone users get a reply like `Failed to handle WeCom message: [object Object]` with no actionable reason, and the log line loses the errcode too.

## Change

- Add a pure `formatPublicError()` in `wecom-bridge/src/lib.mjs`: renders `{errcode, errmsg}` objects as `errcode=<n>: <msg>`, falls back to `error.message`, then to a bounded `JSON.stringify`.
- `publicBridgeError()` in `src/index.mjs` now uses it (token redaction unchanged).
- Unit tests for the object, Error, string and undefined shapes.

Verified against a live rejection (errcode 846608) during a long-running turn.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: feat(tasks): pause the task wall clock for answerable human waits
prs.body:
## What and why

Upstream's turn layer already treats human waits as outside the budget — `crates/runtime/src/turn_budget.rs`: "the budget bounds what the agent spends on its own, not how long a person takes to answer." #6118 already suspends the task idle watchdog while an approval is pending. The durable task wall clock, however, still bounds a run parked on its own prompt — task_manager's #6118 note records that bound deliberately ("`0` waits indefinitely by configuration; the wall deadline still bounds the run"). For an automation run with no operator at the keyboard, that bound interrupts the run at the wall deadline, withdrawing the pending approval on the host's behalf (`ApprovalOutcome::Cancelled` — a withdrawal, not a denial) and discarding the run.

This pauses the durable task wall clock while a prompt on the run itself awaits a decision — deliberately relaxing that documented bound, and only where a decision surface can actually answer:

- `TaskManagerConfig::human_waits_answerable` (default **false** — TUI-managed tasks behave exactly as today). The app-server runtime API opts in: its tasks are answerable via `POST /v1/approvals/{id}` and `submit_user_input`.
- While a prompt is pending, the wall deadline moves with each closed window (preserving #5898's crossed-first attribution — a crossing before a window still terminalizes `WallTimeout` at the moved deadline). A 24h aggregate fail-safe cap (`human_wait_cap`, new `human_wait_timeout` terminal reason) bounds the exclusion across the whole task, and Cancel/Shutdown classification outranks a spent cap so a canceled task is never mislabeled.
- Parked decision polling backs off 200ms → 2s; a decision wakes it immediately.
- Idle handling composes with #6118 (unchanged): a window close restarts the idle budget fresh.

`[approval] timeout_seconds` is unchanged and remains the lever for bounding the wait on the human's side; this changes only the task supervisor's accounting. The feature row `thread-scheduled-turns` in docs/features.toml is updated (its `api` surface is where the opt-in lives).

## Issue

No-Issue: extends the documented turn-layer human-wait philosophy to the durable task layer; complements #6118 (unchanged).

## How I tested it

- Red-on-base evidence via mutation runs recorded in the commit (raw wall clock, cap hoisted above cancel/shutdown, aggregate arm removed, gate removed, server flag off — each flips a named test).
- Targeted suites: `human_wait`/`execution_guard` filters → 21 passed, 0 failed (two new ordering/attribution pins included: cancel outranks a spent **parked** cap; `WallTimeout` attribution at the moved deadline); task_manager module → 101 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; app-server `server_task` pins → 2 passed; `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` → 2 passed.
- Zero-regression pin: an unanswerable (default) surface still wall-times out through a prompt, asserting no window is armed.
- Honest limits: the `run_http_server` call-site hop is not test-pinned (pinning it requires booting the server); the two runtime_api pins cover the builder and executor-forward hops.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] User-facing feature: docs/RUNTIME_API.md updated and the `thread-scheduled-turns` row in docs/features.toml updated (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` passes)

prs.title: fix(workspace): stop a home workspace from refusing its own junctioned state directory
prs.body:
## What and why

A session started in the user's home directory treats that directory as its
workspace, and four call sites then hold it to workspace confinement. That is
wrong on its own 鈥?home is not a repository 鈥?but it breaks outright for the
supported layout where `~/.codewhale` is a directory junction onto another
volume (on Windows, `mklink /J C:\Users\<user>\.codewhale D:\CodeWhaleData`).
The junction reads as a link escaping the workspace, so the state directory is
refused as a whole:

- **skills**: 60 of 90 skills silently disappeared, leaving only `~/.agents`,
  with one warning (`Refusing symlinked path C:\Users\<user>\.codewhale`).
- **fleet roster**: every profile under `~/.codewhale/agents` was skipped.
- **subagent coordination**: the shared ledger never appended
  (`state path must not traverse symlinks`).
- **workflow journal**: `workflow-runs.jsonl` could be neither read nor written.

This follows the same class of failure as #6947, #6949 and #7098 鈥?a
user-owned relocated root treated as if it were untrusted repository content.
Those three already fixed the session, artifact and sub-agent state paths; the
four entry points here were never converted.

`workspace_is_user_home` and `workspace_state_path` put that decision in one
place. The root a link walk starts from is the whole question, because
`reject_linked_path` never examines the root itself:

- A **home** workspace resolves its own `~/.codewhale` once and uses the target
  as the root. The junction is where the user chose to keep state, and
  everything below it is still walked.
- **Every other** workspace keeps itself as the root with `.codewhale` still
  inside the walked path, so a repository-supplied link is refused exactly as
  it was before. Lowering the root instead would have made
  `<repo>/.codewhale` transparent 鈥?readable profiles with their `trust` and
  `permissions` fields, a journal writing outside the repository, and a lock
  creating directories through the link.

A state directory that exists but cannot be resolved falls back to the strict
root, so an unreachable junction fails closed rather than starting a second
state tree beside the one that cannot be reached.

The skills exemption is per directory rather than per workspace: only the home
state directory skips confinement, so links under any other home directory are
still refused and still warn.

## Issue

No-Issue: repairs state-path resolution for a home workspace; related junction reports are already closed.

## How I tested it

Reported honestly as it stands. CI owns fmt, clippy, the Linux suite and the
Windows build on the final base; the runs below were made on this branch before
it was carried onto current `main`, so the counts are what they were there, not
a claim about the merge commit.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 鈫?passed.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-util` 鈫?**41 passed; 0 failed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-skills` 鈫?**174 passed; 0 failed**.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the draft when the command palette inserts a command
prs.body:
## What and why

Picking a command that takes an argument from the palette, such as `/rename`, replaces the composer with `/rename `, and whatever you'd typed is gone. History search can't find it either, because nothing stashed it. With `my draft` typed, then Ctrl+K, `rename`, Enter, Alt+R and `my`:

Before:

```
╭History search ──────
│my
│  No matches
```

After:

```
╭History search ──────
│my
│ ▸ my draft
```

The hotbar does the same insert in `prefill_composer` and calls `clear_input_recoverable` first. The palette's `InsertText` arm now does too.

Stashing goes through `clear_input`, which releases the command claim, so the insert now claims the line when its text starts with `/`. Without that, a typed `/xyz` replaced by `/rename` and then pasted past 16,000 characters goes to the model as prose instead of being held. An empty composer already did that on `main`; it holds now too. Palette entries that insert a bare name stay unclaimed.

## Issue

No-Issue: inserting a command from the palette loses the composer draft; I searched and found no issue for it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at b157e004b in a pseudo-terminal at 100x34 with an empty HOME and the steps above; the rows above come from those runs. The hold above came from pasting 17,600 characters after the insert and pressing Enter: over a typed `/xyz`, `main` holds it, and over an empty composer `main` sends it, while this change holds both and the mock server gets no chat request. I didn't run the bare-name entries.

prs.title: fix(compaction): repair pre-v0.10.0 topology checkpoint placement on restore
prs.body:
## What and why

Sessions saved by v0.9.10–v0.9.12 that compacted with live sub-agents place the agent-topology checkpoint at the END of the history (`messages.push`, since de062ebd1); the save-time placement anchor landed only in 1f5f3a7e6 (first released in v0.10.0). On current main, restoring such a session rewrites the sidecar in place, and the request-time reorder in `build_chat_messages` moves only the summary — leaving a `tool → user` role adjacency that strict Chat-Completions templates reject with `HTTP 400: response_role: "user"`.

This repairs the misplaced sidecar at restore time:

- `relocate_restored_compaction_topology` moves the carrier to the same anchor save-time placement writes (derived from the save-time predicate, not a parallel definition; a shared `carries_tool_result` so save and restore cannot drift). Relocate-only — nothing is deleted; pasted summary headers are never moved; the boundary is era-aware (post-provenance vs legacy).
- The save-time retire now removes both live and restored-display carriers, so restore → re-compact cannot persist a superseded duplicate beside the fresh checkpoint.
- The checkpoint-less restore path no longer drops wire-format checkpoints (production derives the checkpoint from the history itself, so this was unreachable; it matches the legacy branch's documented intent).

Disclosed boundaries: the TUI App mirror (`install_restored_api_messages`, serving /fork //branch //import) stays projection-only and engine-authoritative — a transient mirror divergence self-heals on the next engine `SessionUpdated`. In pre-provenance histories a pasted legacy header is still read as the summary boundary (era-qualified and pinned by tests). A carrier saved directly after an assistant-like message with no checkpoint in its window stays in place (wire-legal, no 400). Engine-saved sessions placed by the current anchor restore byte-identical; a host-imported history carrying an older summary before an anchored carrier is shuffled (wire-legal; self-heals at the next save via the both-forms retire).

## Issue

No-Issue: repairs sessions saved by v0.9.10–v0.9.12; the wire-role family itself landed via #6857/#7017 — this closes their restore-time gap.

## How I tested it

- Red first on current main: `restore_relocates_pre_anchor_topology_sidecar_saved_after_tool_result` failed with the carrier directly after the tool result (expected the anchor after the user prompt).
- After the fix: `scripts/dev-test.sh engine restore_` → 34 passed, 0 failed (10 new compaction tests + 1 wire-level test in `client/chat.rs`, all named in the commit body).
- Full engine lib suite on this machine: 88 failures on both the fix run and pristine main (environmental; the sets differ by ~3 timing-flaky tests per side, 85 common). Each new test also passes individually by name.

prs.title: fix(engine): match brace and nested-directory globs in grep_files
prs.body:
## What and why

`grep_files` drops several ordinary glob forms without saying so. With these as `include` it returns no matches and no error, so the model reads that as "nothing here":

```
{"pattern":"needle","include":["*.{txt,md}"]}
{"matches":[],"total_matches":0,"files_searched":0,"truncated":false}
```

In a tree with `root.txt`, `root.md`, `src/a.txt`, `src/b.md`, `src/deep/c.txt`, `src/deep/er/d.txt` and `deep/e.txt`:

```
*.{txt,md}         none -> all 7
**/*.{txt,md}      none -> all 7
{src,deep}/*.txt   none -> deep/e.txt and the 3 .txt under src
**/deep/*.txt      none -> deep/e.txt, src/deep/c.txt, src/deep/er/d.txt
src/**/deep/**     none -> src/deep/c.txt, src/deep/er/d.txt
**/deep/**         missed deep/e.txt, now includes it
```

`exclude` goes through the same function: `*.{txt,md}` excluded nothing, and `**/deep/**` left `deep/e.txt` in.

`matches_glob` had no brace support, and the text after `**` was only tried against one path component, so anything with a `/` in it could never match. It now expands `{a,b}` first and lets `**/` cover zero or more directories when what follows names a path. An unclosed `{` or one with no comma stays literal, and so does a pattern past 64 brace combinations, since each one is tried for every file.

Two things get narrower. `**/a/b` used to match `xa/b` through `ends_with`, and now needs a directory boundary. And a wildcard after `**` now has to match the file itself: `src/**/*.txt` used to take `src/vendor.txt/main.py` because a directory on the way matched. A literal such as `**/deep` still covers what's under that directory. Not touched: `[ab].txt` still matches nothing, and `*` in `src/*.txt` still crosses directories, which the `node_modules/*` example in the schema relies on.

## Issue

No-Issue: brace and nested-directory globs in grep_files silently match nothing; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at f4978e8fa in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server that scripts the tool calls, and read the results it received, for 28 patterns. Only the ones above changed, plus `{src,deep}/**/*.txt`, `{src,deep}/**/*.{txt,md}`, `**/src/**/*.txt`, `**/er/*.txt` and a multi-pattern include; `*.txt`, `src/**`, `src/*.txt`, `**/deep` and `exclude: ["src/**"]` return the same files on both. 20 `{a,b}` groups return nothing on this build; I didn't time it.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-engine --lib`, twice: 6962 of 7053 passed, with 68 `tools::search` and glob tests among them. The 91 failures are the same ones that fail on f4978e8fa without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-engine`: clean. `cargo clippy --no-deps -p codewhale-engine` with CI's flags on 1.99 reports errors in 13 files, none of them `search.rs`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on f4978e8fa; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one

prs.title: feat(bridges): accept media and voice messages on the WeCom bridge
prs.body:
## Problem

The bridge rejects every non-text frame with `目前仅支持文本消息`. For a phone user that is the most natural interaction being unavailable: send the photo/video/file you want the agent to work on. Voice messages (which WeCom transcribes) are equally dropped.

Two extra defects while wiring this up:

- Media frames carry **no text**, and `stripGroupPrefix` returns `accepted: false` for empty text — media would be dropped **silently** if routed through it.
- Download links in media frames are valid for **~5 minutes**, so the download must start immediately and failures must tell the user to re-send.

## Change

- `video` / `file` / `image` frames: reply "downloading…", fetch via `client.downloadFile(url, aeskey)`, save under a configurable directory (`WECOM_MEDIA_DIR`, default `<workspace>/media`) with a sanitized filename, reply with the saved name, size and path. Failures name the 5-minute expiry.
- `voice` frames: the transcribed `voice.content` is used as the prompt text.
- Other message types get an explicit polite answer instead of the blanket refusal.
- `sanitizeFilename()` in `src/lib.mjs` with unit tests (path separators, control chars, leading dots, length cap, fallback).

Verified live: a 100 MB-class video and photos sent from the phone land in the media directory and the follow-up instruction can reference them. WeCom media caps (video 10 MB for sending back, links expire ~5 min) are documented in the PR for reviewers.

No-Issue: live defects found while running the WeCom bridge against a real bot; each fix carries its error evidence and tests

prs.title: fix(bridges): cap WeCom reply chunks by UTF-8 bytes
prs.body:
## Problem

WeCom caps a single message at **4096 UTF-8 bytes**. `splitMessage` counts characters, so a Chinese reply of 3500 chars (~10.5 KB) was sent as one chunk and WeCom delivered it **silently truncated** — no error to the bridge, no log, the user just receives cut-off text. Observed live with a 10 KB Chinese report rendered in three different ways on the phone vs. on disk.

## Change

- `bridge-core` `splitMessage(text, maxChars, maxBytes = 0)`: when `maxBytes > 0`, any chunk whose UTF-8 size exceeds it is re-split on code-point boundaries (never mid-character). Opt-in; all existing callers keep current behavior.
- `wecom-bridge` `replyText` passes `config.maxReplyBytes` (default 3800, ~8% headroom; env `WECOM_MAX_REPLY_BYTES`).
- Tests: CJK text over the byte cap splits into byte-bounded chunks that reassemble to the original; short/mixed stays single; cap stays opt-in.

Verified live: a ~10 KB report now arrives complete in multiple messages.

prs.title: fix(subagent): only scan nested repositories at the worktree anchor
prs.body:
## What and why

`git_repo_root` (worktree isolation for subagents) scans the children of every ancestor while walking up to `MAX_PARENT_LEVELS`. Now only the anchor itself may adopt nested checkouts (a harness or session directory wrapping one repository); ancestors are probed for containment only. The narrowing also removes base's silent single-repo ancestor adoption — a non-repository workspace under a directory containing exactly one unrelated repository was silently adopted before. That removal is intentional: the same defect family as the multi-repo ambiguity error.

No-Issue: incident-driven fix (a live multi-agent session's workspace walked up to the home directory and reported the user's other projects).

prs.title: fix(engine): report file_search results from the workspace root
prs.body:
## What and why

`file_search` with a `path` returns matches relative to that path, while `read` and the other tools resolve from the workspace. So a search that's scoped correctly hands back a path that means a different file. In a repo with `package.json` at the root and in `packages/app`, `{"query":"package.json","path":"packages/app"}`:

Before:

```
[{"path":"package.json","name":"package.json","score":1.0}]
```

Reading that path gives `{"name":"root"}`, with no error. The file it found holds `{"name":"app"}`.

After:

```
[{"path":"packages/app/package.json","name":"package.json","score":1.0}]
```

The other shapes went wrong too: a `path` naming one file returned `""`, and `{"query":"**/*.json","path":"packages"}` returned `app/package.json`, which doesn't exist. They now return `packages/app/package.json`.

The reported path is now built the way `grep_files` builds its own: strip the workspace or its canonical form, and leave anything outside it absolute. Ranking and exclusions still use the path relative to the search root, so what matches doesn't change. A search with no `path` returns what it did. I didn't run a search outside the workspace; going by the code, that returns absolute paths where it used to return ones relative to the search root.

## Issue

No-Issue: file_search paths are relative to its path argument, so reading a result can open a different file; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at f4978e8fa in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server that scripts the tool calls, and read the tool results it received; the results above come from those runs. The cases were `packages/app`, `./packages/../packages/app`, the absolute path, a single file, a glob under `packages`, and no `path`. The server scripted the `read` too, so a real model picking that path is my inference.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-engine --lib`, twice with this change and once on f4978e8fa: 91 tests fail on `main`, all of them here too, and 41 `file_search` and `tools::search` tests pass. One more fails here both times, `auto_review_force_prompt_is_denied_without_opening_a_modal`: run alone with this change it failed 2 of 5, and it's in the failures on #7205, which only touches the TUI. In the second round `lifecycle_bulk_followup_preserves_mappings_and_retries_without_duplicate_workers` hung and I ended it after 69 minutes; it passed in 2.6 s in the first round.

issues.title: [Feature]: Support keyterm prompting in ElevenLabs batch transcription

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.

issues.title: [Feature]: Search and send native Zalo stickers through the existing zalouser channel

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Support native sticker search and sending in the official Zalo Personal plugin using the existing `sticker-search` and `sticker` message actions.

### Problem to solve

An OpenClaw extension author built a [patch for `@openclaw/zalouser`](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md) so group replies could include a native Zalo sticker selected by an emotion keyword. The [implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js) locates and rewrites the installed plugin's generated JavaScript, then calls `getStickers`, `getStickersDetail`, and `sendSticker` on its existing client. This is a concrete use case for sending a platform sticker object from an OpenClaw group conversation; an image attachment or emoji is a different output.

At [OpenClaw main `82c8ad576b31`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts), the plugin exposes only `react` as an additional shared message action. Its separate [`zalouser` tool](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts) accepts text, image, link, directory, profile, and status operations, with no sticker operation. Users of the official channel cannot perform this task through its supported actions.

The patch is historical, with its latest commit dated June 8, 2026. The same author's current [Setup project](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-setup/blob/0f12991d9787c1d3cf331b8b9ba1a256df2d559f/README.md) says the old integration and Sticker add-on were retired in favor of a maintained alternative channel. That is a valid solution. This request concerns supporting the same native object in the existing official channel, without maintaining a private patch or adopting another channel runtime. Current demand to migrate back to the official channel is unknown.

### Proposed solution

Extend the existing `zalouser` channel action adapter; add no new core action, tool, SDK surface, credential store, or channel.

- `sticker-search`: for the selected account and an authorized group conversation, accept a bounded keyword query and return a bounded set of native sticker choices. Each choice must include a send-compatible selector carrying the native sticker ID, category ID, and type. Reuse the existing `query`, `limit`, and `stickerId`/`fileId` fields where appropriate. Exact selector encoding is a plugin implementation decision.
- `sticker`: send exactly one selected native sticker to that group using the same account/profile and existing target resolution and action authorization. Return the platform message ID and normal channel delivery result. Reject malformed selectors and unsupported targets before sending.
- Reuse the current plugin's API/session owner and cancellation/effect-boundary handling. Include the native `/api/group/sticker` POST in its dispatch tracking. Stop before submission if the admitted operation is canceled or no longer current. An ambiguous network outcome must not trigger a blind resend or a claim of confirmed delivery.

Initial scope is explicit group sticker search and send. Suggested search budget: default 5, maximum 10 choices; these are proposed resource bounds, not Zalo API limits. No automatic interpretation of `[Sticker: ...]` in ordinary text, automatic emotional replies, mention changes, sticker uploads, whole-catalog collection, or DM support is requested.

### Alternatives considered

- **Alternative channel:** [OpenClaw Zalo Connect](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-zalo-connect/blob/0e5908c6ccc00cde6f539a82fd82086fc90285de/README.md) already advertises native stickers and many other actions. It is a valid option. The remaining proposed benefit is for installations retaining the official `zalouser` channel and its current account/session owner; no claim is made that all OpenClaw users are blocked.
- **Patch the generated plugin:** the cited implementation targets generated `zalo-js-*.js` files. It expresses the exact missing behavior, but does not establish compatibility with current main. We have not executed it.
- **Skill or separate tool:** a skill can call supported tools, but cannot obtain this missing behavior from the official tool's closed action enum. A separate code plugin could own another Zalo connection or use an alternative channel's bridge; the official channel's client implementation is private. This does not establish a missing generic SDK contract.
- **Send an image, emoji, or reaction:** these remain useful existing outputs but do not send a native sticker object.

### Impact

- Affected: users who retain the official Zalo Personal channel and want native sticker replies in groups. A historical plugin patch demonstrates the task; the current affected population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: this particular output is unavailable through the official channel; text, media, and reactions remain usable. No urgent incident or quantitative severity has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Keyword-based group replies are described by the source; no usage frequency has been measured.
- Practical consequences: the documented approaches are patching generated plugin code or using a different channel. No time savings, user counts, or account-migration failure rates are claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original task and patch](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md), plus [native lookup/send implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js), commit `6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2`. This is implementation evidence, not an independently observed live send.
- [Current channel action adapter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts) and [optional tool schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts). A pinned scan of the plugin's non-test TypeScript, JSON, and Markdown found no sticker implementation.
- The plugin already pins [`zca-js` 2.2.0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/package.json). That package's published Git revision `dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9` contains [`getStickers`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickers.ts), [`getStickersDetail`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickersDetail.ts), and [`sendSticker`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/sendSticker.ts). The last accepts `id`, `cateId`, and `type`, supports group targets, and returns `msgId`.
- [Shared action vocabulary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts) and [schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/agents/tools/message-tool-schema.ts) already contain sticker search/send concepts. This is an adapter gap, not a new common contract.
- PRs [#27905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/27905) and [#29075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/29075) concern `zalo` Bot API inbound handling and emoji replies; neither supplies `zalouser` native sticker sending. Both are closed and unmerged at the research time.

Research is static. No dependency installation, external patch execution, paid service, account login, or authenticated Zalo delivery was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Implementation entry points are the plugin's `channel.ts` action descriptor/handler, its lazy `channel.runtime.ts` exports, the private `zca-client.ts` API typing, and the existing `zalo-js.ts` API/session owner. The existing [`send-context.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-context.ts) checks cancellation and current effect authority; its message dispatch path matcher currently excludes `/sticker`. Reuse that owner and [`send-receipt.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-receipt.ts) rather than introducing a second sender. These are implementation suggestions, not a claim that the change has been built.

Preserve plugin lazy loading, existing account isolation, target and access policies, credential ownership, and current delivery outcome semantics. No configuration migration, new persistent catalog, new authorization scope, or dependency upgrade is proposed. Search can return fewer choices when detail lookup is partial; it must not claim catalog completeness. The existing unofficial Zalo integration and its account/platform limitations continue to apply. No implementer has committed. Selector encoding and the exact bounded search defaults remain owner decisions.

Acceptance criteria:

1. In an authorized group conversation on a configured `zalouser` account, search a keyword, choose one returned selector, and send it through the shared message tool. Zalo displays one native sticker in that group and the tool reports its platform message ID.
2. The selected account/profile is used for lookup and send. Another configured account is not silently selected; malformed selectors and unsupported non-group targets do not issue a sticker POST.
3. Cancellation or retirement during lookup/session preparation prevents a later send. A recorded accepted send retains its ID; an uncertain outcome is not reported as confirmed or blindly retried.
4. Empty/partially unavailable search results are bounded and explicit. Existing text/media/react paths continue to work, and ordinary text containing `[Sticker: ...]` does not acquire a new side effect.

An implementer should run focused action, routing, send-context, and receipt tests, then the affected plugin checks and startup profiler. A real authorized Zalo group is needed to verify native rendering and actual transport outcomes; mocked API responses alone cannot establish that acceptance criterion.

issues.body:
### Summary

The header-probe timeout from #187150 is fixed by #187197 (in 2026.11.5-beta.1), but on an affected install the fix can't be reached with `openclaw update`. From 2026.10.10, updating to 2026.11.5-beta.1 fails with the same `spawnSync node ETIMEDOUT` in `package-update`. The probe that times out is the installed 2026.10.10 one, not the candidate's: the `package-update` step runs it through the retained update runtime, a copy of the installed package. So the fixed release does not help the installs that need it most.

### Environment

- From OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), npm global install
- To 2026.11.5-beta.1 (also tried 2026.11.1, the current `latest`, which doesn't include #187197)
- Ubuntu 25.10, x86_64, Node v24.22.1, 4 vCPU
- Update run from ssh in the user systemd manager (`systemd-run --user ... openclaw update --tag 2026.11.5-beta.1 --yes`), gateway running
- About 160k files under the state dir. The probe worker takes 10.3 s for 32.6k of them and 44 s for all of them, so one batch of everything can't finish in 10 s.

### What happened

1. `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.5-beta.1 --yes` failed in `validating`:
   ```
   Update safety checks ran in the candidate updater (2026.11.5-beta.1).
   Failed: package-update — Exit code: 1; Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. ...
   Failing check package-update (global-install-failed): ... | spawnSync [redacted-path]
   ```
   `stderrTail` in the saved failure JSON: `... | spawnSync /usr/local/bin/node ETIMEDOUT | ETIMEDOUT`. The "Original state capture is unavailable" warning shows the same ETIMEDOUT, before `package-install` has even run.
2. The retained runtime (`/usr/lib/openclaw-update-runtime-*/tree/.../openclaw`) has `package.json` version `2026.10.10` and the same `dist/backup-sqlite-snapshot-BdHXmJd5.mjs` as the installed package: one `spawnSync` over every path with `timeout: 1e4`.
3. I changed only the installed `dist/backup-sqlite-snapshot-BdHXmJd5.mjs`, replacing `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders` with the 4,096-path batched version from 2026.11.5-beta.1. The candidate package and the state were left alone.
4. The same update command then passed every step: `candidate-state-snapshot`, `candidate-doctor`, `candidate-gateway-startup`, activation, restart and verification. The updater detected the local dist edit, kept it in a recovery bundle and didn't replay it (as documented for `--reapply-local-overrides`), so the result is the clean 2026.11.5-beta.1 package.

### Expected

The fix for a backup-path bug should also cover the backup the updater runs on the way to the fixed version. Possible fixes:
- run the `package-update` pre-install backup (and the original-state capture) with the candidate's backup code instead of the installed copy, or
- backport #187197 to the 2026.10.x / 2026.11.x stable line (and to `extended-stable`), so there is an intermediate release whose own updater can get through, or
- when the installed updater's probe times out, say so and point to a supported way forward, instead of the generic "check that the source files are readable" message.

### Workaround for anyone else stuck on 2026.10.10

Take your own SQLite backups first (`sqlite3 <db> ".backup <out>"` for each `*.sqlite` under the state dir). Then replace `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders` in the installed `dist/backup-sqlite-snapshot-*.mjs` with the batched version from 2026.11.5-beta.1 (`src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts` after #187197), and run `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.5-beta.1` again. The updater keeps the edit in `~/.openclaw/update-recovery/` and installs the clean package.

Related: #187150 (fixed by #187197), #192991, #193591 (another 2026.10.10 → 2026.11.1 failure with the same stderr).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In the macOS app’s realtime Talk interface, spoken replies repeatedly stopped after a few words while the transcript continued, and temporary gateway instrumentation confirmed client-requested cancellations with reason playback-overflow.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed reproduction on the affected installation (not yet reproduced on a clean upstream build):
1. Open the macOS app and start realtime Talk using OpenAI with gateway-relay and agent-consult.
2. Keep the microphone unmuted and ask for a three-sentence response.
3. Listen to the reply and compare it with the live transcript.
4. Repeat over several exchanges.

Cutoffs recurred after fully quitting/reopening the app, with macOS Voice Isolation both enabled and disabled.

### Expected behavior

Multi-sentence replies should play to completion. As a concrete local comparison, after the combined workaround described below, the reporter completed three consecutive back-and-forth exchanges with multi-sentence replies and no audible cutoffs. No known-good unmodified version has been established.

### Actual behavior

Spoken replies frequently stopped after the first few words. The live transcript could advance beyond the audio heard, making text and speech appear mismatched. Temporary cancellation-reason logging identified playback-overflow in two test sessions; this does not establish the cause of every earlier cutoff.

### OpenClaw version

Control UI 2026.9.4; build 2026.9.4-release-3a9d69db306c-2026-09-10T22-53-16.719Z

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2

### Install method

Native macOS OpenClaw app with embedded Control UI and local gateway; bundled Node.js 24.19.0

### Model

Realtime configured model: gpt-realtime-2.1; main text agent: openrouter/auto

### Provider / routing chain

macOS embedded Control UI → local gateway → OpenAI realtime; brain=agent-consult; main text agent routes through OpenRouter

### Additional provider/model setup details

Realtime mode=realtime, transport=gateway-relay, brain=agent-consult, provider=openai, voice=cedar. During diagnosis: vadThreshold=0.92, silenceDurationMs=2000, talk.silenceTimeoutMs=2000, talk.interruptOnSpeech=false. No credentials are included.

### Logs

```shell
Temporary diagnostic added to the gateway talk.session.cancelOutput handler; only allowlisted cancellation reasons were recorded. Sanitized excerpt:

[gateway] [voice-diagnostic] cancel reason=playback-overflow

The same reason was observed in two sessions. Normal logs showed talk.session.cancelOutput requests but did not include their reason.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Installed-code inspection: in control-ui-boot-shared-Bhb-1aO7.js, the PCM playback queue had a 10-second queued-audio limit and a 320-source limit. An overflow result triggered cancellation of the current output with reason playback-overflow.

Synthetic reproduction: a harness extracted the installed queue implementation and used a mocked Web Audio context. It supplied 60 chunks of 250 ms PCM16 audio at 24 kHz, advancing the playback clock by 25 ms per chunk (15 seconds of audio arriving in approximately 1.5 seconds).
- At the 10-second limit, overflow occurred at approximately 1.1 seconds of simulated playback.
- At a 60-second limit, all 15 seconds queued successfully.

This demonstrates overflow under bursty delivery, not that the live provider delivered this exact pattern. The mock does not reproduce browser scheduling, microphone behavior, or actual provider timing.

### Impact and severity

Observed on one macOS installation. Repeated cutoffs blocked normal back-and-forth voice conversation across multiple tests. Text could remain visible while the corresponding speech was incomplete. Frequency was repeated during testing; no broader prevalence or data-loss claim is made.

### Additional information

Local workaround and limitations:
- Increased playback queue limits from 10 to 60 seconds and from 320 to 2048 sources.
- Removed the independent amplitude-based barge-in cancellation call from the microphone pump.
- Paused microphone transmission during output playback and for approximately 350 ms afterward.
- Served modified Control UI assets under a fresh versioned path, then restarted the app and gateway.

The reporter then completed three consecutive exchanges with multi-sentence replies and no audible cutoffs. Earlier changes and cache clearing had not reliably resolved the issue. Fresh asset URLs removed stale-code ambiguity, but stale caching was not independently proven. Multiple changes remained active, so this is not an A/B confirmation that a larger queue alone resolves the live issue. Microphone gating prevents normal spoken interruption during playback; the workaround is not proposed as a production-ready patch.

Manual microphone muting had helped in an earlier test. Unexpected user transcripts were also observed, but their cause and relationship to overflow remain unverified. No test against current upstream main has been performed.

Suggested investigation: examine the fixed queue limits under bursty realtime output, bounded buffering/backpressure, transcript/playback consistency after cancellation, and default logging of cancellation reasons.

Prepared with AI assistance and checked against observed logs and user-reported tests. No API keys, authentication material, personal conversation excerpts, session identifiers, or raw logs are included.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

During macOS setup, onboarding remained stuck after OpenRouter credentials/model were configured through the CLI and gateway inference succeeded; recovery required clearing the pending onboarding preference and completing the skip/local-connection flow.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

Once the local provider configuration supports successful inference, onboarding should allow reaching the normal app. The grounded comparison is the same installation after the recovery steps below: text chat worked using the same OpenRouter configuration. No known-good earlier release has been established.

### Actual behavior

The user could not complete initial API-key onboarding. The displayed setup was for OpenAI, while the available key was for OpenRouter. Credentials and model were then configured through the CLI. A setup inference probe initially reported no OpenRouter key; after restarting the gateway, OpenRouter inference succeeded, but the native onboarding flow remained stuck. It was eventually recovered by clearing openclaw.onboardingSystemAgentPending, choosing Set up later, selecting the Local connection, and restarting the app.

This report concerns the stuck onboarding/recovery state. It does not claim that an OpenAI credential field should accept an OpenRouter key, that the key was invalid, or that the preference alone caused the failure.

### OpenClaw version

Observed 2026-09-12; contemporaneous gateway log identifies native client OpenClaw/2609000490. Exact semantic app version at that moment was not captured.

### Operating system

macOS; contemporaneous client log reports Darwin/25.6.0. System subsequently checked as macOS 26.6.2.

### Install method

Native macOS app, reinstalled using the desktop installer; local gateway

### Model

openrouter/auto configured during recovery; initially no working model configuration

### Provider / routing chain

Native macOS onboarding → local gateway → OpenRouter using openai-completions; OpenAI-oriented key setup was initially displayed

### Additional provider/model setup details

The OpenRouter credential was saved through the supported CLI auth command, and openrouter/auto was configured as the default model. No credential values or authentication database contents are included. Gateway restart was part of the recovery.

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized observations from the 2026-09-12 gateway log (local timestamps; identifiers and filesystem paths omitted):

18:22:13 config hot reload applied (auth.profiles)
18:22:26 config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.openrouter, agents.defaults.model, agents.defaults.models)
18:22:44 setup-inference probe: No API key found for provider "openrouter"
18:24:35 gateway startup: agent model openrouter/openrouter/auto
18:24:52 model-fetch response: provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=openrouter/auto status=200
18:27:19 model-fetch response: provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=openrouter/auto status=200

These logs corroborate provider recovery. The stuck native onboarding state and preference recovery were observed during troubleshooting, not established by these gateway log lines alone.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Historical sequence from the affected installation, not a deterministic clean-install reproduction:
1. Reinstalled the native app and attempted onboarding with an OpenRouter key while an OpenAI setup screen was shown.
2. Saved the OpenRouter key through the CLI and configured openrouter/auto.
3. Restarted the gateway; a text inference test succeeded.
4. Native onboarding remained stuck.
5. Removed the openclaw.onboardingSystemAgentPending preference, used Set up later, selected Local connection, and restarted the app. Normal text chat became usable.

No screenshot or exact UI error string from the initial failure was retained. The currently working installation has not been reset to reproduce this issue.

### Impact and severity

Observed during one user’s macOS reinstall/onboarding attempt. It blocked completing setup through the ordinary UI and required CLI configuration plus manual onboarding-state recovery. Frequency across other installations is unknown.

### Additional information

Please investigate how native onboarding reconciles externally configured provider credentials and model readiness, and whether a pending system-agent setup can leave onboarding blocked after inference succeeds. issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a channel using the default reply mode (`messages.visibleReplies` unset → `automatic`), a `message(action=send)` to the current conversation without `final: false` ends the turn: the assistant's final text is never delivered and nothing is logged. Worked in 2026.10.9; first observed on 2026.10.10.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a channel with default reply settings (`messages.visibleReplies` and `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies` unset → `automatic`). A third-party channel plugin is fine; the drop happens in core before the plugin is called.
2. In one turn, call `message` with `action=send`, an explicit `to` equal to the current conversation, non-empty text, and no `final` field.
3. End the same turn with a normal assistant text block.

### Expected behavior

Both messages arrive: the tool payload and the final assistant text. This is what 2026.10.3 through 2026.10.9 do on the same install and the same channel.

### Actual behavior

- The `message` tool payload arrives.
- The final assistant text is never sent: no warning, no error, no delivery record.
- The text does exist in the stored transcript, so the turn looks complete from the gateway side.
- Repeating the identical turn with `final: false` on the tool call delivers both messages.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (7dc3350), npm global. Also checked 2026.11.1 (`latest`): same code path, same missing gate.

### Operating system

Windows 10.0.19045 (x64), Node 24.22.1

### Install method

npm global (`npm i -g openclaw`)

### Model

tokenrhythm/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> tokenrhythm (OpenAI-compatible gateway) -> deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Additional provider/model setup details

Default agent model; no per-agent overrides. Model choice appears irrelevant: the drop happens after the model returns a normal final text (`stopReason: "stop"`).

### Logs

Channel-side log (NapCat `run.log`) around the affected turn — three sends, then nothing:

```
19:26:27 [info] 鲸汐 | 发送 -> 群聊 [group] 【测试1】...
19:26:27 [info] 鲸汐 | 发送 -> 群聊 [group] 【测试2】...
19:26:36 [info] 鲸汐 | 发送 -> 群聊 [group] 【测试3】...
(no send and no error at 19:26:51, when the final assistant text was produced)
```

Gateway log for that second contains no `channel/qq` activity, only unrelated provider lines.

Message-tool result from the same turn:

```json
{
  "channel": "qq",
  "to": "<group id>",
  "via": "direct",
  "result": { "channel": "qq", "messageId": "1593727536", "deliveredAt": 1793877988433 },
  "deliveryStatus": "sent",
  "payloadOutcomes": [{ "index": 0, "status": "sent", "resultCount": 1 }],
  "sourceReplyRoute": "current-source"
}
```

```json
"messageDelivery": {
  "status": "settled",
  "primaryPlatformMessageId": "431090118",
  "partialDelivery": false,
  "createdThreadIds": [],
  "sourceReplyDelivered": true
}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Transcript row exists for the undelivered text (`stopReason: "stop"`, same turn, message id `51666fa9-a9a6-48b3-8917-5a3cd76d8c61`); the channel log has no send for it. That contrast is the core evidence: generation succeeded, delivery never reached the channel.

Code comparison (read from unpacked dist of the published tarballs):

2026.10.9, `dist/builtin-openclaw-BxzDR6yL.mjs:13691`:

```js
function installMessageToolOnlyTerminalHook(params) {
    if (params.sourceReplyDeliveryMode !== "message_tool_only") return;   // gate present
    ...
        if (resolveMessageToolSourceReplyFinal(argsRecordForToolCall(context))) return {
            ...hookResult,
            terminate: true
        };
```

2026.10.10, `dist/sdk-B0aTjN8h.mjs:856` (2026.11.1: `sdk-DEC4X1Rn.mjs:856`), installed from `builtin-openclaw-4RNo5CR8.mjs:8986` with identical arguments:

```js
function installMessageToolTerminalHook(params) {
    let finalSourceReplyDelivered = false;        // no mode gate
    const previousCompletion = getInternalToolTurnCompletion(params.agent);
    setInternalToolTurnCompletion(params.agent, (context) => {
        const completed = finalSourceReplyDelivered;
        finalSourceReplyDelivered = false;
        return previousCompletion?.(context) === true || completed;
    });
    ...
        if (delivered) {
            finalSourceReplyDelivered ||= final;
            params.onDeliveredSourceReply?.();
        }
        return delivered && final ? { ...hookResult, terminate: true } : hookResult;
```

`onDeliveredSourceReply` sets `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool = true`, which marks the run as already replied, so the final text is filtered out.

`isDeliveredMessageToolOnlySourceReplyResult()` stays mode-aware but returns `true` for any send whose result carries `sourceReplyRoute: "current-source"`, which an ordinary in-chat send does:

```js
if (params.sourceReplyDeliveryMode !== "message_tool_only" && !confirmedCurrentSourceRoute && params.allowExplicitSourceRoute !== true) return false;
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every channel on the default `visibleReplies: automatic` whose agent uses the `message` tool for intermediate sends (QQ, Telegram, Discord, Slack, third-party plugins).
- Severity: High — the final answer is lost with no signal.
- Frequency: always, when the turn contains such a send; observed 2/2 today.
- Consequence: users see progress messages but no answer; support burden lands on operators because nothing is logged.

### Additional information

Last known good: 2026.10.9. First known bad: 2026.10.10 (still bad in 2026.11.1). Rollback is not practical here because 2026.10.10 migrated the agent database schema forward.

Workaround: pass `final: false` on every `message` send that is not the turn's answer. Verified to restore delivery on 2026.10.10.

If ending the turn on a tool-authored send is intended for `automatic` channels, it needs to be opt-in; today it silently removes the channel's only visible delivery path.

Related but distinct issues checked before filing: #162217 (closed, Codex harness, opposite direction — `final: false` sends lost the final answer), #176092 (open, cron announce, delivery-evidence check ignores the `final` flag), #187827 (open, claude-cli/WebChat, transcript mirror; fixed on main by #175560, not backported), #167271 and #177093 (same design area, different symptoms).

`docs/concepts/messages.md` in 2026.10.10 says the turn ends "once delivery is confirmed on the current source message", but does not say this now applies to `automatic` channels where the final text is the delivery path.

issues.body:
### Summary

After updating an npm install from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.5-beta.1, every sandboxed agent turn fails with:

```
Sandbox image not found: openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim. Build it with scripts/sandbox-setup.sh before enabling Docker sandboxing. ... | sandbox_provisioning
```

#176595 changed the default sandbox image from `openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim` to `openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim`. The update rebuilds nothing and warns about nothing. Every validation step passed (`candidate-doctor`, `candidate-gateway-startup`, verification: "service running; version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready; core ready"), and so did a later `openclaw doctor --fix`. The first scheduled agent turn then failed. With `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode = "non-main"`, the same applies to every channel conversation (Telegram etc.), not only automations.

### Environment

- 2026.10.10 (7dc3350) to 2026.11.5-beta.1 (bc061f9), npm global install, Ubuntu 25.10 x86_64, Node v24.22.1
- `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "non-main"`; no image pinned in config
- `openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim` was present (built from `scripts/docker/sandbox/Dockerfile` at the installed commit)

### Why it is hard to recover on npm installs

The error says to run `scripts/sandbox-setup.sh`, but the 2026.11.5-beta.1 npm package doesn't ship it, or `scripts/docker/sandbox/Dockerfile` either (checked in the published tarball). On 2026.10.x, `openclaw doctor`'s "Build base sandbox image now?" failed with "Unable to locate scripts/sandbox-setup.sh"; I haven't checked the beta's doctor path. Recovery means fetching `scripts/docker/sandbox/Dockerfile` for the installed commit from GitHub and running `docker build -t openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim` by hand.

### Expected (any of)

- Update admission or validation checks that the default sandbox image for the target exists when sandboxing is enabled, and fails or warns before activation.
- The update (or `doctor --fix`) builds the new image, or keeps using the old one until the new one exists.
- The npm package ships the sandbox Dockerfile and setup script so the error's own instruction works.

### Workaround

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/<installed-commit>/scripts/docker/sandbox/Dockerfile -o Dockerfile
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -t openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim .
```

The next sandboxed turn succeeded without a gateway restart.

Related: #193962 (same update, header-probe timeout).

### Summary

The agent creates a one-shot reminder in the same turn with `mcp__openclaw__automations` (`action: "add"`). The add succeeds, the job is enabled and `nextRunAtMs` is set. The reply then says something like "I'll remind you on Sun Nov 8 at 9:00", and OpenClaw still appends:

Expected: no note, since a reminder was successfully scheduled in the same turn.
Actual: note is appended. The reminder still fires on time, so the note is false.

A successful automations add in the turn, through any tool name or alias (`cron`, `automations`, `mcp__openclaw__automations`), counts as backing the commitment. Optionally the fallback could also match `job.owner?.sessionKey`.

## Summary
#170847 still reproduces on **2026.10.5** (npm, Linux), even though fix PR #170853 merged 2026-10-13. 2026.10.5 was published 2026-10-18. The `media-persistence` migration still fails on a large zstd transcript archive with `Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters`, and that blocks every later migration and the update to 2026.10.7.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), npm global install, systemd user service
- Linux 6.8.0 x64 (Ubuntu 24.04), Node 24.22.1
- Update target: 2026.10.7 (stable channel)

## What happens
- `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw doctor --fix` both stop at `media-persistence`:
  `Failed migrating transcript archive ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/<id>.jsonl.deleted.<ts>.zst: Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters`
- `session-entry-state`, `transcript-directives`, `profile-workspace` and `plugin-migration-preparation` then report `blocked-by-prior-refusal`. The data/settings upgrades for the discord, codex, firecrawl, perplexity and camofox-browser plugins stay "unfinished".
- A managed update to 2026.10.7 sat in `validating` for 28535s (~8h) and was then marked `abandoned` (`inactive-driver-dead`).
- `openclaw triage` (Codex) reached the same diagnosis and found no supported repair path.

## The archive
- A single explicitly deleted session's archive: 17 MB zstd, more than 512 MiB of decoded JSONL. The next-largest archive is 4 MB.
- The canonical copy is the SQLite blob, so moving the derived `.zst` file aside doesn't help.

## Expected
Per #170853, valid large canonical archives should stream through the migration and should not block Doctor or the update.

## Questions
- Is #170853 on the 2026.10.x release line? The merge commit isn't an ancestor of the v2026.10.5–v2026.10.7 tags, but it could have been cherry-picked.
- If it's only on main, which release will include it? The update path runs this migration, so installs in this state can't update until a fixed build exists.

The Gateway keeps serving normally on 2026.10.5. The install just can't move off that version.

### Summary

After recalling a previous prompt in the Control UI composer, moving the caret inside that prompt does not restore ordinary vertical caret navigation. ArrowDown replaces the entire prompt with the reserved unsent draft instead of moving to the next line.

### Reproduction

On current main source `428ca7daffc`, using an isolated production Control UI build and Playwright Chromium with a synthetic Gateway:

1. Open a conversation whose previous user message is `Review the first section\nThen review the second section`.
2. Type `Unsent draft`, move to the start, and press ArrowUp to recall the previous message.
3. Press ArrowRight to move inside its first line.
4. Press ArrowDown.

Expected: the recalled text remains and the caret moves to the second line.
Actual: the composer is replaced with `Unsent draft`.

The focused browser regression fails at the exact text-preservation assertion (expected the two-line prompt; received `Unsent draft`). This is not a fixture/startup failure. No real conversations, provider calls, or live Gateway configuration were used.

### Scope

The input-history key owner only checks caret boundaries when entering history; an active traversal intercepts arrows after caret repositioning. Preserve the documented ArrowUp/ArrowDown history actions at the start, while leaving interior caret movement native.

## What happened

A Telegram callback on a media card can remove the original card (or clear its buttons) before its replacement text message is accepted. If the replacement send fails, the original interactive surface is already gone.

## Expected behavior

Keep the original card and controls when replacement delivery fails. Retire the old card only after the replacement succeeds, preserving the existing stale-button cleanup when deletion fails.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced on source revision `eb77d91994befa7194122199a963d75087b7739e` through `createTelegramCallbackMessageActions` with the real grammY HTTP transport connected to an isolated loopback server:

1. Start with a media callback card and request a text replacement.
2. Return Telegram's `no text in the message` edit error, triggering the existing replacement path.
3. Reject the replacement `sendMessage`.
4. Observe request ordering: `editMessageText -> deleteBusinessMessages -> sendMessage`. The deletion happened before the failed send.

The regression fails on the unchanged production code. This is production-owner/HTTP integration evidence, not a live Telegram Test Server observation. Live Test Server proof remains outstanding because the designated QA broker authentication is unavailable. No production bot, user data, or credentials were used.

## Environment

Source checkout on Windows; Telegram plugin using its existing grammY transport and business/topic payload handling. The defect is the ordering in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts`, not a new Telegram API contract.
