issues.body:
## Summary

`chunkText` / `chunkTextRanges` in `packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.ts` treat a `NaN` chunk limit as a real bound. Every guard and loop comparison against `NaN` is false, so the first range ends at `NaN` and callers that slice by the returned ranges send an **empty string** — the entire outbound message silently vanishes. `chunkMarkdownIR(ir, NaN)` returns no chunks at all for the same reason.

## Reproduction

```js
import { chunkText, chunkTextRanges } from "@openclaw/markdown-core"; // packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.ts
import { chunkMarkdownIR, markdownToIR } from "@openclaw/markdown-core"; // ir.ts

const text = "Hello from OpenClaw — this outbound message must never vanish.";

chunkText(text, NaN);                       // actual: [""]        (expected: [text])
chunkTextRanges(text, { limit: NaN });      // actual: [{ start: 0, end: NaN }]
chunkMarkdownIR(markdownToIR(text), NaN);   // actual: []          (message lost)
```

Observed on `main` (ce8b7add7b00), Node 24.16.0, Windows 11:

```
chunkText(text, NaN)            -> [""]
chunkTextRanges(text, {NaN})    -> [{"start":0,"end":null}]
sliced via ranges (plugin view) -> [""]
chunkMarkdownIR(ir, NaN) texts  -> []
```

## Expected behavior

The `chunkText` docstring promises: "Returns the original text as one chunk when the limit is non-positive." A limit that is not a number at all cannot bound anything and should take the same path. The sibling helpers in `src/shared/text-chunking.ts` (`chunkTextByBreakResolver`, `splitLongTextLine`) already return the whole text for `NaN` because their loop condition is false for `NaN`, so the two chunking implementations disagree today.

Note: `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` in the same package deliberately shatters `NaN` into per-character chunks (pinned by `render-aware-chunking.test.ts`, and its comment explains the intent for non-finite limits). That behavior is loud and visible; the empty-chunk result here is the only *silent* one. This report is not about changing that pinned behavior.

## Root cause

`normalizeChunkLimit` (packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.ts) returns `NaN` unchanged:

```ts
return Number.isFinite(limit) && limit > 0 ? resolveIntegerOption(limit, 1, { min: 1 }) : limit;
// Number.isFinite(NaN) === false, so NaN falls through the ternary unchanged
```

Downstream, `normalizedLimit <= 0` is false for `NaN`, `text.length <= NaN` is false, `start + NaN` is `NaN`, and the produced range `{ start: 0, end: NaN }` slices to `""`.

## Impact

`chunkTextRanges` is part of the public plugin surface (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking`) and is used by bundled channel plugins (e.g. Zalo) for outbound delivery. First-party channels resolve limits through `resolveTextChunkLimit`, which filters non-positive values, so this does not trigger through built-in config today — but a plugin or channel adapter that computes its limit dynamically (`Number(envValue)`, arithmetic on optional settings) gets empty sends instead of an intact message, with no error anywhere.

## Environment

- OpenClaw main @ ce8b7add7b00 (2026.11.1)
- Node v24.16.0, Windows 11 (also reproduced in the repo's Vitest harness)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On `main` at `6d7347b2da3`, a Control UI page with two running sidebar sessions uses a median 12.2% of a CPU core in
headless WebKit, including 1.9% in the WebKit GPU process. The same bundle with the rings' pre-#189847 border art
uses 8.7% with no GPU-process work.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `main` at `6d7347b2da3` and build the production Control UI with the e2e helper
   (`startProductionControlUiE2eServer` in `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts`).
2. Serve it with `scripts/lib/control-ui-bench-gateway-server.ts` and open `/chat` in Playwright WebKit 1.64.1
   (headless, 1440x1000, device scale 1). Install the mock Gateway (`installMockGateway`) with a `sessions.list` of
   16 rows: `main`, two rows with `hasActiveRun: true, status: "running"`, one queued, 12 idle.
3. Wait 8 s, then read cumulative CPU time (`ps -o time=`) of the Playwright browser process tree and its WebKit
   helpers (WebContent, GPU, Networking) before and after a 20 s window with no input.
4. Repeat with an init style that restores the pre-#189847 ring:
   `.session-glyph__ring { background: none !important; mask: none !important; border: 1.5px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 20%, transparent); border-top-color: var(--accent); }`
5. Repeat with the rings stopped:
   `.session-glyph__ring, .session-run-spinner, .session-glyph__trace-run { animation: none !important; }`

The probe used for these steps is attached as `idle-probe.mts.txt` (about 300 lines). Rename it to
`idle-probe.mts` and run it from the repository root with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`.
A manual check in Safari (Activity Monitor, two running sessions in the sidebar) was not done.

### Expected behavior

Same as before #189847 (`v2026.11.5-beta.1` and earlier draw these rings with borders): two visible running rings
cost no WebKit GPU-process time, and total CPU stays near the border-art figure (8.7% median here).

### Actual behavior

The only running animations on the page are the two sidebar rings (`document.getAnimations()` reports 2
`btn-spinner-spin` animations on `.session-glyph__ring`). Headless WebKit, % of one core over 20 s, interleaved runs:

| Page state | Runs | Total median (range) | WebContent median | GPU process median | UI process median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, rings spinning | 6 | 12.2 (9.9 to 12.7) | 6.8 | 1.9 | 3.5 |
| main + pre-#189847 border art | 3 | 8.7 (6.6 to 8.8) | 5.1 | 0 | 3.3 |
| main, rings stopped | 3 | 4.5 (4.2 to 4.6) | 2.7 | 0 | 1.3 |

Every masked spinner in `ui/src` has the same structure: the rotating element carries
`background: currentColor; mask: <svg>`. For example `.session-glyph__ring` and `.btn__spinner` in
`ui/src/styles/components.css`, and `.activity-pill__spinner` and the `.activity-pill__atlas` strip in
`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-activity-pills.css`.

### OpenClaw version

main `6d7347b2da3` (package version 2026.11.1). Not in any release: `v2026.11.1` and `v2026.11.5-beta.1` don't
contain #189847.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (26B123), Mac Studio (Apple M3 Ultra)

### Install method

Source checkout, production Control UI bundle built by the e2e helper, served by the bench Gateway server

### Model

Not applicable (mocked Gateway, no model request)

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable (mocked Gateway, no provider)

### Logs

```shell
# one run per line: total, WebContent, GPU process, UI process (% of one core, 20 s window)
main      12.4 6.8 1.9 3.9 | 11.9 6.7 1.8 3.6 | 9.9 5.2 1.5 3.3 | 12.6 6.8 1.9 3.9 | 12.7 7.2 2.2 3.4 | 11.4 6.4 1.7 3.4
border     8.7 5.1 0   3.4 |  6.6 3.3 0   3.2 | 8.8 5.4 0   3.3
stopped    4.5 3.0 0   1.3 |  4.6 2.7 0   1.7 | 4.2 2.7 0   1.3
host load average (1 min) during runs: 17 to 45 on 32 cores
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No visual symptom: the rings look correct. The cost shows up only as CPU and GPU-process time.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: the browser Control UI in WebKit (Safari's engine) on builds that include #189847 (currently `main`
  only), while a spinner is visible in the Control UI page; measured in Playwright WebKit, not in Safari. The
  sidebar run rings stay visible for as long as a session runs. In one check of a debug macOS app build of `main`,
  the Dashboard showed no running spinner (WebContent 0.2% over 60 s); app impact was not measured.
- Severity: annoying (extra CPU, GPU and battery use while idle)
- Frequency: every measured run of the Control UI page with a running sidebar ring (6 of 6 headless runs, 3 of 3
  headed windows). A static test page with the same spinners shows no measurable cost.
- Consequence: about 3.5 more points of a core than the border art for two rings in this setup, including
  GPU-process work every frame. Chromium is not affected: the same page measures a median 1.5% total, with 1 to 2
  style recalcs and 0 layouts per 20 s.

### Additional information

- Last known good: `v2026.11.5-beta.1` (border spinners). First known bad: `main` at `6feb40ee5b4` (#189847,
  2026-11-01).
- Same page against a real isolated loopback Gateway (a local stub model keeps two runs active, no provider
  traffic), steady state, 5 runs: median 7.6% with 1.3% in the GPU process. With the border art: 4.2% and 6.4%, no
  GPU-process time. Rings stopped: 3.1% and 3.2%.
- Headed Playwright WebKit on a MacBook display (refresh rate, laptop model and macOS version not recorded), same
  real-Gateway setup, 60 s idle windows, 3 per arm interleaved (load average 3.1 to 4.2, 1 min): `main` median 30.0% (25.9 to 30.3) with 4.2% in the GPU process.
  With the mask moved to a static child of the rotating ring: 20.1% (16.8 to 20.8) and 0.5%.
- The cost depends on page context. A static page with all 18 masked spinner variants spinning shows no measurable
  WebContent or GPU-process time in the same WebKit build, with or without the masks.
- Related but different: #138918 reports idle WebKit/WindowServer load on 2026.9.x to 2026.10.9. Those builds
  predate the masks.

issues.body:
## Summary

Background Skill Workshop reviews cost credits two ways, and neither is covered by #173889:

1. **Every skill the review edits changes the reusable prompt prefix** of the running session.
2. **The review session itself never reuses its own cache**, because its history is rewritten each pass.

Together these dropped ~16.7M tokens in a single evening on one deployment.

## Environment

- Prefix-caching deployment, self-hosted Gateway, gateway with a turn subscription plan
- Workshop `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "auto"` (default)
- Observed 2026-10-19, 20:36-23:03 CST
- OpenClaw **2026.10.5** (build `1b58cb9`)
- Prefix-caching routes observed on this deployment: `anthropic-messages` and `openai-completions`

## Vector 1 - learned-skill metadata sits at the head of the system prompt

Learned skills are surfaced into the system prompt as `name` + `description` + path. That is the *earliest* cacheable segment of the prompt, so editing one description string invalidates the entire reusable prefix for the next turn - even though the conversation body is unchanged.

Between 20:36 and 23:03, **9 skill files were edited**. The main session recorded **37 cache drops, 27 of them larger than 100k tokens** (typical 230k-400k per drop).

This is a different insertion point from the runtime-context-at-tail behavior in #158898, but the same class: mutable content placed inside the reusable prefix.

## Vector 2 - the review session's own cache never survives

The background review forks the conversation and its history is rewritten on each pass, so its own prefix is discarded every time:

```
20:36:36   466432 -> 0
20:47:19   510208 -> 1024
22:36:43   576256 -> 15360
22:59:39   585984 -> 16384
```

Totals for the window:

| session | tokens dropped |
|---|---|
| review session | 7.71M |
| main session | 9.0M |
| **combined** | **~16.7M** |

## Timestamps align

```
20:36:10  windows-wrapper-script        -> main   20:40:42  269312 -> 1024
                                          review 20:36:36  466432 -> 0      (+6s)
20:46:45  openclaw-plugin-update       -> main   20:46:44  279552 -> 1024
20:47:58  openclaw-update-install-fail -> review 20:47:19  510208 -> 1024
22:51:41  lossless-claw-maintenance    -> review 22:59:39  585984 -> 16384
```

## The review reviews the *entire* conversation

This is the structural reason the cost scales badly, and it is the part that seems hardest to justify.

A background Skill Workshop review is not scoped to the turn that triggered it. It forks the conversation and reviews the whole of it. An assistant session is normally long-running, so the cost of "review my recent work" grows with **session length** instead of staying bounded.

Concretely on this deployment: after context compaction had already brought the main session down to **~300k tokens**, a background review was observed running with a context of **~500k tokens** - larger than the session that triggered it - and this recurred across multiple reviews in the same window.

That also appears to be in tension with #173889, which states a cap of at most 64 events / 32 KiB. The most likely reading is that the cap bounds what the review **reads**, not the size of the **request** that carries the forked conversation. If so, the transport cost of every review still scales with session length even though the reviewed slice is small.

A housekeeping task that runs in the background on every qualifying turn should not be able to exceed the context of the session that scheduled it.

## What #173889 already fixed, and what it does not

#173889 correctly bounded the *per-review* cost: at most 64 events / 32 KiB, `skill_workshop` as the only exposed tool, bootstrap/catalog/client instructions and cache/delivery context stripped, low reasoning, 2048 output tokens, and 15/30/60-minute backoff after rate limiting.

That bounds one review. It does not address:

- **Frequency.** The counter is 10 model iterations per session, but a single user message that uses 12-24 tool calls already produces 12-24 iterations. On this host, 48 user messages produced **235 model iterations**. In addition, any turn that *read* a learned skill queues a review regardless of the counter.
- **Prefix invalidation** caused by the resulting skill edits (Vector 1).
- **The review session's own cache** (Vector 2).

## Requested behavior

1. **Return background review to a schedule** rather than firing every 10 model iterations.
2. **Or gate reviews on actual skill usage** - e.g. review a skill only after it has been used N times, or after a correction was observed on it - instead of on raw iteration count.
3. **Consider placing the learned-skill catalog outside the reusable prefix** (or emitting descriptions only when they change), so a skill edit does not invalidate the whole conversation prefix.
4. **Avoid rewriting the review session's history** between passes, so its own cache can be reused.
5. **Scope a review to the turns that actually changed** instead of the whole session, so review cost does not scale with session length. A truncated or incremental review is acceptable - reviewing the turns since the previous review would cover the same lessons.

Config note: `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "off"` stops the reviews, and `/learn`, prompted skill creation, and *Learn from history* remain available - so the mechanism can be deferred without losing the ability to save lessons.

## Related

- #158898 - runtime context message appended last on every model call (same class, different insertion point)
- #172313 - fix(agents): source metadata changes invalidate the reusable prompt prefix
- #141969 - mid-turn overflow recovery and silent exec completion cause full-context LLM reruns
- #173889 - fix(skills): keep background reviews out of saturated token budgets
- #176227 - tools.toolsBySender changes the tool list and system prompt, so the prompt cache misses

```

```

This has happened repeatedly. So far the only reliable recovery is a full Gateway restart.

**Root cause (found via gateway.log)**
A companion-app (macOS node) connection briefly drops while an agent turn is using computer/node tools:

```
... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=UNAVAILABLE: COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE: macOS app exec host unreachable ...
... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=UNAVAILABLE: UNAVAILABLE: screen snapshot failed ...
```

Right after that, the same websocket connection starts failing every `chat.metadata` request for that session, repeatedly:

```
[ws] res chat.metadata errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=ChatMetadataSnapshotUnavailableError: prepared chat metadata owner is unavailable for agent "main" conn=...
```
(33 repeats over ~33 minutes in one occurrence, same conn id, same session)

**Unconfirmed hypothesis, now falsified in practice**
In one log sample, the failing connection recovered right after an unrelated config hot-reload event (`agents.entries.main.identity` change). We hypothesized a lightweight config hot-reload could substitute for a full restart, and set up a log-tailing automation (Gateway `schedule.kind="stream"` job watching for this error string) so the agent could self-heal without the user needing to restart.

**This did not work.** On the next real occurrence:
1. The user waited, nothing recovered, no proactive notice arrived, so the user restarted the Gateway manually (as before).
2. Checking afterward, the self-heal automation job itself was gone — a session-owned `schedule.kind="stream"` automation does not survive a Gateway restart, so it never got a chance to fire.
3. Separately, even if the automation did fire while the connection was stuck, there is no guaranteed way to notify the user through the very same broken connection/session before it recovers — so a silent "trying to fix it" state is possible, which is worse than just restarting.

**Ask**
1. Ideally: the per-connection "tool authority snapshot" / "chat metadata snapshot" should be invalidated/regenerated automatically when the underlying node connection recovers, so no external trigger (config reload or restart) is needed at all.
2. If a lighter recovery command is added (e.g. per-session/per-connection reset instead of full Gateway restart), it should be reachable/effective even while that session's own delivery path is degraded — otherwise self-heal from the affected agent is not reliable.
3. If automations are expected to help with self-recovery scenarios like this, they should be able to survive/re-arm across a Gateway restart (or there should be a gateway-level watcher independent of any single session).

**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.9.3
- macOS 26.6.2, Control UI (webchat) client

issues.body:
## Bug type

Reliability / delivery race — an **ordinary inbound channel message** arriving mid-turn drops the in-flight turn's reply and stalls the session queue.

## Summary

If a WhatsApp message arrives while a turn is already running on the same session, two things happen:

1. The **in-flight turn's reply is silently dropped.** The model call returns `200` and the reply is persisted, but it is never handed to the channel — there is no `[whatsapp] Sending message` line for it.
2. The **queued message is held for minutes** before dispatch, even though the model call completed seconds earlier and the lane goes idle.

Net effect: send two messages in quick succession, get **one** reply, several minutes late, answering only the later message. The first reply is gone permanently.

This looks like the same defect class as #135132 (closed NOT_PLANNED) and closed PR #127122 — dispatch not consulting the reply-run registry that channel-delivered turns register in. The difference, and the reason I'm filing separately: **#135132 requires a cron `announce` job to collide with the turn. This needs nothing but a user typing a second message while the agent is working**, which is ordinary conversational behaviour and makes the blast radius much larger.

Notably, the `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads` diagnostic quoted in #135132/#112259 **does not appear** in my logs. This drop leaves no log evidence at all — the only signal is the *absence* of a send line after a successful model response.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.6.34** (`5c38f99`), macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), Node v22
- Channel: WhatsApp (Baileys)
- Provider: local OpenAI-compatible proxy → Codex `gpt-5.6-terra` (previously reproduced on `gpt-5.5` — model-independent)
- `agentRuntime`: default (not `claude-cli`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a WhatsApp message to the agent; it begins a turn.
2. While that turn is still running (a few seconds in), send a second message.
3. The first turn's reply never arrives.
4. The second message sits queued for several minutes, then dispatches and replies.

## Evidence

Gateway log (`~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log`), 2026-09-08, local time, numbers redacted:

```
23:25:18.863 [whatsapp] Inbound message <A> -> <B> (direct, 85 chars)
23:25:19.982 [model-fetch] start  provider=freerouter model=codex/gpt-5.6-terra
23:25:24.937 [whatsapp] Inbound message <A> -> <B> (direct, audio/ogg; 1247 chars)   <-- arrives mid-turn
23:25:25.434 [model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=5451 contentType=text/event-stream
                                    <-- NO "[whatsapp] Sending message" for this turn. Reply dropped.
23:29:11.989 [whatsapp] Inbound message <A> -> <B> (direct, 73 chars)
                                    <-- no model call at all; swept into the same hold
23:31:51.790 [model-fetch] start  provider=freerouter model=codex/gpt-5.6-terra
23:31:55.830 [model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=4038
23:31:56.561 [whatsapp] Sending message
23:31:56.734 [whatsapp] Sent message (174ms)
```

Contrast with the two healthy turns minutes earlier on the same session, where each `model-fetch response` is followed within ~1s by `Sending message`:

```
23:09:45.029 start -> 23:09:50.612 response 200 -> 23:09:51.332 Sending message  ✓
23:09:56.141 start -> 23:10:00.211 response 200 -> 23:10:13.147 Sending message  ✓
```

The model is never the problem — every call in the failing window returned `200` in 4–6s.

## Hold duration is not a fixed constant

Four prior observations of the hold clustered tightly at **~736s** (735.237s, 736.201s, 736.245s — the last two matching to 44ms). The occurrence above released after **~387s**, roughly half.

So the delay is **not** a single hardcoded timer. I previously scanned both the host `dist/` and the WhatsApp plugin `dist/` for integer literals in `700000..780000` and found none outside theme colors — consistent with the value being composed rather than configured. Whatever computes it is state- or load-dependent.

One caveat I can't fully exclude: a read-only `channels.status` RPC was issued ~116s before the 387s release. I see no mechanism by which a status read would drain the queue, and the hold did not release immediately, but I'm flagging it rather than asserting a clean self-release.

## Ruled out

- **Stuck-session watchdog / #140401** — `grep -c 'stuck session'` over the entire live gateway log returns **0**. Also inapplicable: that abort fires on long *generations*, whereas the dropped reply here completed in 5.4s.
- **Lane starvation / #54488** — lane idle, `compactionCount: 0`.
- **The model** — all calls `200` in 3–7s.
- **WhatsApp disconnect** — no reconnect in the window; sends immediately before and after succeed in <200ms.

## Impact

Silent message loss during normal use. The user sees an unanswered message and no error; the agent's tool calls from the dropped turn **do** apply, so state advances while the confirmation vanishes. There is no retry, no dead-letter, and — unlike #112259 — no log line.

## Workaround

Wait for a reply before sending a follow-up. A mid-turn message costs several minutes *and* eats the previous reply.

## Related

- #135132 — same defect class, cron-announce trigger (closed NOT_PLANNED)
- PR #127122 — "serialize agent-command turns against live reply runs" (closed, not merged)
- #112259 — silently dropped inbound turn, no retry/dead-letter
- #54488, #90240 — inbound held for tens of minutes, different mechanisms

issues.body:
## Summary
If Voice Call persistence is interrupted after chunk rows are committed but before the metadata row is committed, the chunks become unreachable and survive every restart. Repeated interruptions consume the bounded chunk namespace and can eventually evict chunks belonging to retained call history.

## Environment
- Commit: `1e028b5193a490221f222091d559a4b32fe011a1` (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Voice Call call-record persistence and startup restore
- Host: macOS 27.0 arm64, Node 26.1.0, source checkout with real plugin-state SQLite

## Steps to reproduce
1. Persist a small `ringing` record for one call through `persistCallRecord()`.
2. Persist an `answered` update with a 100 KB transcript in a second OS process.
3. Kill that process immediately before its metadata registration. Current ordering has already committed the new chunk rows at this point.
4. Inspect the two namespaces, then call `loadActiveCallsFromStore()` to simulate startup restore and inspect them again.

## Expected
An interrupted write leaves no chunk rows without a metadata owner. Startup recovery also removes any debris left by older chunk-first writers while preserving the previous complete `ringing` record.

## Actual
The interrupted update leaves three unreachable chunk rows beside the one complete prior record. Startup restores the prior `ringing` state but leaves all three unreachable rows in SQLite.

## Root cause
`extensions/voice-call/src/manager/store.ts:256-272` registers every chunk before the metadata owner:

```ts
for (let index = 0; index < encoded.meta.chunkCount; index += 1) {
  await stores.chunks.register(buildChunkKey(eventKey, index), encoded.chunk(index));
}
await stores.events.register(eventKey, { ...encoded.meta, ...order });
```

The mirrored delete path at `:276-287` deletes metadata before chunks. Restore at `:416-429` reads only metadata-owned records and performs no reconciliation, so either interruption shape can leave permanent debris.

## Sibling surfaces
The legacy Doctor importer uses deterministic keys and retains its source for replay, so its retry contract is different. The runtime writer creates unique event keys and has no replay source. Novelty searches for Voice Call chunks, interrupted persistence, and unreachable rows found this PR but no issue that documents the defect.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: An interrupted Voice Call write leaves SQLite chunks that no metadata row can reach and startup never removes.
Real environment tested: Production `persistCallRecord()` and `loadActiveCallsFromStore()` at commit `1e028b5193a490221f222091d559a4b32fe011a1`, across separate Node processes and a real on-disk plugin-state SQLite database. The only injected seam kills the writer immediately before metadata registration.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: Run `voice-repro.mts seed`, `voice-repro.mts crash`, and `voice-repro.mts inspect` in separate processes with the same `STORE_PATH`; the crash process exits from SIGKILL at the metadata registration boundary.
Evidence after fix:
```text
seeded_state=ringing
crash_point=before_metadata_register
crash_exit=137
commit=1e028b5193a490221f222091d559a4b32fe011a1
metadata_rows_before_restart=1
chunk_rows_before_restart=4
unreachable_chunks_before_restart=3
restored_state=ringing
metadata_rows_after_restart=1
chunk_rows_after_restart=4
unreachable_chunks_after_restart=3
db_present=true

EXPECTED
unreachable_chunks_before_restart=0
unreachable_chunks_after_restart=0
restored_state=ringing
```
Observed result after fix: Three ownerless chunks remain before and after restart while only the previous complete call state is reachable.
What was not tested: No live telephony provider call was placed. The metadata-first delete interruption was confirmed in source but was not killed separately. Namespace exhaustion and the eventual eviction of older live chunks were not driven in this run.

issues.body:
## Summary

`voice_call` `initiate_call` accepts a `dtmfSequence` for any configured provider, but only the Twilio provider ever consumes the pre-connect TwiML it is encoded into. On `plivo` and `telnyx` the digits are built, logged as if they were applied, never placed on the carrier request, and the caller still gets `{success: true}`. The agent believes it dialed an extension or an IVR selection before the callee answered; nothing was dialed.

The core of this report is an asymmetry between two near-duplicate paths:

- Mid-call DTMF is gated. `sendDtmf` at `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts:422-424` checks whether the provider implements the capability and refuses with `{success: false, error: "<provider> does not support outbound DTMF"}`.
- Pre-connect DTMF is not gated. `initiateCall` at `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts:167-179` validates the digit alphabet and the call mode, and performs no provider check at all.

Same operation, same digit string, same live call, same provider. One path refuses honestly. Its near-duplicate reports success and drops the work.

## Environment

- Commit: `3a54b13977eb4078d470426c4522e0e655b9ee93` (worktree pinned for this run)
- Also live on `origin/main` `144adb922ad38284b2f30aecd432156866f421f1`. Every file in the chain is byte-identical between the two, and to intermediate `71e436920cc9e4e3f2ff057b86679c6ed39c5115`:

```
extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts   c60ab3bd9b622b84862d9d630ec061aa309a5b83  (identical at all three)
extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts   7142817c118caddc0fbc69f8b248826b9b85c5d3  (identical at all three)
extensions/voice-call/src/providers/plivo.ts    032c1941a577c99fe4acfb8eaf14931096ac5148  (identical at all three)
extensions/voice-call/src/providers/telnyx.ts   e611f10b8807b8f6876a93b35f8e04ee3623adbf  (identical at all three)
extensions/voice-call/index.ts                  d43eae50eedc3c9dc4193c0169bc838abec35540  (identical at all three)
```

- Surface: `@openclaw/voice-call` outbound call initiation, providers `plivo` and `telnyx`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the voice-call plugin with `provider: plivo` (or `telnyx`) and a `fromNumber`.
2. Invoke the `voice_call` tool with `action: "initiate_call"`, a `to` number, a `message`, `mode: "conversation"`, and `dtmfSequence: "ww1234#"`.
3. Observe the tool returns a successful initiation and the runtime logs `preConnectDtmf=yes`.
4. Inspect the request the plugin actually sends to the carrier API. It carries no digits and no `<Play digits="..."/>` TwiML.
5. For contrast, call `action: "send_dtmf"` with the same digits on the resulting call. That path refuses with `plivo does not support outbound DTMF`.

## Expected

Either the digits are delivered to the carrier, or the request is refused at validation time the way the mid-call sibling refuses it. A caller must not be told a pre-connect DTMF sequence was applied when the provider has no path to apply it.

## Actual

`initiateCall` returns `{success: true}`. The digits are silently discarded between the manager and the provider.

## Root cause

`initiateCall` validates `dtmfSequence` without ever asking whether the provider can honor it (`extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts:164-179`):

```ts
const dtmfSequence = opts.dtmfSequence;
...
if (dtmfSequence) {
  const validationError = validateDtmfDigits(dtmfSequence);
  if (validationError) {
    return { callId: "", success: false, error: validationError };
  }
  if (mode !== "conversation") {
    return {
      callId: "",
      success: false,
      error: "dtmfSequence requires conversation mode",
    };
  }
}
```

It then encodes the digits into TwiML (`:250-254`) and passes that to the provider unconditionally (`:268-278`):

```ts
} else if (dtmfSequence) {
  preConnectTwiml = generateDtmfRedirectTwiml(dtmfSequence, ctx.webhookUrl);
  console.log(
    `[voice-call] Using pre-connect DTMF TwiML for call ${callId} (digits=${dtmfSequence.length}, ...)`,
  );
}
...
const result = await ctx.provider.initiateCall({
  callId,
  from,
  to,
  webhookUrl: ctx.webhookUrl,
  inlineTwiml,
  preConnectTwiml,
  ...
});
```

`preConnectTwiml` is a TwiML string, so only the Twilio provider has anywhere to put it (`extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts:557-558`):

```ts
if (!input.inlineTwiml && input.preConnectTwiml) {
  this.twimlStorage.set(input.callId, input.preConnectTwiml);
```

No other provider reads the field. Grepped on the pinned commit:

```
$ grep -n "preConnectTwiml" extensions/voice-call/src/providers/plivo.ts extensions/voice-call/src/providers/telnyx.ts
(no matches, exit 1)

$ grep -rn "preConnectTwiml" extensions/voice-call/src --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.ts'
extensions/voice-call/src/types.ts:173:  preConnectTwiml?: string;
extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts:245:    let preConnectTwiml: string | undefined;
extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts:251:      preConnectTwiml = generateDtmfRedirectTwiml(dtmfSequence, ctx.webhookUrl);
extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts:274:      preConnectTwiml,
extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.ts:292:      `[voice-call] Outbound call initiated: ... preConnectDtmf=${preConnectTwiml ? "yes" : "no"} ...`,
extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts:545:   * If preConnectTwiml is provided, the first webhook request receives that
extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts:557:    if (!input.inlineTwiml && input.preConnectTwiml) {
extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts:558:      this.twimlStorage.set(input.callId, input.preConnectTwiml);
```

The tool schema advertises the parameter with no provider restriction (`extensions/voice-call/index.ts:55`):

```ts
dtmfSequence: Type.Optional(Type.String({ description: "DTMF digits to play before connect" })),
```

The log line at `:292` prints `preConnectDtmf=yes` for every provider, so the runtime log also asserts the digits were applied when they were not.

Suggested direction: refuse `dtmfSequence` at the `initiateCall` validation step for providers that cannot honor it, mirroring the mid-call `sendDtmf` refusal, rather than encoding it and dropping it downstream. Delivering the digits natively per carrier is a larger piece of work; the honest refusal is the small one and removes the silent loss.

## Sibling surfaces

- `twilio`: unaffected. It stores the pre-connect TwiML and serves it on the answer webhook. Confirmed in the run below by the `Stored Twilio initial TwiML ... (kind=pre-connect)` line, which appears for Twilio only.
- `mock` provider: not a user-facing carrier, not covered here.
- The mid-call path (`sendDtmf`) is correct on all three and is what the fix should mirror.

## Why it matters

Pre-connect DTMF is how a caller navigates an IVR, enters an extension, or enters an access code before a human picks up. Silently skipping it means the call lands on the wrong endpoint, or sits on a menu prompt that never advances, while the agent proceeds believing the digits were dialed.

## Novelty

Distinct from both existing DTMF items, which concern the MID-CALL path only:

- #113739 (open PR, `fix(voice-call): flush stream audio before DTMF`) is about ordering: during realtime Twilio calls, mid-call DTMF was emitted only after buffered Media Stream speech drained. It touches `twilio.ts`, `twilio/realtime-dtmf-handoff.ts`, `webhook.ts` and `webhook/realtime-handler.ts`. It does not touch `manager/outbound.ts` initiation validation, and it is Twilio-only, so it cannot reach a provider that never receives the field.
- #139066 (open issue, `sendDtmf` tears down the realtime media stream) is about mid-call `sendDtmf` on Twilio ending the live call. Its subject is the provider that does implement DTMF; this report is about the two providers that do not, on the other code path, where no refusal happens at all.

Neither covers pre-connect `dtmfSequence` on `plivo` or `telnyx`, and neither covers the missing provider check in `initiateCall`. Searches run: `voice-call dtmfSequence`, `preConnectTwiml`, `plivo DTMF`, `telnyx DTMF`, `pre-connect digits`, `voice-call DTMF provider`, `DTMF`, `dtmf digits`, `voice-call ivr extension`, plus the open voice-call issue and PR listings. `preConnectTwiml` returns zero hits across issues and PRs.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: pre-connect `dtmfSequence` requested on a plivo or telnyx outbound call is discarded while the caller is told the call was initiated.
Real environment tested: real voice-call manager `initiateCall`, real `PlivoProvider` / `TelnyxProvider` / `TwilioProvider`, real SSRF-guarded provider API client, real SQLite-backed call record store, at commit 3a54b13977eb4078d470426c4522e0e655b9ee93, byte-identical to origin/main 144adb922ad38284b2f30aecd432156866f421f1 for every file named above. Only the outbound socket was redirected, to a local HTTP listener that records the exact bytes the plugin wrote.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/audit0919-preconnect-dtmf/repro.ts` from /home/ubuntu/oc-tk-verify, driving `initiateCall(ctx, "+15550000002", undefined, {message, mode: "conversation", dtmfSequence: "ww1234#"})` once per provider, then `sendDtmf` with the same digits on the same resulting call.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, 3a54b13977eb4078d470426c4522e0e655b9ee93 == origin/main 144adb922ad38284b2f30aecd432156866f421f1)
--- provider=plivo dtmfSequence=ww1234# ---
manager initiateCall result: {"callId":"a491dee6-48be-4a31-b34d-172de4875bfe","success":true}
outgoing HTTP to carrier: POST https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/MAXXX/Call/
outgoing HTTP request body: {"from":"+15550000001","to":"+15550000002","answer_url":"https://example.com/voice/webhook?provider=plivo&callId=a491dee6-48be-4a31-b34d-172de4875bfe&flow=answer","answer_method":"POST","hangup_url":"https://example.com/voice/webhook?provider=plivo&callId=a491dee6-48be-4a31-b34d-172de4875bfe&flow=hangup","hangup_method":"POST","hangup_on_ring":30}
digits "ww1234#" present in outgoing request body: false | any <Play digits=...> TwiML present: false
runtime log: [voice-call] Using pre-connect DTMF TwiML for call a491dee6-48be-4a31-b34d-172de4875bfe (digits=7, initialMessage=yes)
runtime log: [voice-call] Outbound call initiated: callId=a491dee6-48be-4a31-b34d-172de4875bfe providerCallId=plivo-req-1 mode=conversation preConnectDtmf=yes initialMessage=yes
mid-call sendDtmf on the same call: {"success":false,"error":"plivo does not support outbound DTMF"}

--- provider=telnyx dtmfSequence=ww1234# ---
manager initiateCall result: {"callId":"378ada31-6be1-4480-b1ab-4bf0a2e2966c","success":true}
outgoing HTTP to carrier: POST https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls
outgoing HTTP request body: {"connection_id":"conn-1","to":"+15550000002","from":"+15550000001","webhook_url":"https://example.com/voice/webhook","webhook_url_method":"POST","client_state":"Mzc4YWRhMzEtNmJlMS00NDgwLWIxYWItNGJmMGEyZTI5NjZj","timeout_secs":30}
digits "ww1234#" present in outgoing request body: false | any <Play digits=...> TwiML present: false
runtime log: [voice-call] Using pre-connect DTMF TwiML for call 378ada31-6be1-4480-b1ab-4bf0a2e2966c (digits=7, initialMessage=yes)
runtime log: [voice-call] Outbound call initiated: callId=378ada31-6be1-4480-b1ab-4bf0a2e2966c providerCallId=telnyx-cc-1 mode=conversation preConnectDtmf=yes initialMessage=yes
mid-call sendDtmf on the same call: {"success":false,"error":"telnyx does not support outbound DTMF"}

# BASELINE ON THE SAME RUN (twilio, the one provider that consumes the field)
--- provider=twilio dtmfSequence=ww1234# ---
manager initiateCall result: {"callId":"47fb71d0-97a6-4414-8d49-ba36fdc3655e","success":true}
outgoing HTTP to carrier: POST https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/ACXXX/Calls.json
runtime log: [voice-call] Using pre-connect DTMF TwiML for call 47fb71d0-97a6-4414-8d49-ba36fdc3655e (digits=7, initialMessage=yes)
runtime log: [voice-call] Stored Twilio initial TwiML for call 47fb71d0-97a6-4414-8d49-ba36fdc3655e (kind=pre-connect)
```

issues.body:
## Summary

After the agent replies into a captured conversation turn, the next keyed user message into the same session fails with the internal error `Session transcript anchor was not returned: <entryId>`. The reply capture path writes a side-mode audit artifact into the transcript, that side append marks the whole session's transcript projection index dirty, and while the index is dirty the active-anchor read returns `undefined`. The keyed-user dedup path in `SessionManager.appendMessageWithTranscriptAnchor` turns that `undefined` into a hard throw instead of degrading. The window lasts from roughly 0.5 seconds to over 10 seconds on my runs, so a user replying promptly lands inside it.

## Environment

- Commit: `3a54b13977eb4078d470426c4522e0e655b9ee93` (the tree I drove)
- Still live on `origin/main` `71e436920cc9e4e3f2ff057b86679c6ed39c5115`: all six files named below are byte identical between the two SHAs (`git diff HEAD origin/main -- <file>` empty for each)
- Surface: session transcript persistence, reached from every keyed user ingress (`SessionManager.appendMessage` delegates to `appendMessageWithTranscriptAnchor`), triggered by the auto-reply conversation turn capture path

## Steps to reproduce

1. Persist a session with an assistant entry and then a keyed user turn (an ordinary channel ingress with an `idempotencyKey`).
2. Let the agent reply into a captured conversation turn. `src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-turn-capture.ts:234` writes its audit artifact with `appendMode: "side"`.
3. Immediately read the active transcript anchor for the keyed user entry, or let the channel re-deliver the same keyed user message so the dedup branch runs.
4. The anchor read returns `undefined` and the append throws.

Driven directly with:

```
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/audit0919/lane-sessions/anchor-dirty.mts
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/audit0919/lane-sessions/anchor-order.mts
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/audit0919/lane-sessions/anchor-window.mts
```

Each script calls the real `appendTranscriptMessage`, `appendTranscriptEventSync`, `readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchor` and `SessionManager.open` against a real on-disk SQLite agent store. Nothing is stubbed.

## Expected

An ordinary agent reply must not make the next user message fail. If the projection is momentarily not authoritative, the keyed-user dedup path should either re-resolve the projection on demand before reading, or degrade the way the rest of the codebase already degrades on a missing anchor.

## Actual

`appendMessageWithTranscriptAnchor` throws `Session transcript anchor was not returned: <entryId>`, for the entire duration of the dirty window.

## Root cause (if known)

Three parts, all on this SHA.

1. The anchor reader refuses to certify a dirty projection. This part is correct and should stay:

```ts
// src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-anchor.ts:24-27
  // Branch changes retain old projection rows until deferred reconciliation.
  // An anchor must never certify those rows as the current active path.
  if (sessionTranscriptIndexNeedsReconcile(params.database.db, params.resolved.sessionId)) {
    return undefined;
  }
```

2. A side append marks the whole session's index dirty, so every anchor read for that session starts returning `undefined`, not just reads for the side entry:

```ts
// src/config/sessions/session-transcript-index.ts:307-316
    if (
      isSessionTranscriptLeafControl(params.event) ||
      isSessionTranscriptSideAppendEntry(params.event)
    ) {
      // Leaf controls repoint the active branch and side appends attach off
      // the main chain; the visible path must be re-resolved rather than
      // guessed at append time.
      watermark = markSessionTranscriptIndexDirtyInTransaction(db, sessionId);
      return true;
    }
```

3. The consumer converts "the projection is not ready yet" into a hard failure:

```ts
// src/agents/sessions/session-manager-entries.ts:331-336
        const anchor = this.persistenceTarget
          ? readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchor({ ...this.persistenceTarget, entryId: current.id })
          : undefined;
        if (this.persistenceTarget && !anchor) {
          throw new Error(`Session transcript anchor was not returned: ${current.id}`);
        }
```

The trigger is production code, not a harness hook. `src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-turn-capture.ts:234` is the only literal `appendMode: "side"` producer in `src/` outside support files: the remaining `appendMode = "side"` assignments (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager.ts:148`, `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-entries.ts:217`) are in-memory view reconstruction and read-back, not store writes.

The condition does self-heal. `scheduleTranscriptProjectionReconcile` at `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-store.ts:250-267` defers a reconcile to post-commit publication, so the anchor comes back once a full projection rebuild finishes. That bounds the severity, but it does not remove the failure: the rebuild is scheduled after the gateway yield and its cost scales with the transcript, so the window is seconds, not microseconds.

The fix boundary is the consumer, not the anchor. The same codebase already models the correct degradation twice: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/pre-persisted-user-turn.ts:113-115` and `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-entries.ts:282-284` both do `if (!anchor) { return undefined; }`. Either degrade the same way, or reconcile on demand before the read; `reconcileSessionTranscriptIndexInTransaction` is already used in production at `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-generation-copy.ts:283` and `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-import.ts`, and `waitForSessionTranscriptIndexReconcile` exists as the async seam.

## Sibling surfaces

Not separately proven, but the same window opens without any side append: `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-index.ts:298-305` also marks the index dirty on any sequence gap from an out-of-band writer (`params.seq !== watermark.indexedSeq + 1`). A gateway and a CLI writing the same store should therefore reach the identical throw with no conversation turn capture involved.

Closest existing report is issue #150204 (`Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`, Talk on `gemini-3.8-live`). That is the adjacent throw in the same function, but a different mechanism: there a realtime voice transcript moves the current-turn anchor before the embedded run adopts its pre-persisted turn. Here the current turn is correct and the projection index is simply dirty, so the anchor read is refused. Open PR #142018 refactors this exact dirty-marking code, but it preserves side-append dirtying (`isSessionTranscriptSideAppendEntry` still returns the prepare-failure that marks dirty) and touches neither the anchor reader nor the throwing consumer, so it does not cover this.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a side-mode append written by the agent reply capture path makes every keyed-user append into that session throw for seconds.
Real environment tested: real OpenClaw runtime at commit 3a54b13977eb4078d470426c4522e0e655b9ee93 (real on-disk SQLite agent store, real appendTranscriptMessage / appendTranscriptEventSync / readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchor / SessionManager.open, nothing stubbed)
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/audit0919/lane-sessions/anchor-dirty.mts`, then `anchor-order.mts`, then `anchor-window.mts`
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, 3a54b13977eb4078d470426c4522e0e655b9ee93) - anchor-dirty.mts
anchor BEFORE side append: {"agentId":"main","sessionId":"anchor-dirty-session","sessionKey":"agent:main:dashboard:anchor-dirty-session","storePath":"/tmp/oc-anchor-dirty-FLNjpX/openclaw-agent.sqlite","generation":"87997313ca9d4c3e9d885e2c1b81d245","entryId":"ingress-persisted-user","rawSeq":2,"effectiveParentId":"existing-assistant","activeMessagePosition":1,"idempotencyKey":"anchor-dirty:user"}
side append result: {"ok":true,"value":true}
anchor AFTER side append: null
dedup append THREW: Session transcript anchor was not returned: ingress-persisted-user

# OBSERVED - anchor-order.mts (realistic ordering: side append first, keyed user persisted after)
side append result: {"ok":true,"value":true}
keyed user persisted AFTER the side append
anchor AFTER side append: null
dedup append THREW: Session transcript anchor was not returned: ingress-persisted-user

# OBSERVED - anchor-window.mts (how long the anchor stays null, by transcript size)
turns=5 anchorBeforeSideAppend=ok anchorImmediatelyAfter=NULL healedAfterMs=NEVER(>4s)
turns=50 anchorBeforeSideAppend=ok anchorImmediatelyAfter=NULL healedAfterMs=1078
turns=200 anchorBeforeSideAppend=ok anchorImmediatelyAfter=NULL healedAfterMs=1469
turns=600 anchorBeforeSideAppend=ok anchorImmediatelyAfter=NULL healedAfterMs=6816

# EXPECTED (correct behavior on identical inputs)
anchor AFTER side append: {"entryId":"ingress-persisted-user", ... same active identity as BEFORE ... }
dedup append OK: entryId=ingress-persisted-user appended=false
```
Observed result after fix: an ordinary agent reply leaves the keyed-user append path throwing `Session transcript anchor was not returned`, and the anchor stays null from hundreds of milliseconds up to several seconds afterward, scaling with transcript size.
What was not tested: the throw itself was driven on running code in two orderings, but the escape to the user was traced statically only. `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-agent-dispatch.ts` hands a dispatch rejection to `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.ts:210-275`, where the run is terminalized as `status: "failed"` and a lifecycle error is published; that chain was read, not driven end to end through the gateway, so this is not an end-to-end gateway reproduction. The sibling sequence-gap trigger at `session-transcript-index.ts:298-305` was read, not reproduced. The `turns=5` row did not recover inside its 4 second probe window, which on that first-measured session also pays one-time reconcile worker startup.

issues.body:
### Summary

Session-level model pins/overrides (set via the Control UI model picker, `/model <id>`, or `sessions.patch`) replace the agent's entire candidate list with that single model. When the pinned model's provider fails (rate limit, usage limit, outage), the run surfaces the error instead of consulting the agent's configured fallback chain.

Proposal: **pinned models should inherit the agent's fallback chain** (pinned model first, then the configured fallbacks), with an opt-out for deliberate "this model only" pins.

### Current behavior

Agent config carries a real chain:

```json5
agents.entries.toolbuilder.model = { primary: "kimicode/k3", fallbacks: ["zai/glm-5.3", "kimicode/k3"] }
```

But a session pinned to `openai/gpt-6-astra` (subscription OAuth) fails hard when the subscription hits its usage window:

```
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed
  requested=openai/gpt-6-astra candidate=openai/gpt-6-astra reason=rate_limit next=none
  detail=Codex error: The usage limit has been reached
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: ... decision=surface_error reason=rate_limit
  attempt=1 retry=0 rotations=0 from=openai/gpt-6-astra
```

`next=none` is the tell: the candidate list contains only the pinned model. The user sees "The agent run failed before producing a reply." Meanwhile sibling sessions on the same agent (unpinned) fail over astra → sol → glm correctly, so the chain itself works — pins just don't carry it.

Reproduced on 2026.9.4 across two incidents (2026-09-15 and 2026-09-18) during a multi-day ChatGPT-subscription usage-limit window: every pinned-to-astra session failed with `next=none` while unpinned sessions on the same agents kept working via fallback.

### Expected behavior

When a session is pinned to model M, build the candidate list as `[M, ...agents.<agent>.model.fallbacks]` (deduped), so provider failures on the pin fall through to the configured chain instead of terminating the turn.

Possible shapes (any would resolve the incidents):

1. **Always inherit** — pins always append the agent's configured fallbacks.
2. **Opt-out flag** — inherit by default; `--no-fallback` / UI toggle for deliberate single-model pins.
3. **Config default** — e.g. `agents.defaults.modelPins.inheritFallbacks: true | false | "explicit-only"`.

Related: `agents.defaults.subagents.model` accepts a bare string (no fallbacks) or `{primary, fallbacks}` — task/spawn sessions created before this field was set in object form had the same single-candidate failure mode. Making string-form model refs everywhere resolve as `{primary: <string>, fallbacks: <agent chain>}` would close the remaining gap.

### Why this matters operationally

Subscription usage windows (ChatGPT 5h/weekly caps) and prepaid-credit exhaustion can last hours or days. During those windows, any session pinned to the capped model becomes unusable and requires manual intervention (re-pin to a healthy model, or `/model default`), even though healthy fallbacks are configured on the agent. Pins silently downgrade resilience to zero.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)
- macOS 26.3.1 (arm64), node 24.20.0
- Agents: 16 configured agents, all with `{primary, fallbacks}` chains; pins set via Control UI model picker

### Related issues

- #116315 — session overrides silently bypass the fallback chain (observed as one symptom of a larger incident; this FR proposes the design fix for that aspect)
- #141115 — 429 from primary terminates session instead of consulting fallback chain
- #149785 — usage-limit error surfaces without mid-run fallback on first occurrence

# `-05` A 块 · **D1 脱敏最小复现**：ACP 会话清理失败（每分钟刷屏 + stop 报错误导）

> **用途**：可提交 OpenClaw 上游的缺陷复现报告。**已脱敏**：路径用 `$HOME` / `<acp-session-id>` 占位，**不含任何凭据、密钥、会话内容**。
> **本地证据附录**（含真实路径与原始日志）另存，**不随本报告外发**。
> **采集**：2026-09-18 · 环境：WSL2 · OpenClaw `2026.9.4` · `@openclaw/acpx`（本机安装于 `$HOME/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-acpx-052d680d6d`）· `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`（claude 通道）· `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` `1.6.2`

---

## 0. 一句话

**ACP 会话清理失败在持续刷屏**（实测 **每分钟 4 条**、今日累计 **3440 条**），且**程序化 `stop` 会报一条与事实相反的 `AcpRuntimeError`**（报失败、实际已停），**`openclaw doctor --fix` 修不掉**。

---

## 1. 版本与创建方式（复现前提）

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | `2026.9.4` |
| acpx | 作为 OpenClaw 插件启用（`plugins.entries.acpx.enabled = true`），`acp.backend = "acpx"` |
| ACP 适配器 | `claude-agent-acp`（claude 通道）· `codex-acp@1.6.2`（codex 通道） |
| 启动方式 | systemd 用户服务 `openclaw-gateway.service`（`Restart=always`） |
| 会话创建方式 | 由 OpenClaw 经 acpx 派发 ACP 任务（`runtime="acp"`）；会话键形如 `agent:<role>:acp:<uuid>` |

---

## 2. 现象 A：**会话清理失败持续刷屏**（每分钟 4 条）

网关日志**稳定**输出（每分钟一次，各 2 条）：

```
[tasks/task-registry-maintenance] Failed to close terminal ACP session during task maintenance
[tasks/task-registry-maintenance] Failed to close orphaned parent-owned ACP session during task maintenance
```

**实测统计（单日，`$HOME` 环境）**：

| 指标 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 当日总条数 | **3440** |
| `terminal ACP session` | 1720 |
| `orphaned parent-owned ACP session` | 1720 |
| 节律 | **每分钟 4 条**（21:34:01 / 21:35:01 / 21:36:01 … 每小时稳定 4×60） |

**关键观察**：**1720 与 1720 严格相等** ⇒ 像是对**同一批**残留会话**两条路径各试一次、各失败一次**（terminal + orphaned），且**每次都没能清掉**（否则不会持续复现）。

**期望**：任务维护在发现终态/孤儿会话后应能**清掉**它们；若清不掉，应给出**一次**可诊断的错误（含 `session id` 与失败原因），而不是**每分钟重复同一行**。

---

## 3. 现象 B：程序化 `stop` 报错误导（报失败实则成功）

**操作**：对一条已存在的 ACP 会话执行程序化停止（`openclaw sessions delete agent:<role>:acp:<uuid>`）。

**结果**：命令**返回失败**，错误文本：

```
AcpRuntimeError: ACP session "<acp-session-id>" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator.
Stop the Gateway and run "openclaw doctor --fix" to migrate ownership without losing history, then restart.
```

**但实际状态**：
- 该 run 变为 `agent run aborted`；
- **进程树被回收**；
- `acp_sessions` 表中该会话变为 `idle`。

⇒ **报失败、实际已停**（与退出码语义相反的误导）。

**按报错指引执行 `openclaw doctor --fix`（离线）之后，同一错误依旧复现** ⇒ 不是"未迁移"那么简单。

---

## 4. locator / ownership 结构（供定位用）

- 报错关键词：**"unqualified or unverifiable backend locator"** ⇒ 提示该会话的 **backend locator 不可解析/未授权限定**；
- 会话键：`agent:<role>:acp:<uuid>`（挂在**主 agent** 名下，非独立 agent）；
- `doctor --fix` 的迁移**未改变**该判定 ⇒ 要么迁移不覆盖这类记录，要么判定条件与迁移目标不一致。

**期望**：① 定位器可解析时给出**明确**的不可验证原因（缺哪个字段/哪个字段不合规）；② 若 `stop` 实际生效，**退出码/错误面应反映真实结果**（或至少措辞区分"已停但记录有疑"）。

---

## 5. 停止与清理各自的结果（对照表）

| 动作 | 报告结果 | 实际结果 | 一致？ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openclaw sessions delete agent:<role>:acp:<uuid>` | ❌ 报 `AcpRuntimeError` | ✅ 已停（run aborted、进程树回收、`acp_sessions=idle`） | **不一致（误导）** |
| `openclaw doctor --fix` | 执行成功 | ❌ 同一错误依旧 | **无效** |
| 任务维护清理（每分钟） | ❌ `Failed to close …` | ❌ 未清掉（持续复现） | 一致但**无进展** |
| `/acp cancel` · `/acp close` | — | 仅**操作员**命令（agent 侧不可用） | — |

---

## 6. 期望修复（上游）

1. **任务维护**：对**同一条**残留会话**不要**每分钟重复同一失败；给出**一次**可诊断错误（含 `session id` / locator / 失败原因），并给出可执行的清理路径；
2. **`stop` 的语义**：状态与退出码**一致**（已停 ⇒ 不报失败）；或明确区分「已停但记录可疑」；
3. **`doctor --fix`**：要么真能修（含"unqualified/unverifiable locator"这一类），要么明确说明**不覆盖**该情形；
4. 允许 agent 侧有**优雅 cancel**（不必依赖操作员命令）。

---

## 7. 我方止损（非上游问题，供参考，**不要求上游处理**）

我们已用 **不依赖退出码**的停止路径规避（判据 = 执行组整体退出 + 观察窗口内无新输出/写入；输出三态 `STOPPED_CLEAN / STOPPED_DIRTY / STOP_UNKNOWN`），因此现象 B **不再阻塞我方流程**；现象 A 仍**持续污染日志面**。

---

## 8. 未覆盖 / 已知局限（诚实声明）

1. 本报告的证据取自**一台特定 WSL2 主机**的**单日**窗口；**未**在第二台机器或干净环境复核；
2. `Failed to close …` 的**内部失败原因**未能取到（日志只给了结论行，无 `session id`/原因字段）——这**本身也是缺陷的一部分**（不可诊断）；
3. 现象 B 的复现**依赖一条已存在的 ACP 会话**；本报告记录了**操作与结果**，但**未能**给出"零依赖最小脚本"（需要先建会话）；
4. **未**测 `codex` 通道下的同类现象（仅 claude 通道观测）。

issues.body:
﻿## Summary

On Windows, deleting an `explicit` session can fail with `ENOENT` when the session ID contains characters that are invalid in Windows filenames, especially `:`.

The session remains visible in the session list even though it has no active run and is otherwise deletable.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11
- OpenClaw: `2026.9.2 (3928bad)`
- Session store: SQLite
- Install type: npm/global dist build

## Reproduction

A session existed with the key:

```text
agent:main:explicit:agent:main:kv-prefix-marker-final-20260913
```

Its `sessionId` was:

```text
agent:main:kv-prefix-marker-final-20260913
```

The session had no active run.

Dry-run deletion succeeded:

```text
openclaw sessions delete "agent:main:explicit:agent:main:kv-prefix-marker-final-20260913" --agent main --dry-run --json
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "would_delete"
}
```

But the real deletion failed with an `ENOENT` filesystem error during transcript archival.

## Root cause

The delete lifecycle archives the transcript before removing the SQLite session state.

In `session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle-state-*.js`, the archive filename is derived from `sessionId` through:

```js
resolveRegisteredArchiveSessionIdComponent(sessionId)
resolveSqliteTranscriptArchivePath(params)
```

The current logic hashes the session ID only when it exceeds `MAX_REGISTERED_ARCHIVE_SESSION_ID_BYTES`:

```js
function resolveRegisteredArchiveSessionIdComponent(sessionId) {
    if (Buffer.byteLength(sessionId, "utf8") <= MAX_REGISTERED_ARCHIVE_SESSION_ID_BYTES) return sessionId;
    return `session-${createHash("sha256").update(sessionId).digest("hex")}`;
}
```

That means a short session ID containing `:` is used directly as a filename component.

On Windows this produces an invalid path similar to:

```text
...\sessions\agent:main:kv-prefix-marker-final-20260913.jsonl.deleted....
```

Because `:` is illegal in a Windows filename, archive materialization fails before the delete transaction can complete.

## Expected behavior

Deleting a session should work regardless of whether its logical/session ID contains characters that are unsafe for the host filesystem.

## Proposed fix

Use a filesystem-safe component for registered transcript archive filenames. Hash not only overlong IDs, but also IDs that are unsafe as a filename on Windows.

For example, treat these cases as unsafe:

```text
< > : " / \ | ? *
```

Also account for Windows reserved device names (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`...`COM9`, `LPT1`...`LPT9`) and trailing spaces/dots.

A minimal approach is to fall back to the existing deterministic SHA-256 form:

```text
session-<sha256(sessionId)>
```

whenever the raw `sessionId` is not safe as a filename component.

## Local validation

I patched `resolveRegisteredArchiveSessionIdComponent()` locally so that unsafe Windows filename components are hashed.

After restarting the Gateway:

1. The previously undeletable `explicit` session deleted successfully.
2. Session count dropped from 7 to 6.
3. A fresh full session listing confirmed the session was gone.
4. Transcript archival completed successfully using a hashed filename such as:

```text
session-1bf6bef288be6187a9bfd760f49f1bfc2bf0a80c06b356f7b83f03f759acef78.jsonl.deleted....
```

So this appears to be a Windows filename-sanitization bug in the SQLite session deletion/archive lifecycle rather than a UI-only issue.

issues.body:
## Summary

The `markdownDetails` runtime capability is granted purely on `channel === "webchat"`, without any reference to which client is actually attached to that channel. Any client connecting on the webchat channel is told the surface renders collapsible disclosures — including clients whose renderer has no `<details>` support. Those users see raw `<details>`/`<summary>` tags as literal text.

## Where

`src/agents/runtime-capabilities.ts`, in `collectRuntimeChannelCapabilities()` (shipped as `dist/runtime-capabilities-Bbg598wa.mjs:223` in 2026.9.4):

```js
const internalChannelCapabilities = params.channel === "webchat" ? ["markdownDetails"] : [];
```

The capability flows into the system prompt at `dist/system-prompt-params-BOlFEPMI.mjs:681`:

```js
const collapsibleDetailsSupported = runtimeCapabilitiesLower.has("markdowndetails");
```

which produces the "This surface renders `<details>` disclosures" prompt section. The model then emits disclosures in good faith.

## Why it is wrong

`collectRuntimeChannelCapabilities(params)` only receives `channel`, `accountId` and `cfg`. It has no client identity in scope at all, so it cannot condition on the renderer even in principle.

Meanwhile the actual `<details>` implementation is browser-only: it is a markdown-it rule in the browser Control UI bundle (`dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-boot-shared-*.js`, the `markdownDetailsStack` rules that emit `<summary>`/`</summary>`). A client that does not load that bundle has no disclosure widget, regardless of what the handshake was told.

There is already a correct fallback for this exact situation — `flattenMarkdownDetails()` in `src/infra/outbound/protocol-scaffolding.ts`, documented as "Flattens model-authored details blocks for transports without native disclosure widgets" — but it is only reached through `sanitizeForPlainText()`, i.e. for plain-text transports. A webchat client that cannot render disclosures gets neither the widget nor the flattening.

## Deeper problem: this is not a session-level property

The capability is resolved once, at agent startup, and baked into the system prompt. But clients connect, disconnect, and can read the same session concurrently from different surfaces. "Can the reader render `<details>`" is a property of a live connection, not of a session or a channel name, so no startup-time value can be correct for the whole session's lifetime.

## Suggested fix

Gate on a client-advertised handshake capability rather than on the channel name. The codebase already has the mechanism: `GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/client-info.ts`, read via `hasGatewayClientCap(client?.connect?.caps, …)` — the same pattern used for `task-suggestions` and `inline-widgets`.

Concretely:

1. Add `MARKDOWN_DETAILS: "markdown-details"` to `GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS`.
2. Have the browser Control UI advertise it (it is the surface that actually ships the markdown-it rule).
3. Replace the `params.channel === "webchat"` test with a `hasGatewayClientCap()` check, threading client info into `collectRuntimeChannelCapabilities()`.
4. When the capability is absent, run outbound webchat text through the existing `flattenMarkdownDetails()` so a model that emits disclosures anyway still degrades to readable text instead of raw tags.

Letting the renderer declare what it can render is also the only version that stays correct when a second client with different capabilities joins the same session.

Gating on `isBrowserOperatorUiClient()` (already in `src/.../message-channel.ts`) would be a smaller change, but see the open question below — it may not discriminate.

## Open question for maintainers

I could not determine which client id the Windows Companion's native chat window uses. `GATEWAY_CLIENT_IDS` has `MACOS_APP`, `LINUX_APP`, `IOS_APP`, `WATCHOS_APP`, `ANDROID_APP` — but no Windows entry, and `normalizeGatewayClientId()` rejects unknown ids. The only handshake in my retained gateway logs is:

```
gateway/ws webchat connected client=openclaw-control-ui webchat v2026.9.4
```

from a Windows host. If the Companion also presents as `openclaw-control-ui`, then client-id-based discrimination cannot work and the advertised-capability approach above is the only correct fix.

## Repro

1. Open a webchat session from a client whose renderer lacks `<details>` support.
2. Observe the runtime advertises `capabilities=markdowndetails`.
3. Ask for an answer with optional depth; the model emits `<details><summary>…`.
4. The tags render as literal text.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (`3a9d69d`), build `2026.9.4-release-3a9d69db306c`
- Gateway on Linux 6.1.0-31-amd64, node 24.21.0
- Client: Windows 11, OpenClaw Windows Companion

issues.body:
### Summary

Restore a per-account inbound debounce for multi-account channels (at least WhatsApp). Since #113174 ("retire redundant settings"), `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.debounceMs` is migrated into the single `messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp`. Two accounts that serve agents with opposite pacing needs can no longer have different values.

### Problem to solve

The per-account key was not redundant with the channel key. On a multi-account WhatsApp gateway each account is usually bound to a different agent, and they need different batching:

- **Account `default` → internal operations agent** (team DMs and groups). Needs `0`: people expect an immediate answer, and messages are usually single, complete requests.
- **Account `sales` → public-facing sales agent.** Leads type in bursts ("hi" / "I want info" / "about the course" / a question, 10–30 s apart). With `0` the agent answers each fragment separately. It falls behind its own FIFO queue, re-asks things the lead already answered, and answers stale topics. We measured this before the upgrade: 35 inbound messages in 11 min produced 35 turns at 40–50 s each, and the processing lag grew monotonically from 10 s to 390 s. `debounceMs: 30000` on that account fixed it (≈35 turns → ≈9).

What 2026.9.2 did on upgrade (`migrateWhatsAppDebounce` in the legacy-config migrations):

```
channels.whatsapp.debounceMs = 0                         (root)
channels.whatsapp.accounts.sales.debounceMs = 30000
→ messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp = 0                (value of `defaultAccount`/"default" wins)
  "Collapsed conflicting WhatsApp debounce values …; account-specific debounce is no longer supported."
```

After the upgrade the sales agent's p95 time-to-first-reply dropped from ~31 s to ~8.5 s. That looks like an improvement, but it is the batching disappearing. The migration note only appears in doctor/migration output: nothing at runtime says that a conflicting value was dropped. We found it by diffing config backups two weeks later.

There is no workaround inside the config today:
- `messages.inbound` only accepts `debounceMs` and `byChannel` (a `byAccount` key fails validation);
- `messages.queue.debounceMsByChannel` is per channel too;
- `/queue` per-session settings don't scale to a public account where every lead is a new session;
- any single value is wrong for one of the two agents: `30000` adds 30 s to every internal text reply, and `0` breaks the sales agent.

### Proposed solution

Add an account layer to the existing resolution order, keeping `byChannel` as the canonical surface:

```json5
messages: {
  inbound: {
    debounceMs: 0,
    byChannel: { whatsapp: 0 },
    byAccount: { whatsapp: { sales: 30000 } }   // new
  }
}
```

Resolution: `overrideMs → byAccount[channel][accountId] → byChannel[channel] → debounceMs → 0`.

Most of the plumbing already exists in 2026.9.2:
- `resolveInboundDebounceMs({ cfg, channel, overrideMs })` already takes an override;
- the WhatsApp monitor already threads `tuning.debounceMs` → `attachWebInboxToSocket({ debounceMs })` → `resolveInboundDebounceMs({ overrideMs: options.debounceMs })`;
- but `gateway.startAccount` calls `monitorWebChannel(…, { statusSink, accountId, channelRuntime })` without `debounceMs`, so the override is always `undefined`.

The resolver would also need `accountId`, so that a hot reload (`loadConfig()` is re-read on each message) picks the new value up without reconnecting.

A doctor migration could reverse the collapse for configs that still have the pre-9.x backup values. It isn't necessary: operators can re-add the key.

### Alternatives considered

- **Per-agent** (`agents.list[].inbound.debounceMs`): it matches the real intent (pacing belongs to the agent persona), but routing to an agent happens after the debounce key is built, so per-account is the simpler cut.
- **Per-group debounce** (#54565): complementary. It solves group-level pacing, not DM pacing on a public account.
- A **plugin**: the hooks we use (`message_sending`, `reply_payload_sending`) act on output. We didn't find a documented inbound hook that can hold and coalesce messages before dispatch.

### Impact

- **Affected:** any gateway with more than one account on the same channel bound to agents with different audiences (internal team vs. public leads is the common case).
- **Severity:** medium. It silently degrades conversation quality on the public agent (repetition, stale answers, more turns and tokens), with nothing in the logs.
- **Frequency:** every inbound burst on the affected account.
- **Consequence:** operators must pick which agent gets the wrong batching.

### Evidence/examples

- Retirement: #113174 (merged 2026-07-24). Its description groups the WhatsApp debounce keys with genuinely duplicate UI/typing settings.
- Upgrade path observed on 2026.9.2 (3928bad): the per-account value was present in every backup up to the upgrade, and absent from every backup after it. `messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp` took the default account's `0`.
- Runtime code paths referenced above: `src/auto-reply/inbound-debounce.ts` (`resolveInboundDebounceMs`), the WhatsApp extension monitor (`attachWebInboxToSocket`, `createWhatsAppInboundMessageDebouncer`) and channel `gateway.startAccount`.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Not right now. We can test a build on a real two-account WhatsApp gateway.

### Additional information

Related: #54565 (per-group debounce), #146117 / #146178 (image coalescing on WhatsApp). Note that `shouldDebounceTextInbound` never batches media or empty-text interactive messages, so per-account debounce addresses text bursts only.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in, single-owner escalation provider for Active Memory so a plugin can decide whether to start deep recall after the deterministic lane has no strong hit.

## Problem to solve

Active Memory has a sound two-lane architecture: the deterministic lane is cheap, while the deep lane runs a blocking embedded agent only when escalation is warranted. In the default escalate mode, however, the escalation decision is closed inside the bundled plugin and based on a built-in lexical intent matcher.

That leaves operators with only three choices:

- off: never run deep recall;
- always: pay for a blocking recall agent on every eligible turn;
- escalate: depend on the built-in matcher.

The matcher has already required language-specific repairs, including CJK support and the current PT-BR work in #135085 and #136502. A third-party plugin cannot replace only this decision: prompt-build hooks compose rather than claim the decision, and replacing the bundled Active Memory plugin also means taking ownership of its session isolation, privacy rules, timeouts, cleanup, caching, circuit breaker, status and deep-recall orchestration.

The missing capability is not another recall engine. It is a supported extension point for the small decision immediately before deep recall.

## Proposed solution

Expose an optional, lifecycle-aware Active Memory escalation provider through the plugin SDK.

Conceptually:

- a plugin registers one provider by id;
- Active Memory selects it through an optional escalationProvider config field;
- the provider runs only in escalate mode, after the deterministic lane has no strong hit and before the embedded recall agent starts;
- it returns recall, skip, or abstain;
- the provider receives an AbortSignal and a short bounded timeout;
- absent, missing, timed-out, failed or abstaining providers fall back according to an explicit, documented policy;
- off, always and strong deterministic hits retain their current behavior;
- existing configurations and defaults remain unchanged.

A dedicated provider is preferable to a general accumulating hook because exactly one component should own this decision. The SDK contract should not require or bundle any model. Implementations could be deterministic, local learned classifiers, or another policy chosen by the operator.

I plan to open a focused PR containing the SDK contract, registry/lifecycle handling, Active Memory integration, config/schema/UI hints, documentation and tests. It will not add a model, weights, network request or new runtime dependency.

## Alternatives considered

### Keep adding language-specific matcher rules

This preserves zero-dependency behavior but does not provide a scalable customization path. The PT-BR gap demonstrates that operators cannot currently supply a better policy without replacing the whole plugin.

### Run a generic LLM completion before recall

This adds another serial model request, authentication/failure surface, cost and latency to the path whose purpose is deciding whether to pay for deep recall.

### Replace the bundled Active Memory plugin

OpenClaw supports config plugins overriding bundled plugins, but this forces a third party to duplicate and track the full deep-recall implementation merely to change one decision.

### Use an ordinary prompt-build hook

Prompt-build hook results compose and do not offer a single-winner handled/cancel contract for this decision.

## Impact

Affected users and systems:

- multilingual personal-assistant deployments;
- operators with local or domain-specific recall-intent policies;
- latency-sensitive agents that cannot use always mode;
- plugin authors who want to improve escalation without owning memory retrieval.

Severity: medium. The current default works for covered formulations, but uncovered language or semantic forms can silently skip deep recall, while always mode adds a blocking agent run to ordinary turns.

Frequency: every eligible conversational turn reaches this policy after a weak deterministic result.

Consequence: either missed historical context, unnecessary latency, or downstream maintenance of a private Active Memory replacement.

## Evidence/examples

- PT-BR recall-intent gap: #135085
- PT-BR matcher repair: #136502
- Prior CJK matcher repair: #117419
- Blocking Active Memory latency report: #72015
- Active Memory documents that lane 1 makes zero model calls and lane 2 is a real agent turn:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/concepts/memory-architecture.md
- Current decision is internal to:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The intended PR is additive and opt-in. It preserves the current built-in policy as the default and keeps model selection, datasets and classifier artifacts outside OpenClaw core. I will include focused provider lifecycle, sync/async, timeout, error, missing-provider, mode, strong-hit and embedded-run boundary tests.
