issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`relocateCandidateRange` in `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-rehydrate.ts` re-finds a stored recall candidate by scanning the whole live note for its snippet. It carries no prefix/suffix context, it accepts containment matches, and `normalizeRangeSnippet` compares the live range to the stored snippet after nothing but `trim()` and whitespace collapsing.

Two consequences, measured on one production workspace with all 512 live `short-term-recall` entries:

- **Ambiguous anchors:** for **89 of 512 candidates (17.4%)** the top-quality match occurs at more than one disjoint place in the file. The shipped tie-break then decides by line distance alone.
- **Fragment anchors after a normalization mismatch:** **22 candidates** relocate to a *fragment* of their stored snippet (quality 1), **14** resolve to nothing, 476 resolve at their stored range. All 22 fragment cases have an HTML comment inside the live range and none in the stored snippet. Stripping HTML comments from the live text restores containment for **22 of 22**.

In the worst three cases the stored 695-character snippet occurs **0 times** in the live note, while the fragment the promoter anchors on occurs **26 times**.

The W3C Web Annotation Data Model §4.2.4 introduces prefix/suffix precisely "to distinguish between multiple copies", and §4.2 requires a consuming agent to pick one when several sequences match. Brush, Bargeron, Gupta & Cadiz, *Robust Annotation Positioning in Digital Documents* (CHI '01, doi:10.1145/365024.365117) report that users preferred orphaning over partial-match repositioning (§5.3.3, §5.3.4).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Let memory-core record a `short-term-recall` candidate for a range in a memory note.
2. Add an HTML comment inside that range in the note, or let any tool that writes HTML comments do it.
3. Trigger rehydration for that candidate.
4. Observe the returned range: `normalizeRangeSnippet(lines, start, end)` no longer contains the stored snippet, so the scan falls back to a quality-1 fragment match and returns a different range, or `null`.

To reproduce the ambiguity independent of that cause, store a candidate whose snippet text also appears elsewhere in the same note and observe that the returned range is decided only by line distance.

### Expected behavior

- The stored snippet and the live range pass through the same normalization, so a note that only gained an HTML comment still resolves at its own range.
- When no unique match exists, the candidate is reported as lost (orphaned) instead of anchoring on a fragment that occurs many times in the file.

### Actual behavior

- The recorded snippet and the live range are normalized differently, so a range that merely gained an HTML comment stops matching.
- The promoter then anchors on a fragment and reports a relocation, or drops the candidate.
- Where several places match equally well, the pick is silent and distance-based.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4, and current `main` (`6a7b1e41`) is unchanged in this respect: `normalizeRangeSnippet` still calls only `normalizeSnippet`, which is `trim()` plus whitespace collapsing.

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global install

### Model

Not model-dependent. The measurement calls the shipped function directly; no model is involved.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable.

### Logs

No error is logged. The defect is silent: relocation and drop are ordinary outcomes of the scan.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The measurement is pre-registered and runs the shipped code rather than a paraphrase. Bytes 49203..59195 of `dist/short-term-promotion-Dn3jonZ9.mjs` (region SHA-256 `30c829d8e1641a38309f86c3e985b2c9b5b438cd770cad4f584d783c40a7151d`) were copied verbatim into a harness; only imports and an export were added. An instrumented copy with unchanged scoring collected every top-quality window; the shipped function's own answer was inside a top-quality place in 512 of 512 cases, so harness drift would have shown up as a mismatch rather than as a finding.

Population: all 512 live `short-term-recall` entries of one workspace (123 range entries, 389 claim entries), read read-only. Classification and headline numbers were fixed before the run.

| | n |
|---|---|
| resolved at the stored range | 476 |
| relocated | 22 |
| dropped (no match) | 14 |
| anchor matches more than one disjoint place | 89 (17.4%) |
| quality-1 fragment anchors | 22 (all relocated) |

A separate falsification inserted k lines above a stored range in memory only: two of three inspected candidates hold for k = 0, 2, 4 and jump to a different copy of the same boilerplate at k = 8, 16, 24. The third holds at every k tested, so the failure is data-dependent.

We can share the harness, the perturbation script and the anonymized census rows (ranges and outcomes only, no note text) if that helps.

### Impact and severity

Silent and latent rather than loud: a promotion anchored on a fragment can carry the wrong lines of the right file into a later turn, and there is no signal that it happened. It grows with note age, because every HTML comment written into a note after recording makes the stored snippet unmatchable.

### Suggested fix

1. Send the stored snippet and the live range through one shared normalization. This alone restores 22 of 22 cases in our data.
2. Treat a quality-1 fragment match as a lost candidate and report it, instead of promoting the fragment.
3. Require the chosen window to be unique in the file; otherwise orphan the candidate, or store prefix/suffix context so that the pick can be justified.

issues.body:
## Summary

Workboard operations (`list`, `show`, `promote`, and dispatch flows) hydrate **the entire card universe on every call**. The SQLite store runs:

```sql
SELECT * FROM workboard_cards ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC
```

followed by JS-side filtering in `WorkboardStore.list()` — there is no SQL-level status/board filter and no pagination, so every operation pays for all cards, including the ever-growing pile of `done` ones.

## Measured impact (self-hosted gateway)

- Universe: **1,156 cards** (1,053 `done` = 91%), ~13.9k events
- `workboard list --status ready`: **16.7s** wall — CPU-bound (9.7–11.1s user time), and identical wall time for a full list vs a ready-only list, confirming full-universe hydration either way
- SQLite itself is exonerated: `EXPLAIN` on a copy runs in 0.007s — the cost is JS materialization, not the DB
- Slow transaction holds grow with the universe (125→131 per 24h on our box); cron jobs with 30s timeouts start failing under parallel operations (21.8–28.3s wall observed)

## Requests

1. **SQL-level filtering/pagination for list/show/promote** — push the `status`/`boardId` filters into the SQL query (and optionally a `--limit`), so operations don't hydrate the done-card universe
2. **Archive/prune capability for done cards** — the schema already has an `archived` notion (counts expose `cards_archived`) but the CLI (2026.9.4) exposes no archive/prune command. Without it, retention isn't operable, universes grow forever, and every operation keeps slowing down

## Workaround in use

Direct SQLite retention (`.backup` snapshot + delete `done` cards older than N days) — it works, but it's outside the tool and easy to get wrong with the DB in WAL mode.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (linuxbrew install), workboard plugin, ~1.1k+ cards
- Checked existing issues (#94555, #118725, #116359, #116395 — archive semantics only): no duplicate found for the hydration/performance issue

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

I've been running 2026.7.1 with ~/.openclaw bind-mounted from a Windows drive (Docker Desktop, WSL2) for months. Every version I've tried since 2026.9.3 exits on startup on the same mount: right after writing a file, OpenClaw can't read it back (ENOENT), treats the write as failed, rolls it back and exits.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an empty folder on a Windows drive, e.g. `D:\oc-test`
2. `docker run --rm -v "D:\oc-test:/home/node/.openclaw" ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.11.5-beta.1 node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured`
3. Container exits with code 1 after ~17s.

### Expected behavior

Gateway starts and `/health` returns 200, like 2026.7.1 does on the same mount.

### Actual behavior

Exit code 1 before the gateway serves anything.

What happens: OpenClaw writes the file and renames it into place. That works; the file is on disk with the right content and shows up in the directory listing. Then it checks the file it just wrote, while still holding it open. On this mount that check gets ENOENT, so the write is treated as failed and rolled back.

Not an ownership issue: same result after `chown 1000:1000` on the folder.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5-beta.1

### Operating system

Windows 11 Enterprise 26300, Docker Desktop 4.95.0 (WSL2 backend), WSL 2.6.3.0

### Install method

docker (ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw image)

### Model

N/A — exits before any model loads

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — exits before any model loads

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# OpenClaw startup
Doctor could not complete maintenance. Check the reported service state and resolve the failure.
Config was written to /home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json, but post-write processing failed: ENOENT: no such file or directory, fstat
The config write was rolled back.

# Same mount, plain Node, no OpenClaw: write tmp file, rename it while the fd is still open
fstat before rename -> dev=69 ino=1125899908462790
renameSync(tmp,dst) -> ok
fstatSync(fd) -> ENOENT
statSync(dst) -> ENOENT
lstatSync(dst) -> ENOENT
openSync(dst,'r') -> ENOENT
readdirSync(dir) -> ok ["dst.json"]
closeSync(fd) -> ok
statSync(dst) after close -> ok ino=1125899908462790 sameInoAsBefore=true
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Mount inside the container:
`9p D:\ rw,aname=drvfs;path=D:\;uid=0;gid=0;metadata;symlinkroot=/mnt/host/,cache=5,access=client,msize=65536,trans=fd`

Calling fs-safe 0.26.13 directly on the same mount (native addon loaded), every atomic write fails the same way. The file ends up on disk with the expected content:

```
ENOENT: no such file or directory, fstat (errno -2)
  at fstatSync
  at AtomicFile.statExact (atomic-io.js)
  at inspectFileIdentity (strict-file-identity.js)
  at AtomicTempOwner.assertCurrent (replace-file-temp-owner.js)
  at AtomicTempOwner.assertPublished (replace-file-temp-owner.js)
```

`replaceFileAtomic`, `writeTextAtomic`, `replaceFileAtomicSync`: all fail. Native `root().write`: `helper-failed`, cause `inspect staged child: No such file or directory (os error 2)`. Same calls on a named volume: all pass.

Root cause is the plain-Node case in Logs. Looks like microsoft/WSL#8443.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Docker Desktop on Windows, state dir bind-mounted from a Windows drive.
- Severity: gateway won't start.
- Frequency: every run (2026.9.3, 9.6, 9.7, 11.5-beta.1 all fail).
- Consequence: stuck on 2026.7.x unless the state dir moves to a named volume.
- Why not just use a volume: a named volume works, but then I can't edit openclaw.json, skills and workspace files directly from Windows, which is the whole point of the bind mount.

### Additional information

- Last good: 2026.7.1 (fs-safe 0.4.1). First seen bad: 2026.9.3 (fs-safe 0.8.5). 7.35 and 8.x not tested.
- Workaround: put the state dir on a named volume (healthy in ~97s on 11.5-beta.1).
- Possibly the same root cause as the `lstat` ENOENT in #142653 (that one is the read side, not confirmed).
- I can share the repro scripts or test a patched build.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Android realtime Talk does not follow the conversation selected in Chat: speech transcripts are persisted to a separate device-scoped session instead, making voice history absent from the displayed conversation.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on one Android device connected to the same Gateway:

1. Select an existing conversation A in the Android app and start realtime Talk from its chat screen.
2. Speak with the assistant and end the call.
3. Repeat with a different existing conversation B.
4. Inspect both conversations: neither contains the spoken exchange.
5. Inspect the device-scoped session (`agent:main:node-<redacted>`): finalized user and assistant speech records are present there, with `provenance.kind = realtime_voice` and `sourceChannel = talk`.

The user performed the phone interactions; the investigation independently inspected Gateway history, logs, and a local upstream source checkout. No automated phone reproduction or patched-client acceptance test was performed.

### Expected behavior

Starting Talk from a selected chat should preserve that conversation's ownership and history, or the UI should explicitly identify a different voice conversation before starting. Switching visible conversations should not silently leave Talk attached to an unrelated device conversation.

The installed `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md` states that finalized user and assistant utterances are appended to the active agent session so chat and voice share history. The observed destination is not the conversation displayed in Chat.

### Actual behavior

Both selected chats appear to have no voice history. The speech is not lost: it is saved in the separate device-scoped session. In this installation that session was also archived; three `talk.client.toolCall` requests were rejected for that archived destination, even though audio conversation and transcript persistence continued.

This report focuses on **selected-chat versus Talk session binding**. Archived-session startup admission is separately reported in #175027; please do not treat restoring the device session as a fix for the selected-conversation mismatch.

### OpenClaw version

Gateway: `2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9`). Exact installed Android app version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Operating system

Client: Android, Xiaomi 17; exact Android version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.
Gateway: Linux x64, kernel `7.0.0-38-generic`, Node.js `26.8.2`.

### Install method

Gateway: npm global. Android app distribution/install method: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Model

Talk provider: Google. Live catalog default: `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`; no explicit realtime model override in the inspected config. Saved speech records identify provider `google`, model `realtime-voice`. The exact provider model negotiated for the captured call was not independently logged.

### Provider / routing chain

Android Talk -> Gateway Talk relay -> Google realtime voice; agent consultations target the device-scoped agent session rather than the selected dashboard conversation.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Relevant non-secret configuration:

```json
{"talk":{"realtime":{"provider":"google"}}}
```

### Logs

Redacted Gateway journal, 2026-10-25, UTC+08:00:

```text
12:15:35.394 [ws] res OK talk.session.appendAudio
12:16:13.984 [ws] res ERROR talk.client.toolCall INVALID_REQUEST
  Session "agent:main:node-<redacted>" is archived. Restore it before starting new work.
12:18:10.211 [ws] res ERROR talk.client.toolCall INVALID_REQUEST
  Session "agent:main:node-<redacted>" is archived. Restore it before starting new work.
12:19:11.814 [ws] res ERROR talk.client.toolCall INVALID_REQUEST
  Session "agent:main:node-<redacted>" is archived. Restore it before starting new work.
```

Bounded history inspection of that exact device session returned finalized user and assistant voice records from the captured conversation (not just UI captions). Private speech content and device/conversation identifiers are intentionally omitted.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source inspected at upstream commit `40b7aeb145090f8c38a663e88c7638fbaa937538` (not asserted to be the exact installed APK revision):

- [NodeRuntime.kt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/40b7aeb145090f8c38a663e88c7638fbaa937538/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/NodeRuntime.kt): `resolveNodeMainSessionKey()` at line 1134 constructs the device-owned session; `prepareMainSessionKey()` around line 2275 pushes that key into `talkMode.setMainSessionKey(resolvedKey)`.
- In the same file, `applyChatSessionSelection()` around line 5182 calls `chat.switchSession(sessionKey, ownerAgentId)` but does not update Talk's session binding.
- [TalkModeManager.kt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/40b7aeb145090f8c38a663e88c7638fbaa937538/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt): around lines 1118-1133, realtime creation uses `change?.sessionKey ?: mainSessionKey` for `talk.session.create`.

These source paths are consistent with the observed device-session destination; the exact installed APK source revision remains unverified.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed Android installation, with realtime Talk used from two selected conversations.
Severity: conversation continuity is broken; voice content is invisible in the selected chats. Agent work also failed when the hidden device-scoped destination was archived (three recorded rejected consultations).
Frequency: reported for both selected conversations; exact total number of calls is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.
Consequence: users cannot continue a voice exchange in the displayed text conversation and may incorrectly believe the transcripts were lost.

### Additional information

No configuration, archive state, transcript files, or app code was changed during this investigation. No last-known-good version is established.

Suggested acceptance checks: start Talk from chat A, verify both sides' finalized speech in A; repeat in B and verify no cross-write into A/device-default; verify defined behavior when changing chats during a call. Preserve archive intent: do not silently unarchive or migrate private history as a workaround.

issues.body:
> **Update 2026-11-05:** the remaining historical-state recovery (#164445, `e02ae3ecb66`) is on `main` and passes its tests at `c4d8a5ae171` (14/14). It first ships in the prerelease `v2026.11.5-beta.1`; it is **not** in stable `v2026.11.1` or `v2026.10.10`. Plan: leave open until it is in a stable tag, then comment the release and close as completed. See the latest comment. Original report below.

**Build:** OpenClaw `2026.9.2 (3928bad)`. Backend: `claude-cli`. Both defects reproduced live with control arms in both directions, then traced to source in the installed `dist/`.

Two independent defects in the swarm collector path. **D2 is the serious one**: it is a silent, unbounded hang with a green status surface, and it is the *default* behaviour rather than an edge case. D1 is filed with it because D1 is what usually *triggers* D2 — but they are independent, and fixing D1 alone leaves D2 armed.

---

## D2 — a collector child that calls `sessions_yield` strands its parent forever, while the status surface reports "done"

### Symptom

A `collect: true` child that calls `sessions_yield` ends up with:

- `execution.status: "terminal"`, `execution.outcome.status: "ok"` — the run genuinely finished
- `pauseReason: "sessions_yield"` in `subagent_runs.payload_json`
- **no collector completion record written, ever**
- `agents_wait` pends forever — no error, no timeout of its own, no diagnostic
- `subagents(action="list")` `recent` reports the same run as `status: "done"`
- `subagents(action="list")` `tasks` reports the same run as `status: "running"`

Three surfaces, three different answers, for one run. The one an operator is most likely to check (`recent` → `done`) is the one that says everything is fine.

### Why children reach for it

`sessions_yield` **is** in a collector child's tool catalog. `structured_output` is not (that is D1). So a child instructed to "submit structured output" reaches for `sessions_yield` as the nearest available thing. Two of the first two test children did this unprompted, with no mention of yielding in their prompt.

### Minimal reproduction

```
sessions_spawn({ task: "Reply with the single word gamma.", collect: true,
                 groupId: "g", label: "arm", model: "haiku", lightContext: true })
agents_wait({ ids: [runId], timeoutSeconds: 30 })
```

| arm | `outputSchema` | child called `sessions_yield` | `agents_wait` result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (positive control) | no | no | `status:"done"`, `result:"gamma"` — **5.1s** |
| B | yes | no | `status:"failed"`, `schemaError:"structured_output was not called"`, `result:"delta"` — 7.4s |
| **C** | **no** | **yes** | **never returns.** `recent`: `done`, `endedAt` set, `runtimeMs` 15855, 52576 tokens. `tasks`: `running`. |

Arm A proves the harness observes success. **Arm C carries no `outputSchema` at all** — `sessions_yield` alone is sufficient to hang the parent, so D2 does not depend on D1.

### Root cause

In `dist/subagent-completion-admission.store-*.js`, three separate paths exempt `pauseReason === "sessions_yield"` unconditionally, with no check for `entry.collect`:

```js
// result-capture path — aborts before any completion state is created
const liveEntry = params.runs.get(entry.runId);
if (entry.pauseReason === "sessions_yield" || liveEntry?.pauseReason === "sessions_yield"
    || context.newerGenerationOwnsSession(entry)) return false;
const completion = ensureCompletionState(entry);
```

```js
// resolveFinalizedSubagentTaskState — returns undefined, so `tasks` reports "running"
if (typeof endedAt !== "number" || !outcome || entry.pauseReason === "sessions_yield"
    || completion?.resultText === void 0 && typeof completion?.capturedAt !== "number") return;
```

```js
// listPendingCompletionRunsForSession — run is skipped entirely
if (entry.pauseReason === "sessions_yield") continue;
```

The exemption looks correct for an **announce** child: a yielded child is paused and will resume, so admitting a completion early would be wrong. But a **collector** child has no resume path and no announcement — the collector completion record is its *only* output channel. The same guard that is right for announce children permanently strands collector children, and the `recent` projection reads `execution.endedAt` directly so it happily reports `done` over the stranded row.

### Suggested fix shape

Gate these three exemptions on `entry.collect !== true`, so a terminal collector run admits its completion regardless of `pauseReason`. Failing that, at minimum: make `agents_wait` surface a terminal-without-completion run as a `failed` result with a real diagnostic instead of pending forever, and reconcile `recent` / `tasks` so they cannot disagree.

A cheaper partial mitigation would be to keep `sessions_yield` out of a collector child's tool catalog entirely — it has no meaning for a one-shot collector — though that alone would not fix a run already in this state.

---

## D1 — `structured_output` is never injected into `claude-cli`-backed collector children, so `outputSchema` is silently inert

### Symptom

Passing `outputSchema` to a `collect: true` spawn on a `claude-cli` backend has no effect on the child. `agents_wait` then returns `status: "failed"` with `schemaError: "structured_output was not called"`. The child's answer is still present as raw text in `result`, so the caller gets a "failed" result that actually contains the correct answer.

Asked directly, the child reports: *"A tool named `structured_output` was not present in my tool list."*

### Root cause

`createStructuredOutputTool` is present in the tools bundle (`dist/openclaw-tools-*.js`), but the string `structured_output` does not appear in **any** `dist/cli-backend*.js` — nor does `forceToolNames`. The CLI backend has no code path that injects the synthetic tool or forces the model to call it. The schema is accepted at the API boundary and then dropped on the floor for this backend class.

### Impact

`outputSchema` is not merely unenforced — it is accepted, documented, and silently ineffective for every `claude-cli`-backed agent. The failure is also mislabelled: `status: "failed"` on a run that succeeded trains callers to ignore the status field.

### Suggested fix shape

Either inject the synthetic tool on the CLI backend path, or **reject `outputSchema` at spawn time with a clear error** when the resolved backend cannot support it. Accepting a parameter that cannot be honoured is the worst of the three options.

---

## Relationship to existing issues

- **#138018** (*Swarm collector can freeze missing structured output before a valid terminal tool call is recorded*) — related but distinct. That issue is a **race**: `structured_output` *is* called, and arrives after the freezer has already recorded the missing-output failure. D1 here is the case where the tool is **never injected at all**, so it can never be called and there is no late callback to lose. A fix for #138018 would not change any arm above.
- **#132765** (*`agents_wait` ignores `timeoutSeconds`*) — adjacent. Note the interaction: D2 produces a wait with no completion record to ever return, so `agents_wait` timeout behaviour is the only thing standing between a caller and an unbounded hang.

## Workarounds currently in force on our fleet

1. Never pass `outputSchema`; ask for JSON in the child's final text and parse it parent-side.
2. End every collector child prompt with *"do not call `sessions_yield`; end your turn normally."*
3. Give every parent wait loop its own wall-clock deadline — never trust `agents_wait` to terminate.

All three are a standing tax on every swarm caller, and because a fix upstream would be silent (the workarounds keep working afterwards), we run a daily tripwire against these code paths to know when to drop them.

issues.body:
## Summary

Sixteen production call sites across eleven files throw or return the **byte-identical** string
`Session "<key>" changed while starting work. Retry.` No discriminator — no reason code, no call-site
tag, no cause field — reaches the log or the thrown error. When this fires in production, **which of
the sixteen branches ran is not knowable from the output.**

This is the diagnosability half of the family that #118873 / #117096 / #116694 / #121269 covered
behaviourally. Those are all closed and the stuck-session behaviour is fixed. The string is not.

## Verified against `main`

`587c7524e58`. `rg 'changed while starting work' src --type ts`, excluding tests and comments:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts` | 573 |
| `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts` | 333 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts` | 259 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` | 166 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-prepare.ts` | 185 |
| `src/sessions/session-diff-baseline.ts` | 41 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-entry-persistence.ts` | 98 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts` | 241, 284, 292 |
| `src/agents/agent-command-recovery-owner.ts` | 110, 132 |
| `src/agents/agent-command.ts` | 213, 220 |
| `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.ts` | 73 |
| `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` | 57 (the shared helper) |

Three of these are in one function's three branches (`reply-turn-admission.ts:241/284/292`), so even
narrowing to a single file does not narrow to a single cause.

## Why it costs an operator a diagnosis

Production, `2026.8.1-beta.2`, one Discord channel session: **27 rejected runs across 4 inbound user
messages** between `09:58:05` and `10:24:09` (-03:00), each aborting in 4–8 ms with exactly this
string. Worst case, 9 attempts over 6 min 11 s before one user message ran. Every cluster started
within ~90 s of a gateway restart.

```text
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord outcome=error duration=4ms
  error="Error: Session \"agent:<redacted>\" changed while starting work. Retry."
```

The three plausible causes on that path — an `expectedSessionId` mismatch, a recovery-owner claim
returning `invalidated`, and the abort check — call for three different operator responses. The log
distinguishes none of them, so triage is guesswork or a source read per occurrence. Filing this
separately because a fix here is useful whether or not any specific admission bug is open: the next
one in this family will produce the same undiagnosable line.

## The seam already exists

`src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` already owns the discriminating helper:

- `resolveSessionWorkStartError()` already distinguishes *deleted* / *changed* / *still initializing*
  / *archived*, and
- `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED_ERROR_CODE = "SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED"` (line 24) is already
  the shared code.

Roughly fourteen sites route through that helper. The sixteen above bypass it with a hardcoded
template literal, which is what makes them indistinguishable.

## Suggested shape

Not a behaviour change and not a message rewording — the retryable contract and the operator-facing
sentence can stay exactly as they are.

1. Give the helper a `reason` discriminator alongside the message (e.g.
   `session-id-mismatch` | `recovery-owner-invalidated` | `aborted` | `entry-deleted` |
   `initializing` | `archived`).
2. Route the sixteen hardcoded literals through the helper so the reason travels with the error.
3. Log the reason on the rejection path.

Happy to send the PR if the shape is agreeable — I would rather have the reason names settled by a
maintainer first than guess at the taxonomy.

## Version

`2026.8.1-beta.2` for the production data; source claims verified against `main` at `587c7524e58`.

> **Form note (edited 2026-10-08):** this is a feature request that was filed in bug shape. The sections below add what `feature_request.yml` asks for (alternatives, implementation intent) without changing the evidence above.

## Environment (form fields)

- Production data: `2026.8.1-beta.2`, npm global install, Linux (Debian in a Proxmox LXC).
- Model / provider routing chain of the 27 rejected runs: **unknown** — not recorded with the 2026-08 occurrences. The string is emitted before any model call, so the defect is model-independent.
- Steps to reproduce / actual: this is a diagnosability gap, verified by source inspection (table above) and confirmed by ClawSweeper on current `main`; no runtime repro on current `main` was run.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Status quo — read the source per occurrence.** What we do today; it costs a source read per incident and still cannot separate the three branches inside `reply-turn-admission.ts`.
2. **Reword the sixteen messages.** Rejected: it changes an operator-facing sentence and the retryable contract, and the next caller that copies the template literal is undiagnosable again.
3. **A stable public `reason` field on the shared error.** Possible, but it creates a compatibility obligation. ClawSweeper's recommendation — bounded **diagnostic-only** labels in operational logs, retry codes and public messages unchanged — is the shape we prefer.

## Implementation intent

We will open the PR once a maintainer settles the open question (diagnostic-only labels vs public field, and the label names). Not before: we would rather not pick the taxonomy unilaterally.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
In `enforce` mode, `session.maintenance.maxEntries` and `maxDiskBytes` are silently exceeded without bound because thread/channel/topic session entries are treated as protected and skipped by all three reclaim paths (age prune, entry cap, and disk-budget last-resort eviction).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Configure `session.maintenance` with `mode: "enforce"`, `maxEntries: 500`, `maxDiskBytes: "400mb"`.
2. Operate a busy Slack/Telegram deployment so thread/channel session entries exceed 500 and the sessions directory exceeds 400mb.
3. Observe the store keeps growing past both limits: `pruneStaleEntries`, `capEntryCount`, and `enforceSessionDiskBudget` all call `shouldPreserveMaintenanceEntry`, which returns `true` for thread/channel entries, so they are never removed and the configured limits are never met.

### Expected behavior
In `enforce` mode the store is bounded by the configured `maxEntries` and `maxDiskBytes`. Hard resource ceilings apply even to conversation sessions.

### Actual behavior
The store grows unbounded. Observed: 562 entries and ~420MB with `maxEntries` effectively 500. Because only unprotected entries are removable, the reclaim evicts the wrong sessions (see #112637, `agent:main:main` eviction) instead of bounding the store.

### OpenClaw version
2026.7.1

### Operating system
Linux (Docker container, linux/arm64) on macOS host

### Install method
Docker (docker compose)

### Model
openai/gpt-5.6-terra

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> openai

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence
- `src/config/sessions/store-maintenance.ts`: `pruneStaleEntries` and `capEntryCount` skip entries where `shouldPreserveMaintenanceEntry` is true.
- `src/config/sessions/disk-budget.ts` (`enforceSessionDiskBudget` last-resort loop): `if (shouldPreserveMaintenanceEntry({ key, entry, preserveKeys })) continue;` — protected thread/channel entries are skipped even under disk pressure.
- `isProtectedSessionMaintenanceEntry` unconditionally protects `:thread:`, telegram topics, and group/channel keys.
- Observed store: 546 Slack thread entries across allowlisted channels; directory ~420MB.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: any active Slack/Telegram deployment in `enforce` mode.
- Severity: Medium-High — unbounded entry and disk growth; a configured hard limit that is silently exceeded; directly forces the wrong-session eviction in #112637.
- Frequency: Continuous on active deployments.
- Consequence: Disk exhaustion risk and eviction of unprotected sessions instead of honoring the operator's configured budget.

### Additional information
Proposed fix (PR to follow): keep thread/channel sessions protected from age-based `pruneAfter` (preserve idle-but-under-budget conversations), but make them evictable oldest-first under genuine `maxEntries`/`maxDiskBytes` pressure; always protect `agent:<id>:main` (#112637). If maintainers prefer to preserve today's unbounded default, the same behavior can be gated behind a `session.maintenance` opt-in flag.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), npm global install
- macOS 26.2 (arm64), node v26.5.0, zsh
- Gateway runs as launchd service (gui/501)
- Telegram channel; agent sessions use code-mode exec (guest JS sandbox calling the exec tool global)

## Symptom
After the gateway runs for roughly 10–30 hours, EVERY shell invocation through the exec tool starts failing with zsh parse errors raised by the generated wrapper script itself (not by the command):
- zsh:2: parse error near ')' (most common)
- zsh:3: parse error near ')' / near '}'
- zsh:1: missing end of string; zsh:2: unknown file attribute: 0
The failing line number varies with the call payload; even trivial commands like `echo hi` fail. PTY mode fails identically. Fresh agent sessions (isolated cron jobs, newly spawned subagents) keep working — the corruption appears tied to long-lived session bridges, but at least once it broke a fresh isolated session too.

## Timeline (single machine, reproducible 3x)
- 2026-11-03: upgraded 2026.10.4 → 2026.10.10 (release day). Exec broken from the first post-upgrade restart.
- 2026-11-04 15:21 HKT: `openclaw update repair` + gateway restart → exec fully working again (verified: cron list, npm, launchctl all ran fine).
- 2026-11-05 ~02:03 HKT: exec broken again (~10h later), no restart in between. `openclaw gateway restart` at 02:10 → fixed again.
- 2026-11-05 09:28 HKT: still working.
- 2026-11-06 ~08:20 HKT: broken again (~23h later). Fresh spawned subagent sessions run the same commands with exitCode 0 — only long-lived session bridges are affected (but see timeline above for the isolated-session case).

## What we ruled out
- Not ENOSPC: disk had 4.3Gi free when it recurred; freeing space did not help.
- Not shell startup configs: ~/.zshenv/.zshrc/.zprofile/.profile parse fine; errors carry no sourced-filename attribution.
- Not exec-approvals state file: restored it from backup; no effect.
- Not the command content: fails on `echo hi`.

## Workaround
Gateway restart clears the corrupted bridge state temporarily; corruption returns within ~10–30h. Downstream impact: any agent turn that needs shell (cron payload scripts, tool calls) starts failing until the next restart.

## Request
Fix the wrapper/state corruption in the code-mode exec bridge so it does not degrade over uptime, or surface the corruption with a self-healing bridge rebuild.

issues.body:
### Summary

Set a default operational `contextTokens` cap (128k) for metered API providers (`openai-api`) and expose a context budget control in the Control UI to prevent long-context cache-write billing spikes and TPM lockouts.

### Problem to solve

Catalog models under `openai-api` (e.g., `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-luna`) declare `contextWindow: 1050000` with no lower `contextTokens` budget.

Because `resolveCompactionContextTokenBudget` schedules auto-compaction against `contextTokens ?? contextWindow` minus the reserve, persistent sessions with tool calls grow past 600k tokens before compaction triggers.

On metered APIs, crossing 128k tokens causes three failures:
1. Long-context cache-write drain: Dynamic tool outputs break prefix caching (~24% read ratio), triggering repeated 600k-token writes billed at the `cache writes, long context` tier (~$0.75 to $1.50 per turn).
2. TPM exhaustion: A single 600k-token prompt exceeds standard 100k TPM tier limits, causing cascading 429 retries.
3. Failover crashes: Failing over a 600k-token session to a fallback provider with a 128k ceiling immediately fails with context overflow.

### Proposed solution

Reuse the existing `contextTokens` contract in `resolveConfiguredContextTokenLimitsForModel` with minimal surface area:

1. Backend defaults:
- Set `contextTokens: 128000` (while keeping `contextWindow: 1050000`) on metered `openai-api` catalog entries, matching the pattern already used in `openai-chatgpt-responses` migrations.
- Enable `agents.defaults.compaction.midTurnPrecheck.enabled: true` by default so large tool outputs trigger compaction before the next provider call.

2. Control UI (Solid 2):
- Expose a simple "Active Context Budget (`contextTokens`)" selector in Model/Agent Settings (e.g., `128k Safe API Cap` vs `Full Model Window`), paired with a toggle for `midTurnPrecheck`.

### Alternatives considered

Manual edits in `openclaw.json` (`contextWindow: 128000`, `keepRecentTokens: 32000`, `midTurnPrecheck: { enabled: true }`). This works well in production but requires inspecting internal config schemas that non-technical users cannot easily discover.

### Impact

- Affected: Operators using metered API keys (`openai-api`, direct provider keys) in persistent sessions or group topics with tools enabled.
- Severity: High (rapid prepaid credit depletion and 429 rate-limit loops).
- Frequency: Consistent on any long-lived thread with bash/MCP tool outputs.
- Consequence: Unexpected billing spikes ($35+ in <50 tool turns) and broken failovers.

### Evidence/examples

Observed in a persistent Telegram topic session (`OpenClaw 2026.10.9`):
- Transcript grew to 644,764 tokens across 844 events without triggering auto-compaction because `gpt-6.1-sol` reported a 1.05M window.
- OpenAI billing recorded 9.55M total tokens across 48 requests ($36.82 total), with $35.84 (97.3%) billed exclusively to `gpt-6_1-sol, cache writes, long context` (7.3M cache-write tokens vs 2.3M cache-read tokens).
- Workaround verified in production: capping the model window to `128000` with `keepRecentTokens: 32000`, `softThresholdTokens: 80000`, `maxActiveTranscriptBytes: "2mb"`, and `midTurnPrecheck: { enabled: true }` kept recent context intact, triggered zero-cost safeguard compaction around ~100k tokens, and reduced per-turn API cost to a few cents.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

`resolveContextWindowInfo` (`context-window-guard`) and `resolveConfiguredContextTokenLimitsForModel` (`context-resolution`) already prioritize `effectiveConfiguredTokens` (`Math.min(contextTokens, contextWindow)`). No new runtime engine logic is required.

issues.body:
**Environment:** OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55), Node v24.22.1, Docker on Linux x64, `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` (`boundary-aware:anthropic-messages`), about 25 concurrently active dashboard sessions at peak, one paired macOS node that advertises computer use.

**Summary.** "Add to chat" (selection comments) sends a webchat user message with **empty text** and the comments as `selection-comment.txt` attachments (`kind: document`, `text/plain`). If the session is idle, this works: the turn runs and the agent answers each comment. If the session is **busy**, the message is persisted while another run is in progress and never gets a turn of its own. The next run's orphan repair then drops it, and the user's replies are lost without any error.

**Evidence (two sessions, same day):**
1. **Opus session, embedded runner.** A user message with empty text and 4 selection-comment attachments was persisted while a run was active. The next run logged:
   ```
   [agent/embedded] Removed already-queued orphaned user message to prevent consecutive user turns. runId=… sessionId=… trigger=user
   ```
   `mergeOrphanedTrailingUserPrompt({prompt, leafMessage})` only merges the leaf's **text** into the next prompt. Here the text was empty, so nothing was merged ("Removed", not "Merged and removed"), and the leaf's `__openclaw.media` facts were discarded. The agent never saw the 4 comments, and the UI still shows the message as sent.
2. **Codex app-server session.** A user message with empty text and 9 selection-comment attachments was persisted at 19:38:43 while a run was finishing. At 19:39:38 an inter-session message arrived, and the next turn answered only that message. None of the 9 comments, which included merge approvals, was ever addressed, and no log line mentions it.

Control cases on the same gateway the same evening: an Opus session and a Codex session that were **idle** when the user sent "Add to chat" both answered every comment.

**Impact.** Users reply to an agent's report with "Add to chat", see their message in the transcript, and assume it was delivered. In our case, PR merge approvals and a production go-ahead were lost for hours.

**Suggestions:**
1. Orphan repair should carry the leaf's media facts into the merged prompt, not just its text.
2. Never drop a user message that has attachments. If it can't be merged, give it its own turn.
3. Steering or queued input on the Codex path should include attachment-only messages.
4. If a message is dropped anyway, mark it in the UI ("not delivered, resend").

Related: #193303 (the same orphan-merge path also rewinds the leaf and forces a full history rebuild), #155600.

issues.body:
### Summary

Since plugin generation capture landed (#144252, first shipped in 2026.9.6), a Gateway with an external or workspace plugin that has a large package or dependency tree blocks its event loop for minutes. It happens at startup, and again whenever the prepared model runtime republishes. While the loop is blocked the Gateway accepts TCP connections but answers nothing, including `/healthz`, WebSocket RPCs and channel polling.

`capturePluginGenerationArtifact` (`src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts`) copies the plugin package synchronously on the main thread. When no `entryFile` is set, `copyPackage` copies the whole root. It then walks and copies the dependency tree through `capturePluginDependencies` → `linkDependency` → `copyPackage` → `copy`.

### Evidence

**Isolated repro on origin/main `4d4d99d`**, using a synthetic 878 MB context-engine plugin:
- The Gateway stalls for 219 s before it starts listening, then for another 168 s.
- It logs `prepared model runtime startup degraded after 120000ms (workspace plugins; agent main)`.

**Production Gateway on 2026.9.6.** The plugin root is a Bun global install: a 134 MB package whose sibling `node_modules` hold 1.5 GB across 221 packages.
- **Startup:** the process started at T+0 and logged `http server listening` at T+2m20s. `/healthz` timed out until about T+7m.
- **Stacks:** four inspector samples taken during the hang all show the same stack:
  ```
  realpathSync / path.join
  ← pluginNativeNamespaceMemberPath / resolvePreparedSource
  ← copy (recursive)
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← linkDependency ← capturePluginDependencies ← captureDependencies
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← capturePluginGenerationArtifact
  ← bindPluginInstanceModuleLoader ← loadPluginModule ← loadRuntimePluginCandidate
  ```
- **Earlier, during a prepared-runtime republish:**
  - The event loop was blocked for 124 s (`eventLoopDelayMaxMs=124352`).
  - Telegram polling stalled.
  - `config.patch` took 125 s and returned `UNAVAILABLE`, followed by `prepared model runtime reload failed after config commit: prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out; restarting gateway`.
  - The Gateway then restarted, and startup blocked again.
  - Separately, the Control UI's provider sign-in stayed on a blank tab for the whole outage. That is covered by #160954.

A `thinkingDefault` patch alone hot-applies in 50 ms in the isolated repro. The republish in production was probably already pending. Candidate cause: #160120, a refresh loop triggered by an auth profile that fails to resolve. That link is being verified.

### Impact

- Any install with a large external or workspace plugin.
- The Gateway becomes unreachable for minutes on every startup and on every prepared-runtime republish.
- Config hot reloads can escalate into restarts, which block again.
- 2026.7.35 is not affected; 2026.9.6 (npm `latest`/`beta`) is.

### Expected

Capture should not block the Gateway event loop for more than a bounded time. An unchanged plugin should reuse its existing capture instead of being recopied.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.6** (fe06181), Node v26.12.1, Linux (Proxmox host, x64)
- Provider: `opencode-go` (OpenAI-compatible), primary model `glm-5.3-flash` with model fallbacks
- Prompt cache mode: `boundary-aware:openai-completions`
- Multi-agent setup: ~17 configured agents, cross-agent handoffs via `sessions_send` with inline wait; ordinary turns run 2-6 tool calls each
- Channels: Telegram forum topics + Home Assistant Assist through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.enabled: true`)

## Symptoms

Every model request logs `cache read dropped N -> 0`, so the full prompt (14k-27k tokens) is reprocessed from scratch on **every** call — including consecutive calls **within the same turn**. Each call costs 1-8 s of stream time (measured window: 41 calls, median 4.1 s, max 14 s), and a user message needing a 4-11 call chain takes 20-50+ s end-to-end. Synchronous clients (voice Assist) hit their timeout and disconnect mid-turn (`ClientDisconnectError`).

## Evidence (gateway journal, sanitized)

1. Within-turn drop with NO tracked change (request 3 of the same run, 5.5 s after request 2):

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] cache read dropped 14592 -> 0 runId=<redacted> request=3
for opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash via boundary-aware:openai-completions;
no tracked cache input change; requestGapMs=5544 promptTokens=18176 providerPrefix=prefix-match
```

2. historyRewrite because the user-message envelope is re-stamped on every request:

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] message 0 (user) differs from the previous request;
history must be append-only; changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw
```

```
cache read dropped 15104 -> 10240 ... historyRewrite(message 27 (user) differs ...;
changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw, envelope.idempotencyKey);
requestGapMs=31690 promptTokens=17043 providerPrefix=message:2
```

3. Runtime-context carrier invalidating the provider history mid-turn (request 8 of the same run):

```
cache read dropped 13056 -> 0 ... request=8 ...
runtimeContextCarrier(runtimeContextCarrier changed provider history);
```

issues.body:
## Summary

Long-running Anthropic sessions suffer frequent prompt-cache invalidation even when consecutive requests are seconds apart and well inside the provider cache TTL. We traced this on a busy multi-session deployment (Discord channel sessions, `anthropic-messages` API through an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible proxy) using `diagnostics.cacheTrace` plus wire-level capture, and found **two independent mechanisms**, both reproducible.

Measured impact before fixing: across a 5-hour trace window we observed ~70 confirmed cache breaks (multi-million-token cache re-writes each on large contexts), the majority attributable to these two mechanisms.

## Mechanism 1: sender-dependent owner-only toolset flaps the `tools` block

`GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS` (`cron`, `gateway`, `nodes`) is resolved **per turn, based on the sender of the message that woke the agent** (`src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` + the `ownerOnlyGatewayDeny` branch in tool resolution):

```js
const ownerOnlyGatewayDeny = params.senderIsOwner === false || surface === "http" && params.senderIsOwner !== true ? [...GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS] : [];
```

In any session where a trusted non-owner sender (a notification bot, another human in the channel) wakes turns, the toolset oscillates (e.g. 36 ↔ 33 tools) between consecutive requests. The `tools` block sits at the top of the Anthropic payload, so every flip invalidates the cache prefix for the **entire context** — system prompt and full history included.

`cacheTrace` reason codes show this directly (`"36 -> 33 tools"` + `"system prompt digest changed"` pairs), and each occurrence cost a full re-cache of 1-4M tokens in our sessions.

Workaround we validated: adding the bot sender to `commands.ownerAllowFrom` stops the flap completely (zero occurrences since, previously dozens/day). But that grants the bot owner privileges — a blunt instrument.

Suggested fix direction: resolve the owner-only toolset per **session** (its owner/binding), not per waking sender — or at minimum keep the toolset stable across turns within a session and enforce sender restrictions at invocation time instead of registration time.

## Mechanism 2: late message enrichment moves cache breakpoints

Messages that arrive while a turn is in flight are appended to the session in a bare fast-path shape:

```json
{"content": "...", "role": "user", "timestamp": 1787402400121}
```

On the next turn, the same historical message is re-serialized in enriched form — sender metadata attached and a slightly different timestamp:

```json
{"__openclaw": {"senderId": "...", "senderIsOwner": false, ...}, "content": "...", "role": "user", "timestamp": 1787402396925}
```

(Byte-level diff from `cacheTrace` with `includeMessages: true`; exactly one historical message changed between two requests 14s apart, and cache reuse collapsed from ~800k to ~140k tokens.)

The metadata itself never reaches the wire — `convertMessages` serializes only `{role, content}`, which we confirmed both statically and by capturing wire bodies at the proxy. The cache still breaks because breakpoint placement is sensitive to the message's flags: `convertMessages` opts `runtimeContextCarrier === true` messages out of `cache_control` breakpoint placement, so when enrichment flips a message's carrier status, the markers land on different messages and the provider's prefix anchoring shifts — content identical, caching behavior different.

Suggested fix direction: append mid-flight messages in their final serialized form the first time (or freeze the carrier flag at append time), so a message's cache-relevant identity never changes retroactively.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2, Linux x64, Node 24
- `anthropic-messages` API via an Anthropic-compatible proxy endpoint; also reproduces against direct Anthropic in so far as the mechanisms are provider-independent (tools/messages bytes change)
- Evidence gathered with `diagnostics.cacheTrace` (`includeSystem`, later `includeMessages`) + proxy-side request-body capture

## Summary

The `advisor` plugin's review path fails on **every** review attempt with `fork_failed`. The advisor never
produces a review, so the feature is effectively dead while remaining enabled.

```
[plugins] advisor: review failed for session agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>: fork_failed
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent durationMs=5 error="prepared model runtime owner was not published for /Users/vicmini/.openclaw/agents/main/agent" errorName=Error
```

The advisor calls `api.runtime.subagent.forkSession(...)` to fork a reviewer lane. That fork performs a
**read-only** prepared-model-runtime lookup, and the lookup finds no published owner for the main agent dir,
throwing `PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError`.

This is **not** the same failure mode as #158592 (post-sleep/wake publication timeout): this log contains
**zero** `prepared model runtime publication ... timed out` lines and **zero** `host timing gap detected`
lines. There is no sleep/wake involvement — the fork's read-only lookup simply never finds a published owner.

## Reproduction

On a healthy gateway with the advisor enabled, any session that reaches an advisor review trigger fails:

1. `plugins.entries.advisor.enabled = true`, config `everyToolCalls: 10`, `everyMinutes: 20`.
2. A session accumulates enough tool calls / wall-clock time to trigger a review.
3. The advisor forks a reviewer lane → the fork's read-only prepared-model-runtime lookup finds no published
   owner for the agent dir → `PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError`.
4. The review is reported as `fork_failed`. The attempt fails fast (~5 ms) and never recovers.

No gateway restart, config change, or provider error is required to trigger it.

## Evidence

Measured over 2026-11-03 → 2026-11-05 in `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log`:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Real `advisor: review failed ... fork_failed` lines | **103** (86 dashboard sessions, 17 heartbeat session) |
| Distinct dashboard sessions affected | 5 |
| Successful reviews (`advisor: steered active run`) | **1** (2026-11-03 22:14:12) |
| First failure | 2026-11-03 15:17:37 ET |
| Last failure | 2026-11-04 22:07:00 ET |
| Per day | 37 on Nov 3, 66 on Nov 4 |
| `publication ... timed out` lines | **0** |
| `host timing gap detected` lines | **0** |

Every attempt fails in **2–6 ms**, so it is cheap and breaks nothing except the advisor's own review — the
surrounding agent turns continue to work normally. The failure is **not** restart-scoped: it recurred across
every dashboard session since Nov 3 15:17 and survived multiple gateway restarts.

## Code path

- Fork call site: `dist/extensions/advisor/index.js:278`

  ```js
  const result = await withSettledTools(reviewSignal, () => api.runtime.subagent.forkSession({
    sessionKey, message, timeoutMs: REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS, signal: reviewSignal
  }));
  ```

- Throw sites for the error text: `dist/prepared-model-runtime-D1pViiyf.mjs:2367` and `:2964`

  ```js
  if (!owner.snapshot || input.readOnly && !preparedModelRuntimeConfigsMatch(owner.input.config, input.config))
    throw new PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError(`prepared model runtime owner was not published for ${input.agentDir}`);
  ```

The `input.readOnly` branch looks like the relevant one: the fork asks for a runtime projection with
`readOnly`, and the check at `:2367` rejects it because the owner's config no longer matches.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.10** (7dc3350), npm global install
- macOS 15.7.9 (x64), Node v26.13.0
- Single gateway, agents: main, apollo, hermes, heph, heartbeat
- Only the `main` agent dir is affected (`/Users/vicmini/.openclaw/agents/main/agent`)

## Not fixed by the current release

2026.11.1 (published 2026-11-05T09:48:37Z) was compared against 2026.10.10: the only file touched under the
advisor is `extensions/advisor/package.json` (version bump). Neither `extensions/advisor/index.ts` nor the
`prepared-model-runtime` module changed, so **this bug is still present in 2026.11.1**.

## Expected behavior

A review fork should be able to obtain a read-only model-runtime projection for the same agent dir the parent
session is already using. Either the read-only lookup should fall back to the parent's already-published owner,
or the config-mismatch condition at `:2367` should not apply to a read-only projection that is not requesting a
replacement.

## Workarounds

- Disable the plugin: `plugins.entries.advisor.enabled = false`
- Otherwise accept the 2–6 ms failures — they are cheap and do not block agent turns.

## Notes for maintainers

Two observations that may be relevant:

1. The failures stopped appearing on Nov 5 **without any code change**. Nov 5 has **zero** `dashboard` session
   references in the log (Nov 4 has 118), so the advisor likely never got a review trigger that day. That points
   to the bug being **dormant rather than fixed** — expect it to return as soon as dashboard sessions resume.
2. The single successful review (2026-11-03 22:14:12) was on a different session id than the surrounding
   failures, which may be relevant to a race in owner publication versus the fork.

# [Bug]: macOS app Settings sluggish after opening a conversation; input fields not visible in dark theme

## Summary

On OpenClaw.app 2026.10.10, Settings is responsive immediately after restarting the app, before opening the affected conversation. After opening that conversation, Settings becomes sluggish through both the Dock context menu and the lower-left account/avatar menu. The browser Control UI remains responsive against the same Gateway.

This was noticed after a macOS upgrade, but an OS regression has not been established. A dark-theme input visibility problem was also observed: selecting a light theme restores input visibility but does not resolve Settings slowness.

## Environment

- OpenClaw macOS app: 2026.10.10, build 2610001090
- Gateway: 2026.10.10, local, reachable
- macOS: 27.3, build 26C5035r
- Architecture: Apple Silicon / arm64
- WebKit WebContent version reported by sample: 22626 (22626.1.12.11.4)
- Node: v26.12.1
- App location: /Applications/OpenClaw.app

## Steps to reproduce (observed on one installation)

1. Fully quit and restart OpenClaw.app.
2. Before opening the affected existing conversation, right-click the app's Dock icon and open Settings. Settings is responsive.
3. Open the affected existing conversation in the app.
4. Open Settings again via the Dock context menu. Settings is now sluggish.
5. Open Settings via the lower-left account/avatar menu. The same slowness occurs.
6. Compare with the browser Control UI connected to the same Gateway: the browser is responsive.
7. Select a light theme: input visibility is restored, but Settings remains sluggish in the app.

The observed trigger is loading the conversation, not which Settings entry point is used. The exact conversation content is private and has not been minimized into a shareable reproduction. A fresh/empty-conversation control has not yet been tested. No precise latency measurements are available.

## Dark-theme input visibility (additional observed symptom)

In the macOS app with a dark/black theme, input fields are not visually discernible. The user switched to a light theme through the browser Control UI, after which the input fields became visible again in the app. The browser was reported normal while the app was affected.

This is a user-observed visibility defect; no screenshot or computed-style capture is available. It has not been established whether the field background/border, entered text, or multiple visual elements are affected. Do not interpret this as a confirmed loss of input functionality. The relationship between this visibility defect and the Settings slowness is unknown: light theme fixes visibility but Settings remains sluggish after opening the conversation.

## Expected behavior

Opening a conversation should not make subsequent Settings navigation sluggish. Settings should remain responsive through either entry point. Input fields should remain visually discernible and usable in both light and dark themes.

## Actual behavior

Settings becomes sluggish after opening the affected conversation. WebKit reports the embedded page becoming unresponsive. Restarting the app permits the responsive pre-conversation control case again.

## Sanitized diagnostic evidence

App unified logs on 2026-11-04, local time UTC+8:

```text
16:33:04.833 WebProcessProxy::didBecomeUnresponsive
16:33:04.833 WebPageProxy::processDidBecomeUnresponsive
16:41:46.966 WebProcessProxy::didBecomeUnresponsive
16:41:46.966 WebPageProxy::processDidBecomeUnresponsive
16:43:54.115 WebProcessProxy::didBecomeUnresponsive
16:43:54.115 WebPageProxy::processDidBecomeUnresponsive
```

Repeated font warnings were also present (association only, causality unknown):

```text
Serialized font InstrumentSans-Regular reconstructed to Helvetica.
Subbing system-ui; may result in garbled text.

Serialized font Geist-Regular reconstructed to Helvetica.
Subbing system-ui; may result in garbled text.
```

A short WebContent sample included this call path:

```text
ScriptedAnimationController::serviceRequestAnimationFrameCallbacks
JSRequestAnimationFrameCallback::invoke
JS callback (minified/unsymbolicated)
jsElement_scrollHeight
Element::scrollHeight
Document::updateLayoutIfDimensionsOutOfDate
Document::resolveStyle
RenderLayerCompositor::computeCompositingRequirements
```

Important limits: the samples were not synchronized to a sustained freeze. Most main-thread samples were in the run-loop wait state. These frames are investigation leads, not proof of an infinite layout loop, a specific JavaScript function, or a WebKit regression. A separate sample after app restart also included layout/style/compositing work but did not establish the blocking cause. No sustained RegExp hot stack was identified in these captures.

## Related but not established duplicates

- #143713: macOS Control UI hangs in JavaScriptCore RegExp while handling WebSocket messages. Similar WebContent hang symptom, but no matching regex stack established here.
- #149361: umbrella for WebUI performance and stability.
- #156789: native SwiftUI chat hangs while searching inline-math transcript; different observed trigger and sampled stack.

## Scope and uncertainty

- Confirmed user observation: browser normal; app affected after opening an existing conversation; both Settings entry points affected.
- Confirmed user observation: light theme restores input visibility but not responsiveness.
- Not established: macOS upgrade is the cause; dark-theme visibility and slowness share one root cause; every conversation triggers it; exact content trigger; frontend lifecycle/retained view versus WebKit defect.
- No conversation text, credentials, raw logs, personal paths, or raw process samples are attached.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.10.10 (also checked 2026.11.5-beta.1)

**What happens**
For agents running on a CLI backend (`agentRuntime: claude-cli`), plugin `before_tool_call` hooks receive an empty `ctx.requester` for tool calls made by the CLI: no `senderId`, no `channel`, and `senderIsOwner` is never `true` — even when the run was triggered by the owner via the Control UI/app or by a Slack message from a known user.

**Why it matters**
Plugins cannot tell who triggered the current run, so owner-only policies in `before_tool_call` (e.g. "this tool may only run in a turn the owner started") can never pass on CLI backends. The embedded-runtime tool path builds `requester` from the run's sender options (agent-tools), so this looks specific to CLI backends.

**Where it seems to come from**
`resolveMcpRequestContext` (gateway MCP loopback, `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts`) builds the request context with `senderIsOwner` only and has no field for `senderId` / `messageChannel`; the CLI native-tool permission path builds `requester` from `run.senderId` / `run.messageChannel`, which also arrive empty in our runs.

**Expected**
`ctx.requester` for CLI-backend tool calls carries the same `channel`, `senderId` and `senderIsOwner` as for embedded runs (e.g. via the loopback client grant context).

**Repro**
1. Agent with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, a plugin logging `ctx.requester` in `before_tool_call`.
2. Send the agent a message as owner (Control UI) and let it run a shell command.
3. Logged requester: `{}` / `senderIsOwner: false`.

issues.body:
**Env:** OpenClaw 2026.9.7, `@openclaw/facetime` 2026.9.7, `openclaw-facetime` 0.1.3 (Homebrew), macOS 27.0 (arm64), Xcode 27.0 (27A266a). SIP: Debugging Restrictions disabled via `csrutil enable --without debug`.

On macOS 27 the FaceTime plugin can't reach a working state. Two independent blockers:

### 1. `facetime.installDriver` fails with Xcode 27

The pinned BlackHole v0.7.1 project sets `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 10.10`. Xcode 27 now treats this as an error instead of a warning:

```
BlackHole.xcodeproj: error: The macOS deployment target 'MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET' is set to 10.10, but the range of supported deployment target versions is 12.0 to 27.0.x. (in target 'BlackHole' from project 'BlackHole')
** BUILD FAILED ** (65)
```

On macOS 27, Homebrew refuses to install `openclaw-facetime` unless Xcode 27 (and CLT 27) are installed, so macOS 27 users hit this every time.

**Workaround that worked:** temporarily put a root-owned Xcode 26.6 at `/Applications/Xcode.app`, run `facetime.installDriver` (succeeds, `driverStatus: current`), then restore Xcode 27.

**Suggested fix:** pass `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0` (Xcode 27's minimum) in the `xcodebuild` invocation in `extensions/facetime/scripts/install-driver-root.sh`, and update the pinned `expectedInstallerDigest` in `install-driver.applescript` accordingly.

### 2. Helper injection rejected by FaceTime / Phone on macOS 27

With SIP debugging disabled, driver current and `realtime-provider` ready, `facetime.setup` leaves `helper-facetime` and `helper-phone` stuck in `repairing`:

```
LLDB did not confirm that FaceTimeHelper.dylib initialized
```

LLDB attach succeeds, but `dlopen` of the signed helper (TeamIdentifier `FWJYW4S8P8`) returns NULL. `dlerror()` inside the FaceTime process:

```
code signature in <...> '~/Library/Containers/com.apple.FaceTime/Data/tmp/FaceTimeHelper-<ts>.dylib' not valid for use in process: mapping process is a platform binary, but mapped file is not
```

Same result for Phone.app. Disabling SIP debugging restrictions no longer seems sufficient on macOS 27: platform binaries reject non-platform-signed code. The only bypass I know of is disabling AMFI, which shouldn't be part of the setup.

**Possible directions (for maintainers to judge):** avoid in-process injection on macOS 27+. For example, dial via `facetime-audio://`, answer/hang up via Accessibility, and keep the existing virtual mic and process-tap audio path, which doesn't need injection. Otherwise, document macOS 27 as unsupported until there's a supported approach.

All other `facetime.setup` checks report `ready` (xcode-tools, developer-tools-access, system-integrity-protection, owner-handles, native-package, runtime, audio-driver, capture-binary, paired-driver-mic/feed, physical-output, process-tap, realtime-provider).

issues.body:
Running `npx openclaw@latest` and choosing Quick start skips “Keep OpenClaw running in the background?”. The Gateway stays attached to the terminal, so closing it stops the agent and leaves the dashboard reconnecting.

Installing the service manually with `npx openclaw gateway install` has the underlying problem: the service can point into the disposable npx cache. Once that cache is cleared, the service cannot restart.

#191454 fixed the terminal-close problem for durable installs and explicitly left npx support as a follow-up. Its issue, #191453, also excluded temporary runs. This is that follow-up.

Proposed fix: offer the background-service choice to npx users on supported hosts. Before installing the service, install the same OpenClaw version under `~/.openclaw/npm` and launch it from there. Keep temporary cache directories out of the service PATH and run install lifecycle scripts with the current Node. Use the same durable-install path for `gateway install`.

Closing the terminal or clearing the npx cache should not prevent the background Gateway from running and restarting.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Mattermost channel silently drops every inbound post whose `type` is not empty, so an ordinary user message that carries a message attachment (`type: "slack_attachment"`) never reaches the agent.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect an agent to a Mattermost server with `@openclaw/mattermost` and allow a user in direct messages (`dmPolicy: "allowlist"`).
2. On the Mattermost server, have a plugin add a message attachment to user posts in `MessageWillBePosted` with `model.ParseMessageAttachment` (a link-preview card, for example). Mattermost then stores the user's post with `type: "slack_attachment"` and `props.attachments`.
3. As the allowed user, send the bot a direct message that triggers the card.
4. Send a second direct message that does not trigger it.

### Expected behavior

Both messages reach the agent. A post of type `slack_attachment` written by a person is a normal user message with a card under it. Only real system posts (`system_join_channel`, `system_add_to_channel`, …) should be skipped, which the same file already does elsewhere with `post.type?.startsWith("system_")`.

### Actual behavior

The second message is answered. The first one produces no agent turn, no reply and no log line at the default log level. With verbose logging the plugin reports `mattermost: drop post (system post type=slack_attachment)`. The post is present in the channel when read through the REST API.

The check, in `dist/.setup/monitor-*.mjs` of `@openclaw/mattermost` 2026.10.10 (same code in 2026.11.1):

```js
if (normalizeOptionalString(post.type) !== void 0) {
	monitor.logVerboseMessage(`mattermost: drop post (system post type=${post.type ?? "unknown"})`);
	return;
}
```

The thread backfill has the same rule (`… || post.type || !post.user_id …`), so such messages are also missing from recovered thread history.

Changing both conditions to `post.type?.startsWith("system_")` fixes it locally: the same direct message then starts a turn and is answered. No configuration key controls this today.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (7dc3350), `@openclaw/mattermost` 2026.10.10

### Operating system

Debian 12 (official Docker image), x86_64

### Install method

Docker image `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw`, Mattermost plugin installed from npm

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra (not involved: the message is dropped before any model call)

### Provider / routing chain

Codex harness, default routing (not involved)

### Logs

```
mattermost: drop post (system post type=slack_attachment)
```

Reported by an AI agent account on behalf of its operator.

issues.body:
### Problem

Managed headless Chromium advertises `HeadlessChrome` in its native user-agent. Some ordinary website login routes challenge that identity even when the same browser, platform, profile and network can use a native `Chrome` identity. This proposal addresses that narrow compatibility difference, not IP reputation, CAPTCHA solving, or general stealth.

### Proposed improvement

Derive the user-agent from the browser actually launched, replace only `HeadlessChrome/` with `Chrome/`, and apply it process-wide before returning the managed browser. Preserve explicit `--user-agent` flags, headed browsers and remote CDP browsers. Do not pin a browser version or invent another platform.

### Current-source reproduction

On main `46943d587ace8d66012467d9b4c5dfc833469945`, a launcher regression supplies Chromium's native discovery identity `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux aarch64) HeadlessChrome/153.0.0.0 Safari/537.36`. The final managed launch has no normalized `--user-agent` flag. The matching test fails, while the headed and explicit-override controls pass (1 failed, 9 passed). This is synthetic launcher-boundary evidence, not a new live-site login test.

### Tradeoff and scope

Chromium's complete user-agent is available through its running CDP endpoint, so the proposed implementation needs one owned-process relaunch when the marker is present. It keeps the same persistent profile and uses the existing bounded shutdown owner. A failed identity read leaves the working browser available; cancellation still closes its exact owned process. No new configuration or proxy dependency is proposed.

Related: #59849 discusses broader datacenter/proxy restrictions and is closed as implemented. Its proxy support does not apply this native-identity normalization. This request does not claim every site can be made accessible by changing a user-agent.
