issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On main at de98df8efd1 with a remote Gateway, reopening a closed macOS Dashboard starts a new WebKit WebContent process and leaves the previous one resident, so after open, close, reopen and close, with no OpenClaw window open, the app held 2 WebContent processes (389.3 MB) where it held 1 (288.5 MB) before the Dashboard was first opened: one extra process and about 101 MB more. High CPU with no window open (one WebContent at 30.7% of a core on 2026.10.10) is a field observation that did not reproduce in the controlled run, where Gateway traffic was light.

### Steps to reproduce

On a stock install (the field observation below on installed 2026.10.10 followed steps 4 and 5; the controlled run below shows the same on main):

1. Configure OpenClaw.app for a remote Gateway (`connectionMode: remote`, SSH) and let it connect. Quit Safari, Mail and other apps that embed WebKit.
2. In Activity Monitor, search `com.apple.WebKit.WebContent` and note the PIDs. From a terminal instead: `ps -axo pid,lstart,rss,command | grep '[c]om.apple.WebKit.WebContent'`.
3. Open the Dashboard, wait for it to load, then close its window. The app stays in the menu bar.
4. Open the Dashboard again, wait for it to load, then close it again.
5. With no OpenClaw window open, compare the WebContent PIDs with step 2: the reopen added a PID, and the PID that rendered the earlier open is still listed.

The trigger is remote mode. Local mode was not tested.

Controlled reproduction (optional; the method behind the table under Actual behavior):

1. Launch a build of main at de98df8efd1 beside any installed app with `open -n --env OPENCLAW_PROFILE=perfmain <OpenClaw.app>`, configured with `openclaw-mac configure-remote --profile perfmain` for a remote Gateway over SSH on its own local port. Do not open the Dashboard. Wait 30 s, then sample for 60 s.
2. Open the Dashboard (the run sent a reopen event, `open <OpenClaw.app>`). Wait about 100 s, then sample for 60 s with the window open. In the run another app was frontmost, so the window was likely occluded.
3. Close the Dashboard window with its close button; the app keeps running in the menu bar. Sample 0-60 s after the close.
4. Reopen the Dashboard the same way, then close it again. List the WebKit pids right after the reopen and right after the close. Sample 162-222 s after that close.

Sampling: `ps -o pid,rss,time,command` at the start and end of each 60 s window, CPU% = delta(cputime) / 60 s. A WebKit process counts for the build only if its pid did not exist before the build launched (pid-set attribution; WebKit helpers are children of launchd, so `ps` cannot name their client).

### Expected behavior

Reference: the same build right after launch, before the Dashboard was ever opened (row "Launched, Dashboard never opened": 1 WebContent process, 288.5 MB; on main this is the never-shown remote preload, kept on purpose for a fast first open). After the Dashboard is closed, and after any later reopen and close, the app should hold no more WebContent processes than that, and a reopen should reuse or release the previous page process instead of leaving it resident.

### Actual behavior

Controlled reproduction: debug build at de98df8efd1 (app 2026.11.1, build 2611000190), isolated profile `perfmain`, remote Gateway 2026.11.1 over SSH, native-device auth with a token, the Gateway's ordinary event stream, no agent run started. Pid-set attribution against 4 WebKit pids present before launch; the pid set was unchanged at the start and the end, and every sample window was attribution-safe. 1/1 run.

| State | WebContent count | WebContent RSS total | WebContent CPU | App group CPU over 60 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Launched, Dashboard never opened | 1 | 288.5 MB | 0.0% | 3.5% |
| Dashboard open, another app frontmost | 1 | 361.5 MB | 0.3% | 3.4% |
| Closed, 0-60 s | 1 | 371.0 MB | 1.2% | 4.4% |
| Closed after reopen + close, 162-222 s | 2 | 389.3 MB | 0.1% | 3.2% |

- Opening the Dashboard created no new WebContent process: the process that rendered it was 27503, started with the app (the remote preload).
- After the first close, 27503 stayed resident (371.0 MB).
- The reopen started a new WebContent process, 28198, while 27503 (364.1 MB) stayed resident.
- After closing again, with zero Dashboard windows, both stayed resident: 27503 at 347.3 MB and 28198 at 42.0 MB, 389.3 MB together, still present 162-222 s after the close. That is one process and 100.8 MB more than before the first open.
- CPU stayed low in every state (WebContent 0.0-1.2%, app process 3.0-3.5%).
- A window hidden by an experience switch was not exercised in this run.

Field observation, which the controlled run did not reproduce for CPU: installed OpenClaw.app 2026.10.10 on macOS 27.2, remote Gateway over SSH, zero OpenClaw windows on screen. `ps` over 60 s windows, CPU% = delta(cputime) / 60 s (100% = one core).

- As found (Dashboard window off screen; when it was last closed is unknown): app 7.93%, node worker 4.95%, WebKit GPU 8.50% (79 MB), WebContent 61706 1.12% (332 MB), Networking 1.13%, WebContent 72130 30.68% (1463 MB). Total 54.32%.
- Then the Dashboard was reopened and closed again: total 15.8%. WebContents 72130 1.52% (1209 MB), 81442 0.38% (717 MB), 61706 2.37% (362 MB), 2288 MB together. 81442 is the process the reopen created; 72130 stayed resident. This is the same reopen pattern the controlled run shows.
- Attribution: only one `com.apple.WebKit.Networking` process existed (61707, started 7 s after the app: 2026-11-04 19:35:09 and 19:35:16 PST) and Safari was not running, so every WebContent process belonged to OpenClaw. For the second state, the WebKit pids before and after the reopen were compared: 81442 is the only new one.
- A process sample of the hot WebContent process (72130) showed JavaScript microtasks and rendering work.
- 72130 was gone by 15:22 the same day while the app kept running (same app pid). Why it exited is not known; WebKit may reclaim such a process later.

### OpenClaw version

Controlled reproduction: source build of main at de98df8efd1, app 2026.11.1 (build 2611000190), Gateway 2026.11.1. Field observation: installed app 2026.10.10.

### Operating system

### Install method

### Model

Not applicable: reproduces with the Dashboard closed and no agent run started by the app

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: OpenClaw.app Dashboard (WKWebView) -> remote Gateway WebSocket; no model request involved

### Additional provider/model setup details

The field observation used a remote Gateway (`connectionMode: remote`, SSH). The controlled reproduction used a separate `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=perfmain` profile with its own SSH tunnel port to the same Gateway, so the installed app and its state were untouched (its windows stayed closed and its WebKit pids were excluded).

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshot: with the window closed there is nothing on screen; the process lines above are the evidence.

WebKit probe (standalone Swift app, macOS 27.2, local WebSocket server sending 2 KB messages; 500 messages per second): a page in an ordered-out or closed window reports `visibilityState == "hidden"` and gets 0-1 rAF per 2 s (a never-shown page also reports hidden), but kept processing 333 to 500 messages per second; its WebContent CPU went from 18% (ordered out) to 71% (closed, after 22 s) as state accumulated. Unloading to about:blank stopped the CPU but kept RSS (103 MB). Unloading to a cross-site blank page swapped the process and the old one exited.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: macOS app users who close the Dashboard while the app keeps running, which is the normal menu-bar workflow.
- Severity: performance and memory. On main at de98df8efd1, a reopen after close added a WebContent process while the previous one stayed resident with no window open. In the field, the same state also held a sustained share of a core.
- Frequency: 1/1 controlled run plus 1 field observation.
- Consequence: memory held with no visible UI. In the controlled run the extra process was still resident 162-222 s after the close; in the field, the retained 1.2 GB process (72130) was later gone while the app kept running, so how long it stays resident is not known. In the field, also CPU with no visible UI.

### Additional information

The CPU part depends on what the retained page receives. The controlled run had no agent run and a light Gateway event stream, and its closed pages stayed at 0.0-1.2% CPU. The probe above shows a hidden or closed page keeps processing WebSocket messages, so CPU while closed likely scales with Gateway traffic. That link was not measured on the app.

Likely cause (source reading, not observed directly): closed Dashboard windows keep a live Control UI page whose Gateway WebSocket keeps delivering events. WebKit marks the page hidden and throttles its timers, but every message is still parsed and applied.

Source pointers at de98df8efd1, unchanged on main 57ab01eab30:
- Reopen after close builds a second page: `handleWindowClosed` clears the displayed route (`DashboardManager.swift:1378`), so `requiresIsolatedDashboardDocument` returns true for a remote route (`DashboardManager+Construction.swift:305-319`) and `replaceWindowController` (`DashboardManager.swift:921`) creates a new WKWebView; `detachWindowForReplacement` (`DashboardWindowController.swift:473`) calls `stopLoading()` on the outgoing page and does not unload it.
- Close calls `stopLoading()` and does not unload the page: `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardWindowController.swift:1116`. The main controller and its WKWebView stay owned by `DashboardManager.controller` (`handleWindowClosed`, `DashboardManager.swift:1369`).
- An experience switch keeps the page live with no end (not exercised in the controlled run): `DashboardWindowController.swift:427-443` (`hideForExperience`, `orderOut`).
- Never-shown preloads (#106997 local, #185435 remote) stay live by design, for a fast first open: `DashboardManager.swift:446-462` (`preloadIfConfigured`) and the `retainHidden()` call at `DashboardManager.swift:1283`. In the controlled run, the preload's process is the one that rendered the Dashboard and stayed resident after close.

Related: #185963 (open) unloads closed native-auth Dashboards to about:blank, which stops their CPU; the probe above shows about:blank keeps the process's memory. #168743 is the reconnect loop that PR targets. #192667 reports WebContent work in the visible app after opening a conversation; possibly the same accumulated page state, different trigger.

issues.body:
## Summary
When a parent session yields while awaiting child subagent runs, a later revocation of the requester operator authority makes the child completion delivery fail permanently. The parent never receives the completion and stays in a waiting state. The failure is reported with a constant error string that does not say why the authority was revoked, so the failure cannot be attributed from logs.

## Environment
openclaw 2026.9.8, shipped bundle (dist).

## Where (verified against the shipped bundle)
File: dist/session-followup-completion-<hash>.mjs

- :174  async function withRequesterCronAuthority(params, run)
- :183  if (authority.operatorAuthority) throw new Error("Requester operator authority is no longer current");
- :195, :200  if (!current()) throw new Error("Requester operator authority is no longer current");

The same module contains the currency check isCurrent(authority), which returns false when:
- the operator authority is no longer current;
- authority.lifecycleGeneration !== getAgentRunLifecycleGeneration();
- the session authority set no longer contains this authority.

The module also exports revokeRequesterCronAuthority / revokeRequesterCronAuthorityBatch, i.e. revocation is an explicit, supported path.

## Observed behaviour
- A child run ends cleanly (status: done, execution: finished) while its recorded delivery status is failed, with failure text referencing the error above.
- The parent session that was awaiting children never wakes; no completion event arrives; the interface remains in a waiting-for-subtasks state indefinitely.
- The child result is not lost: it can still be read back from the child session.

## Gaps
1. The thrown Error carries only the constant message. No reason code, no cause detail, nothing that identifies which currency condition failed or which code path revoked the authority.
2. Because of (1), a failed delivery cannot be traced from logs alone; identifying the cause required reading the bundle source.

## Impact
- Parent-side waits can hang indefinitely with no signal to the requester.
- Automated flows that depend on yield/completion handoff stall silently.
- Self-diagnosis is not possible for operators.

## Requests
1. Include a machine-readable reason (and, where safe, a short cause detail) in the thrown error and in the recorded delivery failure.
2. Provide a recoverable or at least observable failure path (for example a delivery-failure event the requester can observe and re-attach to), instead of leaving the wait unresolved.
3. Document which actions revoke a pending requester authority.

## Reproduction caveat
We could not build a deterministic minimal reproduction, because the revocation path is not logged. The above is based on the shipped bundle source plus observed behaviour. We are happy to test a build that logs the revocation reason.

issues.body:
## Summary

**At least 28** failures on stable **2026.10.5**; child effects unproved; no fix.

```text
service child cleanup identity lost: Error: Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission
```

## Environment

- Ubuntu **24.04.5 LTS**, Linux x64 **6.8.0-147-generic**.
- Node.js **24.21.0**.
- Stock npm OpenClaw **2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)**, managed user Gateway service.
- Official `v2026.10.5` tag resolves to commit
  `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`.
- No locally patched core files were carried into this stable update.
- No deliberate concurrent schema mutation, forced workflow, restart,
  database repair, integrity bypass or child replay was used to reproduce it.
  The triggering operation was an already occurring ordinary scheduled turn.

## Actual Evidence And Timing

Original native event clocks, UTC:

| Evidence | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Host-exec request event | 2026-10-19T19:05:14.174Z |
| Native error result event | 2026-10-19T19:05:15.134Z; `isError:true` |
| Event-clock difference | 960 ms; not measured child runtime |
| Admitted helper stdout | None returned |
| Child start/exit/reap/cleanup receipt | None returned; lifecycle unknown |
| Repetition count | At least twenty-eight unique ordinary native-exec failures, including intervening successful ordinary turns |

Opaque SHA-256 digests of the retained canonical events (no event payloads
or identifiers are published):

```text
request event:
ae50b2c38b43da7eeaa4661d8c5a36ff8e4c58b2a0280c511be60b0775b6f345

error result event:
dcab76a3549ce54435f8b1245466fb17c4624f85b4c06ab4ef7d6a6b68e9a31b
```

### Subsequent Ordinary Observation: Did Not Recur

The next untouched normal turn exercised the same pure preparation path:

- Native request: 2026-10-19T19:34:48.783Z, event digest
  `71b87546c13fb672d52fa4a8351e939a5e38e7e59056a77b6f57ded597e6d488`.
- Admitted result: 2026-10-19T19:34:49.693Z, `isError:false`, `ok:true`,
  event digest
  `5f6fb687db628e2c9d9ccb80141195c0c5226716dd392155740503c9a63275b6`.
- The owning turn then genuinely persisted its question and source attempts,
  validated the written plan successfully, completed normal delivery/release
  and reached native terminal at 19:36:16.953Z. At 19:36:43Z the read-only
  handoff check found no matching runtime processes or active OAuth leases.

Intervening independent success required no core patch or restart; it neither repaired nor replayed the earlier unknown child outcome.

### Recurrence On A Different Local Read

A subsequent untouched ordinary turn returned the same full error on a
different local Python command that reads retained JSON research context:

- Request event: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.112Z, digest
  `e9b1da906778bf797fd8fc53bf117112a83053f26dc9aa253eb84005504cfa61`.
- Error result: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.751Z, `isError:true`, digest
  `70720e276fc1c900f1d3a01c94001c691ad8b1d89f045bde0c6b012965916bd5`.
- Event-clock difference: 639ms, not measured child runtime. Again, no helper
  stdout or child start/terminal receipt was admitted; actual child outcome
  remains unknown.

The turn continued using independent retained facts and fresh provider observations, without a same-reference retry, deliberate invalidation, core change, restart or forced workflow. That continuation does not prove the rejected child's outcome.

The local helper is a pure structural preparation operation: its relevant
branch imports no SQLite/OpenClaw state, Node runtime, claim or database
reader. A separate direct local structural invocation succeeds. That control
does **not** exercise native service-child admission and is not a repaired
native-exec result.

The owning workflow retained the failed preparation/persistence disposition;
it did not obtain completed question registration or attempt persistence
through this rejected call. The turn later completed its mandatory reporting
and bookkeeping. Those later technical flags do not prove the rejected exec
operation healthy, its persistence completed or any financial action cleared.

## Installed Source Boundary, Not A Captured Stack

Package-relative locations in this exact installed build:

- `dist/openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs:97`:
  `prepareOpenClawStateDirectReader` rejects if the integrity revision differs
  from its epoch, or an existing-schema context lacks integrity/proof.
- `dist/exec-approvals-store-B7WwLRrI.mjs:218`:
  `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead(context)` prepares this direct reader;
  its returned guard independently rechecks admission and reads current policy.
- `dist/plugin-node-host-YOtba4hi.mjs:102`:
  plugin-exec authorization captures the worker context and prepares that
  current-policy reader. The approvals store has another authorization
  settlement caller; this error alone does not select between them.
- `dist/child-DMrKblk4.mjs:702`:
  service-child `loseIdentity` wraps its message as
  `service child cleanup identity lost: ...`.

The retained tool error is **not a JavaScript stack**. It does not reveal the
exact caller branch, concurrent writer, integrity epoch/revision/proof values,
schema operation, or ordering relative to process spawn. The source matches
identify a boundary to investigate, not a proven root cause or proof that
Python itself accessed shared state.

Exact installed artifact SHA-256s:

```text
openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs
591be6e4250c8d18e3a788b98a578b0488ea6415e44df2dc549b7098c4e5aad7

8065787d49ea90be0af69e2f45deaf003e11db127fbe6c8d3769a06bb246228e
```

## ClawSweeper Follow-Up

The [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6275795871)
requests an isolated failing native stable case, payload-free admission and
child-lifecycle diagnostics, and the same case on pinned main. **These behavioral
proof requests remain unfulfilled.** No repair PR or incident-matched fix is claimed.

Source inspection confirms that merged [PR #169584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169584),
commit `d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88`, replaces the
[stable direct-reader policy preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L148)
with a [worker-prepared current-policy owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L286).
The changed path is a relevant candidate, not proof it resolves this incident.
Its separately reported synthetic allow/revocation evidence is not this case.

Inspected suites, an inconclusive bounded attempt and successful native controls
are recorded below, not a failure repro or suite verdict. Consumer/invalidator,
integrity values and child outcome remain unknown. Keep open; do not duplicate
existing repairs, manufacture revocation, patch/restart core or replay unknown work.

## Existing Repair And Duplicate Check

[PR #167486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167486) already fixes
redundant schema initialization invalidating prepared exec integrity proof.
Its merge `5a0baa04e5bbe68767a9691497324c47c1ba3f96` is an ancestor of this
installed stable commit; GitHub compare reports behind=0. Its existing
real-worker/native-printf proof is useful prior work. This observation does
**not** establish that the same schema producer ran or regressed, nor justify
reimplementing that repair.

Distinct related boundaries, not duplicate evidence:

- [#176353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176353), fixed by
  [#176413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176413), concerns
  `Exec approval policy is unavailable or changing before execution`
  during Allow Once approval bookkeeping. This report has a different exact
  integrity error and no observed Allow Once trigger.
- [#161171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161171) concerns
  session-accessor prepared-admission tests, not this observed exec guard.
- [#161439](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161439) tracks
  shared-state responsiveness. No event-loop/SQL-wait attribution was captured
  for the 960-ms event interval here; this is not evidence of its historical
  ordinary-workload stall.
- [#139887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/139887) concerns a
  macOS EPERM process-group cleanup observation, not Linux integrity admission.

Read-only repository searches for the exact full error, `Direct shared-state
reader`, `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead`, and related integrity/exec-approval
terms found the merged repair above but no issue tracking this exact new
stable-release observation. Search results are not proof that no duplicate
exists; please consolidate under an existing exact owner if appropriate.

## Reproduction Status And Proposed Minimal Isolation

**No deterministic failing stable/main case or before/after repair proof exists.**
Use a credential-free Linux/Node24 scratch fixture and actual native consumer:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approvals-schema-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Existing #167486 first-read/profile/provenance/bound-approval/audit and reopen
cases are starting points; the older-checkout attempt below timed out without
a verdict. A harmless native request may use
`python3 -c 'import json; print(json.dumps({"ok": True}))'`; direct Python is
not equivalent. Expand only from an observed failure.

Capture payload-free consumer, captured/current revision+epoch/proof, generation,
invalidating writer/committed outcome and ordered launch/exit/reap/cleanup.
Authorized execution must settle once; genuine authority changes must deny.
Unknown outcomes, blind replay and integrity bypass are not repair evidence.

## Evidence Ledger / Remaining Gaps

Supplied: pinned stable environment, canonical timings/digests, artifacts and repair/duplicate checks. At least28 distinct failures are retained. Positive controls and later ordinary success are not failing reproductions or fixes. The failing consumer, admission invalidator, child lifecycle, matched-main regression and repaired exactly-once/real-revocation behavior remain unproved.

## Further Ordinary Recurrence (2026-10-19)

An untouched later ordinary turn returned the identical full native exec error
twice more, bringing the retained total at that observation to four unique native errors:

| Local operation | Request UTC / SHA-256 | Error UTC / SHA-256 | Event-clock gap |

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

Filed as a behavior bug because there is no performance option: the output is correct, the work is redundant.

### Summary
In the shared native chat UI (iOS and macOS), each change to the transcript rebuilds the source cards of every cited reply in the session, not just the reply that changed. On a 500-message session with 100 cited replies, that is 6.5 to 8.6 ms of main-thread work per transcript update on an M3 Ultra, and an agent turn with 20 tool calls triggers it about 43 times. The cards shown are correct; the problem is the repeated CPU work.

### Steps to reproduce
1. On `main` (9f3ed313782, unchanged at 6b959f4ca63), build `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` in release.
2. Build a 500-message transcript of 100 agent turns. Each turn has a user message, an assistant message with `web_search` and `web_fetch` tool calls, a search result with 8 rows, a fetch result with about 6 KB of text, and a final answer of about 1.5 KB citing 3 of the result URLs (1.49 MB of JSON in total). The transcript builder is under "Additional information".
3. Call `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` with it, then call it again with one more message appended, as `OpenClawChatViewModel.messages.didSet` does (`ChatViewModel.swift:16-18`) for each persisted message of a running turn.
4. Time the second call over 60 iterations.

### Expected behavior
A reply's source cards depend only on that reply, the earlier messages of its own run and the source context. Appending a message from another run, or reloading identical history, should not rebuild the cards of replies whose inputs did not change.

### Actual behavior
`ChatSourcePreviewProjector.project` (`ChatSourcePreviews.swift:84-121`) reuses parsed links and result fields for unchanged messages, but still calls `previews(links:entries:...)` for every cited reply on every call (`:109`). That re-runs URL canonicalization, result matching and redirect resolution for all 100 replies.

Measured median per `ChatSourcePreviewState.update`, release build, Apple M3 Ultra, macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2, 500 messages:
- one message appended: 6.5 to 8.6 ms
- unchanged messages: 6.6 to 6.8 ms
- history reload with the same ids: 10.2 to 14.3 ms

Streaming text deltas do not go through this path; only persisted messages do. An agent turn with k tool calls updates `messages` about 2k + 3 times (user echo, each tool call and result, the final answer, the history refresh), so a turn costs about 85 to 112 ms of main-thread work at k = 5 and 280 to 370 ms at k = 20.

### OpenClaw version
main at 9f3ed313782 (package version 2026.11.1)

### Operating system
macOS 27.2 (measured). The same shared code runs the iOS chat.

### Install method
Source build of `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` with `swift test -c release`.

### Model
Not applicable (client-side transcript projection; no model call involved).

### Provider / routing chain
Not applicable (client-side transcript projection).

### Additional provider/model setup details
None.

### Logs
```
BENCH transcript: 500 messages, 1492301 JSON bytes, 100 messages with previews
BENCH unchanged array (same values): median 6.755 ms (n=60)
BENCH append one new message: median 6.332 ms (n=60)
BENCH history refresh (re-decoded, same ids): median 10.236 ms (n=60)
BENCH ChatSourcePreviewState.update(append): median 6.509 ms (n=60)
```
(Second run: 6.597, 7.887, 14.291 and 8.606 ms. The host was shared with other work.)

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Code path: `ChatViewModel.swift:16-18` (`messages.didSet`) -> `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` (`ChatViewModel+SourcePreviews.swift:14-16`) -> `ChatSourcePreviewProjector.project` -> `previews(links:entries:context:...)` for each cited reply.

### Impact and severity
Affected: iOS and macOS chat users with long sessions that contain researched answers (replies citing `web_search` or `web_fetch` results).
Severity: performance; main-thread work that grows with the number of cited replies in the session.
Frequency: every persisted transcript message, every final event and every history refresh.
Consequence: 6 to 9 ms per transcript update at 500 messages and 100 cited replies on an M3 Ultra (measured), so 85 to 370 ms per agent turn of 5 to 20 tool calls (computed from the measured cost). Not measured on a phone, and not measured as frame time in the running app.

### Additional information
The projector's per-message cache of parsed links and result fields came with the source previews in 27292a116b0 (#148906); the per-reply card build sits outside that cache.

<details><summary>Transcript builder and timing loop (Swift Testing, in the OpenClawKitTests target)</summary>

```swift
import Foundation
import OpenClawKit
import Testing
@testable import OpenClawChatUI

struct SourcePreviewUpdateRepro {
    static func wrap(_ text: String, _ name: String) -> String {
        let source = name == "web_search" ? "Web Search" : "Web Fetch"
        return "<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id=\"0123456789abcdef\">>>\nSource: \(source)\n---\n\(text)\n"
            + "<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id=\"0123456789abcdef\">>>"
    }

    static func lorem(_ n: Int, seed: Int) -> String {
        let words = ["alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta", "echo", "foxtrot", "golf", "hotel", "india", "juliet",
                     "kilo", "lima", "mike", "november", "oscar", "papa", "quebec", "romeo", "sierra", "tango"]
        var out = ""
        var i = UInt(seed)
        while out.utf8.count < n {
            out += words[Int(i % UInt(words.count))] + (i % 13 == 0 ? ".\n\n" : " ")
            i = (i &* 31 &+ 7) % 1_000_003
        }
        return out
    }

    static func turn(_ t: Int) -> [[String: Any]] {
        let meta: [String: Any] = ["runId": "run-\(t)"]
        let urls = (0..<8).map { "https://site\($0 % 5).example.com/turn-\(t)/doc-\($0)" }
        let rows: [[String: Any]] = urls.enumerated().map { i, url in
            ["url": url, "title": wrap("Result \(i) for turn \(t)", "web_search"),
             "snippet": wrap(lorem(250, seed: t * 10 + i), "web_search")]
        }
        let external: (String) -> [String: Any] = { ["source": $0, "untrusted": true, "wrapped": true] }
        let user: [String: Any] = ["role": "user", "timestamp": Double(t * 10), "__openclaw": meta,
                                   "content": [["type": "text", "text": lorem(200, seed: t)]]]
        let call: [String: Any] = ["role": "assistant", "timestamp": Double(t * 10 + 1), "__openclaw": meta,
                                   "content": [["type": "text", "text": lorem(120, seed: t + 1)],
                                               ["type": "toolCall", "id": "call-\(t)", "name": "web_search",
                                                "arguments": ["query": "query \(t)"]],
                                               ["type": "toolCall", "id": "fetch-\(t)", "name": "web_fetch",
                                                "arguments": ["url": urls[0]]]]]
        let search: [String: Any] = ["role": "toolResult", "timestamp": Double(t * 10 + 2), "__openclaw": meta,
                                     "toolCallId": "call-\(t)", "toolName": "web_search",
                                     "content": [["type": "text", "text": "search results"]],
                                     "details": ["kind": "results", "results": rows,
                                                 "externalContent": external("web_search")]]
        let fetch: [String: Any] = ["role": "toolResult", "timestamp": Double(t * 10 + 3), "__openclaw": meta,
                                    "toolCallId": "fetch-\(t)", "toolName": "web_fetch",
                                    "content": [["type": "text", "text": "fetched"]],
                                    "details": ["url": urls[0], "finalUrl": urls[0], "status": 200,
                                                "title": wrap("Fetched page \(t)", "web_fetch"),
                                                "text": wrap(lorem(6000, seed: t + 3), "web_fetch"),
                                                "externalContent": external("web_fetch")]]
        let cites = (0..<3).map { "[source \($0)](\(urls[$0 * 2]))" }.joined(separator: ", ")
        let answer: [String: Any] = ["role": "assistant", "timestamp": Double(t * 10 + 4), "__openclaw": meta,
                                     "stopReason": "stop", "phase": "final_answer",
                                     "content": [["type": "text",
                                                  "text": lorem(1500, seed: t + 4) + "\n\nSources: " + cites]]]
        return [user, call, search, fetch, answer]
    }

    static func decode(_ json: [[String: Any]]) throws -> [OpenClawChatMessage] {
        try JSONDecoder().decode([OpenClawChatMessage].self, from: JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: json))
    }

    @Test @MainActor func `update after one appended message`() throws {
        let base = try Self.decode((0..<100).flatMap(Self.turn))
        let extras = try Self.decode(Self.turn(100))
        let state = ChatSourcePreviewState()
        state.update(base)
        var samples: [Duration] = []
        for i in 0..<60 {
            samples.append(ContinuousClock().measure { state.update(base + [extras[i % extras.count]]) })
        }
        print("median update:", samples.sorted()[samples.count / 2])
    }
}
```

Run with `swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing --filter SourcePreviewUpdateRepro` from `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`.

</details>

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

A subagent spawned with `sessions_spawn` can finish just before its parent calls `sessions_yield`. When that happens, its completion event is appended to the parent transcript during the yield's abort/settle, **before** the `openclaw.sessions_yield` context message. No follow-up parent turn ever starts. The parent's hook run reports `outcome=error`, and the session stays parked on the yield marker until something outside OpenClaw retries it.

This looks like the same lost-wakeup class as #137710, but on the embedded runner with `sessions_spawn` (OpenAI Responses provider), not the native Codex runtime.

### Version

OpenClaw 2026.10.5, embedded runner, provider `openai` / `openai-chatgpt-responses`. The run was an unattended `/hooks/agent` turn (`deliver:false`).

### Timeline (one parent session, UTC)

Parent transcript (`<session>.jsonl`), entry types only:

```
00:31:17  assistant  toolCall sessions_spawn
00:31:21  toolResult sessions_spawn   {"status":"accepted","mode":"run", ...}
   ... parent keeps working (exec/read) ...
00:32:06.526  assistant  toolCall sessions_yield
00:32:07.280  toolResult sessions_yield   {"status":"yielded","message":"Turn yielded."}
00:32:07.294  user  "[Internal task completion event] source: subagent ..."     <- child completion, 14 ms after the yield result
00:32:08.760  custom_message  customType=openclaw.sessions_yield  (triggerTurn: false)
              <end of transcript: no further entries>
```

Gateway journal:

```
00:32:02.424 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ agent.wait 41061ms                     <- child run had already finished
00:32:09.946 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron ... sessionKey=agent:<id>:hook:<key> outcome=error duration=121623ms error="⚠️ 🛠️ Exec failed"
00:32:09.949 [hooks] hook agent run returned non-ok status status=error summary=⚠️ 🛠️ Exec failed
```

Trajectory `session.ended`: `status: "success"`, `aborted: false`, `timedOut: false`.

### Expected

Whether the child finishes before or after the parent yields, exactly one follow-up parent turn should start with the completion as its input.

### Actual

The completion is consumed into the run that is ending (it reads as if it were steered into the active run during the yield abort settle). The yield marker is then persisted after it, and nothing wakes the session. The same agent yielded to subagents 39 other times that day. In every one, the completion arrived after the `openclaw.sessions_yield` marker, and the parent resumed 25 to 35 s later as expected.

### Secondary (cosmetic)

The run's error summary `⚠️ 🛠️ Exec failed` came from an earlier `exec` call in the same turn that failed schema validation (`command: must have required properties command`, empty arguments). The model had already recovered from it. Surfacing it as the run outcome makes the lost wake look like an exec failure.

### Workaround on our side

Our grader's retry sweep now treats a transcript that ends on the `openclaw.sessions_yield` marker, with the completion event just before it, as an ended turn after 2 quiet minutes, and re-fires it.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let an isolated agent-turn automation delegate its inference account to the agent it is assigned to. The job would then run with whatever model, account and auth order that agent is configured with at run time. Today host-managed jobs retain a separate account binding even when their model follows the agent's configuration.

### Problem to solve

On 2026.11.1, an agent-turn job that would use a stored OpenClaw auth profile is refused unless the job itself records an inference account (docs: automation/cron-jobs/payloads "Inference account continuity"). We already manage models, fallbacks and auth order per agent, so per-job bindings are hard to operate:

- **Account authorization is managed per job.** The private recorded binding is omitted from public job details, even though an explicitly pinned profile can appear in `payload.model`.
- **Account changes need job-level reauthorization.** The documented CLI repair is `automations edit <id> --model provider/model@profile`. In our installed 2026.11.1 CLI, `automations edit` takes one job ID and has no bulk account-edit option. After repairing triage, our read-only sweep found 21 other enabled agent-turn jobs without bindings.
- **We discovered missing bindings through failed runs.** After the upgrade from 2026.10.8 to 2026.11.1, retained history shows seven consecutive account refusals between 06:25 and 10:25 on 6 November for a triage job scheduled every 30 minutes. An annual reminder due at 07:00 also failed before delivery. We have not established which change introduced the missing bindings or whether an upgrade-time warning was shown.

Our expectation when assigning a job to an agent was that the job follows however that agent is set up.

### Proposed solution

An explicit, opt-in delegation mode. For example `automations edit <id> --inference-account agent`, or an agent-level default such as `agents.entries.<id>.automations.inferenceAccount: "agent"` (names illustrative):

- The job records that it delegates to agent `<id>` rather than to a specific profile. This is still an explicit, recorded operator decision, not a guess from current defaults.
- An authorized operator explicitly selects the agent's automation account policy. Each occurrence resolves that policy once and pins the selected account for the whole run, including retries and fallbacks.
- Changing that policy requires account-owner authorization. Revoked or replaced credentials fail closed; delegation must not silently adopt a replacement credential or another person's account.
- Existing boundaries still apply: delegation only to an agent the job's owner may use, no crossing into another person's personal account, and reassigning the job to a different agent re-confirms delegation.
- Run history records the resolved account, so billing changes stay visible after the fact.
- Optionally, a bulk path (`doctor --fix` or `automations edit --all`) to adopt delegation for existing jobs.

### Alternatives considered

- **Per-job `model@profile` (current behaviour).** Works, but couples every job to one profile and multiplies edits on any account change.
- **A local script that rebinds every job.** Possible, but it reimplements something that belongs in the scheduler.

### Impact

This would let operators manage an explicitly authorized automation account policy once per agent, while retaining per-job pins for jobs that need a fixed account. It changes the scope of authorization; it should not weaken account-owner or revocation checks.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), macOS arm64, single operator.
- The refusal comes from the cron run path (`trigger === "cron" && !binding && authProfileId`).
- Related: #188761 (preflight when changing an agent's default model), #191936 (account selection in the Automations editor), #178812 (scheduled-run authority).
- Unlike #191936's account picker and recovery UI, this asks for an explicit ongoing delegation policy. Legacy account adoption and diagnostics are separate; #193418 was closed as a duplicate of #191936.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On every Control UI reload, the accent palette is projected onto the document root three times with the same inputs, and each pass forces a full-document style recalculation. In the cold-load benchmark this costs about 105 ms of CPU time per reload (from CPU profiles) and delays the first route being ready.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `main` at `3fed691416b3`, run `pnpm install` and `pnpm ui:build`, and copy `dist/control-ui` to `/absolute/base/control-ui`.
2. Run the committed cold-load benchmark with CPU profiles on the chat route (built-in synthetic fixture, no environment or seam color configured):
   ```
   node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
     --gateway-http --bundle-dir /absolute/base/control-ui --runs 3 --cpu-profile
   ```
3. In the source-mapped profiles, look at `applyControlUiAccent` and `applyControlUiPresentation`.
4. Optional: run untraced with `--untraced --thread-cpu-time` (no `--cpu-profile`) and read `threadCpu.styleMs`.

Where the three passes come from on `3fed691416b3`:

- `ui/src/app/config.ts:229` applies the operator seam color, which runs `applyControlUiAccent`.
- `ui/src/app/bootstrap-theme.ts:76` applies the user accent, which runs `applyControlUiAccent` again.
- `ui/src/app/config.ts:92-98` imports `control-ui-environment-presentation.runtime.ts`, whose `applyControlUiPresentation` (`control-ui-environment-presentation.runtime.ts:19`) applies the seam color again. The import condition includes `root.style.getPropertyValue("--ring")` (`config.ts:96`), and `applyControlUiAccent` always writes `--ring` (`control-ui-presentation.ts:282`), so this pass runs on every reload even with no environment and no seam color.

Each pass removes about 18 root custom properties (`control-ui-presentation.ts:238`), calls `getComputedStyle(root)` (`control-ui-presentation.ts:245`), then mixes `setProperty` writes with `resolveThemeColor` reads, so each read after a write forces a recalculation.

### Expected behavior

A reload projects the accent once, because the inputs (accent or seam color, theme, mode, palette stylesheets) do not change between the three calls. The environment presentation pass only runs when there is an environment or a seam color to apply or clear. #193338 removed the same kind of unchanged reapply for profile appearance on reload.

### Actual behavior

CPU profiles (3 runs) show `applyControlUiAccent` at a median of 105.1 ms inclusive per reload, `resolveThemeColor` at 93.1 ms, and `applyControlUiPresentation` at 86.7 ms, with no environment or seam color configured. Untraced, the renderer spends a median of 180.9 ms on style CPU per reload, with 3 long tasks per reload.

### OpenClaw version

main @ 3fed691416b37f91b0db8dd77446f739e7bf92af (timings measured on d999f7b1b675; the only `ui/src` changes between the two are e2e test files)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Apple M3 Ultra), Google Chrome 156.0.8078.80

### Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm ui:build`, production bundle served through the Gateway HTTP handler by `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts`

### Model

Not applicable: Control UI boot only, no model request is involved.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: Control UI boot only, no provider request is involved.

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

```shell
CPU profile attribution, base, 3 runs, inclusive ms per reload [min, median, max]
  applyControlUiAccent             ui/src/app/control-ui-presentation.ts            99.3  105.1  128.0
  applyControlUiOperatorSeamColor  ui/src/app/control-ui-presentation.ts            86.9   91.4  106.3
  resolveThemeColor                ui/src/lib/theme-color.ts                        86.7   93.1  117.3
  applyControlUiPresentation       ui/src/app/control-ui-environment-presentation.runtime.ts  84.5  86.7  98.8
  syncControlUiSystemChrome        ui/src/app/control-ui-presentation.ts             1.5    1.8    2.1

Untraced, 10 base runs (chat route), median [Q1, Q3] ms
  threadCpu.styleMs                180.9 [175.8, 183.7]
  threadCpu.taskMs                 842.5 [825.7, 861.8]
  firstRouteReadyMs                523.3 [511.1, 534.7]
  long tasks per reload            3 (range 3 to 4)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No visual symptom: the final colors are correct, the cost is CPU time during load. Evidence is the profile attribution and benchmark numbers above. A fix and before/after measurements are in the linked PR.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every Control UI reload, for all users. It does not depend on an environment or seam color being configured.
- Severity: annoying (slower reload, no wrong output).
- Frequency: always (every profiled and untraced run).
- Consequence: about 105 ms of extra main-thread CPU per reload on the test machine, and a later first route ready.

### Additional information

Not a regression from a known version; the triple projection is how the current boot order works. Searches of open issues and PRs for "accent palette", "seam color", "applyControlUiAccent", "control-ui-presentation" and "accent reload" found no duplicate. #160399 (open) changes System theme handling in `bootstrap-theme.ts` and `theme.ts`, which is separate from this. A PR with a fix is linked.

issues.body:
### Summary

When a replication tool such as Litestream replicates `state/openclaw.sqlite`, the Gateway logs `Shared-state WAL maintenance failed ... WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader` on every non-quiet maintenance pass, indefinitely, even though the WAL stays bounded. That works out to roughly 150 warnings a day on our host.

Litestream holds a read transaction by design and checkpoints the WAL itself. OpenClaw's PASSIVE checkpoint is therefore always blocked, `consecutiveBlocked` never resets, and the warning policy from #172121 (two consecutive blocked passes, or an oversized WAL) fires on every later pass.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.1, Linux (arm64)
- Litestream 0.5.17 replicating the shared-state DB and agent DBs (continuous replication, hourly snapshots)

### Observed

```
[state/db] Shared-state WAL maintenance failed error="openclaw-state WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader" path=.../state/openclaw.sqlite checkpoint={"state":"blocked","walBytes":11058112,"databaseBytes":34516992,"logFrames":1,"checkpointedFrames":0,"lastCompletedAtMs":null,"consecutiveBlocked":2171,"warning":true,"activeReaders":[],"readerDiagnostics":[{"scope":"current-thread","blockingOwner":"unknown",...}]}
```

- `walBytes` stayed exactly 11,058,112 for more than two days while the database grew from 25 MB to 34.5 MB, so the WAL is bounded: Litestream checkpoints it. Litestream reported no errors and completed hourly snapshots throughout.
- The size rule (`walBytes > max(2 × databaseBytes, journalSizeLimit)`) never fires. Only the consecutive-count rule does.

### Why it matters

The real-danger case (a WAL that grows) uses the same message, so a genuine problem gets buried under constant false alarms. This differs from #164294, where an in-process reader pins the WAL and it grows without bound. Here the WAL is bounded.

### Proposal

Keep logging at once on WAL growth, when the size ceiling is exceeded, and on the first sustained block after a completed checkpoint. Repeat an unchanged, bounded block at most once per interval (hourly is proposed; it's a single constant). Health, `status --deep` and Doctor stay unchanged. I have a small PR with a real-SQLite regression test ready and will link it here.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Cloning a cron job in the Control UI drops its explicit `failureAlert.threadId`, while preserving its normal `delivery.threadId`. The copied automation can therefore send failure alerts to the normal delivery topic instead of the separately configured alert topic.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with a job whose normal delivery and failure alerts use the same Telegram chat, with normal `delivery.threadId: 7` and explicit `failureAlert.threadId: 41`. The latter is a supported setting, including through `openclaw cron edit <id> --failure-alert-thread-id 41`.
2. In Automations, choose **Clone** for that job. Leave its delivery and failure-alert settings unchanged and save the copy.
3. Inspect the `cron.add` payload: normal delivery retains topic 7, but `failureAlert` no longer contains topic 41.

I reproduced the payload loss through the production `startCronClone → addCronJob` functions in the existing UI test harness. I did not run a browser session, invoke a model, or deliver a Telegram alert.

### Expected behavior

Clone preserves the source job's explicit failure-alert topic, just as it preserves the other persisted failure-alert fields and the normal delivery topic.

### Actual behavior

The source alert configuration:

```json
{"channel":"telegram","to":"123","threadId":41}
```

becomes this configuration in the clone request:

```json
{"channel":"telegram","to":"123"}
```

The normal delivery still has `threadId: 7`. The failure-alert resolver can inherit that normal topic when the channel, recipient, and account match; the explicit override has been lost before scheduling or delivery.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1 source tree, executed at `ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d`. The causal UI builder and failure-alert resolver are unchanged on main `2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1; Node.js 26.12.1. Focused UI domain test, no browser/platform interaction claimed.

### Install method

Official source checkout with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

### Model

Not applicable; reproducing the clone request does not invoke a model.

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI cron form → `cron.add`. Telegram destinations in the fixture are synthetic; no external delivery was performed.

### Logs

```text
Expected failureAlert: { channel: 'telegram', to: '123', threadId: 41 }
Received failureAlert: { channel: 'telegram', to: '123' }

Tests: 1 failed | 6 passed | 33 skipped
```

The failure is the added clone regression. The five existing clone cases and an edit control passed. In that control, renaming the source job and applying its resulting patch through `mergeCronFailureAlert` preserves topic 41.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Minimal addition to the existing [“clones exact persisted fields” table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/ui/src/lib/cron/index.test.ts#L473-L500):

```ts
{
  delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "telegram", to: "123", threadId: 7, bestEffort: false },
  failureAlert: { channel: "telegram", to: "123", threadId: 41 },
},
```

Run that table with:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/cron/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern 'clones exact persisted fields'
```

The [builder receives the source alert configuration but omits `threadId`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts#L146-L178). Editing happens to retain it through [the backend's existing-state merge](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/src/cron/service/delivery-merge.ts#L145-L167); creating a clone has no old state to merge. The [resolver's normal-topic fallback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts#L215-L227) explains the routing consequence.

### Impact and severity

Affected: users cloning automations with a separate, explicit failure-alert topic. The clone silently changes where failure notifications are addressed, so people monitoring the alert topic may miss them. The payload omission is deterministic in the focused reproduction; real-world incidence and external delivery were not measured. The source job remains unchanged, and the cloned job can be corrected with the supported CLI setting.

### Additional information

Related prior work: [#129302](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/129302) preserves other cron form fields during clone/edit. This report concerns the remaining `failureAlert.threadId` field, rather than reopening those fixes. A focused repair should retain the explicit topic on clone and preserve normal edit/inheritance behavior when no explicit topic is set.

issues.body:
### Summary

Load the IP literal part of the `MEDIA:` remote host guard on demand, so the Control UI chat boot bundle no longer ships `ipaddr.js`.

### Problem to solve

Every cold load of the chat route downloads, parses and compiles `ipaddr.js` and `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` as part of the chat boot bundle, but first paint never uses them. They are only needed to classify an assistant `MEDIA:` line whose https host is an IP literal (for example `MEDIA:https://8.8.8.8/a.png`), which is rare in real transcripts. Hostname URLs never need the IP parser.

The import chain at `6e7ee204e1b1fef223c794dbbed42de069a2623e`:

- `ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.ts:23` imports `splitMediaFromOutput` from `src/media/parse.ts`.
- `src/media/parse.ts:2` imports `splitMediaOutput` from `src/media/parse-output.ts`.
- `src/media/parse-output.ts:1-10` statically imports eight helpers from `@openclaw/net-policy/ip`, which wraps `ipaddr.js`. They are used only by `isBlockedRemoteMediaHostname` (`src/media/parse-output.ts:95-127`).
- `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json` lists `node_modules/ipaddr.js/lib/ipaddr.js` and `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` in the chat boot set.

The chat boot bundle is also close to its gzip budget: 1,293,984 B against a limit of 1,294,735 B (751 B of headroom), so any small chat change can trip `pnpm ui:check-performance`.

Reproduce on the commit above:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm ui:build
pnpm ui:check-performance
# chat boot JS: 20 requests, ... limits: 20 requests, 1294735 B gzip
grep -l ipaddr dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-boot-chat-*.js
# prints the chat boot chunk
```

### Proposed solution

Split the remote host guard in two:

- A small module, used by the browser, that decides plain hostnames itself (they can never parse as an IP) and sends anything an IP parser could read to the full guard.
- The full IP literal guard, loaded as its own chunk. Until it is installed, those hosts are rejected (fail closed, never looser). The chunk loads the first time such a host appears, and chat items built before it loads are rebuilt once it is installed.

Server code keeps importing `src/media/parse-output.ts`, which installs the full guard at import, so the Gateway's decision stays synchronous and unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep the guard in the boot bundle: costs about 4.3 KB gzip on every chat cold load for a rare case.
- Reimplement IP literal parsing without `ipaddr.js`: duplicates a security-sensitive parser that `@openclaw/net-policy` already owns.
- Swap the module per build with a Vite alias: the browser and server would run different guard code under the same import path, and the unit tests would no longer cover what ships.
- Load the guard eagerly when the chat route starts: the boot manifest generator then counts it as boot code and puts `ipaddr.js` back in the chat boot set.
- Preload it at idle time after the chat route mounts: it then downloads on every cold load, and the lazy chunks (served without content encoding) cost more transfer than the boot bundle saves.

### Impact

- Affected: every Control UI user who cold loads the chat route.
- Severity: low. About 4.3 KB gzip (16 KB minified) of boot JS that first paint does not need, plus budget pressure on the chat boot bundle.
- Frequency: every cold load of the chat route.
- Consequence: extra boot bytes; on the base commit the chat boot bundle is 751 B under its gzip limit. A local cold-load benchmark did not show a timing difference beyond its A/A noise.

### Evidence/examples

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts 6e7ee204e1b1fef223c794dbbed42de069a2623e` with the proposed change applied:

```text
chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1293984 B -> 1289715 B (-4269 B); requests 20 -> 20
new boot JS gzip vs base: 800440 B -> 800493 B (+53 B); requests 15 -> 15
startup JS gzip vs base: 90484 B -> 90483 B (-1 B); requests 3 -> 3
```

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself. A PR is linked.

### Additional information

OpenClaw version: `6e7ee204e1b1fef223c794dbbed42de069a2623e` (main). No open issue or PR covers this (searched open issues and PRs for "ipaddr", "MEDIA host guard", "MEDIA IP literal", "chat boot bytes", "chat boot ipaddr", "control-ui boot chunk" and "parse-output").

# [Bug]: Android Archived threads stops at 200 conversations without indicating more are available

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Android's Threads → Archived loads only the first 200 archived conversations without a next-page action or incomplete-list indication. “Oldest first” sorts that loaded window rather than bringing the oldest stored conversations into view.

### Steps to reproduce
Source-verified scenario, not an executed Android reproduction:

1. Use one agent with 201 archived, visible, non-internal conversations. Give them unique titles and distinct `updatedAt`/`lastActivityAt` values in the same order; leave them unpinned and keep the current selection outside those 201 rows.
2. Connect with an identity allowed to view those conversations. Open Threads → Archived with an empty search query.
3. Scroll to the end, then choose Oldest first.
4. As a recovery control, search the unique title of the omitted 201st conversation while online.

### Expected behavior
Allow browsing subsequent archived pages and indicate incomplete/loading states accurately. The Gateway already supports pagination for archived sessions; server-backed search should remain available alongside browsing.

### Actual behavior
The initial request explicitly uses `limit = 200, archived = true`. The controller parses pagination metadata, applies the rows, then clears paging state for archived results. `loadMoreSessions` also refuses archived requests. Threads consumes the loaded rows without a Load More action or completeness warning; changing sort only reorders those rows locally.

A distinctive server-side search can find the omitted conversation. That recovery does not make the unfiltered archive complete.

### OpenClaw version
Source commit `57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160`.

### Operating system
Affected source: native Android. Device/OS runtime reproduction: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method
Source inspection in an isolated checkout; no installed app tested.

### Model
Not applicable; browsing requires no inference.

### Provider / routing chain
Android Threads → `sessions.list` → archived roster projection. No live Gateway/provider exercised.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- [Threads initial 200-row request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/SessionsScreen.kt#L172).
- [Archived results clear paging state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt#L4844).
- [Load More refuses the archived scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt#L1308).
- [Existing Gateway test establishes archived pagination](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-list-archived.test.ts#L66).

A 200-row archive is the complete-list control; 201 rows exposes the missing continuation. Search is a separate recovery control. These are source-derived expectations, not executed test results.

### Impact and severity
Suggested P2: people cannot browse older archived conversations and may mistake the oldest visible row for the oldest stored row. Data remains on the Gateway and a distinctive search can recover it. This affects navigation and conversation continuity, not permanent history loss. Incidence on real devices: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information
[#101102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101102) introduced server-backed search beyond the fetched window; it does not paginate the unfiltered archive. The sidebar's existing Load More action cannot recover this scope because the controller explicitly rejects archived continuation.

Use the existing pagination contract in Threads, including Archived. Cover 201 rows, the complete 200-row control, online search, status changes, local sorting, and preservation of loaded rows if a later page fails. No new backend endpoint is needed.

### Acceptance criteria

- Establish a failing 201-row archived regression and retain the complete 200-row control. Reuse the existing roster pagination owner and backend contract rather than increasing the initial limit.
- Carry the archived scope through continuation requests, and preserve the expanded loaded window on refresh. A next-page action must not switch silently to active conversations.
- Expose continuation, loading, and retry states in Threads. A later-page failure must retain loaded rows; retry must complete the same archive without breaking active-roster pagination, sorting, or online search.
- Validate the flow in an isolated Android app and Gateway with comparable before/after UI evidence. Extend the existing active-roster pagination tests with the archived path.

These criteria incorporate the [source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193828#issuecomment-6673454964); no Android runtime execution is claimed for this report.

issues.body:
# Operator-approved bounded session facts for user-installed plugins

## Environment and problem
OpenClaw 2026.10.10. An operator-installed local plugin uses the documented `api.runtime.gateway.readSessionFacts({ sessionKeys })` API to verify its exact assigned worker sessions before recovery/rebinding decisions.

The host rejects this API with `Session facts are only available to bundled or trusted official plugins`. The plugin correctly treats the result as unknown and refuses automated rebind; ordinary local-plugin installation does not provide a supported narrow grant. We are not requesting blanket official/bundled trust or a workaround that spoofs provenance.

## Requested supported capability
Provide an explicit operator/admin-approved, per-plugin read-only grant for bounded exact-key session facts, or document an existing supported route if available.

Preserve the existing caller-authority and session-visibility checks, incognito filtering, bounded key count/length, lifecycle retirement checks and typed response. The plugin identity must come from the host invocation context, not plugin parameters. The grant must not allow session enumeration, profile identity access, arbitrary gateway requests or writes. Prefer the minimum run-state/identity fields required for safe worker-liveness decisions rather than message previews.

## Acceptance criteria
- An ungranted local plugin remains denied.
- An operator-granted plugin can read only authorized exact session keys.
- A plugin cannot grant itself this capability or escalate to other APIs.
- Revocation takes effect through the supported runtime lifecycle.
- Audit records identify the plugin and capability grant/revocation without exposing secrets or message content.

Please advise whether this requires a host change or whether an already-supported least-privilege route exists. No private paths, credentials, transcripts or business records are included in this report.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (misdisplay without crash) — UI rendering / live-chat ↔ history handoff.

### Summary

When a gateway-injected **delivery mirror of a system notice** (e.g. the skill-workshop "Learned" notice) lands *after* a run's final assistant reply, the Control UI webchat reconstructs the thread with the notice as the turn's last visible bubble and demotes the real reply into the collapsed tool-steps area. The persisted transcript is clean — exactly one verbatim copy of the reply, `droppedMessages: false` — so this looks like lost conversation but is purely a rendering/grouping defect.

Observed after a Gateway restart (webchat closed `code=1012 service restart`, reconnect forced a full history reload), but a **plain page reload reproduces the stable state**: the full-history projection regroups identically. The restart only guarantees the delta path resets.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), stable npm channel, Debian 13 arm64 VM, Gateway as `systemd --user` service.
- Control UI webchat over HTTPS, single browser tab, Node v26.12.0.
- Model provider: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving a reasoning model (`api: openai-completions`); assistant records persist `openclawDelivery.textPhaseRequiresTerminal: true` and `responseModel: "keepalive"`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a webchat session, complete a turn whose terminal assistant text reply is delivered (multi-tool turn; with a reasoning-completions provider the text phase is held until the terminal snapshot — `if (isReasoningCompletionsText) return;` in `builtin-openclaw-*.mjs`).
2. Before the next user message, let a gateway-injected notice deliver: the transcript gets an assistant mirror — `api: "openclaw-transcript"`, `provider: "openclaw"`, `model: "delivery-mirror"`, `openclawDeliveryMirror.kind: "channel-final"`, `stopReason: "stop"` — **and no `__openclaw.runId`**, unlike the run's own messages.
3. Reload the page (or restart the Gateway to also exercise the transient variant).

### Actual behavior

The thread tail renders the notice text as the last assistant bubble of the previous question's turn card; the run's real final reply is visible only inside that card's collapsed step list. The exchange reads as "answered with a system notice".

### Expected behavior

The run's terminal reply stays the turn's visible answer bubble. The notice renders as its own standalone notice, outside turn cards, and never participates in bubble selection.

### Evidence (storage layer is clean)

- Session history tail shows reply at seq N (full text, `stopReason: "stop"`), mirror at seq N+1 (no `runId`); `droppedMessages: false`, `contentRedacted: false`.
- 2026.10.5 dist pointers:
  - `chat-history-handler-*.mjs`: a `channel-final` mirror inside a history delta forces `{ kind: "reset" }` → client refetches full history, so every reload re-derives the same wrong grouping.
  - `chat-display-projection.history-*.mjs`: `isDuplicateAssistantDelivery` hides a mirror only when its text equals the previous visible reply; a distinct notice survives into the tail slot.
  - Control UI chat bundle (`control-ui-boot-chat-*.js`, turn-grouping): settles **without `runId`** fall back to the last external user message as card start, and visible-bubble selection surfaces the latest successful settle — so the runId-less mirror joins the still-open card and steals the bubble. The client already imports the transcript-only classifier (`provider: "openclaw"` × models {`delivery-mirror`, `gateway-injected`} / kinds {`channel-final`, `channel-final-suppressed`, `message-tool-source-reply`, `cron-direct-delivery-context}`) but does not apply it to turn grouping.
  - The commentary-vs-final phase exists only as transient live-stream metadata and is never persisted; the durable `openclawDelivery.textPhaseRequiresTerminal` only means "hold text until terminal snapshot", which is not enough for replay to recover terminality.
  - Server-side precedent for the right filter exists: the reports kernel (`session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-reports.kernel-*.mjs`) skips rows with `mirrorOrigin` unless `runTerminal === true`; the webchat projection emits no comparable fact.

### Proposed fix direction

- **Client (primary):** exclude transcript-only mirrors from prior-turn card attribution and from the answer-bubble pool (render as standalone notices); pick the bubble as the last settle whose `runId` matches the card and whose `stopReason` is terminal (or `__openclaw.runTerminal === true`).
- **Server (hardening):** stamp `runTerminal: true` on the run's final delivered text at append time, and attach `__openclaw.turnBoundary` after gateway-injected notices — the `turnBoundary` machinery already exists for heartbeat/cron pairing.

### Relation to existing issues

Same live↔history handoff family, complementary symptom:

- #153671, #149153 — final reply rendered **twice** (storage holds one copy).
- #136250 (closed) — duplicate renders after WS reconnects / gateway restarts.
- #146472 — stale client state, duplicated assistant bubbles.
- Pattern-adjacent on other surfaces: #162554 (WhatsApp — delivery notice silently replaces the real reply), #165038 (iOS — new answer folded into "Worked for Xs", previous bubble shown).

The Control UI variant where a runId-less notice mirror **displaces** the last answer into collapsed tool steps appears untracked; filing with root cause so maintainers can fold it into the family as they see fit.

### Notes

Recurring weekly on this install: 2026-10-16 (after old dashboard sessions re-armed) and 2026-10-19 (notice delivered at +1 s before a planned Gateway SIGTERM; WS close `code=1012` at +4 s). Both times cost a transcript-rescue cycle because the reply genuinely looked lost. Restart is not required for the stable misdisplay; step 3 alone (reload) reproduces it once the mirror follows the run terminal.

# [Bug]: iOS Share removes indentation and blank lines from imported text

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Sharing structured text into OpenClaw on iOS changes its contents before the user sends it: the share draft strips indentation from every line and removes internal blank lines. A Python example that arrives intact from the share provider becomes invalid code in the draft.

### Steps to reproduce
The provider/extractor/composer sequence below was executed with the production Swift sources on macOS; the iOS share-sheet UI and Gateway send were not exercised.

1. Provide this plain text through an `NSExtensionItem` with an `NSItemProvider` registered as `UTType.plainText`:

```python
def greet(name):
    message = f"Hello, {name}"

    return message
```

2. Run the extension's `ShareContentExtractor.extract(from:)`. Its `payload.text` still equals the input.
3. Pass that payload to `ShareDraftComposer.compose(from:)`, as `ShareViewController.prepareDraft()` does before `setDraft`.
4. Inspect the resulting draft.

### Expected behavior
Preserve indentation and internal line breaks in non-scaffold shared content. The existing cleanup of complete historical scaffold lines and duplicate URL handling should keep working.

### Actual behavior
The resulting draft is:

```text
def greet(name):
message = f"Hello, {name}"
return message
```

No omitted-content warning is produced. `sendCurrentDraft()` sends this edited draft; its outer whitespace trim cannot restore the removed indentation.

### OpenClaw version
Source commit `57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160`.

### Operating system
Production Foundation path executed on macOS 27.0.1, arm64, Swift 6.4.2. Affected caller is the iOS Share Extension; no installed App Store build was tested.

### Install method
Isolated compilation of the unchanged extractor/composer and their production payload/string dependencies; real Foundation item providers with synthetic text.

### Model
Not applicable; no inference.

### Provider / routing chain
iOS Share provider → extractor → draft composer → editable share draft. No external delivery tested.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
One provider-to-draft reproduction confirmed the altered output above. Controls confirmed unchanged simple prose and `Text: legitimate content`; the raw provider text was independently compared with the original before composition.

The causal operation is the per-line trim and empty-line filter in [ShareDraftComposer.swift](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/ios/ShareExtension/ShareDraftComposer.swift#L22). The real caller is [ShareViewController.prepareDraft](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/ios/ShareExtension/ShareViewController.swift#L58).

### Impact and severity
This affects shared text where whitespace carries meaning, including code and structured examples. It changes the material the user is asking the agent to inspect, rather than only its visual style. The original source remains intact, and the editable draft allows manual repair or pasting the original. P2 appears appropriate for this bounded defect; population frequency is unknown.

### Additional information
[#103453](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103453) fixed overbroad scaffold-prefix removal, and [#116430](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/116430) fixed mirrored URLs. Neither preserves indentation through this per-line sanitation. The proposed scope is the existing draft composer: retain original non-scaffold lines, with provider-level regression coverage and the existing scaffold/URL controls. No new share-inbox behavior or delivery policy is needed.

### Acceptance criteria

- Establish a failing real-provider regression for the indented example and its internal blank line, then verify preservation after the repair.
- Normalize line values only for exact scaffold comparison; retain original non-scaffold content rather than replacing it with the normalized comparison value.
- Keep exact legacy scaffold removal, legitimate prefixed text, ordinary prose, and URL deduplication working. Run the existing extractor/composer Logic suites and validate the editable iOS share draft with the production extension build.

These criteria incorporate the [source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193821#issuecomment-6673318304). The Foundation reproduction above was executed locally; the bot did not independently run it, and iOS UI validation remains work for the repair.
