# [Bug]: iOS deletes a finished voice note when other attachments fill the upload budget

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Finishing a voice note in a nearly full attachment draft can discard the recording before it becomes an attachment. The combined-size check correctly refuses it, but cleanup deletes its only file and resets the recorder, so removing another attachment cannot recover the note for retry.

### Steps to reproduce
Source-verified sequence, not an executed physical recording:

1. In a connected iOS conversation, add a file that fits the Gateway's advertised attachment budget but leaves less room than the next recording. For the default decoded budget of 19,464,192 bytes, a 19,400,000-byte file leaves 64,192 bytes.
2. Record a voice note whose encoded bytes exceed the remaining budget but stay below the individual 5,000,000-byte voice limit. Use the actual file size, not a duration estimate.
3. Finish the recording. The aggregate admission path reports `Too large to send: voice-note-….m4a` without adding a voice attachment.
4. Remove the first attachment. The discarded recording has no retained file or retry action; it must be recorded again.

### Expected behavior
Keep the upload limit while preserving a finished recording rejected at this handoff until it can be retried or explicitly discarded. Successful staging can still remove the temporary file after the attachment owner holds its bytes.

### Actual behavior
`addVoiceNoteAttachment` unconditionally deletes the input file in a `defer`. `stageAttachment` returns false on an aggregate-budget failure before appending the recording, and that result is ignored. The caller then invokes `completeStaging`, returning the recorder to idle whether or not the recording was admitted.

Recording admission does not check the remaining budget. The existing upstream `all staging paths count existing attachment bytes` test explicitly expects this rejected voice file to be deleted; it verifies size enforcement and cleanup, but does not provide a recovery path for the unique capture.

### OpenClaw version
Source commit `57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160`.

### Operating system
Affected path: native iOS/shared Swift chat. Device-specific runtime reproduction: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method
Isolated source inspection; no App Store or development app launched for this case.

### Model
Not applicable; failure precedes sending or inference.

### Provider / routing chain
Voice recorder → native composer staging → attachment budget. No live provider was used.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- [Voice staging and unconditional file deletion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatViewModel%2BAttachments.swift#L148).
- [Caller completes recorder state regardless of admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatComposer.swift#L1434).
- [Existing test expects deletion after aggregate rejection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatFileAdmissionTests.swift#L124).

The positive control is an otherwise identical recording without the preceding attachment: admission transfers bytes to an attachment before temporary cleanup. This control and the failing path are established by source inspection here, not claimed as executed tests.

### Impact and severity
Suggested P2: a newly recorded, unsent note can be lost in a nearly full draft. Re-recording is available, but cannot recover the original captured audio. The defect does not require process death or a network failure and does not corrupt sent messages or Gateway history. Real-device incidence: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information
[#159667](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159667) introduced aggregate admission and protects already-staged drafts rejected at send time. This report concerns an earlier rejection before the voice note joins that draft. [#101236](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101236) protects offline/outbox delivery after staging; [#191195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191195) concerns process-death persistence.

A focused repair should retain a refused recording under the existing recorder/composer owner, allow retry of the same bytes after freeing space, and preserve cleanup on successful handoff or explicit discard. Keep aggregate limits, session ownership, and duplicate-staging controls intact.

### Acceptance criteria

- Establish a failing regression for aggregate rejection before changing cleanup expectations: the finished recording must remain owned and recoverable when no attachment has accepted its bytes.
- Remove another attachment and retry the original recording through the product flow. Verify identical audio bytes, exactly one staged attachment, and the original conversation owner; no re-recording should be required.
- Verify temporary-file cleanup after successful transfer or explicit discard, while rejection preserves the pending recording. Retain aggregate and individual size limits and duplicate-staging protection.
- Validate the physical recording sequence described above in an isolated iOS conversation. A pre-recording remaining-budget check alone cannot replace safe handoff, because the final encoded size is not yet known.

These criteria incorporate the [source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193813#issuecomment-6673082640); they do not claim that recording or retry has already been executed.

# [Bug]: iOS Rewind overwrites text and attachments added while the request is pending

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Native iOS chat keeps the composer editable while Rewind is pending, but its successful completion unconditionally replaces text and attachments added during that wait; the current source establishes this same-session overwrite.

### Steps to reproduce

Source-verified sequence, not an executed device or simulator reproduction:

1. Open an idle native iOS conversation with an earlier user message and no queued sends.
2. Choose **Rewind to Here** on that message. Keep the same conversation selected and hold the successful `sessions.rewind` response in an isolated test transport.
3. While it waits, type `Keep this newer note`. Optionally select a small attachment.
4. Complete the response with `editorText: "Earlier prompt"` and `editorAttachments: []`.
5. The completion path assigns the earlier prompt over the newer text and replaces the attachment list with an empty array.

The ordinary trigger is editing during a slower request. Holding the response makes that ordering deterministic; it does not require a rapid sequence of taps or an active model run.

### Expected behavior

Complete the requested history rewind while preserving newer composer edits. If the composer has not changed since Rewind started, restore the earlier prompt and images as it does today.

The Control UI already preserves newer drafts through this operation after [#140066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140066). Native same-session edit preservation is the missing counterpart; switching to another session is already guarded.

### Actual behavior

In `rewindToMessage`, the post-request check verifies only that the initiating session is still current. It then clears `replyTarget`, sets `input = result.editorText ?? ""`, and calls `restoreEditorAttachments`, which replaces the full array. No composer revision is captured or compared.

The iOS composer remains enabled based on connectivity/offline queue availability. The outbox branch guard protects delivery ordering, not edits to that composer.

### OpenClaw version

Source inspected at `57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160`; no installed App Store build is claimed.

### Operating system

Affected source: native iOS shared Swift chat path. Device/OS-specific runtime reproduction: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method

Source inspection in an isolated checkout; app not launched for this report.

### Model

Not applicable: the overwrite occurs during session rewind and composer restoration, without inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Native chat → `sessions.rewind` → native composer restoration. No live provider was exercised.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- [Native Rewind owner and unconditional restoration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatViewModel%2BSessionActions.swift#L571).
- [Complete attachment-array replacement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatViewModel%2BAttachments.swift#L97).
- [iOS editor remains enabled while connected](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift#L157).
- [Existing native completion gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelSessionActionTests.swift#L1024) can hold the actual rewind request, edit the real view model, release the response, and assert preservation. Retain the existing unchanged-draft restoration and different-session controls.

No screenshot or runtime execution is presented as evidence here.

### Impact and severity

Suggested P2: users who edit an enabled native composer during Rewind can lose newer unsent text or attachment selection. This affects mobile conversation continuity; canonical history corruption and loss of accepted messages are not established. Reattaching an original file or retyping is possible. Device incidence and system undo recovery: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information

[#140066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140066) repaired the web composer only; its changed files do not include Swift. Merged [#161799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161799) guards native action results after switching to another session. This case keeps the same session selected and changes its draft during the request.

The draft that existed **before** choosing Rewind is intentionally replaced by the earlier prompt; this report concerns only edits made **after** the request began. A focused repair should preserve that existing unchanged-draft behavior and stay with the native composer owner.

### Acceptance criteria

- Establish failing regressions through the existing controlled-completion gate for text-only, attachment-only, and combined edits while Rewind is pending; all must preserve the newer draft after the repair.
- Keep successful history rewind and branch reconciliation running even when composer restoration is skipped.
- Preserve both existing controls: an unchanged draft restores the earlier prompt/images, and a response for a different session does not change the current composer.
- Reuse the native owner's revision tracking where appropriate, but cover attachment edits explicitly: the existing input observer advances the text revision only. A text-only guard is incomplete. No Gateway semantics or web draft-ledger migration is needed.

These criteria incorporate the [source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193817#issuecomment-6673198642); they are requirements for a future repair, not tests already executed for this report.

# [Bug]: Android accepts video attachments that exceed its WebSocket limit and remain queued

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Android accepts videos up to 20 MiB, but sends their Base64 content in one OkHttp WebSocket message with a 16 MiB outgoing-queue limit. A 13 MiB video already exceeds that limit. The failed enqueue closes the connection and returns the durable message to Queued, where reconnecting retries the same oversized payload and later sends in that session/branch wait behind it.

### Steps to reproduce
Source-verified scenario; no Android app or socket was executed for this report:

1. Connect the Android app to a test Gateway. Use a conversation with an empty outbox.
2. Select a valid 13 MiB MP4. It fits the native composer's 20 MiB video limit.
3. Send it, then reconnect after the connection closes.
4. Send a short text later in the same session and branch.
5. As recovery, delete the queued video and select a smaller clip.

### Expected behavior
An attachment admitted for sending must fit the supported transport, or the composer should explain the actual limit before clearing the draft. A permanent size mismatch must not be presented as a transient connection problem that reconnecting will fix.

### Actual behavior
The pinned OkHttp implementation rejects a frame larger than its queue capacity even when that queue is empty: it enqueues close 1001 and returns false. `GatewaySession` maps false to `GatewayRequestNotEnqueued`; the chat owner records Queued, marks health false, and stops draining. Replay retains the same bytes, so reconnection does not fix the size condition. The bubble says “Queued — sends when reconnected”.

### OpenClaw version
Source `57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160`, declared OkHttp 5.5.1.

### Operating system
Affected source: native Android. Device/OS runtime reproduction: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method
Isolated source inspection including the pinned dependency. No installed app tested.

### Model
Not applicable; the enqueue fails before the request reaches a model.

### Provider / routing chain
Android composer → durable outbox → `chat.send` JSON → OkHttp WebSocket. No live Gateway/provider exercised.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- [Video admission limit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatCommandOutbox.kt#L54) and [composer admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatComposer.kt#L388).
- [Inline Base64 serialization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt#L3612).
- [False enqueue mapped to retryable exception](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/gateway/GatewaySession.kt#L1475).
- [Pinned OkHttp admission check](https://github.com/square/okhttp/blob/parent-5.5.1/okhttp/src/commonJvmAndroid/kotlin/okhttp3/internal/ws/RealWebSocket.kt#L446), with the 16 MiB constant at line684.
- [Exception returns the command to Queued](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57ab01eab302cb7acc27ae8d57e4fb3ac22c5160/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt#L6086).

Independent Base64 encoding confirms that 13,631,488 input bytes become **18,175,320 ASCII bytes**, exceeding **16,777,216** before adding JSON. The check precedes transport compression; a faster connection cannot make this frame admissible. This arithmetic is not a runtime test of the app. An 8 MiB control produces 11,184,812 Base64 bytes and fits this particular bound, without proving delivery.

### Impact and severity
P1 is a candidate because a supported media send can repeatedly break the connection and block later sends in the same session/branch. P2 is also plausible given the large-video scope and visible Delete recovery. The outbox retains the message; there is no demonstrated loss of Gateway history. Other sessions are not claimed to be permanently blocked. Queued commands also expire to Failed after 48 hours when reconciled. Field incidence: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information
The relevant limit is the Android client's transport, not just the Gateway's larger payload budget. Related [#116188](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/116188) advertises Gateway limits; [#160071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160071) addresses Control UI/Gateway aggregate admission. Neither establishes that native Android's 20 MiB admission fits OkHttp.

A focused repair should align admission with the complete serialized request and supported transport, preserve queued data, and distinguish oversize from transient connection failure. Validate a real 13 MiB MP4 frame, smaller control, reconnect, subsequent same-session text, and Delete recovery without invoking a model. Keep FIFO ordering intact.

### Acceptance criteria

- Establish a failing regression with production serialization and the pinned OkHttp transport for a valid 13 MiB video; verify admission rejects the complete oversized request before clearing the draft.
- Cover an oversized item already persisted in the outbox, not only new admission. Preserve its data as an actionable permanent failure and allow later same-session sends to proceed through the existing failed-row handling.
- Verify the smaller 8 MiB control, reconnect, subsequent text, and Delete recovery in an isolated Android/Gateway flow. Distinguish permanent oversize from transient backpressure or disconnection; preserve FIFO for valid queued messages.

These criteria incorporate the [source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193810#issuecomment-6672952578); runtime regression and Android flow validation remain work for the repair.

### Summary

`cron.list` already filters by `sessionKey` on the Gateway, but the agent cron tool's `list` and `openclaw cron list` can't pass it. So "which automations run in this conversation" is only answerable over raw RPC.

### Problem to solve

The Gateway decides which jobs belong to a session (a `session:<key>` target, the job's `sessionKey`, its source conversation), and `cron.list` with `sessionKey` returns exactly those ([cron-list.ts#L80-L93](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38776e59e870c4a878f5342e218a10080052ed34/src/gateway/server-methods/cron-list.ts#L80-L93)).

Neither caller exposes it:
- the cron tool's `list` sends `includeDisabled`, `compact`, `agentId`, `limit`, `offset` only ([cron-tool.ts#L328-L349](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38776e59e870c4a878f5342e218a10080052ed34/src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts#L328-L349));
- `openclaw cron list` has `--all`, `--agent`, `--query` ([register.cron-add.ts#L60-L65](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38776e59e870c4a878f5342e218a10080052ed34/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts#L60-L65)), and its page filters are typed `Pick<CronListPageOptions, "includeDisabled" | "agentId" | "query">` ([list-jobs.ts#L38](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38776e59e870c4a878f5342e218a10080052ed34/src/cli/cron-cli/list-jobs.ts#L38)).

A client can't redo the binding itself: the public job drops the source conversation, and the compact row has no `sessionTarget` or `sessionKey` ([cron-list-projection.ts#L69-L106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/38776e59e870c4a878f5342e218a10080052ed34/src/gateway/server-methods/cron-list-projection.ts#L69-L106)). An agent asked "what's scheduled for this chat?" can only list everything and guess.

Same on v2026.11.1 and main (38776e59e8).

### Proposed solution

1. Cron tool `list`: optional `sessionKey` passed through to `cron.list` (maybe `"current"` for the calling session). Older Gateways reject it with `unexpected property 'sessionKey'`; the tool could fall back the way it already does for `compact` (`isOlderGatewayRejectingParam`).
2. CLI: `openclaw cron list --session <key>`.
3. Optional: `sessionTarget` in the compact row.

### Alternatives considered

Calling `cron.list` directly over the Gateway protocol. That works (it's what our Open WebUI integration's status panel does now), but agents and CLI users don't have that path.

### Impact

Affected: agents and chat UIs that show or check "automations for this conversation" (e.g. an agent checking its own wake-ups before adding another).
Severity: low, workaround exists only for RPC clients.
Frequency: every time an agent is asked what's scheduled in the current chat.
Consequence: agents list everything they can see and guess, or answer wrong.

### Evidence/examples

Repro on main / v2026.11.1:
1. In a chat session `S`, add an automation with `sessionTarget: "session:S"` and one with `sessionTarget: "isolated"`.
2. Raw RPC `cron.list {"sessionKey": "S"}` returns only the first.
3. The cron tool's `list` and `openclaw cron list` have no way to ask for that; their rows don't say which job is bound to `S`.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

# OpenClaw update failure report

<!-- openclaw-update-report:local-manual-2026-11-05 -->

- OpenClaw version: 2026.9.8
- Platform: linux/x64 (Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, single-user VPS)
- Node version: 24.22.2
- Update action: owner-triggered `/update` (managed handoff, `openclaw update --yes --channel stable`)
- Installation method: npm-global (user-owned `~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`, gateway as systemd **user** service, umask 0002)
- Update target: 2026.11.1 (also failed: 2026.10.10)
- Failed phase: package-swap
- Failure stderr: `Package publication recovery permissions are unsafe`
- Recovery outcome: verified serving 2026.9.8; recorded verification: service running; version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready
- Current health: Gateway answered on the recorded port (2026.9.8). This observation supersedes saved claims that the Gateway is stopped; other recovery constraints still apply.

## Phases (latest run, 2026-11-05)

```
requested (95.58s) → staging (104ms) → validating (618.64s, npm succeeds)
→ FAILED: package-swap — Exit code 1
   Package publication recovery permissions are unsafe
```

`candidate-doctor-lint` exits 0 immediately before the swap every time (0 errors, 13 advisory deferred warnings). Admission checks: config ok, database-schema ok, node-runtime ok, plugin-availability ok.

## Attempt history (identical signature; recovery always rolled back clean)

- 2026-11-03: 2026.9.8 → 2026.10.10, several managed campaigns
- 2026-11-04: 14:32, 15:09 (×2), and 16:4x runs — all `package-swap` / same message
- 2026-11-05: 10:52 run, then owner `/update` at 16:07 → died 16:19:21 EST
- Total: ≥9 attempts across two different candidate builds, one driver (2026.9.8)

## Full remediation performed BEFORE the final attempts (none changed the outcome)

All validated against the gate rules read from `package-update-activation-*.mjs` (`privatePackageActivationIdentity`: owner-uid, `mode & 0o77 === 0`, `nlink == 1`, no legacy layout):

1. Orphan activation journal from an Oct 3 crash moved out of `node_modules` (kept as backup)
2. Rejected config keys removed repeatedly (`meta.lastTouchedAt`, `skills.workshop.approvalPolicy`) — verified 0 occurrences before the last two attempts
3. Entire npm-global chain (`~/.npm-global` → `lib` → `node_modules` → `openclaw` → `bin`) tightened from 775 (npm's default group-writable scaffold) to **700**
4. Entire agent state tree tightened (5,489 group/world-readable objects → only symlinks remain, which the gate does not mode-check)
5. All journaled sqlite files verified 600 / links=1 / correct uid; control dir 700 / links=2
6. No live updater, no lock contention, 775 GiB free, same-filesystem confirmed
7. **`openclaw update repair --yes` run from an independent shell → exit 0** (reconciled stranded campaign, converged service definition, restarted + verified gateway). Owner re-fired `/update` after that; died at the same line within 24 min.

## Diagnosis request

Every object the gate can name is provably compliant between attempts, yet the swap still throws. This implies the rejected object is **transient — created by the swap's own preparation step** (staged anchor/control/helper, or a snapshot copy of a sqlite DB whose `nlink` becomes >1 during hardlink snapshotting), and is therefore unreachable by any pre-flight remediation an operator can perform. If so, from-2026.9.8 first-hop upgrades are deterministically doomed on this layout regardless of host hygiene — and there is no operator-visible error naming the object.

Related reports with identical signature (found via search): #167861 (closed), #167283 (hard-link race, closed), #170032 (closed), #171636 / #170076 (open package-swap trackers, other platforms). This report adds: Linux/npm-global/systemd-user corroboration, post-repair re-fire evidence, and the transient-object analysis.

Questions:
1. Can the gate log **which path** failed the permission check?
2. Is the hardlink-snapshot nlink>1 case (per #167283) the same failure on current builds?
3. Supported escape route for a user-owned install locked at 2026.9.8? (`npm install -g openclaw@stable` as the same user — safe, or does it corrupt managed state?)

Sanitized triage bundles for the 16:19:21 failure are on the host (`~/.openclaw/logs/support/openclaw-diagnostics-2026-11-05T21-25-39-452Z-*.zip`); happy to attach on request.

### Summary
On Windows, Gmail integration dependencies resolved through `resolveExecutable` can launch a lower-priority installation despite an earlier PATH match. A `.cmd` wrapper anywhere on PATH outranks an `.exe` in an earlier directory.

### Environment
Fresh main ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d; native Windows11 x64; Node24.22.1.

### Real reproduction
Create separate `first` and `later` temporary directories. Copy the current Node executable to `first/gcloud.exe` (real native executable) and create `later/gcloud.cmd` printing `stale-lower-priority-install`. Set process-only PATH to `first;later`, PATHEXT `.EXE;.CMD;.BAT;.COM`.

Call actual `runCommandWithTimeout(["gcloud", "--version"], { timeoutMs: 10000 })`: returns `v24.22.1`, correctly selecting the earlier installation. Call the same production runner with `[resolveExecutable("gcloud"), "--version"]`, as `src/hooks/gmail-setup-utils.ts` does: returns `stale-lower-priority-install`. Baseline resolver points at `later/gcloud.cmd`. No cloud API, login, live account, or real installation is used.

### Expected
Honor PATH directory precedence; preserve the existing CMD/EXE wrapper preference within a single installation directory.

### Actual
`resolveExecutable` collects matches from every PATH directory and applies global CMD preference, allowing a stale lower-priority installation to override the chosen one. Production callers also include gog and tailscale.

### Fix and proof
Apply the existing suffix preference only within the first PATH directory containing a supported match. Native replay returns `v24.22.1` in both direct and resolved flows. A filesystem-backed focused regression fails before repair (1failed26passed10existing skips) and passes after (27passed10existing skips); retained tests protect within-directory preference and PATHEXT behavior.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The native iOS Sessions page treats a partially loaded session list as a complete result when a later page fails. Conversations from the missing page disappear from the list without an incomplete-result warning or a retry action, even though the shared loader explicitly reports `isComplete: false`.

### Steps to reproduce

This is a source-reproducible report, not an executed device reproduction. The following controlled scenario follows the current production call path:

1. Connect the iOS app to an agent with 201 visible, active secondary sessions. Open **All Sessions**.
2. Let the first `sessions.list` page return 200 entries, `totalCount: 201`, `hasMore: true`, and `nextOffset: 200`.
3. Make the request at offset 200 time out while the same Gateway route remains current.
4. Inspect the result consumed by `CommandSessionsScreen.refreshSessions`: the loader returns the first 200 entries with `isComplete: false`, but the screen stores only `roster.sessions` and leaves `loadErrorText` unset.

### Expected behavior

Keep the sessions already loaded, indicate that more sessions could not be loaded, and offer a refresh/retry path. The native sidebar already handles this exact loader result by displaying “Showing N sessions; M total. Refresh to load the rest.”

### Actual behavior

In the current source, the later-page error is converted into a partial snapshot rather than thrown. The Sessions consumer drops the completeness metadata, so its error branch does not run. Its header counts only the returned entries and the list has no incomplete-result indication or retry control.

This makes an unavailable page look like absent conversations. It does not delete sessions or overwrite the complete offline cache.

### OpenClaw version

Source reviewed on main `2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab` (2026.11.1 source tree). The two affected files are identical to the locally inspected `ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d` versions.

### Operating system

iOS native app source; no device/OS runtime reproduction claimed.

### Install method

Source inspection of the official repository.

### Model

Not applicable; listing sessions does not invoke a model.

### Provider / routing chain

iOS Sessions → `loadChatSessionRoster` → Gateway `sessions.list`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The source establishes the complete failure path:

- [The collector preserves earlier pages and returns `isComplete: false` after a later-page error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/ios/Sources/RootSidebarModel.swift#L29-L54).
- [Sessions clears the error, awaits that snapshot, and assigns only its entries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift#L1210-L1238).
- [The existing sidebar consumer preserves completeness and displays the partial-load warning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/ios/Sources/RootSidebarModel.swift#L573-L588).
- [Only complete loads replace the offline session cache](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/ios/Sources/RootSidebarModel.swift#L142-L147).

No runtime logs or screenshots are attached because this report is based on source inspection.

### Impact and severity

Affected: iOS users whose session list spans multiple pages and encounters a later-page failure. The list conceals an incomplete read, making older conversations harder to find and giving no explanation for their absence. Closing/reopening Sessions or switching status and returning can trigger another load; the stored conversations remain intact. Runtime frequency is not measured.

This appears to be a bounded navigation/recovery bug, rather than data loss.

### Additional information

The loader's partial-result behavior is useful and already supported by the sidebar. A focused repair can preserve that behavior while making Sessions consume its completeness metadata.

Useful regression cases: a later-page failure retains loaded rows and exposes partial/retry state; retry restores access to the remaining row; complete loading does not show a warning. A collector-only test would not cover the missing presentation in this consumer.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Native chat's Markdown preprocessing removes timestamp prefixes and entire `[message_id: …]` lines from inside fenced code blocks. The code block renderer and its **Copy code** action receive the altered text, so a literal log example can lose information when read or copied.

### Steps to reproduce

Use this Markdown as the message body:

````markdown
```text
[Fri 2026-11-06 12:34 UTC] job started
[message_id: example-42]
[Fri 2026-11-06 12:35 UTC] job finished
```
````

I reproduced the transformation by compiling the unmodified production `ChatMarkdownPreprocessor.swift` and `ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenter.swift`, then calling:

```swift
let cleaned = ChatMarkdownPreprocessor.preprocess(markdown: input).cleaned
let blocks = ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenter.segments(markdown: cleaned, isComplete: true)
```

The native message renderer calls these owners in that order. This is a focused native-code reproduction on macOS, not a device UI or clipboard test.

### Expected behavior

The fenced block retains the literal timestamp prefixes and message-ID line. Passing the same input directly to the production Markdown segmenter preserves all three lines, providing a control for the expected parsing behavior.

### Actual behavior

The resulting code block contains only:

```text
job started
job finished
```

Both timestamps and the entire ID line are absent. This happens before rendering: the preprocessor applies metadata-removal expressions to the complete Markdown string without checking whether the matching lines are inside a code block.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1 source tree, executed at `ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d`. The affected preprocessor, renderer, and code-copy consumer are unchanged on main `2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1, Apple Swift 6.4.2, Swift Markdown 0.9.0. The affected chat code is shared by the native iOS and macOS apps; iOS UI execution was not performed.

### Install method

Official source checkout; focused Swift executable using the original production files and the pinned Markdown dependency. The harness supplies only the platform image alias needed to link those files.

### Model

Not applicable; the input is synthetic Markdown and no model is invoked.

### Provider / routing chain

Native message Markdown → preprocessing → block segmentation → code block display/copy.

### Logs

```text
Direct segmenter control: timestamps and message-ID line retained
Preprocessor → segmenter: "job started\njob finished"
Ordinary fenced code without these markers: unchanged
Timestamp envelope outside code: still removed as intended
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- [The renderer preprocesses before segmenting Markdown](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownRenderer.swift#L195-L211).
- [The preprocessor invokes metadata removal on the whole input](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownPreprocessor.swift#L133-L143), including [line removal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownPreprocessor.swift#L234-L248) and [multiline timestamp substitution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownPreprocessor.swift#L280-L283).
- [Copy code receives `block.code`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2049dfc8e2d5bdb7228a160ee1c516b08ccde0ab/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift#L23-L40). Its connection to the reproduced transformation was verified in source; I did not exercise the system clipboard.

### Impact and severity

Users sharing or copying literal log examples can lose the timestamps needed to correlate events, as well as whole identifier lines. The transformation is deterministic for the input above; real-world frequency is not measured. This changes rendered/copied code, not the stored conversation or original log file. The scope is the matching metadata-like syntax inside code, rather than arbitrary code blocks.

### Additional information

[#113904](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113904) previously preserved image syntax inside literal Markdown contexts. It deliberately retained the metadata sanitizer, so it does not cover this remaining case; this report does not attribute the defect to that change.

A focused fix should preserve literal code content while keeping intentional envelope/metadata cleanup outside code. The existing preprocessor tests can cover the fenced input above alongside the current outside-code cleanup cases.

prs.title: improve(control-ui): reload faster by applying the accent palette once
prs.body:
Closes #193850
Related: #193338, #193954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Control UI reload spends extra main-thread time applying the same accent colors three times.

## User Impact

User impact: Control UI reloads use less main-thread time, and the first route is ready sooner. In the cold-load benchmark (20 interleaved pairs with a base vs base control), style CPU drops by a paired median of 46 ms, task CPU by 51 ms and first route ready by 27 ms. Colors, theme switching, custom palettes, seam colors and environment stripes behave as before. The CI performance check passes on current main (details under Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

A reload ran the accent projection from the config seam pass, the theme pass and the environment presentation pass, all with the same inputs. Each run removes the accent properties, forces a style recalc to read the theme palette, and writes them back.

#193954 skips the repeated operator seam publication, which removes one of these three passes. The two changes compose: merging #193954 into this branch has no conflicts, and the accent tests pass together. This change also skips the theme pass that repeats the seam pass inputs, so after #193954 lands a reload goes from 2 projections to 1 instead of 3 to 1, and the style gain measured below is roughly halved.

- `applyControlUiAccent` returns early when nothing that feeds the projection has changed and the `--ring` it last wrote is still on the root. The key is every input that can change the result: the resolved accent or seam color, `data-theme`, `data-theme-mode`, the palette stylesheet revision, and the text of the custom theme style tag. A palette sheet finishing its load, a custom palette edit, a theme or mode switch, or anything that resets the root style rebuilds the projection. Only projections that wrote an accent are remembered: a pass that finds no hex accent (for example before any palette applies) leaves nothing to match, so the next pass always projects.
- Palette readiness comes from its owner, `theme.ts`. `themePaletteRevision()` changes whenever `syncThemePaletteStylesheet` sees a palette link loaded or failed, including a link the boot script created that had already loaded. The projection does not query the DOM for stylesheets.
- The callers are unchanged. The environment presentation pass still runs as before; its accent call now returns early when nothing changed.

Why a last-input check instead of removing a caller: each of the three callers is the owner of one input (operator config, user preferences, environment presentation) and must re-project when its own input changes. The projection owns the combined inputs, so the check sits there as a single slot that the next real change replaces.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: a win only if the gain is beyond base vs base noise, meaning the paired median gain is larger than the control's paired median and head is lower in most pairs.

Workload: `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts`, chat route, production bundles of base `04d93fb8469c` and this change served through the Gateway HTTP handler, built-in synthetic fixture, untraced. One invocation of 60 runs in 20 cycles of base, base copy, head: 20 samples per arm, and the base vs base control comes from the same cycles. Mac Studio (M3 Ultra), Chrome 156. The run started once the one-minute load average fell below 14; it was 6.5 to 13.8 during the run. The commit is rebased onto `abe11702825e` with the same patch.

```
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --gateway-http --bundle-dir /absolute/base/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir /absolute/base-copy/control-ui --compare-bundle-dir /absolute/head/control-ui \
  --runs 60 --untraced --thread-cpu-time
```

| Metric (ms) | Base median / p95 | Head median / p95 | Paired median delta | Head lower | Base vs base delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer style CPU | 142.2 / 151.2 | 95.2 / 100.9 | -46.2 | 20/20 | +0.1 |
| Renderer task CPU | 777.3 / 844.7 | 715.7 / 760.3 | -51.2 | 19/20 | +0.9 |
| Renderer script CPU | 361.7 / 398.3 | 358.0 / 402.3 | +0.9 | 10/20 | +5.4 |
| Renderer layout CPU | 14.8 / 15.9 | 13.9 / 15.4 | -0.9 | 15/20 | -0.1 |
| First shell interactive | 188.3 / 217.0 | 181.1 / 201.6 | -7.4 | 16/20 | +3.4 |
| First route ready | 409.0 / 466.3 | 378.2 / 440.6 | -27.2 | 17/20 | -4.6 |

p95 is nearest-rank (the second slowest of 20). Script CPU does not move beyond the control (+0.9 ms vs +5.4 ms); the other five metrics do. Head p95 is lower than base p95 on every metric except script CPU (402.3 vs 398.3 ms). Accent projections per reload with the default theme go from 3 to 1; with a built-in palette theme the projection runs again each time the theme owner settles the palette sheet. Long tasks per reload: base median 1 (1 to 2), head 1 in every run. Per-run values with the load average are in the attached CSV.

Separate CPU-profiled runs of an earlier form of this change (3 per arm, attribution only): `applyControlUiAccent` 105.1 to 14.2 ms inclusive per reload and `resolveThemeColor` 93.1 to 11.8 ms.

`pnpm ui:check-performance:base abe11702825e31e250244fd2ea1f0abd22dc0c24` (the command CI runs, with this commit applied to that main tip) passes, exit 0:

| Budget (gzip) | Base | Head | Change | Fixed limit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 90215 B | 90240 B | +25 B | 90856 B |
| Largest JS chunk | | 547.1 KiB | | 547.2 KiB |
| Chat boot JS | 1288491 B | 1288287 B | -204 B | 1288198 B |
| New Session boot JS | 797107 B | 796973 B | -134 B | 797620 B |
| CSS (startup, chat, new, total) | unchanged | unchanged | +0 B | |

That main tip is already 293 B over the fixed chat boot cap; this change lowers it by 204 B. On `04d93fb8469c`, where main is under the cap, the same check gives chat boot -98 B, New Session -134 B, startup +25 B, and the largest chunk stays under its 547.2 KiB cap. Request counts are unchanged. The budget is not changed here.

Tests:

Shard 1: 762 files pass. prs.title: fix(secrets): accept limit-sized stdin values with trailing newline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw secrets store set --value-file -` rejects a valid 65,536-byte value when a pipe adds a trailing LF or CRLF.

## User Impact

Users can pipe a value at the documented limit with the usual line ending. Values above the limit still exit 2 without changing the stored value. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stdin reader counted the optional line ending before removing it. Allow two framing bytes during the bounded read and retain the existing canonical validation of the normalized value. File and dotenv import limits are unchanged.

Related boundary-fix precedent: #188681 (external contributor anmol0b, merged by RomneyDa on November 5). This is a separately reproduced bug in the secrets CLI, not a follow-up change to that PR.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 24.22.2, isolated fresh state, synthetic env-kind value `"é".repeat(32768)` (65,536 UTF-8 bytes). Ran the real `pnpm openclaw secrets store set/get` commands through the normal built CLI, with persistence and SHA-256 readback checks.

| Actual CLI input | Base | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact-limit file | exit 0, exact readback | exit 0, exact readback |
| Exact-limit raw stdin | exit 0, exact readback | exit 0, exact readback |
| Exact-limit stdin + LF | exit 2, old value unchanged | exit 0, exact 65,536-byte readback |
| Exact-limit stdin + CRLF | exit 2, old value unchanged | exit 0, exact 65,536-byte readback |
| 65,537-byte normalized value, raw/LF/CRLF | exit 2, old value unchanged | exit 2, old value unchanged |

Minimal reproduction (use an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`):

```sh
node -e 'process.stdout.write("é".repeat(32768) + "\n")' | pnpm openclaw secrets store set FRAMING_VALUE --kind env --value-file -
pnpm openclaw secrets store get FRAMING_VALUE --json
```

Base stderr for the rejected LF/CRLF inputs: `Stdin input exceeds 65536 bytes.` The proof makes 17 real CLI calls, verifies stored bytes rather than just exit status, and checks rejected writes preserve the prior value. No live credentials or external service is involved.

Regression: `pnpm test src/cli/secrets-store-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — base 2 failed / 18 passed (the LF/CRLF cases), fixed 20 passed. The tests drive the CLI parser and real stdin reader/validator; their store is mocked, while the separate CLI proof above uses real persistence.

Focused typecheck passed. Typed lint passed with the repository-supported pinned Bun backend (`No problems in 2 files`, 9.49s); native oxlint crashed internally in `oxc_allocator` on this host, so no native-oxlint pass is claimed. oxfmt/Bun formatter parity and test-line ratchet passed. Final committed-head `pnpm build cliStartup` passed. All 17 real CLI calls completed and the proof reported `failures: []`. Exact-value SHA-256 before/after: `80ad92d4f363d1af78eed07669eecdbb4410e28d38875188de8feeb30b98d6d9`.

Author simplification: reuses the existing value validator; production +2/-1 lines, tests +16 with an exact allocation. No new helper, API, dependency, or configuration. Independent host-agent review of the complete three-file committed diff at `a8b764ae3cb1f3b30c567e45e30bba2e6d10bbc5`, base `4aea2c089cb710fc619d92bf0de28749236c87b2`: no actionable findings. This was an independent agent review, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper run.

prs.title: fix: recognize the MCP-exposed scheduler tool name in the reminder guard
prs.body:
Closes #193958

## What Problem This Solves

A one-shot reminder scheduled in the same turn through the MCP tool (`mcp__openclaw__automations`, action `add`) is created and enabled, but OpenClaw still appends "Note: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically." The reminder fires on time, so the note is false and makes the user think the reminder is missing.

## User Impact

Any agent on the claude-cli / MCP tool path that schedules a reminder in the reply turn delivers a contradictory message: a confirmation plus a note saying nothing was scheduled. Reported as a regression on 2026.10.3.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reminder guard suppresses the note when a cron add succeeded this turn (`successfulCronAdds`). That counter is incremented only when `isAutomationsToolName(toolName)` is true, and `isAutomationsToolName` matched only the bare `automations` name and the `cron` alias, not the `mcp__<server>__automations` form the MCP runtime exposes. So an add over MCP was never counted, and the guard fired.

`isAutomationsToolName` now strips a leading `mcp__<server>__` prefix before matching, so the MCP tool name and its `cron` alias both count. This is scoped to the tool-name match; the issue's optional `job.owner?.sessionKey` fallback for prior-turn coverage is left out to keep the change focused.

## Evidence

Added `src/agents/tools/automations-tool-name.test.ts`: the canonical name and `cron` alias match; `mcp__openclaw__automations` and `mcp__openclaw__cron` match; `read` and `mcp__openclaw__memory_search` do not. The MCP-name cases fail on the base revision, which is the reported path.

I was not able to run the suite in my environment, so CI is the first run.

prs.title: fix(windows): resolve the system-encoding probe through the install root
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, the system text-encoding probe spawns a bare executable name rather than a resolved path. Whenever `PATH` does not contain the Windows PowerShell directory — a service host, an AppContainer launch, a sandbox that trims the environment — the spawn fails, the failure is cached as `null`, and every legacy-encoded file is then decoded as UTF-8 with replacement characters. Nothing is logged, so the symptom is mojibake rather than an error.

The console probe in the same file already avoids this: it resolves through `getWindowsCmdExePath`. The system probe was the one place still relying on `PATH`.

## Root cause

```ts
cachedWindowsSystemEncoding = probeWindowsEncoding(
  () => "powershell.exe",
  ["-NoLogo", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", "[Text.Encoding]::Default.CodePage"],
);
```

`spawnSync` with a bare name goes through `PATH`; `probeWindowsEncoding` catches the resulting `ENOENT` and returns `null`. `resolveWindowsSystemEncoding` memoises that `null`, so a single failed probe poisons the process for its whole lifetime, and `createWindowsTextFileDecoder` falls through to `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { ignoreBOM: true })`.

## What this changes

```ts
cachedWindowsSystemEncoding = probeWindowsEncoding(
  getWindowsPowerShellExePath,
  [ ... ],
);
```

`getWindowsPowerShellExePath` is the sibling helper already used by the other native probes: it builds `<SystemRoot>\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` from the install root (honouring the environment's `SystemRoot`), so the probe no longer depends on the caller's `PATH`. `probeWindowsEncoding` already accepts a `() => string` resolver, so this is a one-argument change; no behaviour changes on the success path, where the same executable answered before.

## Evidence

New `src/infra/windows-encoding.system-probe.test.ts` mocks `spawnSync` to model a trimmed-`PATH` host: any non-absolute command throws `ENOENT`, an absolute one reports code page 1252. `platform` is pinned to `win32` and modules are reset per test so the encoding caches start empty. It then decodes a byte pair that is invalid UTF-8 through `createWindowsTextFileDecoder` and asserts both the selected encoding and the decoded text.

- before the change: `expected 'utf-8' to be 'windows-1252'` — the probe threw, `null` was cached, and the bytes came back as replacement characters.
- after the change: `decoder.encoding === "windows-1252"` and `0xE9 0x0A` decodes to `"é\n"`.

Full run in the isolated harness (Vitest 5.0.5 / Node 24 / Windows 11), new file plus the repo's existing `src/infra/windows-encoding.test.ts`:

```
✓ src/ocwin/src/infra/windows-encoding.system-probe.test.ts (1 test)
✓ src/ocwin/src/infra/windows-encoding.test.ts (17 tests)
Tests  18 passed (18)
```

So the new behaviour is additive: the existing decoder, BOM, prefix-window and OEM-page cases still pass unchanged.

`oxfmt --check` with the repo `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` (printWidth 100) reports no diff on both files.

Evidence boundary: the probe is exercised with a mocked `spawnSync`, not a real trimmed-`PATH` service host — I did not run OpenClaw as a Windows service here. What is proven is that the command handed to `spawnSync` is an absolute install-root path and that a host which cannot resolve bare names now still selects the right code page; the real host environment from the report is unverified in this run.

## Ratchets

`config/test-lines-allocations/windows-system-encoding-probe.txt`: 32 lines, equal to the new test file (LF count).

prs.title: fix(ios): keep local device settings available without Dashboard
prs.body:
Related: #139514

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iPhone and iPad users cannot change local appearance, voice, or permission/device controls when offline, connected with Limited access, or unable to open the embedded Dashboard through native Cloudflare Access authorization.

## User Impact

Device Settings is available at the top of the native fallback and through Device in the connected-admin Settings toolbar. Local access does not grant Gateway scopes or expose credentials. Gateway administration keeps its existing gates.

**Draft — qualification incomplete:** the recovered repairs are now published at `7fb156ad5b16a98ec40f6c28e28a18eba349f24a`. The seven repaired Swift source blobs match the runner's tested source; the extra TS consumer migration has independent red/green source-gate proof. This is not a fresh Mac run or hosted-CI pass. The model-screen UI failure, inherited Typography lint findings, and real permission/route/upgrade/visual/physical-voice qualification remain open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier Dashboard consolidation intentionally removed duplicate native settings. This restores only a small local-device projection, not native copies of Gateway work pages. Native controls and the authenticated WebKit adapter share IOSDeviceSettingsActions and the existing consent, permission, snapshot, and preference owners.

No configuration keys, schemas, durability policy, dependencies, or protocol versions change. The simplify pass removed the bridge-only forwarding wrapper and kept one setting-effect implementation. The subsequent fixture-array extraction satisfies the inherited function-length gate without changing message content or suppressing the gate.

## Evidence

### Published source and recovered-input identity

Current head `7fb156ad5b16a98ec40f6c28e28a18eba349f24a`, tree `98d5d0361e2e5b940bb41da3d01a687819162adf`, directly advances `a3e98bc461650d7f36eaa61fa41114a0857b287c`. The approved revision changes eight files (+1914/−1813), mostly moves; verified complete PR scope is 19 files (+2559/−1984). History, attribution, existing cleanup, localization, and native/WebKit guards are preserved. No dependency, configuration, schema, protocol, or permission-policy change.

The [complete tested attachment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191524#issuecomment-6608865390) has five documented base64 parts. Archive SHA-256 `128c19c99ce2aa99f2674ac19685303d78306f917570dfde1a6f850c74320830` and all 13 inventoried member hashes were verified. Both `repair.patch` (SHA-256 `33fe0dc71e6e729cfa8a8b8c2aa2f6712d978755f727774330dce581e687b0b9`) and the saved tested patch independently produce declared source tree `84ec7f2e6f3a928fd27c1586d9ca3722a0f825d1` on declared base `a3e98bc…`. That base matched the then-public source exactly, so no prior public fix was reversed or reapplied.

**All seven Swift repair blobs are byte-identical to that tested source tree.** The only additional change is `test/scripts/ios-release-fastlane-gates.test.ts`: its static consumer now reads main, Chat, and Helpers files for the same XCTestCase. It failed on the exact recovered source with missing `captureReleaseScreenshot`, then passed with this migration. Positive and negative oracles are unchanged. Supplemental generated Xcode inputs, standalone proof projects/launchers, private test keys, dependencies, and caches are not publication inputs.

The split retains one XCTestCase/app owner, all 60 entrypoints, and all 683 existing assertion-opening lines; one failure assertion was added for a missing notification-denial action. Notification dismissal is title-specific and runs only for `screenshotMode:true` before the unchanged readiness assertion; live/offline false-mode flows bypass it. Fixture-only model repairs derive selected provider from the existing catalog and use nil for inherited thinking overrides, with set/reset/clear regressions. Real Gateway model policy and permission currentness are unchanged.

### Available checks rerun on the exact published source tree

- Selected release-screenshot source consumer: **one passed**, 15 other cases deselected; no test skip/oracle change.
- Covered root-scripts typecheck, targeted TS lint, TS formatting, and test-line ratchet: **pass**.
- Native inventory: **4,575 entries, changed=false**; whitespace/index checks and exact remote/local tree equality pass.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1: **0/7 repaired Swift files require formatting**.
- Fresh independent **whole 19-file P0–P2 source review** of this exact tree: no actionable finding. This is not native execution.

**Partial pinned SwiftLint remains red:** 0.65.1 Linux static reports three inherited `OpenClawTypographyTests.swift` findings, reproduced from the a3 base blob: `force_try` at671, function-body length174 at215, and `optional_data_string_conversion` at659. The former four UI size failures no longer appear in the scoped eight-file run after the split, but this is not a blanket lint pass. SourceKit access is prohibited, so `custom_rules`, `literal_expression_end_indentation`, and `statement_position` are skipped. No suppression, expected-failure exception, budget raise, or gate waiver. The normal build's source-only lint list is not equivalent to expanded test-inclusive Mac/SourceKit lint.

### Runner-reported native evidence — source matched, not freshly replayed

The [latest simulator report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191524#issuecomment-6606243790) originally used a3 plus local repair patches, now recovered and committed as the seven matching Swift blobs. It reports **44 settings tests**, **13 render tests**, **six fixture tests**, and passing offline-settings/composer growth/menu UI flows. Follow-up `ChatModelMenuPresentationTests` and `LocalFixtureModelSelectionTests` report **12 passed, zero failed/skipped**, including two previously counted fixture regressions: **do not add all 12 to those counts or substitute this selection for the earlier 72**.

The [earlier clean-tracked-tree receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191524#issuecomment-6594867082), on `60ab831850f0bbece0229ddea32753ac227791fe`, reports the normal app/Share/Watch build and **72 logical tests in eight suites, zero failures, 54.349 seconds**, plus offline UI **one test, zero failures, 39.100 seconds**. Its xcresult count84 includes device/configuration/parameter cases, not 84 logical tests. Retain valid prior cases for unchanged behavior; no broad replay is demanded solely for equivalent formatting, movement, or generated-only changes. Mac dependencies were linked from a prepared installation, not a new frozen-install qualification.

The source correspondence is verified, but no new Mac/native execution is claimed for the complete current commit or TS derivative, and skipped/permission-blocked hosted checks are not passes. Generated build inputs were captured at attachment time; historical execution-byte identity is not independently established. The coordinator has not independently replayed the Mac runs or inspected raw media.

### Known failure and proof boundaries

`testChatActionsModelRowsScreenshot` remains a reported failure: expected `Default (Auto)`, actual `Off`. Presentation-owner inspection and its passing unit contract support showing the effective level without a default caption; the effective Auto-to-Off resolution is still **unverified**. This is not green full model-screen acceptance. No assertion, baseline, or skip was weakened to hide it.

The public attachment supplies source repairs and supplemental proof inputs. Raw runtime logs, xcresult bundles, and screenshots remain runner-local, not downloadable runtime evidence. The earlier three after-only captures are not matched baseline/after proof. Source hashes do not establish complete execution-input identity or hosted-CI success.

There is **no new real permission post-grant proof**. Earlier notification probes (22.970/27.368/27.128 seconds) failed before successful OS-alert acceptance and post-grant observation; a final serving preference of false proves neither a production defect nor correct effect rejection. The transient-scene/currentness completion concern remains source-supported but unconfirmed. Before initiation, cancellation must prevent OS requests/app effects; after initiation an OS grant cannot be undone, while retired work must reject later app-owned commits. Native consent/live-currentness and WebKit admin/document guards remain; local preferences do not gain an admin requirement.

Still open: actual notification acceptance with scene/currentness and serving/APNs results after reactivation; canceled/retired native and unauthorized/revoked Dashboard final-effect checks; differing Health/location callbacks; live Limited/Access/connected-admin and upgrade scenarios; baseline-red/fix-green evidence; matched uploaded editor screenshots; physical Voice/Talk; inherited lint disposition and applicable full Mac qualification. The weak typography token smoke test remains low-priority cleanup, not a confirmed product/security defect. Prior ClawSweeper assessments are not approval of this new head; unresolved authority/visual asks remain.

prs.title: perf(ui): retain unchanged meeting and plugin row content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing installed plugins recreated 1,000 unchanged status badges. Opening a meeting refreshed its list and reformatted all 100 unchanged dates and row times.

## User Impact

Meeting navigation and installed-plugin refresh do less rendering work while preserving the same content, status changes, pending/error states, and Gateway requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rows already had keys, but rendering depended on whole refreshed objects. A view-owned keyed projection retains unchanged meeting fields. A row-local state memo prevents an equal plugin state from recreating its badge. Neither change adds a shared cache, request policy, or invalidation lifecycle.

The engine harness gains opt-in `--mutation-audit` diagnostics over the document and open shadow roots: per-write value equality, retained moves versus identical-content replacement candidates, Intl/locale formatter calls, and viewport pixel differences. Candidate matches are not automatically called waste; equal snippets can belong to different visible entities. Diagnostics run separately from timing/profiling. The stale Skills pending-state label is corrected, and an explicit browser-local deferred-response marker makes plugin refresh application time measurable without driver/defer wait time.

## Evidence

Production bundles with synthetic Gateway data, headless Chromium and WebKit, same Mac. No live Gateway/provider latency claim. The acceptance rule was ≥5% target-flow improvement with 20 rotated base/head/base observations per engine, an unchanged control, A/A, no attributable regression beyond the timing band, unchanged appearance, and no raised size ceiling. All 360 observations passed.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): define accountless node enrollment
prs.body:
Related: #192352

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an accountless, owner-approved identity and bootstrap contract before they can reach a claw through the OpenClaw ID relay and tunnel.

## User Impact

This draft defines the protocol layer only; it does not yet enable node connectivity in the running product. Nodes get a separate W-only key class, never owner or member privileges. All changes revise the unshipped v1-draft in place.

**Stack dependency:** this targets `openclaw-id/pr-ui-people`. Gateway, Discovery and node-host consumers follow in the implementation stack. A minimal existing Gateway consumer repair refuses accountless member-redemption mail with `audience_mismatch` through the normal settlement/acknowledgment path; valid member handling is unchanged. Test fixtures initialize the new empty draft state and preserve their concrete human-sender types. Full node dispatch, persisted-state initialization and snapshot re-signing remain in the following stack, without adding legacy compatibility readers here.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Owner-signed `NodeInviteCap` plus a proof key registers directly at the Gateway. W-signed `NodeRedemption` proves the invite and becomes pending, admitting nothing.
- Owner/R-signed `add_node` and `remove_node`, denial and peer revocation use the existing membership authority. Nodes have listing seqs, limits, inactivity clocks and pairing-cleanup events; snapshots carry `node_peer_keys`.
- W-signed bearerless Discovery requests can only mail a node redemption before admission; verified admitted nodes can read the descriptor and snapshot. Relay admission includes the new snapshot list.
- Strict fragment-only join links contain only the invite and claw pin/routing fields. `--discovery-url` (or deployment configuration) supplies the separate Discovery origin; clients never infer it from the hostname/relay and never weaken pin verification.

The simplification pass reused owner verification, sequences, invite proof-key derivation, retention and signature transport. Shared invite expiry policy has one implementation, and key-class collision checks use direct predicates rather than allocating a combined key list. Necessary net growth is 597 production lines, 478 test lines, 225 fixture/vector lines and 195 documentation lines. This is the smallest complete protocol stage: wire schema, authority behavior, strict bootstrap decoder and independent vectors must agree before the separately owned consumers can integrate. No runtime transport, persistence or UI implementation is added here.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: independent physical worktree install passed; donor checkout unchanged.
- `pnpm test packages/openclaw-id-protocol --maxWorkers=1`: **164 tests / 24 files passed** (final run: 5.15s Vitest, 10.01s wrapper).
- Targeted strict tsgo of the protocol public barrel and affected protocol tests, plus canonical `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src`: passed, 66 files.
- Package-config boundary lint also passed (66 files) after successful declaration emission; the original Gateway consumer type error is resolved.
- Package format check, docs MDX check, changed-source line-cap ratchet and staged whitespace check: passed.
- Test-line allocation: 476 = original 436 + exactly 40 new mailbox regression lines. Two fixture initialization lines use existing slack; the shared scalar is unchanged. The allocation protects forgery/class-separation and bootstrap boundaries, not test-volume growth for its own sake.
- Existing claw-store and member-profile persistence tests: 8 tests / 2 files passed (89.99s Vitest including 67.5s one-time worker preparation; 96.21s wrapper).
- Mailbox reader: 6 tests passed; new regression failed before the guard and passed after it. Existing callback/acknowledgment tests remain green. Final run: 86.19s Vitest including 80.55s one-time worker preparation, 94.02s wrapper; regression itself 7ms. CI timing is not yet available.
- Deterministic v1-draft JSON regenerated from the vector builder; fixtures test byte-for-byte agreement.
- Independent read-only review found one P2 (Discovery origin absent from link bootstrap). Verified and resolved through the explicit configured-origin/default-and-override contract, preserving the requested link fields. No other verified P0–P2 findings in the original review. A follow-up review of the small consumer repair completed but its result was unavailable; publication proceeds with coordinator approval on the original review and passing affected checks.

Protocol boundary coverage includes forged/wrong-key and mailbox approval refusal, pending-only redemption, owner capability/sequence checks, node/human key separation in both directions, limits, denial, removal events, revocation replay, inactivity, strict links and W-signed request path binding. Deployed Gateway/Discovery enforcement and real tunnel traffic remain named integration gates for the following stack, not claims made by these tests.

prs.title: fix(markdown-core): treat a NaN chunk limit as unbounded instead of dropping the message
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chunkText(text, NaN)` returns `[""]` and `chunkTextRanges(text, { limit: NaN })` returns `[{ start: 0, end: NaN }]`. Callers that slice the text by those ranges (the plugin-facing `chunkTextRanges` export, and `chunkMarkdownIR`, which builds its slices from `chunkText` output) end up with an empty outbound message and no error anywhere.

```js
const text = "Hello from OpenClaw — this outbound message must never vanish.";
chunkText(text, NaN);                     // [""]                     expected [text]
chunkTextRanges(text, { limit: NaN });    // [{ start: 0, end: NaN }] expected [{0, text.length}]
chunkMarkdownIR(markdownToIR(text), NaN); // []                       expected [one slice]
```

## Root cause

`normalizeChunkLimit` (`packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.ts`) only repairs limits that are finite and positive:

```ts
return Number.isFinite(limit) && limit > 0 ? resolveIntegerOption(limit, 1, { min: 1 }) : limit;
```

`Number.isFinite(NaN)` is `false`, so `NaN` falls through unchanged. Downstream, `normalizedLimit <= 0` is false, `text.length <= NaN` is false, `start + NaN` is `NaN`, and the emitted range slices to `""`. `Infinity` accidentally works because `text.length <= Infinity` is true; `NaN` is the one non-finite value that reaches the broken path.

This is also an internal inconsistency: the sibling helpers in `src/shared/text-chunking.ts` return the whole text for `NaN` because their loop condition is false for it, so the two chunking implementations disagree on the same input.

## What this changes

One early return in `normalizeChunkLimit`: `NaN` is normalised to `0`, which every caller already treats as "no limit" and returns the text as a single chunk. That is the behaviour the `chunkText` docstring already promises for a non-positive limit, and it gives all three public entry points (`chunkText`, `chunkTextRanges`, and transitively `chunkMarkdownIR`) the same answer.

Deliberately not touched: `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit`, which shatters non-finite limits into per-character chunks. That is pinned by `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` and its comment states the intent; it is loud and visible rather than silent, so it is out of scope here.

## Evidence

`packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.test.ts` gains two cases:

- new: `NaN` returns the whole text from `chunkText`, `chunkTextRanges` (default mode) and `chunkTextRanges` (preferred mode).
- new: `0`, `-5` and `Infinity` keep returning the whole text from both functions, so the existing unbounded paths are pinned against regression.

Results, Vitest 5.0.5 on Node 24 / Windows 11, repo test file plus a scratch copy of the new cases:

- before the source fix: `1 failed | 3 passed` — `expected [ '' ] to deeply equal [ 'Hello from OpenClaw — …' ]`.
- after the source fix: `6 passed` (4 in `chunk-text.test.ts`, 2 in the scratch copy of the same cases).
- reverse proof: reverting only the `Number.isNaN` branch with the new tests kept in place puts the `NaN` case back to red (`1 failed | 1 passed`); re-applying it returns `2 passed`.

Also checked: `oxfmt --check` with the repo's `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` (printWidth 100) reports no diff on both files, and `tsc --noEmit` on `chunk-text.ts` (isolated project, strict) exits 0.

Evidence boundary: I did not add an IR-level test for `chunkMarkdownIR`, because that would need the full `markdownToIR` fixture stack in the same file. Its `[]` result is a direct consequence of `chunkText` returning `[""]` — the relationship is visible in `chunkMarkdownIR`'s `if (!chunk) return;` loop — but it is verified by reading, not by a test. I also could not run the repo's full `pnpm` test suite locally (no installed workspace), so the CI run is the authority for cross-package regressions.

## Test-lines ratchet

`config/test-lines-allocations/chunk-text-nan-limit.txt` requests 19 lines, equal to the net new test lines in `chunk-text.test.ts` (LF count, `main` vs this branch).

prs.title: fix(update): run package-update backup with the candidate's probe
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #193962, #187197. A SQLite header-probe timeout leaves operators with generic file-readability advice even when an older installed updater is the reason the fixed candidate cannot be reached.

## User Impact

Probe timeouts now name the cause, report the deduplicated discovery path count, preserve the original error, and link the documented manual package-manager hop. Other worker errors keep their existing guidance. Backup refusal, batching, deadlines, rollback, and data-at-risk blocking are unchanged.

**TASK 1 verdict: (b), installed-side ownership. This is the diagnostic-only fallback requested for that verdict.** This PR does not make an unchanged 2026.10.10 updater use candidate backup code, and that old updater also cannot gain this new diagnostic from its target release. The 2026.10.10 hop needs separate stable-line backport/intermediate-release work outside this lane, or the documented manual replacement. A repaired intermediate updater must actually be installed; merely targeting it with the old updater cannot replace code already running. Preserve a verified backup before that manual hop.

## Why This Change Was Made

“Safety checks ran in the candidate updater” describes candidate admission, not transfer of the update driver. On pinned main `f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b`:

- The installed driver passes its own `runResolvedUpdate` callback to admission ([update-command.ts:639–651](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts#L639-L651)); admission applies the candidate facts and calls that callback ([update-command-candidate-admission.ts:245–274](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-candidate-admission.ts#L245-L274)).
- Original-state capture imports the local implementation ([initialization-run.ts:234–250](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-initialization-run.ts#L234-L250)), which calls local `createUpdateDatabaseBackup` ([baseline-capture.ts:349–359](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts#L349-L359)). That owner imports local backup discovery ([update-database-backup.ts:126–138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-database-backup.ts#L126-L138)) and runs it before its backup worker ([606–613](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-database-backup.ts#L606-L613)). Changing only the worker root would therefore miss parent-side discovery.
- Default worker selection captures the updater's generation; only an explicit root selects another package ([state.inspection.ts:76–86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-candidate-state.inspection.ts#L76-L86)). Retention resolves the running updater root ([retained-runtime.ts:103–108](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-retained-runtime.ts#L103-L108)) and binds workers/imports to that copy ([269–272](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-retained-runtime.ts#L269-L272)). `package-update` itself is a generic exception projection ([package-update-steps.ts:721–735](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/package-update-steps.ts#L721-L735)), not a separate candidate backup selector.

The **v2026.10.10 sources were read through GitHub's contents API, without fetching a tag**. They confirm the same installed-side continuation ([candidate-admission.ts:244–258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-candidate-admission.ts#L244-L258)), local capture import ([initialization-run.ts:223–230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-initialization-run.ts#L223-L230)), parent-side discovery before the worker ([update-database-backup.ts:442–445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/update-database-backup.ts#L442-L445)), full inventory discovery ([backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts:254–265](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts#L254-L265)), and one all-path `spawnSync` with a 10-second timeout ([sqlite-header-probe.ts:14–24](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts#L14-L24)). A candidate-path regression would assert a behavior this published driver does not provide; the focused regression here proves the main-controlled diagnostic instead.

## Evidence

Commands ran one at a time under `timeout`; no live Gateway/state was changed.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `timeout 120 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on base with only the new test | **RED:** timeout case fails against generic readability text; ENOENT control passes. 37.17s wrapper wall, 35.09s Vitest duration. |
| Same named command with fix | **GREEN:** 2 passed, 0 skipped. 40.16s wrapper wall, 34.83s Vitest duration; 30ms assertions. Cold compiler preparation dominates these runs. |
| `timeout 120 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 2 passed, 0 skipped: real batched worker and refusal to publish an archive for unreadable discovery. 12.09s wrapper wall, 10.31s Vitest duration, 336ms tests. |
| Targeted typecheck | Passed repository `run-tsgo.mjs` with a temporary config extending root, `rootDir` at the repository, and only the two touched TS files as roots (`include: []`, no emit). |
| `timeout 90 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.test.ts` | Passed. |
| Named-file oxfmt and `git diff --check` | Passed. |

prs.title: improve: avoid closed-menu layout when mounting chat composers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a fork or a second chat pane synchronously measures a closed composer menu while the new transcript is still being laid out.

## User Impact

Chat composer mounts do less layout work. The capability menu keeps its viewport limit, keyboard navigation, and resize behavior. Performance qualification is still in progress; auto-merge is off and this PR must not merge until the pending checks below are assessed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The menu is the only consumer of the measured height. Size it on the existing bubbling `overlay-show` event, after lazy content insertion and before native opening/focus. Observe resize only while that panel is actually open. This removes the initial geometry read and subtree MutationObserver without adding a visibility state or cache.

The observer retains at most one panel reference until its next opening or composer disposal. A removed panel no longer matches `:popover-open`.

Related: #183800.

## Evidence

Synthetic production UI, localhost, desktop, 20 rotating base/head/base-control triplets per action; Chromium 4×. These measure renderer work, not provider latency. Acceptance: a useful measured CPU/latency gain, no attributable user-facing regression over 20%, and preserved menu/stream/scroll behavior. A/A and thread CPU distinguish host noise from changes.
