prs.title: feat(models): customize provider names and artwork
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Custom model providers cannot choose a recognizable name and artwork independently of routing identity.

## User Impact

Optional `models.providers.<id>.name` and `icon` leave provider IDs, model references, credentials, routing and sessions unchanged. Omitted fields retain existing appearance. Fragment for an otherwise configured provider:

```json
{
  "name": "Workstation",
  "icon": { "source": "file", "path": "icons/workstation.png" }
}
```

Other sources: `{ "source": "url", "url": "https://example.com/icon.png" }` and `{ "source": "builtin", "name": "server" }`.

PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP inputs are limited to 2 MiB, 4096 pixels per side and 16 megapixels, then normalized to static PNGs at most 256 pixels per side. SVG is unsupported. Relative files resolve from the active config directory, with existing home expansion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Presentation is projected from current config after model visibility policy, not inserted into inference catalogs. Settings, pickers, account/model controls and usage views reuse the connection-scoped catalog and authenticated resource transport. Precedence: configured artwork/bundled icon → provider brand → effective-name initial.

The asset route reads only configuration-selected artwork, never request-supplied paths. HTTPS uses bounded SSRF-protected fetching with redirect/DNS checks. Source paths/URLs never cross the catalog wire. Current authorization, including paired-device credentials, is revalidated after loading and before delivery, including cache hits. Invalid/unavailable artwork falls back safely.

## Evidence

**Published head: `0c4bb441487270b5d49529a302242d7bb35ca0bb`; tested tree: `66452b2945af7b2744559992f688a3170add2f4f`. Current-head performance passes. The one underlying failed UI lane now has concrete historical-main attribution under the documented scoped exception—not a native matching-signature classification. CI remains red; protected merge admission and live writer qualification are not yet complete. Actual PR-media browser verification is complete, without waiver. No merge has been requested or performed by this implementation session.**

### Current source and guard closeout

Qualified main is **`d999f7b1b675d8702b38fb65760475f59f203130`**. Upstream **`cf80b26f093deb3444189f63cf55a243b4167275`**, “keep shared Markdown from loading Chat on other pages,” changes real shared-chunk membership and its associated existing main chat cap from **1,294,292 to 1,294,735 B**. Both base and candidate were built against that complete, unmodified upstream contract. No threshold was copied independently of its implementation, and no feature-authored checker, baseline, classification or allocation change is retained.

The original feature genuinely exceeded the older exact CI cap; that historical failure is not relabeled inherited or waived. Bounded source simplification experiments did not close that old gap and were reverted, not published. This source update integrates the specifically changed upstream graph and guard, not merely advancing main, and makes no performance-optimization or latency claim.

Commit-only inventory, isolated preparation and the primary merge were conflict-free. Source commit **`090b46f91f0201f17380feb77833415b5e0ec062`** and publication retain the exact automatic-merge tree above. There was no manual conflict resolution or new provider runtime logic. Existing provider-key/native-image fixes, security behavior, verified human credit and **887** feature-test allocation remain unchanged. Earlier generated config-baseline repairs were canonical, and the picker import resolution preserved both `ModelCatalogEntry` and `ProviderPresentation` without changing its runtime body. No global cache, service, filesystem, proxy or credential settings were changed during source recovery.

### Exact current-tree verification

On tree **`66452b2…`**, base **`d999f7b…`**, Node **24.22.1**, the official `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` passes with the current upstream policy unchanged:

| Metric | Base → candidate | Existing cap |

| Startup JS gzip | 90,476 → **90,493 B** | 93,565 B |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,293,906 → **1,294,702 B** | 1,294,735 B |

Chat has **33 B** headroom. Startup/Chat/New JS growth is **+17/+796/+380 B**, not an optimization claim. [Current-head CI performance also passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103613470/job/127513366880).

- Ledger: **6,505,333 ≤ 6,505,348**, 15 slack; allocation **887**, unchanged.
- The exact width-1280 owner-assignment flow passes through the bundled UI and real Chromium on Node 24: **1 passed / 13 skipped**. Isolated replay is not whole-shard stability or the basis of inherited attribution below.
- Earlier full build, broader browser flows, backend security tests and isolated stable-to-candidate lifecycle evidence retain their original source pins. No latest-head external-model inference, full package/systemd upgrade or fresh full package build is claimed.

### Scoped current-CI attribution

The sole underlying failed lane in current run **42103613470**, attempt 1, is [UI E2E 4/7, job 127513367394](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103613470/job/127513367394). **Qualifications retained:** the Playwright call logs are not byte-identical. Main reaches “performing click action”; the PR stops while waiting for actionability. This is not renderer-root-cause proof. The [native failure table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103613470/job/127538372902) still calls the row **new**, because it selected newer main run **42093790888**, job **127479149518**, whose job passed, and explicitly says **“selected scope not compared.”** We do not claim a native matching-signature result or relabel the table.

That is resolved by the separately verified current graph/guard, not inherited attribution. ### Owning-boundary and review proof

After repair, **56 runtime/catalog/artwork, 15 wire and 2 config tests passed**, including real paired-token held-load and cached-image revocation. No provider identity, authorization or stored-data migration was introduced.

Independent local Codex **P0–P2** reviews of the provider-key and artwork-style repairs completed **scoped clean** with actual owner context. They were static reviews, not independently executed tests or visual approval. The documented autoreview fallback left unrelated local ClawSweeper state untouched. prs.title: fix(markdown-core): chunkText drops the whole message when limit is NaN
prs.body:
Closes #193928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `chunkText`, `chunkTextRanges`, and `chunkMarkdownIR` silently drop the entire outbound message when the chunk limit is `NaN`. `normalizeChunkLimit` returns `NaN` unchanged, and since every `NaN` comparison is false the chunkers fall through to a first range of `{ start: 0, end: NaN }` / an empty string slice, so nonempty text vanishes instead of being sent.

## User Impact

User impact: callers that pass a `NaN` chunk limit (e.g. an unset `textChunkLimit` that reached the chunker without being rejected) now receive the full text as one chunk instead of an empty payload, so outbound messages no longer disappear.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeChunkLimit` is the single boundary where `NaN` can be intercepted before any comparison-based loop runs. Treating `NaN` as `Infinity` (unbounded) makes the existing `text.length <= normalizedLimit` early return fire and returns the whole text — the same behaviour `Infinity` already had. This repairs `chunkText` and `chunkTextRanges` directly, and `chunkMarkdownIR` which delegates to `chunkText`. The render-aware chunking contract is untouched: it does not call `normalizeChunkLimit` and keeps its own `NaN` → per-character behaviour.

## Evidence

Ran the package's vitest suite locally on `main` source with only `chunk-text.ts` swapped:

**Before (main, no fix):** `chunkText("Hello ...", NaN)` → `[""]`, `chunkTextRanges("Hello ...", { limit: NaN })` → `[{ start: 0, end: NaN }]` (slices to empty), `chunkMarkdownIR(ir, NaN)` → `[]` (message lost).

**After (this fix):**

```
packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.test.ts
 ✓ normalizes positive fractional limits without emitting empty chunks
 ✓ preserves nonempty text when the limit is NaN instead of dropping it
 ✓ keeps grapheme boundaries and surrogate-safe progress in each chunking mode
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The new `NaN` regression asserts `chunkText(text, NaN) === [text]`, `chunkTextRanges(text, { limit: NaN }) === [{ start: 0, end: text.length }]`, and that slicing the ranges back out yields the full text. The two pre-existing tests still pass. The broader suite (`ir.test.ts`, `render-aware-chunking.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/text-chunking.test.ts`) was not run locally; CI covers it.



## Real-behavior proof (re-review)

Beyond the vitest assertions above, a terminal capture exercises the shipped markdown-core chunkers with a **plugin-computed NaN chunk limit** and shows the outbound payload preserved. The proof script imports the actual package source (`chunkText` / `chunkTextRanges` — the public exports a channel payload-prep caller consumes) with the real `@openclaw/normalization-core` dependencies resolved, computes a NaN limit the way an unset config field reaches the chunker (`Number(undefined) === NaN`), runs `chunkTextRanges(text, { limit: NaN })`, and slices the returned ranges back into the outbound message chunks (the `extensions/zalouser/src/send.ts` consumption shape). Run against both current-`main` source and this PR's source:

```
--- MAIN (current main, no fix) ---
chunkTextRanges(outbound, { limit: NaN }) = [{"start":0,"end":null}]
outbound payload (ranges sliced back out) = [""]
=> outbound message LOST (0 chars delivered)

--- FIX (this PR) ---
chunkTextRanges(outbound, { limit: NaN }) = [{"start":0,"end":75}]
outbound payload (ranges sliced back out) = ["Hello from OpenClaw — this outbound message must never vanish when chunked."]
=> outbound message PRESERVED (75 chars delivered)

SUMMARY: main delivers 0 chars (message LOST); fix delivers 75 chars (message PRESERVED).
```

(`end: null` is `JSON.stringify(NaN)`; the runtime value is `NaN`, and `"text".slice(0, NaN)` is `""` — that is why main loses the message. The fix maps NaN to `Infinity` so the `text.length <= normalizedLimit` early return fires.) No IPs, API keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints in the transcript. Full capture + script details in the proof comment.

prs.title: perf(ui): retain structured draft validation across equal config receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An equal Gateway config receipt recreates configuration-node parameter objects. Optional structured fields consequently validate their absent value again, even when their schema, value, required status and draft ownership did not change. AI Agents pays for this across the form while nothing changes on screen.

## Solution

Give each existing node a four-input memo with equality before resolving its initial structured draft. The canonical validation helper, draft lifecycle and live callbacks keep their existing responsibilities. The helper's narrowed parameter type documents its actual inputs. There is no shared cache, new owner or invalidation lifecycle.

## Evidence

Production bundles with synthetic Gateway data, headless desktop Chromium/WebKit. Twenty rotated base/head/base triplets per engine for AI Agents, Advanced and Plugin Settings; a separate twenty-triplet Usage sort control. Ten additional AI Agents/Plugin Settings triplets and ten additional Usage triplets check the initially noisy control tails. Counts and fresh profile are separate from uninstrumented timing.

Acceptance: at least 5% improvement on the target flow, no attributable sibling/control regression beyond the campaign timing band, no size ceiling increases. Chromium claims use script/task CPU; WebKit claims use application time. The existing debounce can set an elapsed-time floor.

All 660 observations passed. AI Agents, Plugin Settings and Usage have 30 triplets per engine; Advanced has 20. Host load median was 12.31, p95 16.57 (range 7.54–18.49). Values below are median / p95 milliseconds.

| Flow / metric | Base | Head | A/A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AI Agents: Chromium script | 51.193 / 54.185 | 47.472 / 50.397 | 50.645 / 53.326 |
| AI Agents: Chromium task | 61.803 / 65.482 | 58.085 / 61.349 | 61.306 / 64.396 |
| AI Agents: Chromium application | 117.1 / 119.3 | 117.0 / 118.6 | 117.55 / 119.2 |
| AI Agents: WebKit application | 118 / 121 | 117 / 120 | 118 / 120 |
| Advanced: Chromium task | 222.765 / 246.911 | 214.600 / 237.592 | 227.354 / 243.118 |
| Advanced: WebKit application | 216 / 235 | 212 / 221 | 214.5 / 234 |
| Plugin Settings: Chromium script | 56.532 / 65.092 | 55.821 / 70.251 | 55.401 / 69.976 |
| Plugin Settings: Chromium task | 73.106 / 82.269 | 72.894 / 87.677 | 72.196 / 87.153 |
| Plugin Settings: WebKit application | 116 / 120 | 115.5 / 119 | 117 / 120 |

AI Agents gains 7.27% script and 6.02% task CPU; application time remains bounded by the existing debounce. No ≥5% WebKit latency gain is claimed. AI style median is 0.753 → 0.780 ms (+3.52%, p95 +0.23%). Plugin Settings' script/task p95 is +7.93%/+6.57%, while identical-base p95 is also +7.50%/+5.94%; head versus A/A is +0.39%/+0.60%. The medians are flat or lower. These tails are disclosed as loaded-host variance rather than an all-metrics improvement. Advanced script p95 +0.31% is below the campaign's noise threshold.

Usage control: Chromium script 9.886/11.101 → 9.824/10.734 ms; task 60.872/66.218 → 60.672/68.432 ms (A/A 61.241/65.339). Application 128/150.7 → 127.65/179.9 ms (A/A 127.15/162.2). WebKit application 134/188 → 161.5/183 ms, while A/A is 159.5/191 ms. The +20.5% WebKit median versus the first base is not presented as a passing elapsed comparison: the identical second base is itself +19.0%, and head versus A/A is +1.25%. An independent source audit shows the changed config-form chunk is absent from Usage’s 29-chunk static dependency graph; all 1,269 mapped source entries in that graph have identical content in both builds. This unchanged-flow timing spread is host/driver noise, not evidence of a faster control. The changed form flows meet the CPU acceptance rule; no WebKit latency gain is claimed.

Memory limitation: Advanced post-action `JSHeapUsedBytes` median is 51.77 → 51.82 MiB, but p95 is 59.06 → 77.37 MiB (A/A 59.02). These snapshots include uncollected transient allocations; there is no forced-GC retention result. The added memo has one fixed four-field input per mounted node, with no growing collection or listener. No memory improvement or stable memory-tail claim is made.

Fresh source-mapped profile: AI Agents structured-draft validation samples 7.504 → 0 ms; Advanced 9.371 → 0 ms. Zero sampled time means the hot path disappeared from this profile, not an exact zero-time guarantee. Other schema validation stays in its existing owners.

- Regression fails on base (three validations instead of one after unrelated updates) and passes on head; all six draft-lifecycle cases pass. It also verifies value, schema, required status and draft-owner transitions.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed.
- Paired production build and strict performance comparison passed: startup 90,280 → 90,280 B gzip, one startup CSS request; total CSS unchanged. Total JavaScript adds 83 B gzip. No budget raised.
- Fresh independent review with complete node/helper/caller context: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Simplification pass keeps one local derivation. Solid checklist: memos 12 → 13; effects, listeners, queries, flush calls and new owner APIs 0 → 0.
- `pnpm deadcode:knip` passed on the final candidate head.

| Touched file LOC | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Config node | 432 | 447 |
| Draft helper | 37 | 37 |
| Draft-lifecycle tests | 151 | 202 |
| Test allocation | 0 | 1 |

Visual proof: four inspected synthetic Chromium/WebKit captures preserve the page. All changed pixels are in the 44×10 footer build ID; recorded document and config-host computed styles match. The inspected before/after images are attached in [the proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193976#issuecomment-6677754112).

prs.title: fix(apple): Gateway stays disconnected after a network drop during the device-token retry
prs.body:
Closes #190150

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Apple apps stop reconnecting ("Gateway token is out of date") when the network drops during the one device-token retry the Gateway grants after rejecting a rotated shared token.

## User Impact

User impact: after a Wi-Fi handoff or timeout during that retry, the app reconnects on its own with its still-valid paired device token, without a restart or re-pairing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel marked the granted retry as used while it built the connect request. A transport failure before the Gateway answered therefore left the retry spent, and later attempts sent only the stale shared token until reconnect paused.

The retry now stays pending until the Gateway answers the connect request:
- A scope-suppressed retry is still dropped up front.
- A Gateway rejection of the device token still pauses reconnect, as before.
- The 250 ms fast retry now applies only to the rejection that grants the retry. An outage during a pending retry keeps the normal exponential backoff instead of retrying four times a second.

This touches the same catch block as #191424, which clears a rejected device token that was the only credential. The two changes are independent.

## Evidence

New regression test `transport loss during the device-token retry keeps the stored device token for recovery` in `GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests`. It runs twice: once where the connect send fails, and once where the socket is lost before the connect response.
- A fake Gateway rejects the rotated shared token with `canRetryWithDeviceToken`, drops the first device-token retry, and accepts only the stored device token.
- The test asserts that the same channel then connects with the device token, and that the backoff after the drop is above the 250 ms fast path.

I ran `GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests|GatewayChannelConnectTests` (20 tests) three times with `swift test --skip-build`, with a private `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`:

| Code | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` (63e1079af) | Fails 4 checks, the same 2 in both cases: `connected`, and the recovery connect carries `deviceToken`. |
| Channel change only, old backoff | Recovers, but fails the backoff check in both cases: the drop got the 250 ms fast retry. |
| This PR | 20/20 pass. |

Also:
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` succeeds.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, SwiftLint and SwiftFormat on the three changed files, and `git diff --check` are all clean.

Gaps:
- Not yet run against an isolated real Gateway with a rotated shared token and an interrupted retry.
- `GatewayNetworkPathRecoveryTests`, the other user of the backoff, was left to CI. It only records with `pendingDeviceTokenRetry: false`, which this change does not affect.

prs.title: fix(plugins): expand home-relative load paths when matching a plugin on uninstall
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins uninstall <id>` reports success but leaves a home-relative entry in `plugins.load.paths`, so the plugin is still discovered and shows up as `disabled` / `record-missing`:

```
$ openclaw plugins install --link --force --accept-capabilities ~/plugins/demo-tilde
# plugins.load.paths: ["~/plugins/demo-tilde"]     (the form the plugin docs use)
$ openclaw plugins uninstall demo-tilde --force
Uninstalled plugin "demo-tilde". Removed: plugin settings, install record.
# plugins.load.paths: ["~/plugins/demo-tilde"]     expected: removed
$ openclaw plugins list | grep demo-tilde
| Demo Tilde | demo-tilde | openclaw | disabled | ~/plugins/demo-tilde/index.js | 1.0.0 | record-missing |
```

The same path written absolute is removed correctly, so this only hits the documented `~/...` form.

## Root cause

`loadPathMatchesInstallPath` in `src/plugins/uninstall-package-config.ts` compared the two paths as given:

```ts
return (
  loadPath === installPath ||
  resolveRealpathOrAbsolute(loadPath) === resolveRealpathOrAbsolute(installPath)
);
```

`resolveRealpathOrAbsolute("~/plugins/demo")` fails the realpath and falls back to `path.resolve`, which treats `~` as a literal directory name — it can never equal the absolute install path. Discovery (`resolveUserPath` in `src/plugins/discovery.ts`) and `buildLoadPathHelpers` (`src/plugins/update-config.ts`) both expand `~` first, so uninstall was the one comparison with a different idea of what a load path means.

## What this changes

Both sides go through `resolveUserPath` before the canonical comparison:

```ts
if (loadPath === installPath) {
  return true;
}
return (
  resolveRealpathOrAbsolute(resolveUserPath(loadPath)) ===
  resolveRealpathOrAbsolute(resolveUserPath(installPath))
);
```

The fast path for an exact string match is kept, and `resolveUserPath` leaves non-`~` paths alone (it only resolves them), so absolute and already-canonical entries behave exactly as before.

Scope note: `loadPathMatchesInstallPath` backs `removePluginInstallOwnerFromConfig`, `removePluginRuntimePolicyFromConfig` and `hasMatchingPluginLoadPath` (the update/replace path in `plugin-package-update.ts`), so this one change covers all three call sites rather than only the uninstall CLI.

## Evidence

New `src/plugins/uninstall-package-config.test.ts`, driving the exported `hasMatchingPluginLoadPath` with `OPENCLAW_HOME` pinned to a temp dir (the same resolution source `resolveUserPath` uses in production):

- `["~/plugins/demo-tilde"]` vs `<home>/plugins/demo-tilde` → `true` (the reported bug).
- absolute path vs the same absolute path → `true` (unchanged behaviour).
- `["~/plugins/other-plugin"]` vs `<home>/plugins/demo-tilde` → `false` (no over-matching).

Results, Vitest 5.0.5 / Node 24 / Windows 11, isolated harness that keeps the real `uninstall-package-config.ts` and the real `src/infra/home-dir.ts` (`resolveUserPath`) and stubs only the neighbouring path helpers:

- before the source change: `1 failed | 2 passed` — the home-relative case returns `false`.
- after the source change: `3 passed`.
- reverse proof: reverting only `loadPathMatchesInstallPath` with the test kept puts the same single case back to red; the absolute and different-plugin cases pass in both directions, so the red is specific to the missing expansion.

`oxfmt --check` with the repo `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` (printWidth 100) reports no diff on both files.

Evidence boundary: this is a helper-level proof, not an end-to-end CLI run. I did not add a case to `src/plugins/uninstall-load-paths.test.ts` (the real temp-dir + symlink uninstall flow) because that suite needs the full install-record store; the helper is the only place the comparison happens, and the issue reporter already captured the real CLI before/after on `main`.

## Ratchets

`config/test-lines-allocations/uninstall-home-load-path.txt`: 52 lines, equal to the new test file (LF count).

prs.title: chore(ios): compare balanced cold archive cache overhead
prs.body:
Related: #193940, #193896

## What Problem This Solves

The previous signed compilation-cache experiment mixed cold-cache overhead with first-run preparation, so its failed cold-start result cannot isolate the cost of enabling the cache.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. **Do not merge this draft.** This branch runs signed archive/export diagnostics only. It has no Apple upload, release staging, release notes, screenshot capture, or Discord publication path.

## Why This Change Was Made

One unmeasured canonical archive absorbs first-run lint, package and SDK preparation. Four measured archives then run OFF/ON/ON/OFF on one disposable `xcode-27-xlarge` runner, with identical source and release metadata within each pair. Every archive removes DerivedData and all compiler-cache storage. No compiler-cache restore or save runs. Output comparison waits until all measured builds finish.

Application/archive/comparator inputs remain identical to `5581460a5710088e5c6c918782ff47138470b945` (application base `1595dd24770799485a9631c757ccfb7740c12be2`), except this diagnostic workflow and harness. This deliberately preserves the earlier warm-replay and changed-source correctness evidence when Xcode also matches. Both earlier failed campaigns and their original reports remain unchanged.

## Evidence

### Prospective acceptance rule — recorded before dispatch

1. Order: unmeasured cache-disabled preparation, pair 1 OFF/ON, pair 2 ON/OFF. Every measured case has empty CAS and fresh DerivedData; source, toolchain and per-pair release metadata must match.
2. For pair `i`, overhead is `100 × (ON wall seconds[i] / OFF wall seconds[i] − 1)`. **Each pair and the arithmetic mean of the two percentages must be strictly below 20%.** The direct comparison `ON < 1.20 × OFF` enforces the boundary without percentage rounding.
3. Each pair's maximum-process-RSS ratio must be strictly below `1.20`. CPU time and resource timelines remain diagnostic evidence, not invented performance claims.
4. Both signed export semantic comparisons must pass; pair 1 must reject all six existing corruption controls. Existing metadata, signature, team, architecture, executable/dSYM UUID and payload validation remains enabled. Cold candidates must show shared-module misses and zero shared-module replay hits.
5. This measures cold compiler storage on an equally prepared runner. Two pairs on one machine provide a bounded follow-up, not statistical production qualification. A success does not rewrite either prior failure or enable production caching.

Local report-entrypoint proof accepts valid data and rejects the exact 20% boundary, excess wall/RSS, stale CAS declaration, wrong cache mode, metadata/source/order mismatch, warm shared replay, semantic failure, and missing negative controls. Node syntax, targeted scripts lint, Ruby syntax, and workflow actionlint/zizmor pass.

Fresh independent review against `5581460a5710088e5c6c918782ff47138470b945`: scoped-clean at P0/P1, with no actionable findings. Required macOS workflow-focused batch finished: **1,235 tests passed**, 8 skipped. The production screenshot-job guard fails because this intentionally nonmergeable workflow has no screenshot job. The workflow-evidence suite cannot build with the existing borrowed install because `@lancedb/lancedb` and `quickjs-wasi` are missing. No guards or shared dependencies were changed. These are recorded gaps, not a passing aggregate test claim.

Hosted campaign: [42168700554](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42168700554), running the pinned candidate. The prospective rule above was published and read back before dispatch.

Pinned candidate: `73aabf12f9f9ecb402a4b0717d188a5624223069`. The two prior report SHA-256 values were rechecked unchanged: `36702a380bade4d30403f3a51af18a014d53cff080116999b4528e391d4367ee` and `a90f1664e3cae9257bfc14681a95782affa11c21e15038b23b64316e0bca4b41`.

prs.title: fix(test): keep the reap fixture's writer in the process group on macOS
prs.body:
Closes #192785

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `test/helpers/openclaw-test-instance.test.ts` fails on macOS (4 of 4 runs on `main`), because "reaps terminal children with inherited stdio before starting a new gateway" expects a process that left the owned process group to be gone.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers can run this file on macOS without this failure. Spawn inputs on Linux are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture starts its writer with `detached: true`, so the writer leaves the anchor's process group. On Linux, when the native owner is admitted, the anchor is a child subreaper, adopts that writer and reaps it, which is what this test asserts. macOS custody is the process group, and `docs/reference/test/runner-internals.md` says descendants that escape the owned group are outside that contract. So macOS does not promise what this assertion expects, and the test's `process.platform !== "win32"` gate admits macOS anyway.

The fix keeps the `terminal-drain` writer in the group where the group is the owner. No assertion changes. `detached` stays `true` on Linux for both kinds, and `refusal-drain` stays detached everywhere.

Alternatives rejected:

- Gating the test to Linux would drop macOS coverage of the failed start and the restart after it.
- Flipping the assertion on macOS would race the writer's own 5-second exit.
- Tracking escaped writers in the supervisor would change a contract the docs state on purpose.

Accepted limit: on macOS this test no longer exercises a writer that escaped with only stderr inherited. That case has no replacement. `child.service-lifecycle.test.ts`, listed in `test:macos:ci:1`, covers a neighboring one: an escaped child that retains lineage stays alive and cleanup refuses at the hard deadline.

## Evidence

Run on macOS 27.2 (arm64) with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0, one run at a time, at load about 20 on 18 cores.

| Tree | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |

prs.body:
Related: #176315

> **Investigation placeholder — intentionally draft, not ready for review or merge.** No implementation patch exists yet. The root cause and current-main reproduction remain unproven; no native Windows before/after result or passing regression is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

A Windows-node command submitted through Code Mode can remain pending without returning native output, an exit status, or an actionable failure, even when discovery and native Codex session listing succeed.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is for remote Windows commands to return their actual output and exit status, or a truthful denial, timeout, cancellation, or unknown-outcome result. There is no delivered behavior change yet. Authorization and unknown-outcome safeguards must remain intact; uncertain requests must not be replayed automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issue #176315 reports this failure with a Linux Gateway and native Windows node running OpenClaw 2026.10.4. The failing owner has not been identified, so this draft deliberately does not propose a speculative repair.

The next step is one bounded, harmless absolute-path `codex.exe --version` probe in an isolated paired environment, using normal supported approvals. Correlate the Code Mode bridge request with exec entry, preparation, approval disposition, node invocation, native process completion, terminal-result acceptance, and Code Mode continuation. Only then select the smallest fix at the responsible boundary.

## Evidence

**Completed investigation — source analysis, not native execution:**

- Read the report and complete comments, traced the execution and result-return owners, and compared release `383c124cc32f` with inspected main `76985e4c31c4`.
- The release sets `bridgeDispatchStarted` before `runBridgeRequest`; it does not establish that exec or a Windows process started. [Release source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af/src/agents/code-mode-state.ts#L570-L573).
- Last confirmed incident boundary: an outstanding Code Mode `bridge:callValue`. First unconfirmed boundary: entry into the nested exec implementation and node-target resolution. Later execution and return stages remain unconfirmed for that request.
- Compared #168523 (headless approval delivery), #104798 (bare-name allowlist precheck), PR #166140 (open at the October 29 inspection) (Windows shell-wrapper policy), and merged PRs #175949 and #128440 (Code Mode lifecycle repairs). Similar symptoms do not establish a shared cause or prove that this report is fixed.

**Required before this can become an implementation PR:**

- [ ] Verify actual Gateway/node builds, Node versions, transport, capabilities, and effective approval policy in the isolated test environment.
- [ ] Capture the bounded native Windows failure and its first stalled boundary; reconcile the request before any control or retry.
- [ ] Compare the equivalent supported direct node-exec path with Code Mode, keeping policy and command equivalent.
- [ ] Add a regression that fails on the base and passes with the owner-correct repair.
- [ ] Capture native Windows before/after stdout and exit delivery; verify relevant denial, error, cancellation, and disconnect cases.
- [ ] Complete targeted tests, typecheck, lint/format, and independent review; replace this draft's pending statements with exact results.

Native Windows access and an isolated paired Gateway were unavailable in the investigating session. No implementation tests were run, and no production service, approval policy, or unrelated session was changed.

Reported by @ceo633 in [#176315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176315).

prs.title: feat(plugin-sdk): publish access-policy revisions for retained rechecks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated operator-authority revalidation enters the access-policy plugin runtime even when its decision inputs have not changed.

## User Impact

Plugins may opt into revision-published caching for explicitly classified non-effect rechecks. Existing plugins and every unclassified `assertCurrent()` caller retain live checks. Credential use, tools/commands, external effects, and publications continue through the live/default path.

**Security tradeoff and review request:** this trusts an opting-in plugin to publish every dependency change and declare a truthful validity bound. Assertions with untracked mutable invocation inputs must not opt in. Request independent review from **@openclaw/openclaw-secops** before merge. This PR is for maintainer review; do not merge without that review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin publishes revisions through an optional SDK subscription; reading a revision does not enter plugin runtime scope. The operator-access-policy owner holds one allow slot per captured authority. Cache hits require the same plugin publication, registry, ambient request scope, and an unexpired deadline; profile/config changes also replace the retained-grant slot. Unknown revision, callback errors, retirement, and expiry force a live check. Weak request-scope references avoid retaining completed request graphs. No denial is cached.

`assertCurrentForEffect()` and parameterless `assertCurrent()` stay live. Rechecks require explicit propagation; copying an authority and replacing its live guard cannot silently inherit the old cached path. The visitor plugin publishes grant changes and supplies the grant's actual expiry, so delayed timer execution cannot extend access.

| Site | Classification | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admitted operator `readCurrentRoleFacts` | Recheck, only with explicit owner opt-in | Reads retained role facts; performs no effect |
| Gateway/channel/recovery `retain` | Recheck | Acquires lifetime custody; later effects revalidate live |
| Channel/recovery source-change notifications | Recheck | Revalidates retained work without performing effects |
| Recovered role reads | Recheck | Preserves the exact live recovery claim and identity/config guards |
| Default assertions, effect entry, recovery `assertPolicyCurrent` | Live | Preserves execution/publication and unclassified callers |
| HTTP/WS access checks and tool/command callers | Live | Existing parameterless path is unchanged |

Follow-ups after #182066: classification in `lane-controller.ts`, `run-attempt-dispatch.ts`, harness `host-capability.ts`, `host-trajectory.ts`, `tool-authority.runtime.ts`, and `tools/gateway-caller-context.ts`. Those callers remain live in this PR; none of their files is modified.

Production LOC delta is **+318** (+453 / -135, excluding tests, test support, and docs). It grows because the approved contract requires plugin publication and validity, generation/error fencing, bounded cache storage, and a purpose split while preserving live effect checks. There is no new config option, schema, durable state, TTL heuristic, or Gateway-generated policy revision.

## Evidence

- Baseline recovered-owner work-count regression: 183 plugin assertions for 60 role reads and three live effects; failed the expected count of three. Candidate: three after warming the allow (-180, -98.36%). This is an owner fixture, not a measured whole cron scheduler/model turn.
- Initial complete focused run: 126 tests passed across seven files, including revision/expiry/error/retirement, principal and ambient-scope isolation, copied claim guards, recovery, managed plugin registration, and visitor lifecycle.
- Core typecheck and the export-collision guard passed. Both required import-closure files passed (22 tests); the final affected recovery/visitor rerun passed (39 + 11 tests). Changed-file core and extension lint passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings after resolving ambient-scope contract ambiguity, including a final review of publication and fixture lifecycle cleanup. The configured helper rejected its provider route before inference; configuration was not changed.
- Owner allocation campaign: predeclared five paired samples per scenario, fixed work, synchronized warm starts, swapped interleaved CPUs, shared guard. Results pending quiet-slot admission. No GC/promotion/latency claim from the sampled allocation pass.

Production signal after deployment: fewer access-policy plugin assertions and plugin-scope allocation during retained role reads, with unchanged live effect counts and immediate revocation/expiry enforcement. Whole-Gateway latency, promotion, and the remaining unclassified assertion family are not established by this owner proof.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation files</summary>

- `src/plugins/gateway-access-policy-registration.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/operator-access-policy.github-login.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/operator-run-authority.worker.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.test.ts`
- `src/agents/admitted-run-context.test.ts`
- `extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts`
- `extensions/visitor-access/src/visitors.authority.test.ts`
- `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`
- `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`

Commands: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <focused files> --maxWorkers=1`, changed-file `oxfmt`/`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-export-name-collisions.mts`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproducible owner probe adapter (applied identically to baseline and candidate)</summary>

The existing `scripts/perf/operator-authority-measure.ts` stays unchanged in this PR. This task-local adapter supplies an opting-in synthetic policy and 20 role reads before each live effect. Run its generated script with the existing harness flags (`--scenario recovery-source --iterations 2000 --warmup 200`), adding `--recheck-turn` for retained-work samples; omit that flag for the live-effect control. Use separate synthetic state, the shared quiet-slot lock and guard, synchronized `--start-at`, and swapped interleaved CPUs.

```python
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('scripts/perf/operator-authority-measure.ts')
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('    iterations: { type: "string", default: "20000" },', '    "recheck-turn": { type: "boolean", default: false },\n    iterations: { type: "string", default: "20000" },')
s = s.replace('  signal: controller.signal,\n  assertCurrent()', '  signal: controller.signal,\n  recheckValidUntil: Infinity,\n  assertCurrent()')
s = s.replace('registerGatewayAccessPolicy({\n  authorize', 'registerGatewayAccessPolicy({\n  subscribeRevision(publish) { publish("synthetic-policy-1"); return () => {}; },\n  authorize')
s = s.replace('      counts.recoverySource++;\n      authority.assertCurrent();', '''      counts.recoverySource++;
      if (values["recheck-turn"]) {
        for (let read = 0; read < 20; read++) {
          assert(authority.readCurrentRoleFacts);
          authority.readCurrentRoleFacts();
        }
      }
      authority.assertCurrent();''')
s = s.replace('    includeCollected: true,', '    includeCollected: true,\n    roleReadsPerWork: values["recheck-turn"] ? 20 : 0,\n    effectsPerWork: 1,')
assert 'roleReadsPerWork' in s and 'subscribeRevision(publish)' in s
Path('scripts/perf/buf7-authority-adapter.ts').write_text(s)
```

</details>

## CI attribution

The first-head changed-plan PDF-tool failure is inherited from the newest scheduled main run (created 2026-10-24 07:31:48Z), head `068022e6e8df38c35d39cc5dadff40e8f58eac2d`: [main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40074498223/job/120815064175), [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40075489577/job/120818124451). Both fail `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts:397:35`, “reports omitted images for a text-only model and supplies Codex instructions,” with byte-identical assertion annotations after removing terminal color codes. No CI rerun was requested.

The first-head requester E2E failure was a stale assertion after main's [#182285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182285), commit `5d47168b9170d92c45aeb82cd7680719f211b89a`: preparation capacity is released on Gateway acceptance, not model settlement. The scheduled main inventory does not include this E2E, so no matching scheduled-main claim is made for it. The test-only correction now proves three accepted restored model turns remain open, an ordinary probe progresses, and no duplicate restored wake appears. The existing registry preparation-bound test retains the separate two-slot admission invariant. No product behavior changes for this repair. A local focused replay was stopped when its wrapper attempted a broad runtime build. Changed-file format/lint and independent review passed; CI provides the E2E execution proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the proxy-abort CI regression when the origin finishes its finite response before the downstream abort reaches it.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Restores the fixture for upstream cancellation and capture correctness.

## Why This Change Was Made

Abort cases send 64 KiB, advertise one more byte, and keep the origin response open. Socket buffering can no longer finish that response before cancellation. The backpressure case retains its complete 16 MiB response.

All existing cases and assertions remain: upstream close without finish, exactly one error associated with the original flow, no successful response capture, and a healthy follow-up request. Whole change: **5 additions / 5 deletions**, **591 test LF before and after**, no baseline changes, retries, skips, timeout increases, or production changes.

## Evidence

- Unchanged head: `06cee0c36d32c98a25467535d99880fed031c623`.
- Original [scheduled main failure, compact-large-12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41820856266/job/126543595750), head `3f9bc028d1ab2b7cbd81a26c5523f9ce09229341`: `closes upstream and captures one error on downstream abort (reset=true)` expected `{ closedResponses: 1, finishedResponses: 0 }`, received `{ closedResponses: 1, finishedResponses: 1 }`.
- The bounded source-derived fixture probe using real Node HTTP and the actual helper/listen/respond source reproduced `finishedResponses: 1` on base and `0` on the candidate with a single-chunk buffer envelope. This diagnoses fixture completion; it does **not** cover the proxy, persistence, the original 16 MiB envelope, or the full Vitest file. Probe wall time was under one second per revision.
- Same-snapshot named-file syntax lint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: pass. Fresh independent source autoreview against pinned base `c5ad793d657beeb61c55a2aa07204a9ce9af2c29`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**. Missing cancellation and duplicate/misclassified captures remain detectable through the unchanged assertions.
- Fresh remote observation of [normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41830987763): applicable checks and published CI, security, and dependency gates are successful on this exact PR head. Its [changed-test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41830987763/job/126578572773) passed; test-step wall time was 64 seconds. This alone does **not** confirm either original abort case executed.
- The previously unread [preflight log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41830987763/job/126577816310) was acquired through one permitted new route. It records merge checkout `0920d64e05bdfea72747a438c92eb82deae64a12` of the exact PR head into `87495305c729b15ba7cbb2910a092f1c2c0aa388`, changed paths containing only `src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts`, and three planned Node rows. It does not print the resolved row targets or runtime case results.

prs.title: fix(cli): lowercase the infer web --provider flag before dispatch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`infer web search --provider Brave` and `infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl` fail before any provider runs, while the same command with `--provider brave` / `--provider firecrawl` works. Every bundled web provider id is lowercase, and the config keys `tools.web.search.provider` / `tools.web.fetch.provider` are already matched case-insensitively (#177836), so the CLI flag is the one surface that still compares raw.

```
$ openclaw infer web search --provider Brave --query openclaw --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Unknown web_search provider \"Brave\"." } }
$ openclaw infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl --url https://example.com --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { ... "web.fetch provider \"Firecrawl\" is not available; check it with `openclaw infer web providers`." } }
```

## Root cause

`src/cli/capability-cli/web.ts` passed the flag through as read (`const provider = opts.provider as string | undefined;` in both the `search` and `fetch` actions). The same value is lowercased for secret scoping and plugin loading, but the explicit-selection guards downstream compare it verbatim: `web-search/runtime.ts` does `providers.some((entry) => entry.id === explicitProviderId)` and `web-fetch/runtime.ts` does `providers.find((entry) => entry.id === providerId)`. Neither matches `Brave` against `brave`, so search throws and fetch resolves to null.

## What this changes

One helper next to the command registration:

```ts
function readProviderFlag(value: unknown): string | undefined {
  return value === undefined ? undefined : normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(value);
}
```

Both actions now read `readProviderFlag(opts.provider)`, so the normalisation happens once at the boundary instead of being duplicated in the two runtime guards. `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` is already imported in this file, and the flag is still `undefined` when omitted, so the "no flag → tool fallback" branch for `infer web fetch` is unchanged.

Removing the two `as string | undefined` casts lowers this file's non-const assertion count from 3 to 1, so `config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt` shrinks the entry from `3` to `1` — a tightening, not a widening.

## Evidence

New `src/cli/capability-cli/web.test.ts` builds the real command tree through `registerWebCapabilityCommands` with a recording stub for `commander`, then invokes the captured actions and asserts what the provider lookup received.

- `--provider Brave` on `web search` → `runWebSearch` receives `providerId: "brave"`.
- `--provider Firecrawl` on `web fetch` → `resolveWebFetchDefinition` receives `providerId: "firecrawl"`.
- `--provider brave` stays `brave`, and an omitted flag stays `undefined` (fetch still takes the tool-fallback branch).

Results, Vitest 5.0.5 / Node 24 / Windows 11, isolated harness that mirrors the module layout and stubs the neighbouring CLI modules:

- before the source change: `2 failed | 1 passed` — the two mixed-case cases receive `Brave` / `Firecrawl` verbatim.
- after the source change: `3 passed`.
- reverse proof: reverting only `web.ts` while keeping the test puts the same two cases back to red; re-applying the fix returns `3 passed`. The already-lowercase/absent case passes in both directions, so the red is specific to the missing normalisation.

`oxfmt --check` with the repo `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` (printWidth 100) reports no diff on both files.

Evidence boundary: this is a unit-level proof of the flag-to-dispatch contract, not an end-to-end CLI run — I could not run `node --import tsx src/entry.ts` here (no installed workspace), so a real `infer web search` invocation with a live provider is unverified. The issue's reporter captured the real CLI behaviour before and after an equivalent patch on `main`, and CI is the authority for the surrounding suites.

## Ratchets

- `config/test-lines-allocations/web-provider-flag-case.txt`: 51 lines, equal to the new test file (LF count).
- `config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt`: `src/cli/capability-cli/web.ts` 3 → 1.

prs.title: fix(ui): make Models look ready on a fresh install
prs.body:
Related: #193892, #193507

## What Problem This Solves

On a fresh install, **Settings → Models** looked broken before the user had done anything:

- The page header showed the raw translation key `subtitles.modelProviders`.
- A "Couldn't load models from acp-opencode, openai. Try again." warning appeared with a Retry button, even though nothing was configured.
- The **Add provider** dialog titled a provider that already has config by its id (`tencent-tokenhub`) instead of its name.

## User Impact

- The header reads "Global model defaults and provider access for your agents."
- With no connected provider and no default model, no listing-failure warning is shown; the "Set up a model" prompt is the call to action. Once any provider is connected or a default model is saved, listing failures warn exactly as before.
- The add dialog uses the same display name as the provider picker ("Tencent Tokenhub").

## Why This Change Was Made

These are audit problems 8 and 12, the fresh-install polish.

- **Subtitle:** the page reads the route subtitle catalog but never registered it, unlike the Channels, Search and Skills pages. It now registers the catalog the same way.
- **Warning:** on a fresh install, `models.authStatus` lists no providers. The catalog reports `acp-opencode` (ACP runtime, CLI not installed) and `openai` (no credentials) as unavailable. Auth status can't tell those apart from a set-up keyless local server, which also has no auth row. The view can tell, though: it knows whether any provider is connected and whether a default model is saved, so the rule lives there. Saved defaults with a momentarily empty catalog keep their warning, which an existing catalog test checks.
- **Title:** the dialog fell back to the raw id when the provider wasn't in the unconfigured list. It now falls back to `providerDisplayLabel`.

## Evidence

- **New real-Gateway E2E** (`model-providers-fresh-install.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`): a fresh install with default plugins and no keys.
  - Fails on main: the raw subtitle key is shown, and the visible alert reads "Couldn't load models from acp-opencode, openai."
  - Passes with this change: real subtitle and no alert.
- **`model-add-provider-to-chat` E2E** now checks the dialog title for a provider that has config. Main shows `tencent-tokenhub`; with this change it shows "Tencent Tokenhub".
- **`view.test.ts`:** a new case fails on main and passes after. With the same failure and an unconnected provider row, the fresh view stays quiet while a view with a saved default shows the alert.
- `ui/src/pages/model-providers` unit tests (250/250), `vitest-ui-e2e-config` and `ci-workflow-guards` pass.
- Related E2Es pass: `model-setup-provider-errors`, `model-key-save-check`, `model-providers` (mocked).
- Autoreview (Claude engine): no findings.
- CI skips the real-Gateway UI shards, so the E2E runs above are local.

**Not addressed:** the display label is derived from the id ("Tencent Tokenhub", where the vendor writes "TokenHub"). Fixing it means adding display names to the provider label table for each vendor, which is a separate change.

Before / after: the Models page on a fresh install, and the add dialog title.

prs.title: fix(telegram): show help for bare ACP commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: selecting `/acp` in Telegram opens an action keyboard whose Spawn button sends an incomplete command instead of explaining how to start an ACP session.

## User Impact

Bare `/acp` reaches the existing help response, including the harness ID and options needed for `/acp spawn`. Explicit commands and action autocomplete remain available. The shared registry also avoids incomplete ACP argument menus in Slack and Discord.

## Why This Change Was Made

ACP actions accept free-form arguments, so a one-click action menu cannot supply a complete command. Remove ACP's automatic menu at the shared definition rather than adding Telegram-specific handling. No ACP backend, authorization, or session-creation behavior changes.

## Evidence

- All 96 focused tests pass: registry (39), ACP help/lifecycle (38), and Telegram native delivery (19). The Telegram regression exercises `bot.handleUpdate` through the Bot API fixture and verifies that bare `/acp` is dispatched without an inline keyboard. Whole-file wall times: 13.43s, 19.62s, and 79.81s respectively; combined runner 124.48s. The existing Telegram file is slow because it exercises actual bot ingress, scheduling, persistence and delivery; the added test itself took 3.56s. Hosted CI timing is pending.
- The initial implementation run and independent reviewer reported both added regressions red before the fix and green afterward.
- Targeted format and typed lint pass for all three changed TypeScript files. `git diff --check` passes.
- Fresh Codex autoreview at P2: no actionable findings. Reviewed the complete 4-file patch against c50ff4fbe5410609d00066642c72213e4354ee23 on an existing authenticated Mac; SHA-256 of each reviewed working file matched the publishing checkout. The reviewer used an isolated reconstructed snapshot, not the full repository.
- Production LOC: +1/-1; regression tests: +25/-0. The separate 25-line test allocation covers the registry contract and actual Telegram delivery boundary.
- Live Telegram/ACP backend spawning is not claimed. The isolated Telegram Test Server doctor could not find authenticated Convex launchers or broker credentials; no live instance was changed or restarted.

<details>
<summary>Root-cause and source inspection</summary>

The shared ACP definition opted into automatic argument menus. Native transports consume that definition before command dispatch, intercepting bare `/acp` before its existing help handler. Action choices and argument parsing are retained. Reviewed the Telegram, Slack, and Discord consumers, the ACP help and lifecycle handlers, and current main; the same bad menu flag remains on main. No overlapping open fix was found by targeted PR search.

The retained automatic-menu line is traced to 9c7823350bf61ca2998920c72b31be3fd2de92c6 / #54088 (author and merger: @Takhoffman, 2026-03-25). This is provenance of the retained definition, not proof that it was the first user-visible occurrence.

</details>

prs.title: feat(models): customize provider names and artwork
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192792

## What Problem This Solves

Custom model providers need meaningful names and artwork throughout the Control UI without changing routing identities or exceeding the existing Chat boot budgets.

## User Impact

Operators can customize provider labels and artwork while model selection, account identity, catalog refreshes, and fallback icons keep using canonical provider data. This includes configured providers with no model rows. Quota identity and Usage links appear immediately; optional metrics and artwork cannot retire the composer if a chunk fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the credited maintainer replacement for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192792. The original branch reports `maintainerCanModify=false`, and the landing diff needed conflict resolution, one canonical provider-presentation path, and a boot-budget repair. The signed replacement source commit retains RoboClaw's author identity and Jacob Tomlinson's coauthor credit.

Provider presentation belongs to the existing authorized catalog producer and cache, not routing state or a second presentation store. The Settings page deliberately reads the configured catalog, so unrestricted, unfiltered configuration views now include provider presentation even without model rows. Session-, role-, provider-filtered, and `all` views retain their existing disclosure boundaries. Ordinary brand rendering stays eager; configured artwork, model-less reactive presentation, and quota metrics remain lazy. The quota slot retains its known row count and geometry while the Usage link and account identity stay usable.

Cloud-placement identity is a separate domain from model-provider identity. Its existing data and renderer now live in the neutral `route-controls-runtime` chunk instead of the shared model-provider icon module. No cache, compatibility reexport, new request, or increased budget is introduced.

## Evidence

- Exact source: `025885ba9a9d226e8cf11173ed897e2a6b2d5e4d`. Native baseline integration incorporates `c50ff4fbe5410609d00066642c72213e4354ee23`, preserves current-main restart/update notice tests plus the row-specific provider regression, and regenerates the owned config baselines.
- `pnpm config:docs:gen` and `pnpm config:docs:check` pass. The integrated divider/system-notice tests pass (36 tests).
- Gateway provider-presentation and role-policy tests cover empty configured models, default/configured/provider-config views, and session/provider/role filtering. The actual mounted Models-page loader/controller test proves an empty-model provider's admitted name and builtin icon display and refresh. The related Chat/Models-page UI run passes 148 tests.
- Provider artwork, alias, fallback, invalidation, and cloud-identity tests pass. A held metrics import preserves the Usage link, focus, and row count; a rejected presentation import preserves the composer and notice icons. The final cloud/provider/placement/chunking set passes 64 tests across six files.
- `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` passes: shared 1110 / New 132 / Chat 663 modules. The two cloud modules emit in the existing neutral controls chunk. Quota metrics and reactive provider presentation remain outside boot groups.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance:base c50ff4fbe5410609d00066642c72213e4354ee23` passes with one pinned toolchain: Chat 1,288,500 → 1,287,589 B normalized gzip (−911 B); New 797,116 → 797,373 B (+257 B); startup unchanged at 90,215 B. Requests remain 20 / 15 / 3. Largest shared JS is 560,072 B against the unchanged 560,350 B cap (278 B headroom); total CSS decreases 5 B.
- Fresh full-range review through `9582e703e1b30487059b21bcdf6a81e4f51a3e59` and exact final-delta review through `025885ba9a9d226e8cf11173ed897e2a6b2d5e4d` are scoped-clean, with final-source verification and no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Production LOC: +1,030/−333 (net +697); tests/support: +1,242/−161 (net +1,081). Production growth supplies the provider configuration/wire/authenticated-artwork capability and canonical presentation owner. The cloud split itself is net-neutral source restructuring.
- [Retained source visual and image-authority evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192792#issuecomment-6660246981) covers provider cards/pickers, builtin symbols, artwork and fallbacks. The replacement's [prior ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193952#issuecomment-6677212500) verified the image route and paired-token revocation test were byte-identical and marked that behavior proof sufficient. Its model-less Settings finding is repaired above. Hosted CI and the requested exact-final-head ClawSweeper review are tracked separately; older reviews are not presented as current-head clearance.

## Follow-up

- **Optional placement-dialog chunk isolation:** `ui/src/components/session-placement-move-dialog.tsx` still has pre-existing imports of `ui/src/pages/new-session/cloud-target.ts` and `draft-cloud-machine-state.ts`, which share the New renderer chunk. Those imports are unchanged by this PR. The new cloud identity modules are independently assigned to the neutral controls chunk, and measured Chat boot does not gain the New renderer. Removing the older optional-dialog coupling is separate follow-up work.

prs.title: fix(ui): prevent RTL boot shifts and measure configuration matrix
prs.body:
## Problem and change

The engine census previously fixed the browser to English, light appearance and device scale 1, leaving other supported configurations unmeasured. Add one-axis configuration selection to the existing harness: all built-in themes in light/dark, zh-CN/ar/de, device scales 2/3, reduced motion and forced colors. Runs retain configuration identity, rotate configurations and A/A controls, and record applied preferences, resource timing/bytes, fonts, computed styles and CLS. Usage and streaming selectors now work with translated labels.

The census exposed an Arabic startup layout shift: the critical frame painted left-to-right before the lazy locale catalog applied RTL. Generate initial direction in the existing Vite locale plugin before the body paints, using the canonical saved/system locale policy. Translation loading, active locale and document language keep their existing owner and successful-load behavior.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Configuration parser | 18 tests passed |
| Real Vite HTML / pre-body direction | 49 tests passed; five new cases fail on base |
| Typechecks | UI, scripts and UI-app test leaf passed |
| Targeted lint / production Knip | Passed |
| Configuration screen | 540 observations: 539 passed; one baseline WebKit streaming ResizeObserver notification retained for confirmation |
| RTL fix | 480/480 passed: 20 rotated base/head/base-A/A pairs; cold/warm, English/Arabic, Chromium/WebKit; 100 ms profile |
| Independent local review | Actionable findings resolved; final delta clean |

### RTL paired results

Each cell has 20 samples. Readiness uses the later of transcript/composer readiness and configured-locale application. Numbers are median / p95 milliseconds. This is a layout-stability fix; no latency speedup is claimed.

| Browser | Locale / boot | Base readiness | Head readiness | Head median delta | A/A median delta | Base → head CLS median |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| chromium | en / cold | 956.9 / 989.4 | 964.5 / 979.0 | +0.80% | -0.33% | 0.001469 → 0.001469 |
| chromium | ar / cold | 1000.1 / 1031.5 | 997.2 / 1030.3 | -0.29% | -0.91% | 0.708414 → 0.000411 |
| chromium | en / warm | 713.1 / 723.7 | 712.6 / 726.4 | -0.07% | +0.31% | 0.000396 → 0.000396 |
| chromium | ar / warm | 967.9 / 974.5 | 968.5 / 975.0 | +0.06% | -0.06% | 0.749007 → 0.000341 |
| webkit | en / cold | 1065.0 / 1099.0 | 1069.0 / 1123.0 | +0.38% | -0.28% | unavailable |
| webkit | ar / cold | 1195.0 / 1230.0 | 1196.5 / 1227.0 | +0.13% | +0.59% | unavailable |
| webkit | en / warm | 746.0 / 770.0 | 749.0 / 772.0 | +0.40% | +0.60% | unavailable |
| webkit | ar / warm | 850.5 / 884.0 | 867.5 / 890.0 | +2.00% | +1.12% | unavailable |

Readiness medians stayed within −0.3% to +2.0%; p95 changes ranged from −1.1% to +2.2%. Arabic CLS fell by >99.9%. Chromium has a small unrelated header/label shift in both sides; WebKit has no CLS API here.

All five Chromium candidate-confirmation groups have completed (260 observations). None confirms a configuration slowdown above 20%; repeated typing, Usage filtering, picker and warm-boot candidates returned near default. Streaming CPU is close to default (scale 3 task CPU +4.26%); A/A frame tails are noisy, so frame-tail differences are not attributed. WebKit confirmations and the bounded Chromium 6× pass continue. The screen is not presented as proof of configuration regressions.

### Confirmed locale transport cost

The separate 100 ms locale comparison passed all 200 observations (10 rotations per browser/locale/boot cell, plus English A/A). Localized warm readiness is measurably later:

| Browser | English | zh-CN | Arabic | German | English A/A change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chromium | 708.7 ms | 967.1 ms (+36.48%) | 967.4 ms (+36.51%) | 966.2 ms (+36.34%) | +0.29% |
| WebKit | 723.5 ms | 835.0 ms (+15.41%) | 847.0 ms (+17.07%) | 832.5 ms (+15.07%) | −0.76% |

All 30 Chromium warm locale samples have no completed namespace requests at raw composer readiness and 14 completed namespaces at localized readiness. By localized readiness, JS counts are 38 versus 21 default; encoded JS bytes are 1,196,529 (zh-CN), 1,203,597 (Arabic), and 1,200,712 (German), versus 1,109,214 default. The additional graph includes the locale entry, lazy-catalog helper and namespace files. The same bundled Latin font is fetched; no extra downloaded CJK/Arabic font explains the delay. System glyph fallback is not identified by the computed font-family list.

Follow-up priority: trace and overlap required locale/catalog work, and defer namespaces that do not serve the active page, while preserving lazy boundaries and replacement behavior. This PR fixes the independently proven RTL shift; it does not claim to remove the locale request phase. Theme/media confirmation and the Chromium 6× screen continue separately.

### CI lifecycle synchronization repair

Run 42162495922 at `5486b60e9bb` failed the allowlisted Skill Workshop enable case when its final external disable raced unfinished plugin lifecycle work (`UNAVAILABLE`, `mutationAccepted: false`). The latest completed scheduled main run 42156649901 passed the same case, so this is not labeled inherited.

The test now joins the successful browser `plugins.setEnabled` response before reloading and issuing another mutation. Runtime publication intentionally precedes activation/cache/lease cleanup; the RPC response follows it. Existing user-visible and durability assertions stay intact. No retry or production change was added. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 finding. The exact previously failing case passed locally: 7.2 s test body, 49.2 s Vitest duration (runtime preparation separate); the other case was intentionally excluded by the failure filter. E2E test typecheck and test-line ratchet passed.

Both sides built on the same machine. No ceiling or baseline is raised.

| Surface | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 90,280 B | 90,280 B | 0 |
| Startup CSS gzip / requests | 36,574 B / 1 | 36,574 B / 1 | 0 |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,289,152 B | 1,289,152 B | 0 |
| New boot JS gzip | 796,962 B | 796,962 B | 0 |
| HTML gzip | 10,859 B | 11,291 B | +432 B; no extra request |

After integrating main at `65bdef354387`, both final bundles were rebuilt for the size comparison; the direction change is unchanged. WebKit does not expose the Layout Instability API, so its CLS is unavailable rather than zero. Browser resource sizes are distinct from the normalized gzip budget numbers. Streaming comparisons include responsiveness metrics rather than treating the fixed stream duration as latency.

The simplification pass removed a redundant runtime direction companion: HTML owns initial direction; the translation owner retains interactive changes. The 148-line allocation covers parser/RTL regression proof and the existing real-Gateway test’s response barrier.

prs.title: perf(ui): skip unchanged operator accent publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An unchanged Gateway config receipt reapplies the operator accent palette. The presentation owner clears and rewrites document-wide CSS variables and samples computed colors, forcing style work across an otherwise unchanged page.

## User Impact

Repeated equal config receipts retain the applied accent. A changed operator accent, user override, theme change, or new document still uses the existing presentation path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skip publication when the operator seam and document root are unchanged. This is a six-line check in the existing owner; it adds no scheduler, shared cache, or invalidation lifecycle. User/theme accent calls remain independent.

## Evidence

Acceptance: production bundles, synthetic Gateway, headless desktop Chromium and WebKit; 20 rotated base/head/base triplets per engine, Activity and Secrets equal-config targets, Usage sort control. Judge Chromium script/style/task CPU and WebKit application elapsed; no attributable control regression beyond the 5% band, with A/A controls on the same loaded host. Instrumented census/profile samples are separate from uninstrumented acceptance.

All 360 observations passed. Values are median / p95 milliseconds.

| Target and metric | Base | Head | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Activity: Chromium style CPU | 46.226 / 47.590 | 0.666 / 0.766 | −98.6% |
| Activity: Chromium task CPU | 97.349 / 101.382 | 48.351 / 52.947 | −50.3% |
| Activity: Chromium script CPU | 36.173 / 38.452 | 34.919 / 38.452 | −3.5% |
| Activity: Chromium application | 125.200 / 139.300 | 125.350 / 126.800 | +0.1% |
| Activity: WebKit application | 281 / 291 | 125 / 127 | −55.5% |
| Secrets: Chromium style CPU | 76.053 / 78.388 | 0.287 / 0.397 | −99.6% |
| Secrets: Chromium task CPU | 100.470 / 105.407 | 21.468 / 24.491 | −78.6% |
| Secrets: Chromium script CPU | 11.889 / 13.094 | 11.200 / 12.758 | −5.8% |
| Secrets: Chromium application | 107.200 / 107.800 | 107.300 / 108.400 | +0.1% |
| Secrets: WebKit application | 367 / 378 | 107 / 109 | −70.8% |

The unchanged A/A base matches: Activity style 46.226/45.746ms and WebKit 281/280.5ms; Secrets style 76.053/75.908ms and WebKit 367/368.5ms. The existing config debounce bounds Chromium elapsed time even after the style work disappears.

Usage control now has 30 rotated triplets per engine (the initial 20 plus 10 additional control pairs). Chromium script CPU was 9.960/10.406 → 9.936/10.717 ms and task CPU 61.391/65.331 → 61.823/65.608 ms; the identical-base control task CPU was 61.115/65.386 ms. Chromium application was 128.2/151.7 → 131.2/182.3 ms: +2.3% median, with a noisy +20.2% p95. WebKit application was 161.5/241 → 149.5/190 ms; the identical-base control was 161.5/198 ms, itself a 21.7% p95 spread. One Chromium head control sample spent 401.7 ms elapsed but only 66.261 ms task CPU. The unchanged control never enters the operator-accent path. Per the loaded-host rule, acceptance uses the stable CPU and structural control rather than claiming clean elapsed tails. Shared-host load 1 was roughly 11–18.

Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --control-bundle-dir <base> --engines chromium,webkit --viewport desktop --steps page-activity-push,page-secrets-push,data-usage-sort --pairs 20`. Instrumentation stays off for this run.

- Regression: one case checks zero style writes for an equal seam, real changed-seam writes, user override priority, and restoring the latest seam. Base fails; head has 6 passing tests.
- Fresh current-main paired production builds and strict comparison pass: startup 90,280 → 90,280 B gzip, one CSS request. Total CSS is unchanged at 324,697 B; chat boot JS falls 1,289,152 → 1,288,946 B. Existing base cap excesses add no growth; no size ceiling changes.
- Fresh profile attributes the old cost to operator seam → accent application, including style reads. Relative-time formatting stays live.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Solid checklist: no effects, listeners, DOM queries, owner APIs, or flush calls added to production.

| Touched LOC | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Presentation owner | 300 | 306 |
| Presentation tests | 290 | 320 |
| Test allocation | 0 | 1 |
| Existing favicon browser test | 489 | 492 |

Inspected before/after screenshots and computed-style evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193954#issuecomment-6677231890. The four complete synthetic captures are byte-identical within each engine; document and row styles match.

CI follow-up: the first full run found that the favicon test relied on an equal environment update incidentally clearing a manually injected primary color. It now explicitly resets through the existing accent owner before checking the theme palette. Production theme/mascot updates already use that owner. The disabled-field Chromium assertion fix from main (#193949) is merged; it waits for the browser to blur a newly disabled control. No runtime changes were added by these corrections. Fresh P0–P2 review is clean. The two focused browser files passed locally (favicon 9/9, form controls 21/21); replacement CI run 42166093235 has a successful ci-gate CheckRun, including both repaired UI shards. The legacy ci-gate status subsequently completed and native auto-merge merged the exact reviewed head without an admin exception.
