When idle close reuses a posted answer, reasoning stays with opening prose on the preview card when both fit, and otherwise follows the answer once. With block and preview streaming on, quoted and list-opened `block` tables after prose post once in tested batches. A fenced example of the table no longer splits the card.

With tables off, a partly accepted fallback or recovery prose card lets later text send without replaying its content. A final whose remainder is rejected whole reports accepted receipts and sends its attachment. Only the idle close keeps that failure bare, so the matching final still sends only the remainder. A thrown close can leave a stale preview visible and unreported. The unchanged post renderer draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

In `block`, the table post names retained prose and tail at close. A later extension, final, block or retry sends only what follows an accepted prose tail, and a later final or block that repeats it names it. A preview that ends the run with no later final or block reports its late post to no caller. Block post receipts carry their image. A recovery card carries only added prose. Receipts list IDs in creation order. After settlement, a new message keeps its equal tail and repeated prefix. An overlapping message boundary can lose or interleave preview text. A retry after a rejected late chunk keeps prose accepted before a soft line break. An accepted converted table repeats on retry. A new row checks the following sentence arrives once. With tables off, idle does not retry the rest. Plain-table early drains repeat preview text. Main's #192482 owns the double tail of a completed card, and this PR keeps that behavior. With tables off, preview-only closes still omit receipts.

## Why this change was made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Core calls the channel's `beforeSendAttempt` hook before recording a formatted send as started, so recovery can resend after a stop during Feishu's first runtime load. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. It declares `block` as Feishu's table default.

The generated channel baseline gains two entries, `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. The core and plugin counts are main's. This exception is not maintainer approval. The allocation covers 7,153 net test lines for table conversion, chunking, receipts and recovery. The PR leaves the shared scalar alone. Baseline cuts consume headroom.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` at `b8952d477f0c` seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. Proof head `effbf8c7a8ab` used that state and main `29fc232d40be` a copy, in fresh worktrees with separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both Gateways exit 78 on the schema 24 agent database until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. Both databases stay readable. The cause is undiagnosed. This proves compatibility, not a clean upgrade. Credentials were synthetic, with Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object stays byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff adds no `src/state` change or migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof at stable `b8952d477f0c` and main `29fc232d40be` resolves `code` for unconfigured and legacy-only accounts, but `auto` routes pipe-bordered tables to raw cards with native grids. Legacy keys do not select the mode. Proof head `effbf8c7a8ab` resolves `block`, retaining those grids. Other modes convert before routing.

Standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, quoted and list-opened tables take posts. Messages needing multiple static cards also take posts, using `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments convert raw rows to `code`.

A `code` default fences those grids in cards, shown at `outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:662` in `948b2088919`. `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:126-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

Hosted CI on `d56ccf17129e` merged with main `0cc3586362cb` passed 79 checks, with 52 skipped and neutral CodeQL. No hosted CI result is claimed for `f1acbc1dfb87`.

Local runs passed 1,533 Feishu tests and the extension type lanes at `d56ccf17129e`, and 272 Feishu database-worker tests and 179 core delivery tests at `cea11348420c`. The generated-file checks passed on `f1acbc1dfb87` with the matching install. Typed lint, formatting and `tsgo:scripts` last passed at `ff39b7bb3adc`. All ten ratchets against `c50ff4fbe541` passed, test-lines with 163 lines of slack. The PR adds 7,153 lines and matching credit. Main's seven #192482 rows pass. Five upstream rows fail with old test setups. Updated rows preserve their assertions.

### Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. They compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49` and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Later merges retain those rendering files and the off-mode projection. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping changed, so that row rests on regression tests rather than these captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds one reasoning-only post and keeps two receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The captures used no Gateway or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Results apply to the named commits.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` rejected `tables` with exit 1 and refused Gateway startup with exit 78. At `08c0c469de4`, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and Doctor kept the Markdown keys.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042), real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.

prs.title: fix(zalouser): sanitize outbound tool traces
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem / value:** Zalo Personal's custom monitor callback bypasses its standard adapter, so a `message_sending` hook can reintroduce internal tool traces immediately before transport. This patch keeps recipient text and captions clean while preserving configured Markdown-table rendering.
- **Relevance:** Independent P1/security report #90684 tracks this leakage class. Merged #112621 sanitizes the standard adapter only; current `main` still leaves this distinct callback seam open.
- **Smallest complete fix / review map:** Keep configured table conversion in `delivery.preparePayload`, where durable final delivery sees it, and sanitize only the effective post-hook payload in the custom callback. Scope is 4 files, `+76/-20`: two small helpers, two focused regressions, and the boundary wiring.
- **Risk / proof:** Risk is limited to ordering between two existing transforms. Exact head `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`; full Zalouser `221/221`; changed-file format/lint, extension production/test types, branch ratchets, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass. The exact deterministic wrapper has only untouched frozen-base Codex/dead-export debt.
- **External proof limit:** Authenticated recipient-visible transport is `blocked_external` because no safe configured account/recipient route exists. Exact-head tests reach both lifecycle boundaries; no live send is claimed.
- **Non-goals:** Standard adapter, sanitizer parser dialects, Zalo Bot, authentication, configuration schema, and protocol changes.
- **Maintainer ask:** Please apply `no-stale` while authenticated recipient proof is coordinated; the assigned-PR age clock otherwise ignores substantive updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Zalo Personal's custom inbound-reply path in `monitor.ts` can deliver a post-hook payload without passing through the standard outbound adapter. That leaves one route for compact tool-failure lines or tool XML to reach recipients. The repair must also preserve `channels.zalouser.markdown.tables` for final replies handled by durable delivery. Related: #90684.

## User Impact

Recipients get intended assistant text and media without internal tool-trace scaffolding, while existing table preferences such as `markdown.tables: "bullets"` continue to apply to durable final replies. Ordinary prose, captions, chunking, and media delivery remain unchanged; users have no migration step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `delivery.preparePayload` owns configured table conversion before the lifecycle can return through durable delivery.
- The private custom callback owns sanitization after `message_sending`, so a supported hook cannot reintroduce internal traces.
- Merged #112621 covers the standard adapter only; this remains a narrow, distinct callback repair.

## Evidence

- Exact signed candidate head: `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9` on frozen maintenance base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/zalouser`: `33` files and `317/317` tests passing, including configured bullet-table preparation before durable delivery and post-hook trace sanitization at custom delivery.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passing.
- Changed Zalouser scope passes type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Repository-wide extension lint's only failure is unchanged frozen-base debt in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` (`max-lines`).
- Deterministic `openclaw-pre-pr.sh` gate: passed for frozen base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`, exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`, and merge tree `1d2e0ad6dc09fd07dfa21423c38602b80e92ae9d`.
- Current-`main` negative control: the custom monitor callback still resolves and delivers the post-hook payload directly. This head restores pre-durable table preparation and sanitizes immediately before custom text/caption resolution.
- Remaining proof state is `blocked_external`, not a claimed live pass: authenticated recipient-visible proof still requires a safe Zalo Personal account and recipient route.

AI-assisted change, manually reviewed and validated.
## Exact-head refresh (2026-10-26)

<!-- clawsean-head-refresh-2026-10-26 -->
The current signed PR head is `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`, rebuilt on frozen base `f4a0d4875912103be54dd672e32db17064d003db` with a four-file patch and clean merge tree `f44ddf096cf52e14aadcf50b892f2ea4b8765eee`.

- Disposable Linux/arm64 proof used Node 24.22.1 and a fresh frozen-lockfile install; the full Zalouser suite passed `221/221` across 30 files.
- Changed-file format/lint, production and test extension typechecks, conflict/line-cap/assertion/SQLite/plugin-boundary ratchets, doctor-contract tests, media/runtime guards, and import-cycle checks passed.
- Independent exact-diff review found no P0-P2 findings. GitHub and the fork ref read back this exact head, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass with none pending or failed.
- Authenticated recipient-visible Zalo proof remains externally blocked: no consented safe recipient route is available, so no private recipient was used and no live-send claim is made. The deterministic negative path, exact-head full suite, and hosted execution are the strongest contributor-safe evidence currently possible.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(android): make sidebar session parentage explicit
prs.body:
Related: #150054 — Android-specific context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150054#issuecomment-5848447065

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs an unambiguous choice between starting a new root chat and creating a child of the selected chat. Previously, implicit Gateway parentage could make a supposedly independent chat a child, while explicit children and grandchildren could appear at root in Threads.

## User Impact

- The sidebar header **+** starts an independent root session. There is no second, competing independent-session button.
- The selected eligible session's overflow menu offers **New child session**. Children and grandchildren retain their hierarchy in Threads.
- Existing sessions are not migrated or reparented. Connection, busy-state, write-access, and selected-parent guards remain.
- These creation actions require a Gateway supporting the new intent fields. An older Gateway gets an update-required error; the app does not silently fall back to different parentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair carries explicit child intent through creation, persisted session metadata, reset preservation, list/describe/event projection, and Android rendering. Ordinary New sends `independent: true`; child creation sends `explicitChild: true` with the selected parent. Existing upstream standalone/direct-chat behavior and visibility admission remain intact.

The public API rejects conflicting independent/parent intent and adoption of existing keys. A review-discovered edge case is also fixed: explicit child creation without a key cannot take the main-session reset shortcut and reset its parent.

This is an Android proposal, not a web Control UI `/new` change. **Maintainer acceptance of the public `sessions.create` fields and Android product behavior remains separate from this repair.** No upstream merge is requested by this update.

## Evidence

### Final conflict refresh — October 31

prs.title: fix(telegram): drop native commands from DM senders dmPolicy does not admit
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a stranger's ordinary DM is dropped silently, but their builtin native command (`/think`, `/login`, ...) gets the reply `You are not authorized to use this command.` — confirming to an unknown sender that a bot is listening. Scoped direct-chat allowlists could still reach an earlier refusal even after the first repair.

## User Impact
Unadmitted DM senders, including senders excluded by a scoped direct-chat allowlist, are now ignored for native commands exactly as they are for ordinary messages. Senders admitted by dmPolicy but denied by `commands.allowFrom` keep the deliberate refusal; explicit command grants, owners, and group-command behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Native dispatch has more than one visible authorization-refusal boundary. A scoped direct `allowFrom` rejection happens during base-access evaluation, before final command authorization, so a final-only silence check left that path visible. The shared refusal path now applies the same DM-admission decision at every visible boundary. The final gate uses the latest owner result, while earlier boundaries preserve their existing explicit-grant and scoped-restriction semantics.

## Evidence
- Registered Bot pipeline with an owned loopback Bot API fixture: on the previous head, scoped-direct `/think` still produced the refusal (base-red). After the repair, account-level and scoped excluded senders produce no outbound reply and start no turn. An admitted command-denied sender still receives the refusal, an explicitly authorized sender retains the `/think` argument menu, and the existing group refusal regression stays green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against `bot-native-command-dispatch.routing.test.ts`, `.delivery.test.ts`, and `.concurrency.test.ts`: 38/38 passed. `bot-native-commands.registry.test.ts`: 8/8 passed, including `requireAuth:false` plugin commands. Node 24.22.1.
- Both extension production and extension-test tsgo lanes passed. Targeted extension lint completed with 0 warnings/errors across 292 rules, oxfmt passed, the SQLite worker ratchet passed against the PR merge base, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader local coverage is not claimed green: `pnpm test:extension telegram` timed out after 30 minutes with the first 11 files passing and no observed test failure; it did not finish. The full changed-check also reports existing dead-export findings outside this diff.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof was not run: the standalone doctor found no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair, so no live trace or live cleanup is claimed. Independent `autoreview` produced no verdict because Codex returned HTTP 403.

prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore native commands from senders the DM policy rejects
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves

With `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a normal message from a sender who is not on the list is dropped. The same sender's native command (`/status` and the rest of the menu) got the reply "You are not authorized to use this command." That tells a stranger a bot is listening.

## User Impact

Senders the DM policy does not admit get no reply to native commands, the same as for ordinary messages. A sender who is admitted but is not allowed to run the command still gets the refusal. Pairing still replies, so a first contact can finish the challenge. `commands.allowFrom` denials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#131408 made the refusal text deliberate for a channel-admitted sender who lacks command permission. This path was also used when `dmPolicy` itself rejected the sender. The command authorization result now carries that distinction, and the native-command dispatch returns without sending when the denial is `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` or `dm_policy_disabled`.

## Evidence

Regression in `src/channels/message-access/telegram-native-owner.test.ts`: a native command as sender 300 with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and `allowFrom: ["999999"]` must not call the handler and must not send a message. The existing owner-admission cases still expect the refusal text.

I could not run the OpenClaw suite on this machine. CI is the run that counts.

prs.title: fix(markdown): NaN chunk limit silently drops the whole outbound message
prs.body:
Closes #193928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an outbound message can silently vanish when a channel plugin passes a `NaN` text-chunk limit, because `chunkText`/`chunkTextRanges` treat `NaN` as a real bound — every comparison against `NaN` is false, the first range ends at `NaN`, and callers that slice by the returned ranges send an empty string. `chunkMarkdownIR` returns no chunks at all for the same reason.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin and channel-adapter authors using the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking` surface no longer lose an entire message to a bad computed limit (`Number(envValue)`, arithmetic on optional settings); the text is delivered whole instead, matching the documented "non-positive limit returns the original text" contract. No behavior change for any finite limit, so first-party channels (which resolve limits through the already-guarded `resolveTextChunkLimit`) are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeChunkLimit` in `packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.ts` let `NaN` fall through unchanged (`Number.isFinite(NaN)` is false), and the NaN value then defeated every downstream guard. Non-finite limits now take the non-positive path, keeping the text whole. This is the single owner of the broken normalization: fixing it there also repairs `chunkMarkdownIR`, which delegates to `chunkText`. The sibling helpers in `src/shared/text-chunking.ts` already return whole text for `NaN`, so this also removes a divergence between the two chunking implementations. The deliberately loud per-character `NaN` behavior of `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` (pinned by `render-aware-chunking.test.ts`) is intentionally left untouched.

## Evidence

Environment: Windows 11, Node v24.16.0, source checkout at `main` ce8b7add7b00 (2026.11.1).

Repro executed against the real package sources with the repo's tsx runner (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs repro.mjs`):

Before (main):

```
chunkText(text, NaN)            -> [""]
chunkTextRanges(text, {NaN})    -> [{"start":0,"end":null}]
sliced via ranges (plugin view) -> [""]
chunkMarkdownIR(ir, NaN) texts  -> []
```

After (this branch):

```
chunkText(text, NaN)            -> ["Hello from OpenClaw — this outbound message must never vanish."]
chunkTextRanges(text, {NaN})    -> [{"start":0,"end":62}]
sliced via ranges (plugin view) -> ["Hello from OpenClaw — this outbound message must never vanish."]
chunkMarkdownIR(ir, NaN) texts  -> ["Hello from OpenClaw — this outbound message must never vanish."]
```

Tests:

- New regression test in `packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-text.test.ts` fails on main (`[""]` / `{start: 0, end: NaN}`) and passes with the fix.
- Full `packages/markdown-core` suite: 11 files / 197 tests pass (`vitest run`), including `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` with its pinned NaN behavior intact. Focused runs of `src/plugin-sdk/text-chunking.test.ts` and `src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts` (81 tests) pass via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Targeted gates green: `tsgo:core` typecheck, type-aware `oxlint` (0 warnings/errors), `oxfmt --check`, and the test-lines/max-lines/line-cap ratchets.

Not tested: live channel sends (Telegram/Zalo) — no first-party caller passes `NaN` today; the affected surface is the public plugin SDK contract, exercised here through the real package entrypoints.

This change is AI-assisted (Kimi Code) and fully tested as described above.

prs.title: fix(devices): avoid stale-request errors when clearing pending repairs
prs.body:
Closes #127622

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw devices clear --yes --pending` empties the pairing table but reports `unknown requestId` when a paired device also has a pending repair request.

## User Impact

Clear succeeds for paired repairs and reports the exact committed device/request IDs in one JSON document. Device-token callers retain their existing self-only and role restrictions. A transaction failure leaves pairing and bootstrap state unchanged.

The CLI requires a Gateway supporting `device.pair.clear`. Its handshake capability check refuses an older Gateway before sending any deletion, with an actionable update/restart message. There is no sequential legacy fallback. If post-commit worker cleanup fails, the result retains the committed IDs, includes `cleanupFailedDevices`, and exits 1 so operators can inspect Gateway logs.

**Maintainer decisions still required:** accept this new RPC/Gateway-upgrade compatibility requirement and provide the security-sensitive review for the current head. This PR does not claim either approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

The former CLI loop read a snapshot, removed a paired device (also deleting its repair), then tried to reject the stale request ID. The new RPC selects and clears through the existing SQLite worker transaction, capturing repair IDs before cascading removal. It preserves bootstrap/APNS cleanup, notifications, live authority checks, and credential revocation. Default clear also revokes the bootstrap credentials of repairs removed with their paired device, while leaving unrelated pending requests and credentials intact. The caller receives its final result before its removed connection closes; no database schema or permission expansion is required.

## Evidence

Current repair: head `c2eca741fbcc0ec2b14aec4d71b6d0afa80372a8`, merged with main `78e97d169703a32ee97221f91593ab20200bc05f`. Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.19.0, pinned pnpm 12.12.1; local Vitest uses the documented `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` option.

- Resolved both merge conflicts using main's current Gateway capability-test table and consolidated device-handler mocks. Retained the PR's capability refusal, response-before-close behavior, and main's newer lifecycle cleanup. A merge simulation against subsequently advanced main `45c780ab54` was clean.
- Reproduced and fixed a credential-revocation bug: default clear (`pending=false`) cascaded paired repair requests but left their bound bootstrap credentials valid. The regression issues and verifies real bootstrap credentials through the production owner. Before the fix, the removed repair's credential still returned `ok: true`; after the fix it returns `bootstrap_token_invalid`, while an unrelated pending device's credential remains valid. Revocation now occurs in the same SQLite transaction as pairing/APNS removal. The SQL-failure regression checks rollback with both pending flags.
- The focused CLI, transport, worker, handler, dispatcher, method-registry, and real-Gateway suites passed **272 tests across 11 files** in 44.05s wrapper time. These include the real WebSocket/SQLite proofs for mixed operator/node denial and queued clear after a real admin client's credential-revocation RPC. Both preserve pairing, repair, and bootstrap state when authority is refused; their authorization and database owners are not stubbed.
- Production core and infra test type checks passed. Gateway methods/root test type graphs also passed on the merged candidate. Type-aware lint on all 22 changed TypeScript files, formatting on all 24 changed files, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- `PROTOCOL_SINCE_BASE_SHA=78e97d169703a32ee97221f91593ab20200bc05f pnpm protocol:check` passed: registry, generated schema, Swift/Kotlin contract determinism, and the new method's `2026.10` release train. The method table exceeded the current lint line limit; extracting its existing unadvertised observation policy resolves that without changing behavior. An executable comparison confirmed all **551 existing method descriptors** exactly match merged main, with only the new `device.pair.clear` row added.
- Fresh independent review after the credential fix completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final policy-constant extraction is covered by the descriptor-equivalence check. Tests and static review are separate evidence.
- Simplification: reuse the existing pairing transaction, admission, revocation, and publication owners; no new schema, production test hook, or legacy fallback. Whole PR delta against merged main: production +228/-39, tests +698/-12, docs +18/-0. The remaining cross-layer growth provides the atomic clear operation and its distinct authority, transaction, transport, and cleanup proofs.

**Current-head verification (2026-10-21):** [CI for `c2eca741fbcc0ec2b14aec4d71b6d0afa80372a8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39461668212) completed successfully, including its aggregate CI job; no CI job failed. GitHub reported the PR as mergeable, and an independent merge simulation against main `d2590fe90720b0ed6cae0b2f1fbd62602d082e80` completed without conflicts. No source change or CI rerun was needed for this status check.

The remaining red commit statuses are `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and the security-aware `openclaw/ci-gate`. Both explicitly report that a maintainer must approve the current PR revision. The [Security Review workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39466560699) itself completed successfully and intentionally published these blocked statuses; this is an outstanding human approval, not a failing build or test.

### ClawSweeper before-merge checklist reconciliation (2026-10-21)

The [visible ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167137#issuecomment-6058069453) reviewed `24b59415d4e1ee6b06c4445aab624be5c33bdc11`, not current head `c2eca741fbcc0ec2b14aec4d71b6d0afa80372a8`. Its five unchecked items overlap; evidence submission and reviewer acceptance are separate steps.

| Bot checklist item | Current evidence / remaining action |
| --- | --- |
| Add real behavior proof | The two production-path authority scenarios below are present and passed on the current head. The PR body now includes their command, output and final-state assertions. **Fresh ClawSweeper review requested:** [re-review request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167137#issuecomment-6316237688) posted for current head `c2eca741fbcc0ec2b14aec4d71b6d0afa80372a8`; awaiting the updated assessment. |

| Complete next step | The same outstanding maintainer security approval as item 2; not a second code defect or separate approval. |
| Resolve maintainer decision | **Pending a recorded maintainer decision** accepting the new Gateway RPC requirement and refusal of older Gateways without a sequential fallback. |

Current-head authority proof was rerun on 2026-10-21 using the isolated Gateway harness, synthetic credentials and temporary SQLite state:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.device-pair-clear-authz.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

Selected output (startup/cleanup logs omitted):

```text
PASS preserves paired repairs and bootstrap state when a non-admin mixed-role device clears (205ms)
PASS refuses the queued clear after another client revokes its caller (41ms)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       2 passed (2)
Duration    33.60s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 36.64s
```

- [Mixed operator/node denial](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c2eca741fbcc0ec2b14aec4d71b6d0afa80372a8/src/gateway/server.device-pair-clear-authz.test.ts#L75): a real paired mixed-role device connects with its operator token and only `operator.pairing` scope. Its WebSocket clear RPC returns `device pairing clear denied`. The complete pairing/pending snapshot and bound bootstrap context equal their pre-request values.
- [Actual revocation while clear is queued](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c2eca741fbcc0ec2b14aec4d71b6d0afa80372a8/src/gateway/server.device-pair-clear-authz.test.ts#L106): the existing pairing lock holds work while a separate authenticated admin client's real `device.token.revoke` RPC and the device client's clear RPC queue in that order. Releasing the lock commits revocation; queued clear rejects with `DevicePairingAuthorityRefusedError`. Pending requests and all paired device IDs remain unchanged, the caller's token has a real `revokedAtMs`, and the bound bootstrap context is unchanged. The test intentionally permits the administrator's revocation; it does not claim that revocation leaves the entire database unchanged.
- The test harness starts the actual Gateway and uses the production authentication, pairing admission and SQLite owners. The queued-case spies forward unchanged arguments/results to the real clear/revoke functions and only observe ordering. They do not supply a mocked permission decision or database result. Unrelated model/channel services are isolated by the standard Gateway harness. The source and final-state assertions therefore address the bot's specific concern about mocked handler owners and injected authority callbacks.

**Proposed compatibility decision:** accept the Gateway upgrade requirement, preserving capability refusal before any mutation and the actionable update/restart message. A sequential fallback would reintroduce the non-atomic operation behind the original stale-request/partial-result problem. This is the contributor's proposal and matches the bot's recommendation; it is **not recorded maintainer acceptance**.

prs.title: fix(macos): Dashboard widgets fail to load over Remote over SSH
prs.body:
Fixes #145522

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dashboard widgets and MCP Apps stay on "Waiting for the connection" (or "Widget sandbox host is unavailable") when the macOS app connects to a loopback-only Gateway through Remote over SSH.

## User Impact

User impact: widgets and MCP Apps load over Remote over SSH without a manual `ssh -L` for the sandbox port.

The app opens a second SSH connection for the widget sandbox. `BatchMode=yes` means it never asks for a password or a 2FA code. Setups that confirm each SSH sign-in, such as an agent approval dialog or a security-key touch, ask twice when the app connects.

## Why This Change Was Made

Widgets load from the remote Gateway's sandbox listener, on the Gateway port plus one. Without `mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin`, the Control UI looks for that listener on the tunnel host at the same port number. The app's tunnel forwards only the Gateway port, so nothing answers there.

The tunnel manager also keeps a sandbox forward, `127.0.0.1:P` on this Mac to `127.0.0.1:P` on the remote host, in its own `ssh` process:

- **Kept apart from the Gateway connection.** If the sandbox forward can't bind or exits, the app logs it and tries again later. The Gateway tunnel and its route stay as they are. The forward is retired together with the Gateway route.
- **Checked before binding.** The app opens the forward only when nothing listens on `127.0.0.1:P` or the wildcard address. The bind address is explicit, so the ssh_config options `GatewayPorts` and `AddressFamily` can't move it. When the port is in use, or belongs to a Gateway this Mac hosts beside the remote primary, the app skips the forward and logs why. It checks again on later Gateway route lookups and waits at least 30 seconds after a failed attempt.
- **Hosting beside a remote primary.** A tunnel that holds the hosted Gateway's ports is retired before that Gateway starts. Ports are reserved only while hosting is on.

Limits:

- A remote `mcp.apps.sandboxPort` other than the default isn't forwarded. Set `mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin` on the remote Gateway instead.
- With hosting on in the default layout, the hosted Gateway owns the adjacent port, so widgets from the remote Gateway stay unavailable.
- An `AddressFamily inet6` ssh_config entry for the host makes the IPv4 sandbox bind fail. Only the widget forward fails, and the app logs it.
- If a wildcard listener appears between the port check and ssh's bind, it can coexist with the loopback forward.

## Evidence

Live run at 6c66f5f: a remote Gateway (`openclaw@2026.11.1`, loopback only) ran in a macOS VM with an HTML widget on its Dashboard. On the host, two system `ssh` processes used the options `RemotePortTunnel` builds: the Gateway forward `18789:127.0.0.1:18789`, and the widget forward `127.0.0.1:18790:127.0.0.1:18790` in its own process. The Control UI loaded through them in headless Chromium.

With only the Gateway process running, the sandbox request to `127.0.0.1:18790` fails with `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, and the Dashboard stays on "Waiting for the connection":

![Dashboard waiting for the connection with only the Gateway SSH process](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fbba562a-1467-4d8a-9700-865431b0995a)

With both processes running, the widget forward listens on `127.0.0.1:18790` only, and the widget loads and runs its script:

![Widget rendered through the separate widget SSH process](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d4157b7-2724-4726-a722-9ee4286c357a)

After the widget `ssh` process exits, the Gateway process keeps running and the Control UI still answers with HTTP 200.

Tests:

- `RemoteTunnelManager` fixture: compiles the real tunnel manager against a stand-in SSH process. It checks that a failing or missing sandbox forward never replaces or ends the Gateway tunnel, that a working forward runs beside it, and that both are retired together. Passes.
- `ConnectionModeCoordinator` fixture: checks that a stale tunnel is retired before a hosted Gateway starts. Passes.
- `RemotePortTunnelTests`, using real sockets:
  - a port held by a `0.0.0.0` or `127.0.0.1` listener counts as unavailable
  - a hosted Gateway's ports are reserved only while hosting is on
  - the sandbox forward uses its own process with a pinned bind address
- `LowCoverageHelperTests`: the orphan matcher recognizes the sandbox forward.
- Focused macOS suites: 173 tests in 12 suites pass at 57b4435, including tunnel, PortGuardian, hosting configuration, coordinator, endpoint store and autostart. The head commit changes only a log line, docs wording and a test name; both fixtures pass at the head. Swift lint and format pass, and so does the docs lint.

Not covered:

- The app's own process launch and PortGuardian ledger, end to end. The live run used the system `ssh` with the same options.
- Hosting on and off through the app UI.
- A crash followed by orphan cleanup against the real tunnel ledger.

Related: #116680, #146230
