prs.title: chore(ios): qualify signed archive cache reuse and invalidation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iOS release archives repeat compilation on fresh runners. This diagnostic campaign measures compilation-cache reuse against current main and checks that a changed Swift input cannot replay stale output.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. **Do not merge this draft.** It temporarily replaces this branch's release workflow with signed archive/export qualification. Uploads, staging, release notes, review submissions, and Discord notifications are absent. Its final commit deliberately changes a linked string solely as an invalidation fixture.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier campaign measured an 82.19% adjusted median archive-wrapper reduction but failed its original exact-content gate. That failed result remains unchanged in #193896. Saved-artifact investigation reconstructed appearance-record ordering, identified a bounded App Intents clock field, and compared full native symbol/source tables and inline range boundaries. This is a new prospective qualification, not a waiver of the earlier result.

Unchanged package compilation is required on a clean archive; deleting compilation, reducing optimization, or omitting release checks would change the product. Xcode's content-addressed compiler cache reuses that necessary output. DerivedData is never reused.

## Evidence

Application source base: `1595dd24770799485a9631c757ccfb7740c12be2` (current origin/main when this campaign began). Qualification tooling is one commit; a second commit changes only the declared linked OpenClawKit string. Ordinary tooling source: `5581460a5710088e5c6c918782ff47138470b945`. Controlled changed-source revision: `e90e9afcfb5a45e4fba9f6a35055b413a47057f4`. Both source revisions must stay clean and their exact SHAs are recorded in each archive.

### Acceptance rule, recorded before the first run

- One cold signed seed, then five serial baseline/candidate pairs in ABAB order on one fresh `xcode-27-xlarge` runner. Baselines explicitly disable compilation caching; every candidate restores the original immutable seed through the pinned cache action. Delete DerivedData and rematerialize tracked source before each archive. Warm verified Watch RTC device libraries and Swift package downloads equally for both arms. Record and require the same toolchain for all cases.
- Seed uses revision 0/build 100; ordinary pair N uses revision N/build 100+N and a distinct fixed metadata timestamp. Both arms of a pair use identical source and release identity. Run the canonical archive/export/IPA validator. No remote release identity is allocated and no Apple upload is possible in this workflow.
- Strictly verify the exported app and nested signatures before removing signature bytes from extracted copies. Preserve all expected architectures, signing teams, entitlements, bundle identities, requested build/version/source/timestamp metadata, and archive dSYM/executable UUID agreement. File path sets, modes, symlinks, metadata, entitlements, and signature-normalized executable bytes must match within each pair.
- No blanket generated-file exclusions. Catalog differences are accepted only if relocating the exact two observed appearance records and their associated references reconstructs the complete candidate byte-for-byte with the same Any/Dark values. App Intents differences are accepted only in the observed eight-byte field 64 bytes from the decompressed end, with each value within its own archive's actual time interval; every other decompressed byte stays exact. Unexpected paths, bytes, schemas, or record changes fail.
- Exported symbol files must match their executable UUID inventory. Differing files are decoded by selected-Xcode Apple libatos/CoreSymbolication in a write-denying, Mach-lookup-denying sandbox. Compare complete counted symbol and named-variant records, addresses/ranges, source paths/lines/columns/discriminators/ranges, and ordered inline results at every exposed symbol/source range start and final byte. Only the two previously observed full Xcode 27.1 SDK prefix aliases are normalized. No filename, line, address, symbol, or other path normalization is permitted. Exact files remain exact. Record decoder fingerprints. Private APIs are diagnostic only; this does not claim every instruction or undocumented field is checked.
- Copied-file negative controls must reject changed rendition data, an appearance value, a non-time NLU byte, a decodable symbol source filename, a file mode, and executable content. Preserve originals and bind retained resources to their manifest hashes.
- Require replay hits for Protocol, Kit, and Chat UI in all five ordinary candidates. Measure complete archive-wrapper wall time, including preparation, signing, export, and canonical validation. Charge actual Actions restore time plus the entire seed save duration to every candidate. Report all samples, median, nearest-rank p95, and range. Require at least 30% lower adjusted median and no worse adjusted p95. Record compressed cache bytes and transfer durations.
- CPU median must not regress. Maximum process RSS median and p95 must each regress by less than 20%. Cold seed wall time must regress by less than 20% against baseline median. Keep resource timelines and host pressure observations; maximum process RSS is not aggregate host memory. A missing metric or failed condition prevents acceptance.
- Finally, run one changed-source baseline/candidate pair from the second clean commit, excluded from the five-pair performance statistics. Restore the original seed CAS, never a changed-source cache. Seed main executable must contain the old linked string and omit the new marker. Both changed-source exports must omit the old text and contain the new 76-byte marker; normalized payload checks still pass within the pair. Require an OpenClawKit replay miss and an unchanged OpenClawProtocol replay hit. A changed executable hash alone does not prove invalidation because Git metadata also changes.

### Validation before dispatch

Saved historical pair 2 passes the final comparator: 313 exact files and 31 specifically explained generated differences. All six negative controls reject at the intended boundary; a separate appearance-slot mutation also rejects. Workflow validation, targeted JavaScript lint, JavaScript/Ruby syntax, and diff whitespace checks pass.

The focused test batch passed 1,220 tests. Two production-workflow guards fail because this deliberately nonmergeable draft removes screenshot jobs and adds an experimental cache writer; those guards remain unchanged. The workflow-evidence suite could not build against the reused local dependency installation because `@lancedb/lancedb` and `quickjs-wasi` are absent. No test exceptions were added.

Fresh local autoreview against base `1595dd24770799485a9631c757ccfb7740c12be2`, including the untracked qualification scripts and controlled source marker, completed scoped-clean at P0/P1 with no actionable findings. Hosted execution and private Apple API behavior remain prospective checks. Simplification review retained only the single serial experiment, comparison rules, and instrumentation needed for this qualification; none is proposed as permanent production machinery. The original campaign result remains failed.

## Hosted result: qualification failed the cold-start requirement

Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42161600259
Evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42161600259/artifacts/13479054283

All 13 signed archive/export validations succeeded. All five ordinary pairs and the changed-source pair passed the published comparison rules. The six copied-resource corruption controls rejected at their intended boundaries. This is equivalence under the explicitly bounded rules above, including exposed symbol/source range-boundary queries, not every undocumented symbol-file field.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Complete archive-wrapper median | 348.19s | 46.81s | Warm archive |
| Adjusted median, including restore + full producer save | 348.19s | 56.81s | 83.69% lower; pass |
| Adjusted nearest-rank p95 | 396.01s | 71.51s | Pass |
| Archive-wrapper CPU median | 970.51s | 96.28s | Pass |
| Maximum process RSS median | 3.58 GiB | 1.88 GiB | Pass |
| Maximum process RSS p95 | 3.81 GiB | 1.93 GiB | Pass |
| Cold seed vs baseline median | 348.19s | 473.34s | **35.94% slower; fails <20% rule** |

Compressed immutable seed cache: 440,720,065 bytes. Save: 6s. Ordinary restores: 5s, 5s, 5s, 4s, 4s. Each adjusted candidate includes its actual restore and the entire producer-save time.

Controlled invalidation passed: the seed contains exactly one original linked string and no new marker; both changed-source exports contain exactly one new marker and no original string. The changed candidate has three OpenClawKit misses and no Kit hits, while unchanged OpenClawProtocol has three hits and no misses. Its normalized payload matches the fresh changed-source baseline.

Cold-start investigation: the seed's Xcode build-log interval is 438.74s, versus 326.13s for the median-wrapper baseline. Outside that interval the complete wrappers spent 34.60s and 22.06s, respectively. Both dependency-download caches restored successfully; sampled memory pressure stayed normal. Most of the excess is inside archive compilation, and only about 12.54s is outside the build-log interval. Baseline wrappers also vary from 302.72s to 396.01s across the serial run. This single first-position seed does not isolate cache-population overhead from runner/filesystem warmup or scheduling variation. The failed threshold remains a failure.

**Do not merge. No Apple upload occurred, no production caching was enabled, and no acceptance rule was relaxed.** The earlier failed campaign and its report hash remain unchanged. The next investigation should isolate cold cache-population cost before proposing production behavior or another qualification campaign.


### Cold-start follow-up from saved artifacts

The first-position seed paid 22.41s for SwiftFormat plus SwiftLint, versus 0.72s in baseline 1. Both checks execute in every archive; the 21.69s first-run difference accounts for most of the 25.27s extra interval before main-app compilation. The project invokes them at `apps/ios/project.yml:100–119`; no checks were skipped.

Against baseline 1, the seed's complete 77.33s excess consists of 10.24s outside the build log, 0.03s clean/log-boundary difference, 6.94s less time before Chat UI compilation, 21.08s more Chat UI compilation, 25.27s more between Chat UI and main-app compilation, 25.73s more main-app compilation, and 1.91s more finishing the archive. These nonoverlapping timeline intervals locate time; they do not provide a complete dependency DAG or causal attribution.

The seed has the same 24 whole-module Swift compilation tasks as every baseline, plus 44 additional explicit Clang module tasks. Baseline wrapper times vary from 302.72s to 396.01s. All sampled memory-pressure levels are normal, with no swap-outs. Whole-host sampled disk I/O is 6.60 GB for the seed versus 4.26 GB for baseline 1, which does not isolate compiler-cache writes.

This establishes a first-run measurement confound, not an acceptable cold-cache overhead. Even subtracting only the observed lint difference as a diagnostic counterfactual leaves 29.71% above the original baseline median. **The original cold-start failure remains unchanged.** The next targeted experiment should equalize first-run preparation and counterbalance fresh-cache enabled/disabled archives before making a production decision. No new builds or source changes were made for this follow-up.

prs.title: fix(cli): diagnose unreadable configuration in validation and setup
prs.body:
Closes #159029. Thanks to @masatohoshino for the report and prior closed, unmerged #159030.

## What Problem This Solves

Distinguishes unreadable configuration from settings that need correction. A missing include or failed file read should produce its underlying read error and retry guidance before setup offers changes or writes anything.

## User Impact

Validation, setup, configure, onboarding and bare startup retain the read-failure diagnosis. Malformed JSON and invalid schema keep their existing recovery paths. An unknown configuration does not authorize setup writes; include ownership, revision, path and writer checks stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing classifier and terminal-safe diagnostic owner supply the error. Bare startup keeps definitive engine-selection failures; validation uses the same failure kind for text and JSON. Shared `readSetupConfig` guards offline and Gateway-routed planning before writes. No new config option, runtime manager, permission, schema, protocol or dependency override is introduced.

## Evidence

November 6 author maintenance integrates official main `c50ff4fbe5410609d00066642c72213e4354ee23` into `623056f849c7e0be4465c21775a6e939cd3a5c0b`. The merge conflict was confined to the imports in `src/cli/fresh-install-config.ts`. Both the author’s read-failure diagnostic and main’s first-write and pre-migration onboarding detection are present. Current author head `e27aaf9612848c71e0ded4b6cdd83b1e858267d2` contains reviewed tree `e7f2daabe3cd1a1ae3a652bbd6ff012a6159bd25`.

- Ten focused files passed 241 cases, including initial install, bare CLI, validation, setup, guided and noninteractive onboarding, and wizard ownership. The Vitest project durations totaled 650.25 seconds. The configure test was rerun after removing a single-use fixture alias and passed 17 cases with the same assertions.
- Production and affected test type checks, core typed lint, formatting, and staged whitespace passed. A fresh P0–P2 source review covered the full author diff and the final allowance and test-fixture supplement.
- Net test growth is 236 lines against the integration parent. The separate 100-line record funds the measured shortage without changing the shared scalar or other allocations. The native ratchet passed on the staged tree and on the merge preview against `dad4fc1a037821f2e503df81fe43171bf61af656` immediately before push. Test lines OK: 6527475; ceiling: 6527475; slack: 0.

### Previous CI repair

Previous author CI repair (2026-10-29), **623056f849c7e0be4465c21775a6e939cd3a5c0b**, carries the exact change from official [#187339](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187339), commit `230619948b35fedb88bf5dbc528c7fd3f2fb07df`, preserving Shakker's original author identity, date and commit message. It changes one test file and no production code or fixture API. The test now selects the release branch/tag through the existing `--target-ref` option, verifies the retained context, then moves that actual ref before asserting resume rejection. No publication, live Actions dispatch or release operation was performed; the local fixture uses private Git repositories and synthetic GH/npm transports.

### Failing CI and attribution

At previous head `55e74290f5ac0fc7d72d8c2a09dde147d6d5836d`, [CI 40822099308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40822099308) checks merge `b5e543264b0bec435af26634224a19b856fde640` against base `f3c816eb4a3e1902153382eff5ccd656f898f9b2`. Its sole failed leaf is `check-test-types-core-3`: the release-candidate test passes `releaseRef` after the shared fixture API removed that property, producing TS2353 at line 335. `ci-gate` fails as a consequence.

The native classifier reports **pre-existing — failure signatures match main; selected scope not compared**. Independent source comparison confirms that the failing test, its two fixture owners, type config, wrapper, manifest and lock are byte-identical in that CI base, merge and PR head. The upstream repair merged at 05:13:17 UTC, after this CI fixed its base. That existing upstream repair is credited rather than claimed as an authored feature or new contribution.

That CI's budget job already **passed**: **6,248,290 / 6,321,421**, slack **73,131**. Those are CI-merge counts, distinct from the fixed-main local counts below; neither this fact nor the repair relabels the failed historical run.

### Current repair verification

- **Exact-head natural CI:** [CI 40825895608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40825895608) completed **successfully** at `623056f849c7e0be4465c21775a6e939cd3a5c0b` on 2026-10-29 06:10:58 UTC (14:10:58 Asia/Shanghai). The previously failed `check-test-types-core-3` is successful, and `ci-gate` reports that CI and applicable security requirements passed. No old run was rerun. This does not classify the retained Doctor/launcher timeouts or grant upstream merge approval.

- The affected test-consumer graph first reproduces the same **TS2353** (77.21 s), then passes after the exact upstream patch (51.73 s). The complete failing CI leaf, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`, also passes (50.42 s); this is not a claim that the entire core stripe or CI ran locally.
- The two affected branch/tag resume cases pass through the actual local CLI fixture (23.30 s wrapper time). The 23 other cases are unselected by the focused command, not disabled or treated as passing. Both rejection and no-dispatch assertions remain, and selected-context verification is stronger.
- Typed lint (55.50 s), format, line-cap, whitespace and native budget pass. The repair removes 11 test LF lines. Local total **6,247,655 / 6,321,032**, slack **73,377**; the effective ceiling is unchanged official scalar **6,320,412** plus unchanged official allocations **620**. The total remains below the scalar alone. No author allowance, baseline, counting rule, timeout, ignore or expected failure is changed.

Fresh local **autoreview** of the complete one-file delta against `55e74290`, P0-P2, is scoped-clean with no actionable finding. Snapshot `767c70e25dc4635179254f41dd48aee805778241`, tree `40171d512430356b180b23a70b8f59eb09759c37`. This is static review of the delta and supplied fixture/wrapper context; the full internal CLI implementation was not supplied and the reviewer did not execute tests.

### Prior CLI integration remains qualified

The original 22 introduced CLI/configuration files, production tree, manifest, lock and their callers are unchanged from `55e74290`; the only new tracked change is the official candidate-test repair. Their prior 197-case proof, production/test-consumer types, lint, native guards and complete 22-file review (`77e25911`, against pinned main `85180528`) therefore retain unchanged-input qualification. They are not counted as newly executed tests on this head. That normal integration preserves main's permission controls, service-installation context, pre-engine inspection and proxy owners; it applies no author budget raise.

### Retained failures and remaining proof

- Both historical failed runs remain failed: the older `bbcd3f84` budget failure (CI 40753429576, 6,310,774 / 6,310,560) and the `55e74290` inherited type failure above. No job was manually rerun or reclassified, and no administrative merge exception is claimed.
- The prior Doctor subprocess's unchanged **30 s timeout remains unexplained**. Its last completed trace was `doctor.external-config` at 29,977.1 ms; maintenance-ready was the next start label. Passing replays and this unrelated fixture repair do not prove that cause repaired. No deadline or assertion is extended.
- The earlier private ordinary `pnpm openclaw` attempt did not finish its normal source rebuild within 600 s and never reached the config-read branch. Current source/boundary tests do not establish an installed upgrade, Windows permission-denial, Bun, real-provider or operator-Gateway pass.
- New-head CI and required owner review remain separate. This is a contributor branch update, not upstream merge approval. No real Gateway was restarted or reconfigured and no paid testing resource or publication exception was used.

<details>
<summary>Historical causal controls and prior-head verification</summary>

The earlier registered `config validate` negative control used canonical main working bytes with the reviewed regression overlaid. Both text and JSON cases failed: text reported `Config needs correction` and suggested schema inspection, while JSON reported `OpenClaw config is invalid` for a real missing include. The 743.31 s wrapper included first-time compilation. This was an owning-command control, not a certified pristine-main deployment; all overlaid source/index bytes were restored. It is historical evidence, not a fresh 8518 execution.

An integration control also showed why main's inline configure owner must stay: keeping the formerly extracted helper bypassed terminal-value tagging and failed the existing ANSI/bidi/newline test. The final proposal preserves canonical tagged rendering instead of keeping that duplicate helper.

At `92fac2b005d24a755c7de8f148644ab534dc34f6`, historical proof qualified 244 distinct cases across 10 files in separate runs (183 CLI, 41 command, eight wizard and 12 queue-owner cases), not one 244-case execution. The initial batch retained two failures: a stale materialized-fallback expectation was corrected against the preset retirement, while the unchanged 120 s non-JSON initialization timeout remained unclassified despite later passing replays. The stricter exact queue matcher, authored/raw absence, no-write and workspace assertions remained. Current 197-case proof above is reported separately, without adding overlapping old counts.

At `bbcd3f84958539217f6e68966e39bb7fa30c20d6`, the subsequent main integration retained the original repair and canonical signal handling. The existing profile scope expectation was corrected to WRITE while targetless dispatch remained ADMIN; main now independently owns that correction, so its file is removed from the introduced diff. The old Node fallback's 37 CLI cases, selected permission contract and queue check remain old-head evidence. The separate Doctor 30 s failure and prior Bun CI classifications remain unresolved as described above.

Earlier full-proposal and scoped follow-up independent reviews stay tied to their recorded revisions (`ba1be3b8`, `5ce18634`, `28e3a046`, `afce0f77`); they do not substitute for the current complete review.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction, while prepared workspace registration inventories content again before its first binding.

## User Impact

Explicit branches/tags/commits and existing pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. The actual snapshot base reaches session binding, and current repository access remains required.

Verified expanded worker code is reused through exact package aliases. Damaged or missing code uses verified archive installation, lease cleanup preserves package code, and each node process still performs requested prewarm. Negotiated result fields preserve the strict response contract shipped in v2026.11.1.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, prepared-workspace, and installer owners serve the flow. Registration records immutable receipts; first binding verifies content, and bound replay preserves private edits. Bundle validation is shared by the installer and native image-preparation command. No config, database schema, or protocol-version change.

## Evidence

- Before/after warm two-lease workload: redundant archive extractions **2 → 0**. Initial registration inventories **1 → 0**, with content verification retained at first binding. No live cloud latency claim.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): two-hop Details prewarm [arrival stop]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A warm reload should show complete cached Details with its first transcript rows. The campaign evidence records 14 intermediate states on a signed-in dashboard deep-link reload; this lane targets the Details stage using synthetic proof only.

**One attempt completed; stopped at the five-pair arrival gate. The PR remains closed.** The candidate is staged and uncommitted; the existing PR diff/head is historical and does not contain this experiment. No cap line changed and no further grouping or trigger candidate was tried after timing began.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous shared trigger had the right timing but pulled the loader, idle-import owner and body preload tables into Startup. The rejected chat-graph trigger saved bytes but started too late. This attempt restores the shared-trigger shape, then uses exactly one conditional dynamic import of the existing loader from snapshot prewarm and calls its existing prepare entry. The existing `createIdleImport` owners load composition/Session and Environment in parallel. Session's lazy binding consumes the same owner, deleting its duplicate dynamic import.

The generated manifest places the loader in Chat and the idle-import helper in Shared. A standalone leaf loader had five preload dependencies but raised Chat to 21 requests against a cap of 20, so it was rejected before timing. Sharing the already-preloaded chat-only virtualizer chunk retains 20 requests and the same five-item static closure. No static Details body import, new registry, pane barrier, boot reorder, configuration, protocol, server-state change, or L295 source edit.

## User Impact

The two-hop shape largely recovers early module arrival and avoids the shared startup payload, but it does not meet the required co-frame reliability. Cached geometry remains complete when Details populates. This result is not proposed for landing.

## Evidence

### Frozen source and method

Pinned main `abe11702825e31e250244fd2ea1f0abd22dc0c24` includes the generated-name normalization and current 64 B build variance. The `ce3502d5` shape rebased onto it is control `baeb252507239f3ecaaf66cb964651acfc9e21c8`, tree `12e9ad8d59bb86df4fbf426c28e235e3f82082f8`. Candidate tree `59dd0b709a807e4114b893c973cf432f74e9f121`; candidate patch SHA-256 `eaff169f079d1980419d860f0a02c9bb8a59a0788564ea8ecf006cd4b52fc544`; control patch SHA-256 `bc5da30848a61717736650280edf624d5a8a3de90d568359731ac7ea5c1e1dfe`. Both full-lane patches were applied with `--index` and exact trees/hashes verified on the box. Benchmark corrections are retained; the rejected chat-graph tree is preserved only as an artifact.

Dedicated AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, repo Playwright Chromium, signed-in synthetic native Gateway, 1720×1180, 80 ms latency profile. Five unprofiled interleaved AB/BA pairs per chat, with closed dashboard secondary, against the rebased shared-trigger control. These are **unscored arrival checks**, not the full main/A/A native+Team gate. Source and box stayed fixed. Resource `responseEnd` is file arrival, not evaluation/import-promise completion.

Lease `cbx_1da6b1d9160a`; [run_63427e67db0201d55dfd572b3ab632b4](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_63427e67db0201d55dfd572b3ab632b4).

### Exact built startup import

CI-owned build: `control-ui-connection-wmCfWnSD.js` dynamically imports `virtual-core-runtime-D0TpNokk.js` (27,396 raw bytes, including the existing virtualizer). The direct target is already modulepreloaded in the Chat route template and absent from New's template. Vite's exact dependency array for this site is:

```json
[
  "./control-ui-boot-shared-Ry6mcluZ.js",
  "./solid-runtime-i9JxUR86.js",
  "./control-ui-boot-shared-styles-zzc2a7O6.js",
  "./chat-english-k1NbtRFk.js",
  "./control-ui-boot-shared-styles-Jytlu0jy.css"
]
```

These are map indices `[0, 1, 2, 3, 8]`. Vite names the direct loader target in `import()` separately from this array. The loader, `createIdleImport`, Session and Environment body sources are absent from Startup; body preload tables remain in the loader's chunk. Chat boot requests are **20/20**. No request cap was raised. The idle-import owner remains in `control-ui-boot-shared-Ry6mcluZ.js`, giving the loader a static dependency on Boot Shared. No import-ready/evaluation marker was collected, so file response times do not establish where the remaining readiness delay occurs.

### Arrival gate

Required: candidate co-frame at least 4/5 on **both** chats.

| Route | Control co-frame | Candidate co-frame | Candidate lag median [Q1,Q3] ms | Worst candidate lag ms | Complete geometry excluding Subagents, control/candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|

### CI-owned normalized bytes against rebased main

`corepack pnpm ui:check-performance:base abe11702825e31e250244fd2ea1f0abd22dc0c24`. Only these owner-check values are used for budget conclusions.

| Surface | Main B | Candidate B | Delta | Existing cap / result |

Startup passes and New rises only 120 B, below the permitted 256 B rise and below its unchanged cap. Main itself reports Chat 293 B over its cap; this inherited red is preserved in the owner reports. Candidate Chat is +417 B versus that measured main. The conditional exact Chat raise would be 1,288,908 B **only after a full gate pass**; the failed arrival gate voids it. New needs no raise. **No cap line was edited.**

Largest JS is a separate unapproved cap, not covered by Chat/New permission. Boot Shared raw bytes rise **1,819,791 → 1,819,828 (+37 B)**: **35 B** for the disposable cached docking schema and **2 B** from compiler binding changes in unchanged select-picker source. New-route mapped growth is exactly 239 B in startup prewarm + 35 B docking schema + 2 B bindings, with no unmapped raw growth. The schema receipt is required to validate the cached dock state against its layout; deleting it would remove this lane's no-flip contract. Normalized shared gzip is 560,308 → 560,379 B; main has only 42 B headroom, so the candidate exceeds by 29 B. The same CI report's served-gzip field falls 564,512 → 564,478 B, but that does **not** override the normalized CI gate. No identifier shortening, budget-input hiding, unrelated source deletion, or cap workaround was attempted.

### Focused checks and remaining proof

Recorded remote exits: `{"controllers": 1, "line-cap": 1, "lint": 1, "prewarm-unit": 0, "reload-e2e": 1}`. An exit of 1 is a retained failure, never a passing replay. See the exact failure classification below before considering another attempt. Local snapshot-prewarm unit tests pass 12/12 (`pnpm test … --maxWorkers=1` wall 3.24 s). The local five-case reload smoke is 3 passed / 2 failed, with archived/open-dashboard frame-zero Details false (Vitest duration 22.79 s; not a performance comparison). No assertions were weakened.

Remote snapshot-prewarm unit tests pass **12/12** (runner wall 3.56 s). Remote five-case reload e2e is **2 passed / 3 failed** (duration 38.90 s): the held-Environment and closed-destination cases pass; active chat and open dashboard fail first-frame Details at line 325; archived chat also reaches an `expected false to be true` assertion (bundled trace maps to line 267). These are retained assertion failures, not classified as infrastructure failures. No main replay was run after the arrival stop, so inherited versus candidate attribution is not established for the e2e failures.

The source guards also fail: `chat-details.tsx` has **702 counted lines against 700**, causing both the line-cap ratchet and oxlint failures; the controller ratchet rejects **one manualImport against zero** in `chat-snapshot-prewarm.ts`. Other controller ratchets pass. These are actual guard findings on this tree, not setup errors; neither baseline was changed. The requested trigger shape introduces that manual import. The remote build passes, but none of these reds is treated as a passing gate. They remain unresolved because this attempt already fails its mandatory arrival escape hatch.

The native/Team 11-pair+A/A score, final-head full UI e2e suite, exact-head CI, new P2-clean review/commit, and ready transition were **not run or claimed** after this stop. The paired rows bar in a future scored gate remains against main, not this shared-trigger control. No merge.

### Source size and files

Tested staged tree versus pinned main, excluding test/test-support/docs per the requested stat: **+189 lines (245 added, 56 deleted; 16 files)**. UI runtime: **+42 lines**. Growth carries the disposable cached layout receipt and existing parallel import owners; superseded serial Environment preload re-export/onLoaded chain and redundant docking placement reads remain removed. This retry adds only the two-hop trigger, shared Session import binding and count-neutral grouping; it does not introduce another state owner.

Five retry files: `chat-snapshot-prewarm.ts`, `chat-details-desktop-loader.ts`, `chat-details.tsx`, `ui/config/control-ui-chunking.ts`, regenerated `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json`. The full lane retains the cache/header/schema and existing benchmark/probe corrections. Source remains staged on the lane branch; no new code commit or push.

### Cleanup

The 1,872,751,250-byte evidence archive was downloaded and validated through tar EOF and gzip CRC (3,038 entries; 217 extracted proof files). AWS confirms **released** lease `cbx_1da6b1d9160a` and server `i-01392419b06f02591`. No local Gateway was started; the released instance held the synthetic remote Gateway/browser processes. Source remains staged at tree `59dd0b709a807e4114b893c973cf432f74e9f121`, with no new commit or push. The attempt is stopped. No further grouping or trigger variant was attempted.

## Final round: predeclared acceptance (2026-11-05)

The maintainer authorized one final two-hop arm A and mandatory fallback B to the rebased shared-trigger shape. Main is pinned to `f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b`; control is `3a133212ece619a95b2aa5977b61c8186c6c0b4c` (the rebased baeb2525/ce3502d5 shape). Full gate for the selected arm: pinned main comparison, native and Team-scale archived chat, active chat and closed dashboard, 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A; painted Details co-frame >=9/11 on both chats, cached Environment complete at first population, Subagents movement reported/excluded. On a pass, final-head full UI e2e, exact-head CI and clean independent P2 review remain required; no merge is authorized. This PR stays closed while the experiment runs.

prs.title: fix: avoid loading Chat for shared route helpers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents, Memory and Skill Workshop fetch Chat's renderer and styles on their first visit even though they only need shared Markdown or text-diff helpers.

Related: #193922, #193895.

## User Impact

These routes can load their own content without fetching Chat. Rendering and CSS declarations remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Assign the shared Markdown HTML renderer to the existing Markdown chunk, and move the unchanged deletion-first LCS walker into a neutral helper in the existing deferred-support chunk. This removes the helper-only import edges without adding a new chunk or changing startup ownership.

Extend the engine benchmark's existing page scenarios to accept the 100 ms network profile. Preserve guards for other interactions, measure resource completion against browser-local readiness, and allow settled Chat as an explicit origin for comparisons with prior route work. Report HTTP/1.1 capacity waves as a lower bound, not dependency depth.

## Evidence

Draft while the required 20 rotated base/head/base pairs run in Chromium and WebKit. Acceptance: desktop first visits and warm returns for Agents, Memory and Skill Workshop at localhost and 100 ms; at least 5% target-flow improvement, no attributable regression beyond the 5% band, no new CLS, unchanged CSS declarations and no raised ceiling. A/A controls and host load are recorded. A separate all-route RTT census and matched-origin Cron/Sessions measurements will be added before ready.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused UI tests | 33 passed across the three touched/owning suites |
| Chunk-ownership regression on base | Fails on base, passes on head |
| Focused script tests | Passed (profile delivery and observer timing boundaries) |
| UI and scripts typechecks | Passed |
| Targeted lint/format; production Knip | Passed |
| Independent review | No actionable findings |
| Startup JS gzip | 90,280 B → 90,280 B |
| Startup CSS gzip / requests | 36,574 B / 1 → unchanged |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,289,106 B → 1,288,860 B (−246 B) |
| Total CSS gzip | 324,697 B → unchanged |
| Strict comparison to merge base | Pass, no violations; no ceilings raised |

The base already exceeds absolute Chat/total-CSS caps; the exact-base comparison permits no growth. Settings→Chat has a pre-existing small desktop CLS observation (0.000945); this is disclosed rather than reported as zero. Current RTT profiles have no bandwidth cap, so historical 10 Mbps timing results are not directly comparable.

LOC across touched files: UI production 1,788 → 1,791; tooling 3,281 → 3,418; tests 969 → 1,118; docs/allocation 70 → 94. UI effect/listener/query/flush/owner counts stay 0 → 0. Tooling growth supplies the missing RTT measurement and resource-boundary evidence.

Remaining route audit, final distributions, before/after screenshots and rejected byte screens will be added before ready.

prs.body:
## Summary

The terminal recovery fixtures omitted `terminal.open`, so the disabled-terminal and read-only-operator rows could both pass through the missing-feature guard. Advertise it alongside the normal default methods to exercise each intended guard. Keep both cases, recovery copy, zero-open-RPC assertion, new-session navigation and composer check.

The four-line growth retains its exact per-change allocation; the shared ceiling is unchanged. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Historical behavioral proof

On original head `6c2e2c648d77398334963c8872c2eb832fdacb69`:

- Unchanged baseline, repaired suite and native published-head validation each passed both cases.
- With each actual configuration/admin guard temporarily omitted, the old fixture stayed green and the repaired fixture failed only its intended row. All production mutations were restored.
- A separate enabled/admin/advertised browser probe recorded one `terminal.open`; it is not an additional official case.
- Scoped UI types, typed lint, formatting, ledger MDX, whitespace and the line ratchet passed. Changed-check planning was a dry run.

These browser checks use an owned mock Gateway; they do not prove live terminal execution.

## Integration correction

Signed candidate `7f69f3c9208a18bfe9334cb5ab36647af655cc89` integrates pinned baseline `285829cbf0277d4a1661669109542bb36d2b907e` through the retained native workflow. The sole conflict resolution is the audit ledger. The native three-way merge preserves the current “The terminal is unavailable.” copy and applies only the original capability-fixture delta. The allocation is unchanged, and production bytes equal the baseline.

The ledger preserves landed history, records the verified UI repair and worker-cleanup outcomes, reconciles the completed frozen UI source census, and keeps the unresolved read-coalescing recorder follow-up excluded. Source closure is not repository-wide runtime completion.

Code-only checks confirmed clean signed source/baseline parents, exact intended three-file scope and expected blobs, preserved copy, and `git diff --check`. Candidate-local tests were not run: the retained physical installation does not match the baseline package/lock inputs. Original execution remains historical. Fresh read-only committed-range review of `285829cbf027..7f69f3c9208a` found no substantive correctness or security findings and confirmed the integration finding resolved. Fresh [CI42165900059/attempt1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42165900059) passed with32 successful and28 skipped jobs, including the UI E2E shard. prs.title: perf(ui): retain Usage analytics while sorting and paging
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sorting or paging Usage sessions unnecessarily retires and rebuilds the unchanged analytics above the roster.

## User Impact

Usage analytics remain mounted while a new session order or page loads. The roster still clears stale results during the request, and changes to the actual analytics selection keep their existing query fences.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway computes analytics before sorting and paging the session window. The UI's retained filter/analytics projection nevertheless treated those roster-only fields as a new analytics scope. Keep that projection for equal selections using the existing owner; no new cache, timer, state copy, or lazy import is added.

## Evidence

Production bundles at `0b090326c3fd5c9f515ff9718d067f42e0ea77f7` and this change, synthetic Gateway, headless desktop Chromium/WebKit. Twenty rotated base/head/base triplets per engine, with an unchanged Model Providers filter control (240 observations, all passed). Shared-host load: 12.7–20.7. Values below are median / p95 in milliseconds.

| Usage sort | Base | Head | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chromium script CPU | 17.667 / 18.296 | 10.418 / 11.227 | −41.0% |
| Chromium style CPU | 7.120 / 7.400 | 4.088 / 4.224 | −42.6% |
| Chromium task CPU | 80.394 / 82.287 | 64.720 / 67.322 | −19.5% |
| Chromium application elapsed | 147.650 / 152.200 | 144.350 / 147.100 | −2.2% |
| WebKit application elapsed | 185.500 / 197.000 | 154.500 / 177.000 | −16.7% |

The Chromium application gain misses the initial 5% application-time target: its request/debounce wait dominates the span. The measured CPU reduction and WebKit application win are the reason to land. No attributable regression appeared. A/A Usage script medians were 17.667 / 17.861 ms; WebKit application medians were 185.5 / 182.5 ms. Control script CPU was 0.642 → 0.646 ms with a lower p95; application work was at or below 1 ms in both engines.

The separate mutation audit reduced identical replacement candidates **189 → 27** and formatter calls **499 → 308** in each engine. Fresh native profiles confirm the eliminated render/style work. Instrumented observations are diagnostic, excluded from the timing table.

- The two sort/page regression cases fail on the base because the analytics subtree disappears; all 12 tests in `usage-page-query-ownership.test.ts` pass on the change.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:scripts` pass. Paired strict production performance check passes: normalized startup **90,280 → 90,280 B gzip**, one startup CSS request; Chat/New boot bytes unchanged. No ceiling changed.
- Benchmark command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --control-bundle-dir <base> --engines chromium,webkit --viewport desktop --steps data-usage-sort,page-model-providers-action --pairs 20`.
- The benchmark now uses native select type-ahead so the application boundary is a trusted input event.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. No Solid effects, listeners, owner APIs, or DOM queries added to production.

| Touched lines of code | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Usage owner | 752 | 755 |
| Query ownership tests | 496 | 569 |
| Existing Usage benchmark | 358 | 359 |
| Test allocation | 0 | 1 |

Visual proof and computed-style comparison are recorded below. All captures use synthetic data. Screenshots are aligned to the analytics/session elements because the old teardown also changes WebKit's scroll position.

### Visual proof

Inspected synthetic Chromium captures after sorting; typography, geometry, colors and selected control state are unchanged. Computed styles and geometry match for the overview, charts, grid and session card.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Usage before](./round2-usage-visual/chromium-base-page.png) | ![Usage after](./round2-usage-visual/chromium-head-page.png) |

Production Knip passed. Targeted formatting/lint passed for this commit; broader Round 2 harness checks are tracked separately.

![chromium-head-page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ced173cd-f1f6-4e46-9324-914f943b0a4d)

prs.title: fix(github): publication fails with PostgreSQL session or state stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes GitHub publication requests failing when either shared state or the source session uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

Publication works with SQLite, PostgreSQL, and mixed engine configurations. A concurrent source writer remains excluded until publication settles. No configuration, schema, permission, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication worker read the SQLite identity anchor instead of the configured session store and reserved the destination anchor instead of its PostgreSQL connection. Use the existing engine opener and transaction owner, retain admitted engine identities, and keep receipts attached to the existing anchors. Empty lock attempts release acquired reservations before retrying.

This reimplements the intent of `ada7d22ab01` against current main rather than importing its patch. Simplification keeps PostgreSQL lock acquisition with the PostgreSQL transaction owner and removes the anchor-only data path; no new state owner or production test hooks.

## Evidence

- Real disposable PostgreSQL, all four SQLite/PostgreSQL state/session pairs: the conformance proof now exercises the production requester, canonical identity/profile, operator role/session policy, source reservation and durable-admission owners. It demonstrates authorized creator success, rejection of an equally scoped foreign principal, and committed runtime-policy revocation while a separate request waits on its real source reservation. Final durable assertions retain the authorized requester snapshot and exclude the denied publication.
- Pinned negative control: reverting only the six affected production owners to the original parent produces 3 failures / 1 pass (`session_nodes` missing or unavailable source reservation). The candidate passes 24/24: four mixed-engine authority flows and 20 source-fence regressions. Those six baseline owners are unchanged in the inspected current-main context. This is an owner-reversion control, not a complete baseline checkout run.
- Gateway publication consumers: 42/42 passed, including a fresh continuation run. The combined continuation runner timed out after its Gateway shard passed and before the infra shard completed; the separate source-fence rerun passed 20/20. The timeout is retained as an observation, not relabeled a passing combined run.
- Existing deferred-commit proof verifies PostgreSQL and SQLite source-writer exclusion through destination settlement. Rollback, cancellation, aliasing, contention and lost-reply regressions remain covered.
- Fresh full-candidate independent autoreview at P0–P2 with 13 production-owner contexts: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Core/infra-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Published proof commit `c7393f4518f24f985f8c7aa0b39baa37f1ac884d` directly extends the previously reviewed head. Its entire tree and all three changed blobs match the tested local candidate; the human co-author trailer is preserved. New-head CI was attached and pending at publication; no final-green claim is made here.

The tests use real PostgreSQL and production authority/storage owners with synthetic WebSocket transport and isolated state. They are not a live Gateway/model/provider or end-to-end GitHub publication acceptance run.

The test allocation is now 367 lines, covering only this PR's configured-engine, commit-boundary and authority regressions and fixtures. The pinned base's existing 80-line debt is not absorbed into this allocation.

prs.title: fix(telegram): surface inbound media failures on the console log with their errno
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On an NFS-backed state volume (Longhorn RWX, EFS, ONTAP), every inbound Telegram document or photo failed at the media-save step and the bot answered "⚠️ Failed to download media. Please try again." while `kubectl logs` showed nothing at all. The filesystem half of that report is already fixed upstream: `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.27.1 publishes no-replace moves through an identity-checked `linkat`/`unlinkat` fallback when `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` answers `EINVAL`, and `src/media/store.read-scope.ts` already calls `mediaRoot.move(..., { overwrite: false })`. What stayed broken is the diagnostic path that made the incident a five-week mystery.

The inbound media catch in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-pipeline.ts` reported both the oversize and the fetch-failure case with `logger.warn`. That `logger` comes from `getChildLogger({ module: "telegram-auto-reply" })` in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-core.ts`, and the base logger built by `src/logging/logger.ts` (`type: "hidden"`, one file transport) has no console sink, so the warning only ever landed in the rotating log file. A deployment that only exposes container stdout therefore saw a user-visible failure with zero operator-visible cause, and nothing named the errno.

This change adds `logInboundMediaFailure` to `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.media.ts` — the module that already owns Telegram media error classification — and routes both call sites through it. It writes with `createSubsystemLogger("telegram/media")`, which emits to the file log and the console sink with the existing redaction boundary, and it walks the `cause` chain to record the deepest `code`, so `EINVAL` (unsupported no-replace move) and `EEXIST` (a real destination collision, which must stay a failure) are now greppable instead of being flattened into a generic download error. Message text, chat warnings, retry classification and the no-overwrite contract are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New cases `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.media.test.ts`: red on `main` (`TypeError: logInboundMediaFailure is not a function`, 2 failed / 9 passed), green with the fix (11 passed). They assert the JSON console record `{ subsystem: "telegram/media", level: "warn", message: "media fetch failed", code: "EINVAL" }` for a `MediaFetchError` wrapping an `EINVAL` cause, and that an `EEXIST` collision still surfaces its errno.
- Regression: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.media.test.ts` 11/11 pass (9 pre-existing cases unchanged).
- Reverse proof: reverting `bot-handlers.media.ts` and `bot-handlers.inbound-pipeline.ts` while keeping the new tests fails exactly the 2 new cases and leaves the 9 existing ones green.
- `oxfmt --check` passes on all changed files (repo `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`, printWidth 100).
- `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-media-failure-console.txt` accounts for the 71 added test lines.
- Not verified: no real NFS mount and no end-to-end Gateway run. The Telegram handler e2e (`bot.media.warning-topics.e2e.test.ts`) cannot start its session-transcript worker in this offline mirror (the worker loses the TS loader and fails on `agent-database-readers.js`); that failure reproduces identically on unmodified `main`, so it is an environment limit, not a result. A scoped `tsc --noEmit` over the three changed files produced no diagnostics for them, but the run is noisy because this partial checkout has no built `openclaw/plugin-sdk` declarations.

prs.title: fix(sessions): bound the plaintext archive read cache by size and entries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`materializeSessionArchiveForRead()` writes one decompressed copy per archive into `/tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache`. The only reaper was an hourly sweep that unlinks entries older than 24 h, so the directory grew with the whole compressed archive set (495 files / ~620 MB on a 1 GiB tmpfs in the report) and stayed there for a day. The file's own comments already refer to "budget eviction" that did not exist.

This adds a 128 MiB / 64-entry budget with LRU eviction, runs it before the first write of a new copy, and refreshes an entry's mtime on a cache hit so "recently used" is meaningful and the TTL becomes idle time.

## Evidence

- `archive-cache-budget.test.ts` (6 cases, temp-dir fixtures): under-budget untouched, byte-budget eviction removes the oldest, entry-cap eviction keeps only the newest, `.tmp` writers are never evicted, missing directory is a no-op, shipped entry cap is 64.
- `oxfmt --check` passes on all three changed files.

## 问题原因

`materializeSessionArchiveForRead()` 会把每个 `.jsonl.zst` 归档解压成明文副本，落在
`/tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache`。这个目录只有一条清理路径：`sweepMaterializedArchiveCache()`
每小时最多跑一次，且只删 `mtime` 超过 24 小时的条目。没有字节上限，也没有条目数上限。

结果就是缓存目录的大小等于「全部归档解压后的总和」，并且要停留一天。报告里 495 个文件 / 623 MB 直接吃掉
1 GiB tmpfs 的 62%，之后读写 `/tmp` 的会话保存、更新暂存、截图都可能失败。值得注意的是 `archive-compression.ts`
里两处注释已经写着 "budget eviction"（"archives deleted by budget eviction"、"cache itself cannot outgrow
the archives"），但代码里并没有预算逻辑——这次把注释说的东西补上。

## 修改机制

新增 `src/config/sessions/archive-cache-budget.ts`：

- `MATERIALIZED_ARCHIVE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES = 128 MiB`、`MATERIALIZED_ARCHIVE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 64`。
- `evictMaterializedArchiveCacheOverBudget(cacheDir, budget?)`：读目录（`readdirSync` + `statSync`，跳过
  非普通文件），按 `mtime` 升序删到同时满足字节与条目上限；上限可注入，便于测试用小夹具。
- 跳过 `.tmp`：并发写入者的临时文件名是唯一后缀，删掉它们会打断正在进行的物化。
- 目录不存在、条目在扫描与删除之间消失、平台拒绝 unlink 打开中的文件，都只是跳过，不抛错。

`archive-compression.ts` 侧两处改动：

1. 首次写入前调用一次 `evictMaterializedArchiveCacheOverBudget(cacheDir)`（在 `mkdirSync` 之后），
   保证新增副本落地时目录已经在预算内，而不是等下一次每小时清扫。
2. 命中缓存时 `utimesSync` 刷新 mtime。这就是「最近使用」能成立的前提：不刷新的话，热归档在预算看来
   仍是最旧的一份。副作用是 24 小时 TTL 从「物化后 24 小时」变成「闲置 24 小时」，与预算配合更合理。

## 验证与证据

新模块的 6 条单测（`archive-cache-budget.test.ts`，node 环境，临时目录夹具）：

| 用例 | 断言 |
| --- | --- |
| 目录在预算内 | 不删任何条目 |
| 字节超限 | 删最旧一条，中间与最新保留 |
| 条目数超限（都很小） | 只留最新一条 |
| 存在 `.tmp` 写入者 | `.tmp` 保留，普通条目按预算清掉 |
| 目录不存在 | 不抛错 |
| 默认常量 | 条目上限为 64 |

`oxfmt --check`（仓库配置，printWidth 100）对 3 个改动文件通过。

## 证据边界（未验证项）

- 没有跑端到端物化：该路径需要 sealed temp-root runtime 才能解析 `/tmp/openclaw`，本机 sandbox 起不来。
  因此「495 个归档只保留 ≤64 份」这个整体效果是策略层面的推论，不是实测。
- 128 MiB / 64 条是我选的默认值（1 GiB tmpfs 下约 12%），不是维护者给过的数字；如果需要按部署调，
  更合适的后续是把它们做成配置项（issue 里的建议 2），本次没做配置层。
- 只按 mtime 做 LRU，`relatime` 挂载下 atime 不可信，所以没用 atime。
- 测试行净增 84 行，已申请 `config/test-lines-allocations/session-archive-cache-budget.txt` 等额额度。

prs.title: fix(oc-path): reject the redaction sentinel used as an object key
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`oc://data.jsonc/items/+` and `oc://data.jsonl/+` accepted `{"__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__":1}` and wrote the redaction marker into the file as a JSON object key, while the same object inserted into a YAML sequence was refused with `OC_EMIT_SENTINEL`. The plugin documents the guard as covering every kind, so this is a coverage gap in the emit guard, not a policy difference.

Both renderers guarded each entry's value but never its key: `jsoncValueToJson()` passed `entry.key` straight into `Object.fromEntries`, and `renderJsoncValue()` passed `e.key` straight into `JSON.stringify`. Keys now go through the same guard, fail closed, and leave the file untouched.

## Evidence

- New case in `tests/scenarios/sentinel-cross-kind.test.ts` is red on `main` (`expected [Function] to throw an error` for both set and append) and green with the fix.
- Full `extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/tests/` suite in an isolated harness: 33 files / 404 tests pass.
- Reverse proof: reverting the two source files and keeping the new test fails only the new case (3 others stay green).
- `oxfmt --check` with the repo `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` (printWidth 100) passes on all three changed files.

## 问题原因

`oc-path` 的红字哨兵守卫只覆盖「值」，不覆盖「对象的键」：

- `jsonc/edit.ts` 的 `jsoncValueToJson()` 递归时先 `guardSentinel(entry.value)`，再以 `entry.key` 直接拼 `Object.fromEntries`。
- `jsonl/edit.ts` 的 `renderJsoncValue()` 同样只对 `e.value` 递归守卫，`JSON.stringify(e.key)` 直接落到输出。

YAML 分支不同：值最终走 `formatFrontmatterValue` / yaml 序列化，键被当作标量一并检查，所以同一个对象插进 YAML 序列会抛 `OC_EMIT_SENTINEL`。结果是文档承诺的「所有 kind 一致」在 JSONC / JSONL 上不成立，`oc://data.jsonc/items/+`、`oc://data.jsonl/+` 会把 `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` 当作键写进文件并返回 exit 0。

## 修改机制

- `jsonc/edit.ts`：在 `Object.fromEntries` 的 map 回调里先 `guardSentinel(entry.key, \`${guardPath}/${entry.key}\`)`，键与值共用同一指针前缀。
- `jsonl/edit.ts`：键在 `entries.map` 中单独检查，命中时抛 `OcEmitSentinelError(\`${guardPath}/${walked.join("/")}/${e.key}\`)`，与现有嵌套值报错路径风格一致（`oc://file/L2/<key>`）。

两处都是 fail-closed：抛出发生在 `applyEdits` / 行拼接之前，文件内容不变。守卫仍是子串匹配，`prefix__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__suffix` 这类键同样会被拒绝。

## 验证与证据

隔离 harness（`jsonc-parser` + 本目录源码闭包，vitest）里跑 `extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/tests/` 全量：

| 阶段 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 修复前，新用例 | 红：`setJsoncOcPath` 与 `appendJsonlOcPath` 均未抛错，返回值正常（`expected [Function] to throw an error`） |
| 修复后，新用例 | 绿：jsonc 抛 `sentinel literal at oc://config/x/__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__`，jsonl 抛 `OcEmitSentinelError`，两次都断言 `ast.raw` 未变 |
| 修复后，全量 | 33 个测试文件 / 404 条用例全绿（含 `sentinel-cross-kind.test.ts` 原有 3 条） |
| 反证 | 回退两个源文件、保留新测试：仅新用例 1 条失败，其余 3 条仍绿 — 说明用例测的就是这个缺口 |

`oxfmt --check`（仓库 `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`，printWidth 100）对 3 个改动文件均通过。

## 证据边界（未验证项）

- 没有跑完整 `openclaw` CLI 端到端（本机 `git fetch` 不通，只有 Oct 30 的镜像），因此「`openclaw path set ... --json` 返回 exit 1」这一层是靠单元级 `OcEmitSentinelError` + 未改动文件断言推导，未直接在进程里复现 issue 的第 3 步。
- 只覆盖 `jsonc` / `jsonl` 两条写入渲染路径；`md` / `yaml` 未改（它们本来就拒绝）。
- 测试行净增 18 行，已在 `config/test-lines-allocations/oc-path-sentinel-object-keys.txt` 申请等额额度。

prs.title: fix(ci): retain precise contract selection for mixed UI changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mixed UI/TypeScript changes fall back to both contract jobs because UI source and test-line budget records are treated as unknown inputs.

## User Impact

PR CI retains TypeScript proof while avoiding unrelated Rust work. Deletions, incomplete comparisons, unknown paths, and shared Rust inputs retain full coverage. The shared Solid/Vitest plugin now explicitly triggers TypeScript conformance; other UI configuration remains conservative.

## Why This Change Was Made

Of 47 post-landing PR runs that exercised the selector, only three skipped Rust. Replaying the exact diffs from [run 42162475248](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42162475248) and [run 42159751815](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42159751815) retains TypeScript and removes two Rust jobs that took 88 and 96 runner-seconds. This is a historical replay estimate, not measured billing or critical-path savings.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: replay the recorded complete diffs through the actual workflow script; omit those two Rust jobs, retain TypeScript, and preserve deletion/unknown/shared-input fallbacks.

prs.body:
Closes #148323.

Supersedes #148325. **Still Draft:** conflict repair, public-code review and synthetic browser validation are complete; real expired-xAI authorization and credential persistence have not been exercised.

## What Problem This Solves

An expired OpenClaw-managed OAuth account in Models has no profile-level action to restart its provider's advertised authorization flow.

## User Impact

Reconnect opens the existing Gateway-owned OAuth/device-code wizard for an eligible expired account, then refreshes its status after completion. It does not change the active model. The recorded test demonstrates that UI path with fictional data, not compatibility with the real xAI service.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing login runner already owns authorization, mutation admission, cancellation and stale-result handling. This change reuses that owner instead of adding a credential store or authentication RPC.

Reconnect requires an expired OAuth profile, a positive Gateway `reconnectSupported` ownership capability, exactly one advertised OAuth/device-code route, and existing write/busy admission. Config display provenance and logout eligibility are not ownership authority. External or inherited profiles, missing local-ownership metadata and ambiguous routes fail closed; the Gateway excludes external IDs even if they overlap the local set. Existing logout behavior is unchanged.

### Conflict repair — 2026-10-25

Resolved the two conflicts in the login controller and its browser suite. Reconnect now lives in current main's inline `providerActions` getter; removed single-use helper wrappers were not restored. prs.title: fix(models): preserve unknown prices and limits across 12 discovery providers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Missing model prices and token limits were converted into free pricing or invented capacities, while ClawRouter discovery used static cards instead of the selected account's advertised inventory.

## User Impact

Unknown prices and limits remain unknown. Selected endpoint pricing takes precedence by presence: absent inherits global pricing, explicit null stays unknown, and zero/partial rates remain intact. Explicit zero prices and authoritative billed totals, including zero, are preserved. Models stay listed when limits are absent; Anthropic requests require an explicit or qualified output bound before dispatch. Chat shows unknown cost separately from a recorded zero.

When ClawRouter advertises a supported discovery offer, the selected proxy credential retrieves its complete catalog. A successful empty catalog suppresses static seeds. Supported families are Cerebras, NVIDIA, Chutes, Venice, Baseten, Arcee, Novita, Featherless, DeepInfra, Bifrost, LiteLLM and Requesty.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime types now permit partial prices and absent output limits. Resolution, persistence, usage aggregation and reporting preserve that absence instead of filling it with zeros or default capacities. Discovery uses exact provider contracts through the existing guarded reader/cache, with credential and endpoint isolation, cancellation, bounded refresh and no anonymous or upstream-key fallback.

Worker transcript projection also omits unavailable cost properties before launch hashing. Partial/unknown costs now retain the same identity across JSON transport; recorded zero and provider-billed totals remain intact. Receipt validation and timeout policy are unchanged.

This combines the dependent pricing, limits and acquisition slices: acquisition needs the optional runtime types to materialize truthful executable rows. It removes the catalog cost-completion helper and the reached fabricated defaults, without adding a separate discovery framework.

**SDK compatibility:** consumers must handle optional model cost/rates and maxTokens, and possibly incomplete estimated usage cost. Known complete values retain their behavior. A local execution budget is not advertised provider capacity. No deployment, live provider request or new server capability activation is included.

## Evidence

Candidate: `8f65e2bc007f17cfdae0d0636858b88c2e5c9e2b`. Supported native preparation integrated exact `aedae9dc410202f22504c6183823fd411699f723` to consume known UI and unused-export corrections. The explicit 5-second timeout, all four expected proxy keys, profile denials and request counts are unchanged. All 35 speech cases pass on Node and Bun; extension test types, scoped formatting/lint and normal commit hooks pass. Production auth/deadline code and the test-line allocation are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(memory): report duplicate Markdown blocks
prs.body:
Related: #176036

## What Problem This Solves

Operators consolidating copied Markdown memory need source locations for repeated content, rather than only more diverse search results.

## User Impact

`openclaw memory duplicates` reports identical blocks and their file/line references without changing files or printing memory text. Both same-file and cross-file repeats are included. `--agent`, `--min-chars`, `--max-groups`, and `--json` support focused local inspection.

This is a proposed optional CLI feature, not an accepted product direction. It follows existing offline CLI ownership rules and refuses another plugin's memory slot. File paths can still be sensitive and should be reviewed before sharing reports. Maintainer edits are disabled because the author has not authorized fork workflow/secrets access.

The first version is local-workspace-only: configured remote mappings overlapping any scanned root, and declared or registered Memory ownership at scan paths, their ancestors or descendants of recursive roots, are rejected before local discovery. It never substitutes Gateway-local files for remote-owned files. Bundled product acceptance still needs a maintainer decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Memory Core's existing Markdown discovery, authorized file reader, and chunker. Group exact, non-overlapping chunks locally, normalizing CRLF and empty boundary lines. Return bounded location lists with explicit total and omitted counts. No new model-facing tool, database, user configuration setting, background task, deletion, or search-ranking change. The existing workspace-owner SDK gains one narrow local-scan admission assertion; it exposes no registry or provider paths.

The command inspects live files, not persisted index contents. It does not find paraphrases or arbitrary matching substrings across chunk boundaries. Repeated content can be intentional; consolidation remains a separate manual decision.

The review repair preserves the existing `declareAgentWorkspaceAccess` / `getAgentWorkspaceAccess` contract: stopped or unavailable workspace adapters must not expose a stale local copy. Offline CLI loading may not register that adapter at all, so configured `file-transfer` mappings are checked against all actual discovery roots and the selected workspace itself. This includes normalized extra directories/files, mapped descendants of recursive roots, shared directories, and existing canonical aliases. The workspace participates only in remote-ancestor/equality checks, not descendant checks: it is not a recursive scan root, and its canonical identity remains relevant when every default memory root is absent. Declared ownership is checked by the existing workspace owner on canonical workspace/scan-root ancestry, every discovered path, and declared descendants of recursive scan roots, even when those descendants are empty or absent. No remote transport or competing registry is added. Patterned extra roots conservatively refuse overlap even when a narrower pattern might exclude it; use a narrower local root instead. Unscanned remote siblings remain allowed.

## Evidence

### Current main integration — 2026-11-06 (`f1185780adba53f88d5c3cc06413f890a4eaca1b`)

Merged main `7349fd516c645ec49ca0708e94f8527988e2a9cf` into the original branch, preserving `dac8077688546c263dd9d4d23c0720cad7cf4ccf` as a parent. prs.title: feat(skills): import personal skill bundles from URLs
prs.body:
<!--
Required PR title: type: user-facing description.
Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled so maintainers can help update the branch.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Personal skill imports require manual downloads and uploads even when a skill and its companion files already have an HTTPS source.

## User Impact

Import an HTTPS `SKILL.md` or archive bundle through **Plugins → Skills → My skills → Import skill**. Recognized GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea/Forgejo folder-link shapes are normalized without a browser hostname allowlist. Companion files, nested relative paths, and binary files use the existing bundle representation. File, folder, ZIP, and ClawHub imports remain available.

Operators can permit private-network downloads with `skills.library.import.allowedOrigins`: exact HTTPS scheme/host/port entries, absent or empty by default. Grants apply to everyone already authorized to import. An explicitly approved loopback-literal origin retains the shared guard's exception; metadata/link-local destinations and unrelated private origins remain protected. This grants network access, not repository authentication: the Gateway still needs corporate DNS/VPN and TLS trust, and browser login cookies or publishing credentials are not forwarded.

Repository archives must fit the existing download/extraction limits before directory selection, so a small skill inside a large repository can fail. Use a smaller direct bundle URL and selected directory in that case. Unknown forge webpages need the explicit archive fallback; ambiguous refs can use the ref/directory overrides.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replacement is a source adapter into the existing guarded HTTP, safe extraction, canonical bundle, scanning, install-policy, and personal-save owners—not a separate installer. The same import RPC gains a closed URL source alternative. Remote files/archives retain truthful third-party, mutable, network source facts rather than being classified as user-authored local files. Current write authority and private-origin grants are checked across awaited work.

The GitHub-only repository importer, chooser, and superseded policy/test plumbing are retired. There is no Git clone/sparse-checkout system, browser host-list expansion, or fetched-script execution. Canonical validator regeneration causes large numbering changes, but independent normalization isolated the semantic change to the import-parameter predicate.

## Evidence

The branch is integrated with pinned main `1c2d67466484`. The generated-validator conflict was resolved canonically; the full PR contains 19 paths. The previously failing **check-docs**, **check-test-types-core-2**, and **checks-fast-baseline-ratchets** now pass on `ee31fce393b5`. Other CI checks were still running at verification time.

**Intentional config-surface change:** the approved `skills.library.import.allowedOrigins` option adds four containing namespace/list entries. Core config budget is **2622 → 2626**, with the canonical baseline regenerated. Removing exactly those entries reproduces all four prior baseline hashes. This explicit operator control supports private-network sources without weakening the public-only default or granting permissions through an import request.

### Current hosted review

[ClawSweeper completed review of `ee31fce393b5`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192781#issuecomment-6631028784). Its findings section is **None**, and it confirms the earlier code findings are addressed. It rates readiness/proof **1/6** and patch quality **3/6**, keeping the PR blocked before merge on proof—not identifying a new concrete source defect.

The requested merge evidence remains:
- A real authenticated Gateway and transport run showing allowed publication, source-policy denial, and read-only/revoked profiles and revoked origin grants rejected before the relevant request/publication effects. This also covers the review's security-attention and merge-risk items.
- Latest-stable upgrade proof retaining existing settings, stored skills, and revisions.
- Public matched before/after captures of this URL-import dialog.

The import-dialog pair in the original discussion is this PR's own pinned-main/candidate capture; **no editor media from PR #180566 is relied on as evidence here**. Work-session links below provide attribution/provenance, not public media URLs, and protected discussion contents have not been republished.

<details>
<summary>Local validation, integrity and input-scan repair</summary>

- **18 Gateway importer tests passed on the final repair bytes.** The exact Gateway-methods test-type leaf was demonstrated red on the earlier source and green after JSZip produced an owned `ArrayBuffer`, fixing all three Fetch-body errors without casts or reduced coverage. HTTP transport is mocked; extraction, policy execution, SQLite ownership and publication are real.
- The unchanged UI retains **22 passing upload tests**, full UI typecheck and matched visual evidence. Core typecheck, schema/origin smoke and canonical protocol/runtime generation passed on the preceding integrated snapshot; the repair adds help and test/documentation metadata, not a new production import path.
- Final targeted lint/format, config-doc generation/check, docs formatting, max-lines and whitespace checks passed. Pinned-main and actual-CI-base budgets passed with **326 net test lines / 326 allocated** and 11 lines of slack; the shared test scalar was not increased.
- Fresh independent review verified the five repairs and all 19 source hashes/blobs/modes, finding no actionable P0–P2 issue. Reviewed/published tree: `62896720b168307c1835b2e0f7911e79235d9b8c`. Generated predicates and the remaining feature implementation are unchanged from the prior reviewed snapshot.
- **Two maintained bundled-UI capture tests passed** for a matched 1280×900/light pair using synthetic Gateway data. The entire UI subtree matched pinned main for the baseline; candidate files and index were restored and verified. The pair and earlier URL-handoff/companion/binary captures are attached in the original discussion.
- The [earlier hosted attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42086188372) stopped before code review at input scanning. Redacted diagnostics localized a credential-shaped synthetic URI. The test now creates fresh UUID userinfo through the URL API while retaining all five malformed-origin cases. No scanner ignore, encoding workaround, policy exception or real credential was introduced. The subsequent current-head hosted scan and code review completed; the failed attempt itself was never counted as a review.

</details>

**Remaining operator-bound limits:** local autoreview was unavailable and did not run. Full real-Gateway/private-source and stable-upgrade proof still need a qualified prepared isolated runtime; the available preparation path reaches a managed-runtime permission boundary. The last approved public-image publication attempt returned HTTP401, and no authentication repair or successful public hosting has been confirmed. Screenshots are attached in the protected discussion, not public inline assets. CI/security/review gates still apply; this is not a merge-ready claim. No live policy, credentials, services or deployment changed.

Requested by and developed with product direction from @jacobtomlinson.
