prs.title: fix(delivery): resend routed Telegram finals and hand unconfirmed delivery to the agent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram users sometimes get a fixed message saying "I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat, so I won't resend it automatically. Please ask for any missing remainder." The message arrives on their next message, which can be hours later, even when a newer reply has already arrived. It is not written by the agent, it adds nothing the user can act on, and it often refers to a reply the user already received.

## Root cause

PR #168738 already lets Telegram resend an ordinary text final reply once after an ambiguous network failure, accepting a rare duplicate. Only the inbound dispatcher (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`) opted in. Routed finals (exec completions, followups, session events) go through `src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.ts`, which did not opt in. The same `read ECONNRESET` therefore ended as unknown custody. The owed debt (`pendingDeliveryNotice`, #121833) was then posted as fixed text by `deliverPendingDeliveryNotice` on the next inbound message. Nothing expired it or cleared it after a newer reply had already reached the chat.

## Evidence from production (Peanutto, logs since 2026-09-16, plus every agent transcript)

- 8 sends ended `unknown_after_send`; 4 notices were posted. They arrived 13m10s, 45m36s, 4m49s, and 7h28m37s after the lost reply.
- In the first three cases the user's next message was "well?", "^", or "pls answer". The replies were really lost, and the notice didn't spare the user from asking.
- The 2026-11-04 notice followed an exec-completion reply that hit `sendRichMessage failed: network request failed transport={"code":"ECONNRESET","syscall":"read"}`. Recovery then logged `delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay`. A newer reply at 09:00 was delivered; the notice still went out at 16:07.
- Inbound final replies that hit the same `read ECONNRESET` (2026-10-20, 10-24, 10-26) were resent automatically about 6 seconds later (`retrying an unconfirmed final text reply`) and never produced a notice.
- Not stale keep-alive reuse: a raw keep-alive connection to `api.telegram.org` (nginx) stayed open for 300s idle, and OpenClaw closes idle Telegram sockets at 30s (`extensions/telegram/src/fetch.ts`). The same host also logs `read ECONNRESET` against OpenAI and Telegram file downloads, so these are network-path resets. The Bot API has no idempotency key, so a reset after the write is genuinely ambiguous.

## Comparison: NousResearch/hermes-agent @ `71736c9f`

- Retries connection resets (`connectionreset`, `network`, `remotedisconnected`, …) up to 2 times, accepting duplicates; only read timeouts are left alone (`gateway/platforms/base.py:1746`, `:3532-3640`; `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:1470-1477`).
- When retries run out, it sends a localized failure notice right away, not on the next message (`base.py:3633-3640`).
- Crash redeliveries carry a visible "may be a duplicate" marker (`gateway/delivery_ledger.py:41-43`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Rule: no silent loss, no duplicates beyond the accepted Telegram tradeoff from #168738, and no stale or context-free system text.

1. **The channel owns the replay decision.** `ChannelMessageDurableFinalAdapter.replayAmbiguousFinalText` declares that a channel prefers a rare duplicate over a lost reply; Telegram sets it. Callers only mark a reply as an agent final (`retryAmbiguousFinalText`). `deliver-queue.ts` grants the existing bounded replay only when both hold and the payload is ordinary final text. Route-reply now marks `replyKind: "final"`, so exec completions and other routed finals get the same single resend as inbound finals. Other channels stay off.
2. **No fixed text in the chat.** `admitPendingDeliveryNotice` (replacing `deliverPendingDeliveryNotice`) offers owed debt to the turn being admitted on the same route as a system event. The debt stays owed until `drainFormattedSystemEvents` actually puts it in a prompt, which then acknowledges it. A restart or a turn that never reaches the model leaves it owed, and the next turn offers it again. The agent sees that its reply may not have arrived and decides whether to restate it. The channel send, transcript append, and queue-owner lookup are removed.
3. **A later delivered reply settles older debt.** When a newer final is fully delivered to the same route, `projectPendingFinalDeliveryState` marks older owed or unresolved debt acknowledged.

Kept from #121833/#154417: debt is persisted and survives restart; there is no notice during an in-flight send; one intent never owes twice; there is no time-based expiry. Stored `unresolved` debt from the old sender is handed to the agent once.

The Telegram E2E harness gains `telegramApiReject.reset` (`before-forward` / `after-forward`), which resets the Gateway connection either before Telegram sees the request or after Telegram accepted it. The second mode reproduces the production `read ECONNRESET`.

## Evidence

### Telegram Test Server, real QA user (TDLib), Convex-leased bot

Scenario: the user asks for a background check; the mock model starts `exec` (`sleep 4; echo BG_DONE_MARKER`, `yieldMs: 1000`). The exec completion produces a routed final `ROUTED_FINAL_MARKER …`. The proxy resets the first `sendMessage` containing that marker. At 45s the user sends `FOLLOWUP_PING`; the mock answers `PONG_MARKER SAW_DELIVERY_NOTE` only if the delivery note reached the model.

| Case | Base `4b13fade` (main) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request reset before Telegram saw it | Routed final never appears; on the next message the user gets the fixed "I couldn't confirm…" text | Routed final resent once and visible; no fixed text; next turn `NO_DELIVERY_NOTE` |
| Telegram accepted, then reset (`read ECONNRESET`) | Routed final visible once; next message still gets the fixed "I couldn't confirm…" text (false alarm) | Routed final visible twice (accepted #168738 tradeoff); no fixed text |
| Both attempts reset before Telegram | — | No fixed text; next turn `SAW_DELIVERY_NOTE` (agent informed) |

These runs used the candidate before the review fix that moved acknowledgment from offer time to prompt consumption. That fix does not change what reaches the chat or what the next prompt contains; it only decides when the persisted debt is marked acknowledged.

A later base rerun of the before-forward case was skewed by host load: the follow-up arrived before the routed final was sent, so it is not used as evidence.

### Tests

- New regressions that fail on the base and pass here:
  - `route-reply.ambiguous-final.test.ts`: a routed final is resent once after `read ECONNRESET` when the channel opts in. A channel without the opt-in, and a non-final reply, still refuse blind replay.
  - `session-pending-final-settlement.test.ts`: a later delivered same-route final settles older owed and unresolved debt. Debt is kept when the later reply went to another chat, and newer debt is owed when the later reply is also unconfirmed.
- `pending-delivery-notice.test.ts` and `.integration.test.ts` now prove the next turn receives the debt once, with no chat send. They also cover concurrent admissions, route/account/thread mismatch, the global-session owner, in-flight sends, and replay after restart.
- Harness: `telegram-test-api-proxy.test.mjs` covers both reset modes.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed (typecheck, lint, line-cap and dead-export guards, import cycles).
- `pending-delivery-notice.test.ts` also covers acknowledgment only after a prompt consumes the offer, and a lost offer being re-offered.
- Independent review (autoreview, Claude engine, P1). The first pass found that debt was acknowledged at offer time, which a restart could lose; fixed as above. Its other finding was not a defect: replay was already Telegram-only on main. The second pass was `scoped-clean`. Remaining notes below threshold: an offer queued just before a newer final supersedes the debt can still reach the agent as a stale hint the agent can ignore. If the event belongs to a different session than the current one, acknowledgment uses the default store path, which leaves the debt re-offered rather than lost.

prs.title: fix(ci): detect imported asynchronous transaction callbacks
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193842

## What Problem This Solves

The transaction boundary check incorrectly passes asynchronous callbacks and commit hooks reached through imports, option spreads, and PostgreSQL connection methods.

## User Impact

Internal tooling only; no user-visible runtime change. No SQLite schema/version, DDL, migration, persisted-format, public API, or runtime configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing native TypeScript owner to inspect resolved callback results and effective commit hooks, and identify PostgreSQL methods by their declaration owner. This replaces the file-wide async-name heuristic while preserving asynchronous preparation and unrelated async transaction APIs.

Static proof remains conservative for mixed overload sets, erased mutable options, and detached async effects. The guard does not claim exhaustive async safety.

## Evidence

- Actual relocated CLI regression: the baseline exits 0 on ten invalid cases; the repaired CLI reports all ten with exact locations and exits 1.
- All 16 focused tests pass, including valid synchronous overrides, computed keys, lexical shadows, reassigned callbacks, replaced mutable hooks, and unrelated async APIs.
- Targeted tsgo, lint, formatting, and the guard against the complete source checkout pass. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42164947454) and the [build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42164947386) both passed.
- Independent review corrections removed stale options-initializer inference, fixed computed-key precedence, and restored void-erased shorthand-hook rejection (red/green regression verified).

<details>
<summary>Tooling and regression scope</summary>

The guard adds 106 net tooling lines for resolved dependency/owner contracts, while deleting the old name set and literal-only hook scan. The separate allocation grants exactly 189 net test LF for the actual CLI boundary and distinct precision regressions; the shared test ceiling is unchanged.

Release-note context: internal CI guard hardening only; no migration or operator action.

</details>

prs.title: fix(plugins): install native dependencies when stage execution is denied
prs.body:
Related: #193772

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin installation rejecting a complete native dependency when a sandbox denies execution inside the writable install stage.

## User Impact

Staged native packages can pass completeness validation using filesystem metadata. Actual execution still requires existing runtime and OS authority. Missing or incomplete packages still receive one fresh-cache retry; persistent failure preserves the previous generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old installer asks for `X_OK`, which can fail with `EPERM` even when staging filesystem operations are permitted. Check the existing admitted path for a regular file and Unix executable mode instead; Windows `.exe` files do not require Unix bits. Genuine metadata errors still fail verification. Admission, integrity, aliases, native declarations, backup and publication remain with their existing owners.

Thanks to @RalphPepperoni for the report, Seatbelt reproduction and prepared patch in #193772. This adapts the metadata/mode portion only; no verified source-commit identity was supplied for a reporter author trailer. Their reported 11/11 built-module results are supporting reporter evidence, not an independent pass for this change.

## Evidence

- Deterministic owner/installer tables cover mocked X_OK/EPERM denial with no installer execute probe, missing/nonregular/Unix-mode and mocked Windows.exe controls, genuine stat EACCES/EPERM, aliases, any complete vendor target, nonnative/no-bin, once-only repair and retained prior generation. Mock results cannot establish native OS behavior.
- The new Seatbelt case is explicitly selected by existing `test:macos:ci:1`. It uses real npm/loopback registry/publication and the real source installer subprocess, with a fixed hosted-Xcode native fixture and stage-only execution denial. It requires actual X_OK/spawn EPERM including the real pre-publication native path, complete B publication, incomplete C retry/failure, stage cleanup and exact old/source byte/mode/link preservation. Unsupported macOS controls fail; Linux skips are not native proof.
- Prior [7109 run42144406540](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42144406540) actually selected the named case: 1failed/not skipped, test4.083s/file8.09s, before installer entry due to workspace-package resolution. Lint core2 also reported a Promise executor return. The approved repair in `342c3df5099e33bef4c2788a72eb4521d5d93851` fixes only these two fixture defects: repository cwd only for the source installer child, and a void block for registry cleanup. Existing TSX flags/aliases, explicit isolated npm/state/config/cache/registry paths and all denial/publication assertions are unchanged. The loader owner documents foreign-cwd alias loss; repository context is canonical. No new loader hook, dependency/build/artifact/Swift/workflow/producer or permission change.
- One new canonical main-tier CI dispatch [42147441632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42147441632) targets exact `342c3df5099e33bef4c2788a72eb4521d5d93851` on the same workflow revision. Actual checkout and named native execution/phase results remain pending. The prior failures are not relabeled green; no rerun or additional push was made beyond this approved repair. PR remains draft.
- Fresh complete-candidate P0–P3 independent source-only Codex subagent review: **0 actionable findings**, base `589214aaffb8d36c62903e37322f3085f1f47551`, reviewed/published tree `866c577d32696d345a37748d1f2e76ee77647057`, full diff SHA256 `2d49ff0fb0d1ed60ed56435f6194204f69568f0482cf39d1b6e21bbd5bd048ca`. - The source installer does not call CLI record retirement, so the test compares the whole old project without marker exclusions or fabricated metadata. No official published-native-artifact qualification is claimed.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the conversation when a stopped first Claude CLI turn has no operator authority
prs.body:
Related: #181945
Follow-up to #181966

## What problem this solves

Stopping the first Claude CLI turn still clears its native conversation when the run has no operator model authority. The stopped-first-turn guard from #181966 never runs on that branch, so the next turn starts a new native session even though OpenClaw's host history still retains the original user message.

## Fix and user impact

Always pass the existing composed `assertCurrent` into CLI preparation, including runs with neither operator model execution nor a cron generation. The assertion already checks the caller's abort signal, caller assertion, model authority and cron generation in order. Their composition and authority remain unchanged; the existing guarded publication of a stopped first native binding now runs on the ordinary no-operator path too.

Because the caller's own abort reason can now propagate unchanged, trajectory recording also recognizes identity with that run's `abortSignal.reason`, rather than relying only on a generic `AbortError`. This keeps a caller's `TimeoutError` classified as aborted without treating unrelated errors as cancellation by name.

Users can stop a fresh Claude CLI reply and continue the same native conversation on the documented loopback `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` path. Existing authenticated operator behavior is preserved. No new config, permission, SDK surface, store, schema or credential behavior is introduced.

## Evidence

[Independent real-Claude Gateway, native JSONL, provider-history and regression evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186380#issuecomment-6457381257).

- Main: `591b7795fe8b64aba2b84ee5764534da545b3869`.
- Runtime candidate: `897c0cb639ee5eccf02baf09cf9aae58847b60ba`.
- Final head: `cfc8bb94a9633f5bfa25e6c8904e7b1c83ec8759`; only test consolidation follows the runtime build, so production source is identical.
- Full builds succeeded for both refs inside secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. The **genuine Claude Code 2.1.312 CLI** runs non-root with task-owned native homes, workspaces, Gateway profiles and state. No real Anthropic credentials, personal Claude login, stub CLI, seeded database or fabricated native ID is used.

Public WebSocket `sessions.create` → first `chat.send` with a unique marker → actual native exec tool work (`sleep 3`) and a flushed native assistant checkpoint → hold the following real Messages stream → `chat.abort` → follow-up `chat.send`. The external Messages fixture derives its follow-up answer from the actual received history, not the selected ref or an unconditional marker response.

| Case | Native conversation ID | Original marker in actual follow-up provider history | Public reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main, auth:none, run 1 | changed | absent | `UNKNOWN` |
| Main, auth:none, run 2 | changed | absent | `UNKNOWN` |
| Candidate, auth:none, run 1 | unchanged | present | original marker |
| Candidate, auth:none, run 2 | unchanged | present | original marker |
| Main, authenticated operator control | unchanged | present | original marker |
| Candidate, authenticated operator control | unchanged | present | original marker |

All six public host histories retain the original first user message unchanged. Native IDs are independently matched between Claude's actual JSONL files and the real Messages request metadata. The requests identify their client as `claude-cli/2.1.312 (external, sdk-cli)`.

Focused tests: **19/19 pass** across the stopped-partial-output and trajectory owners. The same no-operator case fails on main with `clearCliSessionBinding:true`; the caller-timeout case fails on main with generic `AbortError` instead of its original `TimeoutError`. Targeted type-aware Oxlint: **0 warnings / 0 errors**. Oxfmt passes on all four changed files.

The no-operator case now shares the existing stopped-first-turn table, preserving flushed/unflushed, refused-write, superseded and resumed controls. Both disabled-trajectory controls remain in a shared table. Whole-PR production delta **+6/-2**; test delta **+50/-55 (net −5)**. No test ceiling change.

### Scope and limits

The real-flow proof covers normal loopback WebSocket chat and authenticated operator controls through the actual Claude runtime against a deterministic local Messages fixture, not Anthropic's real service. Other non-operator ingresses share the runner branch but were not live-tested here. Other native CLI backends were not exercised end to end.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the previous checkpoint behavior without migrations or stored-data rewrites. Blast radius is shared CLI run checkpoints and CLI trajectory cancellation classification; an incorrect assertion could reject a valid CLI turn or mishandle its stopped binding. Existing caller/authority guards and stopped/resumed/timeout controls remain intact.

prs.title: improve(control-ui): drop the IP address parser from the chat boot bundle
prs.body:
Closes #193832

## What Problem This Solves

Every cold load of the Control UI chat route downloads and compiles `ipaddr.js` and `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` (about 17 KB minified) in the chat boot bundle, although first paint never uses them. They are only needed to check an assistant `MEDIA:` line whose https host is an IP literal.

## User Impact

The chat boot bundle is 4,487 B (gzip) smaller with the same 20 requests, and `MEDIA:` host decisions are unchanged. Cold-load timing did not change measurably.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `MEDIA:` host guard is split at the point where the IP parser is needed:

- `src/media/remote-media-host.ts` normalizes the host and decides plain hostnames on its own. A host goes to the full guard if it has any character outside `[a-z0-9._-]`, or if every label is decimal or `0x` hex. That covers every input the canonical, loose or legacy IPv4 parsers can read. Until the full guard is installed, those hosts are rejected.
- The full guard is the existing IP literal check, unchanged, written as `createRemoteMediaIpHostnameGuard(ip)` over the `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` module. `src/media/parse-output.ts` stays the server entry point: it imports the full guard statically and installs it at import, so the Gateway's existing importers keep the same synchronous result.
- In the browser, the Control UI message normalizer installs the guard with one dynamic import of `@openclaw/net-policy/ip`, the first time a host is rejected only because the guard was missing.
- `ui/config/control-ui-chunking.ts` keeps `ipaddr.js` and `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` in the lazy `link-reader-response` chunk. The link reader panel and hovercard import the parser too and already preload that chunk, so readers need no extra request and the guard is one request.

<details><summary>Per-file details</summary>

- The parser body moves to `parse-output-core.ts`, which the browser imports. Apart from the guard import it is unchanged (`git diff -B -M` reports a 93% copy); it has to move because the existing server import path must keep the synchronous guard, while the browser needs the same body without a static import of the IP parser.
- `src/media/remote-media-host-ip.ts` binds the full guard to the static `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` import for `parse-output.ts`. The server graph has no dynamic import of the guard, so `pnpm build` reports no ineffective dynamic import.
- The Control UI normalizer calls `splitMediaOutput` from the core. Its previous `splitMediaFromOutput(text, { extractAudioDirectives: false })` call never enabled markdown image extraction, so the result is the same. A message whose media host was rejected only because the guard was still loading is not cached, and the computation that built it subscribes to the guard's load.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.ts`: the transcript item cache treats guard readiness as part of its structural identity, so a message that had no visible content while the guard loaded (a captionless `MEDIA:` line) gets its row once the guard is installed. The first guard load in a page therefore rebuilds every cached session transcript once, including transcripts with no IP literal media; it happens at most once per page load.
- `src/media/remote-media-host.ts` keeps its hostname helpers module-private; only the guard entry points are exported.
- `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json` is regenerated with `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen`. The chat set drops `ipaddr.js`, `net-policy/src/ip.ts`, `media/parse.ts`, `media/parse-output.ts` and `markdown-core/src/image-spans.ts`, and adds `media/parse-output-core.ts` and `media/remote-media-host.ts`.
- `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` lists the three new modules that `parse-output.ts` now imports.
- Without the chunk rule, the bundler emits the parser as a new `ip-*.js` chunk. That adds an entry in the middle of the shared boot chunk's preload table and renumbers every later preload index in the file: +27 raw bytes, but +79 B gzip, over the shared chunk's cap. With the rule, the table is unchanged; the link reader chunk keeps the three modules it had on main and gains the parser.

</details>

The guard chunk is not preloaded. A speculative idle preload was measured at an earlier revision and rejected: on every cold chat load it fetched the guard code (16.2 KB transferred), which is more than the boot bundle saves.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before the timing runs: chat boot JS gzip drops with the same request count; no other boot budget grows beyond build variance; cold-chat transfer bytes drop in every pair; no timing metric moves beyond its A/A control.

Production builds on one Mac (Node 24.22.2, Darwin arm64), base `4aea2c089cb710fc619d92bf0de28749236c87b2`, measured in a checkout without `dist/`, no budget changes:

```sh
pnpm ui:check-performance:base 4aea2c089cb710fc619d92bf0de28749236c87b2
```

| gzip bytes (asset hashes normalized) | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat boot JavaScript (20 requests both) | 1,288,491 | 1,284,004 | -4,487 |
| New Session boot JavaScript (15 requests both) | 797,107 | 797,114 | +7 |
| Largest JS chunk (`control-ui-boot-shared`) | 560,308 | 560,315 | +7 |
| Startup JavaScript | 90,215 | 90,215 | 0 |
| CSS (startup, chat, new session, total) | unchanged | unchanged | 0 |

The check exits 0. The chat boot bundle on the base is 293 B over its 1,288,198 B limit; with this change it is 4,194 B under. The shared chunk stays 35 B under its 560,350 B cap, with the same raw size as the base (1,819,791 B); its only difference is the order of two existing entries in the reader preload lists. New Session stays under its 797,620 B limit, and no module enters or leaves its boot set. The emitted `control-ui-boot-chat` chunk no longer contains `ipaddr.js`.

Run the comparison in a checkout without `dist/extensions` (before `pnpm build`, or after removing `dist/`). The candidate build folds the packaged plugin inventory it finds there into `control-ui-boot-shared-*.js` (`ui/src/plugins/control-ui-distribution.ts`), while the archived base does not, which adds a few hundred bytes to the shared chunk regardless of the change under test.

Real Gateway run (built UI from `pnpm build`, isolated Gateway with a seeded transcript, Playwright Chromium headless shell, every https request answered locally, on this revision and base): a captionless `MEDIA:https://8.8.8.8/a.png` message shows no image while the guard request (`link-reader-response-*.js`) is held, and its image is requested 26 ms after the chunk is released and renders. Eight blocked hosts (`127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254`, `[::1]`, `0x7f.1`, the private-range fixture `192.168.1.10`, `100.64.0.1`, `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]`, `localhost`) are never requested and never appear in the transcript; `https://8.8.8.8/a.png` is the only https request among 57.

Transcript after the guard chunk is released (the image card above "History ends here."):

![Transcript after the guard chunk loads: the image card (a decoded 1x1 grey fixture) renders above the closing text](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/raw/5eebcfdac5aa4ce5844416927478bf45376dc8f7/real-gateway-guard-loaded.png)

While the chunk is held, the same transcript shows only the prompt and the closing text: [real-gateway-guard-held.png](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/5eebcfdac5aa4ce5844416927478bf45376dc8f7/real-gateway-guard-held.png). Full request log, Gateway origin redacted as `<gateway>`: [real-gateway-media-ip-host.json](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/5eebcfdac5aa4ce5844416927478bf45376dc8f7/real-gateway-media-ip-host.json).

<details><summary>Network summary from the request log</summary>

| ms after navigation | event |
| ---: | --- |
| 378 | `GET <gateway>/assets/link-reader-response-*.js` (held) |
| 560 | transcript shown |
| 2,071 | public IP images in the transcript while held: 0 |
| 2,384 | guard chunk released |
| 2,410 | `GET https://8.8.8.8/a.png`, the only https request of 57 |
| 2,495 | image rendered and decoded |

Requested: none of `https://127.0.0.1/loopback.png`, `https://169.254.169.254/metadata.png`, `https://[::1]/loopback-v6.png`, `https://0x7f.1/hex-loopback.png`, `https://192.168.1.10/private.png`, `https://100.64.0.1/shared.png`, `https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/mapped.png`, `https://localhost/name.png`. All other requests go to the Gateway origin.

</details>

At an earlier revision the real Gateway run also passed with the `chat-thread.ts` change reverted, because something else in that page rebuilds the transcript after the guard loads. The unit test below is the regression guard for that change.

Cold load with the committed bench, measured at the previous revision of this change on base `6e7ee204e1b`, 20 interleaved base / base (A/A) / head triplets per profile, untraced, cold chat route, production Gateway HTTP handler, Playwright Chromium headless shell, same host and toolchain for all arms. Since then the guard's load path (now one request to the reader chunk), the transcript cache for IP literal hosts and the base changed; the bench fixture has no IP literal host and never loads the guard. The byte figures above are current; the timing table is not rerun.

```sh
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --gateway-http --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --runs 60 \
  --first-load --cold-http-cache --untraced --thread-cpu-time --critical-path --face chat \
  [--network-latency-ms 100 --download-kbps 10000]
```

| Cold chat, median (paired median vs preceding base) | Base | A/A | Head | A/A paired | Head paired |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Local: transfer bytes | 1,573,162 | 1,573,162 | 1,569,245 | 0.0% | -0.2% (-3,917 B in every pair) |
| Local: first transcript ms | 390.1 | 378.6 | 381.1 | -1.4% | -2.3% |
| Local: first enabled composer ms | 175.8 | 174.3 | 172.8 | -2.4% | -0.3% |
| Local: main-thread task ms | 1,035.3 | 1,039.8 | 1,025.4 | +0.4% | -0.2% |
| Remote (100 ms, 10 Mbps): transfer bytes | 1,573,162 | 1,573,162 | 1,569,245 | 0.0% | -0.2% (every pair) |

The host was shared (1-minute load average median 58 local, 39 remote). Every timing difference is inside the A/A spread (paired p95 of 1.2% to 12.3% across these metrics), so this change shows no cold-load timing gain, and no regression beyond A/A. At 10 Mbps the saved bytes are worth about 3 ms out of about 1,420 ms, below what this bench resolves. The claim is the byte reduction, which is deterministic: the A/A arm is 0 B and the head arm is 3,917 B smaller in all 40 pairs.

Tests (all pass at the head):

- `src/media/parse-output.host-guard.test.ts` pins 87 end-to-end decisions (85 hosts plus two scheme and URL parser cases) through `splitMediaOutput` and `splitMediaFromOutput`: special-use dotted IPv4; shorthand, octal, hex and integer IPv4; IPv6 loopback, unspecified, link-local, ULA, multicast and documentation; IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 embeddings; localhost, `.local`, `.internal` and dotless names; public IPs and hostnames that look like IPs; non-https, credentials, and hosts the URL parser refuses. The same file passes unchanged on the base.
  Because the table runs through `parse-output.ts`, it also shows that the server entry installs the full guard at import: the public IP literals would be rejected otherwise.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-media-host.test.ts`: a captionless IP literal `MEDIA:` message has no row before the guard loads and gets one after, through `buildCachedChatItems` and through the transcript stream source inside a computation, with no history change. Both cases fail without the `chat-thread.ts` change.
- `ui/src/app/control-ui-chunking.test.ts` pins `ipaddr.js` and `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` to the `link-reader-response` chunk.
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.media-files.e2e.test.ts` (Control UI e2e, shipped bundle, mocked Gateway): a public IP literal `MEDIA:` image renders and loads, and a `127.0.0.1` one is dropped. It passes on this branch and, with only the test added, on the base.
- `pnpm test src/media/`, the Control UI normalizer, chat thread, chat route and router outlet tests, `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`, `node scripts/check-control-ui-controllers.mts`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (within the ratchet), `pnpm build` (no ineffective dynamic import for `src/media` or `net-policy`), `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` (output identical to the committed manifest) and `pnpm ui:check-performance:base`, all on current main. The full Control UI test lane, including the browser projects, has the same failing set on this branch and on main on this machine (none of those files touch media, chat thread or chunking). `pnpm lint` exits 1 with the same findings on this branch and on main, none in a file this change touches.

The screenshots above are behaviour proof for the delayed IP literal attachment. Rendered output does not change for any message once the guard has loaded.

Risks:

- Tradeoff for maintainers: this saves 4,487 B of chat boot JavaScript, and in exchange an assistant `MEDIA:` attachment whose host is an IP literal appears after one extra request (about 21 KB raw, 6.6 KB gzip) on the first such message in a page load. Hostname URLs are not affected. The parser moves rather than disappears: in a session with no IP literal media yet, the first link reader open downloads about 5 KB gzip more in its existing `link-reader-response` request, and the link reader panel no longer imports the chat boot chunk statically. If that delay is not acceptable for IP literal media, this change should not land.
- If `link-reader-response-*.js` cannot load (offline, deploy skew), messages with IP literal hosts keep their attachment hidden and retry the import on each normalization until reload. That stays fail closed; there is no error shown for it.
- A new server caller that imports `parse-output-core.ts` or `remote-media-host.ts` directly, without `parse-output.ts`, rejects IP literal hosts, because only `parse-output.ts` and the Control UI install the full guard. That is safe, but different. The module headers say so.

prs.title: fix: bound reloadable chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain more transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history, releases evicted bodies from presentation caches, and keeps older/newer navigation reversible.

## User Impact

Ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Source atomicity, the current reader packet and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks. Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. A local command after an authoritative empty-history read stays before the first later turn, including after resident-prefix retirement and older-page admission. Unloaded or unknown history never implies the beginning. Command replies retain transient custody and retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. The owner accepts that product tradeoff after investigation; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership controls trimming, reopening, continuity and retirement. SQLite and actor-memory reads certify same-snapshot Stop continuation; UI admission revalidates a fresh selected packet. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits, prepared bodies do not. One synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and accepted-prefix receipt adoption. Visible fitting reads commit without an unnecessary fallback/staged read, while sparse/raw progress, smaller-envelope retries and cancellation retain their existing contracts.

Accepted raw source facts and one canonical publication owner govern local-output placement; empty views, stale reads, pending inputs and unavailable outbox storage do not confer authority. Local occurrence placement preserves consecutive command order without inventing durable sequence zero. Edge-only history traversal advances navigation while preserving the original held packet bodies, certificate and opaque endpoints; actual cuts or body changes still revoke that custody.

One native offset producer supplies paging/follow facts before callback-induced rendering, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Presentation-owned partial retirement releases dormant bodies while preserving safe survivor seeds. Weak terminal-row revision reuse preserves exact digest bytes and supported content/block/reaction updates. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts; releasing nonempty quote bodies still invalidates their previews.

Integration retains frozen main12265's app-context receipts, bounded composer context-window display, medium-transcript fragmentation/preparation, indexed selectors and asset policy alongside deferred row notifications, pending steering, canonical streaming geometry, catalog continuation, monotonic retry, reply-adjacency facts, prose/tool ordering and context-usage equality. It retains bounded source retirement, per-caller cancellation, private staged authority and immutable native-scroll facts. Pending accepted row notifications flush before forwarding the already-captured native-scroll primitive; current native measurements are acknowledged before virtual writes. Stable host capabilities release first-render snapshots and old renderer-owned DOM on the same useful host; reusable Markdown templates keep their separate bounded owner. Validators and boot inventory use canonical generators. M3 adds no dependency, configuration, SQLite-schema or protocol-version bump; inherited main changes are not attributed to this feature.

## Evidence

The published predecessor is signed **e3d47ee7600d1355979d69f9bc2dc75a8efaff5e**, qualified against frozen main57ab. GitHub reported CONFLICTING/DIRTY against pinned main **12265e76a349ad11dcd38c4e167a06d6d3eae5a9**. The supported signed two-parent successorb515 joins those histories; its exact eight-path follow-through is now signed **e0a23b37af8103a6ef4252e3a6a367cd9b1b70e6**, tree **3c4cc47d0d45d6c961435d3939942e083f37d97c**. All221 reviewed Git blobs/modes match the clean current checkout. Full source manifest: **1d7784c1ef3576ac99d5153123fa447aaa4f97f5056231ba9aa4e33f5b305a65**, totaling4,637,285B. Local signed-source/runtime/UI/strict qualification is complete at the scopes below; current native validation, publication and hosted landing proof remain pending.

- Complete primary and bounded independent owner/caller/history/dependency reads support the committed12265 join: context-window display moves into the canonical snapshot contract; medium completed-run fragments retain weak revision ownership, chronological coverage and final-answer keys; native `data-row-size` receipts do not replace current DOM height authority. Incoming app-context receipts, pending-steering, indexed selectors and target New/CSS policy remain intact. No compatibility wrapper, duplicate cache owner or synchronous global Solid flush was added. The normal isolated frozen-lock install qualified the one incoming rerank workspace link; the installed lock equals the pinned workspace document.
- Canonical whole-pool validator generation/check passed with567 exports. Public compiled history/startup continuity and app-context admission controls exercise the real generated predicates, including cardinality, bounds and closed-object rejection; schema-only checks are not substituted for that proof. The eight-stage join pack passed compiler/schema/generator45, real Gateway history/send/steer56, Node index/long-run/mounted-retention70, cache/warm-composer/preparation89, standalone geometry18, resize/handoff/notification15 and shared-Chromium geometry28, plus targeted formatting. Packs can overlap and are not summed into a new global total.
- Prepared-row coverage is composed of30 original passes plus the two failed cases corrected at the native-height fixture boundary; no production guard or expected bound changed. Follow-up static/type/style/assertion/max-lines gates passed. Fresh app-context UI/chunk controls and canonical BOOT capture passed; requested entries match12265, with1,085 shared/130 New/700 Chat modules. These are current source/graph facts, not timing or memory measurements.
- The default **20-pass source review** of the actual eight-path follow-through against real signedb515 is scoped-clean: all20 provider completions are complete/correct/findings empty, with exact raw/provider/saved-report equality and no unknown/partial attempts. It includes44 whole authored owner/guide contexts and installed dependency context. Committed joins are context and separately evidenced owner review, not model-targeted changes; no whole221-path model verdict or reviewer-executed test claim is made. Historical47/two-P2 dispositions, corrected seven-pass review, CSS/checker review and the e3 eleven-pass review retain their original source scopes.
- One genuine12265 image was rebuilt using its byte-exact product overlay plus five shared harness files under nativeb515/indexd98, then the candidate's221 source postimages were restored exactly. This is explicitly dirty-overlay execution, not a clean signed12265 checkout. The earlier failed readiness expectation was corrected to the actual dirty-source scoped flags without replaying runtime. Fresh signed **e0a qaRuntime and exact-head readiness passed** with both stamps bound toe0a, clean inputs, matching signatures, static assets and equivalent-input admission disabled. The normal UI build, full immutable seed/replay, both precompression checks and strict assets passed at this signed head. - The original strict report rejected only Chat by374B against the provisional1,303,981B cap; it remains a failure. On exactly those measured assets, a separately admitted functional diagnostic passed all eight cases. The final policy decision then set only Chat's cap to **1,304,547B = measured1,304,355B +192B generated-name headroom**. Matched genuine12265 Chat is **1,295,651B**, an actual **+8,704B (~0.67%)**, with20 Chat requests in both images. New is786,109B; CSS is1,672,333B raw /323,532B gzip against unchanged target limits1,672,449B/323,616B. The strict-only refresh passed with empty warnings/violations and exactly equal metrics/baseMetrics; other caps, request/startup/largest limits, evaluator and global192B variance are unchanged. Historical561B headroom was an earlier coordinator choice, not a fixed rule. This accepts bounded residency/native ownership's payload cost, not traversal speed, RSS, RAM or Firefox-crash recovery.
- The fresh dirty-source diagnostic passed **eight distinct cases: realGateway3 plus workspace5**, including the original seven subset and inherited scratch-expiry case. Cold hide/rapid-reveal kept the same semantic key with0.4375px drift under the unchanged2px oracle, one actual selected transcript, two cancelled attempts then one restore, one runtime-module request and one80-row/content262144 around read. The59-row reply retained the target at index29 and following context; fullwire263776B includesmetadata. The test overlay was restored after owned-child settlement. Real-Gateway prebuilt runtime and ordinary temporary production-client scopes remain explicit: the diagnostic did not establish sealed signed normal-UI serving. Signed e0a's4,814 functional outputs are exactly equal to the accepted diagnostic's immutable seed, excluding only the four canonical identity-owned files; full seed/replay qualification covers their canonical refresh. This source-and-functional-byte proof carries the eight-case result without a redundant browser cohort; it adds no OS visibility, Firefox, crash or whole-RAM claim.
- Historical continuity repair retains SQLite/incognito causal failures before parity GREEN: a256KiB display-content budget had incorrectly bounded the raw anchor before projection. Removing only that override preserves the canonical8MiB predecode source bound, continuity authority/no-archive rule, lower-reader explicit limits and final response budgeting. A separate stale reply-predecessor test oracle refreshes only the boundary group while319 other survivors remain identical in both views/directions, and published predecessors stay unchanged. The actual failed47 review and69 distinct corrected runtime cases retain those scopes.
- Same-host Node retirement proof retains both active surviving-index and wheel-takeover variants: each releases523 retired DOM/source/frame objects while preserving useful survivor navigation. Stable host-bound capabilities remove first-render snapshot retention; fixture geometry-spy histories were separately released. Reusable Markdown templates retain their separate bounded owner. Historical signede3 runtime/UI/strict/eight-case proof remains predecessor evidence, not current12265 qualification. Remote allocation previously settled unavailable with zero product proof; the trusted native local fallback supplied these current checks.

Historical proof remains bounded by its executed source:

- Historical **816 distinct UI/core/protocol cases**, **11 public continuity-validator probes**, **38 budget-policy cases**, **83 chronology owners** and **124 window/Stop/packet consumers** retain their original scopes. D1 integration refreshed202 executions and pure equality118. Paging had two isolated held-import cases plus59 packet/autofill/retirement cases. Later UI1 59, UI2 198, phone2 and relocated-view133 controls covered actual fixture/type/acquisition corrections. These packs overlap. The actual six-pass correction review was scoped-clean; the later five-pass review reported only stale INDEX relocation findings, resolved by exact staging and the normal hook rather than verdict rewriting.
- Historical signed e622 runtime/UI/strict and original UNTRACED900→1→900 operator proof passed. Its Chat1,287,083B versus D1 1,277,758B and original cap1,288,037B remain historical measurements. D1's intended post-metrics residency failure retained900entries/3,978,127units; e622 held at most400entries/1,768,201units. The same genuine D1 image, produced under native15d with dirtyD1 inputs, was admitted through explicit equivalent-input readiness without stamp rebinding. Historical627 frozenD5 strict used its separate genuine D5 artifact. Historicalf6 used its genuine7e93 image. Historicale3 used its separate genuine57ab artifact. The current comparison uses the new genuine12265 artifact; none substitutes the oldD1 image.
- **Actual then-latest stable v2026.10.9 writers**, release source `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`, wrote DB4/projection1 cache and durable composer text/Blob in the same browser origin. Executed a109 retired stale cache/metadata, refetched history, restored text/attachment without sending and warm-reloaded projection14. Thirteen storage/account/recovery owners remain unchanged; changed optional schemas/comparison were inspected. Carry is semantic storage compatibility under a109, not a new current migration run or blanket input-disjointness.

### Same visual checkpoint

**Before — pinned D1.** Original 900-row corpus, 1440×900 viewport, tail checkpoint. Browser proof retained 900 entries and the intended residency assertion failure.

![Before: pinned D1 at the original tail checkpoint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f94faf0-69f4-4ae3-9dbc-9c78c160f463)

**After — signed e622.** Same corpus, viewport, gestures and checkpoint. The complete operator case passed with at most 400 resident entries.

![After: bounded resident history at the same tail checkpoint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3f1e741-ccdf-4978-8417-c1d6bb747ad7)

Portrait/status and model/effort controls use identical privacy masks. Images show visual behavior; the resident bound comes from the executed browser assertions, not a RAM measurement.

### Performance investigation and accepted product tradeoff

Historical **87d** ten interleaved baseline→candidate pairs remain **REJECTED**: wall median **1,481.747→2,827.432ms (+90.82%)**, renderer CPU **269.290→541.696ms (+101.16%)**,30/36 raw cells worse and over20%. All ten candidate functional cases passed; baseline failures were solely original post-metrics residency assertions. Raw result **59,972 B / `24b2898562c295174d730971f08e78b39e1f5042c912c8a0cd15e80b0010557f`** remains unchanged. No additional pairs or rewritten stop outcome.

The predeclared >20% rule requires investigation. The owner accepts the disclosed bounded-residency/bulk-traversal tradeoff after that investigation. RPC/history/window counts are workload facts constrained by absolute budgets, cursor continuity and coverage; layout/style counts receive no exemption. Timing/CPU/heap/frame measurements remain raw. There is no final-head matched cohort or numeric performance acceptance.

One historical1152 additive observer run preserved original gestures, waits, assertions and engine→wall→two-GC order. Older pages required **two existing idle attempts (526.95–534.35ms)** versus newer pages **one (214.69–217.69ms)**; all four gesture-ready waits passed first try in2.77–4.20ms. This excludes cooldown only as the dominant gesture-wait cost in that capture. It does not explain all CPU or make it unavoidable. Browser/host clocks differ; host WebSocket callbacks are not network/server RTT. Later events followed closed phases, consistent with later endpoint gestures; exact per-event causes were not marked. Observer CPU/wall/heap is affected by instrumentation; no subtraction or speedup claim.

Historical observer artifact **29,248 B / `adcf5ef7e9160bd7c31ce2050b00cdd0cbf749dc84e9178fd9e2f5f4471f334b`**: five phases,86 browser/11host scalar events, no drops/truncation, exact source/output/seal restoration. No new profiler/cohort.

prs.title: fix(cli): recheck a saved account before each paired-node Claude invoke
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A paired-node Claude turn checks that the saved account still exists, then waits for skill setup, history authorization, and an approval retry. Removing the account during one of those waits could still submit the turn.

## Evidence

A loopback Gateway pairs a node over its websocket. The run calls `executeNodeClaudeRun` against that Gateway's live node registry. The node records `node.invoke.request` frames and answers them. The account is a real saved profile, removed with `removeAuthProfilesAcrossOwnerStores`.

Head `e9bf6dc3e8a3b8`, with the rechecks in place:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/node-claude-account-removal.test.ts
TRACE retained account: node received 1 node.invoke.request and returned exit 0
TRACE preparation: account removed before the post-setup dispatch check; node frames=0
TRACE history authorization: account removed during the wait; node frames=0
TRACE approval retry: account removed while the approval was pending; node frames=1 and no second invoke
```

The command exited 0.

The same loopback run with both saved-account rechecks commented out, not committed, still dispatched after removal:

```console
TRACE retained account: node received 1 node.invoke.request and returned exit 0
TRACE BASE preparation dispatched exit=0 frames=1
TRACE BASE history dispatched exit=0 frames=1
TRACE BASE approval dispatched exit=0 frames=2 approvals=1
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A retained saved account is dispatched to the paired node. Removing that account before the post-setup dispatch check, during history authorization, or while an exec approval is pending sends no further invoke frame.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, worktree `/tmp/oc-f098`, head `e9bf6dc3e8a3b8`. The Gateway listens on loopback. The node connects with the Gateway client, is paired, and receives `node.invoke.request` on that socket. The approval case uses the Gateway's exec approval request and an operator client that allows the retry only after the account is removed.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/node-claude-account-removal.test.ts` from `/tmp/oc-f098`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The command output above. One frame and exit 0 when the account remains. Zero frames and `CliCredentialRemovedError` when it is removed before dispatch or during history authorization. One frame, then `CliCredentialRemovedError` and no second frame, when it is removed while the approval is pending.
- **Observed result after fix:** The node sees the Claude command only while the saved account still exists. The approval retry does not send another invoke after the account is removed.
- **What was not tested:** A physical paired computer running the Claude binary. The node here is a paired loopback client that returns the invoke result.

## Summary

Recheck the saved account before a paired-node Claude frame is sent, including after history authorization and on the approval retry.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): unified cached child activity in Details [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A warm signed-in chat reload can insert ordinary child activity into Details after its first populated frame, pushing Outputs and Automations down by 112 px. This revises closed #193894; GitHub refused to reopen its rebased branch, so this replacement tracks the same lane branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary children now extend the existing scoped `subagents` receipt and `projectDetailsSubagents` projection. Bounded collection and ordinary previews share rows, total and existing counts. The parallel receipt, tally, projection and write path are removed. Optional facts contain only the displayed preview; no transcript or live query authority is cached. Admission and activity-observer writes use the same collection ordering. Empty or unavailable live results retire saved facts while preserving already admitted parent facts. Cached display confers no navigation or stop actions.

The activity body stays behind its existing route-local `createIdleImport` owner. Only open Details with cached ordinary rows prepares the same lazy component before admitting the native Details siblings. This avoids an earlier prototype's mistake: its Session body was complete, but Progress/Automations appeared before Session and moved when it arrived. No shared startup import or app boot-order change.

## User Impact

The native attribution candidate shows the full cached Subagents body in the first populated Details frame. Outputs and Automations stay in place when live data answers. Qualification is incomplete: keep this PR draft and do not merge.

## Evidence

Three unscored interleaved native pairs, quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, repo Chromium, 80 ms RTT, active chat with one seeded ordinary child:

| Run | Base first/final Subagents height | Candidate first/final height | Base Outputs / Automations movement | Candidate movement | Base CLS | Candidate CLS |

| 1 | 51 / 112 px | 112 / 112 px | 61 / 61 px | 0 / 0 px | 0.003106 | 0.000855 |
| 2 | absent / 112 px | 112 / 112 px | 112 / 112 px | 0 / 0 px | 0.004947 | 0.000855 |
| 3 | absent / 112 px | 112 / 112 px | 112 / 112 px | 0 / 0 px | 0.004947 | 0.000855 |

This starts at the first **any visible Details group**, including Progress/Automations, rather than a later Session frame. Snapshot bytes: 114,592 → 114,812 (+220). Attribution head: `7bd93c5057b599d36061fcc0c307d4dcce6c2559`; base: `4aea2c089cb710fc619d92bf0de28749236c87b2`; lease `cbx_1e08e7b322c4` (released). These three pairs qualify geometry attribution only; no scored timing or secondary pass is claimed.

The separate native reload regression seeds two ordinary children through the normal first visit and snapshot persistence. It fails on baseline at the first populated frame (0 child rows, expected 2) and passes the attribution candidate. Commands use `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-details-subagents-reload.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: base wall 26.05 s; candidate 24.75 s.

Focused tests: arrival 11 pass (3.39 s wall), snapshot cache 40 pass (2.88 s), Details consumers 18 pass (3.92 s), collection rendering 6 pass (3.02 s), observer receipt/run/connection 1 pass (2.96 s). Changed behavioral tests use the existing dedicated allocation, exactly +322 lines. Independent local review is clean through P2. UI runtime: **+80 net LOC**; required growth retains bounded display facts and live-only action boundaries. Two single-use tally/order helpers and redundant forwarding memos are removed.

The later reader-allocation simplification passes the CI-owned source byte gate with unchanged caps: Chat 1,288,500 → 1,288,398 B (−102), New 797,116 → 796,998 B (−118), startup unchanged. Shared JS is under its cap. These measurements belong to head `afc09e8e85c6f3a426d0152fdf87060f06157d1b` against base `b9dd240237f2321ec8776d6497c1b9055833d8d4`; artifact/full-build sizes are not byte-gate evidence. That head also repeats native geometry3/3 and browser red/green. Changed-file typechecking then found a Solid generic error in the readiness memo. The current repair explicitly resolves readiness to boolean, passes18 Details tests (3.84s wall), and is reviewed clean throughP2. Full UI e2e has not yet run; the type failure was owned and fixed, not classified as inherited.

Current head: `b39af98d2e12c48a21ab8ccdf00c2a66bb966e00`; current pinned base: `8e2f635ecaedc211d0bf68dc6a495d010589e708`. Pending: exact source-owned bytes, 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A for native and Team-scale active/archived/dashboard routes, all hard secondary metrics and per-pair tables, final inspected synthetic Details strips, full UI e2e with baseline classification, and exact-head CI. prs.title: fix(ui): show website identity in dashboard gallery (#178467)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/index.test.ts (2/2 pass).
- TypeScript check: pnpm tsgo:ui (0 errors).
- Linter checks: pnpm lint:ui:styles and pnpm lint:ui:no-raw-window-open (0 errors, 0 warnings across 6091 files).
- Build check: pnpm --dir ui build (clean build of 6325 modules in 1m 19s).
- Visual evidence: Playwright browser verification with system Chrome confirming recognizable card rendering with globe icon and widget title, and 0 iframes mounted.

Fixes #178467

prs.title: fix(clickclack): print inbound failure warnings on the operator console
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClickClack inbound turns that fail leave no trace in the gateway console. The worst case: the model returns an empty completion, `handleClickClackInbound` drops the turn, and the user gets no reply while `openclaw gateway run` output stays silent — the only record is a line in the JSONL log file. The same gap hides bot-pair loop suppression and agent progress/activity publish failures, all of which only an operator can act on.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handler logged through `runtime.logging.getChildLogger(...)`. That logger is built by `buildLogger()` in `src/logging/logger.ts`, which attaches a single transport — `fileLogTransport.enqueue` — so nothing reaches the console. The console-capable owner is `createSubsystemLogger()` in `src/logging/subsystem.ts`: it writes the same record to the file log and to the console, honoring `console.level` and `logging.console.subsystems`.

This mirrors the owner decision already landed for Telegram media warnings (#193256, `c45dd756633`), which moved the same kind of message off the handler's child logger with the comment "The child file logger never reaches stdout, where container operators look."

Deliberately not changed: the file-level pre-gate in `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-logging.ts` (making every plugin warning console-visible would push all plugin noise to stdout), and the discussion-routing warnings in `extensions/clickclack/src/discussions/*`, which are a separate path and a separate bug.

Message text, control flow, suppression window, and reply delivery are unchanged: the empty-completion branch still returns before any send. The file record keeps the same granularity — the binding becomes `{"subsystem":"clickclack/model-reply"}` instead of `{"plugin":"clickclack","feature":"model-reply"}` — and the console line renders as `[clickclack] ...`.

## User Impact

Operators running the gateway in a container or under a service manager now see on the console the four conditions that previously only existed in the log file:

- `[<account>] ClickClack model reply produced no sendable text` — the turn was dropped and no reply was sent
- `[<account>] ClickClack bot-pair loop suppressed for Ns`
- `clickclack progress publish failed: ...`
- `clickclack activity publish failed: ...`

Warn-level console lines go to stderr, which `docker logs`, `journalctl`, and `kubectl logs` collect alongside stdout. Deployments that set `logging.console.subsystems` keep the existing filter behavior. No reply content, prefix handling, session routing, or suppression timing changes.

## Evidence

RED on base, GREEN with the fix, same test (`extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts`: the existing "no sendable text" case, now asserting the console sink instead of the removed child-logger call):

```
# base source (git checkout origin/main -- extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.ts)
AssertionError: expected '' to match /\[service\] ClickClack model reply produced no sendable text/su
 Tests  1 failed | 22 skipped

# with the fix
 Tests  1 passed | 22 skipped        (whole file: 23 passed)
```

Real-process matrix — the two logger paths driven by the real owners (`createRuntimeLogging().getChildLogger` vs `createSubsystemLogger`) in a plain Node process with the real file transport and the real console sink:

```
--- console (operator-visible stderr) ---
BEFORE-FIX console lines: 0
AFTER-FIX  console lines: 1
console excerpt: [clickclack] AFTER-FIX [service] ClickClack model reply produced no sendable text

--- log file ---
{"0":"{\"plugin\":\"clickclack\",\"feature\":\"model-reply\"}","1":"BEFORE-FIX ..."}
{"0":"{\"subsystem\":\"clickclack/model-reply\"}","1":"AFTER-FIX ..."}
```

The file transport keeps both records: the fix does not trade file evidence for console visibility.

Full ClickClack extension suite `pnpm test extensions/clickclack/src --maxWorkers=1` → 24 files, 251 tests passed. Changed-file lint (`oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json`) 0 warnings / 0 errors, `run-format.mts --check` clean, `check:test-lines-ratchet` OK, production LOC net 0.

What was not tested: no live ClickClack server was available, so the flow was not exercised end to end against a real workspace; the handler-level test plus the real-process logger matrix stand in for it. The repo's `tsgo` / `run-oxlint` wrappers refuse worktrees with a symlinked `node_modules`, so types came from `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json` (0 errors in `extensions/clickclack`; the other 932 are pre-existing missing optional dependencies in this install) — CI remains the authority for types.

Related open PRs: #190322 also edits `extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.ts` (inbound attachments, a different bug). Overlap is limited to the import block and the surrounding region, so whichever lands second takes a trivial rebase.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: initial Discord thread messages lose the account’s normal formatting and named mentions when created with the message tool’s `thread-create` action.

## User Impact

User impact: new public-thread, forum-post, and media-post starters use the same account-scoped markdown and mention rendering as regular Discord sends, before transport chunking. No configuration changes, migrations, or new permissions are needed.

**Draft / not ready:** required live Discord product proof and inspected before/after client screenshots are not yet available. This PR must remain draft until those gaps are resolved; loopback payload tests are not live Discord or visual evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thread creation chunked raw starter content instead of using the existing outbound-text owner. Reuse that renderer with the account already resolved by the Discord client; keep existing thread creation, chunking, title fallback, and follow-up delivery behavior.

## Evidence

- Regression through the public `thread-create` action and actual REST client against a loopback HTTP server: text, forum, and media parents all sent `__Ready__ @alice` on the unchanged base instead of `**Ready** <@523456789012345678>`. Three cases failed on base; all pass with the fix. Synthetic account/mention data only.
- Focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/actions/message-bodies.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.creates-thread.test.ts extensions/discord/src/markdown.test.ts extensions/discord/src/mentions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **94 passed**, including chunking, partial receipts, title fallback, and whitespace siblings.
- Targeted source-aware typecheck passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/lane05-tsconfig.json --noEmit` (extends the repository extension-test config; touched files plus standard declarations, full imported production graph, no suppressed diagnostics). Ordinary focused lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed. Type-aware lint is pending: SDK declaration preparation hit its default 300-second timeout; a bounded retry using the preparation owner’s supported compiler-budget override is running. This is not a passing typed-lint result.
- Independent local review against base `eb77d91994befa7194122199a963d75087b7739e`: no actionable findings; reviewed patch unchanged.
- Test budget: dedicated allocation of 21 net regression-test lines covers the three parent-type cases in the existing boundary suite; no shared ceiling change.
- **Live gap:** the repository Discord readiness helper failed during Convex lease acquisition, before any Discord checks or messages. A diagnostic using the same lease owner reports all existing Convex launchers unavailable; no authenticated broker environment pair is provisioned. No CLI was installed, no login attempted, and no production Discord/Gateway state was used. This is a setup blocker, not proof of a Discord permission or authentication failure. Required QA Lab doctor/product scenario and real-client before/after captures remain pending.
- No full package build or hosted CI result is claimed. This plugin-local rendering change adds no package/export/build boundary; required broad proof remains exact-head CI.

prs.title: fix(cron): restore automation run history for administrator chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes administrator chats being able to inspect an existing automation while reading its run history fails with `Automation not found`, including managed dreaming jobs.

## User Impact

Administrators can read an existing automation's run history using their admitted management authority, including selecting a specific run. No permission changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing management grant to `cron.runs`, as already happens for `cron.get`. Keep the management and recovery tool schemas and descriptions consistent with that capability. Existing caller restrictions, grant validation, and current-job restrictions still apply.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through a real authenticated administrator chat: `get` succeeded while `runs` failed. After deploying the fix, both succeeded and the native tool returned all eight retained dreaming runs.
- Added a regression using the real automation tool, grant binding, Gateway handlers, and persisted SQLite history. It fails before the fix, passes afterward, and verifies that a call without the management grant is still denied.
- All 89 focused tests passed, covering run visibility, grant/context handling, management and recovery schemas, requester authority, and tool-prefix stability.
- Production typecheck, targeted lint/format, documentation validation, and runtime build passed.
- Independent autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The isolated PR checkout matches the tested and deployed source byte for byte.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and timing</summary>

Focused suites: `cron.runs.test.ts`, `cron-tool.management.test.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts`, `requester-cron-authority.integration.test.ts`, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, with `--maxWorkers=1`.

The new regression took 2.165 seconds. The run-history suite took about 26 seconds of test execution and 159.34 seconds wall time; the remaining focused suites took 327.82 seconds wall time, largely compilation. The integration test crosses the grant-forwarding boundary that isolated handler tests missed. CI timing is pending.

Additional checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:check`, `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs`, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm build:runtime` (2 minutes 45.6 seconds).

</details>
