prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

| Shorthand before | Shorthand after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shorthand before the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9596a8ed-17fd-4809-9c45-f0bc359d40af) | ![Shorthand after the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd794946-ed7c-4567-a1bf-4862d23afb6d) |

| Native desktop | Plugin desktop |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/333e056f-5322-429d-a30e-f3d785d89120) | ![Plugin GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef691381-28d5-4da0-9261-6b99f58de6b5) |

prs.title: fix: keep earlier attachments when continuing an interrupted chat
prs.body:
Related: #193900. Follow-up to the earlier-media limitation documented in #193381.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes earlier image and video attachments disappearing from the model request when replay combines consecutive user messages after an interrupted turn.

## User Impact

The next turn can see both the orphaned attachment and the current attachment. Stored user messages stay separate, and existing runtime-context boundaries and Bedrock role alternation remain protected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Materialize each message's media before merging its content for the provider. This removes the sanitizer's premature user merge and reuses the existing merge at the provider boundary, preserving each row's pinned image decisions without inventing combined media metadata or cache identities.

The main runner and `/btw` share the same merge policy. Bedrock resolves the provider handoff before converting its request, retaining its strict role alternation and existing unsupported-video notice. Its media conversion and base64 decoding live together in a private sibling module so the oversized stream module shrinks.

The production diff is +159/-99 lines across eight files. The additional 254 net test lines cover distinct persisted/runtime facts, video projection, ordering and pinned omissions, context boundaries, the Gateway-to-provider regression and the Bedrock SDK request; the separate allocation grants exactly those 254 lines without changing the shared scalar.

## Evidence

- Actual isolated Gateway `chat.send` → persistence → continuation → serialized HTTP Completions request: on the base, the earlier red image is absent; on the candidate, both distinct image payloads arrive and `chat.history` retains two user rows. The first turn uses an injected pre-model sandbox setup failure to leave the orphan. The HTTP provider runs locally with synthetic replies.
- 374 focused and adjacent tests passed across 29 files, including image replay, signed/tool-result replay, orphan session boundaries, native provider authority, transport preparation and prompt-prefix stability. The 13 Bedrock files passed in separate wrapper invocations (164 tests); the aggregate package invocation exhausted local disk in its compiled-child setup.
- Targeted TypeScript import-closure check passed with the repository's ambient declarations; type-aware Oxlint and formatting passed. Test-line, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, timeout-race and mock-export ratchets passed; staged diff/credential-pattern/large-file checks passed.
- Fresh independent Codex source review found no remaining P0–P2 issues after repairs. The local autoreview CLI timed out refreshing its model catalog and produced no verdict.
- No live vendor, native UI, busy-session or Codex app-server reproduction is claimed. This repairs the embedded replay/provider path; no build or package boundary changed. AI-assisted implementation and local automated verification.

prs.title: fix(ui): arrow navigation replaces recalled multiline prompts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #193927.

After recalling a multi-line prompt, repositioning its caret and pressing ArrowDown could replace the entire text with the unsent draft. ArrowUp could similarly jump to another prompt instead of moving the caret.

The existing history owner only checked caret boundaries before entering history. Apply that guard during active traversal too, leaving interior arrows to the browser. Preserve Up at offset0, Down at offset0 (documented behavior) or at the end, stable recall snapshots, IME/modifier guards and saved-draft restoration. No new state or keyboard/rendering owner.

Preserves AmelioMansour's original fix commit. A contributor PR appeared during the pre-publication re-check, so the maintainer work was added here rather than opening a competing PR.

## Evidence

[Inspected before/after screenshots, exact offsets, controls and reproducibility details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193935#issuecomment-6677026892).

Real Chromium and Linux WebKit against a built Control UI served by a built Gateway. Two synthetic prompts are committed using public RPC and a deterministic local provider; the browser reads the real transcript. Main once per engine replaces text on interior arrows; exact head once per engine keeps it and moves the native caret. Controls verify Up at start, Down at start, Down at end and exact unsent-draft restoration. No additional sends occur during editing.

Linux WebKit uses the disclosed proof-driver-only correction retaining MiniBrowser's native disabled PushAPI default. No product/page API or platform spoof.

Focused owner/composer tests: **19 passed**; the amended regression fails on main because the interior arrow is wrongly handled. Consolidated coverage into the existing owner test instead of adding a separate mocked-Gateway browser fixture: **tests net0**, no allocation; production **+3/−2 (5 gross)**. Documentation is unchanged because Down at start remains supported.

Canonical paired gzip comparator against merged main `c50ff4fbe5410609d00066642c72213e4354ee23` passes: startup **0 B**, Chat **+15 B**, combined **+15 B**, using the repository's current generated-hash-normalized accounting. No caps or allowances changed.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior behavior; no persisted-state migration or public-contract change. Blast radius is composer history navigation after caret repositioning. Native textarea movement and existing history lifecycle remain their respective owners.

prs.title: fix: Windows dependency lookup runs a stale install listed later on PATH
prs.body:
Closes #193806

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Windows, dependency commands such as `gcloud`, `gog` and `tailscale` run a stale, lower-priority installation when a `.cmd` wrapper exists in a PATH directory listed after the one PATH already selected.

## User Impact

User impact: a tool installed earlier on PATH is now the one that actually runs, so Gmail setup and watcher flows stop silently falling back to an older install. Choosing between a wrapper and its own executable inside a single installation directory is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

PATH order is the installation priority, but the `.cmd`-over-`.exe` preference was applied to candidates gathered from every PATH directory at once. The preference is now scoped to the first directory that contains a match, so no later directory can outrank an earlier one.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

`resolveExecutable()` accumulated matches from all PATH entries into one list, then selected `.cmd` over `.exe` from that combined list. With `PATH=first;later`, `first/gcloud.exe` lost to `later/gcloud.cmd`.

</details>

## Evidence

Red-on-base, green-on-fix on native Windows (`win32`, Node 22) against the real filesystem. Both implementations were loaded from actual source: the `resolveExecutable` body from upstream `main` and the body from the patched file, then replayed over every scenario the existing suite already asserts.

```text
host platform: win32

  ok  existing: {cmd,exe} same dir -> .cmd (#74881)   old=PASS  new=PASS
  ok  existing: tailscale {exe} -> .exe               old=PASS  new=PASS
  ok  existing: gcloud {ps1} PATHEXT=.PS1             old=PASS  new=PASS
  ok  existing: input already .cmd -> unchanged       old=PASS  new=PASS
  ok  existing: no match -> bare name                 old=PASS  new=PASS
 FAIL NEW #193806: first/exe vs later/cmd             old=gcloud.cmd  new=PASS
  ok  NEW control: first/{exe,cmd} vs later/exe       old=PASS  new=PASS

total: 7 | old failures: 1 | new failures: 0
```

- The five `existing:` rows are the cases already covered by `src/infra/executable-path.test.ts`. Both implementations pass them, so the same-directory wrapper preference from #74881 and the `PATHEXT` handling are preserved.
- The failing row is the reported defect: base resolves `later/gcloud.cmd`, the patch resolves `first/gcloud.exe`.
- The last row is a control where the earlier directory holds both wrappers, confirming the preference still applies inside the winning directory.

`executable-path.test.ts` gains a `it.runIf(process.platform === "win32")` regression test for the reported case. The test is Windows-gated because `resolveExecutable` splits `PATH` on `;` unconditionally and returns early on other platforms.

**Gap:** `pnpm test src/infra/executable-path.test.ts` and `pnpm check:changed` were not executed locally. A full checkout of this repository could not be completed in this environment (a blobless clone did not finish), so CI is the first real run of the new test. The behavior it asserts is proven above on native Windows.

prs.title: fix(ios): mount Control UI pages under the advertised base path
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191177

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS app's embedded Control UI pages (the Settings tab's Dashboard, session Dashboards, Terminal and Desktop) show the Gateway's "Not Found" when the Gateway serves the Control UI under `gateway.controlUi.basePath` and the app is connected by discovery or by host and port, a connection URL without a path.

## User Impact

User impact: iOS users with a Control UI base path can use those pages without re-pairing by QR code. Connections whose URL already has a path (setup codes since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161620) keep it.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141 made the Gateway advertise its Control UI mount in hello-ok (`controlUiBasePath`) and made macOS use it: the connection URL's path wins when it has one, else the advertised mount. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190199 proposes the same rule for Android. On iOS, `AuthenticatedControlUI.pageURL`, which builds the URL for every embedded page, used only the connection URL's path, and the operator session dropped the hello-ok field.

This change applies the same rule at the same owners:
- `GatewayNodeSession` admits `controlUiBasePath` from hello-ok next to the methods, scopes and limits it already keeps for the current route, and clears it on disconnect.
- `NodeAppModel` copies it onto the active connect config before it marks the operator connected, because the pages build their URL when they appear on that flag. The field stays out of the connection and WebView identity inputs (`controlUIInputs`, `hasSameConnectionInputs`): it is learned after connect, and putting it there would replace the WebViews and their bridges on every connect.
- `AuthenticatedControlUI.pageURL` uses it, percent-encoded, when the connection URL has no path. All seven callers follow without edits. The native bridge checks that trust a page's origin (`ControlUINativeGatewayAuthHandler.isAvailable`, `IOSDeviceSettingsBridge.isTrustedSource`) derive from the same URL, so they narrow to the mount too, and the chat source preview (`IOSSourceResourceLoader`, through `nativeControlPageURL`) resolves resources under it.

Accepted edge case: a page opened before the operator hello arrives, or kept open while the Gateway changes its mount, keeps its old URL until it is opened again. The Settings Dashboard is not affected: it appears only once the operator is connected, which happens after the mount is stored.

Size against the merge base `eb4881915a0`: production +29/−1 in 4 files, tests +70/−3 in the existing `SessionDashboardScreenTests` and `GatewayNodeSessionTests` suites.

## Evidence

Tested on a real iPhone (iOS 26.7.1) with the iOS app built without and with the fix, against an isolated Gateway (own state, no channels, placeholder token) with `gateway.controlUi.basePath: "/gateway"`. The same UI script ran on both sides: launch with onboarding reset, connect from **Settings → Gateway** by host and port only with the token, relaunch on the Settings tab, and read the embedded page.

The device builds carry one extra proof-only commit on both sides, which this PR does not include. Current main's iOS app needs the iOS 27.1 SDK (`\.toolbarVerticalEdge` in `apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift`, from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187045), which the build Mac's Xcode 26.6 lacks. An older base does not help here, because every commit with the hello-ok field from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141 also needs that SDK. So the extra commit replaces the three `#available(iOS 27.1, *)` branches in `ChatProTab.swift` and `OpenClawProComponents.swift` with their `else` branches, which are what iOS 26.7.1 runs anyway, and drops the iOS 27.1-only `ChatToolbarStatusPopover` they used. The fix's diff on the proof branch is identical to this PR's first commit; the second commit only adds tests.

Before (main `eb4881915a0` + the SDK commit):

```text
Settings tab: Dashboard shown for the admin operator   met
Embedded page does not show "Not Found" (held 3 s)     not met
Control UI settings page shown (within 10 s)           not met
```

After (the same + this PR's fix commit):

```text
Settings tab: Dashboard shown for the admin operator   met
Embedded page does not show "Not Found" (held 3 s)     met
Control UI settings page shown (within 10 s)           met
```

Observed result: on main, the embedded page opens `/settings` (the page path without the mount) and shows "Not Found", together with the banner "This Gateway's Dashboard is older than the app" (that banner is the subject of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174957 and is not changed here). With the fix, it opens under `/gateway/` and shows the Control UI settings page.

![Settings tab: Not Found on main, the Control UI settings page with the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261102-185141-ios-control-ui-base-path/before-after-settings.png)

Recording of both runs side by side: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261102-185141-ios-control-ui-base-path/before-after-settings.mp4

Tests: the new test in `SessionDashboardScreenTests`, `dashboard URL mounts under the advertised Control UI base path unless the URL has one`, checks both halves of the rule through `pageURL`: a host:port URL with an advertised `/gateway` mount gives `/gateway/focus/dashboard/...`, and a URL with its own path `/openclaw` keeps that path. On the iOS Simulator (Xcode 26.6), with the SDK commit above on both sides, the suite passes 7 of 8 on main `eb4881915a0` with the test file carried in, the new test failing on its first assertion (the URL without the mount), and 8 of 8 with this PR's fix. To compile on main, that run also carried this PR's `GatewayConnectConfig.swift`, which only adds the field. Its host is now `gateway.example.com` (`http://gateway.example.com:18789/gateway/focus/dashboard/main/~key/main`); the 8 of 8 result below covers that version.

The new test in `GatewayNodeSessionTests`, `control UI base path follows the current hello route`, checks the admission: a hello-ok with `controlUiBasePath: " /gateway "` is kept trimmed as `/gateway` for the current route and not returned once the route is gone (disconnect). It has no run on main, where the field does not exist. The suite belongs to the OpenClawKit package, and the cloud runner used here runs only the iOS app's test target, so the suite ran there on the iOS Simulator with copies of two OpenClawKit test files (the suite and its state-directory trait): on this PR's head with the SDK commit, `GatewayNodeSessionTests` passed 95 of 95 and `SessionDashboardScreenTests` 8 of 8.

Checks: `pnpm check:changed` passes every step except three that fail for reasons outside this PR: formatting (only untracked local scratch files; the formatter matches none of this PR's files), typecheck (`extensions/qa-lab` cannot resolve `@openclaw/crabbox-provider` in the local install) and lint (oxlint could not load its JS plugin locally). None of these steps covers Swift. As on every ordinary pull request, this PR's CI skips the macOS Swift and iOS build jobs.

Overlap: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163765 edits `GatewayConnectConfig.swift`, `GatewayNodeSession.swift` and `authUserScript` in `AuthenticatedControlUIWebView.swift`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172205 edits `GatewayConnectConfig.swift`, both in other places, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174957 edits the Dashboard's error page, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190961 adds a persistent data store in `AuthenticatedControlUIWebView.swift`, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158051 changes `SessionDashboardScreen.swift` and the `authUserScript` call; none of them changes how page URLs are built.

Not covered: the device proof and the tests ran with the SDK commit above, not on this PR's exact base. The device run connected by host and port, not by discovery; both give a connection URL without a path. Terminal, Desktop and session Dashboards were not driven on the device; they use the same `pageURL`, and the session Dashboard case is in the regression test.

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A primary model configured with `@profile` can block Chat or event-Cron fallback to another CLI provider by treating the configured account as a conversation-wide pin.

## User Impact

Fallback can use the destination runtime's account. Explicit user/user-link pins retain priority and are checked after preparation waits. Scheduled inference keeps its recorded-account and current-credential checks. Explicit native CLI account adoption remains supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth owner records configured-account provenance as a runtime-only fact and distinguishes a native login's selected identity from a forwarded credential ID. Existing admission and dispatch owners carry those facts to the final effect. Legacy V1 CLI registration signatures remain source-compatible; the additive V2 execution contract carries the required admission capability. The compatibility window remains owner-controlled and undated.

Current head `187f8c07b720ef84fd72e1a24122fe29cbe45b80` normally merges official main `982f3b1ee2b668afafe69c352d48baef470d2d20` into author head `a03c06e`, preserving earlier contributor history and the prior `669193e` integration. This resolves an actual CI semantic merge: a newly added Anthropic test helper still referenced the V1 type name after the SDK import migrated to V2. Its parameter now uses the required V2 context, also restoring the callback's contextual type. No cast, `any`, compatibility alias, new test lines or production behavior was added for this repair. The package version `2026.10.10` comes from official main; no author version bump, schema/protocol change or dependency override is proposed.

## Evidence

Current committed tree `ee890ea01c49eeace583561c6f999e60032f8c46` matches the reviewed candidate.

- **Type regression:** the pre-fix tree exactly matched GitHub's tested merge `b5e5ddedc8098203ca9503c9d819150ae0676f20` (main982f + authora03). The real extension-test type graph failed with the missing context type and its implicit-any callback (64.38s). The one-line repair passes the same graph (12.25s), typed lint including SDK declarations (169.20s), format and whitespace checks.
- **Actual Anthropic process behavior:** all four task-ownership cases pass through the existing transport and owned subprocess fixtures (133.34s wrapper). They cover held current input, nested local-agent/workflow answers, and a descendant outliving its foreground parent. No real vendor authentication or inference was used.
- **Shipped built-entry Gateway / NativeV2:** the current187f candidate passed both coupled flows below in82.54s. A unique named profile, fresh synthetic state, owned HTTP endpoint, physical local plugin and real Node executable exercise normal CLI/Gateway/RPC/account owners. Configured primary A receives an authenticated HTTP402; ordinary fallback selects B, awaits real V2 admission, launches the child, writes the prompt and returns its reply through public history. During a second preparation wait, public `sessions.patch` changes B to C with the same session incarnation/lifecycle; the real account guard rejects with an un-aborted signal and zero child I/O. Zero I/O by itself was not accepted as proof. All owned Gateway/child/broker processes exited, and source/index/head stayed unchanged. Raw RPC/HTTP/child/owner/source records are independently checked.
- **Build:** `pnpm build:runtime` completes on187f in222.65s with matching build-info version/commit. Its advisory UI performance report lists five threshold overruns; this is not a UI-performance or release-validation pass.
- **Fresh source review:** the complete69-file candidate against pinned main982f received a fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview in two complete partitions, with no actionable findings. This is source review; reported runtime checks were not independently rerun by that reviewer.

Current head-linked [CI run41976118069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41976118069) completed **success** at2026-11-05 06:20:05 UTC (14:20 Asia/Shanghai). The ratchet job records actual test merge `b0f904096a7346d4c1caa46928a8c750c45d0ef6`, combining official main `57382781c4c0620e672644f2a187163f79ec67db` with187f. Its native test-line result is6,480,836 /6,480,842,with6 LF spare. This is a different source execution from the pinned982f local controls below; no author allocation or shared baseline was raised to obtain it. Maintainer dependency/security authorization still remains pending, so this is not an all-green merge gate.

The following failures remain recorded for the pinned main982f / standalone candidate comparison. Their assertions, budgets and outcomes were not weakened or retroactively relabeled by the later merged-CI success:

| Check | Current candidate / earlier PR CI | Exact main982f control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native test-line ratchet | 6,479,375 LF /6,479,326 ceiling; over49; own delta and allocation both1,277 | 6,478,098 /6,478,049; already over49. Zero growth exits0 while explicitly retaining that debt. |
| Goal child authority owning flow | Prior CI receives `gateway not connected` while expecting a FORBIDDEN response at line569 | The same real owning test reproduces the same assertion on Node24.22.1 (296.79s wrapper). Its later assertions were not reached. |

The Goal test and relevant role-policy/client owners are unchanged between that main and the tested PR merge. Main proactively closes a socket whose requested scopes no longer fit the revoked role. The source and control point to a transport expectation that no longer holds after role-policy socket invalidation. This remains an unresolved failure; no unrelated role-policy repair is included here. The named1,277 LF author allocation stays unchanged, and cannot pay the inherited49 LF debt. The earlier a03 cleanup independently removed a redundant mocked provenance-handoff case/import and shrank its allocation1,297→1,277; the four distinct admission controls remain.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The worker transport test retains its caller-owned client when an early assertion skips shutdown.

## User Impact

Register test-finished cleanup immediately after acquiring the fixture. It resolves the owned synthetic duplex closure and awaits the existing client release. All four declarations and five expanded cases retain their inputs and shutdown-order assertions. There is no production change, global reset or new test seam. Four added test lines have an equal separate allocation; the shared ceiling is unchanged.

## Integration Correction

Two historical landing attempts returned HTTP502. A later native recovery stopped before dispatch because the audit ledger conflicted with main. The signed correction integrates baseline `4aea2c089cb710fc619d92bf0de28749236c87b2` while preserving its complete ledger history and current qualification. Only the existing pending entry gains the original repair proof and recovery status. The repaired test and allocation are byte-identical to reviewed head `e964ee7102727f5f147a9e3c64dee05b3a431c17`; production is baseline-identical. No landing is claimed.

## Evidence

- Historical original-head proof: baseline, repaired and published suites each pass all five cases. Identical temporary early-failure probes retain one intentional failure and four passing siblings; after normal hooks, the original retains its exact client while the repair releases it. Diagnostic cleanup follows observation, and temporary edits were restored.
- Original-head scoped checks and independent review passed. [Historical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41808929496) and [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41809655407) passed for that original head; these are not proof of the integrated candidate.
- Integrated candidate `d80ab31b2a31d3c2a22ba8d20d9b843b4b067bae`: signature, parent order, complete three-file scope, exact test/allocation preservation and whitespace check verified. Fresh independent high-reasoning, read-only review of the complete baseline-to-candidate range found no actionable findings and cleared security; it independently verified the ledger conflict resolution and preservation.
- Candidate-local dependency-backed checks remain unrun: the retained physical installation does not match the integrated baseline inputs. No manual or shared install was used. Fresh [CI attempt1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42158728018) passed30 jobs with29 skips, including the required aggregate and changed-test jobs. [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42159692871) passed for the exact PR/head/CI-run/attempt tuple; all three required statuses are successful. Native completed-hosted validation selected this exact new head, using CI and Workflow Sanity; no Testbox was dispatched. These hosted results are not a claim that five candidate cases were individually observed in a retrieved job log.
- The custody proof exercises actual client/transport behavior through a synthetic duplex; it does not claim a real native process or live Gateway leak.

prs.title: perf(ui): keep shared helpers out of Chat stylesheet closure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

First visits to Debug, Meetings, Skills, Skill Settings, Templates, and Security unnecessarily load Chat's stylesheet through shared JavaScript helpers. Keep those helpers in existing neutral chunks and separate the lightweight session-title registrar from Markdown display code. Fold the single-use template URL classifier into its Markdown caller and remove its old file.

No renderer, CSS declaration, route, host tag, or selector changes. The benchmark adds an explicit warm-return phase while retaining its default phase selection. This fixes dependency ownership rather than changing stylesheet order or moving route code into startup.

## Evidence

Replacement head: `6bea4d5730b`. Production bundle/timing evidence is from `755ebd486da`; the only later change renames a test-local callback variable after CI caught shadowing.

Exact base: `4aea2c089cb710fc619d92bf0de28749236c87b2`, built on the same Mac. The initial PR failed normalized Chat gzip by 7 B beyond the allowed build variance; this replacement repairs that regression without increasing any ceiling.

| UI and scripts typechecks | Pass |
| Emitted dependency regression | Pass on head; fails on exact base at Templates → Chat edge |
| Rendered template links / delayed registrar cleanup | 3 / 1 tests pass |
| Production Knip and targeted lint | Pass |
| Independent P0–P3 review | No actionable findings |
| Strict relative bundle check | Pass |
| 20 rotated base/head/base triplets, Chromium + WebKit | 1,080/1,080 observations pass |
| WebKit typing follow-up / timeline | 30/30 untraced + 60/60 traced observations pass; details below |
| 1×/6× desktop/mobile appearance and styles | 64/64 observations pass; all 32 computed appearance pairs match |
| Cold boot and rendered session-title/progress-card probe | 8/8 observations pass, Chromium and WebKit |

| Normalized gzip surface | Base | Head | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup JS | 90,280 B | 90,280 B | 0 |
| Startup CSS | 36,562 B / 1 request | 36,562 B / 1 request | 0 |
| Chat boot JS | 1,289,149 B | 1,289,089 B | −60 B |
| New Session boot JS | 797,620 B | 796,945 B | −675 B |
| Total CSS gzip/raw | 324,608 / 1,676,530 B | same | 0 |

Largest ordinary JS is 546.6 KiB, below the unchanged 547.2 KiB cap. Chat is already above its absolute cap on the base and decreases here. All lazy boundaries remain. No budget or baseline raised.

### Final runtime timing

Twenty rotated triplets per flow and engine, exact base vs runtime source `755ebd486da`; final head changes only a test-local name. Host 1-minute load min/median/max: 11.03 / 14.73 / 27.38. WebKit values are browser-local application elapsed time, not CPU. Chromium Security readiness median +2.00% and p95 −7.85%; task CPU −7.26%, style CPU −30.47%. Sub-1% warm-tail movements are within the stated noise rule. The initial WebKit typing p95 +3.90% versus A/A +5.19% received ten more triplets. Across 30: base/head/A/A median 68.5/70.5/70 ms; p95 81/84/81 ms. This is not a typing speedup. Twenty separate profiled triplets show script median 27.066/26.900/25.844 ms and p95 27.900/29.333/29.064 ms; style medians 9.746/9.801/9.592 ms, layout 6.101/6.091/5.996 ms. Style/layout pass counts are unchanged (60/33 on base and head). The sub-millisecond head-versus-control script tail and stable work counts do not support an attributable regression; the 3 ms untraced tail remains a disclosed limitation. WebKit profile values are elapsed Timeline/ScriptProfiler intervals, not thread CPU or aged CPUProfiler utilization.

### CI

The first replacement run caught a test-local shadowed variable; the final commit fixes it. One real-Gateway rerun addressed the Workshop test's transient plugin/config-operation busy response and passed. The latest scheduled main run had that test passing, so it was not waived as inherited. No admin exception or skipped gate is requested.

## Census, rejected changes, and limits

All 56 route definitions were surveyed at census base `454088a9018a226808d9e6b74d430747659bc03c` in Chromium at 1×/6×, desktop/mobile. The final affected-route comparisons use the newer exact base named above. The table below records activated sheets, the first following main-frame style pass, element counts, elapsed time and document fraction. Co-delivered sheets share the same pass: do not sum them. These instrumented timings diagnose work, not user latency. Page scenarios support localhost only; no 100 ms RTT claim is made.

The census found existing nonzero CLS on unrelated routes. This change does not claim to fix it. Required lazy preview CSS is retained; a readiness boundary before preview completion is not proof of unstyled content. Mixed dependencies on Activity/Agents/Cron/Memory/Workshop/Terminal are retained pending their own complete, measured cutover. Custodian renders Chat messages and Settings redirects to Chat.

Removing needed settings/About keyframes left 379 mobile elements restyled. Style CPU changed Connection 15.627 → 15.295 ms and About 16.679 → 15.979 ms; desktop Connection worsened 14.815 → 15.509 ms. Rejected: no structural reduction or qualified 5% win. Moving the full display module without separating the registrar grew New Session by about 109 KB or 30 KB, depending on destination; rejected.

Author simplification: one registrar owner retained, obsolete helper removed, existing chunks reused. Touched source/test files: 6,775 → 6,849 LOC (+74); production 5,448 → 5,464 (+16), tests +58. The test-line allocation records only this net regression coverage. Solid runtime call counts are unchanged; no component/reactivity implementation changed.

prs.title: feat(providers): add Opper provider
prs.body:
Closes #192775

## What Problem This Solves

Opper users have to hand-write an OpenAI-compatible provider entry today, with no onboarding choice, model discovery, or pricing.

## User Impact

User impact: Opper is selectable in onboarding (`--auth-choice opper-api-key`), the model picker lists the models the key can use with live prices, and `opper/claude-sonnet-5-5` works as a default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Opper is a European AI gateway with an OpenAI-compatible API. The plugin follows the Requesty provider: API-key onboarding, a three-model static catalog, and strict live discovery from `/v3/compat/models?view=simplified`, which lists each model once. Its rows use OpenRouter's fields, so prices go through the shared `normalizeOpenRouterModelPricing` reader rather than a second parser.

Disclosure: Opper is my startup.

## Evidence

All runs used a GitHub Actions runner (ubuntu-24.04, the repo's `setup-node-env`) on head `07f0c350c`, with a real Opper key held as a runner secret. Output below is redacted (key, IPs, pairing tokens).

### Shipped flow, fresh state

`pnpm build`, then the built CLI (`OpenClaw 2026.10.10`):

```
$ openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health --mode local --auth-choice opper-api-key --opper-api-key "$OPPER_API_KEY" --secret-input-mode plaintext --no-install-daemon ...
Updated config: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
[exit 0]

$ openclaw models list --provider opper --refresh
Model                                      Input      Ctx         Local Auth  Tags
opper/claude-sonnet-5-5                    text+image 1000k       no    yes   default,configured,alias:Opper
opper/gpt-6-luna                           text+image 1050k       no    yes
opper/gemini-3.8-flash                     text+image 1049k       no    yes
... (291 discovered models)

$ openclaw agent exec "Reply with exactly: ok" --model opper/claude-sonnet-5-5
[agents/agent-command] [agent] run ... ended with stopReason=stop
ok
[exit 0]
```

The first run of this turn warned that `opper/claude-sonnet-5-5 returned no token usage`. Opper sends a final usage chunk for `stream_options.include_usage` (checked with a direct streamed request on all three default models), so `07f0c350c` sets `compat.supportsUsageInStreaming` on the static and discovered models; the warning is gone in the run above. `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` on this state completes.

Control UI after pairing through `openclaw dashboard --json` (Gateway on loopback): Settings, Models shows `claude-sonnet-5-5` with the Opper icon as the default, and Opper under Provider access as "API key, 291 models, Ready".

![Control UI, Models page with Opper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Felixkw12/openclaw/opper-proof-media/opper-proof/model-providers-opper.png)

![Opper provider row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Felixkw12/openclaw/opper-proof-media/opper-proof/opper-provider-row.png)

### Upgrade from a release

Set up with a release build: a custom OpenAI-compatible provider pointed at Opper as the default model (`custom-api-opper-ai/gpt-5.4-mini`), plus an operator-authored row under `models.providers.opper` (`mistral-large-2512`). Then the PR build on the same state, for both `openclaw@2026.10.10` and `openclaw@latest` (2026.11.1):

- `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` stops at `session-entry-state (step-refused)` on the agent database. Both releases are cut from release branches that diverged from main on 10-15, so main has a pending state migration for them; this PR does not touch session, state or database code. From 2026.11.1 the CLI also reports that the config was written by a newer version, since main still carries 2026.10.10.
- `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (the documented path) completes, after which:

```
$ openclaw models list
Model                                      Input      Ctx         Local Auth  Tags
custom-api-opper-ai/gpt-5.4-mini           text+image 128k        no    yes   default,configured
opper/claude-sonnet-5-5                    text+image 1000k       no    yes
opper/gemini-3.8-flash                     text+image 1049k       no    yes
opper/gpt-6-luna                           text+image 1050k       no    yes
opper/mistral-large-2512                   text       256k        no    yes
[exit 0]

$ openclaw agent exec "Reply with exactly: ok"
ok
[exit 0]
```

The default model, the custom provider and the authored row are preserved. Comparing the config before and after, `models`, `auth` and `agents.defaults.model` are identical; Doctor only added its own `meta.migrations` markers, `wizard` metadata and three disabled skill entries. `models list --provider opper --refresh` then lists the discovered models next to the authored row.

### Checks

- `pnpm test extensions/opper --maxWorkers=1`: 3 files, 16 tests passed. The suite now covers a row without pricing (kept free, as Opper documents it) and a row whose pricing does not parse (left out instead of published at zero).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` and `pnpm config:docs:check`: clean. `pnpm lint`: no findings in `extensions/opper`. `pnpm format:check`: no findings in files this PR changes.
- Test-line budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/opper-provider.txt` records the 429 added lines. `check:test-lines-ratchet --base 5f3763ffe` reports "over by: 60; net delta: +429", so the net delta equals the allocation and the 60 lines are already over the ceiling on the base commit.
- Earlier live suite, `pnpm test:live -- extensions/opper/opper.live.test.ts`: discovery of the three defaults, a streamed reply with a thinking level, and a tool-call round trip on each default, 5 of 5 passed.

prs.title: fix(state): avoid PostgreSQL allocation during SQLite startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary PostgreSQL runtime object allocation when SQLite state owners are imported.

## User Impact

SQLite startup no longer constructs unused PostgreSQL SQL/catalog/fragment objects. This is an allocation repair, not a Gateway CPU/RSS qualification claim. No schema, admission, authority, retention, durability, dependency, or performance-threshold change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generator now emits a factory; the state engine owns one lazy cached result. PostgreSQL access and the existing database-port operation request it explicitly. Existing main migrations and the database-port consumer require two mechanical adaptations beyond the seven-file candidate repair; none changes their data or policy.

Related generator checks now share one canonical generation result instead of running the same generator five extra times. All 106 normalized assertion statements across the three regression files remain present, including the repeated-generation determinism check and allocation ceiling.

## Evidence

- Cold SQLite import/open/close/reopen/read regression: original eager source fails the sentinel, repair passes.
- Complete generated runtime deep/serialized equality: 421,986 bytes, 44 fragments, 2,021 catalog facts (all nine runtime keys). Canonical generation verification passes.
- Final head `5b7507c236bb925d74f6dcff2eb964f4c8a49f1f`: 21 focused tests across the three regression files pass in 39.91s; the generator's 19 cases take 3.007s. The SQLite test includes 32.483s of cold compiler preparation. Targeted tooling types, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. CI timing is unavailable while the PR remains draft.
- Production is unchanged from `d5be3401e09abfd0256fe13a4766f2c2b5158b24`; its 28-test run, core/scripts/state/root types, canonical generation verification, complete runtime equality, and sourcePerformance build remain evidence for those unchanged inputs, not newly rerun results.
- Fresh restricted same-host independent P0–P2 review covers the final source in six completed passes with no actionable finding. One metadata-only pass is not behavioral proof; the full assertion diff is covered separately. This replaces the earlier P0/P1-only review scope.
- **Known landing blocker:** the unchanged native test-line ceiling. Genuine consolidation saves 20 lines, leaving this PR's net addition at **62 lines**. The tree totals **6,462,394** against **6,462,272**, or **122 over**, including the inherited 60. No allocation/ceiling changes or coverage cuts are included. Native exact-head review remains **NEEDS WORK**; no preparation or merge was submitted.
- PostgreSQL server-dependent connection tests require a configured server and were skipped locally; complete generated PostgreSQL runtime equality was exercised separately.

## Exact candidate qualification — failed

The unchanged signed seven-file C-based adaptation `eb1c7df2cd81fdf186e97ab82db08a065bb07624` completed Actions run **41827575387**, attempt **1**, on November 4, 2026 at 12:46:47 UTC: **10 FAIL / 5 PASS. Not performance-qualified.** Tested workflow `c9ec846673e4e8aee83bed12160b56cfc0188392`; Node 24.22.1, OCM 0.2.48, Kova `bc1d0fe34b4ab6734a343bc47971e73af7a2bbe1`. The artifact bundle and all 521 indexed files verified.

| Scenario / state | Repeats 1 / 2 / 3 |
|---|---|
| Fresh install / fresh | FAIL / FAIL / FAIL |
| Fresh install / onboarded | PASS / FAIL / PASS |
| Bundled-plugin startup / fresh | FAIL / FAIL / FAIL |
| Agent cold/warm / mock provider | PASS / PASS / PASS |
| Gateway performance / many plugins | FAIL / FAIL / FAIL |

All 15 complete threshold policies, controls, scenario/state/repeat keys, state definitions, and normalized fixture/phase commands match both retained baselines (original 12 FAIL / 3 PASS; rejected experiment 11 FAIL / 4 PASS). Failures remain real: fresh Gateway CPU lower bounds 684.6–763.4% exceed 345%; bundled-plugin CPU lower bounds 361.7–428.8% exceed 360%; every many-plugin Gateway and Gateway-tree CPU budget fails. Onboarded repeat 2 peaks at 1808.5 MB against 1800 MB, and many-plugin repeat 3 Gateway-tree peaks at 2184.8 MB against 2100 MB.

**Window limitation:** 12 of 18 raw Gateway windows end before readiness +10 seconds. Bundled-plugin cold windows are 5.267–5.329 seconds and restart windows 2.203–2.319 seconds; many-plugin cold windows are 9.856–9.911 seconds and restart windows 2.234–2.360 seconds. These limitations also exist in the original harness; unchanged commands do not establish full +10-second coverage. Fresh/onboarded windows exceed 10 seconds; local-agent turns have no Gateway-ready window.

The isolated-module 724,120-byte median retained-heap reduction remains narrow allocation evidence, not multiplied worker RSS, exclusive CPU savings, or whole-startup qualification. Cross-run results do not isolate causation. This candidate is not integrated or release-approved; all original, rejected, and final qualification evidence is retained.

prs.title: fix(matrix): keep credential store writes and reads on the runtime state dir
prs.body:
Closes #192706

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Matrix credential saved successfully can be invisible to account resolution — the account reads `configured: false` and message sends prepare `null` — whenever the plugin runtime's state-dir resolver pins its own directory and the caller's env carries an explicit `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Today this is observable on Windows, where the test harness pins `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` per worker and two `actions.credentials.test.ts` variants fail deterministically; with the bundled Gateway runtime the two sides happen to agree, so the divergence is latent in production.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible change for the bundled Gateway runtime (its resolver honors the env override, so behavior is byte-identical there). Extension test contributors on Windows get a green `pnpm test:extension matrix` again, and any present/future host runtime that pins its state directory independently of caller envs can no longer split Matrix credential writes from reads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: `matrixCredentialsStoreOptions` (the store-open path used by writes) let a caller env's `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` win over the installed runtime's resolver, while `captureMatrixCredentialsEnv` (the read path behind `resolveMatrixAccountAsync`, `hasConfiguredStateAsync`, and `prepareSendPayload`) resolves through the runtime. The two precedence orders disagreed.

The fix resolves the runtime's state dir first whenever a runtime is installed, so both sides share one store by construction. Scope boundary: only `matrixCredentialsStoreOptions` in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials-read.ts` changes; `captureMatrixCredentialsEnv`, the store contract, and all other channels are untouched. No config, schema, or public API change.

Regression coverage: one new platform-independent test in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials.test.ts` crosses the write path (`saveMatrixCredentials` with a foreign `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`) against the capture-based read path; it is red on the base commit and green with the fix. The previously failing `actions.credentials.test.ts` pair is the integration-level guard on Windows.

## Evidence

Real environment: Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200), Node 24.16.0, source checkout at `0c3f04813f6f` + this patch, vitest with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`.

Before the patch (same checkout, isolated single-file run):

```text
FAIL  extensions/matrix/src/actions.credentials.test.ts > ... (runtime=true)
FAIL  extensions/matrix/src/actions.credentials.test.ts > ... (runtime=false)
- Expected: account.configured: true, configured: true, prepared: { text: "hello" }
+ Received: account.configured: false, configured: false, prepared: null
```

Source-level confirmation of the divergence (temporary probe, since removed): `store.lookup` right after `register` found the record, `loadMatrixCredentialsAsync(process.env, ...)` found it, `loadMatrixCredentialsAsync(captureMatrixCredentialsEnv(process.env), ...)` returned null, and a physical scan located the written token under the harness-pinned `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (`...\state\openclaw.sqlite`), not the runtime's state dir.

After the patch:

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  15 passed (15)   # matrix/credentials.test.ts + actions.credentials.test.ts
```

Red proof for the new regression test: with only the fix reverted, `keeps credential writes and capture-based reads on the runtime state dir` fails (`Tests 1 failed | 12 passed`); with the fix it passes.

`check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with the accompanying 20-line allocation (`Test lines OK ... slack: 6`).

`pnpm check:changed`: all content checks on the changed files pass (format, assertion-safety ratchet, SQLite dialect ratchet, doctor contract tests, import guards). Three checks failed for machine-local reasons unrelated to the change, on this below-supported-Node (24.16.0), slow-disk host: the SQLite worker ratchet (`spawnSync rg ENOENT` — no ripgrep installed), the Knip dead-export scan (600s timeout), and the extension lint's plugin-sdk boundary dts preparation (300s timeout); the lint retry result is noted in the checks thread. Pre-existing environment-only failures in the full extension lane (two 120s+ handler timeouts and one temp-dir EPERM) are identical on the base commit and unchanged by this fix. Targeted oxlint on both changed files finishes clean (`Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`).

Shipped-entry-point trace on the patched build (same Windows host, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`HOME`, loopback mock homeserver answering `/_matrix/client/versions`, `whoami`, and `/sync`; no external endpoints, no real credentials — the token is synthetic). The inline token is then removed from config so account resolution can only succeed through the stored credential — proving the repaired read-after-write path rather than inline config auth:

1. **Registration** — `openclaw matrix account add --homeserver http://127.0.0.1:8421 --user-id "@bot:example.org" --access-token synthetic-proof-token --json` exits 0 and returns `{"accountId": "default", "configPath": "channels.matrix", ...}` after persisting the credential through the real plugin-state store.
2. **Unmasking** — `openclaw config unset channels.matrix.accessToken` → `Removed channels.matrix.accessToken`. The config now carries only `homeserver` + `userId`; no inline or environment auth remains.
3. **Stored-credential account resolution** — `openclaw channels list`:

   ```text
   Chat channels:
   - Matrix default: installed, configured, enabled
   ```

   `configured` here can only come from the plugin-state credential store (`loadMatrixCredentialsAsync` behind `resolveMatrixAccountAsync`) — the exact read path this patch aligns.
4. **Send preparation** — `openclaw message send --channel matrix --target '!proof:example.org' --message 'stored-credential send prep' --dry-run --json`:

   ```json
   { "action": "send", "channel": "matrix", "dryRun": true, "handledBy": "core",
     "payload": { "channel": "matrix", "to": "!proof:example.org", "via": "direct", "mediaUrl": null, "dryRun": true } }
   ```

After/before divergence trace, outside any test runner — one probe script driving the production store code (`saveMatrixCredentials` → `captureMatrixCredentialsEnv` → `resolveMatrixAccountAsync`, real `createPluginStateKeyedStoreV2`, no store mocks) with the runtime pinned to dir `M` and the caller env pointing at dir `H`, run against `origin/main` and against this patch head:

```text
# origin/main (before)
write: saveMatrixCredentials with caller env OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=H committed
read via caller env (H): FOUND
read via captured env (runtime): NULL
resolveMatrixAccountAsync.configured: false
physical store M: ...\oc-proof-runtime-...\state\openclaw.sqlite exists=false
physical store H: ...\oc-proof-caller-...\state\openclaw.sqlite exists=true

# this patch (after)
write: saveMatrixCredentials with caller env OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=H committed
read via caller env (H): FOUND
captureMatrixCredentialsEnv resolves: <M>
read via captured env (runtime): FOUND
resolveMatrixAccountAsync.configured: true
physical store M: ...\oc-proof-runtime-...\state\openclaw.sqlite exists=true
physical store H: ...\oc-proof-caller-...\state\openclaw.sqlite exists=false
```

Before: the write lands in `H\state\openclaw.sqlite` while capture-based account resolution reads `M` and finds nothing — `configured: false`. After: the write is pinned to `M`, the same store the read path resolves, and the account is configured. All tokens are synthetic; all paths are local temp dirs.

Note on production reachability: with the bundled runtime the resolver honors the caller env, so base and patched builds behave identically through shipped entry points — no shipped process can pin a state dir independently of the caller env, which is exactly why the bug is latent in production. The shipped trace above proves the repaired register → resolve → prepare flow against stored-only credentials on the patched build; the pinned-resolver contrast above proves the after-fix behavior for hosts that pin locality.

Full `pnpm test:extension matrix` lane: the previously failing credential tests pass; remaining failures are the pre-existing environment timeouts listed above. What was not tested: a live Matrix homeserver exchange (no real homeserver account involved); the change only selects which state directory the plugin-state store opens.

Review note: AI-assisted fix (analyzed, reproduced, and patched with an agent). Local review engines (Codex/Claude CLIs) are unavailable on this machine, so no independent local review pass ran; happy to apply feedback from ClawSweeper or maintainers.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid unnecessary cold-start initialization
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## Problem

Cold Gateway startup imports configuration, authentication, recovery, command execution, and shared-state code that the requested operation does not need. On constrained ARM64 systems, this consumes memory before startup completes.

Current candidate: `b54151df`. Source validation passes after integrating main’s catalog registration lifetime fix; fresh ARM64 packaging and runtime qualification remain pending. This PR does not yet establish a working 1 GiB Gateway.

## Changes

- Keep catalog construction on captured inputs and narrow metadata owners. Defer OAuth, command execution, session-event delivery, and dispatch code until their operations are requested; recheck existing authority after awaited imports.
- Prepare only the requested shared-state query owner before fresh admission. Preserve synchronous query results, transaction ownership, cleanup, and post-commit ordering.
- Reuse receipt-invalidated empty-publication recovery state. Preserve nonempty queues, late inserts, unknown outcomes, and unreported results.
- Defer historical PostgreSQL migration construction in SQLite workers. Keep the same 13 PostgreSQL plans and cached identity on first use.
- Place npm installation-record mapping and its type contract in the existing registry metadata module. Keep command helpers and command options unchanged, without a type-import cycle.

No configuration options, memory limits, database schema, retention rules, or permission semantics change.

## Evidence

- **Merged catalog lifetime repair:** integrate main at `4aea2c08`, preserving the narrow AuthStorage and model-planning boundaries. Independent merge review passes. All 37 focused config, heap retention, secrets, authority and cold-import tests pass, along with core types, typed lint and formatting. Final local ClawSweeper review of `4aea2c08..b54151df` found no actionable correctness or security defects (confidence 0.86).

- **Latest type-owner correction:** the actual architecture gate fails on `324f5a52` with one type-inclusive cycle and passes with zero cycles on the fix. All 20 changed files emit identical JavaScript. Core types, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and 47 focused metadata/helper/cold-catalog tests pass. Independent source review passes; final local ClawSweeper review of `324f5a52..838cf7fb` found no actionable correctness or security defects (confidence 0.97).
- **Runtime-source coverage:** 271 targeted npm/update, plugin management, hook, CLI, installation-record and real cold-catalog tests passed on the JavaScript-equivalent `324f5a52`. That candidate's previously failing npm/update CI shard now passes. Earlier focused catalog, session-delivery, placement/restart, shared-state, broker, ACP/transcript and hook-lifecycle regressions remain passing evidence for unchanged code.
- **Preserved database contract:** all 13 PostgreSQL migration plans remain byte-for-byte identical (1,326,318 serialized bytes); SQLite imports perform zero historical plan construction. Database-worker inventory and baseline ratchets pass without changing shared allowances.
- **Review:** prior full and incremental local ClawSweeper reviews found no actionable correctness or security defects. The `82730ad7..324f5a52` metadata extraction review completed with confidence 0.90. These are source reviews, not ARM64 runtime acceptance.
- **Current CI:** [the `b54151df` run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42158220780) succeeded. All 136 jobs settled with no failures. The previous head’s inherited UI inventory failure does not require an exception for this candidate.
- **ARM64 build status:** the prior `838cf7fb` package completed all eight build/retention/closure stages and 18 commands, then passed extraction, owner capture and the 13-role startup gate. It is retained as prior-head evidence. The merged `b54151df` changes catalog lifetime behavior and requires a fresh exact-head package and runtime run; its canonical source export passes.
- **Previous ARM64 result:** `ef49927a` passed canonical packaging, integrity/configuration and static startup-boundary gates, then failed runtime acceptance. The Gateway was OOM-killed during health checking after about 29.6 seconds: outer peak 955,490,304 bytes, three OOM events, one kill, zero swap. No completed health CLI, model response, or soak was established. The 512 MiB trial was skipped. All owned processes, VM resources and temporary credentials were settled; the original credential remained unchanged.

## Remaining acceptance

Build and inspect the exact `b54151df` ARM64 package. Pass the unchanged strict 1 GiB profile: readiness, completed health CLI, a real-model `CARDPUTER_GATEWAY_OK` response, 60-second soak, peak at most 928 MiB, and zero OOM. Evaluate 512 MiB only after that pass. Complete current-head CI and native landing gates before merge. Prior-head CI does not qualify this candidate.

prs.title: perf(ui): avoid Chat stylesheet invalidation in Dashboards
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening saved Dashboard previews also loaded Chat's stylesheet and restyled the unchanged sidebar. The native trace recorded a 6,592-element style pass after that late stylesheet arrived, despite only 16 Dashboard cards being mounted.

## User Impact

Dashboards open faster with the same cards, previews, appearance, and interactions. No settings, public APIs, or data formats change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The captured Chat boot group owned shared Board/MCP runtime leaves. Move that complete shared closure into the existing deferred support chunk, so BoardDocument and BoardView no longer import the Chat boot chunk. There is still one provider/state/security implementation, and all lazy boundaries remain intact. The diagnostic harness also records fetched versus attached Chat stylesheets and enables JavaScript stacks in native-audit mode.

The candidate preserves Chat's animations and all CSS. Preview/menu/composer containment and removing only Chat keyframes did not establish a qualifying win in preliminary copied-bundle screens; they are not part of this change.

## Evidence

Synthetic production-bundle Gateway fixture: 1,000 represented Dashboards, 16 mounted desktop cards, nine initial preview reads. Headless Chromium and WebKit, 20 serial rotated base/head/A/A triplets per timing cell. WebKit numbers are application elapsed time, not CPU. The original slash/terminal/diff scenarios were also split into individual actions for the invalidation audit; their compound totals are not single-action latency claims.

| Surface | Base gzip | Head gzip | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup JS | 90,666 B | 90,675 B | +9 B |
| Startup CSS | 36,821 B | 36,821 B | unchanged, one request |
| Chat boot | 1,295,819 B | 1,295,883 B | +64 B |
| New Session boot | 802,421 B | 802,436 B | +15 B |

Both builds pass the strict performance checks. Request counts and all size ceilings are unchanged; byte deltas stay within the 64-byte build-variance allowance.

| Dashboard opening | Base application median / p95 | Head application median / p95 | Median change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Chromium 1× | 285.70 / 310.00 ms | 251.90 / 265.30 ms | −11.83% |
| Chromium 6× | 2,105.20 / 2,216.20 ms | 1,868.45 / 2,086.00 ms | −11.25% |
| WebKit 1× | 1,325.50 / 1,395.00 ms | 1,242.50 / 1,303.00 ms | −6.26% |

Dashboard style CPU fell 34.23% at 1× and 30.72% at 6×; task CPU fell 10.24% and 9.53%. Every target p95 improved. Host one-minute load ranged 9.33–18.59.

Typing and sorting remain within the noisy-host control band. An initial 6× typing CPU shift triggered exactly ten additional triplets; all original observations were retained. Across 30 triplets, task median is unchanged (470.17 → 470.06 ms, p95 +0.63%); script median is +2.75% versus the A/A control’s +4.27%. Application median is −2.29%; its +4.73% tail is below A/A’s +11.79%. At 1× typing task median is +4.87% with a sub-1% p95 change; the application tail moved +21.34%, matching the unchanged A/A slot at +20.34%. Sorting task medians are +0.63% / +1.85% at 1× / 6×. Sorting has no trusted input boundary, so its WebKit result is a wall-time control, not an application-latency claim. All 570 untraced observations passed their behavior checks.

Eight final native captures passed (desktop/mobile, base/head, 1×/6×). Desktop cumulative elements recalculated fell 16,372 → 9,792 at 1× and 16,855 → 10,690 at 6×, removing roughly one document-wide style pass. Mobile scope counts were nearly unchanged; no mobile speedup is claimed. Explicit layout-root node IDs were not emitted by Chromium and remain unknown in the trace report.

Computed styles and rectangles for the first card, preview, and SVG match exactly across all 120 Dashboard opening/sorting observations per engine (base/head/A/A). Inspected before/after screenshots use only synthetic data. Chromium stops fetching Chat CSS on Dashboard; WebKit can still prefetch it through the existing idle New Session preloader, but it is no longer attached as a stylesheet.

Validation: UI and script typechecks, nine focused chunking tests, production Knip, targeted lint and formatting. Independent local Codex autoreview covered the complete change at P0–P3 and found no actionable issues. Initial script typechecking caught a structured diagnostic record that violated the harness's numeric evidence contract; that temporary capture was removed from the patch and the script typecheck passes.

Build configuration LOC: 730 → 740. Harness LOC: 1,868 → 1,876. No renderer/state code changes and no new abstractions or dependencies.
