prs.title: fix(ui): surface bounded cron run diagnostics on summary pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI cron run history requests `view: "summary"` (since #173965), and summary projection deleted `diagnostics` entirely. Warn-level operator notes (for example delivery destination owned by another chat) never reach the Runs list, while full-view pages still carry diagnostic entries. Operators cannot tell why a delivered run looks odd without opening a full transcript.

## User Impact

On the cron Runs list, a delivered run with warn-level diagnostics shows only status/facts. After this change it also shows a muted `Diagnostics: …` note under the header. Execution/delivery failures still use `RunError` and still mark the run as failed; a diagnostics note never overrides `OK` / `Delivered`.

## Why

Issue #168687 (P2, assigned obviyus). Summary pages exist to bound payload size (#173965 stripped `diagnostics`/`delivery`/`failureNotificationDelivery`), but the bounded `diagnostics.summary` string is operator-facing and small. Entries (16KB payloads) stay full-view only. Keeping summary only—without delivery traces—preserves the size gate while restoring the note.

## Evidence

Red on base / green with fix:

1. **Summary projection** — `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.runs.test.ts`: base red missing `entries.0.diagnostics.summary` on the summary page. Fix green (14/14): summary keeps `diagnostics` as `{ summary: "Diagnostic-only search", entries: [] }`, and both `delivery` / `failureNotificationDelivery` are still absent on `summary` while present on `full`.
2. **Size gate** — `src/cron/run-history.test.ts`: summary page keeps `diagnostics.summary`, ships no `diagnostics.entries` and no `delivery` trace, and `diagnostic-payload:` stays absent from summary JSON; full view still contains it. Green (11/11).
3. **Rendered note** — proven end to end below against a shipped Control UI build and an isolated Gateway (Playwright `cron-run-diagnostic-note` `noteCount: 0` → `1`). The note is display-only and never rewrites status.

Local checks:

- `oxfmt --check` on all 7 files: clean.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: this change adds no test lines (gateway paging assertions folded into the existing case, net delta ≤ 0), so it stays green even while `main` itself sits over the ceiling. No allocation file required.
- Typecheck: `tsconfig.core.json` and `tsconfig.ui.json` pass under `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo`, including the UI test shards.
- Targeted suites green: `cron.runs.test.ts` 14/14, `run-history.test.ts` 11/11.

**Shipped Control UI + isolated Gateway before/after** (source `startGatewayServer`, token auth, built Control UI root, Playwright chromium, synthetic OK+Delivered run with `diagnostics.summary` + entries + delivery trace):

- **Before** (base UI): Runs activity shows `OK` + `Delivered`, **no** `cron-run-diagnostic-note` (`noteCount: 0`).
- **After** (head UI): same row still `OK` + `Delivered`, muted note `Diagnostics: Provider returned a bounded advisory note without failing delivery.` (`noteCount: 1`).
- **Response output** (`cron.runs` `view: "summary"` from the browser WS join and Node admin client): `diagnostics.summary` retained; `diagnostics.entries` is `[]`; `delivery` trace absent; `status: ok`, `deliveryStatus: delivered`.

Before:

![before cron summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8168904b-d71d-4e49-aee3-b6baf3246642)

After:

![after cron summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad4f8766-9112-41d9-a4c2-b5f645c70b79)

Local proof artifacts (not committed): `/tmp/cron-diag-proof/{before,after}-evidence.json` + PNGs from `scripts/capture-cron-diag-proof.mts`.

## Merge Danger

- **Payload size:** summary still cannot ship `diagnostics.entries` or `delivery` traces; SQL `jsonRemovePaths` strips entries before the page crosses the driver, and the size gate still forbids `diagnostic-payload:`.
- **Status semantics:** note is display-only; `completionStatus` / `RunError` path unchanged.
- **Search:** still runs on the full record before prune (`SEARCH_KEYS` unchanged).
- **Scope:** 7 files; no config/schema/durability changes. Protocol comment only documents existing summary behavior.

Closes #168687

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.1 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, next to the existing `extraPaths` glob matcher in the memory host SDK, is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main: production +67/-8 in 15 files; tests +148/-3; docs +15/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2631 -> 2635 on main `c50ff4f`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `6d9ace7` (on main `cd20cf7`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.1` from npm (npm 11.20 skipped the package's install scripts by default; the CLI ran without them). The branch CLI on `6d9ace7` reported `2026.10.10` because main had not bumped its version string yet. An earlier run from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.1 and existing data:** 2026.11.1 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.1, v27 -> v40), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.1, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.1 OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.318 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.310 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.303 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.296 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.290 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.1): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.1): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (6d9ace7) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.1 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v40 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.1 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.318 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.310 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.303 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.296 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.290 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.

prs.body:
# Summary

Attachment downloads used by media understanding now recover from temporary HTTP 429 responses instead of failing on the first rate limit.

# Why This Change Was Made

The shared media fetch owner already retries temporary network/server failures, but excluded 429. Preserve Retry-After on HTTP errors, use the existing retry runner, and refuse recovery when the origin asks for a wait beyond the configured delay budget. Missing/malformed timing uses normal backoff; explicit caller pacing keeps its existing override.

No retry-count increase, new configuration, dependency, or transport bypass. This replaces the unresolved early-retry policy in closed/unmerged #122553; no equivalent open repair was found immediately before publication.

# Evidence

- **Regression first:** buffer/store recovery cases fail on baseline (2 failures); over-budget no-early-retry control already passes.
- **Real production boundary:** actual `MediaAttachmentCache`, real loopback HTTP origin, normal SSRF guard, no mocked fetch: first response 429/Retry-After:1, second 200. Baseline stops after 1 request; patched returns the expected 26 bytes after 2 requests, with 1052.2 ms between requests. No live channel/model run claimed.
- Focused final wrapper: `src/media/fetch.test.ts` **44 passed**; direct consumer `src/media-understanding/attachments.cache.test.ts` **30 passed, 1 existing skip**. Covers both buffer/store paths, missing/malformed timing, caller overrides, budget refusal, and existing cancellation behavior.
- Native Windows Node 24.22.1 four-phase tsdown build passed; scoped core lint (0 warnings/errors), core types, messaging-test types, source/docs formatting, media-helper guard, and 16,443 internal links passed. Whole-docs formatter encountered the existing Windows command-line-length limit; scoped formatting passed; hosted CI remains required.
- Canonical independent Codex autoreview, local scope against `ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d`, P0–P3: **scoped-clean**, no findings, complete single review, source-integrity checks passed. Reviewer did not independently execute the project.

## What Problem This Solves

Evaluated whether removing the pane-wide Incognito tint selector could recover more of the 400-message scrolling CPU regression after #183800.

## User Impact

**Not shipping this candidate.** The full 4× comparison did not establish enough total CPU improvement to justify the new lifecycle binding. Main retains the existing implementation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate marks the pane only while its Incognito composer input is mounted, replacing the pane-wide relational selector. It preserves specificity, pending-creation behavior, cached-pane visibility, and cleanup when a banner replaces the input. No privacy or retention policy changes were proposed.

Related: #183800, #193920.

## Evidence

Exact frozen base `7349fd516c64`, candidate `843df724afd8`. Twenty serial, position-rotated base/head/base-control triplets, Chromium at 4×, production UI with synthetic Gateway transport. CPU uses untraced renderer thread ticks; this is not real-provider latency.

| Metric (ms, median / p95) | Base | Candidate | A/A control |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Upward Task CPU | 4169.67 / 4437.68 | 4078.88 / 4293.94 | 4147.94 / 4447.62 |
| Downward Task CPU | 4181.60 / 4487.53 | 4185.60 / 4574.42 | 4080.52 / 4424.76 |
| Upward style CPU | 869.60 / 915.49 | 833.31 / 876.02 | 857.51 / 915.83 |
| Downward style CPU | 1005.12 / 1073.44 | 977.80 / 1076.51 | 979.51 / 1067.50 |
| Upward native blocking | 188.00 / 385.40 | 179.00 / 251.60 | 194.00 / 348.25 |
| Downward native blocking | 571.50 / 877.10 | 590.50 / 941.45 | 554.00 / 804.80 |
| Upward per-run frame p95 | 83.40 / 85.01 | 83.40 / 83.40 | 83.35 / 85.01 |
| Downward per-run frame p95 | 83.40 / 100.00 | 83.40 / 100.93 | 83.40 / 99.91 |

Upward Task CPU is −2.18% median / −3.24% p95; downward is +0.10% / +1.94%. Paired candidate/control medians are −1.45% upward and +2.43% downward. The initial three-triplet result of about 7% did not survive the complete comparison. Downward native blocking p95 is +7.34%, while A/A improves 8.24%. Frame tails remain stable; all 120 directional endpoints are exact, with zero correction attempts or whole-viewport geometric blanks. Partial geometric coverage remains on both sides and is not painted-pixel proof.

Post-GC heap remains about 52.18 MiB, with 548 transcript elements on both revisions. This is a 400-message endpoint check, not the unrun 2,000-message retention qualification.

The controller was stopped only after all twenty 4× triplets completed. The remaining 1×, WebKit, repeated-retention and synthetic-tint capture work was not run because the candidate failed the useful-win criterion. No full qualification or merge is claimed.

Focused validation passed: 23 tests across the two changed files; UI typecheck, scoped stylelint and formatting; independent full-candidate and callback-delta reviews with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Same-machine strict assets have zero comparison violations: startup 90,280 B gzip and one CSS request unchanged; Chat +56 B, New Session unchanged, total CSS +2 B. No cap was raised.

Production adds 11 TSX lines and replaces two CSS selectors. It adds one paired lifecycle hook, no signal/effect/listener/observer/cache. Because the benefit did not qualify, that additional ownership is not being landed.

A separate exact-head diagnostic pair confirms the intended pane-level relational invalidations fall from 2,164 to zero. Remaining row and group invalidations persist. This is attribution, not a substitute for the untraced total-CPU comparison above.

Fixes outbound text disappearing when a plugin passes a NaN limit to Markdown chunking helpers.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject timestamps passed as recurring expressions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recurring automations being accepted but running only once when an ISO timestamp is supplied as their cron expression, for example `--cron 2027-02-01T09:00:00Z`.

## User Impact

Mistyped create/edit requests are rejected instead of silently replacing a recurring schedule with a one-shot. API errors direct callers to `schedule.kind="at"`; valid one-shot reminders and cron expressions are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Croner accepts both cron expressions and absolute timestamps. Require its parsed cron pattern in the scheduler and expression validator so a timestamp cannot masquerade as a recurring schedule. This reuses the existing parser rather than adding another expression grammar.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `36e52993c9f`: the actual CLI schedule resolver accepts the timestamp, expression validation returns true, and next-run calculation yields one occurrence followed by no upcoming run. Both new regression cases fail on the base.
- Fixed focused schedule suite: **15/15 pass**, including existing DST, historical-timezone and year-limited cases. Final command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/schedule.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; Vitest wall time **7.65s**, wrapper wall time **12.84s**. Exact-head CI workflow wall time: **7m53s**; file-specific CI timing is not separately reported.
- Actual production `createJob` rejects the mislabeled timestamp; the same value as an `at` job is accepted with the expected timestamp and normal one-shot retention. Actual CLI resolver rejects it. Five-, six-, seven-field expressions and `@hourly` remain accepted.
- Focused type-aware core lint: zero warnings/errors. `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental`, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(models): replies truncate at 8192 output tokens when a model has no known output limit
prs.body:
Related: #71045, #119259, #126458, #126611

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

When OpenClaw does not know a model's real output limit, it makes one up. That made-up limit was 8192 tokens (4096 for custom providers added through onboarding), so long answers and large tool calls got cut off. This PR raises the made-up limit to 32768. Small local models stay safe: when the context window is known and small, the default drops to half the window so the prompt still fits, and it never goes below the old 8192 unless the window itself is smaller. Any limit the user, provider config, or catalog sets still wins unchanged.

### What Problem This Solves

Fixes: replies and tool-call JSON truncate at 8192 output tokens when a model has no authored, provider, or catalog `maxTokens` (custom providers, self-hosted servers, OpenRouter and other live-catalog rows without an output limit, discovered local Ollama models).

### User Impact

Models without a known output limit can now produce up to 32768 output tokens per turn instead of 8192. Models with a context window under 64K get half of that window (for example 16384 on a 32K window, 8192 on a 16K window). Explicit `maxTokens` on a model, `models.providers.*.maxTokens`, `params.maxTokens`, and catalog limits are unchanged.

Existing configs that onboarding already wrote a numeric `maxTokens` into (for example `8192` from older self-hosted setup or `4096` from the custom-provider wizard) keep that saved value; this PR does not rewrite persisted config. Those users can raise or delete the saved value.

### Why This Change Was Made

#126611 tried to drop the cap for custom reasoning rows and was closed after review found two problems: an omitted cap was later refilled with the 200000-token context fallback during prepared model resolution, and the materialized model type still promised a numeric `maxTokens`. This PR keeps a numeric cap everywhere, so neither problem applies: the model contract is unchanged and no path can widen the cap to the context fallback.

One resolver now owns the invented cap, `resolveDefaultModelMaxTokens(contextWindow?)` in `src/agents/defaults.ts`, exported for bundled plugins from `plugin-sdk/provider-model-shared` next to `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS`:

- unknown window: 32768
- known window: `min(32768, max(min(8192, window), floor(window / 2)))`

Callers that used their own copy of 8192 now call it with the window they already know, using the served window where one exists (`contextTokens`, llama.cpp `n_ctx`, vLLM `max_model_len`, LM Studio load length, the 32K local Ollama `num_ctx` cap):

- config materialization (`applyModelDefaults`), using `min(contextTokens, contextWindow)`
- self-hosted discovery and setup (`SELF_HOSTED_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS`, now equal to the shared default): vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio, llama.cpp, LiteLLM, Bifrost
- Ollama local discovery (hosted Ollama keeps its catalog or context-sized budget)
- OpenRouter dynamic models, live catalog rows, the Auto row, and the capability cache
- GitHub Copilot, Copilot Proxy setup, Hugging Face, DeepInfra, Baseten, Synthetic, Hermes import, generic live-catalog normalization
- the non-Azure custom-provider wizard (was 4096)

Bedrock is unchanged: its adaptive-request filter for synthesized caps (4096, 8192, 16384) keeps forwarding 32768, because a user can author that exact cap and #97343 deliberately forwards configured caps. A configured Bedrock row that falls back to the new default therefore sends 32768, which current adaptive Claude models accept. A regression case pins that an authored 32768 cap reaches the request.

Left unchanged on purpose: the Mistral unknown-model repair value stays 8192 because Mistral rejects caps that fill the context window (#53054); the Doctor metadata-corruption fingerprint stays 8192 because it matches historical writes; plugin authoring scaffolds keep their example values.

Known tradeoff: a provider that hard-rejects any `max_tokens` above its own limit, with no limit in OpenClaw's catalog, can now see a 400 where 8192 used to pass. Setting `maxTokens` on that model fixes it, the same remedy users already needed for truncation.

### Root Cause

- `src/config/defaults.ts` set `DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS = 8192` and `applyModelDefaults` wrote `min(providerMaxTokens ?? 8192, contextWindow)` into every configured row that had no model or catalog `maxTokens`. The number dates to the January 2026 onboarding wizard and became the generic fallback when `maxTokens` turned optional.
- The same 8192 was copied into `SELF_HOSTED_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS`, the Ollama local budget, the OpenRouter fallbacks, Copilot, Hugging Face, DeepInfra, Baseten, Synthetic, Hermes import and live-catalog normalization, and the custom wizard used 4096.
- Before this change, a real local agent turn against a custom OpenAI-compatible provider with no `maxTokens` sent `max_completion_tokens: 8192` (see proof below), regardless of a 262K or unknown window.

### Real behavior proof

Real `openclaw agent --local` turns, built from each checkout (`pnpm openclaw`), with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `HOME` and no provider keys in the environment. The provider is a local fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint that logs the output-cap fields of each `/v1/chat/completions` request and streams `ok`. Config (`models.mode: "replace"`, `api: "openai-completions"`):

```json
{ "id": "big-unknown" }
{ "id": "small-32k", "contextWindow": 32768 }
{ "id": "tiny-16k", "contextWindow": 16384 }
{ "id": "explicit-8k", "contextWindow": 262144, "maxTokens": 8192 }
```

Before (base `938a72d4c1e`), request log:

```
{"model": "big-unknown", "max_tokens": null, "max_completion_tokens": 8192}
{"model": "small-32k",   "max_tokens": null, "max_completion_tokens": 8192}
{"model": "explicit-8k", "max_tokens": null, "max_completion_tokens": 8192}
```

After (this branch), request log; every turn finished with `finalAssistantMessageRawText: "ok"` and `stopReason=stop`:

```
{"model": "big-unknown", "max_tokens": null, "max_completion_tokens": 32768}
{"model": "small-32k",   "max_tokens": null, "max_completion_tokens": 13349}
{"model": "explicit-8k", "max_tokens": null, "max_completion_tokens": 8192}
```

- `big-unknown`: the new default reaches the wire.
- `small-32k`: the materialized default is 16384 (half the window); the existing per-request Completions budget then trims it to 13349 because the default agent prompt and tools take about 19K tokens. The defaults clamp matters most for transports without that per-request trim (native Ollama `num_predict`, Anthropic Messages).
- `explicit-8k`: an authored cap is untouched.
- `tiny-16k` (control): the turn stops before any request with the existing context-overflow precheck (`estimatedPromptTokens=18600`, `promptBudgetBeforeReserve=16384`); the default agent prompt does not fit a 16K window. Unrelated to this change.

### What was not tested

- No real hosted provider (OpenRouter, Copilot, Hugging Face, DeepInfra, Baseten, Synthetic, Bedrock) was called; their call sites are covered by unit tests or by the shared resolver tests, and the wire proof above uses a local fake endpoint.
- No real local inference server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) was run; discovery mapping is covered by unit tests with their wire shapes.
- Not proven that a model actually emits more than 8192 tokens; the proof shows the cap sent on the wire.
- The upgrade proof covers config-driven custom providers only; provider plugins' discovered rows were not upgrade-tested. This PR changes no stored data or schema.

### Saved data after upgrade from 2026.11.1

The published `openclaw@2026.11.1` (installed from npm into a scratch prefix) ran four `agent --local` turns on a fresh isolated state directory, then this branch ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (the normal upgrade step; head refuses the 2026.11.1 state until Doctor migrates credential custody, which is unrelated to this change) and the same four turns on that state. The config adds a provider with a saved provider-level `maxTokens: 4096`: one row with no model cap, one with a wizard-style saved `maxTokens: 4096`. Request log:

```
2026.11.1   provider-capped   max_completion_tokens 4096
2026.11.1   wizard-4096       max_completion_tokens 4096
2026.11.1   explicit-8k       max_completion_tokens 8192
2026.11.1   big-unknown       max_completion_tokens 8192
head        provider-capped   max_completion_tokens 4096
head        wizard-4096       max_completion_tokens 4096
head        explicit-8k       max_completion_tokens 8192
head        big-unknown       max_completion_tokens 32768
```

Every turn on both versions replied `ok`. After the upgrade the `models` section of `openclaw.json` is identical to what 2026.11.1 used; Doctor only stamped its usual `meta`, `wizard`, `agents` and `skills` fields. Saved model and provider caps are honored as before; only rows with no cap anywhere get the new default.

## Evidence

- New and updated tests fail on base and pass on this branch: `src/config/defaults.test.ts` (base: 4 failed / 37), `src/config/defaults.ollama-output-cap.test.ts` (base: 5 failed / 30), `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-normalize.tokens.test.ts` (base: 2 failed / 6).
- Matrix covered in `defaults.test.ts`: unknown window, large window, 32K, 16K, 4K, smaller served `contextTokens`, explicit model cap below and above the default, provider cap, provider cap on a small window.
- Provider paths with direct assertions: self-hosted discovery (`max_model_len` 32K and 8K) and setup, custom wizard, llama.cpp (`n_ctx` 64K/32K/8K), LM Studio, Ollama local discovery, setup and native `num_predict`, OpenRouter dynamic contract and capability cache, Synthetic, Bedrock authored 32768 cap forwarded.
- Performance: `applyModelDefaults` over 500 rows without output caps (50 warmup runs, then 40 samples of 20 runs each, base and head alternated twice): base median 0.136 / 0.144 ms, head 0.152 / 0.136 ms per call. Within noise.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/defaults.test.ts src/config/defaults.ollama-output-cap.test.ts src/plugins/provider-self-hosted-discovery.test.ts src/plugins/provider-self-hosted-setup.interactive.test.ts src/plugins/provider-self-hosted-setup.test.ts src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts src/commands/onboard-custom-config.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-normalize.tokens.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-upstream.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/openrouter-model-capabilities.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts src/agents/models-config.model-input-presence.test.ts src/agents/models-config.ollama-secretref.test.ts src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.outcomes.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-onboard.connection.test.ts src/commands/onboard-auth.config-shared.test.ts`: all passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` per extension: `extensions/ollama` (546), `extensions/lmstudio` (195), `extensions/llama-cpp` (308, then `src/external-server/models.test.ts` again with the 3 new cases), `extensions/openrouter` (292), `extensions/github-copilot`, `extensions/huggingface`, `extensions/deepinfra`, `extensions/baseten`, `extensions/synthetic`, `extensions/migrate-hermes`, `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts`: all passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, line-cap, import cycles and the other changed-file guards pass. One unrelated failure on current `main`: `changelog attributions` flags `CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`, which this PR does not touch. The full-tree dead-export scan also reports an unrelated `src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test-support.ts` export.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports`: passed.

prs.title: fix(android): match Control UI page scheme to the gateway socket
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A discovered gateway on a non-loopback address opens a TLS socket even when its Bonjour record omits `gatewayTls`. The Android Control UI page did not use that decision. It chose `http` or `https` only from `endpoint.tlsEnabled`, so the page stayed on cleartext while the socket was TLS.

The Terminal, dashboard, and desktop screens load that page after the operator session connects. The page origin is where the signing bridge answers a challenge. A cleartext page is the wrong origin for a connection the socket policy already refused to leave on cleartext.

Manual LAN cleartext is unchanged. A stored pin still does not upgrade that page to HTTPS, matching the socket. A manual remote host whose cleartext toggle is off stays on HTTPS, also matching the socket.

## Evidence

API 34 emulator, play debug build, head `8f4143070ae`. The production `ControlUiWebView` loaded a page on the emulator's private LAN address `10.0.2.15`. The discovered endpoint had `tlsEnabled` false and no advertised fingerprint. The manual endpoint used the cleartext toggle.

```console
$ adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner
OK (2 tests)

url=https://10.0.2.15:36997
page=https://10.0.2.15:36997/ wss://10.0.2.15:36997 NATIVE_AUTH

url=http://10.0.2.15:34079
page=http://10.0.2.15:34079/ ws://10.0.2.15:34079 NATIVE_AUTH
```

![Discovered LAN page loaded over HTTPS and installed native auth](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/https-discovered.png)

![Manual LAN cleartext page stayed on HTTP](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/http-manual-lan.png)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The Control UI WebView origin follows the socket. A discovered private-LAN host with no gatewayTls advertisement loads HTTPS, and the native auth bridge publishes a wss gateway URL. Manual private-LAN cleartext stays HTTP and publishes a ws URL.
- **Real environment tested:** Android emulator API 34 google_apis arm64, play debug app `ai.openclaw.app.debug`, head `8f4143070ae`. The page host is the emulator guest address 10.0.2.15.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Installed the play debug apk and ran `adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The WebView document and the screenshots above. Discovered LAN showed `https://10.0.2.15:36997/` plus `wss://10.0.2.15:36997` and `NATIVE_AUTH`. Manual LAN showed `http://10.0.2.15:34079/` plus `ws://10.0.2.15:34079` and `NATIVE_AUTH`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The production WebView loaded the HTTPS page for the discovered case and the HTTP page for manual cleartext. Both documents received the native auth payload for that origin.
- **What was not tested:** A physical phone. This was not a full OpenClaw gateway login. The page is a local document served to the production WebView so the loaded scheme and the installed auth bridge are visible.

## Summary

The page URL is built from the same TLS decision as the gateway socket. No changelog entry.

prs.title: fix(redact): don't redact non-sensitive storage.encryption values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`redactSnapshot` was masking every `storage.encryption` string that looked sensitive, even when the value is ordinary encryption configuration rather than a credential. That hid useful diagnostics in config snapshots and made support harder.

This patch only redacts a candidate string when the value is concrete-sensitive **and** the key is either marked sensitive by a hint or sits on a sensitive path, so genuine credentials stay masked while harmless configuration remains readable. Ref #176229.

## Evidence

- Traced `redactValue()` through the config snapshot path: `storage.encryption` values without a sensitive hint or sensitive path now pass through unchanged, while hint-marked values still resolve to `[REDACTED]`.
- The existing config tests and lint/typecheck jobs pass on this revision; the change is limited to the redaction predicate.

prs.title: feat(cron): skip scheduled runs when a shell precheck finds no work
prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.

prs.title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent while a sibling waits for its reply
prs.body:
Closes #164334
Related: #164241, #158603, #161114

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished subagent's result never reaches its parent when another child in the same yielded batch has paused with `sessions_yield` `waitFor: "message"` and its pause notice was already delivered.

## User Impact

A parent that receives a child's "paused awaiting continuation" notice now still gets its other children's results as they finish, whether or not it has sent that continuation yet. The paused child's own result arrives separately after it resumes. Previously the parent stayed idle with zero wake attempts, even though `sessions_yield` had just told it the sibling's completion "will arrive as a later turn". In the reported case, that lasted about six hours until a human sent a message.

Plain `sessions_yield` pauses without a notice keep their existing one-combined-delivery behavior. There is no config, schema or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A consumed pause notice hands the paused child's continuation to its requester. The child still sat in its frozen yield batch, and the batch waits for every member. The paused child was waiting for its requester, and the requester was waiting for the batch.

Consuming the notice now detaches that child into its own completion wave (`batchRunIds: [self]`), keeping its own completion custody. Frozen batch membership is mutual: wave selection, the wave's descendant scope and kernel outcome settlement skip a member whose own batch no longer lists the settling run.

Requester cron/operator authority follows the split. A yield authority still covers only its original cohort, requester session, operator and rearm generation, but each detached wave of that cohort can use it. It is narrowed as waves settle and released after the last one. Settled operator rows keep their binding, so a stray retry fails closed exactly as `discard()` already requires. The cohort rules and frozen-wave selection moved into small sibling modules to stay within the line caps.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the in-memory requester final attachment is keyed by the cohort's original run IDs and is never remapped. Resuming a paused child already created a new run ID, so a cohort containing a message-wait pause could not match it before this change either.

## Hardening and authority boundaries

- Each detached wave retains the original operator, requester incarnation and frozen cohort generation; no newer authority is borrowed.
- Admitted turns retain their own lifecycle while earlier waves settle. Custody releases only after both scoped work and admitted delivery acknowledgements finish; original-source revocation still cuts it off immediately.
- Exact admitted-wave retries may retrieve the Gateway's cached result, but cannot create new input/execution if the cached outcome is missing.
- Operators without Cron-management entitlement receive lifecycle-only acceptance tracking, never a Cron capability or new permission.
- No persisted schema, config option, orchestration registry or live Gateway change.

## Evidence

Raw red/green excerpts, reproducible commands, SHA-256 bindings, postcommit build metadata, and proof limitations: [proof behind the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366#issuecomment-5974580321).

Reviewable immutable source: [Gateway admission regressions](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts), [receipt/lifecycle tests](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/agents/subagents/requester-cron-authority-cohort.test.ts), and [actual acceptance boundary](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts).

Exact candidate: `a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8`.

- **Real Gateway admission + SQLite proof:** `server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts` runs the public `agent` method through the actual Gateway handler, admission/actor identity and runtime stores. Original operator revocation, expired authority, requester reset, late retirement, cached retry, cache eviction and a retired delivery claim are exercised. The agent-command/provider bridge is synthetic; this is not a live model or ordinary outside-harness UI demonstration.
- **Non-Cron negative control:** an `operator.write` client with no admin override and no Cron entitlement originally reached execution/input staging twice after cache eviction. The repaired code replays without changing transcript/admission count, rejects cache-missing retry, and still delivers the next detached completion. Cron authority stays undefined.
- **Original-source liveness:** cached retries and their captured dispatch assertion reject independently revoked channel-owner grants and registry lifecycle rotation while the operator profile and requester session remain unchanged. The after-await case is owner-level assertion proof on a genuinely admitted/cached wave, not a raced public transport request.
- **Timing reproductions:** late-wave retirement, ambiguous sibling/final acknowledgements, and zero-scoped-turn unsettled receipts failed before their repairs. Immediate revocation remains covered. Prior fixture-reference errors are not counted as bug reproductions.
- **Coverage retained:** 18 Gateway cases and 37 authority/cohort cases pass; retirement tests were moved intact into a coherent sibling module to meet the line-cap ratchet. Existing registry/lifecycle/completion/outbox/codec cases remain.
- **Validation:** full `pnpm check:changed` passed including production/test types, lint, dead exports, runtime cycles and line caps. `git diff --check` and six-file format validation passed.
- **Independent review:** final full-delta autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for this exact head. Earlier actionable findings were reproduced and repaired, not waived. The reviewer assessed supplied source/test evidence; its isolated sandbox did not independently execute the repository.
- **Build:** postcommit `pnpm build` passed in 378.64s; `dist/build-info.json.commit` matches this exact head. An earlier build was invalidated by removal of temporary review inputs during compilation; it was not credited, and the stable-namespace rerun passed.
- **CI/security:** current-head CI/ClawSweeper reconciliation and authorized upstream security approval remain pending. No merge/deployment has been performed.


---

prs.title: fix(test): retain selected Bun through isolation
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A launcher selects the pinned absolute Bun executable before isolating test HOME/cache. `pinnedBunEnv` carries only PATH, so a nested formatter resolves a new empty cache and stages the same runtime again. This was observed while qualifying https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186469: its existing dirty-to-formatted fixture entered the Bun stager and downloaded a second executable archive.

## Canonical fix

Carry the already-selected absolute executable in the existing `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` provision. Keep relative CI `bun` PATH-only. The resolver, checksum/revision admission, explicit-override behavior, isolated HOME/cache and formatter policy remain owned by their existing modules. `test-live` already binds the selected local executable before changing child CI defaults; this applies the same ownership invariant to all callers of the shared provision.

Production +11/-6 (net +5), justified by preserving runtime identity across the child-environment ownership boundary; tests +25/-1 (net +24). Reuse existing cache-resolution cases and the two-route launcher proof; no extra child or test matrix. The cache case resolves under a different HOME/cache with only the provision and requires the original executable, no second stage and no isolated cache creation. The launcher child also retains its cache/exit/argument assertions. It already inherits an explicit path, so it is supporting integration proof rather than the discriminating regression.

## Prospective qualification rule — recorded before benchmark execution

- Real flow: reuse the committed `changed-lanes.test.ts` dirty-file to formatted-file check and its actual changed-plan → package script → `run-format` → formatter chain. Two formatter invocations per body; identical diagnostics, file selection and source bytes; dirty exits 1, formatted exits 0.
- Counts first: after local selection of a verified absolute Bun and before HOME/cache isolation, carry only the shared provision. Candidate must use that selected executable and perform zero additional staging/downloads against an empty isolated Bun cache. The existing injectable resolver fixture establishes the baseline extra-stage red case without a network download. Mock staging counts are resolver evidence, not formatter timing.
- Comparable timing: preseed both isolated caches from identical already-verified Bun bytes/stamps outside measurement. Warmup separately; five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs on the same host. Cold empty-cache behavior is reported separately, not timed as a failed baseline versus successful candidate.
- Record host load, wall/user/system CPU/peak RSS, median/p95/spread and exact output parity. Every measured metric must hold or improve; a 20% adverse move is an immediate stop, and smaller regressions require explicit acceptance. Otherwise retain the draft.
- Use only committed workloads, existing focused runner and existing dependency ownership. No new cache, fixture framework, benchmark service or paid box allocation.

## Observed qualification

At exact head `a94d7d5b31adddda7f496a708cb82b636e58235a`, the native physical checkout passed the frozen install and 114 tests across pinned-Bun, launcher, and dev-tool suites. The tooling-test typecheck, production and changed-test lint, targeted formatting, and the committed real dirty-to-formatted case also passed. That last run executed one selected test; 67 other tests were intentionally skipped.

A separate before/after resolver probe used the complete production owner with the existing injectable synthetic stager. Baseline selected a different executable and staged again after HOME/cache isolation; candidate retained the selected executable, performed zero additional stages, created no isolated cache, and left the parent environment unchanged. These are resolver work-count results, not network-download or formatter timing measurements.

Independent review of all five callers and local autoreview found no actionable code issue. The latest exact-head ClawSweeper review requested the formal qualification above and real-flow/performance evidence; performance evidence remains open.

The draft is retained because the promised alternating A/B performance comparison has not run. The unchanged committed case creates an unpredictable worker HOME and resets XDG_CACHE_HOME inside test setup. There is no existing independent Bun-cache selector or preseed seam, so outer-cache preparation cannot satisfy the prospective requirement to preseed both actual isolated caches outside timing. An independently owned baseline checkout can solve dependency availability, but cannot solve that cache-preparation constraint. No setup hook, runtime override after isolation, or fixture change will be introduced to manufacture a passing comparison.

No benchmark has run for this candidate. No ordinary Actions billing reduction is claimed: the relative workflow-provisioned `bun` path stays unchanged. Release-owned changelog; this is development/test runtime ownership.

prs.title: fix: Doctor stays silent when personal recall lacks Active Memory
prs.body:
Closes #183700

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor stays silent when cross-conversation recall defaults on for a personal install but the required bundled Active Memory plugin is disabled by default.

## User Impact

Doctor and Doctor lint now warn about the missing prerequisite and name both existing choices: set `plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled=true`, or opt out with `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations=false`. The plugin is not enabled automatically; recall defaults, privacy/session eligibility, UI/RPC behavior, and memory status are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing effective plugin-activation owner once per Doctor operation instead of a separate availability policy that treated an absent entry as enabled. Keep the plugin's internal disable switch and the existing warning severity. This is diagnostic-only: no configuration migration or automatic repair is introduced, and the excluded-session-source informational note remains unchanged.

## Evidence: latest-stable upgrade validation (2026-11-04 UTC)

**Branch status at this evidence update:** the PR still points to `30b9fb5ff40de17ce9b0783e8ad84fd86541c990`; the requested current-main refresh and new-head CI verification are pending. Runs 6 and 4b exercised this PR’s diff on `main` `7c2ff8f`, not this PR head. No equivalence to a refreshed PR head or exact-head upgrade pass is claimed. The full-policy follow-up is separate and is not being awaited for this branch refresh.

Source: [supplied redacted validation records and limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183729#issuecomment-6636615805). These are external macOS observations, not commands executed by this Team session.


Scope: head `30b9fb5ff40de17ce9b0783e8ad84fd86541c990`, latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.10` (`7dc3350`, `latest` dist-tag, published 2026-11-03T02:26:08.904Z). macOS arm64, Node 24.22.2, npm 11.19.1, pnpm 12.16.1. Each run used a fresh disposable HOME, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, TMPDIR, npm prefix and pnpm home/store, with inherited `OPENCLAW_*`/`npm_config_*`/`PNPM_*` variables unset. Synthetic data only. User `.npmrc` had `min-release-age=7` in every run. In pnpm runs, the pnpm global config also had `minimumReleaseAge: 10080`. Redacted records: attached `pr-183729-latest-stable-evidence-v4.zip` (README inside maps each claim to a file).

In every run, the old state was created by the installed 2026.10.10 CLI: agents `main` and `personal`, FTS-only memory, no `session.dmScope`, no `plugins.entries.active-memory`, and 3 synthetic markers indexed. On that state, 2026.10.10 Doctor prints no Active Memory line, and `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/memory-search --json` exits 0 with `findings: []`. That reproduces #183700 on the latest stable.

**Baseline install deviation (all runs).** 2026.10.10 is younger than the 7-day policy, so a plain `npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.10` fails with `ETARGET` (recorded probe). The baseline was installed with an explicit `--min-release-age=0` (npm runs). In the pnpm runs, it was installed before `minimumReleaseAge` was set. The policy was active for every upgrade step. A baseline install under the policy becomes possible at 2026-11-10T02:26:09Z; that run is not done yet.

| Run | Upgrade path | Candidate | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | published 2026.10.10 updater, npm-owned | exact head `30b9fb5` (package version 2026.10.7) | **Refused** at candidate admission: `agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "heartbeat"` |
| 3b | same, after `openclaw config unset agents.defaults.heartbeat` (as the refusal text suggests) | exact head | **Refused and rolled back** at `candidate-gateway-startup`: binary 2026.10.7 is older than config last written by 2026.10.10 |
| 6 | published 2026.10.10 updater, npm-owned | this PR's diff on `main` 7c2ff8f (local build, version 2026.10.10) | **PASS** (diagnostic + upgrade + preservation). Not policy-preserving: npm got `--min-release-age=0` |
| 4 | published 2026.10.10 updater, pnpm-owned, `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` | same local build | **Refused by pnpm policy** (`ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION`, 11 `@openclaw/fs-safe*@0.27.0`, published 2026-10-30) and left 2026.10.10 intact. The policy held through the updater. |
| 4b | as run 4, plus `minimumReleaseAgeExclude: ["@openclaw/fs-safe", "@openclaw/fs-safe-*"]` | same local build | **PASS** (diagnostic + upgrade + preservation). Policy enforced on every other registry package |

### Runs 3/3b: the exact head cannot be installed over 2026.10.10
The head's package version is 2026.10.7, and its base predates the 2026.10.10 config schema (`agents.defaults.heartbeat` is in `src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts:24` at v2026.10.10, but not at `30b9fb5` or at `main` 7c2ff8f). The updater's downgrade and config guards correctly refuse. Both runs ended on 2026.10.10 (`7dc3350`) with memory files, chunk rows and settings unchanged. This is caused by the stale base, not the diff. The PR diff (3 files) applies cleanly to current `main` with `git apply --check`, but not to v2026.10.10. **A rebase is needed before the head itself can take the latest-stable upgrade path.**

### Run 6: npm-owned updater, PR diff on main
- `openclaw update --tag <candidate.tgz> --no-restart --yes --json` exited 0 with status `ok`. All 19 steps passed, including `candidate-gateway-startup` (a temporary check, not a service start) and `package-swap`. Version is now `2026.10.10 (d7fc880)`. No manual config step was used.
- Recorded npm step: `npm i -g ... <candidate.tgz> --no-fund --no-audit --loglevel=error --min-release-age=0`. Age audit: 16 of 494 registry name@versions were younger than 7 days at install time.

### Runs 4/4b: pnpm-owned updater route
- The updater ran `pnpm add -g --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@file:<candidate.tgz> --config.global-dir=... --config.global-bin-dir=...`, with no freshness flag. Its env still gets `npm_config_min_release_age=0` (`src/infra/update-global-env.ts:60-61`, `src/infra/npm-install-env.ts:306-324` at v2026.10.10). That is npm's key, and pnpm ignores it. Recorded probe: `pnpm add openclaw@2026.10.10` with exactly that env still fails `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION`. Run 4 shows the same through the real updater.
- Run 4b age audit (`pnpm list -g --depth Infinity`): 438 registry name@versions. The only ones younger than 7 days are the 11 explicitly excluded `@openclaw/fs-safe*@0.27.0`. `chrome-devtools-mcp`, `playwright-core` and `@openclaw/ai` are bundled inside the candidate tarball and are not resolved from the registry, so they are outside the audit, like the candidate itself.
- For contrast, the npm-owned route always adds `--min-release-age=0` or `--before=<now>` (`src/infra/update-global.ts:1131-1163`, `src/infra/npm-install-env.ts:295-304`; documented as intentional in `docs/install/updating/update-methods.md:425-428`).

### Results after upgrade (runs 6 and 4b, identical)
- Normal `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` exits 0 and warns once for each agent: "Remember across conversations is effectively enabled for agent "main" (and "personal"), but the Active Memory plugin is disabled. Set plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled=true or set memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations to false."
- `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/memory-search --json` exits 1 with 2 findings (`main`, `personal`).
- Controls (lint exit/findings): default 1/2; `plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled=true` 0/0 (normal Doctor has no prerequisite line); enabled + `config.enabled=false` 1/2; enabled + `plugins.deny=["active-memory"]` 1/2; enabled + `plugins.enabled=false` 1/4 (adds the 2 existing `plugins.slots.memory` warnings); `rememberAcrossConversations=false` 0/0; `session.dmScope=per-peer` 0/0; restored 1/2.
- Without-PR control on the same state: in run 4, 2026.10.10 stayed installed, and the same controls gave default 0/0, back-to-default 0/0 and restored 0/0.
- Preservation:
  - The 7 workspace/memory `.md` files are sha256-identical.
  - Index chunk rows were byte-identical to baseline both before and after the first post-upgrade search: main 2 rows `9ea842df...`, personal 11 rows `86906c94...`. No rebuild was needed.
  - All 3 markers were found in the right files, and cross-agent searches returned `[]` both ways.
  - Kept: `agents.defaults.workspace`, `memory.search.{enabled,provider}`, `gateway.port`, `logging.level`, and both agent entries.

prs.title: fix: retain WebChat participants when reply admission is busy
prs.body:
Related: #185225

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing participant attribution when an authenticated WebChat input is persisted while another reply operation already owns the session admission slot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The busy admission completion path already has the resolved session target and prepared authenticated participant. It now records that participant through the existing owner, guarded by the transcript recorder's persisted-input state. Restart recovery remains outside this PR.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`
- Result: **1 test passed**.
- The proof starts a real local Gateway with a temporary SQLite state directory and a loopback OpenAI Responses fixture.
- Alice and Bob use separate authenticated WebChat profiles. The test records Bob's `sessions.list` result before admission, while Alice holds the provider response, and after admission releases.
- Before and during busy admission, Bob's Involving me query excludes the shared session. After busy completion, the same query contains exactly one session and Bob's profile is present in `people`.
- Before releasing Alice's held provider response, Bob's `agent.wait` remains `pending` or `timeout`, provider request count remains exactly `1`, and Bob's session is absent from discovery. The proof logs this as `busyBeforeRelease` and `providerRequestsBeforeRelease`.
- Replaying Bob's exact idempotency key returns the same run id and does not increase provider request count.
- Base/head regression evidence: on base `e990b80e`, the focused busy-admission regression failed `1/1`; on the PR head before this Gateway proof, the same focused regression passed `1/1` and persisted the profile participant.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts`, `pnpm exec oxlint test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The current main test-lines budget and justification are preserved; no dependency or lockfile changes are included.

Redacted terminal trace from the Gateway proof:

```text
real local Gateway / authenticated WebChat
aliceProfileId: <redacted>
bobProfileId: <redacted>
beforeBusy: []
duringBusy: []
busyBeforeRelease: timeout
providerRequestsBeforeRelease: 1
afterBusy: ["agent:qa:pr185353-<redacted>"]
duplicateRunId: <same as busyRunId>
providerRequestsAfterBusy: <unchanged after duplicate>

```

The proof records the busy checkpoint before releasing Alice's held provider response; `timeout` is the bounded `agent.wait` result proving Bob's run had not completed yet.

The proof uses only local fixtures and loopback services. It does not require Android, a cloud account, an external endpoint, or an external model provider.
