prs.title: fix(models): avoid reloading plugins on catalog refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model catalog refreshes reload unchanged provider plugins and retain redundant configuration graphs when a shared catalog worker alternates between workspaces.

## User Impact

Remote model rows and pricing refresh without rerunning unchanged plugin registrations. Workspace configuration, source provenance, and current or removed credentials remain isolated. No configuration changes or operator action are required.

There is no final-candidate RSS or latency claim. The retained-root census is not complete heap accounting; earlier intermediate RSS measurements did not establish a consistent saving.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate registration identity from remote catalog identity, regenerate remote-derived descriptors using the existing registry, and keep one immutable runtime/source config pair per worker generation. Publication owns its detached capture so inactive captures can collect. This removes remote-driven registration rebuilds and moves immutable memoization out of the shared capture primitive; live input keys no longer pin retired publication captures through that memo. Request auth facts bind the decoded, generation-owned, and actual published config identities; existing closed scopes propagate through policy overlays and registration captures before plugin registration.

The repair preserves config, environment, workspace, inventory, provenance and source invalidation. Scope expansion acquires replacement resources before retiring predecessors and rolls back failed work. It adds no product configuration, public API, cache, or private Node-cache mutation.

## Evidence

- Compiled worker regressions cover remote rows/prices, metadata-elided requests, failed scope expansion, borrowed callbacks, and collection of retired snapshots/captures. Remote changes reuse registrations; config changes replace them. Registration and capture counts are `1, 1, 2, 2` across remote/config changes.
- Two workspaces with 256 configured models exercise aliased and distinct runtime/source pairs, policy overlays, immutable values, changed provenance, equal-valued publication deduplication, and changed/removed credentials. Both `runtime.config.current()` and `api.config` observe current facts with zero external worker auth probes. The retained callback also performs real local provider HTTP after resolving auth through the production model-auth path; the matrix below covers allowed requests and denial before egress.
- Explicit config census plateaus at 674,736 estimated bytes / 4,694 objects / 8 roots for aliased pairs and 899,768 / 6,260 / 10 for distinct pairs; both are untruncated. These are enumerated-root estimates, not RSS or complete heap measurements.
- The baseline-combined candidate passed the focused compiled-worker regressions, all nine secrets cases, 71 config publication/projection/value-fact tests, and five retained-census tests. A stale Claws-to-Templates fixture call found after integration was repaired; its two failed cases passed on the focused rerun. The repaired two-case runner took 22.43s; the four config/census files took 11.04s. Compiled-worker tests exercise real registration, worker transport and GC ownership that isolated mocks cannot establish.
- Core, agents-root and plugins-platform typechecks; targeted type-aware lint; changed-file formatting; the test-line ratchet; and `git diff --check` passed. The full combined `pnpm build` passed in 212.92s, including declarations and SDK exports. Emitted-worker parsing, cold emitted-registry import guards and both source import-boundary tests passed. The build reported nonfatal UI boot gzip warnings (chat 1265.9 KiB versus 1265.6; new-session 784.3 versus 783.7). UI and budget sources are unchanged, but without a matched baseline build their attribution remains unknown. Exact-head CI passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42154694852. The current-head ClawSweeper review accepted the local HTTP proof, found no actionable defects, and lists no pre-merge actions: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193903#issuecomment-6675597042.
- Fresh P0–P3 autoreview and separate owner-boundary review found no remaining actionable source defect. The integrated baseline preserves removed configured projections, immutable admission, published-source ownership, Templates provenance and asynchronous registry/SQLite inspection.

The HTTP fixture uses a real local socket server and native fetch, with no mocked auth or fetch. Its callback is created during plugin registration and resolves `api.config` on each invocation. The server counts every request before validating the current fake bearer; a rejected HTTP request still fails a zero-egress assertion. Every response and denial is awaited.

| Retained callback case | Observed effect |
| --- | --- |
| Initial registration with key A | Authorized HTTP; checked response marker |
| Remote refresh to key B | Same callback and registration count; HTTP accepts only key B |
| Neighboring workspace, otherwise identical | Auth-scope error; zero HTTP |
| Authoritative credential removal, including metadata-elided repeat | Missing-auth error; zero HTTP |
| Equal-valued publication reused in another workspace | Correct workspace reaches HTTP; authored-workspace mismatch sends zero HTTP |

Both aliased and distinct config cases passed using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.config.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (2 tests; runner 40.79s). This is real **local provider HTTP** through compiled workers and production auth paths, not a vendor-live test.

Runtime changes: +143/-64 lines (net +79), necessary for registration/config lifetime ownership, publication provenance, request auth-scope derivations and explicit roots. Diagnostics: +99/-13 (net +86). Tests/helpers/routing: +1238/-79 (net +1159). The scoped 1,158-line test allocation matches the ratchet's actual LF growth and covers distinct refresh, rollback, collection, provenance and credential-consumer regressions, including real local HTTP; the shared scalar is unchanged.

Follow-ups outside this change: prepared-descriptor reuse with weak registry provenance; installer-context worker heap sizing; and releasing temporary foreign-publication auth bindings after complete request/resource settlement. Existing auth scopes can retain the latest facts for historical workspace identities while a publication owner survives. This change shares those scope objects without increasing map cardinality; the explicit census does not traverse weak auth maps.

prs.title: fix(deepseek): retain reasoning for Responses tool continuations
prs.body:
Related: #192506

Draft: full Gateway/upgrade-incident reproduction remains outstanding.

## What Problem This Solves

DeepSeek Responses tool continuations lose the plaintext reasoning emitted by the provider, including after session reload.

## User Impact

Explicit `deepseek` + `openai-responses` routes can replay the provider's `reasoning.content` rather than dropping it. This required replay payload is retained in the local session transcript. Other providers keep their existing reasoning privacy behavior; the default DeepSeek Chat Completions route is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Responses normalizer clears nonempty reasoning content both when receiving output and when preparing replay. Transcript storage clears it again, and the stateless replay path discards reasoning without ciphertext when item IDs are disabled. DeepSeek emits plaintext `reasoning_text` rather than OpenAI encrypted reasoning, so all of these boundaries must preserve its replay payload.

The exception is limited to the `deepseek` provider. No new configuration, dependency, retry, or separate replay owner is introduced. The existing storage sanitizer retains only typed `reasoning_text`/text pairs for that route. Documentation makes the storage tradeoff explicit.

## Evidence

- Production SDK regression covers managed and package-direct streams, HTTP 400 rejection of missing reasoning, tool results, canonical transcript preparation/reload, and the outgoing serialized replay. It extends the existing storage regression rather than adding another harness. OpenAI and native ChatGPT remain controls.
- A storage privacy table covers DeepSeek versus OpenAI and an unrelated custom Responses provider.
- Live DeepSeek Flash package-provider probe: warm tool continuation and replay after transcript sanitization both returned the correct synthetic tool result; each outgoing request retained 110 reasoning characters. The base normalizer sent zero reasoning characters on both requests. **The current live endpoint also accepted the baseline requests**, so this is evidence of restored payload fidelity, not a live reproduction or proof of the original HTTP 400. No full Gateway/upgrade/restart reproduction was performed; #192506's restart hypothesis remains unverified. This PR is related to that issue, not an assertion that its full incident is resolved.
- Pre-fix SDK tool-continuation regressions fail with the expected missing-reasoning HTTP 400 fixture, and the final DeepSeek storage privacy case is also red on the base. Both pass with the fix.
- Six focused suites: 79 passed, one skipped. The final focused wrapper took 7.08 seconds; the changed storage suite took 3.31 seconds including compilation (individual tests under 30 ms), and the sanitizer suite 133 ms. CI duration is not yet available.
- Production core and affected agent-test typechecks, targeted oxlint/oxfmt, whitespace checks, and the affected AI package build including declarations were run locally.
- Native independent code review of the complete production change against `abe11702825e31e250244fd2ea1f0abd22dc0c24`: no actionable findings. Canonical autoreview was unavailable; no autoreview or full Gateway verification is claimed.
- Author simplification pass retained the existing normalizer/replay/storage owners. The separate test-line allocation covers only the net regression growth for tool continuation, reload, and provider privacy boundaries.

prs.title: fix(ios): refuse an invalid custom header name before it looks saved
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, Gateway Settings, Custom Headers, a name such as `X Client ID` can be added with no warning. The new row appears and the fields clear. After leaving the screen and opening it again, the row is gone. A name such as `X-Client-ID` stays.

Storage already drops a name that is not one HTTP token. The editor treated that drop as a successful add.

## Evidence

The Custom Headers editor uses `GatewayCustomHeaders.isValidName`. Add Header stays disabled for a bad name, the footer explains the token rule, and the draft stays on screen. A valid name is stored by the Add Header button and is still listed after leaving the screen and opening it again.

The shots below are from that walk on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27.2), head `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604`. The test opens Gateway settings, types `headers.example.com` into Host, opens Custom Headers, types `X Client ID` and a value, then replaces the name with `X-Client-ID` and taps Add Header.

Invalid name, draft kept, Add Header disabled:

![Invalid header name stays in the field with the token explanation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SebTardif/openclaw/proof/193595-header-shots/proof/invalid-name-kept.png)

Valid name after leaving the editor and opening it again:

![Saved X-Client-ID is still listed after the editor is opened again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SebTardif/openclaw/proof/193595-header-shots/proof/valid-name-reopened.png)

```console
$ xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests \
    -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=9CFD7CAB-3B71-45D1-90F9-EF3B770C0ABE' \
    -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen
Test Case '-[OpenClawUITests.OpenClawSnapshotUITests testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen]' passed (53.147 seconds).
** TEST SUCCEEDED **
```

The same interaction and assertion sequence was run again on the base and on this head. That run used an iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Light mode, and a separate XCTest runner bound to the laboratory Debug bundle.

Base `1bf13d4df5c1` fails `XCTAssertFalse(add.isEnabled)` after `X Client ID` is entered. Add Header stays enabled. The run took 40.064 seconds.

Before, the invalid name still enables Add Header:

![Before: invalid name still enables Add Header](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ab4b498-4222-4b85-816b-e96f006489c9)

Head `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604` passes. The invalid name stays in the draft, Add Header is disabled with the explanation, and `X-Client-ID` is still listed after leaving the editor and opening it again. The run took 52.153 seconds.

After, the invalid name is rejected and kept:

![After: invalid name is rejected and retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/746c7131-d694-44a9-b863-74018bebef00)

Valid header after leaving and reopening:

![Valid header after leaving and reopening](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09c03a8a-f399-42d9-a44e-580ccb1fa2d4)

The four existing `GatewayCustomHeadersTests` passed in a dependency-free Swift package, using the unchanged test file and the shared production file. Both app builds passed. The synthetic header was removed through the UI, and it was absent after the editor was opened again.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** An invalid custom header name is refused in the editor instead of appearing as a saved row that disappears on the next visit. A valid name remains after the editor is opened again.
- **Real environment tested:** iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.2, Xcode 27, macOS, worktree `/tmp/oc-193490` at `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604`. The base comparison used an iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Light mode, base `1bf13d4df5c1`, and the same head.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=9CFD7CAB-3B71-45D1-90F9-EF3B770C0ABE' -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen`. The base comparison used that same native sequence on base `1bf13d4df5c1` and on this head.
- **Evidence after fix:** The invalid shot shows `X Client ID` still in the name field and the footer "Header names cannot include spaces or other characters outside a single HTTP token." There is no saved Headers section. The second shot, after Add Header and reopening the screen, shows `X-Client-ID` under Headers and an empty draft. The base shot shows Add Header still enabled for `X Client ID`. The later head shots show that name kept with Add Header disabled, then `X-Client-ID` still listed after reopen.
- **Observed result after fix:** Typing the invalid name left Add Header disabled and kept the draft. Tapping Add Header for `X-Client-ID` stored that header, and it was still listed after leaving the editor and opening it again. On the base build, the same invalid name left Add Header enabled.
- **What was not tested:** A physical iPhone, and the next gateway connection sending the stored header. The value is a secure field, so the shots do not show it.

## Summary

Closes #193490

prs.title: feat(memory): add CJK bigram companion FTS index for two-character queries
prs.body:
Resolves #170997

## What Problem This Solves
When using `store.fts.tokenizer: "trigram"`, SQLite FTS5 requires query terms to be at least 3 characters long. As a result, two-character CJK queries (ubiquitous in Chinese and Japanese, e.g. "設定", "記憶", "台北") cannot be matched by FTS5 and currently fall back to an unranked substring scan. This causes:
1. **Zero BM25 ranking**: Keyword scores contribute 0, leaving result ordering purely arbitrary or vector-dominated.
2. **Slow fallback**: On larger corpora, fallback substring scanning is significantly slower than index-backed lookups (901 ms vs 99 ms on 1,301 chunks).

Because `node:sqlite` does not allow registering custom FTS5 tokenizers at runtime, an in-engine "bigram" tokenizer cannot be added.

This PR adds an opt-in companion Han bigram FTS index (`memory.search.store.fts.cjk: "bigram"`).

### Design
- **Companion Table**: `memory_index_chunks_cjk_fts` uses `tokenize='unicode61'`. Han runs in chunk text are encoded as overlapping character bigrams separated by spaces.
- **Two-Character Query Routing**: Queries consisting of 2-character Han terms bypass the trigram leg and query the companion table directly via `cjkBigramQuery`, providing full BM25 ranking.
- **Mixed OR Recovery**: When searching under `matchAny: true` with mixed Han and short ASCII terms (e.g. `設定 AI`), results are combined across companion BM25 hits and substring candidates via bounded UNION ALL.
- **Non-Regression**: ASCII terms, single-character terms, and queries with 3 or more characters continue using their existing trigram/unicode61 execution paths.
- **Derived State & Lifecycle**:
  - Enabling or disabling `store.fts.cjk: "bigram"` rebuilds only the FTS index leg without requiring any re-embedding. When disabled, `dropDisabledMemoryFts` drops the companion table.
  - Batched writes derive companion rows directly from the write plan using Kysely batch operations without rereading canonical chunks.
  - Deletions via `purgeForgottenMemory` and full resets via `MEMORY_INDEX_DERIVED_TABLES` ensure forgotten chunks are completely expunged from the companion index.
  - Reused schema admissions skip redundant schema scans or DROP queries.
- **Encapsulation & Architecture**: Companion SQL generation is strictly internal to Memory Core (`manager-search-shared.ts`). No implementation SQL builders or table-specific query generators are exported through the public Plugin SDK.

## Evidence

### Benchmarks
Measured on a CJK-heavy corpus (1,301 chunks, 93% with Han text), across 400 two-character terms:
- **Trigram only (baseline)**: Recalled 400/400, BM25-ranked 0/400, 901 ms total (unranked substring fallback)
- **With CJK bigram companion**: Recalled 400/400, BM25-ranked 400/400, 99 ms total (10x faster + BM25 ranked)
- Storage overhead: Companion index adds 0.84 MB alongside the 3.89 MB trigram index.

### Real Behavior Proof & Attributable Environment
- Environment: Node v26.3.1 (darwin-arm64)
- Commit SHA: `ea85ef260dd` (PR head)
- Shipped CLI Build Stamp: `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (ea85ef2)`

#### 1. Vitest Test Suite Execution

v26.3.1
$ git rev-parse --short HEAD

$ pnpm vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search.cjk-bigram.test.ts

   ✓ memory keyword search CJK bigram companion index > ranks a two-character Han query with BM25 70ms
   ✓ memory keyword search CJK bigram companion index > recalls a two-character Han query that trigram cannot match 12ms
   ✓ memory keyword search CJK bigram companion index > keeps three-character Han queries on the trigram leg 12ms
   ✓ memory keyword search CJK bigram companion index > keeps ASCII queries on the trigram leg 13ms
   ✓ memory keyword search CJK bigram companion index > keeps single-character Han queries unranked 12ms
   ✓ memory keyword search CJK bigram companion index > falls back to the substring plan without the companion index 9ms
   ✓ memory keyword search CJK bigram companion index > keeps the companion index aligned with the chunk writer 9ms

#### 2. End-to-End Execution on Memory Core Engine
Demonstrating ranked two-character Han retrieval (`設定`), session transcript exclusions, and fallback OR recovery:

prs.title: fix(macos): recognize installed asdf Node and pnpm CLI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS app users could not start their local Gateway with an asdf-managed Node runtime and a pnpm-installed CLI, even though both worked in Terminal. Supported Node 26.1.0 was reported as `(unreadable)`, followed by `Command "openclaw" not found`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the Node version probe and the downstream Gateway CLI version probe now preserve the app's inherited environment and override only PATH with the discovered search paths. Previously, passing a PATH-only environment removed HOME and caused asdf to fail. CLI discovery also searches `~/Library/pnpm/bin`, retaining the existing parent-directory layout and path precedence.

## User Impact

Users can reuse supported asdf Node and pnpm CLI installations without adding manual symlinks. The change stays in macOS app discovery and includes updated installation documentation.

## Evidence

### Actual asdf/pnpm installations

Following ClawSweeper's review, I tested the compiled native app's `GatewayEnvironment.check()` (used by Connection Recheck) and `CLIInstaller.status()` (used by onboarding) with **actual installed asdf 0.18.0, Node 26.1.0, pnpm 12.2.1, and OpenClaw CLI 2026.9.3**.

Each run had a fresh isolated Foundation HOME/defaults store and no remembered CLI path. Symlinks exposed the actual installed asdf shim and pnpm CLI at `~/.asdf/shims/node` and `~/Library/pnpm/bin/openclaw`; `ASDF_DATA_DIR` pointed to the existing Node installation. The initial PATH contained system/Homebrew directories. Assertions checked the selected shim, discovered CLI, exact versions, and final native statuses. Actual installed executables and package contents were readable, while operator configuration, Gateway state, Keychain services, and network access remained blocked by an OS sandbox.

**Before this follow-up**, on the initial PR head `19d53cd0`, the real installation run confirmed ClawSweeper's downstream concern:

```text
Node: ~/.asdf/shims/node -> 26.1.0
CLI: ~/Library/pnpm/bin/openclaw
GatewayEnvironment.check: kind=error, node=26.1.0, gateway=nil
CLIInstaller.status: ready=true
```

**After preserving the downstream probe environment** (follow-up commit `a97eb115`), a separate fresh HOME/defaults run passed:

```text
Foundation HOME matches isolated HOME; no cached CLI preference
Node: ~/.asdf/shims/node -> 26.1.0
CLI: ~/Library/pnpm/bin/openclaw
GatewayEnvironment.check: kind=ok, node=26.1.0, gateway=2026.9.3
CLIInstaller.status: ready=true
CLI validated: 2026.9.3; compatible with app 2026.9.3
Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed (exit 0)
```

The temporary proof harness called the actual compiled app methods and was removed from the submitted sources. This proves native discovery and downstream validation with actual installations; signed-app GUI interaction and starting an operator Gateway were outside this run.

### Regression and repository checks

- The initial HOME-dependent Node and pnpm-layout regression cases failed before their respective fixes. The new downstream CLI-to-Node-shim regression failed on `19d53cd0` and passed after the follow-up.
- All 24 selected Swift tests passed, including runtime compatibility, both pnpm layouts, downstream CLI validation, path precedence, profile isolation, and inherited SSH environment behavior.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` passed with only the submitted test sources after removing the temporary proof harness.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base d9216e894e89cec406d42607c175aeecf4a13ee9` passed, including 1,141 macOS-related Vitest tests, SwiftLint, formatting, dependency guards, and the native state schema guard.
- Independent autoreview confirmed that the working-tree follow-up repairs the downstream defect. Its sole INDEX-only finding referred to the previous PR revision; the reviewed repair is included unchanged in this update.
- Native i18n verification, the changed document's MDX check, and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix(text): streaming Markdown checkpoint must settle after a closed legacy bracket block
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an assistant reply delivered to the user contains a *closed* legacy bracket tool-call block (`[TOOL_CALL]…[/TOOL_CALL]`), the streaming Markdown checkpoint never settles — `settledLength` stays 0 for the entire reply. Because the Gateway runs stream processing synchronously on its event loop, every appended chunk re-scans the whole prefix, so a 64KB reply blocks other conversations for ~73.7s and a 128KB reply for ~191s (same failure class as #186667 / #192831 / #187400, and it corrupts no text).

- Problem: `findTextCheckpoint` treats any line containing `[` as needing the full paragraph context and returns `offset = retainStart` (= 0); and `scanLegacyBracketToolCallBlocks` sets `pending` from the last `[` anywhere in the reply, so an ordinary unmatched bracket (e.g. `Array index [0`) also keeps the reply pending. Both pin the checkpoint boundary at 0.
- Solution: a completed `[TOOL_CALL]`/`[TOOL_RESULT]` tag line with no other open bracket or link is allowed to settle immediately; and `pending` is narrowed so only a partial `[TOOL_(CALL|RESULT)` header keeps the reply pending.
- What changed: `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` (`findTextCheckpoint`) and `src/shared/text/assistant-text-transforms.ts` (`scanLegacyBracketToolCallBlocks`), plus one regression row in `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: unclosed labels, reference definitions, inline code, and link targets still force the conservative full-paragraph fallback; a genuinely partial `[TOOL_C` header still keeps the reply pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two guards conflated "contains a bracket" with "needs full context". Only the legacy tool tag line is provably closed on a single line, so it is the only bracket line eligible to settle early. The `pending` heuristic is narrowed (not removed) so a stray `[` no longer blocks settlement. This is the best available fix: minimal, no new abstraction, and no behavior change for real open labels/links. Risk: none observed — the full `src/shared/text` suite (664 tests) is green, including the existing batch/streaming consistency contracts.

## User Impact

Streaming replies that contain a closed legacy bracket tool-call block now settle their prefix incrementally instead of stalling the Gateway event loop. Operators see no text change; they avoid multi-minute stalls on 64KB+ replies.

## Compatibility

- Preserved: unclosed bracket labels, reference definitions, inline code, and link targets retain the conservative full-paragraph fallback; partial `[TOOL_(CALL|RESULT)` headers still keep the reply pending.
- Related: same failure class as #186667 / #192831 / #187400 (streaming re-scan stalls), fixed at the checkpoint/legacy-bracket layer.
- Not claimed: a reply whose trailing line ends with a genuinely unmatched open bracket `[` (e.g. `Array index [0`) still keeps that final line un-settled — that is intentional conservative behavior, not part of this fix.

## Evidence

Live runtime check of the regression shape (source = `[TOOL_CALL]{}\n[/TOOL_CALL]\n` + 4096 chars of ordinary prose, streamed in 4-char chunks via `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")`):

```console
$ node --import tsx <script>.mts
PRE-FIX (origin/main):  scannedChars=12025421 settledLength=0     sourceLen=4096 settledPct=0.0   textMatches=true
POST-FIX (this branch): scannedChars=1332715  settledLength=3949  sourceLen=4096 settledPct=96.4  textMatches=true
```

Behavior matrix (regression shape):

```text
input form                               => pre-fix                                => post-fix
closed [TOOL_CALL]…[/TOOL_CALL] + prose  => scannedChars 12,025,421; settled 0%    => scannedChars 1,332,715; settled 96.4%
```

`scannedChars` is the total characters fed to `RegExp.prototype.test` across the whole stream — a direct proxy for the re-scan cost. Pre-fix re-scans the entire ~4KB prefix on (almost) every append; post-fix stays bounded (~1.33M total, ~9× lower). The regression test `bounds ordinary legacy bracket block streaming work` asserts `settledLength > 90%`, `scanned < 512× source length`, and `markdownOwnershipWork.scannedCharacters < 16× source length`; it is RED on origin/main and GREEN on this branch.

- What was not tested: a reply whose trailing line ends with a genuinely unmatched open bracket `[` (e.g. `Array index [0`) still keeps that final line un-settled by design; this is the correct conservative behavior and is outside the scope of this fix.
- Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and changed-file lists for `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts`, `src/shared/text/assistant-text-transforms.ts`, and `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts`; no open PR touched these files. My open PRs at push time = 19 (< 20). Branch rebased onto latest `origin/main`.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): add the tunnel transport, OpenClaw ID sign-in and relayed-device Gateway auth
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A linked claw must be reachable from an owner's or member's browser through the OpenClaw ID relay, and the Gateway must authenticate those relayed devices by their membership, not by headers or other credentials. This PR adds the tunnel transport, OpenClaw ID sign-in for the Control UI, and the Gateway auth changes that admit relayed devices.

## User Impact

No user-visible change while the `gateway.openclawId.enabled` Labs switch is off (the default): no tunnel child, no ingress listener and no tunnel principal resolver exist, and every auth path behaves as on `main`.

With the switch on and the services configured, the Gateway runs a supervised tunnel child, the local operator can sign in with OpenClaw ID and link the claw, and admitted devices reach the Gateway through the relay with their owner, operator or viewer role. Automations, condition scripts, shell commands and stream watchers that a relayed device creates keep running across restarts under that device's authority, and stop when the device is removed or its role changes.

**Security-relevant:** this PR changes Gateway authentication, ingress attribution, the browser-origin check, the plugin cookie handoff and how scheduled work restores its creator's authority. Those changes are listed separately below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #192335 (Gateway membership authority), now merged to `main` as `428ca7d`. It also needs the iroh Node binding, #191470: the tunnel child loads `@openclaw/iroh-node` at runtime and reports the transport unavailable (and keeps the Gateway running) when it cannot.

**Tunnel transport** (`src/gateway/openclaw-id/`):

- `tunnel-child/**`: a separate child process that owns the iroh endpoint. It authenticates each device key W in the QUIC handshake, refuses keys that are not admitted before any stream, and proxies HTTP and WebSocket streams to the Gateway over a private Unix socket with a per-boot proxy token. Client-supplied ingress and identity headers are replaced with authenticated facts.
- `tunnel-supervisor.ts`, `tunnel-ipc.ts`, `tunnel-runtime.ts`: start, health-ping, RSS-limit, backoff and stop the child (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL); push membership changes to it; report `running`, `unavailable`, `relay denied` or `crash looping`.
- `ingress-listener.ts`, `tunnel-api.ts`: the private listener marks each request as `openclaw-id-tunnel` with W and a synthetic per-device address, and serves the small tunnel API that owner devices use behind the loader.
- `remote-signout.ts`: signs out one relayed browser (closes its connections and revokes its tokens) without removing the device.
- `service.ts`: starts the tunnel runtime when the switch is on, publishes the tunnel principal, device-token binding and claw-origin resolvers, and requires the running endpoint key for linking.

**OpenClaw ID sign-in** (`account-sign-in.ts`, `openclawId.authority` `account_*` actions): an OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE for the Control UI's account menu, direct loopback only. The Gateway holds the verifier and redeems the code; it keeps only display claims (`sub`, name, email) in the claw record.

**Gateway auth changes (security boundary):**

- `auth.ts`: a request the tunnel listener attributed to W authenticates as a `trusted-proxy` principal in every auth mode: owner devices act as the Gateway owner, members carry `openclaw-id:<account_id>` as the user. A key the authority no longer admits is refused (`openclaw_id_not_admitted`), and a tunnel request never falls back to the Gateway's other credentials.
- `ingress-attribution.ts`: adds the `openclaw-id-tunnel` transport (never direct loopback, rate-limited per device key). While the switch is on, identity headers (Cloudflare Access, `Remote-User`, `X-Remote-User`, the configured `userHeader`/`requiredHeaders`) also disqualify loopback locality, so a proxy that omits client-address headers cannot reach the local-only link ceremony. With the switch off this rule does not apply and attribution is unchanged.
- `ws-connection/*`, `operator-role-policy.ts`, `http-auth-user-profile.ts`: members are capped by their role's operator policy (operator: read, write, approvals, questions, talk; viewer: read only) on WebSocket and HTTP. Pairing within that ceiling is approved automatically for relayed browsers; owner devices pair with what they request.
- `device-token-binding.ts` users (`connect-auth.ts`, `connect-device-pairing.ts`, `http-auth-utils.ts`): a device token issued over the tunnel is bound to the W that obtained it; presenting it from another W, or from ordinary ingress, is refused and logged.
- `origin-check.ts`: a relayed WebSocket may also use the linked claw's own origin (`https://<claw hostname>`), read from the current owner-signed binding.
- `http-auth-plugin-cookie.ts`, `control-ui-plugin-auth-cookie.ts`: a signed plugin cookie cannot replace a relayed device's current membership, and none is issued to a tunnel request (it could be replayed on ordinary ingress).
- `gateway-owner-profile.ts`, `connect-device-pairing.ts`: an owner device acts as the Gateway owner when named `gateway.roles` are configured, like a token or password client.

Docs: `docs/gateway/remote.md` (OpenClaw ID alongside Tailscale, Cloudflare Access and Gateway credentials) and `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` (identity headers deny loopback locality).

## Review

An independent review (GPT-6 Astra) of this PR found four issues; three are fixed here with tests, one is narrowed:

- Fixed: plugin read cookies were issued to tunnel requests and could be replayed on ordinary ingress for their five-minute life. Tunnel requests no longer get them.
- Fixed: owner devices were refused when named `gateway.roles` were configured, because they carry no user. They now take the owner path.
- Fixed: the identity-header locality rule applied even with the switch off. It now applies only while OpenClaw ID is on.
- Fixed (decision in #192335): device tokens issued over the tunnel stay bound to their device key across a Gateway restart with the switch off. #192335 reads the saved bindings at Gateway start; here both ingress checks (`connect-auth.ts`, `http-operator-device-token.ts`) await that read. `http-auth-utils.paired-device.test.ts` saves a binding in the real claw store, starts a fresh service with the switch off, and shows the token refused on HTTP, including for a request that arrives before the read finishes. The test fails without the Gateway-start read.

**ClawSweeper's review of `9049570`: a removed owner could still invoke tools (P1), fixed here.** An HTTP request kept only the role it was admitted with. A `POST /tools/invoke` waiting in a before-tool-call hook therefore still ran its tool after its device was removed: closing the tunnel connection does not stop a request the Gateway already holds. Every authority check on a relayed HTTP request now also asks the membership authority whether the device is still admitted with the same kind, account and role (`isOpenClawIdTunnelPrincipalCurrent`, read from the claw record already loaded, in `http-auth-user-profile.ts`). If the device is removed, its role changes, or OpenClaw ID turns off, the request's next check fails. That includes the last check before the tool runs, which answers 403 "Gateway requester authority changed". `http-auth-utils.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts` drives the real HTTP authorization path and fails without the fix. The same review's P2, four test fixtures missing `getGatewayServer`, was fixed earlier.

**Work that outlives a request keeps the device that authorized it (maintainer decision, 2026-11-05).** Rather than refusing these features for tunnel devices, they keep working under the original device's authority. Independent reviews of each step found the gaps fixed below, each with a regression test that fails without the fix:

- **Canonical profile.** HTTP and WebSocket members use the Gateway user profile keyed by their verified OpenClaw ID account (#192335), never an email fallback.
- **Live authority on WebSocket and runs.** A member removed or downgraded while connected is closed with `4001` at its next request, and its runs stop. An operator member keeps its membership role when `gateway.roles` names a reader default. An explicit tunnel request is attributed before the ambient Tailscale checks.
- **Scheduled and recovered work.** A job, condition script, script payload, shell command or stream watcher created over the tunnel stores the original device's authority with the job: claw, root, the seq at which the device was listed and, for owner devices, the device itself. That authority does not depend on which conversation runs the job. Every run, restart and recovery checks it against the local membership record, and a removal, re-approval, role change or switch-off cancels the work, including a running shell command's process tree. Recovery waits only for the local record to load, not for the relay or Discovery.
- **Stream watchers.** The authority for the watcher's process is kept apart from the authority for the work its output triggers. Editing what the output does never changes who authorized the running command. Re-enabling the watcher or changing its command takes a current authorized operator, who becomes the process's authority.
- **Edits by someone else.** An admin who changes another person's schedule or enables their job keeps that person's authority on the job: the edit never makes a member's job run as the admin. Changing what another person's job runs needs that person or an ownership transfer. A Control UI continuation is owner-only only while its retained scopes include `operator.admin`.
- **HTTP execution.** OpenAI-compatible runs, `/tools/invoke` and HTTP session creation carry the admitted device's principal.
- **Gateway stop.** A stopped Gateway ends local OpenClaw ID authority, even when the first authority load is still in flight.

The stored source format adds a standalone variant beside the existing parent-bound one; jobs created before this PR load unchanged. An ownership transfer still retires the previous person's authority, as on `main`.

ClawSweeper's review of `e164242` raised the same restart gap (now fixed, see above) and one doc finding, fixed here: `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` now says the Cloudflare Access, `Remote-User`, `X-Remote-User` and configured-header locality rule applies only while OpenClaw ID is on, and the Tailscale rule always applies.

Rebased onto #192335 at `9269511` and `main` at `06acff14158`. `service.publication-refresh.test.ts` now waits for startup publication, which #192335 moved beside the lifecycle queue.

Rebased with #192335 onto `main` at `0809cf31e69` (#193146 merged), without conflicts.

Rebased onto `main` at `49f8a60f227` (after #192859). Two files this PR touches had gone over the 700-line lint cap, so two self-contained pieces moved out, unchanged:

- `verifyHttpOperatorDeviceToken`, the HTTP device-token fallback that holds the tunnel-binding check, moved from `http-auth-utils.ts` to `http-operator-device-token.ts`.
- The config-derived settings helpers moved from `openclaw-id/service.ts` to `openclaw-id/service-settings.ts`.

Rebased with #192335 onto `main` at `0afeaad457c`. Main's person-ingress recovery (#193098) changed the same recovery owners; its person sources and this PR's device sources are separate kinds in the same recovery codec, and both restore paths run.

Rebased onto `main` at `36e52993c9f` after #192335 merged. The only conflict was the database-worker list in `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server-paths.mjs`: #192335's final head had already sorted its two persistence tests there, so this PR now adds only its own tests, in sorted order. The changed lines are otherwise identical to the previous head.

## Evidence

- On `305b6cd` (after the rebase), on a macOS arm64 host through Crabbox: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint on the 181 changed files, and `pnpm test` over the 40 test files this PR adds or changes, `src/gateway/openclaw-id` and `test/vitest-cli-ownership.test.ts` all passed.
- On `609efde7166`: the OpenClaw ID, auth, operator-run, cron-stream, cron-source, HTTP execution, session-sharing and cron-method Gateway suites, 90 files, 1,098 tests passed; the cron suites (operator sources, condition scripts, execution context, store, command runner, stream schedules, isolated runs), 77 files, 726 tests passed, 1 skipped. prs.title: perf(skills): avoid rebuilding row status on every search character
prs.body:
Related: #193807

## What Problem This Solves

Searching a large installed Skills inventory repeatedly rebuilt unchanged row status text on every character.

## User Impact

Filtering Skills uses less renderer work while preserving the existing rows, status labels, verdict updates, and detail actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page publishes a new view-state object as the filter changes. Each row's plain verdict accessor let that broad update reach its status formatter even when the verdict stayed identical. A row-local memo supplies the equality boundary; the existing Skills owner still supplies authoritative skill and verdict data.

## Evidence

Acceptance: at least 5% improvement on the 1,000-skill search, 20 rotated base/head/base pairs in Chromium and WebKit, with the discovery search as a control. Chromium reports renderer CPU; WebKit reports first-input-to-final-commit application time, including inter-input driver gaps. Timings use production bundles and synthetic Gateway fixtures, not provider latency.

| Viewport | Flow | Engine / metric | n | Base median / p95 | Head median / p95 | Head Δ median / p95 | A/A Δ median / p95 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| desktop | page-skill-settings-action | chromium scriptMs | 20 | 128.377 / 136.180 | 44.904 / 48.529 | -65.02% / -64.36% | -0.22% / -0.88% |
| desktop | page-skill-settings-action | chromium taskMs | 20 | 160.897 / 170.390 | 67.596 / 73.660 | -57.99% / -56.77% | -1.07% / -0.69% |
| desktop | page-skill-settings-action | webkit applicationMs | 20 | 215.000 / 229.000 | 138.000 / 156.000 | -35.81% / -31.88% | +2.09% / +7.86% |
| desktop | page-skills-action | chromium scriptMs | 20 | 2.994 / 3.403 | 2.994 / 3.231 | +0.03% / -5.05% | -2.79% / -5.32% |
| desktop | page-skills-action | chromium taskMs | 20 | 8.195 / 9.329 | 8.139 / 9.134 | -0.69% / -2.09% | -1.96% / +0.19% |
| desktop | page-skills-action | webkit applicationMs | 20 | 4.000 / 5.000 | 4.500 / 5.000 | +12.50% / +0.00% | +25.00% / +0.00% |
| mobile | page-skill-settings-action | chromium scriptMs | 20 | 125.729 / 131.088 | 43.403 / 45.569 | -65.48% / -65.24% | -0.87% / +5.15% |
| mobile | page-skill-settings-action | chromium taskMs | 20 | 155.730 / 163.389 | 64.906 / 67.975 | -58.32% / -58.40% | -0.45% / +4.41% |
| mobile | page-skill-settings-action | webkit applicationMs | 20 | 234.000 / 259.000 | 146.000 / 164.000 | -37.61% / -36.68% | -1.07% / -3.47% |
| mobile | page-skills-action | chromium scriptMs | 20 | 2.571 / 2.730 | 2.560 / 2.742 | -0.43% / +0.44% | -1.26% / +1.28% |
| mobile | page-skills-action | chromium taskMs | 20 | 8.881 / 10.048 | 8.904 / 9.922 | +0.26% / -1.25% | -0.13% / +1.70% |
| mobile | page-skills-action | webkit applicationMs | 20 | 3.000 / 3.000 | 3.000 / 3.000 | +0.00% / +0.00% | +0.00% / +0.00% |

480/480 scenarios passed. The 32-core host load ranged from 9.48 to 28.51 (median 15.81). The tiny desktop WebKit discovery control moved 4 → 4.5 ms at the median, while its identical-base control moved 4 → 5 ms; all three p95s were 5 ms. Chromium control task medians changed −0.69% desktop / +0.26% mobile. This is warm filtering after inventory readiness, not a cold-load claim.

Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --control-bundle-dir <base> --steps page-skill-settings-action,page-skills-action --viewport both --engines chromium,webkit --pairs 20`. Base `938a72d4c1e4`; head source tree committed as `fcd960169c7`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| UI typecheck | Pass |
| Skills view tests | 24/24 pass; 4.24 s runner / 5.70 s wrapper |
| Targeted lint, formatting, diff check | Pass |

| Production builds and strict performance comparison | Pass; startup 90,666 → 90,669 B gzip, one CSS request; chat boot 1,295,819 → 1,295,781 B gzip |

Before/after screenshots below use synthetic data. All 118 emitted CSS assets are byte-identical. Computed styles and element geometry match for the toolbar, input, row and status across both engines, both viewports, and initial/filtered states. The supplemental capture reuses the existing engine scenario and fixture.

Production LOC: 692 → 692. Tests: 825 → 862 (+37 lines for retained status updates after filtering, changed verdicts, and changed missing requirements). One createMemo added (23 → 24); effects, manual listeners, DOM queries, untrack, flush, and owner capture remain zero. The scoped test-line allocation covers those 37 lines. No dependencies, runtime owners, or size ceilings changed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node Runtime Conformance starts a Rust toolchain and workspace proof for TypeScript-only PR inputs. Rust configuration and sidecar fixture changes are also missing from ordinary event admission.

## User Impact

CI skips the independent contract proof when an exact, complete PR comparison selects only the other owner. Shared inputs retain both. Deleted, unknown, malformed or capped inputs and failed lookups retain both; manual and scheduled validation keep their existing policies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing TypeScript and Rust scheduled input lists for PR selection, bind the lookup to event base/head revisions, and keep omission conditional on an explicit false output. This also admits the Rust configurations and sidecar fixtures already consumed by the proof.

Fourth slice of the adaptive-CI work tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191191; stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193834. Requested by repository maintainer Vincent.

## Evidence

- Full native workflow-cost suite: 171 tests passed, covering owner selection, deleted/unknown/malformed/capped/API-error fallback, string-output transport, and scheduled/manual/draft behavior.

prs.title: fix(chat): hide restart recovery input from the chat feed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the long Gateway restart recovery instructions appearing in chat when interrupted work resumes.

## User Impact

Recovery continues without a user-visible restart message. Original requests and continued answers stay visible; actionable update outcomes remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing chat projection now hides internal restart inputs without changing their canonical transcript or agent delivery. Hidden restart inputs retain the next reply’s turn boundary. Explicit status summaries are single-line and bounded to 64 characters including their label; necessary details remain intact rather than being clipped. The existing notice owner is reused; there is no new schema, prompt policy or recovery mechanism.

## Evidence

Comparable real Control UI renders with synthetic Gateway history. Before: the recovery/ownership paragraph is shown. After: it is absent and the continued answer remains visible. No live Gateway restart or provider execution was performed.

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop | ![Desktop before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22ae55af-6e27-42a8-93d9-9d65f432f2df) | ![Desktop after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58781df2-0b93-45f6-8f9e-ac65e3753ec7) |
| Phone | ![Phone before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08e5ddc8-030c-4c93-ba51-5f1dabd504b3) | ![Phone after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0905eedf-c5f5-414c-a37c-307402bbded9) |

- Regression failed on the baseline because the recovery input was displayed.
- Focused tests cover unchanged agent input, persisted transcript preservation, pending/live/reloaded history exclusion, reply turn boundaries, bounded summaries, ordinary-user lookalikes and actionable update outcomes.
- A dedicated 105-line test allocation covers this change’s exact net regression-test growth; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- 36 Node boundary tests and 35 final focused UI tests passed. Baseline regression failed as expected.
- Targeted core/UI lint, core/UI typechecking (including core-test shards), formatting, i18n and `git diff --check` passed.
- Test-line allocation check passed: +105 net regression-test lines, no shared baseline change.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all applicable checks passed except an inherited changelog-attribution failure in untouched `CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md` and a timeout while UI typechecking waited for the artifact lock. The separate supported `pnpm tsgo:ui` rerun passed.
- Author simplification pass retained the existing display/notice owners; no new recovery mechanism, persistence or prompt policy. Whole-change production delta is +30 lines, tests +105, docs +11 (plus allocation metadata). The growth covers display suppression, turn boundaries and bounded status-copy projection.

### CI follow-up

- Initial CI found a 68-byte chat-startup gzip overage. The status projection was simplified without changing the performance budget, suppressing actionable failures, or changing restart recovery delivery. Final paired performance validation passed against the CI base: chat +86 B gzip (within the existing variance allowance), new-session boot -132 B. The 35 focused UI tests, UI typecheck and targeted lint passed. Budgets were not changed.
- checks-ui (2/3) failed in form-controls.browser.test.ts:192 (disabled agent selector retained focus border). The isolated case reproduces with the exact same expected/actual colors. Its stylesheet/test/helper inputs are unchanged from this PR's base, and it imports no changed chat-notice module. This is an inherited, unrelated CSS defect, not a passing rerun; no broad CSS repair is included.
- ClawSweeper reports that autofix is retired and it now reviews only. Hosted review was accepted/queued by the trusted dispatch; local repairs remain single-writer.

Production Gateway, personal state and channels were not changed or restarted.

prs.title: improve(chat): stop recompiling preview regexes while rendering native chat
prs.body:
Closes #193737

## What Problem This Solves

Native chat on iOS and macOS recompiles the same link and source preview regular expressions every time a message bubble is rendered or a preview page is parsed.

## User Impact

User impact: chat bubbles and link previews do less main-thread work. In the native macOS run, link detection over every bubble took about a third as long and Open Graph parsing about a quarter as long. There is no visible behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bare URL, HTML attribute, HTML title, HTML entity and external content frame patterns are constants, but each was compiled inside the function that used it, in some cases once per Markdown text node or once per `<meta>` tag. They are now load-once constants, like the existing `NSRegularExpression` constants in `ChatReactions.swift` and `ChatSessionSidebarModel+Titles.swift`. Patterns, options and the `try?` fallbacks are unchanged.

Left as is on purpose: patterns built from runtime input (progress card closing tag, session title prefix), the hover card `match(_:_:)` helper that takes its pattern as an argument, and `ChatProgressCardMarkdown`, which builds its expressions per call by design. Caching the link preview result per message would also skip the Markdown parse (about 78 us of the remaining cost), but that needs a cache with its own invalidation and belongs in a separate change.

## Evidence

### Native runtime proof

Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080 (both jobs passed)
- `workload p3`: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080/job/127651498957
- `focused suites p3`: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080/job/127651499397

Artifacts (90 days): `chatui-perf-proof-p3` (summary.md, counts.json, per-sample JSON, transcript screenshots, probe placements, instrumentation diffs, build and test logs, os_signpost export) and `chatui-perf-proof-p3-focused` (focused suite logs).
Reproducible workload: fork branch `etzelm/openclaw:proof/chatui-perf-p3` at `9e25db1dd95` (README explains each phase). Nothing from it is part of this PR.

**Toolchain:** GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runner (image macos26 20261026.0455.2, Apple M1 virtual, 3 cores), Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Apple Swift 6.3.3, macOS 26.6.2. Real Xcode toolchain, no shims or macro stand-ins. Xcode 27 is not on the hosted image.

**Exact code:** the job fetches base `9f3ed313782` from openclaw/openclaw, applies this PR's diff and refuses to continue unless the tree equals the head `3b90189fde1` tree `e6c9e906`. Tree check passed: 2 files, +22 -14.

**Workload:** the real `OpenClawChatView` and `OpenClawChatViewModel` in an `NSHostingView` in an `NSWindow`. A 60-turn cited web_search transcript comes in through an `OpenClawChatTransport` (`requestHistory`), giving 210 rows, 140 user and assistant bubbles and 210 source cards. Each assistant answer is a multi-paragraph Markdown message with three cited links and one bare link. Phases:
- load
- scroll (64 positions)
- resize (4 widths)
- append (10 turns)
- stream (24 deltas)
- bubbleScan: 20 passes of `chatFirstPreviewURL` over every bubble's display text. This is the function `ChatMessageBubble.linkPreviewURL` calls from `body`.
- openGraphParse: 50 `parseChatOpenGraph` calls on fixture HTML, alternating a page with `og:title` and one that falls back to `<title>`. The parser is called directly; the tap and network fetch are unchanged and not driven.

Base and head are built in release with identical scratch call counters. The probe sets match apart from line numbers, and the added lines are identical on both sides. Samples are interleaved base, head, 5 rounds, with a fresh process per sample. NSRegularExpression compiles are counted per pattern family by swapping `-initWithPattern:options:error:` inside the test process only, so product code is not changed.

Rule: head compiles each pattern at most once per process, outputs (row fingerprints, Open Graph results, screenshot) are identical, and no phase is slower at equal work. Counts are the claim; times are reported with spread.

#### NSRegularExpression compiles per phase (median of 5, range if it varied)

| Phase | Pattern | Base | Head | Work in phase (base and head) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| load | bare URL | 3569 (3459 to 3569) | 1 | same 3459 to 3569 text-node scans |
| load | external content frame | 360 | 1 | 360 frame strips |
| scroll | bare URL | 1912 (1802 to 2951) | 0 | same 1802 to 2951 text-node scans |
| append | bare URL | 3122 | 0 | 3122 text-node scans |
| append | external content frame | 60 | 0 | 60 frame strips |
| stream | bare URL | 220 | 0 | 220 text-node scans |
| bubbleScan | bare URL | 77000 | 0 | 77000 text-node scans |
| openGraphParse | HTML attribute | 125 | 1 | 50 parses, 125 meta tags |
| openGraphParse | HTML title | 25 | 1 | 25 title fallbacks |
| openGraphParse | HTML entity | 100 | 1 | 50 parses |

In every phase and sample, base compiles equal the work count: one bare URL compile per Markdown text node, one frame compile per wrapped title or snippet, one attribute compile per meta tag, and two entity compiles per parse. Head compiles each pattern once per process, on first use, and 0 times after that. Over the whole workload, per process: bare URL 85823 compiles on base vs 1 on head, external frame 420 vs 1, attribute 125 vs 1, title 25 vs 1, entity 100 vs 1. One unrelated pattern is compiled twice on both sides.

#### Output unchanged

- Per-row fingerprint (SHA-256 of the bubble's link preview URL, every preview URL in its text, and its source cards with title, domain, excerpt and cited URLs) for all 210 rows: one digest `4beda980...e168` on all 5 base and all 5 head samples.
- Open Graph results for both fixtures are identical on base and head (title, image URL, decoded entities).
- Transcript screenshot (960x720 `NSWindow`, user bubble with its link preview card, cited assistant answer): PNG bytes are identical on base and head, SHA-256 `e41500f1...8800`, in every sample.

#### Timings (bonus; counts are the claim)

Shared hosted runner, load average 19 to 26 on 3 cores. 5 samples per side.

| Measure | Base median | Base p95 | Head median | Head p95 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `chatFirstPreviewURL` over all 140 bubbles, per pass (us, n=100) | 65521 | 77394 | 23623 | 32566 | -63.9% |
| `parseChatOpenGraph` per call (us, n=250) | 144.0 | 434.2 | 35.1 | 80.5 | -75.6% |
| load phase (ms) | 652 | 926 | 516 | 750 | -20.9% |
| append phase (ms) | 1543 | 1764 | 1424 | 1529 | -7.7% |
| stream phase (ms) | 131 | 187 | 105 | 144 | -19.9% |
| resize phase (ms) | 79 | 100 | 80 | 87 | +0.3% |
| scroll phase (ms) | 2587 | 3253 | 3161 | 3601 | +22.2% |

The scroll cell does not show a regression. How many bubbles SwiftUI materializes while scrolling is bimodal, about 1,900 or 2,951 text-node scans per sample, and head landed on the larger count in 4 of 5 samples (base in 1 of 5). At equal work the two sides overlap:

| Scans per sample | Base scroll (ms) | Head scroll (ms) |
|---:|---|---|
| about 1,900 | 2388 to 2597 (4 samples) | 2142 (1 sample) |
| 2,951 | 3253 (1 sample) | 2960 to 3601 (4 samples) |

Normalized per text-node scan (the two sides materialized different numbers of bubbles in load and scroll): load 0.183 vs 0.149 ms (-18.6%), scroll 1.327 vs 1.120 ms (-15.6%). The compiles avoided in scroll are a small part of that phase. The time saving shows clearly in the bubbleScan and openGraphParse measures, where head p95 is below base median.

#### Gaps

- macOS `NSHostingView` only; the iOS simulator was not run. Wall times come from a shared virtual runner and are not a device frame-time claim.
- The os_signpost recording is partial: the base trace kept 5 of the 7 phase intervals, and the head trace timed out while saving. No claim rests on it; the counts and timings above come from in-process measurements.
- No committed benchmark. OpenClaw has no committed native chat workload to extend. The change has no behavior to assert, and counting compiles needs the method swap shown above, which belongs in a proof harness, not in the test suite. The rig branch is the reproducible workload: it pins base, diff and head tree, holds the workload and counters as source, and reruns end to end with one push to a fork (about 33 minutes) or locally with `bash rig/run-lane.sh prepare|focused|build|workload 5|summary`.

### Tests

- Xcode 26.6, unmodified code: `swift test --filter 'ChatSourcePreviewTests|ChatLinkPreview'`, 44 tests in 12 suites passed on base and on head ([focused suites job](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080/job/127651499397)).
- Full OpenClawKit `swift test` on the same head tree (`e6c9e906`), same Xcode: 2532 tests in 226 suites passed ([job](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42122411213/job/127577896743), from an earlier run of the proof branch).
- SwiftFormat 0.63.0 with `config/swiftformat`: 0 files need formatting.
- No new tests: behavior is unchanged, and compile counts are only observable through the method swap used in the proof above.

<details><summary>Earlier package benchmark (Command Line Tools)</summary>

Acceptance rule: same machine, release build, base and fixed code interleaved ABAB, 12 samples per side per run, 5 runs; the fix counts if `chatPreviewURLs` on a realistic message improves by more than run-to-run spread, no workload regresses, and outputs are identical.

Apple M3 Ultra, macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2 (Command Line Tools), host shared with other builds (load average 25 to 35 on 32 cores):

| Workload | Base median (us) | Fixed median (us) | Base p95 (us) | Fixed p95 (us) | Median change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chatPreviewURLs`, 1.4k char message, 37 text nodes, 15 links | 288 to 299 | 146 to 152 | 298 to 448 | 150 to 178 | -48.5% to -49.3% |
| `chatPreviewURLs`, one-line reply | 11.3 to 11.9 | 7.2 to 7.6 | 12.0 to 12.1 | 7.6 to 8.4 | -35.6% to -36.3% |
| `parseChatOpenGraph`, page with 33 meta tags | 432 to 453 | 151 to 158 | 446 to 799 | 159 to 263 | -65.0% to -65.2% |

Ranges are across the 5 runs. The fixed p95 is below the base median in every run. The harness is a local package (base and head copies of the parsing section of `ChatLinkPreview.swift`), not committed.

- Compile cost per pattern: 3.6 us (bare URL, title), 5.5 us (entities), 7.4 us (attributes), 9.0 us (external content frame). For scale, `Document(parsing:)` of the same message is about 78 us.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw onboard` registers `--team` (`src/cli/program/register.onboard.ts:273`) and `openclaw setup` registers the same flag (`src/cli/program/register.setup.ts:67`), but `docs/cli/onboard.md` is the page that enumerates the onboarding flags and its `## Flags` list has no `--team` entry — a grep for `--team` in that page returns nothing. `docs/start/wizard.md` explains the team flow and `docs/cli/setup.md:99` even refers readers to "the same small-team onboarding as `onboard --team`", so the referenced flag is undocumented exactly where a user looks it up.

- Problem: `--team` is missing from the `openclaw onboard` flag reference: what it creates, how `--agent-name` interacts with it, where member workspaces land, and which onboarding modes reject it.
- Solution: add a `--team` bullet to `## Flags`, beside the `--agent-name` bullet it modifies, with the roster, the coordinator naming rules, the per-member workspace layout, the rejected mode combinations, the existing-roster refusal, and a link to the wizard section that owns the flow narrative.
- What changed: `docs/cli/onboard.md` (12 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only. `docs/start/wizard.md` and `docs/cli/setup.md` keep their existing team text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flag belongs in the per-command flag list rather than only in the narrative page, because `## Flags` is where this page documents every other onboarding option, including `--agent-name`, whose behavior `--team` changes. The wording states the numbers that come from code (the `coordinator` fallback name, the four roster ids, the `<workspace>/<agent-id>` layout) and leaves the recovery, receipt, and `systemAgent` semantics to `/start/wizard`, which already documents them, so the page keeps one owner per fact instead of duplicating the wizard's prose.

## User Impact

Users see that `openclaw onboard --team` creates a coordinator plus researcher, writer, and reviewer instead of one agent, know that `--agent-name` names the coordinator and that omitting it yields `coordinator`, know each member gets its own workspace subfolder, and learn up front that `--team` is refused with classic, remote, or import onboarding and with an existing agent roster. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**CLI registration** — `src/cli/program/register.onboard.ts:273` declares the option and its help text, and `:188` narrows it before it reaches the command layer:

```typescript
team: opts.team === true ? true : undefined,
```

`src/cli/program/register.setup.ts:67` registers the identical option for `openclaw setup`, which is why `docs/cli/setup.md:99` can point at `onboard --team`.

**Runtime default** — the documented `coordinator` name is the code fallback, not a schema default: `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local.ts:358` is `const firstAgentName = opts.agentName ?? (opts.team ? "coordinator" : "main");` and the interactive path derives the same suggestion from the preset at `src/commands/onboard-first-agent.ts:35` (`const defaultName = teamPreset?.coordinator.id ?? "main";`), whose prompt message switches to **"What should we call your chief of staff?"** at `:41-43` when a team is selected. `loadAgentTeamPreset` (`src/agents/agent-roles.ts:90`) reads `docs/reference/templates/roles/presets/team.json`, which lists `coordinator` plus the specialists `researcher`, `writer`, and `reviewer` — the exact ids the new bullet names.

**Consumer** — three runtime paths consume the flag, and each documented constraint is one of them. `src/commands/onboard.ts:502-512` rejects `--team` when the mode is remote, when `--import-from`, `--import-source`, or `--flow import` is set, or when classic interactive setup is requested, with "--team supports local guided or non-interactive onboarding." `src/commands/onboard-guided.ts:118-121` (guided) and `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local.ts:350-356` (non-interactive) both refuse `--team` when `hasAuthoredRoster` is true and point at `openclaw agents team create`, and `src/commands/onboard-agent.ts:92-98` repeats that guard at creation time. On the effect side `src/commands/onboard-agent.ts:136-143` calls `createAgentTeam({ coordinator: firstAgentName, workspaceRoot })`, and `src/agents/agent-team.ts:133` sets each member's workspace to `path.join(workspaceRoot, member.id)` — the `<workspace>/<agent-id>` layout in the bullet.

**Not a dead flag** — `--team` is not CLI-parser-only: the same value reaches `createAgentTeam`, which writes roster entries, per-member workspaces, and coordinator delegation config. The chosen coordinator also becomes part of the local onboarding state (`teamCoordinatorId`, `src/state/local-onboarding-state.ts:48`), and `src/commands/onboard-guided.ts:122-125` reads it back so an interrupted team run resumes with the same coordinator instead of prompting again.

**Test** — `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local.default-agent.test.ts:358` ("creates a role team through non-interactive onboarding and keeps coordinator ownership") runs `runSetup({ workspace, team: true, json: true })` and pins `Object.keys(agents.entries)` to `["coordinator", "researcher", "writer", "reviewer"]` at `:376-381` plus `workspace: path.join(workspace, "coordinator")` at `:384`. `src/commands/onboard.test.ts:865` pins flag parsing through the guided route ("keeps `--team` on guided onboarding") and `src/cli/program/register.onboard.test.ts:254` parses `--non-interactive --accept-risk --team`.

**Sibling docs** — `docs/start/wizard.md:186-206` already states the local-only restriction, the `openclaw agents team create` alternative for an existing roster, and the `--workspace` parent-directory rule; the new bullet reuses that vocabulary and links its `#choose-one-agent-or-a-team` heading instead of restating it. `docs/cli/setup.md:99-100` already documents `setup --team` and the coordinator naming.

**Docs toolchain** — all run against this exact head:
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/cli/onboard.md` — pass, 1 file
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,399 internal links, 0 broken
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check` (`pnpm format:docs:check`) — clean, 1,413 files
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — documentation only; the onboarding flag, its validation, and team creation are unchanged, so no runtime reproduction applies. The behavior the bullet states is pinned by the existing tests named above.

**Exact head** — `5cfa237c06459db007e93701ad00f30f0ec25117`

prs.title: test(ui): measure interactions in aged Control UI tabs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The existing working-day soak checks retention, but does not measure whether interactions become slower in the same long-lived Control UI document.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Maintainers can compare a churned tab and a long-idle tab with two freshly loaded controls in the same browser process, using a production build.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an opt-in ageing census that reuses the working-day driver and the existing interaction, timing, resource and heap collectors. Fixed 400-message probe conversations remain separate from the 200-session/50-turn soak. Checkpoints rotate typing, session switch, Settings route switch, sidebar toggle and model-picker actions; each records application elapsed time, host load, resource counts, document identity, computed styles and synthetic screenshots. Chromium records task CPU and verifies native hidden idle. Optional trace/heap passes stay separate from untraced timings.

The shared driver's picker search is scoped to the active pane and uses a term present in both fixture catalogs. No production UI, CSS, dependency, size budget or build-graph changes.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Production build | Pass; 90,280 B normalized startup JS gzip, 1 startup CSS request |
| Existing build report | Chat boot reports 1,289,149 B against 1,288,198 B; this tooling-only diff does not alter its inputs |
| Chromium and WebKit qualification | Pass: 2 samples/action, one full churn round, idle-first input and final checkpoint |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:scripts` pass |
| Targeted lint and format | Pass |
| Production Knip | `pnpm deadcode:knip` passes; exact documented entry added |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Full ageing census | Running: 20 rotated samples/action, rounds 0/1/5/10, two-hour idle, Chromium + WebKit |

The long experiment is now running independently per engine. The first combined attempt completed Chromium round 10, then stopped on a WebKit `timeOrigin` equality check; document identity now uses a document-start UUID, retaining clock origins as diagnostics. The long experiment's result will be added here after completion. There is no claim of a production slowdown or performance improvement in this PR. Renderer fixtures exclude service-worker, real Gateway and provider latency. WebKit idle remains visible; Chromium idle is verified hidden. Input-to-last-commit spans include gaps between native inputs in compound actions, so raw driver tails remain available and noisy A/A results require CPU/count attribution.

Reproduce:

```sh
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 pnpm ui:build
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
  scripts/bench-control-ui-aged-tab.ts --samples 20 --rounds 10 \
  --idle-minutes 120 --output .artifacts/aged-tab/production
```

Scope/size: new benchmark 0 → 618 lines; guide 0 → 54 lines; existing files +5/−3 lines. All collectors and scenario owners are reused. Reports and generated captures stay outside Git. No remote lease or Docker was used.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: new Venice setups default to `zai-org-glm-4.7`, which is no longer Venice's default model, and the Venice docs still describe it as the "live default trait".

## User Impact

User impact: onboarding Venice now selects `venice/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-uncensored`, which Venice's `GET /models/traits?type=text` currently returns for both `default` and `function_calling_default`. Existing configs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Points the manifest `defaultModel` and onboarding alias at the current Venice default, and adds that model to the offline catalog. Its specs come from Venice's public `/models` API: private, 1M context, 131k max output, text and image input, and $0.33 / $1.32 / $0.00825 per 1M tokens for input, output and cache read. The provider docs examples, default row and catalog table are updated to match.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension venice`: 4 files, 27 tests passed
- `oxfmt --check` on changed files and `pnpm format:docs:check`: clean
- `curl 'https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/models/traits?type=text'` returns `"default":"deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-uncensored"`
