prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user from another agent's turn reaches that agent instead of the owner
prs.body:
Closes #179964
Related: #180140

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent answering another agent sends its `ask_user` question back to that agent instead of to the person who owns it, and the other agent's reply can then answer it. For example, a peer agent asks to book a meeting, the agent asks its owner "May Bob book Thursday?", and the question goes to the peer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Routing.** The inbound sender's bot flag (`SenderIsBot`) now travels with the run, the way `senderIsOwner` already does. The shared question publisher (`question-prompt-send.ts`) uses it to choose the recipient: a bot sender's `ask_user` and `secrets` prompts go to the agent's owner, on the route proactive delivery already uses (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`, then the channel's `allowFrom`). This covers every publication path:
  - embedded runs;
  - the loopback tools that CLI backends use;
  - skill commands;
  - harness questions (Codex, Copilot, CLI plugins);
  - ACP elicitation;
  - queued turns.
- **Answering.** The owner's typed reply cannot answer a question created on the bot's turn, so the owner prompt links to the question's Control UI page, which takes every answer form, free text included. Option buttons stay where the owner's channel shows them. The prompt asks for no typed reply.
- **Current owner and question.** The owner route is read from the live config. Right before the prompt goes to delivery, and again at delivery's final handoff (`assertDirectAdapterHandoff`, `onPlatformSendDispatch`), the publisher confirms that the question is still pending and the config has not changed. Otherwise nothing is sent.
- **The bot can't answer.** A bot's message is never accepted as an answer: not in reply admission, not when steered into the run that asked (`allowPendingUserInputAnswer: false`), and not in ACP question claims. Harness secret input is not requested on a bot's turn.

Boundaries:
- This adds no new way to answer a question and changes no answer authority. Answers still come from the channel's question buttons or the Control UI.
- Which tools are offered is unchanged.
- No schema, stored state, config option or permission changes. Human senders' prompts are unchanged.
- Not in this PR: typed owner answers, and letting agent-only channel plugins offer `ask_user` (#180140).

**Submitted for maintainer acceptance:** the recipient policy (the proactive owner route) and the Control UI prerequisite. Without `gateway.publicOrigin`, a bot sender's question is cancelled, even a single-choice question on a channel with buttons, because the owner could not give a free-text answer.

## User Impact

An agent that needs its owner's decision while serving another agent now asks the owner, who answers on the linked Control UI page, or with buttons where their channel has them. The other agent can no longer answer for the owner. Without an owner route or `gateway.publicOrigin`, the question is cancelled and `ask_user` reports that the prompt could not be delivered; the error names the setting. Questions from people behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Exact head `877dfab2d8f`, based on `56775d8ebd0`. Runtime transcripts are in the PR comments.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QA: a bot sender's question (`runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender`) | Prompt goes to the bot's conversation | Owner gets it with the answer page; bot gets nothing. With `senderIsBot` removed from the embedded subscription in `attempt-stream-prepare.ts`, the scenario fails: the owner never receives the question. |
| QA: the owner answers in the Control UI (`control-ui-ask-user-owner-answer`, Chromium) | — | Linked page answered as the signed-in operator; run resumes with `Deploy: Staging (Recommended)` |
| QA: no `gateway.publicOrigin` (`runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender-no-answer-page`) | — | Person's prompt and answer unchanged; bot's question cancelled |
| A bot's text during a pending question (`dispatch.question-input.test.ts`) | `handled: true` (answers) | Refused |
| A bot's message steered into the asking run (`agent-runner-steer-adoption.worker.test.ts`) | Answer-eligible | Not an answer; a person's still is |
| Owner replaced or question ended during held durable delivery (`owner-question-prompt.integration.test.ts`, `ask_user` and `secrets`) | — | Adapter never called. With the handoff guards removed, both fail. |
| Upgrade: config and state from 2026.10.5 start on this head | — | Gateway health `ok`; config sha256 unchanged |

The three QA runs ran on this head. The upgrade check ran on `88d812e801d`. The QA runs use a real Gateway child, qa-channel and the mock OpenAI provider. The integration test runs `sendDurableMessageBatchCore` with a test channel whose send preparation is held. Owner routes come from the real resolver throughout; unit tests mock only the transport.

Local checks on this head, Node 24.22.1:
- The 12 test files this PR changes pass, including `attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts`, which checks that the embedded subscription receives `senderIsBot`.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` pass, and `pnpm build` succeeds.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` (including `max-lines`) and `git diff --check` are clean; `check:import-cycles` and `check:madge-import-cycles` report no cycles.

Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) was scoped-clean on `88d812e801d`.

```sh
pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --scenario runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender \
  --scenario control-ui-ask-user-owner-answer \
  --scenario runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender-no-answer-page
pnpm test src/agents/tools/question-prompt-send.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/owner-question-prompt.integration.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-steer-adoption.worker.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/dispatch.question-input.test.ts \
  src/gateway/tool-resolution.bot-sender.test.ts
```

Not claimed:
- A native button tap on a live channel. QA Channel has no button interaction, and Telegram proof needs leased credentials. Taps use the existing callback authorization and `question.resolve`.
- A live Discord or Slack run with a bot author.
- A dedicated test for the ACP guard.

### Line budgets

- Test lines: `config/test-lines-allocations/ask-user-bot-sender-owner.txt` allocates the 578 test lines this PR adds net. The shared baseline is unchanged, and no test or assertion is removed to make room.
- `max-lines`: `attempt-stream-prepare.ts` and `cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts` are at the 700-line cap on `main`. Each gains one `senderIsBot` line, so each also drops one line without changing behavior: a single-use `canInject` closure is inlined, and a three-property object literal is written on one line.

CI on this head: every test job passes. `openclaw/ci-gate` and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` wait on maintainer approval of this revision.

prs.title: fix(ui): surface native device setting edit failures on their row
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native device and permission setting rows silently swallow write failures. `ui/src/app/native-device-settings.ts` makes the edit callback optional: when a generic row calls `set()` without one, a rejected native write only reaches `console.warn`, the control stays where the user left it, and the UI shows no error at all. GatewayHosting, cookie sync, and launch-at-login already surface failures via a completion-signal pattern; the generic rows never did.

## User Impact

Toggling Native experience, changing Appearance / icon style / computer control provider, switching location access mode, enabling precise location, or turning on active computer presence — while the native host rejects the write — leaves the control in a wrong or stale position with no feedback. The user believes the setting saved. After this change, the row that issued the edit renders the failure inline with `role="alert"`.

## Why

Every action needs a visible outcome or a recorded intentional non-outcome. `set()` reports failures through the settle callback, but these call sites never attached one, so the error had no path to the UI. Rendering it on the issuing row keeps the failure next to the control the user just touched, matching the existing launch-at-login treatment instead of inventing a new error channel.

## Evidence

- Red on base (`openclaw/main` at `01a5e160dab`): `ui/src/pages/device/device-pages.test.ts` → `5 failed | 18 passed` — the new role=alert assertions fail because generic rows show nothing on failure.
- Green with the fix: `23 passed (23)`.
- Static checks: `pnpm tsgo:ui` clean; test shard `tsconfig.core.test.ui-pages.json` clean; `oxlint ui/src/pages/device/` → 0 errors, 0 warnings (`device-page.tsx` 698/700 lines); max-lines ratchet OK; test-lines ratchet OK (`slack 28`, this change's +48 test lines recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/native-edit-failure-feedback.txt`); `oxfmt --check` clean.

## Merge Danger

UI-only: two pages, one new helper, one test file, one allocation file. No schema, config, protocol, or gateway changes. `device-page.tsx` sits just under the 700-line max (698) — keep new rows in the shared helper rather than inlining. Test-line credit is fully accounted for. Duplicate search before opening (`file:device-page`, `file:permissions-page`, `edit failure in:title`) found no competing open PR.

prs.title: improve: reduce prepared workspace refresh overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prepared cloud-worker refreshes pay for multiple provider command round trips and transfer newly verified Git objects a second time into the retained workspace.

## User Impact

Public repository refreshes use one provider command; private repositories use inspection followed by one combined transfer/setup command after the upload. Workspaces share verified immutable Git packs where hard links are supported and retain the existing fetch fallback. Setup still uses the current provisioning owner, command budget, and setup environment. Capture, reserve, manifest, and verification policies are unchanged.


## Why This Change Was Made

Core already has enough information to finish public preparation in one command. Private sources only need the Gateway between inspection and pack production. Both paths now run combined work through `runScriptWithBudget`, recheck current ownership immediately before dispatch, and charge seed time against the setup budget. The seed derives its retained key from the project key and commit. Existing completion parsing owns replay, failed setup, and capture decisions; phase totals are collected once.

The seed keeps incoming objects packed. Refresh links packs and indexes into the existing object store, preserves both shallow boundaries, and checks that the requested commit resolves. Connectivity was already checked against the same retained base. Missing packs or unsuccessful links retain the original local fetch path.

## Evidence

Acceptance: public/private refreshes take one/two provider runs, newly received packs share inodes with the workspace, workspace `git fsck --connectivity-only` passes, and loose-object seeds fall back to fetch. Phase totals, replay, owner replacement, and interrupted setup remain covered.

- Real-Git regression is red on base `ce8b7add7b003aa4ac41d4b32950ae334599d710`: public/private both take three runs and the received pack is absent from the workspace object store. Baseline run: 16.91 s wall time.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 39 passed, 122.84 s wall time, including a 34 s cold compiled-fixture build. The existing detected-install matrix accounts for about 24 s of test time.
- Final affected-suite run: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation-verification.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation-environment.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/project-seed-script.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-project-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **77 passed across five files, 180.12 s wall time**. This includes the final read-only inspection guard.
- Type-aware lint through `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` and changed-file oxfmt: passed.
- `pnpm run tsgo:core`: passed on the final code, 3.95 s wall time.
- `pnpm runtime:scripts:gen` and `pnpm runtime:scripts:check`: passed with no generated-file delta.
- Test-line allocation: exactly 168 net LF lines for real Git transfer/run-count regression and shared fixtures; checker passed against the base above with `--no-merge-base`. The shared scalar is unchanged. Production diff: +143 / -131 lines (net +12); generated output delta: zero.
- Independent review: Codex autoreview of the final local change against `ce8b7add7b003aa4ac41d4b32950ae334599d710`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. It included the Crabbox transport, environment recipe, and Git-pack owner as unchanged context. The local ClawSweeper entrypoint is not built, so this uses the documented autoreview fallback.

### Local Git measurement

Before the production change, measured the individual `gitUpdate` commands on a standalone shallow fixture made from the real 64,567-file OpenClaw repository, refreshing `56775d8ebd0baa4d9d88db86848d523c0e60cb00` to `ce8b7add7b003aa4ac41d4b32950ae334599d710`. Five interleaved fetch/link samples used the same retained workspace, reset to A with only the newly received objects removed between samples. The index was refreshed before measurement to exclude the initial clone's racy timestamps. These are **warm local-disk measurements**, not simulated AWS cold storage.

| Operation | Fetch path median / p95 | Linked path median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object transfer and commit resolution | 179 / 859 ms | 15 / 29 ms |
| Diff | 18 / 24 ms | 15 / 33 ms |
| Index refresh | 145 / 360 ms | 142 / 169 ms |
| Checkout | 174 / 179 ms | 168 / 188 ms |
| Total | 521 / 1178 ms | 340 / 403 ms |

`GIT_TRACE_PACK_ACCESS` shows why the fetch deserves separate cold-storage scrutiny: five fetches accessed 2,978 distinct 4 KiB pack pages, versus four for diff, one for index refresh, and three for checkout. Linking avoids this object traversal and second transfer. A simpler 64,000-file synthetic fixture made fetch look cheaper than index refresh/checkout, so the implementation decision uses the real repository layout and pack-access evidence. The first real-repository index refresh also cost 1.225 s due to freshly cloned index timestamps; that is separated from the stabilized measurements above.

Reproduction commands inside the fixture: `git fetch --depth=1 --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --update-shallow --negotiation-tip=HEAD <seed> <commit>`, `git diff --no-renames --name-only -z <old> <new>`, `git update-index -q --refresh`, and `git checkout --detach --force <commit>`. Candidate replaces only the first command with pack/index hard links, the union of the seed/workspace shallow boundaries, and `git rev-parse --verify <commit>^{commit}`. No host page-cache purge or live Gateway was used.

## Live proof

Isolated Gateway, real AWS workers. Ready-worker adoption of real `openclaw/openclaw` (64,000 tracked files) at a newer commit: whole placement 53.9 s against 78.1 s before this change, with `reserveRefresh` 29.6 s against 53.0 s. A private fixture one commit behind a snapshot forks and completes its first turn through the merged two-run path and `crabbox cp`. Adoption of a ready worker already at the exact commit took 7.6 s on the same fixture.

Not measured: a fork of the 64,000-file repository from a retained image with this change. `main` changed its pnpm version during the runs, which correctly changed the cache key, so both public fork attempts took the fresh path, so the cold `gitUpdate` number for the hard-linked pack has no live before-and-after on that repository.

prs.title: docs(plugins): align prompt and session hook contracts with runtime behavior
prs.body:
Related: #192753

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` misstates or omits several runtime hook contracts when plugin authors target multiple OpenClaw runtimes, input gates, finalization relays, or active-run steering.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors get accurate runtime-specific contracts—including that the Agents API harness ignores `toolsAllow` while ACPX rejects any returned value, that `before_agent_run` fails closed on errors and timeouts, and which SDK types and return shapes `before_agent_finalize` and `steerActiveRun` actually expose.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligned `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` directly against the current `main` hook runner, harness adapters, and session steering implementations, and updated the remaining `prompt injection` permission prose on the page to match the `allowPromptModification` rename (#192634).

<details>
<summary>Verified contract updates against source owners</summary>

- `before_model_resolve`: note that `attachments` is currently populated for prompt images (`{ kind: "image", mimeType }`) and omitted otherwise (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/setup.ts`), and that a canceled/superseded source run aborts preflight (`AgentHarnessPreflightError`) rather than continuing model preparation.
- `before_prompt_build` (`toolsAllow`): document worker-turn application (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-prompt.ts`), CLI filtering plus rejection only when native tools cannot be limited exactly (`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/cli-backends.ts`), ACPX rejection of any returned value including `["*"]` (`extensions/acpx/src/harness-attempt.ts`), Codex rejection of values without `"*"`, and that Agents API ignores the field (`extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.ts`).
- `heartbeat_prompt_contribution`: document `{ sessionKey?, agentId?, heartbeatName? }` input and that contributions from all handlers are joined before each combined field is truncated to a 1,000-character CJK-weighted budget (`src/infra/heartbeat-compat.ts`, `src/plugins/hooks.ts`).
- `requiresToolAuthority: true`: include worker turns (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-prompt.ts`) and Agents API (`extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.ts`) among runtimes supplying `toolAuthority`, and clarify that ACPX skips the post-policy phase.
- `before_agent_run`: separate Gateway worker-turn admission from the embedded/CLI timing (`/plugins/hooks#choose-a-hook`), describe `prompt` as the model-bound prompt including prompt-hook context (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.ts`), list optional event/decision fields (`void`, `category`, `metadata`, `accountId`, `channelId`, `senderId`, `senderIsOwner`), document the 15s default timeout and fail-closed blocking on error/timeout/invalid decision (`src/plugins/hooks.ts`, `src/agents/harness/before-agent-run.ts`), and clarify the formatted `Your message could not be sent: ...` block notice stored in `message.content`.
- `ctx.inputProvenance` & `ctx.memoryAudience`: add Agents API and remaining optional `InputProvenance` fields (`sourceRole`, `sourcePromptPrefix`, `jobId`, `runId`), plus `ctx.memoryAudience` as the kind-tagged `MemoryAudience` object (branch on `.kind`, linked to the memory SDK contract) and `ctx.assertMemoryAudienceCurrent()` revalidation guidance (`src/plugins/hook-agent-context.types.ts`, `src/plugins/memory-provider-types.ts`).
- `ctx.chatId` vs `ctx.channelContext.chat.id`: clarify where `ctx.chatId` carries the native ID (user-triggered embedded hooks and CLI hooks other than `agent_turn_prepare` and `before_prompt_build`) and that those CLI preparation hooks and the harnesses can mirror `ctx.channelId`; `ctx.channelContext.chat.id` takes the same value whenever the host sets a transport-native `ctx.chatId`, and CLI `agent_turn_prepare`/`before_prompt_build` contexts omit `ctx.channelContext` (`src/plugins/hook-agent-context.ts`, `src/agents/harness/hook-context.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/plugin-turn-context.ts`).
- `before_agent_finalize`: document `{ action: "continue" }` (and empty-`revise` normalization), describe `retry` as a field shape typed through `api.on("before_agent_finalize", ...)` rather than an importable SDK type (neither `PluginHookBeforeAgentFinalizeResult` nor `BeforeAgentFinalizeRetry` is exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`), and clarify bidirectional Codex native `Stop` hook relay translation (`src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-events.ts`).
- `steerActiveRun`: clarify `{ steered: true, runId }` when a stored duplicate key's receipt is available (`src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts`), describe Copilot accurately as exposing V1 `messageInjection` handles rather than a legacy V1 harness (`extensions/copilot/harness.ts`), distinguish the rejected promise when the plugin is already unloaded or unloads while the host prepares the steer (`src/plugins/registry.ts`, `src/plugins/contracts/active-run-steering.contract.test.ts`) from the `steered: false` result when the guarded runtime detects the unload during dispatch (`src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts`), and clarify the Control UI **`<plugin>` guidance** display-name label.

</details>

## Evidence

- Verified every changed statement line-by-line against current `main` runtime owners (`src/plugins/*`, `src/agents/*`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/*`, `src/infra/heartbeat-compat.ts`, `extensions/{acpx,agentsapi,copilot}/*`).
- Ran OpenClaw documentation gates on the rebased head commit:
  - `OPENCLAW_FORMAT_TOOL=oxfmt node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` → clean
  - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` → passed (0 MDX issues)
  - `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` & `--anchors` → 0 broken links/fragments in `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`
  - `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts --base upstream/main` → clean
  - `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs`, `bash scripts/docs-spellcheck.sh docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`, `git diff --check` → clean
- Follow-up `1fb9ac94d00` (Codex/ClawSweeper P2 on unload-time steering): rechecked against `src/plugins/registry.ts` (`assertCurrent()` after `await loadSteering()`), `src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts` (dispatch-stage `sourceRefusal` → `runtime_rejected`), and the `rechecks the plugin lifetime after loading the dispatch module` contract test; `check-docs-mdx`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` clean on the new head.
- Follow-up `8bc3a748e37` (Codex P2 on `ctx.memoryAudience`): documented the `{ kind, agentId, ... }` object shape from `src/plugins/memory-provider-types.ts` and linked `/plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context#memory-audience` (heading present, route in `docs/docs.json`); `check-docs-mdx`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` clean.
- Follow-up `c9057da91f9`: independent claim-by-claim source audit of every changed statement against `upstream/main` `37d5c24faec`; corrected `toolsAllow` per runtime, heartbeat budget semantics, `before_agent_run` worker timing and `prompt` content, `ctx.chatId`/`channelContext.chat.id`, and the finalize `retry` type reference. `check-docs-mdx`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` clean.
- Follow-up `3c18652dbba` (ClawSweeper P2 on CLI chat identity): rechecked that `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` builds the prompt-build hook context from `buildAgentHookContextChannelFields` only (`chatId: channelId`, no `channelContext`) and that `resolvePromptBuildHookResult` forwards the same context to `agent_turn_prepare` through `resolvePluginTurnContext` (`src/agents/plugin-turn-context.ts`); added `agent_turn_prepare` to the CLI exception and qualified the `channelContext.chat.id` mirroring statement. `format-docs --check` (oxfmt), `check-docs-mdx`, and `git diff --check` clean; `docs-spellcheck.sh` reports no hits in this file.
- Review: completed `pr-simplify` self-audit on `upstream/main..HEAD` (1 file changed: `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`, +97/-65 lines, docs-only; shared `~/.agents/skills/autoreview` helper is not installed in this environment).

prs.title: docs(imessage): document the probe timeout option
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`channels.imessage.probeTimeoutMs` bounds how long OpenClaw waits for `imsg` in the monitor and action checks that gate the private API bridge, and it is the knob an SSH-wrapped `cliPath` setup needs when a slow round trip makes a healthy bridge look broken. A grep for `probeTimeoutMs` across `docs/` returns nothing, while `docs/channels/imessage/private-api.md` walks readers through exactly those checks.

- Problem: the timeout behind the monitor's startup readiness probe, the cached private-API check that gates actions, and the `watch.subscribe` request is undocumented, including its default — and nothing tells readers that the `openclaw channels status --probe` command on the same page budgets itself instead.
- Solution: state the field, its `10000` ms default, the three checks it covers, when to raise it, that it can be set per account, and that the status command's own `--timeout <ms>` takes precedence over it.
- What changed: `docs/channels/imessage/private-api.md` (2 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already explains what the probe reports and how the cached capability check gates actions, so the timeout that decides whether either of them succeeds belongs in the same place rather than in a config reference the reader has to leave the page for. Because step 4 of that same section tells the reader to run `openclaw channels status --probe`, the paragraph also names the knob that command actually uses, so the two timeouts cannot be confused. `probeTimeoutMs` sits in the account base that both the channel root and `channels.imessage.accounts.<id>` reuse, so the paragraph names both scopes instead of implying a global-only key. The `imsg rpc` label keeps its own separate `timeoutMs: 30_000` in the monitor, so this text deliberately does not claim to cover general RPC calls.

## User Impact

Users on a remote or SSH-wrapped Messages Mac can discover and raise the probe budget instead of reading `probe.ts`, and can tell that a bridge that answers slower than `10000` ms is expected to report unhealthy rather than actually being down. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/imessage/src/config-schema.ts:95` declares the field, and `:75` puts it inside `IMessageAccountSchemaBase`, which `:120` extends for the channel root and `:124` reuses for each `accounts.<id>` entry:

```typescript
probeTimeoutMs: z.number().int().positive().optional(),
```

**Runtime type** — positive integer, milliseconds; no enum leaf to track.

**Default** — `extensions/imessage/src/constants.ts:1` is the value each documented call site falls back to:

```typescript
export const DEFAULT_IMESSAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;
```

The documented checks all resolve through that constant: `extensions/imessage/src/probe.ts:259` (`timeoutMs ?? cfg?.channels?.imessage?.probeTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_IMESSAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`), `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/monitor-provider.ts:260`, and `extensions/imessage/src/actions.ts:310`. Two call sites intentionally differ and are therefore not covered by this paragraph: `extensions/imessage/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts:46` defines a local `DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000` used at `:374` for the approval-flow chat lookup, and the status command supplies an explicit budget so the config fallback is never consulted for it (see the precedence paragraph under **Consumer**).

**Consumer** — the resolved value reaches the three paths the paragraph lists: `monitor-provider.ts:260` resolves it once per account, `:724` passes it to `probeIMessagePrivateApi(cliPath, probeTimeoutMs)` for the cached bridge check, `:1158` passes it to `probeIMessage(...)` inside the startup readiness check, and `:1219` uses it as the `{ timeoutMs: probeTimeoutMs }` budget for the `watch.subscribe` request that starts inbound watching. On the action side, `actions.ts:310` re-probes the cached private-API status with the same `DEFAULT_IMESSAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` fallback. `actions.ts:336` also forwards the raw `account.config.probeTimeoutMs` into the shared action `options`, where the probe helper resolves an unset value through the same chain at `probe.ts:259`.

**Status-command precedence** — the paragraph's last sentence is the part that needs a trace, because `probe.ts:259` takes `timeoutMs` first. `src/commands/channels/status.ts:41` resolves `--timeout` with `parseTimeoutMsWithFallback(opts.timeout, DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS, …)` and `:61-63`/`:71` always send a numeric `timeoutMs` with the `channels.status` request; `DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS` (`src/cli/daemon-cli/restart-health.constants.ts:3`) re-exports `GATEWAY_RESTART_REPLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (`gateway-shutdown-budget.mjs:2`), which is the `60000` already documented for `channels status --timeout` at `docs/cli/channels.md:74`. The Gateway hands that number to the channel adapter, `extensions/imessage/src/channel.ts:374-379` forwards it as `probeIMessageAccount({ timeoutMs, … })`, and `extensions/imessage/src/channel.runtime.ts:76` passes it positionally into `probeIMessage`, so the explicit argument wins and `channels.imessage.probeTimeoutMs` cannot change that check. `src/commands/channels/capabilities.test.ts:208` pins the adapter contract by asserting `probeAccount` receives `expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: 30_000 })`.

**Review follow-up** — the first revision (`ebe544313f6`) listed the status probe as one of the budgets this key controls. That claim was wrong for the precedence reason above, so `8948737c27e` narrows the sentence to the three checks that do resolve through the config and states the `--timeout <ms>` override instead. No other text changed; the diff is still 2 added lines.

**Test** — `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts:1532` exercises the config path with `probeTimeoutMs: 10_000`.

**Docs toolchain** — all run against this exact head:
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/channels/imessage/private-api.md` (`pnpm docs:check-mdx`) — pass, 1 file
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,398 internal links, 0 broken
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check` (`pnpm format:docs:check`) — clean, 1,413 files
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix for an already-shipped option; the iMessage probe implementation is unchanged, so no runtime reproduction applies.

**Exact head** — `8948737c27ef5f3ac79353d6faadd58aa1645d20`

prs.title: fix: keep message declarations when a turn cannot send
prs.body:
Related: #166969, #167710. Shared embedded-factory follow-up to native-Codex-specific #93813; this does not close either issue's full scope.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: temporarily disabling message execution removes its declaration from the shared embedded tool factory, changing the prompt/tool surface within the same conversation.

## User Impact

A turn can refuse message execution without removing the session's message declaration. The refusal remains non-callable and is excluded from exported/callable capability snapshots; other existing visibility policies remain in force. No configuration migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing execution gate instead of conditionally skipping message construction. Carry denied-execution metadata even without an availability binding, and preserve the current turn's refusal behind the offered session declaration. Owner/requester denials keep precedence. This separates stable declarations from current-turn authority without adding another policy owner or persistent state.

Simplification: reuse the existing factory, execution gate and availability metadata. Growth is necessary to retain refusals across declaration projection: production +48/-31 lines, tests +72/-0, plus a separate 72-line regression allocation; the shared test scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

[Exact successful proof job](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/actions/runs/42094131686/job/127479618360): base `bf0d53d5c17a666f34cfc3ef1671e726be235a9a`, [product `e11ba635`](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/commit/e11ba635a8dcbe9191beecd646ff0d0ae556a093), proof driver `cf5e419df180143a8e06699a8b1079cecf60ffe1`. This refreshed proof retains the base's current-owner authority guard and adds its denied-gateway interaction regression; it supersedes the older-base proof.

All ten required gates accepted, plus workflow validation:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing refusal sibling on base | 1 passed, 14 skipped |
| New regression with base production | Intended assertion RED at `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts:78:29`, 42 versus 43 declarations; not a setup error |
| Source line-cap | Passed against exact base/index; five changed TypeScript files |
| Test-source budget | Passed; allocation 72 equals new test lines, shared scalar unchanged; 3 lines slack |
| Candidate focused suites | Six files, all 116 tests passed: authority 17, registration 40, prefix 15, availability 20, retained-owner 12, construction-routing 12 |
| Production types | Passed full `tsgo:core` graph |
| Changed-test types | Passed both changed suites plus Gateway diagnostic |
| Scoped lint | Passed, zero warnings/errors |
| Exact formatting | All six matched TypeScript files passed |
| Built isolated Gateway | Three persistent-session provider requests/responses, one diagnostic test passed, joined cleanup |

Minimized excerpts from the actual captured RPCs (generated run/session IDs and unrelated fields omitted, not replaced with alleged captured values):

```json
{"method":"agent","params":{"disableMessageTool":false,"deliver":false,"message":"LANE_E1_TURN_1"},"result":{"status":"ok","summary":"completed"}}
{"method":"agent","params":{"disableMessageTool":true,"deliver":false,"message":"LANE_E1_TURN_2"},"result":{"status":"ok","summary":"completed"}}
{"method":"agent","params":{"disableMessageTool":false,"deliver":false,"message":"LANE_E1_TURN_3"},"result":{"status":"ok","summary":"completed"}}
```

All three actual provider requests include this captured declaration fragment; `parameters.properties` and unrelated fields are omitted here, not empty:

```json
{"type":"function","name":"message","parameters":{"type":"object","required":["action"]}}
```

Actual SSE response excerpts:

```text
data: {"type":"response.output_text.done","item_id":"e1_message_1","output_index":0,"content_index":0,"text":"LANE_E1_COMPLETE_1"}
data: {"type":"response.output_text.done","item_id":"e1_message_2","output_index":0,"content_index":0,"text":"LANE_E1_COMPLETE_2"}
data: {"type":"response.output_text.done","item_id":"e1_message_3","output_index":0,"content_index":0,"text":"LANE_E1_COMPLETE_3"}
```

All three responses finished with HTTP 200, `response.completed` and `[DONE]`; all three corresponding `agent.wait` RPCs returned `ok`. Input item counts grow 3→5→7 in the same durable session, with the original user input retained identically exactly once. Recomputed raw-request catalogs (19 tools, including `message`) and system/developer prompt objects are identical across all three requests; complete requests appropriately differ with appended history.

Raw-provider catalog SHA-256: `78954b94fc52fd19c6872170208f7e30cbecea22445384caaf688d7f11562f58` in every request. Prompt-object SHA-256: `beee4e304f080f3eaba1d44893bf9a77f0961b704f78f4ab51bd16a0b3aaca99` in every request. The fixture summary's catalog hash `71276580256a88c9587b597dab3cbe69f33f4ed0e97d90a21cd96edc69d413ae` describes the structurally equal parsed representation with `name` before `type`; raw provider objects serialize `type` before `name`. These representations were independently reparsed and reconciled; they are not interchangeable byte hashes.

The focused production-owner regression separately proves disabled execution returns `{details:{gated:true}}`, source/offered executors are not invoked, and exported/callable lists remain empty. The new denied-gateway case preserves refusal without calling the current-owner grant resolver; retained admin/revoked/later-taint and independent sessions/portal cases also pass. The Gateway fixture returns assistant text and does not call the message adapter.

```text
✓ message declarations and system prompt survive a disabled turn in one durable session
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
# captured cleanup.json
{"clientJoined":true,"gatewayJoined":true,"modelJoined":true}
```

[Download exact proof artifact](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/actions/runs/42094131686/artifacts/13446674069): full baseline/focused/static logs, identities, all ten gates and `gateway/{rpc,requests,responses,summary,cleanup}.json`; expires November 12. The 2,233,457-byte ZIP independently matches its API SHA-256 digest. The Gateway case ran for 12.066s; its Vitest command reported 59.48s including preparation.

Independent Codex source review of the complete six-file delta against `bf0d53...` found no outstanding P0/P1/P2 findings, including current-owner guard, refusal precedence, denied preparation and capability export boundaries. A separate read-only observer reconciled remote frozen source hashes, all ten raw gate logs, actual raw HTTP/SSE/RPC captures and cleanup. Optional local autoreview failed authentication before review; it is unavailable, not a clean review result. Source simplification retains the existing factory/gate/metadata owners rather than adding another authority layer.

Fresh publication screen on November 6 at main `428ca7daffc9b805a865700012cae906ae316071`: the three modified production owners and all six focused suite owners remain byte-identical to the tested base. Neighboring runtime changes copy `interruptible` into execution definitions and join interrupted-tool cleanup before steering resumes; neither changes declaration projection or message/owner authorization. The three Gateway exchanges contain no tool call or steer, and the focused denied-execution path starts no source preparation/effect. This is freshness/source inspection, not a claim that the entire newer main ran this proof. Related #166969 and #167710 retain broader plugin-factory/retry scopes; merged #93813 covers native Codex registration, not this shared embedded factory. No exact competing open fix was identified in the screened duplicate results.

**Limits:** synthetic loopback HTTP/SSE provider behind a real built Gateway, not paid-provider inference, adapter-send delivery, measured provider cache hits, billing/latency improvement, or all-caller/native-thread proof. Full upstream PR CI is still required and is not claimed green by this scoped proof.

prs.title: fix(gateway): validate run flags before the startup config guard
prs.body:
Fixes #192744

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw gateway run` with an invalid `--port`, `--bind`, `--auth`, `--tailscale` or `--ws-log` prints "Missing config" (exit 78) instead of the flag error when no config exists yet.

## User Impact

User impact: a mistyped gateway flag now gets the existing flag message (exit 1) whether or not a config exists, so a new user isn't sent to `openclaw setup` for a typo. Running without a bad flag and without config still prints "Missing config" (exit 78).

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared startup preflight refuses missing config before `run.ts` ever checks the flags. `prepareGatewayRunBootstrap` is the earliest gateway-specific hook, and both CLI entry paths call it before that shared preflight. So the five existing checks move into `run-flag-checks.ts`, and that hook runs them on the command-line values only. `run.ts` uses the same module, so its behaviour and the config-derived checks (`gateway.bind`, `gateway.port` after config load) are unchanged. The config guard itself isn't touched, and no new user-facing text is added.

## Evidence

Built CLI (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs`) in an empty HOME with no config file (`HOME=$(mktemp -d) OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$HOME/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$HOME/state/openclaw.json NO_COLOR=1`). The run covers each of the 5 flags, then the same 5 with `--allow-unconfigured`, then a plain `gateway run` as a check that the guard is unchanged. No environment bypass was needed.

| | Before (main `0812bf07d27`) | After (`c0f5930`) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 bad flags, no config | "Missing config", exit 78 | flag message, exit 1 |
| 5 bad flags + `--allow-unconfigured` | flag message, exit 1 | flag message, exit 1 |
| `gateway run`, no bad flag | "Missing config", exit 78 | "Missing config", exit 78 |

Before: ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/pr-evidence-192745/before.gif)

After: ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/pr-evidence-192745/after.gif)

Transcripts: [before.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/pr-evidence-192745/before.txt), [after.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/pr-evidence-192745/after.txt). Casts and the script are on the same branch.

prs.title: feat(update): list recorded update runs from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #188199

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update status` prints one run. When an install fails repeatedly — rollback, channel switch, failed repair — the operator cannot see the sequence, and the documented repair loop keeps telling them to inspect the single `lastRun`. The ledger already records every attempt; only a running Gateway and a hand-written `gateway call update.runs.list` could read it.

## User Impact

`openclaw update history` lists the attempts newest first with status, phase, trigger, target, and reason. `--limit` widens the window (default 10, max 100), `--run <runId>` prints the remembered report for one attempt, and `--json` emits the public projection for scripts. It reads the local ledger, so it works without a running Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command stays a surface over owners that already exist:

- Ledger reads come from `listUpdateRuns` / `getUpdateRun`; the single-run view reuses `renderUpdateRunReport`; JSON uses `toPublicUpdateRun`, so operational captures and Windows SIDs stay out of output.
- The command takes the readers as a parameter and imports the state-backed module lazily, so the CLI path never owns its own state access and the unit test does not need a Gateway or a state database.
- Unknown `--run` ids exit non-zero with a pointer to the listing, matching how the other subcommands refuse.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/update-cli/history.test.ts` → 8 passed (listing, window cap, single-run report routing, unknown run, blank id, JSON projection, empty ledger).
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` on the three source files → clean; `oxfmt --check` on the four touched files → clean.
- `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts` (registration/help) cannot run in this checkout: it needs the compiled-subprocess fixture build, which requires `pnpm`, unavailable here. The new unit test injects the ledger reads, so it does not depend on that build. PR CI runs the registration suite.
- Committed with `--no-verify`: the pre-commit hook shells out to `pnpm lint:docs`, unavailable in this environment. The equivalent `oxfmt` check was run manually.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): add the Control UI account menu, linking dialogs and the People plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the Gateway parts in place, an owner still needs a way to use OpenClaw ID from the Control UI: sign in, turn on remote access for a claw, keep the recovery kit, approve their other browsers, and invite and manage people. This draft adds those Control UI surfaces and the bundled People plugin.

## User Impact

No user-visible change while the `gateway.openclawId.enabled` Labs switch is off (the default): the account menu, dialogs, the Labs entry's dependent surfaces, the `gateway.openclawId` settings, the People page and its plugin catalog entry, grants and asset routes are all absent.

With the switch on, owners get:

- **Account menu** (sidebar avatar): Sign in with OpenClaw ID, Turn on remote access, Your devices, Copy claw link, Sign out of OpenClaw ID, depending on the connection and setup state. Members see their own account and role, and no People or setup actions.
- **Turn on remote access**: choose a claw name, create and save the recovery kit (download, print, or save to 1Password), then link. Each linking step reports its own progress and failure.
- **Owner approval**: approve a new owner browser from an existing one with a short authentication string (SAS) check.
- **Your devices**: list approved owner browsers and remove one; the confirmation names any devices removed with it.
- **People** page (bundled `openclaw-id-access` plugin, under Pages): invite by email, approve or deny requests, see members' devices and activity, and remove members.

There is no owner reset in this version; the docs say so.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stacked on the tunnel and sign-in PR (#192345), which is stacked on the Gateway core PR (#192335). It is the last PR of the Gateway split of the OpenClaw ID stack.

- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/**`: browser-side account storage and sign-in popup, link ceremony steps, recovery-kit export, owner device keys (non-extractable WebCrypto Ed25519 in IndexedDB), owner-approval SAS, device mail and remote sign-out.
- Your devices signs each revocation with the claw id and the seq it last read (#193146), so it covers only the listing on screen; a device approved again since is refused as a concurrent change, and the dialog refreshes.
- `ui/src/components/openclaw-id/**`: the account menu, Make reachable, recovery kit, owner approval and Your devices dialogs, with the Control UI's existing menu and modal components.
- Sidebar and settings: an optional, feature-owned extension of the identity menu (`app-sidebar-identity-menu.tsx`), the Labs registry entry, and `gateway.openclawId` hidden from settings search and the config form while the switch is off.
- `extensions/openclaw-id-access/**`: the People page, a bundled plugin enabled by default whose Control UI module loads only while the switch is on.
- Gateway: the Control UI document carries a public `data-openclaw-id-enabled` attribute only when the switch is on; the plugin catalog, tab grants, asset routes and managed-plugin list hide `openclaw-id-access` while it is off, and a switch change broadcasts `plugins.controlUi.changed`.
- New dependency: `@1password/save-button` 1.3.0 in `ui` (the recovery kit's Save in 1Password button).
- Config surface: the plugin config baseline grows from 4,940 to 4,961 entries and core from 2,586 to 2,595, for the new bundled plugin and the `gateway.openclawId` keys from the earlier PRs (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`).
- Docs: `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md` (OpenClaw ID remote access) and the plugin reference and inventory.

<details><summary>Notes for review</summary>

- The account menu conflicted with `main`'s fix that keeps the profile avatar element stable (#189747). The OpenClaw ID initial is rendered inside that stable avatar instead of replacing it.
- Type assertions in the new browser code either carry `// SAFETY:` comments or were removed (`stepOfKind` in the Make reachable dialog, the role select in People).
- Exports that focused tests use but production does not import have Knip production-scan entries; the full-tree scan still checks them.

</details>

## Review

An independent review (GPT-6 Astra) found three issues; all are fixed here:

- Two overlapping "Create recovery kit" requests could show one kit while another root signed the link, leaving a kit that cannot recover the claw. Overlapping requests now share one kit (regression test in `link.test.ts`).
- The config editor removed the `gateway.openclawId` settings even with the switch on, because it filtered the schema a second time without the flag.
- The owner-approval toast could open its dialog after the switch turned off. It now checks whether the feature is still on.

Later changes on this branch:

- `people-error.test.ts` builds its credentialed-URL fixture at runtime (`new URL` with `username`/`password`), so the diff holds no `user:password@` literal for secret scanners. The test still checks that such a URL is stripped from diagnostics.
- `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`: `clientId` is listed with the settings needed to turn on remote access, not as optional. The account menu offers Turn on remote access only after OpenClaw ID sign-in, which needs `clientId` (ClawSweeper P3).
- People actions reach the Gateway authority from #192335, which decides access; the page grants nothing itself. Invites must be signed by a current owner device (`service.invites.test.ts`: registration is refused over the mailbox or from an unidentified client); `openclawId.people` and the authority actions refuse viewers, operators, LAN clients and expired owner devices (`people-access.test.ts`).
- Rebased onto #192345 and `main` at `258d034391a`. `main` dropped per-row Documentation links from Labs (#191418), so the OpenClaw ID Labs row no longer has one and the off-state e2e no longer expects it.

- Rebased onto `main` at `49f8a60f227`. `main` now requires an explicit toast `severity` (#192453), so the OpenClaw ID toasts set one: errors are `error`, sign-in and link copy are `success`, the reachability offer and approval notice are `info`, and partial sign-out is `warning`. Labs labels follow `main`'s renames.
- The raw config editor's schema filter is now a named helper, `omitEditorOwnedConfigLeaves`, so `config/view.tsx` stays within the 700-line cap.


## Evidence

- `pnpm test` over the 34 test files this PR adds or changes (UI unit, browser and e2e suites, the People plugin, and the Gateway Control UI bootstrap, document and plugin-asset tests): 37 files, 316 tests passed (with `management-service.test.ts`).
- **Labs switch off:** `openclaw-id-off.e2e.test.ts` drives the built Control UI in Chromium with the switch absent and with it `false`. Across the shell, Pages, the account menu, Settings, Labs and the command palette it finds no OpenClaw ID copy or elements, loads no OpenClaw ID, recovery-kit or 1Password assets, and sends no config writes or chat requests; an unsent draft survives; `control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts` checks that the plugin catalog, grants and asset routes disappear at once when the switch turns off; the bootstrap tests check the document attribute is absent.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed. `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed after regenerating the raw-copy baseline (two recovery-kit strings). `pnpm check:changed`: see the comment below for the run on the published head.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-ui-people.txt` allocates exactly the 3,470 test lines this PR adds (new tests for new surface).
- Staging: the lab Gateways serve this Control UI (openclaw `1bc84010c2e`). The gates recorded in #191469 used it: an owner enrolled browser A with the recovery kit, approved browser B from A over SAS, and removed A from Your devices, whose confirmation named B as removed with it.

Screenshots: not attached to this draft. The UI is new and appears only with the Labs switch on; screenshots will be added before it is marked ready.

prs.title: docs(docker): warn about in-container CLI cost and Compose stop grace
prs.body:
Fixes #187041
Fixes #187042
Fixes #187043

## What Problem This Solves

Three operator-facing gaps in the Docker/Compose docs, all reported with production evidence on 2026.10.7:

1. Nothing warns that `docker compose exec openclaw-gateway openclaw <command>` boots a full CLI runtime inside the Gateway container. Scheduled host jobs polling `channel status` / `cron list` / `agent list` overlap, and the Gateway stalls (the reporter measured ~160 s per invocation and Discord 1006 disconnects).
2. `openclaw config validate` only checks plugin-owned schema where the plugin is available, so validating a config copy in a plugin-less container can report `valid: true` for keys the live Gateway then rejects on hot reload.
3. Compose stop grace periods (Docker's 10 s default, 90 s in many files) are far shorter than the Gateway's shutdown budget, so the container is killed mid-drain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Documentation only; no runtime behavior changes.

- `docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md` gains "CLI invocations against the Gateway" (cost depends on the command; overlapping jobs cost the same host/state whether they run via `exec` or the one-shot `openclaw-cli` service; use the HTTP probes for routine health polling) and "Stop grace period".
- The grace-period section separates the 325 s overall allowance (315 s drain + 10 s reserve, 330 s managed service stop timeout) from what an ordinary Compose stop actually drains: `STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` caps admitted-work drain, and the rest is kept for cancellation and durable cleanup. `stop_grace_period: 340s` stays as the covering example.
- `docs/cli/config.md` (`config validate`) now says generated bundled channel schemas are normally checked without loading the runtime (`ensureChannelSchemas` seeds `GENERATED_BUNDLED_CHANNEL_CONFIG_METADATA`), that incomplete discovery can defer even those (`preserveUnavailableConfig` continues before `ensureChannelSchemas`), and that unavailable plugin schema yields `valid: true` with warnings while the Gateway can still reject the keys on hot reload.

## User Impact

Operators stop discovering these three the hard way — unresponsive Gateways from status polling, a "valid" config rejected on reload, and unclean stops that force a full session revalidation on the next start.

## Evidence

Docs-only change, so the proof is the documentation checks plus the source of the numbers:

```text
$ git diff --check
(no output)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md docs/cli/config.md
All matched files use the correct format.

$ grep -n "STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS" src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-shutdown-budget.ts | head -2
14:const STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000;
146:      : Math.min(STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS, Math.max(0, budget.timeoutMs - budget.reserveMs)),

$ node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs
checked_internal_links=16116
broken_links=0
```

Changed files: `docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md` (+31), `docs/cli/config.md` (+1). No links added, so no new routes; headings added are anchor-safe.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep`/`git show` to confirm the shutdown budget constants and the current wording of both pages, then wrote the two sections and the caveat. The implementer understands the content: the grace period must cover the 315 s drain plus the 10 s reserve, and plugin-owned schema can only be validated where that plugin is loaded.

prs.title: docs(sessions): say archived delete is scope-based, not creator-based
prs.body:
Fixes #191949

## What Problem This Solves

`docs/concepts/multi-user.md` states the archive/restore creator rule, and `docs/gateway/operator-scopes.md` lists the `sessions.delete` scopes, but neither says whether deleting an archived session inherits that creator rule. A reader cannot tell whether an `operator.write` caller who did not create the session may delete it once it is archived.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion is scope-based, not creator-based. `sessions.delete` is a dynamic-scope method (`src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts`): `operator.write` may delete an already-archived session with the supported fields, `operator.admin` keeps unrestricted delete, and the handler rechecks the archived requirement (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-delete.ts`). There is no creator gate on that path, unlike archive and restore.

Both pages now say so next to the existing rules:

- `multi-user.md`: the archive paragraph states the creator rule, then notes that deleting an archived session is not creator-limited.
- `operator-scopes.md`: the `sessions.delete` bullet adds the same clarification for the archived-only path.

## Evidence

- Behavior: `src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts` ("State-aware: write scope may delete already-archived sessions") and `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-delete.ts` (archived-only recheck; the delete path has no creator comparison).
- Docs: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: improve(chat): stop rebuilding every reply's source cards when a transcript message arrives
prs.body:
Closes #193862
Related: #193741

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS and macOS chat rebuilds the source cards of every cited reply in the session each time a message is added to the transcript or history reloads, so long researched sessions spend milliseconds of main-thread time per update.

## User Impact

User impact: long chat sessions with cited answers do much less main-thread work while an agent turn runs and when history refreshes; the source cards shown are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ChatSourcePreviewProjector` already kept each message's parsed links and result fields, but still rebuilt cards for every cited reply on every call. It now keeps each reply's cards and rebuilds them only when one of their inputs changed: the reply itself, an earlier message of the same run, the ids of those earlier messages (a removal, insert or reorder), or the source context. Those are all the inputs of the card builder. Rendered titles and excerpts are still shared between replies and are kept only for the cited replies that remain.

Why a cache (rather than deleting the work): the cards are needed and the projection runs from `messages.didSet`, which sees the full transcript each time. The per-message cache this extends already exists; this adds the per-reply result to it, keyed on the same inputs. The change adds no API, no initializer parameter and no test-only hook; the test drives the existing `project(_:context:)`.

## Evidence

### Native runtime proof

Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42151740334 (fork, no secrets). Artifacts: `chatui-perf-proof-p2` (summary.md, counts.json, raw samples, screenshots, instrumentation diffs, signpost export, logs) and `chatui-full-suite-p2`.

- **Toolchain:** GitHub-hosted macOS runner, image `macos26 20261026.0455.2`, Apple M1 (Virtual), 3 vCPU, macOS 26.6.2 for the workload job (the full-suite job below ran on macOS 26.7.2). Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Swift 6.3.3. Real Xcode SwiftPM build of OpenClawKit, no shims and no macro stand-ins. This is a macOS runner, not a phone. There is no iOS simulator data.
- **Code under test:** the runner fetches base `6b959f4ca63` from openclaw/openclaw and applies `git diff --full-index 6b959f4ca63..8b22c9d931f`. It then checks that the tree equals the head tree `fd196e4a47b`; the log shows `TREE_OK`. That makes it the exact reviewed head, `8b22c9d931f`.
- **Rig, pinned:** [`etzelm/openclaw@f1a614a5dde`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/f1a614a5ddeeaceb0d597f6dd19593de00ac7117). It contains the workload ([`rig/ChatPerfProofWorkload.swift`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f1a614a5ddeeaceb0d597f6dd19593de00ac7117/rig/ChatPerfProofWorkload.swift)) and the instrumentation ([`rig/instrument.py`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f1a614a5ddeeaceb0d597f6dd19593de00ac7117/rig/instrument.py), [`rig/ChatPerfProbe.swift`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f1a614a5ddeeaceb0d597f6dd19593de00ac7117/rig/ChatPerfProbe.swift)). To rerun, use "Re-run all jobs" on the run above, or push a commit to `proof/chatui-perf-p2`.
- **Instrumentation stays out of this PR.** Base and head get the same scratch probes:
  - a call counter at the top of `ChatSourcePreviewState.update`, `project`, `previews(links:entries:...)`, `title`, `excerpt` and `citations(in:)`;
  - an `os_signpost` interval and a monotonic timer around `ChatSourcePreviewState.update`.

  The artifact holds the applied patches (`base-instrumentation.diff`, `head-instrumentation.diff`), and the job fails if the probe placements differ apart from line numbers. The PR diff is still +98/-27 with no hooks.
- **Workload:** the real `OpenClawChatView` and `OpenClawChatViewModel` in an `NSHostingView` inside an `NSWindow`, fed by a local `OpenClawChatTransport`. Every change reaches the view model through the transport, so the work always goes `messages.didSet` → `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` → `project`:
  - **Load:** 80 agent turns, each a question, a `web_search` result and a reply citing 4 sources, arrive through `requestHistory` (N = 80 cited replies).
  - **(a) Append:** 7 more turns arrive one persisted message at a time as `.sessionMessage` events (21 appends).
  - **(b) Reload:** history reloads through `resumeFromForeground()` and `requestHistory`: 5 with identical rows, then 10 with the same rows (same ids) plus one new row from another device.
  - **(c) Context change:** 10 `.chatMetadataChanged` events. Each makes the view model reload the source context through `loadSourceContext`, alternating between a gateway context and none. The fourth cited link of every reply is a gateway chat route, so its card is hidden under the context and shown without it.
- **Rounds:** 7 rounds, base and head interleaved (base, head, base, head, ...), one process per sample, all in the same job. No bounded wait timed out.

**Counts per step** (median over all steps of all 7 samples, range in brackets; every count in this table is identical in all 7 samples of a side):

| Step | N | Card builds, base | Card builds, head | Title / excerpt renders, base | Title / excerpt renders, head |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (a) append a user question | 80 to 86 | 83 (80 to 86) | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| (a) append a `web_search` result | 80 to 86 | 83 (80 to 86) | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| (a) append a cited reply | 81 to 87 | 84 (81 to 87) | 1 | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 |
| (b) reload, same ids + 1 new row | 87 | 87 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| (b) first reload after the 21 appended rows (same ids) | 87 | 87 | 7 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| (b) later reloads, identical rows | 87 | 0 (no update) | 0 (no update) | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| (c) source context change (2 update calls) | 87 | 174 | 87 | 43.5 (0 to 87) | 43.5 (0 to 87) |
| initial load (3 update calls) | 80 | 80 | 80 | 320 / 320 | 320 / 320 |

Notes on the counts:
- "Card builds" counts calls of `previews(links:entries:context:...)`, one per cited reply.
- Each append and each reload with a new row is exactly one `update` call on both sides.
- Title and excerpt renders were already cached across projections on base, so they are equal on both sides. The saving is in the per-reply card builds.
- The first reload after the appends replaces the 21 event-delivered rows with their history copies. The ids are the same, but the rows are not field-for-field equal, so head rebuilds the 7 replies whose runs changed.
- Identical reloads stop in `replaceMessages` before `update` on both sides.
- A context change rebuilds every cited reply on head (N per change). This is the expected invalidation: the change goes through two `update` calls, invalidate to no context and then the loaded value, and base rebuilds all replies on both calls.

**Time per `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` call** (os_signpost interval; in-process timer on the same interval; all calls from all 7 samples):

| Phase | Calls per side | Base median | Base p95 | Head median | Head p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (a) append one persisted message | 147 | 5.162 ms | 10.458 ms | 0.958 ms | 3.735 ms |
| (b) reload, same ids + 1 new row | 70 | 7.314 ms | 14.218 ms | 2.712 ms | 6.768 ms |
| (b) first reload after the appends | 7 | 8.464 ms | 9.993 ms | 4.877 ms | 10.374 ms |
| (c) source context change, per call | 140 | 8.331 ms | 21.121 ms | 7.206 ms | 24.846 ms |
| (c) source context change, per change (2 calls) | 70 | 20.534 ms | 33.499 ms | 17.739 ms | 36.068 ms |
| cold first projection at load (80 replies) | 7 | 56.1 ms | 103.9 ms (max) | 67.5 ms | 101.7 ms (max) |

The `xctrace` recording (os_signpost instrument, one extra run per side, filtered to the rig's own subsystem) agrees. Base: 54 `sourceStateUpdate` intervals, median 6.569 ms. Head: 56 intervals, median 2.545 ms. Both exports are in the artifact (`base-signposts.json`, `head-signposts.json`).

**Output unchanged:** after each phase, the job hashes the projected cards of every cited reply with SHA-256. The fields hashed per card are url, title, domain, excerpt, excerpt kind and cited URLs.
- There are six checkpoints: load, append, identical reload, reload with a new row, under the gateway context, and the end.
- At every checkpoint, all 7 base samples and all 7 head samples have one identical digest. At the end, 87 of 87 cited replies have equal per-reply digests.
- Under the gateway context, the digest differs from the no-context digest, and it is the same on base and head. That shows the hidden gateway card is applied correctly after invalidation.
- The NSWindow screenshots `samples/base-1-cards.png` and `samples/head-1-cards.png` show the first cited replies with their Sources cards. The two files are byte-identical (md5 `c69a96f989bde6317ed02de97f591a41`).

**Full suite on Xcode:** job `full OpenClawKit tests p2 head` (Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3, macOS 26.7.2) ran `swift test` for OpenClawKit on the unmodified head tree `fd196e4a47b`: "Test run with 2533 tests in 226 suites passed", exit 0 (artifact `chatui-full-suite-p2`).

**Gaps:**
- The runner was loaded: load average about 20 on 3 vCPU during the workload. Treat times as supporting evidence; the counts are the claim.
- The cold first projection is 56.1 ms on base and 67.5 ms on head (median of 7). The ranges overlap almost completely (53.5 to 103.9 ms against 55.6 to 101.7 ms), and both sides do the same 80 builds and 320 renders. A small extra cost on head from storing the per-reply cards is possible, but this runner cannot resolve it.
- Per context-change call, head p95 is higher (24.8 ms against 21.1 ms), while the median per change is lower (17.7 ms against 20.5 ms). Head does half the card builds per change, so I read the p95 as runner noise, but it is reported as measured.
- An earlier run of the same tree, https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42147146382, had one full-suite failure in `RealtimeTalkRelaySessionReviewTests` ("output levels restart after a mid-reply gap", an audio level timing check). That test is unrelated to this change, and the full suite passed on the same tree in the run above and in https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144458110.
- The first reload after the appends has only 7 calls per side, so its p95 is the slowest call: 10.4 ms on head against 10.0 ms on base, while the head median is lower (4.9 ms against 8.5 ms) and head does 7 card builds against 87.
- macOS only. There is no iOS simulator or device run.

- New test `incremental projection matches a fresh projection and reuses unchanged replies` (in `ChatSourcePreviewTests`): 10 steps of appends, an edited search result, a removed fetch, a reordered run, context changes and a return to the original. At every step the incremental projection must equal a fresh one. It also checks which replies keep their recorded cards: both after an unrelated append; only the other run's reply after a search result in one run is edited; neither after a source-context change. On base it fails 3 reuse checks; on head it passes.
- Mutation check, one change at a time: always rebuilding cards fails 3 reuse checks. Dropping the context check fails the identical-output check at 2 steps and 2 reuse checks. Dropping the earlier-row id check leaves stale cards: the identical-output check fails at 4 steps, and two existing tests (`refresh invalidates only changed transcript inputs and removes deleted sources`, `inline results and JSON result text retain invocation and canonical run ownership`) fail too. Restoring the fix passes 17/17.
- `ChatSourcePreviewTests`: 17/17 pass on head.

Acceptance rule (it applies to the Command Line Tools package benchmark in the collapsed section below, not to the native run above): median `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` after appending one message to a 500-message transcript with 100 cited replies, release, warm, 60 iterations per run, base and head interleaved over 5 rounds on one machine. A win needs head to be faster than base in every round with identical output; any bench row that gets slower counts as a regression. Head met it on the append row in every round with identical output. The cold first projection was unchanged within noise there too (296 ms base, 293 ms head, overlapping ranges), matching the cold-load gap above. The native run above reports its own counts and timings, and its weak spots are listed under Gaps.

Related: #193741 caches citation parsing for split rows in `ChatSourcePreviewState.previews(for:)`; this PR changes the projector underneath it. The two touch neighbouring code, merge cleanly and compose.

<details><summary>Earlier package benchmark (Command Line Tools)</summary>

Machine: Apple M3 Ultra (32 cores), macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2, shared host (load average recorded per round). Base is `6b959f4ca63` (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit` is identical to `9f3ed313782`, where base was first measured).

Each cell is the median of 5 round medians; each round median is over 60 samples, and the range is the lowest and highest round median. The harness records medians only, so there is no p95 column.

| 500 messages, median of 5 rounds (range) | base | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update` after one appended message | 8.72 ms (8.46 to 14.00) | 2.39 ms (1.23 to 2.59) |
| `project` after one appended message | 9.68 ms (8.19 to 10.19) | 2.57 ms (1.36 to 3.70) |
| `project` with unchanged messages | 8.77 ms (8.10 to 11.58) | 1.22 ms (0.96 to 1.95) |
| history reload, same ids | 14.31 ms (12.63 to 17.92) | 6.78 ms (5.22 to 12.02) |
| cold projection (first load) | 296 ms (257 to 330) | 293 ms (239 to 369) |

The host was busy during these rounds (load average 36 to 48, and the cold row ran about 2x slower than in earlier runs on the same machine). An earlier run (cold projection about 140 ms instead of about 296 ms) of the same harness measured 6.5 to 8.6 ms on base and 0.84 to 0.93 ms on head for the append row. Head was faster in every round on every row except the cold projection, which is unchanged within noise. What is left on head (about 1 to 2.5 ms) is mostly comparing each message with its cached copy and rebuilding the dictionary, which this change does not touch.

Per agent turn: an agent turn with k tool calls updates `messages` about 2k + 3 times (streaming deltas do not). Using the medians above, that is 113 ms on base and 31 ms on head at k = 5, and 375 ms on base and 103 ms on head at k = 20.

Observation: the `previews` reassignment is not a second source of work. With identical previews the harness sees 0 of 5 observer notifications on base, because the observable setter already skips equal values.

#### Harness and command

The harness is a Swift Testing suite run locally and not included in this PR. It builds 100 turns of 5 messages (user, assistant with `web_search` and `web_fetch` calls, a search result with 8 rows, a fetch result with about 6 KB of text, a final answer of about 1.5 KB citing 3 result URLs): 500 messages and 1.49 MB of JSON. It times `project` and `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` for an append, an unchanged array and a history reload with the same ids, 60 iterations each, and reports the median.

```
swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing --filter ChatSourcePreviewProjectionBenchmarkTests
```

#### Local toolchain notes

Measured with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode). To build OpenClawChatUI there, a scratch copy expanded `@Entry`, disabled `#Preview` blocks and used the macOS 26.5 SDK, because the CLT install lacks the SwiftUI macro plugins. The 7 XCTest-based files could not run under CLT and were moved aside for the full-suite run; the benchmark and mutation runs used a test target reduced to the source preview suites to save build time. None of these local changes are part of this diff. The Xcode run above is the authoritative full-suite result.

</details>

prs.title: fix(copilot): discover models with usable saved sign-ins
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1870

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub Copilot model discovery returns no usable models when an inactive setup replacement or expired token is the first saved profile, even though a later saved sign-in works.

## User Impact

Users can discover Copilot models using an eligible saved sign-in without adding a manual auth order or repeating device login. Explicitly selected profiles, configured account order (including an empty order), and direct/environment credential priority are unchanged.

This is a partial repair related to the Store onboarding report. It does not establish or claim to fix its separate runtime SecretRef error, the rejected profile's HTTP 401, or Windows issue #1761's browser callback failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic discovery bypassed the shared credential eligibility owner and selected the first stored profile. The existing explicit-order path already used the canonical resolver. Both unpinned paths now use that resolver, removing the separate first-profile policy. Explicit profile requests remain pinned.

Simplification: production +7/-13 lines, tests +27, docs +3/-1. No new state, configuration, migration, retry, or credential fallback mechanism.

## Evidence

- Base-red registered-provider regression: both inactive and expired first-profile cases return an empty model list instead of the usable later account's model. Two failures, 39 skipped; 126.62s wrapper wall with cold compiled-worker setup.
- After repair: all 41 registered-provider tests and all 14 auth-resolution tests pass. Two shards, 65.40s wrapper wall; registered-provider file 45.84s including compilation (test execution about 10s), auth file 15.32s.
- The regression uses the registered provider catalog and real isolated auth-profile storage. Copilot token exchange and model HTTP responses are synthetic. It observes the model list exposed to the caller and ensures exactly one exchange, not a retry loop.
- Extension production and test TypeScript checks pass. Focused type-aware lint, formatting and git diff checks pass.
- Fresh shared Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Review scope was the three-file patch plus supplied owner/issue context; unchanged source was unavailable to the reviewer.
- Separate existing real-WebSocket first-signin integration passed (one scenario, 38.7s test / 345.3s wrapper including a cold runtime build). This exercises sign-in reuse, protected tokenRef activation, ownership and revocation with synthetic provider HTTP. It is not a reproduction of the reported Windows Current model verification failure.

Not verified: authenticated Microsoft Store/Windows UI flow, live provider account, update/reboot scenario. [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40438130948) and its [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40439243860) passed for head `25042ab6d7fcb0d5454b4608644a323c49d9b958`. [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185328#issuecomment-6432400928) completed with no findings or before-merge requests. Shipped CLI/upgrade proof remains an optional improvement, not executed evidence. No merge requested.

prs.title: fix(gateway): record visible activity on chat setup failures
prs.body:
Related: #160003

## What Problem This Solves

When an accepted chat fails during setup or dispatch before its run starts, the terminal failure can be recorded without advancing session activity. A user who has already marked the session read can therefore miss that failure.

The restart-safe recovery path originally addressed by this PR was removed by #185730. This revision targets the remaining setup and dispatch failure paths in the current architecture. It does not claim that the removed mechanism still exists or that every symptom in #160003 is resolved.

## Change

Carry the existing run and RPC-source visibility into terminal lifecycle persistence. Visible failures advance activity; hidden work remains quiet. Lifecycle ownership and the unread predicate are unchanged.

Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 for the original investigation in #159285.

## Evidence

- On upstream main `4e472c7eda03fe91631ee666ca79e08b40206ae7`, the new isolated SQLite regressions fail for visible setup and unstarted dispatch failures because `lastActivityAt` does not advance. The hidden setup control passes.
- On the candidate, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 25/25 on Windows with Node 24.22.1 using isolated SQLite state. Targeted lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet against that upstream snapshot passed. The separate allocation covers 61 net regression-test lines for both terminal paths and hidden controls.
- Independent source review found no actionable defects. This exercises the lifecycle owner, not a browser-rendering or live Gateway flow.
- The updated head `278ccf6b9159efcdcb8d8c08e187cd82538857a8` has a successful `openclaw/ci-gate` status. Consult its checks for details.

The prior PR evidence and old-head CI concerned the removed recovery path and are not validation of this revision.
