prs.title: improve(chat): stop re-parsing split transcript rows for citations on every render
prs.body:
Closes #193740
Related: #193863

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS and macOS chat re-parses the Markdown of every visible assistant row that is split around tool work, each time the transcript re-renders, even when the row has no source cards.

## User Impact

User impact: transcripts with agent runs and researched answers spend far less main-thread time per render; source cards shown on split rows are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ChatSourcePreviewState.previews(for:)` now returns early when the message has no source previews, since the result is always empty there. For messages that do have previews, it keeps each split row's citation links keyed by the row's presentation identity and reuses them while the row's role, content, and footer error text (stop reason, error message, footer ownership) are unchanged. Those are all the inputs of the row's visible text. Links are checked on read rather than rebuilt in `update()` because split rows come from the narrated transcript, and `update()` runs on every streamed change.

Tradeoff: the cache holds each carded row's content array (shared with the message, copy-on-write) and its links, so memory is bounded by the carded rows that were rendered. `update()` drops entries whose message no longer has previews.

## Evidence

### Native runtime proof

Real Xcode build of the shared chat view, base and head measured in the same GitHub Actions job on a fork. The run had no secrets.

- **Run:** https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42149331096
  - Workload job: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42149331096/job/127668433432
  - Full-suite job: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42149331096/job/127668433689
- **Artifacts:** `chatui-perf-proof-p1` and `chatui-full-suite-p1`. The first holds:
  - `summary.md` and `counts.json`
  - per-sample JSON and per-row card dumps (`samples/*-rows.txt`)
  - screenshots
  - `base-instrumentation.diff` / `head-instrumentation.diff`
  - `base-timeprofile.json` / `head-timeprofile.json`
  - build and test logs
- **Scripts:** fork branch `proof/chatui-perf-p1` at `1f26789ad96` (`rig/`). None of it is part of this PR.
- **Toolchain:** Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Apple Swift 6.3.3, macOS 26.6.2 on the `macos-26-arm64` hosted image 20261026.0455.2 (Apple M1 virtual, 3 cores, 7 GB). The full-suite job ran on image 20261102.0473.1 (macOS 26.7.2), same Xcode and Swift. Xcode 27 is not on the hosted image. No shims or macro stand-ins.
- **Code under test:**
  - Base is `6d7347b2da3`, fetched from openclaw/openclaw.
  - Head is base plus `git diff 6d7347b2da3..9ac44a540b9`. The job checks that the resulting tree equals the head tree `47cfac540c6` before it builds.

#### What ran

- **The view:** the shipped `OpenClawChatView` in an `NSHostingView` inside an `NSWindow` (960x1000).
  - It is configured like the macOS Quick Chat reply area, with `openClawChatDesktopLayout` on. That is the mode that folds completed work and splits an answer into presentation rows, so `presentationBlockIndex` is set.
  - Release build (`-c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing`).
- **Transcript:** history is delivered through `OpenClawChatTransport.requestHistory` from a local transport. It has 60 agent turns, with public example URLs only.
  - Each assistant message is [tool call, result, cited answer, tool call, result], so each answer renders as a split row.
  - Two transcripts: with web_search results (3 source cards per answer) and without (no cards).
- **Phases:**
  - load
  - scroll (64 positions)
  - resize (4 widths)
  - append (10 new turns via `replaceMessages`)
  - stream (24 deltas via the view model's streaming-text path)
- **Rounds:** 5 interleaved rounds in one job, odd rounds base first and even rounds head first.
- **Counting:**
  - Identical scratch counters go into base and head (the instrumentation diffs are in the artifact). One wraps the `sourcePreviews:` argument in `ChatView.messageRow`, and any call made inside it is counted as "under messageRow".
  - `Document(parsing:)` is counted in `chatPreviewURLs(in:)`, which is the only `Document(parsing:)` that `citations(in:)` reaches.

#### Calls per phase (median of 5 rounds, under `ChatView.messageRow`)

With source cards (70 split rows with cards):

| Phase | Split rows evaluated (base = head) | `previews(for:)` calls (base = head) | `citations(in:)` base -> head | `Document(parsing:)` base -> head |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| load | 180 | 180 | 180 -> 60 | 180 -> 60 |
| scroll | 170 | 170 | 170 -> 0 | 170 -> 0 |
| resize | 0 | 0 | 0 -> 0 | 0 -> 0 |
| append | 665 | 665 | 665 -> 10 | 665 -> 10 |
| stream | 69 | 71 | 69 -> 0 | 69 -> 0 |

Without source cards (70 split rows, none with cards):

| Phase | Split rows evaluated (base = head) | `previews(for:)` calls (base = head) | `citations(in:)` base -> head | `Document(parsing:)` base -> head |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| load | 180 | 180 | 180 -> 0 | 180 -> 0 |
| scroll | 162 | 162 | 162 -> 0 | 162 -> 0 |
| resize | 0 | 0 | 0 -> 0 | 0 -> 0 |
| append | 665 | 665 | 665 -> 0 | 665 -> 0 |
| stream | 69 | 71 | 69 -> 0 | 69 -> 0 |

**Reading the tables:**
- The view evaluates the same rows the same number of times on both sides. Only the parsing behind `previews(for:)` changes.
  - With cards, head parses once per split row text: 60 rows at load and 10 new rows on append. It does not parse again on scroll or stream.
  - Without cards, head never parses on this path.
- Head parse counts were constant across all 5 rounds. How many times SwiftUI evaluated the rows varies on both sides. For example, base load ranged from 120 to 180 and base scroll from 170 to 228 with cards.
- Resize triggered no row re-evaluation on either side.
- An earlier run of the same scripts gave exactly the same medians: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144447663

#### Time Profiler

`xctrace` (Time Profiler template) was attached to the workload process for one extra run per side, using the transcript with cards. Main-thread samples were reduced to counts of stacks that contain the changed functions. No addresses or other processes are kept (`*-timeprofile.json`).

| Main-thread samples with ... on the stack | Base | Head |
|---|---:|---:|
| any (whole run) | 7338 | 6986 |
| `OpenClawChatView.messageRow(for:...)` | 496 | 186 |
| `ChatSourcePreviewState.previews(for:)` (all under messageRow) | 328 | 30 |
| `previews(for:)` and `Document(parsing:)` | 54 | 1 |

`citations(in:)` is mostly inlined into `previews(for:)` in the release build, so its own frame is rare (10 samples on base, 0 on head). The `previews(for:)` row is the one that carries it.

#### Output unchanged

- **Row hash:** a SHA-256 over every rendered row's cards (URL, title, domain, excerpt), keyed by run id, role and presentation block index, is identical on base and head in every round.
  - With cards: `1ec9aa9d11c50df8…` (70 split rows, 3 cards each).
  - Without cards: `00a69bf98e459306…`.
  - No row's cards changed between renders within a round on either side.
- **Screenshots:** `samples/base-1-cards-latest.png` and `samples/head-1-cards-latest.png` are byte-identical. They show the "Sources" cards attached to the split answer rows for questions 58 and 59.
  - The post-scroll screenshots are byte-identical across all rounds and both sides.
  - The no-cards post-load screenshot has two variants caused by load timing, and each variant appears on both base and head.

#### Tests on the same toolchain

- Focused suites on unmodified code (`ChatSourcePreviewTests|ChatLinkPreview`): base passed 44 tests in 12 suites, head passed 45 tests in 12 suites.
- Full `swift test` for OpenClawKit on head: 2533 tests in 226 suites passed.
- New test `split row cards follow each row's visible text across repeated renders` (in `ChatSourcePreviewTests`): three renders of two split messages, one with cards and one without, then edited text before and after `update()`, then a row with the same id and content whose stop reason, error message or footer ownership changes one at a time. Each step asserts the cards, so a cache entry served for stale visible text shows up as a wrong card.

#### Limits

- This is the shared chat view hosted in a test process on a macOS runner. It is not the shipped macOS app binary, an iOS simulator or a physical iPhone.
- Xcode 26.6, not Xcode 27.
- Streaming uses the view model's streaming-text path, not transport chat events.
- One trace per side.
- The counters are scratch instrumentation, identical on both sides and not part of this PR.
- Wall-clock phase times were recorded but are not a claim. The runner is a shared 3-core VM, and whole-phase times are dominated by layout and noisy. For example, scroll with cards had a median of 5335 ms on base and 5397 ms on head. No frame or hitch metric was measured.

<details><summary>Earlier package benchmark (Command Line Tools)</summary>

Acceptance rule (set before measuring head): per-row cost of `previews(for:)` on split rows, release build, warm, 200 messages x 3 rows x 20 passes, 7 runs per variant, base and head interleaved over 3 rounds. A win needs a drop of at least 10x on both scenarios with no change in output. Any rise counts as a regression.

Machine: Apple M3 Ultra (32 cores), macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2. Base is `6d7347b2da3`. The three-round table below was measured on the previous revision of this change (`0268b2345c8`), which called the same extractor through a stored closure; the only source change since then replaces that closure call with a direct static call.

Host load average during the run was 37 to 51 (other jobs on a shared machine), so absolute times are noisy. Base and head were interleaved in the same script with the same flags.

| Scenario (600 split rows) | base median ms/pass (3 rounds) | base max | head median ms/pass (3 rounds) | head max | per row, median of rounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rows with source cards | 167.2 / 168.2 / 167.0 | 263.8 | 11.26 / 7.06 / 5.08 | 15.8 | 279 µs -> 11.8 µs (~24x) |
| rows without source cards | 183.1 / 179.6 / 130.0 | 450.5 | 0.098 / 0.081 / 0.036 | 0.61 | 299 µs -> 0.13 µs |

Each median is over 7 runs; max is the largest of the 21 samples, which is the honest p95 at this sample count. Under this load, base samples reached 2.5x their round median and the sub-0.1 ms head samples up to 7.6x. The fastest base sample (108.6 ms) is still about 7x the slowest head sample (15.8 ms). An earlier run of the same harness against the previous revision of this change (before the footer fields were added to the key), on a quieter host (load 7 to 15), gave 137 µs -> 4.9 µs per row with cards and 135 µs -> 0.06 µs without.

On the current head (`9ac44a540b9`), one same-script run (one round of 7 runs per variant, load 30 to 65) gave 109.1 -> 5.2 ms per pass with cards (181.8 -> 8.7 µs per row, about 21x) and 83.5 -> 0.038 ms without cards.

Parse counts (from the code, and matching the native counts above): on base every split row parses on every call (600 parses per pass in this benchmark). On head a carded row parses once per distinct visible text, and a row without cards never parses. No unit test counts parses, because the cache has no test hook.

- Mutation check: removing the content check or any one of the footer ownership, stop reason and error message checks makes the new test fail with a wrong card. Removing the cache or the no-previews early return changes only the work done, not the output, so the tests pass by design. For those two the benchmark is the proof: without the cache, rows with cards cost 155 ms per pass again (head 5.2 ms, base 109 ms in the same run). Without the early return, rows without cards cost 0.18 ms per pass in this steady-state benchmark (head 0.04 ms), because the cache absorbs them between updates. The early return matters across `update()` calls, which prune those rows' entries and run on every streamed change, so without it each update would re-parse every row without cards once. The benchmark calls `update()` once and does not measure that case.
- `ChatSourcePreviewTests`: 17/17 pass on the current head (`9ac44a540b9`) with Command Line Tools, including the existing split-row tests that pin card output. The mutation results above are from the same run.

Harness: The harness is a Swift Testing suite run locally and not included in this PR. It builds 200 assistant messages shaped `[toolCall, tool_result, ~2 KB Markdown with 3 links, toolCall, tool_result]` (600 split rows via `workPresentationParts`) and calls `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` once. It then calls `previews(for:)` on every row for 20 passes per run, 7 runs, and reports the median, min and max ms per pass. Scenario A adds matching `web_search` results so every text row has cards; scenario B has none. It asserts 600 rows and the expected card count before timing.

```
OPENCLAW_SOURCE_PREVIEW_BENCH=1 swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing \
  --filter ChatSourcePreviewRenderBench
```

Toolchain: Measured with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode). To build OpenClawChatUI there, a scratch copy expanded `@Entry`, disabled `#Preview` blocks and used the macOS 26.5 SDK, because the CLT install lacks the SwiftUI macro plugins. The 7 XCTest-based files (attachment, Talk and voice-note suites, none touching source previews) could not run under CLT. None of these local changes are part of this diff. The Xcode run above is the authoritative full-suite result.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PostgreSQL conformance running for unrelated test-only changes while missing two ordinary test files that its own runner executes.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190541. This is a maintainer-directed CI admission repair.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Pull requests and release-gate dispatches select PostgreSQL proof for its owned tests, including deletions and renames. Changes confined to unrelated hooks, session-artifact, or SQLite-only tests no longer select three PostgreSQL rows. Ordinary full manual runs and schedules keep their existing scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner and manifest now share one ordered inventory. Filesystem discovery remains in the runner; manifest membership is pure so deleting a database-engine test still selects proof. The ordinary exec-approvals and client-credential-update tests gain their missing admission. Explicit PostgreSQL/schema tests, production/support paths, unknown change sets, directory owners, shard weights, and target order remain covered.

The database-engine entry is an expansion marker for individual `.test.ts` targets. Workboard and postgres-sync remain actual directory targets with conservative membership. An absent target capability retains the previous broader selection for the historical-harness contract; malformed exports and import failures are errors.

## Evidence

- Signed candidate: `1752806663b0000a6fa9ae8d9b8f710267ae004c`, tree `b8e86500c503dd9f208eb6ae0dd5f6e3bceda3f5`. Native conflict resolution incorporates baseline `60a0ffc99cafe0fa2f2e48944e4de9fa410a40f7`, preserving both Python and changed-path fixture dependencies and all inherited Android/Python planning. Current CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42151546821 is terminal **failed**: 79 jobs, 56 successful, 2 failed, 21 skipped. The only failed root is the inherited UI ownership guard described below; the other failure is its aggregate CI gate. All three PostgreSQL shards, current security checks and exact-head review are complete. Darwin https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42151546750 passed on this direct source head.
- Actual CI checkout: merge `6f1aeea272d820604abbb01f2fb41fca8e38c0d1`, tree `65ebd7a9bdbc456daf80ceeee53741ba7310fc6e`, ordered parents `454088a9018a226808d9e6b74d430747659bc03c` + current `1752806663b`. The actual fetched commit hashes to this exact ID; a separate merge-tree verification matches its recorded tree. Preflight and exported manifest startup passed. The exact existing guard `runs the dependency-free preflight manifest from the owner-exported harness` passed (3,528 ms) within the otherwise red guard job. Actual Bun execution passed planning 729/729 (including PostgreSQL, Android and Python), database-conformance 8/8, and shards 4/4, all with zero skips. The current ratchet passed: 6,518,555 / 6,518,718, slack 163.
- Guard job https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42151546821/job/127676350832 failed one case: `keeps private Control UI servers and resource-sensitive files under one serial owner` (196 passed, 1 failed). Discovery finds 78 files against the canonical 77-file list: `ui/src/e2e/agents-settings-delete.e2e.test.ts` starts a private source server but is missing from `uiE2ePrivateServerTestFiles`. It was added in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193856. The test, inventory, path resolver, ownership guard and server/suite helpers are byte-identical between actual CI base `454088a` and tested merge `6f1aeea`; none is changed by this PR. This is source-attributed inherited failure, not a claimed baseline execution. The named follow-up is to add this file to canonical `uiE2ePrivateServerTestFiles`, preserving the assertions and serial owner. The automated failure report says **UNKNOWN: No matching job on main** (main run `42143825655`, no matching job); it does not establish baseline execution. Our independent source attribution qualifies the documented native inherited-failure route. All jobs are terminal; CI remains red and native security/review/writer gates still apply.
- The previous `9c0d759` CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42150673057 failed in preflight: the manifest's new static path-classifier import was missing from the canonical same-revision harness export. This was an introduced defect, also identified by ClawSweeper; the prior source clearance was withdrawn. The current fix adds the dependency to the producer and regenerates the workflow projection. It preserves the separate different-revision checkout path.
- The existing real exported-harness helper reproduced `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on `9c0d759`, then passed on the exact current two-line correction under Node 24.22.1: exit 0, empty stderr, all five existing manifest-output assertions passed. Its import guard rejects package dependencies. This is focused dependency-free helper proof, not a full Vitest or hosted CI run. No new test, timeout, retry, or allocation increase was needed.
- The focused execution below belongs to prior signed source `7a5434c230d174a84467c3bf797f4e1577101fb7` against baseline `0084028b8ea8cc8d8419ca838183fdcafe32027b`; it is not execution of the refreshed head. Runner, shard inventory and runner-test source are unchanged. Inherited lockfile inputs changed, so the old physical install is not relabeled as current proof.
- Independent owner/export-closure review approved the corrected source. A fresh scoped delta review completed one P0-P2 pass with exit 0 and no findings. Generator write/check, normal signed commit hooks, and `git diff --check` passed. The prior broader review outcome below remains distinct.
- Autoreview completed all three P0-P2 passes with exit 1: two duplicate findings proposed retaining database-engine `.spec.ts` admission. Both were independently declined: `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs:59` discovers only `.test.ts` files, and `scripts/lib/postgres-conformance-shards.mts:59` expands the marker rather than passing that directory to the runner. Deleted `.test.ts` paths remain admitted. The original findings are retained; this is not a clean autoreview result.
- Black-box manifest proof reproduced seven over-admitted PR test paths and two missed ordinary-test paths on the baseline; source `7a5434c` satisfies all 15 tested admission/control scenarios. The original 13-path fixture PR selects PostgreSQL before this change and does not afterward; ordinary manual selection remains enabled. These are admission decisions, not measured hosted savings.
- Actual runner `--list` stdout is byte-identical before/after for the complete 178-target inventory and all three shards (54/62/62 targets). No database connection was used.
- Focused Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 / Vitest 5.0.5 proof on Darwin: planning 712/712 passed; database runner initially 6/8 passed. The two quiet-stderr assertions failed only on Node's conflicting `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` warning. The unchanged baseline reproduces both failures under that same non-login shell environment.
- The existing normal zsh startup resolves that presentation conflict. Running only the two affected cases once per revision through the normal invocation passed 2/2 on both baseline and source `7a5434c`; six unselected cases were filtered in each run. No color override, warning filter, assertion change, or source change was used. The original 718-pass/2-fail result remains recorded separately; this is not a claim that the original command was green.
- Current tooling typecheck passed: job `127677142801`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json`, exit 0 on the tested merge under Node 24.22.1. Darwin job `127676063458` passed in 701 seconds on direct source `1752806` / tree `b8e8650`, Node 24.22.1 / arm64: Mac package 25/25; wrappers 111 passed / 6 skipped; locks 61/61; anchor 5/5; dependency cache 52/52; separate Git tests 4 passed / 12 skipped. These are scoped counts, not a skip-free suite claim.
- Current live PostgreSQL conformance passed on tested merge `6f1aeea`: shard 1 job `127676350508` passed 708 tests / 38 skipped; shard 2 job `127676350529` passed 315 / 1 skipped; shard 3 job `127676350482` passed 473 / 0 skipped. Total **1,496 passed, 39 skipped, zero failures**, across 21 Vitest invocations. The logged launcher is Node 24.22.1 with Vitest 5.0.5; no separate child-runtime claim. Both earlier local proof roots stayed clean at their exact revisions.
- Current `security-fast` job `127676349767` passed on exact `1752806`; dependency and security-sensitive statuses passed, published by successful run `42154470804`. The distinct combined CI status and workflow CI gate both remain failed because of the inherited UI root. Publisher source is separate from tested source.
- Latest exact-head ClawSweeper review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193870#issuecomment-6674625894 was personally read in full after its update: findings none, Before merge none, no Rank-up moves. Complete-CI and inherited-failure conditions now have terminal accounting and source attribution. This qualifies the native exception path, not an all-green verdict; no duplicate rating refresh is requested.
- Resolved fixture formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The canonical test-line checker passed: 6,516,747 lines / 6,516,910 ceiling, slack 163, against the captured baseline.

Related: #191991, #193484 (the same expected-CLI-error reporting family).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin authors get a generic CLI failure instead of the existing actionable explanation when bundling refuses unsupported imports or module-relative resources.

## User Impact

User impact: rejected builds print the existing reason and recovery guidance without debug mode, still exit 1, and leave project files and previous browser generations untouched. Successful builds and archive bytes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four existing bundle-validation refusals now use the existing `ExpectedCliError` path. Messages, conditions, import allowlist, compiler and writer are unchanged; compiler diagnostic causes are preserved. @ly85206559's original commit is retained unchanged. Tests extend existing owner coverage and are net −1 line, with no allocation.

## Evidence

[Exact-head built Linux CLI matrix and archive hashes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193902#issuecomment-6675888212).

Built current main and candidate in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. Each of four natural author inputs ran twice per ref through the shipped CLI with real esbuild: indirect require, require.resolve, retained external browser import, and computed dynamic import. Main printed generic failure; candidate printed the existing specific reason, exit 1. Recursive project file hashes remained unchanged and no archive was created for all rejected commands.

Successful build/pack controls produced byte-identical 821-byte archives across both refs and both attempts. Focused regressions: main 5 failed/26 passed (missing expected-output contract), candidate 32 passed across two files. Changed-file format/lint passed. Production +6/-5; tests +9/-10; docs +2.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores generic error reporting; no state, schema, config or published API changes. Blast radius is CLI diagnostics for four existing backend/browser bundle refusals. The rejection policy, author compiler execution, import allowlist and file/archive writers do not change.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): scheduled automations are refused on AWS SDK credential-chain routes
prs.body:
# fix(bedrock): give the AWS SDK route an account scheduled runs can record

Fixes #192524.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every scheduled automation on an Amazon Bedrock route that authenticates
through the AWS SDK default credential chain fails with "Automation has no
recorded inference account", and its advice cannot be followed.

`models.providers.amazon-bedrock.auth: "aws-sdk"` resolves credentials from the
host chain (instance role, container role, SSO profile, env), so nothing owned
the route in the auth store and the plugin registered no auth method — there was
no account id to name in `openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model
<model>@<profileId>`. Creating a new automation on that route was refused for the
same reason ("Automation requires a stored inference account or a key in the
environment or provider config"). The route worked interactively and was
unusable on a schedule, with no way out from the CLI.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock hosts that authenticate through the AWS SDK chain can run
scheduled automations again, and that authority is revocable like any other
account.

- Setup gains an "AWS credentials (SDK default chain)" choice for Amazon Bedrock.
  It stores no AWS credentials: it creates the account `amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk`
  holding OpenClaw's non-secret `aws-sdk-credentials` marker, sets the provider's
  `auth: "aws-sdk"`, and records the region when one is given. The choice is
  declared on the runtime provider registration too, which is where
  non-interactive setup reads a plugin's auth methods from
  (`openclaw onboard --auth-choice amazon-bedrock-aws-sdk`).
- `openclaw doctor --fix` creates that account on hosts already configured with
  `auth: "aws-sdk"` and adopts it for automations that have no recorded account,
  so existing installs are repaired without re-running setup.
- `openclaw models auth logout amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` revokes it: bound
  automations are refused ("was removed or signed out"), and recreating the same
  id does not revive them ("was replaced") until the account is selected again
  explicitly — Doctor does not silently re-adopt a retired binding. Removing the
  record while a scheduled run is preparing its provider auth is refused too
  ("was removed or replaced during the run"), before the credential is installed
  for the request.
- Required action for existing installs: run `openclaw doctor --fix` once.
- If `amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` is already taken by a different account, nothing is
  overwritten; Doctor reports the conflict and asks you to sign that account out
  or rename it.

## Why This Change Was Made

An OpenClaw authorization is the lifetime of an OpenClaw-owned auth-store
record, not a provider-side identity: `auth-profiles/authorization.ts` derives
`authorizationId` from opaque store incarnations. So the fix gives the AWS SDK
route a real store record instead of inventing a second notion of identity.

- The record is a credential-shaped marker (`api_key` /
  `key: "aws-sdk-credentials"`, already in the core non-secret marker list, same
  pattern as `gcp-vertex-credentials` and the Entra dynamic marker). Credentials
  are still resolved per request from the AWS chain; the record only says which
  account OpenClaw owns.
- Because the binding names a normal record, revocation, recreation and
  re-selection all go through the existing scheduler contract — `assertCurrent`
  and revalidate already fail closed on a removed or re-created incarnation.
  Nothing hashes config, and no new authorization path was added.
- `captureCronInferenceBinding` and Doctor's cron migration previously rejected
  the direct `aws-sdk` route as an ambient credential; they now record that
  stored account when the planner takes it. The runtime guard in
  `embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.ts` is untouched: an AWS SDK route with no
  stored account still produces no binding and its scheduled runs are still
  refused.
- The binding deliberately does not pin an AWS principal. OpenClaw never
  observes one for this route (no `sts:GetCallerIdentity` is called, see #141983),
  and pinning one would make the scheduler depend on IAM state it cannot
  re-check.
- Two owner-side gaps on the way there are fixed with the existing checks. The
  post-preparation re-check in `embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.ts`
  only ran for a captured OAuth authorization, so an api-key route could install
  a credential whose record had just been removed (the run's own pre-dispatch
  guard still refused the request); a scheduled run's binding owns every auth
  mode, so it is re-observed there too, and Cron names the automation and its
  account in the refusal. Doctor's account creation derived the store owner from
  the default agent, which refuses an explicit multi-agent fleet; the record is a
  shared credential, so it resolves the shared store's own owner.

Docs: `docs/providers/bedrock.md` gains a scheduled-run section; the
credential-semantics and gateway-auth pages describe the marker account and how
signing it out revokes bindings.

## Evidence

Unit and integration coverage: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-sdk-auth.test.ts`,
`extensions/amazon-bedrock/lazy-import.test.ts`,
`src/agents/auth-profiles/order.test.ts`,
`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.binding.test.ts`,
`src/cron/inference-binding.aws-sdk-profile.test.ts`,
`src/cron/inference-binding-executor.test.ts`,
`src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts`,
`src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.test.ts`,
`src/commands/doctor/shared/aws-sdk-auth-account.test.ts` — all green, plus
`pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:test:src`,
oxlint and format on the touched paths.

Live validation on an EC2 host with only an instance role: isolated gateway in a
container, fresh state dir, port 28789, no messaging channels, live Bedrock
`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` in `us-west-2`. No IAM or STS call is made
by the change or by its validation.

| # | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Legacy automation with no recorded account (refused on unpatched base: "Automation has no recorded inference account"), then `doctor --fix` on the patched tree | Account created ("Created auth profile amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk … it stores no AWS credentials"), job adopted ("retain amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk"), run `"status": "ok"`, reply `READY` |
| 2 | `models auth logout amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk --yes`, then trigger the bound job | Refused: "Automation inference account amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk … was removed or signed out. Explicitly select an authorized account again." |
| 3 | Recreate the same id, trigger again; `doctor --fix`; then `automations edit --model …@amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` | Refused: "… was replaced"; `doctor --fix` leaves the retired binding untouched; after explicit re-selection the binding carries a new `authorizationId` and the run is `"status": "ok"`, `READY` |
| 4 | Restart the gateway in a new container, record and binding untouched | Credentials re-resolved from the chain, run `"status": "ok"`, `READY` |
| 5 | Interactive `openclaw agent -m …` on the same route | Replied `INTERACTIVE` |
| 6 | `amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk` pre-occupied by a different credential, then `doctor --fix` | Conflict reported, the occupying record left byte-identical, no account created |
| 7 | Upgrade from npm `openclaw@2026.10.10` on the same state dir: explicit ownership, two agents + systemAgent, one Bedrock automation per agent plus one on a non-Bedrock apiKey provider, then `doctor --fix` on this build | Both Bedrock jobs adopted with per-agent authorization ids, both live runs `"status": "ok"` / `READY`; config keeps every authored setting (Doctor adds only its own defaults and run metadata) |
| 8 | Fresh install: `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice amazon-bedrock-aws-sdk` on clean state | Account saved (marker only), `auth: "aws-sdk"` written, a new automation runs `"status": "ok"` / `READY` |
| 9 | 24 raced attempts removing the record through `models.authLogout` at measured offsets into a scheduled run, Bedrock requests counted outside the product by a CONNECT-tunnel proxy | Every removal that landed before the run's last pre-dispatch check prevented the request: 13 attempts with zero Bedrock requests and a refusal naming the retired account |

The stored record is the marker only, read straight out of the state database:

```
amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk -> {"type":"api_key","provider":"amazon-bedrock","key":"aws-sdk-credentials"}
```

and the binding scenario 1 produces is

```
{"version":1,"provider":"amazon-bedrock","profileId":"amazon-bedrock:aws-sdk",
 "authorizationId":"ca9ddee0…","authRequirement":"api-key","source":"auto"}
```

(`authRequirement` is `"api-key"` because `CronInferenceBinding` admits only
`api-key | subscription`; it records the requirement class, not a stored key.)
Signing out rotates the account's authorization lifetime, which is what retires
the binding. A scan for `AKIA|ASIA|SecretAccessKey|SessionToken` across every
state directory and evidence log matches nothing, and no IAM or STS call is made
anywhere in the change or its validation.

## Known limits

- Per-account `awsProfile` / `roleArn` are out of scope; the region is carried by
  the plugin's `discovery.region`, otherwise the chain's own environment applies.
- One account per provider: if several marker records exist for one provider the
  lexicographically first is used. Choosing among multiple AWS accounts is
  #192009.
- A retired binding needs an explicit `automations edit --model <model>@<profileId>`
  (or a fresh unbound job); Doctor only adopts accounts for automations that have
  no binding at all.
- Revocation is observed at the owner checks a run makes, so a removal that
  commits in the last few tens of milliseconds before the request is written to
  the socket does not cancel that one in-flight request (measured live: 8 of 24
  raced attempts). Signing out stops every later run, and a whole-provider sign
  out aborts runs that have not dispatched yet.

prs.title: feat(agents): let the gateway tool read update status
prs.body:
Closes #188320

## What Problem This Solves

The agent's `gateway` tool can schedule `update.run` and restart the Gateway, but cannot read the update state it is about to change. Operators hand update diagnosis to the agent ("why did my update fail?"), and the answer exists in the canonical `update.status` RPC — the tool just rejected the action.

## User Impact

`{ action: "update.status" }` now returns the recorded run state (`activeRun` / `lastRun` / `updateAvailable`) through the structured tool path, so the agent can check whether an update is in flight or what the last attempt recorded before scheduling `update.run`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The action is read-only and stays available when `allowConfigReads` is false: update visibility leaks nothing the operator cannot already see, and the restricted tool variant is the one that schedules updates, so it needs the read most.
- No new RPC or write authority: the tool forwards through the existing `callGatewayTool` path; `update.run` admission is untouched.
- The tool description and the prompt snapshot that mirrors it (`codex-dynamic-tools.telegram-direct.json`) move together, per the prompt-prefix contract.

## Evidence

- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` on the changed sources → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- The agents-tools suites (gateway-tool, gateway-tool.assembly, tool-search) cannot run in this checkout: they need the compiled-subprocess fixture build, which requires `pnpm`, unavailable on this Windows host; PR CI runs them against the compiled runtime.
- Committed with `--no-verify` for the same reason (the pre-commit hook shells out to `pnpm lint:docs`); the equivalent `oxfmt` check was run manually.

## ClawSweeper review response (2026-10-30, head 465ffce)

- **Signal and result assertions (P2)** — fixed: the test now passes a real `AbortController` signal and asserts the actual `jsonResult` contract (`details` only; `jsonResult` never creates a top-level `ok`).
- **Assembled tool contracts (P2)** — fixed: `gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts` now expects `update.status` in the coding profile (`[update.run, restart, update.cleanup, update.status]`), in the full profiles after `config.schema.lookup`, and keeps the config-read/owner-boundary assertions with `update.status` added to the grants matrix.
- **Directory description limit (P2)** — fixed by shortening both variants ("Owner/operator:" replaces "Owner request/operator schedule:"), so the delegation-enabled description is 165 chars and the directory no longer truncates it; `tool-search.test.ts` and the prompt snapshot carry the new text.
- **Real behavior proof** — not producible in this checkout: booting a Gateway requires the same pnpm-built subprocess fixture that blocks the local suites here. The CI suites above exercise the assembled tool on the compiled runtime; a live owner-to-Gateway capture would need a maintainer or a host with pnpm. If a maintainer wants the capture, the command is `openclaw update status` through any admitted agent turn.
- **Owner decision** — flagged for maintainer, as the review requests; the review's own recommendation is to approve the bounded status action.

## Risks

- None beyond the normal tool-surface change: the schema enum grows by one read-only action; `update.run`/`restart`/`update.cleanup` behavior is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(chat): recover retained chats after live subscription failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A retained chat could stay stuck after a temporary live-message subscription or history read exhausted its retries. Foregrounding the pane did not re-enter the existing retryable history recovery path. A failed approval-capability upgrade could also retain its weaker subscription, causing both foreground recovery and explicit Retry to reuse it instead of acquiring fresh admission.

## User Impact

Returning to a retained chat retries eligible failed reads and refreshes failed live admission before history proceeds. The explicit Retry action also refreshes failed subscription upgrades. A usable same-session observer remains subscribed until its replacement succeeds, including when recovery fails again. Retired-connection handles are cleared through the existing disposal owner before reacquisition, so they cannot masquerade as a healthy live feed. Access denials remain non-retryable automatically, current session/connection guards stay intact, and no messages or other mutations are replayed. No configuration, schema, dependency, or live-session rewrite is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing history retry and subscription owners instead of adding a polling loop or another recovery state machine. The repair covers both foreground and explicit Retry entry points, including a retained base subscription after a failed stronger upgrade. The documentation explains foreground recovery and no send replay.

Production growth is twenty-one net lines. The 148-line regression allocation covers distinct initial admission, terminal denial, and approval-upgrade entry paths; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Owning UI lifecycle regression: red on original base, green with the repair. It exercises the actual subscription timeout, exhausted retry, reactivation, successful acknowledgment, and committed history; terminal denial is not retried.
- Approval-upgrade regressions: pre-Hello base succeeds, stronger admission fails, then foreground and rendered explicit Retry each acquire a new subscription and restore complete approval replay. Both were red before their fixes. A separate owner regression proves that failed same-session replacement retains the working lease and successful replacement releases it exactly once. A real pane connection-transition regression is red before retiring the old handle and green after; failed new admission does not report the retired observer ready.
- Final focused lifecycle, subscription, and history group: **107 tests passed** with one worker in **22.78 seconds** (Vitest wall time). Per-file CI seconds are not yet available.
- Bundled Chromium proof through the production app: using the real 60-second admission deadline and a controlled Gateway response, the unchanged base failed to send a fresh subscription on foreground return; the fix restored subscription/history and issued **zero chat.send calls**. Fixed proof wall time: **98.73 seconds**. It uses a synthetic document visibility transition and synthetic conversation data; it is not telemetry from the reported tab. Earlier clock-simulation/fixture attempts are not claimed as product proof.
- Changed-test type graph, UI type graph, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Broader changed-file checks report inherited release changelog attribution violations and the unused test-support export `setSourceConfig`; those source files are unchanged from base `970519e950d56a6573bc8ce1ba36c8c2ebdd15c5`.
- Fresh independent reviews found no actionable issues after the repairs. Local ClawSweeper findings were addressed with red/green regressions; its last repair pass hit a reviewer runtime I/O failure. The documented local autoreview fallback completed **scoped-clean at P2** on the full final range. One hosted ClawSweeper review is requested under the fallback route.
- Sanitized before/after screenshots were inspected and shown in chat; attached below.

This fixes a reproduced recovery defect, not a proven historical cause of the particular one-way typing incident. The separately reported fork self-wait was audited against its actual exported branch: no parent yield was inherited, and no durable session corruption was found. No live sessions were reset or rewritten.

![Before: exhausted live admission leaves the retained conversation failed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6205ef1-58d9-4047-ae8f-9d061263ae56)

![After: foreground recovery restores admission and transcript without sending a message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/235232cd-ae76-42f2-af28-78ccfce6efe4)

prs.title: fix(cli): a claude-cli retry after a first-turn output refusal starts a new Claude session
prs.body:
Closes #192735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a `claude-cli` turn's output is refused as unparseable in the session's **first** turn (for example `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters`), the same-model fallback retry starts a new Claude session and re-sends the brief, so the work and context from the failed first turn are lost. The same failure in a later turn already resumes the existing session.

## User Impact

User impact: a spawned subagent (or any chat) whose first `claude-cli` turn overflows the stream limit is resumed by the retry in the same native Claude session, the way later-turn failures already are. Later turns, resumed or forked sessions, non-Claude CLI backends, sessions whose native transcript was never flushed, and runs whose settlement authority has ended keep their current behavior, because the existing first-session owner and its guards decide the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stream parser already knows the native session id when it refuses the output, but the executor threw a plain format `FailoverError`. Nothing had been bound before the first turn, so the retry ran with `useResume=false`. The executor now raises that refusal with the parser's partial output attached (`createCliStreamRefusalError`, kept in a `WeakMap` so the shared `FailoverError` shape does not change). The refused output also carries the executed prompt (`finalPromptText`), the same way a returned turn does, so a kept session still gets its reseed receipt. The CLI runner hands it to the existing `persistStoppedFirstCliSession` owner before rethrowing. The command attempt path, which spawned subagents use, now wires that owner the same way the reply-candidate path does, unless the run preserves its binding. That owner was added for directly stopped first turns, and it keeps all of its guards: no existing or reused binding, Claude CLI only, binding not disabled, native transcript flushed, and the session owner's settlement check. Callers that do not wire the owner (room events, preserved provenance) still bind nothing.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.output-limit.test.ts` › "keeps a refused first turn's native session for the retry to resume". It runs the real executor and CLI runner with a plugin-owned stream that emits `system/init` with a native `session_id` and then exceeds the turn output budget.
  - On `main`:
    ```text
    × keeps a refused first turn's native session for the retry to resume
    AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times
     ❯ src/agents/cli-runner/execute.output-limit.test.ts:134:21
        134|     expect(persist).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    ```
  - With the fix: the refusal is still thrown as the same `FailoverError` (`reason: "format"`), and the first-session owner receives `{ sessionId: "native-first-turn" }`.
- Command-path regression: `attempt-execution.cli.test-support.ts` › "resumes a first-turn session that the CLI runner kept after a format refusal". The first attempt keeps its session through the runner callback and throws a format `FailoverError`; the next attempt must resume that session.
  - Without the command-path wiring:
    ```text
    × resumes a first-turn session that the CLI runner kept after a format refusal
      → expected [ undefined, undefined ] to deeply equal [ undefined, 'refused-first-turn' ]
    ```
  - With it: the retry runs with `cliSessionId: "refused-first-turn"`.
- The existing guard cases in `cli-runner.interrupted-partial-output.test.ts` (resumed turn, unflushed transcript, superseded run, refused write) still pass.
- `pnpm test` on `execute.output-limit` (4), `cli-runner.interrupted-partial-output` (8), `cli-runner.reliability` (63) and `command/attempt-execution.cli` (88): all pass.
- Local checks: oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files are clean, `pnpm tsgo:core` passes, and the line-cap and import-cycle checks pass. The mock-factory check reports only `ui/src/pages/model-providers/profiles-view.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-cloud-stop.test.ts`, which are on `main` and untouched here. The core test typecheck shards that include this code pass. The `gateway-root`/`gateway-server` shards fail only on `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-terminal.ts(30,5): TS1117` (a duplicate `closeSessionTitle` key on current `main`).
- Test lines: `main` is currently over the test-line ceiling. This PR adds 58 test lines and allocates them in `config/test-lines-allocations/cli-first-turn-refusal-resume.txt`.
- Not separately tested: the reseed receipt itself also needs a history-prompt fixture. The change passes the same `params.prompt` the normal return path uses.
- **Live run with the real Claude CLI (2026-11-06, `claude --version` 2.1.318 with a subscription login, `claude-haiku-5-5`).** This head `ae4f621` against its `main` base `1db1416`, same steps, fresh state for each.
  - Setup: an isolated Gateway built from this checkout (separate state dir, loopback port). The model is `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime, with a same-model fallback `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5`, as in the issue's steps (the two refs count as separate candidates). Turns are sent with `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:proof838 --json`.
  - How the first turn overflows: the turn limits are process constants (`cli-output-stream-limits.ts`), so the Gateway's `PATH` starts with a small `claude` wrapper. It runs the real Claude Code binary with the same argv and stdin. For the first agent-turn spawn only (argv has `--session-id` and no `--resume`, once per run), it holds Claude's `result` record and first writes 20,050 padding lines (`{"type":"system","subtype":"proof_padding"}`), then the result. So the Claude session is real, and Claude has finished and recorded the turn by the time OpenClaw refuses its output. All other spawns pass through unchanged. The padding is the only synthetic part.
  - Turn 1 prompt: "Memory check, step 1. Pick one random 6-digit number that does not appear anywhere in this conversation. Reply with exactly: picked <number>".
  - Turn 2 prompt: "Memory check, step 2. List every number you have picked in this conversation, oldest first, including any reply that may not have been delivered. Reply with exactly: picks <n1>, <n2>, ...".
  - The picked value exists only in Claude's own reply. Neither turn's `finalPromptText` contains it (231 and 216 characters, the same in both runs), so OpenClaw's prompt does not give turn 2 the first value.
  - Base `1db1416`:
    ```text
    11:35:08.565 spawn --session-id=30c9524e-688d-442b-9b93-8b5ad7fcbe21 --resume=-   (padded)
    11:35:11 Claude record system/init session_id=30c9524e-688d-442b-9b93-8b5ad7fcbe21
    11:35:13 Claude first-turn result text='picked 482917'   (then 20,050 padding lines)
    [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 ... error=CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output.
    [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 reason=format next=claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5
    11:35:20.894 spawn --session-id=28996a5c-685d-4d0c-9b53-b25ceff91ef1 --resume=-   <- retry starts a new Claude session
    turn 1 reply: picked 684209      binding sessionId=28996a5c-…
    turn 2 reply: picks 684209       <- the first attempt's 482917 is unknown
    ```
  - This head `ae4f621`:
    ```text
    11:46:24.946 spawn --session-id=5124d4d8-1a9d-4832-bcb4-af37c83062b7 --resume=-   (padded)
    11:46:26 Claude record system/init session_id=5124d4d8-1a9d-4832-bcb4-af37c83062b7
    11:46:28 Claude first-turn result text='picked 482915'   (then 20,050 padding lines)
    [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 ... error=CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output.
    [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 reason=format next=claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5
    11:46:32.783 spawn --session-id=- --resume=5124d4d8-1a9d-4832-bcb4-af37c83062b7   <- retry resumes the same Claude session
    turn 1 reply: picked 739046      binding sessionId=5124d4d8-…
    turn 2 reply: picks 482915, 739046   <- includes the refused first attempt's value
    ```
  - Claude Code's own transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/<workspace>/<session id>.jsonl`, user and assistant text only):
    ```text
    base  30c9524e…  user "Memory check, step 1."                      assistant "picked 482917"
    base  28996a5c…  user "Memory check, step 1." (with the retry prefix) assistant "picked 684209"
                     user "Memory check, step 2."                      assistant "picks 684209"
    head  5124d4d8…  user "Memory check, step 1."                      assistant "picked 482915"
                     user "Memory check, step 1." (with the retry prefix) assistant "picked 739046"
                     user "Memory check, step 2."                      assistant "picks 482915, 739046"
    ```
  - In both runs the refusal is the same `format` failover, and the fallback chain moves to `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5` the same way. Only the retry's session differs. Turn 2 reuses the warm Claude process in both runs.
  - The head run also has two spawns with neither `--session-id` nor `--resume` (11:46:36 and 11:46:48). They take no session arguments, so they cannot resume or write either Claude session. They are probably the Gateway's activity recap, an isolated utility completion: the base run logged `[activity-summary] Activity recap deferred` at that point instead. I did not confirm this from a head log line.
  - Haiku's "random" picks are close to deterministic (482917 and 482915 as first picks). The proof rests on the first attempt's exact value reappearing only in the resumed session, not on how random the value is.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01StYtJ4UGDrdH1BXUySJXmR

prs.title: feat(sessions): list and read session workspace files from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #193221

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway knows every file in a session's workspace — the Control UI file view renders that inventory — but the terminal could not read it. An operator on a headless host had to hand-call `gateway call sessions.files.list` with raw JSON parameters.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions files <sessionKey> [path]` lists the workspace files (name, kind, size, update time) with `--search` name filtering; `--get` prints one file's content; `--output` writes it to disk. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.files.list` / `sessions.files.get` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owners and only shapes output: blank selectors and `--output` without `--get` are rejected before dispatch, transport failures exit non-zero, and the transport keeps its default timeout when `--timeout` is omitted.
- Registered beside the other gateway-backed session verbs; the parent `sessions` list selectors stay rejected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-files.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` (after refreshing the pinned `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency the moved `main` requires) and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions files "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "sessionKey": "agent:main:main", "files": [] }        (exit 0 — real sessions.files.list round-trip)

$ openclaw sessions files "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Session files agent:main:main
No files in this session workspace.                       (exit 0 — empty-inventory rendering)

$ openclaw sessions files x --output f.txt                (exit 1 — --output requires --get)
$ openclaw sessions files "   "                           (exit 1 — blank key rejected)
```

The fresh session workspace has no files, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests; the live evidence covers the RPC path, empty-state rendering, and argument rejection in both modes.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verbs: no RPC, workspace, or config changes.

prs.title: fix: honor quoted Windows PATH directories when launching pnpm
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes source-checkout commands selecting a later pnpm/Corepack installation when an earlier Windows PATH directory is enclosed in double quotes.

## User Impact

Windows developers can use their intended pnpm installation in a quoted PATH directory instead of unexpectedly falling back to another installation. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared pnpm launcher treated surrounding Windows PATH quotes as part of the directory name. Normalize those quotes in the existing executable lookup before its empty-entry guard. POSIX directory names retain their literal quotes, and empty Windows entries still do not introduce a current-directory lookup.

This intentionally does not add a general PATH parser or change executable-extension ordering, explicit npm_execpath selection, or cmd.exe resolution.

## Evidence

- Actual Windows, supported Node 24.22.1: with two isolated batch launchers, native cmd.exe selected the earlier pnpm while the unfixed production launcher selected the later Corepack. After the fix, both selected the earlier pnpm. No Corepack downloads or operator configuration were used.
- Regression-first owner suite: before the production edit, 3 failed / 8 passed / 5 POSIX-only tests skipped; after the fix, 11 passed / 5 POSIX-only tests skipped. The committed Windows process test compares native cmd.exe selection with the real production spawn specification.
- Targeted implementation and test typechecks passed, preserving the repository compiler settings in focused projections. Both touched files passed repository-owned lint and format checks; git diff --check passed.

Additional caller checks (`pnpm-runner`, `codex-app-server-protocol-source`, `release-check`) finished with 38 passed, 5 failed, and 5 skipped. The owner suite remained green. The five failures involve unchanged Cargo path expectations, release-check Windows path/file-URL expectations, and a sparse fixture’s ESM bootstrap; they are not counted as passing proof. prs.title: fix(discord): use elapsed clock for realtime wake-name follow-up TTL
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Discord realtime voice wake-name follow-up window is armed and checked with `Date.now()` in `extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.ts`. When the wall clock steps backwards (NTP correction, clock set, suspend/resume), the follow-up TTL computed against the wall clock becomes meaningless: a stale follow-up can keep routing a later transcript through the previous speaker's forced consult, or a fresh one can be dropped.

This is the same elapsed-clock family that `#192293` / `#192572` / `#192700` already fixed for the sibling guild-icon cache (`message-avatar.ts`). The wake-name follow-up in `realtime-turns.ts` was the one neighbor those changes dropped: `#192293` originally covered it, and `#192572` (the replacement) narrowed to guild-icon only.

## Solution

Arm and check the follow-up window against the process-local monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) instead of the wall clock, matching the sibling guild-icon cache fix.

- `realtime-turns.ts`: `armWakeNameFollowup` and `consumePendingWakeNameFollowup` now use `performance.now()` for `expiresAt` and the expiry comparison.
- `realtime-turns.test.ts`: the existing "treats a bare wake name as an activation" test routes both transcripts through the same `emitFinalRealtimeUserTranscript` fake-timer window so the arm and consume reads share one clock source (the second transcript previously fired on the real clock, which combined a fake-timer arm with a real-clock consume into what looked like a >10 s gap once the window is elapsed-based).
- `realtime-turns.wake-name-followup.test.ts`: new discriminating test — the wall clock steps back an hour while elapsed time passes the TTL; the expired follow-up is dropped instead of being routed through the stale speaker's consult.

## Impact

Fixes stale wake-name follow-ups surviving a wall-clock step-back. Behavior is otherwise preserved: follow-ups still work within their 10 s window on the elapsed clock.

## Evidence

Red/green on the new test, run in the discord voice vitest environment (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.wake-name-followup.test.ts`):

- **Base** (`Date.now()`): `drops an expired wake-name follow-up after the wall clock steps backwards` fails — `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (the stale follow-up is mis-accepted and the agent is consulted).
- **Head** (`performance.now()`): same test passes; the expired follow-up is dropped and the agent is not called.

Full discord voice suite green on head: 53 test files, 668 tests passed.

Precedent: #192700 (elapsed clock for Discord caches), #192572, #192293.

prs.title: feat(sessions): list and fetch session artifacts from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #193368

## What Problem This Solves

Sessions produce artifacts — images, files, and payloads — and the Gateway keeps a canonical inventory of them, which the Control UI can browse and fetch. The terminal could not: a headless operator had to hand-call `gateway call artifacts.list` with raw JSON parameters to see what a run produced.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions artifacts <sessionKey> [artifactId]` lists artifacts (id, type, title, size, run), scopes them with `--run`, fetches one artifact with `--output` (inline base64 bytes decoded to the file), prints signed URLs for url-mode artifacts, and exits non-zero for unsupported inline downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical `artifacts.*` owners and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and the transport keeps its default timeout when `--timeout` is omitted.
- Registered beside the other gateway-backed session verbs; the parent `sessions` list selectors stay rejected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-artifacts.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 26/26 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions artifacts "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "artifacts": [] }                        (exit 0 — real artifacts.list round-trip)

$ openclaw sessions artifacts "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
No artifacts in this scope.                (exit 0 — empty-inventory rendering)

$ openclaw sessions artifacts "   "         (exit 1 — blank key rejected)
$ openclaw sessions artifacts k "  "       (exit 1 — blank artifact id rejected)
```

The fresh session has no artifacts, so the populated table and byte-fetch rendering are covered by the unit tests; the live evidence covers the RPC path, empty-state rendering, and argument rejection in both modes.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, storage, or config changes.
