prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): add Gateway membership authority and publication behind the Labs flag
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw ID remote access needs a Gateway-side owner for each claw's membership: who the owner devices and members are, how signed changes from them are accepted, and how the claw is published to Discovery. This draft adds that owner, without any transport, sign-in or UI, so it can be reviewed on its own.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Everything here sits behind the `gateway.openclawId.enabled` Labs switch, which is off by default. With the switch off the Gateway starts nothing, opens no sockets, makes no OpenClaw ID, Discovery or relay calls, hides the `openclawId.*` methods and events from `hello`, and answers every `openclawId.*` call with "off" or a refusal.

With the switch on, a claw still cannot be linked from this PR alone: linking needs the tunnel endpoint key, and the tunnel lands in the next PR. Linking is refused with `tunnel_not_running` until then.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the third PR of the OpenClaw ID stack. It builds on the protocol package (#191469, merged) and on #193146 (merged), which makes revocations replay-safe and bounds invites. The next PRs are:

- the tunnel transport, OpenClaw ID sign-in and the Gateway auth changes for relayed devices (stacked on this branch; it also needs the iroh binding, #191470);
- the Control UI and the People plugin.

What this PR adds, all in `src/gateway/openclaw-id/` unless noted:

- **Membership authority** (`authority.ts`, `claw-store.ts`, `binding-check.ts`, `claw-migration.ts`): the durable claw record in the shared state database. It applies owner-signed statements through the protocol package's authority rules, keeps invite reports, approval times and device-token bindings in separate rows written in one transaction, deletes spent invites with their reports before each write, and runs the link ceremony (`prepareLink`/`commitLink`). A claw's root never changes: there is no owner reset (it was removed from the protocol package and is redesigned separately).
- **Admission and classification** (`channel.ts`, `connection-identity.ts`, `tunnel-principal.ts` types, `device-token-binding.ts`): a client is `local_operator` only when the handshake attested direct loopback, and `tunnel` only when it carries a relayed device key (set by the next PR). People, owner devices and invites are disclosed only to the local operator or an active owner device.
- **Publication** (`publisher.ts`, `publication-retry.ts`, `registration-recovery.ts`, `discovery-client.ts`, `gateway-key.ts`, `stale-seq.ts`): publishes the descriptor and a K_gw-signed membership snapshot to Discovery, retries failures with backoff, refreshes before the snapshot ages out, and recovers a registration that Discovery lost.
- **Mailbox and notices** (`mailbox-reader.ts`, `owner-notices.ts`, `device-mail-relay.ts`): reads the claw's Discovery mailbox (invite redemptions and owner-signed changes) and mails owner notices.
- **Removal effects and People events** (`removal-effects.ts`, `member-activity.ts`, `tunnel-connections.ts`, `people-events.ts`, `owner-expiry.ts`, `owner-lifecycle.ts`, `invite-expiry.ts`): removing a device closes its connections, cancels its runs and revokes its tokens; owners get a keyless `openclawId.people.changed` invalidation.
- **Service and RPC** (`service.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/openclaw-id*.ts`): `openclawId.status`, `openclawId.people` (owner only) and `openclawId.authority` (`check_name`, `prepare`, `commit`, `publish`, `submit`, `register_invite`, `device_mail`).
- **Gateway wiring**: the service is created in kernel state, reconciled after ready and on config reload (`gateway.openclawId` is hot-reloadable), and stopped with the Gateway. `GatewayClientRegistry` gains `subscribeChanges` so People events can observe connections without replacing another owner.
- **Config**: `gateway.openclawId` (`enabled`, `issuerUrl`, `clientId`, `discoveryUrl`, `relayUrl`, `loaderDomain`, `ownerDeviceInactivityDays`, `memberDeviceInactivityDays`) with schema, labels, help and docs.

<details><summary>Notes for review</summary>

- `core-descriptors.ts` was at the 700-line `max-lines` limit, and the protocol-since check needs new methods inline in that table. To fit the three `openclawId.*` rows, the `cron.status` share policy object is now written on one line. Formatting only.
- Exports that only the next PR consumes in production (`device-token-binding.ts`, `tunnel-child/keyfile.ts`) have Knip production-scan entries with a note to drop them with that importer. Focused tests cover them here.
- `tunnel-child/keyfile.ts` is in this PR because K_gw (`gateway-key.ts`) uses the same 0600 key-file loader; the tunnel child itself is in the next PR.
- The `openclawId.people.changed` event is allowlisted for iOS and Android: the People page is Control UI only.

</details>

## Review

An independent review (GPT-6 Astra) found four issues in the code carried over from the staging branch. All are fixed here, with regression tests:

- Two concurrent first loads of the claw record could each read it; a late read could replace a committed change (for example restore a removed owner device). The first read is now shared.
- Turning the switch off did not cancel a mailbox long-poll already in flight; its response could still be applied. The request now carries the stop signal, and a stopped reader applies nothing more.
- `openclawId.authority` `publish` did not check ownership, and its result names the owner account. It now requires a current owner, checked before and after publishing.
- A config reload while running ignored changes to `discoveryUrl`, `loaderDomain` and the inactivity windows. A change now restarts the service.

ClawSweeper's review of `fbdae28` found three more; all are fixed in `e9522d1`, each with a regression test:

- **Token restriction kept until revocation is confirmed.** A removal used to delete a tunnel token's device-key binding before revoking the token, so a failed revocation left a valid, unbound token that ordinary ingress would accept. Now the token is revoked first and only confirmed revocations (or already-absent tokens) drop their binding. A token whose revocation failed stays bound to its removed key, so every ingress keeps refusing it, and the next start retries it (`orphanedTokens`: bindings whose key is no longer in the membership).
- **Each mailbox statement settles before the next.** A `root_statement` message with several statements now applies each committed statement's effects (close connections, cancel runs, revoke tokens) before the next is submitted, so a later failure cannot discard an earlier removal's effects.
- **Stop cancels Discovery.** Every Discovery request carries the service's lifecycle signal, which stopping remote access aborts, and a 30-second deadline that also covers reading the body (long polls get their wait plus 30 seconds). Startup publication no longer holds the reconcile queue, so turning the switch off or stopping the Gateway is never queued behind a stalled publication.

A second ClawSweeper pass (on `e9522d1`) found two more, fixed in `9269511` with tests:

- **Device mail rechecks authority at the network boundary.** The relay now rechecks the caller and the exact owner-device certificate it signed with immediately before the request leaves for Discovery, not only after the response. A device removed (or the switch turned off) during signature verification sends nothing.
- **A stopped mailbox reader submits nothing more.** Within one `root_statement` message, the reader's stop signal is checked before each statement; a statement already committed still gets its effects.

**Fixed, maintainer decision (2026-11-04): read saved token bindings at Gateway start even with the switch off.** A token whose revocation failed, or any token issued over the tunnel, stays bound to its device key across a restart with the Labs switch off:

- `service-token-bindings.ts` reads the local claw record once at Gateway start (`server-runtime-state-prepare.ts`, before any listener admits a connection). It publishes the binding owner only when saved bindings exist, so a Gateway without them behaves exactly as `main`. No process, socket or remote service is touched; `service.inert.test.ts` gains a case for this read.
- `checkDeviceTokenPeer` is now async and waits for that read, so a connection that arrives during boot cannot slip past it.
- Fail closed: if the claw record cannot be read, every device token is refused (`device-token-bindings-unreadable`) until the switch turns on or the Gateway restarts, and a security warning is logged. Shared-token and password auth are unaffected, so the owner keeps a way in.
- This replaces the earlier "switch off reads nothing" contract with "switch off reads only the local claw record".
- Tests: `service.token-bindings-start.test.ts` (restart with the switch off, a check that arrives mid-read, no saved bindings, unreadable record) and `device-token-binding.test.ts` (the read gate, unreadable refusal). The ingress callers arrive in #192345, which adds an HTTP test against the real claw store.


**ClawSweeper's review of `08d444e`: replayed mailbox revocations (P1), fixed by #193146.** A captured revocation replayed through the mailbox after an owner approved the device again removed it again. The repair is in the protocol package (#193146, credited to @SebTardif's #192230): a revocation now names its claw and the seq its signer saw, and removes only keys listed at or before that seq. This PR adds the Gateway side:

- `mailbox-reader.test.ts` drives the real authority through `applyMailboxMessage`: revoke, approve again, replay. The replay is refused with `seq_conflict`, the device stays admitted, and no removal effects run. The test fails when the protocol's seq check is removed.
- Invites stay bounded: the sweep that expires pending redemptions now also deletes spent invite records (cap expired, nothing pending) with their reports (`service.invites.test.ts`).
- **Claw record size.** The two-row split described in the previous revision was not enough at every cap; see the storage fix below.

**ClawSweeper's review of `f7b57d3`: member details and record size (two P2s), fixed with a maintainer decision (2026-11-05).**

- **Member names and emails survive invite expiry.** They used to live only in the approved invite report, which the expiry sweep deletes. They now live in the Gateway's existing user profiles, keyed by the exact OpenClaw ID account (provider `openclaw.id`). The reported email is display data only: it is never an alias, never merges profiles and grants nothing. Approval times are kept in their own row. Existing approved reports move into profiles on load, before their name and email are cleared.
- **Every row fits at every cap.** The claw record is stored as rows for the core record, owner devices, members, invites, invite reports, approval times and token bindings. They are written in one transaction and read from one snapshot, so a reader never sees half of a write. At every protocol cap, with every text field at its longest in escaped control characters, CJK and emoji, the largest row is 845,313 bytes, under the 1,048,576-byte limit. A missing row fails closed; a record in the earlier layout loads and moves to the new rows on its next write.
- **An uncertain write does not leave stale authority.** If storage commits a write but reports a failure, the authority is withdrawn until a re-read shows which state is durable. It never restores a removed device.
- Unsigned Discovery fields (owner account, mailbox cursor, verified account id) longer than 256 characters are refused, not stored or truncated.
- An independent review of the repair found two further issues (a lost write acknowledgement and a re-added member losing their details); both are fixed with regression tests.

**ClawSweeper's reviews of `ee1977a` and `d204141`: one P2, fixed with a test.**

- **A stop during owner-notice preparation sends nothing.** `notifyOwners` captured the service lifetime only after importing the notice sender, so turning remote access off during that import let the notice adopt the next lifetime's signal. It now captures the lifetime first. `service.owner-notices-stop.test.ts` holds that import, turns remote access off, then releases it and checks that no notice is sent; it fails when the capture follows the import.
- CI guards: the three `openclawId.*` methods are marked `since 2026.11`; the config schema is in the PR wrapper inventory; chained type assertions are gone and new assertions carry `SAFETY` notes; the type-only cycle between `authority.ts` and `binding-check.ts` is removed; the profile provider constant is renamed so it is not counted as an environment variable; the profile reader is listed as worker-only; and the experimental-features page has the OpenClaw ID section that the config docs link to.
- The mocked token-binding round-trip test is removed: real persistence and reopen coverage already exercises it.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/openclaw-id` plus the profile owner's tests: 30 files, 202 tests passed on `90b82ce603c`, including the review regressions. `service.stall.test.ts` runs the real service and Discovery client against a Discovery that never answers: turning the switch off completes and aborts the publication and mailbox requests, well inside the request deadline (it times out against the previous head). The config schema, `hello`, method, broadcast-scope, config-reload and client-registry suites also pass.
- `authority.test.ts` checked the stored record for secrets by matching any `kit` substring, which random signature text can contain, so it failed intermittently. It now matches secret-named fields and the `OCK1-` kit text.
- **Labs switch off** (new `labs-off.test.ts`, plus `service.inert.test.ts` and the `hello` test): with the switch absent or `false`, even with a linked claw record and every service URL configured, the service spawns no child, opens no `net`/`dgram` socket and calls no `fetch`; every `openclawId.authority` action and `openclawId.people` is refused for the loopback operator; `openclawId.status` reports `off` and no link; `hello` advertises no `openclawId.*` methods or events.
- Rebased onto `main` at `0afeaad457c`. The only conflicts were two generated config-baseline files, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, the core test typecheck, `pnpm build`, changed-file lint and `pnpm config:docs:check` pass on this head.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-gateway-core.txt` allocates the 4,446 test lines this PR adds, and the ratchet passes on this head. They are new tests for new surface; no existing tests were replaced.
- **Stored data:** a claw record in the earlier one- or two-row layout loads unchanged and moves to the new rows on its next write (`claw-store.persistence.test.ts`). The protocol's new listing seqs and invite creators are optional, so staging records load unchanged. `claw-migration.test.ts` loads pre-allowlist records and rewrites them once. No released OpenClaw version has OpenClaw ID state, so there is nothing to upgrade from a stable release.
- The staging lab Gateways run this code (openclaw `1bc84010c2e`, whose Gateway and UI sources match this stack before the rebase fixes). The staging gates recorded in #191469 exercise this authority through the tunnel: removing an owner device also removes the device it approved, the next published snapshot lists neither, and the 21st owner device is refused with `limit_reached`.

## Production-path proof and landing

This stage cannot be exercised end to end on its own. Nothing on ingress calls `checkDeviceTokenPeer` until #192345, and a relayed device needs that PR's tunnel plus the iroh binding (#191470). The maintainer decided (2026-11-05) to land this stage on the unit and real-storage evidence above, and to supply production-path proof (allowed access, removed-device refusal before effects, saved bindings enforced after a restart with Labs off) on a real Gateway once #192345 and #191470 are in. The notice-preparation race is in-process and has no I/O to observe; its regression test above is the proof.

**Inherited CI failure:** `checks-node-compact-small-13` fails `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` ("keeps private Control UI servers and resource-sensitive files under one serial owner"). Main's #193856 added `ui/src/e2e/agents-settings-delete.e2e.test.ts` without registering it with the Control UI e2e owner. This PR changes no UI or e2e files, and the test passes on this branch without the merge.

prs.title: fix(ios): Rewind overwrites text and attachments added while the request is pending
prs.body:
Closes #193817

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unsent text and attachments added to the iOS composer while a Rewind request is in flight are silently overwritten when the request completes.

## User Impact

User impact: people who edit the composer during a Rewind now keep their newer text and attachment selections, while the history rewind and branch reconciliation still complete. When the composer is untouched, Rewind restores the earlier prompt and images exactly as before. No migration or user action needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewindToMessage` restored the editor text and the full attachment array unconditionally once the request succeeded. The change captures the composer's text and attachment revisions when the request starts and restores the rewound prompt and images only when the composer stayed unchanged, treating the composer as one draft so rewound content is never mixed into newer edits. Attachment edits now advance their own per-session revision (the existing revision tracked text only), and programmatic restores are excluded so they are not mistaken for user edits.

## Evidence

Not run yet: this package builds and tests only with Apple tooling (macOS/Xcode), which was not available while preparing this change, so nothing has been compiled or executed. CI on this PR is the first validation; please treat the change as unverified until the macOS Swift package suite runs.

- New regressions in `ChatViewModelSessionActionTests` cover text-only, attachment-only, and combined composer edits through the existing controlled-completion gate, and assert that history refresh still completes when restoration is skipped. Each fails against the pre-change code, where the restore was unconditional.
- Existing controls are preserved by construction of the guard: the unchanged-composer case (`rewind seeds editor and refreshes history`) still restores, and the different-session completion case in `ChatSessionCompletionOwnershipTests` is untouched.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed against current main (85c39026a90f).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes a missing response join in a Workshop browser fixture that can reload or issue another plugin mutation before its enable request finishes. Separate lifecycle contention remains under investigation.

## User Impact

prs.title: docs(signal): document the group ingest option
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/channels/signal.md` enumerates the supported fields of `channels.signal.groups` twice — once in the Groups section and once in the Provider options list — and both enumerations stop at `requireMention`, `tools` and `toolsBySender`. `ingest` is a live field of the same group entry: it is what makes mention-skipped group messages reach the internal `message:received` hook, and nothing in the Signal docs points at it.

- Problem: `channels.signal.groups.*.ingest` is undocumented while the pages that claim to list the group-entry fields omit it.
- Solution: add `ingest` to both enumerations and state what it does, what it does not do, and how the `"*"` entry and the default behave.
- What changed: `docs/channels/signal.md` (3 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two enumerations are the places readers already go to for per-group overrides, and each is written as an exhaustive list, so the missing field reads as "not supported" rather than "not mentioned". Telegram documents the identical group `ingest` option on its own access-control page, so leaving it out of Signal breaks the cross-channel symmetry users rely on. The wording follows the runtime contract verified below: mention-gated messages stay in the group history window, `ingest` only adds hook delivery, and the check is strictly `=== true`.

## User Impact

Users can discover and set `ingest: true` to observe mention-skipped group messages through `message:received` hooks — for example to log or route group chatter without waking the agent — and can tell that it never starts a turn, that `"*"` supplies the value for entries that leave it unset, and that omitting it keeps the hook silent. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/signal/src/config-schema.ts:155-160` declares the field on the group entry:

```typescript
const SignalGroupEntrySchema = buildGroupEntrySchema(
  { ingest: z.boolean().optional() },
  { omit: ["skills", "enabled", "allowFrom", "systemPrompt"] },
);
```

**Runtime type** — plain `z.boolean().optional()`, no enum leaf to track. `buildGroupEntrySchema` (`src/channels/plugins/config-schema.ts:75-89`) starts from `ChannelGroupEntrySchema` (`:60-69`: `requireMention`, `tools`, `toolsBySender`, `skills`, `enabled`, `allowFrom`, `systemPrompt`) and drops the four omitted keys, so the documented set `requireMention`, `tools`, `toolsBySender`, `ingest` is exactly the accepted set for a Signal group entry.

**Default** — off. `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:1060` requires a strict `true`:

```typescript
(signalGroupPolicy.groupConfig?.ingest ?? signalGroupPolicy.defaultConfig?.ingest) === true
```

The fallback chain is per-group entry, then the `"*"` entry (`src/config/group-policy.ts:128`: `const defaultConfig = groups?.["*"]`), then unset — so an omitted `ingest` never fires the hook.

**Consumer** — `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:1020-1092`, inside the `isGroup && requireMention && canDetectMention && mentionDecision.shouldSkip` branch. The skipped message is logged, recorded into the group history window, and then — only under the condition above — handed to `fireAndForgetHook(triggerInternalHook(createInternalHookEvent("message", "received", …)))` before the branch `return`s without dispatching a turn. The event name matches the canonical hook documented in `docs/automation/hooks/event-types.md:33` (`message:received`). Scope comes from `extensions/signal/src/config-schema.ts:162` and the account base, so it applies to `channels.signal.groups` and `channels.signal.accounts.<id>.groups` alike.

**Test** — `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts:243` exercises the inherited form with `"*": { requireMention: true, ingest: true }`.

**Docs toolchain** — all run against this exact head:
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,398 internal links, 0 broken
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass, 1,421 files, 1,381 fences validated
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md` (`pnpm docs:check-mdx`) — pass, 1,425 files
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check` (`pnpm format:docs:check`) — clean, 1,413 files
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix for an already-shipped option; the Signal mention-gating implementation is unchanged, so no runtime reproduction applies.

**Exact head** — `ee27e7b2fef6f232dfd3372a303601c79041aeb1`

prs.title: fix(browser): release extension debugger when idle and keep user color scheme
prs.body:
## Problem

With an `extension`-driver profile (Chrome/Dia signed-in browser via the OpenClaw extension), the browser keeps showing **"OpenClaw started debugging this browser"** long after any agent work has ended, and attached tabs report `prefers-color-scheme: light` even when the OS is in dark mode.

Two causes:

1. `connectBrowser` caches the Playwright adapter per CDP URL for the life of the browser service. While that client stays connected, the relay keeps `chrome.debugger` attached to every tab it touched, so the infobar never clears.
2. `connectOverCDP` applies Playwright's default context overrides to the browser's default context, including `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia` with `colorScheme: "light"` and focus emulation. On a user's own browser this changes how their sites look.

## Fix

- **Idle release:** when the last profile operation lease ends on an `extension` profile, schedule `retirePlaywrightBrowserConnectionExact` after `EXTENSION_IDLE_RELEASE_MS` (60 s). New work cancels the timer; work in progress is never interrupted. The next operation reconnects. Role refs survive through the existing target-keyed ref cache; frame-scoped refs need a fresh snapshot, as after any reconnect. Managed (`openclaw`) and other drivers keep the current caching.
- **noDefaults:** the extension relay connection passes Playwright's `noDefaults: true`, which skips the default media/focus overrides on the default context. Explicit `browser emulate` still works.

## Proof

- New `server-context.extension-idle-release.test.ts`: releases after idle, timer restarts on new work and never fires during work, managed profiles untouched.
- `vitest run` on the new test + `server-context.stop-running-browser`, `extension-relay/relay-lifecycle`, `pw-session-cdp-transport`: 16/16 pass. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean.
- Live, on a Mac node host (2026.10.10-beta.4 with the equivalent dist patch) driving Dia through the extension: `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` is `true` after attach (was `false`), and 60 s after the last action the node logs the adapter retirement and close for the profile.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #192896. This repairs the same invocation-cancellation gap for `infer audio transcribe`.

The CLI does not forward its existing invocation abort signal into the existing media execution context. Ctrl+C is accepted, but the transcription provider request remains pending until the normal launcher terminates the process instead of completing cooperative cancellation.

## Fix

Preserve @wangmiao0668000666's fix: obtain the existing async-work signal and pass it to `transcribeAudioFile`'s existing `MediaExecutionContext`, with its normal abort fence. No new cancellation owner, retry policy, flags, schema, auth, model-facing guidance or video behavior change.

Remove explanatory comments, the new test-registration helper and its duplicated option builder. Keep attribution/hints coverage in its original suite and add audio to the existing local/Gateway cancellation matrix, retaining its no-output and resource-cleanup assertions. Update the existing Audio CLI documentation.

## Evidence

[Built CLI / real PTY before-after receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193893#issuecomment-6675585631).

Independent Linux runtime builds, secretless `node:24.22.1`, shipped `openclaw.mjs` entry point in a genuine controlling terminal. Reused #192896's PTY driver. After a complete valid WAV multipart upload is pending, a real Ctrl+C/VINTR produces SIGINT to the terminal foreground process group. Normal launcher behavior is preserved; there is no OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN override, second interrupt, or harness kill.

Faithful local OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/transcriptions` fixture: valid ordinary response after 10 seconds processing latency, passive peer-close observation, synthetic local-only key. No fault injection or provider mocks imported into the CLI.

| Build / interrupted run | Exit | SIGINT → exit | SIGINT → HTTP close |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Main 1 | SIGKILL (`waitpid -9`) | 2022.3 ms | 2020.3 ms |
| Main 2 | SIGKILL (`waitpid -9`) | 2229.1 ms | 2226.9 ms |
| Candidate 1 | **130** | **116.7 ms** | **3.6 ms** |
| Candidate 2 | **130** | **102.8 ms** | **2.1 ms** |

All interrupted cases make one request, complete zero provider responses, and print no success envelope/transcript. Candidate output is only the normal interrupted/cleanup notice; PTY bytes are drained through EOF and fixture handlers observed through completion. All harness safety-kill flags are false.

Uninterrupted controls on both builds exit 0 and complete exactly one response. Captured request/envelope equality is asserted after normalizing only owned filenames and unique run/transcript markers: same provider openai, model gpt-4o-transcribe, language en, audio.transcribe envelope, 16,044-byte WAV and SHA-256. No external provider or live user state is used. Separate explicit profiles/HOME/config/state/workspaces; exact binary config/SQLite paths verified. This local path starts no Gateway. Config bytes stay unchanged.

116 focused controller/lazy-registration tests passed; final exact infer controller coverage 110/110. Typed lint, focused test typecheck and formatter passed. The consolidated audio cancellation row fails on frozen main; 109 other controller cases pass.

Whole-PR deltas: production **+10/-5 (net +5; 15 gross)**; tests **+13/-15 (net -2)**; docs +3/-0. Contributor commits preserved. No allocation file or test-only production hooks.

Private test-host details from the previous body have been removed. The complete proof is reproducible using only task-local loopback endpoints; retained evidence is under `proofs/193893/pty-a3/`.

## Merge risk

Low: only the audio CLI supplies an already-supported execution context. Normal transcription request hints, provider attribution and successful output remain unchanged in the paired control. Cancellation uses the existing invocation and media owners. Reverting restores process escalation on interrupt; no stored-format, configuration, protocol or migration concern.

prs.title: fix(pr): accept historical CI after later branch pushes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prior-CI admin admission rejects a valid completed run after another commit is pushed to the same PR. This blocked the reviewed recovery for #193843.

## User Impact

Maintainers can reuse qualified historical CI through the existing native workflow after a later branch push. There is no product UI change.

## Why This Change Was Made

GitHub refreshes `pull_requests[].head.sha` inside historical workflow responses to the PR's current head. The completed run's top-level `head_sha` continues to identify the tested commit. Admission now uses that immutable field for the tested head and the associated PR number/base repository for provenance. Run, attempt, workflow, conclusion, job gate, reviewed delta, ancestry, and current authority checks retain their existing owners.

The observed successful run [42147390163, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42147390163/attempts/1) reports tested head `e9431ed0322bdec896987d4a6e9333e975a8e61a` while its associated PR snapshot reports later head `39e7fe68d101b31b329c68d9752a633a94b32a5d`.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New historical `pull_request` integration case on original production code | Fails at the observed provenance rejection (4.68 s) |
| Native prior-CI admission suite | 116 passed, 242.47 s test time / 243.56 s wrapper wall time |
| Tooling test typecheck and focused lint | Passed |
| Formatting, JavaScript syntax, diff and test-line checks | Passed |
| Independent Codex review of final change with complete owner context | No actionable P0–P2 findings |

The regression uses the existing native Git/GitHub fixture boundary, exercises the REST squash outcome, retains dispatch coverage, and verifies rejection of a different immutable run head. The full owner suite also covers authority revocation, repository/publisher mismatches, merge ancestry/tree, security, stale review, and cancellation evidence. Its subprocess-based native admission checks account for the suite's runtime; no local broad suite or live merge probe was run.

Production owner LOC: 1,316 → 1,315. Test/support LOC: 2,182 → 2,186; the four-line regression allocation matches that growth. Documentation adds three lines. No new abstraction, runtime state, dependency, or policy exception.

Fixes: chat image navigation and the item counter disappear when each reply contains only one image, even though the thread contains many assets. Inline Markdown images also bypass the gallery.

- Images embedded in Markdown share the image gallery with user uploads and assistant attachments; repeated URLs retain their own positions.
- Recovered messages retain their effective document-mode rendering, so visible remote and oversized recovered images also open correctly.
- Escape restores the original trigger focus. Image/video gallery separation, per-message source authority, foreign-session exclusion, lazy resource loading, and unloaded-history boundaries remain intact.
- Sidebar image activation retains its one-argument callback contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expand the existing cached transcript-membership owner from turn to thread scope and migrate every internal caller. Discover eligible inline slots lazily using canonical sanitized Markdown rendering rather than a second parser, loader, or mounted-DOM thread scan. Rendering and slot discovery share `resolveMessageMarkdownRender` for the effective source and options, including recovered document mode. Disclosure belongs only to its own mounted message, never sibling messages. Preserve the current upstream Markdown preparation/options helpers, regenerate the boot-module manifest, and document the behavior.

## Evidence

- Missing counters were reproduced through the bundled UI for a single-image reply among eight loaded images and for inline Markdown images. Synthetic before/after screenshots are below.
- The recovered-image finding was reproduced through actual mounted-renderer clicks: a short remote-image Markdown recovery and a 40,001-character full-message recovery both displayed an image but called `onOpenImage` zero times on the previous head. Both pass after sharing effective source/options.

The documented per-change allocation records exactly this growth; the shared scalar is unchanged. Proof-only screenshot I/O is not retained in committed regression tests.

prs.title: fix(matrix): message bursts become separate turns despite messages.inbound debounce
prs.body:
Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: chore(codex): test warm claim settlement and scope revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Tests-only regression coverage; no runtime source change or production fix in this PR.** The proof target here is that a failed owner leaves no orphan native-thread claim and a later attempt can reuse that thread.

A Codex-backed conversation can reject the next turn as “claimed by active work” after failed ownership settlement, even though the failed attempt is no longer running. The existing cleanup lacks targeted coverage at the warm-claim cleanup and monitor-setup revocation seams.

Related: karmaterminal/openclaw#1431 (the queue-behind-*genuinely active* work request is separate and remains open).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. These tests protect the existing claim-release behavior against regressions that could strand subsequent Codex attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inject a lease-settlement failure after proving warm claim transfer (without a cold resume), and separately revoke session binding authority during monitor setup. Assert cleanup clears each claim and the same native thread can be claimed by a follow-up attempt. The latter is **scope revocation, not a simulated binding-store lease expiry**. The tests complement the existing lifecycle cleanup; they do not implement queueing behind active work.

## Evidence

- Based on upstream `main` `6ba6ad224ae` (2026-10-25); two Codex app-server test files only.
- Focused Codex app-server suites: 2 files, 21/21 tests passed on upstream base.
- Exact PR head 14bf56f9ea33: [GitHub Actions changed-extensions-config](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121349722824) ran both changed test files, 21/21 passed. Its log includes the warm lifecycle injected-failure test and the monitor-failure binding-scope revocation test; the latter asserts a completed follow-up turn on the same native thread with the claim cleared. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121351049271) passed. These are fixture-driven in-repo assertions, **not** a shipped Gateway/CLI lease-loss trace.
- Extension test typecheck, targeted format and lint pass; line-cap ratchet passes against `upstream/main` for the two changed files. (The default local ratchet base is `origin/main`, a divergent fork, and falsely flags unrelated upstream files.)
- No live service change or end-to-end field reproduction claimed.

**Follow-up proof correction (2026-10-27):** A Claude source review found the monitor case calls `releaseBindingAuthority()` (binding scope, not simulated lease expiry); the warm case now asserts ownership is held at the injected settlement fault and no cold `thread/resume` occurs before it. Updated head `71d416664521dc5f51bf3e6ac2a435786f91f07c`: focused Vitest 21/21, extension-test tsgo, targeted oxfmt/oxlint and diff check passed locally. Hosted CI is pending; no live lease-expiry or production fix is claimed.

prs.title: fix(postgres): settle staged authority at physical commit
prs.body:
### problem and change

PostgreSQL write transactions omitted the shared staged commit-preparation phase. Unknown native outcomes also unwound through ordinary rollback callbacks, which can restore authority whose revocation may already be durable.

Prepare staged predicates and authority fences at the physical writable COMMIT. For canonical unknown outcomes, an acknowledged COMMIT followed by guard failure, or failed rollback cleanup, invalidate all staged savepoint state before retiring the connection. Confirmed rollback and known rejected COMMIT retain their existing settlement.

This uses the existing publication invalidation contract and SQLite sibling behavior. It adds no recovery mechanism.

### scope and review

- Production: **+22 net lines**, confined to the PostgreSQL transaction owner.

prs.title: fix(telegram): route bound conversations when agent selection is ambiguous
prs.body:
Closes #159334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram conversation with an active session binding fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` on a multi-agent install that has no channel-wide Telegram route, so its messages are never processed.

## User Impact

User impact: runtime-bound Telegram conversations reach their bound agent regardless of how many agents are configured. Conversations without a binding, or whose binding names no agent, keep today's behavior — including still requiring an explicit channel owner. A binding revoked or replaced while a message is being routed no longer leaves the former owner selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareTelegramConversationRoute` asked ordinary agent selection for a route before looking at the binding, and ordinary selection refuses an ambiguous roster. It now selects the base route inside the SDK's `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync({ resolveRoute })` (and `inspectRuntimeConversationBindingRoute({ inspection, resolveRoute })` for route-owner inspection): the binding owner's canonically classified `boundAgentId` arrives before ordinary selection, and when it is set the base route is derived from session-only config with that agent as the default. This is the shared binding-owner selection Slack, Discord and iMessage use, so Telegram no longer re-implements the session-key/metadata classification. Topic overrides, configured bindings, and the runtime-binding step that follows are unchanged.

### Binding changes during resolution (review follow-up)

An earlier revision chose the agent from a synchronous binding read and then let `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync` read the binding again after an `await`, so a binding revoked in between could leave the former owner selected; that revision guarded it with a re-prepare/retry loop.

Since merging current `main` (`4ee4606`), agent selection runs inside the `resolveRoute` callback of the single awaited inspection, so the agent and the binding facts come from the same read. There is no second read to diverge from, and the retry loop is gone. The same applies to `prepareTelegramConversationRouteInspection` (new on `main`), whose `resolve(inspection)` now selects the agent from the inspection it is handed. `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` shares the inbound path with `touchBinding: false`.

## Evidence

New cases in `conversation-route-owner.test.ts`, all on a two-agent config with no route bindings:

- inbound `resolveTelegramConversationRoute` selects the bound agent and session, reports `runtime-bound`, and touches the binding once;
- `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` selects the bound agent without touching liveness;
- a sentinel `global` session with `metadata.agentId` selects that agent;
- a binding that names no agent still rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED`;
- a binding revoked just before the awaited inspection rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` instead of routing to the former owner;
- a binding replaced just before the awaited inspection routes to the new owner and its new binding.

Negative controls: with `main`'s `conversation-route.ts` (`4ee4606`), 4 of these 6 fail with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` (the bound-agent, inspection, sentinel-metadata and replacement cases); the no-agent and revocation cases pass there, as intended, since both assert that rejection.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts
19 passed (19)
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram
passed 63 Vitest shards
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
0 errors
```

Focused regression cost: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts` — 19 tests, 16.4 s Vitest duration / 20.8 s wall time locally. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the assertion SAFETY ratchet are clean on the changed files. The test fixture uses `agents.entries` (the authored shape since `agents.list` was retired on `main`).

**Live Telegram proof:** not included. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` harness needs Convex-leased team credentials, which I don't have as an outside contributor. The evidence above is unit-level through the real binding-routing SDK with a test adapter.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the change and ran the tests and negative controls above locally.

prs.title: fix(onboard): keep IPv6 discovery hosts bracketed in remote URLs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The remote-setup wizard rebuilt the direct WebSocket URL from the **bare** discovery host
(`wss://${host}:${port}`), dropping the IPv6 brackets that `buildGatewayDiscoveryTarget`
already adds via `formatHostForUrl`. When a discovered Gateway advertises an IPv6 host, the
wizard produced an unparseable URL like `wss://2001:db8::1:18789` and used it as the actual
connection target (`discoveryRemote.url`), so direct connection failed.

The same bare host also leaked into the connection-method label and the trust prompt.
The SSH tunnel hint is left raw after `@` on purpose: OpenSSH cannot resolve a bracketed
destination (`ssh <user>@[::1]` fails with `Could not resolve hostname [::1]`), so URL
authorities get brackets while the OpenSSH destination keeps the raw host.

Precedent: #190942 (bracket IPv6 discovery hosts in gateway-status / discovery), #192029
(IPv6 proxy listener URLs).

## Why This Change Was Made

`onboard-remote.ts` decodes `{ host, port }` from `target.endpoint` and rebuilds the URL by
hand instead of consuming `target.endpoint.wsUrl` (which `resolveGatewayDiscoveryEndpoint`
already brackets correctly). The fix routes the host through the same existing
`formatHostForUrl` helper used by every sibling consumer (`gateway-status.ts`,
`bonjour-discovery.ts`, `gateway-discovery-targets.ts`, `proxy-server.ts`), applied once as
`hostLabel` and used for the label, direct URL, and trust prompt. The SSH hint keeps the
raw `host` for its OpenSSH destination (brackets are invalid in an `ssh user@host` command).

No new helper, option, or config surface. Non-IPv6 hosts are unchanged (`formatHostForUrl`
returns the input as-is when it contains no colon).

Production LOC is `+3/-3, net 0` (plus one import line).

Classification: `behavior-preserving`

## User Impact

Operators connecting to an IPv6-advertised Gateway through discovery now get a working
`wss://[2001:db8::1]:18789` URL instead of a broken `wss://2001:db8::1:18789`. Hostname and
IPv4 discovery hosts (the common case) behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Shipped-CLI real behavior proof (terminal logs)

Drove the real `openclaw onboard --mode remote` wizard over a PTY in an isolated
container, on head (`1d213ff6adc`) and base (`d2a166c6ac6`), with a synthetic
`avahi-browse` fixture advertising an IPv6 beacon (`[2001:db8::1]:18789`, TLS pin
`sha256:abcdef...`). Full reproduction:

1. Build `dist-runtime` matching the exact head/base (`build:docker` + runtime-postbuild, stamps clean).
2. Run `openclaw onboard --mode remote` under a PTY with `PATH` pointing at a stub
   `avahi-browse` that emits the IPv6 beacon (no real mDNS host needed).
3. Feed the wizard: QuickStart(enter) -> Bonjour confirm(yes) -> pick the discovered IPv6
   Gateway -> connection method -> trust(confirm) -> accept the suggested URL -> save.
4. Capture the raw terminal log; redact nothing further (fixture host/pin are synthetic).

**HEAD `1d213ff6adc` — direct mode (GREEN, bracketed):**

```text
◇ 找到 1 个 Gateway
◆ 选择 Gateway
  ● IPv6 Gateway ([2001:db8::1]:18789)
◆ 连接方式
  ● Direct gateway WS ([2001:db8::1]:18789)
◆ 信任这个 Gateway？主机：[2001:db8::1]:18789 TLS 指纹：sha256:abcdef...
◇ 直接远程访问
  直接远程访问默认使用 TLS。
  Using: wss://[2001:db8::1]:18789
  TLS pin: sha256:abcdef...
◆ Gateway WebSocket URL
  wss://[2001:db8::1]:18789
...
Updated config: <state>/openclaw.json
远程 Gateway 已配置。
```

Saved config at `<state>/openclaw.json`:

```json
"gateway": {
  "mode": "remote",
  "remote": {
    "url": "wss://[2001:db8::1]:18789",
    "transport": "direct",
    "tlsFingerprint": "sha256:abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789"
  }
}
```

**HEAD `1d213ff6adc` — SSH mode (raw OpenSSH destination, unchanged):**

The SSH hint keeps the raw host after `@` on both base and head. Brackets are only valid
inside a URL authority; OpenSSH passes the literal text after `user@` to `getaddrinfo` and
fails with `Could not resolve hostname [::1]` when brackets are present, so the destination
host is deliberately **not** bracketed (see #190942, which explicitly keeps raw hosts at the
OpenSSH boundary).

```text
◇ SSH 隧道
  Start a tunnel before using the CLI:
  ssh -N -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 <user>@2001:db8::1
  Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/remote
```

**BASE `d2a166c6ac6` — same feed (RED, unparseable):**

```text
◆ 连接方式
  ● Direct gateway WS (2001:db8::1:18789)
◆ 信任这个 Gateway？主机：2001:db8::1:18789 TLS 指纹：sha256:abcdef...
◇ 直接远程访问
  Using: wss://2001:db8::1:18789
  TLS pin: sha256:abcdef...
◆ Gateway WebSocket URL
  wss://2001:db8::1:18789
```

```text
◇ SSH 隧道
  Start a tunnel before using the CLI:
  ssh -N -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 <user>@2001:db8::1
```

Base saved `gateway.remote.url: "wss://2001:db8::1:18789"` — an unparseable authority (the
`::1` interior colon is ambiguous as a port separator), which is the defect this PR fixes.
The direct URL (and label, trust prompt, saved URL) is bracketed only on head; the SSH
destination stays raw on both.

The final head behavior splits the two surfaces: URL authorities are bracketed
(`wss://[2001:db8::1]:18789`), the OpenSSH destination is not (`@2001:db8::1`).


The synthetic host `2001:db8::1` is the documentation-only IPv6 prefix (RFC 3849) and the
TLS pin is a fixture value; no real host, credential, or endpoint is disclosed.

### Exact-head proof receipt

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `1d213ff6adc`
- Current-main RED baseline: `d2a166c6ac6`
- Production entry: `promptRemoteGatewayConfig` in `src/commands/onboard-remote.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `formatHostForUrl` in `src/infra/net/hostname.ts` (existing helper)
- Decision surface: direct `suggestedUrl` (and the SSH hint) built from a discovery beacon's IPv6 host
- Recorder/readback boundary: resulting `gateway.remote.url` value in the wizard result
- Acceptance RED: on `d2a166c6ac6`, an IPv6 beacon host produces `url: "wss://2001:db8::1:18789"` (unparseable)
- Acceptance GREEN: on `1d213ff6adc`, the same beacon produces `url: "wss://[2001:db8::1]:18789"`
- Legal control: hostname beacon (`gateway.tailnet.ts.net`) keeps `wss://gateway.tailnet.ts.net:18789` unchanged
- Cleanup: tests use the existing in-memory wizard prompter and mocked discovery; no Gateway,
  session, token, or config touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN

`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/commands/onboard-remote.test.ts
--config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts -t "IPv6"` on Node 24.13.1.

RED (base `d2a166c6ac6`, production code stashed):

```text
FAIL keeps an IPv6 discovery host bracketed in the direct URL
- Expected  + Received
-     "url": "wss://[2001:db8::1]:18789",
+     "url": "wss://2001:db8::1:18789",
      Tests  2 failed | 25 skipped (27)
```

GREEN (head `1d213ff6adc`):

```text
✓ keeps an IPv6 discovery host bracketed in the direct URL
✓ keeps the raw IPv6 host as the OpenSSH destination in the SSH tunnel hint
```

Legal control (hostname beacon, covered by existing "pins a trusted discovery endpoint" shape
and the pre-existing suite): `url` stays `wss://gateway.tailnet.ts.net:18789`.

### Verification

- `sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/commands/onboard-remote.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts` — 26 passed; the one failure (`pins a trusted discovery endpoint`) is a pre-existing token-redaction mismatch in this local shell environment and fails identically on the untouched base. The two new IPv6 tests pass on head and fail on base.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts` — clean
- Shipped-CLI: real `openclaw onboard --mode remote` wizard driven over a PTY with a
  synthetic `avahi-browse` IPv6 beacon fixture (head GREEN / base RED), see
  "Shipped-CLI real behavior proof" above.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+3/-3` (net 0) plus one import
- Test LOC: `+33`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing `formatHostForUrl` helper; no new
  validator, option, or config surface
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none

prs.title: feat(models): end the first provider add in a working chat
prs.body:
Related: #193507, #193655, #193467

## What Problem This Solves

On a first-run agent, adding a provider's API key from **Settings → Models** left the page at "Model required". To reach a working chat, the user still had to open *Set up a model*, find the saved key among 20+ rows, run **Test & use** and then go back to chat. Measured with an instant provider, that took 21.7 s and 6 clicks.

## User Impact

- **Agent with no usable model yet:** **Save provider** now also activates the saved key, and the dialog ends on "Added {provider}. {model} is ready to chat." with **Start a new chat with {model}**. That is the same action the sign-in flow already ends with.
- **Agent that already has a model:** keeps it. Adds behave as before, with only the save-time check from #193507.
- **Activation outcomes:** a rejected key (auth or billing) keeps the dialog open with the reason, as the save-time check does. Any other failure leaves the key saved, closes the dialog and points to Test access (#193655).

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the last of the Models UX audit's top three fixes. Activation reuses the existing owner and check behind **Test & use**: `openclaw.setup.activate` with `saved-auth:<profileId>`, where the profile comes from the `models.authSetApiKey` receipt. There is no new Gateway method or protocol change. Activation replaces the save-time probe on this path, so the provider still gets one check, not two. Native session catalog consent stays at its default (off), as in Model Setup.

The add dialog's handlers move from the page controller into `config-actions.ts`, which already owned the add save. This keeps the controller under its line cap (735 → 729 lines). The activation and Start chat logic lives in a new sibling, `add-provider-activation.ts`.

## Evidence

**New real-Gateway E2E** (`model-add-provider-to-chat.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`): a first-run agent and a fake provider that answers immediately.
- **On main it fails:** the dialog never offers a chat.
- **With this change it passes:** Add account → choose Tencent → paste key → Save provider → Start chat → send "Hello" → reply "pong", without visiting *Set up a model*.
- Measured from Add account to the reply: **4.7–6.4 s, 4 clicks before typing** plus Send. The audit baseline was 21.7 s and 6 clicks.
- The model is written to config, and every chat request carries auth.

**Updated:** `model-setup-provider-errors.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`. Adding its first provider now runs one check (the upstream returns 500, so the dialog closes). The test asserts that, then counts Test & use's requests from zero, so it still proves one request with no retry ladder.

**Also pass:** `model-key-save-check`, `model-provider-remove-in-use`, `model-api-keys` (real Gateway), `model-providers` and `model-provider-usage-outcomes` (mocked), `ui/src/pages/model-providers` unit tests (249/249), and `vitest-ui-e2e-config` (15/15).

- Autoreview (Claude engine): no findings.

prs.title: fix(update): Gateway stays stopped when an update is interrupted during Doctor
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway stays stopped when an update is interrupted by a signal during Doctor, and `openclaw update repair` does not bring it back.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C, `SIGTERM` or a supervisor stop during an update now ends with a running Gateway: rolled back to the previous version when activation had not finished, or on the new version once verified. If the updater itself is killed, `openclaw update repair` restarts the Gateway the update stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Problem

A signal during an update's activation stage (Ctrl-C, `SIGTERM`, a supervisor stop) while the update's Doctor runs left the Gateway stopped. The update reported `Database rollback could not finish (data at risk: rollback-state-unverified)`, and `openclaw update repair` exited 0, named `openclaw gateway start`, and left it stopped. Reported in the update-reliability sweep by #193263's native lanes.

### Root cause

The signal cancels the CLI's command work scope (`CliPluginInvocationResources.beginClose`). Everything still running in that scope reads an aborted `getAsyncWorkSignal()`, including the rollback the updater had just committed to. `assertGatewayOwnerLeaseStopped` threw `AbortError: CLI stopping (SIGTERM)`, which surfaced as `failed to acquire gateway state ownership` and was labelled data at risk, before anything had been restored.

Native cause chain from a patched build:

```
GatewayLockError: failed to acquire gateway state ownership
  cause: AggregateError: Gateway owner lease inspection and cleanup failed
    cause: DOMException [AbortError]: CLI stopping (SIGTERM)
```

### Fix

- `runMutableUpdateRecovery` (the mutable-signal owner) runs recovery in the CLI's cleanup scope, which exists so command cancellation does not abort the reads needed to release resources. Forward commands are still stopped through their own forward scope.
- Rollback compensation, database restore, activated-state inspection, finalization, terminal preparation and the recovery unwind all use it.
- Recovery may record receipts after the signal. Forward writers before activation are still refused.
- A direct `openclaw update` records its `service-stop`, so `openclaw update repair` restores the Gateway when the updater itself is killed. Before this only the managed handoff recorded it.
- Restarting a stopped service no longer refuses on a `gateway.state.lock` left by a dead non-Gateway owner such as a killed Doctor.
- An interrupted restart reports `the update was interrupted` instead of a generic `AbortError`.

No schema, protocol or config changes.

### Accepted limits

- A signal that kills Doctor while it holds an unresolved spawn reservation still fails closed: `Doctor processes remain unsettled, data-at-risk` and `Another update executor owns this installation` from repair. That refusal is deliberate process-custody safety and is unchanged here; seen once at the post-plugin Doctor kill point.
- Pre-activation interruption still reports `unexpected-error` (`Could not record update step ...: requester-revoked`) with the Gateway healthy and untouched.
- Doctor's step can still show `requester-revoked` beside the interruption, because that error is how interruption reaches forward guards.

Production change is small and has one owner (`update-command-mutable-signals.ts`); call sites only opt in.

## Evidence

Native proof on Crabbox AWS Linux, systemd user Gateway, real `openclaw update`. Base `f3739110ca5` reproduced the bug and showed its cause; the green builds came from this branch rebased on `ec702e83388`, target package relabelled 2026.11.99. The last two commits only change test fixtures and move one import.

| Kill point | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SIGTERM`, first Doctor | exit 143, unit inactive, `rollback-state-unverified` | exit 143, rolled back after 144 s, unit active, `/readyz` ready, `rolled back: interrupted` |
| `SIGTERM`, post-plugin Doctor | restart refused (`GATEWAY_RESTART_PREPARATION_REFUSED`), unit inactive (rebased build without the lock fix) | rolled back after 100 s, unit active, ready |
| `SIGKILL` of the updater group, first Doctor, then `update repair` | repair exits 0, unit stays inactive | repair refused once while the surviving Doctor child held state, retry exits 0: `Managed Gateway started and verified after update repair`, unit active, ready |
| `SIGTERM`, plugins / restarting / finishing (earlier head of this branch) | `post-update-failed` | Gateway healthy at all three; `rolled back: interrupted` or `update failed: interrupted` |

The #191201 managed `update.run` kill points were unchanged on `5ded78c6572`: pre-swap ready +130 s rolled back; mid-swap ready +190 s recovered; candidate Doctor ready +185 s recovered; no recovery rows left.

Tests: `update-command-interrupted-recovery.test.ts` (rollback acquires state ownership after CLI cancellation, and the same acquire is refused in the cancelled scope), a stop-intent test in `update-command-service-maintenance.test.ts`, and a stale-lock test in `gateway-owner-lease.test.ts`. A targeted run passed 201 of 202 with one skip; CI is the broad proof.

Not proven: Windows and macOS natively (Linux only), and a published release as the driver. The helper and updater come from the version that starts the update, so published 10.10 and older keep today's behavior until a release contains this. No stored data format changes: `service-stop` is an existing ledger step, so ClawSweeper's data-model compatibility ask does not apply here.

Reviews: `$autoreview` scoped-clean, independent Codex review NO FINDINGS (both on `5ded78c6572`).

prs.title: chore(perf): measure slash menu phases independently
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The compound slash-menu benchmark mixed four open/filter/navigation cycles, which hid first-use loading cost and the cost of reopening an already loaded menu. Add opt-in isolated open, reopen, and filter cases, plus a series case that records a separate native input-to-DOM-commit interval for each phase. Catalogs contain 54 built-in commands plus 0, 50, 100, or 200 synthetic plugin commands.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers can separate cold-open, warm-open, and filtering costs instead of ranking one compound action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime windowing experiments were rejected. This investigation PR is closed unmerged: no runtime candidate met the phase’s performance and size gates. Mounting 13 options instead of 254 reduced rendering work, but the lazy window added opening overhead, regressed short-list reopens, and grew both route boot surfaces. Rechecking with main’s generated-name normalizer (#193843) leaves +333 B on Chat and +333 B on New Session; no budget was raised. Combining the window with the existing options boundary moved roughly 9 KB into New Session preloads. This PR retains the reproducible workload and changes no UI code, styles, dependencies, or budgets.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | Passed |
| Focused script lint / format | Passed |
| Native-input timing review | Independent P0–P2 review: no actionable finding |
| Production-bundle census, Chromium and WebKit, desktop/mobile | 144 observations passed; three rotated base/candidate/base pairs per cell |
| Chromium 6×, desktop/mobile | 72 observations passed; three rotated base/candidate/base pairs per cell |

Timing results are discovery evidence, not a 20-pair performance acceptance claim. WebKit has no CPU-throttling API. The experiments use the existing synthetic Gateway and production HTTP server, so they do not measure live Gateway/provider latency. The per-phase measurements exclude the driver's initial delivery prefix; compound outer timing is not used to rank these phases.

LOC: +92 benchmark lines; 0 production UI or test lines retained. No changelog entry: benchmark tooling only.

## Verdict

No qualifying full-flow crossover was found at 54, 104, 154, or 254 commands. Filtering starts to pay around 104 commands at native speed; warm reopens start to pay around 154 under Chromium 6× and around 254 in WebKit. First-open and short-list regressions prevent a general recommendation. These are three-pair discovery results with A/A controls, not a twenty-pair acceptance claim.

Representative native application medians (milliseconds):

| Flow | Base → lazy window |
| --- | --- |
| WebKit desktop, 54 commands, reopen | 15 → 26 |
| Chromium desktop, 254 commands, first open | 49.4 → 72.2 |
| Chromium desktop 6×, 254 commands, first open | 422.9 → 519.4 |
| Chromium desktop 6×, 254 commands, reopen | 145.5 → 94.1 |
| WebKit desktop, 254 commands, filter | 17 → 7 |

The bare catalog is 54 commands. Nine bundled plugin command registrations and eligible workspace/user skills may increase it; the source does not establish how common hundreds of commands are. The 254-command fixture deliberately adds 200 synthetic plugin commands.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep asset hash renames out of size budgets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated asset hashes change compression dictionaries across the Control UI graph. A CSS-only or tiny code change can consume hundreds of bytes of JavaScript budget without comparable code growth; name churn can also hide real compressed-code growth.

## User Impact

Budget checks now distinguish code size from generated-name noise. The application and served assets are unchanged. Reports keep actual served gzip, Brotli, and raw bytes beside normalized budget bytes (JSON schema 2).

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing collector, shared by the strict check and `ui:check-performance:base`, replaces only the eight-character hash suffix of known built assets before compression. Stems and extensions remain intact. Build and collector share compression eligibility, including the case where a rename makes an asset gain a sidecar. Unchanged inputs reuse their compression result. Module attribution continues to report served gzip.

The generated-name allowance drops from 192 B to the 64 B toolchain floor. Main's normalized measurements set the route caps and startup baseline; no ceiling increases. The existing 512 B intentional startup-growth allowance remains. Main's raw CSS ceiling is preserved.

## Current-main calibration

Built runtime from main `ce8b7add7b0` after resolving the shared cap conflicts:

| Surface | Normalized gzip | Served gzip | Budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 90,280 B | 90,664 B | baseline 90,280 B + existing 512 B growth + 64 B variance |
| Chat | 1,288,134 B | 1,295,896 B | 1,288,198 B |
| New Session | 797,556 B | 802,742 B | 797,620 B |
| Largest JS | 560,286 B | 564,246 B | 560,350 B |
| Total CSS | 324,608 B | 324,898 B | 324,672 B |

## Evidence

Two production builds of `970519e950d` on the same Mac used the same fixed build identity. The only experimental change selected hexadecimal instead of base64 asset hashes; it was removed before commit. All **2,794 emitted JS/CSS bodies** match byte-for-byte after normalization. Raw bytes and request counts are unchanged. All normalized gzip and Brotli deltas are **zero**.

| Surface | Served gzip before | Served gzip after rename | Served delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 90,589 B | 90,527 B | −62 B |
| Chat boot | 1,295,038 B | 1,294,388 B | −650 B |
| New Session boot | 801,801 B | 801,030 B | −771 B |
| All JS | 17,668,681 B | 17,664,881 B | −3,800 B |

All-JS served Brotli moved −7,428 B. Startup retains 3 JS requests and 1 CSS request. These are measurement corrections, not application transfer savings.

### Historical attribution

Each row compares the named change's retained or reconstructed pair. These deltas cannot be inferred from cap changes alone.

| Change / Chat JS | Normalized gzip delta | Name contribution | Served gzip delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| #193666, reconstructed original source pair | +506 B | −83 B | +423 B |
| #193689, retained pair | +282 B | −299 B | −17 B |
| #193807, refreshed retained pair | −17 B | +34 B | +17 B |
| Selector indexing, retained final pair | 0 B | +180 B | +180 B |

#193666 was rebuilt from `b5c8a1f3f03` → `db80d94ca0b` with identical dependencies, build identity, and 23 byte-identical plugin inputs. Chat raw bytes shrink 103 B but normalized gzip grows 506 B; normalized Brotli shrinks 275 B while served Brotli grows 455 B. Its deleted original +429 B result cannot be decomposed exactly: this row is a controlled reconstruction.

#193689 adds 776 B raw; New Session is unchanged after normalization despite −248 B served gzip. In #193807's refreshed pair, New Session is −18 B normalized versus −69 B served; the earlier +419 B claim is not this retained pair. Selector indexing's +221 B New Session served delta is entirely name noise; its earlier +812 B experiment was discarded.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Controlled strict base/renamed comparison | Pass; zero normalized deltas |
| `control-ui-performance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 47 pass, including real growth, missing sidecars, and archived-base CLI proof |
| Rename regression against original collector | Fails on Brotli equality (98 B vs 78 B); green with fix |
| Module attribution / Vite precompression tests | 1 + 1 pass |
| UI, tooling-test, scripts-test types; targeted lint | Pass |
| Final build / strict budget evaluation / production Knip | Pass |
| Independent P0–P2 review | Five clean scoped reviews across implementation and conflict resolutions |
| Final exact-head CI | `42150420409`, attempt 1, passed on `39e7fe68d10`; required app suites completed |

An initial CI-only tuple inference error was corrected with a const assertion and the exact scripts-test leaf passed. One prior-head form-controls focus-style timing failure passed focused tests on both base and head, then passed a single diagnosed CI rerun. Final-head CI passed.

Production/tooling LOC: **1,990 → 2,055 (+65)**. Tests: **1,285 → 1,351 (+66)**. The focused diff is 198 additions / 57 deletions in 10 files. No dependency was added. No visual behavior changed, so screenshots are not applicable.

Landed through native cancelled-request recovery as `00ddcde27521ca792ec20faf21347c68ba233fa2`, using successful same-head CI and an empty admission delta. The native landing-parent audit and managed-worktree closeout completed. The separately discovered historical CI provenance bug is tracked in #193904.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first streamed output in a long session repeats persisted-history preparation. This follow-up to #183800 retains that prepared data in the existing bounded pane/session/projection cache, while preserving the canonical live placement and grouping path. Live builds copy mutable wrappers and sets; changed history/display inputs invalidate preparation, and successful older-page prepend releases it.

**Qualification is still in progress; auto-merge is off.** Published head: `3c469ce3f71e3f26327727d31bb65d0c071f0e6f`. Refreshed local runtime: `17a6f22aa4a87f8e6d5c9da66db37e40d33c6142`, based on main `9d9bda2f1cee1ca5e63a889af1742514b89ea85a`. Local `0e411c13fee` adds benchmark-only error timing. The results below use the refreshed frozen runtime; earlier distributions are superseded and are not pooled.

| Incremental history | 31 tests passed; onset work-count regression fails on base. Covers history/display invalidation and live Canvas isolation. |

The frozen FRV2 node-worker launch-wire test exceeded its 240-second whole-test budget in run 41801390334, job 126478301449. The single hosted diagnostic reproduced that timeout and directly recorded the abort during the final Gateway restart. It does not establish a failed worker launch or a causal timing repair. A local unchanged-source replay passed; that is not a flakiness verdict.

This task-scoped draft adds only a push-triggered diagnostic workflow and the previously exercised logging-only patch. - Requires a new non-default branch and run attempt 1; later pushes and reruns do not repeat the test. No dispatch, schedule, or test retries.
- Uses read-only contents permission, no sudo or secret inputs, and a 30-minute job limit. Uploads only synthetic source/patch, runner, runtime, install/build/test, and phase evidence, including on failure.
- Deliberately omits the original privileged semantic-check provisioning and preceding shard tests. Those differences remain interpretation limitations.
- Does not modify production/test source on this branch, the ready candidate export, main, or any release artifact. Keep this PR a draft; no normal-CI/FRV rerun or merge is requested.

[Run 41812802068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41812802068), attempt 1, [job 126515974323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41812802068/job/126515974323), head `33d9f32f98580e2bb6dc0b19300ee1f795cc6ac2`: **failed at the original test timeout**.
