prs.title: feat(agents): explain the effective tool set for a session
prs.body:
Closes #192712

## What Problem This Solves

When a tool the agent expects is missing, the operator had to guess why. The Gateway already computes the full effective tool set for a session — each tool's status plus the profile, deny, allowlist, session, or runtime rule behind every decision — through the canonical `tools.effective` RPC, but no CLI verb exposed it.

## User Impact

`openclaw agents tools <sessionKey>` prints the effective profile, the Gateway's filtering notices, and one row per tool with its status and the deciding reasons; `--json` returns the raw diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owner and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and transport failures exit non-zero in both output modes.
- Registered under `agents` because the `tools` root is deliberately reserved.
- The command defaults its runtime to `defaultRuntime`, matching the other agents commands that are invoked without an explicit runtime from the registration wrapper.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents-tools.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` → 32/32 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`). The first live run exposed a real defect (the command was invoked without a runtime, crashing the error paths) which was fixed before this head; the fixed build shows the correct failure contract:

```text
$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "unknown session key \"agent:main:main\"" },
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:main" }            (exit 1)

$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Tools diagnostics failed: unknown session key "agent:main:main"
                                                (exit 1)
```

The Gateway log confirms both live requests (`⇄ res ✗ tools.effective ... errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown session key`). The isolated store has no sessions, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, tool-policy, or config changes.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): ignore commented and escaped wikilinks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`wiki lint` treats commented-out and escaped `[[wikilinks]]` as live links. It reports false broken-link warnings and writes incorrect Referenced By relationships into otherwise valid pages. Active links and genuinely missing targets must keep their existing behavior.

## Fix

Reuse the existing mdast literal ranges when extracting links, and respect odd/even backslash runs before the opening brackets. Keep the title, human Notes and OKF code-range helpers code-only through their existing default behavior. No new link syntax, semantic retrieval policy, schema, storage format or prompt text.

The original @zhangguiping-xydt commit is retained. Its added standalone CLI test is consolidated into existing strict Markdown, lint and related-index fixtures; earlier active, missing-link and backlink oracles are unchanged. The allocation file is removed. Whole-PR deltas: production +30/-16 (net +14, 46 gross); tests +5/-5 (net 0), with no allocation or scalar changes.

## Evidence

[Normal built offline Linux CLI proof, raw captures and inspected generated pages](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193469#issuecomment-6675152479): Node 24.22.1, Docker `--network none`, real `openclaw wiki init` / `wiki lint`, four independent vaults/profiles and persistent native SQLite with a stored plugin blob. Main twice reports four false warnings plus the true missing target and writes a false Literal backlink. Candidate twice reports only the true missing target and writes no false backlink.

Controls in all four runs: ordinary and even-backslash links retain their backlinks; genuinely broken links still warn; inline/fenced links stay literal; code-only titles are unchanged; authored bodies and human Notes (including café, comments and trailing spaces) remain byte-identical. No model, Gateway, bridge or external Obsidian acceptance is claimed.

Focused Markdown, lint, related-index, OKF and Notes checks pass (56-case batch plus the final related-index recheck). Main rejects the strict link/lint fixtures and final backlink graph oracle for their intended literal-link failures. Repository type-aware lint and formatting pass. The follow-up commit changes tests/bookkeeping only; production runtime-proof inputs are unchanged.

## Compatibility and Risk

Two-way door: revert restores the prior link-counting behavior. Blast radius is Memory Wiki link extraction and derived lint/backlink output. Human blocks, code-only title/Notes masking, source selection, retrieval ranking, authentication, Doctor/update behavior, storage formats and retention policies are unchanged.

prs.title: docs(tlon): document the configWrites key
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The configuration reference table in `docs/channels/tlon.md` lists the keys a Tlon section accepts — `enabled`, `ship`, `url`, `code` and the rest — but omits `configWrites`, the gate that decides whether the channel may apply `/config set` and `/config unset` requests arriving from chat. Users cannot find it from this page.

- Problem: `channels.tlon.configWrites` is missing from the Tlon configuration reference.
- Solution: document the key, its enabled-by-default behavior, the commands it gates, and the per-account inheritance.
- What changed: `docs/channels/tlon.md` (1 line).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key is live configuration: `tlonCommonConfigFields` declares it and both `TlonAccountSchema` and `TlonConfigSchema` spread that same shape, so `channels.tlon.configWrites` and `channels.tlon.accounts.<ship>.configWrites` are accepted, and the shared config-write policy consults the key for every channel-originated write. The wording follows the row already used for the same key in `docs/channels/signal.md` and `docs/channels/whatsapp.md`, and the table it lands in is the same reference list the neighbouring `enabled` row belongs to.

## User Impact

Users can allow or deny Tlon-initiated config writes per ship account without reading source, and see that writes stay enabled until the key is set to `false`. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/tlon/src/config-schema.ts:31` declares the key inside `tlonCommonConfigFields` (line 28):

```typescript
configWrites: z.boolean().optional(),
```

`extensions/tlon/src/config-schema.ts:51-52` spreads the same shape into `TlonAccountSchema`, and `:55-56` spreads it into `TlonConfigSchema`, which adds `accounts: z.record(z.string(), TlonAccountSchema)` at line 60 — so the key resolves at both root and per-account scope.

**Runtime type** — `extensions/tlon/src/types.ts:11` derives `TlonAccountConfig` from `z.input<typeof TlonConfigSchema>`, so the key reaches the plugin as an optional boolean. The equivalent slot in the shared messaging-account contract is `src/config/zod-schema.channel-messaging-common.ts:79` (`configWrites` inside `CommonChannelAccountSchema`, line 75).

**Default** — the runtime default is enabled, from `src/channels/plugins/config-write-policy-shared.ts:66-67`:

```typescript
const value = accountConfig?.configWrites ?? channelConfig.configWrites;
return value !== false;
```

Anything other than `false` allows the write, so an omitted key allows it.

**Consumer** — `src/channels/plugins/config-write-policy-shared.ts:52` (`resolveChannelConfigWritesShared`) resolves account-then-channel scope through `resolveChannelAccountEntry` at line 61 and is reached through `authorizeConfigWrite`, which `src/channels/plugins/config-writes.ts:16` aliases to `authorizeConfigWriteShared`. `src/auto-reply/reply/config-write-authorization.ts:20` calls it with `{ channelId, accountId }` taken from the message origin, which is how a Tlon turn is evaluated.

**Test** — `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-gating.test.ts:449` ("blocks disallowed /config set writes") drives the denial path with a channel that sets `configWrites: false` and asserts no config file write happens; `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts:227` pins the account-level path `channels.telegram.accounts.work.configWrites`, the same resolver this key reaches.

**Docs toolchain**
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,398 internal links, 0 broken
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/channels/tlon.md` — pass
- `oxfmt --check docs/channels/tlon.md` — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix; the config-write policy is unchanged. No runtime behavior proof applies.

**Exact head** — `5f64c007bd76941fafd2a12980ca7ccee03543b4`

prs.title: fix(release): accept qualified candidate plugin artifacts without repacking
prs.body:
Related: #136392

## What Problem This Solves

Release preparation rejects a qualified candidate's already-produced plugin npm artifacts when publication tooling comes from a different reviewed commit, blocking reuse of the original artifacts and risking unnecessary repacking.

## User Impact

Release operators can carry the qualified candidate's original plugin package bytes into publication preparation while retaining distinct publication tooling. This is a prerequisite tooling repair only: it does not select a publication commit, establish release eligibility, or publish a release. No version changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing prepared-npm authentication owner across preparation, sealing, reload, package loading/consumption, dispatch, and publication. The original candidate (Q) remains the npm artifact producer and immutable policy source; publication tooling (P) retains publication decisions and ClawHub dispatch. Preserve exact artifact/archive checks and revalidate the original FRV attempt and live authority at the effect boundary instead of treating Q's artifacts as P-produced.

## Evidence

- The real dispatch-prepare CLI entry path fails on the unchanged base with normal exit 1 for the Q/P descriptor mismatch. With the repair it persists the original Q descriptor, preserves distinct P tooling, reads Q policy, and dispatches only the ClawHub dry run. Revoking live authority before dispatch denies the POST.
- Original archive/tarball authentication and consumption have separate owner-level proof. The CLI regression uses in-process execution and synthetic external GitHub/git transport; it is not a hosted operation or ordinary standalone Node-startup proof.
- Final affected validation: 12 suites, 579/579 tests (33 unit-fast + 546 tooling), zero skipped. Focused owner replay: 25/25; corrected fixture suites: 233/233; unchanged baseline: 132/132 after supplying the missing real unzip prerequisite. No archive-verifier relaxation or mock unzip was used.
- Changed-path formatting, scoped production/test lint, tooling-test and scripts typechecks, and the full workflow checks passed. The initial workflow check refused empty local token bindings; the read-only check passed after removing those empty bindings.
- Fresh independent review of the exact integrated patch: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Structured local autoreview: scoped-clean; unchanged repository context was unavailable to that review. The product and test sources remain byte-identical to that reviewed tree; the subsequent budget-only change was separately checked below.
- The first PR CI run, [42129886341](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42129886341), exposed the test-line ceiling: this change adds exactly 505 net regression-test lines. All other baseline ratchets passed. A narrow tracked `config/test-lines-allocations/qualified-candidate-plugin-artifacts.txt` allocation records those 505 lines for real CLI adoption/revocation, original-byte authentication/consumption, and affected workflow fixtures. The shared scalar, test sources, and assertions are unchanged. The local test-line ratchet was reproduced red before the allocation and passed with the staged allocation; `git diff --cached --check` passed.

Remaining boundaries: this does not prove hosted authentication, OIDC, environment grants, actual npm publication, release-line eligibility for 2026.9.37, or final exact-C/Q/P full release validation. Those remain separate release-coordination gates. The independent review predates the final aggregate validation completion; the final validation record supplies the completed totals above.

Prepared source commit: `55e79b83a596816b95bc1e98c889a84077a74200`, based on `071ea8338d93e55c9a55e0504ac0ea95257dad23`. The reviewed source patch covers 13 paths (+855/-59); its retained artifact SHA256 is `e550834bff18dd542a507580abaea451a67d65500280727a3635a67fb04e32ce`. Per-path diff content matches the commit exactly (patch ordering/index abbreviations differ). The budget-only follow-up adds one four-line allocation file, for 14 paths total (+859/-59). Existing human coauthor credit is preserved without amending the original commit.

prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): avoid warm chat reload backtracking
prs.body:
**Draft — final-head qualification refresh underway.** Current candidate `92b7d95f2026a1aa55148532408a7bf69e6ec2dd`, rebased onto `bc47d05a49fb9a051798e3a9f9f3a27738d5030c`. Full P2 review is clean, including current-main measurement-marker integration. The runtime is unchanged by the lint repair; duplicate browser frame waits were consolidated and exact test allocation is now **251**. **All numerical performance/full-suite results and images below are prior-head evidence from `c82c9becb7dce1406b57243e0dc8a2c4e0d0b0bb`, not final-head execution.** Native, changed-file, quiet-AWS paired, full UI and CI proof is being refreshed before readiness.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload of an active chat initially follows estimated row heights. New rows are then measured and the transcript moves backward to the real end. A later tool-group completion can repeat the correction. This changes a complete cached page after it has already painted.

In the Team-scale synthetic fixture, one replacement produces 278 px of retained-row movement, including 76 px of excess movement; two rounds produce 346 px, including 144 px of excess movement. The prior-head candidate produces 202 px of forward movement and no backtracking in all 11 pairs of each variant; the bounded same-instance one-round repeat confirms another 11/11 (22/22 one-round pairs overall). Readers away from the end remain fixed in all 11 pairs of both variants, with no missing anchor frames.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic end follow now chooses its destination from the existing native measurement batch, after the mounted destination viewport and virtualizer sizes agree. It no longer starts a scroll against provisional row growth. Arrival retires the existing scroll command through its owner. Manual smooth scrolling retains its synchronous destination preparation.

Warm reader restoration joins the same batch rather than performing a competing synchronous measurement during commit. Actual insertion of older history keeps the existing before-paint measurement contract at the prepend-anchor owner. This distinction is necessary: simply delaying every anchor until the next native batch regresses continuous reading across older-history insertion. The full destination viewport is prepared when several turns arrive at once.

No new store, configuration, protocol field, database or cache shape is introduced. This replaces the competing warm measurement/scroll path; it does not add a second layout pass for warm replacement.

## User Impact

Cached transcript content retains its rendered height until its content actually changes. A reader's position stays fixed. A view following the end moves forward once per real replacement, without reversing. In the two-round fixture the first append adds 168 px and the later tool completion adds 34 px; the candidate follows those two real changes without the baseline's provisional 240 px target and 72 px correction.

**Documented lead exception:** visible movement is the campaign's primary harm. The lead accepted removal of backtracking (76 → 0 px and two-round 144 → 0 px in 11/11 pairs), with the painted reader excursion fixed, despite the historical cost of **+34 ms total blocking, +19 ms blocking and +21 ms forced style/layout in the 700–1300 ms replacement window, and +7 ms final rows**. The lead determined that this cost delays no visible content and accepted it under the same precedent as #190925. **This is an explicit lead exception, not a passing blocking secondary.** The final-head measurements below are reported separately; this exception does not silently waive a newly discovered cost.

## Evidence

**Prior-head qualification; final-head refresh is running.** Frozen candidate `c82c9becb7dce1406b57243e0dc8a2c4e0d0b0bb`, control `ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d`. All comparisons use the same quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge` lease, `cbx_5d2725c38aa6`, repository Chromium, the existing Team-scale bench and `live-fast` latency profile. Measurements are unprofiled, with the standing LoAF/mutation and RPC probes. There are 11 interleaved pairs per block. The tables below retain all **132 completed pair deltas**: the required 88 plus A/A controls and one bounded repeat for each noisy secondary block. No adverse block has been discarded. The supplemental run reused the same instance; two immediate preflight CPU samples were 100% idle.

[Native/performance/full UI run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2c891a8416a6f338af15dc58babeb359); [bounded same-instance A/A and end repeat](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_67634abe4989bd035f6e2a22a928782b).

Current paired medians: one-round total blocking **+28 ms**, window blocking +4 ms, window forced style/layout −10 ms; its bounded repeat is **+27 ms total blocking**, +10 ms window blocking and −6 ms window forced style/layout; two-round total blocking +11 ms, window blocking +2 ms, window forced style/layout −5 ms. These do not turn the blocking exception into a passing claim. Hello handled, FCP and first cached rows show no qualified adverse result on any route. RPC count and census payload deltas are zero in all 132 pairs.

**Final-row timing is inconclusive, not a passing claim for the original block.** The original one-round raw final-row DOM result is **+64.4 ms (10/11 worse)**. The bounded same-box repeat reverses to **−36.3 ms (7 better / 4 worse)** with overlapping IQRs. Its A/A is **+16.3 ms (4 better / 7 worse)**; the original A/A is **−40.8 ms (8 better / 3 worse)**. Both candidate blocks and both controls remain in the tables. This does not establish a repeatable final-row regression under the campaign's controlled/noise rule; it does not broaden the blocking exception.

The fresh reply is complete when it appears, so this case is not explained by a hidden tooltip. Original request sent / history received / DOM after receipt paired deltas are **+2.3 / +68.2 / −3.8 ms**; the repeat is **−6.9 / −41.1 / −3.5 ms**. Response receipt is stamped before application dispatch. A separately labelled two-run queue-eligibility capture, excluded from the gate, locates the wait before dispatch: eligible→dispatch **101.2 / 158.2 ms**, handler **0.5 / 0.6 ms** (control/candidate). It locates the late timer delivery; it does not prove an unrelated network cause. All 132 gate pairs use the unmodified committed probe and fixture.

Dashboard's original window forced style/layout increase is +16 ms (10/11 worse); its bounded repeat is 0 ms with mixed signs, and A/A is −2 ms with mixed signs. Both blocks and the control remain below. These do not establish a repeatable dashboard regression.

### CLS and painted-frame attribution

At the bench viewport, the retained long reply stays 3706.65625 px high from cached paint through live replacement in both arms. Its descendant-text count can gain the same 10-character accessibility label in both arms without changing height. Current main already retains the same displayed long-reply content; the remaining motion is caused by provisional new-row heights and the real tool-completion height change, not a cached-text expansion.

One-round end CLS is 0 in both arms. Two-round end CLS is **0 → 0.0013041388 in all 11 pairs**. This residual is caused by the candidate's measurement/end-follow ordering around a real tool completion; it is not presented as an improvement.

In the separate final-head frame attribution, the tool group grows **69.5 → 103.5 px**. The following `div.chat-virtual-row` user row moves **y 895 → 929**, and the assistant row **992 → 1026** (its visible clipped region shrinks; its actual height stays 71 px). Chrome records the candidate layout-shift entry at **1239.9 ms**, delivered at 1255.2 ms. DOM sampling sees the growth at 1232.2 ms, the end correction occurs at 1258.0 ms, and the next settled geometry sample is 1268.9 ms. Main has the same content growth at 1235.4 ms and corrects at 1242.5 ms, recording CLS 0. The sampled candidate filmstrip has captures 31 and 32 at 1235.880 and 1268.610 ms around that entry; it can miss intermediate compositor frames, so there is **no claim that the shift was unpainted**. A bounded small compensation attempt did not eliminate the shift and was removed. This source is documented under the lead's requested residual-CLS path.

One-round reader CLS is 0.005196936 → 0; two-round reader CLS is 0.005200725 in both arms. Archived-chat CLS is 0; dashboard CLS is 0.000014081 in both arms.

### Reader-excursion finding

The reported **220 px excursion was in the rejected candidate**, not main: main had 0/11 and that candidate had 2/11. A separate capture reproduced painted excursions in that rejected candidate. Its path was commit → prepend update → synchronous row measurement → virtualizer resize compensation → scroll write. Joining the native measurement batch removes that competing warm path. The final candidate has zero reader movement/excursion in all 11 pairs of both warm-reader variants; continuous reading, older-history insertion, Home-to-end and a trusted native-wheel reader are also covered by the final-head native tests.

### Reproduction

Build the control and candidate UI bundles separately, then run the committed bench on the fixed AWS instance. The two-round end command is:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --gateway-http --warm-reload --untraced --face chat \
  --pane-chrome-facts --details-session-facts --latency-profile live-fast \
  --capture-ms 3500 --runs 22 --transcript-witness --active-transcript \
  --active-transcript-two-round \
  --bundle-dir <control-ui> --compare-bundle-dir <candidate-ui> \
  --init-script <loaf-mutation.init.js> --init-script <ws-rpc-census.init.js> \
  --output <new-output-directory>
```

Remove `--active-transcript-two-round` for one round; add `--active-transcript-reader` for the reader variants. Compare control against itself for A/A. The existing fixture supplies the sidebar preferences, a native persisted snapshot, a retained long reply, new turns and a pending tool group that later completes. Both native regression tests and this proof use the same fixture/probe owners.

### Validation and cost

Final-head focused unit tests: **243/243 across 12 files**. Native browser geometry: **28/28**. Native smoke: prepend **14/14**, continuous reading **3/3**, motion **5/5**, warm reload **6/6**, inline views **2/2**, Home/end **4/4**; separate trusted-wheel desktop reader **1/1** on candidate and **1/1** on pinned main. The new warm regression on pinned main is **3 passed / 3 failed as expected**: both single-append end cases backtrack, and the eight-pair append does not land its destination in one step. Candidate is **6/6**. Script, UI, UI-chat and UI-components type checks pass.

Literal AWS `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times: controller **7.116 s**, prepend anchor **3.937 s**, initial range **3.903 s**, warm native test **35.73 s**, inline-view native test **28.74 s**. Offset-observer and browser-geometry cost receipts and changed checks are pending. The full UI suite completed once on this final head (Vitest **6,112.40 s**, wrapper-observed phase **1 h 44 min 4.6 s**, including setup/cleanup): **933 files, 928 passed / 1 failed / 4 wholly skipped; 3,561 tests passed / 1 failed / 5 skipped**. The sole failure is QA Lab automation management; the same configured-owner/admin/non-owner test fails on clean pinned main with the same POSIX mutation-boundary error. All transcript tests pass. [All 933 file outcomes and main-control classification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193217#issuecomment-6673979357). Exact-head CI will run after readiness. Draft-skipped CI is not counted as proof.

Official fixed-identity performance gate passes: warm-chat startup **1,294,481 → 1,294,538 bytes (+57)** against cap **1,294,735**, leaving 197 bytes. Requests **20 → 20**. CSS **132,377 bytes / 3 requests** in both arms. No budget line changed.

Independent final-diff autoreview is clean through P2. All 15 lane commits rebased patch-identically; current-main renderer/geometry contracts were also supplied for a fresh integration review. The proof probe now reads the existing renderer-owned data-row-size marker after main removed the style marker, completing that consumer cutover.

Runtime is **+51 net LOC**. Retained shared fixture/probe tooling is **+365 net LOC**. The requested filtered stat is **566 insertions / 143 deletions = +423 net LOC** (the filter also retains `.test.tsx` files). Growth is forced by the measured-destination/reader ownership contract, preserving existing older-prefix anchoring, and the requested reusable native regression/paired proof. Test allocation is raised to the **exact 251-line total**, with no slack: native regression 158, shared fixture 81, controller 5, initial range 3, prepend 7, less 3 removed inline-test lines. Constructor-only test/support migrations add no behavior-test allocation.

Trimmed out of the patch: one-off extent/column/block/expansion diagnostics, a standalone capture hook, duplicate witness/re-export and phase/visibility/mode fields. The remaining tooling is used by the regression tests or the reproduction command. Scroll-write, queue-eligibility and detailed CLS attribution probes remain private scratch and are not shipped.

### All paired results

Values are median [Q1, Q3]; deltas are candidate − control. “Backtracking” is the probe's excess movement: sum of absolute anchor displacement minus net displacement. Forced style/layout is accumulated duration from LoAF script attribution, not a count of layout events. The window includes frames starting from 700 ms through before 1300 ms. “Final rows DOM” includes changes to descendant text, including invisible descendants; it is not a standalone visible-paint timestamp. prs.title: fix(test): avoid repeated release fixture compiler starts
prs.body:
Related: #186423

## What Problem This Solves

Release checklist tests repeatedly start Node to strip identical fixture programs for each scenario.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. This removes repeated test setup while retaining every scenario, fresh sandbox, real fixture repository, mock, assertion and cleanup path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare each of six fixed programs lazily at the test-file owner using Node's existing strip-only helper and vm.Script. Reuse compiled code only; each evaluation still creates a fresh VM context. The two singleton checklist programs stay unchanged. Filtered-out programs do no preparation. Selected Node, warning suppression and parser isolation remain unchanged under both Node and Bun.

Production: 0 lines changed. Tests: net -6 lines. No new helper, runtime option, retry, timeout, mock or weakened assertion.

## Evidence

Initial compiled-Script variant, exact head e0295c1056c4bf6c3386118abb096abdc31ee765: **HOLD**. Actual stripping children fell 58 -> 8; every complete run retained the same ordered 149 passing cases. Node26.12.1 and pinned Bun1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 both passed; each representative filtered run passed its one selected case and started zero stripping children. Type-aware lint, formatting and independent source reviews passed for this head.

Five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs; one count-instrumented warm-up per revision excluded. Timed runs used the original, uninstrumented Node helper. Values are median / nearest-rank p95 [min, max]:

| Metric | Baseline | Initial candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall seconds | 17.720 / 18.990 [12.960, 18.990] | 12.840 / 14.130 [10.910, 14.130] |
| Body seconds | 13.545 / 14.836 [9.957, 14.836] | 9.156 / 11.080 [8.406, 11.080] |
| User CPU seconds | 8.720 / 9.800 [7.160, 9.800] | 5.920 / 6.150 [4.720, 6.150] |
| System CPU seconds | 4.670 / 5.000 [3.380, 5.000] | 3.530 / 3.820 [2.910, 3.820] |
| Peak RSS MiB | 479.281 / 484.438 [454.531, 484.438] | 482.531 / 483.422 [477.375, 483.422] |

Median wall improved 27.5%, but median RSS increased 0.7%; the recorded rule is not met. Load averages during timed samples ranged 14.439-22.557 (one minute). The count-only probe explicitly preloaded actual selected-Node parser children; an initial failed probe was discarded because test isolation clears inherited NODE_OPTIONS.

A strings-only alternative restores baseline VM compilation while retaining one-time stripping, but its natural formatted change adds nine ratcheted test lines. Independent source review found no honest removable setup within these two files; it is not being forced past the existing ceiling. That uncommitted alternative was discarded. The retained compiled-Script head remains on performance hold; this draft is not ready to merge.

Acceptance rule, recorded before the first benchmark: run the two complete files in their original case order with supported Node26.12.1 on the same qualified macOS checkout, serial maxWorkers=1, five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs after one excluded warm-up per revision. Measure actual stripping children separately, require identical ordered case names/results, and report wall/body time, user/sys CPU, peak RSS, median/p95 and host load. Counts must be58 -> 8; wall/body/CPU/RSS must hold or improve; record a regression as a hold. Keep cold preparation separate from steady comparisons. Also run complete-file Bun parity and representative filtered checks to prove unused programs stay unprepared.

Any future changed candidate needs fresh source review, full runtime parity and a prospective baseline/candidate comparison; these timings qualify only the retained head.

No Windows, hosted-minute or billed-cost saving is claimed.

prs.title: fix(agents): a quota-class failure should prefer the model chain over a same-profile auth rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a quota-class provider failure (HTTP 429 with a usage/plan-limit body), the embedded agent rotates the auth profile and re-runs the **same** model before the configured model-fallback chain is consulted. When the provider has exactly one usable profile - or when the rotation re-selects the profile that just failed - that rotation is a no-op: it spends a provider attempt against the same exhausted plan and delays the chain that could have recovered the run.

The `rate_limit` path already has a rotation cap that escalates to the model chain (`MAX_RATE_LIMIT_PROFILE_ROTATIONS`), and the `overloaded` path escalates through `overloadProfileRotationLimit`. What is missing is the rule that **a rotation which lands on the same profile is not a rotation at all**.

## User Impact

A quota-class failure now advances the model chain in the same failure instead of burning an attempt on the exhausted profile first. A run that has a working fallback chain configured recovers on the first quota error rather than the second.

## Why This Change Was Made

`advanceAuthProfileCandidate` advances by **index** over the prepared auth attempts. When two prepared attempts carry the same profile id (an OAuth attempt and an inline attempt for the same profile, or two routes for one profile), the "rotation" re-selects the profile that just failed and still reports success. The caller then retries the same model against the same exhausted plan.

The fix keeps profile rotation useful whenever it can actually change the credentials:

- The rotation is reported as a rotation only when the active profile changes.
- When the rotation re-selects the failed profile and a model chain is configured, the controller reports "no rotation", so the failover policy resolves to `fallback_model` and the chain advances immediately.
- Without a configured chain the existing same-profile retry is preserved, so a single-model deployment loses nothing.

Scope notes:

- The `overloaded` path is untouched.
- The session/request model-pin contract (#151980) is untouched; this change is about auth profiles, not model pins.
- The failed profile is still marked in cooldown exactly as before; only the decision to *retry* the same profile changes.

Related: #141115 (a 429 must consult the chain - this PR is the ordering half of that class), #151980 (session model pins stay strict; this change touches auth profiles, not model pins), #186418 (the request-level ladder half, carried by #186420).

## Evidence

Focused test run on this branch (rebased onto main at `fdeb8f7e`):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent-run.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts
    -> Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  42 passed (42)

New coverage in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts`:

- a quota-class rotation that re-selects the failed profile reports no rotation, so the caller advances the model chain;
- a quota-class rotation that moves to a different profile still reports a rotation and still counts toward the rotation cap;
- without a configured model chain the same-profile rotation still retries, so single-model deployments keep their existing recovery.

One existing fixture was updated: "waits for the provider floor before exhausting recovery and rotating credentials" used an `advanceAttemptAuthProfile` stub that returned `true` without moving the active profile. A successful rotation moves the active profile, so the stub now does the same; the assertions are unchanged.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): cached child activity in Details [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload can insert ordinary child-session activity into Details after its other sections, pushing Outputs and Automations down. The original cold-load campaign recorded 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds; this experiment isolates the remaining Subagents insertion.

## User Impact

The proposed change restores the last child-activity preview alongside the populated Details section, then adopts live child results in place. Saved display facts never hydrate the child query or enable child navigation. The experiment is stopped and closed at the unchanged asset-budget gate. The candidate is retained for lead review; no geometry or latency improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Details snapshot retained collection subagents but omitted ordinary child-session activity. Its lazy activity body also had a separate empty loading boundary. The candidate retains a total, tally and at most three preview rows in the existing scoped snapshot, including only displayed labels, status, activity, timing and plan progress. Cached activity joins the existing Details loading boundary; the renderer remains lazy and its projection stays outside the Chat boot module. Live parent-derived activity remains visible if an optional child read fails, while the saved receipt retires.

Runtime growth is **+135 UI lines**. This exceeds the +80-line aim because the complete preview needs bounded validation, observer-derived display capture, and a separate display path that cannot acquire live query or navigation authority. The old tally helper is removed. The prescribed non-test diff is 315 additions / 51 deletions; that command also includes the changed TSX unit test and test helpers. No config option, server record, protocol, SQLite schema, changelog, or performance cap changes.

## Evidence

Unscored native attribution on a dedicated AWS c7a.4xlarge reproduced the lazy-body chain. This attribution used the merged composer PR's source, not the final current-main scoring baseline; its timings are not before/after results.

| Warm capture | First populated Details | Subagents height sequence | Later Outputs / Automations movement |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 1 | 1435.2 ms | 51 → 112 px | 61 / 61 px |
| 2 | 1364.7 ms | absent → 51 → 112 px | 112 / 112 px |
| 3 | 1303.5 ms | absent → 51 → 112 px | 112 / 112 px |

The new native-DOM browser regression seeds ordinary children through the shared fixture, persists the first visit normally, holds reconnect on reload, and checks the first populated frame and the live handoff. It does not fabricate persisted receipts. The native browser red/green case was authored but not executed: the byte gate stopped qualification. The lifecycle unit regression fails against the original production owners and passes with the candidate. Local focused tests passed: Details arrival 11, live activity 1, handoff/activity 28, Details consumers 18. Latest `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-arrival.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`: 3.26 s wall. Other focused files: 3.22 / 2.96 / 3.28 s wall. The exact 293 added test lines have a dedicated allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.

Codex local review is clean through P2 after preserving known live parent facts on child-read failure. No performance win is claimed yet.

### Stop: unchanged byte gate

Matched full builds on one AWS c7a.4xlarge, candidate `407d09f590c8be83df47f0bc5a7328fd8a0d6ce8` against base `605bd6f405dc4619bf77416a9244ac4afd12ee34`, using the repository-owned performance checker:

prs.title: fix(oc-path): stop extra path segments from overwriting frontmatter
prs.body:
Related: #192995 (terminal selector handling for `find`; this fixes concrete resolution and writes).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw path set` silently edits the wrong frontmatter location when an address continues past a key: `name/absent` overwrites `name`, and `name/+added` inserts an unrelated top-level key.

## User Impact

User impact: invalid frontmatter addresses now fail with the existing errors without changing any file bytes. Normal leaf writes and direct container insertions keep working. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Frontmatter keys are terminal leaves. Concrete resolution must consume the whole address; insertion must target the frontmatter container, not a descendant. The existing field-only in-memory calling convention remains supported. @zhangguiping-xydt's original commit is retained; regressions are consolidated into existing owner tables with no net test growth or allocation, and the CLI documentation clarifies the boundary.

## Evidence

[Exact-head built Linux CLI before/after proof, hashes and focused tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193878#issuecomment-6675095173).

Built current main and candidate in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker and ran the shipped CLI with the loaded compiled bundled plugin on real Markdown files. Main incorrectly overwrote/inserted for the two invalid addresses. Candidate returned `unresolved` / `not-writable`, exit 1, preserving the original SHA-256. A normal leaf set and direct container insert produced identical expected bytes on both refs. Literal bare `name/+` already refused on main; the defective insertion was keyed `name/+added`.

The four regression cases fail on main while its other 53 cases pass. Candidate owner suites passed 182 tests; final consolidated universal suite passed all 57. Changed-file format/lint passed. Production +6/-3; tests +15/-15; docs +3.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior behavior; no state migration, schema or public API changes. Blast radius is Markdown frontmatter concrete resolution and insertion through OC Path. A wrong check could reject a valid frontmatter edit; normal leaf/direct-container controls and field-only resolver coverage remain in place.

prs.title: fix: recover conversations after accidental session resets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: accidentally choosing `/reset` clears the visible conversation with no recovery action in chat.

## User Impact

The latest recoverable manual reset now offers **Undo** in the existing Session reset divider, with confirmation. It restores earlier history and the next agent's context. Messages sent after the reset remain on another branch instead of being deleted or silently merged. Undo does not reverse tool actions or file changes.

Automatic or tail-preserving resets are not undoable. Active, queued, or unadopted input must settle before Undo; the operation does not cancel it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing rewind, transcript, and mutation owners rather than adding a recovery store. A deliberate leaf selection opens the requested reset window while ordinary stale controls remain fenced. Validated navigation records exactly which reset IDs were reopened; the planner consumes those facts, and later resets revoke them.

History and model-context projections share one complete navigation-field contract, so restoring the UI also restores the actual model request. Authority and the latest boundary are revalidated before mutation. No database table or migration is added.

## Evidence

### Current published raw-source-hash inventory repair

- Published head: `591578e4a775106f83f791bbc8f3e8a3b165f3e6`, tree-identical to approved source commit `80dbcf7d60a78c3da9ef7ee46388d78031c304b8`, with the exact Jacob coauthor trailer verified. Managed publication completed as `roboclaw-bot`; no main integration or PR merge was performed for this update. Its only source delta from prior published `912b13e7d0597099a05bf0352347d766e790b069` is **one added entry**, `en-chat-reset-confirmation.ts`, in the authoritative `sourceFiles` inventory in `scripts/lib/control-ui-i18n-catalog.ts`.
- The exact prior-head CI failure was reproduced locally before editing: `ui/src/app/vite-config.node.test.ts` → **includes every English dependency in the raw source-hash input** failed with the same reset-confirmation assertion (**1 failed, 43 unselected skipped**). The fragment was already consumed by the catalog composition and its modal; its complete raw bytes were missing from the maintained hash-input inventory. No test, collector, hash contract, snapshot or missing-file guard was weakened.
- After the one-line owner fix, **111 full consumer tests pass**: all **44 Vite-config/source-hash tests**, all **30 catalog tests**, and **37 catalog-verification/deadcode tests**. Scripts and UI type lanes, scoped owner lint, formatting and whitespace pass. These are **implementation-owner-run** results, not independent reviewer-run tests. No test source growth was added; the **853-line allocation is unchanged**.
- The same retained independent reviewer approved the frozen one-line artifact with **no findings**. The committed diff matches reviewed SHA-256 `af632061bb367b63843e4a68510f44578853fefeec25cfda03d0095f21533a59`; whole-checkout/index checks confirmed only that intended path and entry. This approval is limited to the inventory repair, not overall readiness, a performance waiver or a new runtime repair.
- Managed inspection at this updated head reports **open, unmerged, mergeable: false / dirty**. This did not prohibit the authorized branch publication; it does prevent a conflict-free/readiness claim. The reviewed upstream pin remains `9d8bbfbbaf162cda2f5cd620816b6ac8a8bd5d00`. New-head CI must establish its own outcome; **the prior-head run and performance measurements below are not CI evidence for this new head**. No automatic moving-main integration, performance experiment, Android retry or denied upgrade attempt was used to publish this one-line fix.

### Prior 912-head CI and integrated proof — historical scope

- The prior `912b13e7` tree matched reviewed integration `17345dd8af2c24640941d50385244c93021573c5`. Its branch integration restored normal CI eligibility; this was not a PR merge. The single generated-predicate conflict was resolved through canonical generation/check, while source/UI changes auto-merged.
- Exact prior-head [CI run 42132165125](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125) **completed with failure**. Its aggregate selected three failing lanes: [UI source-hash job 127611975030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611975030), repaired locally above; [Android access job 127611975286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611975286), which failed while preparing the Emulator SDK ZIP with **Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel**, before Gradle or tests; and [performance job 127611974700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611974700). Android's setup failure is not product proof, a proven inherited defect or a passing run, and it was not retried. Baseline-ratchets job 127611974942 passed separately.
- The prior cloud performance annotation says **1264.7 KiB chat-boot gzip exceeds 1264.4 KiB**. These rounded values are not the exact local measurements below. A truncated check listing must not be interpreted as all green, and a Security Review target/workflow_run result is not a normal CI result for another head.
- Earlier integrated owner proof passed **368 core/tooling tests**, **90 affected UI tests**, **14 prefix-stability tests**, all five maintained type lanes, targeted core/scripts/root-test lint, formatting, source-line and whitespace gates. These retain their earlier source scope and were not all rerun for the one-line repair.
- The prior test-line checker passed **6,510,614 ≤ 6,510,672**, with **853** allocated regression lines. Earlier full core lint was not green: plugin-model-catalog (702) and supervisor (701) exceeded max-lines with files/config byte-identical to pinned upstream. No suppression or unrelated edit hid them. Complete integrated P2 autoreview returned two chunks with zero actionable findings; that review and the independent pipeline audit below are not passing CI or upgrade proof.

### Final symmetric local asset comparison — failing, independently audited

This measurement belongs to the **prior 912-source candidate**, compared with pinned 9d8; it was **not rerun after the one-line raw-source inventory repair**. Both source roots were prepared with their maintained native UI builders and metadata finalizers for the same **eight declared plugin UIs / 21 assets**, using **Node 26.12.1, Vite 8.3.5 and Pako 3.0.3**, the same installed/remapped dependencies and fixed comparison build identity. The actual performance checker and cap were unchanged.

| Local profile | Chat-boot gzip | Requests | Against the 1,294,735 B cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pinned 9d8 baseline | 1,294,874 B | 20 | **139 B over** |
| Prior 912-source candidate | 1,295,475 B | 20 | **740 B over** |
| Candidate minus baseline | **+601 B** | 0 additional | Not a waiver |

Population records are byte-identical, including generations, normalized declarations and asset names; emitted plugin asset paths/revisions/printed sizes also match. Both have the same 1,751 mapped eager module IDs. The generated plugin-distribution carrier is **3,689 raw / 807 standalone-gzip bytes on both sides**. The preserved archive contains eight manifests, eight package identities and all 21 assets; the auditor verified all 21 recorded asset hashes. Individual module gzip estimates are not additive shipped-bundle attribution.

**Interpretation:** this is a failing symmetric **local** comparison: an independently over-cap local baseline plus a **601 B candidate increment**. It is neither wholly inherited nor a 740 B candidate-only regression. **It does not prove the cloud baseline failed**, identify the exact cloud byte gap, or establish a safe code cut. No asset cap, checker, integrity guard or inventory filter was relaxed.

#### Audit qualifications and recovery evidence

- Preparation used each root's maintained builder, real builder paths, ownership helper and metadata finalizer. The auditor found no argv impersonation or fabricated lease. **Per-root preparation ownership ends before population capture and direct Vite execution**; the adapter does not establish an uninterrupted lease through measurement. The implementation owner ran the recorded preparation/build stages serially, launched no intervening source/artifact writer, and retained clean-tree/diff-identity receipts. Equal emitted inventories corroborate this particular run, not a general concurrency guarantee.
- Baseline source came from the pinned Git archive with workspace-dependency remapping. Candidate measurement used the owned working checkout; its HEAD label alone is insufficient, so clean-tree receipts and equality with reviewed/published source are retained alongside the reports.
- The optional consumed-input signature failed because `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-chat-reset-confirmation.ts` is **absent in the pinned baseline** but present in candidate: **897 bytes**, SHA-256 `2bdf7a36a70c0778e7767528c84c0524922b469e0c06f815090cafafe2a77637`. This is explicitly recorded absence, **not a successful signature check or filtering of missing inputs**. Resume built the baseline normally and ran the unchanged checker; setup failures are not product verdicts.
- CSS normalization used the baseline's own authored CSS and rewrote compression sidecars, not CSS source. Original packaged generations, manifests, hashes, reports, source-tree receipts and the task-only preparation/resume adapters remain in the implementation worktree's recovery evidence. The retained audit was read-only; it did not rerun builds, tests or cloud access.

Two bounded lazy-Undo prototypes saved **152 B** and **76 B** relative to the same candidate profile; their plugin asset rows matched the control. Neither closed the gate, and their additional asynchronous/ordinary-reset coupling was not justified. **Both were restored exactly; neither was committed or published.** No further justified narrow production cut was identified. Larger boot-performance work needs explicitly agreed scope rather than speculative refactoring or a cap waiver. The unresolved performance gate and separate operator-only compatibility proof remain blockers to readiness.

### Superseded asymmetric and historical measurements

The first 9d8 pair reported candidate **1,295,475 B** versus baseline **1,294,201 B** (+1,274 B), but used **21 plugin assets/eight plugins versus seven assets/three plugins**. Settings-only preparation built a subset while the producer consumed all existing completed distributions. The extra distributions were **not shown stale or corrupt** and were not removed. Therefore the entire earlier +1,274 B must not be attributed solely to Undo; the symmetric 139/601/740 accounting above supersedes that attribution.

The [older c531 performance gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42104571414/job/127517378885) reported **1,294,739 B**, four bytes over the unchanged cap. Historical d999 before/after copy-only measurements reported **1,295,147 → 1,294,950 B** (197 B less), raw **4,152,210 → 4,151,855 B**, 20 requests unchanged, and an older 215 B local overage. Those are historical results, not cross-base comparisons, cloud-equivalent measurements or passing evidence for this head.

### Prior source repair and test-allocation rationale

- Source `142914988afb9621516ad0089f2e14c85611c8e6` moved five **unchanged** reset-confirmation strings into the already-lazy modal's English fragment. Before/after snapshots proved complete `chat.board` and `chat.sessionReset` key/value identity; explicit catalog merges preserve both namespaces. Modal props, markup, lifecycle, recovery controllers and authority checks were unchanged by that copy-only repair.
- The [test-lines failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42104571414/job/127517379831) reproduced locally: required regressions added **851 net lines**, plus two catalog-consumer lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/session-reset-undo.txt` therefore records exactly **853 justified net regression-test lines**, as the fix workflow permits. They cover state/Gateway/model-context fencing, retained-history/UI confirmation, real-Gateway/upgrade-fixture proof and catalog ownership. **The shared scalar and shrink rules are unchanged by this PR. Retain this rationale in the squash body.**
- On that earlier tree, 39 UI tests, full catalog/wrapper closure, types, lint, format and line gates passed. All 30 changed-catalog tests passed with one worker in **9.49 s Vitest / 10.46 s wrapper**. These are historical local costs, not current CI estimates. The copy-only delta received a complete P2 pass with zero actionable findings; other earlier reviews retain their stated scopes, not exhaustive independent reproduction.
- Both hosted P2 findings were repaired: generated locale/translation-memory changes were removed under publisher ownership, and the catalog owner preserves eager reset keys alongside lazy Undo copy. Canonical generation/keyless baseline were run, not hand translations. No generated locale/translation-memory changes are shipped by this source PR.
- Earlier pinned proof passed the three CI consumer guard suites (**234 tests**), selected catalog regression (**1 passed, 29 unselected skipped**), owner suites (**104 tests in three shards**) and UI suites (**39 tests in four files**). The interrupted earlier full catalog attempt is not green.
- The [serial-owner gap](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42095199598/job/127484325920) and [trusted wrapper import gap](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42095199598/job/127484325315) reproduced; repairs passed 219 full guard tests and scoped review. Later [E2E inventory assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42098710378/job/127497159725) were repaired using independently declared expected sets, preserving inventory/sharding/phase/worker-cap/parallelism assertions and both provider-removal and reset-Undo cases. No ignore, snapshot waiver or guard weakening was introduced.
- An earlier broad changed-check exited 143 at its deadline amid repository I/O waits. Subsequent checks passed selected SQLite worker/dialect, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race and mock-factory gates on their selected snapshots. Historical results do not replace current-head CI.

### Released-data upgrade proof — BLOCKED

The opt-in fixture uses genuinely installed **OpenClaw 2026.11.1** and its dependencies outside the source checkout, avoiding candidate tsconfig alias contamination. It is designed to create released settings/transcript, stop and snapshot state, replace only the executable, then verify continuity, Undo, reload, next provider request and branch switching.

**No successful upgrade run is established.** The standalone-prefix repair resolved initial source-alias setup failures. The released Gateway subsequently started and created the session, but baseline `chat.send` was explicitly refused by the agent/subagent attribution boundary. The fixture exposes stdout and stderr to make the refusal visible.

This is authority-blocked, not passing compatibility proof or demonstrated migration breakage. **No alternate CLI, WebSocket, browser or CI retry, marker stripping or guard weakening was used.** Human/operator invocation or a boundary-owner-approved attributed fixture route is still required. This separate blocker does not justify bypassing security or declaring source readiness.

### Earlier behavior evidence

Regressions reproduced automatic/tail-reset eligibility, queued/unadopted input preservation, lost model-context navigation and nested-reset fencing. Tree/worker, prefix-stability, model-context siblings, Gateway policy/storage/reader and UI suites passed; `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed on that earlier snapshot.

A real browser, isolated Gateway, actual agent execution and SQLite exercised reset → Undo/confirmation → reload → next provider request containing earlier but not later context → retained/restored branch round trips. Inference was deterministic/local, **not a live LLM**; actual provider input was inspected. The final scenario passed assertions but cleanup hit the infrastructure deadline; recorded child PIDs were later absent. An earlier complete harness run passed. Neither result replaces the blocked upgrade proof or establishes all-green current-head evidence.

Earlier inherited findings included a 701-line `chat-pane-render.ts` count on base and candidate against the 700-line rule, and four medium Zizmor action-pin/version-comment mismatches in unchanged workflows. No suppressions or timeout increases hid them.

### Visual proof

Inspected real Control UI captures with synthetic hiking-plan content and a mock Gateway. Real-Gateway persistence and actual agent-request verification are reported separately above. [Public proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193459#issuecomment-6657339349).

prs.title: feat: preview recommended templates in a compact dialog
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Recommended Templates need an inline preview that lets users inspect their contents without losing their conversation or opening stacked, resizing dialogs.

## User Impact
Users can open a creator-attributed Template reference, inspect workspace files, skills, plugins and automations in one compact dialog, and Add through the existing consent and setup flow. Add opens the new agent’s main session without sending a synthetic chat message or changing the original conversation. No migration or manual production deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made
The approved single-column design uses a viewport-clamped 960 × 680 shell, fixed header/footer, content-only scrolling, accessible arrow-only Back controls and centered detail titles. Named files and View all remain available. Shared file rendering and existing catalog/Add/consent/review/install/session-selection owners are reused; reference-card UI loads on interaction.

Prerequisite #193765 is merged and integrated once for correct test-allocation attribution. Its 96 inherited lines remain separate; this feature retains its +79 allocation, including the retained-navigation regression within the existing ceiling. Patrick explicitly approved the measured +4,379 B raw / +1,386 B gzip CSS growth and +239 B Chat boot JS gzip limit adjustment; no other performance limits or request counts are relaxed.

## Evidence
Actual source Control UI with a **synthetic Gateway** and synthetic Template metadata. These images do not prove real package installation, filesystem materialization, provider/model execution or scheduling, and are not claims about the published Peterbot package. Inspected before/after images were delivered in the originating chat before this branch was uploaded.

### Before
![Before: expanding Template detail layout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0dd8cbd9-c1d3-4ed3-a874-ddcd9da67b9c)

### After
![After: compact single-column overview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34cbf197-6f6d-4bed-87a7-633a6dc6712d)

![After: narrow-screen dark-mode overview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6860cfb1-a741-4f42-9d9c-1d3e2239c48a)

![After: shared workspace-file rendering with fixed chrome while scrolling](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acefbfa9-d302-4d65-8d03-e9499d2beb0f)

- Focused UI/Markdown tests: 16 passed; catalog/Add composition observes one templates.add.apply and zero chat.send. The fixed-shell regression failed on the base and passes with this change.
- Performance-budget tests: 46 passed. Matched base/candidate build comparison passes: total CSS 1,675,194 B raw / 324,708 B gzip; Chat boot JS 1,294,974 B gzip, 20 requests.
- Chromium/WebKit desktop/mobile, light/dark; error/retry/loading, empty categories, named files/View all, long scrolling, keyboard and focus restoration inspected.
- 203 related Markdown/document/streaming/file-preview tests passed. UI/core-test/script typechecks, touched format/lint/stylelint, i18n, controller and safety guards passed.
- Separate baseline and feature test-line checks pass with zero spare credit.
- Own-change simplification: reused the shared document renderer and Add feedback, removed duplicate URL validation and synthetic send handoff, consolidated test fixtures, and removed an introduced unused export. New code is limited to inline reference presentation and the compact preview.

Known inherited local check failures remain explicit: unchanged changelog Thanks-attribution records and unused enqueueSlackRun in a test helper. Production and script dead-export scans pass after removing this change’s unused export. These are not represented as green; exact-head CI and the repository’s supported inherited-failure policy still apply.

Hosted ClawSweeper is the selected independent automated review route. Its original-head review found the missing browser-location parser regression; that finding is repaired and a current-head review is requested after this update. No retired autofix/automerge command is requested.


### CI repair evidence
- The Node transcript-search failure is repaired by skipping browser-specific Template decoration when location is absent; all 23 parser/search tests pass.
- Overlay lifecycle and dismissal move behind the existing lazy reference view rather than loading at chat boot. Hidden-pane teardown now retires intent. Before the lifecycle repair, returning to a retained pane reopened the old preview (1 dialog instead of 0); afterward hover/card dismissal, focus-out dismissal, direct click, focus restoration, session navigation and return all pass with no browser errors. The existing browser regression now covers navigation away and back.
- Integrated repaired-head validation: 23 parser/search tests and 13 catalog/browser tests pass; UI typecheck, touched lint and controller guard pass. One pre-existing transcript-registration reactivity warning remains unchanged.
- Matched build against merged prerequisite 70018ce4a1ce37128efca5b4e7a9ad6e53112528: Chat boot JS 1,294,930 B gzip (44 B below the approved 1,294,974 B ceiling), 20 requests; total CSS 1,674,935 B raw / 324,671 B gzip, below the unchanged approved ceilings.
- Test-line ratchet passes: 6,509,945 lines, ceiling 6,510,091, slack 146; feature allocation remains +79.
- Repair-only simplification removes the eager reference factory (92 net lines); admission stays in the transcript, the lazy UI owns listeners/timers/modal presentation, and the catalog retains Add/consent/setup authority.



### Final navigation and performance repair
- Both latest P2 findings are repaired: the keyed anchor owns its dismissal listeners/timer, and shared package-relative navigation selects included instruction files without leaving or stacking the preview. Each failure was reproduced before repair and passes in the retained browser regression afterward.
- Shared document rendering is separated from modal registration, duplicate Markdown traversal/parsing is removed, and comment pins are lazy while their stylesheet remains eager. No ceilings, request counts, test allocation or assertions were relaxed.

prs.title: fix(subagents): kept child session is deleted by session maintenance before the parent consumes its completion
prs.body:
Related: none. I found no existing issue or PR for this symptom (searched open and closed PRs and issues for `shouldPreserveSubagentForMaintenance`, `requesterSettleWake`, `capEntryCount`, and the touched file paths).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `cleanup: "keep"` sub-agent session is deleted by session maintenance (the `session.maintenance.maxEntries` cap) after the child finishes but before the parent has consumed its completion, so the parent's continuation can no longer read the child it was told to keep.

## User Impact

User impact: when a parent is still busy (or yielded) at the moment its child finishes, a new session that triggers a cap pass no longer removes the kept child. The parent's resumed turn can read the child with `sessions_history`, and the child's lineage/tool-policy snapshot stays valid until the completion settles. Once the requester settles, the child becomes ordinary cap-eligible again on the next maintenance pass. No config, schema, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`completeCleanupBookkeeping` stamps `cleanupCompletedAt` in the same step that arms `requesterSettleWake`. `shouldPreserveSubagentForMaintenance` returned `false` as soon as `cleanupCompletedAt` was set, so the child dropped out of maintenance protection while the requester still owed the completion. Sub-agent keys are disposable for the cap, so `capEntryCount` could delete the row inside that window.

The fix preserves the child while `requesterSettleWake` exists, and carries only the wake's `status` in the compact maintenance projection (`projectSubagentRunForMaintenance` / `SubagentRunMaintenanceRecord`) so persisted-only and live reads agree. This matches what the registry sweeper already does: it does not archive a run while its wake is outstanding (`subagent-registry-sweeper.ts`, the `entry.requesterSettleWake && !isCompletionAuthorityRetired` skip) and it resumes the wake every pass. Existing settlement paths clear the wake, which releases protection with no new timer, flag, or retry.

A one-line doc qualification in `docs/reference/session-management-compaction/maintenance.md` states the exception, since that page described sub-agent sessions as unconditionally disposable.

**Known boundary (not changed here):** if a requester session row disappears out-of-band (not through `sessions.delete`/reset, which drain and retire the obligation), the resume path keeps the wake owed by design ("the durable wake stays owed"), so it never clears. Before this PR that state already pinned the registry run; with this PR it also pins that one child row. Giving the wake owner a terminal outcome for a permanently missing requester is a separate change to deliberate temporary-unavailability behavior, so I left it out of this fix.

AI-assisted: written and verified with Claude Code; reviewed by a separate Codex pass and a separate Claude pass before filing (findings below).

## Evidence

**Regression tests fail on stock source and pass with the fix.** Stock = `git checkout origin/main -- src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-delivery-state.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.types.ts` with the new tests kept; base `85c39026a90`.

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-maintenance.completion.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-maintenance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Stock (red):

```
 × ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a pending requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 × ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a dispatching requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 × ...maintenance.completion.test.ts > retains completion policy through maintenance until requester settlement
   → promise rejected "Error: completion requester policy changed" instead of resolving
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'agent:main:subagent:child' ]
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  3 failed | 5 passed (8)
```

Fixed (green):

```
 ✓ ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a pending requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 ✓ ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a dispatching requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 ✓ ...maintenance.completion.test.ts > retains completion policy through maintenance until requester settlement
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

The tests assert both sides: the child is protected (and its captured policy stays current) while the wake is `pending` or `dispatching`, across persisted-only and live reads; after the wake clears, protection is released, the next cap pass deletes the row, and the captured policy check rejects. The completion test runs real maintenance (`applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation` with `maxEntries: 1`) through the host SQLite broker, so it is registered in the existing forked lane `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`.

**Checks on the changed files:** `check-test-lines-ratchet` OK (124 added test lines allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/subagent-maintenance-settle-wake.txt`), `oxfmt --check` clean, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` clean, `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` exit 0, `git diff --check` clean.

**Live runtime proof on two isolated gateways (red vs. green).** Bundle: https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-193869/README.md

Same config overlay `session.maintenance = { mode: "enforce", maxEntries: 2 }` on both. Red = upstream main `95a3ccde141` plus other pending patches that do not touch the subagent registry or session maintenance; green = red plus this PR's source change, nothing else. Parent on the Claude CLI, children `cleanup: "keep"`. The cap pass runs on session creation, so each scenario opened a side session while the parent was still busy or yielded (wake owed).

| Scenario | Red | Green |
|---|---|---|
| Parent busy (spawn, then long tool calls); side session created while wake pending | kept child row deleted with wake `pending` | row survived; released by the first cap pass after the wake cleared (~2 s later) |
| `sessions_yield` with fast + slow child | both kept rows deleted before settlement (wake `pending`, then `dispatching`) | both kept; released ~2 s after delivery settled |
| Same yield flow; resumed turn calls `sessions_history` on the fast child | `No session found: agent:main:subagent:<id>` despite `cleanup: "keep"` | `sessions_history` succeeded; rows released after settlement |

Red lost the kept row in 3/3 runs that hit the window; green kept it in 3/3 and released it after settlement (deletion timestamps: `deleted-archives-red.txt` / `deleted-archives-green.txt`; per-run wake state: `runtime-proof.json`). Two earlier runs per build did not hit the window and behaved the same on both.

Red, resumed parent reads its kept child:

![red: No session found](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-193869/R5-red-no-session-found.png?raw=true)

Green, same step:

![green: sessions_history ok](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-193869/G5-green-history-ok.png?raw=true)

Gap: these runs reproduced the missing kept session, not a fail-closed policy-rejection log line; the policy-snapshot consequence is covered by the completion test above.


<details>
<summary>Pre-filing review findings and what I did</summary>

- Both reviewers: an out-of-band removed requester leaves the wake owed forever, which now also pins its child row. Not changed; disclosed above as a known boundary (the registry run was already pinned in that state).
- Codex: the maintenance doc described sub-agent sessions as always disposable. Fixed with a one-sentence qualification.
- Claude: a run whose completion authority is retired in memory keeps protection until restart. Same as existing kill-tombstone protection in this function; not changed.
- Checked and not real: retry cap exhaustion and terminal dispatch failure both clear the wake; `cleanup: "delete"` deletes the child before the wake is armed, so this does not block deletion; protected rows above `maxEntries` are already handled (the cap picks only unprotected victims); the SQLite maintenance projection does not strip `requesterSettleWake`.

</details>
