prs.title: docs(nextcloud-talk): document the configWrites key
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The "Provider options" list in `docs/channels/nextcloud-talk.md` enumerates the keys a Nextcloud Talk account accepts, including `enabled`, `replyToMode` and `markdown.tables`, but omits `configWrites` — the gate that decides whether the channel may apply `/config set` and `/config unset` requests coming from chat. Users cannot find it from this page.

- Problem: `channels.nextcloud-talk.configWrites` is missing from the Nextcloud Talk provider options.
- Solution: document the key, its enabled-by-default behavior, the command it gates, and the per-account override.
- What changed: `docs/channels/nextcloud-talk.md` (1 line).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key is live configuration: `NextcloudTalkAccountSchemaBase` declares it and `buildMultiAccountChannelSchema` reuses that same base for the root section and for `accounts.<id>`, while the shared config-write policy consults it for every channel-originated write. The sentence follows the wording already used for the same key in `docs/channels/signal.md` and `docs/channels/whatsapp.md`, and the account-override note matches the `replyToMode` bullet two lines below.

## User Impact

Users can allow or deny Talk-initiated config writes per channel or per named account without reading source, and see that writes stay enabled until the key is set to `false`. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/config-schema.ts:32` declares the key inside `NextcloudTalkAccountSchemaBase` (line 28):

```typescript
configWrites: z.boolean().optional(),
```

`extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/config-schema.ts:66-67` feeds that same base into `buildMultiAccountChannelSchema`, so both `channels.nextcloud-talk.configWrites` and `channels.nextcloud-talk.accounts.<id>.configWrites` are accepted.

**Runtime type** — `extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/types.ts:22` derives `NextcloudTalkConfig` from `z.input<typeof NextcloudTalkConfigSchema>`, so the key reaches the plugin as an optional boolean. The equivalent slot in the shared messaging-account contract is `src/config/zod-schema.channel-messaging-common.ts:79` (`configWrites` inside `CommonChannelAccountSchema`, line 75).

**Default** — the runtime default is enabled, from `src/channels/plugins/config-write-policy-shared.ts:66-67`:

```typescript
const value = accountConfig?.configWrites ?? channelConfig.configWrites;
return value !== false;
```

Anything other than `false` allows the write, so an omitted key allows it.

**Consumer** — `src/channels/plugins/config-write-policy-shared.ts:52` (`resolveChannelConfigWritesShared`) resolves account-then-channel scope through `resolveChannelAccountEntry` at line 61 and is reached through `authorizeConfigWrite`, which `src/channels/plugins/config-writes.ts:16` aliases to `authorizeConfigWriteShared`. `src/auto-reply/reply/config-write-authorization.ts:20` calls it with `{ channelId, accountId }` taken from the message origin, which is how a Nextcloud Talk turn is evaluated.

**Test** — `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-gating.test.ts:449` ("blocks disallowed /config set writes") drives the denial path with a channel that sets `configWrites: false` and asserts no config file write happens; `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts:227` pins the account-level path `channels.telegram.accounts.work.configWrites`, the same resolver this key reaches.

**Docs toolchain**
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,398 internal links, 0 broken
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/channels/nextcloud-talk.md` — pass
- `oxfmt --check docs/channels/nextcloud-talk.md` — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix; the config-write policy is unchanged. No runtime behavior proof applies.

**Exact head** — `a3da1c6d1fce3803e3588e5b45f4f4ee8c40f183`

prs.title: fix(postgres): preserve the first Gateway operation after host suspension
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the first Gateway operation failing after a suspended host resumes with dead PostgreSQL sockets retained by shared-state or update-bookkeeping workers.

## User Impact

The first resumed operation can use a new idle connection without restarting the Gateway. Transactions and uncertain writes still fail closed; dispatched SQL is never replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport already reconnects and validates idle connections on pool checkout. Retained connections never take that path. Reuse that same owner when the last completed server response was idle, and measure the existing one-second validation threshold with wall time so host suspension counts. No caller retry, new recovery service, schema change, or configuration switch.

The simplification pass retained 14 net production lines, 54 net test lines, six documentation lines and the required allocation. Existing transaction status supplies the safety boundary.

## Evidence

- Exact contribution range: `938a72d4c1e4136d07f32156ed633f2f86a524a1..af098d8271d85899991b20b3b2b15423a8ed39e6`.
- The committed shared-state/update-bookkeeping regression expectations were run before changing production at `7e0ec3e59fad329618c43314d796529cf3ed59cc`: both failed (2 failed, 11 filtered/skipped; 12.07s), reporting `Shared-state worker retained a closed PostgreSQL connection` and `Existing-state writer retained a closed PostgreSQL connection`. These same regression cases pass with the fix. This base-red control is separate from the compiled Gateway comparison below.
- All 55 focused tests pass on this contribution head with real disposable PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector 0.8.7 (135.50s Vitest / 176.86s wrapper). Includes retained/pooled reconnect, suspension with only wall time advancing, lost-transaction refusal and shared-state historical migrations.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped typed lint and formatting pass. Independent agent review of the complete range found no actionable issues. This was not a local ClawSweeper/autoreview run.
- Real compiled Gateway comparison on the deployed integration source plus exactly this patch: baseline `7e0ec3e59fad329618c43314d796529cf3ed59cc` versus candidate `636cff64f7b83879d597c0936452745a3d900c34`. Relevant transport owners are byte-identical between baseline and this PR's upstream base. This is integration-build evidence, not a claim that upstream main was fully built.

<details>
<summary>Real Gateway reproduction and observed output</summary>

Use an isolated Gateway home, unique PostgreSQL schema/application name, and synthetic data. Create a coach through `agents.create` and a conversation with transcript messages. Freeze only that Gateway with `SIGSTOP`, wait 1.2 seconds, terminate its 17 application-scoped idle backends using `pg_terminate_backend`, then `SIGCONT`. Make `agents.create` the first post-resume RPC; do not retry it.

Baseline: first RPC returned `UNAVAILABLE` / `session_actor_reconciliation`; log contained `Shared-state worker retained a closed PostgreSQL connection`. Roster remained bootstrap + coach.

Candidate: first RPC returned `ok: true` in 2.726 seconds. New agent appeared; original bootstrap/coach entries, session ID and exact returned transcript messages were preserved. Transcript SHA-256: `825f9a4b6008b986200e7c2c89fefad402b8423d52a82b35254fe153f2915006`. Candidate run took 27.61 seconds, then shut down cleanly.

This is macOS process-freeze/socket-loss proof with real PostgreSQL, not a GCE suspend test or model-inference test. An ancillary cron-maintenance `Agent database resources are closing` warning occurred during new-agent provisioning; creation and transcript checks passed with no PostgreSQL reconnect error. Existing blackhole timeout and sub-second validation window are unchanged.
</details>

The integration source's full package build passes (4m54.3s), with its existing nonfatal UI gzip advisory. Its state test-type leaf has an unrelated unchanged `sqlite-file-copy.test.ts:142` callback/options mismatch; no aggregate `pnpm check` pass is claimed. Hosted CI remains separate.

The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193875#issuecomment-6674773643) covers this exact head, finds no actionable correctness issues, and rates the real Gateway proof sufficient. Its requested base-red detail is supplied above. The small wall-clock unit contract is retained deliberately: a real terminated-backend test can recover through an already-observed socket error even if long-idle validation uses the wrong clock. The unit test advances only wall time and verifies validation before BEGIN and its absence inside an active transaction; the real PostgreSQL tests separately prove recovery and no write replay. No new review request is needed for this evidence clarification.

prs.title: docs(discord): list the accepted presence status values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/channels/discord/events.md` shows `status: "idle"` in the Presence configuration example but never states which values the schema accepts or what an omitted key sends. `invisible` appears nowhere in the Discord docs even though `resolveDiscordPresenceUpdate` forwards it to the gateway.

- Problem: the accepted `channels.discord.status` values and the fallback when the key is omitted are undocumented.
- Solution: state the four accepted values, the `online` fallback on omission, what `invisible` does, and the per-account override in the Presence configuration accordion.
- What changed: `docs/channels/discord/events.md` (2 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accordion already explains which fields trigger a presence update and how `autoPresence` maps health states, so the accepted value set belongs in the same place rather than in a separate page. The page documents the sibling `activityType` values the same way (an explicit list under its example), so this follows the page's own convention.

## User Impact

Users can set or verify a bot presence value, know that an omitted `status` sends `online`, and use `invisible` to keep the bot connected while it appears offline, without reading `presence.ts`. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts:290` declares the leaf directly:

```typescript
status: z.enum(["online", "dnd", "idle", "invisible"]).optional(),
```

**Runtime type** — the value is forwarded unchanged to the gateway contract, `extensions/discord/src/monitor/presence.ts:38`:

```typescript
status: (status || "online") as UpdatePresenceData["status"],
```

**Default** — the same `presence.ts:38` is the runtime fallback: an omitted `status` resolves to `"online"`, which is what is documented. The enum at `config-schema.ts:290` is strict, so anything else — including `""` — is rejected by config validation before the resolver runs; the resolver's empty-string branch therefore never comes from a validated config and is not documented as a supported value.

**Consumer** — `extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.startup.ts:76` sends `gateway.updatePresence(resolveDiscordPresenceUpdate(readyDiscordConfig))` on startup, and `extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.ts:82` and `:114` build each periodic update from the same resolver. Scope comes from `extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts:198` and `:245`, where the presence keys live on the account base inherited by both `channels.discord` and `channels.discord.accounts.<id>`.

**Test** — `extensions/discord/src/monitor/presence.test.ts:5` ("returns online presence when no config is provided") pins the `online` fallback and `:14` ("uses configured status") pins pass-through of a configured value.

**Docs toolchain**
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,398 internal links, 0 broken
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/channels/discord/events.md` — pass
- `oxfmt --check docs/channels/discord/events.md` — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix; the Discord presence implementation is unchanged. No runtime behavior proof applies.

**Exact head** — `314d0c95e4feb8ac6282a5dac1696cfca0ef528c`

prs.title: fix(agents): forward hook-stamped _meta on bundle-mcp tool calls
prs.body:
Related: #151413

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin's hook-stamped `_meta` identity silently never reaches MCP servers on bundle-mcp tool calls — and the first revision of this fix would have carried model-written `_meta` onto that same trusted identity lane.

Hooks land identity (the brayer `harness/agent/session` stamp) by rewriting tool params with a `_meta` field, but JSON-RPC `_meta` lives *beside* `arguments`; the executor forwarded params verbatim as `arguments`, so servers saw no stamp (the last open seam of the #151413 identity transport). Forwarding any object named `_meta` instead would promote model-forged input to the identity channel. The execute-factory extraction also snapshotted `disposal` at factory creation — retained forms never observed run end — and tested a restriction-map *entry* instead of the map, so an established map lacking a server produced `undefined` instead of an explicit empty grant.

## User Impact

Hook stamps now arrive as request-level `_meta` on every bundle-mcp path — embedded agent runs, client tool definitions, and gateway `/tools/invoke` — so servers consuming the identity lane see them. Model-supplied `_meta` keeps behaving as an ordinary tool argument: tool schemas that declare an object-valued `_meta` argument are unaffected. Retained MCP form callbacks reject with `MCP run has ended` once their run disposes, and an App view whose server is absent from an established restriction map keeps an explicit empty tool grant (interaction stays possible; only a never-bound map means read-only).

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the review's recommended **separate trusted metadata lane** without expanding the plugin hook contract: each before_tool_call boundary (agent wrapper, tool-definition adapter, gateway tools-invoke) diffs the hook's input against the params that will execute, and publishes only `_meta` the pipeline *added or changed* through an async context. The bundle-mcp execute factory reads that context and forwards the value as `runtime.callTool(..., { _meta })`, stripping it from `arguments`. Provenance, not naming, decides trust — unchanged `_meta` never leaves `arguments`, so model-forged identity cannot reach the request channel.

Both lifecycle behaviors date to `6046d4fcb687` (MCP Apps session/requester/approval/workspace boundaries): App views outlive their run, so run-end checks must read disposal *live* rather than a creation-time snapshot; and an explicit empty grant is deliberately distinct from a never-bound restriction map (`requireMcpAppInteraction` treats `undefined` as read-only, an empty set as granted-but-empty). The factory now reads disposal through a live reader and tests map existence before the empty-set fallback, restoring both intents.

## Evidence

**Red/green matrix** — committed in `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-executes.test.ts`; every revision's defect is caught by a test, and the fixed head is fully green:

| test | base `fb530875` | reviewed head `f9f467d8` | this revision |
|---|---|---|---|
| hook-authored `_meta` forwarded as request metadata, out of `arguments` | red — never forwarded | green | green |
| model-supplied `_meta` kept in `arguments` (no hook runs) | green | **red** — unconditional hoist | green |
| model-supplied `_meta` kept when a hook passes it through | green | **red** — unconditional hoist | green |
| retained elicitation rejects after the view disposes | green | **red** — wrong error (form notice, not run-ended) | green |
| explicit empty App grant when the restriction map lacks the server | green | **red** — `undefined` ≠ `Set {}` | green |

The forged-stamp legs are rows 2–3: with no pipeline-authored `_meta`, the value stays inside `arguments` and never appears as request-level `_meta`. The retired-authority leg is row 4: after `dispose()`, a retained elicitation handle rejects before any form work. Unit coverage for the provenance diff and the scope (publish / read / nested shadowing / restore) lives in `src/agents/before-tool-call-request-meta.test.ts` (9 tests).

**Gates on this head (`c539c75d`):** full CI green — 0 failures, including `PR context and evidence`, `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, `check-lint`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Local: all touched suites green (13 files, 305 test executions, 0 failures — bundle-mcp materialize/harness/tools/identity, before-tool-call e2e + approval policy, tool-definition adapter, gateway tools-invoke http/mcp, and both new files); `pnpm tsgo:core` and the core test shards covering the changed agents/gateway paths clean; oxlint and format clean on all changed files; wrapper-shadowing, deprecated-api-usage, import-cycle, and knip files/dependencies checks green. Two ratchet remedies are committed exactly as their outputs prescribed: `config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt` shrinks `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts` 3 → 2 (the App-view `details` mutation became a typed `details` argument), and `config/test-lines-allocations/bundle-mcp-meta-provenance.txt` records the +248 test-line delta — both re-verified on a true merge tree of this branch and `main` with the ratchets' own `--base main` invocation (assertion-safety OK; test-lines OK, slack 28). A ui type error that appears when running the *full* root shards against this branch's stale base alone exists only there — `ui/src/components/browser/browser-panel-render.tsx` is byte-identical to `fb530875` and was fixed on `main` (`.split("\n")[0]` → `.split("\n", 1).join("")`); CI evaluates the merge tree, where it does not apply, and the changed-path shards for this PR do not include it.

**Publish sites and scope:** provenance is published at the three boundaries that run `before_tool_call` and then execute tools — `agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts`, `agent-tool-definition-adapter.ts`, and `gateway/tools-invoke-shared.ts` — and consumed in `agent-bundle-mcp-executes.ts`. The requester-connect projection, MCP App operations, and direct harness executes keep their existing behavior (no hook boundary in path, or their own `_meta` lane).

**Delta vs reviewed head `f9f467d8`:** +119 / −52 production lines across 5 files, +248 test lines in 3 new files, plus 2 insertions / 1 deletion of ratchet bookkeeping in 2 config files; vs merge base `fb530875`: +547 / −164 across 10 files. Removed with this revision: unconditional `_meta` hoisting (replaced by the provenance gate), the creation-time `disposal` snapshot, the restriction-map entry test, two unchecked type assertions (the App-view `details` mutation and the `_meta` hoist), the execute factory's dead `mcpAppsEnabled`/`isRequesterScopedServer` parameters, nine dead imports in `materialize`, and a duplicate type import.

prs.title: fix(test): stop launcher disconnect fixture from timing out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the launcher handoff test timing out after its resumed child has already exited on IPC disconnect.

## User Impact

Restores reliable launcher regression coverage in CI. Runtime behavior and handoff assertions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicitly disconnecting IPC can omit the aggregate child `close` event. Join process exit and drain stdout/stderr independently, including cleanup. The existing cases still require silence before handoff, exit 0 with payload output after commit, and exit 1 with empty output after disconnect.

The three net test lines have their own exact allocation; no test cases or timeouts are added. Production code is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Original failure: [FRV tooling job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42138981831/job/127634741092), disconnect case timed out at 120 seconds.
- Node 24.22.1 baseline `f60402fd`, with identical launcher fixture/test source through base `7b021629`: commit passed; disconnect timed out at 120 seconds. Instrumented replay observed exit 1 and drained pipes without a child `close` event.
- Exact candidate `e17fa3750d77cdc06b7d8227a3ebc2957d828d71`: `pnpm test test/node-host-launcher.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes all 14 cases on Node 24.22.1 (38.67s wall; 3.413s file tests) and pinned Bun 1.4.4 (32.21s wall; 2.134s file tests). Disconnect finishes in 40ms/30ms, respectively.
- Targeted root-test typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, diff whitespace, and test-line ratchet pass. The candidate uses its own physical frozen dependency installation.
- Full uncached local ClawSweeper review of `7b0216295799f6cd47d8cdcdc5bcf3df005f0851..e17fa3750d77cdc06b7d8227a3ebc2957d828d71`: complete, no actionable correctness/security findings; zero cache hits. Independent source review also approved.
- Broad exact-head PR CI and CI seconds are pending.

prs.title: perf: reduce style matching during Control UI interactions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A global chat-search highlight selector adds style-matching work when interacting with unrelated Control UI elements.

## User Impact

Reduces Chromium style CPU during typing, sidebar toggling, picker search, and Cron typing, while keeping chat-search highlights and other computed styles unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The search owner only registers `.chat-text` blocks and creates every highlight range inside those blocks. Scope the existing highlight rule to that class; nested text inherits its highlight colors. No new classes, state, handlers, dependencies, or lazy imports are needed.

Production change: `ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css`, **3 insertions / 2 deletions; 3,369 → 3,370 lines**. The extra comment line records the existing range-owner constraint. Solid lifecycle/effect/listener/DOM-query counts are unchanged (this is CSS only).

Related: #183678, #193468.

## Evidence

### Attribution and acceptance

Baseline: `d0b0fc80a34d`; source change: `979c41d4f18`.

Chromium 156 emits selector statistics with `disabled-by-default-blink.debug`. Collected 18 desktop/mobile census traces and six real-Gateway Usage action traces at 1×; 3,716 canonical selector entries, 3,540 mapped authored entries and 176 native user-agent entries. All 54 Usage stylesheet identities are mapped to verified assets or inline sources. Coalesced rules retain multiple source owners rather than inventing attribution. **Selector-stat timings are diagnostic only and are not used to claim a speedup.**

| Leading family | Instrumented µs | Attempts | Fast rejects | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `::highlight(openclaw-chat-search)` | 9575 | 16293 | 0.0% | ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css:247 |
| `& svg` | 4520 | 978 | 0.0% | ui/src/styles/chat/startup-layout.css:452 (nested); ui/src/styles/chat/startup-layout.css:475 (nested) |
| `.sidebar-region:has(> .sidebar-region__header .chat-pane__connection) :is(.chat-gutter-stack, .chat-main__conversation-column > .chat-topbar-notices)` | 3651 | 16293 | 44.5% | ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css:444 |
| `:is(.session-row-badge, .session-row-trail, .sidebar-child-session-toggle__count, .sidebar-session-group-count, .sidebar-agent-roster__unread, .sidebar-issues-button__count, .viewer-avatar--overflow, .sidebar-session-tree__show-more)` | 3165 | 18840 | 0.0% | ui/src/styles/components.css:3500 |
| `& > :is(.chat-message-images, .chat-assistant-attachments, .chat-assistant-attachment-card, .chat-pairing-qr-notices, .chat-thinking, .chat-tool-card__widget-host, .chat-text, .chat-message-disclosure, .chat-message-avatar-anchor, .chat-tools-inline)` | 2960 | 18840 | 0.0% | ui/src/styles/chat/text.css:1412 (nested) |

Acceptance set before measurements: ≥5% style-CPU improvement in a real flow, preserved computed styles, and no attributable regression beyond the campaign band. Use 20 rotated base/candidate/control pairs per cell and an A/A control on the same machine. All browsers headless, native 1×. No concurrent builds or other browser benchmarks.

### Uninstrumented ablation

**1,000 successful observations, zero failures.** Five flows × two engines × five CSS variants/control roles × 20 pairs. Chromium uses untraced renderer thread CPU; WebKit uses untraced wall time and does not expose comparable CPU counters. Synthetic production UI fixtures; these are renderer measurements, not provider/Gateway latency claims.

| Flow | Chromium style ms, median / p95 (before → after) | Median change | A/A style ms |
|---|---|---:|---|
| chat-typing-prefocused | 2.999 / 3.472 → 2.793 / 3.195 | -6.9% | 3.014 / 3.380 |
| sidebar-toggle | 58.543 / 62.640 → 54.359 / 58.772 | -7.1% | 58.501 / 62.858 |
| model-picker-open-search | 11.707 / 12.645 → 10.753 / 11.306 | -8.2% | 11.301 / 11.880 |
| sessions-search | 8.681 / 9.562 → 8.831 / 9.525 | +1.7% | 8.815 / 9.523 |
| cron-search-typing | 4.802 / 6.023 → 4.455 / 5.674 | -7.2% | 4.732 / 4.972 |

Sessions is neutral relative to its A/A control. WebKit does not establish a speedup: the sidebar candidate shifts +4.5% while its identical-build control shifts +4.6%; Sessions tail movement also stays below its A/A control. Chromium Cron had a noisy wall tail (127.893 → 143.334 ms) despite lower style CPU; a separate rebuilt-source confirmation is recorded below.

### Rebuilt-source confirmation

The rebuilt-source campaign completed **480 observations with no assertion failures**. Same 1× engines, 20 rotated base/head/base pairs per cell.

| Flow | Chromium style ms, median / p95 (before → after) | Median change | WebKit wall ms, median / p95 (before → after) |
|---|---|---:|---|
| sessions-open | 6.297 / 6.596 → 6.264 / 6.562 | -0.5% | 114.315 / 143.681 → 112.919 / 133.008 |
| cron-open | 7.832 / 8.129 → 7.084 / 7.287 | -9.5% | 154.311 / 178.125 → 148.052 / 164.470 |
| cron-menu-open | 5.889 / 6.293 → 5.486 / 5.829 | -6.8% | 161.376 / 164.204 → 161.321 / 164.404 |
| cron-search-typing | 4.994 / 7.004 → 4.587 / 5.142 | -8.2% | 211.431 / 229.815 → 213.105 / 324.066 |

Chromium Cron typing confirms the CPU win (style p95 also improves) and removes the earlier wall-tail regression: 107.760 / 171.065 → 110.320 / 127.210 ms. Its A/A median is 107.830 ms. WebKit Cron typing has two early head spikes despite a neutral median; a targeted independent 20-pair tail check is recorded below.

WebKit Cron timing needed a role crossover because two runs had isolated long tails on a busy shared host. All results are retained, rather than treating a noisy p95 as a speedup. The initial copied-CSS run and the final role-swapped rebuilt-source run both fall inside the acceptance band. The final 20-pair crossover has **base 212.105 / 228.740 ms, head 211.087 / 229.034 ms, identical-base control 212.214 / 214.788 ms** (median / p95): median −0.5%, p95 +0.13% (below the campaign's 1% noise threshold). No WebKit speedup is claimed.

| WebKit Cron run | Base median / p95 ms | Head median / p95 ms | A/A median / p95 ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial copied-CSS ablation, 20 pairs | 196.290 / 213.002 | 196.074 / 213.183 | 195.979 / 212.707 |
| Rebuilt source, 20 pairs | 211.431 / 229.815 | 213.105 / 324.066 | 212.871 / 254.781 |
| Targeted repeat, 20 pairs | 212.053 / 261.459 | 212.484 / 295.106 | 211.600 / 230.177 |
| Rebuilt source with head/base roles swapped, 20 pairs | 212.105 / 228.740 | 211.087 / 229.034 | 212.214 / 214.788 |

Host load exceeded 30 during the targeted repeat; the identical-base p95 varied by about 12% from the other baseline. All 2,681 application JS files match after normalizing emitted asset hash references; only the generated service-worker build timestamp/integrity inventory also differs (service workers were blocked in these runs). The change has no JavaScript behavior delta. Across all campaigns: **1,600 untraced observations, zero assertion failures**.

### Rejected candidates

- Splitting the connection selector: +82 raw / +3 gzip CSS bytes; style medians −1.0% sidebar, −3.5% picker (same as A/A), +1.0% typing, +1.1% Sessions. No qualifying win; not included.
- Grouping nine simple field leaves while retaining the six ancestor branches: saves 2,456 raw / 244 gzip bytes, but style medians +3.4% typing, +2.8% sidebar, +3.0% Sessions, −1.0% picker. No clean CPU result; keep #193468's separately indexed rules and existing ceilings.
- Header SVG rule: its current callers have no common class and include nested wrappers/custom trigger content. A direct-child rewrite would not preserve behavior; not included.

### Correctness and budgets

- 12 Chromium/WebKit × light/dark × 400/820/1280 fixture pairs: equal normal/highlight computed styles and geometry, byte-identical settled screenshots. Covers direct/nested text, links, code, notice and typing preview.
- Real transcript search: both engines, desktop/mobile, expected registered ranges and colors, retained draft and restored focus on close. prs.title: fix: avoid full-tree work when refreshing prepared workers
prs.body:
Related: #193756, #193667

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing a prepared worker to a nearby commit repeats full-tree hashing, Git transfer/checkout/verification, toolchain setup, and dependency installation.

## User Impact

Snapshot forks and ready-worker adoption retain unchanged files, hashes, and toolchains, and skip detected installation when dependency inputs are unchanged. Missing or unusable retained state falls back to fresh preparation. Live AWS validation is pending; this PR must not merge before the coordinator evaluates the phase timings below.

A root install lifecycle script that reads other tracked content does not rerun on a content-only refresh. Script and devcontainer recipes retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared hashes were looked up in machine HOME even though the captured memo belongs to the prepared HOME. The manifest now consumes that memo separately from prior-manifest semantics; full-hash bytes remain identical, including when source and prepared digests match.

Move an owned, pristine retained seed into staging, preserve its objects/index/worktree, and negotiate from detached HEAD explicitly. Public fetches retain their credential/network restrictions and validate incoming objects. Private pack production receives the retained commit and emits a thin pack; absent remote donors fall back to a full snapshot. Reused seeds check new connectivity while fresh seeds retain full fsck. A failure after moving a donor consumes it, so the next attempt starts fresh.

Reuse the captured Node/Corepack setup only when requirement, package-manager identity, and executable links match. Detected-install invalidation includes nested manifests, lockfiles, package-manager configuration, tracked Yarn plugins/releases, patches, and supported Node declarations. No new configuration or manifest format is introduced.

## Evidence

Acceptance workload: real Git A-to-B refresh, warm local Darwin disk, 1,000 files of 32 KiB each and one added file; five independently prepared, counterbalanced pairs. Preserve manifest bytes and unchanged inodes, reduce full-tree content/object work to the diff, and improve total median/p95. Runtime and generated-script diff is +144/-60 lines; test LF growth is exactly 283, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/prepared-refresh-diff-cost.txt`.

| Measurement | Baseline | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total median / p95 | 2,706 / 3,146 ms | 1,656 / 1,772 ms |
| Seed content hashes | 1,003 | 1 |
| Prepared content hashes | 1,003 | 1 |
| Seed incoming objects / bytes | 1,009 / 32,835,982 | 4 / 24,782 |
| Workspace incoming objects / bytes | 1,006 / 32,811,271 | 3 / 24,725 |
| Seed verification median / p95 | 294 / 358 ms | 57 / 58 ms |
| Seed checkout median / p95 | 239 / 249 ms | 36 / 38 ms |
| Seed manifest median / p95 | 234 / 1,034 ms | 186 / 190 ms |
| Workspace Git update median / p95 | 438 / 495 ms | 167 / 315 ms |
| Prepared manifest median / p95 | 269 / 332 ms | 213 / 269 ms |
| Seed transfer median / p95 | 249 / 571 ms | 338 / 463 ms |

Total median improves 38.8% and p95 improves 43.7%. **The seed-transfer median regresses 35.7%; it is unresolved performance evidence, not a claimed win.** A narrow profile attributes most of the slow local sample to strict thin-pack indexing. Incoming counts measure newly stored Git objects/pack bytes, not network wire bytes. An independent `file://` server probe sends 32,811,271 bytes without an explicit negotiation tip versus 24,782 bytes with `HEAD`.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/project-preparation-phases.mts <scratch-root> <baseline-checkout>` on the #193756 baseline.

- Red: the frozen baseline rehashes the unchanged large file and replaces its seed inode; private preparation omits the retained commit; toolchain refresh fetches release metadata again.
- Green: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation-verification.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/project-preparation-environment.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/repository-git-pack.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 58/58, 150.40 s wall. Covers real scripts/Git, A-B-A, equal/distinct manifest digests, cold-hash equality, seed fallbacks, dependency invalidation, and private authenticated HTTP thin packs.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/node-toolchain.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 13/13, 11.84 s wall. Linux-emulated setup proves no network/Corepack work on reuse and full preparation for missing shims or changed identity.
- Type-aware core and benchmark lint, `pnpm run tsgo:core`, `pnpm runtime:scripts:check`, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the exact-base test-line ratchet passed. Generated manifests were regenerated with `pnpm runtime:scripts:gen`.
- Yarn plugin follow-up: the focused detected-install regression failed before the fix (23.38 s) and passed afterward (61.54 s, including compilation), with tracked plugin and bundled-release paths added. Final independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2): scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. Reviewed the complete staged change against `39757c60c7aa56d2972f1cd877976ad5ae7c61fc`; the final commit `773157fb1fe8f945566de4389fd2328bb4a4ce59` is patch-identical after rebasing onto the landed prerequisite/current main `2049dfc8e2d`. The seed-indexing timing caveat remains unresolved.

Live proof on an isolated Gateway with real AWS workers:

| Real `openclaw/openclaw` (64,000 tracked files) | Before | Fork from a current-generation image | Ready-worker adoption |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Whole placement | 452.0 s | 306.5 s | 78.1 s (126 s before) |
| `seedTransfer` | 37.6 s | 8.2 s | 1.1 s |
| `seedManifest` | 10.9 s | 6.7 s | 3.7 s |
| `gitUpdate` | 23.3 s | 40.8 s | 1.1 s |
| `toolchainPreparation` | 29.7 s | 0.4 s | 2 ms |
| `detectedInstall` | 13.9 s | skipped | skipped |
| `preparedManifest` | 54.9 s | 3.9 s | 3.7 s |

A private repository fixture forked from a snapshot one commit behind passes end to end, including its first model turn, in 148.5 s: `seedTransfer` 1.8 s, `gitUpdate` 1.6 s, `toolchainPreparation` 2 ms, through the real thin-pack and `crabbox cp` path.

Known limits, stated plainly. `gitUpdate` on a cold fork is slower than before (40.8 s against 23.3 s, one sample each), so that phase remains a target; the whole placement still gains. The first fork from an image captured before this change gets worse `seedManifest` (41.8 to 114 s) and keeps the old toolchain cost, because old images overwrite the seed memo when source and prepared digests match; the next published image clears this. Stale `.memo` files stay in the captured home across generations, about 6 MB per generation at this repository size. Fresh Gateway-side timing varied between 2 s and 44 s in `workspacePreparation` on the loaded test host.

prs.title: docs(discord): document the auto-thread per-channel keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts` defines four auto-thread keys on each guild channel entry, and the Discord monitor reads all four on every guild turn, but `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md` documents none of them. The page already refers to "auto-threads" when explaining `thread.inheritParent`, so readers meet a feature name with no way to turn it on or tune it.

- Problem: `autoThread`, `autoThreadName`, `autoArchiveDuration` and `includeThreadStarter` are missing from the Discord docs (a grep for `autoThread` across the Discord doc tree only reaches an unrelated mention in `access-control.md`).
- Solution: document each key with its accepted values, runtime default, applicable scope, and per-account override in the existing "Thread behavior" list.
- What changed: `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md` (4 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each key is live configuration with regression coverage, so the "History, context, and thread behavior" accordion is the place readers already look for thread keys, next to `thread.inheritParent` which is documented there. The wording follows the `channels.discord.guilds.<guild>.channels.<channel>.<key>` pattern already used by the `requireMention` bullet two lines below, and the `generated` naming note restates the JSDoc shipped with `autoThreadName`.

## User Impact

Users can now enable auto-threads per guild channel, choose between message-derived and model-generated thread names, pick one of the four archive windows, and drop the thread starter from follow-up context, without reading `threading.auto-thread.ts`. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts:67-88` declares all four keys on `DiscordGuildChannelSchema` through `buildGroupEntrySchema`:

```typescript
includeThreadStarter: z.boolean().optional(),
autoThread: z.boolean().optional(),
autoThreadName: z.enum(["message", "generated"]).optional(),
autoArchiveDuration: z.union([z.enum(["60", "1440", "4320", "10080"]), z.literal(60), ...]).optional(),
```

**Runtime type** — the enum leaves are inline at line 76 (`["message", "generated"]`) and line 80 (`["60", "1440", "4320", "10080"]`, also accepted as numbers), so no value outside those sets is documented.

**Default** — `autoThread` is off unless set, since `extensions/discord/src/monitor/threading.auto-thread.ts:158` returns early without a truthy `channelConfig.autoThread`. The archive window falls back to `60` at `threading.auto-thread.ts:204-206`. `includeThreadStarter` defaults to true at `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.ts:295`:

```typescript
const includeThreadStarter = channelConfig?.includeThreadStarter !== false;
```

**Consumer** — `threading.auto-thread.ts:158` gates creation, `:161-169` skips forum, media, voice and stage channels, `:195-199` skips bot-authored messages, `:204` passes `autoArchiveDuration`, and `:220` renames the new thread only when `autoThreadName === "generated"`. `message-handler.context.ts:190` and `:295` consume `autoThread` and `includeThreadStarter` for context assembly. Scope is confirmed by `extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts:198` and `:245`, where `guilds` sits on the account base inherited by both `channels.discord` and `channels.discord.accounts.<id>`.

**Test** — `extensions/discord/src/monitor/threading.auto-thread.test.ts:37` and `:62-64` exercise `autoThread: true`, `autoThreadName: "generated"` and `autoArchiveDuration: "10080"`; `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context-history.test.ts:356` covers `includeThreadStarter: false`.

**Docs toolchain**
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,398 internal links, 0 broken
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md` — pass
- `oxfmt --check docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md` — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix; the auto-thread implementation is unchanged. No runtime behavior proof applies.

**Exact head** — `cf5d02b262fc4e4fe5a874a332ea162b2539a392`

prs.title: fix(update): recover interrupted managed updates on 2026.11.2
prs.body:
Related: #188303. Backports #172784, #175890 and #188497.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recovery paths that leave an update-owned Gateway stop unresolved after an interrupted update, recoverable finalization failure, or completed repair on **release/2026.11.2**.

## User Impact

Restore an owned Gateway only after recovery verifies service ownership, runtime identity, and safe state. Operator stops, named data risks, custody grace, process census, and unknown-owner refusals remain intact. Unowned services receive manual-start guidance rather than failing completed maintenance.

This does not establish that every incident in #188303 is resolved. An already-running old updater cannot acquire these fixes retroactively.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adapt the three existing fixes to the release’s current-core and inline helper owners. Preserve compatible failure history, accept the release’s actual finalizer response, and select the verified installed ledger/terminal writer before post-core repair can migrate state and fail. No plugin-cohort subsystem, recovery-owner restructuring, release metadata, versions, or production schema change is included.

Preparation base: `1bec8184bcd9849061bedf7f4e5cc9405039801a`. The seven commits since original proof base `fc9b9635e6d4142ff42d0409f41d7e306f14c5d0` do not overlap the backport. Original author and human coauthor credit are preserved.

## Evidence

- Original release-base restoration regression failed before the fix and passed afterward. Finalizer-response and operator-stop regressions also reproduced before correction.
- Retained original-base results: 48 finalizer/cleanup, 23 custody, 7 ledger compaction/capture, and 150 recovery sibling tests passed. These are reused results, not current-head reruns.
- Final release-base **13 interrupted-helper tests pass**, including two terminal-failure regressions that fail on the uncorrected head. They exercise detached helper/publication/persisted terminal-record paths with a synthetic finalizer.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass for the correction. Original-base core/infra typechecks passed. Rebound CLI typecheck is blocked by the wrapper refusing linked declaration dependencies outside this checkout; no current-head CLI typecheck pass is claimed.
- Canonical autoreview via authenticated OpenClaw engine, P0–P2, covered the full prepared range. Its remaining finding was the old indexed terminal writer while the working-tree fix was present; after staging the fix, a fresh correction review against `6189a2636644a0777df90e8ef26a94b738cb66b0` was scoped-clean. Final correction commit: `0e783c4874dd14aff32561b81b96370a521ac8a7`.

**Draft / remaining gates:** native macOS/launchd and packaged actual-candidate/real-agent upgrade proof are unavailable. Emulated managers and synthetic failure paths do not establish real cross-version migration or native incident resolution. PR CI, CODEOWNERS review, and release validation remain pending.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(ios): keep rejected shares from reporting sent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the iOS share sheet reporting **Sent** and dismissing its draft when the Gateway ignored an oversized message or rejected its attachments.

## User Impact

Rejected shares stay editable with an actionable error. **Sent** means the Gateway admitted the request for agent dispatch, not that the agent finished. Older Gateways cannot confirm admission: the sheet keeps the draft and asks users to check the destination session before retrying and update the Gateway. Retries are not deduplicated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `NodeEventResult` contract for explicit admission/rejection. Publish the decided receipt before an incognito session's existing accepted-work drain, without releasing actor custody or weakening connection checks. The share extension checks that receipt instead of treating RPC success as admission. No protocol/schema/config or dependency changes.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(update): preserve operator stops and failed repair outcomes
prs.body:
Related: #188303.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three recovery defects exposed while validating release backports: restarting a later operator-stopped Gateway, failing completed repair when service ownership is unavailable, and losing the terminal failure record after schema-changing repair fails.

## User Impact

Interrupted recovery preserves later operator stops. An unowned service stays stopped with manual-start guidance, and failed post-core repair records failure using the verified installed runtime. Existing data-risk, custody, identity, and live-authority checks remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check durable stop intent before recovery and immediately before native startup, including launchd retries. Use the existing manual-warning path for nonowned verdicts. Select the verified candidate terminal writer at finalize entry, retaining staged fallback before verification. Main’s plugin-cohort handling is unchanged; no production schema change is included.

## Evidence

Base: `85c39026a90f58164595249f69c311ed71b44df8`; reviewed head: `29250b1840baa1ed26772df373273a2adad71135`.

- All **five added regression cases fail on original main** and pass with the fix: both ownership verdicts, superseded stop intent before recovery and during inspection, and failed terminal settlement after synthetic schema incompatibility.
- A mutation removing only the early stop check fails the early-guard test despite retaining the final startup guard.
- **16 interrupted-helper, 23 repair-service, and 43 native-lifecycle sibling tests pass**; final five-case rerun passes.
- Core, CLI-update and infra-test typechecks; targeted lint, format, test-line ratchet, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent review and canonical autoreview via authenticated OpenClaw engine (P0–P2), covering the full base-to-head change, found no actionable findings.

**Draft / remaining gates:** real detached processes and ledger operations are exercised, but native managers and schema incompatibility are emulated. Native macOS and packaged actual-candidate/real-agent upgrade proof remain unavailable; CI and enforced reviews remain pending. This does not close #188303 or address the separate #191847 SQLite OOM report.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): idle macOS node worker polls Claude session folders every second
prs.body:
Closes #193879
Related: #192144 (same function, independent retry-clock change, merges cleanly in either order)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app's node worker rescans the Claude session folders every second, for as long as it runs, after the Claude sessions list has been shown once.

## User Impact

User impact: once nothing has listed Claude sessions for 60 seconds, the macOS app's node worker stops rescanning `~/.claude/projects` and the Claude Desktop session store. Listing works as before. The first list after an idle period does one full rescan (15 ms vs 13 ms for 960 transcripts in the source harness). Any client that lists Claude sessions keeps the watches armed for the next 60 seconds, because the Gateway asks every connected node for its list; the saving applies once no client has listed for 60 seconds. Event-backed watches, the normal case under Node, are unchanged.

This removes one steady idle cost. On the laptop where it was found, a packaged worker drops from 2.02% to 0.06% of one core once idle. That is about 2 points of the 4.15-7.95% (mean 6.15%) measured earlier on the installed worker there, not all of it (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

fs-safe's `auto` mode polls every 1000 ms when no qualified event transport exists: always under Bun (fs-safe's `docs/watch.md`: "TSFN lifetime and shutdown have not been qualified"), on Node without the native addon, and on macOS when FSEvents admission fails. The catalog's two tree watches were armed on the first list and never closed. A watch that reports `poll` mode now closes after 60 s without a catalog read, matching the Desktop overlay's existing 60 s refresh. The next read sees `"all"`, takes the existing full-rescan path and re-arms the watch. The change keys on the watch's reported mode, not on the runtime or its version. While the catalog is in use, incremental dirty tracking still applies, so unchanged trees still cost no extra reads.

<details><summary>Root cause, alternatives, details</summary>

Root cause:
- `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-tree-watch.ts:30` (base) calls `watch(authority, { mode: "auto", ... })`. Under Bun, fs-safe 0.27.1 selects `poll` (watch health for the 960-transcript tree: `{"state":"ready","mode":"poll","directories":41}`, same on base and head), with a 1000 ms main-thread rescan.
- Armed for `~/.claude/projects` at depth 2 from `session-catalog-scan.ts:284`, and for `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude-code-sessions` at depth 3 from `session-catalog-desktop.ts:567`, on the first `anthropic.claude.sessions.list.v1`.
- Nothing closed either watch. The Control UI stops listing while hidden (`ui/src/components/session-data-catalog.ts:166`), so the polling continues with no reader.

Change (`session-catalog-tree-watch.ts`, +33):
- `takeDirty()` records the last read time (`performance.now()`).
- After `ready`, a poll-mode subscription schedules an unref'd idle check. Reads inside the window push the deadline out. After 60 s with no read, it closes the subscription, sets `dirty = "all"` and `retryAt = 0`.
- The next `takeDirty()` returns `"all"` and restarts the watch. The callers already handle `"all"` with a full rescan (scan: full snapshot; Desktop: overlay refresh, as in #141147).
- `start()` clears the idle timer, so the timer always belongs to the current subscription. A polling watch that fails and comes back event-backed is not closed by a leftover timer.
- `close()` clears the timer.

Why 60 s: it matches the Desktop overlay's `CLAUDE_DESKTOP_SCAN_TTL_MS = 60_000` (`session-catalog-desktop.ts:354`) and sits below the projects snapshot's `CLAUDE_SESSION_SCAN_HARD_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000` (`session-catalog-scan.ts:12`), after which a full rescan happens anyway. The only new cost is that reads spaced 60 s to 5 min apart become full rescans instead of incremental ones.

Alternatives considered:
- Skip the watch entirely in poll mode (first attempt, dropped). Every read became a full rescan, and 2 quiescence tests in `session-catalog.test.ts` failed: they assert that unchanged trees cost no home I/O, and that suite also runs under Bun. Keeping the watch while the catalog is in use preserves that contract.
- Lengthen the poll interval. It still costs something forever, and it slows change detection while the list is open.
- Poll on demand (`pollIntervalMs` very long plus `reconcile()` per read). Every read would become a guarded scan, which breaks the same "unchanged trees cost no home I/O" contract.
- Qualify a Bun event transport in `@openclaw/fs-safe`. fs-safe keeps Bun on polling because native-callback lifetime and shutdown are not qualified there, and OpenClaw already runs Bun file watchers in polling mode elsewhere (#150655). Changing that is a dependency and pin change, outside this fix. Once `auto` yields events, this idle close no longer applies.
- Close watches from UI visibility. The node does not know who its readers are (several Control UIs, CLI). The watch owner sees every read, so it decides.

</details>

**Risks**
- Under poll mode, the first list after 60+ s idle does a full rescan plus re-arm: 15 ms vs 13 ms on the base for 960 transcripts (an earlier run on the same host: 19 ms vs 9 ms). Larger trees are unmeasured.
- A client that lists more often than every 60 s keeps the watch armed. That is intended.

## Evidence

Packaged macOS app: debug, ad-hoc signed builds of the base and this head beside the installed app, one at a time, separate profiles, real `~/.claude`, bundled Bun 1.4.4 in both, remote Gateway 2026.11.1. "Listed" rows: one `anthropic.claude.sessions.list.v1` call (`nodes invoke`, limit 20, 20 rows), then three 60 s windows starting about 150 s later. CPU is the `ps` CPU-time delta per 60 s window, mean (range). The worker pid stayed the same within each state.

| Build | Worker CPU (% of one core) | `__getattrlist` / `lstat` (8 s sample, top of stack) | RSS, last window |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base `ec702e83388`, listed | 2.02% (1.95 to 2.08) | 7 / 99 | 290 MB |
| Fix, listed | 0.06% (0.03 to 0.10) | under 5 / under 5 | 603 MB |
| Base, control windows, listed by another client | 1.80% (0.43, 2.07, 2.90) | under 5 / 89 | 673 to 674 MB |
| Fix, control windows, listed by another client | 1.42% (0.37, 1.25, 2.65) | under 5 / 48 | 612 to 604 MB |

`sample` prints only entries of 5 or more. RSS is not part of the claim: the base worker's RSS fell from 583 to 285 MB inside its first listed window.

Difference on this laptop: 1.96 points of one core. The window ranges do not overlap.

The control rows are not a never-listed baseline. The Gateway log shows a Control UI connection calling `sessions.catalog.list` inside both contaminated windows, and no catalog list during either listed-state measurement. In both builds that list reached the debug worker during the second control window (worker RSS 385 to 673 MB on the base, 375 to 612 MB on the fix, probe frames in both control samples). Both builds behave the same while a client keeps listing: the watch stays armed, and the fix saves CPU only once no client has listed for 60 s.

After the fix build had closed its watch, listing Claude sessions again returned 20 rows, the same count as the first list, and the `sample` taken right after showed `lstat` 40 at the top of the stack, so the watch re-arms on demand.

For context, the installed 2026.10.10 worker on the same laptop was measured earlier at 4.15-7.95% of one core (mean 6.15%, 19 windows of 60 s taken 10 minutes apart; the earlier windows include exec traffic routed through that node during the investigation). This change accounts for about 2 points of that. The base debug build idled at 2.0% after one list, so the rest of the earlier figure did not reproduce in this setup and is not explained by this PR.

Regression tests in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-tree-watch.test.ts`:
- "retires an idle polling watch and re-arms it on the next catalog read" forces poll mode and checks keep-alive while reading, retirement after the idle window, a full rescan for changes made while unwatched, and dirty tracking after re-arm. Base `ec702e83388`: fails (`expected 'ready' to be 'closed'`).
- "keeps an event-backed replacement armed after a polling watch restarts" covers a polling watch that becomes unavailable and restarts as an event-backed watch. Without the `start()` timer reset: fails (`expected 'closed' not to be 'closed'`).
- This branch: 4 of 4 pass.

Test cost: `pnpm test extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-tree-watch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 4.8 s of Vitest time on a warm run (7.3 s wall, 83% transform; about 55 s cold), and the four tests take 0.4 s (new cases 285 ms and 107 ms). CI: pending (filled in after the first CI run). Test-line growth (+77) is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/anthropic-catalog-poll-watch-idle.txt`. Both regressions need a real poll-mode subscription and fake timers at the watch owner, and no cheaper layer proves them. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged`: OK, slack 15, the same as the base.

<details><summary>Consumers, source harness, checks, #192144</summary>

Consumers: all 7 Anthropic session-catalog suites pass, 69 tests (`pnpm test` on `session-catalog{,-tree-watch,-desktop,-runtime,-history,-home,-transcript}.test.ts`, `--maxWorkers=1`). The two production callers of `createDirtyDirectoryWatch` (scan, Desktop overlay) are covered by `session-catalog.test.ts` and `session-catalog-desktop.test.ts`.

Idle cost, source harness (Bun 1.4.4 on a busy Mac Studio, load average 12 to 29; 960 synthetic transcripts in 40 projects; 65 s after the last read, process CPU over 30 s; n=1 per row). The control runs the same harness and imports without calling the catalog.

| Case | Idle CPU (% of one core) | RSS |
|---|---|---|
| Base, control, no catalog read | 0.04% | 39-40 MB |
| Base, one read | 1.51% | 50-52 MB |
| Fix, control, no catalog read | 0.06% | 39 MB |
| Fix, one read | 0.09% | 47-48 MB |

With #192144 applied on top, the file passes 5 of 5. The restart test passes the retry backoff on both the wall clock and the monotonic clock, so it holds in either landing order.

`pnpm check:changed --staged`: 31 lanes pass, including format, lint, extension typecheck, extension test typecheck, plugin boundaries and runtime import cycles. Two fail, both outside this diff and with identical output on the base `ec702e83388`: changelog attributions (26 "Thanks @" lines in `CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`) and the dead-export scan (`readUpdatePhysicalDatabaseGenerations`, `enqueueSlackRun`).

</details>

Local review: autoreview (openclaw/agent-skills `02f3158`, helper `source-sha256:fe60ad81...`), Claude engine `claude-fable-5` because Codex CLI was unavailable, branch mode `ec702e83388..cd6636c0706`, all priorities (`--max-priority P3`), 1 pass with the changed file, its test and both callers as source context. Outcome: 0 findings, "patch is correct" (confidence 0.8). It added two notes below its threshold: a retired subscription can still be closing when its replacement starts, which is harmless because the reference is dropped first and late invalidations only widen `dirty`; and mode is read once at `ready`, which fs-safe documents as fixed after readiness. Stated gap: the reviewer did not run the tests or read the fs-safe watch SDK. Self-reported; no hosted review requested.

prs.title: fix(github): recover saved repository publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repository-backed sessions can publish against their selected source branch instead of the current default branch, and saved publication requests cannot recover from pre-effect outages or retained-worker reconnects.

## User Impact

Publication integrates the accepted checkpoint with one observed target tip in private worker Git state. It preserves later edits, the editing index, the original request, and existing PR metadata. Explicit retries revalidate the original requester and publisher; they never force-push or adopt an unmatched external head.

New capture still requires the exact authoritative disk. Existing App-publication restrictions remain unchanged. Live Gateway-to-GitHub publication and cloud acceptance are not yet verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing checkpoint, publication receipt, placement/runtime recovery, and transfer owners. Retained Git ancestry is used only when its tree matches the saved input. Publication holds the editing reservation only while capturing that input, admits retained compute before reconnect, and keeps subsequent merge work private. A background ref fetch does not delay activation. Failure receipts retain safe transport facts without command output.

No database schema or existing protocol version changes. The node feature is guarded by the existing workspace-result capability, absent from stable v2026.11.1. Main's existing restored-transfer custody and intentional App-publication prohibition are preserved.

## Evidence

- Source-ref destination and same-key pre-effect retry regressions failed on the pinned main base before their fixes.
- Real Git plus Gateway HTTP transfer verifies retained-history reconstruction, the nonmatching-history conflict control, unchanged HEAD/index/later edits, and preserved transfer snapshot custody.
- Passing focused runs cover restart/retry (9 tests), worker receipt/source isolation (23), compute/reconnect/conflict transport (3), requester authority (45), workflow authority (28), and node connection/workspace behavior (42). Targeted reruns cleared the observed deferred-session failures.
- The added managed-merge regression failed on the first implementation and passes after the review correction: a later publication contains upstream changes, the original request retries, a lost push reply is reconciled, and the checkpoint and PR body remain unchanged.
- Core and focused test typechecks, targeted lint/format, docs MDX, and diff checks passed. The full build completed before the final commit-validation correction; that correction was subsequently tested and typechecked. The build reported an advisory chat-boot budget warning (1264.8 KiB versus 1264.4 KiB); no budget was changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing work signal when a chat is waiting on subagents or still has task-owned background commands running.

prs.title: fix(gateway): agent.run can carry a fallback ladder so a pinned model no longer dead-ends on a quota 429
prs.body:
Closes #186418
Related: #151980, #141115, #181981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation caller that pins a model on the WebSocket agent.run request loses the agent's configured model-fallback ladder, so a quota-class 429 ends the run instead of advancing to the next candidate.

The request schema had no way to express a chain, so the only lever an automation caller had was to pin a model - which silently suppresses the configured ladder. Operators who configured a working fallback chain for the agent had no caller-side way to keep it alive.

## User Impact

User impact: automation callers can now send an explicit fallback ladder with their agent.run request, so a provider quota window on the pinned model no longer ends the run - the run advances to the next candidate the caller named.

This is opt-in and additive. A request that pins a model and sends no ladder behaves exactly as before: the pin stays strict and the configured chain stays suppressed, which is the contract #151980 asks to keep.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway already had the pieces to carry a run-scoped chain, but the wire protocol could not express one. Rather than relax the strict-pin contract, this change adds an explicit field so the caller states the chain it wants:

- agent.run accepts an optional fallbacks array of provider/model refs. Entries are trimmed, de-duplicated, and bounded to 16.
- The ladder is authorized exactly like a model override: a caller without the model-override scope is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST and a clear message.
- Every named model is checked against the agent's visible model set and the caller's operator authority before the run starts, so a caller cannot widen model access by naming extra chain entries.
- The chain travels with the run as a request-scoped override, so it is used for this run only and does not become session state.

The request-level pin remains the primary model; the ladder only adds candidates behind it.

## Evidence

Focused test runs, both green on this branch (rebased onto main at d2491817):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 33 passed (33)

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 44 passed (44)

Typecheck:

    pnpm tsgo:test:root -> exit 0 (all root shards)
    pnpm tsgo:test:packages -> exit 0

New coverage:

- src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts - a request that carries both a pinned model and a ladder keeps the ladder and reports it as request-scoped; a request with a ladder but no model-override scope is rejected; a request with no ladder leaves the override unset.
- src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts - a request-supplied ladder survives a pinned model during model selection, and a request-supplied chain that names a model the agent cannot use is rejected before the run starts.

Behavior with no fallbacks in the request is unchanged, so existing agent.run callers are unaffected.

prs.title: fix(onboarding): keep npx Gateway services running after cache cleanup
prs.body:
Fixes #192328

## What Problem This Solves

Quick start skips background-service setup for npx/dlx users, so closing the terminal stops the Gateway. A manually installed service can also depend on files that disappear when the runner cache is cleared.

## Solution

On supported hosts, Quick start offers background operation. A service installed from npx, pnpm/Yarn dlx or bunx runs the same OpenClaw version from a durable npm copy under the profile's state directory (`<state>/npm`). This applies to `openclaw gateway install`, onboarding/configure/Doctor setup and `openclaw node install`.

- **Planning decides, and never installs.** The runtime and wrapper are validated first, including generated macOS/Windows wrappers, which planning clears. The service entrypoint is planned from the running copy (same version, same layout), so the argument builder never probes a copy that may not exist yet. Repair and Doctor planning reuse an existing copy only when it matches this version and passes integrity checks. When the copy is missing or does not match, they report an explicit reinstall command instead of installing, and Doctor keeps the service's current CLI, so planning never points a service into the runner cache.
- **The swap happens inside the service install.** Under the package lock, the install checks the durable copy and reuses it when it still matches this version and passes integrity checks. Otherwise npm stages and verifies the copy while any existing service keeps serving the old one. The staged copy must contain the planned entrypoint. The package updater's activation gate releases the swap from `service.install`'s mutation hook, under the service operation lock. The updater's transaction keeps the previous copy until the install settles:
  - **Rule: the previous copy is restored only on proof that native recovery settled.** That proof is the optional, internal `beforeRecovery` hook on `GatewayServiceInstallArgs`. Each platform's recovery calls it after stopping the replacement and before restarting the previous service: systemd stops the unit, runs the hook, then starts it; launchd runs it after `bootout` once launchd has unloaded the label and every booted-out PID has exited, the replacement's and the previous agent's (bootout can return while a job is still exiting), before the previous plist is restored and bootstrapped. If such a process outlives launchd's stop deadline, the hook is skipped, the previous plist is still restored and bootstrapped, and the install reports the wait's error; a Scheduled Task runs it after ownership checks, disable, `/End` and process settlement.
  - **Every other failure after publication keeps the new copy and its backup, and warns.** This covers a failed swap, admission or readback failures, recovery that refuses, whose process cleanup is uncertain, or whose replacement never exits, and update-owned installs. Main never rolls back, so this is never worse than main. A failed first install keeps its new copy, since there is nothing to restore.
  - After a successful install, the backup is retired once the service is verified loaded.
  - Installs that pass no hook keep each platform's existing recovery, and the shared recovery wrapper is unchanged.
- **One package lock.** Gateway and node services share the durable copy but not a service lock, so one file lock on the durable npm prefix covers the check, staging and settlement, including a reuse. A failed install's restore therefore cannot undo another install's swap, or the copy another install's service now runs. Only a dead holder's lock is reclaimed. **`openclaw update` does not take this lock.** It updates the copy in place under its own ownership, so an update running at the same moment as a Gateway or node install from npx is not serialized with it. Every rollback a failed install starts is therefore fenced, whether its publication completed, stopped part way or its service activation failed. The fence is passed to the package rollback as its authority, which the rollback runs synchronously right before each rename, after its backup verification. It admits only trees the install owns, by directory identity: its validated candidate (the directory the swap renames into place), the copy that was live when the transaction was registered, that copy as the backup, or none while it is moved aside. If an update has replaced the copy at any point before the restore's renames, the install keeps it, keeps its own backup and warns. A concurrent `openclaw update` during a failed install can leave the new copy in place, same as main today. The durable copy is published in the service install's `beforeMutation` hook, which runs before the service's runtime-pin check, so a `gateway install --force` whose runtime pin another install changed while npm staged the copy can leave the new copy in place when the pin check then refuses the install; the service keeps its definition and runs that copy on its next restart.
- **PATH and lifecycle.** The service PATH gets the durable launcher folder and excludes disposable runner paths. npm lifecycle scripts run with the current Node. Standalone runtimes and genuine wrappers don't use a durable copy.

## Evidence

- **Targeted tests:** the affected daemon, setup, planning, Gateway-install and node-install test files pass with `--maxWorkers=1`. `tsgo:core`, the affected test-typecheck shards, lint, format and the test-lines ratchet (against current main) pass. The test-line allocation records the change's 1177 net added test lines.
- **Regressions:** each fails on the commit before its fix and passes on this head. They cover:
  - an unsupported `--runtime bun` rejected before any package work;
  - generated-wrapper planning;
  - swap, restore and backup retirement around the service install;
  - first Gateway and node installs through the real argument builder;
  - a staged copy missing the planned entry;
  - a failed Gateway install's restore racing a node install that either replaces or reuses the shared copy;
  - Doctor run from npx with no durable copy keeping the service's CLI instead of planning the `_npx` entry;
  - systemd recovery running the hook between stopping the replacement and starting the previous unit, and not at all when the stop fails; launchd recovery running it only after the booted-out PID exits, both when the replacement loaded and when its bootstrap failed after the previous agent was booted out, and skipping it while still restoring the previous plist when the PID never exits; Scheduled Task recovery running it after ending the replacement and before the previous task runs;
  - a settled recovery restoring the previous copy, and the new copy kept when the restart's process cleanup is uncertain, when definition readback fails after a successful native install, or when Scheduled Task recovery cannot settle a still-queued replacement;
  - through the real package swap and rollback, a settled recovery restoring the previous copy, a failed launcher copy keeping its partly published copy, and no restore over a copy that `openclaw update` published while the install's updater was finishing, before the restore started, or while the rollback verified its backup.
- **Live Linux proof (`7c54aca2d47`, which does not include the current planning, locking and recovery code):** it used a fresh npx Quick start in a throwaway user with its own systemd manager.
  - The Gateway survived closing the terminal, deleting the `_npx` cache and restarting the service.
  - The service ran from `<state>/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`, with the durable `npm/bin` and no `_npx` on its PATH.
  - An npx reinstall/upgrade from published `2026.10.10` kept settings and an existing session.
  - Model responses were mocked; install, migration, storage and systemd were real.
- **Not verified:** standalone installs end to end, macOS/Windows hosts (launchd recovery is covered by the fake-launchctl tests only), real-model inference, an `openclaw update` run of the durable copy, and a live repeat of the install/upgrade proof on the current head.

## Hosted CI

CI for the current head has not been checked here.

prs.title: fix(mattermost): person posts with a link-preview card are dropped as system posts
prs.body:
Fixes #193811

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Mattermost silently ignores an allowed person's message when a server-side link-preview plugin attaches a card, and omits that message from recovered thread history.

## User Impact

User impact: person-authored posts with attachment cards can start normal turns and remain available in recovered history. Real system posts remain ignored; sender, self and bot admission rules are unchanged. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mattermost reserves `system_*` types for system events; `slack_attachment` is a person-message attachment type. Both live ingress and history now use that distinction, matching the existing draft-stream classification. Typed posts stay separate from text batches. The original fix by @kaguranananana is retained, with consolidated owner-level regressions and channel documentation.

## Evidence

[Real-server before/after results and focused regression evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193836#issuecomment-6674602030).

Built main and exact candidate ran against real Mattermost preview 12.0.2 with a real server-side preview hook. A URL-only human DM produced no turn/reply on main and one turn/reply on candidate. Plain messages remained successful; real system joins/header changes, denied senders, self and bots remained ignored. An older typed thread root was absent from main's model history and present on candidate. The model endpoint was a deterministic local HTTP/SSE fixture; the Gateway, compiled bundled plugin, server and delivery were real.

Main's targeted regressions failed in both affected paths while its plain-message case passed. Candidate focused suites passed 91 tests; final selected regressions passed all three cases. Changed-file format/lint passed. Tests are net zero lines; no allocation is added.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the old filtering behavior; no persisted schema, configuration or published API changes. Blast radius is Mattermost inbound non-system typed posts and recovered thread history. If classification is wrong, those posts could be incorrectly admitted or discarded, but existing sender/self/bot checks and batching policy remain in place.
