prs.title: fix(update): cleanup blocks forever on a rollback original already gone after an interrupted cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update cleanup blocks forever on a rollback original that is already gone after an interrupted cleanup.

On a real Mac install, `openclaw update cleanup` kept reporting two originals as `artifact-verification-failed`: "artifact is unexpectedly missing". An earlier cleanup run had recorded consent to dispose them (a `pending-disposal` receipt in the `intent` phase), then stopped. The files and their claim names were then removed outside cleanup. Nothing was left on disk, but every run refused them. A blocked original also pins the other originals from the same migration.

## User Impact

User impact: an original whose consented disposal was interrupted and whose bytes are already gone is recorded as disposed. It no longer blocks cleanup. Originals that were never selected for disposal stay reported as missing, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A `pending-disposal` receipt is written only after the user has confirmed retirement of that exact selection. When both the original and its `.cleanup-*` claim are absent, there is nothing left to verify or protect. Cleanup already settled this state for the `unlink-pending` phase. It now does the same for `intent`:

- The artifact check returns "nothing left" for any `pending-disposal` receipt with no bytes on disk, instead of throwing.
- Destination verification is skipped for such a receipt. It protects only bytes that are about to be removed, and there are none. Before this change, an already-unlinked original behind a reboot-renumbered or replaced destination blocked forever.

Nothing changes for originals still on disk, or for `retained` receipts whose files are missing. Those keep the existing "missing originals" report and are not marked disposed.

## Evidence

Reproduced on `origin/main` d0b0fc80a34d with real SQLite. The fixture is a migration original whose destination's recorded `dev` differs from the live file and which is written after the "reboot". A later update has completed, the receipt is set to the given state, and the original is removed.

`src/commands/update-automatic-cleanup.test.ts`, base vs this branch:

| Receipt | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | blocked: `artifact-verification-failed` "artifact is unexpectedly missing" | `disposed` / `completed-interrupted-disposal`, receipt `disposed` |
| `unlink-pending` | blocked: `destination-verification-failed` "Recovery destination device changed ..." | `disposed` / `completed-interrupted-disposal`, receipt `disposed` |
| `retained` (negative control) | reported as a missing original, receipt `retained` | unchanged |

Related suites (21 files, found with `git grep` on the retirement and cleanup entry points): 271 passed, 3 skipped (existing skips), 0 failed.

**Stored-data compatibility** (`src/commands/update-cleanup.stored-manifests.test.ts`, which now holds both #193743's remount case and this case on one shared stored-manifest builder): the test writes two startup-migration manifests as raw JSON in the exact shape 2026.10.x stored them on the affected install, with synthetic paths and IDs:
- an interrupted run with three targets, each holding a `pending-disposal` `intent` receipt with its own `.cleanup-*` claim path, where the main database's original and claim are both gone;
- a run that was never selected for cleanup, with a `retained` receipt whose original is also gone.

The destinations are real SQLite files written to afterwards, and a later update completes.
- Base: the gone original is blocked with "artifact is unexpectedly missing", and its two siblings are `protected` as `retained-recovery-dependency`, so the whole group is stuck.
- Head: the gone original is `disposed` / `completed-interrupted-disposal`, and both siblings are removed. In the interrupted manifest only the disposal receipts change; every other field is deep-equal to what was stored. The never-selected run is still counted as a missing original, and its manifest file is byte-identical.

This proves receipts already on disk from earlier interrupted cleanups load unchanged and settle without a migration. It also proves that originals nobody selected are not marked disposed.

Test-line growth after merging main (with #193743): +72, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/update-cleanup-gone-original.txt`.

Related: #193743, which fixes the `destination-verification-failed` refusal for originals still on disk after a reboot.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve native identity for managed headless logins
prs.body:
Closes #193446. Related: #59849.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed headless Chromium can be challenged on ordinary website login routes because its native user-agent advertises `HeadlessChrome`.

## User Impact

The returned managed browser uses its own native version and platform with only the headless marker removed, consistently across HTTP requests, tabs and workers. Explicit user-agent arguments, headed browsers and remote CDP browsers retain their existing behavior. The browser change adds no schema or configuration migration. Same-state release adoption exercised the existing native agent-database migration described below.

**Tradeoff:** reading Chromium's complete native identity requires one owned-process relaunch. Its first discovery launch may restore saved tabs and make requests with the original headless identity before the normalized browser is returned. This is not a promise of challenge-free startup, CAPTCHA bypass, or access to every site. It keeps the persistent profile and uses the existing graceful, bounded child shutdown owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

A fixed user-agent would go stale or invent a platform, and per-tab patches miss workers and later CDP clients. Read the launched executable's identity and apply the native process-wide flag. Explicit overrides take precedence. If identity discovery is unavailable, retain the working browser; cancellation still cleans up its exact owned child. The existing guarded CDP-version reader moves with this identity responsibility without changing its error handling.

## Evidence

**Shipped-path proof now attached below, on exact head `ff8fb23429d04fb4e0d889f0ecd6ca052834f2af`:** official npm latest `2026.11.1` supplies the released-state control; the candidate CLI → isolated Gateway → real Chromium 153 preserves its browser settings, cookie and localStorage, and normalizes HTTP/tab/worker identity. A separate fresh profile passes the same identity checks. Public Gateway `/stop` during pending startup rejects that startup, removes its owned Chromium children and preserves another running profile. Client disconnection intentionally preserves shared startup.

The release fixture first receives the native agent-schema v27→v40 refusal; prescribed `doctor --fix --non-interactive` saves backups and migrates it before the successful adoption. Candidate package label `2026.10.10` predates released `2026.11.1`, so this is same-state compatibility/adoption proof, not a chronological version upgrade or a claim that all migrations are unnecessary. The browser patch changes no stored-data schema.

- On upstream `46943d587ace8d66012467d9b4c5dfc833469945`, the new native-launcher identity case fails because no normalized flag is emitted; 9 controls pass. An initial headed-fixture failure was corrected by seeding an existing profile, so the final red result isolates the missing identity normalization.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.headless-launch.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-identity.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.launch-early-exit.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/system-profiles.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **26 pass**, 12.80 s command wall time on the final repair. The 118-line test allocation covers the identity launcher and cancellation/probe-failure regressions; the fixture repair uses existing budget slack. Both required hosted checks pass on exact current head `ff8fb23429d04fb4e0d889f0ecd6ca052834f2af`, including the documentation follow-up.
- **Real Chromium 153, Linux ARM64:** launched through the actual modified `launchOpenClawChrome`, controlled over CDP, with a synthetic loopback HTTP site. After each completed startup, request headers, `navigator.userAgent` in 2 new tabs and worker identities agree on native `Chrome/153.0.0.0`, with no `HeadlessChrome` marker. Repeated across 2 browser generations; a persistent synthetic cookie survives graceful shutdown and restart. The initial-discovery restoration limitation above was observed in this test and remains explicit.
- Full `pnpm build` succeeds (4m51.6s). The first build reports an absolute UI boot-size advisory (800809 B vs 800791 B); the native base comparison subsequently passes at 800191 B vs base 800002 B, 15 requests in both cases. No UI sources or size limits change, and the earlier advisory is not claimed repaired by a UI change.
- Extension and extension-test typechecks, focused typed lint, formatting, line-cap and test-budget checks pass through hk; independent P0–P2 autoreview reports no actionable findings. The CI architecture failure came from a type-only `chrome → chrome-identity → chrome` cycle. The identity owner now infers the launch/stop handle without importing the launcher; the native Madge gate passes with **0 cycles**, without a runtime behavior change.
- The broader CI browser bundle exposed 2 stale cookie-scratch assertions. [#192368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192368), commit `c16858baa256a33134f35970df04519f48d3d7ed`, intentionally retains a per-installation SQLite staging namespace. The unchanged fixture expected its parent to be empty. The pre-fix local run reproduces **2 failures / 24 passes**. The corrected fixture requires exactly one correctly named namespace and verifies it contains no scratch; it still rejects extra parent entries and all leftover scratch files/directories. No SQLite runtime or cleanup policy changes.
- Broad changed checks report unrelated existing unused exports in `scripts/pr-lib/cache-lifetime.mjs` (`recoverDependencyCache`) and `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog-state.ts` (`SessionWatchdogWaitKind`), both unchanged from the baseline.

The real-browser proof uses synthetic state and cookies, not production profiles or credentials. No fresh external-site login, booking or payment is claimed.



## Documentation and owner decision

Commit `ff8fb23429d04fb4e0d889f0ecd6ca052834f2af` fixes the review finding in [Browser configuration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ff8fb23429d04fb4e0d889f0ecd6ca052834f2af/docs/tools/browser/configuration.md#profile-behavior): direct preference seeding avoids a temporary preference-bootstrap browser, while native identity discovery can still require a second launch. The guide now states the additional startup work, initial restored-tab traffic, explicit override precedence and headed/remote behavior. Native Markdown lint checks 1,403 files with no issues; format and diff checks pass. This commit changes documentation only.

The browser owners still need to decide whether automatic normalization should replace the deliberate single-launch default. This proposal does not claim that an owner has approved that tradeoff. Existing explicit `--user-agent` control remains supported.

### Historical affected-site motivation

The initiating observation was an anonymous same-host comparison on November 4 using Chromium 153 and the then-installed OpenClaw beta. Stock headless contexts stayed on a Cloudflare verification page at the Uber login route; changing only the headless user-agent marker while preserving the observed native version/platform and client hints reached the phone/email identifier form. A fresh-context control observed after 30 seconds showed the same difference. Adding a timezone override supplied no additional benefit. These were previously recorded observations, not fresh login trials against this PR, and do not establish universal site access or eliminate IP-reputation effects. No account details or authentication material are included here.




## Inspectable shipped CLI/Gateway proof

Recorded commands and redacted output excerpts follow, with a complete standalone reproduction helper. The helper launches the shipped `openclaw.mjs` entry points; it imports no repository source modules. Identity and continuity use shipped CLI commands. The in-flight lifecycle race uses the public Gateway WebSocket protocol to send stop before start finishes. All state and services belong to disposable loopback fixtures.

Output excerpts cover the recorded stages, including the initial migration refusal and the corrected interpretation of client cancellation. The final helper includes direct HTTP equality assertions; candidate and fresh-profile runs passed those assertions. Browser-owner acceptance of the automatic relaunch policy remains outstanding.

```javascript
   record('lifecycle cancellation: target running=false; exact owned children gone; independent running profile unchanged');
  }finally{ws.close();}

 }
 record(`PASS phase=${phase}`);
}catch(error){record(`FAIL phase=${phase}: ${error.stack||error}`);process.exitCode=1;}
finally{await stopGateway();if(site)await new Promise(r=>site.close(r));await fs.writeFile(path.join(dir,`${phase}-summary.txt`),trace.join('\n')+'\n')}

```

</details>

The exact identity-read AbortSignal regression remains in [chrome-identity.test.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ff8fb23429d04fb4e0d889f0ecd6ca052834f2af/extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-identity.test.ts#L41). The deliberate shared-start cancellation contract is covered by [the existing lifecycle tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ff8fb23429d04fb4e0d889f0ecd6ca052834f2af/extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.ensure-browser-available.waits-for-cdp-ready.test.ts#L115). The native stop race above supplies real-process proof of the separate lifecycle cancellation path.

Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193830.

## What Problem This Solves

Android pull requests always run phone and Wear unit-test rows even when their changed sources affect only one owner.

Phone-source-only PRs can skip Wear unit tests; Wear test/debug-only PRs can skip the two phone unit rows. Shared, build, missing and unknown inputs keep all rows. Scheduled, release and compatibility coverage stays complete.

Broad native workflow run: 700 passed, with one inherited Python fixture failure fixed by the parent. Final eight Android owner cases, tooling typecheck, focused lint, generated-owner check and test-line ratchet pass. Hosted CI remains pending.

prs.title: feat(gateway): keep agent questions answerable across Gateway restarts
prs.body:
Related: #167266

## Problem

Gateway questions lived only in memory. On restart, `stopOperatorInteractions` -> `questionManager.close()` -> `reset()` dropped every pending question:
- Reconnecting clients got `QUESTION_NOT_FOUND`, and the Control UI showed "Unavailable" with no reason.
- An agent waiting on `ask_user` lost its question. The restart-resume turn then told it to "resume your work" with no answer, so the human had to ask again.

## Solution

This replaces the closed 20k-line durable-question stack (#168900, #168912, #168917, #193220, #171666, #171682, #168399, #171710). None of that code or those branches is reused. There are two commits on one owner: the question manager plus one shared-state table.

### 1. Persist questions; dropped ones come back visibly expired (6fbda2a3be82)

- **New table:** a first-use shared-state table `gateway_questions (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, record_json TEXT) STRICT`, modeled on `durable_background_processes`. It is owned by `src/gateway/question-store.ts`. Writes go through a state worker op and the startup read through the read worker; no SQL runs on the main thread. PG fragment and catalogs were regenerated.
- **Writes:** `QuestionManager` upserts on `request` (never awaited by the RPC) and deletes the row when the question reaches a terminal state. Writes are serialized per entry, joined by shutdown drain, and best effort (a failure logs a warning).
- **Shutdown guard:** once the Gateway scheduler is aborted (the first step of `prepareClose`, which closes the same `runtime.scheduler` the aux handlers use), or once the manager is closed, no rows are deleted.
- **Restore:** non-resumable rows come back as `status: "expired", resolvedBy: "gateway-restart"` (existing status and field), kept until the original expiry. The Control UI shows "Expired — Gateway restarted".

### 2. Keep agent questions answerable across restarts (this push)

- **Classification:** there is no wire flag and no marker. A question is resumable when it is ordinary (not secret, no `secretStore`), has no `presentation` (MCP forms), was requested without host `authorizeClient` (which excludes session-communication approvals), and has a `sessionKey` plus a sessionId resolved from `getAgentRunContext(runId)`. That covers `ask_user` and harness questions; secrets-tool and form questions keep the expired-on-restart behavior. Resumable rows store `resume: true`.
- **Restore:** a resumable pending row whose deadline has not passed comes back as a *detached* pending entry: no requester, no waiter, original expiry. `question.list` and `question.get` show it as pending. A resumable row that is already terminal, or whose deadline has passed (the crash path), admits its continuation at startup.
- **Answer, skip, or expiry of a detached entry** admits exactly one new turn in the original session (`src/gateway/question-resume.ts`). It uses the restart-resume sequence: `prepareSessionSystemTurnAuthority({ preserveRecordedSource: true })` -> `captureSessionEventTargetForHost` -> `enqueueSessionEventForHost(text, { source: "tool_handoff", contextKey: "question:<id>", expectedTarget, onAdopted })`. `onAdopted` deletes the row.
  - Answers to detached entries go through `resolveWithCommit`. Its commit upserts the answered row first, and the existing unknown-write-outcome handling is reused. The live synchronous `resolve()` is untouched.
  - If admission fails, an assistant transcript notice (idempotency key `question:<id>:undelivered`) carries the result and the next step, and the row stays for the next start. If the conversation was reset since the question, the notice is written and the row is retired.
- **Continuation text:** one formatter shared with `ask_user`'s `answeredResult`/`noAnswerResult` (exported from `ask-user-tool-normalization.ts`). It produces `ask_user answer (question asked before the Gateway restarted):\n<Header>: <values>`; expired or skipped questions get the existing no-answer note. It is never longer than `answeredResult`'s text for the same answers.
- **No false cancels:** `ask_user` and the harness question path no longer send their abort-time `question.resolve {cancel}` when the abort reason is a Gateway restart (`isAgentRunRestartAbortReason`). Shutdown therefore does not broadcast a false cancel.
- **Restart resume:** a restored session with a pending resumable question records `awaiting-question` and skips `GATEWAY_RESTART_RESUME_TEXT`; queued inputs still continue. The model resumes when the question is answered or expires.
- **During shutdown,** answers to resumable questions return `UNAVAILABLE` ("Gateway is restarting; answer after it reconnects.").
- **Maintainer defaults:** a late answer still resumes even after an unrelated new user message. The continuation runs under the recorded-principal authority, like restart resume.
- **Size:** the answer canonicalization moved verbatim from `question-manager.ts` to `question-answers.ts` to stay under the 700-line cap. Errors are still built by the manager.

## Impact

- After a restart, an `ask_user` or harness question stays answerable until its original deadline, and answering it continues the conversation in a new turn that carries the answer.
- Secret and form questions show as expired after a restart.
- No new Gateway RPC or protocol fields, no change to the model-facing `ask_user` tool definition, no new config, and no CI jobs.
- The table is additive and first-use; the state schema version is unchanged. Rollback leaves the rows untouched.

Accepted edge cases:
- A crash between adoption of the continuation turn and the row delete duplicates the continuation on the next start.
- A crash in the milliseconds before a question's row commits leaves that question unavailable after restart.
- A failed best-effort delete can resurface an answered prompt (as expired, or as pending for a resumable live question) after a later restart.
- Answers sent while the Gateway is shutting down get `UNAVAILABLE` and must be resent after reconnect.
- A skip (cancel) of a restored question is not committed before its continuation, so a crash in that window brings it back pending.
- Own-run (narrow) clients cannot select restored records, because requester authority is never stored. Broad `operator.questions` and admin clients can.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests** in `src/gateway/server-methods/question.restart.test.ts`:
  - *Expired on restart* (commit 1): an ordinary and a secret-store question registered through the handlers, a shutdown cascade (scheduler aborted, requester authority released, manager closed), then a new manager on the same state DB. `question.get` returns `expired`/`gateway-restart` for both. Red on base (`QUESTION_NOT_FOUND`) and red without the scheduler-abort guard.
  - *Resume after restart*: an `ask_user`-shaped question with a resolvable sessionId, then a restart.
    - `question.list` shows it pending.
    - `question.resolve` enqueues exactly one session event, with `source: "tool_handoff"`, `contextKey: "question:<id>"`, and text equal to the formatter output. The continuation text is no longer than `formatAskUserAnsweredText` for the same answers.
    - A second resolve fails with `QUESTION_ALREADY_TERMINAL`.
    - A restart before adoption re-admits exactly once.
    - After `onAdopted`, a further restart restores nothing and the row is gone.
    - Red on base: there is no restore, so the question is not found.
- **End to end on an isolated real Gateway** (temp state, token auth, port 19437) with the repo's QA **mock-openai** provider (`openclaw qa mock-openai`; no real model credentials):
  1. Started an agent turn with the `ask_user` fixture; `question.list` showed it pending.
  2. SIGTERM, then restart on the same state. The startup log showed `startup restart resume: [{"agentId":"main","resumed":0,"skipped":1,"reasons":{"awaiting-question":1}}]`.
  3. `question.resolve` on the restored question returned `answered`.
  4. The mock provider logged exactly one new model request after the answer (3 total: 2 before the restart, 1 after), and that request carried `ask_user answer (question asked before the Gateway restarted):\nDeploy: Staging (Recommended)`. The session gained one new assistant reply.
  5. `gateway_questions` held 0 rows afterwards.
- **Touched and consumer tests pass:**
  - question restart, handler, recovery, own-run, session-access, hosted-caller and communication suites
  - `question-manager`, `server-aux-handlers`, `session-restart-resume`
  - `ask-user-tool`, `ask-user-tool-normalization`
  - harness `gateway-question`, `gateway-question-dispatch`, `gateway-question.authority-worker`
  - `mcp-app-form-resources`
  - `agent-tools.prefix-stability`
  - commit 1's UI question-prompt, question-page and chat-thread question suites
- **Checks:** `tsgo:core`, core test typecheck, `tsgo:ui`, PG and kysely verify, `lint:kysely`, the SQLite worker ratchet (T1 168 -> 168), the line-cap ratchet, and `check:changed` (see below).
- **Test-line ratchet:** this PR adds net +111 test lines against merge base 349859e09efc, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/gateway-question-restart-expired.txt`. The check passes with slack 29; without the allocation, this PR alone would exceed the ceiling by 82. The baseline is unchanged.
- **Inventory doc:** `docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access-inventory.md` is already stale on main. This PR adds the reviewed classification for `question-store.ts` but does not commit an unrelated regeneration.

Gaps:
- No before/after Control UI screenshots of the "Expired — Gateway restarted" label (a text-only change). Restored resumable questions render through the existing pending path.
- No upgrade-from-latest-stable run. The table is additive, first-use, and does not change the schema version.
- The e2e run used the mock provider, not a real model.

Size against merge base, excluding generated PG artifacts:
- About 509 net production lines. That includes the 65-line verbatim move of answer canonicalization and 11 lines of inventory classification. Commit 1 was about 184 lines; this push adds about 324 net, of which about 260 is new logic.
- Tests: +111 net.

pr-simplify pass:
- The continuation reuses the restart-resume admission sequence and the `tool_handoff` session-event source.
- The answer commit reuses `resolveWithCommit` and its unknown-outcome handling, and the manager reuses the existing statuses, grace constant and publication scope.
- No new owner, status, RPC field or config.

`check:changed` (base 349859e09efc): everything passes except two checks that also fail on main and do not involve this PR's files: changelog attributions (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`) and the dead-export scan (`src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test-support.ts: setSourceConfig`). The `lint core` max-lines findings are in files this PR does not touch.

prs.title: perf(ui): reduce style work during typing and navigation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Typing, sidebar toggles, and Usage filtering spend style CPU testing unkeyed selector lists against unrelated elements.

## User Impact

Reduces browser style work while preserving rendered styles, markup, themes, and lazy loading. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

[Chromium's rule-set tests](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/156.0.8078.4/third_party/blink/renderer/core/css/rule_set_test.cc#L384) put multi-member subject `:is()` / `:where()` in the universal bucket; single-member wrappers can use class indexes. [WebKit's rule-set implementation](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/d761c4ce1bc75dcda0b892372b9872a1374744c2/Source/WebCore/style/RuleSet.cpp#L298) uses the same single-selector gate. This splits 30 ranked rules in 11 existing stylesheets, preserving specificity, nesting, and cascade position. Zero-specificity branches retain individual `:where()` wrappers.

A narrow Stylelint rule prevents new safely splittable, unkeyed class/ID lists. Its exact per-file selector/context allowances preserve 146 existing occurrences and only shrink. No runtime code or build transform is added.

The upper-bound copied-bundle experiment split 270 rules and improved Chromium style CPU by 11–19% on typing, Usage, sidebar, model picker, and Sessions entry. A 9/16/32-rule comparison isolated the useful subset. Broader build transforms added more CSS and hash-related Chat bytes; the literal source edits are the smaller tradeoff. Universal pseudo-elements and other remaining lists are deferred.

<details>
<summary>Subset selection and transform comparison</summary>

The subset experiment used 20 rotated five-way pairs on the same machine (300/300 observations passed). Chromium style median changes:

| Copied-bundle candidate | Typing | Usage | Sidebar | CSS raw / gzip delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 9 rules | +1.4% | −2.9% | −2.8% | −45 / −17 B |
| 16 rules | −3.4% | −3.0% | −6.4% | +1,634 / +147 B |
| 32 rules | −3.3% | −6.6% | −12.1% | +1,633 / +134 B |
| A/A | +0.4% | −0.8% | −0.4% | 0 / 0 B |

The final source patch drops two overlay rules because that sheet also ships inline in JS. Broad pre-hash and class-only build transforms caused +812 B and +440 B Chat JS gzip from generated-name changes, respectively. Both implementations were discarded. This PR adds no transform. The remaining 146 eligible authored occurrences and universal/pseudo-element subjects are deferred.

</details>


## Evidence

Baseline: `58155d2bae4c2581e90fb50a84096d9bc69a8837`. Headless production bundles with synthetic fixtures; 20 rotated baseline/head/baseline-control pairs per cell. Chromium CPU uses CDP Performance threadTicks; instrumented selector durations are attribution only. WebKit uses browser-local application span. A/A and host load accompany each run.

**Final head: 510/510 timing observations passed**, including the bounded ten-pair follow-ups below. Desktop rows use 20 pairs per role; mobile uses 30.

| Chromium flow | Style CPU median / p95, base → head | Median change | A/A median / p95 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Typing | 3.097 / 3.439 → 2.879 / 3.332 ms | −7.0% | 3.108 / 3.472 ms |
| Usage filter | 21.544 / 22.798 → 20.020 / 21.858 ms | −7.1% | 21.453 / 22.613 ms |
| Sidebar toggle | 54.011 / 56.446 → 48.055 / 50.489 ms | −11.0% | 54.443 / 56.362 ms |
| Mobile typing, 6× | 38.680 / 46.543 → 35.969 / 46.136 ms | −7.0% | 37.792 / 46.288 ms |

Typing keeps exactly 61 style passes and 33 layouts in every desktop observation; mobile keeps 61/32. This removes work within style passes. Desktop median total task CPU falls 1.0–3.7%. Mobile total task CPU is 328.635 / 437.701 → 337.239 / 424.857 ms: +2.6% median with lower p95, within the acceptance band. Host load was recorded on every observation; desktop load median/p95 was 13.45/22.70, mobile 8.79/12.32.

**Limits and follow-up:** WebKit has no application CPU counters in this untraced harness, so this PR makes no WebKit CPU/speedup claim. After an additional ten rotated pairs for typing and Usage, application median/p95 is 61.5/82 → 64.5/86 ms for typing and 749.5/763 → 736.5/787 ms for Usage (30 pairs); sidebar is 260.5/316 → 265.5/282 ms (20 pairs). Typing's paired median delta is +1 ms; its descriptive bootstrap interval crosses zero, and final-input→commit remains 0 ms median/1 ms p95. The small tail increases remain disclosed, including the 140 ms typing outlier; none was removed. Usage's separate follow-up was flat, 736.5/754 → 734/754 ms.

The initial 20-pair mobile sample had higher task p95, so it received ten additional pairs. The combined total-CPU result above meets the band. Mobile script CPU remains a subphase limitation: +6.5% marginal median / +2.6% p95, but +2.529 ms paired median with an interval crossing zero; the follow-up's paired increase was only +0.368 ms. This is a measured style-work win, not a claim that every submetric improves.

Upper-bound experiment: 840/840 desktop and 60/60 mobile observations passed. Broad mobile 6× typing was neutral (37.050→37.138 ms style median), with lower p95 (46.292→42.711 ms).

Computed styles: **84/84 cells identical** across Chromium/WebKit × 400/820/1280 px × light/dark × seven fixtures. Every computed declaration on elements/open-shadow descendants and applicable pseudo-elements is compared in baseline/candidate/restored-baseline order. The initial harness applied motion neutralization before chat readiness, causing 18 WebKit setup failures; correcting that setup resolved them. Six narrow sidebar/picker cells needed full-capture A/A stabilization for deferred virtual-row size measurement; those then passed without excluded properties.

| Bundle surface | Base | Head | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup JS gzip | 90,566 B | 90,568 B | +2 B |
| Startup CSS gzip | 36,821 B | 36,811 B | −10 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Chat JS gzip | 1,294,836 B | 1,295,016 B | +180 B |
| New Session JS gzip | 801,247 B | 801,468 B | +221 B |
| Total CSS raw | 1,670,761 B | 1,672,385 B | +1,624 B |
| Total CSS gzip | 323,339 B | 323,552 B | +213 B |

All 38 startup/Chat/New JS assets are identical after normalizing generated filenames. The existing 192 B Chat comparison allowance covers its hash variance; startup/Chat/New caps do not change. Total CSS caps move to the measured head plus 64 B, within the authorized 1.5 KiB gzip tradeoff.

Focused proof: five Stylelint guard tests, full stylesheet lint, targeted JS lint/format, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, production build and strict base/head performance comparison, `pnpm deadcode:knip` (passed). Initial CI caught the missing scoped allocation for those 92 test lines; the allocation correction is the only follow-up change, and the failed ratchet now passes locally. Fresh independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. `ci:full` requests all UI suites.

Changed-file LOC: 21,743→22,230 (+487); most growth is the Stylelint guard, tests, and shrink-only allowance data. CSS itself changes by +11 lines. Reports and benchmark output are not committed. The separate 92-line test allocation covers five independent lint regressions: unsafe new subjects, keyed exceptions, normalized legacy identity, non-transferable file/context allowances, and mandatory pruning. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

Screenshots below show the baseline and candidate sidebar and model picker with synthetic data; each pair is byte-identical.


| Sidebar before | Sidebar after |
|---|---|
| ![Sidebar before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdc389aa-1b98-4c82-9edf-9d802b752641) | ![Sidebar after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3075f364-9e58-41e7-b2a3-79ff36cba3d0) |

| Model picker before | Model picker after |
|---|---|
| ![Model picker before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f792d90-67d2-4509-a705-1094ea967e9e) | ![Model picker after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8bfbd2a3-1d70-4e60-994a-e4c42a86a344) |


<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Build the pinned baseline and candidate with the repository's frozen dependencies, retaining the baseline under `.artifacts/selector-indexing/baseline`.

```sh
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .artifacts/selector-indexing/baseline \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .artifacts/selector-indexing/baseline \
  --steps chat-typing-prefocused,sidebar-toggle,data-usage-model-filter \
  --viewport desktop --engines chromium,webkit --pairs 20 \
  --output .artifacts/selector-indexing/final-desktop

NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .artifacts/selector-indexing/baseline \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .artifacts/selector-indexing/baseline \
  --steps chat-typing-prefocused --viewport mobile --engines chromium \
  --cpu-throttle 6 --pairs 20 --output .artifacts/selector-indexing/final-mobile
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(update): recover interrupted managed updates on 2026.11.2
prs.body:
Related: #188303. Backports #172784, #175890 and #188497.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recovery paths that leave an update-owned Gateway stop unresolved after an interrupted update, recoverable finalization failure, or completed repair on **release/2026.11.2**.

## User Impact

Restore an owned Gateway only after recovery verifies service ownership, runtime identity, and safe state. Operator stops, named data risks, custody grace, process census, and unknown-owner refusals remain intact. Unowned services receive manual-start guidance rather than failing completed maintenance.

This does not establish that every incident in #188303 is resolved. An already-running old updater cannot acquire these fixes retroactively.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adapt the three existing fixes to the release’s current-core and inline helper owners. Preserve compatible failure history, accept the release’s actual finalizer response, and select the verified installed ledger/terminal writer before post-core repair can migrate state and fail. No plugin-cohort subsystem, recovery-owner restructuring, release metadata, versions, or production schema change is included.

Preparation base: `1bec8184bcd9849061bedf7f4e5cc9405039801a`. The seven commits since original proof base `fc9b9635e6d4142ff42d0409f41d7e306f14c5d0` do not overlap the backport. Original author and human coauthor credit are preserved.

## Evidence

- Original release-base restoration regression failed before the fix and passed afterward. Finalizer-response and operator-stop regressions also reproduced before correction.
- Retained original-base results: 48 finalizer/cleanup, 23 custody, 7 ledger compaction/capture, and 150 recovery sibling tests passed. These are reused results, not current-head reruns.
- Final release-base **13 interrupted-helper tests pass**, including two terminal-failure regressions that fail on the uncorrected head. They exercise detached helper/publication/persisted terminal-record paths with a synthetic finalizer.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass for the correction. Original-base core/infra typechecks passed. Rebound CLI typecheck is blocked by the wrapper refusing linked declaration dependencies outside this checkout; no current-head CLI typecheck pass is claimed.
- Canonical autoreview via authenticated OpenClaw engine, effective `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, covered the full prepared range. Its remaining finding was the old indexed terminal writer while the working-tree fix was present; after staging the fix, a fresh correction review against `6189a2636644a0777df90e8ef26a94b738cb66b0` was scoped-clean. Final correction commit: `0e783c4874dd14aff32561b81b96370a521ac8a7`.

**Draft / remaining gates:** native macOS/launchd and packaged actual-candidate/real-agent upgrade proof are unavailable. Emulated managers and synthetic failure paths do not establish real cross-version migration or native incident resolution. PR CI, CODEOWNERS review, and release validation remain pending.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: docs(whatsapp): document the markdown.tables rendering mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/channels/whatsapp.md` describes markdown conversion before chunking but never documents `channels.whatsapp.markdown.tables`, even though the shared channel account shape accepts it and every WhatsApp send resolves the mode at runtime. Users have no documented way to change table rendering for WhatsApp, while Signal, Telegram, Twitch and Nextcloud Talk all document the same key.

- Problem: `channels.whatsapp.markdown.tables` is missing from the WhatsApp docs.
- Solution: document the accepted values, the runtime default, the `block` fallback and the per-account override in the text chunking accordion, and list the key in the configuration pointer table.
- What changed: `docs/channels/whatsapp.md` (2 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key is live configuration, not a schema leftover: `buildChannelAccountSchemaParts` injects `markdown` into the shape WhatsApp spreads into both the root section and each named account, and `resolveMarkdownTableMode` reads it on the outbound and monitor paths. The wording mirrors `docs/channels/signal.md` ("`off | bullets | code` (default `bullets`); `block` falls back to `code`") because WhatsApp applies the identical fallback in `markdownToWhatsAppChunks`, so the two channel pages now agree on the same shared key.

## User Impact

Users can discover the table mode for WhatsApp, its `bullets` default, that `block` is accepted but renders like `code`, and the `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.markdown.tables` override without reading source. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `src/config/zod-schema.channel-messaging-common.ts:78` declares `markdown: MarkdownConfigSchema` inside the shared account shape; `src/config/zod-schema.providers-whatsapp.ts:29` spreads `accountShape` into `WhatsAppCommonShape`, which `WhatsAppAccountSchema` (line 45) and `WhatsAppConfigSchema` (line 52) both use.

**Runtime type** — the enum leaf is `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:491`:

```typescript
tables: z.enum(["off", "bullets", "code", "block"]).optional(),
```

**Default** — `extensions/whatsapp/src/shared.ts:212` sets the channel plugin default that the resolver falls back to:

```typescript
defaultMarkdownTableMode: "bullets",
```

`src/config/markdown-tables.ts:47` reads that plugin default, so an omitted key renders `bullets`, not the generic `code` fallback.

**Consumer** — `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.ts:134` and `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.ts:399` both call `resolveMarkdownTableMode({ cfg, channel: "whatsapp", accountId })`, and `src/config/markdown-tables.ts:26-37` prefers `accounts.<id>.markdown.tables` before the channel root. The `block` degradation is explicit in `extensions/whatsapp/src/targets-runtime.ts:327`:

```typescript
tableMode: tableMode === "block" ? "code" : tableMode,
```

**Test** — `extensions/whatsapp/src/text-runtime.test.ts:46-54` (`honors table mode %s`) asserts `block` produces the same fenced table as `code`, which is the documented fallback.

**Docs toolchain**
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,398 internal links, 0 broken
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/channels/whatsapp.md` — pass
- `oxfmt --check docs/channels/whatsapp.md` — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix; the WhatsApp send path is unchanged. No runtime behavior proof applies.

**Exact head** — `5b941d640a62f7e7998d48ec45fdc4b5b4bdfe3d`

prs.title: docs(himalaya): update skill search, compose and send examples for Himalaya 2.x
prs.body:
Related: #192675

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent following the bundled `himalaya` skill on a current Himalaya install (2.x; Homebrew ships 2.2.1) runs commands the CLI rejects at argument parsing: `himalaya folder list`, `himalaya envelope list from … subject …`, `himalaya template write`, `himalaya template send`, and in the composition reference `himalaya message reply 42 --all`, `cat message.txt | himalaya template send` and `himalaya message write -H …`. The open #192685 fixes `folder list` (the line #192675 reports); this PR fixes the other six and the composition reference.

- Himalaya 2.x moved filtered listing to `envelope search <query>`, removed the `template` commands (raw messages go through `message send`), and builds replies, forwards and new messages from flags instead of an editor (`--to`, `--body`, `--attach`, `--send`).
- **Scope boundary:** only `skills/himalaya/SKILL.md` and `skills/himalaya/references/message-composition.md`. `himalaya folder list` is left to the open #192685, and `himalaya account configure` (Setup) and `references/configuration.md` to the open #176276; this PR does not touch those lines. The copy/move/delete/flag lines already fixed in #182376 are unchanged. The MML syntax sections of the reference are unchanged; the reference now says that Himalaya 2.x no longer compiles MML itself.

## User Impact

User impact: the skill's read, search and write examples now run on Himalaya 2.x, so an agent no longer burns turns on `unrecognized subcommand` errors before falling back to `--help`. The examples now use 2.x syntax only; a host still on Himalaya 1.x would need the old `template` and editor-based forms (Homebrew and the GitHub releases install 2.x).

## Why This Change Was Made

Each changed line is the 2.x form of the same operation, taken from the 2.x `--help` output: `envelope search from alice@example.com and subject invoice` (the 2.x query language combines conditions with `and`); `message compose` with `--to/--subject/--body`; `message send` reading the raw message from stdin or a file; `message reply <id> --body …` and `message forward <id> --to …`. In 2.x, `compose`, `reply` and `forward` print the message unless `--send` is given, so the skill says that next to the examples. `message compose --help` points richer composition (multipart, MML) to a standalone composer such as `mml` piped into `message send`, and Himalaya's [migration notes](https://github.com/pimalaya/himalaya/blob/v2.2.1/MIGRATION.md) say "Composition and reading moved out to pimalaya/mml"; the reference intro now says the same.

## Evidence

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** every `himalaya` command line in the two skill files, before (main) and after (this branch).
- **Real environment tested:** Linux. Official Himalaya release binaries v2.2.1 and v2.0.0 (`gh release download` from pimalaya/himalaya, SHA-256 matched against the release asset digests), run in `docker run --rm --network none node:24-slim` with an offline Maildir account (`maildir.root`, `mailbox.alias.trash`; inbox with two messages from Alice "Invoice 42" and Bob "Lunch"). A script extracts each `himalaya …` line from the files, substitutes a real message id for `<id>`/`42` and `Archive` for `<folder>`, and runs it on a fresh copy of the Maildir. Exit 2 is Himalaya's argument-parse error. No SMTP account is configured, so `--send` and `message send` stop at the send backend.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `docker run --rm --network none … node:24-slim /check.sh` with the branch's command list, then the same with main's list, for v2.2.1 and v2.0.0.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```console
main:        folder list, envelope list from …, template write, template send (×2), message reply 42 --all, message write \, message delete <id>
this branch: folder list (left to #192685), message delete <id> (unchanged line; `message delete` is not in 2.0.0 and is present in 2.2.1)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** running the real `himalaya` 2.2.1 binary in `docker`, none of the commands this PR changes fails argument parsing; the branch's one remaining parse failure is `folder list`, which #192685 fixes. Compose, reply and forward print a message starting with its `From:` header. The commands that end in `--send` or `message send` get past parsing and stop only because the test account has no SMTP backend. On 2.0.0 the remaining parse failures are `folder list` and the pre-existing `message delete` line, neither changed here.
- **What was not tested:** sending through a real SMTP/IMAP account; the MML syntax sections and the standalone `mml` composer; Himalaya 1.x (these examples now target 2.x only).
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the account is a local Maildir, so IMAP-specific behaviour is not exercised; message ids are Maildir ids rather than IMAP UIDs.

prs.title: fix(chat-ui): fenced code blocks lose literal timestamps and message-ID lines to metadata stripping
prs.body:
Closes #193799

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native chat's Markdown preprocessing removes timestamp prefixes and entire `[message_id: …]` lines from inside fenced code blocks, so the code block renderer and its **Copy code** action receive altered text and a literal log example loses information.

## User Impact

User impact: fenced code blocks keep their literal timestamps and message-ID lines verbatim, on screen and in copied text; the chat-metadata stripping outside fences is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`stripMessageIdHints` filtered matching lines and `stripPrefixedTimestamps` ran a multiline regex over the whole message, both without checking whether the matching lines sit inside a fenced code block. A new `fencedCodeLineFlags` helper classifies lines belonging to CommonMark fenced code (backtick and tilde fences, up to three spaces of indent, at least three fence characters, closing fence of the same character at least as long with only whitespace after, unclosed fence running to the end) and both strippers skip those lines. The preprocessor's image flattening was already fence-aware through the swift-markdown document walk; this brings the two line-based strippers to the same standard.

## Evidence

- Focused Swift harness built from the **unmodified production files** (`ChatMarkdownPreprocessor.swift`, `ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenter.swift`) plus only a platform-image alias, exactly as the issue describes — compiled and run locally against swift-markdown:
  - unpatched: fenced block renders `job started\njob finished` — both timestamps and the message-ID line gone (matches the issue's OBSERVED output);
  - patched: the fenced block retains all three lines byte-identical (`[Fri 2026-11-06 12:34 UTC] job started`, `[message_id: example-42]`, `[Fri 2026-11-06 12:35 UTC] job finished`), tilde fences likewise preserved, and a non-fenced control still strips (`Intro\n[Fri …] job started\n[message_id: …]\njob body` → `Intro\njob started\njob body`).
- Regression tests added to `ChatMarkdownPreprocessorTests.swift`: fenced backtick case, tilde-fence case (both assert byte-identical output), and a non-fenced control asserting stripping still works. These run in the OpenClawKit test suite in CI.
- `swiftc -parse` passes on both touched files. This machine has no full Xcode install (Command Line Tools only), so the local gate could not run `lint:swift` (SwiftLint cannot load `sourcekitdInProc` without Xcode) and its `macOS app CI tests` lane hit a pre-existing environmental flake (`codesign-mac-app.test.ts` "limits plugin library loading…", which passes 71/71 in isolation on both unpatched main and this head); CI runs both lanes with the full toolchain.

## Not covered

- The native iOS/macOS UI bubble and clipboard itself were not screenshotted (no Xcode); the harness output above is the pre-rendering text the renderer and Copy action consume.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep saved group and icon across fresh runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #166216.

An isolated automation's logical session is naturally renewed for each run. Its fresh-session preference whitelist keeps labels/display names/sidebar placement but omits the stored custom category and icon. A filed automation therefore falls out of its chosen group and loses its icon after its next run.

## Fix

Preserve @AmelioMansour's two-line fix: add `category` and `icon` to the existing `FRESH_CRON_CARRIED_PREFERENCE_FIELDS` whitelist. The existing sanitization owner continues to drop ambient routing/runtime context. No new owner, schema, configuration, auth, retry guidance, model-facing text or scheduler policy.

Consolidate presentation regression coverage into the existing forced/stale reset matrix and retain its runtime/routing-drop checks; do not maintain another helper-only persistence replay. Existing bounded-header and worker-custody preparation coverage is unchanged. Remove the allocation file and clarify the existing fresh-session documentation.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway scheduler proof and focused checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193820#issuecomment-6674211490).

Secretless Docker **node:24.22.1**, independent installed/built main and candidate runtimes, shipped `openclaw.mjs` entry point, faithful local model fixture. Separate explicit profiles, task-owned HOME/config/state/DB/workspaces/loopback ports, with exact binary config/SQLite paths verified. No direct database edits, clock changes, reset helpers, manual run RPC or fault injection.

Create a disabled isolated 10-second recurring job, prepare its logical session through ordinary public RPCs with label, distinct stored displayName, sidebarRoot, category and icon, then enable it once. Let the **real scheduler** complete two natural renewals and read back each result through public RPCs:

| Build | Renewal 1 | Renewal 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Main `f66f7ae67b9f` | category and icon absent | category and icon absent |
| Candidate | category `Renewal proof`, icon 🤖 | category `Renewal proof`, icon 🤖 |

Every renewal has a new UUID matching its successful cron-history receipt. Label, raw stored displayName, effective public displayName and sidebarRoot remain unchanged in both builds. The initial transcript marker is excluded from all cron model requests and the final transcript. A 10-minute temporary status note is cleared before expiry: unrelated runtime state is not broadly copied. Jobs are disabled after observations; config bytes remain unchanged. No external provider/channel delivery or model-quality claim.

The public displayName prefers label; the separate stored displayName is verified via identity-fenced no-op `sessions.patch` readback with only key/expectedSessionId, never re-supplying preference values. Category membership is independently checked through filtered `sessions.list`; `sessions.describe` checks public metadata.

21 focused tests pass across session resolution and preparation, along with typed lint, focused canonical test typecheck and formatter. The final owner regression copied to frozen main has exactly one failure: missing category/icon; 14 other cases pass.

Whole-PR deltas against merge base: production **+2/-0**; tests **+8/-9 (net -1)**; docs +1/-1. No allocation file or shared ceiling changes. Contributor commits remain intact.

## Merge risk

Low: only two presentation preferences join the existing whitelist. Existing labels/display names/sidebarRoot and model-selection preferences retain their behavior; ambient routing, native handles and old transcript context still do not carry into a new run. prs.title: fix(facetime): build the paired audio driver with a supported deployment target
prs.body:
Related: #165206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the paired FaceTime audio driver cannot be built with Xcode 27, because the pinned BlackHole 0.7.1 project declares `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 10.10` for the BlackHole target and Xcode 27 rejects a target below 12.0 as a hard error instead of a warning.

## User Impact

User impact: `facetime.installDriver` completes on a current Xcode, so `OpenClaw-Mic` and `OpenClaw-Feed` are installed and the FaceTime carrier's audio path is reachable. Without this, the driver install fails outright on macOS 27 hosts with Xcode 27, and `facetime.setup` never reaches a usable state. The deployment floor of the installed driver moves from 10.10 to 12.0, which stays below the macOS 14.4 the FaceTime plugin already requires, so no supported host loses the driver.

## Why This Change Was Made

`install-driver-root.sh` invokes `xcodebuild` against the pinned BlackHole project without overriding the deployment target, so the build inherits `10.10` from the vendored project and fails on Xcode 27. This pins `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0` on the `xcodebuild` invocation instead of editing the vendored project, keeping the pinned tarball and its checksum untouched.

The privileged wrapper checksums the installer it is about to run, so `expectedInstallerDigest` in `install-driver.applescript` is updated to match the modified installer. Without that, every install would abort on the digest comparison before reaching the build.

A new test fails if the installer stops pinning a deployment target of at least 12.0, and fails if `expectedInstallerDigest` no longer matches the installer. Those two drift apart silently otherwise: the digest mismatch only surfaces at install time, as an administrator-prompted failure with no indication which file changed.

## Evidence

### 1. The build, before and after

Same Xcode 26.6, same pinned BlackHole 0.7.1 tarball (sha256 `e9de179da54ed55ff27876990f3a2dcfefa66e6bd6cfcba448a8564eabdf3e89`), same `xcodebuild` flags apart from the added build setting.

Before, with the inherited target:

```
base build exit=0
base deployment-target diagnostics:
  /.../BlackHole-0.7.1/BlackHole.xcodeproj: warning: The macOS deployment target 'MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET' is set to 10.10, but the range of supported deployment target versions is 10.13 to 26.5.99. (in target 'BlackHole' from project 'BlackHole')
base built minos:
    version 10.10
      minos 11.0
```

After, with the target pinned to 12.0:

```
patched build exit=0
patched deployment-target diagnostics:
  (none)
patched built minos:
      minos 12.0
      minos 12.0
```

### 2. The digest pin the wrapper checks

`install-driver.applescript` copies the installer into its protected directory and compares the copy's checksum against `expectedInstallerDigest` before running it. Reproducing that comparison against the modified installer:

```
pinned=060835a26dfe8870e1736b47673eaf5e91ed63d0e7a808b23a8f8bb478dd41a8
actual=060835a26dfe8870e1736b47673eaf5e91ed63d0e7a808b23a8f8bb478dd41a8
MATCH
```

### 3. The new test is red on the base installer and green here

```
$ sh extensions/facetime/scripts/test-driver-deployment-target.sh
install-driver-root.sh does not pin MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET
exit=1

$ sh extensions/facetime/scripts/test-driver-deployment-target.sh
driver deployment target 12.0 and installer digest pin agree
exit=0
```

The same test also catches the digest drifting out of sync, which is the failure mode the pin exists to prevent:

```
$ printf '\n# drift\n' >> extensions/facetime/scripts/install-driver-root.sh
$ sh extensions/facetime/scripts/test-driver-deployment-target.sh
expectedInstallerDigest does not match install-driver-root.sh
  pinned: 060835a26dfe8870e1736b47673eaf5e91ed63d0e7a808b23a8f8bb478dd41a8
  actual: 0b3707d1b25a0a3a34ec14032a36f4313e26b3330c5ee9082ad3b31030999923
exit=1
```

### 4. The rest of the plugin's script suite still passes

```
$ for t in test-driver-deployment-target test-driver-transaction test-uninstall-inventory test-xcode-trust; do sh extensions/facetime/scripts/$t.sh; done
test-driver-deployment-target         PASS
test-driver-transaction               PASS
test-uninstall-inventory              PASS
test-xcode-trust                      PASS
```

Package inspection is unchanged: `npm pack --dry-run` ships no native source, generated driver, dylib, `.build`, or BlackHole artifact.

### Gap

This host has Xcode 26.6, where the stale target is a warning and the build still exits 0, so the hard Xcode 27 error is not reproducible here. What the local build does prove is that the pinned target removes the diagnostic entirely and produces a driver whose floor is 12.0. The Xcode 27 acceptance path itself needs a host with Xcode 27, or CI.

No SIP, developer-tools, or macOS privacy setting is touched by this change.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.

Deliberately kept in English: Active Memory, Cron, Dreaming, Heartbeat, Loopback, Markdown, Self-hosted.
- `ru-navigation.json`: **created from scratch — 12 tabs, 55 groups** (8.6 KB), mirroring the English navigation structure.

No page content, no build scripts, no English strings touched: two data files only.

## Verification

- Every path in `ru-navigation.json` was checked against the repository tree (1,385 `.md` files): 0 broken links, 55 unique anchors.
- Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`: 12/12 Russian tabs, 55/55 groups, pages resolve as `ru/index…`.

## Why

The Russian locale is the largest non-English audience for OpenClaw docs and currently has English headings over Russian text. These two files are the smallest, highest-leverage change: no translation work, but the sidebar and the inline glossary switch to Russian immediately.

## Visual proof

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.
- Exact-head CI pending after publication; not claimed green.

prs.title: fix(ios): sessions list looks complete after a later page fails to load
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #193789

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where iOS users opening **All Sessions** (Command Center → Sessions) would silently lose conversations from the list when a later `sessions.list` page failed (timeout, dropped connection): the shared loader returns the already-loaded rows with `isComplete: false`, but the Sessions screen dropped that completeness metadata, so the partial roster was presented as the full result with no warning and no retry path.
- The native sidebar already handles this exact loader result correctly ("Showing N sessions; M total. Refresh to load the rest."); the Sessions screen did not.
- **Related:** #193789 (clawsweeper source-repro review confirmed the current-main failure path and asked for a consumer-level repair plus regression).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** On a partial roster, Sessions keeps the loaded rows visible, shows the same incomplete-result notice the sidebar uses, and offers an in-screen **Refresh** retry that clears the notice after a successful complete load.
- The message derivation moved into a shared `ChatSessionRosterSnapshot.incompleteLoadMessage` computed property so both consumers (sidebar `applyRoster` and `CommandSessionsScreen`) render identical, already-localized copy instead of diverging duplicates. Setting `loadErrorText` alone was rejected because that branch replaces the list and would hide the retained rows.
- **Out of scope:** No loader (`collect`) behavior change, no gateway change, no changes to the full-failure/cached-fallback path beyond clearing the partial notice.
- **Highest-risk area:** The retry wiring reuses the existing `.task(id: refreshID)` refresh mechanism by adding a `refreshNonce` component to the ID.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The nonce only ever triggers the same `refreshSessions()` path already exercised by scope changes; the notice is cleared on every settled load result (success sets it from the roster, error clears it).

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** With a 201-session roster where the offset-200 page fails, Sessions now lists the 200 loaded sessions and shows "Showing 200 sessions; 201 total. Refresh to load the rest." with a working Refresh button; a complete load shows no notice (unchanged).
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift` (partial-load banner + `refreshNonce` retry), `apps/ios/Sources/RootSidebarModel.swift` (shared `incompleteLoadMessage`, sidebar behavior unchanged), regression tests `sessions consumer surfaces an incomplete-load notice after a later-page failure` and `incomplete-load notice stays silent for complete and cached rosters` in `apps/ios/Tests/RootTabsPresentationTests.swift`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Source-level verification in an isolated worktree at `origin/main` (`abed61f6400`). No macOS/Xcode toolchain is available on the contributor machine, so the Swift test lane runs on CI's macOS runner (CI lanes pending at creation time).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Static verification of the consumer wiring and shared message helper:
  rg -n "incompleteLoadMessage|partialLoadText|refreshNonce" apps/ios/Sources apps/ios/Tests -g '*.swift'
  # SwiftFormat constraint checks (max width 120, no bare .font(. shorthand in CommandCenterTab):
  git diff -U0 | rg '^\+' | awk '{ if (length($0)-1 > 120) print }'   # no output
  rg -c '\.font\(\.' apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift    # no match
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift:1255:            self.partialLoadText = roster.incompleteLoadMessage
  apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift:902:                if let partialLoadText {   # banner rendered alongside retained rows
  apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift:912:                            self.refreshNonce += 1   # in-screen retry
  apps/ios/Sources/RootSidebarModel.swift:31:    var incompleteLoadMessage: String? {
  apps/ios/Sources/RootSidebarModel.swift:590:        self.sessionErrorText = roster.incompleteLoadMessage   # sidebar copy unchanged
  apps/ios/Tests/RootTabsPresentationTests.swift:216:        #expect(snapshot.incompleteLoadMessage == "Showing 200 sessions; 201 total. Refresh to load the rest.")
  ```
  The regression test replays the issue's exact scenario through the production loader: first page returns 200 of `totalCount: 201` with `hasMore: true`, the offset-200 request throws `URLError(.timedOut)`, and the consumer-facing message is asserted.
- **Observed result after fix:** The 200 retained sessions stay listed; the incomplete-result notice with the total count appears above them; Refresh retriggers `refreshSessions()` via `refreshID`.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** Before: `refreshSessions` stored only `roster.sessions` (old CommandCenterTab.swift:1210-1238), `loadErrorText` stayed `nil` on a partial roster, and the list rendered with no indication that a page was missing.
- **What was not tested:** No simulator/device run and no local `xcodebuild test` (Linux contributor machine, no Swift toolchain); the new Swift Testing cases and the iOS build lane execute on CI's macOS runner. Sidebar rendering path was refactored to the shared helper with identical output but not re-run on device.
- **Proof tier:** L1 (source-level; runtime proof deferred to CI macOS lane)
- **Proof limitations:** iOS runtime behavior cannot be exercised locally; correctness of the notice text and retry wiring is established by source analysis plus the added consumer regression test pending CI execution.
- **Review state:** blocked until live proof (iOS CI lanes on this PR head)

prs.title: fix(ui): return focus to the People filter trigger after selection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selecting someone in Activity's People filter closes the popover but strands keyboard focus on BODY. The next Tab starts from the document rather than continuing from the filter. Escape already returns focus correctly.

Use the existing overlay's `request(false, "return")` when a person is selected, matching Escape instead of introducing another focus owner. Filter values, requests and mouse selection semantics remain unchanged. Preserves huwei-xydt's commits; current main is merged.

## Evidence

[Inspected Chromium and real Linux WebKit before/after screenshots, observations and method](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193310#issuecomment-6674117128).

Built Control UI served by a built Gateway, synthetic session created over public RPC. In each engine: main once leaves focus on BODY; exact head once returns focus to the People trigger. Escape restores trigger focus on both refs. Mouse Everyone selection still closes the popover and clears the actual Gateway `involvingProfileId` filter on both refs. Traces and raw Gateway frames retained. Linux WebKit uses the disclosed driver-only PushAPI native-default correction, not a product change or page API mock.

Focused suites: **27 passed**. The same browser regression on main fails only the focus assertion (four controls pass). Reuses the canonical Activity fixture; tests **net0**, production **+1/−1**. No allocation.

First canonical paired bundle comparison against main `bd7d3415f62847f4577923488e1ce3c8f4cd2792`: Chat **+104 B**, startup **−7 B**, combined **+97 B**; comparator passes without cap changes.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior behavior; no persisted-state or public-contract change. Blast radius is focus restoration after selecting an Activity People filter; existing overlay lifecycle and Escape handling remain the owners.
