prs.title: fix(mcp): avoid false missing-command errors for paths containing spaces
prs.body:
Related: #171620

## What Problem This Solves

`mcp doctor` reports working stdio commands as missing when their configured working directory or a PATH directory contains leading or trailing spaces.

## User Impact

Users can diagnose servers installed in literal whitespace-containing directories without a false command-not-found error. No configuration rewrite or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launch/configuration path preserves literal paths, but doctor still trimmed cwd and each PATH entry. Doctor now uses the existing nonblank-string reader for cwd and preserves PATH entries, including the existing meaning of an empty entry.

## Evidence

- Registered real `mcp doctor --json` command, no mocks, synthetic on-disk configuration: before, both `/proof/bin /proof-mcp` (PATH lookup) and `/proof/app /proof-mcp` (relative command with cwd) reported command-not-found; after, both report `ok: true`, with no issues. Independently spawning the two actual executables completed MCP initialize and tools/list (`ping`) with exit 0.
- Regression before the fix: normal relative PATH passed; whitespace in cwd, a padded PATH entry, and a whitespace-only PATH entry each failed. Final focused regression: all four pass (33.49s Vitest / 168.03s wrapper, dominated by worker compilation and module setup). The regression extends an existing real-filesystem CLI test by 8 lines, with a matching allocation. The existing command-level harness is needed to exercise persisted configuration and filesystem executable discovery together. Windows keeps the original ordinary-path case; POSIX-only whitespace fixtures are excluded there.
- Simplification: removed destructive trimming at the existing diagnostic owner; production net -2 lines, test net +8. No new production helper, option, or state.

- Full touched CLI suite: 44 passed, 1 failed, 1 Windows-only test skipped (154.52s Vitest / 329.78s cold wrapper including worker compilation). The existing initialize-timeout probe test first exceeded its 1.5s timing assertion; focused reproduction reached a probe `ExitError`. Repeating it with the original base production module produced the same probe failure. That `mcp add` path does not call the changed doctor resolver. This known local failure is recorded, not counted as a passing suite.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and test-line ratchet passed. Typechecking used the documented `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo` fallback. Hosted checks for this unchanged head passed (CodeQL is neutral; a superseded auto-response was cancelled).

- An independent reviewer inspected the complete final diff at `def42739e70f0f41fb77e56b6a0cf156bea1027f`, its runtime consumers, red/green evidence, and the unrelated baseline probe failure; no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview is unavailable in this environment because its provider preflight rejects the configured `stream_max_retries` field. This is an independent review, not a successful autoreview run.

### Normal CLI behavior proof (2026-11-06)

Ran the normal `pnpm openclaw mcp doctor --json` launcher at unchanged head `def42739e70f0f41fb77e56b6a0cf156bea1027f` on Linux, Node 24.22.1, pinned pnpm 12.15.0. The normal launcher built its runtime from this source tree; the actual doctor command then ran in a secretless container with `--network none`. No handler imports, Commander harness, mocked filesystem, edited source, or handwritten build stamps were used for this run.

Both the relative command with a literal trailing-space cwd and the command resolved through a literal trailing-space PATH directory return `ok: true` and no issues. Exit code: 0.

<details>
<summary>Literal paths, config, command, and raw output</summary>

Created executable files at these exact paths (the space before `/proof-mcp` is part of the parent directory name):

```text
/proof/app /proof-mcp
/proof/bin /proof-mcp
```

Each file is the existing synthetic MCP fixture with executable permissions and a Node shebang. The prior separate process proof completed initialize and tools/list for these fixtures; this new run verifies the normal shipped diagnostic entry point itself.

Config at `/proof/state/openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "path": {
        "command": "proof-mcp",
        "env": {
          "PATH": "/proof/bin "
        }
      },
      "cwd": {
        "command": "./proof-mcp",
        "cwd": "/proof/app "
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Command inside the isolated container:

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/proof/state \
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/proof/state/openclaw.json \
pnpm openclaw mcp doctor --json
```

Raw stdout:

```json
{
  "path": "/proof/state/openclaw.json",
  "ok": true,
  "servers": [
    {
      "name": "cwd",
      "ok": true,
      "issues": []
    },
    {
      "name": "path",
      "ok": true,
      "issues": []
    }
  ]
}
```

Raw stderr:

```text
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs mcp doctor --json
```

The launcher used the supported Node build runtime with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_BUILD_IDS=memory-core`, and `OPENCLAW_INCLUDE_OPTIONAL_BUNDLED=0`. Build preparation used network access to obtain pinned native build dependencies. Its initial automatic heap preflight stopped; the normal build subsequently completed with the documented `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352` setting. The doctor run above was offline.

</details>

The earlier registered-handler and MCP handshake evidence remains supporting evidence. The new run covers normal CLI startup and the changed static diagnostic. `mcp doctor --probe`, a Gateway, and a latest-stable upgrade were not exercised; this read-only diagnosis change neither writes nor migrates configuration.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep Gateway downtime visible without losing drafts
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191925

## What Problem This Solves
Opening the Control UI while the Gateway starts or reconnects can leave people with a loading screen or sign-in form that does not explain what is happening.

## User Impact
The available Web UI opens its normal shell and shows connection feedback inside the workspace. Cold transport retries keep that shell; genuine authentication failures still lead to sign-in. Existing conversations retain their own connection feedback rather than being replaced by a cold-start page.

On phones, cold-start navigation and action buttons stay hidden until they can be used, including the swipe-open gesture. Desktop keeps a static, muted sidebar placeholder. Automatic recovery does not compete with manual retry buttons; manual controls appear when automatic recovery has stopped.

When app assets are unavailable, the standalone HTTP page checks automatically and resumes checking after browser Back/Forward. A fully stopped listener or host outage still needs the deployment’s existing ingress or cache; this change does not add an always-on server.

**Original snapshot:** published at Vyctor’s request. The avatar refinement and horizontal mobile OpenClaw wordmark are now implemented in the branding follow-up below. No merge or deployment is requested here.

## Why This Change Was Made
Use the existing connection/lifecycle owners and the real application shell instead of a separate persistent holding overlay. Serve available static UI resources before request-runtime materialization while preserving dynamic-request gates and proxy-attribution rejection. Keep unknown failures distinct from confirmed startup or restart states.

Work from @vincentkoc and @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b8649caa-d20c-4494-95ae-bc7a3b47f943)
- [Earlier implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/35425098-5c2c-4ddc-878f-bd74ab2a14d3)

## Validation

- Repaired head: `911b3cb8e3abf839fa166d1cf794b16733bbd4b8`. The branch is rebuilt as two scoped commits on main `57953680cdf7a0ce0e0cfda500545eff8b29f81b`, replacing the unnecessary history merge. Scope check: 35 files, +2,097 / -155; no paths outside the original implementation file set plus the designer’s six branding files. The PR base comparison was refreshed to main.
- 58 focused UI tests and 21 HTTP tests passed during the final refinement. The six affected HTTP maintenance tests passed again after the last fallback-copy changes.
- 14 browser scenarios passed; the five affected fallback scenarios passed again after the last copy changes. Coverage includes cold connections and automatic recovery at desktop/mobile widths, restored navigation, authentication boundaries, bootstrap retry exhaustion/manual reload, missing-assets HTTP recovery and browser Back/Forward.
- Production UI types, UI E2E types, scoped lint/stylelint, source i18n verification and `git diff --check` passed. Generated foreign-locale metadata parity still reports drift; it is not claimed as passing.
- Captures below use the actual built UI with simulated Gateway/network/bootstrap conditions and emulated mobile viewports. They are state captures, not a current-main before/after comparison or proof of a live production restart.
- Full isolated Gateway process-restart acceptance for this revised implementation remains unverified: its runner refused to establish separation from managed Gateway artifacts on this host. No isolation guard was disabled. Binary upgrade, host reboot, current-head CI and fresh independent review are not claimed as complete.

## Branch-repair validation

- Replayed only the original implementation patch, then the designer’s six-file branding patch. Kept current-main changes while resolving two overlapping hunks; removed one obsolete import introduced by the replay.
- 58 focused UI tests and 21 HTTP tests passed on the repaired base; final production UI and UI E2E typechecks passed.
- The browser rerun failed before test execution with Vite’s TypeError: code.charCodeAt is not a function, with both the explicit and default loader. Earlier browser evidence below is not presented as a new repaired-head pass.
- The original branding SVGs contain trailing-whitespace warnings under git diff --check; the same warnings reproduce on the original branding commit. Those assets and the branding patch were retained unchanged.
- The pre-repair head is retained locally at backup/pr-191935-before-repair-20261106. The remote replacement used a lease pinned to 37542fc1414afbd08db635ff5976d0544c6b74d7; no concurrent contribution was overwritten.

## UI captures before the branding follow-up

The agent avatar treatment and missing horizontal mobile wordmark visible here predate the branding follow-up below.

![Current desktop cold connection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fd5a50c-0573-4e25-bcfc-6f313ead4466)

![Current emulated mobile cold connection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/303d64d9-9968-418b-8c26-0198f1235bfe)

## Historical evidence from the original implementation

The prior isolated restart result and three screenshots below belong to the original `d899b9ea8312bae1c680ab9028f17275a66b3727` implementation, not the revised source tree. They are retained for provenance, not current-head validation.

[Original isolated Gateway restart run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41666997098/job/126025740291)

<details>
<summary>Original implementation state captures</summary>

![Original implementation: connected with history and draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aaea8b63-2256-4f79-9605-9c17c093abe0)

![Original implementation: holding notice over retained conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c12e370-861f-4f1f-8161-ef65fc1e066a)

![Original implementation: recovered with history and draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/750cea6a-00fe-4437-b608-6a11b416a70a)

</details>

## Branding follow-up — designer requests

Original branding commit: `37542fc1414afbd08db635ff5976d0544c6b74d7`. Cherry-picked on top of the repair as `911b3cb8e3abf839fa166d1cf794b16733bbd4b8` with Vyctor’s authorship preserved. Its six-file patch has the same stable patch ID; both wordmark assets are byte-identical. Newer main styling outside that patch is retained.

- The holding message now uses the existing theme-aware OpenClaw vector at 48px, without a background container. Agent placeholders reuse the same vector and no longer have a pink circle.
- The cold-start mobile header uses local copies of the official [dark-text](https://openclaw.ai/brand/openclaw-horizontal-dark-text.svg) and [light-text](https://openclaw.ai/brand/openclaw-horizontal-light-text.svg) horizontal wordmarks, selected by the UI’s resolved theme mode.
- Removed the duplicate inline mascot SVG and spinner/dot styling. Connection, draft, retry and recovery behavior are unchanged.

Validation for this follow-up:

- Scoped format, TypeScript/Solid lint, CSS lint, `tsgo:ui`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- 35 nearby unit tests passed (`gateway-connection-view.test.tsx`, `app-shell-view.test.ts`).
- All 9 `gateway-status.e2e.test.ts` scenarios passed against the production build using the standard UI E2E runner.
- All 8 before/after capture scenarios passed. They load the actual source UI against the existing mock Gateway, assert the real connect request, hold its response for capture, then resolve it and verify recovery. No DOM or application-state injection. Viewports: 1440×900 and 390×900, each in light and dark mode. The captures are synthetic-data/browser-viewport evidence, not a live Gateway restart.
- An exploratory source-mode run of the broader Gateway-status suite exposed a desktop placeholder-count assertion (also reproduced on the original `9dfc4a1f1ca` head) and a build-mismatch reload timeout. The supported production-build run above passes; the exploratory source run is not claimed as passing.
- Local Codex autoreview of the branding delta relative to `9dfc4a1f1ca9868c399e141b84f2a49b045f5bd5`: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Review used diff context; unchanged repository context was not included.

prs.title: fix(ios): discard stale wake commands after chat or Gateway changes
prs.body:
Related: #165515 (focused-chat routing; intentionally unchanged here).

## What Problem This Solves

Buffered Voice Wake recognition can outlive a chat, agent, or Gateway change and create another command after the previous command was canceled.

## User Impact

Destination changes discard pending commands and buffered results from the old capture; fresh listening resumes through existing admission gates. **Ready for review and CI; current native validation remains outstanding—not merge-ready. This does not fix main-versus-focused-chat routing**, which remains separate in #165515.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing VoiceWakeManager owns recognition retirement: destination invalidation tears down the old pipeline/generation and cancels its command; internal start/teardown use cancellation-only bookkeeping to avoid recursive invalidation. Phone-focus and selected-agent changes invalidate before assignment independently of Talk's session-key shortcut. Watch-started Talk can already hold the next phone destination or next agent's main key, so that shortcut alone cannot retire the old capture. Current main's focus persistence, selected-agent cleanup, configured-route authority, and restoration ordering are preserved. No new routing owner, generations, configuration, automatic resend, or basic focused-routing callback changes.

## Evidence

### Current reconciled source and available checks

- Published head `635677b8c2d83b1849d633760f674aa59b20d935`, tree `64632771fb218fa5824823faee0db560c57454e3`; native-accepted comparison base `828623faa84e0cdd9cb64f8560cd0c5052291c17`. The publisher preserves prior PR history through base-integration commit `4e6f8b2621023dd15189788d9a1e7c57ea970264`. Base-scoped feature diff: four files, +117/−3; no workflow, dependency/lock, generated-localization, or shared-fixture changes. The maintained upstream fixture supersedes the earlier extraction repair.
- Focus invalidation retains main's assignment → connected-Gateway-scoped persistence → Talk synchronization order. Selected-agent invalidation also precedes assignment, including when Talk already targets that next agent. The production recognition-callback regression includes focus, Gateway, Watch-target coincidence, and agent coincidence; its `@MainActor` throwing receive helper and existing cancellation/stale/fresh assertions remain. **These current native cases are authored, not executed.**
- Owned frozen install passed on supported Node 24.20.0 with exact pnpm 12.15.0, without age-policy waivers or declaration changes. Canonical offline localization sync, verify, and strict local check passed: 4,633 entries, no inventory/catalog/InfoPlist changes, zero contradictions. Affected native/Apple i18n **script tests: 2 files / 53 passed—not Voice Wake behavioral tests**.
- Docs formatting and exact-base whitespace passed. The exact-base test-line ratchet passed with supported direct-base mode; inherited ceiling overage remains unchanged and Swift cases add no counted TypeScript lines. Simplify completed. The prior whole four-file LOCAL P0–P3 review and a fresh exact-base LOCAL review of the compiler repair returned scoped-clean with no findings. The native compiler subsequently exposed a missed test-access error in the prior head, recorded below; static review is not native runtime proof.

### Published native compiler failure and test-only repair

- On prior head `fe5ba009e8efcf08e5b6ce5e44713f1921a191f1`, [iOS build-for-testing job 127606656994](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42130712487/job/127606656994) failed with exit 65: `VoiceWakeManagerStateTests.swift:262:31` accessed private `focusedChatSessionKey`. This was an introduced test compile defect, not an executed production-retirement failure; downstream missing-report scan failures are dependencies.
- This follow-up changes only that test (+3/−1): two throwing preconditions establish old non-main phone focus **before recognition generation and pending-command capture**, and the post-switch assertion uses observable `chatSessionKey == mainSessionKey` alongside the beta-main assertion. Cancellation, stale-generation rejection, and fresh delivery assertions remain. No production visibility, hooks, pipeline, persistence, docs, workflows, or dependency changes. Exact-base whitespace/ratchet passed; the unchanged 53 i18n script tests are reused evidence, **not fresh Voice execution**. **Native build-for-testing is GREEN; Voice runtime assertion execution remains UNRUN.** The [iOS consumer build job127641476237](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42141006681/job/127641476237), associated with current head `635677b8c2d83b1849d633760f674aa59b20d935`, logged `TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED` at 2026-11-06 01:18:11 UTC and packaged `OpenClawTests.xctest`. This is test-bundle compilation, not test execution. The partial log tail omits initial checkout identity, so no exact bare-head checkout is asserted. The 14 new-head workflows were terminal (8 success, 6 skipped); that is not full native acceptance or a no-findings ClawSweeper verdict. Main iOS-build/release-e2e/macOS-Swift placeholders were skipped, not passes. [Screenshot artifact13467169876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42141006851/artifacts/13467169876) was observed as metadata only, not inspected images; its name identifies merge source37203d8…, whose exact checkout binding was not independently established here.

### Historical native receipts—not this composition

The [requester report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191521#issuecomment-6606242554) reported VoiceWakeManagerStateTests **six declarations / eight executions, zero failures/skips**, normal app/Share/Watch simulator build, and focused lint/format on `0fb71abd0c385bdb3b132b0baa0c2004ee173ff6` plus local uncommitted repairs. The [complete repair attachment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191521#issuecomment-6608862109) was recovered and hash-verified; the prior published tree `b5ff2ebea106c5ca8fde0318c00918a1a7887e3d` matched that repaired source. This preserves that historical source-equivalent receipt, **not a fresh Mac execution, hosted-CI pass, or current-main composition pass**. Native logs/xcresults/commands were runner-local, not independently replayed here; execution-time generated-project byte identity remains unverified.

The [earlier qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191521#issuecomment-6591318088) remains historical: correct hosted selection/build exited 65 before execution at inherited fixture lint; an earlier Logic selection exited 0 with **zero tests—not a pass**. Later repairs do not relabel failed, skipped, or permission-blocked attempts.

No fresh repaired-head UI/permission-flow or upgrade proof, or inspected screenshot evidence, was obtained. The change is nonvisual. Duplicate basic focused-routing hunks and speculative send guards remain excluded.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): keep warm composer controls stable through reconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload of a chat/dashboard deep link changes composer labels and geometry after the pane mounts, although its loaded facts have not changed. The campaign's measured 14-state reload timeline motivated keeping cached regions complete while reconnecting. This isolates the composer part: a late selected-window badge moves the model controls/context ring **44.08 px**, and an erased inherited permission default changes `Default` to `Full access` and shifts the trail **19.58 px**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep window/run-action display in the existing composer snapshot. Hand cached session settings to live settings at the existing session-row observation readiness, deleting the superseded history-based predicate. Read inherited permission defaults from the existing agent owner, rather than the pane's history-delayed agents projection. While that owner is unresolved, preserve the cached default. When its read resolves, record or retire only the inherited default, including genuine absence. Explicit live row permissions win immediately.

The snapshot writer uses that same canonical owner, so pending agent metadata cannot erase the cached default. Remove the passed default projection, unused aliases and separate event census. No new store, configuration, Gateway protocol or durable server shape.

## User Impact

The real pane composer renders its loaded labels and dimensions immediately, then updates actual changed values in place. A cached Stop retains its appearance and stays disabled until live action authority returns; a real live run ID always wins over cached inactivity. Real changed or absent inherited defaults and explicit row permissions still update the same control.

This proof starts at the first visible **real pane controls**. Inspected preceding surfaces still contain the inherited critical-entry skeleton; this PR does not claim to remove that earlier entry frame or complete the entire page-reload campaign.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): shared-state WAL warning repeats every maintenance pass behind a replication reader
prs.body:
Closes #193845

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway logs "Shared-state WAL maintenance failed ... blocked by a reader" on every non-quiet maintenance pass, indefinitely, when a replication tool such as Litestream holds a read transaction and checkpoints the WAL itself, even though the WAL stays bounded.

## User Impact

Operators running a documented continuous-replication setup (Litestream) stop getting a warning roughly every ten minutes forever. The warning still logs at once when the WAL grows, when it exceeds the existing size ceiling, and on the first sustained block after any completed checkpoint; a bounded, unchanged block repeats hourly. Health, `openclaw status --deep` and Doctor are unchanged and still show the warning on every blocked pass.

## Why This Change Was Made

#172121 made non-quiet checkpoint logs follow the warning policy (two consecutive blocked passes, or an oversized WAL) and explicitly left deduplication out. With a permanent external reader, `consecutiveBlocked` never resets, so every later non-quiet pass logs. The checkpoint owner now remembers its last blocked report (monotonic time, WAL size, last completed checkpoint) and skips repeats while the WAL has not grown, the size ceiling is not exceeded, the streak is unchanged, and less than an hour has passed. This changes only log reporting; the recorded health and `warning` flag are untouched. This is a deliberate change to the #172121 reporting policy; the interval is one constant if maintainers prefer a different value.

Accepted edge case: the limit is per checkpoint owner, so a newly opened connection logs its first sustained-block observation once.

## Evidence

Observed on 2026.11.1 (Linux, Litestream 0.5.17 replicating `state/openclaw.sqlite`), about 150 warnings/day:

    [state/db] Shared-state WAL maintenance failed error="openclaw-state WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader" path=.../state/openclaw.sqlite checkpoint={"state":"blocked","walBytes":11058112,"databaseBytes":34516992,"logFrames":1,"checkpointedFrames":0,"lastCompletedAtMs":null,"consecutiveBlocked":2171,"warning":true,"activeReaders":[],"readerDiagnostics":[{"scope":"current-thread","blockingOwner":"unknown",...}]}

`walBytes` stayed exactly 11,058,112 for more than two days while the database grew from 25 MB to 34.5 MB, so the WAL is bounded (Litestream checkpoints it); the size rule never fires (11 MB < max(2 x 34.5 MB, 64 MiB)), only the consecutive-count rule.

- New real-SQLite regression in `src/infra/sqlite-wal-checkpoint.test.ts`: a pinned reader with a bounded WAL logs once, stays silent at +59 min, logs again at +60 min, logs immediately on WAL growth, and logs again for a new streak after a completed checkpoint with the WAL size unchanged. Red on the base (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times`), green with the fix.
- `pnpm test src/infra/sqlite-wal-checkpoint.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 12 passed.
- Consumers: the sqlite-wal, sqlite-wal-reclamation, state-db-open, state-db WAL and session WAL suites (11 files): 125 passed, 5 Linux-only skips.
- `oxfmt --check`, `run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm check:changed` (format, lint, core and core-test typecheck, SQLite ratchets) pass; the only `check:changed` failures are pre-existing on `main` in untouched files (CHANGELOG record attribution, a Knip unused export in `src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test-support.ts`).
- Gap: no isolated-Gateway run with a live Litestream sidecar; the reader is simulated with a second SQLite connection holding a read transaction.

prs.title: fix(chat): queue human input behind quiet automation runs
prs.body:
## Problem

When a scheduled `session:<key>` automation run owned an existing conversation, a message from the human looked stuck:

- The Control UI took the human send as the running turn. It showed an elapsed timer with a working phrase ("19m · Tiding…") but no tool calls, and nothing said an automation owned the session.
- Steering could put the human message into the automation turn. That turn's prose is audit-only (#182262), and a `no_change` result publishes nothing, so the human's answer could disappear.
- Dispatch finalization called `markIdle` with no conditions. Diagnostics then reported the session `idle` while the automation kept running.

## Fix

- **Reply ownership:** `resolveReplyBackendQueueMessageMismatch` now treats a scheduled automation invocation (`readAutomationDisplayState !== "ordinary"`) like a hidden run. It cannot own a new human answer, so the input goes to FIFO follow-up custody and later runs as its own visible turn.
- **Gateway projection:** pending inputs parked behind a scheduled run now carry `waitingFor: "automation"` (new optional protocol field). The parked follow-up input is no longer offered as `inFlightRun`, so reconnect and history do not restore it as a running turn. Shared predicate: `isRpcSourceParkedFollowup`.
- **UI:** the queue row reads "Waiting for automation to finish". When follow-up custody arrives, the optimistic ACK adoption is released. A session whose only active run IDs are parked inputs no longer counts as a local run, so there is no timer and no Stop. Progress appears once the queued turn starts through its own lifecycle.
- **Diagnostics:** when a message finishes, the lifecycle consumes its queue count but projects `processing` while another operation still owns the session. Controller retirement projects idle when that owner ends.

Unchanged: quiet `no_change` checks stay quiet, the single final-result publication is the same, and the automation's intermediate output stays hidden.

## Product question for Josh (not implemented)

Should intermediate automation tool and assistant output appear in an existing conversation? Making it appear changes the intent of #182262. The smallest option: show it only while a human message is queued behind the run, or only for runs that exceed N minutes or perform effects. In both cases periodic quiet checks would stay hidden. This PR shows only that an automation owns the session.

## Not addressed (unproven, per investigation)

- Why steering was unavailable during the incident. With this change, a scheduled run declines steering by design.
- The cause of the ~120 s chat-send preparation.

## Evidence

- New real-Gateway Control UI e2e: `ui/src/e2e/automation-session-queue.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`. It uses the built Gateway, the real cron tool, admission, persistence and browser; only the provider is scripted. The test holds a `session:<key>` automation at its model call, has the human send a message, and asserts:
  - a queued row labeled "Waiting for automation to finish";
  - no elapsed timer and no Stop control, both live and after a reload;
  - after release, the automation result publishes, then the human turn runs exactly once and gets its own visible reply, and the session ends idle.
  - On base, the queued row never appears (only the timer). With the fix, it passes.
- `quiet-automations.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` passes. Quiet checks, recency, message counts and the single result are unchanged.
- The reply-promotion contract test has a new `scheduled` case. It fails on base (injection accepted) and passes with the fix.
- A diagnostics integration test (a message finishes behind an active owner, then the owner completes) fails on base (`idle`) and passes with the fix.
- A UI unit test checks that the optimistic adoption is released and the queue item carries `waitingFor`.
- Passing checks: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:src`, `tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint on changed files, `protocol-registry:check`, the native protocol check, `ui:i18n:verify`, and focused gateway, logging and chat suites.
- Pre-existing failure, not caused by this PR: `chat-steer-deferred-custody.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (`OPENCLAW_STEER_CUSTODY_PROOF=fixed`) fails the same way on base `30f4dc262adc` and on this branch (it never sees `agent.input.settled`).

Size: about 100 production lines, plus regenerated validators and tests. Screenshots are in the comment below.

prs.title: fix(macos): HEIC-only screenshots fail to paste into web chat
prs.body:
Supersedes #170362, thanks @trukhinyuri.

Related: #165117

## What Problem This Solves

HEIC-only HDR screenshots can silently stage no attachment when pasted into the macOS embedded Control UI.

## User Impact

This remains an unfinished regression-only draft. Production paste behavior is unchanged, and this head must not merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Swift composer recognizes HEIC, while the embedded Control UI uses a separate native WebView path. The intended repair is a small adapter for a single HEIC-only screenshot, preserving existing web attachment admission and ordinary WebKit paste.

This draft currently adds only a synthetic native regression fixture. No production conversion or handoff has been implemented. Credit: Yuri Trukhin (@trukhinyuri), `1245379+trukhinyuri@users.noreply.github.com`.

## Evidence

**BLOCKED: actual HEIC paste/conversion/cleanup proof is incomplete.**

- [Existing Apple CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41805022075) tested head `50bfddf13c71f7d9458d8aa8fa6f6d34d9175699`, based on main `db6ac584cf205ea9a72de7ae83a4e65199b926a4`. The app test bundle compiled; app job `126503866092` finished with a failed Swift test.
- [Native logs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41805022075/artifacts/13312905667) show `DashboardHEICPasteTests.swift:59`: expected one pasted file, received zero. Fixture elapsed time was 150.397 seconds within the concurrent full suite. The assertion sits inside an unlabeled PNG/HEIC loop, so the artifact does not identify the failing format. This is not unambiguous HEIC-specific red-before evidence. No fixed-green result or conversion/cleanup proof exists.
- The separate browser test “deliberate interruptions keep the page without failure UI” also failed for `stop`, with a timeout waiting for settlement. [Main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41799644616) fails that same test for `download` and `stop`, but at the tab URL assertion. The differing signatures have not been accepted as an inherited-failure waiver. Other broad CI failures also remain unresolved; no merge gate has been bypassed.
- Shared autoreview of the fixture returned scoped clean through P2, explicitly limited to static review. Hosted review likewise keeps this regression-only draft unfinished. Those reviews do not substitute for native runtime proof.
- Production +0/-0, tests +86/-0, docs +0/-0. `git diff --check` passes. Contributor code was read only and never checked out or executed. Native execution used synthetic data in disposable Apple CI; no operator clipboard, screenshots, Gateway, app deployment, or local native execution was used.

The draft and original PR remain open. No further test dispatch or code publication was made during recovery.

prs.title: fix(ci): drain sibling runs after aggregate rejection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation can stop draining while sibling runs are still active when a release aggregate rejects an unwaived failure. The collector also loses that completed child's observed jobs.

## User Impact

Operators receive the completed child evidence and the remaining sibling results. An unwaived failure still fails validation; log-read and provenance errors still stop immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate aggregate validation verdicts from failed GitHub reads, retain the authoritative child snapshot, and evaluate uncapped errors when deciding whether drain must stop. Release eligibility and decision mode keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the evidence loss and premature stop through the production collector. The final regression fixture fails on the base in six cases and passes all 22 cases under both Node 24 and the pinned Bun runtime, including an injected ambient CI run ID.
- The affected collector and summary suites cover another 264 cases per runtime. Three existing Node assertions required removing conflicting color flags; only those three failures were rerun. The Bun run passed all 286 affected cases together.
- Real collector CLI probes verify sibling draining, immediate log-read failure and immediate provenance failure with isolated GitHub responses; no live network or release operation.
- Targeted production/test lint, tooling typecheck, formatting and normal signed-commit hooks passed.
- Final full committed-range local ClawSweeper review: no findings, confidence 0.91, security cleared. The CI-identity fixture finding was fixed and reproduced red/green.
- Added exactly 144 LF of allocation for retained-evidence and CLI-boundary regressions. The shared scalar baseline is unchanged.

Existing FRV documentation already promises complete sibling results with fail-fast disabled. No configuration, storage or release publication changes.

prs.title: chore(ci): diagnose disk reserve refusals in large41
prs.body:
## Problem

[CI 41784433080 / large41](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41784433080/job/126423702015) at `bcae09093b5a06099cd3a3f0f3d5f4e4b499ad7f` failed 20 cases: 16 printed 3.3–3.4 GiB available against the unchanged 4 GiB reserve; four omitted the preparation Result. The retained logs do not identify disposable job-owned bytes. Two sibling jobs ended during runner shutdown without a bound external cause.

## Change

Add opt-in metadata on a serial, throwaway GitHub-hosted job: filesystem counters at capacity refusal and bounded footprint snapshots between child invocations and after normal disposal. Each snapshot cooperatively stops after 1 second or 250,000 entries, yields every 128 entries, and reports incomplete roots. It does not enumerate symlink targets, read contents, print paths/inode identities, or infer exclusive reflink ownership/reclaimable bytes.

Record first parent signal, native child exit tuple, and bounded error-kind/code/process-tree state while preserving cleanup, rethrow, exit and signal behavior. Expose failed preparation Results without serializing successful ownership bindings. Keep all assertions, authority/data contracts and the 4 GiB reserve.

A task-scoped workflow opened one probe on this draft branch only. It checked out original `bcae0909` and overlaid the exact diagnostic files from `60839b5c4593426ed85daf52061dd4aa5591f6d4`; the original encoded three-group large41 composition included all 63 gateway runtime/state files, startup-fixture lifetime, worktree preparation, dispatch and command/daemon groups. No shared CI driver or runner routing changed.

## Evidence

[Probe 41802517967 / job 126481483255](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41802517967/job/126481483255) is **terminal FAILURE** at diagnostic head `60839b5c4593426ed85daf52061dd4aa5591f6d4`:

- Original composition passed: three completed invocations, zero failed invocations. All 20 originally failing case names match passing cases in this log. This is a passing replay, not a proven repair.
- Focused footprint and existing lifecycle tests: 62 passed; 7.17 seconds wrapper wall time, 5.29 seconds Vitest duration. New footprint suite: two tests, 4 ms. Syntax, format and touched-script lint passed.
- Test lint failed on the new cleanup variable shadowing its `root` helper; Gateway-test lint was not reached. Follow-up `fb3d00e767ad61eadce9938f8e20dfa3f3e24d38` only renames two references. The exact failing rule was checked locally RED on the original text and GREEN on the correction with pinned oxlint; this limited check does not replace full repository lint. The failed probe is preserved, with no second reproduction or current-head CI-green claim.
- Independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2: scoped-clean on the complete diagnostic snapshot against `1ba543b6dd6ffe014139c02a4b62a7904c52a2a2`; the subsequent identifier-only lint correction is recorded above.
- Exact own test-line allocation: 83 LF, shared scalar unchanged. It covers footprint safety/budget contracts, termination metadata in existing lifecycle cases, and missing preparation detail.

The supported `ubuntu-24.04` label and four-CPU class matched, but physical conditions differed: original Intel Xeon 6975P-C versus probe AMD EPYC 7763; the probe sampled **75.635–76.612 GiB free**, far above the original shortage. The compiled-worker aggregate was 274.215 MiB and returned to an empty 4 KiB root after verified disposal. The scan completed worker/cache roots but exhausted its budget partway through dependencies; the pnpm store was unvisited, not zero-sized. The original runner's physical allocation/ownership inventory was never captured and is not recoverable from retained logs. No safe deletion target or causal leak fix is established.

prs.title: feat(node): allow trusted writable volume ancestors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node session hosting and terminal uploads reject writable volume ancestors even when a dedicated deployment isolates the volume from other writers.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly trust named ancestors through `OPENCLAW_NODE_TRUSTED_WRITABLE_ANCESTORS`. The default stays strict. This requires external storage isolation and a node restart; the setting does not make a shared volume safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node admission activates one immutable policy shared by workspace transfers and node temp-root selection, including terminal uploads. Generic temp-root imports do not activate it. Only the listed ancestors' writability check is relaxed; private-directory permissions, ownership, path integrity, and workspace lifecycle checks remain. Worker subprocesses do not inherit the setting.

**Draft dependency blocker:** this requires the `trustedWritableAncestors` API proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1073. OpenClaw's package and lockfile must be updated after that feature is released; the currently published dependency does not support it.

## Evidence

`439d6eb82e2` plus this change, tested against the matching source-built fs-safe candidate: 104 tests passed; two Windows-only cases and one existing root-permission case skipped on Linux; the relevant typecheck graph, focused lint, formatting, and test budget passed. New tests use real filesystems and fresh processes. Original OpenClaw source still rejects the opted-in ancestor with patched fs-safe, confirming the integration is needed. Local independent review flagged the dependency blocker above and found no additional actionable defect.

The 146-line test allocation covers policy capture, subprocess isolation, real workspace admission, and terminal upload/recovery without mocks.

The same production change was also built from the current OCE-pinned OpenClaw (`513c127`) and matching fs-safe source. Its nonroot suite passed 102 tests (two Windows-only skips). prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.

- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. prs.title: perf(ui): speed up theme color readback and audit native rendering work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Theme changes repeatedly read pixels from tiny canvas surfaces, while the existing CPU census cannot distinguish native style, layout, painting, and layer work inside `(program)`.

## User Impact

Appearance updates settle faster without changing colors or layout. Benchmark users can inspect native categories and composited layers using the existing production route and interaction scenarios.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request frequent readback for the one-pixel theme-color canvas. The change preserves the color calculation and avoids adding a cache or changing theme ownership. The same option is already used by the session background contrast sampler.

The opt-in `--native-audit` mode captures Chromium traces, exclusive native category totals, correlated `(program)` samples, and before/after LayerTree inventories. Missing CPU clocks remain null; sample correlation is not presented as consumed CPU. Paint clip extents are not presented as raster damage, and the report records when Chromium omits `layerPainted` events. Defaults and lazy UI boundaries are unchanged.

Related: #193771.

## Evidence

Measurements use production assets, the existing synthetic Gateway fixtures, Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and WebKit 27.2, desktop 1440×1000 and mobile 390×844. The canvas ablation changed only a copied bundle before the source edit. Twenty serial pairs rotate and reverse baseline/candidate/baseline-control positions. Application time excludes the initial automation delivery prefix; Chromium thread CPU is reported separately. No live Gateway/provider latency claim.

| Appearance application time | Base median / p95 | Readback median / p95 | A/A median / p95 | Paired median change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Chromium desktop | 118.15 / 130.3 ms | 95.1 / 106.6 ms | 118.8 / 127.6 ms | −20.07% |
| WebKit desktop | 206.5 / 214 ms | 191 / 199 ms | 206.5 / 216 ms | −6.73% |
| Chromium mobile | 124.75 / 138.3 ms | 97.35 / 108.1 ms | 127.65 / 138.2 ms | −19.41% |
| WebKit mobile | 210 / 222 ms | 189.5 / 200 ms | 210 / 223 ms | −10.88% |

All 480 ablation observations passed. Chromium Appearance thread CPU remained approximately flat (+1.0% desktop, +0.38% mobile paired medians). The unrelated secret-dialog control had flat median application/CPU time. Its Chromium tails were noisy in both candidate and A/A, so no tail-latency improvement is claimed. Host load ranged 7.57–20.15. WebKit results use browser application time, never utilization-derived CPU.

Cold-boot readiness paired medians improve 6.85% desktop / 6.76% mobile in Chromium and 2.97% / 3.95% in WebKit. Chromium boot CPU paired medians change +1.60% / +1.00%; A/A medians are +0.52% / +0.37%. WebKit A/A tails are noisy, so no tail win is claimed. All 240 boot observations and 12 theme/built-head observations pass. Theme values match exactly after normalizing the fixture server origin.

The complete diagnostic census covers 348 cells per rate: 347 passing at 1×; 346 passing at 6×; one unsupported mobile hover skip at each rate. The original 6× mobile log-refresh cell timed out because its fixture replayed the same 500-line tail on every two-second poll, growing the retained buffer after reset. This PR makes that response cursor-aware. The failed original cell remains excluded from the native totals; a corrected replay is separate evidence.

| Exclusive renderer-main native wall time | 1× ms | 6× ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| Style | 6,260.34 | 48,155.87 |
| Layout | 5,023.84 | 32,642.72 |
| Pre-paint | 959.64 | 6,748.70 |
| Paint | 2,262.74 | 14,632.98 |
| Layerize | 1,672.48 | 9,455.08 |
| Commit | 770.61 | 6,002.57 |
| HTML parsing | 91.83 | 809.88 |
| CSS parsing | 119.55 | 853.67 |
| Script compilation | 102.11 | 828.22 |
| GC | 748.46 | 3,062.05 |
| **Total** | **18,011.59** | **123,191.74** |

Recognized spans overlap 34.70% of later `(program)` sample weight at 1× (10,851.19 / 31,273.05 ms), and 58.27% at 6× (80,413.64 / 138,011.39 ms). The remaining 20,421.86 / 57,597.75 ms is unexplained. These are sampled wall-time correlations, not CPU consumption or retroactive attribution of the earlier 41.66% capture. Missing thread clocks remain unknown. The recorded interval includes tracing/profiler lifecycle overhead; these diagnostics do not establish the ablation speedup above.

Native work varies materially by flow: streaming totals 1,936.89 ms desktop / 1,792.52 ms mobile at 1×, with substantial paint/layerize time; mobile terminal opening totals 439.59 ms and diff opening 435.23 ms, dominated by layout. Those transcript flows are handed to the long-session lane. Layer median/max is 12/411 at 1× and 11/411 at 6×. Sidebar fixtures expose about 200 resting transformed labels; a copied-bundle diagnostic removed their resting identity transform. Total layers remained 410: the 200 text layers were replaced by 200 adjacent clock-aside layers. Idle CPU changed 105.851 → 108.365 ms (+2.37%); scroll/resize changed 247.543 → 226.775 ms (−8.39%) in one pair. This is inconclusive timing evidence and no structural layer reduction, so the CSS is unchanged and no speedup is claimed from that probe. Intentional blur, animated characters, sticky/fixed positioning and paused status rings stay intact.

Typing dirties 87 desktop / 73 mobile node IDs, while desktop hover dirties 31. Paint recording clips include viewport-sized and unbounded extents; they do **not** establish raster-damage area. Chromium emitted no `layerPainted` events even though retained-layer paint counters advanced (7,593 increments at 1×, 7,172 at 6×). Geometric RGBA estimates are not measured GPU memory.

Per-flow concentration reanalysis covers 635/688 retained profiles (333 at 1×, 302 at 6×) and identifies 60 source-frame/cell combinations at ≥10% self time, including 38 application frames. Workspace scroll callbacks reach 70–74% and were handed to the long-session owner. Modal opening reaches 18–26%; Dashboard geometry reaches 18–21%; those are native-call boundaries, not established JavaScript loops. Ghostty dependency hotspots are outside the permitted patch scope. Model setup's native `select` concentration is Playwright fill automation. Missing profiles remain explicit rather than reconstructed.

| Validation | Result |
|---|---|
| UI + scripts typechecks | Passed |
| Native accounting regression tests | 7 passed |
| Presentation owner tests | 5 passed |
| Performance budget tests | 46 passed |
| Targeted lint, formatting, diff check | Passed, including refreshed caps and fixture |
| Corrected 6× mobile log refresh | Passed: 500 retained rows, 17 mounted |
| Cold boot, 20 rotated pairs + A/A | All 240 observations passed |
| Theme cycles and built-head Appearance | 12 observations passed; computed theme values match |
| Production Knip | Passed |
| Independent local review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Strict production performance comparison | Passed with measured Chat cap adjustment |
| Startup JS gzip / requests, refreshed main | 90,664 → 90,671 B / 3 → 3 |
| Startup CSS gzip / requests | 36,821 → 36,821 B / 1 → 1 |
| Chat boot JS gzip, refreshed main | 1,295,845 → 1,295,862 B (+17 B) |
| New Session boot JS gzip, refreshed main | 802,420 → 802,351 B (−69 B) |

Current-main and merged-head builds on the same machine pass the strict comparison. Startup grows 7 B (within the 64 B variance allowance), Chat grows 17 B, and New Session shrinks 69 B; raw route JS grows 24 B. Earlier builds measured +354/+419 B gzip as generated names changed. After resolving the real budget-file conflict with the medium-transcript PR, the caps are the newly measured head plus the existing 192 B allowance: Chat 1,296,054 B and New Session 802,543 B. No lazy boundary or request count changes. The original frozen-base comparison remains recorded separately.

The first full CI run passed the UI, browser E2E, real-Gateway, performance, lint, types, and other selected checks. Its only failure was the test-line ratchet: this PR adds 170 justified regression lines. A dedicated 170-line allocation now covers the seven native-accounting cases; the shared scalar is unchanged. The replacement run then passed that ratchet and all functional checks, but New Session gzip exceeded its older cap by 12 B. Its measured +419 B tradeoff is now recorded in the cap; no runtime code changed in either CI repair. The green third run (42138108002) then encountered a real conflict with a newly landed budget change. The branch merges current main, records freshly measured caps, and includes the reviewed log-fixture correction; the replacement head requires fresh CI.

## Scope and size

This is a one-line canvas-option change plus its explanatory comment in the existing color owner. No cache, synchronized state, component lifecycle or theme ownership changes. The rest extends the existing engine harness: separate trace accounting and CDP inventory modules keep instrumentation opt-in. Seven regression cases cover overlap accounting, missing clocks, renderer choice, profiler initialization, signed sample deltas and malformed profiles. No new benchmark harness or dependency.

Touched-file LOC against refreshed main: 3,989 → 4,962 (+973). The UI owner grows by one line; the remaining growth is opt-in benchmark tooling, its seven accounting tests, documentation, allocation, and the bounded fixture correction. Solid refactor checklist counts are unchanged (zero affected effects, owners, JSX, handlers, loaders or state projections). Reports and captures stay outside the committed tree.

## Visual proof

The four first-pair desktop/mobile Chromium/WebKit Appearance captures are pixel-identical (absolute-error count zero). These captures contain synthetic fixture data only.

After, WebKit mobile:

![After: mobile Appearance settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03e87d40-e509-4601-b63e-ce85e51c2f75)

Final refreshed-head CI: run 42140357491 on `5f19cd86af40f55b6bd4a87d46a205866bc4e2c4` passed all 68 jobs, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. No inherited-failure exception or CI retry was needed for this head.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep loaded sessions visible after rejected actions
prs.body:
Fixes #193334.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes All Sessions hiding every loaded conversation when Pin or another session action is rejected.

## User Impact

Users can see the action failure and continue opening their conversations. A rejected Pin leaves its state unchanged, and a later successful Pin updates the list. Initial roster-load failures retain their existing unavailable state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current refreshed branch also contains the Files preview classification/recovery implementation and `AgentWorkspaceFilesUITests`, overlapping #193450. Its current proposed scope is five files: the All Sessions screen and native test, the Files preview screen and native test, and the shared loopback fixture. This fixture-only follow-up preserves that refreshed source rather than replacing it.

All Sessions used the same error state for roster reads and session actions. Keep action feedback separate and display it above the existing rows, following the native sidebar's pattern. Both shared mutation and fork failures use the action feedback. Gateway authorization, storage and transport behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Current fixture-repair head: `0bf3fb21980cb7a9e8483709600881ee03b1b0ea`.

### Current fixture verification (November 6)

The refreshed fixture discarded the second argument to `fail`. The helper now accepts `fail(message, details)` and conditionally serializes `error.details`; one-argument calls are unchanged. Only the two helper lines changed in this follow-up; production classification and existing UITest expectations are unchanged.

Real WebSocket checks on the actual refreshed heads `4e7739c92623` (#193450) and `85c2f3f8a7f4` (#193413) reproduced missing `details.type` for missing/too-large/unsupported. After the identical repair, all six scenarios plus an explicit one-argument compatibility probe passed on each fixture (7 passed, 0 failed per fixture). Parent independently replayed the same controls; these are overlapping confirmations, not additional unique tests. Targeted oxlint, formatting, Node syntax and diff checks passed on both branches.

Current-source native preparation for #193450 compiled the app and UITest runner using Xcode 27.1 with the normal Watch and native lint phases retained. The initial launch and one clean retry stalled in dyld `__open` before the first screen or any fixture RPC. That local startup block is now resolved: XCTest's external build-products `DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH` selected an external WebRTC framework and stalled while opening it. A task-scoped, documented `.xctestrun` override sets only `UITargetAppEnvironmentVariables/DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH` to an empty string, so the same app loads its embedded WebRTC framework. The baseline and recovered configurations differ at exactly that one leaf; Main Thread Checker remains enabled. This does not change app code, binaries, test assertions, global permissions or storage layout. TCC activity was observed, but its underlying policy is not claimed fully diagnosed.

With the unchanged current-production app/test binaries and repaired fixture at `088160685b30ddd768a8b17c56b3f2a2bd1cd850`, `AgentWorkspaceFilesUITests/testPreviewDistinguishesReadFailuresFromSizeAndFormat` passed on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0: **1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; six controls in one case** (52.241 s; command 56.657 s). Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51245 (partial: this fixes the `sandbox explain` diagnostic only; the live Telegram elevated-execution denial steipete kept open in that issue is not addressed here, so the issue should stay open).

Builds on #189343 by @nikolas-sapa. Their commit is cherry-picked unchanged with authorship kept; this PR adds the test change and Linux proof that ClawSweeper asked for on #189343. Credit for the fix goes to @nikolas-sapa. If #189343 lands instead, this can be closed.

## What Problem This Solves
`openclaw sandbox explain --session telegram:slash:<id>` reports `channel: (unknown)` and `allowedByConfig: false` when the CLI's plugin registry has no channel plugins (the sandbox-backends scope is empty for stock docker/podman configs), even with `tools.elevated.allowFrom.telegram` configured.

## User Impact
User impact: `openclaw sandbox explain` shows the right channel and `allowedByConfig: true` for telegram sessions on stock docker/podman setups, so elevated-tool allow lists can be checked without confusing `(unknown)` output.

## Why
- Original fix (@nikolas-sapa, 4e58d9b): fall back to the static bundled channel catalog after the runtime registry misses, for both the stored-delivery and the parsed-key paths.
- Added here: the stored-delivery regression test now uses a session key with no channel (`agent:builder:main`), so only the stored delivery context supplies telegram. It now fails if the stored-delivery fallback is removed (it previously passed because the key also resolved telegram).

## Evidence
Setup: Linux, built CLI, isolated HOME.

Config: `{"tools":{"elevated":{"enabled":true,"allowFrom":{"telegram":["123456"]}}}}`

  enabled: true

After (this branch 46de5b0c90f):

prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).
- **What was not tested:** Live Codex app-server / `@openai/codex` binary round-trip. Proof surface is the real bridge + protocol response object.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

prs.title: test(gateway): channel account routes keep serving after another plugin's config reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel account that serves inbound traffic over HTTP must keep its route when a different plugin's config is edited and the Gateway hot-reloads. Nothing tested that path end to end on a real Gateway. If it regresses, the account still reports as running, but its route returns 404 until a restart.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change; this adds a test only. It protects channels that register an HTTP route when an account starts, such as webhook-style inbound routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

On reload, a retained plugin's routes are projected into the new registry. Today only unit tests in `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` cover that projection. The real-Gateway channel lifecycle tests reload the route's own plugin, not an unrelated one.

The new test follows the existing `server-plugins.lifecycle.*` fixtures and helpers. It starts a channel account that registers a prefix route at `startAccount`. It then hot-reloads another plugin's config three times with `config.patch`. After each reload it checks four things:
- the other plugin really re-registered, with a new instance and a new active registry;
- the account's route still answers 200 from the current registry;
- the route set is unchanged;
- the account was started only once.

Finally, stopping the account still removes the route (404).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channel-routes.test.ts` on current `main`: 1 passed (gateway-server project).
- **Mutation check.** The mutation removes the `target.httpRoutes.push(...)` line from `projectPluginHttpRoutes` in `src/plugins/http-route-owner.ts`.
  - The new test fails at the first reload: `status: 404`, expected 200.
  - Under the same mutation, `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` still passes 3/3 and `plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` fails 3/8.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the file: clean.
- `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`: clean. A type error injected into the file makes it fail, so the file is in that project.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:database-worker-ratchet`, run against the parent commit: OK.

prs.title: fix(codex): settled-turn recovery rejects sessions containing a media-only user turn
prs.body:
Closes #185079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex settled-turn finalization repeatedly fails with `invalid_content` when the session history contains a legitimate media-only user turn — a message persisted with empty text plus ordered `__openclaw.media` facts (for example, a JPEG-only Telegram message) and no upstream-text fallback. The projection validated every earlier message before trimming, so one such historical turn kept rejecting every later finalization context capture on that session.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified historical media-only message no longer invalidates settled-turn recovery. It projects as a bounded, deterministic marker naming the attachment types, and finalization context capture succeeds for sessions that contain one. Empty messages without any well-formed media fact are still rejected, upstream text keeps winning over the placeholder, and current-turn evidence and pairing checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectUserMessage` required non-empty text and threw `CodexHistoryRejection("invalid_content")` for a blank user turn. The persisted representation for media-only turns is exactly that shape (empty `content`, media metadata under `message.__openclaw.media` — the documented "media-bearing user turns use ordered `message.__openclaw.media` facts" convention). The payloads themselves are not replayable through the text-oriented recovery projection, so the fix projects a deterministic `[User media attachment unavailable in this context: <types>]` marker — the same approach the projector already uses for image tool results (`[Image tool result: <mime>]`) — capped at the first eight entries with a `+N more` suffix, always inside the existing byte budgets.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts`: against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the two placeholder-projecting cases fail (media-only turn rejected with `invalid_content`); with the fix all 26 cases pass, including the guards for empty turns without well-formed media facts (still `invalid_content`), upstream-text precedence, and the placeholder cap.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` passes except two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases that fail identically on unpatched `main` on this machine (macOS native process inspection returns a permission error in this environment); the projection suites themselves are fully green.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, and lint extension changed files. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan flagging three exports in files this PR does not touch.


**Remaining proof:** No end-to-end Gateway/Codex recovery run with persisted media-only history has been performed. The regression tests cover the projection boundary; they do not establish the full recovery and finalization flow.

prs.title: fix(update): after a reboot, update cleanup can never reclaim older rollback backups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a reboot, update cleanup can never reclaim older rollback backups.

On a real Mac install, `openclaw update cleanup` (Gateway stopped) kept 18 pre-migration originals, about 66 GB, with `destination-verification-failed`: "Recovery destination device changed from 16777232 to 16777234; destination contents could not be verified against recorded recovery evidence. Originals retained." The volume was the same (same disk and volume UUID). macOS gave it a new `st_dev` at reboot. The same run retired the 6 originals created after the reboot, and every later run refused the older ones again.

## User Impact

User impact: once a later update has completed, cleanup retires rollback originals recorded before a reboot, so their disk space comes back. A destination that was really replaced or restored still keeps its originals.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the recorded device differed from the live one, the destination verifier re-certified only if the live database hashed to the recorded image. A destination the Gateway has written since the migration never matches, so the refusal was permanent.

The device check exists because an inode number can repeat on another volume. Node exposes no stable volume ID (`fs.statfs` has no fsid, and old manifests only record `dev`/`ino`), so the fix uses evidence already on disk: the producer always writes the original next to its destination. If that original (or its durable `.cleanup-*` claim from an interrupted run) is still on the destination's current device with its recorded inode, mtime and size, the two files moved together. That means the volume was renumbered, not swapped. The verifier then records the new device in the manifest and skips the full-database hash.

What still refuses:
- a destination with a different inode (restored or replaced file), through the existing inode check;
- a destination on a different device from its original (an inode collision), which still needs the existing content proof.

Original bytes are still verified by the existing artifact check before anything is removed.

## Evidence

Reproduced on `origin/main` 54d191d45902 with real SQLite. The manifest records a destination `dev` one higher than the live file, the same inode, and the database is written after the "reboot". A later completed update makes the original a cleanup candidate.

Red (base), three consecutive `retireSessionSqliteRecovery` runs:

```
RED run 1: blocked destination-verification-failed :: Error: Recovery destination device changed from 16777235 to 16777234; destination contents could not be verified ... Originals retained.
RED run 2: blocked destination-verification-failed :: (same)
RED run 3: blocked destination-verification-failed :: (same)
```

`src/commands/update-automatic-cleanup.test.ts`, base vs this branch:

| Test | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| retires remounted recovery after its Gateway writes the destination (automatic, Gateway-owned) | fail | pass |
| manual cleanup retires a pre-reboot original from its archive | fail | pass |
| manual cleanup retires a pre-reboot original from its interrupted claim | fail | pass |
| keeps a pre-reboot original when its destination was restored as a new file (negative control) | pass | pass |
| keeps an original when its destination reports another volume than the original beside it (negative control) | pass | pass |
| settles an unlinked pre-reboot original when its destination still matches it (existing content-proof path) | pass | pass |

Mutation checks: dropping the same-device comparison fails the other-volume negative control, and dropping the claim fallback fails the interrupted-claim test.

Related suites (19 files, `git grep` on the retirement/cleanup entry points): 260 passed, 3 skipped (existing skips), 0 failed. Full `update-automatic-cleanup.test.ts`: 23 passed.

`pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format and ratchets pass. It reports two failures that also fail on `main`: changelog attributions in `CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`, and an unused export in `src/auto-reply/reply/queue.test-helpers.ts`.

**Stored-data compatibility** (`src/commands/update-cleanup.remounted-manifests.test.ts`): the test writes a startup-migration manifest as raw JSON in the exact shape 2026.10.x stored it on the affected install. That means `manifestVersion` 3, `openClawVersion`, three `database-backup` targets (two agent databases and the shared state database), `databaseIdentity` with only `dev`/`ino`, identical planned and completed moves, and `retained` receipts. Paths and IDs are synthetic, and every recorded `dev` is older than the live one. The destinations are real SQLite files written after the "reboot", and a later update completes before cleanup runs.
- Base: all three originals blocked with "Recovery destination device changed from … destination contents could not be verified …".
- Head: all three removed. In the stored manifest only `databaseIdentity.dev` (restamped to the live device, no `sha256` added) and the disposal receipts (`disposed`) change. Every other field is deep-equal to what was stored.

This proves manifests already on disk from before this change load through the existing schema and retire under the new rule. It needs no migration and loses no stored evidence.

**Docs:** the update-cleanup section of `docs/cli/update/repair-and-recovery.md` now describes the remount proof, and that a different inode or an original on another device still needs content proof. `pnpm check:docs` passes.

Test-line growth: +256 (+102 regression and controls, +154 stored-manifest compatibility), recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/update-cleanup-remounted-volume.txt`. The existing remount test asserted the buggy refusal ("different content" = refuse); it now asserts retirement after Gateway writes. The negative controls replace that case.

The two `artifact-verification-failed` ("artifact is unexpectedly missing") items from the same run are a separate problem: originals already gone under a disposal receipt. They are handled in #193745.
