prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release validation stopping when GitHub reports a live artifact producer’s expanded job count before all jobs appear in its inventory.

## User Impact

Release operators can continue waiting for the same producer instead of losing a valid running build. No package-runtime behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep an incomplete live observation pending through the existing bounded poll, after checking every returned job’s exact identity. Completed-run and raw-artifact identity consumers retain strict completeness checks; partial inventories never qualify artifacts.

## Evidence

- Observed in full-release-validation run 42103709099, job 127537127877; producer 42110731783 subsequently completed.
- Exact-head focused run 42120328874 passed all 48 waiter tests on Node and all 48 on Bun, including the two added live-inventory/identity regressions. That run was ultimately cancelled after API-diff job 127571878838 exceeded its one-hour limit; its skipped build is not counted as proof.
- Follow-up ordinary CI 42134002432 checked out exact target 2ecbc426f4b52b8752109eea926c733c48427ba4, with separate trusted harness d8011932b5713f9d18977f9e4dae8de44824ffae. Build job 127618260395 passed actual `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`. SDK API-diff job 127618260961 passed and reported no Plugin SDK API changes. The broad diagnostic run has other failures and is not represented as all-green.
- Initial run 42119816284 stopped at the compact-plan limit before runtime tests or build; not a product-test result.
- Original API-diff timeout cause remains unresolved; the newer exact-target report passed, but no inherited-timeout claim is made.
- Independent read-only review and exact-head ClawSweeper review found no actionable findings. Formatting and whitespace checks passed. Local reviewer unavailable; Dallin’s renewed direction is to land known repairs using the completed independent and hosted reviews.
- Local tests/build remain intentionally omitted under the release operator’s remote-first instruction. Alternate Testbox proof never allocated; no execution guard was bypassed.
- Post-fix real-GitHub inventory expansion trace remains unobserved; the next full release validation will exercise the integrated owner.

Marked ready after exact-target build and focused proof completed. Native preparation and required GitHub landing gates remain; no skipped job or timeout is counted as passing evidence.

prs.title: feat(ios): add a Talk microphone mute button
prs.body:
Related: #187722

## New device layout report — November 6 (unresolved)

**Do not treat this PR as merge-ready while this user-visible fault remains untriaged.** The requester supplied a recording and four screenshots showing lost reading position in long chat history while operating Talk, followed by an outgoing user bubble and a newer assistant reply drawing over older assistant content. The overlap remains visible in a screenshot where the Talk card is absent. Later short turns render normally; another supplied screenshot is back inside the older long response. The exact running build is not stamped in the media.

![Real iPhone screenshot: outgoing Testing ping bubble and newer Ping received reply overlap an older long assistant response](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b46564f-ae0c-403a-a419-ea7bc374dd7c)

This crop preserves the overlapping chat pixels and removes surrounding model metadata, header, and composer. The original media is retained unchanged; raw unredacted media was not published.

### What has and has not been established

- The visual overlap and reading-position loss are observed, not hypothetical. The user bubble retains its correct role styling; neither message-role corruption nor persisted transcript corruption is established by these images.
- Personally compared `ChatView.swift`, `ChatScrollCommand.swift`, `ChatTranscriptRows.swift`, `ChatAssistantRunGroup.swift`, `ChatMessageViews.swift`, `ChatMarkdownRenderer.swift`, and `ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift` with base `0499ce287bb8`: all seven are byte-identical in this candidate. The mute UI changes the composer/viewport and can still trigger an existing layout weakness. **Unchanged source is not proof that this exact symptom reproduces on base or that the mute changes are innocent.**
- The existing transcript uses one `LazyVStack` and size-change bottom anchoring. [Related PR #192232](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192232) documents measured lazy-height instability on main and an eager-live-tail repair for blank transcripts after send/reply. It is a plausible related owner, **not a verified fix for this overlap**. No code from that PR has been imported or modified here.
- No new Apple-runtime reproduction or verified repair has been executed for this report. The previously passing mute tests do not exercise this long-row geometry/viewport sequence, and release screenshot CI does not cover it.

### Focused next proof

Use one compact iPhone simulator with several static assistant responses longer than the viewport (for example, 60 numbered paragraphs separated by rules), then toggle Talk/mute, scroll, end Talk, open the keyboard, and send a short message. Compare base, this PR, and the existing eager-tail candidate with the **same** transcript and interactions. Record content height, offset/visible rectangle and actual row positions; assert that visible bubbles do not overlap and that a non-live reading position is preserved. Qualify the existing repair against that failure before proposing another layout owner or claiming resolution. This is one targeted reproduction, not a request for an exhaustive device/provider matrix.

## What Problem This Solves

iOS Talk has no microphone mute button separate from ending the conversation.

## User Impact

Adds a microphone toggle to the Talk activity strip. Works across native speech recognition, Gateway relay, and WebRTC, retaining mute across Talk restarts within the app run.

The UI follow-up uses the composer's scaled 17-point medium SF Symbol styling and retains a 44-point hit target. A crossed-out mic is gray when input is on and orange when muted. The collapsed strip is about 48 points tall at normal text size. Idle muted realtime Talk displays **Connected (Realtime)** above **Microphone muted**; thinking, speaking, connecting, and error statuses remain visible. VoiceOver continues to announce the action and microphone state. While Talk is active, the composer's dictation/voice-note microphone is hidden and returns after Talk ends. Mute stays exclusively in the Talk activity strip, not in the dictation button's position.

**Ready for review; the new layout fault above remains unresolved.** The requester has verified pre-mute word preservation on an iPhone. Returned kit v3 now verifies the Apple build, all 373 selected iOS tests, and all 21 selected shared-package tests for the repaired candidate matching `c22355b8f89a`. Actual normal-size UI screenshots and the requester’s lifecycle recording are now attached below. Remaining physical audio/lifecycle cases, large-text layout, and pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this recording. The confirmed conflict with `main` was resolved in `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`, integrating base `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`. GitHub now reports the branch mergeable. Current-head CI is green (38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures or pending checks at the November 6 check). The requester has also posted current-head targeted simulator red/green results and base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders, summarized below. Earlier Mac-kit results remain evidence for their explicitly identified candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports the Android feature from @davelutztx in #187722, using the existing iOS Talk manager and transport owners. No new configuration, permissions, dependencies, or protocol changes. Shared control defaults leave existing macOS callers unchanged.

Android reference checked on November 5, 2026: still open at `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`.

**Native finalization repair:** [Android feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6547128842) and the [iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033) showed that immediate recognizer cancellation discards pre-mute trailing words. Native continuous Talk now closes the audio tap/engine immediately and calls `endAudio()`, retaining that recognition generation until a usable final result or a two-second fallback. Errors, empty finals, and the deadline use the latest nonempty partial; settlement submits once and retires old callbacks. Quick unmute/re-mute cannot replace the draining recognizer. End Talk/session teardown cancels it, and gateway replacement invalidates its transcript owner. Realtime mute and accepted reply playback paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Conflict-only integration — November 5

- Published head: `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`; verified ancestry includes main `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`.
- The sole manual conflict was the demo fixture helper extraction: main independently made the same extraction with different helper names. Kept main's names and verified the complete fixture file matches that main revision byte-for-byte. The fixture and shared initializer build repairs are now already upstream, reducing the PR-relative diff to 13 files.
- Native mute manager/regressions, WebRTC mute, relay mute, and Talk-strip UI are byte-identical to the earlier Apple-tested candidate. All 13 PR-relative files plus the two upstream build-repair files were verified against the published head.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,637 entries, no drift); base-relative staged whitespace check passed. Fresh full-candidate Auto Review against the integrated base: P0-only, scoped-clean, no findings. No Apple code was executed in this Linux session; these checks do not replace current-head Apple integration validation.
- [Latest completed ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6626345064) covers prior head `c22355b8f89a`: overall Gold, patch quality Platinum, no findings. Its merge-conflict action is now addressed. New current-head simulator red/green and base/head strip-render evidence is summarized below. Remaining physical acceptance concerns audible playback, Talk restart behavior on-device, and large text in the actual chat layout. The requester's successful native trailing-word test remains recorded; the new red run is a targeted source-hunk revert, not an execution of plain base.
- Current-head CI is green as observed November 6: 38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures/pending checks. This includes iOS screenshot/evidence and Periphery build jobs; the dedicated iOS build matrix is skipped, so this is not a claim that every Apple test suite ran in CI. No merge has been submitted.

- Native repair published at `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7`; the three repair files were verified byte-for-byte against the reviewed workspace matching the locally supplied patch.
- **Requester device report, November 4:** tested the supplied native-finalization repair locally and confirmed that words spoken before mute are no longer cut off. This is a manual result for the supplied local patch. Kit v2 subsequently exposed build blockers; kit v3 confirms the build repairs and automated regressions pass, as detailed below.
- `git diff --check` and staged whitespace check: passed.
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` added the source-owned UI wording entries; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,549 entries, no inventory drift).
- Fresh Auto Review of the complete local candidate against `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a`: **P0-only**, scoped-clean, no findings. This does not certify Swift compilation or Apple runtime behavior.
- Separate source-only lifecycle review of the finalization changes and tests: no unresolved concrete issues after preserving the latest partial on empty finals and adding automatic-unmute-resume cases. This was an excerpt-based audit, not executed proof.
- Author simplification pass: finalization stays in the existing Talk manager, reuses its recognition and transcript-processing generations, and splits input shutdown from recognizer retirement. The added bounded pending state prevents pre-mute word loss without a second capture manager or configuration option.
- Added gateway-boundary regressions in `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: final results with/without an earlier partial; error/timeout/empty-final fallback; exactly-once send; quick unmute/re-mute, including no-word automatic resume; stale callbacks; End Talk/session replacement. They exercise actual `GatewayNodeSession` `chat.send` framing with synthetic recognition callbacks and a terminal-aborted acknowledgement to stop at the submission boundary. **Passed on the requester's Mac in kit v3:** all seven regression definitions, including their parameterized cases. This is fixed-candidate green execution; automated red-on-base execution was not performed.
- [Requester device results at `7e0def937e73`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033): iOS app build passed; 27 tests in three iOS suites passed; xAI Gateway relay and OpenAI WebRTC mute/unmute worked on an iPhone. Native recognition lost a word spoken before mute. These are **prior-head results**, not proof of the native finalization repair or revised UI.
- The same report found the shared OpenClawKit test target blocked by a pre-existing `ChatViewModelTests.swift` initializer mismatch, so shared relay tests did not run on that host.
- Apple compilation and automated Swift tests were run on the requester's Mac, not in this Linux session. The returned xcresult summary/tree and Swift XML/logs were independently inspected here. Actual current UI screenshots from the requester's recording are now attached below. Remaining physical lifecycle/input/playback cases still need verification; the silent recording does not establish audio behavior. Chat mockups and render-smoke tests remain separate from runtime screenshot evidence.

### Additional requester evidence on integrated head — November 5–6

All reports below name head `417349df1cf4` and base `0499ce287bb8`.

- [Simulator red/green report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6667982238): on Xcode 27.2, the requester reports **red** after reverting only finalization, muted-recognition, and relay-silence source hunks while retaining the tests: 7 mute tests with 21 issues, and 10 relay tests with 3 issues. **Green** on unchanged PR head: 18 tests across `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests` and `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, plus 10 shared relay tests, all passing. Reported mute-suite time: 721 seconds. This is targeted regression sensitivity, **not a literal plain-base test run**. These are attributed results from the comment; raw xcresult/log bundles for this new run were not supplied to this session.
- [Base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669395455): publicly accessible immutable images were downloaded; normal and large-text active/muted examples and large-text connecting were inspected. They show real SwiftUI `ImageRenderer` output from a fixed 393-point test fixture at 3x, not full-app screenshots. Head adds the expected gray/orange crossed microphone and muted wording. At accessibility3 the muted text wraps mid-word (`Micropho / ne muted`); status/transcript text is also constrained. Treat the real chat's large-text layout as unverified, not accepted based on this fixture.
- [Requester's evidence mapping and remaining device checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669410988): simulator assertions cover finalization, fallback, exactly-once submission, Talk-session restart, quick toggles, and teardown. Audible playback and physical-device lifecycle/large-text verification are still pending. The earlier successful native trailing-word device report remains valid and should not be discarded.

**Restart contract clarification:** mute is retained across Talk stop/start and reconnect within the same app run. It is intentionally not persisted across quitting and relaunching the app. A full-app relaunch retaining mute is therefore **not** an acceptance requirement for this PR; the relevant retention check is restarting Talk without terminating the app.

### Requester real-device lifecycle recording — November 5

The requester supplied a 36-second iPhone recording and explicitly authorized use of the test-chat screen. These are **actual device screenshots, not mockups**. The recording does not display a build commit, so this is requester-supplied visual evidence, separate from the hash-verified kit v3 test run.

![iOS Talk lifecycle: active at 00:04, muted at 00:14, unmuted at 00:22, and ended at 00:34](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3f306d3-3bb9-48a0-84e0-4b23fce03bbc)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/271983e6-399c-4788-b066-920970c21f33

Observed in the recording:
- **00:04:** Listening (Realtime), gray crossed-out microphone in the Talk card, and no composer dictation microphone.
- **00:14:** Connected (Realtime), orange crossed-out microphone and Microphone muted label. The Talk controls remain present and the agent reply appears in chat.
- **00:22:** Unmuted; Listening (Realtime) and the gray mute action return.
- **00:34:** Talk ended; the Talk card is gone and the composer dictation microphone is visible again.
- A stop/restart segment is also present. It is not independently counted as proof of mute retention or capture exclusion because the recording does not expose touch events or microphone input.

Publication edits only: the composer model label is covered, the final iOS Control Center transition is omitted (published clip is 34.5 seconds), and the silent audio track and file metadata are removed. Test-chat text and Talk controls are unchanged. The original recording is retained locally unchanged. Its audio track contains no audible signal; this evidence does **not** prove TTS continuity or post-mute speech exclusion. Normal-size current UI is covered; large-text layout and a pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this clip.

### Returned Mac kit v3 results — November 5

**Apple build and both selected test groups passed. No rerun is needed for the collector's summary error.**

Returned archive: `talk-mute-results-20261105T034708Z-0712fe.zip`, SHA-256 `1fb79eeebf7d716ca593c263e4939da1230e34f6cd28980ba55a78909edf715e`. This was the pinned `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7` base plus bundled build-repair SHA-256 `f0c863e5a3c1ffa1b379908840c256d7ef54f77fb9febc1c5f41c21e813a8684`, not a bare-base run. The six manifest source hashes match the reviewed files published at `c22355b8f89a6abb0ebce72dd0eced45cecb0b93` and remained unchanged during the run.

Environment: Xcode 27.2, Apple Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2 arm64, isolated iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5. Caller-selected Node 26.12.1 and repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 passed preflight. The created simulator was deleted successfully.

| Check | Result | Reported wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS `build-for-testing`, including strict lint | Passed, exit 0 | 568.084 s |
| iOS `test-without-building` | 373 tests passed; 0 failures, skips, or expected failures | 777.116 s |
| Shared `swift test` | 21 tests in 3 suites passed; 0 failures or skips | 174.464 s, including build |

iOS xcresult records 373 test definitions / 429 parameterized invocations. All eight requested suites and all seven required mute regression definitions are present and passed:

- `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: 7
- `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`: 11
- `TalkModeManagerTests`: 51
- `TalkRealtimeVoiceSessionCleanupTests`: 7
- `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`: 258
- `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`: 13
- `OpenClawTypographyTests`: 22
- `LocalFixtureChatTransportTests`: 4

The shared XML and console output independently confirm `RealtimeTalkRelaySessionAudioInputTests`, `ChatTalkControlTests`, and `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests` all passed. This includes relay silence while muted, queued-audio retirement, and preservation of capture/reply playback in the test harness.

**Collector-only defect:** kit v3's top-level summary says `shared: results_unverified` / `attention_required` because it looked only for `shared-results.xml`; Swift emitted `shared-results-swift-testing.xml`. That actual report is present in the returned archive with 21 passing cases and no failures/skips, and the command exited 0. The local collector now reads framework-suffixed reports as well. Its regression reproduces the false warning on shipped v3 and passes after the fix; the original returned ZIP is preserved unchanged. This correction does not alter or rerun the app tests.

The native regression fixtures took approximately 2 minutes for final-result submission and 1 minute 20 seconds each for fallback and quick-toggle groups; these are measured automated harness times, not a physical speech-finalization latency claim. The two-second native finalization deadline remains unchanged. Apple tests are green, but this run does not establish red-on-base automation, physical speech exclusion/playback across every transport, or screenshot acceptance.

#### Earlier v2 blockers — repaired and superseded by v3

Kit v2 reached both builds but executed no tests: strict lint rejected two raw-orange uses in `ChatTalkActivityViews.swift` and the unchanged 210-line demo seed function; shared compilation rejected the old route-lease initializer in `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests`.

The follow-up at `c22355b8f89a` uses existing warning/muted theme tokens, extracts two demo branches unchanged, and updates the routing-test initializer/closure signatures. No lint gate or assertion was disabled; native microphone-finalization code and tests were unchanged. Kit v3's successful build and tests above now verify these repairs on Apple tools.

### Local device test

Check out this PR, follow `apps/ios/README.md` for signing/build setup, run `pnpm ios:gen`, and build/run `apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj` on an iPhone.

- Mute/unmute while an answer plays; verify playback and accepted work continue.
- Speak while muted, then unmute; verify muted speech is not replayed.
- Native regression: say **five four**, mute, then say **three two**. Exactly one request should contain **five four**, excluding speech after mute. Also try muting before the first partial appears, quick unmute/re-mute, and End Talk during finalization.
- Restart Talk while muted, then test standalone push-to-talk after ending Talk.
- Verify the composer mic disappears during Talk and returns after End Talk; mute stays in the Talk card.
- Check the control at normal and large text sizes; capture real before/after screenshots.

The selected automated iOS and shared suites have passed in kit v3; no repeat is requested for unchanged source. The checklist above remains the physical-device acceptance scope.

## Android maintainer handoff (#187722)

The same native lifecycle correction applies to Android: stop new input and ask `SpeechRecognizer.stopListening()` to finalize, rather than snapshotting the current partial and immediately canceling/destroying the recognizer. Preserve the original recognition/session identity until `onResults`, or a bounded `onError`/deadline fallback to the latest partial; settle once before retiring that identity. Muted/draining callbacks must not restart capture or interrupt playback. Quick toggles and End Talk/session replacement must not leak old speech into a new capture or conversation.

The **five four → mute → three two** regression should send only **five four**, once. Also cover a final with no earlier partial, error/timeout fallback, duplicate finals, quick toggles, and teardown. iOS's two-second deadline is an implementation choice to validate on-device, not a prescribed Android timeout. This note is retained here for the Android author/maintainers; no Android code or metadata was changed.

prs.title: fix(infra): keep the scratch scan alive when a pending candidate vanished between passes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scratch maintenance pass silently abandons the rest of a target's scan when the pending candidate retained from a previous budget-exhausted pass was removed between passes.

## User Impact

Scratch cleanup on very large scratch trees keeps making progress across maintenance passes even when the agent removes scratch files between passes. Before, that target's scan restarted from the top on the next pass and the skip was invisible in the result counters.

## Why This Change Was Made

`cleanScratch` retains `cursor.pending` when a pass returns on `ScratchBudgetExhausted(retry=true)` so the next pass can resume where it stopped. The next pass re-stats that candidate before the per-entry `try`, so an ENOENT (the scratch owner removed the entry between passes) reaches the outer `catch`: the directory cursor is closed, the remainder of the target's top-level scan is skipped for the pass, and because the outer catch filters ENOENT, `deferred` does not record it either — the skip is silent and the scan restarts from the beginning on the following pass.

The fix treats a vanished candidate like any other consumed entry: drop the pending entry and continue from the cursor's directory position. Other stat errors keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- New regression test "keeps scanning when a pending candidate vanished between maintenance passes" is red on `main` (1b8e670666e) with `entriesRemoved: 0` (whole scan skipped) and green with the fix (`entriesRemoved: 1`, no errors):
  `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/infra/scratch-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed.
- Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:core:test` chain — passed.
- oxlint on both changed files: 0 problems; `run-format.mts --check`: clean.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK (slack 62).

## Shipped Gateway maintenance proof

End-to-end run through the shipped product path only (`openclaw gateway run` + `openclaw worktrees gc`, isolated state dir): pass 1 retains `.openclaw/tmp/huge` (2.1 M empty dirs) as the pending candidate via the 2,000,000-entry scan budget; the candidate is removed between passes; pass 2 drops it and removes the remaining 25 expired entries (`scanned: 50`, workspace left empty), while current `main` silently skips the rest of that target's scan (`entriesRemoved: 0`, `scanned: 0`, no error recorded) and only recovers on pass 3 by restarting from scratch. Full counters, Gateway `[health]` log lines, and notes: [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193759#issuecomment-6673735839).

prs.title: fix: MCP App selections disappear from sent message history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MCP App selections disappearing from the visible user message after sending or reloading chat.

## User Impact

Selected references retain their titles and safe icons beside the submitted message, including after history reload and queued-message restoration. A later App selection cannot rewrite an earlier message’s references.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing send/outbox/transcript owners carry a bounded, display-only receipt captured when Send is pressed. Model context continues through the existing MCP App path; these receipts do not become additional model input. Hooks that rewrite or redact the original message also drop its receipts. Structured-only selections retain the visible App title without persisting their structured payload.

App receipts, forwarded attribution and Work context render synchronously, preserving wrapped chips, native disclosure state and immediate source navigation. Optional text-selection toolbar rendering and DOM layout load when text is selected; the existing popup owner retains selection admission, cancellation and cleanup. This keeps ordinary chat within its loading budget without another state owner.

This builds on the App workspace presentation fixes merged in #193773. The validator output is regenerated; its +6,020/−5,998 lines account for 93% of the diff, primarily deterministic identifier renumbering.

## Evidence

Verified through a fresh isolated Gateway and a real local model: open Shell Store → select Helmet shell → Add to chat → ask a question → send → reload. The baseline user bubble has no selection chip; the fixed message retains its shell title and icon after reload.

- Send/outbox/capture and transcript regressions passed. The three UI suites that failed on the earlier revision now pass through `pnpm test:ci-failed 193786 --run` (47 tests). The final affected UI batch passed 98 tests, including popup/annotation, submitted references, send handling and Chromium geometry checks. Final Gateway request suite: 46 tests passed; Gateway test types and both UI type leaves passed.
- Canonical same-toolchain performance comparison against merged parent `ad151439` passed: Chat 1,294,027 → 1,294,633 B gzip (cap 1,294,735); New Session 800,629 → 800,861 B; request counts remain 20 and 15. CSS gzip/raw bytes are unchanged. No budgets changed.
- CI lint repair: marked three intentionally pending test-helper calls with `void` and typed the catch parameter as `unknown`. Targeted type-aware lint and both popup suites (20 tests) pass; runtime logic is unchanged.
- The 240-line test allocation covers receipt persistence, redaction, retry identity, structured-only selections, and popup import cancellation; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Existing-data compatibility: an actual conversation written by published stable 2026.11.1 remains readable with identical text, timestamp and idempotency key after supported Doctor migration (agent schema 27 → 40) in disposable copied state. This uses the prepared receipt backend from the pre-rebase head; its receipt handling is unchanged by the restack and UI-only performance repairs. The actual stable browser’s composer.v4 queued record passes the final production decoder with every field preserved and no invented receipt. This proves queue readability; automatic replay was not claimed because the test auth-none → token change alters account recovery scope. Inference was covered by the separate live Shell Store demo, not the upgrade fixture.
- Structured-only selection regression verified red on the base and green with the fix. Focused transcript persistence/redaction tests passed on Node 24 and Node 26 (2 tests each).
- Core/UI production typechecks, core test shards, full build, UI build, formatting and line-cap checks passed after fixing the two issues found by the broader changed check. The other scoped phases passed. The unchanged release record also trips the existing changelog-attribution guard (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`); neither that record nor the guard is changed here.
- Qualification: the initial full transcript run on Node 24 passed all 29 assertions, then hit a 180-second cleanup-hook timeout. The unchanged baseline later passed all 28 tests. Focused candidate tests passed; the cause of the original cleanup timeout remains unproven. No timeouts or cleanup behavior were changed.

Before the fix (after Send):

![Before: submitted message loses its selected reference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d4234b5-8477-419a-b79c-0a396b04f413)

After sending and reloading with the fix:

![After: submitted shell reference survives history reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b4c0862-d85e-4588-bfc6-2869110063b9)

Tracking: https://linear.app/openclawfoundation/issue/OCF-156/p0-build-shell-store-as-a-user-facing-plugin-capability-showcase

Failed previews remain unshareable; reopening an available file displays its current content without stale errors or bytes. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway already supplies structured error types. Reserve the format/size hint for `workspace_file_too_large` and `workspace_file_unsupported`; give other failures safe read-failure and recovery guidance. prs.title: fix(context-engine): durable turn commits drop prompt usage, so engines never see real prompt size
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: context engines never see the real prompt size or prompt-cache usage for turns delivered through durable turn advancement (`commitTurn`), only for the older `afterTurn` path.

## User Impact

User impact: cache-aware context engines such as lossless-claw can again track prompt size and cache state for every turn. On one live Gateway on Nov 5, all 153 lossless-claw telemetry updates on the `commitTurn` path logged `promptTokenCount=null`. The `afterTurn` path had a real count in 22 of 37 updates.

There is no config or migration change. Outbox rows written before this change simply carry no usage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable turn outbox persists a small runtime context (`ContextEngineTurnRuntimeContext`) that is replayed into `commitTurn`. It held only provider, model, window and budget. The attempt's `promptCache` metadata (last-call usage, cache observation, retention, cache-touch time) was dropped when the turn was recorded.

This adds `promptCache` to that record, filled by both producers: `resolveContextEngineCompletionRuntimeContext` for harness attempts and `finalizeHarnessContextEngineTurn` for CLI and worker turns. The value is the same plain-counter metadata `buildContextEnginePromptCacheInfo` already builds for persisted attempt results. It holds no message content or credentials. The payload is a JSON column, so no schema change is needed.

## Evidence

- `context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts`: the finalize, durable outbox, then `commitTurn` path now asserts that `runtimeContext.promptCache` reaches the engine after the SQLite round-trip. Two cases fail without the producer change and pass with it.
- `context-engine-assembly-attempt.test.ts` (new): the harness producer carries `promptCache` for host-owned and native-selection attempts. Both cases fail without the change.
- Also passing: `selection`, `cli-runner.context-engine`, `worker-turn-context-engine`, `attempt-context-advancement`, `attempt-phase-lifecycle`, `context-engine-recovery.projection` and `context-engine-transcript-cursor`. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `oxfmt` are clean. The test-file typecheck is left to CI.

Related: #193779 (context cap fix) and Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw#1284 (merged), from the same investigation.

prs.title: feat(onepassword): sign in to websites with your own 1Password logins (Agentic Autofill preview)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents can't sign in to websites with a person's own 1Password logins. The bundled 1Password plugin only reads operator service-account secrets, and its `get` tool returns secret values to the model and transcript.

## User Impact

Owners can connect their own 1Password account (US Individual/Family, partner preview) and let an agent request specific logins for a task. They approve the request in the 1Password app on their computer through an **Approve sign-in** card in the Control UI chat. The 1Password extension in OpenClaw's managed browser then fills and submits the form. Passwords, tokens, integration keys and the approval link never reach the model, the transcript or the logs. Existing service-account features are unchanged.

The preview is off by default. To try it you need: `plugins.entries.onepassword.config.agenticAutofill.enabled`, plus `extensionPath` (an operator-supplied, unpacked 1Password Nightly extension ≥ 8.12.46.6) and `browserProfile` (a Chromium or Chrome for Testing managed profile; branded Chrome can't load extensions). Approval currently works only in the Control UI and the 1Password desktop app on the Nightly channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

1Password's Agentic Autofill (partner preview) keeps credentials inside its extension: our code only gets statuses and opaque references. OpenClaw can't ship an OAuth client secret, so connecting and token refresh go through a hosted relay at `connect.openclaw.ai` (separate private repo). The relay sees OAuth tokens only long enough to exchange or refresh them. It hands them back sealed to a key the Gateway generates, and it never sees the integration key in readable form.

- **Browser plugin:** a generic, task-scoped extension host (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/browser-extension-host`). It registers a vetted extension before launch, calls the extension's service worker with secrets passed only as call arguments, maps the agent's tab to a Chrome tab ID, and locks the tab while a fill runs.
- **onepassword plugin:** owner-only connect and disconnect through the relay, sealed pickup, token refresh one at a time per connection, and an optional `onepassword_autofill` tool (request, status, fill) that returns statuses only.
- **Approval card:** the approval link reaches the person through a plugin inline view. The saved tool result holds only the request ID. The Gateway keeps the link in memory for up to 10 minutes and gives it only to a current Control UI admin who has access to the session. Clicking the card starts 1Password's status-check schedule.

Review: @joshavant owns the existing 1Password plugin. Please weigh in on the plugin surface and the security model.

## Evidence

**Approval card** (the bundled Control UI end-to-end test with a synthetic 1Password service; cropped to the card)

| | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ready | ![Ready, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/737ea58a-4882-4767-a2ed-d94089e1c664) | ![Ready, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a12e0fbc-489d-4b91-a4f3-d677569c01ad) |
| Waiting | ![Waiting, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d58cb7f1-1473-484b-a9dd-5be77a93cc86) | ![Waiting, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22f8fc37-f22a-4ec4-980f-1016b1da5deb) |
| Approved | ![Approved, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6bbd709-de5f-4190-9947-7938b52c348f) | ![Approved, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88a9483d-9c3c-4ea4-a462-a7a8310bf7de) |

| Not approved | Expired |
| --- | --- |
| ![Denied](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a09201f-804d-4101-a8b6-82a69dfe3c1b) | ![Expired](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b84f4e9-0f50-43ff-8b5a-d2d942a7d848) |

There was no "before" image: this card is a new surface.

**What was checked**
- **Real 1Password extension:** Nightly 8.12.48.7, loaded through the production extension host. The adapter's readiness check returns `ready` about 2.8 s after browser launch. No tokens were used and no access requests were made.
- **Live relay:** session create, pickup (pending and wrong-token 401), the start page with its confirmation code, the redirect to 1Password with S256 and the registered client, a second Continue rejected with 409, and refresh passing 1Password's `400 invalid_grant` straight through.
- **Encryption:** an envelope sealed by the relay's own code opens with the Gateway's code, for both the tokens and the integration key. A wrong session or purpose is rejected.
- **Real consent:** a manual OAuth connect against production 1Password reached the OpenClaw consent screen, with name and icon, and redirected to the relay.
- **End-to-end UI test:** the link is never in the saved chat history; contrast meets AA; keyboard focus works; reduced motion is respected; the card height stays steady across states.

**Earlier local checks (before review repairs)**
- `pnpm test extensions/onepassword --maxWorkers=1`: 138 passed, 1 skipped (existing skip).
- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-host.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed.
- `extensions/onepassword/browser/index.test.ts` (UI Vitest config): passed.
- `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_EXTENSION_E2E=1` real Chromium extension-host test: passed. It was run before the rebase.
- Typecheck for extensions, extension tests and the UI: passed.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`, config baseline and inventory checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.


### Review repairs

- Invocation cancellation and current-session authority now reach the extension adapter separately from serialized vendor arguments. Registration, session attachment, worker initialization, tab mapping, and Agentic Mode enablement recheck authority; the final credential-bearing send is guarded. Cancellation after mode enable still disables the tab's Agentic Mode and releases its exclusive lock.
- The fake-host boundary regression rejects both cancellation and revocation during all five preparation waits; an authorized owner fill sends once. Request creation also rejects cancellation during worker initialization. This is adapter-boundary proof, not the real-account end-to-end flow.
- Classified and inventoried `browser-extension-host`; moved the shared private approval projection to a plugin-local leaf; separated extension launch declarations from runtime gates; moved request types to the existing contract leaf to remove the remaining approval owner cycle.
- Corrected setup documentation to describe the private Control UI approval card and its implemented recovery text. Removed the identified low-value checker test and reduced its allocation by 11 lines.
- Test budget: +114 net browser authority regression lines (including required brace formatting) and +3 service assertion lines require a narrow 117-line allocation. The original workflow/approval tests exceeded the existing allocations by one further line after removing the duplicate; a separate one-line reconciliation records only this PR's tests. Shared scalar and inherited debt are unchanged; the exact ratchet passes; unrelated CI assertion cleanup subsequently removes five net test lines.

### Upgrade/data-model compatibility

The existing service-account config parser, broker (including stored grant/audit/pending value shapes), pending-authorization owner, and credential reader have **no diff** against the PR base `d936d4b5e36d`. The original `grants` V2, `audit`, and `pending` namespaces, capacity/eviction settings, and `credentials/onepassword/service-account-token` path are unchanged. No migration, clear, or rewrite is introduced. Without explicit `agenticAutofill.enabled: true`, registration returns before opening autofill state; opt-in adds only `autofill-connections` and `autofill-requests` namespaces. Existing config, broker, worker, and SecretRef tests passed in the scoped plugin suite. This is focused source-contract and regression evidence, not a live installed-version upgrade.

### Repair validation

- `pnpm test extensions/onepassword --maxWorkers=1` (repository runner): 149 passed, 1 existing skip across two configs; 179.81 s including cold worker compilation. The adapter/service repair pair: 44 passed, 4.54 s wrapper wall; individual adapter: 4.02 s, service: 3.84 s. New-head CI seconds are not available yet.
- Browser extension-host/headless-launch focused tests: 7 passed. SDK package-contract/subpath suites: 35 passed. Private approval view UI tests: 3 passed.
- `pnpm --dir ui test src/styles/sr-only.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed (4.03 s); the prior CI timeout was not reproduced, so no timer/retry/expectation change was made.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles. Additional-boundary CI command: passed. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`: all nine checks passed, including exact test-line budget, config docs and plugin inventory. SDK export sync/check, scoped docs MDX and all docs links passed.
- Local autoreview of the repair snapshot was attempted at P0–P2 with Codex; authentication failed before a report. This is **not a clean independent review**. No hosted re-review was requested.

- Red/green authority proof: the six cancellation/request-creation regression cases fail with the original adapter (credential worker calls occur after authority loss), then pass with the repair. No live credentials are used.
- CI log transport: all requested `gh run view --job … --log-failed` downloads failed with HTTP/2 stream cancellation; HTTP/1 fallback failed with unexpected EOF. Exact check-run annotations were retrieved instead. Canonical `pnpm test:ci-failed 191921` likewise reported unavailable logs, not inherited proof.
- Other prior-red signatures are not classified inherited: recent main annotations did not reproduce them. Main's UI shard passed at `2ac42c830f3e` (run 41644326924/job 125945832763), while this PR's sr-only timeout passes locally. QA Lab killed-run, hooks JSON, WhatsApp delivery-recovery, and browser relay profile-drift checks are separately being reproduced; no blind retries or assertion/timer weakening was used.
- Additional uncovered SDK gate: `plugin-sdk:surface:check` reports 162/161 public entrypoints, 3864/3859 public exports, and 2234/2232 callable exports. The compatibility scan reports no unauthorized removals. Budgets were not raised to hide this result.

**Not yet proven: real connect/approve/fill.** A full real connect, approve and fill against a 1Password Family account through a Gateway. That test remains outside this repair task; no live Gateway was touched. Approving from 1Password's mobile apps isn't available in their preview yet.

<details><summary>Known follow-ups</summary>

- Relay protocol gaps the Gateway side handles conservatively: there's no cancel endpoint after a local disconnect; a failed pickup doesn't return an already-sealed integration key; `expires_in` has no issue timestamp; and a missing key plus a missing `user_id` forces revoke and reconnect.
- Tokens are stored in the plugin's SQLite state, with the same file protection as other OAuth tokens. They are not in an encrypted vault.
- An inline view can't show different text to the model and to the person, so the summary line reads "…Approve it in OpenClaw." everywhere.

</details>

### Additional CI repairs and current limits

- Reproduced browser relay profile name/port drift: old contexts returned `false` after config replacement instead of rejecting. Captured browser contexts now reject when their configured name disappears or endpoint port changes. Existing relay coexistence and hot-reload sibling suites pass: 20 tests, 116.56 s wrapper wall including cold compilation.
- Reproduced WhatsApp recovery failure: durable recovery correctly preserves the selected account and passes `{ accountId: "default" }` to the native listener. The stale fixture now asserts that argument instead of the obsolete four-argument shape; all 6 tests pass (123.25 s wrapper wall including cold compilation).
- Reproduced hooks blank-parent-agent failure: `hooks` preAction intentionally throws the actionable `hooksCliFailure("--agent must not be blank")`; removed the obsolete generic-error fixture branch. The same failed case passes in the prebuilt-runtime rerun; full file passes: 23 tests, 56.99 s wrapper wall (52.64 s test run), using supported prebuilt runtime reuse.
- Extension production/test and UI typechecks passed. Touched onepassword typed lint passed (8 files), browser/WhatsApp typed lint passed (2 files), browser cycle files passed (6 files). Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- A complete runtime prerequisite build passed (7m 43.4s). A subsequent redundant prerequisite build was stopped before source output changes; hooks validation uses the supported prebuilt-runtime mode. One concurrent relay test setup hit a transient removed `extensions/synology-chat/dist` during asset replacement; the later stable-input replay passed and is the reported product evidence.

- QA Lab killed-run replay passed unchanged: `gateway-kill-restart-send.e2e.test.ts`, 1 test, 66.37 s test time. This does not prove a repair or inherited failure; the prior unexpected request signature remains unexplained and is recorded as non-reproduced. The combined baseline replay's only failing test was the stale hooks fixture, independently fixed and replayed green above.
- Final touched-file lint passed, including hooks fixture; final production extension typecheck passed and final Madge scan reports zero cycles. Extension-test and UI typechecks passed. The full baseline suite passed before the two additional CI fixture corrections; final test-line ratchet passes with five lines of slack after those net deletions.

- `plugin-sdk:api:diff --base d936d4b5e36d --head f061b02c1d57`: blocked by the command's host memory limit (16,429 MiB observed versus 16,053 MiB limit) during parallel declaration rendering; no API-diff result was produced. This report covered the original committed SDK introduction; the repair changes only its classification/inventory, not the SDK exports.

- Final complete `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`: all nine checks passed (118.65 s slowest database-worker phase); final source tree `0e69be6822d` is byte-identical to the validated pre-author-correction tree. Four repair commits are authored by Josh Lehman; the final push used an exact lease solely to correct task-owned author metadata.

Closes #193793

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cloning a cron job in the Control UI drops its explicit `failureAlert.threadId` (while preserving the normal `delivery.threadId`), so the copied automation sends failure alerts to the normal delivery topic instead of the separately configured alert topic.

## User Impact

User impact: a cloned job keeps its failure-alert topic; failure alerts continue arriving in the configured alert thread instead of silently falling back to the normal delivery topic. Edit flows can still clear the topic explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

`jobToForm` loads `deliveryThreadId` into the form but had no `failureAlertThreadId` counterpart, and `buildFailureAlert` never emitted `threadId` — so the clone (and any form round-trip) lost the field before `cron.add`. The form state now carries `failureAlertThreadId`, `jobToForm` loads it from the source job, and `buildFailureAlert` emits it with the same edit semantics as the delivery topic (form value wins; clearing it on an update writes `null`; a fresh clone without one omits the key).

## Evidence

- Regression case added to the existing "clones exact persisted fields" table (`ui/src/lib/cron/index.test.ts`) using the issue's fixture: a job with `delivery.threadId: 7` and `failureAlert.threadId: 41` clones with both topics intact (`{"failureAlert":{"channel":"telegram","to":"123","threadId":41}}` on the wire). The reporter's identical minimal case failed on unpatched main (`Expected failureAlert: {channel,to,threadId:41} / Received: {channel,to}`); the pre-existing edit-path control (`mergeCronFailureAlert` rename flow) continues to pass.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts ui/src/lib/cron/index.test.ts` — 39/39 passing; all other cron suites (`form-validation`, `copy`, `action-feedback`, `editor-save.node`, `inventory`, `model-suggestions`, `read-retirement`, `refresh`, `webhook-url`) — 111 further tests passing.
- The 4 added test lines have a matching allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/cron-clone-failure-alert-topic.txt`.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: five qa-channel scenarios (`a2a-allowlist-denied-cross-agent-send`, `a2a-default-cross-agent-send`, `a2a-disabled-cross-agent-send`, `a2a-message-tool-mirror-dedupe`, `thread-reply-current-source-delivery`) always time out when run with the qa-channel driver against the mock OpenAI provider.

## User Impact

No product change. Developers can run these five QA scenarios with `--channel-driver qa-channel` and get a real pass/fail signal instead of a guaranteed timeout. They are currently skipped by the default `smoke-ci` profile (Crabline driver excludes `channelDriver=qa-channel`), which is why the failures were not visible in CI.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The four A2A scenarios expect the mock provider to plan `sessions_send` / `message`. Tool Search is enabled by default, so those tools are only reachable through `tool_search`/`tool_call`, and the mock provider only plans a tool that is declared directly. Setting `tools.toolSearch: false` in each scenario's `gatewayConfigPatch` matches what other qa-channel scenarios already do (for example `cron-isolated-spawn-only-child-delivery` and `message-delivery-decision-inspection`).
- `thread-reply-current-source-delivery` also has a session key bug: it reads the parent channel session (`agent:qa:qa-channel:channel:<room>`), but the thread reply is recorded in the per-thread session (`…:thread:<threadId>`), so it waited on an empty transcript. It now reads the thread session.

Scenario YAML only (+7/−1 across 5 files); no runtime code is touched.

## Evidence

Run on the `v2026.10.9` tag; these five files are byte-identical on current `main`, so the change applies unchanged. Not re-run on `main` itself.

```
pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --channel-driver qa-channel --allow-failures \
  --scenario a2a-default-cross-agent-send --scenario a2a-allowlist-denied-cross-agent-send \
  --scenario a2a-disabled-cross-agent-send --scenario a2a-message-tool-mirror-dedupe \
  --scenario thread-reply-current-source-delivery
```

| `tools.toolSearch: false` only | 4/5 pass; thread-reply still times out |
| Instrumented thread-reply run | Mock planned `message(thread-reply)` and the reply was delivered; the session list contained only the `:thread:<id>` key, which the scenario was not reading |
| This PR | 5/5 pass |

prs.title: fix(telegram): sent-message cache writes fail with "Telegram runtime not initialized" during replies
prs.body:
Closes #193158

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram's sent-message cache write fails with `Telegram runtime not initialized` when a reply callback runs inside a reply run and memory-core or llm-task is loaded (the default bundled set).

## User Impact

User impact: messages the bot sends while it replies are persisted to the sent-message cache again, so after a Gateway restart reaction notifications in the default `own` mode still recognize them as the bot's. The failure was only visible at verbose log level. No config, state or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #184243, reply runs execute inside the prepared-model lease's retained plugin invocation scope, which exits the caller's plugin instance when a `generationOverlap` plugin is loaded. Channel turns already bind `delivery` to the channel's plugin instance, but pass `replyOptions` through unbound. Telegram's reply callbacks therefore run there without the instance, and the draft-stream path `onProviderMessage` -> `recordSentMessage` reads the per-instance runtime and throws.

At turn entry, the function members of the channel's `replyOptions` are now bound to the channel's plugin instance, as `bindChannelDeliveryOwner` does for `delivery`. Data members keep their identity, callbacks the `api.runtime.channel.inbound` facade already bound to the instance are left alone, and members core adds afterwards (`onModelSelected`) stay unbound. The scope exit from #184243 is unchanged: core code inside the lease still has no plugin instance.

The issue's other symptom, spooled retries failing with the same error, was fixed by #193423, which runs ingress monitor pumps in the monitor's plugin instance. This PR does not touch retries, so it no longer needs to land with or after the fix for #193159.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `src/channels/turn/run-channel-turn.delivery.test.ts`, "runs reply callbacks in the channel instance inside a reply run that exits it". On `54ed2bcc74b` it fails with `expected [ 'runtime', 'missing', 'missing' ] to deeply equal [ 'runtime', 'missing', 'runtime' ]`; on this branch it passes. The first read is the control (callback outside the reply run), the second pins #184243's exit, the third is the fix. Resolving the owner when the callback runs, instead of capturing it at turn entry, fails the same way.
- Gateway dry run: the real Gateway and Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API, a scripted model, the same messages and config on both builds, one run each. After a single-question `ask_user` card and its answer, the next three-question card logged `telegram: failed to persist sent-message cache: Error: Telegram runtime not initialized` once on `54ed2bcc74b` and 0 times with this branch. On earlier mains (`f5f27c3ef6e`, `982f3b1ee2b`) that order failed the write in 8 of 8 runs.
- Retries are unchanged: in the same run, the 40 s after a rejected partial answer looked the same on both builds, with 0 `Telegram runtime not initialized` lines, 0 failed spooled retries, and the rejected answer replayed and rejected 6 times at the same offsets (that loop is #193159).
- #193423 covers the retry symptom: the unit repro from this issue, with a real `PluginInstance`, passes on `54ed2bcc74b` and fails its production-shape case at #193423's parent `7edbcd3a30f`.
- Local runs on this branch (2 workers): 69 core test files covering `src/channels/turn`, `src/plugins/plugin-invocation-scope*`, `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime*` (the #184243 tests that pin the scope exit) and the importers of `lifecycle.ts`: 619 tests passed. 19 Telegram files (`bot-message*` and the other tests that import the sent-message cache): 287 passed. `pnpm test:contracts:channels`: 221 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:all` exit 0, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files; each caught an injected violation. Baseline ratchets against `54ed2bcc74b` (`--no-merge-base`) pass. Test lines: +37, allocated exactly in `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-reply-run-sent-message-cache.txt` (a record of 38 is refused; without it the ratchet reports over by 22). The new test takes 134 ms.

Not covered:
- No live Telegram run; the Gateway evidence is the loopback dry run above.
- Other channels on the SDK turn path get the same binding. I did not survey whether their reply callbacks read per-instance runtime.
- `dispatcherOptions` callbacks stay unbound, as in the runtime facade.
- During a channel reload, a bound reply callback that runs after its instance stops accepting calls is refused instead of running without the instance, the same as delivery on this path. Not exercised.

9.8.2

The Gradle team is excited to announce Gradle 9.8.2.

Here are the highlights of this release:

  • Java 27 support
  • Maven mirror settings reuse
  • Linked problem locations in build output

Read the Release Notes

We would like to thank the following community members for their contributions to this release of Gradle: Aman Gautam, Björn Kautler, Eng Zer Jun, Hashim Khan, Julian Krannich, KBS, Labh R Jethe, Mark Dodgson, Maxim, monkey, nataphon-ktsystems, Paul King, Qiu Tian, rg_sandesh, Roberto Perez Alcolea, Sean, Zongle Wang.

Upgrade instructions

Switch your build to use Gradle 9.8.2 by updating your wrapper:

./gradlew :wrapper --gradle-version=9.8.2 && ./gradlew :wrapper

See the Gradle 9.x upgrade guide to learn about deprecations, breaking changes and other considerations when upgrading.

For Java, Groovy, Kotlin and Android compatibility, see the full compatibility notes.

Reporting problems

If you find a problem with this release, please file a bug on GitHub Issues adhering to our issue guidelines. If you're not sure you're encountering a bug, please use the forum.

We hope you will build happiness with Gradle, and we look forward to your feedback via Twitter or on GitHub.

  • Regression: Fix quoting TXT rdata containing semicolons and parentheses (@​alexmit, #427)

Changelog

Sourced from dnsjava:dnsjava's changelog.

11/01/2026

  • 3.7.1 released
  • Regression: Fix quoting TXT rdata containing semicolons and parentheses (@​alexmit, #427)
  • Add support for generating SM3 DS digests (@​alexmit, #428)
  • Fix publishing of -sources and -javadoc artifacts to Maven Central

10/26/2026

  • 3.7.0 released
  • GHSA-m23c-5x5g-5ff6: Missing response validation in DoH Resolver
  • GHSA-rwxq-7vpj-2rm5: Unbounded Pre-allocation via DNS Header Count Fields Leads to Amplified Memory Allocation (DoS)
  • GHSA-hg22-jxmg-ppq9: Message normalization fails on invalid CNAME entries
  • GHSA-whp4-9hfm-h8xr: X25Record accepts Unicode digits and silently converts them into non-digit DNS wire bytes
  • GHSA-m779-jq28-q7v7: TSIG: MAC comparison is not constant-time
  • TSIG: BADTIME responses fail verification because the MAC does not cover the Other Data (@​kakooch, #424)
  • Extend unit test coverage (@​sean-g-rae, #412)
  • New config option dnsjava.secure_random_algorithm property to select SecureRandom algorithm (@​ChrisJr404, #368, #419)
  • Validate SSHFP fingerprint lengths (@​andrew-boutin and @​Mahmoodifar, #414, #415)

prs.title: fix(cli): openclaw agent waits silently when the model asks a question
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187728

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw agent` prints nothing until the question timeout (900 seconds by default) when the model calls `ask_user`, because the terminal cannot show or answer structured questions.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw agent` returns promptly with the agent's question in its text reply, instead of hanging for up to 15 minutes and then continuing with an answer the user never chose. This holds for fresh sessions and for sessions an earlier client, such as the Control UI, already used. Runs with `--deliver` keep the delivery channel's question support.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186653 made the ACP bridge declare the `no-question-input` client capability, so its turns omit `ask_user` and the agent asks in text. `openclaw agent` sent no such declaration, so its turns were still offered `ask_user`.

- The CLI now declares `no-question-input` in its Gateway identity, unless the run is delivered to a channel.
- The tool list follows the capabilities recorded on the session, and only chat.send and channel ingress recorded them, so a session the Control UI used first kept offering `ask_user` to a later CLI turn. The Gateway `agent` method now records the caller's capabilities for visible operator turns, with the same rule chat.send ingress uses (now one shared function). Internal wakes, inter-session input, hidden runs and in-process callers such as plugin `subagent.run` turns, which use synthetic clients, record nothing and keep the recorded capabilities.

Docs for the command, the handshake capability, and `ask_user` availability name the new case.

Accepted edge case: the session keeps the capabilities of its most recent client turn. `openclaw agent` targets the agent's main session by default, which is also the Control UI's main chat. A CLI turn there switches the session's tool list (and its wakes') to the CLI's, without `ask_user`, `screen` or `show_widget`, until the next Control UI turn switches it back; each switch costs one prompt-cache miss. This is the existing contract when two chat.send clients with different capabilities alternate on one session.

Not changed: a CLI message that continues a run already active on the session keeps that run's client capabilities when they are a subset of the CLI's (the continuation rule in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority-inbound.ts`), so a run started by another client can still call `ask_user` until it ends. The `secrets` tool's `request` action also waits for user input and does not read `no-question-input`; that predates this PR and is left for a follow-up.

## Evidence

Both sides ran the built CLI against an isolated loopback Gateway (synthetic token, temporary state directory) and a deterministic OpenAI-compatible fixture provider. When `ask_user` is offered, the fixture calls it with a 30 second timeout; otherwise it asks the same question in text. The second scenario first sends one `chat.send` turn on the same session, as the Control UI does, then runs the CLI. Before ran on the base f25b36e95b0161b324ad772127264fb0021c4d6c (an independent reviewer's clean-base runs); After on this branch at 5424e0bc519.

| `openclaw agent` run | Before (base) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh session | 34.96 s, `ask_user` offered and called, no answer | 3.41 s, not offered, question in the reply |
| Session used by an earlier chat turn | 32.15 s, `ask_user` offered and called, no answer | 1.95 s, not offered on the CLI turn, question in the reply |
| Same session, real model (Gemini 3.8 Flash) | — | 5.72 s, no `ask_user` call, question in the reply |

On the base, the command printed nothing for the whole question timeout (30 s here, 900 s by default), then the agent went on with "No answer arrived, so I will use Blue." The chat.send turn still offers `ask_user` to its own client.

<details>
<summary>Fixture runs (request log condensed to one line per model request)</summary>

Fresh session, before:

```text
$ time openclaw agent --agent main --message "Pick a color for the banner." --json
exit=0 elapsed=34.959759580s

# fixture provider request log
{"call":1,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}
{"call":2,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}

# tool result returned to the model on call 2
"id": "openclaw:core:ask_user"
"text": "No answer arrived; proceed with best judgment.\n\n{\n  \"status\": \"no_answer\"\n}"

# final reply
"text": "No answer arrived, so I will use Blue."
```

Fresh session, after:

```text
$ time openclaw agent --agent main --message "Pick a color for the banner." --json
exit=0 elapsed=3.405619609s

# fixture provider request log
{"call":1,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":false}

# final reply
"text": "Which color should I use: Red or Blue?"
```

Session used by an earlier chat turn, before:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"Hello there.",...}'
$ time openclaw agent --agent main --message "Pick a color for the banner." --json
exit=0 elapsed=32.149766978s

# fixture provider request log (call 1 is the chat.send turn)
{"call":1,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}
{"call":2,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}
{"call":3,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}

# tool result returned to the model on call 3
"id": "openclaw:core:ask_user"
"text": "No answer arrived; proceed with best judgment.\n\n{\n  \"status\": \"no_answer\"\n}"

# final reply
"text": "No answer arrived, so I will use Blue."
```

Session used by an earlier chat turn, after:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"Hello there.",...}'
$ time openclaw agent --agent main --message "Pick a color for the banner." --json
exit=0 elapsed=1.951503544s

# fixture provider request log (call 1 is the chat.send turn)
{"call":1,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}
{"call":2,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":false}

# final reply
"text": "Which color should I use: Red or Blue?"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Real model run (Gemini 3.8 Flash, session used by an earlier chat turn)</summary>

```text
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"Hello there.",...}'
$ time openclaw agent --agent main --message "I need a banner color. Before you pick one, ask me whether I want red or blue." --json
exit=0 elapsed=5.720837965s

# reply
"text": "Would you prefer red or blue for the banner?"
"provider": "google", "model": "gemini-3.8-flash"

# Gateway log: both turns completed; no ask_user tool call
```

</details>

Checks run locally at 5424e0bc519:

- The two regression tests fail on the base and pass on this branch: `uses cli authority with the local gateway for hi` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` (base: `expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'no-question-input' ]`) and `records the operator client's capabilities for later wakes of its session` in `src/gateway/server.agent.rpc-contracts.test.ts` (base: `expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'no-question-input', 'tool-events' ]`). The second test also runs a plugin's in-process `agent` turn on the session; without the synthetic-client check it fails with `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'no-question-input', 'tool-events' ]`.
- `pnpm check:changed --base f25b36e95b0` in a clean checkout of this branch: every lane passed (typecheck core and core tests, core lint, format, line-cap, mock-export, import cycles, docs baseline) except the dead export scan, which lists unused exports in modules this PR does not change.
- Touched and consumer test files, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` 60 passed; `src/gateway/server.agent.rpc-contracts.test.ts` 2 passed; `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` 14 passed; `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-patch.test.ts` 10 passed.

The current head merges main at 195efadb713. The only conflict was the client capabilities table in `docs/gateway/protocol/handshake.md`, which main turned into a table; its `no-question-input` row now names `openclaw agent` without `--deliver`, and the PR's diff is otherwise unchanged. The head also adds `config/test-lines-allocations/cli-agent-no-question-input.txt` for this PR's 47 net test lines: the new Gateway test adds 49 (it proves the `agent` method records the operator's capabilities and that a plugin's in-process turn keeps them) and the CLI test shrinks by 2; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 195efadb713` passes with it.

Cost of the changed test files at 5424e0bc519. Wall times were measured on 2026-10-30 while other test runs shared the machine; the Gateway file's wall time is mostly the Gateway server import (36.6 s), not its two tests.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` | 31.70 s (60 tests, Vitest 24.12 s; 5.3 s of it is the existing first Gateway-authority case, whose assertions this PR extends) | 15.05 s of test time in `agentic-commands-agent-channel` (6 files, Vitest 86.62 s), CI run 40894398605 |
| `src/gateway/server.agent.rpc-contracts.test.ts` | 58.10 s (2 tests, 3.02 + 1.38 s; Vitest 50.88 s) | 3.70 s of test time in `agentic-control-plane-agent-chat-hosted-3` (2 files, Vitest 31.83 s), CI run 40894398605 |

CI run 40894398605 at 5424e0bc519 had one unrelated red, a 1 ms clock slip in `src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts`; its fix, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187763, is in the main this head merges.

Not covered: `--deliver` runs were not exercised end to end; they keep the previous behavior, and the delivery channel decides question support. `--deliver --best-effort-deliver` with no resolvable channel still offers `ask_user`. The embedded `--local` path is unchanged. The recorded-session scenario was primed with a `chat.send` call from the CLI rather than a browser Control UI; both go through the same chat ingress. The fixture runs used a 30 second question timeout instead of the 900 second default.

prs.title: fix(secrets): file references lose whitespace in JSON Pointer keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

File SecretRefs with whitespace at the end of a JSON Pointer select the wrong key through config builders, or fail resolution when supplied directly.

## User Impact

`/token ` selects the literal `"token "` key and remains distinct from `/token`. Missing references retain the correct failure classification and runtime owner. Existing env, store, and exec ID trimming is preserved. No schema, provider permissions, public SDK, or credential-redaction policy changes.

IDs still follow the documented grammar: the single-value ID is exactly `value`, and JSON Pointers start with `/`. Whitespace inside a pointer is literal key data; padded malformed IDs are rejected rather than silently repaired.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing reference-contract owner for source-aware normalization in CLI inputs, resolver grouping, missing-ref matching, and runtime attribution. This is the same input-preservation defect class as recently merged external contribution #192796. Four callers consume that one rule; no new state or fallback is introduced.

## Evidence

Real source CLI on Linux/Node 24, in a secretless container with isolated state and a synthetic private JSON vault; no mocked resolver, live credentials, remote provider, or model calls:

- Persist `config set gateway.auth.token --ref-source file --ref-provider vault --ref-id '/token '`: the original base saves `/token`; the fix saves `/token `.
- With only `{"token ":"SYNTHETIC_SELECTED"}`, `config set ... --dry-run --json` through builder flags and strict JSON SecretRefs: the original base fails; the fix succeeds with one reference checked.
- With only `{"token":"SYNTHETIC_NEIGHBOR"}`, the trailing-space reference: the original builder incorrectly succeeds; fixed builder and raw JSON both fail. Ordinary `/token` succeeds as a control.

The original real-CLI reproduction failed with four violations. The recorded pre-rebase CLI replay passes all six behavior/control checks with zero violations. Regressions cover all three CLI input modes (flags, batch, patch), distinct batched file resolution, exact missing-ref identity, runtime attribution, and non-file compatibility.

Recorded pre-rebase validation: 151 focused tests across seven files, touched format, typed lint, core types, and touched-test types passed. Command: `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli-input.test.ts src/secrets/resolve.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-degradation-attribution.test.ts src/secrets/ref-contract.test.ts src/secrets/exec-secret-ref-id-parity.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.secrets.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Independent static review covered the complete final base-to-HEAD diff and affected consumers, with no actionable findings. Linux/POSIX proof does not establish Windows end-to-end behavior or live model/provider behavior.

Current CI repair: `d7f474b232bebd1bea829805ad1e7df689987301`, rebased onto `38776e59e870c4a878f5342e218a10080052ed34` at the contributor’s explicit request after the previous run failed during a runtime download. The base includes the merged UI repair from #193468.

- The complete nine-file SecretRef patch remains byte-identical to the original patch. This synchronization changes no PR-owned production behavior, tests, allocation, or checker policy.
- The canonical full-index test-line check passes: **6,513,409 lines / 6,513,439 ceiling / 30 spare**. Full-patch equivalence and whitespace checks pass.
- The original budget and five failing UI shards already passed in [previous-head CI 42036925980](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42036925980); the selected Node tests, type checks, and lint checks also passed there. Its remaining UI failure was `session-management.groups.e2e.test.ts:857`, where a saved collapsed top-level session group reopened after reload. The exact base had the [same failure in scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42035744729/job/127273644070).
- Merged maintainer PR [#193468](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193468) supplies the causal repair: automatic group reveal excludes the active top-level row while retaining nested-session revelation. Its original browser regression and nested-session control passed according to the maintainer's recorded proof. This repair is now included in the base, without adding unrelated UI changes to this PR's diff.
- Independent Codex review of the complete final range `38776e59e870..d7f474b232be` found no actionable P0–P2 findings and checked the new base’s affected consumers for compatibility. This was a separate agent review, not an autoreview tool execution.
- Previous-head (`ad16bba7`) [CI run 42046599801](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42046599801) completed. All seven UI E2E shards pass, including the original collapse/reload failure, and the budget, type, lint, and other executed test lanes pass. One Node lane did not reach its tests: [checks-node-changed-compact-small-15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42046599801/job/127311798589) failed in `Install pinned Bun test runtime`, with four HTTP 504 download responses and exit 22. Its dependent aggregate CI gate is also red. This is a setup failure, not a passing test result; other Node lanes using the same setup succeeded.
- A failed-jobs rerun was requested after the run completed, but GitHub rejected it with `Must have admin rights to Repository`. No second attempt was created; the run remains at attempt 1. The explicit user-requested rebase will trigger a fresh run for the new head; that result is still pending. No CI assertion, runtime pin, or workflow was changed to bypass the failure.
- Earlier local CLI/test/type/lint results retain their stated prior-head scope. Previous-head hosted checks above do not establish the new head’s CI result or grant security approval.

Security-sensitive review is a separate maintainer gate: the repository requires an authorized maintainer to approve the current exact revision before merge. Contributor validation does not supply that approval. This PR remains Ready for review.
