prs.title: fix(ci): repair state worker and release validation fixtures
prs.body:
## Problem

Beta full-release validation exposed three independent failures also present on main: compiled state workers omit the existing native TypeScript preload, Liquid adapter fixtures depend on runner scheduling, and the smoke installer accepts incomplete APT indexes.

## Changes

- Add SQLite/shared-state entries to the existing source-host worker preload and extend its native SDK identity regression. The regression consumes and validates the real initial memory announcement before awaiting SDK readiness, and closes the transferred diagnostic port.
- Give Liquid adapter fixtures a controlled monotonic clock, including expiry during image inspection before HTTP. Update the existing clock spy without extracting an unbound method.
- Make incomplete APT indexes activate the smoke image’s existing bounded retry and extend the existing shell regression.

No production timeout, admission guard, or retry count is relaxed. Existing owners and assertions are retained; net test growth is 39 lines with matching scoped allocations.

## Evidence

- Original failures: hosted beta runs 42104932629, 42104936703, and 42104913895.
- Earlier-head CI 42128109661 and 42129210947 exposed a real startup-message ordering mistake in the added worker fixture, formatting in that test, and an unbound-method lint error in the Liquid fixture. These are repaired in ba2ad75977c4 and 8925bf6d5532. The earlier check-docs failure was the same formatting failure; its subsequent documentation-content checks passed.
- Fresh independent source reviews found no blocking findings in the worker receipt repair or bound clock-spy repair. The native-auth assertion proposal was rejected and remains excluded. Hosted ClawSweeper review on exact 8925bf6d5532 completed with no findings (comment 6672594130, run 42132140017). Required local ClawSweeper/autoreview tooling is unavailable; permission to use the hosted and independent reviews instead remains pending.
- Targeted formatting and whitespace checks passed. The diff was simplified using the existing compiler, fixture, and retry owners.
- Exact-head CI 42130655702 passed: 37 successful jobs, 30 skipped, zero failed, including the CI gate. Its bun-all runtime policy executed the worker-artifacts suite (28 passed), Liquid image-inspection deadline regression, and installer suite (71 passed, including both incomplete-index regressions). Separate Node execution on this head is not established; earlier-head Node results are not substituted.
- Exact-head build 42130655648 passed. Job 127606318327 executed pnpm build:ci-artifacts, including compiler, SDK declarations, UI, and plugin assets.
- No local runtime tests/builds were run under the remote-first instruction. Installer evidence covers the shell harness, not full Docker installer E2E; that lane was skipped. These results do not constitute full beta release qualification.

## Other observed failures and limits

- Earlier-head run 42128109661, job 127598465598: the Windows cleanup fixture searches raw JSONL for an unescaped Windows path. The assertion and its logging owners are unchanged from parent 071ea8338d93 (introduced by PR193702). A separate narrow correction is prepared and independently reviewed; it is not included here.
- Earlier-head run 42128109661, job 127598466162: two Node 24.22.1 plugin-reload wrappers exceeded their 120-second outer deadline. The observed continuation completed resume effects, wake and cleanup, then reached followup startup. Same-checkout Bun passed both wrappers, with continuation taking 118,340 ms. Parent Node coverage was skipped, so inheritedness is not established and the added worker preloads' latency impact remains unmeasured. No timeout increase, assertion weakening or speculative preload rollback is proposed. A comparable parent/head Node run remains an evidence gap; current Bun CI does not close it.

After main landing, these fixes will be backported to the existing beta candidate.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): add decision-model recall gate
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Relevant Knowledge page content still needs an agent retrieval step unless the owner has approved an automatic summary; the standing index supplies labels and selected claim headlines, not page bodies.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into per-turn, model-scored recall so useful excerpts are available when the main model starts answering. Existing approved-summary recall and the standing index remain intact. The gate is off without configuration and starts in `shadow` mode; `live` explicitly enables injection.

The Decision provider receives the user message and candidate excerpts even in shadow mode. Live injection uses model-selected page text, not owner-approved summaries. Choose a provider trusted with that data, treat excerpts as evidence rather than instructions, and tune model-specific relevance thresholds in shadow before enabling live mode. No latency or tool-call reduction is claimed by the current verification.

## Why This Change Was Made

Knowledge owns candidate selection, the shared Decision runtime owns execution, and the bundled `rerank` provider owns endpoint/auth behavior. The core runtime gains an optional caller-authority check so revocable Knowledge grants remain live through preparation, physical dispatch, retries and completion; this is not a plugin-only change.

- Default keyword mode shortlists up to ten pages and scores them independently; two relevant pages can both pass. Model-selected label shortlisting remains optional.
- The default whole-gate budget is 1,500 ms; injected context is capped at 6,000 characters and added to the current user turn, not the cached system prefix. Pointer and skip-search hints remain off by default. Unavailability, errors and timeouts omit the optional injection.
- Rerank supports the common `documents` API and a guarded `texts` retry for TEI. Every document must have one score in `[0,1]`; raw logits are rejected, not rescaled or automatically passed through a sigmoid. Keyless local endpoints do not receive the synthetic auth marker.
- Defaults came from the author's private GTE-reranker benchmark. They are not calibrated probabilities or a newly reproduced full-agent benchmark.

The latest integration preserves contributor ancestry, retains main's Knowledge recommended prompts and first-install defaults, and regenerates configuration fingerprints rather than choosing either conflicted checksum.

## Evidence

Current head: `157b7b2b43cc0e35d30c9ce896806f3f2e8d5d93`, integrating main `349859e09efc56b5191ee6e45aaed1655ea5d1ae`. Tested candidate tree: `f4fa4e603c25d540272c1ca714dad808ed4caefa`.

- **79 tests in all eight selected files pass**, across three repository-planned Vitest shards in 129.61 seconds. This includes the six feature files plus current-main retrieval and remember interactions. Coverage includes independent relevance scoring, excerpt budgets, keyless/keyed/TEI transport, Decision-picker advertisement and real hook → Decision runtime → recording HTTP authority boundaries.
- Ungranted audiences send nothing. Revocation before dispatch, before the TEI retry and before publication stops further egress/publication as appropriate. These tests use real production components and synthetic vault/HTTP fixtures, not a live provider or full Gateway run.
- **Test audit:** removed three mocked cases superseded by that stronger boundary proof: **71 LF removed**. Calibration, protocol, picker and authority controls remain. The justified feature allocation is **1,070 LF**, down from 1,141; the refreshed-base test-line ratchet passes with 29 LF slack, without raising the shared scalar.
- Full typecheck, config documentation and the main-relative line-cap guard pass on the refreshed composition. Formatting, plugin boundaries, import cycles, dead-export scan and Knip production/all-export checks also passed on the earlier `9d8bbfbbaf1`-based candidate, with the integration delta qualified below.
- Complete local **autoreview / Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2** found no actionable findings in one full pass with the required source context on the earlier feature candidate `eabae1322b4cd170becacd2644cea4f09c9e67ce`. After the main refresh, supplied TypeScript review context is unchanged except upstream Boolean-default metadata in `stores-config.ts`; the eligibility definition and dependency manifests are unchanged. The affected tests and full typecheck were rerun. The earlier review is not relabelled as a review of an identical new tree, human approval or executed test proof.
- The fresh main checkpoint composed cleanly before publication. [Published-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188057/checks) is running and remains a separate landing gate.

<details>
<summary>Preserved failures and verification limits</summary>

The unchanged original head `1e1b6766ac6` failed three local Decision-picker assertions; two authority cases passed and the remaining planner groups were not reached. All three assertions pass on the current main composition with its frozen dependencies, without weakening them. The original failure is retained; no specific root-cause repair is claimed.

The broad local quality run on the earlier `9d8bbfbbaf1`-based candidate found global max-lines/Solid lint diagnostics and release-changelog thanks-attribution failures in unchanged main files. Reported lint files and the changelog record/checker were blob-compared with that pinned main base: 24 equal blobs, no differences and no changed-file lint diagnostics. The full-tree unused-file guard also reported `src/node-host/node-worker-prepared-workspace.process.test-support.ts`; its file, checker and Knip inputs matched that main base. These outcomes remain recorded rather than deleting another owner's fixture or editing release-owned notes. prs.title: fix(workboard): scope lifecycle hydration to linked cards
prs.body:
Fixes #187811

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard lifecycle processing read every card and all of its child rows before deciding which cards could match a session event or need reconciliation. On a long-lived board that cost grows with history (events, comments, logs, notifications), even though only active cards can change.

In plain terms: every event and every 60-second sweep reopened the whole board and all of its history just to find the few cards that still matter. This change asks the database for that short candidate list first, then hydrates only those cards.

- **Session events**: resolve cards from the event's session/run identity instead of loading the whole board.
- **Sweep**: use a conservative SQL candidate read covering active lifecycle work and terminal worktree cleanup; the existing JS reconciliation predicate remains the final authority.
- The second full-board reload at the end of the sweep is removed; worktree cleanup runs against the same candidate set.
- No schema, config, public RPC, or persistence contract change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The store already had scoped reads (`session-links`, `worker-context`, `page`), but `syncWorkboardLifecycleEvent` and the sweep did not use one. The new `lifecycle` and `lifecycle-event` read scopes keep the selection in SQL and preserve the existing full card/child shape for the cards that are actually loaded.

The event scope is a superset of the existing matcher: exact and execution-only `subagent:workboard-*` suffix keys, derived workboard keys, exact and provisional run IDs, and recorded attempt/event links. The unchanged `workboardCardMatchesLifecycleLink` predicate still decides the final match. Terminal worktree cleanup keeps its own archived-safe branch and requires both `path` and `sourcePath`, so a discharged cleanup is excluded. The selectors use the existing Kysely query owner, not raw `db.prepare`, and both list branches preserve an explicit `boardId` constraint when supplied.

## User Impact

Long-lived Workboard boards stop paying history-sized reads on every lifecycle event and on the periodic reconciliation. Active cards and terminal worktree cleanup behave as before; settled historical cards are no longer decoded.

## Evidence

Real SQLite read against the production store with 500 settled cards, 5,000 history child rows, and one active card:

```text
historyCards: 500
historyChildRows: 5000
fullList: { cards: 501, ms: 62.2 }
lifecycleCandidates: { cards: 1, ms: 5.4 }
```

Focused regression and behavior suite:

```text
pnpm test extensions/workboard/src/lifecycle-sync.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
✓ 48 passed
```

Bounded hydration is asserted directly: a settled historical card gets a child comment with an empty required body, which full hydration would reject; the lifecycle candidate read succeeds and returns only the active card. The sweep test also asserts that the background service calls `store.list({ lifecycle: true })`.

Base red check (production changes reverted, regressions kept): `3 failed | 40 passed` — the failing cases were the scoped event read, session-scoped list, and lifecycle candidate read. Full Workboard suite after the fix: `351 passed | 11 skipped`.

Gateway lifecycle-service proof against a real SQLite store with 500 settled cards and 5,000 history child rows, one of which has an empty required comment body (full hydration would throw):

```text
completionHook: { count: 1, status: "review" }
subagentHook: { count: 1, status: "review" }
sweepListScopes: [
  { sessionKey: "agent:main:active", runId: "run-active" },
  { sessionKey: "agent:alpha:subagent:workboard-service", runId: "run-subagent" },
  { lifecycle: true }
]
fullHydrationError: true
```

Both the completion hook and the real `subagent_ended` path settled their active cards through `syncWorkboardAgentEnded` / `syncWorkboardSubagentEnded`; the periodic service used the lifecycle candidate read. None decoded the invalid historical child row. This host has no PostgreSQL service; the PostgreSQL storage/conformance path is covered by CI.

Independent running-Gateway PostgreSQL benchmark by @etzelm (recovery sweep, this head, production-shaped 336-card board): rows returned `11,616 -> 1,358` (-88%), shared buffer hits `9,402 -> 1,404` (-85%), median DB exec `30.2 ms -> 6.5 ms`. The reporter notes the event path was not exercised; the subagent trace above covers that path at the service boundary.

Running Gateway end-to-end dispatch (not the in-process service harness):

```text
# PR dist, isolated SQLite Gateway, token auth, mock OpenAI provider
$ openclaw workboard create "Gateway completion proof" --status ready --agent main --json
card baf6cbb1-... status=ready

$ openclaw workboard dispatch --max-starts 1 --admin --json
count: 1
started: [{ cardId: baf6cbb1-..., sessionKey: agent:main:subagent:workboard-default-baf6cbb1-..., runId: workboard:baf6cbb1-...:1793509544170 }]
startFailures: []

# Gateway log
workboard.cards.dispatchWithOptions.owner 3379ms
[agent] run workboard:baf6cbb1-... ended with stopReason=stop

# after completion
$ openclaw workboard show baf6cbb1-... --json
status: review
execution.status: review
attempts: [succeeded]

# Workboard SQLite after the run
cards: 1 (status=review)
attempts: 1 (status=succeeded)
activeCandidates: 0
```

The lifecycle candidate read selected exactly the one active card at dispatch (`count: 1`) and returned no active candidates after completion. The mock OpenAI provider served the run (3 bounded request-log records), so this is a real Gateway/subagent end rather than a directly called hook.

The lifecycle-event selector now also constrains provisional `workboard:<id>:` run ids by compatible session identity; a regression covers a settled history card from another session. Merged main; gateway.ts now matches #190093 exactly and is not part of the PR diff.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Traced the lifecycle reads to the SQL selector, added the running-Gateway/subagent proof and the cross-session provisional-run regression, and aligned the owner-handler change with merged #190060.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release operators on `release/2026.11.5` are missing the audited FRV recovery, publication observation, package qualification, and fixture-isolation fixes that landed after the retrospective backport.

## User Impact

Makes release preparation and recovery more reliable on the 11.5 line. This is a tooling backport only: no version bump, release publication, live Gateway change, or blanket package-security allowlist update. Full release validation remains required for any future release candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested follow-up to the RomneyDa / Tideclaw release-tooling audit. Reconciled merged #191633 against baseline `e320598c68279b5a411cfc81cd5ac8ed7b1a7994`; do not duplicate its runtime backports. The requested comprehensive branch batch keeps the related FRV/publication chain together and includes their existing regression fixtures.

### Backported source PRs

- #188743 — fix(release): shorten branch push preflight
- #188814 — fix(release): pin stable OpenCode Go smoke to reachable model
- #188985 — fix(release): install WebKit for repo UI E2E

- #192487 — fix(test): isolate release fixtures from enclosing checkout state

- #192587 — fix(release): exit FRV continue on repeat child failure and flag ghost jobs
- #192392 — fix: reject unbridgeable update compatibility inventories

### Required companion repairs

- #190782 / #190830 — carry the calibrated Kova pin through its live-registry and final-diagnostics fixes to `869493d1be0dcf10b7ddf96371cf35239a9efbd6`, including the matching historical-timeline report adapter. Compared all three Kova commits against this branch’s `88d9a7…` pin: no dependency/package changes; preserved legacy evaluator pin and hard resource ceilings.

- #192628 — regenerated the three canonical JSON snapshots required by #192596, through the branch generator; parsed JSON content is unchanged.
- #192850 — applied only the release-planner private-export cleanup required by #191654; unrelated UI hunks are excluded.
- Addressed local review of #192607: the standalone watcher now observes extended-stable plugin titles and verified Docker-only parents, without weakening the missing-plugin check for ordinary publication.

### Already covered or superseded

#192297, #193195, #193178, #192806, #192586, #192389, #191641, #190755, #190747, #190746, #189748, #189720, #189718, #189715, #187994, #187991, #185258, #180211, #180203, #180201, #180191, #180183, #180180, #180169, #180164, #193199.

- #193178: validated branch handling is already backported; #188743 removes the detached broad-check runner, so its environment-only assertion is obsolete. Exact-source and destination push checks remain.
- #192806/#193195: retain the newer branch-adapted advisory line limits and strict unused-suppression checks.
- #192586: branch already contains the applicable FRV, kitchen-sink, and SQLite admission changes; do not introduce newer SQLite carrier classes.
- #191641: recovery revalidation is already present. The remaining recommended-prompts module inventory is inapplicable because that source module is absent on this line.

### Deliberate exclusions

### Release adaptations and simplification

Kept source `-x` provenance and original authors. No new runtime owner, fallback, or compatibility store.

## Evidence

- Core release/recovery suites passed after branch adaptation; watcher/stable repair suite: 32 tests passed. Both new review regressions failed on the pre-repair head, then passed; the normal missing-plugin refusal remains covered.
- Six adjacent qualification/contract suites: 97 tests passed.
- Script and tooling-test typechecks, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, test-line ratchet, workflow validator (zizmor plus Git-owner/composite-expression checks), and `git diff --check` passed.

Exit 1 was the expected attention result; no workflow was dispatched, approved, or retried.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed baseline `e320598c6827` through `540b79fe812b`, found two P2 watcher cases, and both were fixed with regressions. The final repair review on `0f765938f23e` found no actionable correctness/security defects. The Kova companion delta through `c2777d10eea8` also received a completed local review with no actionable findings; its external three-commit evaluator diff was separately inspected.
- Kova workflow contract: 52 tests passed; historical-diagnostics report adapter: 31 tests passed. Full evaluator/performance campaign not run.
- Companion comparison accounted for the sole absent selected path (`ci.yml`, already equivalent) and sole extra path (fast-prepush documentation); branch-specific content is intentionally retained.

- Focused owning cases from the large CI/planner/Crabbox/PR-wrapper suites: 47 passed; package/model-selection cases: 2 passed. Exhaustive unrelated cases in those large suites were not part of the local qualification.
- No full release, evaluator performance campaign, Docker/macOS/Windows artifact, or live publication validation claimed. PR CI remains the broader check; this PR does not merge or publish a release.

## CI repair follow-up

Investigated the exact failures on `c2777d10eea891d6d0ef21a78de216316bb671e4` (CI run [42125291722](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42125291722)).

- Docker package harness: restored the fixture's missing `release-context.mjs` and `release-version.mjs` dependency closure. The existing dependency-free CLI test reproduced the missing-module failure locally before the repair and passes afterward. Assertions are unchanged. This omission already existed in the release base.
- macOS Periphery: extracted `NSDictionary` construction from a Swift Testing `#expect` macro, preserving dictionary equality. The original expression reproduced the exact Swift 6.3.3 macro compilation error; the repaired expression compiles. The build failure caused the shared-kit scan and intersection failures as well. The defect already existed in the release base; no scan gates were suppressed. Full macOS build proof remains CI-owned.
- Provider scaffold: dependency installation, build, and tests passed; the installed ClawHub CLI then timed out downloading an OpenClaw npm archive after approximately 30 seconds. The scaffold generator, wrapper, and workflow are unchanged. No retry, timeout increase, or suppression was added; this external download failure remains a validation limitation until CI confirms recovery.
- Terminal delivery: backported [#188765](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188765) (`cf83a69f74eed57a3467bba3963d433e25d20743`). A current-run output-limited response must allow the fallback owner to continue; the release baseline incorrectly acknowledged the persisted input as already delivered and skipped the fallback request. Same-run `format`/`length` continuation is now permitted while ordinary retry and other-run no-redelivery boundaries remain covered. - Repair validation so far: all 61 replay-suite cases passed; dependency-free package-harness regression passed; Swift 6.3.3 macro compilation and SwiftFormat passed; changed TypeScript formatting and package-fixture lint passed. Independent review found no actionable defects in either the fixture repairs or same-run fallback boundary.

prs.title: fix(cli): config get spends ~200 ms on an unused schema for agents, channels and plugins paths
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176318

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config get` for paths under `agents`, `channels` or `plugins` spends about 200 ms per call building the full config form schema, which it never reads when the value exists.

## User Impact

User impact: `config get` on those paths returns about 190 ms (18%) faster in the measured setup, with byte-identical output, redaction and exit codes. Not-found paths still print the same "valid but unset" or "Unknown config path" message.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175818 moved the Gateway's redaction-only readers to the lighter `buildConfigRedactionHints`, which merges sensitivity metadata without building or tier-resolving the form schema. The CLI reader `runConfigGet` was left on `buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry`: it used `.uiHints` for redaction and `.schema` only for the not-found message.

- `runtime-schema.ts` gains `buildRuntimeConfigRedactionHintsFromRegistry`, the hint-only sibling of `buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry` over the same registry metadata.
- `runConfigGet` redacts with it and builds the full schema only when the path is not found.
- The Doctor report for externally managed config (`reportDoctorExternalConfigRepairs`) had the same shape and uses the same hint builder.

Redaction reads only `sensitive` and the URL-sensitivity tag. The full schema's hints carry 110 more keys with those fields than the redaction-only hints (bundled registry, 171 plugins). They come from the presentation passes over the merged schema, which copy a matching hint onto the schema paths they visit (for example the `source`/`provider`/`id` fields of SecretRef inputs). A schema-shaped value built at each of those 110 paths redacts identically with both hint sets.

## Evidence

Tested at `0f23ad6c8dc` (base `upstream/main` `94fa98bfd93`).

Merged `upstream/main` `195efadb713` at `21118aa7519`: one import-line conflict in `doctor-external-config.ts` kept both main's `preparePluginDoctorContractModules` and this PR's hint builder, and the PR diff is unchanged. On the new base the two changed tests again fail and pass here; main folded tests in `config-cli.integration.test.ts`, so the other 23 now pass on both. The timings below are from `0f23ad6c8dc`.

Built CLI (`pnpm build:runtime`, `node openclaw.mjs config get <path>`, Node 24, Ubuntu 22.04) under an allowlisted environment with an isolated home and no network. Config: default plus `agents.defaults.model`, a synthetic `channels.discord.token` and a synthetic `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey`. Nothing faked.

Before (base `94fa98bfd93`):

```text
wall time, 10 runs each (ms)
gateway.mode           838 846 844 838 847 843 841 840 841 834   (control: no plugin schema)
agents.defaults.model  1067 1059 1073 1058 1066 1063 1065 1072 1066 1050

CPU profile, config get agents.defaults.model (main thread 1,024 ms), inclusive
  222.5 ms  runConfigGet
  209.8 ms  buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry
  206.6 ms  buildConfigSchemaCore
    4.2 ms  redactConfigObject
```

After (this PR):

```text
wall time, 10 runs each (ms)
gateway.mode           846 839 848 839 834 844 840 845 834 843   (control: unchanged)
agents.defaults.model  868 865 873 866 874 869 869 882 865 870

CPU profile, config get agents.defaults.model (main thread 833 ms), inclusive
   41.4 ms  runConfigGet
   31.8 ms  buildRuntimeConfigRedactionHintsFromRegistry
   29.7 ms  buildConfigRedactionHints
    2.1 ms  redactConfigObject
  (buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry not called)
```

Observed result: found values drop from 1,050–1,073 ms to 865–882 ms while the control stays at 834–848 ms. Stdout, stderr and exit codes are byte-identical between base and branch on 11 paths: `gateway.mode`, `agents.defaults.model`, `agents --json`, `channels.discord.token`, `channels.discord --json`, `plugins.entries.tavily --json`, `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey` (both secrets print `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__`), and the not-found paths `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, `agents.defaults.nope`, `plugins.entries.nope`, `channels.nope --json`.

Tests: the existing redaction case in `config-cli.integration.test.ts` (SecretRef ids, core and plugin schema-sensitive fields) now also asserts that `buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry` is not called. The fail-closed case now injects its failure into the hint builder that found values use. Run on the base and this branch, both fail on the base (the schema builder is called 4 times; the hint builder does not exist yet) and pass here, with the other 25 tests in the file passing on both.

Checks: the touched test file (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, time below), `doctor-health.readonly-config.test.ts` (the Doctor report path), `runtime-schema.test.ts`, `config-cli.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm lint:tmp:export-name-collisions`; the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts` | 10.96 s (27 tests) | 5.18 s of test time in `core-runtime-infra-storage-state-hosted-4` (2 files, Vitest 116.73 s), CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39153325159 |

Simplify pass: the form-schema build disappears from found-value reads in `config get` and from the Doctor report; no new state, cache or option. Behavior still protected: redaction of SecretRef ids and core and plugin sensitive fields, fail-closed output when plugin metadata or hints are unavailable, and the not-found messages. Delta against the merge base: production +24/−15 in 3 files, tests +10/−5 in 1 file.

Not covered: one machine and one plugin set; a config with more plugins should save more, but that was not measured. Accepted edge case: a not-found path under these roots now builds the hints and then the full schema (one run per not-found path, 4 paths: base 1,069–1,080 ms, branch 1,076–1,096 ms); it already ends in an error message. The Doctor report path was exercised only through its existing test, not timed.

prs.title: fix: reduce standalone metadata lookup cost
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces standalone startup and config-validation CPU spent looking up embedded directory metadata.

## User Impact

Standalone metadata lookups avoid repeatedly scanning large directory values while preserving lazy decoding and cached object identity. No new startup imports or runtime-specific branch is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated lookup binary-searched positions in combined key/value text. A single large directory value made both cold lookups and repeated misses scan hundreds of kilobytes. The same lookup owner now searches a small immutable key-and-offset index and decodes only matched values.

## Evidence

- Accepted AOT compiler limitation: the query/fragment gate fails before and after on the carried and stock-main compilers; the rewrite baseline is blocked earlier at host loading and its final query gate also fails. An independent no-OpenClaw repro demonstrates the compiler defect. These remain failed tests, with no passing AOT case regressed; pinned JIT improves to pass.
- Stock-main HTTP parsing fails identically before and after (the same TypeError/HTTPParserError and eight errors in each ordinary synthetic run). Scalar diagnostics are labelled separately; no product workaround is included.
- A profile of the signed config-validation command attributed 72.9% of sampled self-time to this lookup, with one directory row exceeding 424,000 characters. Benchmarks execute the actual old/new generated expressions over the real 332-row directory table: 3,320 misses improve roughly 71–73 ms → 2.3–2.4 ms across pinned and upstream Bun. Warm-cache time is essentially unchanged. Cold traversal of the 18,542-entry scalar file map costs an additional 1–2 ms; application measurements below include that tradeoff.

prs.title: fix: restore standalone AOT module loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor, Gateway startup, and installed-plugin imports failing when a standalone executable is compiled with upstream Bun AOT. It also preserves query and fragment identity in ordinary Bun plugin imports through absolute paths and file URLs.

## User Impact

The host and installed plugins use the same compiled SDK exports without loading another SDK copy from disk. Existing published plugin imports, admission, generation ownership, and lazy source transformation stay unchanged. AOT remains opt-in.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upstream AOT intentionally forbids disk-loaded code from importing virtual image files. The standalone adapter used a physical-parent require for compiled host modules, so even Doctor and bundled-plugin preflight crossed that boundary. Mapped host entries now use image-bound require, and the existing export-object handoff covers emitted ESM and CommonJS. The separate AOT loading trampoline is removed; Jiti remains only for source transformation.

The export hook registers once, when the first external mapping needs it. Compiled host loads leave it inactive. The native capture owner preserves URL suffixes while selecting physical source files. The builder writes compact metadata JSON, avoiding a large formatting allocation without changing the parsed data.

## Evidence

- Accepted AOT compiler limitation: the query/fragment gate fails before and after on the carried and stock-main compilers; the rewrite baseline is blocked earlier at host loading and its final query gate also fails. An independent no-OpenClaw repro demonstrates the compiler defect. These remain failed tests, with no passing AOT case regressed; pinned JIT improves to pass.
- Stock-main HTTP parsing fails identically before and after (the same TypeError/HTTPParserError and eight errors in each ordinary synthetic run). Scalar diagnostics are labelled separately; no product workaround is included.
- Real signed baseline stacks identify compiled WebSocket, temporary-directory, and bundled-plugin helpers using physical-parent require. No fetched plugin was needed to trigger the Doctor/Gateway failures.
- All 43 focused standalone loader/native/resolution tests pass, including the regression for deferred registration. The ordinary PluginInstance suites pass 104 tests on pinned Bun and 103 on Node with one Bun-only skip. Scoped lint, tooling types, formatting, and test-line budgets pass. The final normal build passes. Independent full-branch Codex review is clean through P2.
- Final Developer-ID-signed application builds use the documented hardened recipe without allow-jit for AOT. Refreshed upstream rewrite and the carried compiler pass version, Doctor, readiness, authenticated health, synthetic turn, fetched Teams install/load, CJS/ESM/published and local TypeScript, all 34 runtime API assertions, same-executable npm child/re-entry, real Codex activation/turn, and the real PDF Worker flow. Twelve signed compiler disk-permission probes pass; these are small boundary fixtures, not twelve desktop builds. Pinned JIT passes its seven-gate application run and all four distinct query forms. Its PDF/permission probes were not run.
- Exact-owner ESM-first/CJS-first signed fixtures pass on the carried compiler, both upstream pipelines, and pinned JIT, with compiled source files absent. Plugins share state, functions, defaults, and runtime-only exports; evaluation remains once-only. The physical-parent control retains the intended upstream guard refusal. All owned processes stop.
- Matched final combined-candidate measurements retain all ten cold and ten warm pairs. Pinned JIT readiness improves 3.612 → 3.492 s cold and 3.786 → 3.624 s warm; CLI turns improve 1.790 → 1.720 s and 1.175 → 1.140 s. Gateway CPU improves 6.5%/5.4% and instructions 10.8%/10.8%; every paired CPU/instruction/cycle delta is negative. These measurements include the related metadata-lookup fix and do not isolate this PR's cost. A separate same-executable experiment found that registering an unused onLoad hook increased instructions 9.81% with zero callbacks, motivating the lazy registration.
- All four final desktop builds pass. The prior metadata failure occurred while pretty-printing a 1.12 GB metafile; compact serialization removes 400,629,914 bytes of formatting. Output count was unchanged, and final build input audits match except the expected bootstrap change.

Two upstream limitations remain failed, rather than being counted as passes. Upstream main produces the same HTTPParserError before and after (eight errors each); an explicitly labelled UNDICI_NO_WASM_SIMD=1 diagnostic on the same image reaches and passes the later gates and PDF Worker. No SIMD workaround is included. All tested AOT compilers also retain independently reproduced query/fragment instance failures: upstream pipelines collapse instances and the carried compiler cannot resolve the four forms. No passing AOT case regressed; ordinary pinned JIT now passes all four forms. The resolver returns intact suffixes before the runtime loses them. No compiler-specific branch or URL-semantics workaround is included.

prs.title: fix: honor Windows PATH order when selecting command installations
prs.body:
Closes #193806

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows command discovery selecting a stale installation later on PATH instead of the executable in the first matching directory. This affects Gmail setup (`gcloud`, `gog`) and Tailscale discovery.

## User Impact

The installation selected by PATH order is used. Existing CMD-wrapper preference within the same directory remains unchanged. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing executable-extension preference within the first matching PATH directory rather than across all directories.

## Evidence

- Native Windows 11 / Node 24.22.1, real `runCommandWithTimeout`: first PATH directory contains a real Node executable renamed `gcloud.exe`; a later directory contains a marker `gcloud.cmd`. Before: direct command returns `v24.22.1`, but resolved command runs the later marker. After: both return `v24.22.1`. No process-wide persistent environment edits.
- Filesystem regression fails on base (1 failed / 26 passed / 10 existing skips), passes with fix (27 passed / 10 existing skips; 5.28s Vitest, 10.17s wrapper). Existing same-directory preference tests remain green.
- Scoped formatter, lint (zero warnings/errors), infra-test leaf typecheck, `git diff --check` pass. Native runtime build (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/tsdown-build.mts`) passes all four invocations. Full package/declaration and hosted CI results are not claimed here.
- 16 regression lines are allocated separately: this regression independently proves directory precedence using real filesystem entries. CI seconds are pending hosted execution.
- Independent local autoreview of the complete two-file local change against `ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d`, P0–P3: scoped-clean, no actionable findings, patch correct (0.97). Reviewer consumed diff and supplied native evidence in an empty sandbox; it did not independently execute tests. The subsequently added allocation record is exactly `16`, matching the measured regression growth.

### Inspectable native Gmail-path terminal capture

Fresh processes on native Windows execute the shipped `src/hooks/gmail-setup-utils.ts` exported `runGcloud(["--version"])`, which invokes its real `runGcloudCommand` → shared resolver → real process runner. Baseline owner is unchanged from `ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d`; after is PR head `f53b7f8d18d452a1a08969b61da95d375419489c`. No mocks or authenticated Google calls: the fixtures substitute a real Node executable and a marker CMD wrapper for the two installations. This is the real Gmail helper execution boundary, not an authenticated Gmail CLI setup walkthrough. Temp paths are redacted as `<fixture>`; process-local environment is restored and fixtures removed.

```text
BEFORE platform=win32 node=v24.22.1
PATH=<fixture>/first;<fixture>/later
first/gcloud.exe=real Node executable; later/gcloud.cmd=synthetic marker
resolveExecutable(gcloud)=<fixture>\later\gcloud.cmd
production Gmail runGcloud([--version]) exit=0 stdout="stale-lower-priority-install"
AFTER platform=win32 node=v24.22.1
PATH=<fixture>/first;<fixture>/later
first/gcloud.exe=real Node executable; later/gcloud.cmd=synthetic marker
resolveExecutable(gcloud)=<fixture>\first\gcloud.exe
production Gmail runGcloud([--version]) exit=0 stdout="v24.22.1"
```

Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42136023809 — completed success at the unchanged PR head. Supported watcher exited GREEN; superseded draft-era statuses are not treated as current failures.

prs.title: perf(ui): reduce medium transcript fragment work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After #183800, completed 400-message conversations repeatedly create and dispose small transcript fragments while scrolling. This spends more CPU than the pre-windowing renderer. This change removes some of that work while preserving the 2,000-message window and bounded retention. It follows the WebKit observer repair in #193646.

For 257–512 source messages, completed fragments hold two messages, and idle preparation warms Markdown data rather than mounting unseen DOM. Moving-reader preparation remains paced; visited rows retain their existing keyed DOM. The medium row budgets are halved to preserve the content bound. Larger histories keep the existing one-message policy. Text-only bubbles no longer construct empty image galleries, and committed row sizes are recorded without an unused CSS intrinsic-size write.

## Evidence

Published source: `cebe545f05f` (production identical to measured `c92efa5810f`); merge base: `ee00ba6be09`. Same-machine frozen production builds, headless Chromium and WebKit, synthetic Gateway data. Each timing cell uses 20 serial base/base/head triplets. Chromium uses untraced renderer-thread CPU; WebKit reports application elapsed time, not CPU. All samples are retained, with host load and A/A controls.

Acceptance: less affected CPU or blocking without an attributable user-facing regression, no new endpoint/errors/paint regression, and preserved bounded long-session retention. The original 70% medium-session CPU regression is only partly recovered; this PR does not claim to eliminate it.

| Workload, median / p95 | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chromium 1× upward Task CPU | 884.13 / 918.87 ms | 878.19 / 890.69 ms | −0.7% / −3.1% |
| Chromium 1× downward Task CPU | 940.59 / 971.44 ms | 944.50 / 980.11 ms | +0.4% / +0.9% |
| Chromium 1× upward Script CPU | 400.11 / 417.15 ms | 358.35 / 369.44 ms | −10.4% / −11.4% |
| Chromium 1× downward Script CPU | 366.04 / 383.00 ms | 343.66 / 365.97 ms | −6.1% / −4.4% |
| Chromium 4× upward Task CPU | 4,307.95 / 5,050.38 ms | 4,098.28 / 4,664.24 ms | −4.9% / −7.6% |
| Chromium 4× downward Task CPU | 4,480.42 / 5,467.92 ms | 4,335.26 / 5,251.49 ms | −3.2% / −4.0% |
| Chromium 4× upward native blocking | 328 / 1,012.85 ms | 177.5 / 553.65 ms | −45.9% / −45.3% |
| Chromium 4× downward longest task | 110.5 / 135.4 ms | 82.5 / 128.25 ms | −25.3% / −5.3% |
| WebKit two-direction application elapsed | 2,202 / 2,219.65 ms | 2,142.5 / 2,159.3 ms | −2.7% / −2.7% |

Chromium frame-tail p95 holds: 1× up16.8/down33.3 ms; 4× up107.50→102.58/down116.65→116.75 ms (the latter +0.09%). All head endpoints are exact, with zero geometric whole-viewport blank samples. At 1× there are no scroll tasks over50 ms. At 4× the largest head task is179 ms versus254 ms base/215 ms A/A. WebKit passes60/60 observations, including40 head directional scrolls, with zero native/page errors.

The 4× A/A Task medians/p95 are4,348.72/4,818.41 ms upward and4,607.28/5,211.18 ms downward. Upward layout CPU rises8.8% median; downward style rises3.9%. Total Task and blocking improve. At 1× total CPU is flat despite less script work; downward style rises6.4%. These subphase costs remain disclosed.

A separate filmstrip diagnostic preserves the base's poor upward paint under programmatic jumps: empty captured frames246/268 base and234/255 head. Downward empty frames improve14/167→7/169. Full frames were inspected. Geometric coverage is not compositor paint proof, and this does not claim blank-free scrolling.

The 2,000-message direct and mixed replays each complete three full traversals in base/base/head slots. All36 directional endpoints are exact. Direct final retained elements are442 in all slots; heap69.804/69.899/69.896 MiB. Mixed final elements are463 in all slots; heap84.884/86.390/86.323 MiB. The mixed A/A and head have matching warm conditioning; all three figures are disclosed. Mixed detached counts remain1,062 for all three head cycles, and streaming/search/clear/switch assertions pass.

A head-only direct extension completes eight traversals. Detached counts settle from1,579 on the first cycle to1,221–1,267 in cycles3–8, ending at1,221. Rows remain13 and elements433–442; final heap70.403 MiB. This is bounded observed retention, not an assertion that every detached native node has the same retainer. Existing retained-row and prepared-fragment bounds remain in place.

Production Knip, controller guard, test-line ratchet, formatting, and focused lint pass. Full CI is requested on the pushed head.

| Compressed surface | Base | Head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JavaScript | 90,568 B | 90,574 B |
| Chat JavaScript | 1,295,237 B | 1,295,220 B |
| New Session JavaScript | 801,463 B | 801,215 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 |

These are same-machine macOS measurements. Linux CI on run42133795657 measures Chat1,294,550→1,294,857 B (+307 B), startup90,584→90,589 B, and identical CSS. The Chat delta comes chiefly from the preparation scheduler (initial-range module +740 raw B), with chunk-name/compression differences across builds. Under the campaign's explicit measured-CPU-win allowance, set the Chat cap to1,294,857+192 B existing headroom=1,295,049 B. This accompanies6–10% less scroll Script CPU and about46% less4× upward blocking. No CSS, startup baseline, dependency, or ignore is raised. The checker's `--update-baseline` updates startup only; this is the explicit Chat surface cap, using the measured value plus its existing headroom.

UI typecheck and103 focused tests pass. The tests cover ordered fragment/message coverage, final-answer identity, medium/large boundaries, idle preparation versus retained DOM, and fractional committed geometry. Independent P0–P2 reviews found no unresolved actionable issues. Production changes add26 lines across six UI files (2,610→2,636); touched tests add13 (2,795→2,808). No new effect, subscription, DOM query, owner API, cache, or scheduler.

## Screenshots

Synthetic fixtures only; current same-machine base and head endpoints, inspected before upload. Paired fragments have a small inter-message spacing difference.

| Base | Head |
| --- | --- |
| ![Base completed transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0ae8550-d2bc-4420-9e96-1f503778ce4d) | ![Head completed transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41c5373d-0d48-449a-9698-ec39021bcd98) |

## Reproduce

Build the pinned base and head with `pnpm ui:build` and freeze each emitted directory. Set `BASE_BUNDLE` and `HEAD_BUNDLE` to those directories. Chromium timing command (repeat with throttle4):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --bundle-dir "$BASE_BUNDLE" --compare-bundle-dir "$BASE_BUNDLE" \
  --compare-bundle-dir "$HEAD_BUNDLE" --runs 60 --gateway-http --first-load \
  --latency-ms 0 --frame-gap-ms 0 --boot-route chat --face chat \
  --transcript-messages 400 --long-session --long-session-scenario direct-run \
  --skip-long-session-heap-snapshots --cpu-throttle 1 --untraced --thread-cpu-time
```

WebKit uses `bench-control-ui-engines.ts`, `--steps completed-direct-run-400-scroll --engines webkit --viewport desktop --pairs 20`, base/head/control-base bundles. Memory uses the cold-load command with2,000 messages, three slots, `--long-session-scroll-cycles 3`, and heap snapshots enabled; repeat for `mixed` with `--streaming-reply --streaming-content markdown`. The direct head-only extension uses eight cycles. All capture commands set `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`.

Source review counts across the six production files remain unchanged: 1 effect, 1 untrack, 1 runWithOwner, 1 onSettled, 16 memos and 1 signal; no direct queries/listeners or new ownership APIs. The existing lifecycle sites retain their prior responsibilities.


## Exact-head CI repair and switch follow-up

The previous full-CI head failed only the busy-refusal session-placement E2E. Its immediate cloud-option absence check predates role-granted profile dispatch (fd0403b40c9). The local-session fixture legitimately exposes cloud profiles with operator.write; timing of catalog completion determined whether the stale assertion passed. Removed only that assertion, retaining visible busy refusal, one dispatch, and no abort/replay. The whole placement-menu file passes locally (5/5); independent P0–P2 review is clean. Production remains byte-identical to c92. This is a repaired PR-owned failure, not an inherited exemption. New-head full CI is requested; auto-merge remains off after native cancellation until completed-head recovery.

A follow-up 6× Chromium matrix completes 20 rotating triplets for desktop and mobile (120/120 passing). Desktop application median/p95 is 1,138.75/1,237.46 ms base, 1,091.65/1,158.66 A/A, and 1,087.05/1,201.97 head. Mobile is 1,883.30/1,976.78 ms base, 1,867.35/1,970.77 A/A, and 1,864.80/1,958.94 head. Head is effectively flat against A/A; this is not evidence that the original Census6 switch regression has been recovered. No new functional errors occurred.

The ordinary-opening follow-up also passes all120 observations. Chromium ready median/p95:501.05/542.72→494.20/518.66 ms (A/A498.55/516.09); WebKit693.50/717.55→695.00/720.05 ms (A/A687.00/743.75). The head's median WebKit/Chromium ratio is1.406 versus1.384 base; target1.3 remains unmet. This ordinary2,000-message fixture is separate from the giant completed-run case.


The next exact-head CI repair corrects the test-line allocation12→11 after the stale assertion removal and accepts only the measured307 B Linux Chat increase above. prs.title: fix(agents): preserve trusted daily quota assertions through failover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preserve trusted producer assertions for model-scoped daily quota exhaustion across streamed error projection, retry classification, and fallback normalization.

### Motivating scenario: Provider Cedar

“Provider Cedar” is an anonymized label for the motivating provider scenario, not a new public provider identifier. A producer can distinguish an explicit model-scoped daily limit from transient throttling, but core can lose that distinction while projecting streamed errors or normalizing nested failures. Treating the resulting error as transient can retry the same exhausted model without a useful recovery path.

The regression fixtures model this boundary with synthetic provider/model identities: a trusted producer emits numeric HTTP 429, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and a typed daily-model assertion. The assertion must survive unrelated or truncated diagnostics; conflicting enclosing status/code aliases or request identities must reject it. This is synthetic regression evidence, not a claim of a live upstream daily-limit reproduction.

- Require coherent numeric 429 and RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED facts on the asserting record; reject contradictory transport aliases and provider/model identities across wrappers.
- Capture the accepted assertion before diagnostic clipping or redaction. Diagnostic JSON cannot establish, erase, or resurrect the typed assertion.
- Suppress same-model transient retries only for the coherent typed daily-model assertion. Generic throttling remains unchanged.
- Preserve configured fallback precedence, explicit disablement, and selection locks. Optional same-provider configured-default metadata remains switch-only groundwork.

## Scope

No automatic fallback, resume action, prompt resend, dispatch journal, storage migration, or UI switch implementation is included. Producers own verification of upstream quota dimensions; core checks assertion coherence rather than independently verifying provider limits. Body-only adapters must publish the typed assertion after validating their original facts.

This is independent of other UI work and contains one quota-only commit on an official-main ancestor.

## Evidence

- 131 focused tests passed with the Node test runtime, including projection-to-retry regressions, coherent wrappers, enclosing conflicts, clipped diagnostics, and completed-work replay vetoes.
- Core typecheck, type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and diff checks passed.
- These results cover the byte-identical quota files in the source checkout; the isolated publication branch excludes an unrelated UI-only commit.
- No live quota-exhaustion reproduction or full build is claimed. Broad build/test CI is skipped while this PR is draft; the PR context-and-evidence check passed before this description update.
- The source checkout test-line ratchet reports an inherited one-line overage. The allocation grants exactly 528 added regression-test lines without changing the shared baseline.

## Simplification

Removed diagnostic-body quota inference and reused one coherence validator for streamed and thrown errors. No persistence or lifecycle framework is added. Regression tests protect distinct producer, lossy-projection, classification, and fallback-owner boundaries.

## What Problem This Solves

After a failed chat on an explicitly selected alternate model, switching back to an available same-provider configured default requires finding it in the model picker.

## User Impact

Control UI offers **Switch to configured default** for eligible failed chats. The action changes the model for the next message; it does not retry the failed message, resend the original prompt, or alter completed tool work. Existing confirmation preferences still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action uses the existing selection and session-patch owners, preserves pinned runtime/auth choices, and rejects stale selections, sessions, failures, connections, agent inventories, locks, permissions, or unavailable targets. It only offers catalog-confirmed available models on the exact same provider.

Configured fallback chains remain authoritative. This does not supplement an existing or exhausted chain, implement automatic fallback/continuation, or infer daily quota exhaustion from a generic rate limit.

## Evidence

- 93 tests passed across the recovery action, composer notices, native-runtime restriction recovery, and composer/session-controls suites (11.96 seconds wall time for the final run).

Fixes: the Gateway event loop blocks after every model call when `diagnostics.otel.captureContent` is on and the session's prompts are large.

## User Impact

User impact: with content capture on, every channel on the Gateway stops answering while one large session runs, and the stall grows with the prompt, not with the 128 KiB that is exported. #158116 measured ~150 s blocks per call on a live Gateway. With the 1M-token window below, main reaches 1.2 s `/readyz` latency at 2.1M characters of prompt; this PR stays under 130 ms.

## Why This Change Was Made

`safeJsonString` redacted the whole serialized value only to learn it was over the 128 KiB budget, then retried up to 7 x 9 truncation budgets, redacting every string in full each time. That ran for `gen_ai.input.messages`, `input.value`, `openclaw.content.input_messages`, the output pairs and the tool definitions, on the event loop.

This PR:
- picks the truncation budget from unredacted sizes and redacts only the candidate it exports;
- redacts a clipped string through a window that runs past the cut (4,096 characters, or the longest registered secret if longer), so a secret that starts in the exported prefix is still masked;
- masks a secret the window leaves open (private key without its END line, JWT without its signature, URL password before its `@`, open quoted value) from where it starts, using `findTruncatedSecret` in core;
- keeps whole-value redaction when `logging.redactPatterns` is set, since a configured rule can need any amount of text;
- serializes and redacts each mirrored pair (`gen_ai.input.messages` / `input.value`, the output pair) once.

Core keeps secret matching and the registered-value registry; the plugin keeps the budgets. Three functions are added to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core`: `findTruncatedSecret()`, `getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` and `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()`.

## Evidence

Head `ee8f1612a06` = previous head `e84c7301e2da` + merge of main `2e24ab71b147` + the test-line allocation. The 17 code and test files are byte-identical to `e84c7301e2da`; the merge only touched `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md` and the SDK budget lines (main's 3,859 / 2,232 plus these 3).

**Gateway, main vs this PR.** A real Gateway started through qa-lab with the mock OpenAI provider, `diagnostics-otel` traces and logs, `captureContent: true`, model `contextWindow` 1,000,000 and a local OTLP receiver. 40 turns, each reading a 300,414-character file of log lines with fresh bearer JWTs, a GitLab token and a 5,134-character Atlassian token, while `/readyz` is probed every 100 ms. Same harness, same host, run back to back:

| | main `2e24ab71b147` | this PR `ee8f1612a06` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prompt at turn 40 | 2,095,827 chars | 2,095,643 chars |
| `/readyz` max | 1,226 ms | 126 ms |
| `/readyz` probes > 250 ms / > 1 s | 49 / 7 of 174 | 0 / 0 of 181 |
| Reply time, turn 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 | 586 / 1,024 / 1,797 / 2,373 ms | 420 / 425 / 409 / 440 ms |
| Gateway CPU for the 40 turns | 57.5 s | 24.3 s |
| Gateway `main-thread stall` warnings | 8, max 1,240 ms | 0 |
| Model-call spans / provider requests | 81 / 81 | 81 / 81 |
| OTLP requests not 200 | 0 of 55 | 0 of 22 |
| Largest content attribute | 131,049 chars | 129,287 chars |
| Leak needles in any accepted OTLP body (of 10) | 0 | 0 |

The secrets were in every turn's model input on both trees, and a plain marker reached the export on both. With the default context window, compaction keeps the same session under 315K characters and main's `/readyz` max is 108 ms, which is why the comparison sets 1M. Not covered: image payloads, a real collector, a real channel, Linux; one run per tree on a busy host.

**Fail without the fix.** With main's `service-content-normalization.ts` restored and everything else at this head, the two diagnostics-otel test files give 10 failed, 101 passed: both redaction-work bounds, the URL-password and database-URL cut cases, and `redacts line-start assignments in content that fits without truncation`, where main's normalizer exports the planted secret unmasked (JSON escaping turns the line break into `\n`, which hides a line-start assignment from the text rules). At this head the six changed test files pass 148 of 148; `src/logging` plus `extensions/diagnostics-otel` pass 1,027 with 4 skipped.

**Checks.** `pnpm tsgo:all` passes. `plugin-sdk:surface:check` measures 3,862 / 2,235 public exports against those budgets, and fails with each budget lowered by one. oxlint, oxfmt, and the line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-dialect, timeout-race and mock-export ratchets pass against `2e24ab71b147`.

**Test-line ratchet.** This PR adds 977 test lines and allocates exactly 977 (normalization 772, open-secret 66, registered-secret consumer 63, emitted-body capture 36, registry 31, logging config 9). Main `f5f27c3ef6e` is 10 lines over its own ceiling (6,421,662 vs 6,421,652), and the script fails any change that adds lines while the tree is over, so `test-lines` here fails by exactly those 10 (`over by: 10; net delta: +977`). An allocation of 987 is rejected (`credit 987 exceeds added test lines 977`). It clears when main is back under its ceiling.

CI on `ee8f1612a06`: running at the time of this edit. Expect `test-lines` red by main's 10 lines (above); every other job is judged on its own.

**Simplification pass.** I ran the repo's pr-simplify pass over the whole diff and removed nothing: the log and JSON export paths share one bounded-redaction function, each core fact sits with its existing owner, and every test group fails for a distinct reason (the control above shows the work-bound and boundary groups failing on main). Against `2e24ab71b147`: production TypeScript +426 code / +125 comment lines, -51, in 12 files; tests net +977 in 6 files. One alternative is in the decisions below.

## Decisions this needs from a maintainer

1. Capture completeness: accept that some large values export a truncated prefix or the `max_redaction_work` summary where main (slowly) exported more, as listed under limits below.
2. SDK surface: accept `findTruncatedSecret()`, `getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` and `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core`. The alternative is one core operation that redacts a prefix safely and owns all four concerns; I can switch to that if you prefer it, at the cost of redoing this qualification.
3. Security review of this head: `src/logging/*redact*.ts` and `*secret*.ts` are in the redaction category of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`.

## Capture and security limits

- Whole-value handling covers JSON up to 4x the attribute budget, and eligible open-secret cases within the 8x redaction-work budget. Larger values can be truncated even when their masked form would fit.
- The bounded retry can export less text while any registered value exists. A longer registered value widens every window and leaves fewer items under the work cap; a window larger than the cap exports the `max_redaction_work` summary.
- Configured `logging.redactPatterns` keep whole-value work and can still block on very large captures. The shared configured-pattern path processes long strings in 16,384-character chunks without overlap, a pre-existing limit.
- Identifier prefixes in `SG.` keys, Slack webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens and `FlyV1 fm<digits>_` would need to exceed the lookahead before their secret part; not covered. A JWT header longer than the lookahead can export header parameters up to the cut.
- URL handling is conservative: a database port/path or web URL port that runs to the window end without `/`, whitespace or `@` can be dropped where main keeps it.
- The new SDK helpers return positions, lengths or configuration presence, never registered values.

prs.title: fix(browser): Chrome extension reports "Not installed" when macOS blocks profile reads
prs.body:
Closes #172272

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes OpenClaw reporting an installed, connected Chrome extension as "Not installed / manual setup required" when macOS privacy protection blocks reading Chrome's profile files.

## User Impact

User impact: when Chrome profile files are unreadable, status reports unknown install state instead of "extension missing", and that unknown fact now survives a successful connection check, so the Mac app's Chrome setup card never flips to "Not installed" while the extension shows connected. `openclaw browser extension status` prints the discovery warnings its summary references (including the Full Disk Access remedy), and `setup` steers to the live relay check instead of Store reinstall guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile discovery conflated "cannot read Chrome's profile files" with "extension not installed". Blocked reads now surface as `discoveryBlocked` on status and, as an installation-level fact, inside the setup `installation` projection (CLI JSON, the macOS Swift bridge, and the dashboard card), because the connection reason replaces the inspect reason during verify and previously erased the uncertainty. The CLI status command now prints issue lines before the summary. Review follow-ups from @clawsweeper are addressed: the blocked fact is independent of the connection reason (`installation.discoveryBlocked`, covered by the inspect→verify transition in the new e2e), and human-readable status prints the warnings it references.

## Evidence

Real-machine repro (macOS 27.0.1, OpenClaw 2026.10.3, TCC-blocked Chrome profile, extension connected — the exact contradiction from #172272):

```text
BEFORE (released openclaw 2026.10.3):
  setup --action inspect:
    {"phase":"needs_browser_action","reason":"extension_missing","nextAction":"install_from_store","nativeHostRegistered":true,"installedProfiles":0}

AFTER (this branch, built from source, same machine, same block):
  setup --action verify  (unknown install state survives a connected verify):
    {"phase":"ready","reason":"connected","connection":{"state":"connected","extensionVersion":"2.3.0"},
     "installation":{"installedProfiles":0,"discoveredProfiles":0,"discoveryBlocked":true}}
```

`extension status` on the same machine now starts with the previously hidden warning:

```text
Google Chrome: could not list profiles (Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, scandir '.../Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome'); on macOS, grant Full Disk Access to the app running OpenClaw, then check again
```

After-fix CLI behavior in a clean hermetic environment (owned native-host registration, profile directory made unreadable → same EACCES blocked-read path):

```text
status (human-readable; warnings now printed above the summary):
  Google Chrome profile Default (Preferences): EACCES: permission denied, lstat '.../Chrome/Default/Preferences'
  ...
  Setup:          unknown (Chrome profile files unreadable for Google Chrome; check the warnings above)

setup --action inspect:
  {"phase":"waiting_for_connection","reason":"profile_inspection_blocked","nextAction":"check_connection",
   "installation":{"nativeHostRegistered":true,"installedProfiles":0,"discoveredProfiles":0,"discoveryBlocked":true}}

setup --action verify (relay not running here; no false extension_missing, fact preserved):
  {"phase":"waiting_for_connection","reason":"relay_unavailable","nextAction":"check_connection",
   "connection":{"state":"unavailable"},"installation":{"discoveryBlocked":true,...}}
```

Desktop card before/after — the dashboard row driven through the macOS native bridge reply contract (the same `chrome-extension-setup` reply shape the Mac app posts back), captured via headless Control UI e2e:

- Before (base `ff22ecbe` build): after inspect, the card renders **Not installed**; after a connected verify it renders **Not installed** alongside **Extension connected on this device** — the reviewer's exact P2. Captured card text: `...Not installedExtension connected on this device....`
- After (this PR): inspect renders **Status unavailable** + the Full Disk Access hint; after a connected verify the card keeps **Status unavailable** and the hint alongside **Extension connected on this device**.

Four screenshots below: **before** (base `ff22ecbe` build — the reviewer's exact P2) and **after** (this PR):

Before — inspect says "Not installed", and a connected verify keeps saying it:

![Before fix: blocked inspect renders Not installed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4db56ba5-974b-4d32-9acb-69b7d24dae26)

![Before fix: Not installed alongside Extension connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b06ab479-ad38-4d4b-ad94-b845784dd75d)

After — "Status unavailable" with the Full Disk Access hint, preserved through a connected verify:

![After fix: Status unavailable with Full Disk Access hint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a1601b6-48d3-4abc-8c00-b0e42a2eecc1)

![After fix: unknown survives connected verify](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7ae34e5-6c12-4d9a-9638-ba3939015759)

Regression run for the transition (failing base / passing head):

- Added `ui/src/e2e/chrome-extension-status.e2e.test.ts` → "keeps unknown install state through blocked inspect and a connected verify".
- Base UI build: `FAIL ... expected 'Chrome extensionSet up Chrome on this…' to contain 'Status unavailable'`.
- This head: `✓ keeps unknown install state through blocked inspect and a connected verify 743ms` (`vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`).

Suites on `1e2ad88e`:

- `vitest.extension-browser.config.ts`: 82 passed (incl. blocked status/inspect/verify, survives-verify, CLI warnings test).
- `vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` Chrome setup file: passed; UI unit suites touching the card (`chrome-setup`, `native-device-settings`, `device-pages`): passed.
- `tsgo` extensions, ui, core-test ui-e2e projects: clean. `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, docs format, line-cap + assertion-safety ratchets: clean. Full `pnpm build`: clean.
- The Swift bridge change cannot be covered by CI on fork PRs (`macos-swift` skips); it is verified with a local `swift test --filter ChromeExtensionSetupTests` run, and the result will be posted as a follow-up comment on this PR.

Known-unrelated CI flake observed on the previous head: one UI shard (`chat-transcript-end-follow`, then `canvas-widget-view`) — neither file is touched by this PR.
