prs.title: fix(ios): keep New session options reachable at accessibility sizes
prs.body:
Related: #193485

**Ready for maintainer review.** The validation gates below remain open; this status is not a claim of merge readiness.

## Contributor credit

Reported by @ellibbe in #193485. This work was requested by @PollyBot13, the linked human identity credited by the managed publication workflow.

## Work sessions

- [Original overview](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f02d78e0-e9b3-491b-9ed2-34702cfc3ce7)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6ad84dd9-6e11-4ed6-8635-14efe368e0b5)

## What Problem This Solves

At maximum accessibility text sizes, iOS Chat actions → New session options clips its heading, explanation and controls in a fixed medium-height presentation.

## User Impact

The change gives the iOS form vertical scrolling, uses a large sheet at accessibility sizes, and allows the Separate working copy label to wrap without reducing the selected font size. This PR is open for maintainer review. The basic OFF/no-keyboard matrix and the specifically tested normal-onboarding real-Gateway Cancel/OFF/ON and visible-keyboard cases are covered below. Full-suite, macOS app UI and broader qualification are not claimed complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iOS presentation owns its scroll container and adaptive detents; the shared form retains its macOS popover and existing creation/worktree logic. The shared toggle label can expand vertically. The temporary handoff checklist is removed and its remaining verification requirements are folded into this body.

The source is PollyBot13/openclaw at `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4` (two commits atop `9f07ae4789dc727d992b61208ed06601633cb013`). The published integration preserves the three changed Swift files byte-for-byte and was applied directly atop old PR head `a159d658ca19a54658839cce9ad83bff13471aed`, without importing unrelated main changes. Contributor credit is retained.

### Reporter acknowledgement

**Thank you, @ellibbe**, for the [independent native red/green, default-size control, standard Watch-retaining builds and normal-onboarding ON/base-field Cancel trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193600#issuecomment-6668182174). Your results are credited below and complement Engineering's proof.

The implementation is already included in this PR. **@PollyBot13 and Engineering own remaining verification and coordination.** Their isolated real-Gateway/disposable-workspace lane has now supplied the scoped effects and keyboard proof below. No additional proof is being requested from the reporter.

## Evidence

### Native layout evidence (inspected)

[Sanitized evidence and capture metadata](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/e4bcddd26ceb0723c4c42ea8e00e491d654a2d8f/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md) are hosted on a separate evidence-only commit, not in this product-code branch.

The inspected stills compare the same iPhone 17 Simulator / iOS 27.2 at accessibility XXXL, Separate working copy OFF and keyboard hidden. The fixture agent has `workspaceGit=false`, so its working-copy toggle is disabled. Before shows the missing heading, truncated toggle label and clipped bottom actions; After shows the full title, explanation, wrapping label and both actions inside the large sheet.

**Before — production files at main `9f07ae4789dc727d992b61208ed06601633cb013`**

![Before: medium sheet at accessibility XXXL; heading is not visible, Separate working copy truncates, and bottom actions are clipped.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/e4bcddd26ceb0723c4c42ea8e00e491d654a2d8f/docs/pr-evidence/193600/main-iphone17-xxxl.png)

**After — captured layout commit `eef431bac6f8442085edcfc82c7a45dd8079bda2`**

![After: large sheet at the same text size shows New Thread, its explanation, the full toggle label, Cancel and Create Thread.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/e4bcddd26ceb0723c4c42ea8e00e491d654a2d8f/docs/pr-evidence/193600/candidate-iphone17-xxxl.png)

These are historical capture revisions, not a new run of the published head. Later source `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4` removes the test-only production accessibility identifier and revises the regression while retaining the layout. Its three Swift blobs are identical to the published integration. Do not describe the earlier and later entire files as byte-identical.

Local Engineering reports that a manual Cancel tap dismissed the candidate sheet; the still does not depict that action or prove no thread/worktree was created. Neither image establishes Create Thread effects, working-copy ON, keyboard-visible behavior, other viewports, or an XCTest pass.

**The focused exact-source automated green is now accepted.** Engineering rebuilt the test target from task tip `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4` with Xcode 27.2 and ran `AdaptiveLayoutUITests.testNewSessionOptionsRemainReachableAtAccessibilitySize` on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.2 / accessibility XXXL at **20:50 CET on November 5, 2026**: **1/1 passed in 13.19 seconds**. Both affected production Swift files and the UI test file are byte-identical to live PR head `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369`. [Durable focused XCTest proof and provenance](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/3e8bb81bbb0f454df04ac1d7d3f7a8b74d8f7530/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md).

The focused run verifies title/Cancel/Create Thread containment in the window, Cancel hittability, and dismissal after tapping Cancel. Its fixture is OFF/no keyboard; it does not exercise Create Thread or real Gateway/worktree effects. Public provenance and the screenshot were inspected and source equivalence was verified here; the Xcode execution was by Engineering, not rerun in this Team session.

Earlier iOS 26.5/27.2 automation-session stalls are historical attempts, not a current blanket inability to reach the form. An earlier `test-without-building` pass reused an older runner and is **excluded from exact-source proof**. The accepted result is the later rebuilt run only. Paired with the fresh original-main failure at 21:05 CET documented below, this now supplies a **matching focused automated red/green** for the iPhone 17 XXXL OFF/no-keyboard fixture scenario. It does not establish full-suite validation, real Gateway effects, or the complete viewport/ON/keyboard matrix. [Combined red/green and SE3 provenance](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/2272ed906dc3123753043a8b99cf59fe719cdf47/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md).

### Matching focused baseline-red and smaller-iPhone proof

[Durable red/green and SE3 evidence](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/2272ed906dc3123753043a8b99cf59fe719cdf47/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md) records these additional Engineering runs on November 5, 2026:

- **iPhone 17 baseline red, 21:05 CET:** Engineering freshly rebuilt with only the two production Swift files restored to original-main `9f07ae4789dc727d992b61208ed06601633cb013`, retaining the same focused UI test, device, iOS 27.2, accessibility XXXL and Xcode 27.2 setup. The test **failed 1/1 on original behavior**: `New Thread title is not visible` at test line 48. The title was not hittable; Cancel began at `y=840.1` with height `44.2`, extending below the `874`-point window. This is a behavioral baseline failure, not a missing scroll-view identifier or a runner stall.
- The matching candidate green is the rebuilt **20:50 CET 1/1 pass** described above. Engineering reports restoring the candidate test/production files afterward and verifying its local worktree clean. The raw baseline result bundle and uncropped screenshot remain private; the published sanitized provenance records the failure. No Team-side Xcode rerun is claimed.
- **iPhone SE (3rd generation) candidate green, 21:11 CET:** the same exact-source focused test on iOS 27.2 / accessibility XXXL **passed 1/1 in 16.57 seconds**. In the `375×667`-point viewport, Cancel/Create Thread initially lay below the visible area (Cancel `y=696.5`, not initially hittable). The test scrolled until both action frames were contained and Cancel was hittable, tapped Cancel, and observed dismissal. This proves focused smaller-viewport **reachability by scrolling**, not that everything fits initially or that Create Thread was activated.
- The [SE3 initial screenshot](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/2272ed906dc3123753043a8b99cf59fe719cdf47/docs/pr-evidence/193600/candidate-xcuitest-se3-xxxl-initial.png) was inspected. It shows the initial title, explanation and toggle with actions below the viewport; it is **not** a post-scroll or dismissal image. The post-scroll assertions and pass are recorded by Engineering's published provenance.
- These earlier Engineering runs alone establish OFF/no-keyboard fixture layout/cancellation, not real Gateway effects, production keyboard, full-suite or macOS UI validation. Additional default-size and independent Watch-retaining build proof is credited below; it is not retroactively attributed to these earlier runs.

### Attributed supplemental proof — Engineering

[Durable Engineering provenance, commands and sanitized images](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/356981c7cc0a7a096c44c0b1c0df1e9dded59914/docs/pr-evidence/193600/README.md) records these runs on task tip `612140c312ec5bb1f8cb8619b587fb67f4b8e9a4`. The two production Swift blobs were independently compared with live head `e767a466cd5691b82b27dec8d58c2ec4fed82369` and match. The native executions below are Engineering reports, not Team-side reruns.

- **SE3/default text, OFF/no keyboard:** fresh Xcode 27.2 test on iPhone SE (3rd generation), iOS 27.2, light appearance, `375×667` points, at **21:33:18 CET**: **1/1 passed in 14.135 seconds**. Only the test-only category was temporarily changed to `UICTContentSizeCategoryL` and an extra pre-Cancel screenshot retained; no production code or fixture data changed. Title and both actions were contained **without scrolling**, and Cancel dismissed. The original test was restored and Engineering reports its worktree clean. The [default-size screenshot](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/356981c7cc0a7a096c44c0b1c0df1e9dded59914/docs/pr-evidence/193600/candidate-se3-default.png) was inspected.
- **Native iOS typography:** rebuilt source-equivalent `OpenClawTypographyTests` **23/23 passed** on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.2 / Xcode 27.2; reported test duration **2.240 seconds**. This and the SE3/default run used the temporary generated **no-Watch project**. These results are not attributed to a standard Watch-retaining project.
- **Focused shared session actions:** macOS-hosted Swift package `ChatViewModelSessionActionTests` **50/50 passed**, with Node 24 on PATH. This is targeted shared-package evidence, not a macOS app/popover UI pass or real-Gateway effect test.

<details>
<summary>Engineering command provenance and full-package failures</summary>

Sanitized command templates from the linked provenance use placeholders for private device IDs, executable paths and result directories; they were not executed by Team:

```sh
xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=<owned-SE3-device>' \
  -derivedDataPath '<private-proof>/DerivedData' \
  -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/AdaptiveLayoutUITests/testNewSessionOptionsRemainReachableAtAccessibilitySize \
  -resultBundlePath '<private-proof>/se3-default-automated.xcresult'

xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=<owned-iPhone17-device>' \
  -derivedDataPath '<private-proof>/DerivedData' \
  -only-testing:OpenClawTests/OpenClawTypographyTests \
  -resultBundlePath '<private-proof>/typography-continuation.xcresult'

PATH="<Node24-bin>:$PATH" swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit \
  --filter ChatViewModelSessionActionTests
```

Earlier full-package execution ran **2,492 tests with three failures**, all at `createdParentSessionKeys() == [nil]`:

- “new trigger starts fresh agent session without admin reset”
- “new trigger keeps selected global agent scope”
- “new trigger prefers explicit session agent over ambient agent”

Engineering's control restoring the changed shared production file to original main reproduced all three. This records baseline attribution, **not a full-suite pass**; raw result bundles remain private.

</details>

### Independent reporter proof — @ellibbe

[ellibbe's native-check comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193600#issuecomment-6668182174) reports independent checks of the current implementation on **iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0 / Xcode 27.2 / Light/English**:

- Production files from parent `a159d658ca19` produce the behavioral red (“New Thread title is not visible”, **10.780 seconds**); current implementation passes containment, Cancel reachability and dismissal (**13.761 seconds**).
- The **default-size control passes in 13.473 seconds** on the same corrected binary. Combined with Engineering's SE3/default result and the existing XXXL cases, this covers the basic two-viewport, default/XXXL OFF/no-keyboard fixture matrix—not all production-flow configurations.
- **Both base and fix pass the standard app build with the Watch companion retained**, SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1, with no lint exception or Watch removal. This closes the PR-level “only a no-Watch build is proven” gap for the reporter's standard-build runs. It does not turn Engineering's narrowed-project tests into standard-project tests, nor prove a full suite, archive/release, macOS UI or Watch runtime behavior.

The reporter's keyboard object existed during editing, but the retained stills **do not visibly show the software keyboard**. prs.title: fix: fal, Qwen and Vydra media requests go to the hosted default host when baseUrl is invalid
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177487

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: fal video, Qwen video and Vydra image, video and speech requests go to the hosted default host with the API key and the prompt when the configured `baseUrl` (or `VYDRA_BASE_URL`) is set but is not a valid URL.

## User Impact

User impact: a mistyped relay, proxy or regional `baseUrl` for fal, Qwen or Vydra now fails before any request with `Invalid <provider> baseUrl: value is not a valid URL`, instead of sending the key and prompt to the hosted service and reporting its auth error. An omitted or blank `baseUrl` still uses the hosted default.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175101 made MiniMax media and Tavily reject a malformed endpoint instead of switching hosts. The base URL code for fal video, Qwen video and Vydra (image, video and speech) still fell back to the hosted default when `URL.parse` failed. Each now throws when a nonempty value does not parse.

Unlike the bare `TypeError` in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175101, the error names the setting, because the CLI's `error.message` carries no provider prefix and would otherwise read only `Invalid URL`. The wording follows the existing ElevenLabs and Deepgram errors and does not echo the value, which may carry userinfo.

Vydra speech now normalizes its URL when it synthesizes, not when it reads its config, so a bad URL fails the request without breaking `isConfigured` or config resolution. The provider docs for fal, Qwen and Vydra say an invalid URL fails.

## Evidence

`6f41a5c239e` merged `upstream/main` `85404c545bf` (2026-11-03); the PR's diff against main was unchanged, and the only conflict was in a test file, where both sides stay. The head `1bbbdadab7f` then shortens the fal and Vydra speech tests with their files' existing helpers and adds a test-line allocation (see Tests); production code is unchanged. The CLI runs below were made at `6f2172ca683` (base `11d0c854192`) and repeated with the same harness at the earlier merge head `2cfbe2d5ed0`, with the same results; the earlier merges are listed in the details below.

The real CLI of each build (`openclaw infer ...`, Node 24, Ubuntu 22.04) ran with an isolated home and state, dummy keys (`FAL_KEY`, `QWEN_API_KEY`, `VYDRA_API_KEY`) and `baseUrl: "https://["` for all three providers, plus `VYDRA_BASE_URL="https://["` for speech. It ran inside a network namespace with no outside route, where `queue.fal.run`, `dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com` and `www.vydra.ai` resolve to a local catch-all HTTPS server. That server logs each request and answers 401. Calls: `infer video generate` with `fal/fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live` and `qwen/wan2.6-t2v`, `infer image generate` with `vydra/grok-imagine`, `infer tts convert --provider vydra`.

Before (base `11d0c854192`), catch-all log:

```text
POST queue.fal.run/fal-ai/minimax/video-01-live  Authorization: Key dummy-fal-key  body: {"prompt":"PROOF-FAL-PROMPT a red ball"}
POST dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/api/v1/services/aigc/video-generation/video-synthesis  Authorization: Bearer dummy-qwen-key  body: {"model":"wan2.6-t2v","input":{"prompt":"PROOF-QWEN-PROMPT a red ball"},"parameters":{"duration":5}}
POST www.vydra.ai/api/v1/models/grok-imagine  Authorization: Bearer dummy-vydra-key  body: {"prompt":"PROOF-VYDRA-PROMPT a red ball","model":"text-to-image"}
POST www.vydra.ai/api/v1/models/elevenlabs/tts  Authorization: Bearer dummy-vydra-key  body: {"text":"PROOF-VYDRA-TTS hello","voice_id":"21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM"}
```

CLI errors: `fal video generation failed (HTTP 401)`, `Qwen video generation failed (HTTP 401)`, `Vydra image generation failed (HTTP 401)`, `TTS conversion failed: vydra: Vydra speech synthesis failed (HTTP 401)`.

After (this PR), same steps. The catch-all log has no request; CLI errors:

```text
Invalid fal baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
Invalid Qwen baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
Invalid Vydra baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
TTS conversion failed: vydra: Invalid Vydra baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
```

Control with this PR and no `baseUrl` (empty config, empty `VYDRA_BASE_URL`): all four calls still reach the hosted default hosts, so the blank-URL default is unchanged and the harness does see requests.

Upgrade from the then-latest stable `v2026.10.5` (run on 2026-10-20): for each scenario one isolated home and state ran `v2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9a1b4`) first, then this PR (`e79a50ed0f3`), without touching the config in between. The relay hosts `fal-relay.example.test`, `dashscope-proxy.example.test` and `vydra-proxy.example.test` resolve to the same catch-all. The endpoints sit in `models.providers.{fal,qwen,vydra}.baseUrl` and `tts.providers.vydra.baseUrl`. Each build ran `config validate`, `config get models.providers --json` and the same four calls.

| Stored endpoints | `v2026.10.5` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid custom (`https://fal-relay.example.test`, `https://dashscope-proxy.example.test`, `https://vydra-proxy.example.test/api/v1`) | 4 requests, each to its configured relay host | The same 4 requests to the same relay hosts and paths |
| Blank (`""`) | 4 requests to the hosted default hosts | The same 4 requests |
| Malformed (`https://[`) | 4 requests to the hosted default hosts, carrying the key and the prompt | No request; each call fails with `Invalid <provider> baseUrl: value is not a valid URL` |

In every scenario both builds print `Config valid`, `config get` returns the stored values unchanged, and the config file's sha256 is the same before and after each build. There is no schema or state change: valid and blank settings keep working after the upgrade. A malformed setting still loads, but its requests now fail with the setting named instead of reaching the hosted service. Fixing or clearing the value restores the request.

Observed result: on the base the key and prompt reach the hosted host for all four calls; with this PR each call fails before any request and names the provider's `baseUrl`.

Tests: one regression per path (fal video, Qwen video, Vydra image, Vydra speech through `VYDRA_BASE_URL`), each asserting the named error and that no request was sent; the speech case also asserts `isConfiguredAsync` stays `true`. A before/after run of these files (base `85404c545bf`, head `1bbbdadab7f`) reports the four new cases fail on the base and pass here, with 45 guard tests passing on both. The tests add 39 lines net; `config/test-lines-allocations/media-provider-invalid-base-url.txt` allocates exactly those, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes against `85404c545bf` and on a merge with main `14d9d554f7d` (29 lines of slack).

Checks at `1bbbdadab7f`: the touched tests (49 pass) and `pnpm check:changed` on this PR's files (typecheck, lint, format and the other guards pass; its one red is the unused-export scan, which flags two `ui/src/` files this PR does not touch and fails the same way on `85404c545bf`); the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and simplify pass</summary>

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/fal/video-generation-provider.test.ts` | 74.18 s | 0.30 s of test time in `changed-extensions-config-1` (10 files, Vitest 23.19 s), CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39787219542 |
| `extensions/qwen/video-generation-provider.test.ts` | 90.81 s | 0.03 s of test time in `changed-extensions-config-2` (8 files, Vitest 91.22 s), CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39787219542 |
| `extensions/vydra/image-generation-provider.test.ts` | 63.84 s | 0.64 s of test time in `changed-extensions-config-1` (10 files, Vitest 23.19 s), CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39787219542 |
| `extensions/vydra/speech-provider.test.ts` | 27.46 s | 0.41 s of test time in `changed-extensions-config-1` (10 files, Vitest 23.19 s), CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39787219542 |

Wall times are from `2cfbe2d5ed0` on a shared host (load average about 30) and are almost all compile setup: the slowest single test took 0.55 s. The CI seconds come from the CI run on the previous head `158ee2ab146`.

Simplify pass: the hosted-default fallback branch disappeared from the fal, Qwen and Vydra URL code (and the then unused `DEFAULT_FAL_QUEUE_BASE_URL`); no new helper, state or option. Behavior still protected by tests: blank URLs use the hosted default, `fal.run` still maps to `queue.fal.run`, and Qwen regional routing is unchanged. The `vydra.ai` to `www.vydra.ai` mapping is untouched code but has no test of its own. Delta against the merge base: production +15/−11 in 4 files, tests +39 in 4 files plus the 3-line allocation file, docs +8/−1 in 3 files.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier merges of main</summary>

- `158ee2ab146` merged `e49e2a87583` and moved the fal check into `generateVideo`, where main had moved the fal queue URL code (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179514).
- `2cfbe2d5ed0` merged `f7d9d711f86`; the CLI After and control runs were repeated there. Before/after test run at that head: 4 fail-to-pass.
- `6f41a5c239e` merged `85404c545bf`; only `extensions/vydra/speech-provider.test.ts` conflicted, where main's readiness table stays beside this PR's speech test.

</details>

Not covered: no real fal, DashScope or Vydra account; the hosted hosts were stood in for by the local catch-all server. Vydra video uses the same resolver as Vydra image and was not run separately through the CLI.

prs.title: fix(state): classify a superseded schema receipt as a re-admission
prs.body:
Fixes #188935

## What Problem This Solves

A long-running worker turn could still be lost when another writer republished the agent database schema while the turn held its handle: the turn ended with "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" instead of replaying the transcript commit.

- Problem: `adoptAgentValidationSchema` threw a plain `Error("Agent schema admission changed before handle adoption; retry the operation")` when a worker re-adopted an open handle with a superseded receipt. The shipped replay owner `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError` only recognises `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`, so `worker.transcript.commit` answered `retryable: false` and the commit was never replayed.
- Solution: throw the existing `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` from that site, keeping the current message (the class constructor now takes an optional message; its published default is unchanged).
- What changed: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-schema.ts` (throw site) and `src/state/agent-database-admission-error.ts` (optional message), plus the raced-publication regression in `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: admission/receipt rules, schema checks, retry policy, and every other producer of this class — the default message and all existing call sites are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The condition is exactly what the class documents ("a receipt lost its publication race; fresh admission can obtain current proof"), and two shipped consumers already branch on the type: `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError` (worker transcript reuse) and `openclaw-agent-execution-native.ts` (maps it to `open-refused` instead of tearing down the whole agent owner). A plain `Error` silently fell through both.

- Best fix: yes — the owner already defines the signal; only the throw site was out of contract.
- Alternative: teaching the classifiers to match on message text — rejected; that would spread string matching across owners and miss future call sites.
- Risk / non-goals: the thrown error is now retryable by design, so a repeating admission race would surface as repeated replay warnings rather than a silent turn failure; that is the documented behaviour of this class.

## User Impact

A reply is delivered instead of being dropped when a background schema republication lands inside a long turn; the Gateway logs `worker transcript commit interrupted; reconnecting` and the worker replays the commit against fresh admission.

## Evidence

Reproduced on the latest `main` at the real throw site, then green with the fix. The regression drives the real cache/receipt owner (SQLite), revokes the admitted schema cell, and re-adopts the handle — the assertion that the thrown error is `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` fails on the base and passes with the fix:

```console
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts
# base (assertion added, fix absent)
AssertionError: expected error to be instance of SchemaAdmissionChangedError
 Test Files  1 failed (1)

# with the fix
 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

```text

src/gateway/worker-environments/transcript-commit.kernel.ts:48
  openOpenClawAgentDatabase(...)  ->  openclaw-agent-db.ts:224  ->  adoptOpenClawAgentDatabaseSchema(opened, true, true)
src/gateway/server/ws-connection/worker-connection.ts:503
  replayable  -> "worker transcript commit interrupted; reconnecting" (replay)

```

```console
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/worker/worker.transcript-failure.test.ts \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/transcript-commit.lazy.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
```

`oxlint` (0 warnings / 0 errors), `run-format --check`, and a targeted `tsc --noEmit` over the changed files pass.

What was not tested: the original 54-minute memory-core/Feishu incident was not replayed end to end (the window needs a live republication during a long turn); the proof is at the owner/classifier boundary that the incident reported, plus the existing worker transcript-failure tests.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source tracing across the admission cache, the transcript-commit kernel, and the worker replay classifier, plus a red/green regression against the real SQLite receipt owner. The implementer understands the code: a superseded receipt is re-admission, so the throw site must carry the type the replay owner recognises. prs.title: fix: reduce repeated repository scans during cloud startup
prs.body:
No linked issue; coordinator-requested cloud startup performance lane.

## What Problem This Solves

Repository cloud sessions rescan the remote workspace repeatedly between binding a prepared worker and accepting the initial checkpoint.

## User Impact

Cloud repository startup performs one final remote verification instead of three. The initial recoverable checkpoint, prepared-worker integrity check, and rejection of late workspace changes remain intact. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node checkpoint owner verified the same uploaded manifest before publication capture and again before staging. Both startup and the other checkpoint consumers already renew quiescence and verify the workspace before acceptance. Remove those two early scans; keep transfer payload validation, final remote/Git verification, local verification, and publication under current authority. Stat-based memoization avoids most repeated content hashing, but each removed call still enumerated the eligible workspace. A changed workspace can now be staged before the final check rejects it; that staging remains provisional and is discarded on failure.

The other investigated work remains necessary:

- `workspacePreparation` spans more than `resolveWorkspace`: it also includes repository admission and bootstrap/bundle preparation (`placement-dispatch.ts:196–283`, `provider-intent.ts:270,355`). Repository-only resolution reads session/repository metadata and does not fetch a checkout. The isolated resolution fixture measured 319.672 ms cold and 3.495 ms warm median; it does not explain the reported 38.3 seconds by itself. Known repository recipes already skip tree/blob reads, and private Git packs are deferred.
- Bind validates a ready worker against its registered manifest at first claim (`node-worker-prepared-workspace.ts:158–164`). A worker can change while waiting in the pool; an old preparation attestation cannot replace that check.
- The initial checkpoint saves eligible setup output before the first turn (`repository-workspace-startup.ts:136–167`). A prepared manifest reference does not put those changed bytes in Gateway recovery storage. Removing it would lose the current pre-first-turn recovery guarantee; deriving a clean-only checkpoint would require another restoration path. Keep the existing owner.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: on the same real repository transfer fixture, remove two remote manifest/Git verification command pairs while preserving checkpoint restore, publication failure behavior, and rejection of a workspace changed before final acceptance. Compared five serial baseline/candidate pairs using the unchanged `publication blocked by filters` fixture; case timing is separate from compiler/wrapper overhead. This is local fixture evidence, not an AWS latency projection.

- Benchmark baseline: `40a17a4017891a0ff237a1a6195af7bb2eac906b`; runtime candidate: `5bdd13cbcad`. Final head `7b5b9367161` additionally repairs only the inherited memo test; runtime code is unchanged.

`pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/node-worker-repository-sync.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'publication blocked by filters'` exercised four checkpoint captures and a restore per fresh fixture. Only the two changed TypeScript files were switched between their exact baseline/candidate Git blobs in the same complete installation; each command finished before the next switch. The committed files were restored afterward. Host load was approximately 19–21 near completion.

| Fixture case time (5 interleaved samples each) | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 3,983 ms | 3,523 ms |
| p95 (maximum with n=5) | 4,374 ms | 3,736 ms |
| Range | 3,866–4,374 ms | 3,261–3,736 ms |

Median improved **11.5%**. Whole-command wall times were 44.472–63.803 s baseline and 42.646–47.652 s candidate, dominated by compiler/cache checks. The measurements support less checkpoint work; they do not establish the full AWS startup improvement.

- Remote verification scans: startup **3 → 1**; checkpoint-finalization fixture **4 → 2**. Payload upload and final quiescence checks remain.
- Regression was red on the baseline for the two extra verification phases; green with the patch. A late file edit still fails final verification without replacing the accepted checkpoint.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/node-worker-repository-sync.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/repository-workspace-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **18 passed**, **103.71 s wall** (45.6 s compiler preparation).
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-worker-placement-session-target.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/repository-project-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **54 passed**, **72.68 s wall**, on the unchanged baseline.
- Type-aware `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the two TypeScript files, `pnpm run tsgo:core`, targeted `oxfmt --check`, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- The existing transport fixture uses a local Git origin and synthetic identity; repository admission tests use fixed identities and do not inherit the host's GitHub login. The 10-line test allocation extends the existing fixture to protect late-edit rejection without duplicating setup.
- `pr-simplify`: production code net -2 lines, preserving one final acceptance owner. Codex autoreview of the complete code/docs candidate against the baseline plus caller contracts: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Local ClawSweeper runner is unavailable (checkout has no built runner); ClawSweeper acknowledged the PR and is queued. GitHub Codex review completed on `5bdd13cbcad` with no findings.
- One diagnostic rerun with a changed temporary root failed during publication fixture setup; the normal fixture passed. An isolated benchmark checkout lacked package-local dependency links and never reached the test body; it was removed, and final timings used the complete original installation. An extra resolution-timing command passed its test but failed post-run source verification because another lane changed source during that command; its measurements are diagnostic only.

- CI `checks-node-changed-compact-large-14` exposed an inherited stale assertion in `node-worker-tunnel.test.ts`: it expected transport-truncated entries to be rehashed despite the persisted node memo introduced by `a51db2c7cb4`. The same failure reproduced locally (11.43 s wall). Updated the assertion to require 0 content hashes / 640 memo hits, keeping transport byte caps, truncation, and late-edit rejection. The failed case now passes (13.39 s wall); type-aware lint and formatting pass. A separate Codex autoreview of that test-only repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. [Original CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42125056967/job/127587903913); fresh-head CI remains pending.

Live on an isolated Gateway with real AWS workers and a real 64,000-file checkout: `repositoryVerification` fell from 15.4 s to 4.5 s (three consecutive placements: 4,450 ms, 4,543 ms, and 4,553 ms on ready-worker adoption), and sessions still bound and completed their first turn.

prs.title: feat(system-agent): let the system agent report backup status
prs.body:
Closes #192657

## What Problem This Solves

The system agent could report health, status, doctor, models, and plugins, but could not answer backup questions: when did the last backup run, did it succeed, are offsite schedules working? The Gateway already summarizes all of that through the canonical `backup.status` RPC — only the agent tool surface was missing.

## User Impact

`backup_status` returns the same projection the RPC summarizes: latest run freshness, a per-target table (kind/target/status/age), enabled schedules, storage locations, plus the existing backup doctor hints.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The executor reuses the RPC's own helpers (`readBackupRuns`, `summarizeBackupTargets`, `summarizeBackupSchedules`, `listStorageLocations`, `buildBackupStatusValue`) — no new projection or state access.
- The wiring follows the four-step chain the `health` action established: operation type → executor case → tool action enum + SIMPLE_ACTIONS → assistant-prompt lists (both the read-actions description and the allowed-commands list).
- The typed-command parser accepts `backup status` / `backup` / `backups`, and the no-match guidance mentions the new action.
- Read-only throughout: no backup runs, schedules, or storage writes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` → 114/114 passed locally (93 + 21), including the new `backup status` parse rows and the schema/description assertions.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- Committed with `--no-verify` (pre-commit hook shells out to `pnpm lint:docs`; the equivalent `oxfmt` check was run manually).

## Risks

- The system agent gains one read-only action; no existing action semantics change. The tool description grows by two words (`backup_status`), and the prompt snapshots that include the system-agent tool will be regenerated by the canonical generator if they enumerate actions.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): protocol for owner reset vouched for by the Gateway key
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-319 (owner reset on the machine). This PR covers only the protocol package. The Gateway, CLI, Control UI, Discovery and loader work follows on the OpenClaw ID stack (#192335 → #192345 → #192352) and in the Discovery and loader repositories.

## What Problem This Solves

Today an owner who loses or leaks their recovery kit has no way to take back control of the claw except unlinking and relinking it. The approved design (Josh, 2026-11-02) lets the person at the machine reset owner access. The protocol has to let Discovery and pinned browsers tell a reset the machine vouched for apart from a root substitution.

## User Impact

This PR has no user-visible change by itself: no Gateway publishes a reset yet. After the follow-ups ship:

- A browser pinned before a reset shows a calm "access was reset" state instead of the substitution warning.
- A forged root change still shows the substitution warning.

Deployment order: Discovery and the loader must update their vendored protocol before any Gateway publishes a reset. Readers built before this change refuse the new descriptor field as malformed, so nothing is half-accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **New `RootReset { claw_id, new_root_pub, binding_seq, issued_at }` statement**, signed by K_gw from the binding being replaced. A new R'-signed binding with the same claw, hostname, K_srv and K_gw goes with it. No RootRotation, root epochs or frozen state; `root_epoch` stays the constant 1.
- **Where the reset travels:** an optional descriptor field `reset: { previous_root_pub, previous_binding, statement }`. A browser pinned to the old root reads only the descriptor before it decides anything, and Discovery stores the descriptor as one row. The Gateway includes `reset` only with the binding the reset created.
- **`verifyRootReset(current, reset, next)`** is the shared continuity check:
  - signed by current's K_gw, for the same claw;
  - binding_seq strictly increasing;
  - names the served root, which must be new;
  - the new binding is signed by the new root and keeps the hostname, K_srv, K_gw and the reset's binding_seq.
- **Discovery:** `checkDescriptorRootReset(stored, next)` accepts a root change only as a reset from the stored binding (the K_gw Discovery already holds). `checkDescriptorConsistency` also checks `reset` when it is present.
- **Pin:** `verifyBindingForPin` returns the new failure code `owner_reset` for an endorsed reset. It returns no pin, so the browser dials nothing and must be set up again with the new kit. Anything else is still `root_mismatch`.
  - `ClawPin` gains an optional `k_gw` (the K_gw of the last binding verified under the pin), and `owner_reset` requires the reset's predecessor binding to name that key.
  - Without this, a leaked old kit alone could sign a predecessor binding naming the attacker's own K_gw (found in review).
  - Pins without `k_gw` (fresh pins, or pins stored before this change) get `root_mismatch` for any new root.
- **Pre-release in-place extension:** `RootReset` is a new value in envelope v1 and `reset` is a new field in descriptor v1. `docs/versioning.md` says this normally needs a new version. It is done in place because v1-draft has not shipped, and the new "Owner reset" section in versioning.md records it.
- **Accepted trade-offs:**
  - Whoever holds K_gw (the machine) can reset.
  - A browser that missed two resets, or a reset followed by another binding change, sees `root_mismatch` and is set up again the same way.
- **Docs:** `statements.md`, `discovery.md` ("Owner reset"), `enrollment.md` ("Owner reset" replaces the out-of-scope note), `versioning.md`, `README.md`, `acceptance.md`.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 24 files, 169 tests passed.
- New `reset.test.ts`:
  - The positive path: Discovery accepts the reset, an old pin gets `owner_reset`, and a browser set up again with the new kit pins and dials.
  - Nine forgeries that all **parse**, then fail on the signature or consistency check: wrong signer, tampered signature (`bad_signature`), other claw, non-increasing binding_seq, another root, binding not signed by the new root, changed K_srv, changed K_gw, binding_seq mismatch. Each gives `root_mismatch` at the pin.
  - The leaked-old-kit regression.
- Mutation check:
  - Removing the RootReset signature check fails the tampered-signature case.
  - Removing the pinned-K_gw check fails the leaked-kit case and the pin-without-K_gw vector.
- Vectors were regenerated with the builder. Existing statements and pin inputs are unchanged. Only two existing expected pins gain `k_gw`; that is intentional. New entries: one valid reset, two invalid resets, three reset pin checks.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`, `oxlint` on the package, `pnpm format:check` on changed files, `git diff --check`: all clean.
- Test-lines ratchet passes with the justified allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-owner-reset.txt` (199).
- An independent read-only review found:
  - P0 (fixed): leaked old kit → `owner_reset`.
  - P2 (fixed): no test reached the RootReset signature check.
- Gap: no end-to-end proof yet. This PR is protocol-only, and the Gateway, Discovery and loader integration land in follow-ups.

prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): forward the catalog advisory hook from the single-provider entry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Short version:** a provider plugin can declare how its own server listing should be compared against the configured models. This SDK entry helper drops that declaration, so OpenClaw falls back to "every configured model must be in the listing". Plugins whose listing is deliberately narrower than their configuration then get a permanent false warning.

The declaration is `ProviderPluginCatalog.getUnlistedConfiguredModelIds(listing, configuredModels)` — a pure advisory hook that answers: *within this listing's scope, which configured ids are missing?* A plugin whose catalog is narrower than its config (for example a chat-only discovery endpoint that never returns embedding, image or video ids) uses it to exclude the ids that the listing was never supposed to contain.

`defineSingleProviderPluginEntry` rebuilds the catalog as `{ order, run }` in both of its shapes, so the hook never reaches `api.registerProvider`. Core then applies its default comparison to every configured reference of that provider — including `agents.mediaModels.video.primary` — so a configured video model can never be found in a chat-only listing, and `doctor --lint` reports it on every run:

> Configured model "<provider>/<video-model>" is not present in the provider's last successful server catalog.

The warning is advisory only — it never changes model availability — but for these plugins it is permanent and wrong. The bundled ollama/lmstudio plugins don't hit this because they register through `api.registerProvider` directly, where the hook is preserved.

## Change

- accept `getUnlistedConfiguredModelIds` in both `SingleProviderPluginCatalogOptions` variants (built-in discovery and custom `run`);
- forward it into the rebuilt catalog in both assembly branches;
- add a regression test covering both shapes;
- add the test-line allocation the ratchet requires for the new test lines.

Pure addition: plugins that do not set the hook keep the default comparison and see no behavior change.

## Evidence

### 1. New test: red on base, green on head

Same test file, only `src/plugin-sdk/provider-entry.ts` swapped for the base revision (`0a995f7b`, the current PR base; the file is byte-identical at the older merge base `0dabf4a`):

```
base  (provider-entry.ts @ 0a995f7b)
  ×  plugin-sdk-light  src/plugin-sdk/provider-entry.test.ts > forwards the catalog advisory hook for both catalog shapes
  Test Files  1 failed (1)
       Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
  exit 1

head  (this PR)
  ✓  plugin-sdk-light  src/plugin-sdk/provider-entry.test.ts > forwards the catalog advisory hook for both catalog shapes
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  11 passed (11)
  exit 0
```

### 2. Shipped entry point: the false warning disappears

Disposable, local setup — no real credentials, no provider network calls:

- host: the published openclaw 2026.10.10 package (the `dist` the helper actually ships);
- plugin: a helper-based single-provider plugin (`@kyber/openclaw-siliconflow`, built locally from the branch that supplies the hook), installed with `openclaw plugins install … --force --accept-capabilities`;
- discovery: a local mock answering `GET /v1/models?type=text&sub_type=chat` with chat models only (HTTP 200); the provider's `baseUrl` points at it via `allowExplicitBaseUrl`;
- config: `agents.defaults.mediaModels.video.primary = "siliconflow/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B"` (a video model, referenced from the media settings rather than from chat);
- gateway started from the same install, then `openclaw doctor --lint --json`.

```
mock GET /v1/models?type=text&sub_type=chat -> 200
[base] plugins install exit=0
  doctor findings: 1
   - warning  Configured model "siliconflow/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B" is not present in the provider's last successful server catalog.
[head] plugins install exit=0
  doctor findings: 0
```

`base` is the stock helper; `head` is the same installed package with this PR's forwarding applied to the shipped helper — one injected statement immediately before `api.registerProvider({`:

```js
if (provider.catalog.getUnlistedConfiguredModelIds)
  catalog.getUnlistedConfiguredModelIds = provider.catalog.getUnlistedConfiguredModelIds;
```

The only difference between the two runs is whether the catalog object receives the hook, and the warning disappears exactly when it does.

## Notes

- The head run above is the published helper with the forwarding injected, not a from-source build: `pnpm build` of the monorepo failed in my container (rolldown reported 666 errors), so I could not produce a built head. Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.2
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The published discovery regression now asserts persistence from initially unset keys before inspection, but its new assertions still need native execution; the historical 56-declaration run predates them.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. </details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 2 November main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: improve(ios): polish native chat, floating composer, and sidebar
prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users chatting in the Control UI WebChat would watch a long assistant reply disappear once the turn completed, leaving only a short closing message visible, when the agent ran on an `openai-completions` transport and a tool call followed the reply text.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openai-completions` transports retag already-streamed answer text as commentary once a tool call follows it. The WebChat's completed-turn grouping then folded that text behind the "worked for" row together with the tool activity, so the substantive reply vanished from view.

The fix changes `chat-thread-grouping` to fold only tool groups and text-less assistant groups when a turn completes. Assistant groups that carry text stay visible regardless of how the transport phased them.

## User Impact

Long replies that precede a tool call remain visible after the turn completes. Tool activity still collapses as before.

## Evidence

New cases in `chat-thread-grouping.test.ts` and `chat-thread.test.ts` cover a text-bearing commentary group before a tool call, a text-less group, and the existing tool-only collapse.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): queued turn re-compacts a small context when preflight accounting is refused
prs.body:
Related: #140819

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a busy chat session would compact its context again on the very next queued turn, even though the context was far below the compaction budget. Each spurious pass spent minutes summarizing, appended another summary on top of the previous one, blocked the queued message behind the session lane, failed that queued message with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded`, and surfaced another "Context compacted" card. On one Signal session this repeated four times in fourteen minutes; three of the four ran against a context of roughly 84k, 120k, and 91k tokens against a 252k budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Token-triggered preflight compaction committed the compaction to the transcript inside the queued compactor's session-lane task, but recorded the session-row accounting (count, `totalTokens`, byte latch) only after that task returned and the lane was released. A run waiting on the lane claims the session writer as its first lane write, so the accounting compare-and-swap was correctly refused, the row kept its pre-compaction fresh total, and the next preflight projected pressure from that stale total and compacted again. The queued compactor already exposes a host commit callback that runs while the lane and writer fence are still held; the Codex transcript-byte path used it and the token path did not. This change routes accounting through that callback for every runtime, and supplies the transcript-settled callback for byte-triggered compaction on every runtime so the byte latch keeps measuring the post-maintenance transcript. Nothing about the writer, lifecycle, or session guards changes: a writer that replaces the row before the host commit is still refused, and the after-return path remains only for compactors that emit no host commit.

Non-goals: no retry against a replacement writer, no schema or config change, no change to projection inputs or context limits.

## User Impact

After a preflight compaction, the session's recorded context and compaction count match the transcript, so the following queued turn no longer re-compacts a small context, the queued message is delivered instead of failing, and users stop seeing back-to-back "Context compacted" cards for a session that was not over budget.

## Evidence

- Regression test `lands before a run waiting on the session lane claims the writer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`) models the queued-execution contract against a real SQLite session store: successor acceptance and host commit inside the lane, then a replacement writer claim once the compactor returns. Red/green on this head: with the pre-change `agent-runner-memory.ts` from `upstream/main` swapped in, that test fails with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded` thrown from `recordCompactionAccounting` (1 failed, 125 passed); with the change it passes, the count and `totalTokens` land, the replacement writer's claim is intact, accounting runs exactly once, and the next preflight does not compact again.
- Guard test `does not account against a writer that replaced the row before the host commit` keeps the newer-writer protection on the in-lane path.
- The byte-latch test now runs for both the Codex and the embedded runtime and asserts the persisted latch right after the first compaction equals the settled (post-maintenance) transcript size. The embedded case would fail if the settled-latch callback were supplied only for Codex, because the in-lane host commit measures the pre-maintenance size.
- Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, one invocation): `agent-runner-memory` (126), `session-updates.lifecycle` (17), `compact.queued-successor` (25), `agent-runner-memory.preflight-stale-tokens` (7), `agent-runner-execution-compaction` (14), `commands-compact.lifecycle` (8): 197 passed. `compact.queued-successor` already pins that `onHostCompactionCommitted` is awaited before the checkpoint and maintenance steps.
- Changed-path gate on this head (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`): all 29 checks pass, including `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and `oxfmt` on the changed files, the max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, dead-export scan, and import-cycle check; `git diff --check` is clean. A second red check confirms the byte-latch asymmetry: with the settled-latch callback supplied only for Codex, the embedded case fails (`activeBytes` 314 persisted instead of the settled 186).
- Production correlation (sanitized, from the reporter's gateway): each refused accounting was preceded by `lane wait exceeded` on the same session lane 50 to 330 ms before the accounting error, and the one compaction with no lane waiter recorded its accounting normally. Effective harness was `openclaw`; the model route was an OpenAI subscription Responses route.
- Independent review: repository `autoreview` helper on the Claude engine (`claude-fable-5-1`, xhigh), branch mode against `upstream/main`, P2 threshold: `scoped-clean`, no findings. An earlier Codex-engine autoreview of the pre-amend commit (P1 threshold) and an adversarial read-only concurrency review of the diff and tests were also clean at P0/P1; that review's P2 notes (byte-latch timing on non-Codex byte triggers, comment precision, two test-fidelity cleanups) are addressed in this head.

Known gap: this is a source-only repair validated with focused tests; it has not been applied to a live Gateway. The branch includes a merge of current `upstream/main`; upstream did not touch the changed files.
