prs.title: fix(gateway): ACP bridge photos are missing from Control UI chat history
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**
Additional instructions **MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.
Closes #193659 ## What Problem This Solves - Fixes an issue where users who send a photo through the ACP bridge (for example a Rabbit R1 camera shot relayed by Rabbit Agent) see the assistant answer about the photo, but the Control UI chat history shows only the prompt text. The photo is missing from the original user turn and stays missing after reloading the conversation, while a JPEG uploaded from the Control UI into the same session displays correctly. - **Related:** #51324 introduced inbound-image persistence for `chat.send` and carried an ACP-bridge exclusion plus a test locking that omission in; this PR removes the exclusion. Issue carries `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear` and `clawsweeper:source-repro`. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Intended outcome:** An ACP bridge photo is claimed by the same canonical user-turn media owner as a Control UI upload, so the stored turn keeps a `media://inbound/…` reference and the Control UI renders the photo inline in the original user message, including after a reload. - `prepareChatSendUserTurn()` short-circuited `persistInboundImagesForTranscript()` whenever `isAcpBridgeClient(client)` matched, so no inbound buffer was saved and the resolved user turn carried neither `media` nor `mediaImageLayout`. The image still reached the model because `replyOptionImages` is wired independently from `attachments.parsedImages` — which is exactly the reported "the assistant can read it, the transcript cannot show it" split. The bridge identity gates ACP-only `systemInputProvenance` fields; it does not own media persistence. - **Out of scope:** No change to how the bridge defers its commit to the agent runtime (`requiresRuntimeApprovedChatInput`), no new storage owner, no Control UI change, and no change to what the model receives. - **Highest-risk area:** Sending the same photo to the model twice on the first turn — the concern raised during the review of #51324. - **How is that risk mitigated?** The existing generic suppression is reused, not reimplemented: every persisted inline/offloaded fact is marked `hydrationSuppressed: true`, and `collectCurrentImageAttachments()` drops every suppressed `ctx.media` index, so the persisted path is never re-hydrated into the prompt. The model still receives the photo exactly once, from the inline prompt image. The retained end-to-end regression test asserts this explicitly (`lastDispatchImages` still holds exactly one entry). - **Owner decision — the recorded rationale, re-checked on this head:** The review asks for an owner decision because the exclusion was intentional and test-protected. Provenance from public history: - The gate came from a **contributor-authored** commit inside #51324 ([`6b709d734b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/51324/commits/6b709d734b), "gate image persistence to webchat callers"), landed as `c9449d77b40a`. Its whole recorded rationale is one comment line added by that commit: `// Gated to non-ACP callers: ACP/IDE screenshots are transient and handled upstream.` Later refactors dropped that comment, so on main only the bare `|| isAcpBridgeClient(client)` survives (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts:180-185`) plus the test name this PR replaces. The Greptile **bot** summary restated the same premise ("ACP/IDE screenshot flows … handle persistence upstream", [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/51324#issuecomment-4101468041)); none of the five human review comments there mention ACP. The maintainer-side concern was double-submission, and @obviyus solved it **generically** (`602c0d1e22`: dispatch drops the persisted `MediaPath`s on the current turn, the canonical turn is rewritten after dispatch). - **"handled upstream" is not implemented anywhere in the tree** (audit at `origin/main` `abed61f6400`): `git grep -l -E "saveMediaBuffer|media/store|persistInboundImages" -- src/acp extensions/acpx` → **0 matches**, and "screenshot" does not occur in `src/acp`, `extensions/acpx` or `docs/cli/acp.md`. The bridge only converts image blocks into Gateway attachments (`src/acp/event-mapper.ts:233`), which is what `docs/cli/acp.md:36` documents. There is no "upstream" ACP media owner to defer to. - **"transient" is not true either** — ACP photos are already persisted today, just not where the Control UI can render them: `recordUserPrompt()` clones every prompt content block, image `data` included, into the SQLite replay ledger (`src/acp/event-ledger.ts:21-24` → `createAcpPromptUpdates`, `src/acp/event-ledger.types.ts:48-53`; row bytes are budgeted in `src/acp/event-ledger-bytes.ts`). That ledger feeds ACP `loadSession` replay only. It is exactly the reporter's observation: `acp_replay_events` holds the image block with data while the transcript holds no media reference. So the bytes are already stored once; this PR adds the managed inbound buffer plus a claim-only fact (74 B, no base64 in the transcript) that the existing history/renderer path can resolve. - The bridge identity does not own media anywhere else either: `requiresRuntimeApprovedChatInput()` (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-goal-admission.ts:36-40`) has exactly two consumers — the input-commit decision (`chat-send-input-dispatch.ts:294`) and goal admission (`chat-send-goal-admission.ts:128`). So the question reduces to: should the canonical Gateway durable-media owner cover ACP photos (this PR, +13/-16, reusing existing suppression), or should history rendering instead be taught to read the ACP replay ledger (a much larger change across history projection and the Control UI, and it would still leave non-ledger ACP sessions without media)? @obviyus @fuller-stack-dev — a yes/no here is the only thing this PR is waiting on; if the answer is "render from the ledger", I will close this and open that instead. ## User Impact - **Success criteria:** After a `chat.send` from an ACP bridge client that carries an image attachment, the inbound buffer is saved once under `inbound`, and the resolved user-turn message carries a claim-only `media://inbound/` fact (`kind: "image"`, no `path`, no `workspaceDir`, no base64 `data`) plus its `mediaImageLayout` inline slot, while the dispatched prompt image count stays at 1. - **What should reviewers focus on?** The single condition change in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts` (`prepareChatSendUserTurn`), and the one regression fixture `persists ACP bridge photos as durable user-turn media` in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts`, which replaces `leaves ACP bridge user persistence to the agent runtime` — the test that asserted the omission. The whole change is +13/-16 lines across two files; no test-lines allocation is needed. ## Evidence - **Real environment tested:** Yes — the shipped ACP flow was run end to end twice on an identical harness: a real Gateway started from this branch's source in a temp state dir (real SQLite state, real transcript, real `saveMediaBuffer` writing into `/media/inbound`), the real ACP bridge as a **separate OS process** (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts acp --url ws://127.0.0.1: --token `) driven by a real ACP client over ndjson JSON-RPC on stdio, and the real Control UI (built from this head, `build=2026.11.1-7a5e5a1b3478-…`) loaded in headless Chrome. Only the model provider is faked, at its HTTP boundary (a local server speaking the Anthropic Messages SSE contract that records every request body, so the number of images handed to the model is observed rather than inferred). No Rabbit R1 hardware was available; the gateway log confirms the shipped bridge identity connected: `[ws] client connected client=cli name=ACP mode=cli role=operator auth=token version=acp`. - **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:** ```bash export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.config/nvm/versions/node/v26.12.1/bin:$PATH" pnpm install --prefer-offline # RED: revert only the source fix, keep both new regression tests git checkout origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.test.ts \ -t "persists an ACP bridge photo as a durable user-turn claim" # GREEN: restore the fix, run the full affected suites git checkout HEAD -- src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \ src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.test.ts \ src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts \ src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-attachments.owner.test.ts \ src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts \ src/acp/event-mapper.test.ts # Types + format + lint node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --builders 1 node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts \ src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.test.ts \ src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts pnpm exec oxlint src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts \ src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.test.ts \ src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts ``` - **Real-runtime proof commands (shipped ACP flow, before/after on one harness):** ```bash export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.config/nvm/versions/node/v26.12.1/bin:$PATH" # Control UI assets for the browser step (this PR does not touch ui/) node scripts/ui.js build # -> dist/control-ui, "✓ built in 51.61s" # AFTER: this PR's head node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/tmp-pr193703-acp-media.server.test.ts # gateway RPC proof node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs tmp-pr193703-ui-proof.mts # browser proof # BEFORE: revert only the source fix, rerun the identical harnesses git checkout origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/tmp-pr193703-acp-media.server.test.ts node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs tmp-pr193703-ui-proof.mts git checkout HEAD -- src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts ``` Both harnesses drive `initialize` → `session/new` (`_meta.sessionKey`) → `session/prompt` with `[{ type: "text" }, { type: "image", data: , mimeType: "image/png" }]`, then read the session back through `chat.history`, through the Control UI's own image route `GET /__openclaw__/assistant-media` (meta → ticketed bytes), and through a cold Control UI load in headless Chrome. They are local proof scripts kept outside the PR diff; the committed regression test remains `persists ACP bridge photos as durable user-turn media`. - **Real-runtime proof result (identical harness, only the source fix differs):** | Observation | `origin/main` source (before) | this PR (after) | |---|---|---| | ACP `session/prompt` | `{"stopReason":"end_turn"}` | `{"stopReason":"end_turn"}` | | Images handed to the model (recorded provider bodies) | `[1]` | `[1]` — no duplicate | | `/media/inbound` on disk | `[]` | 1 file, sha256 `862ea60f…5978` == the sent photo | | `chat.history` user-turn `media` | absent | `media://inbound/0ae22fe5-….png`, `image/png`, `kind:"image"`, 74 B, 8×6 | | `chat.history` user-turn `mediaImageLayout` | absent | `{ slots: [{ kind: "inline", factIndex: 0 }] }` | | `GET …/assistant-media?meta=1` (Control UI image route) | nothing to resolve (no claim) | `200 {available:true,mimeType:"image/png",sizeBytes:74,mediaTicket:…}` | | ticketed bytes from that route | — | `200 image/png`, 74 B, sha256 identical to the sent photo | | Control UI in headless Chrome after the reload | prompt text only; the sole ``s are the app icon and community art — no `assistant-media` image | ``, `naturalWidth:8 naturalHeight:6 complete:true` | | harness verdict | fails on the durable-claim assertion (`claim?.url` is `undefined`) | all assertions pass | ```text # AFTER — this PR head 7a5e5a1b347 (gateway RPC harness) PROOF acp prompt stopReason: {"stopReason":"end_turn"} PROOF model input images per provider request: [{"model":"claude-opus-5","images":1}] PROOF durable user-turn media claim: {"url":"media://inbound/0ae22fe5-cfdb-4c45-abf3-8152039e1ea3.png", "contentType":"image/png","kind":"image","sizeBytes":74,"width":8,"height":6} PROOF durable user-turn image layout: {"slots":[{"kind":"inline","factIndex":0}]} PROOF managed media store inbound entries: ["0ae22fe5-cfdb-4c45-abf3-8152039e1ea3.png"] PROOF stored inbound bytes: {"size":74,"sha256":"862ea60fb6fbdf1adb1143d3396b6eeec47ccc1e917fbcbe9efeb5c45b525978"} PROOF assistant-media meta: {"status":200,"body":{"available":true,"mimeType":"image/png","sizeBytes":74, "mediaTicket":"v1.","mediaTicketExpiresAt":"2026-11-05T21:28:56.948Z"}} PROOF assistant-media bytes: {"status":200,"contentType":"image/png","size":74, "sha256":"862ea60fb6fbdf1adb1143d3396b6eeec47ccc1e917fbcbe9efeb5c45b525978"} PROOF sent photo: {"size":74,"sha256":"862ea60fb6fbdf1adb1143d3396b6eeec47ccc1e917fbcbe9efeb5c45b525978"} ✓ keeps an ACP bridge photo in reloaded chat history and sends it to the model once 76376ms # BEFORE — same harness, only src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts reverted to origin/main PROOF acp prompt stopReason: {"stopReason":"end_turn"} PROOF model input images per provider request: [{"model":"claude-opus-5","images":1}] PROOF chat.history user turn: {"role":"user","content":"[Working directory: ~/workspace]\n\nWhat is in this photo?", "__openclaw":{"transport":{"clients":[{"id":"cli","mode":"cli","displayName":"ACP"}]}, …}} # no media, no layout PROOF managed media store inbound entries: [] PROOF stored inbound bytes: none PROOF assistant-media meta: {"status":0,"body":{}} # no claim to resolve FAIL TypeError: .toMatch() expects to receive a string, but got undefined # expect(claim?.url) # BEFORE — headless Chrome on the same reverted source: the reported symptom PROOF rendered assistant-media images: null PROOF page dump: {"url":"http://127.0.0.1:/chat/main/pr193703-ui-proof","imgCount":2, "imgSrcs":["…/apple-touch-icon.png…","…/community-art/community-invite-light.webp…"], "bodyText":"… What is in this photo? … PR193703_ACP_PHOTO_SEEN …"} # model answered, photo absent # AFTER — headless Chrome on this PR head: the photo renders from the persisted claim [ws] client connected client=openclaw-control-ui mode=webchat auth=token build=2026.11.1-7a5e5a1b3478-… PROOF rendered assistant-media images: [{"src":"/__openclaw__/assistant-media?source=media%3A%2F%2Finbound%2F897d1dc9-….png&mediaTicket=&sessionKey=agent%3Amain%3Apr193703-ui-proof&messageId=453b2033-…&agentId=main&variant=thumbnail&width=480&v=4", "naturalWidth":8,"naturalHeight":6,"complete":true}] ``` - **Evidence after fix:** ```text # AFTER — with the fix, rebased on origin/main d999f7b1b67 Test Files 5 passed (5) Tests 214 passed (214) # 9 (acp/event-mapper) + 205 (4 gateway suites) node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --builders 1 -> exit 0 node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs -> Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed files check-test-lines-ratchet.mts -> Test lines OK; slack 14 check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts --base origin/main -> assertion SAFETY ratchet OK pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet -> max-lines ratchet OK pnpm exec oxfmt --check <3 files> -> All matched files use the correct format. pnpm exec oxlint <2 test files> -> exit 0 ``` - **Observed result after fix:** With the fix applied, an ACP bridge `chat.send` carrying an inline PNG saves exactly one inbound buffer and the resolved user turn carries `media: [{ url: "media://inbound/acp.png", contentType: "image/png", kind: "image", … }]` with `mediaImageLayout: { slots: [{ kind: "inline", factIndex: 0 }] }`; the serialized turn contains no `path`, no `workspaceDir` and no base64 payload, the visible text stays `"bridge image"`, and `lastDispatchImages` (the images handed to the model) still holds exactly one entry, asserted in the same regression test. only the prompt text is in the reloaded turn | `` served from `media://inbound/897d1dc9-….png`, decoded at `naturalWidth:8 naturalHeight:6 complete:true` | Screenshots were captured locally for both runs (`control-ui-acp-photo-before-fix.png`, `control-ui-acp-photo-after-fix.png`); no public artifact host is available to link them, so the DOM facts above are quoted instead. - **Ownership provenance audit (commands re-run at `origin/main` `abed61f6400` and at this head):** ```bash git grep -l -E "saveMediaBuffer|media/store|persistInboundImages" abed61f6400 -- src/acp extensions/acpx # -> 0 matches (no ACP-side durable-media owner exists) git grep -in "screenshot" abed61f6400 -- src/acp extensions/acpx docs/cli/acp.md # -> 0 matches (the "ACP/IDE screenshot flows" in the recorded rationale have no counterpart here) git grep -l "saveMediaBuffer" abed61f6400 -- src extensions | grep -v test | wc -l # -> 29 files: channels, browser, cli/media-output, media/outbound-attachment, plugins runtime rg -n "requiresRuntimeApprovedChatInput\\(" -g '!*.test.ts' src # -> 3 hits: the definition plus chat-send-input-dispatch.ts:294 and chat-send-goal-admission.ts:128 gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/commits/6b709d734b --jq '.files[] | select(.filename=="src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts") | .patch' | rg "ACP" # -> + // Gated to non-ACP callers: ACP/IDE screenshots are transient and handled upstream. # (the only recorded rationale; the comment no longer exists on main) rg -n "recordUserPrompt|createAcpPromptUpdates" src/acp/event-ledger.ts src/acp/event-ledger.types.ts # -> event-ledger.ts:21 / event-ledger.types.ts:48 — ACP prompt blocks (image data included) # are already written durably to the SQLite replay ledger ``` The two other `persistInboundImagesForTranscript()` callers (`src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-user-turn.ts:279`, `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts:568`) are different entry points, which is why the runtime proof above observes **one** inbound file for an ACP photo rather than two. - **What was not tested:** The physical Rabbit R1 → Rabbit Agent → ACP bridge chain was not exercised (no hardware); the bridge is represented by its exact shipped client identity (`{ id: "cli", mode: "cli", displayName: "ACP", version: "acp" }`, the tuple matched by `isAcpBridgeClient`) and by the attachments path documented in `docs/cli/acp.md` ("images become Gateway attachments"); on the client side of the bridge the ACP protocol SDK client stands in for Rabbit Agent, while everything from the bridge's `chat.send` onwards (Gateway, media store, transcript, `chat.history`, the assistant-media route, Control UI rendering) is shipped code. Browser-level Control UI rendering of the reloaded turn **was** captured in headless Chrome (system Chrome, Control UI assets built from this head); the deep session route was reached by client-side navigation from `/chat`, because a cold `/chat/main/` document request is only served by a packaged runtime. Full CI lanes are pending on this PR: locally only the affected `gateway-methods` type shard and the five affected suites ran, because this host has glibc 2.31 while the pinned `tsrs` 0.18.0 native binary requires ≥ 2.32 — the shard ran with the also-installed `tsrs` 0.16.0 binary (same `7.1.0-dev.20260929` TypeScript) and the pinned binary was restored afterwards. CI lanes pending. - **Proof tier:** L3 - **Proof limitations:** No live Rabbit R1 / Rabbit Agent capture (no hardware): the ACP client side of the bridge is the protocol SDK client. The model provider is a local HTTP server at the provider boundary, which is also what makes the "exactly one image to the model" claim observable. The two real-runtime harnesses are local proof scripts, deliberately not part of this PR's diff; the committed coverage stays the single handler-level regression test plus the existing shared hydration-suppression cases. The unit-level `saveMediaBuffer` mock in the committed test is now backed by the real filesystem write observed in the runtime harness. - **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.

- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.

The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.

The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(android): keep realtime Talk alive through slow audio acknowledgments
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk over the Gateway relay ends with "Talk failed: request timeout" when the Gateway's answer to one audio append takes longer than 8 seconds, on the phone and through a paired Watch.

## User Impact

User impact: a short network stall or a busy Gateway no longer ends an Android realtime Talk call. Audio past about three seconds in flight is dropped, Talk says "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part", and "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" once the Gateway catches up. A paired Watch shows its own shorter text ("Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part.", "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part.") in place of the elapsed time; each notice stays until the next Talk state change, as on the phone. Talk still ends on an explicit Gateway error, a lost connection, or an append left unanswered for 30 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser relay and the Apple apps already follow this contract (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155839, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572, `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`); https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 did not reach Android. Both Android relays sent every frame with an 8 second deadline, no limit on audio in flight, and ended Talk on the first timeout.

A small `RealtimeInputAudioBudget` owns the three-second budget and the two notices, and both relays use it: the phone's append loop in `TalkModeManager` and the Watch relay in `WearRealtimeTalkController`. To release audio from the budget when the Gateway answers, `GatewaySession.sendRequestFrameForEndpoint` gains an optional success callback, and the Watch relay's send callback now reports success as well as errors. The append deadline is the 30 second liveness limit from the same contract. The Watch shows the notices from its own strings: the relay's snapshot gains an optional `notice` field (older watches ignore it), and the Watch Talk screen shows it in place of "Listening · 0:00" while listening. The notices are registered for translation; the docs page now says Android follows the same budget.

Trade-off: a Gateway that keeps the socket open but stops answering is now noticed after 30 seconds instead of 8, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 states for the Apple apps.

## Evidence

Tested at `170d5c59956` (base `upstream/main` `315fba74e12`). The Before/After runs below used a build of an earlier revision of this branch with the same phone-side code; the stall run was repeated on a build of this head (see "Re-run at this head").

Real app: the Android app (play debug build of each side) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway (empty state directory, loopback port, no outside traffic) whose realtime Talk provider is a local fake that only counts audio. The Gateway is an older source build (2026.9.6, `19afe35954`) on both sides; the bug and the fix are in the Android client. A local WebSocket proxy between the app and the Gateway sets the answer delay: while a stall is on, it holds each `talk.session.appendAudio` answer for a fixed time and logs every 50th held answer as `hold`. Same steps on both sides: open the chat, start realtime Talk, let audio flow, turn the stall on.

Proxy lines are UTC; logcat lines are the emulator's local time (UTC+9), whose clock runs about 1.06 s behind the proxy's. On the proxy clock, Talk closes 8.0 s after the stall starts on the base and 30.0 s after it in the 40 second run.

Before (base, 12 second stall per answer):

```text
11:58:35.244Z req   talk.session.create
12:00:20.447Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
12:00:25.441Z hold  held=51  stallMs=12000      (every frame still sent)
21:00:27.401 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:00:28.448Z req   talk.session.close
screen: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"
```

After (this PR, same stall):

```text
12:17:39.337Z req   talk.session.create
12:17:48.405Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" (held answers start coming back, about 12 s in)
(stall turned off by the operator at about 12.7 s, not logged)
12:18:03.915Z append appends=151
12:18:13.912Z append appends=251
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat, Talk stays on

40 second stall per answer:
12:19:02.948Z hold  held=1   stallMs=40000
21:19:31.897 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:19:32.953Z req   talk.session.close
```

![Before: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/before.png)
![After: "Realtime audio input fell behind" notice during the stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-fell-behind.png)
![After: "Microphone input recovered" notice, Talk still on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-recovered.png)

Re-run at this head (`170d5c59956`, same Gateway, fake provider and proxy, each held answer delayed 12 s; screenshot times are the host clock, which matches the proxy's):

```text
13:14:31.185Z req    talk.session.create
13:14:44.146Z hold   held=1   stallMs=12000
13:15:01.746Z append appends=301
13:15:08      screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
13:15:15.876Z append appends=351      (14.1 s for 50 appends instead of 5 s: frames past the budget were dropped, not sent)
13:15:16      screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part", Talk still on
13:15:20.854Z append appends=401
...
13:17:30.856Z append appends=1701
13:17:57.360Z close  who=client code=1006 appends=1952 held=31   (held: running count of held answers; the operator closed the app)
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat
```

Watch display (rendered by `WearVoiceLayoutTest` under Robolectric, round 192 dp, not on a watch): before this commit the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" while the relay reports the notice; now it shows each notice.

![Watch before: "Listening · 0:00" while input fell behind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-before.png)
![Watch after: "Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-fell-behind.png)
![Watch after: "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-recovered.png)

Mixed versions with the latest stable (`v2026.10.9`, `8b18b5578f6`): the new `notice` field crosses the phone-Watch protocol in both directions while one side still runs the stable release. A throwaway JUnit test (not committed) ran in `:wear-shared` of each tree and passed the real encoded bytes between them: this head's `WearProtocolCodec.encode` of a Talk event with each notice, decoded by the stable `WearProtocolCodec.decode` and `WearRealtimeTalkCodec.decode`, and the stable encoding of a listening event decoded by this head.

```text
head wrote    {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"notice":"INPUT_FELL_BEHIND"}}
stable read   WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(attemptId=attempt-1, active=true, listening=true, speaking=false, status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[])
stable read   (same for INPUT_RECOVERED)
stable wrote  {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"conversation":[]}}
head read     WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(..., status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[], notice=null)
```

An updated phone with a stable Watch keeps Talk working and the Watch shows its usual status text; a stable phone with an updated Watch sends no notice and the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" as before. In the stable release both codecs already share `WearProtocolCodec.json`, which sets `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` and `explicitNulls = false`.

Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same emulator, same isolated Gateway and proxy, no stall): the stable play debug build was installed on a wiped Android 16 emulator, paired with the Gateway (operator and node approved), and the Talk speaker set to "Muted" in Voice settings. This head's build was then installed over it with `adb install -r` (no uninstall; both builds are version code 2026080201, `firstInstallTime` unchanged, `lastUpdateTime` changed).

```text
14:57:11.572Z close  who=client code=1006   (the install stops the stable app)
14:57:14.909Z req    connect                (same device ID, no pairing request, no onboarding)
screen: Overview with Gateway "Online"; Voice settings still show "Enable speaker · Muted"
14:57:44.825Z req    talk.session.create
14:58:05.492Z append appends=201            (Talk "Listening")
```

After the upgrade the Overview's Nodes row shows "Review node access" instead of "1 online": `openclaw nodes list` on the same Gateway shows the node in `pending-reapproval` with the same 7 caps and 14 commands as approved and one changed permission, `microphone` false to true, because the microphone was granted after the node was approved and 14:57:14 was the first reconnect since; the stable build, installed back over this head, reconnects into the same `pending-reapproval` and shows the same row, so it does not come from this change.

Observed result: on the base, Talk ends 8 seconds into the stall; with this PR it drops audio past the budget with the notice, recovers when the answers arrive, and ends only after an append is unanswered for 30 seconds.

Regression tests: `TalkModeManagerTest.stalledAppendsDropInputPastThreeSecondsWithoutEndingTalk` feeds 31 frames while every append is unanswered, expects 30 appends, the fell-behind notice and Talk still on, then answers one append and expects the recovered notice and the next frame sent. It fails on the base (the 31st frame is sent) and passes with this PR. `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest` has the same case for the Watch relay and also asserts the 30 second deadline on every append, which pins the deadline constant both relays share; it changes the relay's callback type, so it does not compile on the base. It also asserts the notice the relay sends to the Watch. `WearVoiceLayoutTest` has two new listening cases with each notice; they fail with the previous Watch screen code (the notice text is not on screen) and pass with this PR, and they check the text fits the round screen at font scale 1 and 1.3 in English and in the German locale (which shows the English text until the native locale refresh adds the translation).

Checks at this head: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.wear.*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.gateway.*' :wear:testDebugUnitTest :wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest :wear:lintDebug` (848 tests, 0 failures); `:app`, `:benchmark`, `:wear` and `:wear-shared` `ktlintCheck`; `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs`; `pnpm native:i18n:verify`; `git diff --check`. `TalkModeManagerTest` was run again on the base with the test file carried over: the new test times out at 31 appends there, and the other 111 tests pass on both sides. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

CI: the previous head failed `preflight` with "Native generated locale artifacts must be isolated from source changes", and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed because of it. That head carried English placeholders in 21 Watch `values-*/strings.xml` files. This head leaves those files unchanged, so the native locale refresh workflow fills them. `node scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs --base 315fba74e12` exits 1 with that message on the previous head and exits 0 on this one.

CI at this head ([run 41094221772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772)): `preflight`, `android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`, `android-test-wear`, `android-ktlint` and `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` passed. `android-access-native (4096, google_apis)` [failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772/job/124196671436) while installing the Android Emulator, before the emulator started or any test ran: `sdkmanager` reported "Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel" while preparing the Android Emulator package, and the job uploaded no test results. `openclaw/ci-gate` is red only because of that job. The same job passed on main in [run 41123124777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41123124777/job/124295092007) (that run is red for unrelated Node and UI jobs). That job has not passed on this head; it needs a rerun.

The CI seconds below come from the JUnit reports of `android-test-play` (phone files) and `android-test-wear` (Watch file). CI tests the PR merged into main, where `TalkModeManagerTest` has 113 tests.

| Test file | Local wall (Gradle, this head) | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` | 0.84 s for the new test (file 17.8 s, 112 tests, Gradle `--max-workers=4` with other modules running) | 0.77 s for the new test (file 14.8 s, 113 tests) |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt` | 0.16 s for the new test (file 1.1 s, 26 tests) | 0.01 s for the new test (file 0.38 s, 26 tests) |
| `apps/android/wear/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/wear/WearVoiceLayoutTest.kt` | two more cases in the existing layout loop (file 7.9 s, 12 tests) | file 4.5 s, 12 tests |

Simplify pass: no change. One budget type serves both relays instead of two copies of the policy, and each new test covers a different relay. Against the merge base: production +147/−15 lines, tests +135/−6, docs +2, Watch English strings +2, translation source +4.

Not covered: no real phone and no real Watch. The phone runs used the Android 16 emulator. No Wear OS device is available, and no Wear OS emulator image is installed; pairing an emulator also needs the Play Store companion app and a Google sign-in. So there are no Watch screenshots or recordings with transport logs from a live call. The phone-side Watch relay is proven by its unit test, the Watch screen by Robolectric renders, and the phone-Watch payload against the latest stable by the codec run above. The device runs used an older Gateway build (see above); the change is client-only. Non-English locales show the English notices on both the phone and the Watch until the native locale refresh translates them.

Follow-up: the microphone transcription stream (`NodeRuntime` `appendTranscriptionAudio`, used by `MicCaptureManager`) also sends `talk.session.appendAudio` with an 8 second deadline. It is a separate feature outside the realtime Talk contract, so it is left for its own change.

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop treating unnamed two-member rooms as DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Before the Matrix `m.direct` cache has loaded, an unnamed room with exactly two members is classified as a direct message. Ingress no longer does that. A room is still a direct message when `is_direct` is set, when the room is stored in `m.direct`, when a recent invite was promoted, or when opted-in per-room recovery allows it.

## Evidence

On commit `567572f5adc51a` the direct-room tracker refuses an unnamed two-member room before the cache seeds, and it still accepts `is_direct` and `m.direct`. The QA harness sets the Matrix wildcard group to accept a reply without a mention, because those smoke rooms are groups now.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > does not treat an exact 2-member room as a DM before the dm cache seeds 24ms
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > still trusts is_direct and m.direct before the dm cache seeds 1ms
 ✓ crabline transport > binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 3065ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 10.89s
```

QA smoke profile 6, which includes `matrix-restart-resume` and `matrix-restart-replay-dedupe`, passed on this head in CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41541733549/job/125608393398

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** An unnamed two-member Matrix room is not a direct message only because the direct-room cache has not seeded. Explicit direct signals still are.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, Node v26.12.1, worktree at `567572f5adc51a` on `fix/matrix-dm-two-member-fallback`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"`
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied below.
```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
 ✓ does not treat an exact 2-member room as a DM before the dm cache seeds 24ms
 ✓ still trusts is_direct and m.direct before the dm cache seeds 1ms
 ✓ binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 3065ms
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 10.89s
```
- **Observed result after fix:** The unnamed room is not classified as a direct message, and `setAccountData` is not called. `is_direct` and `m.direct` still are direct before the cache seeds. The QA Matrix config sets `groups.*` to `requireMention: false`. CI smoke profile 6 passed.
- **What was not tested:** A live federated homeserver. Recent-invite promotion and opted-in per-room recovery are unchanged.

## Summary

Remove the pre-seed two-member fallback in `createDirectRoomTracker`. Recent-invite promotion, opted-in per-room recovery, and an explicit `is_direct` or `m.direct` signal are unchanged.

Crabline smoke rooms are ordinary groups. They only received replies because two members counted as a direct message. The harness sets the wildcard group so those rooms can reply without a mention pill. Product group rooms are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ci): stop flagging the prepared workspace preload as unused
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dependency check reports the prepared-workspace process preload as unused even though a real Node child and its workers execute it.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193662

prs.title: feat(release): publish Gateway beta MSIX and request stable Store approval
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway releases need automatic Windows packaging: signed GitHub prereleases for betas and release-manager-approved Microsoft Store updates for regular stable releases.

## User Impact

After upstream GitHub activation, both release entry points request the exact signed Gateway source:

- **Beta on npm `beta`:** packaging builds and signs the x64, ARM64, and bundle assets and publishes a GitHub prerelease, never Latest. It pins the published version and full source SHA, not the moving beta selector. It never requests Store publication.
- **Regular stable on npm `latest`:** packaging builds the Store bundle, then requests release-manager approval in `openclaw/releases`.
- Alpha, extended-stable, failed activation, and mismatched channel/tag combinations do not enter the intended handoff. MSIX work stays detached from npm/GitHub completion.

**Beta dependency:** merge [packaging #246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/pull/246) first so packaging `main` supports the beta dispatch contract.

**Stable cutover prerequisites remain:** land the central publisher and packaging request-only cutover; configure the release-manager environment/code-review controls and exclusive central Store federation. This PR applies none of those live settings. The existing release GitHub App (`2729701`, `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) needs Actions write and Contents read on core/packaging, plus releases for stable Store requests. Beta tokens exclude releases. **No new PAT or Store secret is needed.** Live installation grants remain unverified.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend one detached `Windows Gateway Release Request` rather than adding a second beta orchestrator. Beta dispatches packaging `gateway-msix.yml` on `main` with `release_channel=beta`, exact `gateway_version`, full-SHA `openclaw_ref`, `signing_mode=official`, and `publish_release=true`. Packaging retains all source/package authorization, upgrade checks, protected signing, and prerelease flags.

Stable retains exact payload/release-identity checks, post-wait authority validation, and the central `{product: gateway, run_id}` approval request. Replay and ambiguous-dispatch evidence remain recovery records; request acceptance is not publication success. Recover retained downstream runs rather than republishing npm or blindly redispatching.

Integrated current main while preserving the original PR head as a parent; no force push. Packaging #212 also combines cleanly with #246 (`git merge-tree`), so no restack or unrelated packaging edits were needed.

## Evidence

Head: `f4d7b24f899260e9f132b0e24773c2d75bda2f6e`.

- **38 focused tests passed:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/release-windows-gateway.test.ts test/scripts/release-publish-finalize.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Handoff: 31 tests / 98 ms; finalization: 7 tests / 4.683 s; wrapper wall time: 7.54 s. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available for this head.
- **Red before green:** five beta handoff/admission regressions failed against the prior stable-only implementation and pass with this change. Coverage retains exact-source stable approval, cancellation, replay, invalid provenance, expired artifacts, and ambiguous dispatch.
- Targeted TypeScript check, script/test/config lint, JavaScript syntax, formatting, LF checks, and base-relative whitespace checks passed.
- `pnpm check:workflows` passed: pinned actionlint, zizmor, generated CI-owner check, composite-input guard, and conflict-marker check. Used task-local Homebrew Python 3.14 / pre-commit 4.7.0.
- Fixed the previous test-budget CI failure using the current per-change allocation policy: 468 lines for the new handoff/admission regression suite; the shared scalar is unchanged. Staged budget against `14d9d554f7d04b0c036c543ff2c2b4592faf958c`: 6,513,096 lines <= 6,513,125 ceiling.
- Independent Codex AutoReview, **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, over the complete base-relative candidate at base `14d9d554f7d04b0c036c543ff2c2b4592faf958c`. Reviewed, signed-commit, and hosted source trees match. Assumes #246's documented beta contract; not live publishing proof.
- `pnpm deadcode:unused-files`: production scan passed with 0 entries. Full-tree scan failed on unchanged `src/node-host/node-worker-prepared-workspace.process.test-support.ts`; no owned handoff path was reported.
- Simplification: reused the existing request owner, removed the obsolete Store-only names, and kept Store credentials/approval exclusively in the central publisher. Full PR delta: 8 files, 1,013 insertions / 2 deletions against the reviewed base, including 468 test lines.
- **Unrun:** live App dispatch/denial, actual Windows builds/upgrades, Azure signing, GitHub asset publication, release-manager approval, tenant-federation cutover, and Store acceptance/certification. Prior ClawSweeper's live-proof request remains a deployment proof gap. No workflow was dispatched, nothing merged, and no live setting or credential was changed. New-head hosted CI/review are separate from local proof.

## Coordinated Store approval rollout

- [Central Store publisher: releases #48](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/pull/48)
- [Evidence-writer prerequisite: releases #47](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/pull/47)

prs.title: improve: install fewer dependencies for mobile releases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mobile release jobs install every workspace even though they only need root release helpers and the native asset workspaces.

## User Impact

No app behavior changes. iOS Store Release/TestFlight and Android Store Release/Internal should spend less time and bandwidth preparing Node dependencies. Local release commands and qualification keep their existing installation paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing frozen filtered-install pattern for Mermaid and native protocol generation. Pnpm retains root dependencies for root-owned helpers and skips unrelated workspaces. No dependency versions, lockfile, or cache policy change.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before measurement: run the committed `node scripts/bench-mobile-release-dependencies.mjs --samples 5` workload, interleaving full and filtered installs on the same source/lockfile. Separate empty-store and warm-store installs, always with absent `node_modules`; record package count, disk allocation, install and install-plus-consumer time, median/p95/range, and host load. Require identical generated Swift/Kotlin protocol and Mermaid assets, at least 25% fewer installed packages, at least 20% lower cold install-plus-consumer median, and no greater than 20% p95 regression in either store state.

Five interleaved full/filtered pairs per store state passed on macOS ARM64, Node 24.18.0, exact source `4c5900caad62240b0cae65bd63dc5f43d667d71a` and the unchanged root lockfile. All 20 installs produced identical Swift/Kotlin protocol and Mermaid outputs. Package counts were 1,479 → 985 (33.4% fewer); cold root dependency allocation was 2,844 → 927 MiB (67.4% lower).

Times in seconds; five samples per cell, so nearest-rank p95 is the maximum:

| Workload | Full median / p95 (range) | Filtered median / p95 (range) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold install | 22.47 / 23.69 (20.50–23.69) | 14.67 / 15.37 (14.02–15.37) |
| Cold install + consumers | 24.84 / 26.14 (22.79–26.14) | 17.28 / 17.81 (16.34–17.81) |
| Warm install | 4.63 / 5.42 (4.38–5.42) | 3.00 / 3.30 (2.90–3.30) |
| Warm install + consumers | 7.03 / 8.08 (6.71–8.08) | 5.32 / 5.74 (5.21–5.74) |

Cold install-plus-consumer median improved 30.4%; warm improved 24.3%. No measured metric regressed. One-minute host load ranged 3.60–9.75 on 10 logical CPUs; the workload records load and free memory for each sample. Installation timing excludes checkout and benchmark cleanup, and consumer timing includes release-tool imports, both version helpers, Android i18n, deterministic native protocol generation, and Mermaid generation. This measures dependency preparation, not the entire release job.

- [Nonpublishing Linux/macOS proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42130121890) passed with the release-pinned Node 24.22.1. It installed the exact candidate, bridged dependencies into a detached source worktree, and exercised the release consumers there. The temporary proof branch was removed; its workflow is excluded from this PR.
- All required `ci-workflow*.test.ts`, Swift cache lifetime, native test launch, and mobile release CLI/CI suites passed through the repository wrapper (two shards). Workflow validation (actionlint/zizmor), targeted lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Complete local ClawSweeper review of `439d6eb82e28a2ef898c96e3688082b540ccc952..4c5900caad62240b0cae65bd63dc5f43d667d71a` found no actionable correctness or security defects. Independent precommit review was also completed.

The implementation adds 33 release/config lines plus the documented measurement workload; no tests, pins, lockfile, permissions, or caches change. No signed native archive, model/store API call, or upload was part of this validation. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42131109854) and the final aggregate/security gates passed: 50 successful checks, no failed or pending checks (54 skipped and one neutral). The automated ClawSweeper review also found no actionable issues. This PR remains ready and unmerged; no merge is requested by this task.

prs.title: fix(infra): resolve the Windows system encoding probe under SystemRoot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #193785. On Windows, the read tool decodes legacy ANSI text files using the system code page. `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts` finds that code page by spawning bare `powershell.exe`, so it depends on PATH. When PATH omits the Windows PowerShell directory, the probe fails and the failure is cached as `null`. Every non-UTF-8 text file is then decoded as UTF-8 with replacement characters, silently, with no setup error.

## User Impact

Windows callers with a reduced PATH (services, sandboxes, scrubbed environments) read their legacy text files correctly again. Normal-PATH behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The console-encoding probe in the same file already spawns `cmd.exe` through the install-root helper (`getWindowsCmdExePath`). The system-encoding probe now does the same with `getWindowsPowerShellExePath()`, which resolves `<SystemRoot>\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`. The probe arguments, timeout, caching and UTF-8 fallback are unchanged.

## Evidence

Local live run on Windows 11 with Node 26.12.1 and system ANSI code page 936 (GBK). The on-disk `ansi.txt` holds the bytes `c4 e3 ba c3 0a` (GBK `你好\n`). Each row is a fresh process calling the real `createReadTool(dir).execute("proof", { path })`, with no mocks. The reduced PATH points at an empty directory, and SystemRoot is kept.

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/193785/proof-193785.png)

| Code | PATH | read result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main 589214a | normal | `你好\n` |
| main 589214a | empty dir (no PowerShell) | `���\n` |
| this PR 32ab4ac | normal | `你好\n` |
| this PR 32ab4ac | empty dir (no PowerShell) | `你好\n` |

Tests and gates:

- `windows-encoding.test.ts` now asserts that both probes spawn absolute executables. That test fails on main and passes here (17/17).
- These also pass: oxfmt, oxlint, the line-cap ratchet, the test-lines ratchet and assertion-safety.

prs.title: fix(apps): scope global usage across configured agents
prs.body:
Related: #126360

## What Problem This Solves

The native iOS and macOS Usage views request global cost totals. On a Gateway with multiple explicitly owned agents, omitting the scope sends the request through implicit agent selection, where the ownerless `main` key is rejected.

## User Impact

Both native Usage views request totals across configured agents. The existing Gateway access check still applies before scope selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set `agentScope: "all"` in the existing native request builders, including the iOS fallback serialization path. This matches the scope of the view and preserves its date and time zone parameters. The related investigation in #153968 identified the same native request gap.

## Evidence

- Compiled the original iOS and macOS request builders and sent their serialized payloads over WebSocket to an isolated Gateway configured with two explicitly owned agents. Both received the ownerless `main` error. Adding only the all-agent scope made both requests succeed. [Baseline run](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/41794902925)
- Compiled the patched builders. Nine Swift tests and three Gateway tests passed. Both captured native payloads returned totals, and removing their scope reproduced the original error. The tests also check the date and time zone parameters. [Candidate run](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/41795993771)
- SwiftFormat, SwiftLint and `git diff --check` passed for the four changed files. [Static checks](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/41796094954)

The runtime proof covers the compiled request builders and real Gateway RPC. Simulator and device UI were outside that test scope.

prs.title: fix: stop goal continuation while awaiting a human decision
prs.body:
Related: #192625

## What Problem This Solves

Active Goals can repeatedly ask for the same authorization because the agent has no immediate way to record a required human-decision wait.

## User Impact

Agents can stop automatic Goal continuation immediately while preserving the unfinished objective, identity, budget, and usage. An operator explicitly resumes the same Goal after the decision; resume itself does not authorize the pending action.

## Why This Change Was Made

`update_goal` accepts `waiting_on_human` with a required decision note and persists it through the existing Core owner as `blocked` with a `Waiting on human:` note. Existing settlement and stale-nudge admission already require `active`. Identical wait retries preserve the recorded wait; paused, completed, limited, and differently blocked Goals cannot be overwritten. A missing note is recoverable input validation, so the model can correct its call instead of being incorrectly told that no active Goal needs updating.

This retains the existing store, persisted format, continuation checks, and operator-resume owner. Ordinary blockers retain their three-turn rule. The immediate required-human-decision exception is an explicit policy change for upstream maintainer review before merge.

The Codex Goal-tool projection fix is already on main via #175918. This PR addresses the immediate human-wait handoff only. Release/backport selection and fail-closed continuation when Goal tools are explicitly denied remain outside this change, so it does not close #192625.

## Evidence

Validated source tree `beea2b661e5e843f4b0170ec81aed4482b33babe`, published as `c0a6f3bf4d4b8052aa8b678d227472ffc22c0e9f`:

- **Typechecking: passed.** The focused tsgo project includes all changed production/test modules, the native live-test file, and the repository ambient declarations. The previously reported four diagnostics disappear with the lockfile-matched dependencies. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` used the repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 and existing fs-safe 0.27.0 allowance; no dependency, lockfile, or release-age rule changes.
- **Runtime build: passed**, 252.4s, including Gateway runtime, bundled plugin assets and Control UI assets. The targeted type-aware oxlint wrapper also prepared the Plugin SDK declaration boundary successfully.
- **Goal tools: 14 passed**, 105.25s including cold compilation. The missing-note correction regression fails on the previous implementation and passes after the repair; it verifies that a corrected call persists the blocker. Existing focused Goal store, Gateway, inbound/continuation, Codex projection, and prefix-stability results remain applicable to their unchanged contracts (196 checks on the previous candidate).
- **Real native Codex/Gateway proof: passed**, 53.94s test time, 221.23s including setup. The model itself records the wait through the Core tool, automatic continuation remains at zero, unrelated chat keeps the Goal blocked, and explicit Resume completes the same Goal. History preservation and duplicate-Resume replay are also verified. The test uses an isolated Gateway, temporary state/home, existing Codex login, and synthetic content. The unchanged operator-pause variant was filtered out for this focused run.
- **Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, diff whitespace, and test-line ratchet: passed.** The 170-line allocation covers the persisted wait, recoverable input, Gateway stop/resume, and real-model wait variant. CI timing is pending.

Terminal capture from the real run (synthetic IDs omitted):

```text
PASS resumes the same local Codex Goal after a human-decision wait through the public RPC
modelRecordedWait=true
continuationTurnsBeforeResume=0
unrelatedMessageKeptBlocked=true
followedEditedObjective=true
preservedHistory=true
completed=true
replayedWithoutNewRun=true
```

Reproduce with an available native model and existing Codex login:

```sh
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_GOAL_RESUME=1 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_MODEL='openai/<available-model>' \
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-live.mts \
  test/gateway-local-codex-goal-resume.live.test.ts -t human-decision
```

The live run selected an empty scratch OpenClaw source state through `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, so it staged only native Codex login rather than reading an older operator agent database. No production Gateway, sessions, configuration, approvals, or Goal state were changed. Release-upgrade and worker-placement live scenarios are not claimed.

Local autoreview (Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, medium; P0–P2) assessed the complete candidate against `42c1bd69a1ae580445ff9b5981a8836582e4b0cc`. Its only finding concerned the old indexed missing-note path; it explicitly verified that the working-tree repair addresses that finding and identified no additional P0–P2 defects. That repaired tree is now staged and published. The hosted review's P2 recovery finding is covered by the red/green regression above; the requested real-agent proof is supplied here. The simplification pass reuses existing owners and the existing native live-test fixture; no scheduler, state machine, protocol status, or mock-only seam was added.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): support thread-bound subagent sessions
prs.body:
Closes #192610

## What Problem This Solves

An agent answering a Mattermost post cannot hand work to a sub-agent in its own thread: `sessions_spawn` with `thread: true` is rejected on Mattermost, which only Discord and Matrix support today.

## User Impact

User impact: on Mattermost, `sessions_spawn({ thread: true, mode: "session" })` now opens a thread under the post that asked for the work, binds it to the new sub-agent, and the sub-agent starts posting there at once. Later posts in that thread reach the sub-agent (no mention needed) until it ends, `/session unbind`, or the idle / max-age limit. `channels.mattermost.threadBindings` (and per-account) take the shared `enabled`, `idleHours`, `maxAgeHours`, `spawnSessions` and `defaultSpawnContext` keys. Nothing changes for deployments that never spawn with `thread: true`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mattermost threads grow from a post, so the natural thread for the worker is the asker's own post. The spawn context already knows the triggering message (`currentMessageId`), so core now passes it to the channel adapter as an optional `sourceMessageId` on the `child`-placement bind input (subagent and ACP spawns). No other adapter reads it; Discord and Matrix are unchanged.

The Mattermost plugin registers a `child`-only session-binding adapter, like Matrix: bindings persist in plugin state and reload on monitor restart, a sweeper ends them at idle / max-age with a farewell post, a `subagent_ended` hook unbinds them, and inbound routing sends posts in a bound thread to the bound session.

`thread: true` must never hand the current conversation to the worker. The asker's post becomes the root only when the requester's conversation is the channel itself (default `replyToMode: "off"`, top-level post) and the post is a live top-level post in that channel. If the requester already lives in that thread (post inside a thread, `replyToMode` `first`/`all`/`batched`, threaded DMs), the plugin posts a new root post titled with the spawn label and binds that thread, as Matrix does. Flat DMs reject `thread: true` with an actionable error.

If the binding store cannot open, the Mattermost monitor logs `mattermost: thread bindings unavailable: …` and keeps serving posts; `thread: true` spawns are then rejected as today.

## Evidence

**Live e2e** on a throwaway Mattermost 11.7.12 + Postgres in Docker (127.0.0.1 only), an isolated test Gateway built from this branch (`OPENCLAW_HOME` under /tmp, `env -i`), and `openclaw qa mock-openai` as the model. A tester user posts in a channel and the mock model calls `sessions_spawn` with `thread: true, mode: "session"`. Config: `chatmode: "onmessage"`, no `threadBindings` overrides (defaults).

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A. `replyToMode: "off"`, top-level post | Thread opened under the asker's post (thread root == asker post id), child posted `CHILDOK` there unprompted, follow-up in the thread answered by `agent:main:subagent:…` |
| B. `replyToMode: "first"` (the asker's post already routes to its own thread session) | New root post `🤖 research` in the channel, bound thread under it; the asker's thread is left to the requester; follow-up answered by the child |
| B2. `/session unbind` in the bound thread | Farewell + `✅ Conversation unbound.`; the next post goes to the ordinary thread session (`…:thread:<root>`) |
| C. `/agents` from the requester's session | `1. agentscheck (binding:<thread root>)` |

The extra top-level `CHILDOK"` posts are the parent session's own mock reply after the tool call (the mock echoes the prompt), not the child.

## What Problem This Solves

Bundled Codex binding guards and Telegram approval routing still select deprecated synchronous persistence adapters.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex retains the existing host's prepared binding inspection across awaited policy checks, validates ownership synchronously before execution and disposes the lease on every exit. An additive export on the existing inspection entrypoint exposes that owner without adding a new state store or widening authority. Telegram uses the existing async capability factory and nativeAsync routing surface.

## Evidence

Fresh independent review and selected local autoreview found no actionable defects after repairing an async snapshot gap. Native commit hooks, the line-cap ratchet and git diff --check passed.

Two new rows in the existing node-binding matrix cover policy changing during preparation and binding changing during the final policy check. Existing Codex claim/detach and Telegram approval tests retain their assertions; a shared fixture prevents growth of the oversized suite. Migration docs cover inspection disposal.

Local dependency-backed execution was not run because native worktree creation refused an escaping workspace dependency link. Draft pending exact-head CI build and affected tests/type/lint/format proof. Full SDK declaration/API-diff proof remains pending; CI artifact builds alone do not prove declaration emission.

This covers the changed SDK declaration/API contract; the separate package/dist declaration writer was not executed and no packaging or release claim is made.

prs.title: fix: enable dictation for session-scoped guests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-scoped guests could send chat messages but could not dictate them. The microphone depended on operator-wide catalog/config access; recording and transcript delivery also required operator privileges.

## User Impact

Guests can dictate into chats they are authorized to write, including starting from the New Session composer. Transcripts remain editable drafts until explicitly sent. Voice settings and conversational Talk remain restricted; no broader guest role permissions or new configuration options are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse session authorization for a minimal transcription-readiness projection and transcription-only sessions. Keep provider/model overrides and full settings restricted.
- Bind recordings to the authorized session and originating connection. Retain that authority for the relay lifetime and recheck it before provider audio, finalization, readiness, and transcript delivery; revoke and clean up together.
- Carry the same live-authority check into the shared provider WebSocket transport. Recheck after asynchronous connection setup and at actual writes and graceful finalization, so queued/reconnected audio cannot outlive its authorization. Discard and revoked cleanup abort without invoking provider finalization. The callback is optional, preserving existing callers without it.
- Prepare a normal session for new-chat dictation and reuse it for the first send, rather than falling back to a shared session or creating a second chat.
- Preserve the prepared target and message idempotency key through interruption. Terminal timeout/error acknowledgments enter the existing persisted failed-message recovery path instead of being reported as accepted.
- Preserve typed speech-provider configuration and existing exports in catalog test mocks; adapt operator-only catalog tests to explicit read authority. Resolve the upstream provider-context import migration without changing the reviewed dictation behavior.

## Evidence

- Guest admission and UI regressions fail on the base and pass with the fix. Additional red/green proof covers provider audio after backing-session deletion, revoked relay finalization, and persisted initial-turn recovery.
- Real Gateway/provider-wire regression was red on `f9b01e4`: explicit discard sent `audio.done`, and reconnect-buffered audio reached the vendor after backing-session deletion. Both now pass, with authorized audio and normal finalization as positive controls and ordered socket-close barriers rather than sleep-based absence checks.
- A real WebSocket regression also proves authority is rechecked after asynchronous credentials resolve, before opening the provider connection. Shared transport: 26 tests passed. Bundled OpenAI, xAI, Mistral, and ElevenLabs provider compatibility: 4 files, 62 tests passed.
- Backend siblings: 3 suites, 20 tests passed, including real authenticated Gateway WebSocket admission and a real multipart HTTP file-transcription sibling with synthetic providers. Together with the new provider-wire case, the final transport repair passed 109 targeted tests.
- Catalog compatibility: 4 suites, 113 tests passed. Initial-turn recovery: 3 suites, 34 tests passed. Complete browser dictation suite: 12 tests passed, including guest-only and mixed read/write authority; those unchanged paths retain their earlier proof.
- Fresh incremental repair review found no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings in its supplied diff. Its unchanged-source and test-execution limitations are not treated as a full clean certificate; the author inspected the owning lifecycle and bundled callers and ran the boundary tests separately. Earlier lifetime-authority, audio-admission, terminal-ack, and provider-flush/finalization findings were addressed.
- Core source, affected core-test graphs, and UI TypeScript checks pass. Changed-file formatting/lint and diff checks pass. Stale max-lines/assertion allowances were removed; mock-export and test-line ratchets pass.
- The separate 1,465-line test allocation records exactly the measured net regression growth, including 259 added lines for the real provider-wire and asynchronous-connection regressions. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged.
- A prior-head Bun permission-picker focus assertion failed once. The focused six-test replay passed without changes, but did not establish inheritance or a fix. Full CI subsequently passed at `f9b01e4`.
- Final head `d93012e1c5ebfd8ef50a0699d3547d2735cbdd84`: 95 successful checks, 73 skipped, 1 neutral, none failed or pending, including [the CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42131955861). Five CodeQL jobs initially failed during result upload; all cleared after retrying only the failed jobs on the same head, without source changes or gate exceptions.
- [Current-head ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193658#issuecomment-6666229145) reports **Findings: None** and `review-state:ready`; [re-review completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193658#issuecomment-6672103838) is confirmed.

[Before/after screenshots and editable-transcript proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193658#issuecomment-6665731560).

No live server configuration was changed, and paid speech-to-text providers were not exercised. Browser audio and provider transcripts use deterministic fixtures; Gateway, provider WebSocket, and multipart HTTP boundaries are real local transports.

## What Problem This Solves

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

prs.title: fix: personal memory hooks miss authenticated webchat users
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal-memory hooks receiving no user identity for authenticated Control UI turns, causing integrations such as Honcho to fall back to an owner peer even when the transcript identifies a different person.

## User Impact

Hooks can observe the verified initiating user for each accepted UI turn, including successive turns by different people in one shared session. This does not add command, tool, or MCP permissions. Expired personal bindings skip hook dispatch or discard returned enrichment instead of becoming anonymous owner turns.

Attribution remains per accepted initiating turn; this does not add separate authorship for every coauthor merged through steering. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI intentionally omits the legacy transport sender to preserve authority boundaries. The fix carries a live, host-bound profile observation through the existing run projections solely for hook context. Dispatch rechecks it before invoking a plugin and before accepting returned results, including cached contexts and delegated ingress. The private observer reads in the captured ingress async context, so a later agent tool context does not misclassify the original human request. Live grant checks still run on every read; plugin callbacks never run in that captured context. Existing channel senders retain precedence, and the private resolver is removed before plugin delivery.

An existing pure finalize-result merger is moved unchanged to keep the edited hook runner within the repository line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against the original Gateway turn preparation path: an authenticated profile was recorded, but the hook sender was undefined.
- Eight focused test files initially passed (248 tests); the final Gateway/requester/hook bundle passed **175 tests** after adding the real agent-context regressions, covering Gateway identity, prepared-run projections, CLI/embedded hook consumers, prefix stability, profile switches, delegated revocation/abort, copied bindings, cached contexts, and revocation while handlers resolve or reject.
- Native core production typecheck and both unused-file inventories passed; the extracted helper is reachable. Diff, format, line-cap, and safety-assertion checks passed.
- Independent source/security review and simplification pass completed; the material revocation and claiming-hook findings were fixed. The finalize-merger extraction was also compared byte for byte after dedenting. Optional autoreview/ClawSweeper tools are not installed on this contributor host.
- Clean native build: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build` passed on Node 24.22.1, including runtime, SDK declarations, Control UI assets and native import/export checks.

A synthetic probe plugin selected the correct personal marker for each model answer; both lookup and `agent_end` received the correct initiating profile.
