prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: fix(runtime): merged Windows env blocks lose PATH entries from differently cased keys
prs.body:
Addresses the `withNodeRuntimePath` duplicate Windows PATH spelling item of #184894.

## What Problem This Solves

A direct call to `withNodeRuntimePath` with both `PATH` and `Path` retains directories only from the first spelling. This proposal concatenates both values before prepending the selected Node runtime.

## User Impact and Open Decision

If differently cased values reach this helper in a production Windows lifecycle, concatenation would retain both lists. That production scenario has not been demonstrated: review notes that the normal spawn caller normalizes duplicate aliases first, and that first-key precedence may be an intentional contract. This PR is a draft until a maintainer decides whether that behavior should change and a relevant Windows flow is demonstrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper currently sorts PATH-keyed variables, reads the first value, and writes it to every spelling. The proposed change instead concatenates the values, retaining the first spelling's order and removing the duplicate runtime entry. Single-key behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- The added helper regression fails on the unpatched base for the dual-spelling input and passes with this change; single-key, duplicate-entry, and no-PATH cases remain unchanged.
- `pnpm test src/process/exec-spawn.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-node-runtime.test.ts src/infra/node-options.test.ts` passed. The lifecycle script test failed identically on the base because the pinned Bun fork could not be staged locally.
- The changed-file typecheck and lint lanes passed; the broader check reported pre-existing unused exports outside this diff.
- No shipped Windows update or recovery path was exercised. The macOS host cannot establish whether duplicate aliases reach this helper or whether combining them is the intended product behavior.

prs.title: fix(gateway): clarify unchanged pull request publication receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a worktree publication found the attributed workspace tree already on its open PR, the transcript said “Published”. An agent could reasonably infer that a new push had started CI.

## User Impact

For confirmed reuse, the receipt and transcript identify the existing PR and explain that the request did not push a commit or trigger CI. Other successful notices give the PR destination. Older clients keep their previous receipt shape. In-process tools and clients advertising `github-publication-unchanged` can read the optional `unchanged: true` field.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receipt uses the recorded source and published heads together with the available effect evidence. A personal account can record an existing-PR lookup as an observation. An interrupted push with different heads cannot qualify solely because its effect is absent. When the record cannot distinguish queued reuse from recovery, the transcript uses neutral wording. Publication execution and database schemas are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the existing-PR, transcript and protocol suites each failed their new assertion. On the final source, four focused suites passed 67/67. The real-Git reuse test checks the PR, commit and push count.
- Four additional Gateway readiness tests passed, covering the legacy client, capability-aware client and in-process agent tool. The published 2026.10.6 validator accepts the legacy shape and rejects the new field without negotiation.
- Changed-file checks passed for all 17 paths, including TypeScript, lint and formatting. Commit hooks and native protocol determinism checks passed against the pinned upstream base. Independent uncommitted review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Six of seven supplemental consumer cases passed. The repository-mode action fixture failed before invoking its handler because Git for Windows rejects the fixture’s existing `//./nul` configuration path. The worktree-mode counterpart passed.



## Follow-up validation on 88ea2d4a

Robo appended the budget repair to this PR. GitHub records the push actor and primary commit author as roboclaw-bot, and links the human coauthor to MertBasar0. The commit changes only the existing readiness test file. Its 34 cases are retained while repeated setup and assertions reduce the file by 51 lines.

- The exact prior CI merge fails at 6,469,966 lines against 6,469,918. Applying the correction to that same merge passes at 6,469,915. The full Linux readiness suite passed, as did 19 selected Windows cases and the formatter. The full Windows run encountered the existing open-SQLite-file rename scenario.
- The actual updated PR CI passed the budget check at 6,473,447 against 6,473,484, leaving 37 lines. [Budget job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41920518177/job/126892104549)
- Independent uncommitted review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the exact test delta.
- The remaining two UI E2E jobs contain four failing test cases whose names and errors exactly match the pre-existing base-run failures. [Updated CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41920518177), [comparison base CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41886748971)

### Real unchanged publication on the deployed Team Gateway

Robo made a new native publication request on its original test session for [#192980](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192980). Distinct first and second receipts returned the same PR, branch and full head 3910a0e1dc1b571b2062c8bad8abbe910b7a7102. The second conversation notice was recorded at 2026-11-04 22:01:11.385 UTC.

Before/after GitHub observations bracket that event from 21:26:59 to 22:02:13 UTC. All 25 branch Actions run IDs and attempts, 25 head-specific run records, 36 check-suite IDs, and 95 check-run IDs/start times are identical. Forty-eight intermediate polls recorded no ref or run-set change. GitHub repository activity shows only the initial branch creation at 19:58:46 UTC. No second branch-changing push or CI rerun was recorded.

The deployed Team version still returns the generic Published notice and omits the new flag. This capture proves the real unchanged-publication condition and reproduces the ambiguous notice. The patched isolated Gateway capture is described separately below.

### Patched Gateway entry-point capture

Built and ran the exact corrected head 88ea2d4ad2c373bda2b06068ceac5665ac441dca in an isolated Gateway. A real model used native github_publish to prepare the existing PR and then made one fresh publication request. The external Git/GitHub transport guard recorded zero write attempts. The native receipt returned published with unchanged: true for the same PR and full head.

The Gateway-authored transcript at 2026-11-04 22:16:56.779 UTC said:

> Reused the existing pull request for openclaw/openclaw branch fix/github-publication-unchanged-receipt: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192940. No new commit was pushed or CI run triggered by this request. Using @MertBasar0 (System).

This reuse probe used the local authenticated MertBasar0 publisher with writes blocked. The preceding correction commit and real fork push were made by roboclaw-bot, with MertBasar0 co-authorship.

Immediate observations at 22:15:41 and 22:17:18 UTC have identical remote head/tree, all 60 branch workflow run records and all 15 exact-head run records including run_attempt, and all 17 check-suite IDs. Existing workflows continued creating jobs, so individual check counts increased from 137 to 140; this is not asserted to be a frozen job inventory.

The released 2026.10.10 client connected without the new capability and its public compiled validator accepted the legacy receipt shape. A real client from the corrected PR connected with github-publication-unchanged and its public validator accepted unchanged: true. Both read the exact same publication request through sessions.github.readiness.

The separate maintainer decision requested for the negotiated public receipt field remains open.

## Conflict-resolution update — pinned main 3e3e2c2f

- Native base refresh integrated `3e3e2c2ff9db412ceed4fdf4a13ede616e1488f8` without flattening upstream ancestry. Merge commit `86d8811bdee9e0e376d077117d1e5d46f85492a5` has parents `88ea2d4ad2c373bda2b06068ceac5665ac441dca` and that pinned main commit. Published head: `12920a85f5f6480c99721fef51ea5ee0f5297fbc`; exact reviewed tree: `5c57c10820b0a2e111d4326cbe82ff7a641909fd`.
- Only the two reported conflict files were resolved from the reviewed transfer: generated protocol predicates and `sessions-github-readiness.test.ts`. The resulting patch against pinned main remains 17 files. Remote Git readback verified the full tree, both resolution blobs, both merge parents, and roboclaw-bot authorship plus MertBasar0 co-authorship on both new commits.
- Operator-supplied validation for this exact tree: 104/104 focused tests; TypeScript, typed lint, formatter, canonical generator check and whitespace checks passed; independent uncommitted Auto Review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Test-line ratchet: 6,509,716 / 6,509,808, with 92 lines of headroom and net eight fewer test lines; no allowance or baseline change.
- Earlier live behavior and compatibility proof above remains prior-head evidence, not a new after-merge runtime capture. New-head hosted CI is separate and is not claimed green here. The maintainer product decision on the negotiated public receipt field remains open.

Declare the existing runtime defaults in both Knowledge configuration schema sources so the schema-driven Control UI can display them. This is a metadata correction, not a change to runtime permissions or generic form behavior.

prs.title: improve: rank Control UI CPU costs across census flows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI census measures individual flows but cannot rank small, recurring CPU costs across them.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The existing benchmark can now emit source-mapped function and file self-time rankings, grouped by flow and owner. No application code, dependency, startup asset, or performance budget changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add Chromium-only `--cpu-profile` to the existing engine harness, reusing its measurement and source-map owners. Aggregate leaf samples once; retain native, GC, dependency, automation and unmapped costs. Report the leading V8 `(program)` profiler initialization interval separately, since the harness awaits profiler startup before running the action. Admit a profile only after capture and cleanup succeed.

Repair stale route and responsive data-page controls in the same harness: Portal, Search, Devices, Cloud environments, Dashboard sort, Logs and Usage. Keep result and request assertions; use the current native controls on both viewport sizes.

This is the scoped Solid migration cross-flow CPU investigation. **No function above 2% has a clean fix.** All 688/688 selected synthetic capture cells pass at Chromium 1×/6× after driver repairs; 31 failed historical attempts were recaptured successfully. The largest app frame is `DraftPlaceState.agents`, below 1% at both rates. Only unattributed browser/native `(program)` exceeds 2%; Solid removal/recomputation did not expose a redundant app operation. No dependency patches or caches were added. Evaluated JavaScript with source positions but no source URL remains explicitly unmapped; file totals keep that category separate from native browser frames.

| Capture | Successful cells | Active sampled ms | Largest application frame | Solid share |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Chromium 1× | 344 | 43128.239 | `agents` 0.865% (90 cells) | 12.85% |
| Chromium 6× | 344 | 290267.880 | `agents` 0.662% (78 cells) | 13.62% |

A single profile identifies costs, not timing gains. No application optimization qualified, so no 20-pair/A–A or WebKit comparative speedup is claimed. The separate-rate rankings retain browser/GC, dependencies and unmapped samples; pooled rankings weight longer/throttled workloads.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Production `pnpm ui:build` and strict `pnpm ui:check-performance` | Pass on `d0b0fc80a34d`; startup 90,561 B gzip, 1 CSS request |
| Frozen production build | 4,768 SHA-256 file hashes unchanged |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, tooling test typecheck | Pass |
| `pnpm test test/scripts/control-ui-cold-load-trace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 21 passed |
| Targeted lint/format and `git diff --check` | Pass |
| Production Knip | Pass |
| Independent Codex autoreview | P0–P2 scoped-clean across collector, initialization correction, and responsive-driver commits; earlier capture-admission finding fixed |

prs.title: fix(update): repair refuses forever when plugin files, config or snapshots changed after the update
prs.body:
Related: #193632, #193132

#193632 has landed (`351af32a`) and is merged into this branch, so the diff now contains only this PR's changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` still fails on every attempt when a plugin's package files, a config file the update wrote, or a plugin's source snapshot changed after the update.

## User Impact

User impact: repair finishes the plugin rollback in these cases too. It keeps the newer files or snapshot, restores everything that still matches, and lists what it kept in the same update warning that repair, `openclaw doctor` and the update report show.

## Why This Change Was Made

#193632 made rollback keep a later plugin migration obligation or install record instead of refusing. Three related checks still refused, and like the earlier ones they wrote nothing before refusing:

- **Package files.** During settlement, `artifactUnchanged` replaces the throwing `assertArtifact`. A payload that a later writer replaced, or an originally absent one that now exists, keeps that plugin's current index entry. So does a missing retained or published artifact entry. Retention markers for those payloads are left alone. The begin-time check still throws, because that path is not a rollback.
- **Config files.** `restorePluginCohortConfigPublication` now returns false when a later writer changed what the publication wrote. Before, its own conflict check threw "Configuration changed after update publication". Settlement keeps that file and moves on.
- **Source snapshots.** If a later writer changed a plugin's source snapshot, settlement keeps that plugin's whole index entry, record and snapshot together, so they can't disagree. `listLaterPluginSourceSnapshotChanges` uses the same comparison as the restore.

These still refuse on purpose:

- config path identity guards, because they protect the write target itself
- SecretRef preflight and config validation failures
- corrupt publication chains, which are journal corruption rather than a later writer

## Evidence

Red on #193632's head `53d4e682e068`, with real install-index files and SQLite:

- `src/plugins/update-cohort-recovery.test.ts`: three cases fail.
  - The snapshot successor fails with "Plugin fixture source snapshot changed after the update".
  - Later package files and a later payload at the originally absent path fail with "Plugin cohort artifact changed".
- `src/infra/update-plugin-cohort-recovery.test.ts`: the config tests fail on the new restored/kept return value. In the same test, a later edit to the publication's own leaf used to throw "Configuration changed after update publication".

Green on this head:

- Both files pass (17 and 16 tests).
- In each kept case, the later value stays, the cohort is deleted, and the update run's warning names the kept item.
- Negative controls:
  - in the package-files case, a second plugin's matching record is restored
  - the config test restores a matching file to its original bytes before the later edit
  - the other snapshot modes restore the original snapshot
- Rewritten instead of deleted:
  - the old record/artifact/chain conflict test is now the chain-only refusal plus a keep case, and the artifact case moved into that keep case
  - the snapshot successor and later-payload cases now assert the kept outcome
- The config path-identity cases still assert refusal.

`node scripts/test-projects.mts` across those two files, plus `src/plugins/update-cohort.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-command.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-handoff.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugin-cohort-handoff.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-plugin-cohort-commit.process.test.ts` and `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-rollback.test.ts`: 127 passed.

Format check passes, `lint:core` has no findings in the touched files, and the import cycle check is clean. Locally, `tsrs` on core and the infra and plugins-platform test shards shows only the existing `packages/ai` error. The test-line allocation matches the 325 lines this PR adds against current main.



After merging #193632's current head, which includes #193132, one repair settlement test needed a new route. It used to reach a half-finished rollback through a config conflict, and a later config edit no longer stops rollback. The test now interrupts the config restore once, after the migration rows were restored, and checks that the verified candidate still finishes the rollback. Disabling the "already restored" check makes it fail. A separate case checks that rollback keeps a later config edit and names the file in the warning. `src/cli/update-cli/update-plugin-cohort-settlement.test.ts` passes 12/12, and the related suites pass with 139 tests.


Review follow-up:

- **Snapshots by installation owner.** `listLaterPluginSourceSnapshotChanges` now returns the later snapshot changes themselves, and they are matched to install-record keys by recorded installation owner. A later `demo` snapshot under the `package-owner` installation used to let that record roll back to its original. Now the record is kept along with the snapshot. The test covers a later record and a later snapshot in the `demo` / `package-owner` shape, with intact payloads so only the later state can stop the restore. It was red before the fix and is green after (19/19).
- **Kept config survives a resumed repair.** A kept config file is now written to the run's `warning:plugin-cohort:later-changes-kept` step before settlement counts it. Every later write merges with the items already recorded instead of replacing them. If the run's history was pruned, settlement still completes. New test: a config edit is kept, then settlement is interrupted after counting the file. Before the fix the next repair reported no warning; now it reports the config file. The helpers moved to `src/plugins/update-cohort-kept-changes.ts`, which keeps the cohort owner under the line limit.
- **Invalid config still refuses.** Autoreview caught that the invalid-config check had been routed through the "later edit" path. A config file that no longer validates now refuses with "Configuration is invalid after update publication", and repair stays pending. Test: red before, green after.
- **Docs.** The npm plugin rollback section also covers package files, source snapshots and config files. It says recovery still stops for a replaced config path, config that fails validation or secret resolution, and a corrupt recovery journal.
- **Stored data.** The released-row compatibility test from #193632 also passes on this branch. This PR adds no stored field. A kept config file is recorded only in the existing update-run warning step.
- **Checks.** Related suites pass with 153 tests. The settlement file is now 15/15 and the config recovery file 16/16. Format, docs MDX, lint on touched files, import cycles and `tsrs` (apart from the existing `packages/ai` error) are clean. Autoreview at P2 is clean after the invalid-config fix.


Second review follow-up:

- **Malformed included config.** An included file edited into malformed JSON5 produces an invalid snapshot with no include provenance. The ownership check used to treat that as a later edit, and settlement kept it. Validity is now checked before ownership is classified, and the restore refuses with "Configuration is invalid after update publication". New test in `src/infra/update-plugin-cohort-recovery.test.ts` with a real `gateway.json5` include: red ("resolved false") before the fix, green after.
- **Kept install records, snapshots and package files on a resumed repair.** Autoreview suggested recording these before settlement advances, the same way config is handled. They don't need that. Settlement recomputes these items from the current index on every attempt, independent of `settledPublications`. A probe interrupted settlement after all three publications were counted, and the resumed repair still reported the kept install record or package files. Config is different because a counted config file is never revisited.
- **Checks.** Related suites pass with 155 tests. Lint on the touched files, import cycles, format, docs MDX and `tsrs` (apart from the existing `packages/ai` error) are clean.


Third review follow-up:

- **Several plugins under one installation.** A package can expose more than one plugin, such as `pack/a` and `pack/b`, under one install owner. When a later writer refreshed only `pack/a`'s snapshot, settlement kept the installation's record but left `pack/b` queued for its old snapshot. The installed-index owner then rejected that with "Plugin pack/b source snapshot restoration no longer matches its install record". A kept installation now drops every snapshot restoration it owns. New test with a real two-entry npm package: red with that error before the fix, green after. The installation-owner tests moved to `src/plugins/update-cohort-recovery.owner.test.ts`, with shared fixtures in `update-cohort-recovery.test-support.ts`, to keep the main test file under its line cap.
- **`update-cli.already-current` CI failure.** "ends unfinished retention at --timeout with the installed package untouched" fails the same way on current `main` (`071ea8338d93`), 3 of 3 local runs, as on this branch, 3 of 3. It isn't caused by this PR.
- **Test-line ratchet.** CI reported "over by: 89" against an older ratchet base. Against current main, the allocation equals this PR's net added lines and the ratchet passes with main's own slack.
- **Checks.** Related suites pass with 156 tests. Lint on the touched files, the line-cap ratchet, import cycles and `tsrs` (apart from the existing `packages/ai` error) are clean. Autoreview at P2 is clean.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes extra Apps-page chrome, blank space above the conversation, generic icons, and a stale composer binding when opening an MCP App beside chat.

## User Impact

Users can open a plugin entrypoint, inspect its App beside chat, and add selections to a working composer with the App’s supplied icon. The visible “App context” heading is removed.

The existing chat pane now owns the embedded conversation within the shell layout boundary. Keyed composer rebinding follows pane identity; the tab and catalog share the same icon renderer. ## Evidence

Verified against a fresh isolated Gateway with the Shell Store MCP App: sidebar entrypoint → live 3D viewer → select specimen → Add to chat → type a question. No personal Gateway state was used.

- Five focused UI suites: 75 tests passed. The composer-rebinding regression fails on the base and passes with the fix.
- UI/core typechecks, UI build, full build, formatting, stylesheet lint, and dead-export scan passed. The changed-check run exposed an overbroad launcher removal; the final change scopes it to the App workspace and retains ordinary-chat launchers.
- Submitted-message context persistence is a separate dependent change.

prs.title: fix(android): clear folder errors after pagination recovers
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves After an Android **Files → Load more** request fails, a successful retry loads the remaining files but leaves “Files unavailable / Could not load this folder.” visible. ## Why This Change Was Made Clear the directory screen's prior error after a successful listing, alongside the existing entries/total update. Failed and pending retries retain their error and loaded rows. This follows the screen's existing full-reload recovery behavior; pagination, protocol, and storage are unchanged. ## User Impact Recovered pagination displays the loaded files without a stale failure message. The production repair is one line. ## Evidence - **Published source:** `28328419c54b3ef02cde5cc956b32139b3a86721`, parent `3fed691416b37f91b0db8dd77446f739e7bf92af`, tree `39a4fb9ed20cd067442ccf8ca1d957f85bd33bed`. Exactly two changed files: production +1 and regression +264. The remotely tested archive has the identical final file hashes below; no APK built at this published SHA is claimed. - **Team-metal remote validation:** identical cleaned Compose/RPC regression is RED on the unpatched owner (one intended stale-error assertion failure), GREEN on candidate (one UI test); all three existing parser tests also pass. Repository-configured touched-file ktlint passes. LEGACY/default graphics are sufficient. - **Independent source review:** repository autoreview helper with exact `claude-opus-5-5`, high reasoning, clean on final two-file contents. Its accepted P3 was fixed by removing screenshot capture and the NATIVE graphics annotation from the committed test; remote tests and review were rerun. - **Regression:** initial 250 of 251 files → two failed page requests → held retry → successful last file. Checks retained rows/error during failure and pending retry, offset 250 on every retry, final row visible, Load more absent, and both stale error texts absent. - Captured media uses a separate one-off Robolectric driver with the same production owner. The committed regression has no capture hook. This is simulated Compose UI against a synthetic server, **not** packaged-app/emulator/device/live-Gateway proof. - Upstream exact-head CI is pending; this draft is not a claim that CI or maintainer review has passed. ### Inspected simulated UI and downloadable proof These are **Robolectric captures**, produced by the separate one-off capture driver using the same production owner. The final committed regression has no screenshot hook and was separately replayed with LEGACY graphics. These images do not claim emulator/device execution. | Before: final page loaded, stale error remains | After: successful retry clears stale error | | --- | --- | | | | [Download inspected proof archive: source identity, original XML, command logs, final patch, one-off captures and clean independent review](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34452374/android-files-public-proof.zip). All payload hashes were verified; task-root paths in public text logs are redacted and the archive manifest records the public bytes. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Android Files retains a failed-pagination error after a successful retry. Real environment tested: self-hosted team-metal Linux x86-64 sandbox; Robolectric API 34 simulated Compose UI, real MainViewModel/runtime RPC transport/parser, and a synthetic loopback WebSocket server. No builds or tests ran on the operator Mac. Exact steps or command run after this patch: repository Gradle wrapper `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.WorkspaceFilesScreenTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.WorkspaceFilesTest`, using isolated Android/JDK homes and `-Drobolectric.graphicsMode=LEGACY` on the team server. Run the identical cleaned test with the single production line removed for the baseline control. Scoped repository `:app:ktlintCheck` also passed. Evidence after fix: inspected baseline/candidate XML, full Gradle/ktlint logs, payload hashes, and one-off before/after simulated UI captures. Final test SHA-256: `8d8452a634fe13c1a3209cf2de7423edf25d164da96da208555c563eb615a2cb`; production SHA-256: `0dac9e17dcadb06b0b2bd80c4de484bb7de7cdbe6c1d03553a57262b276fe468`. Observed result after fix: repeated failed retries keep the error and loaded files; the final successful retry displays file-250.txt, removes Load more, and clears the stale error. Baseline fails at the final error-absence assertion. What was not tested: packaged APK on an emulator or physical Android device, a real Gateway, or live account/provider behavior. The team sandbox has no /dev/kvm; native proof is not inferred from Robolectric. ## Worked on by - @harjothkhara AI-assisted implementation and verification.

prs.title: improve: reduce Gateway startup module-file overhead
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Reduces the many module files loaded during Gateway startup, which correlate with substantial antivirus scanning during first-run Windows setup.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Gateway startup loads fewer files without changing configuration, plugin activation, migration requirements, or Defender settings. No operator action is required. TypeBox and fs-safe remain external to preserve shared registries, error identities, and native resolution.

This is a draft: three Windows startup-benchmark test failures remain **unattributed**, not proven pre-existing. A separate deferred-source Doctor test fails before startup and reproduces with original preflight source. Timings below are warm, noninterleaved samples, **not proof of cold Defender causality**.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Bundle OpenAI and its ws dependency inside the existing AI runtime, with their licenses. Only load legacy session inspection during admission when an existing non-SQLite source needs checking. Keep the original inspection owner and refusal behavior.

An opt-in module-load observer makes file reductions measurable. The benchmark's synchronous Windows memory sampler now leaves an idle interval between samples instead of starving HTTP probe callbacks. This measurement repair is required to compare real readiness.

SEA and V8 snapshots were evaluated but are not shipped: the actual ESM Gateway entry failed the tested SEA/snapshot paths on Node 24/26. Synthetic Node 26 VFS controls do not qualify real plugin discovery, native addons, relocation, or updates.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Base: `7c6a952ba88bf20dd5d22c3971fd0a50e135d4ed`. Tested source snapshot: `c06945d31b351ece668c7e5950862d27dd011aad`, committed unchanged as `a2feabd873cc51a6db898cd890278a358e7a9652`. Windows ARM64, Node 26.13.0, compile cache disabled, isolated synthetic Gateway state, actual `openclaw.mjs`.

| Measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Loaded module files through readiness/RPC | 7,527 | 7,261 |
| Separate OpenAI package files | 264 | 0 |
| Loaded files at observed listener log | 6,733 | 6,384 |
| Median readyz, five runs per arm | 24.381 s | 21.751 s |
| readyz p95 | 24.561 s | 22.679 s |
| Median sessions.list | 19.592 s | 17.722 s |
| Median healthz | 17.728 s | 16.832 s |
| healthz p95 | 17.960 s | 18.254 s |
| Median sampled peak RSS | 1,049.7 MiB | 1,047.2 MiB |

The stable file reduction is 266 (3.5%); listener-log observations are timing-sensitive, not exact socket-open counts. Observer passes are separate from timing passes. All ten timing samples reached healthz 200, readyz 200 and sessions.list. Windows benchmark termination returned code 1 without forced escalation in both arms. No universal tail-latency improvement is claimed.

The actual candidate Gateway also passed healthz/readyz/sessions.list on verified Node 24.22.1 ARM64; that run overlapped checks and is compatibility evidence only.

The tracing coordinator reported sanitized combined fx1103 Companion setup evidence (fixes 1-3, no install prewarm): AI page at 177.1 s, listener verified at 112.2 s, 8,734 payload Defender scans with an 82.7 s scan-interval union. This is a combined observation, not an isolated A/B or evidence that Defender synchronously blocked JavaScript.

<details>
<summary>Commands, review, and remaining gaps</summary>

`npm exec --yes --package=pnpm@12.15.0 -- pnpm` supplied the existing pnpm toolchain where absent from PATH. Windows tsx preloads used file URLs.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | Baseline and complete candidate passed. Baseline UI printed a 0.1 KiB chat gzip budget violation but build returned success. |
| `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental` | Passed. |
| `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` | Passed. |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.scripts.json tsdown.ai.config.ts scripts/bench-gateway-startup.ts scripts/lib/gateway-startup-module-counts.mjs scripts/lib/gateway-bench-probes.ts` | Passed. |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.ts` | Passed. |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json test/scripts/bench-gateway-startup.test.ts test/scripts/tsdown-ai-package.test.ts test/scripts/gateway-bench-probes.test.ts` | Passed. |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt --check tsdown.ai.config.ts packages/ai/README.md scripts/bench-gateway-startup.ts scripts/lib/gateway-startup-module-counts.mjs scripts/lib/gateway-bench-probes.ts src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.ts test/scripts/bench-gateway-startup.test.ts test/scripts/tsdown-ai-package.test.ts test/scripts/gateway-bench-probes.test.ts` | Passed. |
| `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` | Passed before publication. Initial direct invocation could not find pnpm.cmd; rerun with pnpm on PATH passed. |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/gateway-bench-probes.test.ts test/scripts/tsdown-ai-package.test.ts src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts src/commands/startup-config-preflight.deferred-sources.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | Tooling: 2 passed, 1 platform skip; admission: 20 passed, 1 failed with artifact identity changed before startup. Tooling runner ~6.4 s; combined command ~205.7 s including preparation. |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.pristine.process.test.ts test/scripts/bench-gateway-startup.test.ts test/scripts/gateway-bench-probes.test.ts test/scripts/tsdown-ai-package.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | Exit 1. Tooling shard: 3 failed, 44 passed, 3 skipped, ~85.3 s. New observer, sampler and relocated SDK tests passed. |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.pristine.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 3 passed. |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.admission.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "Legacy session store requires migration"` | 1 passed, 13 unselected; real retained-history refusal, ~71.6 s including compilation (~21.5 s test work). |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.pristine.process.test.ts src/commands/startup-config-preflight.deferred-sources.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "preserves current config\|recovers config"` | Original preflight source replay: same separate Doctor artifact identity failure; 2 pristine cases passed, 1 unselected. Not unchanged-base proof for benchmark failures. |
| `node --import <tsx-file-url> scripts/bench-gateway-startup.ts --case default --entry openclaw.mjs --runs 5 --warmup 0 --timeout-ms 90000 --output <arm-json>` | Both arms passed, observer-free, serial/noninterleaved. |
| Same workload with `--runs 1 --module-counts` | Both arms passed; counts are modules, not all filesystem/native/Defender accesses. |
| Verified Node 24.22.1 ARM64 executable, same workload with `--runs 1 --timeout-ms 120000` | Compatibility smoke passed. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed. |

Unresolved benchmark cases:
1. `runs startup benchmark help through a symlinked script directory`: child status 1 instead of 0; filesystem-path ESM preload is a suspected Windows cause.
2. `samples collected startup allocations and stops before post-ready work`: multiline eval rejected by Windows cmd argument safety.
3. `gates both full integrity-check forms on unsealed startup fixtures`: seed subprocess status null instead of 0; cause unresolved.

**None was reproduced on a wholly unchanged baseline.** An existing isolated baseline with ready dependencies and verified ownership was unavailable; all remain unattributed. No failures were masked or baseline exceptions added.

Author simplification retained existing owners and no new runtime manager/public option. Test growth: 77 lines allocated for distinct SDK, module-count and sampler regressions. Fresh independent code-review pass covered the complete base-to-snapshot change and found no significant actionable issues. Reviewer did not rerun tests. The autoreview helper could not execute because Python resolved to an unavailable Store shim; this is independent code-review evidence, not a successful autoreview/ClawSweeper claim.

SEA evaluation: Node 26 non-VFS SEA built but actual entry failed its first relative ESM chunk; snapshot builders failed actual-entry dynamic import with `Not supported` on Node 24.22.1 and 26.13.0. Node 24 SEA is CommonJS-only and lacks `--build-sea`. Synthetic Node 26 ESM VFS imports/relocation worked but cannot combine with snapshots and did not qualify actual Gateway behavior. [Node 24 SEA contract](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.22.1/docs/api/single-executable-applications.html).

No installed Gateways, profiles, credentials, or system/Defender settings changed. Install prewarm and trace tooling belong to separate PRs.

</details>

prs.title: refactor(gateway): isolate agent text pacing
prs.body:
Related: #192609

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway agent-event handling embeds agent-text buffering and pacing alongside subscriber authorization and lifecycle publication.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Streaming order, visibility, currentness checks and pacing remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A narrow delivery helper uses the existing run state and timers. Subscriber authority, transcript publication and disposal stay with the handler.

## Evidence

Existing agent-events, preamble-projection, wire and registration-lifecycle tests cover overdue delivery, coalescing barriers and stale registrations. Independent source review checked the same boundaries.

Fresh independent review and the selected local autoreview found no actionable defects. Native commit hooks and git diff --check passed. Local dependency-backed tests, typecheck and build were not run: native worktree creation refused an escaping workspace dependency link. Draft pending exact-head CI build and affected checks under the repository testing policy.

## Validation status

Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41789553107) at `0e9490646b6b1ed4ae39cd73e3976e8d30e3818a` completed red: 135 successful, 12 failed, 13 skipped jobs. The artifact build, production/test types, lint and SDK API comparison passed; there are no public SDK API changes.

Focused execution evidence for the affected agent-event, preamble, wire and registration-lifecycle tests has not yet been located. The PR remains a draft until that proof is established. Source/type review alone is not test execution.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): cached sidebar rows and scroll [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**STOP: the rows/scroll primary passes, but LoAF regresses at saved offset 1400 on both routes. This experiment remains closed and must not merge.**

A signed-in reload of a chat or dashboard deep link can briefly mount an empty cached sidebar window and lose the saved sidebar scroll offset. The campaign's 14-state reload timeline identified this staged assembly. This change keeps the cached session rows and saved scroll in place while live data arrives.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing sidebar snapshot owner now records only the last mounted session keys and scroll offset. The window starts from those keys before geometry measurement; the existing scroll owner restores a nonzero offset after adoption. The initialized empty window is removed. Current-document destination scroll ownership stays in place, while the reload receipt seeds the new document. The disposable client projection advances to version 5; scope invalidation, deletion pruning and the 512 KiB aggregate cap remain with the existing cache owner.

The complete-avatar reference's actor/avatar/presence/Home enrichment, identity API option, profile-directory fallback and CSS changes are removed. The final runtime is **41 additions / 12 deletions = +29 net lines**, down from +136 in that reference. Experiment-only network collection, pixel parity and their unused helpers/tests are also removed. The retained bench derives its capture type from the probe owner.

## User Impact

Warm reload retains the mounted sidebar rows and scroll position through reconnect and live adoption. Live avatar presentation still updates. Full avatar parity remains a named follow-up at its rendering owner: the accepted attribution below shows that rendering the additional cached identity facts delayed hello, while persisting those same bytes without rendering recovered most of that delay.

## Evidence

Measured branch head [`60446431d856b8da0b80706665bf2042618efb12`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/60446431d856b8da0b80706665bf2042618efb12); pinned main base `41932f3e5cb4a5663ce5f0007baf426d6dfdeceb`. The closed PR ref can retain its older closing head; [this source-pair diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/41932f3e5cb4a5663ce5f0007baf426d6dfdeceb...60446431d856b8da0b80706665bf2042618efb12) identifies the measured candidate. AWS `cbx_ea449afbd652`, one fixed quiet `c7a.4xlarge` (16 vCPU, about 31 GB RAM), repository headless Chromium. Preparation run: [Crabbox run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6abfe3b291ed6f523e470073d9f3b231); the paired comparison continues on that same lease and unchanged checkout.

The operator fixture uses involving-me, category grouping (97 groups / 102 section-order entries), created sort, five collapsed sections, empty groups always, preview false and pinned sessions. Chat and dashboard each test saved offsets 0 and 1400: eleven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, separate correctness captures and eleven candidate/candidate A/A pairs. The live-fast latency profile and fixture clock are fixed. Timing is untraced and unprofiled, with the sidebar presentation observer and pixel capture off; the existing warm metric observer, owner probes and counters remain. Ordinary terminal screenshots occur after the timing snapshot. Correctness uses mutation/scroll-triggered recorded states; it does not claim display-vsync completeness.

### Stop: nonzero-scroll LoAF regression

**This candidate is not qualified for landing. The experiment stays closed; do not merge.** All 12 cohorts are complete and valid: 264 captures, eleven interleaved pairs in every route/offset/correctness/timing/A/A cell. No samples were dropped. A/A controls have no adverse findings. Independent recomputation from the raw summaries and frame files agrees: 1,584 metric/byte values, 792 paired deltas, 648 distribution statistics, 216 sign counts and the primary checks match, with no numerical discrepancies. It examined 462 recorded states, including 220 cached states and 440 ordered-key comparisons.

The primary passes **44/44 candidate runs versus 0/44 on base**: every recorded candidate cached state is nonempty, its ordered mounted/visible row keys equal settled live, and cached/settled scroll retains the actual saved 0 or 1400. There are **zero** recorded candidate empty cached frames.

The hard secondary fails at offset 1400 on both routes. Lower is better; distributions are median [Q1, Q3], and paired delta is candidate minus baseline.

| Route / offset | Base LoAF blocking, ms | Candidate, ms | Median paired delta | Worse pairs | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Chat / 1400 | 303.9 [296.25, 310.55] | 340.9 [335.25, 343.55] | +39.1 ms | 10/11 | Separated adverse IQR and paired regression |
| Dashboard / 1400 | 240.2 [236.05, 248.30] | 293.6 [279.15, 300.70] | +51.9 ms | 10/11 | Separated adverse IQR and paired regression |

Offset-zero cohorts have no hard-secondary regression. Hello handled, first painted rows and final rows do not meet the standing regression rule in either route/offset. Their complete distributions and per-pair values are below, including the positive, mixed-sign final-row deltas at offset 1400. A/A is not subtracted or used to cancel an adverse result.

Regression rule: candidate Q1 above baseline Q3, **or** at least 9/11 worse pairs and median paired rise above max(10 ms, 3% of the baseline median). FCP, CLS and snapshot bytes are reported separately. The largest candidate sidebar record/aggregate is 182,782 B (offset zero); offset 1400 is 182,145 B, below the unchanged 524,288 B aggregate cap.

The failure is confined to the nonzero-offset scenarios in this experiment. These unprofiled gate runs do not isolate scroll restoration/layout from the different mounted content at offset 1400, so no claim that the cost is inherent or solely the setter is made. The accepted complete-avatar attribution below remains historical offset-zero evidence. A new nonzero-scroll attribution or a rows-only variant would be follow-up work; neither was started after this stop.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): keyword search finds current records through superseded wording
prs.body:
Closes #193054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge keyword search reports no record found when a question uses the wording of a record that was superseded, even though its current replacement exists.

## User Impact

User impact: a default `knowledge_grep` search (and memory search backed by Knowledge) also matches the superseded records it hides and returns their current replacements, so agents find the current answer when asked in older wording.

- Replacements come after every direct match, once each, with `matches: ["superseded"]` and `via` naming the earlier record that matched (ID, title, revision; path and hash with `detail: "full"`). The returned record, excerpt and citation belong to the current record, and `snippet.matchLocated: false` marks the excerpt as an opening excerpt, not the match location.
- `kind`, `type`, `tag` and date filters apply to the returned current record. Earlier records rank only among those whose current record passes the filters.
- Replacement hits have `score: null`, so a memory search with `minScore` leaves them out.
- `lifecycle: "superseded"` and `"all"` searches are unchanged: they return superseded records directly and do not follow replacements.
- `total`, `offset` and `nextOffset` cover direct and replacement hits as one list. `index.snapshot` also changes when only a superseded record is edited, so pagination restarts correctly.
- The Control UI Search tab lists replacement hits without showing `via`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each scope keeps a second persistent FTS5 table next to its existing keyword index. It holds the eligible superseded records whose `superseded_by` chain reaches an eligible current record, and it is reconciled by record ID and content hash in the same transaction and snapshot as the main index. A search matches the query against that table and follows each match to its current record, so a search never rebuilds a history index.

Chains step only through eligible superseded records in the same authorized scoped snapshot. A chain that ends in a missing, withdrawn, ineligible or expired record never surfaces a result or affects ranking, and cycles stop. A filtered search ranks within a query-local table of just the histories whose current record passes its filters, the same way the direct index handles filtered searches, so excluded records never shape BM25 statistics.

If either FTS table or its row tracking is missing, the index is rebuilt instead of being served empty under a matching snapshot. This also covers the existing current-record table.

Docs (`docs/plugins/knowledge/retrieval.md`, `docs/plugins/knowledge/tools.md`), the `knowledge_grep` tool description and the `knowledge-recall` skill describe the behavior.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts`, run through the real Knowledge service, vault scan and SQLite state:
  - **Following replacements:** multi-step chains, dedupe against direct matches, withdrawn and looping chains, combined pagination, filters on the current record, unchanged `lifecycle: "superseded"` results, full and compact output schemas. Fails on `main` (no replacement hit).
  - **Filtered ranking:** histories of records outside a `tag` filter do not reorder filtered results. Fails without the filtered ranking corpus (`['bravo_now', 'alpha_now']` instead of `['alpha_now', 'bravo_now']`).
  - **History edits:** editing only a superseded record updates the history index and `index.snapshot`, and a dropped history FTS table with surviving row tracking is rebuilt. Fails on `main`, and fails if superseded records are left out of the snapshot.
- `pnpm test extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 20/20 passed, 234.6 s wall (Vitest 221.7 s, 80% of it transform). The three new tests take 0.50–0.54 s each. CI seconds: not available until CI runs.
- The `lifecycle`, `memory-provider` and `memory-provider-entry` suites pass with this production code (67/67 together with `retrieval`). The full Knowledge suite was not run on this head.
- Test lines: the three tests add 94 lines net. `config/test-lines-allocations/knowledge-superseded-search.txt` allocates them, because each test guards a separate failure (replacement discovery, filtered ranking, history-only edits) and fails without its part of the change. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` passes with 15 lines of slack.
- Knowledge lint, extensions typecheck (source and tests), oxfmt, docs markdown lint and `git diff --check` pass.
- An independent blind red-team review of the search code on this branch found no defect.
- Not run live with a Gateway, agent and model.

### Maintainer landing validation (2026-11-05)

- Reviewed head: `b74a82b3b7ac3d2c652a63c6caac70697c75cd69`.
- Ran `pnpm test extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/memory-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **2 files, 36 tests passed**. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh local autoreview of merge-base `071ea8338d93e55c9a55e0504ac0ea95257dad23` through that head found **no actionable P0–P2 defects**. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable, so the documented autoreview fallback was used.
- Exact-head `openclaw/ci-gate` passed CI and applicable security review.
- The service/vault/SQLite and memory-adapter boundary is validated. The live Gateway/agent/model and latest-stable upgrade gaps noted above remain; derived-index recovery tests are not claimed as a full upgrade run.

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): deliver the group description to the agent
prs.body:
Closes #193766

## What Problem This Solves

A WhatsApp group's description is fetched on every inbound group message and then
discarded before anything can read it. Inbound group context carries the subject and the
participants but not the description, and no extension can recover it.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent in a WhatsApp group can now read that group's description, so
operators can scope the agent from the group itself — one group per customer, each saying
which account it belongs to — instead of adding a config entry per group. Groups without a
description are unaffected: the entry is omitted when `desc` is empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extractGroupMetadata` already returns `desc`, and this extension already asks for it —
both `sock.groupMetadata(jid)` and the connect-time `groupFetchAllParticipating()` query
include a `<description>` node. `summarize()` then kept `subject`, `participants` and
`mentionParticipants` and dropped the rest, so `desc` was gone before the cache, the hooks
or the prompt saw it. Nothing downstream could get it back: no typed hook payload carries
group metadata, and the plugin SDK does not hand one plugin another plugin's channel
client, so a third-party extension can solve the injection half and has nothing to read.

So `desc` now travels wherever `subject` already travels, including both caches — a failed
live metadata fetch falls back to the reconnect cache, and dropping the description only
there would make group scoping fail intermittently.

It surfaces through `channelStructuredContext`, which this extension already uses for
media, contacts and external ad replies. Core needs no change, because it renders
structured context generically, whereas the prompt metadata fields beside `group_subject`
are a fixed allowlist in `inbound-meta`. Structured context is also the right framing:
whoever can edit the group writes the description, so it is untrusted input, and that is
exactly how core labels this block in the prompt.

The alternative — a `group_description` field beside `group_subject` — was not taken: it
changes core for something one channel produces, and would give a participant-editable
string the same weight as host-provided metadata.

## Evidence

`pnpm vitest run extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.metadata-cache.test.ts` → **17
passed**, including three new cases: the description is delivered as structured context,
it is omitted for a group that has none, and it survives a live metadata fetch failure.

Reverting only the three source files and keeping the tests fails the two positive cases
(`expected undefined to be defined`) while the omission case still passes, so the tests
exercise the change rather than restating it.

Also deployed on our own instance as an equivalent patch to the published `2026.10.9`
bundle, where the gateway starts clean and the channel reports healthy. End-to-end
confirmation against a live group is still pending on our side.

prs.title: fix(gateway): strip __controlUiReconnectResume from chat.send params before validation
prs.body:
<!--
Closes: #165433
-->

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `chat.send` requests from non-Operator-UI clients (e.g. webchat on a browser reconnect with a preserved `sessionId`) are rejected with `invalid chat.send params: at root: unexpected property '__controlUiReconnectResume'`. `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` only strips the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker when both `value === true` AND `isOperatorUiClient(clientInfo)` returns true; in every other case the `__`-prefixed marker leaks into the AJV-strict `chat.send` schema and the request is dropped before dispatch.

## User Impact
User impact: Webchat and other browser-based reconnect paths that emit the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker now have their messages admitted and dispatched normally on reconnect. No user-visible change for Control UI clients — their behavior is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made
`__controlUiReconnectResume` is an internal `__`-prefixed wire field added by the Control UI to signal "treat this as a reconnect resume, not a fresh run." Such fields should never reach the public `chat.send` schema. The patch decouples "strip the field before validation" from "record that a resume was requested" — the field is now stripped whenever it is present on the input record, and the `resumeRequested` flag is still gated by both the strict-value check and the Operator UI client check, preserving the downstream semantics. The strict-value check is unchanged on purpose so a non-true value (e.g. `false`, `1`, the wrong type) still does not mark a resume even from an Operator UI client.

## Evidence
- Six focused unit tests added in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-server-timing.test.ts` (new file) cover the regression and the surrounding cases: field absent, non-object input, true value with operator UI client, true value with non-operator UI client (the regression), true value with missing `clientInfo`, non-true values with operator UI client, and input-record immutability.
- A local reproduction on the bundled `dist/chat-server-timing-soo795Of.mjs` (the same logic, minified) confirmed the bug and the fix: pre-patch, a `webchat` clientInfo with `__controlUiReconnectResume: true` returned the marker in the result params; post-patch, the marker is stripped and `resumeRequested` is `false`.
- `diff -u` of the patched file vs. upstream main shows changes confined to the `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` function body; no other exports, signatures, or unrelated fields are touched.

prs.title: Request speakerphone output for Android Talk
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Android, `RealtimeCommunicationAudio` sets `AudioManager.mode =
MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` to start a Talk session but never requests the
loudspeaker as the output device. Android's default routing for
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` is the earpiece unless a Bluetooth/wired headset is
attached, so continuous Talk plays back quietly through the earpiece
instead of the main loudspeaker - unexpected for a hands-free,
phone-away-from-the-ear conversation.

iOS already has an explicit speakerphone setting for Talk (see the Talk
settings page in the iOS app / dashboard). Android has no equivalent
request anywhere in the realtime audio path - this looks like a parity gap
rather than an intentional platform difference.

Any custom realtime voice provider plugin (via `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider`)
used through Android's Talk feature is affected equally to the built-in
OpenAI/xAI providers, since the audio routing logic is shared and
provider-agnostic.

## Evidence

Confirmed from the current Android source
(`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/RealtimeCommunicationAudio.kt`)
that `start()` sets `audioManager.mode = AudioManager.MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`
and requests audio focus, but never calls `setCommunicationDevice(...)` or
`isSpeakerphoneOn = true` anywhere - there is no output-device request in
this file or in the related `RealtimePlayout.kt` / `AndroidAudioInputSession.kt`
/ `TalkModeManager.kt` files (checked via direct source review, not
assumption). This matches standard documented Android behavior: apps using
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` get earpiece-by-default routing unless they
explicitly request another device.

This PR requests the speaker explicitly when a Talk communication-audio
session starts, and releases it cleanly when it ends - using
`AudioManager.setCommunicationDevice()` on Android 12+ (the documented
replacement for the deprecated speakerphone API), falling back to
`isSpeakerphoneOn` on older versions. Existing Bluetooth/wired routing in
`AndroidAudioInputSession` still takes priority when an external device is
actually connected, since device selection there is handled separately by
the OS once a route is active - this change only affects the otherwise-
silent default when no other device is connected.

Not yet verified on-device or via a local build - no Android SDK/Gradle
toolchain was available in the environment this patch was written in. The
change is a minimal, targeted addition using documented public
`AudioManager` APIs, confirmed against the current Android platform API
surface and against this repo's actual current source, but it has not been
compiled or run. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming it's been
tested - would appreciate a maintainer or anyone able to build the Android
app confirming it compiles and actually fixes the earpiece-default
behavior on a real device before merging.

prs.title: feat(ui): show the recorded exec warning in the approval history (reopen of #185200)
prs.body:
Fixes #180242 > **Reopen note:** This is #185200 rebased onto current main. After the branch was force-pushed GitHub refuses to reopen the closed PR, so this replaces it. The fix, evidence, and ClawSweeper verdict are unchanged from #185200; rebase re-pointed the render from the page-local `Cell` helper (removed by #191189) to the standalone `approval-history-row.tsx`, and the exec-warning render now goes through a Solid `` boundary (Solid 2 `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED`). ## What Problem This Solves When an exec approval is shown to a reviewer, the operation's `warningText` — the safety warning attached to a potentially dangerous command — is rendered prominently (live approval page `ui/src/pages/approval/approval-presentation.tsx`, and `****` in channel approval notifications via `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`). The Control UI **approval history** table never rendered it: `HistoryRow` shows `commandText` only, so an operator auditing past approvals cannot see why a command was flagged as dangerous at the moment it was approved. The field is already in the data path end to end, so nothing but the renderer was missing: - `ExecApprovalPresentationSchema.warningText` (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/approvals.ts:134`) - persisted in the full presentation (`src/gateway/operator-approval-store.rows.ts` `stringifyPresentation`) - returned unchanged by `approval.history` (`src/gateway/server-methods/approval.ts` `buildApprovalSnapshot`) ## Why This Change Was Made Implementing the conditional warning note recommended in #180242: reuse the existing presentation field and the existing warning styling, next to the historical command, with no storage, RPC, config, or decision change. - `ui/src/app/approval-presentation.ts` — `execWarningText(presentation)` extracts the recorded warning for exec presentations and returns `null` for other kinds or when absent. This module already owns approval presentation summaries (`summarizeApprovalScopeLabel`), so both approval surfaces now read the same predicate. - `ui/src/pages/approvals/approval-history-row.tsx` — `HistoryRow`'s request cell wraps the command with an optional `ExecWarning` note, rendered through a Solid `` boundary so the reactive read stays tracked. Rows without a recorded warning are unchanged, including the existing `mono` command styling. - `ui/src/styles/components.css` — `.approval-history-warning`: a compact body-font, `--warn`-toned line under the command (the cell is monospace, so the note resets the family instead of looking like more command text). - `ui/src/styles/settings.css` — `.approval-log__request-wrap`: the command cell becomes a block wrapper so the note sits under the truncated command without breaking the grid column. The request cell additionally gained `display: block` so the long-command ellipsis continues to clip inside the block wrapper (regression introduced by the wrapper itself). - `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-approvals.ts` — `approvalHistory.warningLabel: "Warning"`. **Behavior classification: behavior-preserving.** Additive rendering of an already-returned field; no approval, grant, or history read/write path changes. Solid escapes text nodes, so a recorded warning containing markup is displayed literally and never executed (covered by the regression test). ## User Impact Operators auditing approval history can now see the recorded blast-radius warning on the row it belongs to, instead of losing it after the decision. Exec rows that carried no warning look exactly as before, as do the other six columns, the standing-grants table, pagination, and the retention footer. ## Evidence ### Current head (`a9f8cc03cc4`, merged with `ee00ba6be09` main) **Programmatic assertions** — the Control UI e2e harness (`installMockGateway` + `createControlUiE2eSuite` + Playwright, the repository's UI proof path) drives `settings/approvals` at 1200×900 with one warned and one unwarned exec row against a mock `approval.history` payload. The capture test asserts: - exactly two rows are rendered (`rows.count() === 2`), one per `approval.history` entry; - exactly one `.approval-history-warning` node is rendered (`warnings.count() === 1`) — the warned row only; - the rendered warning's text contains the recorded warning string (`textContent` includes `"This command requests external network access."`); - the warned row's command text is truncated by the existing ellipsis clip (long synthetic `pnpm --filter …` command is provided longer than the cell); - expanding the warned row sets `aria-expanded="true"` and reveals the disclosure with the warning still attached to the same row. Both a collapsed and an expanded screenshot were captured during the same run and are attached below (current layout). **Current layout — collapsed** (warned row + unwarned row, long-command truncation in place): **Current layout — expanded** (warned row disclosure open; warning still anchored to the row): ### Prior capture (#185200, pre-rebase file layout) The screenshots below were captured on #185200 against the pre-rebase `HistoryRow` location. The render was moved to `approval-history-row.tsx` and re-shaped around ``; the visible row is the same. Kept here as a before/after reference for the warning itself. **Before** (base `64ab0917`): the warned row shows only the command. ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0123bb4c-921b-4aed-9ae8-56b139f15333) **After** (#185200 head): the recorded warning is rendered under the command in the request cell. ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0545f05a-3f88-4134-b328-0f0df5e3ec97) Close-up, before → after: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![before table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16f81eac-3771-4ef6-a951-f2ed97da528e) | ![after table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5229ebf1-f812-42a5-80f6-8c989bb69693) | The second row (`pnpm test ui/src/pages/approvals`, no recorded warning) is pixel-identical in both captures, which is the "no misfire" control for the conditional render. ### Red on base `git checkout HEAD^ -- ui/src/pages/approvals/approval-history-row.tsx` (source only, new test kept): ```text × |unit| src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx > shows a recorded exec warning beside the command without executing its markup 24ms → expected to have a length of 1 but got +0 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ AssertionError: expected to have a length of 1 but got +0 Tests 1 failed | 12 passed (13) ``` Failure is at the intended assertion (no `.approval-history-warning` node), and only the new test fails. ### Checks (rebased head `2be63aaf894`) ```sh # regression + full file, rebased head on Node v24.13.1 cd ui && node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \ src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx # Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 15 passed (15) pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/pages/approvals/approval-history-row.tsx ui/src/app/approval-presentation.ts # no error; remaining warning is pre-existing on main's DetailRow (verified on pristine main) node scripts/run-format.mts --check # All matched files use the correct format ``` The `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` diagnostic that previously pointed at `ExecWarning` is gone after the `` refactor; the same diagnostic on `DetailRow` exists on pristine `main` (14 instances) and is untouched by this PR. ## Not tested - `pnpm tsgo:core` does not run on this host (the pinned `tsrs` needs glibc ≥ 2.29; host is 2.17), so type checking for the new `execWarningText` signature and the `` boundary is delegated to CI. - No live production Gateway with a real 30-day approval ledger was exercised; the proof is the repository's mock-Gateway UI harness plus the DOM regression test. The history payload shape itself is unchanged and already covered by `approval.history` tests. - Non-English locales: only the English catalog gained `approvalHistory.warningLabel`; foreign translations arrive through the post-merge locale pipeline, not by hand here. - Stacked/mobile layout was not captured; the note is a block inside the existing responsive cell and adds no new column. ## References - Implements the recommendation in #180242 (`Maintainer decision needed → Add an inline warning note`). - Sibling requests in the same table, intentionally not included here: #180243 (approval severity in history) and #180244 (approval scope/blast radius in history). The `ExecWarning` note slot introduced here is the natural place for them if maintainers want one combined history layout. - Existing warning presentation this follows: `ui/src/pages/approval/approval-presentation.tsx` (`role="note"` + `approval-page__warning`), `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts` (channel notification emphasis).
Maintainer edits - `HistoryRow`'s request cell gained one conditional note (`ExecWarning`), plus the `execWarningText` helper in `approval-presentation.ts`; both are additive and file-local, no new exported API beyond `execWarningText`. - Diff: +79/−2 across 6 files (row, app helper, CSS ×2, English catalog, regression test), plus +1/−1 on `settings.css` for the `display: block` ellipsis-clip repair. - No RPC, storage, config, documentation, or approval-decision behavior touched.
Maintainer options - **Land-ready as is:** additive render of a field the history RPC already returns, with regression coverage and inspected before/after captures. - **Wanted instead a dedicated column:** deferred deliberately. A `Warning` column would be empty for most rows and would consume table width; the inline note keeps the seven existing columns and can be promoted to a column later without touching the data path. - **Wanted all three history requests together:** this PR is the smallest of the family and the `ExecWarning` note slot was built to accept the severity (#180243) and scope (#180244) renders. Happy to extend it in a follow-up rather than grow this diff. - **Scope statement:** no visual change outside warned exec rows in the approval history table.
--- ### Prior ClawSweeper verdict (#185200, unchanged by rebase) Diff: +79/−2 across 6 files (rebase re-pointed the render file; no behavioral delta). | Dimension | Result | | --- | --- | | Overall readiness | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** — "unresolved product direction caps the overall assessment" | | Proof confidence | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus — "Sufficient (screenshot): inspected before/after screenshots exercise the actual Control UI settings/approvals route in Chromium … proves the changed rendering boundary." | | Patch quality | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** — "No actionable review findings were identified." | | Recommendation | **"Approve the inline warning: accept this focused addition to the existing request cell without changing the seven-column layout."** | [ClawSweeper review (2026-10-27)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185200#issuecomment-6430379600) — labels `proof: sufficient`, `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`, `status: ⏳ waiting on maintainer`; CI `openclaw/ci-gate` pass. ## Decision requested (not an approval claim) The ClawSweeper `Recommendation` quoted above is an **advisory design suggestion, not a contract approval** — it was written by the review bot, and no maintainer has recorded a decision on this direction. This PR renders an already-recorded field (`warningText`) in the existing approval-history request cell, and it is waiting on an owner decision before merge. | Option | Effect | Cost if chosen | | --- | --- | --- | | **Accept (this PR)** | Auditors see the recorded blast-radius warning under its historical command; unwarned rows are pixel-identical. | A warning-toned note under the command cell; the seven-column layout and all other columns are unchanged. | | **Decline and close** | History keeps showing only the command; operators lose the warning after the decision. | The `ExecWarning` note slot (built to also accept severity #180243 / scope #180244) is unused; nothing else changes. | | **Wanted a dedicated column** | Deferred deliberately; the inline note can be promoted to a column later without touching the data path. | Table width would grow and most rows would carry an empty column. |
