prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).

prs.title: improve(mobile): scope release-note history to public baselines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mobile release-note preparation fetches the complete source history even when the recorded public release is recent. The last successful TestFlight run spent about 110 seconds loading history before collecting its inventory.

## User Impact

Release-note preparation loads the ancestry needed to compare the selected source with each public baseline. First releases and comparisons without relevant file changes skip extra ancestry. Release identities, commit hints, endpoint evidence, saved-note replay, and upload behavior are preserved; full local clones remain full.

## Why This Change Was Made

The evidence collector now owns history loading. It deepens both exact tips until every remaining shallow boundary is shared by them, so missing ancestry cannot affect the comparison or invent path changes. This replaces unconditional unshallowing without relying on dates or a fixed history cutoff.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before measurement: identical inventories and selected evidence, unchanged source and refs, fewer irrelevant history objects and bytes, and lower complete history-plus-evidence time across five interleaved cold samples per variant.

The existing history benchmark now loads the committed baseline collector and exercises both platform inventories. Fresh filtered object stores are served by a task-owned local bare remote; no worktree checkout, model, build, or store API is involved. Diff hash abbreviations are fixed at 12 digits for both variants because Git's automatic abbreviation length depends on object count.

For the exact source and public baseline from [TestFlight run 42097255644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42097255644):

| Metric | Full history | Baseline-scoped history |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| History + inventory, median / p95 | 37.15 / 37.86 s | 13.56 / 13.80 s |
| History + selected evidence, median / p95 | 38.01 / 38.68 s | 14.41 / 14.63 s |
| Complete phase, min–max | 37.74–38.68 s | 14.07–14.63 s |
| Commits loaded | 125,874 | 3,420 |
| Objects loaded, median | 1,002,723 | 62,214 |
| Git object storage, median | 387.89 MB | 32.25 MB |

For the source and public phone/Wear baseline recorded in [Android run 42051110609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42051110609) (both audiences publicly at 2026.10.90):

| Metric | Full history | Baseline-scoped history |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| History + inventory, median / p95 | 39.39 / 39.60 s | 13.12 / 13.17 s |
| History + selected evidence, median / p95 | 40.55 / 40.75 s | 14.25 / 14.31 s |
| Complete phase, min–max | 40.48–40.75 s | 14.22–14.31 s |
| Commits loaded | 125,784 | 3,329 |
| Objects loaded, median | 1,001,909 | 61,864 |
| Git object storage, median | 386.36 MB | 31.55 MB |

All ten evidence hashes match within each platform's workload. Preparation improved by 62% for iOS and 65% for Android, with about 92% less Git object storage. These are local acquisition/evidence measurements, not end-to-end hosted release durations.

- All 56 focused tests passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/mobile-release-ci.test.ts test/scripts/mobile-release-notes.test.ts test/scripts/mobile-release.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (53.17 s test duration; files 25.89 / 7.49 / 19.27 s).
- The real-Git regression failed before the fix because the shallow inventory omitted a phone commit hint; it now matches full history for iOS and Android, including a divergent baseline, while retaining shallow older ancestry and pinned source/refs.
- Generator coverage includes full and shallow clones with separate phone/Wear baselines. Existing first-release, deferred TestFlight, replay, and upload fixtures remain green.
- Script and tooling-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, script erasability, documentation links, diff checks, and the staged test-line ratchet passed.
- [CI passed on the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42113896571), including the test-line gate. The three focused files passed in CI: `mobile-release-ci.test.ts` (23 tests, 15.549 s), `mobile-release-notes.test.ts` (17 tests, 1.811 s), and `mobile-release.test.ts` (16 tests, 8.527 s).
- Local ClawSweeper completed a read-only review of `99ba844a3cd592adea6dac7421f9d9f7a0f7161d..422bf9504e4ad409bff4cb4d1e25b34bb60f453f`; no actionable findings. No duplicate hosted review requested.

The change adds 39 net release-runtime lines and 42 benchmark lines. Its consolidated regressions reduce net test lines by one, without a test-budget allocation. Full-clone preservation is checked in the primary evidence/replay test; the phone/Wear test exercises a shallow source; inventory hints and divergent ancestry have one real-Git owner.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the read-only iOS benchmark</summary>

```sh
git clone --bare --shared "$PWD" /tmp/mobile-history-remote.git
git -C /tmp/mobile-history-remote.git config uploadpack.allowFilter true
git -C /tmp/mobile-history-remote.git update-ref refs/openclaw/mobile-releases/ios/2026.10.90-5 0468e735508a5ceafca5e855479a7a870f99cbc8
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-android-release-history.mts \
  --platform ios --remote file:///tmp/mobile-history-remote.git \
  --source d4e2ec81b16cbada3544e29c45f855f5d81aa5ce \
  --base 99ba844a3cd592adea6dac7421f9d9f7a0f7161d \
  --baseline-ref refs/openclaw/mobile-releases/ios/2026.10.90-5 --samples 5
```

The Android command uses `--platform android --source 0f3287eaa7858d544d3a4d0f8f3816542d1ba375` and repeats `--baseline-ref refs/openclaw/mobile-releases/android/v2/2026.10.9/0/4/2026090530-2026090531` twice, matching its recorded phone and Wear baselines. Seed that ref in the task-owned remote at `2a3f6f3ae78263fb110f349b866cbcdbc504d948` first.

Host: macOS ARM64, 10 available CPUs; initial load average 2.25 / 2.22 / 1.86 for iOS and 2.05 / 2.70 / 2.22 for Android. Each sample uses a fresh object store; the local server and filesystem page cache remain warm. Baseline and candidate samples run serially in ABAB order.

</details>

prs.title: fix(knowledge): keep display truncation surrogate-safe
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge display truncations still use raw UTF-16 `slice`, so a cut at a contract boundary can leave a lone high surrogate in titles, labels, and messages when an emoji straddles the limit. This is the residual sibling of the remember-title fix in #186986.

Affected paths:

- `promptLabel` in the memory index (`max - 1` + ellipsis)
- session activity item titles (`text(200)`)
- relink example titles / subject titles (`text(200)`)
- maintenance vault labels (`maxLength: 160`) and failure messages
- knowledge status `notReady` messages (`text(300)`)

## User Impact

Knowledge panel labels, session activity titles, relink examples, and maintenance vault labels no longer show a replacement character when the stored string is cut mid-emoji. Session activity titles are user-visible in the Control UI session panel.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route those display truncations through the plugin SDK helper `truncateUtf16Safe`, matching the existing pattern in `remember.ts` / #186986.

## Evidence

### Envelope boundary is reachable

TypeBox `maxLength` counts code points, not UTF-16 units. Verified with the repo's TypeBox:

| input | code points | UTF-16 units | passes `maxLength: 200` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 199 x "A" + one emoji | 200 | 201 | yes |
| 200 x "A" + one emoji | 201 | 201+ | no |

So `199 A's + emoji` is an Envelope-valid production title. A hard `slice(0, 200)` leaves a lone high surrogate at unit 200.

### Real Gateway before/after (redacted terminal logs)

Seeded a real Knowledge store with the Envelope-valid boundary title, started an isolated Gateway with bundled knowledge, then called the same RPC the Control UI session panel uses:

```text
plugins.sessionAction { pluginId: "knowledge", actionId: "session_activity", ... }
```

Redacted `PR187423_GATEWAY_PROOF` reports from that real Gateway process:

```text
# BASE (slice(0, 200) at session-activity.ts)
PR187423_GATEWAY_PROOF {
  "boundaryStoredCodePoints": 200,
  "boundaryStoredUtf16": 201,
  "boundaryServedUtf16": 200,
  "boundaryServedWellFormed": false,
  "boundaryServedTailUnits": "41,41,41,D83D",
  "controlServed": "Short control title",
  "controlWellFormed": true,
  "itemCount": 2
}

# CANDIDATE (truncateUtf16Safe at session-activity.ts)
PR187423_GATEWAY_PROOF {
  "boundaryStoredCodePoints": 200,
  "boundaryStoredUtf16": 201,
  "boundaryServedUtf16": 199,
  "boundaryServedWellFormed": true,
  "boundaryServedTailUnits": "41,41,41,41",
  "controlServed": "Short control title",
  "controlWellFormed": true,
  "itemCount": 2
}
```

Interpretation:

- Base serves 200 UTF-16 units ending in `D83D` (lone high surrogate `U+D83D` from the split emoji) → `isWellFormed=false`.
- Candidate drops the incomplete code point and serves 199 `A`s → `isWellFormed=true`.
- Control title is unchanged on both sides.

### Unit / jsdom support

`sessionActivity` unit test (committed) is red on base / green with the fix for the same boundary input. A jsdom Control UI session-panel proof also shows base `199 A's + U+FFFD` vs candidate `199 A's`.

Focused tests:

- `extensions/knowledge/src/memory-index.test.ts`
- `extensions/knowledge/src/session-activity.test.ts`

prs.title: fix(workers): avoid repeated snapshot verification and expose preparation phases
prs.body:
Fixes snapshot-fork preparation overhead.

## What Problem This Solves

Snapshot forks can take as long as a cold start, while preparation reports only the recipe command time and hides verification and manifest work.

## User Impact

Completed worker-owned object stores no longer receive a redundant full `git fsck`. Settings and `warm-images` retain separate preparation timings, including reused and enrolled workspaces. Incoming packs still require size, SHA-256, object, and connectivity checks; changed workspace contents and identities still reject reuse.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preparation owner now measures fixed phases, carries them through the existing diagnostics field, and reuses a source manifest for its exact retained commit/tree. New source captures offer the existing persisted memo to the manifest owner; unchanged completed workspaces do not regenerate their manifests after inspection. This relies on the existing trusted worker OS/user and worker-owned image contract, not a new security boundary. Latent object-store damage is detected when Git consumes those objects; incoming transfer verification remains mandatory.

This branch is stacked on #193662 (`830c10c16130367bac6520b045f22eb8129b7c02`), which is still open. That PR supplies persisted hash memos and the stale copied-index fix. No provider or EBS settings change here.

## Evidence

Red on full `origin/main` (`6e7ee204e1b`) in a separate checkout: unchanged reuse ran one fsck instead of zero; refresh ran two instead of one; diagnostic phases were absent. The focused regression took 45.16 s wall time. The fixed regression proves cold transfer = one, retained reuse = zero, refresh = one, and present finite phase timings. Existing real-pack corruption and changed-workspace/identity rejection tests remain green.

- Five owning suites: 68 tests passed on the first run; one assertion still expected only the old command timing. After updating it and finishing enrolled-inspection diagnostics, the three affected tests passed (48.98 s wall time). The first run covered source transfer, Git corruption, A/B/A refresh, recipe failure, authority, and retained-identity checks.
- Settings: 26 tests passed; warm-image storage: 28 passed (64.90 s combined wall time).
- Real Chromium before/after proof passed (17.38 s and 15.86 s); screenshots below use synthetic fixture data.
- Core and UI typechecks passed; type-aware lint passed after two brace-only corrections in test/benchmark code; changed-file oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the staged test-line budget check passed.
- Live on an isolated Gateway with a real AWS fork of a real `openclaw/openclaw` snapshot (about 64,000 tracked files), the new phases attribute the fork: `retainedManifest` 13.7 s, `seedTransfer` 37.6 s, `seedVerification` 4.6 s, `seedCheckout` 4.5 s, `seedManifest` 10.9 s, `gitUpdate` 23.3 s, `toolchainPreparation` 29.7 s, `detectedInstall` 13.9 s, `preparedManifest` 54.9 s. A second inspection of the same tree took 140 ms, so the first-touch cost is cold storage. This PR adds attribution and removes one repeated check; it does not make that fork faster on its own, because the commit had moved. The repeated work it exposed is addressed separately.
- CI: `checks-node-changed-compact-small-13` failed only in `src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts` ("ends unfinished retention at --timeout") on the Bun shard, a 60-second update budget in a suite this PR does not touch. That test passes locally on this head under Node in 34.67 s.

Local benchmark acceptance: identical prepared manifest, fewer full object scans, lower median and p95 total preparation time. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/project-preparation-phases.mts <scratch-root>` runs five interleaved A-to-B refresh pairs over 1,000 tracked files × 32 KiB, each on an independent copy of the prepared image. The baseline replays the old checks with the same new timing instrumentation. macOS, Node 26.12.1, warm local disk; load averages 12.1/12.9/12.6. Full scans per refresh fall from two to one; unchanged retained reuse has zero.

| Phase | Before median / p95 (ms) | After median / p95 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `retainedGit` | 193 / 201 | 32 / 34 |
| `retainedManifest` | 243 / 325 | 224 / 290 |
| `inspection` | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| `seedPreparation` | 2 / 5 | 2 / 2 |
| `seedTransfer` | 222 / 242 | 210 / 221 |
| `seedVerification` | 288 / 290 | 285 / 288 |
| `seedCheckout` | 253 / 311 | 246 / 268 |
| `seedManifest` | 230 / 239 | 227 / 296 |
| `gitUpdate` | 325 / 359 | 314 / 328 |
| `toolchainPreparation` | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| `preparedManifest` | 267 / 393 | 280 / 362 |
| `onCreate` | 39 / 45 | 43 / 45 |
| Total including script launch and local transfer | 2494.49 / 2761.72 | 2319.44 / 2362.71 |

The table attributes local work, not the historical AWS run's exact 107 seconds. In particular, source and prepared manifest capture were outside the old install-only counter. The recorded AWS first-touch costs (full content read 53.7 s, ignored-path enumeration 17.3 s, fsck 29.5 s) explain why those missing phases matter, but a new AWS run is required to assign them precisely. This PR makes no AWS end-to-end speedup claim. New/changed objects and contents, metadata walks, cache misses, checkout writes, and files loaded by setup/tools still need cold-disk I/O; memo reuse cannot avoid them all.

Runtime delta is 145 added / 25 removed lines; the standalone measurement workload is separate. The 38-line test allocation covers the object-scan count and diagnostics boundary regressions. No schema migration or new state store.

Independent Codex autoreview covered the complete local change against `830c10c16130367bac6520b045f22eb8129b7c02` through P2 and returned `scoped-clean`, with no actionable findings. Only lint-required braces and the matching test-line count changed afterward.

![After: all recorded preparation phases are visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d79e5748-30fd-40e6-9390-81b9f5e3eec0)

prs.title: fix(models): expire live provider catalogs on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A backward wall-clock adjustment keeps live provider catalog entries alive past their configured TTL, so a repeated discovery reuses the stale upstream metadata/document instead of refreshing it.

`src/plugins/provider-live-catalog-cache.ts` measured freshness against `Date.now()`:

- `getCachedLiveCatalogValue` compared `entry.expiresAt > rawNow`, with `expiresAt` stamped from the wall clock.
- `armLiveCatalogExpiry` / `expireLiveCatalogs` scheduled and swept on the wall clock.

After a backwards step, an entry stays "fresh" for the length of the step. The shared upstream metadata feed (`getCachedUpstreamProviderCatalog`, 300 s TTL) is the directly affected document.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expiry now runs on `monotonicNow()` (`src/shared/monotonic-time.ts`), matching the elapsed-clock caches in core and extensions (#191606, #192700, #193147, #193358).

**The published deadline stays on the wall clock.** `consumeLiveCatalog` forwards the entry deadline through `recordLiveCatalogExpiry` to `providerExpiries`, and `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-access.ts:581` filters providers with `expiresAt <= Date.now()`. So the entry carries two fields:

- `expiresAt` — elapsed deadline, owns cache freshness and the sweep.
- `publishedExpiresAt` — wall-clock deadline, still published to catalog expiries.
- `publishedNow` — selects the clock for `publishedExpiresAt` so the `now` test hook keeps driving both.

Precedent: #192700 (`fix: use elapsed time for caches and chat recovery windows`), #193147 (`fix(runtime): expire discovery and room caches on elapsed time`), #191606 (`fix(cache): keep private cache TTLs on elapsed time`), #193358 (`fix(active-memory): expire recall cache on elapsed time`).

## Shipped route (addressing the #193358 exclusion)

#193358 landed the elapsed-cache family without this PR because "the exercised shipped inventory route either uses the static catalog or explicitly bypasses this cache during refresh". The static-catalog half holds; the bypass half does not, for OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go:

- `extensions/opencode/provider-catalog.ts:73` and `extensions/opencode-go/provider-catalog.ts:83` both set `metadataEndpoint` to `https://models.opencode.ai/api.json`.
- `extensions/opencode/index.ts:144` and `extensions/opencode-go/index.ts:80` run the live branch from `catalog.run` → `buildOpencodeZenLiveProviderConfig` / `buildOpencodeGoLiveProviderConfig` → `buildLiveProvider` (`src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-runtime.ts:355`) → `refreshMetadata` → `getCachedUpstreamProviderCatalog` → `getCachedLiveCatalogValue` with `keyParts: ["upstream-provider-catalog", endpoint]` and a 300 s TTL. This matches `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/model-catalogs.md` ("Live builds refresh metadata before deriving static eligibility").
- The refresh bypass only covers the *first* lookup of an acquisition (`consumeLiveCatalogRefresh` consumes the key once). A second metadata lookup inside the same catalog run, and every ordinary (non-refresh) inventory read, takes the cache path.

What is *not* claimed: `prepareOpencodeZenModel` (`extensions/opencode/provider-catalog.ts:96`) really does call `refreshMetadata` outside `catalog.run` and therefore bypasses the cache, and the host-side caller of `buildLiveProvider` reaches it through `catalog.run` only. The proof below drives the `catalog.run` path, including its cache-hit reads.

## User Impact

With a live OpenCode catalog feed, an expired entry refreshes after its elapsed TTL even when the host clock moves backward. Warm entries still reuse the cache, the published expiry handed to the catalog runtime is unchanged, and behavior without a clock step is identical. No new setting, error text, public SDK export, stored format, or migration.

## Evidence

Both sides ran on the remote Linux test host (Docker, Node v24.22.1) through the repository entry `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <path>`. BASE is `origin/main` (`46943d587ac`) archived per side; HEAD is the PR tip. Trees were restored/re-checked per run.

| Test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/plugins/provider-live-catalog-cache.test.ts` — `expires cached catalogs on elapsed time when the wall clock steps backwards` | FAIL | PASS |
| `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-upstream.test.ts` — `reloads the upstream provider catalog after the wall clock steps backwards` | FAIL | PASS |
| `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-runtime.strict.test.ts` (whole file) | PASS | PASS |
| `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared{,.refresh,.cancellation}.test.ts` (whole files) | PASS | PASS |

BASE failure (cache test):

```
AssertionError: expected "spy" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times
 ❯ src/plugins/provider-live-catalog-cache.test.ts:92:24
```

BASE failure (upstream test):

```
AssertionError: expected "spy" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times
 ❯ src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-upstream.test.ts:287:29
```

The clock step is process-local only (`vi.setSystemTime`); the real clock is never touched. Both regression tests step `Date` backwards *and* advance the faked elapsed clock, so they land past the TTL by elapsed time.

**Discovery trace through the shipped `catalog.run` entry (added this revision).** A new regression in `extensions/opencode/index.test.ts` drives `buildOpencodeZenLiveProviderConfig` — the exact run callback `catalog.run` invokes for a configured OpenCode provider (`extensions/opencode/index.ts:149`) — instead of calling the cache loader directly. A `fetchGuard` spy records the upstream metadata download count for `https://models.opencode.ai/api.json`:

| Step | BASE (`Date.now`) | HEAD (`monotonicNow`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First live discovery | metadata download `1` | metadata download `1` |
| Second live discovery inside the 300 s elapsed TTL | `1` (cache hit) | `1` (cache hit) |
| Backwards 1 h wall-clock step + 301 000 elapsed ms | **`1` (stale reuse: deadline stayed "fresh" for the step)** | **`2` (expired by elapsed time; upstream reloaded)** |

BASE fails the third step (`AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2`); HEAD passes. The `fetchGuard` spy records the real metadata URL and a real `RequestInit`, and the fixed `catalog.run` callback path (`runLiveProviderCatalog` → `buildLiveProvider` → `refreshMetadata` → `getCachedUpstreamProviderCatalog`) is unchanged — only the network is substituted, matching the "installed HTTP plugin + local protocol fixture" bar #193358 set.

CI follow-up in this revision: the existing `preserves failure, caches authoritative empty until expiry and supports bypass` test forced expiry with `vi.setSystemTime(1_000)` alone, which no longer moves an elapsed deadline. It now also advances the faked timers by the same span; verified red on `46943d587ac`-equivalent branch state before the test edit and green after (remote run above).

### Impact surface

| File:line | Risk |
| --- | --- |
| `src/plugins/provider-live-catalog-cache.ts:17-25,53,63,76,96,116-165` | Expiry/sweep clock only; TTL, keys, caps, pending sharing unchanged |
| `src/plugins/provider-live-catalog-cache.ts:96` | Published wall-clock deadline preserved for `catalog-access.ts:581` |

### Not tested

- No real clock step on a running Gateway; the regression tests step the process-local clock only.
- Not run against a published build.
- Local `pnpm tsgo` cannot run on this contributor host; type checking is left to CI.

### Maintainer options

<details>
<summary>Land-ready or alternatives</summary>

Narrow fix in one core cache module plus its tests. If the elapsed-clock direction accepted for the rest of the family applies here, land as-is.

Alternative considered and rejected: a single field with a consumer-side conversion. `catalog-access.ts` compares the published value against `Date.now()` in a different call path with no elapsed baseline, so the two fields are separate facts rather than one transformed one.

</details>

prs.title: feat(chat): send pending steers now without stopping the run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message steered into an active run can wait behind a long-running tool even though chat.send acknowledged it immediately. Writers need an explicit way to deliver that correction sooner without stopping the run.

## User Impact

Pending steers keep their normal user bubble, with a small **Send now** text link underneath. Clicking it interrupts supported running tools, records a user-interruption result for the model, and lets the existing steering queue continue the same run. The link disappears after injection. Repeated requests cannot interrupt later work or inject the message twice.

Tools that cannot safely stop show a quiet waiting explanation. Foreground local exec waits for process cleanup; interrupting process polling ends only the wait, preserving the independently managed background command. Code Mode aggregate tools, native/remote runtimes, and node/durable/background execution do not offer tool-only interruption. Cancellation does not undo completed side effects. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pending input retains its captured execution owner and exact queue identity. The writer-authorized chat.steerNow RPC uses that owner to interrupt only admitted tool calls; the run-level abort signal stays untouched. History projects capability through the existing physical session-store matcher, and the UI consumes that projection. No extra store scan or cache is introduced.

Interruption stays blocked while hooks prepare a tool call. The existing execution owner evaluates the final hook-rewritten arguments before making its per-call signal available for user cancellation. This fixes the hosted review finding where local exec could be rerouted to an unsafe remote invocation after the original capability decision.

Handwritten production code is net +679 lines, excluding generated validators, tests, and measurement tooling. The growth implements the new typed action, per-call interruption lifetime, and UI behavior. Pending RPC execution loads on demand while synchronous admission stays with the existing owner; redundant collections, shared rewind completion, and text-action styling were removed.

Release-note context: Control UI writers can send a pending steer immediately by interrupting supported tools while keeping the active run alive; unavailable interruption is explained in place.

## Evidence

The final repair passes 128 focused core/exec/process/hook/prefix tests, including a real Agent-to-exec hook regression that fails on the previous code. It verifies that rewritten remote execution blocks cancellation while a safe parallel sibling continues. Earlier feature proof passed 84 focused Gateway/tool tests covering writer authorization, exact input identity, idempotency, FIFO, physical cleanup, model-visible interruption and continued execution.

Final real Gateway/Control UI proof passed in 35.15 seconds using isolated state, owned ports, a real local exec process and deterministic loopback inference. It verified the visible click, physical tool cleanup before the next model request, one steer consumption, continued original-run output and removal of the link. This is not external live-provider inference evidence. Full synthetic before/after images were inspected and are embedded below. The final UI repair also passes 36 focused UI tests and the original owner-picker E2E at desktop and compact widths. Types, lint, formatting, protocol generation and native contract checks passed. Final isolated Codex autoreview is clean through P2, including the test-only consolidation.

The final pnpm check:changed run passed all selected candidate gates except a new controller-rule finding that was repaired and passed its canonical targeted replay. Its separate inherited release-attribution failure remains recorded: the generic guard does not consume the release candidate's accepted 2026.11.1 tag exception. Exact introducing parent f07f46a62fe0 passes; de04fbe0caa9 (#193427), the task base, and the earlier exact CI main parent reproduce it. This is an unresolved main regression for its owner, not noise or a green check. No release record or guard exception was changed; no timeout or budget ceiling was increased.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): advertise accepted protocol versions in the signed snapshot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After #193688, a client can recognize a protocol version it doesn't implement, but it has no trustworthy way to learn which versions a Gateway accepts. Without that, a client and Gateway that share a newer version can't find it, and a version list served by Discovery could be edited to push clients onto an older one.

## User Impact

None yet. Only v1 exists and the package is still `v1-draft`. Once a second version ships, clients pick the highest version they share with the Gateway, and they only report "update required" when the Gateway's signed list says so.

This changes the v1-draft snapshot format in place: `MembershipSnapshot` gains a required `protocols` field. Gateways, the Discovery Worker and the browser loader must update their copies of this package together. That's acceptable before release, but staging needs a coordinated rollout.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway lists the versions it accepts for new input in its K_gw-signed `MembershipSnapshot`: `protocols: { statement: [...], descriptor: [...] }`. Each list must be non-empty and strictly ascending. `snapshotBody` fills it from the package's supported-version tables, so the Gateway emits it without further changes.
- `assessFreshness` returns `protocols` only on a fresh verdict. Clients use no other source: an edited list fails the signature check, and a list older than one the client has already seen fails freshness.
- `selectVersion(advertised, local)` picks the highest shared version. With no shared version it returns `update_required` or `gateway_outdated`.
- The tunnel isn't listed. Its version is the QUIC ALPN, which is agreed inside the TLS handshake that K_srv authenticates, so a relay can't change it.
- `docs/versioning.md` gains a "Choosing a version" section. It states the security boundary plainly: negotiation only affects compatibility, because the Gateway refuses any version not on its own list. The section also documents two limits. Discovery can replay an older signed list, up to three hours old, to a client that hasn't seen the newer one. And without fresh evidence a client can pick a version the Gateway refuses; that refusal means "get fresh evidence and choose again", not "update".

This is PR 2 of 3. The Gateway, UI, Discovery and loader changes that show an "update required" message are follow-ups. Today they fold `unsupported_version` into their generic errors. They will change once the Gateway stack (#192335 and the PRs above it) is rebased and Discovery and the loader update their copies of this package. Owner reset (OCF-319) is PR 3.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 23 files, 151 tests passed. New `src/negotiation.test.ts` covers version selection, the signed list reaching clients only on fresh evidence, edited lists failing verification, replay after a newer snapshot was seen, and malformed lists.
- Fixtures regenerated. Only the two snapshot vectors change (the new field and their signatures); all other v1 signing inputs are byte-identical.
- An independent review found no P0/P1 issues and two P2 findings, both docs claiming more than the code does (the replay window and the no-evidence fallback). Both are fixed in the second commit.
- Core typecheck, core test typecheck, oxlint, format and the test-lines ratchet pass.

Not covered: Gateway, Discovery and loader integration, and the staging rollout of the new snapshot field.

prs.title: fix(cli): publish CoreDNS config atomically with preserved permissions
prs.body:
Closes #184888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `openclaw dns setup --apply` rewrites an existing CoreDNS `Corefile` (and its `.server` files) by truncating in place, so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write destroys the operator's DNS configuration with no backup and no recovery copy (the file lives outside OpenClaw's state dir).

## User Impact
A failed write no longer destroys the previous Corefile or `.server` contents. Existing file and parent-directory permissions are preserved (the previous code kept them by writing directly); newly created files keep `writeFileSync`'s umask-respecting permissions instead of the helper's restrictive defaults; CoreDNS setups that use a symlinked `Corefile` or a symlinked `conf.d` keep working and now also publish atomically.

## Why This Change Was Made
`writeFileSudoIfNeeded` called `fs.writeFileSync` on the final path (and `sudo tee` as fallback), which truncates before any content is written. It now uses `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s `replaceFileAtomicSync` (temp-file + rename): a failed publication leaves the previous bytes exactly as they were, verified by a regression that injects a `renameSync` failure. Options chosen deliberately: `preserveExistingMode: true` so existing rwx bits survive, `dirMode` pinned to the immediate parent's current mode so helper defaults cannot tighten existing directories, and `mode: 0o666 & ~process.umask()` for new files. Symlinked Corefiles publish to their real target (dangling links resolve the link target, normalizing its real parent when the target does not exist yet). The `sudo tee` fallback is unchanged.

## Evidence
Level A (real CLI entry `dns setup --apply` driven by the repo's test harness with synthetic paths and no operator files touched):
- Rename failure injected: the pre-existing Corefile is byte-identical afterward. Red on base (the truncate path left it partial), green with this change.
- Existing Corefile and parent directory modes preserved after a successful rewrite (0755/0644 fixtures); a newly created Corefile gets `0o666 & ~umask` rather than fs-safe's 0600.
- Real symlinked Corefile, a dangling link, and a symlinked `conf.d` directory all publish correctly and preserve the link itself; a nested dangling case whose target sits inside a symlinked directory also passes.
- All 12 cases in `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` pass (node 24.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --run`).
- Independent Codex review of the final diff found four findings, all addressed and re-verified (restrictive default modes, new-file umask mode, symlink handling, dangling-link parent normalization).
- Known boundary disclosed deliberately: fs-safe's `applyDirectoryMode` chmods the parent directory even when its mode already matches and does not restore it on failure; the privilege-escalation fallback (`sudo tee`) is unchanged and out of this fix's scope.
- Not run locally: tsgo/extension-boundary lanes and a live CoreDNS installation (CI covers the type lanes).

prs.title: fix(workers): avoid rehashing unchanged snapshot workspaces
prs.body:
Fixes snapshot-fork registration rehashing unchanged prepared files.

## What Problem This Solves

Registering a workspace restored from a prepared snapshot loses its in-process hash memo and reads every eligible file again, which is especially slow on lazily restored block storage. First bind repeats that work if it runs in another process.

## User Impact

Unchanged files reuse their attested hashes across snapshot restoration and process restarts. Changed files are still hashed, and a real manifest mismatch still rejects registration or first bind. Missing, malformed, unreadable, or nonmatching memo entries fall back to hashing; no migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest capture owner now saves an optional, private stat-identity/hash artifact beside each manifest. Project preparation carries the prepared tree's memo into the home captured by the snapshot. Registration and bind already use this capture owner, so both benefit without another verification path or protocol/database schema changes.

The local artifact covers the full existing inventory bound; the smaller remote memo limit is unchanged. It contains device/inode, size, nanosecond mtime/ctime and hashes, never file contents or setup secrets. Recent hashes are recorded for later restoration, but the existing two-second ctime safety window still controls reuse. The snapshot scrubber preserves the prepared manifest directory.

Assumption: block snapshots retain inode and timestamp metadata, and reuse additionally requires the same device identity. Providers that recreate files or change the device identity simply rehash. Accepted edge case: a same-size, same-mtime, same-ctime edit with unchanged device/inode can reuse the prior hash, matching the existing memo semantics. No-follow opens, file-type checks and before/after stats remain in place.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on origin/main `2c04aec4eb6f92daf70c7ddab7a4fd938384ecf0`: a second registration in a fresh process reads all five unchanged files (expected zero). Focused baseline command: `pnpm test src/node-host/node-worker-prepared-workspace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'reuses checkpoint hashes'`, 115.77 s wall time.
- With the fix, first registration reads five files; fresh-process registration and first bind read zero; modifying one file reads it once and rejects the mismatch; missing/corrupt memos read all five. The new regression took 73.197 s on the loaded host because it boots six independent Node processes and their real workers, without sleeps or mocked capture results.
- 93 tests passed in eight files, 377.80 s total wall time: the three node-worker prepared-workspace suites, node-worker workspace-manifest, workspace-hash-memo, project-preparation, workspace-manifest-script.runtime, and server-worker-environment-startup. The latter contains the prepared startup tests in the current tree. Existing producer coverage also verifies that the saved memo matches the prepared tree's inode and content; the capped-transport fixture verifies that the local memo retains every file.
- `pnpm run tsgo:core`, type-aware `run-oxlint.mjs` for changed core/test/generated files and the benchmark, `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on changed code/docs, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Local benchmark acceptance: identical manifest; zero candidate content hashes; lower median and p95 verification time. `scripts/perf/prepared-workspace-verification.mjs` creates 4,000 files × 32 KiB (125 MiB), then runs five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, each in a fresh process with an empty in-memory memo and a warm OS cache. macOS, Node 26.12.1, load averages approximately 72/73/74:

| Metric | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Content reads per verification | 4,000 | 0 |
| Median | 887.83 ms | 522.46 ms |
| p95 | 1,509.79 ms | 1,008.30 ms |
| Range | 540.19–1,509.79 ms | 382.42–1,008.30 ms |

This is local capture wall time (excluding process startup), not an AWS end-to-end measurement.  Runtime growth is 36 source lines plus 98 regenerated lines (134 production lines); the test-line allocation covers the fresh-process and producer regressions.

## Live proof

Isolated Gateway, AWS worker, real `openclaw/openclaw` checkout (about 64,000 tracked files), real snapshot fork:

- Before this change the first forced checkout on a fork rewrote 64,382 files in 3,985 ms, because the captured index still described the seed's inodes. After refreshing the index it rewrites 0 files in 77 ms and disk growth stops following checkout size.
- The persisted memo reused 64,326 of 64,385 hashes on a ready-worker adoption; only changed files were hashed again, and an edit still changed the manifest (`aba64…` to `499c6…`, memo hits 7 to 10 in the regression).
- Whole-environment time on that repository moved only from 361 s to 336 s with this change alone. This removes real waste, but the remaining fork time lives in the Crabbox `run` regression and first-touch reads, handled separately.

Independent Codex autoreview covered the complete local change against `cb719feef55c307d473129525a41ec3ebdf1d0d6` through P2. It returned one finding about an adversarial same-UID process forging the local memo. Rejected after checking [the documented host trust model](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/SECURITY.md#deployment-assumptions) and [the paired-node boundary](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloud-workers/native-inference#deployment-and-credential-trust-contract): same-OS-user code can already rewrite node state/environment or process memory, and is not isolated from the node. Snapshot sharing already requires mutually trusted workloads. Managed execution requires a bound workspace; first registration occurs before session attachment. The final comment/docs make this existing boundary explicit. No accepted actionable findings remain; the review itself returned a finding, not a clean verdict.

A second independent Codex review of the final head, including the index refresh, returned no P0 or P1 findings.

prs.body:
## Summary

Talk's shared provider data types also owned host configuration and session-creation contexts. Move the four existing host contexts into the private `provider-contexts.ts` owner and migrate the complete 22-path type cutover, removing the old declarations without forwarding aliases.

Keep provider descriptors and synchronous factories, callbacks, the Gateway-control union, existing SDK names and runtime behavior unchanged. Preserve the current callback-only plugin wrapping/cloneable request config, monotonic-clock controls, and unrelated provider contracts. The voice runtime facades remain private and JS-only.

## Validation

Prepared `b88d9b875bbe2ca5f470f445f466b530241d9430` against `d999f7b1b675d8702b38fb65760475f59f203130` through normal current-owner integration.

- **544 tests passed across 22 files:** 441 main-shard tests plus 103 SDK/provider tests. The repeated tooling summary is one run. No cases or assertions changed.
- Production types, 29 selected test-type graphs, root script test types, scoped typed lint/format/whitespace, line/test/assertion/mock ratchets, SDK export/surface checks, and production/full-tree unused-file scans passed.
- Full build passed. Strict compile-only consumers of actual emitted `core` and `plugin-entry` exercise all four request shapes and both registration forms with `skipLibCheck: false`; no source aliases, casts or factory execution.
- Canonical SDK comparison records 167 reachable-closure changes across 27 public entries, with no entrypoint or direct export-signature changes. All three complete declaration-detail pairs were aligned by source identity: four unchanged declarations moved; remaining data and capability declarations are unchanged apart from type imports.
- Fresh local ClawSweeper review of the exact prepared range completed with no actionable findings and 0.98 confidence. It reviewed source and saved declaration/proof evidence; it did not independently execute tests or compilers.

Measured against the prepared base: production +14 LF, test/support -6 LF, allocation 0. No performance, initialization-cost or LOC-saving claim.

## Recorded limits

Two local export scans remain failed and unwaived: `readUpdatePhysicalDatabaseGenerations` in `src/infra/update-physical-database-generations.ts`, and `enqueueSlackRun` in `src/auto-reply/reply/queue.test-helpers.ts`. Their owners, inspected scanner inputs and named references are unchanged from the prepared base. The base checker was not executed; these local failures do not establish a failing-base run or a diagnosed scanner defect.

The successful build reported a nonfatal chat-boot gzip advisory (1264.8 KiB versus 1264.4 KiB). The initial consumer fixture omitted the existing required `onClearAudio` callback; that proof input was corrected and its strict compile passed, with no source change.

Tests use mocked/synthetic providers and isolated state. Live-provider/operator Gateway and native Linux node qualification are not claimed. The native owner qualified enforced owner/review, current authority and landing admission before the recorded squash merge.
## Hosted CI

[Run 42112292862, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42112292862) completed with **57 successful jobs, two failures and 25 planner skips** at the exact published head. `security-fast`, all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, types, lint and baseline ratchets passed. Skips are not executed passes.

The only non-aggregate failure is [the updater shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42112292862/job/127543561506): `update-cli > ends unfinished retention at --timeout with the installed package untouched`. Timeout output is present, but the run record remains `running/validating` where the assertion expects `failed/finished`. The second failure is the downstream CI gate. Its automated classification is unknown because no matching main job was available.

The complete primary log identifies tested merge `c288fa3e142c25dd798366e3b9bca7ac0e977cce`, with ordered parents `d41332b5b3798623314a0469441dbbf654996f45` and the prepared head. Its first-parent delta is exactly the 22 reviewed Talk paths, all byte-identical to the prepared cut. The updater test, preflight helper and admission owner are unchanged from that CI base; the Talk change preserves executable bodies and value routes. Source inspection qualifies this failure as independent of the type-only extraction. No failing-base test execution is claimed, and the mechanism leaving the updater record nonterminal remains unknown.

One focused diagnostic on the unchanged macOS candidate passed (one test, 18 skipped); it is separate from the **544/22** owning proof and does not diagnose or fix the hosted failure. No CI rerun or updater edit was made. The normal guarded inherited-failure route admitted this scoped attribution while retaining the failed attempt and qualifying independent security, enforced review and live authority. Squash `6e7ee204e1b1fef223c794dbbed42de069a2623e` merged on 2026-11-05 at 22:15:15 UTC, followed by normal COMPLETE closeout. This remains **failed CI**, not a green run.

prs.title: fix(tools): stop warning about canvas-implied show_widget on surfaces without widgets
prs.body:
Related: #158832

## What Problem This Solves

A `canvas` allowlist grant expands to `canvas` plus `show_widget`. On a surface whose tool-listing client lacks `inline-widgets`, the resulting unavailable-widget warning is expected capability absence, not an operator misconfiguration. `group:openclaw` alone does not reproduce this warning.

This PR changes diagnostics only. Tool filtering, family grants, deny handling and execution capability checks are unchanged. It implements the issue's option 2; maintainer acceptance of that diagnostic policy is still required, not implied by the automated recommendation.

## Implementation at 2adae69042f1e03962cb8f48ba811054caf082cd

- The existing client-capability filter records names of tools it actually built and then withheld from the listing because a required capability was missing.
- Gateway tool resolution, embedded tool construction and skill dispatch carry that fact to the allowlist analyzer.
- The analyzer suppresses only family-implied entries recorded as capability-withheld, never a literal configured entry. A disabled canvas host with no channel presenter never builds `show_widget`, so it is not recorded and its warning is retained.
- Callers without construction evidence retain warnings. This includes static name projections, effective-policy/access diagnostics, MCP serving and externally prepared tool inventories.
- `core-tool-facts.ts` remains identical to base, avoiding the earlier Control UI boot-size regression. The memory-flush diagnostic reason moved into its existing setup owner to keep `agent-tools.ts` within its existing file-size limit; its text and conditions are unchanged.

The trade-off is a small construction-to-diagnostics data path instead of a static tool-name exemption; unknown absence reasons deliberately keep warning.

## Evidence

The worker reports the new host-disabled regression failed at a89c221c (1 failed, 27 passed), then passed with this revision. Existing coverage preserves capless family suppression, group-only behavior, literal-entry warnings and unmatched canvas/other unavailable-core warnings. Construction-level tests distinguish capability filtering from a disabled host.

The worker reports 274/274 tests passing across 15 focused files, plus clean oxlint/oxfmt and max-lines ratchet. Typechecking is left to CI: none was run on this host.

Independently verified at e11b5258:

- Fork branch and GitHub PR head both match the named SHA; tracked working tree clean.
- Focused independent Vitest run: **57/57 passed** (17 tool-policy, 28 pipeline, 12 scheduled-widget construction tests). No typecheck.
- Test-lines ratchet passes: 6453971 lines, ceiling 6453971, slack 0. That revision used a 46-line allocation; the current allocation-only follow-up raises it to 69 lines to cover the CI merge-tree baseline.
- `core-tool-facts.ts` is identical to base. The earlier size-only revision measured +0 B chat/new boot; no fresh UI performance measurement is claimed for this revision.

## Real Gateway evidence at 2adae69042f1e03962cb8f48ba811054caf082cd

Three scenarios, each on its own isolated Gateway (fresh synthetic state/config, loopback only, no model turn, no external API). The client connects over the real Gateway WebSocket as the first-party local CLI identity with shared-token auth (authenticated role `operator`, scopes `operator.admin`/`read`/`write`), calls the shipped `tools.invoke` RPC, which resolves tools through `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts`, and captures the Gateway's own allowlist warnings.

| Scenario | Allowlist grant | Client caps | Canvas host | `show_widget` resolved | Unknown-entry warning for `show_widget` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1: family grant, client without capability | `group:openclaw`, `canvas` | none | enabled | no (`not_found`) | **none** (suppressed, as intended) |
| 2: literal entry | `group:openclaw`, `canvas`, `show_widget` | none | enabled | no (`not_found`) | **retained** |
| 3: capable client, host disabled | `group:openclaw`, `canvas` | `inline-widgets` | disabled | no (`not_found`) | **retained** |

In all three, `canvas` is constructed and selected: a deliberately invalid action returns an execution error, not `not_found`. Scenarios 1–2 also list the exact capless inventory through a Gateway-minted `attach.grant` over loopback MCP `tools/list`, and revoke the grant afterwards. `show_widget` is absent from it and `canvas` is present. Scenario 3 cannot use that listing because attach grants intentionally discard caller capability headers, so it relies on the `tools.invoke` presence probes only.

Warnings retained in scenarios 2 and 3 (verbatim):

```
tools.profile (messaging) allowlist contains unknown entries (show_widget). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (show_widget). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
```

The summarizer fails closed on missing or malformed captures, wrong auth scopes or caps, incomplete probes, or a failed listing/revoke. It reported `allExpectationsMet: true` and pins the head SHA plus the blob SHAs of the nine changed source files. Raw logs, tokens and local paths are kept local, and the redacted summary was checked to contain none.

Limits of this evidence: no base-revision control run was captured, so the "before" state for scenario 1 rests on the issue report and the regression tests. In scenario 1, the isolated Gateway's shutdown reported that spawn-broker cleanup could not be confirmed (`ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`). The capture had already completed, and the error is unrelated to this change.

## Remaining decisions

Current main's Doctor tool-schema projection discards policy warnings, so the reporter's released Doctor route is not confirmed. This is why the issue is Related, not Closes.

CI on `2adae690`: all technical checks pass. The only failing check is `openclaw/ci-gate`, and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` is pending; both wait for maintainer approval of the current revision.

A maintainer must accept the diagnostic-policy choice and review/approve the current security-sensitive revision.

prs.title: feat(plugins): prepare automation tools and preserve runtime defaults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automation can be approved or saved without a configured default tool, then fail when its instructions need that tool. Plugins also need to prepare a selection against the creating turn's executable permissions before requesting approval.

`ctx.prepareCronToolSelection` prepares that concrete selection before approval. The submission callback preserves the original proposal and current creator authority through approval and native persistence. Embedded runs bind preparation to completed tool capture after policy filtering and schema quarantine; preparation before capture or after generation retirement is rejected. Incomplete configured MCP discovery remains incomplete when app discovery succeeds.

Configured `cron.defaultTools` extends nonempty effective selections during isolated agent-turn execution for existing and new jobs, without rewriting saved payloads, approvals, or run identity. Downstream permissions and execution-target checks still apply. Saved `toolsAllowMode: "exact"` opts out durably; `"defaults"` resets that choice. Explicit empty selections remain tool-less. Schedule/name-only edits preserve copied selections; a mode-only reset reloads the job, prepares its current tools before approval, and saves against its current configuration revision.

## Current status

**Draft; full acceptance remains incomplete.** Current signed head is `c7074a8eb01b7fc84661af7e0f6dfe9ca4d7df7b`, including captured canonical main `ec702e8338827dee1ef3ec28a931842c6be9826b` through that signed merge.

The supported nonrelease full run [42079940382](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42079940382) targets older source `ab781ec9549e6ae6c815549063a9f10fcd8254c8`, verified by its preflight. Its workflow revision `6869e37c69c3ac2a7ead000d3e866b3e994ae24a` is not the tested source. The run completed with failure. It is not active; its unresolved failures remain under investigation. It does not qualify this newer head. No new full run, retry, or cancellation was requested for this repair.

#187798 (configured defaults before approval) and #186306 (reader-enabled automation guidance) are merged. Those merges do not establish this broader runtime/defaults follow-up's acceptance.

Selected-model capability discovery and live consumer qualification remain open. A supported custom model may expose no shell while the native projection infers `read`/`exec`; a partial native bridge list is not proof of the complete callable surface. Session-target runtime default projection remains separate. This PR does not add a producer capability API or establish live scheduled `read` execution.

## CI repairs in this update

- Removed the unused `operator-recovery.test-support.ts` orphan and unnecessary exports reported by the dependency check. No Knip ignores or baselines changed.
- Updated the scheduled native-child fixture to distinguish the stored inherited ceiling from effective permissions. It resolves the actual accepted child's persisted session through `prepareConversationCapabilityProfile` and the canonical policy pipeline, requiring `read` to remain while `automations` and legacy `cron` are excluded. Hidden-child hard denials enforce this restriction; the test does not invent or claim inherited `selfJobId` authority. The parent scheduling facade is also absent.
- Integrated pinned main for verified existing owner repairs: [#193651](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193651), `7e93c1681b7cc68377dde0c75cb5d0845de8f024`, restores the Swift shared-chat inheritance expectations; [#193642](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193642), `566559c6bd3c2d39b53c2a468f50ca5fd0afefb1`, refreshes native locales; [#193671](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193671), `a7c42ae41d3b5c99ca273f0e7f6bdc6b462d12c4`, refreshes Control UI locales. Generated locale files come from those canonical owner commits. Their inclusion is source repair evidence, not a local Swift/i18n test-pass claim.


Latest integration also reuses canonical macOS fix #193686 (`54ed2bcc`) for the stable real Bun path and bundled identity assertion. The stronger scheduled-child policy test was preserved. No new full run has qualified this head. The older ingress loader failure occurred under Bun while its Node cases passed; a root cause or repaired result has not yet been established.

prs.title: fix(update): name and retry busy files during backup capture
prs.body:
Refs #193673. Builds on the diagnostic transport in #187927 by @wr-web (Wang Rui).

## Problem and behavior

Windows backup capture can fail while reading a retained file's SQLite header without identifying the file. Header discovery now carries the absolute path, code, and numeric errno through the isolated child. Windows `EBUSY`, `EPERM`, and `EACCES` receive two retries, after 50 ms and 100 ms, with the descriptor closed before waiting. Recovery emits a warning. Persistent failures name the file and code, with the home prefix shortened in the operator-facing diagnostic.

Unreadable candidates still refuse capture before archive publication. Check the named file's permissions or close the program holding it, then retry. Core `.sqlite` files bypass header reads; sidecars map to their main database, and real SQLite capture retains the existing verified snapshot owner. Backup/rollback owners and durability contracts are unchanged. The runtime running the probe must contain this fix; a candidate package cannot repair an already-running old updater.

#187927 already carries path/code, including busy reads. It was inactive for over 24 hours at takeover and lacked bounded retries. This PR preserves that approach and original author credit.

## Current-head proof

Head `8926dd997ae29b39899a82f88ccd3419dc7c27ae`; [canonical CI 42106962448](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448), attempt 1. Preflight and individual job logs confirm that selected checkout, separately from workflow-ref SHA `6d7347b2`.

- [Build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448/job/127525512099), production/test types, and [core lint stripe 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448/job/127525514575) PASS. The previously introduced redundant `<void>` was removed in the sole one-line follow-up; exact-head CI confirms the repair.
- [Named capture suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448/job/127525537000): all three cases PASS under Node 24.22.1 and Bun, including injected persistent EBUSY refusal with path/errno, no archive, unchanged bytes, and the declared current-runtime child path.
- All five Windows rows PASS. [Row 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448/job/127525513256) actually selects the new `backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.windows.test.ts`: **2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, win32/x64/Node 24.22.1. Native transient trace is `EBUSY`, errno `-4082`, then a successful 16-byte read. Persistent trace is three native EBUSY reads; refusal, empty archive directory, exact source/config preservation, unlocked control capture, archive verification, and holder cleanup all pass. Cases take 982 ms and 1600 ms.
- The native test uses an external PowerShell FileStream range lock with explicit readiness and unlock acknowledgment in isolated synthetic state. A test-only preload observes real `readSync` exceptions, coordinates transient release after denial, and rethrows the same native error; it does not inject errno or alter production retries. This is production capture-owner source proof, not an installed npm CLI test. EPERM/EACCES fault cases remain unit-only evidence.
- Independent final-content P0–P3 review is clean at committed tree `32535958c776631a4230de7a1259656db5304062`; the complete addition and subsequent one-line repair were reviewed separately. No source changes followed review. Both Wang Rui and steipete coauthor trailers remain intact.

Covers transient/persistent EBUSY/EPERM/EACCES, EIO, non-Windows EBUSY, ENOENT and ELOOP. These injected-error unit cases are separate from the real Windows lock proof above. Earlier base-versus-fix and prior-head `4fa23030` evidence remain supporting prior evidence only.

## Published-stable upgrade and restoration

[Terminal Docker seed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448/job/127525512873) PASS, attempt 1, 20:52:05–22:04:29Z. The [uploaded survivor receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448/artifacts/13457212779) records a real isolated Linux npm-global updater transition from published `openclaw@2026.10.10` to packed candidate `2026.11.1`, scenario `legacy-operator-state`, install mode `updater`, outcome `success`. The canonical resolver selected the newest published stable predecessor below candidate version; this is the tested baseline, not an all-version matrix.

Product checkout is full `8926dd997ae29b39899a82f88ccd3419dc7c27ae`; the harness separately uses `6d7347b2`. The full package build/pack and tarball integrity check pass. Retained update JSON reports build ID `2026.11.1-8926dd997ae2-2026-11-05T20-53-35.276Z`. The upload does not include the numeric candidate tarball SHA256, so no such checksum is claimed. Receipt ZIP SHA256 is `a05947c1c08765aed28488d70c0c02ef9b7664112d03642898643c97b19b68b5`.

The receipt passes automatic migration before standalone Doctor, config/approval/workspace survival, Gateway/cron/agent/plugin checks, and verified backup restoration through the retained **2026.10.10** runtime. Restoration compares three databases' table counts/hashes to the pre-upgrade inventory, verifies raw transcripts without omissions, and reads main/ops sessions with the old runtime (1/0 sessions). prs.title: feat(telegram): add one-message ignore command
prs.body:
Related: #123937

Fresh narrow replacement for #123984, following the message-level-only direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/123984#issuecomment-6380122014.

## What Problem This Solves

Human participants in authorized Telegram groups need a one-message opt-out for side comments that should not enter the agent's context.

## User Impact

User impact: a participant admitted by the existing Telegram group sender policy can send `/ignore <text>` to exclude only that fresh text update from history and agent dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

This handles `/ignore <text>` and `/ignore@ThisBot <text>` after normal sender authorization but before session, cache, reply-chain, media, or agent work. A bare command returns usage help, and an account-level custom `/ignore` command keeps ownership.

The scope is intentionally one-shot. It adds no storage, tombstones, replay or restart persistence, album/caption behavior, edit suppression, reply-chain cleanup, or cross-channel contract. Later edits use Telegram's existing edited-message path and can enter context normally.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `3186b48d8ec70c719b245690dd02e6e47b4fa1bc`.
- Focused parser and inbound-history suites: **25/25 passed**, including authorization placement, custom-command ownership, native-command disablement, and edit reintroduction.
- Full changed-scope gate passed, including formatting, lint, extension and test typechecks, plugin boundaries, import cycles, SQLite guards, repository policy checks, and the justified `124`-line test allocation required by the current test-line ratchet. The final documentation clarification and edit regression also passed their exact focused test, typecheck, and lint reruns.
- Independent exact-head P0-P2 review found no actionable defect after inspecting the unchanged authorization and edited-update owners.
- Telegram Test Server proof is `blocked_external`: the local doctor found no authenticated Convex launcher/broker pair. No live official-client claim is made; that remains the explicit proof gap.

<details>
<summary>Merge brief</summary>

- **Scope:** 5 Telegram-owned product/test/docs files plus one required test-allocation metadata file, 196 additions, no persistence or schema changes.
- **Contract:** fresh, human-authored group text only; normal sender admission still applies.

prs.title: fix(ios): restart Files pagination when the folder drifts under the cursor
prs.body:
Closes #193500

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS Files "Load More" button keeps requesting the same final page without ever completing, when a file is created in the workspace between page loads.

## User Impact

User impact: files that land before the current pagination position now show up — one reload recovers the listing, and Load More finishes or disappears instead of looping on a page that contains only already-listed entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

`AgentWorkspaceDirectoryList.loadMore` used the deduplicated local row count (`entries.count`) as the next server offset. A file inserted before the cursor makes the following page overlap the local list; its rows dedupe away, the local count stops growing, and `entries.count < totalEntries` stays true, so every tap re-requests the same final entry.

The fix tracks server-side pagination progress separately in `WorkspaceListPagination`. When a consumed page reaches the reported end of the directory while local rows are still short, the view reloads the folder once so the inserted rows appear. Failed pages keep the cursor unchanged, so retry after a failed page still works, and `.refreshable` / `.task(id:)` already reset the cursor through `reload()`.

## Evidence

- Root cause verified against current `main` source: the offset request at `apps/ios/Sources/Design/AgentWorkspaceFilesScreen.swift:180` (offset `entries.count`, deduplicated append, button condition at line 71) matches the issue report.
- The pagination state machine is a standalone type; its logic was compiled and executed against the issue's exact scenario (251-entry folder, insertion before the cursor, offset 250 returning `Note 250.md` + `Note 251.md`, then repeated offset-251 requests) plus static-folder completion and reload-recovery cases — all pass:

  ```
  offset 0   → advanced, cursor 250
  offset 250 → driftDetected (252 total, 251 local)
  reload → reset; offset 0 → advanced; offset 250 → advanced, 252 local == 252 total
  ```

- Regression tests added in `apps/ios/Tests/AgentWorkspaceFilesPaginationTests.swift`: static folder completion, insertion-before-cursor drift, and reload recovery. `swiftc -parse` passes on both changed files.
- CI note: the first CI run failed the iOS `SwiftFormat (lint)` build phase because `AgentWorkspaceFilesScreen.swift` violated the pinned swiftformat 0.63.1 rules (`wrapMultilineStatementBraces` ×2, `andOperator`); fixed in `743b206a814` by running the pinned binary with this repo's config, verified lint-green locally, and the redundant stalled-page test flagged by review was removed.
- Native behavior proof (independent contributor run by @ellibbe, [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193660#issuecomment-6667224040)): on iPhone 17 Simulator / iOS 27.0 (Xcode 27.2, Light mode), a loopback WebSocket fixture serves a real synthetic 251-file directory and inserts `A new note.md` after the first response, exercising the real `AgentWorkspaceDirectoryList.loadMore` and its automatic reload. Base `a54bdb3c608f` fails the automatic-reload assertion (stuck at 251 of 252, RPC offsets `[0, 250]`); this head passes — the inserted file appears and Load More disappears after completion (offsets `[0, 250, 0, 250]`; the final passing run also scrolled to the visible end and confirmed Load More is absent). This covers the native behavior proof requested in review; no snapshot-lane expansion is needed for this contribution. Scope caveats from that run: the fixture does not execute the complete Gateway handler, and the app-hosted unit runner compiled but did not start (bounded retry after a simulator restart timed out), so no iOS-hosted unit-test pass is claimed. The run qualified the pre-integration tree (`743b206a814`); it is an independent contributor run, not a maintainer qualification.
- Integration with `main`: merged `main` @ `6b959f4ca63` in `43003185d63`, resolving the `loadMore` conflict with #193504 so its stale-error clearing (`errorText = nil`) runs before `consume`/`reload` — a failed reload keeps its own new error visible. Verified locally: pinned swiftformat 0.63.1 lint 0/1, `swiftc -parse` clean, standalone `WorkspaceListPagination` assertions ALL PASS; the failed-Load-More → successful-retry path is covered by the `AgentWorkspacePaginationUITests` fixture #193504 adds, now on this branch via the merge for CI.
- Validation boundary: this machine has only the Command Line Tools (no full Xcode), so the SwiftUI target build and the XCTest run are left to CI; the standalone logic run above covers the state machine itself. The new Swift test file is not counted by the test-lines ratchet (it tracks `*.test.ts/mts/js` patterns only), so no allocation is needed.
