prs.title: fix(agents): hand delegated failures back to their parent
prs.body:
## Summary
- Return failed subagents' cause and saved progress to their owning parent without waiting on the failed root's descendants.
- Quiet inherited error attention only after durable input/result custody, while preserving child diagnostics, collector ownership and genuine native human questions.
- Keep failure diagnostics in the committed handoff, preserve ready unconsumed failed-collector findings, and count handed-off failures correctly.
- Acknowledge failure custody only for children represented in the committed input. A bounded batch keeps omitted failures unacknowledged and recoverable.
- Collector results: acknowledge only failures whose diagnostics survive in the final persisted tool result, after transcript truncation and detail reduction, and only for the expected host completion. Failures dropped from the stored result stay unacknowledged and recoverable.
- Bind private settle retries to the findings they replay: a retry that reuses the retained message acknowledges only failed runs whose diagnostics are in those exact bytes and that are still in the current cohort. A legacy retained message without that record adds no acknowledgement, and a new run generation under the same ID does not inherit it.
- Keep the 160,000-character findings budget, with its truncation markers, per-result floors, stable order and overflow summary.
- Keep the receipt in cold reads: the compact SQL session-list projection now selects the four `failureHandoff` fields, including the `parentCompletion` mirror. No schema, writer, codec, migration or retention change.
- Leave ordinary session rows unchanged on the wire: `failureHandedOff` is sent only when true.

## Delivery contracts
- Settle (`subagent_settle`): the complete bounded cohort message, including healthy children's findings, is stored as the hidden replay input, exactly as on `main`. Private retries keep their own retained input and failure IDs.
- Direct completion (`subagent_announce`): a healthy child's result stays in runtime context only; a failed child's diagnostics are saved with the handoff.
- Collector: results remain an ordinary durable tool result; failure custody follows what was actually stored.

## Integration with `main`
- This branch merges `main` at `68fbe4a` (#188180) with no conflicts and no resolution edits. All 96 feature files are byte-identical to the pre-merge commit `46ab0a0`.
- Against `main`, the PR changes 96 files, +4189/−392. The larger first-parent diff of that merge is upstream `main`, not new feature code.
- Earlier merges brought in `315380c` (#188047) without conflicts and `445e566` with a conflict in the three Control UI end-to-end test inventory files, resolved by keeping both sides' entries.
- Test repairs merged on `main` and included through the merge: #188178 (widget retention fixture), #188156 (empty-leaf admission), #188195 (thinking-claim ordering) and #188180 (keyed commentary in refreshed history). Earlier: #188047, #187979, #187933 and #188056. None is copied as a separate patch.
- `main` has moved since `68fbe4a`. The Copy-feedback repair landed on `main` as #188311; #188299, which overlapped it, was closed without merging. Separate test-only corrections for the new-session draft and quota tests are being prepared and are not yet published. This branch has not yet integrated the newer `main`.

## Stream-budget test readiness
- `chat-stream-runtime-budgets.e2e.test.ts` ("commits a streamed delta burst in frame-bound transcript batches") could count native pane commits caused by lazily loaded menu translation catalogs. Those landed after the measurement reset but before the first measured delta.
- The test now waits until the menu modules already requested by the page, and their dependencies, have loaded and the active pane has finished updating, before it measures. The original assertion, thresholds, timers and production code are unchanged. A new line allocation of 136 covers this test-only code.
- On `53ee37c`, Linux CI passed all six tests in that file.

## Verification
- Independent QA of the current source (`d70644f`): PASS with notes, no findings or blockers.
  - One fresh private Gateway build and matching Control UI (build `2026.10.9-d70644fb5c3c-2026-10-30T10-03-19.128Z`) ran a real Gateway and browser test through all four modes: default, parent-target, yielded and collector.
  - Each mode asked a native question, survived a reload, accepted a suggested choice or free text, kept durable custody, delivered the final reply in the same run as the answer, and showed no failed-child attention. Each mode verified that the served UI asset matched the build byte for byte.
  - In default mode, a descendant that finished late did not revive the failed child.
  - Five new test cases in four files ran: the four-mode Gateway case, three native legacy and cold-read cases, and one historical import case. The author's 215 tests and 6 boundary checks were not rerun; the two sets overlap and are not added together.
  - The provider was scripted locally, not a hosted model. Screenshots were inspected locally; none are attached.
- Independent review of the `main` integration effects on `d70644f`: PASS with notes, no integration defect or new missing context. All 96 feature files are unchanged, and `main`'s 522 changed paths do not overlap them. The `main` changes to outer authorization, the QuickJS namespace copy, collector inputs and attention inputs leave the delivery, persistence and custody paths unchanged. This is a source assessment, not a new canonical review or tests.
- Current source (`d70644f`, author): 215 tests across 15 files plus 6 targeted boundary checks pass, along with core and UI type checks, four test type graphs, inventory types, lint, format, mock, line-allocation and whitespace checks. Four UI lint warnings are unchanged from `main` and outside the feature's changes.
- Persisted-collector fix (`46ab0a0`): scoped canonical and independent reviews of that change. They do not cover the whole PR.
- Hosted review of `cb024b5` (current head): no findings; the earlier `53ee37c` collector P2 is addressed. It held the PR for data-model compatibility proof, which is added below. That hold stands until a fresh hosted review of a later head.
- Earlier proof is tied to its own source and does not cover `d70644f`:
  - Independent QA of `3a82cc7`: PASS with notes, including the stream-budget mutation checks and a Gateway runtime proof reused from `ad5a535` (build `2026.10.9-ad5a5354de4a-2026-10-30T05-25-28.209Z`).
  - Independent shipping verification of `43ddaef`: PASS with notes, 110 native tests and four Gateway and Control UI modes (build `2026.10.9-43ddaef1f7a6-2026-10-30T04-25-21.835Z`).
  - Scoped reviews: readiness fix (`ad5a535..3a82cc7`, two passes, zero findings), diagnostic step (`4bf61ee..ad5a535`), private-retry fix (`a296cbe..801b1a4`, eight passes, zero findings), `315380c` integration (PASS with notes).
  - Review of `f27f807..a296cbe` (36 passes): incomplete; no clean result is claimed for that range.
  - Baseline review (source `4599951`): eight passes, scoped-clean.
- CI on earlier published heads found missing mocks, test inventory gaps, an unconditional wire field, unbounded findings, a lint miss, the dropped settle findings and the stream-budget failure. Those failed runs remain history.
- Pending, not approval: a fresh whole-PR hosted review of the next head, and passing CI.

## Data compatibility
- This PR changes no schema, writer or retention.
- **Upgrade from the latest stable release (independent, PASS with notes):** data written by the published `openclaw@2026.10.9` package was opened and upgraded by this PR's source (`d70644f`).
  - Stable artifact: npm `openclaw-2026.10.9.tgz` (published 2026-10-29), tarball SHA-256 `43c61a00ef2c73416a072a7216cb3be80555d6740199f07194da2714283b04ab`; npm SHA-512 and SHA-1 integrity checked; signed tag `v2026.10.9` at build commit `8b18b55`. The npm provenance and signature chain was not separately audited.
  - The unmodified published compiled code, with its exact 66 production dependencies and no modules from this PR, wrote 6 sessions, 4 subagent runs and a 7-row transcript (header, 6 events, 4 model messages). The data included a retained private settle input and a collector's structured result and usage.
  - This PR's Doctor command then migrated the stores (shared schema 20→36, agent schema 25→38). Every original registry and transcript column and payload byte was preserved. The migration added the expected transcript navigation-index columns with their default values (for example `navigation_valid` = 1 and `navigation_display` = 0). Existing session-entry fields were preserved, and one expected display title was added. No represented-failure IDs or failure custody were invented.
  - Fresh processes then read the data through the production paths: the full and bounded registry readers, the session manager, Gateway row projection and presentation, and the Control UI attention and tree aggregation. Old failed children without a receipt still show failed-child attention (3 failed children, attention "error").
  - A new native write after migration, then a separate cold reopen, kept both the old and new bytes (7 events, 5 messages, 4 runs).
- **Historical import:** a frozen schema-v24 SQLite fixture went through the current Doctor import and a fresh read-only read. All three rows kept their full payload, IDs, keys, run ID and recovery data; the only changes were `main`'s existing queued→interrupted rule and a new empty `consumed_event_id`.
- A legacy retained settle message, replayed with its original run and idempotency IDs but without a record of represented failures, adds no new acknowledgement.
- Scope: this proves stored-data and schema activation. It does not cover a stable Gateway daemon boot, managed package replacement, service cutover or restart, a full packaged install of this PR, or live user data. Doctor completed both migrations, but its overall health check is not green in this isolated setup (plugin and model setup warnings, unset gateway mode). The stable data had no pending-input mailbox rows, so that path rests on the v24 import proof.

## Limits
- Runtime proof uses a scripted local model on macOS arm64/headless Chromium, not Linux or hosted-model compliance. Active-steering failure timing was not separately exercised. No latest-stable service activation (daemon boot, package replacement or restart) and no PostgreSQL run is claimed.
- The required `openclaw/ci-gate` check is not waived. No live Odin update, restart or deployment. CI and landing remain separate gates.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add LiveKit SIP and native RTC provider
prs.body:
Related: #169991

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who run telephony on LiveKit SIP cannot use Voice Call: it only accepts Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, and mock carriers.

## User Impact

Operators can select `provider: "livekit"` to place and receive phone calls over a LiveKit SIP trunk. Native RTC audio feeds the existing Voice Call realtime bridge, so model, voice, agent consultation, tools, call history, and playback stay with their current owners. Existing carriers are unchanged.

Supported:
- Outbound calls on a selected outbound trunk. Each call gets a unique room, and the plugin correlates the exact SIP participant identity and SID before it publishes audio.
- Signed inbound LiveKit webhooks for the selected inbound trunks. These use the existing inbound policy and caller allowlist.
- Outbound-only operation (`inboundPolicy: "disabled"`) with no public webhook or media WebSocket.
- `fromNumber` as an E.164 number or, for LiveKit only, a 1–15 digit PBX extension. Targets and allowlists still require E.164, and other carriers still require an E.164 `fromNumber`.
- `wss://` by default. `allowInsecureWs` allows `ws://` only to loopback or private literal IPs.

Not supported: classic STT/TTS mode, carrier XML notify playback, pre-connect DTMF and `send_dtmf`, and Twilio answering-machine detection. Restored calls are retired after a restart, not resumed. The Linux musl native binding is not supported.

New runtime dependencies: `@livekit/rtc-node` 1.1.0 (native) and `livekit-server-sdk` 2.19.1. These need maintainer dependency review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider reuses the existing manager, realtime handler, and transcript owners instead of adding a separate LiveKit agent worker. Admission is rechecked immediately before the token-bearing RTC connect. Joined disposal persists final transcripts before the call terminates. Shutdown keeps manager finalization failures visible instead of reporting success after carrier cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Changes since the previously published head (8278146)</summary>

- Merged current `main` (`aeeff2c6340`) to clear the GitHub merge conflict. This is a normal merge commit on top of `8278146`, with no rebase or history rewrite. Conflicts:
  - `extensions/voice-call/package.json`: took main's `2026.10.10` version and kept the two LiveKit dependencies and the description that names LiveKit.
  - `realtime-handler.ts`: kept the extracted `createRealtimeTelephonyBinding`. Main's removal of the "idle monitor armed" log (#191794) is ported into `realtime-call-binding.ts`, and that file's now-unused `idleHangupMs` parameter is dropped. Main's other realtime-handler changes auto-merged and are present: transcription language, transcript start timestamps, playback echo filtering, and greeting protection.
  - Config baseline: regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- Compared with `main`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` is +206/−0 (LiveKit entries only). `extensions/openai` is unchanged, and #189358 (`181342878c0`) is still an ancestor.
- No feature code changed.
- Hosted CI then exposed the new test-line budget gate: this PR adds exactly 2,529 test LF bytes against the captured base. Follow-up `ae5340a` adds only `config/test-lines-allocations/livekit-voice-call-provider-170000.txt`, using the documented per-change allocation mechanism. The record explains the SIP/RTC admission, native audio, joined cleanup and compiled-package regression coverage. The shared baseline scalar, assertions, timeouts and production/build/dependency bytes are unchanged. The staged ratchet passes with 25 lines of headroom; this is not a blanket exception or a claim that the earlier failed hosted run passed.

</details>

## Evidence

Focused source checks used local offline fixtures, not phone calls, inference sessions or production credentials. Tested source head: `59eeeba60a54725524bbfc9c1d132626d9dbd2c5`, merging main `aeeff2c634014c2a75ef56b3d10ecab971a987dd` into `827814672990d541c688c2f11e5398feab405739`. Pinned pnpm 12.15.0 frozen install. Current published head: `ae5340a0e49c8c3fb999df9b0dc55f0603fa94a4`; its only additional file is the measured test allocation described above. The source tests, production and package inputs are byte-identical to `59eeeba`; compiled evidence below remains attributed to `59eeeba`, not relabeled as a new build.

- Voice Call: 754 tests in 56 files pass, plus 178 tests in 14 files in the database-workers shard.
- LiveKit packaging test (`test/scripts/tsdown-livekit-packaging.test.ts`): 3 of 3 pass.
  - On the first attempt the cold `verbose=0` build exceeded its 120 s test timeout while the shared host's load average was 62 on 16 cores, from unrelated jobs.
  - The one retry passed at load 6: the cold build took 9.7 s. The timeout was not changed.
- Typecheck: `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and the Voice Call package typecheck pass.
- Lint: scoped type-aware oxlint on `extensions/voice-call` passes.
- Ratchets: line-cap (27 changed source files, no over-cap growth), assertion-safety, and mock-export all pass against `main`.
- Guards: import cycles (0), the extension and plugin import-boundary guards, plugin inventory, config baseline, and conflict markers all pass.
- Changed files pass format and the docs MDX and config-example checks.
- `tsgo:test:root` fails with 48 errors, all inherited from `main`:
  - A clean `main` worktree at `aeeff2c` with its own frozen install gives the same 48 errors, line for line.
  - None of the failing files are in this PR's diff. They are Bun/DOM `fetch` and stream type mismatches.
- Full-host build and installed proof for `59eeeba` are now recorded below; none of the earlier `8278146` package results are treated as proof of this artifact.

### Evidence: exact compiled package and private-lab runtime

- Maintained complete-host packager, selected `voice-call`: exit 0, 596.90 seconds, peak RSS 3,104,784,384 bytes; tarball integrity passed. Source stayed clean and manifests/lock unchanged. Control UI performance diagnostics were advisory; this is not independent performance qualification.
- Archive SHA-256: `78bffb1b6a3bf4c59d8a4521275520be53d0f7c7ec36305815a3e426bc59d3d1`. Original build ID: `2026.10.10-59eeeba60a54-2026-11-04T21-07-33.125Z`.
- Ordinary fresh-prefix Linux install succeeded (402 packages, 31 seconds). All **16,992 installed dist files** exactly match the original archive, with zero mismatches or unexpected files.
- Compiled plugin loaded with `origin: bundled`, trust `bundled`; initialized durable state, readiness `ready:true` / `failing:[]`, empty active-call and room inventories.
- The actual compiled consumer's public native SDK import supplies all nine consumed exports and the destination Linux GNU binding. A real AudioSource captured 1,280 PCM samples, queued 158 ms, and closed with awaited disposal.
- **Actual private SIP/RTP, not agent speech:** local generated fixture received INVITE, sent 200, received ACK and BYE, with bidirectional RTP counters (13 packets sent, 11 received in the private-WS attempt). Native RTC attachment reached realtime-provider registration, which failed because the isolated runtime cannot resolve its protected OpenAI credential binding. No functioning model session, audible assistant speech or recognition is claimed. A generated test-certificate native TLS failure was separately identified; only this isolated loopback lab uses the provider's explicit private-WS opt-in, with no global TLS or external-policy change.
- **Actual late-answer cancellation:** the installed public end operation succeeded before the fixture's eight-second delayed answer; late 200/ACK/BYE were observed, with zero RTP received by the fixture. After settlement there were zero active calls and zero rooms. This proves observed cancellation/cleanup, not complete late token-bearing I/O or consultation isolation.
- A genuine failed call from this artifact reopened through the public read-only CLI in a separate process after Gateway shutdown; all eight runtime-summary fields matched its richer durable record. This is current-candidate failed-call persistence, not stable carrier-history migration.
- Gateway logged clean shutdown in 117 ms after the failed transport/admission and cancellation attempts, but the launcher reported SIGTERM rather than exit 0. This is not successful post-conversation shutdown acceptance. All owned lab resources, processes and listener ports were cleaned up.
- **Supported configuration upgrade:** an integrity-verified official `2026.10.9` prefix was normally upgraded to the exact `59eeeba` archive. The unchanged config initially failed public CLI admission on legacy `agents.defaults.heartbeat`; the documented `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` migration (not a manual deletion) completed with exit 0. It removed the legacy disabled heartbeat setting and performed ordinary Doctor metadata/agent/skill housekeeping. The original workspace marker and config validation then passed in separate clean-environment processes; 46 mirrored receipts verify by checksum. Exact main already owns this migration; the carrier has no config/Doctor source delta from that parent. This proves the previous-release configuration update path with Doctor, **not current-latest stable carrier-history migration**. npm latest is now `2026.10.10`, whose older official build has a different pre-Doctor contract despite the same version label. No synthetic SQLite history or successful model/consult response was injected.


Private operator testing (summary only):
- The earlier full attempt reached the handset but failed immediately during GPT-Live startup. Later allowlisted diagnostics identified `DataCloneError` at media-worker construction, not a SIP delivery failure. The shared fix is #189358, merged into `main` and now included through this merge.
- On local integration candidate `3488f3f09731c1e1c0f83e9ce7ab7f080b0f70be`, a short two-way conversation completed normally for about 89 seconds. That candidate contained carrier head `9163172`, the #189358 fix, and temporary startup diagnostics. The caller confirmed clear speech and replies. Caller and assistant aggregate finals survived reopening the durable store. **This human-confirmed conversation proof is for that candidate only. Neither `8278146` nor `59eeeba` has a human-confirmed conversation result.** The narrower real private-lab SIP/RTP attempts on `59eeeba` are described above. The historical conversation is not current installed-package, inbound, isolation, consultation, upgrade or production acceptance.
- Room, process, and port cleanup was verified, but that call runtime needed a forced stop. The separate shutdown repair, #189415, is **still open and not merged**, and this PR does not include it.

<!-- carrier-runtime-proof-20261031 -->
<details>
<summary>Event log from the recorded call on candidate 3488f3f (redacted)</summary>

This projection keeps the event timestamps and types from the original Gateway JSONL log. Session IDs are replaced with consistent aliases, and all utterances, endpoints, and credentials are removed.

```jsonl
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:53:41.875Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"session.started","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay"}
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:53:44.728Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"session.ready","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay"}
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:53:46.008Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"output.audio.started","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay"}
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:55:11.056Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"input.audio.committed","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay","final":true}
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:55:11.060Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"output.audio.done","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay","final":true}
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:55:11.061Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"session.closed","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay","final":true}
```

The call ended `completed` after 89,344 ms. Both caller and assistant aggregate finals were saved, and reopening the durable store confirmed them (`quick_check=ok`). Aggregate callback timestamps do not show per-turn latency.

</details>

## Open before merge

- **Maintainer decision:** bundled carrier vs. an external carrier contract, plus dependency approval for the two LiveKit packages. `ci-gate` and `dependency-review` are waiting on this. The author is not requesting or issuing that approval.
- **Remaining live and installed acceptance, not satisfied by the narrower observations above:**
  - installed-package SIP ↔ RTC audio, showing an unselected peer rejected before audio or consultation, and retirement blocking later RTC I/O
  - delayed agent consultation
  - joined graceful shutdown after a real call
  - upgrade from the latest stable release with existing carrier settings and call history
- **Shared prerequisites outside this PR:**
  - #189358 (OpenAI media-worker `DataCloneError`): **merged** as `181342878c0` and included through this merge.
  - #189415 (Linux zombie-only spawn-broker group confirmation during shutdown): **open, not merged**, not included here.
  - A LiveKit SIP-service BYE response timeout is tracked separately in the LiveKit SIP service.
- The isolated model/audio/consultation acceptance is blocked on an owner-authorized usable protected credential binding; supported environment SecretRef activation currently fails before model dispatch. No secret was copied, auth boundary weakened, or alternate provider/model selected.
- Hosted CI at `59eeeba` found the missing per-change test allocation; that original failure remains disclosed. On exact final head `ae5340a`, [technical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41919351599) is terminal: **65 CheckRuns succeeded, 67 skipped, 1 neutral, zero failures/cancellations/timeouts/in-progress**. Both `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and the technical workflow job named `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded; [Darwin tooling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41919351338) succeeded too. Skipped and neutral checks are not counted as passing tests. The separate [admission workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41920604058) completed its resolution/review jobs successfully, but the status contexts `openclaw/ci-gate` (failure) and `openclaw/dependency-review` (pending) still explicitly require a maintainer to approve this revision. They are not technical test failures and were not bypassed.
- No canonical autoreview run covered this head because the tool isn't installed. An independent parent review inspected the merge resolutions, dependency/package scope, preserved upstream behavior and terminal verification logs at `59eeeba`; no actionable refresh-specific findings were identified. The follow-up adds only the exact documented test allocation, not runtime changes. This is not a canonical autoreview or a complete independent re-review of the original carrier implementation.

Status unchanged: ready for review, not ready to merge.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add short starter prompts with activation confirmation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin detail pages need short, useful starting points, with clear confirmation when starting one requires activating a plugin.

## User Impact

Adds 89 starter prompts across 40 bundled plugins. Selecting a prompt opens an editable, unsent chat draft; plugin activation, including background services and exclusive memory-provider changes, requires confirmation first. Prompt cards inherit light, dark, and custom themes.

Third-party compatibility: prompt lists are limited to three entries of 128 Unicode code points each after whitespace normalization. Invalid optional lists can disappear without blocking plugin loading; multiline text is normalized to spaces. This behavior is documented.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing manifest, activation, and draft paths. Preparation failures release the busy state and show a recoverable error, and leaving the plugin page closes any outstanding activation confirmation.

## Evidence

Reuses the completed implementation and proof at `1355997c96bfe23074fb69d690369175f62c3b65` (tree `c5e809d8cf978fd328765177d10a5e9e7540caad`). Local ClawSweeper reviewed the full `e662dae5963e5ccc20e2c6f518a00338b1071856..1355997c96bfe23074fb69d690369175f62c3b65` range for correctness and security: no actionable findings; both earlier confirmation-lifecycle findings resolved. That offline review did not run runtime or visual tests.

Recorded passing validation: 140 native tests, 39 fixture rerun tests, 10 launch tests, 10 theme/layout tests, and 12 affected manifest tests, plus formatting, focused lint/stylelint, docs and diff checks. These are separate runs, not a claimed disjoint total. The final launch suite passed 10/10, with retained failing regressions before the lifecycle repairs. The test-line ratchet has net delta zero; the inherited ceiling overage remains 20 lines. Full local typecheck/type-aware lint were constrained by external shared dependency declarations/path escape; CI supplies the broader check.

CI follow-up at `b4b0cb2c456e87979e2af0c7c936f3bbbbe78cb7` adds the new shared validator to `scripts/native-protocol-inputs.json` (one registration line). The native generator reproduced the original installation failure before this repair; Swift and Kotlin contract/determinism checks and the existing native-protocol artifact tests (2/2) pass afterward. The reviewed product implementation and visual proof are unchanged.

Final lint follow-up at `c20f75856cb36b681879c0d29c38b771da96ebe9` preserves Unicode code-point counting using `Array.from` and repairs test-only braces, bound-method capture, frame waiting and nonmutating sorting. Focused type-aware lint and formatting pass; affected manifest/protocol tests pass 25/25, the launch suite passes 10/10, and the theme test passes 1/1. Test-line growth remains zero. No prompt text, confirmation behavior, or visual output changes in these CI repairs.

Hosted ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review of `c20f75856cb36b681879c0d29c38b771da96ebe9` with no actionable correctness/security findings and no before-merge requests: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193694#issuecomment-6667423839. It also inspected the attached desktop/mobile proof. The recorded real-Gateway proof gap remains explicit below; the optional recording and static-test suggestions do not block this reviewed, maintainer-directed scope.

CI recovery: automatic CI stalled on seven unassigned `blacksmith-32vcpu-ubuntu-2404` shards. The initial hosted recovery at `c20f75856cb36b681879c0d29c38b771da96ebe9` exposed the startup-size context mismatch described below and three Bun icon-test failures. Those superseded runs have been canceled. The repository-native `scripts/pr ci-dispatch 193694` accepted the final integrated head `19ae3aa7b4f3d98233dfe1644c0ccb0633771694` for hosted validation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103611813. Attempt 1 completed all 102 jobs with four inherited failed leaves, their aggregate gate and one canceled browser shard. Security-fast, startup size, core lint, iOS smoke and the API comparison report pass. The browser shard `checks-ui-e2e (3/7)` exceeded its 25-minute job deadline during Ubuntu package downloads for WebKit, before any tests ran. Its cancellation is missing coverage, not success: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103611813/job/127513368979. The native merge verifier refused submission while this coverage was missing. A single targeted infrastructure retry in attempt 2 passed the browser shard: **143 files / 578 tests**, on the unchanged head ([passed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103611813/job/127535956976)). Attempt 2 is complete with all 102 jobs terminal and no canceled/timed-out jobs. GitHub carries the other checks forward; the four failed checks retain identical steps and timestamps, with their original logs and source attributions preserved. Native admission refused before any merge request because GitHub still requires the canceled PR-triggered check from run `42103108185`; the manual fallback is validation evidence and does not own that required check. Verified the full thread-aware review and per-PR required-check inventory. Requested a single recovery of the existing PR run through its documented hosted retry placement: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103108185. The head remains unchanged; no rules or workflow source are changed. No repository variables, production configuration, or Gateway state were changed.

The final integration head is `19ae3aa7b4f3d98233dfe1644c0ccb0633771694`. A required startup-size comparison exposed that exact-head recovery CI built the old branch alone while ordinary PR CI built its merge with current main: the merged build passed at 90,481 startup gzip bytes, while the standalone old branch measured 92,378 bytes under its older budget. Main was integrated once to align those contexts. The stable feature patch ID remains `074d2c5e78faa5dfd2a4d60a913f3e24e87f320c` before and after integration; none of the 60 feature paths changed upstream, and all 25 focused manifest/protocol tests pass after integration. Existing ClawSweeper findings and visual proof still apply to this identical feature patch. Exact-head hosted CI is complete, with the inherited failures explicitly qualified below.

Current-head CI has an inherited `check-dependencies` failure: `readUpdatePhysicalDatabaseGenerations` in `src/infra/update-physical-database-generations.ts` and `enqueueSlackRun` in `src/auto-reply/reply/queue.test-helpers.ts` are reported as unused exports. Both files, every reference to these symbols, the Knip configurations, and the deadcode wrappers are identical to protected-main baseline `d999f7b1b675d8702b38fb65760475f59f203130`. The actual GitHub merge preview `ff56e4ec4e40f0da9a9326ae15e98c188ea40702` and hosted checkout `19ae3aa7b4f3d98233dfe1644c0ccb0633771694` share the complete tree `c523524ac9e879e9a43df6653818076007836057`; no feature code is omitted. Failure log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42103611813/job/127513370662. The same hosted run also reports three Bun-only `chat-transcript-replies.test.ts` search/navigation setup failures (`expected input to be defined`); all 24 cases pass under Node. The complete chat implementation/test tree, UI helpers/components/libraries, normalization-core package, Vitest config, UI package and lock file are unchanged from the same main baseline. prs.title: fix(ui): explain Dashboard disconnect notices when the widget sandbox never responds
prs.body:
Closes #193027
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/116680

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dashboard cards show only “Disconnected” when the widget sandbox never reports ready on a non-loopback Gateway with no mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin configured, even while the Gateway stays connected.

## User Impact

The card keeps its short reconnect notice and adds a collapsed “More info” hint pointing to mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin. If the proxy or tunnel doesn't route the sandbox port, the operator can see that they need a dedicated public origin routed to the sandbox listener. The hint explains a possible cause; it doesn't repair the route automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing sandboxOrigin guidance appears after repeated authorization failures. An unreachable outer sandbox never gets that far. This adds guidance to the readiness-timeout path, without showing it for an explicit sandboxOrigin or a loopback host. The disclosure stays collapsed so the card remains readable.

## Evidence

Inspected commit 669a0ffa0602b3de64a2fd938f77e036795a1a3a against its base, aeeff2c634014c2a75ef56b3d10ecab971a987dd. The added regression cases cover a connected remote Gateway whose outer sandbox never announces readiness, checking the collapsed hint with no sandboxOrigin and its absence with an explicit sandboxOrigin.

On November 4, 2026, git apply --check --verbose passed for all four changed files against upstream main at 70805b3a970ad5e2534ae8cf2acf21cebe746eea. The check used files fetched at that exact revision in a temporary directory; it did not change the branch or shared checkout. This establishes patch applicability, not runtime correctness.

The two board widget test files pass (30 tests, including the collapsed-until-opened check). oxfmt and ui:i18n:verify pass. Screenshots came from a mocked gateway (before/after images follow in a comment).


## Test-line allocation

`config/test-lines-allocations/dashboard-sandbox-origin-guidance-193029.txt` allocates 28 lines, the net test growth after the frame tests started sharing one connected-gateway context. It covers the new ready-deadline notice with and without an authored `sandboxOrigin`, which no existing test reaches.

prs.title: fix(codex): classify busy session retirement as global preflight
prs.body:
Related: #181046

Selectively backports the session-retirement correction from #181204 to `release/2026.10.10`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a claimed Codex thread being reported as an ordinary execution error when a session deletion or context reset is refused.

## User Impact

Classifies the refusal as a model-independent preflight failure while preserving its original diagnostic, active-thread claim, binding, and ownership checks. If propagated to the core fallback owner, that unscoped preflight failure stops before the next candidate. The producer-to-fallback composition has not been demonstrated at a shipped entry point; the evidence below keeps that gap explicit. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release branch already uses `AgentHarnessPreflightError` when releasing a busy retained thread, but its session-retirement path still throws `Error`. Use the same globally scoped preflight contract at that remaining producer. This is the error-class portion of the merged fix; it does not remove an adoption guard or add harness-local scope.

### Published 2026.10.10: partial inclusion of #181204

The [release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/CHANGELOG/2026.10.10.md) correctly credit #181204 for stopping model fallback when a policy change encounters a busy Codex thread. The published tag contains the typed refusal in [thread-lifecycle-warm.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-warm.ts#L243-L257), but [session-retirement.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-retirement.ts#L118-L127) still throws an ordinary `Error` for a claimed thread.

This release backport changes only that remaining retirement producer to the existing unscoped `AgentHarnessPreflightError`. It does not reapply the warm-thread correction, remove an adoption guard, or add harness-local scope. Please evaluate it as completion of the release's error-classification contract, rather than as a new claim that ordinary Gateway reset triggers model fallback. The shipped retirement-refusal-to-fallback composition remains unproven, as detailed below.

## Evidence

### Additional published-release check — November 3, 2026

The remaining error-class correction was included in a selective port installed on official 10.10 packages on macOS and Linux. The combined port's 50 focused checks passed, including the nine session-retirement cases. A successful live parent/child continuation on those installations is operational continuity evidence only: it did not trigger the claimed-thread retirement refusal or prove suppression of a subsequent model candidate. The exact-head contract checks and the unresolved shipped-entry-point gap below remain the evidence for this PR.

- The existing context-reset regression fails on the base because the refusal is an ordinary `Error`. With the correction, deletion and context reset both return an unscoped `AgentHarnessPreflightError` before mutation; the binding and active claim remain, and no session transaction or native request runs.
- Node 24.22.1: 9 session-retirement cases and 16 existing fallback terminal-boundary cases pass (41.60 s including both worker preparations). Extension production and test typechecking, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The full plugin lane was also attempted; its pre-existing local failures are described below.
- Shared autoreview of the complete local delta and surrounding cleanup against `06d598c818155a5ac6ad00c9611bbb4b6ed57d45`, P0–P2: no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected code; tests were executed separately.

This proves the producer contract and the existing fallback owner's terminal behavior with controlled fixtures. A live network fallback was not deliberately triggered.

Local plugin-lane result on macOS: `pnpm test:extension codex --maxWorkers=6` exits 1 in its 433-file batch: 5,053 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped (460.86 s including preparation). The wrapper announces 439 discovered test files; the actual Vitest summary reports 433 executed files. The three failures also reproduce without this session-retirement change, using identical Codex sources from the release base:

- Two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases fail while observing native descendants, with `ProcessInspectionError` (`reason: "permission"`). The unchanged file reproduces 2 failed / 2 passed.
- One `thread-shell-environment.native.test.ts` case expects an empty Git identity after shell-environment filtering but observes a nonempty identity. The unchanged file reproduces 1 failed / 3 passed.

These failures were retained and were not hidden with retries, skips, relaxed assertions, or timeout changes. They do not exercise session retirement; the 9 changed-owner cases and 16 fallback-consumer cases pass. This is not a clean full local plugin run.

**Remaining runtime proof:** the shipped CLI source-runtime build and help entry point pass on this head. An audit of the supported reset, deletion, rewind/branch-switch, and initialization-cleanup callers did not establish a faithful live reproduction of this particular retirement refusal inside an eligible model-fallback chain. Normal reset cancels and retires work first; rewind/history mutation rejects competing work before this participant. Those RPC handlers are outside `runWithModelFallback`. The producer-to-fallback connection remains unproven at a shipped entry point; the tests above establish those contracts separately. No cancelled reset, injected native claim, or run without eligible fallback candidates is presented as that missing proof.


## Exact-head production-path clarification (2026-10-31)

A fresh Linux source audit distinguishes persistent-session reset (`AgentHarness.reset` → `retireCodexAppServerSessionGeneration`) from history context reset (`withSessionContextReset` → this changed deletion producer). Ordinary persistent-session Gateway reset drains work before harness cleanup; history mutation rejects live source work before native context preparation. The mutation RPCs are not a fallback runner. Consequently the combined shipped Gateway reset-refusal → next-model suppression trace remains unestablished; no modified reset flow, injected claim, or artificial combination of boundaries is presented as that proof. A maintainer needs to identify the intended supported caller, or scope acceptance to the actual retirement boundary. See the companion technical clarification comment for exact-head source locations.


**Incognito exception:** this distinction does not cover every reset. `session-reset-service.ts:656–667` routes incognito reset through `deleteIncognitoSessionForReset`; `session-reset-incognito.ts:61` invokes `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle`, and the memory lifecycle owner (`session-accessor.memory-lifecycle.ts:121`) enters `withSqliteSessionDeletions`. Thus an incognito reset can reach the changed deletion hook, after admission drain and harness cleanup. This path still does not establish propagation into an eligible model-fallback chain. Generic maintenance/prepared-write/cleanup callers also exist and are not ruled out by this scoped audit.


### Fresh isolated Linux checks (2026-10-31)

On unchanged exact head `961110a9a073e9c133fb624f17f3e758bf96151a`, Node v24.22.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0: session-retirement **9/9 passed** (384.30 s including worker preparation), fallback terminal-boundary **16/16 passed** (345.72 s including worker preparation). Both repository wrappers exited 0. These are separate production-owner contract tests, not the missing combined live trace. Independent read-only source review confirmed the persistent/incognito distinction and broader cleanup callers; it did not establish the combined fallback flow. No production Gateway, data, or installed packages were changed.

prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.

fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```
 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
    207|       await lifecycle.retire(slot);
  >  209|       expect(retirementCount("closed")).toBe(closedBefore + 1);

 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
  >  253|     expect(retirementCount("failure")).toBe(failureBefore + 1);
```

After the change the same two tests pass, and they check both halves of the symptom against the
real registry and the real log-file transport: a retirement the owner asked for adds a `closed`
count and leaves `exit` unchanged, and a worker that throws on its own adds a `failure` count while
the log file holds one `left without a retirement request` line containing the cause text.

```
 TEST  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts
 ... > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit 87ms
 ... > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause 178ms
```

Adjacent lanes, run locally with the same config:

```
 src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts   Tests 10 passed, Duration 42.94s
 src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts             Tests 7 passed with sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts,
                                          Duration 20.95s
```

Local gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files (28ms), `run-oxlint.mjs` on the core tsconfig
reported "Found 0 warnings and 0 errors" (68.1s), `git diff --check` clean, and
`check-line-cap-ratchet.mts` reported "Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new
violations or over-cap growth". `check-changed.mjs --dry-run` listed the CI gates this diff
selects. Pre-commit hooks ran normally; no hook was skipped.

Cost of the new tests, per the repo validation rules: they add 87ms and 178ms inside a file whose
targeted run takes 26s with a warm transform cache and 212s cold on this machine. Neither test
sleeps, polls, or uses a wall-clock timer; they await the worker `online` event, the slot's own
exit promise, and `flushLogger()`.

Gaps worth naming: the run was Windows, where the six pre-existing cases in this test file already
fail at `fileURLToPath("file:///openclaw/...")` with `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` before this
change and in code this diff does not touch, so those cases are covered here by CI's Linux infra
lane; the two new tests derive their carrier URL from `import.meta.url` so they run on both
platforms. `pnpm tsgo:core` refuses a worktree that shares its install with the main checkout
("Declaration input escapes checkout"), so the typecheck gate was not run locally and is left to
CI. No live Gateway was started on this machine; the log-line half is proven by reading the file
the file transport actually wrote.

CI on head `e129273e8` (server-recorded base `dbb580aed`, which is 171 commits behind current `main`): 129 check runs = 67 success / 59 skipped / 1 neutral (CodeQL) / 2 failure. The two failures are `checks-windows-node-test-5` (completed 2026-10-02T08:19:37Z) and the 2 s aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` that follows it in the same run. The failing case is `test/scripts/write-unified-entry-dts.test.ts > write-unified-entry-dts > reuses unaffected canonical groups while rebuilding runtime after input edits`, and it throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './record-coerce' is not defined by "exports"` from a `package.json` inside that test's own temporary fixture project (`%TEMP%\oc-vt-8AAiWh\openclaw-sdk-declarations-5DFbNf\Project\node_modules\@openclaw\normalization-core`), imported from `src/process/exec-result.ts` in the same temp tree. prs.title: fix(telegram): sibling bot's deleted stream previews corrupt group history
prs.body:
Closes #164958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a group running two OpenClaw bots, one bot's streamed reasoning preview (the 🧠 draft) is recorded into the other bot's persistent message cache as an ordinary message. Telegram never delivers message deletions to other bots, so when the streaming side deletes the superseded preview, every sibling cache keeps its copy. From then on, each group turn's history window carries that foreign reasoning text, and Anthropic rejects the whole turn with `reasoning_extraction`. The issue's live capture shows the orphaned preview surviving in cache long after it disappeared from Telegram.

## User Impact

User impact: multi-bot Telegram groups stop breaking on streamed reasoning previews. Once a preview is confirmed deleted, every account's history cache drops it, so later turns no longer inherit dead draft text from a sibling bot. No config change or migration is needed. The fix handles deletions observed after deployment and does not claim to clean up pre-existing orphans.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix tracks previews precisely instead of classifying by content, which is the direction the review discussion on the issue called for. The draft stream is the one component that knows the exact message id of a superseded preview, and it already waits for Telegram to confirm the delete. It now reports that id through a new `onPreviewRetired` callback, and the dispatch layer fans the retirement out to every configured account's message cache, including the sender's own (its cache recorded the preview too). Each cache drops the entry from the live map and the persisted store: retained group history through a compare-and-delete loop, bounded private-chat history through a map delete plus store delete. Nothing keys on message text, prefixes, or usernames, so ordinary bot messages are never misclassified. If Telegram rejects or never confirms the delete, nothing is retired, because the preview may still be visible and its history copies are then still honest.

## Evidence

- New `preview-retirement.test.ts`: two accounts each holding the same preview id in group (retained) and private (bounded) history, fan-out retires it from both and keeps neighboring messages; a single-account config with no `channels.telegram` section still covers the implicit default account.
- New cache tests: `retireMessage` evicts from the live map and the persisted store, a reopened bucket does not resurrect the entry, repeat retirement returns false, non-native ids are rejected, and other chats with the same message id are untouched.
- New draft-stream tests: `onPreviewRetired` fires exactly once after a confirmed supersede delete, and never fires when the delete is rejected or returns unconfirmed.
- Review round 4 follow-ups (head 8e35a3e79d5, rebased onto current main a134038ad7f): retirement fan-out now keys on the Bot API chat type carried from the inbound message instead of the `-100` id prefix, so a basic group whose id was recycled into the supergroup space stays account-local; `record()` and `retireMessage` serialize per cache key through a writer chain shared across all cache instances over the same bucket, so a record in flight while retirement lands from a separate fan-out handle can no longer write the preview back; the persisted tombstone settles before retirement reports done, keeping the fence across restarts. New regression tests cover the recycled-id basic group, channel fan-out, unknown chat type staying local, and both store paths racing retirement mid-write.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/preview-retirement.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.retained.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed. The same command over `message-cache.test.ts` and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 64 passed. oxfmt and oxlint passed on the five touched files.
- Earlier head `c3677719ea19cfb0f1c7461c70a535153adb4634` had green CI. Current head `e5a3c6a5ae3a7f9c981ef41f861353624649fa66` includes the lint and persisted-retirement follow-ups, with fresh CI required.

- New cross-instance regression in `message-cache.retained.test.ts`: two cache handles over the same bucket, one recording and one retiring the same key. The retire from the second handle completes its fence and delete before the first handle's compare commits; without the shared writer queue the stale observation resurrects the preview. This test fails on the previous per-instance chains and passes after moving `keyWriteChains` onto the shared bucket.
- New persisted-eviction regression: 3,000 rows are seeded with message 1 and preview 2. Reading message 1 makes it newest in memory, then row 3001 evicts preview 2 from the memory LRU while SQLite evicts message 1 by creation order. Retirement previously returned false and left preview 2 persisted; it now deletes the persisted key independently of memory membership and the reopened cache stays empty. Current verification across `message-cache.test.ts`, `message-cache.retained.test.ts`, `preview-retirement.test.ts`, and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 79 passed. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint pass on the changed files.

Gap I want to be explicit about: I could not stage the live two-bot Anthropic reproduction locally, so the end-to-end proof rides on the issue's live capture for the failure side and on the cache/draft-layer tests above for the fix side. The retirement path itself is covered at every layer it touches; a maintainer with two bots can confirm in one group turn by watching the sibling's cache stay empty after the preview is deleted. Latest-stable upgrade evidence with existing history and settings is also still open.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope the JSONL transcript usage estimate to the live window across boundaries
prs.body:
Refs #150579

## What Problem This Solves

A compacted session's transcript usage report (the JSONL artifact seam behind diagnostic reads) counted the whole append-only archive as live context. Content superseded by a compaction or reset stays in the file, and the chars-based estimate summed every user/assistant message ever written, so the reported total kept growing across clean compactions while the model's actual context stayed small.

A second gap sat next to it: once the estimate restarted at a boundary, eligibility was re-derived only from model-tagged assistant entries in the retained window. A summary-only window (the cut names an entry outside the message window) or a retained-user-only window (overflow compaction with a pending user message as its tail) lost the estimate until the next assistant reply, even though the summary and retained text were sitting in the model context.

## Root cause

`aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` fills `totalTokens` from a chars estimate when no per-call usage snapshot provides one. `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` feeds it the full JSONL transcript, and the estimate accumulated `estimatedTranscriptChars` over the whole scanned set with no notion of boundary markers or the retained window they name. The boundary restart also reset `sawEstimateModelIdentity` from the retained entries alone, while `finish()` requires that flag, so any window without a surviving model-tagged assistant reported no estimate at all.

## Fix

- The JSONL reader passes `compaction`/`reset` boundary records through with their `summary`/`firstKeptEntryId` fields, and forwards each entry's id, instead of skipping markers.
- The accumulator keeps per-entry char counts for the current window. At a boundary it keeps the retained tail named by `firstKeptEntryId` plus the compaction summary, matching the model-context contract (compactionSummary + retained entries + post-boundary messages) and the transcript tree selector's fallback (an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window). The previous revision restarted the estimate at zero, which undercounts a compacted session that retains a large summary or window.
- A boundary leaves the window estimate-eligible whenever it holds counted text. A compaction or reset marker is only written by a live model session, so requiring a model-tagged assistant to survive the cut only masked reads taken between the boundary and the next reply.
- Usage snapshots (input/output/cache/cost) still aggregate over the whole record, and a fresh per-call `totalTokens` snapshot still wins over any estimate, unchanged.

## Scope

This change lives entirely in the JSONL artifact seam: `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` reads bounded transcript artifacts and its callers are diagnostic paths. The live budget-preflight path from #150579 reads the SQLite seam, which already scopes to the active context and is untouched here; that preflight symptom stays with #150579 and the PRs addressing it directly. This branch does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `session-usage-estimate.test.ts`: a compaction keeps its 500-char summary plus the 2000-char retained message named by `firstKeptEntryId` while dropping the 4000-char superseded prefix; a reset keeps its named retained tail; an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window but still counts the summary. Three further regressions end the transcript right at the boundary (summary-only window, compaction retaining only user messages, reset retaining only user text), covering the read between the boundary and the next assistant reply; earlier versions of these tests appended that reply, which masked the eligibility drop.
- Red/green: the boundary-terminal three fail on the previous head (no estimate reported); the full file passes 9/9 with the fix.
- Runtime proof on a real compacted session (regenerated after the earlier /tmp artifact expired): isolated Gateway plus embedded agent against the scripted provider; a real injected 400 `context_length_exceeded`, one committed auto-compaction, then one more turn. The committed marker carries a 464-char summary and names a retained 91-char user message as `firstKeptEntryId`, so the boundary leaves a summary-plus-retained-user window. The artifact is the session's real settled transcript events serialized back to legacy JSONL, with redacted variants that drop usage fields and the model-snapshot entry so the chars estimate is what gets measured. The after-fix reader reports `totalTokens: 139` on the redacted prefix ending at the boundary (ceil((464 + 91) / 4), the summary plus the retained user text) and `176` on the full redacted artifact (ceil((464 + 91 + 56 + 90) / 4), adding the post-boundary assistant and user text). On the usage-carrying artifact the reader still reports the real provider aggregates (input 105 / output 25, latest context snapshot 120 total and available), so the estimate path and the snapshot path stay separate.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-usage-estimate.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.markers.test.ts` green; `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts` green; oxlint 0 findings on the changed files; oxfmt clean; tsgo core lane passes; `git diff --check` clean.
- Test cost: `pnpm test src/gateway/session-usage-estimate.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` finishes in about 2.2s wall locally.

[AI-assisted] prepared with Kimi K3; verified locally as described above and reviewed line by line.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): avoid warnings for healthy idle connections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated WhatsApp warning logs after 30 minutes without an inbound chat message, even while the connection continues receiving transport frames.

## User Impact

Quiet, connected WhatsApp accounts keep ordinary heartbeat logs at INFO. A heartbeat warns when transport activity exceeds the existing transport timeout. Watchdog reconnect decisions are unchanged; no configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The monitor already receives the last transport activity timestamp and has the connection controller's transport timeout. Reusing those values makes heartbeat severity reflect transport liveness while retaining message-idle duration in the diagnostic fields.

## Evidence

- The new parametrized regression fails on the original source in both cases: recent transport activity with an old inbound message incorrectly logs WARN, and stale transport without a previous inbound message incorrectly logs INFO. It checks INFO at the exact transport timeout and WARN after the timeout through the real monitor, controller, and logger with fixed socket fixtures.
- All 30 cases in the existing connection-and-logging suite pass on the final commit, including reconnect, quiet-session, and delivery checks. The supported source-suite command is `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. This regression suite uses fixed socket fixtures; the separate real Gateway capture below supplies live-account evidence.
- Final-base targeted strict typecheck, focused syntax lint, formatting, whitespace, and test-line budget checks pass. Full type-aware lint did not reach file analysis: plugin SDK declaration preparation exceeded its 300-second timeout on the ARM64 host. That broader lint remains for CI.
- Production change adjusts the heartbeat condition and warning text (+2/-5 lines). Its 42-line regression allocation covers the added monitor-boundary proof without changing the shared budget. The final run took 1.98 seconds in test execution and 289.7 seconds total, including 195.4 seconds of cold native-worker preparation. CI time is pending.
- Source review and simplification confirmed timestamp initialization, frame updates, the existing timeout boundary, and unchanged reconnect behavior. No standalone local autoreview was run; the real Gateway capture below addresses the upstream proof request.

## Real Gateway behavior capture

Observed on the running, shipped **OpenClaw 2026.10.9 / WhatsApp plugin 2026.10.9**, with the exact heartbeat-severity predicate from this PR already backported locally. This is real linked-account traffic and the real Gateway socket path, with no mocked socket, injected frame, fake clock, restart, forced network outage, or test message used for this capture. The capture supplements the tests of PR head `35d93439c8da040fa0be7068eb441dda64f2745b`; that full newer checkout was not deployed.

Four consecutive one-minute heartbeats from the same connection retain the same inbound timestamp while the transport timestamp advances. All four are INFO after more than 30 minutes without an inbound message:

| UTC log timestamp | Level | Inbound idle (minutes, derived) | Transport idle (seconds, derived) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2026-11-04T06:13:03.549Z | INFO | 31.427 | 0.008 |
| 2026-11-04T06:14:03.548Z | INFO | 32.427 | 8.038 |
| 2026-11-04T06:15:03.548Z | INFO | 33.427 | 2.801 |
| 2026-11-04T06:16:03.548Z | INFO | 34.427 | 3.640 |

The durations above are calculated from the original UTC log timestamp minus `lastInboundAt` / `lastTransportActivityAt`; they are not simulated. The effective production transport timeout is **300,000 ms**: the captured monitor sets that default, and the production channel startup supplies no timeout override.

Allowlisted projection of the original Gateway JSON records follows. UTC time and severity come from the logger metadata; the connection UUID is replaced consistently with `connection-A`. Other fields retain their logged values. Phone numbers/JIDs, IPs, hostnames, endpoints, keys, account identifiers, paths, and message contents are excluded.

```jsonl
{"time":"2026-11-04T06:13:03.549Z","level":"INFO","module":"web-heartbeat","connection":"connection-A","messagesHandled":13,"lastInboundAt":1793770897914,"lastTransportActivityAt":1793772783541,"uptimeMs":12060539,"minutesSinceLastMessage":31,"message":"web gateway heartbeat"}
{"time":"2026-11-04T06:14:03.548Z","level":"INFO","module":"web-heartbeat","connection":"connection-A","messagesHandled":13,"lastInboundAt":1793770897914,"lastTransportActivityAt":1793772835510,"uptimeMs":12120539,"minutesSinceLastMessage":32,"message":"web gateway heartbeat"}
{"time":"2026-11-04T06:15:03.548Z","level":"INFO","module":"web-heartbeat","connection":"connection-A","messagesHandled":13,"lastInboundAt":1793770897914,"lastTransportActivityAt":1793772900747,"uptimeMs":12180539,"minutesSinceLastMessage":33,"message":"web gateway heartbeat"}
{"time":"2026-11-04T06:16:03.548Z","level":"INFO","module":"web-heartbeat","connection":"connection-A","messagesHandled":13,"lastInboundAt":1793770897914,"lastTransportActivityAt":1793772959908,"uptimeMs":12240538,"minutesSinceLastMessage":34,"message":"web gateway heartbeat"}
```

A read-only `openclaw channels status --channel whatsapp --json` call at **2026-11-04T06:25:27.519000Z** also returned `linked=true`, `running=true`, and `connected=true`; its `lastConnectedAt` was **2026-11-04T02:52:03.059000Z**. No `--probe` was requested.

Provenance: the selected records' logger source resolves to the running Gateway's captured installed WhatsApp monitor. That captured file and the installed patched monitor have the same SHA-256, `2b57e008a13df849795820ca94916de676cd4adb93ce2bcaf0e1267c7edf651a`. Its severity branch is:

```js
if (Date.now() - snapshot.lastTransportActivityAt > transportTimeoutMs)
  heartbeatLogger.warn(logData, "web gateway heartbeat - transport inactive");
else
  heartbeatLogger.info(logData, "web gateway heartbeat");
```

This predicate and the message strings match the PR head. The pre-fix condition (`minutesSinceLastMessage > 30`) would select WARN for these same logged snapshots; that comparison is source-based, not a claim that the live Gateway was switched back to the old code. Only the actual INFO capture above is live behavior evidence. Fixture-generated entries from source-checkout paths were excluded from the shared log using the production capture source path and artifact hash.
