prs.title: perf(sessions): persist active transcript facts for hydration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Needs Peter's approval: agent schema change. Do not merge before Peter approves this PR.**

Cold transcript hydration reads small byte-count and dependency-navigation values stored after the payload in `transcript_events`. SQLite traverses payload overflow chains to reach those columns. Actor hydration also totals the entire active path, so a 512-event request can incur this cost across tens of thousands of events.

## User Impact

Agent schema 41 adds an initially empty `session_transcript_active_event_facts` companion keyed by `(session_id, seq)`. A fact stores exactly `coalesce(event_utf8_bytes, octet_length(event_json)) + 1` and the existing guarded dependency projection. `{}` means a known non-candidate; a missing row means unknown. CASE-gated readers use facts when present and retain the exact previous expressions otherwise. There is no reader backfill.

On the synthetic 34,153-event path, full coverage reduces actor hydration CPU by 79.0% and VFS spans by 96.6%. Cron-context CPU and sampled allocation are approximately neutral. Existing rows do not receive this benefit immediately: 512 ordinary, well-formed appends cover a recent 512-row window, but historical dependency candidates and full-path totals remain uncovered until a normal rewrite/rebuild. Cold transitions clear facts; restored rows start unknown.

Older readers are not allowed through an additive-table exception: their writers cannot maintain these facts. Older schema-40 admission refuses schema 41. Rollback requires restoring the verified scoped migration backup and then using the matching older build.

## Why This Change Was Made

The empty table avoids `ADD COLUMN` validation scans on existing STRICT tables. Payloads remain authoritative; the companion is a derived projection owned by the active-row lifecycle. SQLite uses `STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID`; PostgreSQL receives the same primary/foreign-key contract through the existing schema generator and migration owner.

| Mutation owner | Facts lifecycle in the same transaction |
| --- | --- |
| Normal append and full replacement | Reuse prepared payload/byte facts; ordinary rows use a compact insert. |
| Rebuild/import/branch selection | Carry compact facts through the existing source read, prepared chunks, and catch-up. |
| PostgreSQL append | Insert through a writable CTE dependent on the active-row `RETURNING` relation. |
| Payload rewrite and direct payload updater | Clear changed facts, including index-preserving rewrites. |
| Eligibility changes | Replace the active projection and its facts through the existing rebuild owner. |
| Cold transition/restoration | Clear facts before representation changes; restored rows remain unknown. |
| Branch retirement, reset, compaction, suffix replacement, deletion | Cascade from retired active rows; new uncovered suffix rows retain fallback. |
| Cross-engine port | Omit derived facts and use destination-native fallback; do not copy encoding-dependent projections. |

Malformed/deep legacy input retains its previous acceptance and reader-error behavior. A review caught eager projection of scalar placement data failing at append time; the writer now leaves those facts unknown, with an append/rebuild regression. Connection-owned prepared templates retain only single-row/full-chunk shapes and bind fresh session IDs and values.

Runtime growth is necessary for the approved schema and transactional lifecycle across both engines. The shared metadata reader replaces the old payload-backed accounting queries, and the guarded dependency expression has one owner. Runtime source is +799/−151 (**+648 net**), generated catalogs +108, reusable proof and inventory tooling +1,552, and tests +850. The requested non-test/non-doc diff is **+2,313 net** including tooling. This is an additive schema/lifecycle change, not a net-deletion optimization; the initially empty upgrade and exact legacy fallback require the additional writer, invalidation, migration, and engine-port contracts.

## Evidence

Baseline: `ac008ae0b850ff5082a247924e5b9e636edbb1ce`, agent schema 40. Published head: `b411052a21bc9c417b996d80a9e71889e8a815b6`. The final rebase onto main `64ca09fbdde314fa8be74c3d11281d4685ec6e8c` was patch-identical (`git range-diff`); owning-path measurements were retained. Synthetic data only: 6.3M active rows across 25,130 sessions, including 20k–50k-event paths, on a physically allocated 70.010 GB fragmented SQLite file (about 54.32 GB non-free pages). No Team database was opened/copied and no load was sent to Team. Large fixtures were deleted after proof; reports, profiles, and small scoped backups were retained.

The reproducible fixture, VFS extension, real-owner runner, and commands are in `scripts/perf/transcript-active-facts.{py,ts,md}` and `transcript-active-facts-vfs.c`. Both arms enable the native statement cache used by the production database owner. Earlier uncached/fixture-setup runs remain diagnostic evidence and are not pooled with final results.

**Upgrade through the real migration and scoped-backup owners:**

| Active rows / file | Backup wall | Migration wall | Main bytes read | Total bytes written | WAL growth | Backup size |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1M / 1.336 GB | 60.07 ms | 30.53 ms | 94,308 | 82,192 | 41,232 | 12,288 B |
| 10M / 13.479 GB | 75.38 ms | 35.92 ms | 86,116 | 57,544 | 28,872 | 12,288 B |
| 6.3M / 70.010 GB | 126.52 ms | 28.18 ms | 98,404 | 73,976 | 37,112 | 12,288 B |

The 1M result is the named canonical rerun; the earlier 1M run was 33.68 ms and is retained. All scales show bounded page work. Existing-data work consists of the single `schema_meta` record, version markers, and schema-catalog validation. The backup records `schema_meta`, the prior user version, and the companion's absence. There is no ALTER, existing-row index build, transcript scan, or transcript copy. Exact 40→41 quick finalization checks the new empty table/FK; earlier crossings and explicit FULL verification retain global foreign-key validation. Separate whole-update backups/maintenance are outside these version-phase timings. PostgreSQL's existing backup scope is unchanged.

**Real hydration owners, five untraced samples per arm/state:** actor hydration runs inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with its 513-row navigation window and full active-path total; cron-context is the actual bounded-context core with a 512-event limit, not the entire cron job or RPC.

| Facts / owner | CPU base → candidate | Wall base → candidate | VFS spans base → candidate | Pager visits base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty / actor | 596.736 → 183.936 ms | 2264.438 → 248.128 ms | 84,188 → 84,189 | 337,803 → 406,108 |
| Empty / cron-context | 75.659 → 68.112 ms | 76.333 → 83.232 ms | 6,348 → 6,350 | 91,155 → 93,968 |
| Latest 512 / actor | 133.069 → 139.198 ms | 130.631 → 137.266 ms | 84,188 → 82,978 | 337,803 → 435,185 |
| Latest 512 / cron-context | 58.324 → 56.029 ms | 53.929 → 51.247 ms | 6,348 → 5,134 | 91,155 → 89,561 |
| Full / actor | 130.740 → 27.419 ms | 129.970 → 25.664 ms | 84,188 → 2,826 | 337,803 → 142,672 |
| Full / cron-context | 59.406 → 59.844 ms | 53.955 → 50.001 ms | 6,348 → 4,465 | 91,155 → 86,682 |

SQLite page caches were cold (mmap off, 2 MiB cache), while OS cache was uncontrolled. The empty/base mean includes a large first cold-OS-cache outlier; all samples are retained, and no empty-coverage speedup is claimed. VFS spans count requested 4 KiB intersections, not physical disk I/O. Mean host load was 34.2/32.2/31.2 for empty/partial/full. Five samples do not establish p95/p99 or an adverse tail result.

For full coverage, metadata spans per requested row fall 2.432→0.057, actor spans normalized to 512 rows fall 164.430→5.520, and cron-context spans fall 12.398→8.721. Dependency scanning remains necessary: spans per selected candidate fall 16.142→11.819 across 155 candidates. General actor navigation still reads its latest 513 payload rows.

**Separate allocation and append measurements:**

| Owner | Iterations per side | CPU base → candidate | Sampled JS allocation base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Actor hydration, full facts | 200 allocation calls; 5 untraced calls | 130.740 → 27.419 ms/call | 1,600,619 → 1,599,478 B/call (neutral) |
| Cron-context, full facts | 200 allocation calls; 5 untraced calls | 59.406 → 59.844 ms/call | 20,644,870 → 20,655,593 B/call (neutral) |
| Append, mixed payload sizes | 25,000 timing; 10,000 allocation | 2.824699 → 2.890754 ms/op (+0.066055 ms, +2.34%) | 1,380,655 → 1,388,032 B/op (+0.53%) |

Append timing uses five AB/BA pairs and four fresh identical-code A/A pairs, 5,000 operations per arm. A/A signed spread was −5.51% CPU and −10.90% wall, larger than the candidate's +2.34% CPU/+3.52% wall. The small measured cost is within these controls, rather than a proven regression. Retained file growth adds 29.49 B/append; cumulative native writes rise 396,081→403,254 B/op (+1.81%). Allocation uses separate counterbalanced sampling passes with collected allocations included; these are not GC or retained-heap measurements.

**Correctness, plans, and recovery:** full/partial/absent facts return identical actor/context outputs, including reset, compaction, branch changes, pending automation, ineligible assistants, malformed/legacy rows, rewrites, cold storage, and rollback. Both engines use the companion primary key. PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` shows all four payload fallback subplans never executed under full coverage; partial/no coverage exercises the old expressions. The work-count regression runs the frozen main reader against the same real-writer fixture: main performs one native dependency projection and fails the zero-projection assertion; candidate performs zero and passes, with identical events and 441 serialized bytes.

The actual pinned schema-40 admission implementation rejects schema 41 before data reads. The real scoped restore returned both markers to 40, removed the companion, and preserved selected payload bytes in 103.35 ms. This proves the old admission path, not startup of a packaged older Gateway binary. With owners stopped, use `openclaw database restore-migration-backup` with the verified pre-upgrade scoped snapshot before starting the matching older build; manually lowering version markers is not a rollback.

**Adoption/backfill decision:** a recent window takes approximately `512 / active-appends-per-second` seconds to cover; historical totals and dependencies do not age out merely because that window is covered. A proposal-only synthetic probe populated 34,153 facts in 67 batches of at most 512: 25.0 s wall, 4.0 s CPU, 345.5 MB logical reads, 3.0 MB cumulative writes, with a 2.42 s maximum batch. Straight-line 6.3M extrapolation is about 63.7 GB logical reads, 548 MB writes, 12.3 minutes CPU and 77 minutes wall before pacing—not a production forecast. A separately approved after-ready worker with smaller byte/time-bounded batches is the follow-up decision; this PR implements none.

Local proof: 83 focused SQLite tests across seven files, the selected cold-restoration case, seven new migration tests, PostgreSQL schema/catalog verification plus migration/portability/real append cases, required closure/planner/export guards, targeted formatting/lint, matching test typechecks, and `pnpm tsgo:test:root`. Final exact-head [CI run 42110436647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42110436647) completed successfully on `b411052a21bc9c417b996d80a9e71889e8a815b6`; the required `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the previously failing migration shard passed. No reruns were used to chase green. The +850 test-line allocation covers distinct migration, lifecycle, malformed-input, cross-engine, and FK-backed index-recovery contracts.

The first CI run exposed three lifecycle cases in addition to two static guards; all have focused red/green proof and review. Canonical-index repair now handles an FK-backed unique index only after physical verification, with complete integrity revalidation inside the repair transaction; orphans, duplicates, unknown mismatches and physical corruption remain refusals (21 owner tests plus the real reopen regression). Historical PostgreSQL Doctor rebuilds consume admitted predecessor schema facts, while a missing current-schema table remains an error. Schema38/39 upgrades retain their metadata-only precheck and global post-migration FK validation (12 migration tests). SQL annotation placement and the exact worker-only invalidation classification satisfy their guards without raising a baseline. The exceptional damaged-index repair may repeat an integrity scan; the normal upgrade and hydration measurement paths are unchanged.

The third CI run caught three migration test hooks still matching the old version-publication SQL punctuation after adoption of the shared writer. Updated those hooks (including the creator-migration sibling) to match the canonical statement. Both focused files pass all seven tests, preserving independent-reader atomicity, injected-failure rollback, and real maintenance-lease loss. This is a test-only repair with zero net line growth; fresh independent review is clean.

The later dialect guard also caught raw JSON and schema-version sites. These now use the existing engine JSON path/type helpers and canonical version writer. The SQLite predicate and bindings are byte-identical to the measured version; the guard passes with design constructs unchanged and engine-maintenance sites reduced by one. Four focused files pass 25 tests, and a real PostgreSQL probe verifies 12 native JSON type cases. No dialect exemption or baseline was added.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**. The configured autoreview helper refused preflight because its requested route did not match operator configuration; configuration was not changed. Fresh independent runtime and tooling reviews have no remaining accepted P0/P1/P2 findings after fixes.

Limits: no whole-Gateway main-thread CPU, allocation rate, GC seconds/min, event-loop p99, sessions.list p99, RSS, or heap result is claimed. These are synthetic owner measurements; OS-cold physical I/O and full older-binary startup were not measured.

prs.title: fix: preserve crash recovery through slow database preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interrupted chats being abandoned after a crash when database preparation outlasts the interactive startup-admission timeout.

## User Impact

Retained work resumes once when preparation succeeds, even on a slow host. Failed preparation still reports the normal database-admission diagnostics, and shutdown still cancels recovery. No configuration, marker, or schema migration is required; the updated Gateway contains the fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Crash recovery used the bounded interactive write-admission wait. Its timeout disabled unmarked recovery, so later successful preparation changed the interrupted run to `killed` without queuing a resume. Join the existing preparation owner's completion instead. Discovery, migration ordering, write authority, and queue ownership remain with their existing owners.

The separate hypothesis that ordinary discovery consumes markers during the read-ready/write-pending interval did not reproduce: the configured inventory excludes write-pending stores and their preparation owner recovers them later. This change does not establish the cause of the reported five-session Linux failure.

## Evidence

- Controlled SQLite-backed admission/recovery regression: after advancing a fake clock beyond the request budget, the base queued zero resume inputs and persisted `killed`; the fix admits one resume. Managed restart, ordinary crash recovery, prepared queue ordering, genuine preparation failure, and duplicate suppression are covered in the same fixture.
- Focused regression file: 15/15 on Node (51.67 s wall) and pinned Bun 1.4.4 (66.77 s). Five existing admission-recovery scenarios also pass (38.57 s).
- Full `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`: 5/5 on Node (150.08 s wall) and Bun (105.20 s).
- Supplied 12-row SIGKILL matrix: all expected counts on Node (38.89 s) and Bun (33.29 s), with zero additional requests after a second restart. Each run's live control went through the real Gateway to local Ollama `qwen2.5:7b` and returned `LOCAL OK`; remaining requests used a synthetic Responses provider for deterministic counts.
- `pnpm build`, scoped lint, core and gateway test types, all requested ratchets, config docs, and plugin inventory pass. Independent autoreview is clean through P2.

All local proof is macOS arm64. The slow-preparation before/after is a controlled owner-boundary test, not a wall-clock delayed live model run.

Production: +1/-2 lines. Tests: +180/-79 (net +101), allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/restart-preparation-lifetime.txt` because the real startup lifetime and slow-clock regression replace a manually constructed pending-state fixture. No new test-only production seam or recovery owner.

prs.title: fix: reuse ready cloud workers across repository commits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ready cloud workers were discarded when a repository advanced to another commit, so available prepared capacity still led to a fresh allocation and cold setup.

## User Impact

Sessions can adopt a compatible ready worker across commits without allocating another lease. Exact-commit reserves remain preferred. The requested commit is checked out and the refreshed baseline is published before session binding. Failed refreshes retire the spare and fall back to ordinary provisioning; cancellation and lost request authority still abort.

Dependency behavior matches snapshot forks: detected installs and content-update commands follow the existing preparation rules. Devcontainer `onCreateCommand` outputs remain retained, so dependencies installed only there may stay stale unless `updateContentCommand` refreshes them. Detected-install failures remain best effort, as they are for forks. No configuration or schema change is required. Providers without the optional refresh operation retain exact-commit-only adoption.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit identity belongs to content preparation, while reserve compatibility still binds runtime artifacts, profile, recipe, repository instance, and access scope. The optional `WorkerProvider.refreshPreparedProject` operation gives an enrolled worker the same project preparation callback used by forks; Crabbox supplies only transport. The node's prepared-workspace owner accepts replacement manifests only while available and unbound. The existing durable reserve claim prevents a partly refreshed worker from reentering the pool.

Adoption records elapsed milliseconds and exact/refreshed mode in logs and placement phase timings. Maintenance no longer invalidates a compatible spare solely because its commit is older. Explicit builds remain pinned to their requested commit. The change adds about 400 net production lines and 564 allocated regression-test lines; it adds no second checkout implementation, state store, or handshake. `verifyPrepared` is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Maintainer-supplied live proof: on a real AWS rig using `openclaw/openclaw` (about 64k tracked files), `main` advanced past the reserve's prepared commit before dispatch. The reserve was adopted without a new lease and logged `Prepared worker adopted`. `sessions.dispatch` took **126 s**, including **92 s** in `reserveRefresh`, compared with **361 s** for a snapshot fork and **338 s** cold on the same rig. The ctime histogram showed only the **59 changed files** were rewritten; **64,326 of 64,385 hash memo entries** hit. These are individual rig measurements, not a production percentile or proof of the original seconds target; this PR leaves `verifyPrepared` unchanged.
- Baseline `1c2d67466484e9ab397c1daed1db2a0deb334dab`: the same A-to-B dispatch regression failed because dispatch selected a new environment instead of the ready reserve (153.50 s wall time).

prs.title: fix: warn at startup for missing Node certificate patches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compatible Node builds below the recommended certificate security patches start without a clear warning, while installer fallback policy can still require an unnecessary runtime upgrade.

Related: #179992 and #186589. This implements Peter's decision on November 5, 2026; @joshavant for awareness of the follow-through on the original eMudhra protection.

## User Impact

OpenClaw starts when the only problem is Node's missing certificate patch, with one stderr security warning explaining that TLS may trust certificates signed with keys compromised in the October 2026 eMudhra incident. The warning gives the exact upgrade guidance: Node 24.22.1+ on 24.x or Node 26.12.1+. Machine-readable stdout, including `--json`, remains intact.

Missing `node:sqlite`, NUL truncation (nodejs/node#61954), failed data round-trips, and unsafe SQLite WAL-reset versions remain hard refusals. Bun retains its independent runtime/TLS policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

For a certificate-only gap, automatic recovery searches for an already-installed patched Node and uses it if available. It never downloads a runtime solely for this recommendation; otherwise startup warns and continues. Native browser and exact-process relay entrypoints preserve their existing process ownership. Final-process warning ownership avoids duplicates across startup respawns and update preparation.

`package.json` already declares the actual compatibility floors (`>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`) and stays unchanged. Installer fallback engines now match; freshly provisioned defaults remain patched. Explicitly selected historical packages retain their own stricter engines because those releases can enforce them at startup. Installer, Doctor guidance, README, and security documentation now describe the same advisory policy.

The existing warning formatter owns risk text and emission deduplication. The production change adds 75 net lines; 214 net regression-test lines cover distinct recovery, output, installer, and runtime boundaries, with a scoped test-line allocation. Two existing installer tests exposed a Bash 3.2 PATH-quoting defect, fixed at the quote producer without changing the tests.

## Evidence

- Real official Node 24.21.0 (SQLite 3.53.4): starts with exactly one warning when other runtimes are inaccessible; `models list --json` parses successfully with exactly one stderr warning; uses an already-installed patched Node without a security warning when available.
- Real official Node 24.15.0 (SQLite 3.51.3): exits 1 before Gateway startup for NUL truncation, with empty stdout. Official download checksums verified.
- 707 focused tests passed across six shards (194 seconds); four existing skips. Includes launcher/native transport/Bun distinction, installed recovery/no-download behavior, all SQLite refusal types, installer platforms, Doctor, and update preparation. The new update deduplication regression first failed with two warnings, then passed with one.
- `pnpm build:runtime`, core typecheck, focused lint, shell syntax, formatting, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Runtime build emitted an advisory chat boot size overage (1264.8 KiB versus 1264.4 KiB); CI remains the broad gate.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local change against `ba400bcb7cd`, including unchanged runtime/respawn context: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Earlier-head [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42099502230): 50 successful jobs, 26 scope skips, no failures, at `0a31b14d128451a0bcff508b41351782aece06e0`. Runner capacity delayed nine shards; the original run completed when capacity recovered.
- A documented [capacity fallback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42104524593) was canceled after the authoritative PR run passed. Its broader checks exposed three unrelated existing findings: an unused `readUpdatePhysicalDatabaseGenerations` export; the legacy Doctor fixture intercepting an inherited compile-cache respawn before runtime recovery (reproduced with the Node test runner); and a mocked Systems workspace layout-shift assertion (`0.0007013715277777778` versus zero). Their owning source/tests are unchanged by this PR. The seven legacy-entry cases pass with the default Bun runner, which disables that cache. These failures are recorded, not reported as passing. The legacy fixture failure is now fixed: it disables Node compile caching before its instrumented spawn, while the separate cache cases still opt in explicitly. The exact Node-runner/cache reproduction failed before this two-line fixture correction and all seven cases passed afterward. The follow-up also passed independent P0–P2 autoreview, focused lint, formatting, and the test-line ratchet. Final [exact-head PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42108524242/attempts/2) at `c9c3c843ca6b3d6236005fbd857e3a0d94e8d8a4`: 49 successful jobs, 26 scope skips, no failures. Eight shards had waited unassigned for more than 25 minutes; after all other work passed, the documented hybrid recovery canceled that stalled attempt and reran only unfinished jobs on hosted runners. The production code is unchanged.

Release-note context: warn instead of refusing or downloading solely for Node's certificate patch level; retain all SQLite safety checks. No changelog edit because this repository generates release notes at release time.

prs.title: feat(pairing): pair a browser with a short code approved on the host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A browser with no Gateway credential has no way to ask for one. Today it needs a pasted token, or a one-time link from `openclaw dashboard` carried over from the host. On a headless Gateway reached over SSH, both mean moving a secret by hand.

## User Impact

- A browser can pair without a token, link or host browser. Approving its code on the host pairs it as an ordinary operator device with the Control UI's admin scopes. That is the same result as approving it with `openclaw devices approve`, so it appears in `openclaw devices list` and the Devices page, and `openclaw devices remove` ends its access.
- New CLI command `openclaw pair <code>` and a new public route, both documented in `/cli/pair` and `/web/control-ui/connect-and-pair`.
- A browser that is already paired with a revoked or narrowed operator token keeps that limit. Its code is refused, and the message names `openclaw dashboard` or `openclaw devices remove <id>` as the next step. The owner handoff stays with `openclaw dashboard` and onboarding.
- Pairing works when browser storage is blocked or full. The approved token is kept for the life of the page, as the browser's device identity already is, so the page still connects and **Forget this browser** still clears it. A reload in that state needs pairing again.
- When `gateway.roles` is configured, bootstrap connections need a verified identity, so code pairing is refused there the same way `openclaw dashboard` links are.
- **Known low-impact limit:** a network client that rotates its source address can keep the 32-row pending table full, so other browsers see "Too many pairing requests". State stays bounded and nobody can replace another browser's request. Token and `openclaw dashboard` sign-in keep working.
- On a plain `http://` address, anyone on that network can read Gateway traffic after pairing, as with any plain-HTTP Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. The login gate's sign-in card gains a **Pair with a code instead** link. It opens a card that holds only pairing. **Get a code** shows `openclaw pair ABCD-EFGH` and a Browser ID while the browser waits. The link is offered only when the selected Gateway URL matches the page's scheme (`ws:` for `http:`, `wss:` for `https:`), host and base path.

   ![Sign-in card with code pairing link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0598b57-272f-4ea4-9d85-4c476a42c6e4)

   ![Pairing card waiting with command and Browser ID](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f421e08d-c6a2-4cb1-807c-b0885c26c1aa)

   ![Pairing card waiting at phone width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d572f64c-71da-4a82-891a-edd473332bf0)

2. On the host, over SSH if needed, `openclaw pair` shows who is asking and waits for an answer:

   ```text
   A browser is asking to pair with administrator access to this Gateway.

     Code                34EL-ZNRU
     Browser (reported)  Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7) ... Safari/605.1.15
     Address             127.0.0.1
     Page (reported)     http://127.0.0.1:18789
     Browser ID          e2de4320
     Requested           just now

   Approve only if you opened this page yourself and it shows this code and Browser ID.
   If someone sent you this code or command, answer no: approving gives their browser administrator control of this Gateway.
   Approve this browser? [y/N]
   ```

3. The waiting browser keeps its device token for that Gateway and connects with it.

   ![Control UI connected after approval](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6952e4cd-4691-4d4f-81c0-fe40e85439ac)

### How it works

- **`POST <base>/__openclaw__/browser-pair/start`** is public and same-origin. Each filed request spends the source's pairing budget under the Gateway's auth rate limit. It takes a signature from the browser's device key and files one row in a new `device_pairing_browser_requests` table, returning a request ID and an eight-character code.
- **`device.pair.code`** requires `operator.admin`.
  - With `code`, it returns the request.
  - With `requestId` and `decision`, it settles exactly that request.
  - Approval files an operator pairing request for the request's key and approves it through the existing approval kernel, using the approving caller's scopes. The browser's own earlier pending requests are closed, not merged into the grant.
- **`POST .../collect`** returns the outcome only to a signature from the requesting key.
  - After approval it returns the paired device's operator token, read from the device record, until the request expires.
  - Collect has its own budget, spent only by invalid signatures and unknown requests, so filing requests cannot lock a waiting browser out of its answer.
- **Expiry and rotation:** the request deadline and the shared-auth generation are checked again when the database writer takes the approval. An approval that waited past expiry or a shared-secret rotation rolls back. Collect checks the deadline again right before it answers, so a collect that waited past expiry answers `expired`.

### Security properties

- The code names a request and is not a bearer secret.
- On the signed pairing and WebSocket paths, the device token works only with the requesting key. Treat it as a secret, like any operator token.
- Code-paired tokens carry the Gateway's shared-auth generation, so rotating the shared secret retires them, like tokens issued at connect.
- An administrator revoked while their approval waits is refused at the final effect, and nothing is issued.
- A collected token is handed out only while it is the token that approval issued; rotation, revocation or removal ends collection.
- Requests expire after ten minutes. At most 32 are pending. Filing and invalid collects are each limited per source.
- **Origin policy:** the route uses the Gateway's browser origin policy, including the check that a loopback page came from a loopback socket. It is a CSRF guard, not a network boundary; authority comes from host approval and the key proof.
- `Browser` and `Page` are marked `(reported)` because the requester chooses them.
- The request table is covered by the secret-table policy, so redacted backups omit it.
- Without a terminal the CLI approves nothing unless `--yes` is passed. The page never suggests `--yes`.

### Decisions for review

- **Ordinary operator pairing, not the owner handoff.** Approval goes through the same approval rules as `openclaw devices approve`. The result is a normal paired device, so the existing ways of listing it, narrowing its token and removing it all apply.
- **`tokenIssuer` approval option.** The approval kernel gains an optional `tokenIssuer`, so the issued browser token is bound to the current shared-auth generation. Without it, the existing token policy refuses issuer-less browser tokens while shared auth is configured.
- **Page-lifetime token fallback.** When storage rejects a write, the device-token store keeps a page-lifetime copy, as the device identity does. This applies to every user of that store, not only pairing.
- **Separate table for unauthenticated input.** Route input stays out of the list operators approve from, including `openclaw devices approve --latest`. Only an admin's decision turns it into a pairing.
- **One additive protocol method and one additive lazy table.** No protocol version change.
- **Test-line allocation.** `config/test-lines-allocations/browser-pair-code.txt` covers the net test lines this PR adds.

## Evidence

**Gateway suite** (`src/gateway/server.browser-pair.test.ts`, 20 cases): passes against a real Gateway. It covers:
- first-time pairing by code as an ordinary admin device, with the token refused over WebSocket for another key;
- refusing to restore a narrowed operator token;
- closing the browser's earlier pending request instead of widening the grant;
- expiry while the approval waits in the writer queue, and while a collect waits;
- a queued approval refused once its administrator is revoked through the Gateway's live revocation owner;
- rollback when authority ends at any check;
- callers holding only `operator.pairing`, `operator.read` or `operator.write`;
- a browser that still collects its approval after filing spent its source's budget (`maxAttempts=1`), while forged collects are still limited;
- rejection, unknown or expired codes, origin and key checks, and the start rate limit.

**Control UI** (223 cases across the pairing card, device-identity and device-token storage, device credentials and forgetting, the connection page, the login gate, gateway connect and the app root): passes. It includes a browser whose storage rejects writes: it still connects with its approved token through the real connect auth selection, and that token is listed and forgotten through the real forget path.

**Regressions proven:**
- The storage, forget, collect-budget, token-rotation, collect-expiry and incomplete-stored-identity tests fail without their fixes.
- With the expiry recheck, the narrowed-token refusal or the superseded-request cleanup disabled, its test fails.

**Static checks:** core, UI and the touched test typecheck shards, plus oxlint and oxfmt on changed files, are clean. The generated protocol validators, Kysely types and Postgres schema verify.

**Not covered:**
- the full suite;
- a live browser run on this head, including real blocked storage;
- a browser on a different machine from the Gateway;
- trusted-proxy and Tailscale Serve deployments;
- the Postgres state engine;
- an upgrade from the latest stable;
- translated strings, which `control-ui-locale-refresh` adds.

Maintainer security approval is required for this head.

Related: #159660, #120768

prs.title: fix(msteams): let proactive sends start a new channel post
prs.body:
Related: #93288

## What Problem This Solves

A proactive Teams send can reuse the saved conversation root even when the operator wants a new channel post and ordinary channel replies must remain threaded.

## User Impact

Teams operators can request a new post per send with `topLevel: true`. Explicit thread targets retain their placement. For a new channel post, oversized text, multiple attachments, or a captioned inline image fail before dispatch so one request cannot silently create multiple roots. Private and group chats keep their existing behavior. Long text can use a single native presentation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the placement flag through the existing prepared payload, queue and Teams outbound adapter. Durable core sends retain the prepared payload without invoking a provider action shortcut. Existing inbound threading policy and ordinary send behavior stay in place.

## Evidence

- 94 Teams tests, 81 core outbound tests, and 21 outbound contract tests passed on `49463e4d695796331f158727c180cac2bf90e809` in source mode using the repository Vitest configs and the pinned dependencies.
- Coverage includes stored-root suppression, explicit thread precedence, forced-core placement, one outbound card for a long presentation, and two mention entities in one activity.
- Formatting, standard lint, and diff checks passed. Type-aware lint in the sparse checkout reported an unresolved type in an unchanged group-management helper.
- Independent source review identified and the final revision addressed forced-core propagation, explicit reply conflicts, and multi-post/replay behavior. A live Teams canary is pending.
- Compatibility coverage includes channel actions and discovery, thread resolution, delivery handoff, and real SDK request construction for cards, polls, attachments, and mentions with mocked HTTP.
- Native message-tool discovery exposes the placement and presentation fields for both unbound and Teams contexts. The documented test-line allocation passes the local ratchet check.
- The two findings from the hosted review are addressed. Channel limits use the stored conversation type, and captioned inline images are rejected before the SDK can submit two activities. An independent source re-review found no blocking issues. A provider canary in an authorised Teams test channel is still required for live evidence.

## Inherited hosted test-budget failure

The [latest CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42112988988) failed its test-line budget gate. The canonical scanner on the unmodified CI base `d41332b5b3798623314a0469441dbbf654996f45` reports **6,507,445 lines against a 6,507,349 ceiling**, an inherited overage of 96 lines. The test merge reports **6,507,590 against 6,507,494**, the same overage. This PR adds 145 lines and allocates exactly 145. A separate scan of later main `d0b0fc80a34df23e927c5db33670849e6ad5dd60` still reports 84 inherited excess lines. These were staged Git-snapshot scans using the repository scanner and independent index files. No baseline, checker, or unrelated test coverage was changed.

## What Problem This Solves

The filesystem import guard rejects Knowledge's existing synchronous directory fence because its reviewed dependency map omits the new owner introduced in [PR189088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189088).

## User Impact

No runtime change. This fixes the import-boundary check without changing Knowledge publication ordering or directory synchronization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Knowledge owns `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.27.1`. Its identity and publication paths require `syncDirectorySync`; the existing SDK directory-sync facade is asynchronous. Admit only that binding from `@openclaw/fs-safe/durability` in `extensions/knowledge/src/directory-sync.ts`. Other files, symbols, import forms and subpaths remain restricted.

## Evidence

- [Original failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42084864227/job/127448316725): the full import guard reports exactly this owner in both Node and pinned Bun. Determining guard and owner blobs are unchanged on the selected base.
- Maintained `scripts/pr review-tests` in the PR's own full checkout at `b2c0ec101a59624a6e278faf1eb38816a00c768a`: all 22 whole-file checks pass on Node24.22.1 and pinned Bun1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1, including the tracked-source scan and existing negative boundaries. The Bun executable hash matches the repository pin.
- The normal commit hook and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent source review approves the exact one-line entry. Full committed-range ClawSweeper review (`d732e60c642326aed653eb062becb321513775c2..b2c0ec101a59624a6e278faf1eb38816a00c768a`) reports no actionable correctness or security findings.

prs.title: chore(ui): measure native paste and WebKit giant runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI census could not time real clipboard paste, and its giant completed-run probe required Chromium CDP, leaving WebKit fragmentation unverified.

## User Impact

No application behavior changes. Maintainers can now run opt-in native text/image paste and completed-run opening, expansion, and scrolling workloads in both browser engines.

## Why This Change Was Made

The paste scenarios use a trusted keyboard paste and browser clipboard, verify the exact unsent draft or decoded attachment, and record dispatch and ready-frame latency separately. The completed-run scenarios reuse the existing history fixture and scroll sampler, verify the complete history and endpoints, and count fragments and mounted elements. They are desktop-only because mobile WebKit cannot deliver the required wheel input.

Clipboard/PNG preparation stays outside timing. Ready-frame timestamps are not paint timestamps; completed-run opening durations include navigation and awaited readiness. WebKit has no CPU throttle or comparable untraced CPU counter, so its paste result is native-speed only.

## Evidence

Production UI reference `16daab2e6864`, current UI `cf80b26f093d`, same host and frozen bundles. Ten rotated reference/current/reference-control triplets per cell, with A/A controls; selected repeats use twenty triplets. The historical Usage reference is `cb72b4b00823`, with one identical current compiled Gateway behind every UI role.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original 28 unresolved screen cells | 840/840 observations passed. After 60 Appearance/Memory repeat observations: 11 material concerns gone, 17 noise, none confirmed. Noise remains inconclusive. |
| Native paste | 210/210 comparisons plus four smoke observations passed: trusted events, exact 256 KiB text or 2–5 MiB image, no sends/errors. Chromium text latency stays about 74 ms at 1× and 317 ms at 4×; task CPU improves about 16%. The image 4× whole-scenario CPU tail remains higher; diagnostic attribution below separates it from native input. |
| Giant completed runs | 300/300 comparisons plus 20 smoke observations passed. No browser errors or blank visible frames; endpoints within 2 px and full history retained. |
| WebKit completed-run expansion | 400 messages: 571/602 → 93.5/104 ms median/p95; 2,000 messages: 2,454/2,693 → 100.5/107 ms. Clean controls. Both current sizes use six fragments and 188 mounted elements. |
| Direct-run opening, 2,000 messages | Chromium 11,353/12,880 → 671/727 ms; WebKit 8,395/10,790 → 960/997 ms. Clean controls. Current has 202 mounted elements versus 45,196. These are driver-to-readiness durations. |
| Historical Usage CPU | All 120 filters and 12 setup observations completed. The prior +34.65% primary finding is not reproduced cleanly: current model-00/100 ms CPU median is +6.8%, p95 −14.1%, with noisy A/A. Small clean CPU increases remain in other cells; no blanket Usage clearance is claimed. |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:scripts` passed. |
| Lint/format | Changed-script oxlint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. |
| Production Knip | Passed (`pnpm deadcode:knip`). |
| Asset checks | Both frozen UI builds pass the strict performance checker. Current startup JS is 90,552 B gzip, three JS requests and one CSS request. This patch adds no application runtime bytes. |
| Independent review | Codex autoreview of the complete patch against `cf80b26f093d`, P0–P2: scoped-clean after fixing the desktop-only wheel boundary. The final two-line CPU-boundary clarification also received a scoped-clean P0–P2 review. Final head: `14ba8c5d5d0d`. |

A twenty-triplet image 4× comparison confirms a whole-scenario script CPU p95 increase (63.916 → 84.666 ms), while native input median/p95 improves (152.5/172.6 → 141.5/154.6 ms). A separate diagnostic trace found pre-keydown sidebar snapshot work in the generic CPU window; the owner is unchanged between builds. Within keydown-to-ready, traced task time is 118.4/122.9/120.7 ms (reference/current/A/A), with similar paste-handler and Solid-flush costs. This does not prove native-CPU equivalence; it prevents misattributing whole-scenario CPU to paste. No safe small production fix or new paste lane is established.

The remaining transcript scroll, switch, fork, split view, edit/resubmit and streaming-onset work belongs to the existing long-session effort. Its handoff preserves the small 400-message WebKit frame-cadence regression, the 88 ms large-run frame-gap tail, historical switching/CPU findings, and the lack of a fresh isolated streaming-onset measurement. No competing lane is proposed.

Five affected benchmark/docs files: 3,383 → 3,769 LOC (+388/−2). No production code or dependency changes. The additional code provides the missing native-input and cross-engine proof boundaries rather than a second rendering or fixture owner.

Verdict: no remaining optimization worth a lane outside the existing long-session effort. Small Usage and whole-scenario CPU residuals remain recorded rather than classified as cleared.

prs.title: fix: stop channel messages replaying when reply queue fills
prs.body:
Closes #182246

## What Problem This Solves

Durable channel messages discarded by a full follow-up queue were re-claimed and retried as abandoned turns until their retry budget ran out. The Discord fan-in and inbound-debounce wrappers, Telegram spooled replay, Feishu fan-in/broadcast, and Slack logical replay guards also lost the new terminal-drop callback, so the initial queue fix did not reach those channels.

## User Impact

Actual queue-cap evictions now settle once in the failed-message ledger with a policy reason, including through Discord’s and iMessage’s shared composed ingress lifecycle, Telegram’s spooled replay participant, Feishu’s flush/broadcast adapters, and Slack’s logical replay guard. Summary-elision cap eviction has the same terminal disposition. A full queue with no evictable item remains retryable backpressure, not a policy drop. Ordinary abandonment and cancellation remain unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue previously completed cap-dropped sources through the same callback used when a turn never adopted the reply lane. The ingress drain interpreted that as retryable abandonment. The queue now gives deliberate discards an explicit terminal lifecycle disposition; ingress classifies it as non-retryable and retains asynchronous settlement custody before marking the source complete. Channel fan-in and inbound debounce forward that disposition without losing the claims (the same fan-in is used by iMessage). Telegram spooled replay forwards and awaits the terminal disposition through its deferred participant, then settles the durable row. Feishu flush and broadcast carry terminal drops through transport and replay-claim settlement; Slack preserves the callback through its ingress lifecycle and commits its separate logical replay claim on a drop. The all-protected refusal keeps the retry path.

## Evidence

- Initial red-first queue and ingress fossils were added before the implementation on ancestor `7ab64536d3eb75e7020a90ebce0b6eafc06502e4`; the touched four-file suite passed 97/97 after the fix.
- Independent review at `54c515a2` identified the Discord wrapper gap and all-protected backpressure. Three further red-first cases failed on that head, then passed after the correction: composed fan-in→debounce drop (2 claims), protected backpressure, and summary-elision cap eviction.
- Corrected head `1e971137a52124ad9fc2ddf9f341e7328d4aecfc`: prior 51 focused core tests passed; red-first Telegram fossils failed on `0f0f5fb080b6` and passed after correction (processor 19/19 and SQLite ingress 23/23). Slack ingress/message-handler suites passed 38/38; Feishu ingress/broadcast suites passed 24/24, followed by a targeted drop-settlement-failure case 2/2. Core/core-test and extension/extension-test typechecks, touched-file oxlint and oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. That head’s CI had two failing Node shards; they are under attribution, not counted as green.
- Current head `8eb4fe75bba4d4decf2ef906a789673b4a507e80`: red-first Feishu broadcast failure probe now verifies the dropped-lane claim releases when durable settlement fails; Slack success/failure probes verify the logical claim commits only after both lifecycle callbacks succeed. Feishu broadcast 11/11 and Slack message-handler 19/19 passed; extension production/test typechecks, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Current-head CI completed with two gateway test failures: `server.chat-abort-settlement.test.ts` accepted-injection dispatch expected one injection but saw none, and `server.subagent-stop-followup.product.test.ts` parent-stop case observed a missing `killReconciliation`. Both signatures also failed on prior head `1e971137`; the failure report marks them unknown because it found no matching main jobs. A focused local Bun rerun of both files passed 17/17, which is not evidence that the CI failures are fixed or inherited. Exact-head independent review remains pending.
- The required Codex autoreview was attempted but failed authentication. A Claude delta review returned incomplete on a proposed mixed-lane gap; source and the existing passing mixed-lane test show `dropReason` selects terminal drop even when another lane adopted, so the alleged orphan path is not reachable. Neither attempt is presented as a clean whole-PR review. No production deployment was used for this PR; the isolated Gateway proof is below.
- Scope: iMessage uses the fixed shared fan-in/debounce chain. LINE, SMS, and Google Chat pass through their supplied ingress lifecycle. The new direct adapter corrections cover Telegram, Feishu, and Slack logical replay custody.
- Post-fix isolated Discord Gateway proof at `8eb4fe75` is below; the pre-fix fleet evidence remains separate.

### Live evidence (before fix)

**Behavior or issue addressed:** #182246 — queue-cap drops replay durable ingress.

**Before evidence:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182246#issuecomment-6380343974

Live evidence from a deployed fleet, 2026-10-24 03:30–04:30Z, posted at the reporter's request. Discord IDs, session keys and message text are redacted.

**Setup**
- Discord guild channel with 6 agents in one busy room.
- `messages.queue.cap = 10`, `messages.queue.drop = old`.
- The builds carry a bounded-retry change for abandoned ingress (`turn-abandoned` counts as an attempt; 8 attempts, then dead-letter). On upstream `main` the abandonment path releases the claim without consulting the dead-letter disposition, so the same messages would re-queue indefinitely rather than exhaust. That is the "eventual retry exhaustion" open point.

**Observed on two hosts**

One message's history (seat A). The same `<msg-A>` is re-dispatched and abandoned again about every 1–2 min:
```
21:08:45 [discord] ingress: spooled update <msg-A> failed; keeping for retry: turn-abandoned
21:10:13 [discord] ingress: spooled update <msg-A> failed; keeping for retry: turn-abandoned
21:10:48 … turn-abandoned
21:11:50 … turn-abandoned
21:13:42 … turn-abandoned
21:14:42 … turn-abandoned
21:17:14 … turn-abandoned
```
Ingress rows that reached terminal state in that hour (`channel_ingress_events`, status `failed`):

| seat | `retry-limit-exceeded` rows | max attempts | `turn-abandoned` log lines (1h) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (build `03de0ce5d3`) | 9 | 7 | 160 |
| B (build `7d8a1a91c6`) | 16 | 7 | 244 |

Each dead-lettered row's `last_error` is `turn-abandoned`. Each loop iteration re-runs the model. Seat B logged 186 abandons against 12 model calls in 16 min, and the agent stayed mute.

**Attribution caveats**
- The queue-cap drop path does not log, so these rows are not individually tagged as cap drops. The attribution is from the shape of the loop: the same oldest IDs fail together, it only happens under room load, and a fresh or quiet session shows 0.
- Seat A's build also lacks #169107 (stale-actor rebase under the writer FIFO), which produces a different abandonment path. That one logs `refusing replay: Session actor version changed…`. Seat A logged 2 of those against 160 abandons. Seat B logged 0 of them against 244. So seat B's loop is not that race.
- A small log line on policy drops (`queue-cap-old` / `queue-cap-new`, plus the source id) would make this attributable in the field. It might be worth adding alongside #182252.

Related review note on #182252: on the Discord path, `onDropped` does not survive `fanInChannelIngressLifecycles` and `createInboundDebounceFlush`, so Discord drops still fall back to `onAbandoned`. Details will go on the PR.

🌿 frond-scribe, via Claude Code
https://claude.ai/code/session_01Jhynq2GVpzuVQQieebEubg

### Live proof (after fix; isolated Gateway)

Exact PR head: `8eb4fe75bba4d4decf2ef906a789673b4a507e80`. This is an isolated local Gateway running the bundled Discord channel adapter against a synthetic local Discord provider (Crabline) and a local mock model provider, not a production deployment or a live Discord account. A one-off, uncommitted QA Lab probe used the existing `channel-progress-presentation.e2e.test.ts` fixture, held the first model response, and sent synthetic `QCAP-RUNNER`, `QCAP-A`, and `QCAP-B` Discord messages through the channel ingress endpoint. Each policy had fresh Gateway/SQLite state, `messages.queue = { mode: collect, cap: 1, drop: old|new, debounceMsByChannel.discord: 0 }`, and inbound debounce 0. The probe released the held response, then checked the SQLite failed ledger, model requests, and Discord outbound writes after settlement.

The failed row was terminal exactly once (`attempts: 0`) with the dropped source and policy reason; the dropped source did not become a model request. The survivor did become the next model request and received a distinct model reply. The `drop:new` queue-full notice is counted separately from model replies.

Redacted terminal output (all IDs/markers are synthetic; only status, reason, and counts are printed):

```text
QUEUE_CAP_PROOF {"head":"8eb4fe75bba4d4decf2ef906a789673b4a507e80","drop":"old","rows":[{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null},{"status":"failed","reason":"queue-cap-old","attempts":0,"source":"QCAP-A"},{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null},{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null},{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null}],"modelReplies":2,"queueFullNotices":0,"providerRequests":["QCAP-RUNNER","QCAP-B"]}
QUEUE_CAP_PROOF {"head":"8eb4fe75bba4d4decf2ef906a789673b4a507e80","drop":"new","rows":[{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null},{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null},{"status":"failed","reason":"queue-cap-new","attempts":0,"source":"QCAP-B"},{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null},{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null},{"status":"completed","reason":null,"attempts":0,"source":null}],"modelReplies":2,"queueFullNotices":1,"providerRequests":["QCAP-RUNNER","QCAP-A"]}
Tests  2 passed | 16 skipped (18)
Duration  95.47s (tests 87%, transform 8%, import 4%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 107.01s
```

The adapter-propagation note in the historical pre-fix comment above describes the original PR revision; the current head includes those adapter fixes. This proof covers Discord old/new policy behavior through an isolated Gateway. It does not claim a real Discord deployment or independent live proof for the Telegram, Feishu, or Slack adapters, which have separate focused tests described above.

prs.title: fix: stop replaying messages discarded by queue caps
prs.body:
Closes #182246. Maintainer continuation of #182252, preserving the contributor commits. Thanks @emeric-dandelion-cult for the original repair.

## What Problem This Solves

Messages intentionally discarded by the session queue's `old`/`new` cap policies could re-enter durable ingress, replay, and delay surviving messages.

## User Impact

Policy-discarded messages receive a terminal queue-policy outcome without retry-failure notices or resend invitations. Surviving messages retain FIFO ordering. Protected-only capacity rejection remains retryable; surfaces without durable ingress keep visible queue-full feedback, and a refused `/followup` reports that it was not queued.

Policy drops do not count as dead letters in health or Doctor. Retention bounds their replay guards separately from actual failures under the existing TTL. No config option, schema migration, dependency, or manual action is added. Old dropped content can still appear in Discord's independently recovered room history; it does not execute as a separate turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing queue, source-custody, and ingress owners carry a distinct dropped outcome through debounce and channel wrappers. The ingress monitor forwards it through its existing settlement wrapper. Failure reporting and bounded pruning remain with their existing owners. Feishu settles dropped session lanes independently, and summary eviction unbinds a source before awaiting its receipt.

Reload and claim ownership come from merged main, including #193564. The monitor change only forwards `onDropped` through `settleLifecycle`; this PR adds no competing custody or fence mechanism. SDK docs describe forwarding and cleanup. Wrappers without durable terminal-drop custody retain their existing abandonment fallback.

Redelivery while a drop callback's receipt is still pending receives the existing bounded pending refusal; this is accepted, and no eager commit or `onDropped` wrapper is added.

## Evidence

Three dispatch/real-ingress/real-followup composition regressions cover old eviction, new rejection, and summarized eviction. Each verifies a terminal row with attempts 0 and its policy reason, then settled-source same-ID redelivery returns `skipped:duplicate`, makes no second resolver call, and sends no final reply. All three already passed on the merged head before this continuation; they protect composition with #193564 rather than establish a newly fixed post-settlement leak.

Real local-model proof used an isolated Gateway through `pnpm openclaw`, synthetic Discord transport, real shared Ollama `qwen2.5:7b`, and the real queue, ingress ledger, model request and delivery path. These are macOS arm64 results, not live Discord-service or Linux/Windows proof.

- Node 26.12.1 and pinned Bun 1.4.4 each passed reload plus old/new policy survival. Reload produced exactly RUNNER/B/C/D requests and replies in order; A ended `queue-cap-old` with attempts 0. Each surviving source completed with attempts 0. Each runtime logged one recovered unavailable-instance event; generation advanced 2 to 3, health/status answered, and no uncaught exception or unhandled rejection occurred. Old/new produced exactly RUNNER+B and RUNNER+A respectively, with the discarded source terminal at attempts 0 and no retry/resend notice. Combined command wall times: 114.03s Node, 69.73s Bun.
- Both runtimes passed real Gateway non-durable overflow and refused `/followup`: each refusal produced exactly one neutral queue-full terminal outcome, while RUNNER and queued A each received a real model answer. Command wall times: 58.48s Node, 22.59s Bun. All eight scenarios passed; no input was lost, duplicated or left unanswered. All 22 retained runtime/launcher logs were scanned without an uncaught exception or unhandled rejection.

`pnpm build` passed in 279.90s. The focused consumer set passed 895 tests across 37 files with one PostgreSQL-only capability skip in 508.51s. It covers queue/summary, ingress monitor/drain/claim ownership, channel wrappers, SDK fan-in/debounce, plugin replacement, Gateway outcomes, and prompt-prefix stability. All eight scoped production/test typechecks now pass; the first run caught a test-only lifecycle narrowing error. Scoped production/test/script lint and formatting pass after removing an unused import left by main integration. The corrected two-file Node rerun passed all 105 tests in 61.11s.

The build, live runs and full consumer set preceded the final test-only type/import correction; production bytes are unchanged. No production wrapper or eager dedupe commit was added. All ten final-head baseline ratchets pass (53.79s), including assertion safety, line caps, timeout races, mock exports, test lines, database boundaries, configuration docs and plugin inventory.

Current candidate: `7ddd944b651faf57bd935977235a69715768cb7c`. ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review at 2026-11-05 20:15 UTC with no findings, no security findings and no Before merge items. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42100431795) passed on attempt 2 at 2026-11-05 21:24 UTC. Attempt 1 failed only the Bun restart/resume test with `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError` during startup. The affected owner code is identical to main; ten full-file local runs passed on main and this head, and the separate restart/resume admission lane owns that race. Only the failed shard was rerun once. The maintainer lead accepted this evidence and authorized landing; the previously reported CI blocker is resolved.

Local Codex branch autoreview from `54ed2bcc74b746085ddebe28ee59d268cd302fb6` to `7ddd944b651faf57bd935977235a69715768cb7c` through P2 is scoped-clean, with no accepted/actionable findings. The reviewer assessed source; runtime proof is reported separately.

The earlier main comparison reproduced old/new discarded rows remaining claimed rather than reaching a terminal policy outcome, despite a real RUNNER answer; the candidate passed those invariants. That baseline reproduction is retained prior-lane evidence, not a new run here.

Rename-aware delta against merged main `54ed2bcc74b746085ddebe28ee59d268cd302fb6`: production/scripts +527/-185 (net +342); tests/support +1362/-1196 (net +166); docs +40/-3 (net +37). This continuation adds 0 production lines and a net 108 test lines (109 composition lines minus one unused import). Production growth carries terminal outcomes through existing wrappers and separates bounded retention classes. A dedicated 166-line test allocation covers the 58 existing net regression lines after main integration plus this continuation’s net 108 test lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. The composition uses existing fixtures and no real timers or extra Gateway boot.

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): generate catalog-qualified OpenRouter music
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192276

## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter's registered music tool cannot consume its qualified OpenRouter Lyria offers, and provider-wide capabilities would drop their duration or load unsupported reference images before selection.

## User Impact

When a deployment grants either frozen OpenRouter Lyria model, the existing music tool can select its native or manifest transport with only the ClawRouter key. It returns one complete WAV or MP3 track and rejects reference images before loading them. A possibly paid POST cannot trigger another provider attempt after errors, cancellation, lost responses, or local persistence failure. This draft does not activate router offers or qualify live synthesis or dollar pricing.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a focused stack on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192276 at `c4fa75387b0fa42f45e47e09de25725b8d03d0e0`, prepared through the native route with the exact landed SDK outer-deadline correction from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192196. Lyria production/SDK/Google behavior remains unchanged; the current parent additionally carries the exact already-qualified stored-key speech fixture correction and its +1 allocation. It consumes the two text-only declaration contracts from https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/797 (`12f4815ce3c289554f60ec192cf3f01afca905cc`) and the full-output runtime landed by https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/795 (`e47ecdedd4da93bb665431b81f698668468dc8ea`). Source6 owns subsequent composed Worker proof.

The native plugin and proxy consumer share the existing SSE-audio decoder through the existing music-generation SDK barrel; native credential resolution stays in the native plugin. Optional model-specific duration and reference-image maps resolve before normalization/reference loading. Google retains its original capability projection and request/result behavior. The existing registered-tool fixture is shared rather than copied; the native decoder's former private implementation is removed.

The proxy profile requires exact model/upstream/provider/operation/formats and fresh proxy-key offers. It sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, caps the request at256KiB and prompt at32768 UTF-16 units, and requires `[DONE]` plus EOF within32MiB wire/16MiB audio/1MiB transcript. Requested duration is at most180 seconds; it does not promise an output size or completion time. The existing caller signal, remaining deadline and explicit header/body inactivity bound remain authoritative. A qualified Undici body-inactivity timeout is surfaced as a TimeoutError with its original cause, rather than an ambiguous terminated message. The final thrown error retains the post-attempt replay marker; that marker does not determine billing or refunds.

Corrected source: `49743aff29c4adf37188725b130325026d3dad18`, on Lyria parent `c4fa75387b0fa42f45e47e09de25725b8d03d0e0`. This correction uses the existing SDK error-code reader at the ClawRouter provider boundary. The typed wrapper preserves the original error as its cause and receives the existing no-replay marker before it is thrown. Generic TypeError/terminated errors are not classified as timeouts. Google and direct OpenRouter behavior, streamTimeoutMs, operation deadlines, signal precedence, cleanup and accounting are unchanged.

The entire 200-line observation fixture is removed. Allocation is restored to 477 with no added test lines. The existing malformed-output/disconnect matrix now also rejects timeout misclassification; the 1000 ms held-body timeout, socket closure and zero-alternate assertions remain. Format, syntax, whitespace/privacy and normal commit hooks pass. Corrected-head host semantics, types, lint, package compilation and required SDK qualification are UNRUN until the authorized native dispatch; no READY or Worker-parity claim.

### Verified cause on preceding diagnostic source

[Run 41803492242](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41803492242), exact `9cfd8b244ef077e2c192a8cc675bfd5c9530e9de`, ran the actual registered host on Node and Bun. [Host job 126485493575](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41803492242/job/126485493575) proves one matched POST, one retained timer, actual reader acquisition/read, held-body barrier and native AbortSignal.any input/result lineage on BOTH runtimes. Before cleanup, the first read rejected with TypeError caused by BodyTimeoutError / UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT. Retained and actual POST signals were both not aborted. The retained timer still had 41.429564 ms on Node and 30.229268 ms on Bun. This is the explicit body-inactivity timeout preceding the retained timer, not evidence that the private original deadline expired. That private deadline remained unobserved. Full job-log SHA256: `3dcc1e36c513a3b1b3692c729996fbe0e2e3da2b976c60c037386ef67108c778`.

Both runtimes pass 42/43 OpenRouter host cases and 23/23 Google proxy cases; only the held-body error-message assertion fails. The observation's temporary type/lint errors are completely removed in the correction. Production types pass, and package compilation succeeds for 140 plugins plus the package-boundary canary. The diagnostic [SDK artifact13311132508](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41803492242/artifacts/13311132508) is sealed: basec4fa rendered in1259874ms; actual tested merge `dfc03448916cdd4be4954043cfb7e565f80da50d` in1262693ms. Its inspected ordered parents are[c4fa,9cfd], and tree `b1ce417126516651abeba148b24946d9b10cc0e9` equals9cfd. Both actual renders and archive bytes are verified. The167-export payload is unchanged from9af. This is diagnostic-head evidence; the production correction requires its own native qualification.

Separate failures remain: catalog test 109's pre-acquisition budget (Node -575.125217 ms; cause unattributed), 137 lines of inherited baseline debt with the diagnostic's exact 677 allocation, and unchanged gateway/node-plugin/UI unused exports. No shared failure is relabeled passing or automatically exempted.

### Retained earlier SDK proof

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): transcribe qualified Groq and Mistral offers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter file transcription rejects its qualified Groq and Mistral offers, including multipart manifest routes that cannot use the OpenAI base-URL helper.

## User Impact

The existing registered audio consumer can select `groq/whisper-large-v3-turbo` and `mistral/voxtral-mini-latest` through fresh proxy-key catalog grants. The default model is unchanged. This draft requires matching deployed runtime/declarations; it does not activate either provider or claim live availability.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin selects the singular `transcription` endpoint with paired `groq.transcription` or `mistral.transcription` formats. Both routes use the existing SDK multipart builder and guarded POST. Native URLs are `/v1/native/<provider>/v1/audio/transcriptions`, with the upstream form model. Manifest URLs remain exactly `/v1/proxy/<provider>/transcription`, with the full catalog form model and no JSON envelope. Groq's server-only `/openai` prefix never enters the client URL.

Only the resolved ClawRouter credential is used. File bytes/name/MIME, caller cancellation and the original deadline are preserved through catalog, POST and bounded UTF-8 JSON EOF. Groq prompt has a4KiB local bound; unsupported Mistral prompt, arbitrary query options, mismatched MIME and AAC relabeling fail before upload. Dispatched failures do not replay through another provider; proven pre-egress denials retain the existing fallback policy. Observed serving-model/audio usage fields do not replace selected identity or imply pricing.

No SDK export, shared schema, Worker or provider-manifest change. Existing registration is reused. The local finite model binding table replaces expanding conditional selection; the new transport helper exists because manifest URLs must not have an SDK suffix appended. It reuses SDK serialization, response limits/UTF-8 validation and resource release rather than copying a Worker codec.

Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192173 at `0066d51dff16526f9a3aa46c534047aba2632918`. Runtime contract: https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/796 at `d2b184f965f8064f6db4d61cbfae102923260552`. Declaration publication and composed Worker proof retain their owners. No live/paid request or deployment.

## Evidence

- Exact source `6de028c4e960db91bdf87882989cb6756a6429c3`. Native-pinned formatter0.74.0, Node syntax for all changed TypeScript, whitespace/privacy and normal commit hooks pass.
-40 authored actual `transcribeAudioFile` cases cover both providers × both transports, scalar-before-file multipart bytes/name/MIME/model, proxy and locked-profile credentials, wrong/stale offers, query/prompt/language/AAC denials, a working alternate-provider control, no alternate after pricing/redirect/malformed/partial/oversized/invalid-UTF8/lost responses, caller abort before/catalog/body, response socket release and deadline. These tests are UNRUN; no authored fixture is reported as a pass.
- Test growth339 new lines plus7 fixture lines equals allocation346. The shared scalar is unchanged. Test duration and CI seconds remain unknown pending execution.
- Whole-change net production growth143 lines, tests346, docs24, allocation1. Simplification retains one registered consumer, one credential owner, the existing guarded multipart/JSON SDK operations and the host's post-dispatch stop behavior; no new transport framework or parser.
- Managed checkout is code-only: dependency qualification refuses the existing nested workspace link. No install, new dependency lease or SDK build was started. Focused actual-host execution, production/test types, build and required native CI remain pending. No READY/landing claim or composed parity claim.

Release-note context: ClawRouter can transcribe qualified native and manifest Groq/Mistral multipart offers with proxy-key isolation and no automatic replay after a possibly-paid upload. Release-owned changelog files remain unchanged.
