releases.body:
## 2026.11.1

### Highlights

- Safer Mac settings: failed config saves no longer overwrite secrets, and turning off Tailscale exposure keeps Gateway authentication intact. (#187734, #187664) Fixes #187600, #187597 Thanks @anmol0b.
- More reliable channel replies: Telegram, Discord, and webhook conversations keep reaching the agent after request handlers or earlier turns finish. (#179200, #179385, #179704, #189457) Fixes #178554 Thanks @steipete, @LiuwqGit, @jalehman, and @vincentkoc.
- Conversations survive more interruptions: oversized turns retain useful history, and stopping the first Claude CLI turn no longer starts the next message from scratch. (#191146, #181966, #186380) Fixes #191133, #181945 Thanks @Yun-0000, @obviyus, @mirasrael, and @holgergruenhagen.
- Update recovery gets unstuck after crashed or canceled updaters, restores the Windows Gateway after failed verification, and avoids repeated full-database copying during large-state checks. (#177932, #186787, #189647, #182632, #187921) Fixes #177684, #184893, #189620 Thanks @duyufansh2008, @RomneyDa, @fuller-stack-dev, @TheAngryPit, @sukhdeepjohar, @steipete, @syxscott, and @stephen3303.
- Subagents keep their follow-ups through model and session changes, while parent sessions receive child approvals even with a custom session store. (#186238, #183501, #189827) Fixes #179289, #189823 Thanks @steipete, @Marvinthebored, @RomneyDa, and @ekinnee.
- Android End Talk with a compatible Gateway stops listening without canceling accepted agent work, so its answer can still arrive in chat; explicit cancellation remains available. (#172276, #188798) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Provider recovery respects provider-specified rate-limit timing, and Gemini Flash text models use Interactions by default on the official API-key endpoint while custom proxies retain their existing default. (#180280, #189395) Thanks Ayaan Zaidi, @evomach, @sukhdeepjohar, @RomneyDa.

### Changes

- Claude CLI: saved subscription accounts can make configured models available without a separate native login, and operators can opt into native Agent and Workflow orchestration through `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.managedNativeTools`; the default remains off and restricted runs keep their existing tool limits. (#179203, #183765) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Anthropic: API-key setup can record an optional Anthropic workspace ID; existing workspace headers are preserved, and workspace-scoped keys need no extra setting. (#186976) Thanks Ayaan Zaidi, @evomach, @sukhdeepjohar, @RomneyDa.
- Google: Interactions requests honor managed proxy and TLS settings, rotate eligible API keys before streaming after a rate limit, preserve native video input, and forward nucleus sampling consistently; choose `google-generative-ai` when explicit Gemini cache handles are required. (#189395, #190695) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Bedrock Mantle: discovered numbered OpenAI GPT models select the Responses route automatically, while GPT-OSS keeps Chat Completions and Claude keeps Anthropic Messages. Thanks @MertBasar0, @anmol0b, @shakkernerd, @kybrcore, @sukhdeepjohar, @potoior, @RomneyDa.
- Control UI: the model picker shows the configured active context budget rather than only the model maximum, and short session links retain their intended navigation target. (#180870, #183148) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Google Chat: remote HTTP(S) attachments are delivered as visible links alongside captions; local files and native uploads remain unsupported with service-account authentication. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Update diagnostics: detailed readiness separates a ready core from channel outages, allowing repaired updaters to finish with named channel warnings without hiding HTTP 503 or weakening normal service-start checks. Thanks @duyufansh2008, @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- Network and tool safety: ClickClack and ClawHub reject redirects into unrelated private services, Discord CDN downloads no longer inherit browser private-network access, and FIFO native-hook credentials are rejected without hanging the agent. (#190944, #190939, #191458, #191423) Thanks @pgondhi987, @SebTardif, and @Leon-SK668.
- Doctor consent and access policy: noninteractive checks no longer download plugins without repair consent, and explicitly empty group allowlists remain empty instead of being repopulated. (#191523, #174787) Fixes #191420, #173826 Thanks @brandonulrich, @steipete, and @lockhartheavyindustries.
- Recovery data: malformed UTF-8 legacy imports are rejected instead of replacing original content; failed skill restore rollbacks preserve the original copy, and cleanup refuses destructive work when workspace inspection fails. (#180861, #173954, #174195, #176362) Fixes #180782, #180795 Thanks @RomneyDa, @duyufansh2008, @steipete, and @wangmiao0668000666.
- Log redaction: malformed custom entries no longer disable valid rules or built-in secret protection; invalid policy is reported while safe redaction remains active. (#173471) Thanks @skyzhao1223 and @RomneyDa.
- Secret egress: reject chains relying on the distrusted emSign ECC G3 root in the managed proxy and exported subprocess CA bundle; restart the Gateway after updating, and update clients with independent trust stores separately. (#179249) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- macOS connectivity: configured credentials take precedence over stale app environment, typed environment secret references resolve correctly, and remote Settings respects the Control UI base path. (#191468, #185141, #128175) Fixes #164596 Thanks @RomneyDa, @anmol0b, and @goldmar.
- Mac tools and messaging: iMessage remains usable after app updates without re-granting Automation, Peekaboo window inspection accepts valid snapshot references, and node exec preserves results for commands configured without a timeout. (#186107, #172116, #190729) Fixes #178719 Thanks @aniketkrs, @RomneyDa, @anmol0b, @SharkeyDev, @holgergruenhagen, @LiuwqGit, and @etzelm.
- Mac voice and embedded pages: avoid duplicate voice sends and false sent feedback, and show a recoverable load error instead of a blank or stale Mac tab. (#186271, #185432) Thanks @anmol0b, @etzelm, and @RomneyDa.
- Native voice and capture: iOS and macOS Talk tolerate slow audio acknowledgments within bounded buffering, long meeting replies are not cut off merely because generation outruns playback, and oversized Mac recordings fail with size guidance instead of dropping the node connection. Thanks @MertBasar0, @anmol0b, @shakkernerd, @kybrcore, @sukhdeepjohar, @potoior, and @RomneyDa.
- Android and desktop compatibility: Android Chat waits for the role-allowed agent list after switching Gateways, and independently updated Mac nodes can return optional cursor coordinates without a computer-use contract error. Thanks @MertBasar0, @anmol0b, @shakkernerd, @kybrcore, @sukhdeepjohar, @potoior, @RomneyDa.
- Channel recovery: Slack detects dead relay connections without treating ordinary silence as failure, Tlon reconnects stalled streams so unacknowledged events can replay, and managed Tailscale exposure recovers after a daemon restart while local authenticated access stays available. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Channel delivery: Feishu keeps text from before and after tool calls in the same streaming card; Synology confirms delivery only from recipient-matched message IDs; Twitch targets and Zalo unsupported-event text follow their channel handling rather than silently losing usable content. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Channel credentials and notices: implicit Slack default accounts retain complete top-level credentials alongside named accounts, channel secret consumers respect account activation, and Nostr reports failed pairing notifications without undoing approval. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- iMessage storage: recovery cursor keys no longer contain a PostgreSQL-incompatible NUL separator, allowing the channel to start with PostgreSQL-backed state. (#184919) Fixes #184862 Thanks @duyufansh2008, @RomneyDa, and @etzelm.
- Session and agent authority: deleting one agent no longer breaks other agents' tool authority, and local session-capability changes stop inappropriate provider fallback instead of trying every model. (#174918, #179312) Fixes #179290 Thanks @steipete, @chelsealong, @obviyus, and @Marvinthebored.
- Prompt caching: session tool definitions stay stable across turns, including completions, heartbeats, and non-owner requests, avoiding unnecessary prompt-cache misses. (#175309, #176167) Thanks @obviyus.
- Conversation recovery: compaction retains the active human request across repeated summaries; queue overflow summaries retain each visible sender and conversation context; exec completion guidance survives overflow. (#180214, #187833, #190698, #182188, #184216) Thanks @RomneyDa and @aniketkrs.
- Codex continuity: conversation-wide restrictions retain compatible native threads, temporary restrictions preserve the ordinary conversation binding, and a missing thread with recorded history reports an error instead of silently starting over. Thanks @skyzhao1223 and @RomneyDa.
- Codex replies: transient retries can summarize the original request and completed tools without rerunning them; terminal handoffs allow already-submitted steering a bounded chance to confirm consumption and do not automatically replay uncertain input. (#183077, #184062, #181839, #167390) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Shared credentials and model availability: concurrent MCP callers can reuse a fresh OAuth token without unnecessary exclusive locking, rate-limit cooldowns follow provider timing instead of accumulating hours of local backoff, and fresh model publications replace superseded refresh results. (#179997, #180280, #179144) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Claude CLI and scheduled work: canceled cron runs stop reply hooks, interrupted long-running jobs no longer prevent scheduler startup, oversized or invalid CLI streams cancel their subprocess promptly, and managed completions retain the policy-filtered tool catalog. (#181245, #191422, #159931, #172026) Thanks @steipete and @fuller-stack-dev.
- Session history and memory: long transcript decoding releases database read snapshots promptly, bounded history pages keep their requested anchors and adjacent messages, and memory indexing waits for archived transcript materialization. (#164442, #172970, #177937, #182091, #190182, #189284, #188450, #188483, #190690) Fixes #171467 Thanks @RomneyDa, and @etzelm.
- Subagent and restart recovery: live descendants keep their expired parents available for communication, accepted yields settle sibling tool results before handoff, and stale interrupted input no longer blocks a new human message indefinitely. (#179057, #184021, #180853, #181871, #178888, #184041, #184069, #172959) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Agent handoffs: waiting session sends recover the stored long reply instead of returning only a short lifecycle preview, and ACP-created sessions retain the requested working directory for later prompts. (#178271, #176852) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Control UI recovery: silently dead Gateway connections reconnect without replaying uncertain sends, consumed slash-steering messages leave the queue, and routine restart notices stay concise. (#179101, #178642, #180024, #172843) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- GitHub workflows: active sessions can open the reconnect flow, failed follow-up pushes retain the existing PR, and readers no longer hang while discarding response bodies. (#180200, #187835, #191721) Fixes #187832 Thanks @RomneyDa, @anmol0b, @obviyus, and @nocodet888-arch.
- Plugin lifecycle: startup avoids recopying managed binaries, repairs owned stale host links after installation-root changes, and keeps plugin background readers alive for admitted callbacks and cleanup; internal plugin reload resumes stay in the current session rather than using an old external recipient. (#187865, #181140, #182207, #179031, #181270, #179549, #190982) Thanks @Satoshi-Kusumoto, @RomneyDa, @jasonftl, and @obviyus.
- Gateway startup and shutdown: retry transient database locks during stale-claim cleanup and sidecar startup, and exit after clean shutdown instead of waiting for systemd to kill a process with a leaked handle. (#187724, #186920, #191251) Fixes #187723, #186875, #191119 Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, @steipete, @yousan, @bianyuxia-commits, and @davesanvil.
- Update startup and migration: recover with retained worker indexes, avoid crashes in automatic migration recovery from 2026.10.7–2026.10.9, preserve recovery errors, and reject Git targets that require an unavailable newer Node before staging. (#189023, #189713, #191495, #181715) Thanks @RomneyDa and @steipete.
- Update repair: release abandoned cancellation custody and resolve pending package steps without repair loops; restore a suspended Windows Gateway task after failed verification while retaining the original failure details. (#177932, #186787, #189647) Fixes #177684, #184893, #189620 Thanks @RomneyDa, @fuller-stack-dev, @TheAngryPit, @sukhdeepjohar, @steipete, @syxscott, and @stephen3303.
- Update captures and service handoff: ignore Finder metadata when listing recovery captures, recover CLI Node runtimes when launched from `/`, and classify an unavailable automatic-update service handoff as skipped rather than an unrecorded failure. (#186663, #178112, #188405) Fixes #186650, #177739, #188302 Thanks @duyufansh2008, @RomneyDa, @steipete, @woshicby, @downingkeys, and @ARSA31.
- Doctor migrations: bound long Matrix archive filenames, preserve config promotion when only migration guidance changes, run explicitly requested headless repairs, return failure rather than success when required work was skipped, and retain invalid heartbeat quiet hours with actionable validation. (#187443, #190665, #187192, #186305) Fixes #187390, #190658, #187122 Thanks @RomneyDa, @skyzhao1223, @steipete, @dakoller, @saariuslystoned, and @JordanNewell.
- Configuration and store recovery: explain how to recover when an older binary meets newer config; relative session stores resolve against the active state directory, and Doctor merges legacy misplaced stores with backups while preserving conflicting conversations and refusing unsafe retirement. (#187639, #182444, #181554, #180414, #179089) Fixes #152791 Thanks @RomneyDa, @duyufansh2008, @steipete, and @kip-claw.
- Service and backup reliability: repaired updaters distinguish durable database changes from read-only WAL bookkeeping, wait for the serving Mac child to release state, preserve valid replacement config without metadata, and keep unrelated service overrides intact during supported Node repairs. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Diagnostics and provider tools: timeout messages distinguish an unknown tool outcome from a safe retry, Anthropic PDF requests use the selected account's proper authentication, and Gemini/Vertex streams stop at terminal markers instead of consuming later frames. (#180247, #182429, #184434, #178420, #117397) Thanks Ayaan Zaidi, @evomach, @sukhdeepjohar, @RomneyDa, @MertBasar0, @anmol0b, @shakkernerd, @kybrcore, @potoior.

prs.title: refactor(webui): improve task navigation and isolate workflow ownership
prs.body:
## Why

Small edits should start at the behavior's owner and its existing tests, rather than require a tour of the repository or a large shared component. Add a progressive task index and isolate two concrete WebUI workflows without imposing a file-length limit or rewriting the application.

Resolves NAN-413

## What changed

- Link the root agent instructions to task-to-source/test navigation, with a more focused WebUI change map and a state-ownership guideline.
- Move channel pairing requests, subscriptions, polling, snooze and approval into `ChannelPairing`, with the existing popup/input in `PairingCodePopup`. `App` only mounts the feature.
- Move waiting-prompt storage, shared delivery ownership and turn-completion policy behind `useQueuedPrompt`. Keep draft input and UI feedback in `ThreadComposer`, preserving its application-level regression coverage.

## Scope

One independent change based on `main`. No AgentLoop/TUI rewrite, dependency change, API/wire change, storage migration, security-policy change, or intentional UI/copy change.

## Tradeoffs

The new boundaries own state and lifecycle, rather than just moving helpers. Existing broad App and Composer integration suites remain in place; this does not introduce a new test harness or claim measured development-time savings.

| Typical change | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pairing refresh, approval retry, or snooze | State, effects, actions and popup spread through `App.tsx` | `ChannelPairing.tsx` owns the lifecycle; open `PairingCodePopup.tsx` only for input/display changes |
| Waiting-message persistence or completion gating | Store, authorization, turn effects and send logic mixed into `ThreadComposer.tsx` | `useQueuedPrompt.ts` owns queue state and execution; Composer supplies draft content and UI feedback |

The task maps link these owners directly to their retained regression and integration tests. This reduces the unrelated code needed for these tasks, not the repository's total line count.

## Blast Radius

WebUI channel pairing and waiting-prompt execution. The important retained contracts are visibility-aware notification/poll refresh, late approval replies and retry, same-page queue ownership, exact-turn completion, session switching, and draft/attachment retention after rejected sends.

## Verification

- Local source/diff review and `git diff --check`: passed. Checked 125 local Markdown link targets and their heading fragments; none missing. Runtime validation is delegated to remote CI.
- Pairing popup/helper text matches the baseline apart from its export/import boundary. Original App integration assertions and the desktop/mobile `pairing-refresh.spec.ts` browser scenarios remain; a focused snooze-expiry case is added.
- Queue persistence/delivery helpers and store remain text-identical apart from exports and the internal key argument type. Existing `queued-guidance`, `thread-composer`, `thread-shell`, `turn-completion` and queued-guidance browser test files are unchanged.
- Full remote lint, typecheck, tests, browser tests and production build: pending the PR's CI run. No local lint/typecheck/tests/build/browser checks were run.

prs.title: fix(webui): stabilize context usage and session switching
prs.body:
## Why

The live context meter becomes empty (`—`) whenever a new model request advances the graph before reporting usage. Switching sessions also closes the graph, disrupting the single-pane layout. Simply keeping it open leaves the panel tied to a session-keyed composer and its detached alignment target.

## What changed

- Select live usage independently from the displayed graph, keeping the latest known measurement until a new one arrives. Replay stays frame-local, and compaction starts a new measurement baseline.
- Move sidebar ownership out of the keyed composer into the stable pane layout. The composer receives only its usage control; session changes reset graph, replay, and selection without replacing the open sidebar.
- Keep an already-open graph on single-pane session switches and show the target session's context. Loading or unmeasured sessions remain empty/unknown rather than showing the previous session's data. Closed panels stay closed.
- Use the workbench's actual visible pane count: multiple visible panes do not automatically carry the graph into another session. Manual opening remains available.
- Rebind sidebar alignment to the current composer surface when the session-keyed input changes. The viewport reports grid-row movement as well as size changes, so empty/history transitions cannot leave a stale bottom inset.
- Extend existing unit coverage and the history-hydration browser fixture for session switching, deferred history, sidebar identity, geometry, replay reset, and single/multiple visible panes. Update existing composer callers to the new control slot.

## Scope

Frontend presentation and ownership only; no provider accounting, event protocol, persistence, graph physics, or animation timing changes.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` and `bun run build` passed for the current source. The local build was requested to provide an isolated manual-test instance; full automated checks remain on remote CI.
- A real-provider smoke request successfully read two synthetic workspace files and returned their titles through the built WebUI.
- In the real gateway preview, empty/existing-session switches retain the sidebar. A controlled comparison with and without layout animation exposed a position-only alignment gap in the intermediate revision (161.5px); the final implementation aligns the sidebar and current composer bottoms in all four checked cases (0px difference).
- The latest published head awaits remote CI results. The intermediate revision passed WebUI checks/build and Docker; its browser job had not completed at the last bounded status check.
- The [earlier revision's CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42154675129) passed WebUI checks/build and Docker, but the browser job had 415 passes and one failure: the mobile placeholder tooltip remained visible after Escape (`composer-action.spec.ts:189`). That failure has not been reproduced or repaired in this PR; no assertion, retry, or timeout was weakened.

Contributes to NAN-407

prs.title: feat(heartbeat): add heartbeat-specific model override
prs.body:
## Problem

The heartbeat cron job runs on the main agent model for both the execution turn and the post-run notification evaluation. Heartbeat can run frequently (default every 30 minutes) and usually only makes a lightweight decision, so deployments using a premium or auto-routed model pay that cost for routine background checks. `agents.defaults.dream.modelOverride` already lets Dream run on a different model, but heartbeat has no equivalent setting.

## Solution

Add an optional `gateway.heartbeat.modelOverride`. For each heartbeat run, resolve an immutable runtime via `runtime_resolver.resolve_override(model=..., config=...)` (which also resolves the correct provider for the requested model); when the override is unset, snapshot the current default via `runtime_resolver.current()`. The same resolved provider/model is used for both the heartbeat turn and the notification evaluation. The main agent model and provider are never mutated, and unsetting the field keeps today's behaviour exactly.

## Changes

- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — add `model_override` to `HeartbeatConfig` with `modelOverride` / `model` aliases.
- `nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py` — resolve the heartbeat runtime and pass it to `process_direct`; use its provider/model for `evaluate_response`; startup output shows the effective heartbeat model.
- `docs/configuration.md` — document the new option with an example.
- Tests: config alias/serialization cases and a runtime case (default + override) asserting both the execution and evaluation use the resolved model while the main agent model is unchanged.

## Testing

**Environment**
- Runtime: Python 3.13.16
- OS: Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
- Arch: AMD64

**Test Commands & Results**
1. `pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py tests/config/test_gateway_config.py -k heartbeat`
   -> 20 passed, 150 deselected
2. `pytest tests/config tests/cli tests/agent`
   -> 2781 passed, 30 skipped, 0 failed (baseline: 2776 passed, 30 skipped, 1 flaky timing failure; the 4 added tests account for the count difference)
3. `ruff check nanobot tests`
   -> all checks passed
4. `basedpyright nanobot/config/schema.py nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py`
   -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

**Pre-existing Failures**
- `tests/agent/test_runner_injections.py::test_websocket_followup_is_admitted_before_recovery_queue` raised an asyncio `TimeoutError` once during the baseline full run. It passes in isolation and passed in the post-change full run; it has no file intersection with this PR and is a pre-existing flaky timing test.

## Notes for Reviewer

- The earlier attempt #4549 was withdrawn without the feature landing; this re-implements the same requested behaviour against the current code, using the side-effect-free `runtime_resolver.current()` for the default case.
- Kept this PR to a model override only (no separate provider override) to match the issue scope.

Closes #4431

prs.title: fix(api): release idle session locks
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #4883.

Completed API requests with distinct `session_id` values leave their locks in the application's registry indefinitely. Store these locks in a `WeakValueDictionary` so idle entries can be collected, while request handlers and streaming tasks keep strong references to locks that are held or awaited.

The production change updates the registry's typed `AppKey`, local annotation, and initialization. The refreshed branch incorporates main `8b37976d36c2812c62b464321e729a88872b60f9` and preserves its routing and cleanup changes in the runner tests.

## Tests

- Exercise completed requests with 20 distinct session IDs through the real HTTP endpoint in both streaming and non-streaming modes, then verify that no idle locks remain.
- Cover default and custom sessions in both modes, including garbage collection while one request holds the lock and another waits. Request arrival is synchronized with an event, and the requests must still execute serially.
- Allow runner shutdown tests to finish durable cleanup, and verify that verbose Docker smoke status output does not trigger the `grep -q` / `pipefail` failure.

## Validation

Current revision, macOS arm64, Python 3.11.15:

- **163 passed** across API endpoints, API session/stream/attachment handling, API runtime integration, AgentLoop lock lifecycle, runner injections, and Docker smoke-script contract tests. No cases skipped in this focused run.
- Repository Ruff checks, Python import boundaries, dependency consistency, and strict BasedPyright pass: **0 type errors, 0 type warnings**. Dependencies include all extras and channel manifests, matching the documented CI setup.
- `bash -n tests/test_docker.sh` and whitespace checks pass.
- A test-only strong-registry control makes both HTTP cleanup regressions fail with **20 retained idle locks**. The production sources are unchanged by this probe; the normal weak-registry tests pass for both response modes.

HTTP tests use a mocked agent. The Docker script tests use a fake Docker boundary; an image build, the complete repository suite, and Windows/Linux execution were not run locally for this refreshed revision. Fresh CI remains to be evaluated on the updated head.

## Related work

PR #4890 uses the same weak-reference approach. This proposal preserves typed application keys and adds streaming cleanup/serialization coverage.

Legacy installations can reuse one configuration directory with multiple global workspaces. On upgrade, a workspace's shared WebUI transcript could be imported into another workspace because its canonical sessions were still JSONL and the ownership scan only recognized SQLite. Only the legacy import path changes. No automatic repair of already misassigned data, proxy changes, or changes to the 0.4.x compatibility window / 0.5.0 removal TODO.

prs.title: test: separate preparation responsiveness from persistence timing
prs.body:
## Summary

Two Windows checks failed while waiting for several persistence and preparation steps under one five-second deadline. These test changes separate round progress and preparation responsiveness from unrelated command-history writes.

The failed Windows stack shows `/status` waiting in `SessionState.prepare_input` after command dispatch. Its cancellation then drains the accepted write. The response deadline therefore also measures disk persistence, not only whether prompt preparation leaves the event loop responsive.

- Reuse the existing per-model-request progress check in the child-thread test. Each round keeps its five-second deadline. A completed or stalled subagent fails the check. The real tool call, stored history, access checks, and restart assertions remain in place.
- Run the concurrent `/status` probe with the existing non-persistent session policy. Keep its five-second deadline and all heartbeat, cancellation, snapshot, context, and preparation-slot assertions. Other command tests still exercise persistent commands.

Only tests change. This does not change runtime behavior, model requests, cache prefixes, stored user data, update behavior, or public interfaces. No breaking change is intended.

## Verification

- The two original tests fail when each model response takes 2.8 seconds and command-history writes take 5.5 seconds. The changed tests pass the same controlled-delay probe.
- A stalled model still fails the five-second progress check. Moving preparation back onto the event loop still fails the preparation test.
- 135 related local tests and lint pass. Both modified modules also pass all 35 cases with the controlled-delay probe and two workers.
- [PR CI on `e624e7f56`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42149489609) passed on the first attempt: Linux Python 3.11/3.14, native Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, and the aggregate check. The Windows full suite passed 11,117 tests; its separate CLI checks passed 248 tests.

The controlled probes demonstrate the test timing assumptions; they do not establish the exact runner-level cause of the original Windows slowdown. This PR does not publish a release.

prs.title: test(ci): remove Docker output and stdin timing races
prs.body:
## Summary

- Match Docker status markers directly in Bash. This removes the `echo | grep -q` pipe, where an early reader exit can make valid output fail under `pipefail`.
- Wait for the Python child to report readiness before testing stdin. Wait for process completion separately from the write or close acknowledgement, and always clean up the session manager.
- Keep all output, EOF, exit-code, Docker failure propagation, and resource cleanup checks. No runtime or workflow code changes.

## Evidence

The first attempt of [main CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42064479711/attempts/1) reported a missing Docker title that was present in the captured output, plus two Windows stdin test failures before child startup or completion. The unchanged second attempt passed.

The new large-output Docker regression fails before the script change and passes after it. A shell probe reports producer exit 141 with grep exit 0, consistent with the [GNU grep pipefail warning](https://www.gnu.org/software/grep/manual/html_node/Usage.html). The test also verifies that a successful status command with a missing marker still fails and cleans up its resources.

A local-only probe adds 5.5 seconds of Python child startup delay. Both old stdin tests fail; both updated tests pass. The test process budget is 30 seconds, with bounded 10-second readiness and completion waits. This does not change application runtime limits or remove timeout coverage.

## Validation

- 64 focused Docker smoke, exec-session, timeout, and shell-output tests passed locally.
- Both delayed-start stdin probes passed.
- Ruff, Bash syntax, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42139767341) passed on `72e01a6bb13c08b75db1d001e81fa6b425d97f6d`: Linux Python 3.11 and 3.14, Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, and real Docker integration. The Windows full suite passed 11,117 tests; Linux 3.14 passed 11,465. Local Docker is not running.

No breaking change. Installed code, saved data, model requests, prompt caching, and update compatibility are unchanged.

- Document the existing 0.4.0 bridge for unimported JSONL history and per-feature proxy settings. This PR does not remove migration code. Clarify context-graph closure on topic changes and large-graph limits.
- Fix Escape dismissal of the full-placeholder hint in the focused composer. Keep draft, composition and send behavior. Remove the duplicate portal-owned dismissal callback.
- Bound the real-gateway smoke test by observable model-round progress, rather than one deadline for all 16 durable rounds. Keep the original stop, completion and shutdown deadlines and all behavioral assertions. Use cancellable async HTTP for its synthetic checkpoint signal and keep its server loop live during child shutdown.
- Retain small, allowlisted native-probe failure locations without exception values, private journals or credentials. Diagnostic observation changes only instrumented test baselines, not the installed product or its refusal decision.
- Reduce Windows installer and isolated-update startup contention to two workers. Keep the full test sets and their original 90s command / 60s setup bounds. Only the installer job's aggregate budget increases to 40 minutes.

## Current verification

- All 15 current-head PR checks passed: [source CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42078811932). Its tested merge `e9191bcd37b6bdbbd59cfedf1574e6135044e380` has current main and this head as parents and the same tree as the candidate.

Each platform completed nine upgrade/recovery scenarios and 15 journeys. Independent report checks verified source, manifest, wheel hashes, protected-data flags, subsequent updates and cleanup. Windows ran with `LongPathsEnabled=0`. These automated baselines are instrumented version fixtures, not original historical packages.
- A separate macOS arm64 matrix used the original published 0.4.0 wheel and this exact candidate: all nine scenarios and 15 journeys, Dock lifecycle, service recovery and subsequent update passed. Configuration, canonical/display history and pending deliveries were preserved.
- The real 0.4.0 JSONL import bridge, followed by this installed 0.4.1 candidate, preserved public history reads, configuration and original/import-backup file hashes.
- Docker acceptance used the original 0.4.0 source and a same-volume image replacement. Config, SQLite canonical/display history, outbox, authenticated reads, further writes and a second start passed. This is not in-place Docker updating or automatic container rollback.
- Exact installed-package WebUI interaction passed with an isolated real Gateway and synthetic local model: file-context graph, keyboard and canvas-node preview, narrow-screen hint dismissal, topic-change closure and unsent-draft retention. Temporary services exited cleanly. This is not a large-graph performance claim.
- The retained source.git passed full fsck and an independent no-local clone. The repository's complete verifier ran from that source. All five platform wheels plus sdist passed content, RECORD, platform tag, version/build-commit and `twine check --strict` checks. This six-file set totals 249,257,994 bytes; wheel sizes increased 1.22%–1.91% from 0.4.0. The verified files and source are retained independently of CI artifact expiry.
- Current Linux main suite: 11,546 cases, zero errors/failures, 80 skips. Current Windows main: 11,278 cases, zero errors/failures, 158 skips; isolated updates: 86 cases, zero errors/failures, five skips; installers: 81 cases, zero errors/failures, one Unix-only skip. Assertions and per-command deadlines remain enabled.
- Focused before/after checks reproduced the original slow-model deadline and Escape-hint race. The unchanged Escape browser case passed 24 consecutive runs after the fix; all 11 composer browser cases, 241 related component tests, TypeScript and ESLint passed. After integrating #6571, its public-route, source-status, frontend and browser checks passed. Those catalog fixtures are not live third-party installation proof.

## Remaining risks and release gates

Earlier Windows native source-CI runs refused an update before installation (`handoff_failed`, `mutation_started=false`). Later source and exact-candidate matrices passed, but the original refusal's cause is not established. Diagnostic additions are not a claimed product recovery fix. Keep this historical stability risk visible for maintainer review.

The local blocking-wait reproduction explained one test-controller starvation path, not every Linux CI shutdown failure: d154 still failed. The final synthetic checkpoint uses async HTTP and the current complete matrix passes. No failing production-Gateway stack or general reliability guarantee is claimed.

Breaking-change verdict: the preparation's version/test/CI/diagnostic changes do not alter application behavior; the composer change is a non-breaking UI correction. The release includes the already-merged removal of JSONL/proxy importers in #6518. Earlier installations must first run the documented 0.4.0 bridge. Maintainers must confirm this tightened migration prerequisite before publication.

This PR stays draft pending independent review and the release decision. Final merged-source identity must match the approved candidate; a changed commit/build identity requires a new candidate and an updated upload handoff. prs.title: feat(webui): inspect file context in a live graph sidebar
prs.body:
The context control opens a persistent file graph beside the conversation. Users can see files used since the latest compaction, open them in the shared preview sidebar, and replay the graph's growth without interrupting chat.

## Behavior

- Show supplied prompt files, explicit skills, successful text-file reads, and discovered local Markdown references. A loaded node records use during this phase; it does not claim that all of the original text remains in the current model request. File-size indicators estimate the content actually read.
- Start a new replay phase after successful compaction. The next actual request supplies the new graph; existing historical snapshots remain readable. Missing historical snapshots are not recreated from today's files.
- Support node dragging, zoom, click-to-open details, transient labels for newly loaded files, adaptive replay, and smooth whole-panel expansion. Share sidebar surfaces and transitions with file previews, keeping the composer usable in split panes and on narrow screens.
- Move preview/source controls into the file header and simplify related navigation and session panels.

## Ownership and compatibility

- A WebUI observer consumes the ordered tool progress stream. It parses successful `read_file` results in a worker, stores compact read facts in display history, and restores observations across turns and restarts. It never rereads source files or linked targets; parsing failures preserve tool results.
- Prompt builders record raw file-use facts in a turn-local capture scope. A composed observer publishes those facts at the prepared-request boundary, before request lifecycle events. Parsing and token estimation run in the delivery worker, outside model execution. Parallel turns and cancellation keep capture scopes isolated.
- The runner exposes a generic `before_model_request` hook and reports individual request usage separately from accumulated usage. It does not read graph metadata. `loop.py`, context governance, runtime context blocks, file-read tools, session message persistence, and memory consolidation have no changes against the PR base.
- Skill loading shares its existing discovery snapshot and records the resolved source, including aliases. Rebuilding prompt files does not multiply their token estimates. Tool working directories belong to individual progress records, rather than the surrounding batch.
- Successful compaction starts a new phase; failed compaction preserves observations. Shell-command file-read inference is out of scope.
- Optional graph wire fields and compressed, self-contained history records remain supported. Compact history responses retain the `webui.context-graph.references.v1` capability; ordinary inline responses remain supported. No database migration or history rewrite is required.
- Canvas rendering retains keyboard/touch access, reduced-motion support, and suspension while hidden.

## Validation

Current head `355c3b720`: [all CI checks passed](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/41994720141), including `CI required`, WebUI checks/build, 3,551 WebUI unit tests, 408 browser tests, Python 3.11/3.14/Windows, Windows installer/process compatibility, both native-package acceptance jobs, Terminal UI and Docker.

CI follow-up fixes: await the lazy graph scene before replay timing assertions; update browser request expectations for graph encoding and the single preview toggle; verify wide tables remain scrollable; match the narrow-screen preview skeleton button to the real 44px control, eliminating a 12px loading shift. Local verification additionally passed all 63 affected browser cases, browser TypeScript and touched-file lint.

The first Windows Python run hit an unchanged shell test's one-second output wait before its first startup output. Both local Windows wait/timeout tests passed, and the failed CI job passed on one rerun without code or timeout changes. Other successful checks were retained; the final required aggregate is green. This CI result does not remove the mobile graph performance limitations documented below.

## Production performance retest — 2026-11-05

One round per scenario, as requested. Main: `e6127aa32`; PR performance implementation: `8a2a58c7f`. Cache thrashing and large Python-preview overhead improved substantially. Large mobile graphs and continuous graph growth remain slow; this is not a blanket performance sign-off.

### Shared paths (main → PR)

| Scenario | Main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Desktop input to next RAF, P95 | 15.1 ms | 15.4 ms |
| Desktop input during streaming, P95 | 15.0 ms | 13.1 ms |
| Mobile input to next RAF, P95 | 18.7 ms | 21.4 ms |
| Mobile input during streaming, P95 | 22.8 ms | 20.6 ms |
| Mobile streaming frame interval, P95 | 116.7 ms | 116.7 ms |
| Mobile scrolling frame interval, P95 | 33.2 ms | 33.3 ms |
| Desktop large Python preview, main-thread task total | 131 ms | 121 ms |
| Mobile large Python preview, main-thread task total | 480 ms | 514 ms |
| Mobile large Markdown preview, main-thread task total | 711 ms | 642 ms |

Preview numbers use the corrected mobile overlay fixture. Python highlighting limits now match main (100,000 characters / 2,000 lines); both show this 120 KB / 4,200-line file as full plain text. Mobile Python-preview longest tasks were 214/229 ms, so main itself is not free of preview jank. The former PR result was roughly 1,512 ms total with highlighting enabled; that historical comparison spans the newer main typography change as well.

### PR-only graph and analysis

Main has no graph: these are absolute PR costs, with older PR diagnostics used only as historical references.

- Mobile graph cessation: 100 nodes 2.53 s, 500 nodes 14.51 s (historical PR: 12.14 / 27.18 s). Both settle without timing out, and restore the full DPR-3 canvas afterward. This is time from opening until the final draw, not time until first interaction.
- Mobile opening frame-interval P95: 33.4 ms at 100 nodes; 116.7 ms at 500 nodes. The 500-node opening sample still contains 40 long tasks, up to 228 ms.
- Twelve-snapshot replay: 2.64 s, frame-interval P95 50 ms. Continuous growth every 200 ms remains poor: frame-interval P95 200 ms. These remain performance limitations.
- Repeated analysis of twenty approximately 8 KB prompt files: median 13.10 ms, P95 13.66 ms (historical PR median 158.54 ms). Six files: median 5.10 ms. First-use/warm-up tails remain; caching does not make initial parsing free.
- New-content 120 KB Markdown analysis still costs median 51.49 ms in the ordered delivery worker. Repeated content: median 1.66 ms. Non-file observation: about 0.4 microseconds. Closing the UI does not disable backend observation.

### Resources and lifecycle

- Full production entry JS/CSS gzip: 275,943 → 279,220 bytes (+3.2 KiB).
- Entry plus chat static JS/CSS closure: 449,060 → 480,053 bytes (+30.3 KiB). The historical increment was about 41.1 KiB. Graph layout and scene loading are deferred, but other feature code remains eager. Font assets are not included in these JS/CSS totals.
- Read 120 KB: median 3.65 → 3.53 ms; ordinary history write 1.07 → 1.10 ms; history read 1.04 → 1.02 ms.
- Three warm-up opens followed by twelve open/close cycles: stable DOM/listener counts; desktop heap 13.42 → 13.94 MiB, mobile 14.09 → 14.70 MiB, flattening toward the end. Closed-panel draws: zero. No page errors. This does not establish a long-term no-leak guarantee.

### Method and evidence

Windows / i5-13400 / headless Chromium / production builds. Desktop 1440×900 DPR 1; mobile emulation 393×852 DPR 3 with 4× CPU slowdown. Real ThreadViewport, ThreadComposer and preview components, 300 messages, stream updates every 50 ms. No model requests, full authenticated-app latency, real-phone measurement, Lighthouse score or official INP claim. Samples run serially; single-run differences can be noise. No traces were captured during this timing pass.

The primary round has 34 samples. A 14-sample targeted follow-up replaced preview samples with the correct overlay fixture and checked chat input/stream/scroll after adding the message shadow; mobile PR input P95 was 17.4 ms and streaming input 21.1 ms. The final user-requested change restores only the original background utility; that last color correction was visually checked and unit-tested, not performance-rerun. Bundle measurements include the shadow change before that final color-only correction.

Raw results and scripts: `C:/Users/HR/AppData/Local/nanobot-context-graph/perf-retest-20261105`: `frontend.json`, `frontend-followup.json`, `backend-main.json`, `backend-pr.json`, `backend-extra.json`, `settlement.json`, `memory.json`, `bundles.json`. Older comparison values come from the previously recorded report and summaries, not a fresh before-optimization control on the new base.

Tracks [NAN-407](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-407).

### Mobile CPU-only control

Same production fixture/artifact, 393×852 viewport, DPR 3 and touch input; only CPU throttle changed. One run at 1× and one at 4×, serially, with no source changes.

| Metric | CPU 1× | CPU 4× |
|---|---:|---:|
| Opening 100 nodes, frame interval P95 | 16.8 ms | 49.9 ms |
| Opening 500 nodes, frame interval P95 | 33.3 ms | 199.9 ms |
| Replay, frame interval P95 | 16.8 ms | 50.0 ms |
| Continuous growth, frame interval P95 | 33.3 ms | 216.7 ms |
| 100 nodes, last draw after opening | 1.68 s | 2.71 s |
| 500 nodes, last draw after opening | 1.80 s | 19.67 s |

At 1×, the 500-node opening and continuous-growth samples have no tasks over 50 ms, but their P95 frame intervals still indicate dropped frames. The 100-node opening contains one 54 ms task. Both configurations stop drawing once settled and restore the full DPR-3 canvas. Severe sustained jank was observed at 4×; it is inaccurate to claim there is no jank at 1×. This remains desktop mobile emulation, not evidence about real-phone hardware. The 4× result varies from the earlier 14.5 s measurement, illustrating single-run variability.

Artifacts in the same evidence directory: `cpu-control.json`, `cpu-settlement.json` and matching scripts/logs. No production code was changed for this comparison.

prs.title: refactor(commands): own trusted Shell completion outside agent loop
prs.body:
## User and maintenance scenario

A model's shell tool should return a bounded observation and keep the same long-running command available for later checks. A trusted user `!command` should instead wait for its full literal result. Those existing behaviors remain; changing how trusted commands wait or construct their replies should not require the model execution loop to know the concrete Shell implementation.

Resolves NAN-330

## Change

- Make the existing command route directly own trusted user Shell execution, scope setup and full-result handling in `command/user_shell.py`.
- Remove the Loop's Shell-specific callback and concrete ExecTool dependency. This is not a new generic tool/plugin capability or a duplicate execution service: both paths still use the configured Shell tool and existing process/session owner.
- Keep trusted-source checks, workspace/access policy, temporary/log-content scope, turn scopes, literal rendering, model bounded observations and existing timeout/cleanup rules.

The narrow internal `AgentLoop.execute_user_shell_command` method is removed; use the existing command route. No new public SDK/API behavior is promised. This is a concrete maintenance boundary, not a faster shell command, memory optimization or claim that every client/Loop coupling is gone.

## Verification

- **199 Python tests passed**: commands, exec session isolation/tools and task cancellation; real model-observation yield vs user full-result coverage, scope unwinding, existing restricted paths and literal output.
- Touched strict Python types, Ruff, import boundaries and diff checks passed.
- Actual isolated authenticated Gateway + WebSocket user Shell + HTTP saved history: full stdout/stderr/exit status, Markdown preserved literally, restricted traversal rejected. No model request, real credentials, production sessions or daily services. Owned Gateway exited cleanly.

Limits: real process probe on Linux; cross-platform execution is covered only by the selected CI matrix. No merge, deployment or formal review.


## Verified delivery

Head `148289350f6bd1faa693d3c54763960c4fd0e89f`. Final exact-head required gate and every selected check succeeded, including Windows. Out-of-scope WebUI/native/installer jobs were skipped, not run. The initial Windows failure was an unchanged prompt-responsiveness timeout; one bounded rerun passed without modifying the test or relaxing a gate. Its original cause remains unconfirmed.

Ready transition was executed and REST readback confirms OPEN, non-Draft, the same exact head, base main and mergeable. Linear is In Review, not Done; Ready is not approval or merge.

issues.title: [Feature]: ACP tool_call starts should carry rawInput for built-in tools, not only terminal
issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

We run Hermes as an ACP agent from a client that classifies each tool call, for example to flag a write outside the workspace or under `~/.ssh`. For built-in tools the `tool_call` update carries no `rawInput`, so the client only has the display `title` and `content` to work from.

Observed on 0b10b9f (v0.22.2) in the `session/update` stream:

| Tool | `title` | `rawInput` | What the client is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `write_file` | `write_file: /…/outside/dddd…` | absent | The title is truncated; the full path is only in `locations` |
| `patch` (V4A) | `patch` | absent | `locations` is empty, so there is no target path before the call runs |
| `terminal` | `terminal: echo hi` | absent | The actual command, `echo hi > term.txt`, appears only in the display text in `content` |
| `read_file` | `read_file: existing.txt` | absent | |

In `acp_adapter/tools.py`, `_build_tool_start` sets `raw_input` only for an unknown tool with arguments. Every tool with a start-content builder, or in `_POLISHED_TOOLS`, gets `raw_input=None`.

#90553 asks for this for `terminal`. This issue asks for it across the built-in tools.

### Proposed Solution

- In `_build_tool_start`, pass the tool arguments as `raw_input` for every tool. The ACP spec defines `rawInput` as the raw input parameters sent to the tool. If payload size is the concern, large free-text fields such as `write_file`'s `content` could be left out, as long as the identifying arguments (`path`, `command`) stay.
- For V4A `patch`, fill `locations` from the files named in the patch.
- Optionally, carry the Hermes tool name in a structured field such as `_meta`, since `title` is display text.

### Alternatives Considered

Parsing `title` and `content`. They are display strings: titles are truncated, and the terminal title drops shell redirection, so a client cannot rely on them.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop model switch writes no `model_switch` row — the model never gets the `[System: ... changed to <model> via provider <provider>]` injection, and the GUI timeline never shows "model changed"
issues.body:
### Bug Description
On v0.22.7 (Desktop, Windows), switching the model of an **already-established** chat writes **no `messages` row with `display_kind='model_switch'`** — and that one missing row causes three regressions at once:

1. **The model is never told.** The turn really runs on the newly picked model, but the in-context pivot `[System: The active model for this chat has changed to <new_model> via provider <new_provider>. From this point forward, use this runtime metadata when answering questions about what model/provider is active.]` — written only by `_append_model_switch_marker` (`tui_gateway/server.py:1168`) — never reaches the transcript, so the active model has no idea it is active. Verified live: while the turn was genuinely served by `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, the assistant answered "I cannot know which model is active".
2. **The GUI loses the `model changed` notice.** Desktop renders exactly that row as a backend-authored system notice: `NOTICE_DISPLAY_KINDS` contains `model_switch`, and `timelineDisplayContent()` maps it to the literal text `model changed` (`apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/hydration.ts:179,310`). No row ⇒ nothing is rendered at the switch turn, where earlier versions showed "model changed". The user gets no confirmation that the switch was recorded, and neither does the transcript.
3. **The switch is not durable either.** `sessions.model` / `sessions.model_config` keep the pre-switch route, so the next `agent_init` rebuild comes back on the profile default: the conversation silently continues on a **different model than the one the composer shows**.

Impact (why this is not cosmetic):
1. **Silent route divergence.** The model that answers is not the model the UI claims. A user who picks a 1M-context model to keep a long chat alive, or a cheaper model to control cost, keeps running on the profile default with no warning, no error, and no marker in the transcript.
2. **The agent cannot know.** The injected `[System: The active model ... changed to <model> via provider <provider>]` row is the only channel by which a model learns that its runtime changed; dropping it makes every later self-report about the active model wrong (verified below).
3. **No error surface.** The pick reports success, the pill shows the new model, and the loss only becomes visible as "why is this model suddenly behaving differently".

Scope check on this machine: the marker is written only for the **old-style** session ids (`YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_hex`, `source='desktop'`). Canonical local sessions (`local-<64 hex>`, `source='local'`) never get one:
| session id shape | chats | `display_kind='model_switch'` rows |
|---|---|---|
| `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_hex` (`source=desktop`) | 520 | 48 |
| `local-<64 hex>` (`source=local`) | 39 | **0** |
At least 4 of those 39 canonical chats demonstrably used two different models (`session_model_usage` keeps two `task=''` rows with different `model`), so this is not "nobody switched there". The newest such row anywhere in this database is dated 10-27; every switch since then produced nothing.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Desktop on v0.22.7, an **existing** chat that has already run turns — here a canonical local session (`local-f0353a…`, `sessions.source='local'`), profile default `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` via `cmdcode2api`.
2. Composer model picker → pick another model **with a provider** (the picker's canonical payload is `"<model> --provider <provider>"`), i.e. `gemini-3.8-flash-high` via `easycliproxyapi_ws`.
3. Send a message. The turn really runs on the picked model (`agent.log`: `conversation turn ... model=gemini-3.8-flash-high provider=custom`, 9 API calls between 10:29:46 and 10:32:39) — but **no `model changed` notice appears in the chat timeline at that turn**, and asking the model which model is active returns "I cannot know".
4. Send the next message after a rebuild. It runs on the **old** model again (`OpenAI client created (agent_init, shared=True) ... model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at 10:35:15, then `conversation turn ... model=deepseek/...`), and still no `model_switch` row was ever written.
5. `SELECT model, model_config FROM sessions WHERE id='local-f0353a…'` → still the profile default; `SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id='local-f0353a…' AND display_kind='model_switch'` → 0.

### Expected Behavior
A model switch on an established chat should write exactly one durable pivot row, and that one row should feed both consumers, as it does for old-style sessions:
1. the model's context gets `[System: The active model for this chat has changed to <new_model> via provider <new_provider> ...]` from the switch turn onward;
2. the Desktop timeline shows the `model changed` notice at that turn;
3. `sessions.model_config` (and `sessions.model`) are updated to the picked route, so a resume/rebuild restores it and the chat stays on the picked route across agent rebuilds, TTL evictions and resumes.

And if any of those steps cannot be performed, the pick must fail **loudly** (error/toast + pill reverted), never leave a memory-only pin behind.

### Actual Behavior
The pick is applied to the live agent only. Nothing durable is written: the session row keeps the old route, the transcript gets no marker, and the next agent build re-adopts the profile route. The user sees a composer pill showing the new model while the requests are served by the old one — with no error, no `model changed` notice in the GUI, and no log line at any level above DEBUG.

Observed evidence from this machine (all from `state.db` + `logs/agent.log`, same chat):
- `session_model_usage` holds two main-turn routes for the chat: `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` @ `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` and `gemini-3.8-flash-high` @ `http://127.0.0.1:8318/v1` (9 calls, 10:29:46 → 10:32:39).
- `sessions.model='deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash'`, `model_config.gateway_runtime.provider='cmdcode2api'` — unchanged after the switch.
- 0 rows with `display_kind='model_switch'` for that chat; across the whole DB the newest such row is from 10-27, and 0 of 39 `local-<hash>` chats have one.
- 10:35:15 `OpenAI client created (agent_init, shared=True) ... model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` → the rebuild silently restored the profile route.
- The assistant itself answered "I cannot know which model is active" while its own turn was being served by the newly picked model — the missing marker is directly observable in behaviour, not just in the table.

### Affected Component
Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory), Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)
N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report
```shell
No `hermes debug share` upload: that dump carries `config.yaml` (base_urls, provider entries, credentials) and this defect needs no runtime logs — it is provable from `state.db` plus a handful of `agent.log` lines, quoted inline above. Happy to attach a redacted `hermes debug share --local` on request.
```

### Operating System
Windows 10 (10.0.19045.3930), Edge 153.0.4234.32

### Python Version
3.14.9

### Hermes Version
0.22.7 (git b200f5bc)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)
```shell
# agent.log (same chat id, 2026-11-06)
10:29:36 conversation turn: session=local-f0353a… model=gemini-3.8-flash-high provider=custom platform=desktop history=98
10:29:36 Stored system prompt ... has stale runtime identity; rebuilding for model=gemini-3.8-flash-high provider=custom
10:29:46 API call #1: model=gemini-3.8-flash-high provider=custom in=109078 out=569
... (9 calls, last at 10:32:39)
10:35:15 OpenAI client created (agent_init, shared=True) provider=custom base_url=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
10:35:15 conversation turn: session=local-f0353a… model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash provider=custom platform=desktop history=100
# state.db
sqlite> select model, json_extract(model_config,'$.gateway_runtime.provider') from sessions where id like 'local-f0353a%';
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash|cmdcode2api <-- never updated by the switch
sqlite> select count(*) from messages where session_id like 'local-f0353a%' and display_kind='model_switch';
0
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)
The marker row is written in exactly one place — `_append_model_switch_marker` (`tui_gateway/server.py:1168`), called only from `_commit_agent_switch` (`tui_gateway/model_switch.py:280`). Two drop points produce exactly this, and both are fail-silent, so neither leaves a trace to distinguish them at runtime:
1. **`_apply_model_switch` skips the whole commit when there is no live agent** — `tui_gateway/model_switch.py:345` (`if agent:` → `_commit_agent_switch`, `model_switch.py:280`). Everything durable lives inside that call: `_persist_live_session_runtime` (`tui_gateway/agent_factory.py:217`) writes the route into `sessions.model_config`, `_persist_live_session_system_prompt` (`server.py:1127`) refreshes the stored prompt, and `_append_model_switch_marker` (`server.py:1168`) writes the marker. With `agent is None` all three are skipped and the pick survives only as `session["model_override"]` — memory. A later rebuild (TTL evict, interrupt, resume) has nothing to restore, and `_sync_agent_model_with_config` (`model_switch.py:491`) re-adopts the profile route silently.
Note `_set_model` (`tui_gateway/methods_config_set.py:157`) only builds an agent when the pick has **no** explicit provider: `if session.get("agent") is None and not explicit_provider.strip() ...`. The composer picker always carries `"<model> --provider <provider>"`, so that pre-build is skipped by construction — the picker route is the one that lands in the `agent is None` branch.
2. **Even with a live agent, both persistence helpers fail silently.** `_persist_live_session_runtime` wraps everything in `except Exception: logger.debug(...)`; `_append_model_switch_marker` returns early when `session_key` or the db handle is missing. So "switch applied, nothing persisted, nothing announced" produces no warning anywhere, which is why this went unnoticed for weeks.

So the defect class is not just "a missing notice": a **memory-only model pin is treated as a durable one**, and the marker row — the single source for both the model's `[System: ...]` injection and the GUI's `model changed` notice — is never produced.

### Proposed Fix (optional)
1. In `_apply_model_switch` (`tui_gateway/model_switch.py`), when `agent is None` still persist the resolved route into the session row (the durable form of `session["model_override"]`) and call `_append_model_switch_marker` — the marker only needs `session_key` + a db handle, not a live agent.
2. Alternatively/preferably in `_set_model` (`methods_config_set.py:157`), build the agent regardless of `explicit_provider`, so every picker switch goes through `_commit_agent_switch`. The `explicit_provider` exception is what turns a durable switch into a memory-only one.
3. Make persistence fail loud: log at WARNING (not `logger.debug`) and emit a `notification.show` when a switch cannot be persisted, and have `_sync_agent_model_with_config` refuse to overwrite a session route it did not itself adopt.
4. Regression test: `tests/tui_gateway/test_model_switch_marker_role.py` already has the fixture; add the `agent is None` case and assert a `model_switch` row + an updated `sessions.model_config`.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?
- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: Batch delegate_task transcripts hijack their parent's resume (session_read_only lockout)
issues.body:
# Batch delegate_task transcripts hijack their parent's resume (session_read_only lockout)

**Seen on:** v0.22.7, local `b200f5bc60`, Linux. Related: #115092 (same walk, partial fix).

## Symptom

A long-running TUI/desktop chat that has run `delegate_task` (batch) can no longer
be resumed from the dashboard after a `ws_orphan_reap` (service restart). Opening
`/chat?profile=…&resume=<parent-id>` lands on the *subagent's* transcript instead,
which is a history mount: every input is refused with

    gateway.session_controls: prompt.submit refused for profile=default: session_read_only
    field=session_id detail=this stored conversation can be read but not continued

The lockout repeats on every resume attempt while the newest child is a subagent,
so the parent conversation becomes unreachable from the web chat.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py::_DESCENDANTS_SQL` (the #115092 fix) excludes
non-continuation children only via creation markers:

    WHERE json_extract(s.model_config,'$._delegate_from') IS NULL
      AND json_extract(s.model_config,'$._branched_from') IS NULL
      AND NOT (<reset-child>)
      AND COALESCE(s.source,'') != 'tool'

Batch `delegate_task` children get their lineage from the reservation writer,
which stamps `parent_session_id` and `source='subagent'` but **never**
`model_config._delegate_from` (see `agent/runtime_session_child.py`: "The owner
created this row at reservation with its source, lineage and profile"). Verified
live: the row has `source='subagent'`, `json_extract(model_config,'$._delegate_from')`
NULL, `parent_session_id` set. The synchronous worker-child path
(`gateway/session_worker_child.py:63`) does stamp the marker — async batch rows
slip past the predicate, and `_session_latest_descendant` walks into them.

Other code already treats the two as equivalent — `hermes_state_common.py`
("recognised by its source OR by the `_delegate_from` creation marker"). The
descendants CTE never got the memo, and the Python fallback path
(`list_sessions_rich`) filters nothing at all.

## Repro

1. Run `delegate_task` from a chat session (batch mode).
2. Restart the gateway/dashboard so the parent row gets `end_reason='ws_orphan_reap'`.
3. GET `/api/sessions/<parent>/latest-descendant` (or open `chat?resume=<parent>`).
   Expected: `session_id == <parent>`. Actual: the subagent row; the chat is then
   mounted read-only.

## Proposed fix

Exclude by `source` in both walk paths (carry `source` through the CTE so the
fallback filters identically):

    WITH RECURSIVE descendants(id, parent_session_id, started_at, source) AS (...)
    ...
    if rid and parent and str(row.get("source") or "") not in ("tool", "subagent"):
        children.setdefault(parent, []).append(row)

Test: `test_latest_descendant_skips_unmarked_subagent_children` — child created
with `source='subagent'`, `parent_session_id` set, no marker; expects the parent
to resolve to itself. Red at `b200f5bc60`, green with the fix. A writer-side fix
(stamping `_delegate_from` at batch reservation) is probably the fuller answer
but would not repair rows already written.

Local overlay carrying this: `~/hermes-overlay` patch 0001
(`fix(web): descendant walk skips unmarked subagent children`).

issues.title: [Bug]: Multiplexed gateway never prunes the checkpoint stores of served profiles (prune tick runs only in the launch home)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
### Summary
In a multiplexed gateway, "Checkpoint prune tick" is the only per-profile housekeeping chore that is not wrapped in `profile_scoped_chore`. `auto_prune_from_config()` therefore reads the launch home's config and checkpoint base only. The stores of served profiles are never pruned, even with `checkpoints.auto_prune: true` in their own config.

### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.22.5+1711.g9b904dc (2026.9.24), upstream 9b904dcc; macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6, arm64); desktop app.
- One gateway process, launched from `~/.hermes`, serves profile `desktop-local` and eleven others. The launch home has `checkpoints.enabled: false` and no `~/.hermes/checkpoints`.
- `desktop-local` config: `checkpoints.enabled: true`, `auto_prune: true`, `max_total_size_mb: 500`, `min_interval_hours: 24`.

### What happened
- `~/.hermes/profiles/desktop-local/checkpoints/.last_prune` was last written on 2026-10-13. The store was not pruned after that.
- The store grew to 2.8 GB against the 500 MB cap. 1.93 GiB of it were three `tmp_pack_*` files that `clear_stale_tmp_packs` (called from prune) would have removed. `.gc-pending` stays set, because the gc that the take path defers "to the next prune" never runs.
- After I deleted the three tmp packs, a manual `hermes -p desktop-local checkpoints prune --retention-days 3650 --keep-orphans --max-size-mb 0` ran in 18.7 s and reclaimed 306 MB.

### Cause
`gateway/run.py:4536`:

```python
(1, "Checkpoint prune tick", _housekeeping_checkpoint_prune)]
```

The other per-profile chores are scoped, for example `gateway/run.py:4522`:

```python
(60, "Curator tick", profile_scoped_chore(runner, _housekeeping_curator)),
```

Unscoped, `auto_prune_from_config()` (`tools/checkpoint_maintenance.py:425`) loads the launch home's config, and `_resolve_checkpoint_base()` (`tools/checkpoint_manager.py:78`) returns the launch home's base. Here that base does not exist, so the call returns before it touches any store.

### Suggested fix
Scope it like the other per-profile chores:

```python
(1, "Checkpoint prune tick", profile_scoped_chore(runner, _housekeeping_checkpoint_prune)),
```

### Workaround
Run `hermes -p <profile> checkpoints prune ...` daily from launchd or cron.

issues.title: [Bug][Desktop]: project writes in the All-profiles view target the viewing profile, not the declaring profile (5062 no such project)
issues.body:
# Desktop: project writes are scoped to the *viewing* profile, not the project's declaring profile

**Type:** bug
**Labels:** `type/bug`, `comp/desktop`, `comp/tui-gateway`, `area/profiles`, `P2`

---

## Summary

In the Desktop sidebar's **All profiles** view, every write against a project (rename, add folder,
delete, set active, appearance) is sent with `profile = <the currently selected gateway profile>`, not with the
profile that actually **declares** the project. The backend then looks the project up in the wrong `projects.db`
and answers `5062 no such project`.

The project renders correctly in the same sidebar, because the All-profiles tree is a **read** path that merges
every profile's database by folder path. So the user sees a perfectly healthy project in the list, clicks rename,
and gets an error — with a message that names the *wrong action* ("could not create project").

Net effect: **a project can be rendered in the sidebar but be impossible to edit** unless the user happens to have
that project's own profile selected at the moment they click.

## Reproduction

Setup — two profiles, a project declared in one of them, and the Desktop viewing All profiles:

```
profile "default":  project "Hermes服务器维护"  ->  /home/aaron/Project/System Security Audit
profile "clark":    project "Spark服务器维护"    ->  /home/aaron/Project/Spark_DevOps
```

1. In the Desktop, switch the profile selector to **All profiles**.
2. Select **clark** as the active gateway profile (this is what `$activeGatewayProfile` holds; the All-profiles
   toggle only changes `$showAllProfiles`, not `$activeGatewayProfile`).
3. In the sidebar, right-click the **Hermes服务器维护** project -> Rename -> type a new name.

Expected: the project is renamed.

Actual: the rename fails. The backend returns RPC error `5062` `no such project`, and the Desktop shows the toast
**"Could not create project" / "无法创建项目"** — even though this is a rename.

### Backend log

The `projects.update` request carries `profile: "clark"`, so `tui_gateway/server.py::_profile_scoped` resolves
`clark`'s home and `tui_gateway/methods_projects.py::_require_project` looks up the project id in
`profiles/clark/projects.db` — where it does not exist, because it is declared in `projects.db` (the `default`
profile).

```
project: no such project: p_2952a9cf
```

### Direct confirmation, independent of the Desktop

The same project resolves only under the profile that declares it:

```console
$ hermes project rename p_2952a9cf "Hermes服务器维护"          # default profile
Renamed project -> Hermes服务器维护

$ hermes --profile clark project rename p_2952a9cf "Hermes服务器维护"
project: no such project: p_2952a9cf
```

The two databases confirm the split:

```console
$ sqlite3 ~/.hermes/projects.db "select id,name from projects"
p_2952a9cf|Hermes服务器维护

$ sqlite3 ~/.hermes/profiles/clark/projects.db "select id,name from projects"
p_bfa92481|Spark服务器维护
p_c5f26cac|Github管理
```

## Root cause

Two code paths disagree about what "the project" is, and the write path picks the wrong one.

**Read path — merges every profile (correct):**

`apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts::refreshProjectTreeAcrossProfiles` calls
`GET /api/profiles/projects/tree`, which (`hermes_cli/web_routers/profiles.py::get_profiles_projects_tree`) builds
the tree once per profile and folds them together in `_merge_profile_tree`, **keyed by folder path**:

```python
key = _path_key(project.get("path") or project["id"])
project["mergeKey"] = key
```

A declared project (`p_<hash>`) and another profile's auto entry for the same folder merge into one node, and the
declared one wins the identity. The resulting node carries the project id but **no record of which profile declared
it** — `_merge_profile_tree` only stamps the *sessions* with their owning profile (`session["profile"] = profile`),
never the project node itself.

**Write path — scoped to the viewing profile (incorrect):**

`apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts::updateProject` (line 1217) resolves its profile from `writableProjectProfile()`
(line 329):

```ts
// All profiles filters the sidebar. Writes still belong to the live gateway profile.
function writableProjectProfile(): string {
  const profile = normalizeProfileKey($activeGatewayProfile.get())
  if (!profile || profile === ALL_PROFILES) {
    throw new Error('Projects are unavailable while viewing all profiles')
  }
  return profile
}
```

and sends it with the request (line 1243):

```ts
await persistOrRollback(snap, () =>
  gatewayRequestOn(
    context.gateway,
    'projects.update',
    projectParams({ id, ...patch }, context.profile)   // <- the VIEWING profile
  )
)
```

`projectParams` merges `profile` into the RPC params; `tui_gateway/server.py::_profile_scoped` (line 485) resolves it
to a home and rebinds `HERMES_HOME` for the duration of the call, so `pdb.connect_closing()` opens **that** profile's
`projects.db`.

The id in the tree came from a *different* profile's database. The two never meet.

The comment above `writableProjectProfile` states the intent — "Writes still belong to the live gateway profile" — and
for a single-profile view that is right. It is the All-profiles view that breaks the assumption: the view spans N
profiles, but the write can only ever target one of them.

## Scope of the defect

The same `projectParams(..., context.profile)` pattern is used by every project write, so all of these fail
identically when the viewing profile does not declare the project:

| Desktop action | RPC | `projects.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| Rename | `projects.update` | line 1243 |
| Add folder | `projects.add_folder` | line 1336 |
| Delete | `projects.delete` | line 1385 |
| Set active | `projects.set_active` | line 1398 |
| Appearance (color/icon) | `projects.update` | line 1243 |

Not affected: **auto** nodes (a promoted git-repo root, `isAuto: true`, id = the folder path). They have no
`projects.db` row in any profile, and the sidebar already withholds the identity actions from them —
`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/project-menu.tsx:95`:

```tsx
// Rename / add folder / set active — explicit projects only (auto ones lack a
// materialized record).
const identityItems: ActionItemSpec[] = project.isAuto
  ? []
  : [ { icon: 'edit', key: 'rename', ... } ]
```

That is the correct handling, and it is the shape the fix for this issue should take for the
declared-but-foreign-profile case: the action needs to be *possible* (the record exists, in another profile), not
*hidden*.

## Two defects, one symptom

**1. The write is scoped to the wrong profile.** The tree must carry the declaring profile of each project node (the
read path already knows it; `_merge_profile_tree` simply does not record it), and `updateProject` and friends should
use it when the viewing scope is All profiles.

**2. The error message names the wrong action.** `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/project-dialog.tsx` uses the
same `p.createFailed` string for both the create and the rename path:

```ts
// line 111 / 147
notifyError(err, p.createFailed)
// line 157
await runSubmit(() => renameProject(projectId, trimmed))
```

`apps/desktop/src/i18n/zh_projects.ts:44` -> `createFailed: '无法创建项目'`. A failed **rename** is reported as a
failed **create**, which sends the user looking in the wrong place entirely.

## Suggested direction

Not a proposal for the final shape — just the constraint that any fix has to satisfy.

- The All-profiles tree needs to carry the declaring profile per project node (the read path already knows it;
  `_merge_profile_tree` simply does not record it), and `updateProject` and friends should use it when the viewing
  scope is All profiles.
- The backend could alternatively resolve the project by id across the served profiles when the scoped lookup misses.
  That trades a strict per-profile boundary for a cross-profile read, so it is a design decision, not a patch — but it
  makes the id self-describing, which it currently is not.
- Separately, `project-dialog.tsx` should use a rename-specific message.

## Environment

- Hermes `0.22.6` (`74b2ed65e6564bfcafd29236e5fab2447a68fc76`)
- Checked against `origin/main` (`ca43606920`): `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` has **zero** diff between the
  two, and neither `_merge_profile_tree` nor `_require_project` changed — the defect is present on `main` too.
- Desktop app on Windows, connecting to a remote Hermes gateway over the LAN
- Gateway multiplexing active, 46 served profiles
- `hermes debug share` not run — no local logs/config uploaded to a public paste service for this report

## Related

- #81888 — "Profile-specific vs global projects.db desync" (item 5) describes the same underlying split-brain from
  the operator's side.
- #140076 — "[Feature]: hermes project transfer — move or copy a Project between profiles". The underlying reason
  this bug is so hard to hit is that there is no supported way to move a project declaration between profiles at all;
  operators work around it by hand-editing `projects.db`, which is what produced the mismatched declaration in the
  first place.
