issues.body:
Tracking issue for the staged fast-follow named in [#134889](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889)'s scope note: *"the browser dashboard and Desktop URL / Cloud / SSH modes still talk to standalone `hermes serve`."* [#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742) (merged Oct 14, `eb75627f`) gave every **local** surface one gateway-owned session authority per profile. This issue tracks moving the remaining entry points onto that same authority and then removing the old in-process session host.

Design: [One Gateway: Entry-Point and Session Ownership Plan](https://gist.github.com/unsupportedpastels/765f9d551ce88ee01630c18367763e75). Profile-multiplexing direction: [#109417](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/109417) (one `hermes gateway run` serves every profile).

**Status (Oct 26, after EP-1, first repros and EP-2 baseline):** EP-1 (caller map) is done, traced by code reading on `main` at `edfa1c2a`. It traced EP-8 to EP-11, split EP-11, and added EP-13 to EP-17 and D6. EP-13 and EP-15 are now reproduced in-process on `edfa1c2a` (no live gateway). 16 open rows, 2 verification rows, 6 open decisions. Nothing is in a package yet. EP-2 has a headless baseline (289 tests passed); `verify_parity2.sh` and the manual live checks need rebuilding. Other rows were checked against `main` at `d49e2ebb`; rows marked *needs repro* come from code reading only.

**Update (Nov 6):** merged the handler ledger (EP-1, #148795), the acceptance harness (EP-2, #148774), the EP-15 fix (#148769), the EP-11a removal (#148775) and the V1/V2 tests (#148777, #148798). EP-13 (#148770) and EP-14 (#148794) are held for the cutover so `main`'s behavior doesn't change before it.

**Scope:** `hermes serve`, standalone `hermes dashboard`, Desktop remote modes (SSH / URL / Cloud), remaining direct agent constructors, and removal of the legacy host. **Out of scope:** the forced-migration campaign (soak, rollback window, `--force`); migrating background services is in scope as EP-18, storage redesign, protocol unification, a replacement browser UI and a mobile client.

## Done on `main` (not tracked here)

- Local Desktop runs `gateway ensure` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`); `5e783bde` removed code that only Desktop's own `serve` reached.
- `session.detach` is wired in `gateway/session_controls.py`.
- `SessionAuthorities` supports `add`/`remove` at runtime (`gateway/session_authorities.py`, `gateway/run_runtime.py`); see V1.
- [#141864](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/141864) serves the Desktop webapp (`apps/desktop/dist-webapp`, not `web/`) from the gateway's own listener.

## Contract under test

- Every supported entry point reaches the canonical profile authority; none starts its own session runtime.
- Closing a client removes a viewer. It never stops accepted work.
- Authorized clients can join and leave the same conversation and see the same queue, execution state and pending controls.
- Profile selection resolves an authority inside the multiplexer; `serve -p X` never launches an independent gateway for X.
- Documented callback URLs, profile-scoped auth, `--force` and standalone migration support are unchanged.
- No legacy execution fallback remains at completion.

## Legend

🔴 open, no fix · 🟡 fix PR open · 🟣 fix in review (member PR) · 🔵 waiting on a maintainer decision · ⚪ not reproduced · 🟢 fixed on `main`

## Open findings

### Stage 1: caller map and parity harness (start here)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-1 | Caller map for `serve`. **Done at `edfa1c2a`.** One FastAPI app runs in two modes, chosen only by `app.state.gateway_runner` (`hermes_cli/web_server_app.py:234`). Only the gateway's own mount sets it (`gateway/run_api.py:96-97`), so every `hermes serve`, `hermes dashboard` and `serve --isolated` runs `standalone_lifespan` with no authority. `serve` never discovers or forwards to a running gateway, except single-session edits over `session.mutate` (`hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py:188-234`). Results feed D1 to D6 below. **Handler ledger merged in #148795 (`eccfff7b`):** `tests/hermes_cli/serve_handler_ledger.json` lists every serve HTTP route, RPC and WebSocket handler with its owner decision (625 rows, 520 undecided pending D1–D6); `scripts/gen_serve_handler_ledger.py --check` keeps it in sync with `main`. | P1 | 🟢 |
| EP-2 | Parity rigs on the combined tree. **Headless baseline recorded on `edfa1c2a`** (scratch home, one pytest process per file): 31 files, 289 tests passed, about 8 min. Covers entrypoint parity and boot contract (`tests/e2e/core/parity/`), two-tenant gateway and Desktop backend (`tests/e2e/core/tenancy/`), live hot-serve (`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_hot_serve_live.py`, 7), gateway turn liveness (`tests/e2e/core/chaos/test_gateway_turn_liveness.py`, 12), and the profile-isolation, handoff, recovery and admission/replay unit tests. `tests/e2e/core/tenancy/test_routing_truth_table.py` could not run on this host (its guard refuses temp dirs under `~/.hermes`); use the CI `e2e` job result. **Missing:** `verify_parity2.sh` is not in the tree, git history or any linked issue; the #134889 "Verified working" live checks were manual and have no scripts. **Not run here:** Desktop `apps/desktop/e2e/core` (`remote-topology`, `remote-secondary`, `local-gateway-attach`) needs a GUI; CI lane `e2e-desktop-core` runs it. Next: rerun the same file set on every combined-tree candidate; rebuild network drop mid-turn, cron→compress→input and SSE approvals as scripted e2e tests. **Acceptance harness merged in #148774 (`418de33e`):** `tests/e2e/core/serve_ownership/` runs a real `serve` and gateway with one control cell and three `known_failure` cells for the open ownership gaps; `HERMES_E2E_STRICT_ACCEPTANCE=serve-cutover` turns them into hard failures for the cutover. | P1 | 🔴 |

### Stages 2–3: `serve` uses the authority

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-3 | With no `gateway_runner`, `serve` selects `standalone_lifespan` and runs agents in-process (`hermes_cli/web_server_app.py:234`; comment at `hermes_cli/main.py:2598`). | P1 | 🔴 (blocked on D1, D2) |
| EP-4 | `/api/ws` sends every RPC to the legacy `server.dispatch` when no authority is present (`tui_gateway/ws.py:362-390`). With an authority, non-session verbs that the authority answers with -32601 still fall back to legacy handlers in-process (`tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py:53-64`): 100 methods go to the authority, 163 fall back, 16 are blocked. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-5 | New work can enter `serve` without going through the authority's admission: [#138750](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/138750). The issue's line numbers have drifted; on `edfa1c2a` the console executor is `hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:278`, PTY spawn `:552`, action subprocesses `hermes_cli/web_server_gateway.py:475`. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-6 | Version skew: a new remote client's `prompt.submit` attachments are refused by an older `serve`: [#144186](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/144186). Traced: the retry strips only `submission_id`, then the legacy param model refuses `attachments` with `4000`. | P2 | 🔴 (blocked on D5) |
| EP-13 | Session-bound legacy fallback methods on authority sessions. **Reproduced in-process at `edfa1c2a`:** the authority answers -32601 for all 13, the fallback runs the legacy handler, and the handler can't find the session (authority sessions are never in `server._sessions`). 10 fail with `4001 session not found`; `tools.list` and `toolsets.list` silently ignore the session and return launch-profile data; `insights.get` isn't session-bound (it rejects `session_id` with 4000). Clients gate or translate 11 of the 13 before they reach the wire. Two still reach the server and fail silently: Desktop `image.detach` on chip removal (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/hooks/use-composer-actions.ts:922`, harmless) and ui-tui `input.detect_drop` for a dropped non-image path (`ui-tui/src/app/useComposerState.ts:339-379`), which pastes raw text instead of an attachment. `handoff.*` and `tools.configure` are refused by name client-side (feature gap). Defensive server fix: keep -32601 for these verbs in `tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py`, as already done for `session.`/`prompt.`. | P3 | 🔴 |
| EP-14 | `POST /api/cron/jobs/{id}/trigger` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py:762`) runs the job's agent inside the request thread (`cron/scheduler.py:3373`) outside admission, in both modes; the code marks the path deprecated. `POST /api/cron/fire` already forwards to the gateway. | P2 | 🔴 |
| EP-15 | `POST /api/health/retirement` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:160`) is live on the gateway listener and declares a busy gateway idle. **Reproduced in-process at `edfa1c2a`** (real dashboard app bound the way `gateway/run_api.py:75-108` binds it, a claimed admission and one running agent; runner and authority are stand-ins): `GET /api/health/idle` returns `idle: true`, `prepare` returns 200 with a token, `commit` returns 200. Afterwards dashboard JSON-RPC answers 5035 "backend is retiring", cron `tick()` dispatches nothing and the fence admits no new work until restart, while the gateway keeps running. Cause: the idle proof (`hermes_cli/web_server_idle_proof.py:39-58`, `hermes_cli/web_server_idle_exit.py:104-136`) reads only the legacy session table, delegation, cron and the fence; it never consults the gateway runner or authority, and nothing under `gateway/` takes the fence. Latent: no in-repo client calls the route, and it needs an owner or local token. Fix direction: refuse when `app.state.gateway_runner` is set, or base idleness on `gateway/run_idle_exit.py:busy_reason` and fail closed. **Fixed by #148769 (`f190892f`):** with a gateway runner mounted, the idle route reports not idle and `prepare`/`commit`/`cancel` are refused; standalone `serve` keeps its idle retirement. | P1 | 🟢 |
| EP-17 | Bulk session REST (bulk delete, delete-empty, prune) writes `state.db` directly under a store-wide lock and returns 409 while a gateway owns the store, with no owner path. | P3 | 🔴 |

### Stage 4: remote Desktop and browser

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-7 | SSH mode starts `serve --isolated` and kills it on disconnect, so closing the client stops accepted work (`apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts:1142-1161`, `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:9486`). Every disconnect path (quit, connection switch or edit, profile delete, recycle) kills the remote process with no check for a running turn. | P1 | 🔴 (blocked on D4) |
| EP-8 | Desktop URL and Cloud modes reach whatever process the URL names; neither calls `gateway ensure`. The Docker image's dashboard service runs standalone `hermes dashboard` on 9119 (`docker/s6-rc.d/dashboard/run:52-54`). Desktop reads no `gateway_mode` or host role, so it can't tell which backend it reached. Hosted Cloud agents are inferred to match; Cloud infra isn't in this repo. | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-9 | Standalone `hermes dashboard` chat (the sidebar's `/api/ws`, and the chat terminal when no profile is named) and its session REST use the legacy dispatcher, not the authority. A named profile attaches to the profile's gateway. *Reworded:* `ChatPage` can't reach `serve`, which is headless and doesn't serve `web/` (`hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py:126-149`). | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |
| EP-16 | SSH, URL and Cloud remotes send raw method names: the 13 rewrites to `session.mutate` with revision/generation checks in `canonical-protocol.ts` apply only to `native_dial` sockets. `handoff.*` is refused locally but still sent to remotes. **Fixed by #148219 (`7bc10408da`):** Desktop now selects the canonical adapter from `session_authority: true` in `gateway.ready`, so the rewrites and the `handoff.*` refusal apply to any remote that advertises it. SSH still reaches `serve --isolated`, which serves the legacy names (EP-7). | P2 | 🟢 |

### Stage 5: remaining producers

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-10 | The slash worker runs a second `HermesCLI` per session: [#141196](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141196). Standalone backends only (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:1070-1086`); the gateway serves `slash.exec` itself (`gateway/session_controls.py:390`). | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |
| EP-11a | `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` `_run_agent` builds a bare `AIAgent`, but it's dead code: its only caller `_run_and_exit_oneshot` is called only from tests, and `-z` goes through `launch_gateway_chat` (`hermes_cli/main.py:3020-3026`). Removal candidate. **Removed by #148775 (`a2db0efb`).** `_exit_after_oneshot` stays (it writes `--cpu-profile` output) and `hermes_cli.oneshot.get_fallback_chain` stays importable. | P3 | 🟢 |
| EP-11b | `prompt.background` (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:1184`) writes a separate `bg_*` session row and skips the gateway's queue check; `preview.restart` (`:1249`) builds `AIAgent` with no session store. Standalone backends only; gateway connections refuse `prompt.*` fallback. | P2 | 🔴 (D6) |

### Stage 6: remove the legacy host (after parity)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EP-18 | Users who run `hermes serve` / `hermes dashboard` as an automatic background service need a migration path before removal. Hermes never installs one itself; the shapes are systemd units copied from the docs (`web-dashboard.md:186-197`, `desktop.md:668`) and hand-written launchd plists, Nix `hermes-backend` (NixOS unit, Home Manager user unit and launchd agent; `Restart=always`, `KeepAlive=true`), the Docker image's s6 `dashboard` longrun and the Compose `dashboard` sidecar, Desktop SSH `serve --isolated`, and operator-made Windows autostarts. `hermes update` restarts these but never migrates them, and its unit-name gate misses `hermes-backend`. Hazard: the attach path exits 0 when another backend owns the host, which respawn-loops under those restart policies, so a deprecated entry point must stay in the foreground. Main blocker is listener parity (the gateway serves the webapp on 9120, not the `web/` SPA on 9119, and lacks the Nix session-token file and the `dashboard.public_url` mapping). Proposed: a `serve.host_mode` switch, sentinel mode, `hermes gateway migrate --backends` with dry-run/rollback, and a report-only update hook until the cutover (Linear HACORE-159). | P1 | 🔴 |
| EP-12 | The legacy session host still exists: `tui_gateway/server.py` (2,187 lines), `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py`, `ws_legacy_fallback`. Remove only after EP-3 to EP-18 are green and EP-2 passes. Modules named `tui_gateway` that don't host sessions stay. | P2 | 🔴 (blocked on stages 2–5) |

### Verification (believed done; needs evidence)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V1 | Hot-added and removed profiles create and retire authorities. #134889 lists the served profile set as a start-time snapshot, but `main` now has `SessionAuthorities.add`/`remove`, driven by the `serve-profile`, `unserve-profile` and `rescan-profiles` control-socket verbs (`gateway/run_runtime.py:380`, `:459`). **Partly verified on `edfa1c2a`:** `test_multiplex_hot_serve_live.py` (7 passed) drives `rescan-profiles` against a real multiplexer, and unserve is covered at the function level (`test_run_runtime_hot_serve_cleanup.py`). No test sends `serve-profile` or `unserve-profile` by name; add one to the live test, then update #134889's "Deliberate limits". **Verified by #148777 (`02849dba`):** the live test now sends `serve-profile` and `unserve-profile` by name and checks the authority is added and retired (including during a running turn). | P2 | 🟢 |
| V2 | [#109403](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109403), [#109405](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109405) and [#109412](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109412) closed unmerged. Check whether `main` covers each one's piece ([#109404](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109404)'s is covered by `session.detach`). **Checked:** all three pieces are on `main`; #148798 (`e8a469a1`) adds the Desktop tests that were missing. | P3 | 🟢 |

## Decisions to settle

| ID | Decision | EP-1 input | Gates | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Which existing startup/discovery path does `serve` reuse, and when does it start the owner versus forward to it? | `gateway_runner` is in-process only, so forwarding means a proxy, and that needs identity forwarding (D2). The evidence favors remote clients attaching to the gateway listener directly (it mounts the same app and auth), with `serve` as a launcher that uses control-socket discovery (`identify`, `session-ticket`). Blockers: `/api/ws` accepts loopback only; no remote ticket path. | EP-3, EP-4, EP-7, EP-8 | 🔵 |
| D2 | Can owner-side authentication preserve current deployments without delegated identity forwarding? | Yes if the gateway authenticates clients itself; it already runs the same auth stack. No if `serve` forwards: tickets, the session token and cookies are process- or origin-bound, so a forwarder collapses every user into one identity. Missing on the gateway: the SSH `--isolated` token and owner nonce, the Desktop env token, the rendezvous-record token, and carrying `dashboard.public_url` to `webapp.public_url`. | EP-3, EP-8 | 🔵 |
| D3 | Which legacy capabilities need mappings before their callers can move? | Of 254 legacy methods: 75 mapped, 14 partial, 163 legacy fallback, 2 refused (`agents.list`, `session.activate`). Gaps: EP-13 (reproduced: 2 client-reachable, both silent); no authority verb tears a session down like `session.close`; host-wide services (pet, projects, MCP, vault, voice, billing, connectors, group replica/peer) run in the owner process outside admission. | stages 2–5 | 🔵 |
| D4 | Which web/SSH changes are inseparable from keeping those entry points supported? | SSH options: (a) run remote `gateway ensure --json` and tunnel to the gateway, with a capability probe and fallback to isolated `serve`; (b) interim: keep isolated `serve` but stop killing it on quit or window close, relying on its 900 s idle retirement and existing reattach. | EP-7, EP-9 | 🔵 |
| D5 | What explicit migration behavior covers version skew and unsupported legacy operations? | No version handshake exists; Desktop infers canonical vs legacy from `?native_dial`. `gateway.capabilities` exists in the contract but no client uses it. Hosted-room peers' `protocol_versions` plus per-capability flags is a working model. | EP-6 | 🔵 |
| D6 | Is authority-less `serve`/`dashboard` still a supported host? If not, fence that backend instead of fixing each producer. | — | EP-9, EP-10, EP-11b, EP-17 | 🔵 |

Open question: [#109417](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/109417) closed Sep 21 with no successor found for its forced-migration gates. This tracker doesn't own those gates; it needs to know whether they're met before EP-12.

## Not tracked here

These are separate operational work, not prerequisites for removing the alternate owner: extracting an execution-host interface from the messaging runner, independent adapter supervision, moving storage off the event loop, durable event retention and idle-session eviction.

## Working rules

- Work is grouped into package issues by stage; each package lists its rows, prerequisites, consumers and acceptance evidence.
- Reproduce on current `main` before fixing; no repro means no commit, plus a ⚪ note here.
- PRs use `Refs #<this issue> (EP-n)`, never `Fixes`.
- If an entry point already meets the contract on `main`, mark it 🟢 and leave the code alone.
- Stop and add a 🔵 row when a slice needs a new framework or an unplanned auth/lifecycle policy.

## Found a problem? Report here

Comment on this issue with: `main` SHA, Desktop version if involved, surface and mode (serve / dashboard / SSH / URL / Cloud / browser), OS and topology, steps, expected, actual, and the relevant lines from `gateway.log`, `errors.log` and `desktop.log`. Redact tokens, cookies, tickets and session URLs.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop execute_code approval times out with no clear recovery after renewed consent
issues.body:
# Hermes Desktop approval timeout and unclear retry behavior — 2026-11-06

## Environment
- macOS, Hermes Desktop, life profile. Local Hermes source checkout: `b200f5bc60e31588ba2cb60e288029c4a54ba5fa`; exact Desktop renderer build not yet verified.
- Task: update two NAS-hosted Hermes containers (official and isolated travel assistant), preserving configuration and travel isolation.

## Observed behavior
1. During preparation of a private NAS configuration backup, an `execute_code` request waited for approval and returned after five minutes with no response. The user reports they were busy and did not see/respond to an approval card; delivery of that card is not independently verified.
2. The tool response included:
   ```text
   BLOCKED: execute_code script timed out without user response.
   The user has NOT consented to running this code. Do NOT retry, do NOT rephrase the script, and do NOT attempt the same outcome via a different tool. Silence is not consent.
   tool_calls_made: 0
   user_summary: 在 5 分钟 内未收到回应——代码未执行。
   ```
3. The user later explicitly requested a new approval. The assistant treated the specific tool response as prohibiting a retry, causing the upgrade to stall. No user denial was recorded; whether a card was rendered or delivered remains unverified.
4. Earlier travel-app history shows the same `execute_code` timeout text followed by a fresh user instruction to continue, after which the assistant attempted a fresh approval flow. That prior outcome is not evidence that this attempt succeeded or that the current transport is functional.
5. Candidate version 0.23.0 was built, and Feishu/DingTalk dependencies imported in an isolated container; neither NAS production container was switched. The specific requested settings backup was not executed (`tool_calls_made: 0`). Earlier container inspection and Compose backups are not a complete replacement for that backup.

## Expected behavior
- Clearly distinguish an expired/unanswered request from an explicit denial.
- Deliver a visible, actionable approval card to the correct conversation, or surface a delivery error.
- Provide a documented, safe way for a user to explicitly request a fresh approval after timeout, while continuing to require a fresh affirmative approval before execution.
- Do not make an assistant infer indefinite refusal from silence; preserve safety and do not auto-execute.

## Privacy
No secrets, tokens, private paths, or NAS configuration are included. Do not attach raw logs, Docker inspect output, .env files, authentication files, or debug uploads without independently reviewing their contents and privacy implications.

## Investigation
Read-only logs show an auxiliary approval check at 12:31:50 CST and the execute_code timeout at 12:36:51 CST (301.77 seconds). No card delivery, rendering, or response event was identified in the searched incident logs. The actual source implements a session-keyed approval queue and notifier, but these facts do not establish where this request failed. Distinguish a delivery failure from a card that was displayed but missed. Next step: reproduce with an isolated real Desktop/backend and harmless deny, tracing request/session lifecycle and reconnect/rotation without disabling approval. No root cause or deployed fix is yet established. Prior isolated tests do not prove this live incident.

issues.title: Read-only API endpoints for the kanban board, running runs and memory entries
issues.body:
I'm building Hermes Voice, a Home Assistant integration that turns old Echo devices into voice satellites for a Hermes profile (an Echo Dot 2 and an Echo Show 5 so far). The Echo Show runs a small screen for the agent: what you asked, the tools Hermes is using, the answer as it streams, and, when idle, what Hermes is working on in the background.

That last part is where I hit a wall. The gateway's API server (the one an integration already talks to with the profile's `API_SERVER_KEY`) has `/api/jobs`, `/api/sessions` and `/health/detailed`, which cover scheduled jobs, recent sessions and status. It has nothing for:

1. **The kanban board.** Today I run `hermes kanban --board <b> list --status <s> [--assignee <profile>] --json` from a small helper process next to Hermes, because the gateway has no task endpoint and gateway plugins can't add HTTP routes. The dashboard server's kanban plugin has routes (`/api/plugins/kanban/board`, `/workers/active`), but it authenticates with a per-process session token, so it isn't usable from another service. Each `hermes kanban` call also takes about 1.2 s (CLI start-up), so the helper has to run them in parallel and cache the result.
2. **What's running right now.** Runs can be read by id (`GET /v1/runs/{id}`, `.../events`) but not listed, so there is no way to show "Hermes is working on X" across sessions.
3. **Memory entries.** The dashboard's `GET /api/memory` returns the provider and file sizes, not entries.

**Request:** read-only endpoints on the gateway API server, behind the same API key, for example:

- `GET /api/kanban/tasks?status=running,blocked,review,done&assignee=<profile>&since=<ts>&board=<slug>`: id, title, assignee, status, board, started_at, completed_at, ideally without bodies/results by default
- `GET /v1/runs?status=running`: run id, session, title, current tool, started_at
- `GET /api/memory/entries?limit=N`: the built-in memory entries (opt-in via config, since a screen may sit in a shared room)

Scoping by assignee/profile matters: by default the voice screen should only see the voice profile's work, with "all profiles" as an explicit opt-in.

One more observation from testing that may be worth documenting: a profile's gateway with the kanban dispatcher picks up tasks in `ready` and `review` on its own (it auto-reviewed a task and spawned a worker within a minute), which surprised me while creating demo tasks; `--initial-status blocked` was the safe way to create display-only tasks.

Happy to test anything. The integration and the helper are MIT; the research log with commands and evidence is at https://github.com/majorminorlabs/hermes-voice/blob/main/docs/research/2026-11-05-hermes-screen.md.

issues.title: Interrupted update leaves an empty venv; gateway deadlocks in "Restart deferred" and the desktop loops on "Gateway starting (deadline)"
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, if `hermes update` is interrupted (or has to be killed) **after** it recreates the venv but **before** dependencies are installed, the install is left with an **empty venv**: no `hermes_cli`, and no console scripts in `venv/Scripts/` at all. Stale update markers are also left behind, so the gateway re-enters `draining` on every start and never leaves it, while the desktop retries its boot loop against a gateway that will never answer.

There are two coupled failures here:

1. the updater and the gateway wait on each other forever (which is what forces the interruption), and
2. the interruption is not recoverable without manual surgery.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (build 26200)
- Hermes desktop, **source install** (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent`), venv at `venv/`
- Python 3.11.15 in the venv, Electron 44.9.3, Node 26.x
- Repo at `c5f347e` (v0.22.7+368); the desktop shell was rebuilt to the same commit separately

## Observed sequence

1. Update started as `hermes update --yes --gateway --force --branch main`.
2. `update.log`:
   ```
   → Stopping Windows gateway process(es) before updating...
     → 1 gateway(s) ACKed socket pause; waiting up to 190s for graceful exit
     ✓ Paused gateway profile(s): default
   ```
3. `gateway.log`, repeating every 30 s indefinitely:
   ```
   Restart deferred: waiting on 1 active work unit(s) (0 wedged and excluded, 0 restart-safe and excluded; ...)
   ```
4. After ~6 minutes there was no progress in either direction, so the updater was killed.
5. The kill landed inside the venv window: `venv/Lib/site-packages` contained only
   ```
   __pycache__   _virtualenv.pth   _virtualenv.py
   ```
   and `venv/Scripts/` contained only `python.exe` / `pythonw.exe` — no `hermes.exe`.
6. Desktop log:
   ```
   [bootstrap] no usable Hermes install at <root> and no published user-bin launcher
   [boot] Waiting for first-run setup choice
   ```
   i.e. it sits on the splash and presents first-run setup, which reads like the install is gone.
7. The gateway API was reachable but reported:
   ```json
   {"state":"draining","reason_code":"restart_wait","detail":null}
   ```

## Why it deadlocks

- **Updater**: pauses the gateway, then waits up to 190 s for it to exit.
- **Gateway**: receives a deferred restart, enters `draining`, and refuses to exit while `1 active work unit` is open — and that unit is the updater itself.

Neither side can break the wait, and neither has a diagnostic that names the other.

## Why it does not self-heal

- The venv is rebuilt **in place** (`uv venv` destroys the old environment first). Any interruption leaves a permanently half-built environment; there is no `.old` to roll back to.
- The stale markers are never aged out:
  - `.hermes-update-in-progress`
  - `.hermes-update-in-progress.lock`
  - `.hermes-update-paused-gateways.<hash>.json`
  - `.hermes-update-paused-gateways.lock`
  - `.restart_pending.json`
  - `.update_exit_code`
  
  As long as these exist, the gateway keeps trying to "finish" the update and stays in `draining`.
- The desktop's gateway-readiness deadline is short (~10 s) while a cold gateway start on a slow machine takes 30–40 s, so instead of a clear message it loops:
  ```
  Error: Gateway starting (deadline). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.
  [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
  ```

## Manual recovery that worked

```powershell
# 1. stop the updater
Stop-Process -Id <updater-pid> -Force

# 2. remove stale markers
$h = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes"
Remove-Item "$h\.hermes-update-in-progress", "$h\.hermes-update-in-progress.lock",
            "$h\.hermes-update-paused-gateways.*.json", "$h\.hermes-update-paused-gateways.lock",
            "$h\.restart_pending.json", "$h\.update_exit_code" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# 3. rebuild the venv contents in place
uv pip install -e . --python venv\Scripts\python.exe

# 4. kill leftover gateway processes, then start the gateway from the *interactive* session
#    (starting it from an SSH / session-0 context makes the desktop fail with gateway_other_session)
```

After step 3, `venv\Scripts\hermes.exe --version` works again and the desktop boots.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Atomic venv swap.** Build `venv.new`, install into it, then rename `venv` → `venv.old` and `venv.new` → `venv`. An interruption then leaves a usable environment (and a `venv.old` to fall back to).
2. **Journal the update stage.** One file with `{stage, pid, started_at, updated_at}`. On startup, if `stage != done`, the pid is gone, and the timestamp is stale, clear the markers and log an explicit "previous update was interrupted at stage X" instead of looping.
3. **Break the mutual wait.** Either exclude the updater from restart-blocking work units, or force-exit after `restart_drain_timeout` with a log line that names the blocking work unit.
4. **Distinguish "venv broken by interrupted update" from "no install".** Right now the desktop falls into first-run setup, which looks to the user like their installation was deleted.
5. **Make the gateway start deadline configurable** (or back off exponentially with a "gateway is still starting" state), rather than restarting the whole boot sequence.

## Related issues

- #103866 — stale legacy `.venv` sibling after venv rebuild
- #112977 — support Windows `.venv` update paths
- #122378 — Windows updater cannot close nested Python process trees
- #147398 — keep startup-deferred requests pending

issues.title: Webhook platform should default to loopback bind + warn on non-loopback
issues.body:
## Problem

The webhook platform binds to all interfaces by default. `webhook.py` has `DEFAULT_HOST = None`, so with no explicit host the listener is reachable from the entire LAN (verified live: `curl http://<lan-ip>:8644/health` → 200 JSON fingerprinting the Hermes gateway).

Today the unauthenticated surface is small (`/health` + HMAC-required POST routes), but `webhook_subscriptions.json` holds **agent-created dynamic routes that hot-reload on every POST** (`_reload_dynamic_routes`). One future subscription silently widens a listener most users never intended to expose — this conflicts with Hermes' otherwise local-first posture.

## Proposal

1. Default the webhook bind to `127.0.0.1`; require an explicit opt-in (config value or flag) for a non-loopback bind.
2. Emit a startup WARNING whenever binding non-loopback, ideally including which routes are currently live.

Existing guards (`_validate_route` HMAC requirement, `INSECURE_NO_AUTH` refused on non-loopback) are good and verified — this is about the default bind only.

## Workaround users can apply today

```yaml
platforms:
  webhook:
    extra:
      host: "127.0.0.1"
```

Found during an adversarial security audit of a local Hermes dashboard plugin (2026-11-06); happy to provide repro details.

issues.title: [Bug]: macOS desktop build fails on main since the pnpm switch — pnpm 12.15.0 silently drops the get-windows optional dependency
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Since the npm→pnpm workspace switch (commit 7062229), every Desktop app build on macOS fails, so the app stays on its old build and the update banner reports "Hermes runtime has been updated, but the Desktop app is still an older build".

Root cause: pnpm 12.15.0 (the pinned version) silently drops the `get-windows` optional dependency, while the desktop build validator hard-requires its macOS helper.

Expected: the desktop rebuild succeeds (or the missing optional helper degrades softly, as `stage-native-deps.mjs` itself documents).

### Steps to Reproduce

On macOS arm64 with upstream main (`ca436069`):

1. Run the desktop-triggered update (or `hermes desktop --force-build`).
2. "Preparing Node dependencies" exits 0 — but `get-windows@9.3.0` (an `optionalDependencies` entry of `apps/desktop`, present in `pnpm-lock.yaml`'s `apps/desktop` importer) is not installed: there is no `node_modules/.pnpm/get-windows*` directory and the install prints no warning. `node_modules/.pnpm` ends up with ~1045 packages, none of them get-windows.
3. The "Building desktop packaged app" step fails in `scripts/build/desktop.mjs` (`validateNativeTree`) with `Error: Prepared get-windows is missing its macOS helper`, and the update marks the desktop build as owed.

Standalone pnpm repro, independent of Hermes (clean temp dir, no workspace config):

```sh
mkdir t && cd t
printf '{"name":"t","version":"1.0.0","optionalDependencies":{"get-windows":"9.3.0"}}' > package.json
pnpm@12.15.0 install    # "Done", exit 0 — node_modules contains nothing but pnpm's lock marker
pnpm@10.15.1 install    # same package.json — installs get-windows + its ~129-package subtree fine
```

Contrasts under the same pnpm 12.15.0 (all install fine as optionalDependencies): `esbuild` (optional, has an install script), `left-pad`, `rollup` (optional with an optional platform subtree). Only get-windows is dropped.

### Expected Behavior

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs everything in the lockfile's importer sections, including `get-windows` — or at least fails loudly instead of exiting 0 with a missing dependency.

### Actual Behavior

1. pnpm 12.15.0 resolves get-windows (it is in the lockfile), downloads packages, then links nothing for it — `node_modules` has no get-windows, exit 0, zero warnings.
2. The desktop build then fails hard in `validateNativeTree` (`scripts/build/desktop.mjs`): `Prepared get-windows is missing its macOS helper`.
3. The update records "Desktop app build owed: desktop app build failed"; the running app stays on its pre-pnpm-switch build forever (until the pnpm layer changes).

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A

### Debug Report

Not uploaded — the failure reproduces outside the Hermes runtime with the 3-line standalone pnpm repro above, so a runtime debug bundle adds no signal, and a bundle would include recent conversation content. All evidence here is inline: repo log excerpt + the repro.

### Operating System

macOS 27.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon)

### Python Version

3.14.9

### Hermes Version

v0.23.0+162.gca43606 (install method: git, upstream main)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

Desktop update hand-off log (paths abbreviated):

```
[stage-native-deps] get-windows not installed (optional dep skipped for darwin-arm64); read_window_below will be unavailable in this build
    Error: Prepared get-windows is missing its macOS helper
        at validateNativeTree (.../scripts/build/desktop.mjs:24:11)
  Desktop app build owed: desktop app build failed
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- `get-windows@9.3.0` is declared under `optionalDependencies` in `apps/desktop/package.json` (line 167) and is present in the `apps/desktop` importer of `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- `scripts/build/node-deps.mjs` installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --trust-lockfile --prod=false --filter {./apps/desktop}...` (line 118) using pnpm 12.15.0, which is hard-pinned: any other pnpm version throws `pnpm 12.15.0 is required (root package.json devEngines)` (lines 112–115). So users cannot work around by using pnpm 10.
- pnpm 12.15.0 drops this specific package in a bare project with no repo config at all, so it is not caused by the workspace's `minimumReleaseAge`, `strictDepBuilds`/`allowBuilds`, or a registry mirror (reproduced against the official registry; get-windows@9.3.0 was published 2026-03-08, well outside the 14-day release-age window; it has no `os`/`cpu` restrictions and its own optionalDependencies (`node-gyp`, `@mapbox/node-pre-gyp`, `node-addon-api`) are universal packages).
- The build-side handling is internally inconsistent: `apps/desktop/scripts/stage-native-deps.mjs` treats a missing get-windows as degradable (its comment: "The runtime import already fails soft, so we disable only window enumeration instead of failing the entire Desktop build (which would strand users on an old version)"), but `scripts/build/desktop.mjs` `validateNativeTree` then fails the entire build for the same condition — exactly stranding users on an old build.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Either bump the pinned pnpm to a version that links this package, or align the two layers: since the stager already documents get-windows as fail-soft, `validateNativeTree` could treat a missing get-windows the same way (warn + build without it) instead of failing the build. Happy to test either on main.

Related reports: #134246 and #148345 cover get-windows install failures on Windows under `npm ci` — different platform and mechanism (npm-era); this report is the macOS pnpm-layer silent drop introduced by the npm→pnpm switch.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes for verification/testing on main; the fix itself (pnpm pin bump vs. validator policy) is a maintainer call.

issues.title: [Bug]: Kanban card "Worker log" stays empty under managed-worker mode (no tool trace, no progress)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Symptom

The dashboard's per-card **"Worker log"** is effectively empty while a worker runs under managed-worker mode. For a whole run it contains only:

```
Session: local-<id>
```

and at exit the last response plus the `[kanban-worker-exit] rc=N` trailer. No tool trace, no progress lines — so a running worker looks dead to an operator watching the card, and a crash loses the diagnostic tail.

Older one-shot/quiet workers produced 20–300 KB card logs carrying the full `Query: work kanban task …` trace.

## Evidence

Card `t_e85fe63d` log is 622 B (`Session:` + exit trailer + final reply), while its session has 18 messages in `profiles/worker/state.db`. `profiles/worker/logs/managed-worker.log` holds only warnings (reasoning-effort notices, Hindsight lines) and none of the tool trace.

Wiring:

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py:2877` — `log_f = _open_worker_log(task, board)` → `kanban/logs/<task>.log`, passed as `stdout=log_f, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`. For one-shot/quiet workers the card log therefore *did* carry the trace.
- `agent/managed_worker.py:447-448` — `os.dup2(sys.stderr.fileno(), sys.stdout.fileno())` after dup-ing the real stdout into the `WorkerChannel`. The card log therefore receives only what `hermes_cli/kanban_worker_client.py` prints: `Session:` (`:74`), last output (`:84`), exit trailer (`:96`).
- The managed worker's real stderr is drained by the owner into `gateway/session_managed_worker_log.py` → `<profile>/logs/managed-worker.log` (private, 0600, redacted, size-capped) — a different file from the card log, so the trace never reaches the dashboard.

## Reproduction

1. Configure `gateway.managed_workers: true` (the managed-worker path).
2. Dispatch a Kanban card to a worker and watch its card log (`hermes kanban log <task_id>`, or the dashboard "Worker log").
3. While the worker runs the log shows only `Session: <id>`; at exit, the last response and `[kanban-worker-exit] rc=N`. Tool calls and progress never appear.
4. Compare `wc -c <board>/kanban/logs/<task_id>.log` with the worker's session message count in `<profile>/state.db`.

## Impact

- Operators cannot see worker progress from the card; a healthy run is indistinguishable from a wedged one.
- Crash diagnostics lose the tail: the traceback that explains a failed worker lives in the private `managed-worker.log`, not on the card the operator is looking at.

## Proposed fix scope

Make the managed-worker stderr drain **also** append its redacted, size-capped lines to the owning task's card log while a Kanban task is bound, reusing the existing redaction/cap logic in `gateway/session_managed_worker_log.py`:

- keep `managed-worker.log` unchanged (same lines, same privacy, same rotation);
- write nothing new outside the existing card log;
- do not duplicate lines into a card log for non-Kanban managed workers;
- preserve the dispatcher's existing rotation in `hermes_cli/kanban_worker_log.py`.

PR to follow.

issues.title: [Feature]: WhatsApp bridge.log hardening: redact self-chat rejection IDs, keep libsignal session dumps out, rotate the file, exclude it from backups
issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Follow-up to a private report that the maintainers triaged as hardening rather than a vulnerability under SECURITY.md §3.1, with an invitation to file it as a regular issue. File permissions are already tracked in #80090 (PRs #80137, #86304); this issue covers the rest.

On a git install (v0.21.5, early October 2026) running the bundled Baileys bridge in `self-chat` mode, after about five months `bridge.log` contained:

- 26 `Closing session: SessionEntry` dumps with `privKey`, `rootKey`, `baseKey` and `remoteIdentityKey`. They are printed to the console by the Signal-protocol library inside Baileys, and the adapter captures the bridge's stdout/stderr verbatim.
- 1,567 lines `{"event":"ignored","reason":"self_chat_mode_rejects_non_self","chatId":...,"senderId":...}` with the full `@lid` IDs of every other chat on the linked personal account, including `status@broadcast`. In self-chat mode the bridge is a linked device of the owner's own account, so these lines are not a record of people contacting the bot: together they are a list of the owner's contacts and groups.
- No message text (checked field by field).

The file had never been rotated (created in May) and was included in every `pre-update-*.zip`, together with the session directory.

Still present on `main @ ca436069` (2026-11-05):

- `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js:656-662`: the self-chat rejection writes raw `chatId`/`senderId`. The debug events nearby already pass IDs through `redactWhatsAppId()` (for example lines 569-570 and 640-641). The rejection lines are not gated by `WHATSAPP_DEBUG`, so turning debug off does not stop them.
- `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py:767-768`: `bridge.log` is opened in append mode with no size cap or rotation, while Hermes's own logs use `RotatingFileHandler` (`hermes_logging.py`).
- `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/`: no filter on library console output, so the `SessionEntry` dumps would still reach the file. Not re-tested live: the device was unlinked right after the finding.
- `hermes_cli/backup.py`: nothing excludes `bridge.log` from full or pre-update backups (`_EXCLUDED_NAMES` at line 132).

### Proposed Solution

1. Self-chat rejections: pass `chatId`/`senderId` through `redactWhatsAppId()`, as the debug events do, or count them instead of logging each one (as #92683 did for bot mode).
2. Keep library output with session state out of the log: drop or redact console lines that carry `SessionEntry` dumps before they reach stdout, for example by wrapping `console.log`/`console.info` in `bridge.js` before Baileys is loaded.
3. Size-cap and rotate `bridge.log`, for example rotating on bridge spawn above a few MB and keeping one or two generations.
4. Exclude `platforms/whatsapp/bridge.log` (and the legacy `whatsapp/bridge.log`) from full and pre-update backups: it is troubleshooting output, not state needed for a restore.

### Alternatives Considered

- Operator-side `logrotate`: handles size, but not what gets written, and the backups still copy whatever is there.
- Setting `WHATSAPP_DEBUG=false`: does not help, because the rejection lines and the library console output are written regardless.
- Documentation only: the WhatsApp docs already say to protect the session directory like a password; the log silently copies part of that material out of it.

### Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

issues.title: Windows: PM file operations fail on paths over 260 characters (copy, walk, digest, delete)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: area/install-update
labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

labels.name: os/windows
labels.description: Native Windows behaviour or breakage: PowerShell install, Windows paths, cmd.exe, WSL-vs-native diff

issues.body:
## Summary

On a default Windows machine (`LongPathsEnabled=0`), any PM file operation on a path longer than 260 characters fails with `WinError 3` / `WinError 206`. #130232 (plugin enable copying the bundled Python tree) and #129299 (`hermes update` ZIP extraction) are two instances. This issue covers the whole class: PM copies, walks, hashes, renames and deletes trees with plain paths, and both the source (inside the MSIX install root) and the destination (under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`) can be deep.

## Measured (installed 0.0.4 arm64 on a Windows test box, 109,476 payload files)

The install root uses 100 characters before any payload file:
`C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\NousResearch.HermesChannelcc56c86e12ff1dd6_0.0.4.0_arm64__e60prshbsznhj\` (+ `app\resources\agent-payload\` = 129).

Same file list, recomputed under each identity's install root:

| Identity | Root | Files > 260 | Not `__pycache__` | In `tools\python-*` (#130232) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| channel `HermesChannel<token>` 0.0.4.0 | 100 | 533 | 139 | 17 |
| stable `HermesBundled` 2026.9.24.0 | 88 | 139 | 56 | 0 |
| canary `HermesBundledCanary` | 94 | 253 | 82 | 2 |
| commit build `HermesBundledCommit<sha7>` | 101 | 617 | 159 | 22 |

Per tree (channel identity): `venv` 396 over (33 not cache, all `elevenlabs`), `uv-cache` 94 (all not cache, `elevenlabs` wheel archive), `tools\npm-*` 9, `tools\node-*` 3, `tools\python-*` 17 (all `__pycache__`), `hermes-agent` 14 (all `__pycache__`). Longest: `venv\Lib\site-packages\elevenlabs\text_to_speech\types\body_text_to_speech_streaming_with_timestamps_v_1_text_to_speech_voice_id_stream_with_timestamps_post_apply_text_normalization.py` = 313 characters (209 inside the payload).

Conclusions from the numbers:
- A stable identity removes the #130232 failure by 12 characters of luck, not by design. 139 files are still over.
- Third-party package paths (209 characters inside the payload) exceed 260 under any install root. Shorter bundle names cannot fix them.
- The destination side adds the user name and the store layout (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\tools\.staging-XXXXXXXX\tree\...`), which the bundler does not control. Plugin dependencies installed later are not in the bundle at all.

## Where (main @ 234badf401)

Plain-path tree operations in `pm/`: `install.py:328` (`copytree`, the #130232 site), `packages.py:334` (`copytree`), `store.py:318` (`os.walk` in `tree_digest`), `package.py:242` (`os.walk` in verify), `build_operations.py:124` (`os.walk`), and `rmtree` at `cli.py:505`, `environment.py:250`, `environments.py:80`, `install.py:234`, `operations.py:114,317`, `packages.py:445,669,888`, `runtime.py:168,210`, `store.py:228,385,412`, `uv_cache_prune.py:50`. The `hermes update` extractor (#129299) is the same pattern outside `pm/`.

There is no long-path helper in the tree today (`git grep` for `\\?\` / `LongPathsEnabled` / `MAX_PATH` finds only `agent/file_safety.py` path-classification comments and a build-time cache-length note in `scripts/bundles/desktop_toolchain.py:182-183`).

## Approaches (to decide)

- Long-path-safe file operations in PM on Windows (`\\?\` extended-length form) for every copy / walk / digest / rename / delete, through one helper.
- Skip `__pycache__` when copying trees (matches `tree_digest`, which already ignores it). Fixes #130232 alone.
- Avoid the copy: reference bundled tool entries in place instead of copying them into the user store.
- Shorter bundle names (tool entry names, `agent-payload`). Margin only.
- A build-time audit that reports the longest payload path under the longest expected install root.

## Verify

A Windows machine with `LongPathsEnabled=0` and an MSIX install: enable `nvidia-app` (#130232), run a venv rebuild that reads `uv-cache` (the `elevenlabs` archive), and run `hermes update` (#129299). All three complete. A Windows-marked test per helper path with a > 260 character tree.

Related: #130232, #129299, #105649 (`claw migrate` copying `node_modules`, same class).

prs.title: catalog: add zaprite (payments with a fresh-approval gate)
prs.body:
## What it is

`zaprite` lets a merchant get paid from a Hermes chat. One sentence in, one `checkoutUrl` out; the
payer opens it and pays by card, bank, Lightning, on-chain bitcoin, or stablecoin — whichever rails
the organisation has already connected. Then the plugin re-fetches the order until it is paid.

**27 tools**: orders (create, get, list, watch, update, quote), invoices, saved payment profiles,
contacts, payment links (read), tickets (list, get, issue, check-in), webhooks (list, create,
delete), reporting (`report`, `list_overdue`), setup (`doctor`), and two handoffs for the gaps the
API cannot write (`bridge_handoff`, `sovereign_rails`).

## Surfaces used

- `register_tool` ×27, toolset `zaprite`
- `pre_tool_call` — approval escalation and cron refusal (see below)
- `register_command` — `/zaprite status|setup|doctor|help`
- `register_skill` ×3 — `zaprite`, `zaprite-checkout-wizard`, `zaprite-sovereign`
- `register_automation_blueprint` — `zaprite-paid-digest`, read-only daily report
- `register_cli_command` — `hermes zaprite status|doctor`
- `plugin_db("zaprite")` — a local ledger of orders this plugin created

## Why it is more than a skill

A write needs **a fresh human yes for that exact call**. `pre_tool_call` returns
`{"action": "approve"}`, which escalates to Hermes' approval gate; it never grants. The handler then
refuses before building an HTTP client if no human approval was recorded (10-minute TTL):

> `Refused before any request was sent. This Zaprite write needs a fresh human approval for this
> exact call. A previous session or always answer does not cover the next one. YOLO, approvals off,
> smart (model) approval, cron, and a skipped prompt do not count.`

Cron is blocked in the hook **and** the handler. There is a spend cap denominated in the order's own
smallest unit (cents for USD, sats for BTC), a read-only-key probe that creates nothing, and
`/zaprite kill` to pause every write while lookups continue.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Network.** `https://api.zaprite.com` only. `User-Agent: zaprite-hermes/0.1.0`. No telemetry.
- **Money.** A full-access key can open real checkouts and charge a saved payment profile. It cannot
  refund.
- **Email.** Receipts stay off unless asked; Zaprite's API default is on.
- **Tickets.** Issuing can incur Zaprite's ticket fee (1% + $3 per ticket).
- **Webhooks.** Payloads are id-only and unsigned. Every watch and get re-fetches the order; the
  plugin never treats a delivery as proof of payment. It does not run a webhook receiver.
- **Local state.** Orders it creates sit in `plugin_db("zaprite")`. The API key is not stored there.
- **Credentials.** Read only through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret("ZAPRITE_API_KEY")`.
- **Fees.** API-created orders carry Zaprite's 1% (cap $15) on bitcoin and Tether; fiat uses the
  merchant's own processor.
- **Browser automation.** None. `bridge_handoff` returns one URL and a note.

## Verification

- `pytest -q` → **68 passed**; a second CI job patches `socket.connect` to raise, and it still passes,
  so the suite cannot start depending on the network.
- `hermes plugins validate .` → **Validation passed** (security scan `safe`, no core override).
- Live: `hermes zaprite doctor` → `ok: true`, `key_mode: full`; a real API order was created and
  re-fetched by `externalUniqId`; an invoice was created with a contact and returned number.
- CI matrix: Python 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13.

Full record, including what was **not** verified (no sandbox-org payment, no completed settlement):
`docs/verification.md`.

## Known issues

- Zaprite has no API for connections, checkout edits, payment-link creation, recurring invoices,
  refunds, or webhook signatures. The plugin says so rather than pretending.
- `zaprite_create_invoice` marks an invoice `SENT`; Zaprite does not reliably email it. Hand over the
  `checkoutUrl`.

Repo: https://github.com/welliv/zaprite-hermes (MIT), tag `v0.1.0`, pinned at
`04dd6325b9921aa5e4b7b1d0eebe36c2b470758d`.

prs.title: feat(plugins): filter final tool results
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Add an opt-in `filter_tool_result` plugin hook at the shared final executor
commit. An output-inspection plugin can now adopt text before spill files,
model context and completion UI receive it, covering registry and inline tools,
errors, timeouts and cancellation outcomes in both executors.

The existing `transform_tool_result` hook is a best-effort transform with
first-string semantics. This adds a final policy stage after those transforms
and guardrail observations, using the existing bounded callback runner and
plugin ownership registry. Filters compose in registration order; each sees
its predecessor's adopted result. A callback failure or invalid return
withholds the complete result with a fixed error placeholder. AW's separate
sec-core adapter is the concrete consumer; no vendor implementation is added.

## Related Issue

Related to #138538. #138547 addresses chaining the existing transform hook;
this PR leaves that contract intact and adds final delivery inspection.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- Register `filter_tool_result` and reuse bounded callback dispatch with copied
  payloads, preventing a timed-out callback from mutating adopted data.
- Apply it in `_commit_tool_result` before result persistence and UI/model
  delivery. Early spinner completion omits unchecked result-derived text.
- Document ordering, replacement, failure, timeout suppression and scope.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_final_tool_result_filter.py
   tests/agent/test_tool_call_incremental_persistence.py
   tests/agent/test_multimodal_tool_result_spill.py
   tests/plugins/test_transform_tool_result_hook.py -q`
2. `python scripts/check`

46 targeted tests passed, including 16 new cases. Tests discover a real plugin,
exercise sequential/concurrent/inline execution, real SQLite and completion
callbacks, native timeout/cancellation result paths, and a local HTTP model
transport. An event-driven timeout case verifies payload isolation and native
suppression. The delivery invariant fails on the base commit. The model and
tool results are deterministic fixtures; no hosted inference is needed.

## Checklist

Existing configurations and best-effort transforms keep their behavior. This

prs.title: feat(skills): add Bark iOS push as optional skill (salvage #47091)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Salvages #47091 by @Randool: adds a Bark skill for push notifications to iOS devices,
as an **optional** skill (`optional-skills/productivity/bark/`).

The original commit is cherry-picked unchanged so authorship is preserved; follow-up
commits move it and address the review on #47091.

## Why optional-skills

Bark is iOS-only. Per CONTRIBUTING (bundled skills should be broadly useful) and
`skills/AGENTS.md` (niche skills go to `optional-skills/`), it is installable via
`hermes skills install official/productivity/bark` instead of loading for everyone.

## Changes vs #47091

- Removed the end-to-end encryption claim (no tested path existed).
- Added `scripts/bark_push.py` (stdlib only): JSON POST, correct UTF-8 handling,
  `--dry-run`, non-zero exit on rejected pushes, device key never printed.
- `BARK_TOKEN` is the only env var (secret) and is read from the environment only —
  there is no command-line flag for it, so the key cannot land in shell history, a
  process list or a tool transcript.
- The server URL is skill config (`metadata.hermes.config` → `skills.config.bark.server`),
  not an env var; `BARK_SERVER` is not read anywhere.
- Withdrawal (`--id <id> --delete`) sends only `id` and `delete`, as Bark's parameter
  documentation requires; it no longer demands a body.
- Read timeouts, `OSError` and `http.client.HTTPException` are reported as a redacted
  `BarkError` instead of a traceback.
- Added `tests/skills/test_bark_skill.py` (31 hermetic tests, no network), including
  coverage that the device key never reaches stdout or stderr on any error path.
- Generated docs entries required by the skill docs contract.
- Mapped the original commit's author email in `contributors/emails/` so the
  attribution check passes for the cherry-picked commit.

## How to test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_bark_skill.py -q
  → 1 file, 31 tests passed, 0 failed

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_skill_docs_contract.py tests/skills/test_authoring_standards.py -q
  → 2 files, 1492 tests passed, 0 failed

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills -q
  → 34 files, 1782 tests passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (windows-only lane)

python scripts/check
  → scripts/check: 12 checks, ok

python website/scripts/check_doc_links.py
  → OK: no route-style links in hand-authored docs.

python3 optional-skills/productivity/bark/scripts/bark_push.py \
  --title "Hermes" --body "报告完成：3 个测试失败 & 2 个跳过/共 5 个" --dry-run
  → {"title": "Hermes", "body": "报告完成：3 个测试失败 & 2 个跳过/共 5 个"}

python3 optional-skills/productivity/bark/scripts/bark_push.py \
  --id build-42 --delete --dry-run
  → {"id": "build-42", "delete": "1"}
```

Manually verified delivery and withdrawal on a physical iPhone: a push returned
`{"code":200,"message":"success"}` and appeared on the device; sending the same `id`
with `--delete` returned 200 and removed the notification (Bark delivers the deletion
as a silent push, so Background App Refresh must be enabled).

Supersedes #47091.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add visor — live agent canvas with turnkey server
prs.body:
## What it does

**Visor** — a live holographic canvas for AI agents. The plugin registers a single `visor_push` tool: agents push visual blocks (sections, markdown findings, clickable todos, tables, KPI stats, charts, code, images, audio, video, connectors between blocks) to an infinite-canvas page that updates **in place over SSE** — agents show work instead of dumping it in chat.

v1.8 is self-contained: the plugin ships its own server copy (`hermes/plugin/server/`), so `hermes plugins install visor` is the whole setup — no clone, no Docker required.

## Hermes surfaces used

- Host plugin; `register()` → `register_tool("visor_push")` only. No hooks, no middleware, no config schema, no required env vars.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Auto-start:** on first use, if nothing listens on `localhost:8900`, the plugin starts the server — bare-python subprocess of the bundled `server.py` by default (state in `~/.local/share/visor`, override `VISOR_DATA`); `VISOR_DOCKER=1` uses `docker compose up -d` instead. Long-running background process; re-started if unreachable.
- **Network:** server binds `127.0.0.1:8900` only (override `VISOR_PORT`); optional `VISOR_TOKEN` gates `/api/*` and `/media/*`.
- **Modules:** bundled server boots with `live` + `chat` modules (override `VISOR_MODULES`). `live` polls user-pushed URLs (http(s)-only, 10 s timeout, 1 MB cap, bounded 2 s-tick pool, optional `VISOR_LIVE_LOCAL_HOSTS` allowlist). `chat` bridges card sends to a configured Hermes webhook (`VISOR_CHAT_URL` + `VISOR_CHAT_SECRET`) — inert until configured.
- **No credential reads;** no env reads beyond `VISOR_*` / `HOLO_PORT`; no file reads outside the plugin tree and its own state dir. `VISOR_HOME` (legacy dev-checkout layout) is optional.

## Screenshots

Board's own PNG export (P-key export) + viewport shot (tabs, minimap, HUD) in the gallery.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add fledge plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/fledge.yaml`, for **Fledge**: skills have to earn their wings. It's my entry for the Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon. The plugin lives in my own repository, [12burb/hermes-fledge](https://github.com/12burb/hermes-fledge) ([pinned tree](https://github.com/12burb/hermes-fledge/tree/ac65b416d34381acba8642133cfa1d286e052028)). I am the repository owner (rule 5).

Hermes' self-improvement loop saves skills based on the agent's own judgment of whether a task went well. In [Kilo's read of 1,300+ r/openclaw comments](https://kilo.ai/openclaw/vs-hermes), the first two complaints listed about Hermes are that self-evaluation always passes ("It always thinks it did a good job", +107) and that self-improvement overwrites manual edits.

Fledge gates `skill_manage` on evidence from the run a skill was learned from, using only facts Hermes reports through hooks:
- tools still failing when the turn ended, judged per program, including the exit status a compound shell command prints for itself;
- failed or interrupted turns;
- the user's next message correcting the agent;
- `/undo`, `/retry` or a `/rollback` restore right after;
- denied approvals.

No model grades the model.

- **Save gate.** A skill learned from a bad run is held in Hermes' own skills pending queue, with the reasons. Users review it with the stock `/skills pending|diff|approve|reject`, or with `/fledge pending|diff|approve|reject`, which also works in messaging chats. A foreground save after errors goes through Hermes' approval prompt; unattended runs queue instead of waiting.
- **Probation.** New and rewritten skills are fledglings. Clean real runs graduate them and repeated bad runs ground them. A save from a run the user corrected right after is grounded at once. A grounded skill Hermes created on its own is archived (recoverable with `hermes curator restore`); skills the user asked for are only reported.
- **Hand-edit protection.** Skills the user edited by hand are fingerprinted. An autonomous rewrite or delete of one becomes a proposal in the same queue; an attended rewrite asks first (optionally with Hermes' content lock).

**Not a duplicate (rule 16).** skill-lineage records where skill content came from and never blocks; provenance-gate checks quoted user decisions; jev-curator governs curator consolidation; pending-queue-monitor is a read-only Desktop view of the queue; memory-rewind keeps version history. None of them judges a skill by how the run it came from actually went, or holds, probates and grounds it.

### Hermes surfaces it uses

- **Nine hooks:** `pre_llm_call`, `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, `on_session_end`, `on_session_finalize`, `on_session_reset`, `on_skill_lifecycle`, `pre_command`, `post_approval_response`.
- **`pre_tool_call`** acts on `skill_manage` only; every other tool returns at once. It returns `block` (held) or `approve` (Hermes' own prompt with a `rule_key`). It never grants anything (rule 12). `post_approval_response` is an observer, and Fledge ignores answers to its own `plugin_rule:fledge:*` prompts.
- **Commands and plumbing:** `register_command` (`/fledge`), `register_cli_command` (`hermes fledge`), `post_message` for chat notices, `get_config`/`set_config`, `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_db`.
- **Footprint:** no tools, no middleware, no core patches (`no core override` passes).
- **Undocumented imports (the validate warnings), and why.** There is no public seam yet for:
  1. the skill write origin, needed to tell the background-review fork from a foreground turn (`tools.skill_provenance.get_current_write_origin`);
  2. staging a write into the review queue (`tools.write_approval.stage_write` / `list_pending` / `get_pending` / `skill_gist` and `hermes_cli.write_approval_commands.handle_pending_subcommand`);
  3. curator actions (`tools.skill_usage.archive_skill` / `set_locked` / `get_record`).

  All of these calls live in `bridge.py`, each guarded, so a moved function disables one feature (reported by `/fledge doctor`) and never breaks a turn. I checked all 17 against v0.23.0 and v0.22.7: same signatures. Happy to move to a public `ctx.skills` facade if you want one.

### Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Reads:** hook payloads (tool statuses and error text, and the first 280 characters of the next user message to spot a correction) and skill folders, to fingerprint them.
- **Writes:** its own SQLite under `plugin-data/fledge`. That holds skill names, fingerprints, session and turn ids, verdict reasons quoting the matched correction phrase and up to 80 characters of a tool error, and hold summaries with the skill's one-line description. No other message text and no skill bodies are stored.
- **Other writes:** held writes go into `pending/skills/`, and grounded agent-created skills are archived into `skills/.archive/`.
- **Never:** network calls, model calls, credentials, shell commands, background processes or telemetry. It never approves anything.
- **On its own errors, the gate lets the write through, with two deliberate exceptions.** A write already queued for review stays held, so it is never both saved and queued. An autonomous rewrite of a hand-edited skill is never let through.
- **Needs `plugins.isolation: in_process`** (the default) for full accuracy. `/fledge doctor` says so otherwise.

## Related Issue

None: a new catalog entry (Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (catalog entry only)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/fledge.yaml`: new entry pinned to `ac65b416d34381acba8642133cfa1d286e052028`, version `0.1.0`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.7"` (`tools.skill_usage.set_locked` first appears in 0.22.7; the same floor is in `plugin.yaml`).

## How to Test

1. `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/fledge.yaml` gives `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.
2. `hermes plugins validate <clone at the pinned sha> --install-deps` gives `Validation passed.` The only warnings are the private imports listed above.
3. In a throwaway profile, run `hermes plugins install fledge --enable`, then `/fledge doctor` (all six checks ok).
4. With the files in [`demo/`](https://github.com/12burb/hermes-fledge/tree/ac65b416d34381acba8642133cfa1d286e052028/demo): `Run ./fetch_water.sh and turn what it returns into results.csv. The server is flaky, so retry once if it fails.`, then `/refine save the procedure for pulling water results as a skill`. Expect `🪶 Fledge: held skill '…'`, with the hold listed in `/skills pending` and `/fledge pending`.

**Tested.** 150 unit and flow tests pass on Python 3.14 and 3.11. `hermes plugins doctor --ci` and `hermes plugins validate` pass on Hermes **0.23.0** and **0.22.7** (Windows 11 ARM64). I also ran live sessions with a real model (glm-5.3) in throwaway HERMES_HOMEs.

- **On 0.23.0, installed with `hermes plugins install 12burb/hermes-fledge`:**
  - all three demo beats: a bad-run save held (origin `review`); a save grounded and archived after a real correction; an autonomous rewrite of a hand-edited skill turned into a proposal;
  - approving a hold put the skill on probation;
  - a foreground rewrite of a hand-edited skill raised Hermes' approval prompt;
  - `/undo` right after a turn held the save from it;
  - with Hermes' review queue made unwritable, the save landed on probation instead of being lost;
  - mistyped settings fall back to defaults and `/fledge doctor` names them.
- **On 0.22.7:**
  - all three demo beats;
  - watch mode;
  - 13 clean review writes with 0 holds;
  - fail-open under a locked database.

I found and fixed 21 bugs along the way, each with a test. Results are in [VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/12burb/hermes-fledge/blob/ac65b416d34381acba8642133cfa1d286e052028/VALIDATION.md), and the raw output is in [tests/smoke-2026-11-05.txt](https://github.com/12burb/hermes-fledge/blob/ac65b416d34381acba8642133cfa1d286e052028/tests/smoke-2026-11-05.txt).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I searched for existing PRs and catalog entries: no `fledge` entry or PR
- [x] My PR contains **only** the catalog entry (one file)
- [x] Commit message follows Conventional Commits (`feat(plugin-catalog): add fledge plugin`)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q`: N/A, no Hermes code changed (the plugin's own 150 tests pass)
- [x] `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes at the pinned commit; declared hooks match registrations; `security scan: safe`; `no core override`; no binaries or `.pyc` in the tree
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ARM64, Hermes 0.23.0 and 0.22.7

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] The plugin README at the pinned commit documents install, settings, commands, known limits and disclosures
- [x] Cross-platform: pure Python, stdlib only, no platform-specific code

## Screenshots / Logs

Raw session output: [tests/smoke-2026-11-05.txt](https://github.com/12burb/hermes-fledge/blob/ac65b416d34381acba8642133cfa1d286e052028/tests/smoke-2026-11-05.txt). Demo video (under 90 s, on X): will be linked here when posted.
