prs.title: fix(state): fence session ownership across profile stores
prs.body:
## Current revision

The four [new findings](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6676853430) are fixed in `dcdf4190f0a3`. Hosted CI requires maintainer action at the preceding head; acceptance remains pending. The complete repository suite is not claimed green.

- Gateway repoints fence the exact compression CTE plus receipt owners, earlier reset segments and title heads. Boot receipt healing uses the same complete write-set discovery.
- Recoverable unarchive validates every row selected by its actual archive UPDATE and rechecks the chosen tip inside the writer transaction.
- Ambiguous legacy display reads use the existing read-only projection; actual writes still refuse, and inventory/SQLite errors propagate.
- Apply reads inventory-only tombstones without writable acquisition or migration. Current, legacy and minimally readable legacy schemas are covered while live targets remain repairable.

Evidence at `dcdf4190f0a3` (Linux, canonical runner, one worker, zero file retries):

- RED commit `9fa7fda00b43`: **15 failed / 19 passed**, unchanged starting production source. GREEN: all **34** new cases pass.
- **891 passed**, all **30 changed Python test files**; the known real-home guard case is excluded and disclosed. The first concurrent run timed out in the large TUI file with incomplete failure output; only that file was rerun in isolation with zero retries and passed. Both receipts are retained; no assertion failure reproduced in the serial run.
- **182 passed** across **14 affected consumer suites**, including real gateway handoff/restart, compression, recovery, reactions and display reads.
- **14/14 native checks passed** with the explicit inspected PR base.
- Additional controls prove the eight-attempt expansion cap leaves rows/receipts unchanged and all five routing/receipt IDs stay locked through actual COMMIT. Trigger-induced rollback, three-segment owner conflicts, forks/resets, ambiguous writer refusal and stale move/relabel/sever/rekey plans are exercised.
- Fresh baseline diagnostic retains ten known failure IDs. Pinned upstream historical proof and its latest nine-failure/model-projection variance are preserved; the full suite remains unproven.

A fresh independent reviewer could not run because its provider quota was exhausted. Parent semantic review covered the changed helpers and all their callers; independent acceptance is still pending. Native Windows/macOS execution is untested. Upstream base refresh remains required before merge.

---

The earlier PR scope and revision-specific evidence follow.

## What does this PR do?

Session IDs retain one writable owner across profile stores, including compression publication, imports, interrupted adoption and recoverable lineage resurrection. Ambiguous ownership and unreadable inventories fail closed; repair reports existing duplicates without choosing or merging an owner.

An adoption now keeps the complete transfer membership through partial donor retirement:

```text
lock the complete member set
validate donor, target and saved lifecycle evidence
commit imported rows and immutable membership together
retire every recorded donor member and verify completion
```

Profile resume continues only a saved default-store transfer that requested retirement. Copy-only requests retain their intent, and completed transfers do not repeat adoption.

## Related Issue

Fixes #149131 (continued from #148762).

Addresses [the four-path review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6645990092) and [the worker-publish follow-up](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6649586444).

Addresses [the lock-set follow-up](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6668658012) and [the recoverable-unarchive tip follow-up](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6662897210). That review confirms the original four cases and reports 799 passing changed-file tests at the preceding head.

The preceding revision addresses [the linked-repair, retired-display and ancestor-reaction findings](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6673125057). That review confirms the preceding lock fixes, 835 changed-file tests and 14 native checks at `b404ea7195f1`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

## Changes Made

- Hold complete locally connected components around excluded `dual_home` rows, including unkeyed links. Revalidate component membership and ownership before move, relabel, sever or rekey actions; unrelated repairable components still proceed.
- Keep retired non-owner legacy display reads on the existing read-only fallback. Inventory and SQLite errors remain visible, and the live owner still backfills its display index.
- Revalidate the full verified resume lineage before both reaction writers, retaining guards through commit. Bounded expansion releases earlier locks; explicit branch/reset boundaries remain intact.

- Guard valid `compression.publish` child IDs through the real receipt transaction while retaining malformed-input and other-operation validation.
- Guard all import payload IDs through commit; retain permanent deletion fences and batch limits in shared import validation. Profile moves also respect target deletion markers.
- Share physical-store inventory with repair, including tombstoned profiles, without requiring an absent default database to exist.
- Save immutable, generation-bound adoption membership with original lineage/lifecycle evidence and target-history fingerprints. Reject wrong donors, third copies, incomplete/unsupported records and failed authoritative reads.
- Release prior member locks before bounded rediscovery. Refuse mixed managed/standalone pairs and unverifiable store resolution.
- Retry approved partial adoption through the actual profile-resume RPC, rechecking retirement intent under locks and in the transaction. Preserve the journal during separate-output database recovery.
- Validate the resolved compression tip's owner before recoverable unarchive changes any archive/end stamp. Release the earlier lock set before bounded expansion; unstable discovery fails closed.
- Clear the lineage archive flags and recovered tip end stamp in one transaction, so a failing final UPDATE rolls back every archive change.
- Close advisory lock descriptors on acquisition, validation and unlock failures. Use 32 fixed lock stripes, individual-ID owner checks and a single ordered batch acquisition for import and repair; reject nested lock-order inversions.
- Pass each writer's actual SQLite patience to its lineage guard and share one acquisition deadline across the complete lock set and process/advisory phases.
- Keep required topical extractions within file/complexity ratchets; preserve API facade limit overrides at call time.

## How to Test

1. In a temporary managed home, publish a worker compression child whose ID already exists in a sibling store. The operation rejects without creating a local child or advancing its server receipt, parent or assignment.
2. Move an initially local import ID into a sibling immediately before guard entry. Import rejects without recreating it in the original store.
3. Tombstone a duplicate-bearing profile and run `hermes sessions repair-profiles --json`. The report names the blocking physical store and changes no database bytes.
4. Fail retirement of the first or a later compression member, then retry by root/tip or through profile `session.resume`. Complete membership is retained, all donors retire, and the target tip is writable. Copy-only intent and stale-hint controls prevent unauthorized retirement.
5. Seed an archived local `root -> tip` with recoverable tip end reason and an existing live `tip` in a sibling store. `unarchive_recoverable_session("root")` rejects with `SessionIdOwnedElsewhereError`, preserving both stores. An uncontested lineage still reopens, and expanded acquisition starts after earlier locks are released.

Key regressions live in `test_worker_receipt_lineage.py`, `test_fence_review_regressions.py`, `test_adoption_transfer_records.py`, `test_adoption_transfer_safety.py`, `test_adoption_transfer_concurrency.py`, `test_adoption_store_identity.py`, and `test_adoption_retirement_resume.py`.

The new follow-up is covered by `test_recoverable_unarchive_fencing.py`. Its foreign-tip behavior reproduces on `fbe1b7a3df18` with `DID NOT RAISE`; the separate lock-expansion control checks release before reacquisition.

The final outgoing import/inventory/retry tests fail at the intended behavior on original head `44202f9`; the real registered-worker publish test fails separately. Development also reproduced the record, deletion, generation, batch-limit and real-resume failures before their fixes.

The added `test_recoverable_unarchive_adversarial.py` ports the independent model audit's 14 cases. Its atomicity trigger regression fails on `2cdf451c4b66` (13 pass, 1 fail) and passes after `b361e91bf1d3` (14 pass). `test_session_lineage_lock_contracts.py` adds 20 descriptor, contention, low-FD 128/500-session batch, ordering, reentrancy, collision and interruption controls. Ten initial lock regressions fail on `b361e91bf1d3`; all 20 pass at `b404ea7195f1`.

The latest follow-up adds `test_repair_lineage_exclusions.py` and `test_lineage_display_ownership.py`. At failing-test commit `f20838729b53`, the two suites report **8 passed / 14 failed** against the old production code. The fixed source at `42e46dbb72a1` passes all **22** cases. An existing partial-repair test now requires linked children to remain held around a duplicated parent, preserving their parent pointers rather than moving them around the excluded row. Eleven affected repair, display and reaction suites pass **106** tests.

Linux validation uses `scripts/run_tests.sh` with declared test/messaging/ACP/MCP dependencies, isolated homes, per-file subprocesses and no file retries. On current head `42e46dbb72a1`:

- All **28 changed test files: 857 passed, 0 failed**, excluding the separately reproduced real-home I/O guard case.
- The recovery/adversarial/ownership files, including all 14 ported adversarial cases, are included in this current run. The separately quoted required three-file command passed 29 tests at the preceding checkpoint.
- All **14 `scripts/check --commit HEAD --base c5f347ebe9b8` checks pass**, with zero blocking or advisory health findings.
- Hosted [CI](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/42142307534), [Docker](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/42142307526) and [Nix](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/42142307556) at `42e46dbb72a1` report `action_required`; upstream workflow action and review acceptance remain pending.
- The fresh eight-file baseline comparison has **113 passed / 10 failed on the candidate** and **114 passed / 9 failed on untouched pinned upstream `7f42573b64e8`**. Nine failure IDs match. The model-projection case `test_model_options_uses_frozen_selection_without_composer_global_writes` passes in the latest upstream run but has preserved, hash-bound failure evidence on that same unchanged upstream commit. Both upstream outcomes are retained; no rerun was used to force matching results. The known real-home guard case fails on both sides.

Earlier checkpoints, before the recoverable-unarchive follow-up:

- Full state coverage: **1,885 passed, 0 failed, 16 platform-specific skips**.
- Broad gateway/TUI integration: **4,223 passed, 20 failed, 6 skipped** across 555 files. Ten failures reproduce unchanged on untouched upstream in the same environment. prs.title: fix(email): read the requested UID's FETCH reply, not whatever came f…
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`_imap_payload()` reads `data[0][1]`, but imaplib returns every FETCH reply it has buffered, not just ours. RFC 3501 allows untagged FETCH replies after any command, so when the server sends one first (e.g. `* 1 FETCH (FLAGS (\Seen))` after another client read message 1), the header fetch for a new message looks empty. The adapter logs `Unusable pre-authorization headers`, stores `\Seen` and drops the message silently. If another message's literal comes first, that message is read in place of ours.

The fix makes `_imap_payload()` take the literal from the reply that names the requested UID, at both the header and the RFC822 fetch.

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue. Related: #143039 (retries a message listed `UNSEEN` before it can be served — complementary, different lines), #98597 (iCloud `RFC822` returns no literal; not fixed by this), #81429 (same `data[0]` assumption on the RFC822 path, reported with AgentMail), #41340, #18106, #80032.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/email.py`: `_imap_payload()` selects the reply naming the requested UID.
- `tests/gateway/test_email_robustness.py`: `test_replies_ahead_of_the_requested_uid_are_ignored`.
- Compatibility: RFC 3501 requires `UID` in every `UID FETCH` reply. A literal whose reply names no UID (servers that put `UID` after the literal, and the shapes existing tests use) is still used when no reply names the requested UID. Replies naming another UID are never used.
- Known limit: no help when the server sends no literal for the UID at all (#98597, #143039's case). Reproduced against a scripted server; no provider trace of the flag-update case.

## How to Test

1. Run a scripted local IMAP server that sends `* 1 FETCH (FLAGS (\Seen))` while answering `UID SEARCH UNSEEN`, and run real `imaplib` + `EmailAdapter._fetch_new_messages()` against it.
2. On `main`: UID 2 gets `UID STORE 2 +FLAGS.SILENT (\Seen)` and nothing is delivered. With this PR, UID 2 is delivered.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_email_robustness.py`: the new test (flag update, another UID's literal and a stray `)` ahead of our reply at both fetches) fails on `main` and passes here. Over the 10 test files importing the email adapter: 138 passed.

prs.title: fix(local-models): tolerate missing GGUF files and broken symlinks
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A dangling GGUF symlink, such as a model on a disconnected drive, could make `GET /api/local-models/status` raise `FileNotFoundError` and leave Local Models stuck loading. A split model with an unavailable shard could also be listed with a partial size.

Shared staged-model discovery now includes only paths that resolve to files. The status route also handles files disappearing or becoming inaccessible after discovery, skipping only the affected model and logging the reason. It checks split completeness again before summing sizes, so a missing shard cannot turn into a partial-size row. Valid symlinks and complete split models keep working, and restored files return on the next poll without deleting links or restarting anything.

## Related Issue

Reported in [Discord support](https://discord.com/channels/1053877538025386074/1568079623600873492).

Overlap checked against open and closed PRs and current main:

- #133053 filters companion GGUFs. This changes file availability, not companion classification. Both touch `staged_in()`.
- #147421 adds launch-refusal metadata but retains the failing size lookup. Both touch `_staged_row()` and the status comprehension.
- #132794 concerns GGUF tensor accounting. This preserves `split_parts()` and the header reader's existing partial-read behavior.
- #149366 adds model settings and residency services, not this status/discovery fix.
- #122308 is closed without merge and concerns legacy model adoption.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- Filter non-files in shared discovery, including broken first or continuation symlinks.
- Isolate filesystem errors per status row and reject incomplete splits before reporting their size.
- Add two parameterized behavioral tests with 14 cases, using real temporary files and symlinks, the real FastAPI router, deterministic deletion races, permission failures, and next-poll recovery. Mark them for all host CI lanes.

## How to Test

Run through `scripts/run_tests.sh`:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_local_models_missing_files.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_models_routes.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime_gguf_split.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_legacy_models_dir.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime_picker_row.py
python scripts/check
```

Base: `ca4360692055bdb4df3a695c164646e528891da8`. The final regression tests fail 13 cases on that unmodified production code, with the existing missing-shard behavior passing as a control. All 14 pass with the fix on native Windows, including real symlink creation and recovery.

Across the focused runs, all 107 cases pass. The initial six-file run had 106 passes and one Windows socket-aborted failure (`WinError 10053`) in the existing `test_touch_generate_is_the_readiness_proof`. That case passed against unchanged main, then the complete 50-case runtime file and the final 14-case regression file passed together on the candidate (64 passed, zero failures). The other four files passed all 43 cases. This was a native Windows run on Python 3.14.9 through the canonical runner with isolated temporary homes and no live model engine.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide and searched for overlapping work.
- [x] Focused bug fix with behavioral regressions proven on the base.

prs.title: fix(redact): an AWS ARN is not a Telegram bot token
prs.body:
## What does this PR do? `_TELEGRAM_RE` in `agent/redact.py` treats an AWS ARN's `<12-digit account>:` as a Telegram bot token whenever the resource name is 30+ characters (a long SNS topic, IAM role or Lambda function). A plain ARN comes back as `arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:***`. The model then copies `***` into commands and config, and any caller using `redact_sensitive_text(x) != x` as a "contains a secret" check refuses text with no secret in it. The fix adds a leading alternative to `_TELEGRAM_RE` that consumes an `arn:::::` prefix and returns it unchanged, so the token branch never starts at an ARN account. Python's `re` has no variable-width lookbehind, so consuming the prefix in its own alternative is the narrowest way to say "not after an ARN prefix". The region field may be empty (IAM). ## Related Issue No dedicated issue. Related: #145664 (same `_TELEGRAM_RE` false-positive family; its left-boundary fix still matches an ARN's `::`, so it doesn't cover this case — the two changes are compatible and can share tests) and #119138 (digit-run anchor, preserved). ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `agent/redact.py`: ARN-prefix alternative in `_TELEGRAM_RE`; the substitution returns that match unchanged. - `tests/agent/test_redact_aws_arn.py` (new, 13 tests). - Unchanged: bare `123456789:`, the `bot` prefix, tokens inside `https://api.telegram.org/bot/...`, a 12-digit id with no ARN prefix, a token after an ARN in the same text, the 29/30 length boundary, and the #119138 lookbehind. Timing on a 2 MB digit run and 1 MB of repeated ARN-like prefixes stays linear and close to `main`. - Known limit: a 12-digit bot id written right after a fake `arn:

:::` prefix stays unmasked. Real bot ids are shorter, and the redactor guards against leaks, not adversarial input. ## How to Test 1. On `main` (synthetic values; `123456789012` is the AWS documentation account): ```python from agent.redact import redact_sensitive_text arn = "arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:" + "Default_CloudWatch_Alarms_Topic" redact_sensitive_text(arn, force=True) # main: 'arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:***' this PR: unchanged ``` A 29-character resource passes through on `main`; 30 is masked. 2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_redact_aws_arn.py`: 8 of 13 fail on `main` (every ARN case plus "token next to an ARN"), all 13 pass here. 3. `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the 7 redaction test files (447 passed) and `tests/agent/` (12,447 passed; `test_vault_key_storage.py` not collected locally because `keyring` isn't installed, unrelated). ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — ran `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the affected areas instead (see How to Test), not the whole suite - [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs) - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Arch Linux (Omarchy) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — N/A, no platform-specific code - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Screenshots / Logs N/A --- Prepared by an AI assistant (Hermes); ## What does this PR do?

Adds **Crux — Decision Atlas** as a community Desktop plugin, pinned to [`9ef205e8a39a3b6801f09f0000ef21b3d84a7787`](https://github.com/asimons81/hermes-crux/commit/9ef205e8a39a3b6801f09f0000ef21b3d84a7787), version `0.1.0`. I own and maintain the plugin repository.

Crux makes a recommendation inspectable: compare finite options under explicit assumptions and hard requirements, move assumptions in a native decision atlas, inspect exact one-axis switching thresholds, and identify a minimum-cardinality conflicting constraint set when no option fits. For example, a solo project can be cheaper but miss the deadline; relaxing time makes it feasible, while increasing scope can make a specialist cheaper. Saved scenarios preserve the model, inputs, enabled requirements, and recomputed result.

The engine supports affine formulas and one named objective. Exact rational point comparisons and one-axis partitions are distinct from the explicitly sampled two-axis map. prs.title: fix(shell-exec): add raw_stdout opt-in to skip redaction for structured plugin output
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`shell.exec` force-redacts stdout/stderr before returning them across the RPC boundary. That is the right default for user-facing `!cmd` output, but it also corrupts **structured output that desktop plugins parse verbatim**: any random-looking token of 16+ characters gets masked (`1341a55f03ce51f23d46420e9bcd6226` → `1341a5...6226`), and the JSON gets reformatted, so a plugin's `^[a-f0-9]{32}$` check fails and it shows `probe returned invalid snapshot pin` with no data. `shell.exec` is the only command channel exposed to the plugin SDK, so there is no workaround.

This adds an opt-in `raw_stdout: bool = False` parameter to `shell.exec`. When `true`, the handler skips `redact_sensitive_text` on stdout/stderr (still tails to the 4000/2000 limits) so callers that parse the bytes receive them intact. Default `false` preserves the current force-redact behaviour for user-facing calls.

Following @strzhao's option 2 recommendation in the issue: the opt-in flag is the narrowest fix that matches the measured rewrite scope, and it generalises across token formats (the reporter confirmed every shape is masked, so a key-name allowlist would not).

## Related Issue

Fixes #149778

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- **`tui_gateway/contracts/tools_commands.py`** — added `raw_stdout: bool = False` to `ShellExecParams` and `CanonicalShellExecParams`.
- **`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`** — `shell.exec` handler reads `raw_stdout`; the `done` callback branches: `true` tails without redaction, `false` keeps the existing force-redact path.
- **`gateway/session_shell.py`** — canonical `shell_exec` adds `raw_stdout` to the params allowlist, passes it to `_run`, and `_run` branches the same way. Both transports redact today, so both get the flag.
- **`apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`** — `ShellExecParams` and `CanonicalShellExecParams` schemas carry the new `raw_stdout` boolean property (regenerated shape, kept in sync with the Pydantic models).
- **`tests/tui_gateway/test_shell_exec_security.py`** — two new tests:

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: Saved GPT Image 1.5 picks keep working after OpenAI's Dec 1 shutdown (image_gen)
prs.body:
Saved `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` picks keep working after OpenAI shuts GPT Image 1.5 and 1 Mini down on **2026-12-01**: they now run on GPT Image 2 instead of breaking or quietly switching to Klein.

## Why

OpenAI's [deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) (notice dated 2026-06-02, page updated 2026-10-22) shuts down `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5` and `chatgpt-image-latest` on **Dec 1, 2026**. Hermes still lists two of them:

- `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` in the FAL image catalog (fal only proxies OpenAI, so it dies the same day)
- `openai/gpt-image-1-mini` in the OpenRouter Image API list, where it is the only model offering `background=transparent`

## Changes

- Removed `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` from `FAL_MODELS`, plus the `gpt_literal` size style that only this model used.
- New `RETIRED_FAL_MODELS = {"fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5": "fal-ai/gpt-image-2"}`. A config that still has the old id is read as GPT Image 2 by both `_read_configured_image_model` (managed dispatch), `_resolve_fal_model` (config or `FAL_IMAGE_MODEL`), and `managed_backend_for_model` (router + `nous_subscription` status). No config migration needed.
- OpenRouter: replaced `openai/gpt-image-1-mini` with `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and a saved Mini pick (kwarg, `OPENROUTER_IMAGE_MODEL`, `image_gen.openrouter.model` or `image_gen.model`) resolves to Flare via `_RETIRED_IMAGE_API_MODELS` in `_resolve_model_chain`. Flare keeps `background=transparent`; its params come from OpenRouter's live `GET /api/v1/images/models` (9 ratios incl. 16:9, quality auto…max, n≤10, 16 refs).
- Docs (en + zh-Hans): removed the 1.5 rows and aspect column, and added a note about the remap.

## Before / after (stored `image_gen.provider: nous`, `image_gen.model: fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5`)

| | resolved model | managed route | after Dec 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` | FAL | upstream 4xx, generation fails |
| removing the entry with no successor map | Klein fallback (FAL path) | **`portal`**: the dead id is sent to the Portal gateway | wrong backend / failure |
| **this PR** | `fal-ai/gpt-image-2` | FAL | works |

## Validation

- **Live (real managed Nous gateway, runtime interpreter, worktree code):** stored `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5` + provider `nous`. `_resolve_fal_model()` → `fal-ai/gpt-image-2`. Real `image_generate_tool("a red apple…", "square")` returned `success: True` with a fal.media PNG. On main the same config resolves to `fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5`.
- Clearing the map on head makes `managed_route("nous", "fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5")` return `portal`. That routing bug is why the map is needed, not just the deletion.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_image_generation.py tests/tools/test_image_generation_managed.py tests/plugins/image_gen/ tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py tests/tools/test_managed_media_gateways.py tests/hermes_cli/test_nous_subscription.py`: **343 passed, 0 failed**.
- New invariant tests: `test_retired_saved_pick_resolves_to_successor` (OpenRouter) and `TestRetiredModels`, which also covers the `FAL_IMAGE_MODEL` path: each retired id is gone from the catalog, its successor is present, and the retired id resolves to the successor on the FAL path and the managed router. It fails on main, which has no `RETIRED_FAL_MODELS`.
- ruff clean, `scripts/check --only health` ok, `check_doc_links` ok, `check_no_tmp_literals` ok.

## Notes

- Pricing: GPT Image 2 medium costs $0.04–0.06/image on fal, up from 1.5's $0.034. It is already metered on the managed gateway (`_PORTAL_DUPLICATE_OF` maps it), so no portal work is needed.
- Not touched: `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality` (retires Nov 2), which is already covered by open #128430. `openai/gpt-image-1` shut down Oct 23 and was never in Hermes's curated list.
- Timing: the replacement models are live today, so this can merge now or any time before Dec 1.

prs.title: feat(session-input): policy/admitted-transfer/checkpoint primitives with a default-off example plugin
prs.body:
## Why

Two gaps keep every "batch a human burst / deliver a mid-turn message" feature
surface-local:

- `pre_gateway_dispatch` does not fire on Local/CLI/TUI/Desktop/API-server
  input (`website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md`), so a plugin cannot touch
  `/api/ws → prompt.submit`.
- `post_gateway_admission` runs after the slot is taken and cannot fold payloads
  in the admission transaction, cannot resolve a follower's retry alias, and
  cannot hand a committed admission to the **running** generation with a
  settlement fence.

The existing local prototype also had to import gateway helpers from
`hermes_state_runtime`, and it hard-coded windows, display text and a profile
inside the core.

## What does this PR do?

Adds three generic seams; with no provider registered every one is a no-op and
behaviour is byte-identical to today:

1. `session_input_policy` (`session_input_primitives.policy_for`): a
   profile-scoped snapshot fetched **before** the write transaction. Core
   validates the windows/eligibility/signature, then folds a follower into the
   queued FIFO tail in the same transaction as its retry alias. The batch record
   is versioned (`session_input_batch_v1`); the deadline is honored by the claim
   path outside the writer lock.
2. `session_input_admitted` + transfer (`gateway/session_input_transfer`):
   after the admission commit, on **both** doors (`SessionAuthority.submit` and
   `admit_native`), the authority owns registration, the durable
   `steer_session_input` write, delivery as a ticketed steer/redirect, and
   requeue when the turn refuses it. A cancelled caller cannot abort a committed
   hand-over, and a later submit cannot overtake it.
3. `checkpoint_input` (`session_input_checkpoint`): consume the ticket buffer at
   the tool-batch boundary and when a model request is rebuilt; append with the
   transcript prefix intact. Consumption/settlement stay in core; the plugin
   only supplies text formatting.

`session_input_legacy` is a one-module compatibility reader for the two key
names an earlier local inbox wrote; new writes never use them. It is not needed
by the interface and can be dropped once no admitted row carries an old key.

`plugins/session-input-inbox-example/` is a worked provider (default off):
eligibility (text-only, same policy/provenance), windows, the
`[追加消息 n · <ts>]` header, and the steer-vs-redirect choice from an immutable
`TurnPhase`. It never classifies intent.

## Durability contract

Text accepted while the plugin was enabled remains readable, retryable and
settleable after the plugin is disabled, crashes or is removed: the batch record
and alias commit atomically with the admission, and settlement is core's. Only
new batching stops. A physical revert of the primitives is refused while such
rows exist (the local installer implements that guard).

## Tests

The primitives were exercised by a separate offline suite (52 existing cases +
plugin/guard cases) against this branch's tree: real SQLite admission/transfer/
settlement, real control mixin, cancelled-submit races, fault injection
(`session_idle`, `stale_generation`, `not_fresh` requeue), legacy alias retry
after provider removal, and cross-profile isolation. `tests/agent/test_correction_tickets.py`
from PR1 covers the redirect/checkpoint semantics this PR builds on. I can port
the remaining suite into this branch before review if maintainers prefer.

## Non-goals

- No user-visible receipts (see #145150), no Desktop/UI changes (see
  #149051/#149570/#149707), no intent sorting, no host-isolation RPC protocol:
  the provider runs in-process, receives immutable DTOs, and never a SQLite
  connection, live agent or lock. `plugins.isolation: host` support is a
  follow-up that would project the same DTOs over the host wire.
- The example plugin is not enabled anywhere by default.

## Differences from open upstream work

- #149051/#149570/#149707: Desktop-side mid-turn steer presentation/recovery;
  this PR is the admission/transfer contract underneath, with no UI files.
- #145150: per-message receipts. This PR exposes the truthful transfer state a
  receipt could report but adds no user-facing ack.

prs.title: fix(agent): settle ticketed redirects and append corrections at the right seam
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes a mid-turn correction (a redirect) a first-class, settleable ticket and puts
the two append seams where the turn actually consumes text:

1. **Ticketed redirects.** `redirect(text, ticket=...)` records the same
   `(ticket, text)` pairs the steer slot already records, so `withdraw_steer`
   can settle a redirect exactly: `True` while still buffered (removed now,
   other corrections stay), `False` once a drain consumed it. Previously a
   withdrawn hand-over could not distinguish "not delivered, requeue" from
   "already read", which either loses the text or delivers it twice.
2. **Cancel-safe turn-boundary clear.** When a turn ends with corrections still
   in the redirect buffer, `clear_interrupt` hands them to the steer slot (their
   tickets included) instead of dropping them; a hard `/stop` still drops
   everything. A second correction arriving after the aborted request unwound
   joins the same rebuild buffer and does not re-arm the stop flag.
3. **Append order.** The pending steer is consumed right before a tool batch
   executes (a correction wins before any side effect), and text drained while a
   request is rebuilt is appended to that request (after the newest tool result,
   or in place when there is none) instead of being deferred to a later turn.
   The cached transcript prefix is unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_correction_tickets.py` — 9 offline cases, no model/storage:

```bash
HERMES_HOME=$(mktemp -d) python -m pytest tests/agent/test_correction_tickets.py -q
```

Fail (or are impossible) on current main because `redirect()` has no ticket and
the redirect buffer has no fates: withdraw-after-consume returns the wrong
answer, turn-end clear loses collected text, and a second post-abort correction
is refused/re-arms the stop flag.

## Scope / non-goals

No plugin interface, no batching, no window policy, no surface-specific code.
One new module (`agent/correction_tickets.py`) plus three call sites. A
follow-up PR adds the provider seam on top of this ticket contract.

## Differences from open upstream work

- #149051 / #149570 / #149707 fix Desktop **presentation and recovery** of a
  mid-turn steer (which bubble holds it, how the interrupted reply resumes,
  never replaying an uncertain receipt). This PR changes the **core settlement
  contract** those surfaces call into; no UI files touched.
- #145150 asks for opt-in per-message receipts. This PR only makes the ticket
  fate truthful (`consumed` vs `withdrawn`); it emits no user-visible receipt.

prs.title: fix(delegation): a split unit's failed task keeps its own goal
prs.body:
## ELI5

When a background helper task failed, Desktop could list the failure under the wrong task's description, and mark a different task as the one that failed. This happened when the agent's helpers were split into separately finishing groups. A failed task now shows its own description.

## What does this PR do?

`dispatch_async_delegation_batch` stores the whole call's `goals` list on every unit's record, so a result's `task_index` can index it (`tools/async_delegation.py`, "``goals`` is the whole call"). `failed_delegations_for_session` instead paired the unit's own `task_indexes` with that list by position. With `task_indexes=[1]`, `goals=['A goal', 'B goal']` and task 1 failing, it reported `{task_index: 1, goal: 'A goal'}`, and Desktop's goal join then marked task 0's row failed.

Each failed task's goal is now looked up by its index in the call-wide list, falling back to the first goal as before.

| Split unit holding task 1 of `['A goal', 'B goal']` fails | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Failure row's goal | `A goal` | `B goal` |
| Whole-batch and single delegations | correct | unchanged |

## Related Issue

Reported by @BearHuddleston in his review of #149836, which lists it as a known gap.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/async_delegation.py`: `failed_delegations_for_session` indexes the call-wide `goals` by `task_index`.
- `tests/tools/test_async_delegation_failed_surface.py`: the batch test's fixture now has the shape the producer writes (call-wide goals plus the unit's task indexes). A new test dispatches a real split unit through `dispatch_async_delegation_batch` and checks its failure row.

2. With `main`'s `tools/async_delegation.py`, both changed tests fail (`'scan db'` instead of `'scan web'`, `'A goal'` instead of `'B goal'`).

prs.title: Add creature-workshop: a project's shellops lifecycle as tools and a Desktop pane
prs.body:
## What it does

Creature Workshop puts a project's development lifecycle in front of the agent and in a Desktop pane. A project describes itself once in its shellops `.ops/` declaration (its tools by channel, its tests, its lint, its release record); the plugin reads that declaration, runs the project's own `shell/ops`, and shows the result.

## Surfaces

- **Tools** (`workshop` toolset): `workshop_project`, `workshop_install`, `workshop_test`, `workshop_lint`. Every handler returns JSON and never raises.
- **System prompt section**: one short paragraph when the session's directory is a shellops project, naming it, its declared tool count and its latest release.
- **Desktop**: a right-hand pane with Toolchain (live, a green or red dot per declared tool, re-read every 20 s), Declaration and Release tabs, and a status-bar chip that counts installed tools. It reads its own backend in `dashboard/plugin_api.py` through `ctx.rest`.
- No hooks, no middleware, no environment variables.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- The tools run the project's own `shell/ops` as a subprocess, in the project directory, with the project's `.envrc` loaded. Nothing runs outside the project.
- `workshop_install` with `check: false` installs tools, which fetches from the channel the declaration names: the host's package manager, cargo, npm, go, a git repository, Flathub, or an installer script the project ships. With `check: true`, the default, nothing is installed.
- The backend runs `shell/ops install --check` for the pane on a timer and reads files under the project only.
- No network calls of the plugin's own, no telemetry, no credentials, no background processes beyond the subprocess of each call.

## Status

Draft for the Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon. The pin moves as the plugin's merge requests land; screenshots follow. `hermes plugins doctor . --ci` and `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` pass at the pinned commit. The repository vendors shellops as the submodule `shell/.ops`, which is the project's own tooling and not part of the plugin's runtime.

prs.title: fix(profiles): a profile import clears the delete tombstone
prs.body:
## Problem

`hermes profile delete <name>` writes a tombstone at `profiles/.deleted/<name>` before it removes the tree. Three paths can put a profile directory back: `create_profile()`, `install_distribution()`, and `import_profile()`. The first two clear the marker; the third never did.

`import_profile()` moves the archive into `profiles/<name>` and returns the path as if it had worked, but every reader — `profile_exists()`, `list_profiles()`, `profiles_to_serve()`, the CLI resolver and the Desktop surfaces — filters through `named_profile_is_live()`, which is false while the marker exists. The import prints `Imported`, then every command for that profile answers `Profile '<name>' does not exist` until someone removes the marker by hand (the report's operator had five of them).

Measured on `ca4360692` — export a profile, `mark_named_profile_deleted()` + rmtree (exactly what delete leaves), then import:

```
exported: True 785
after delete: dir exists = False | live = False
imported dir exists = True
tombstone still there = True
named_profile_is_live(restored) = False
```

## Fix

Clear the marker after the archive is published, mirroring the clear `create_profile()` already does before it builds:

```python
        shutil.move(str(final_source), str(profile_dir))
    # The archive lands where `delete` left its marker: without this the imported tree is
    # invisible to every reader (the same clear `create_profile` already does). Only after
    # the move, so a refused import never resurrects the deleted name.
    clear_named_profile_deleted(profile_dir)
    return profile_dir
```

The position is deliberate: **after** the move. `import_profile()` refuses plenty of archives (no single root, missing root dir, an already-existing profile dir, a traversal member) and a refused import must leave the deleted name deleted, not clear its marker over a tree that was never published. The second test pins that.

## Why the diff also moves the export redaction pass

`hermes_cli/profiles.py` is at its line cap (2395, its value on main). One call line already failed the gate (`2396 > 2395`), so the code-health remedy — move an existing function into a topical sibling — applies: `_scrub_export_secrets`, `_should_redact_export_file` and their two suffix sets moved verbatim to `hermes_cli/profiles_export_redact.py`, re-imported under the same private name so `export_profile()` and `_default_export_ignore()`'s docstring reference are unchanged. No behaviour change; `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` (108 tests, the whole export/import suite) passes unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_deleted_profile_tombstone.py` (the module that already locks the tombstone contract), two new cases:

* `test_import_over_a_deleted_name_lands_live` — export → delete-shaped residue → import → the restored home is live, `profile_exists()` is true, and the name is in `list_profile_names()`.
* `test_a_refused_import_keeps_the_tombstone` — an archive with two top-level directories is refused and the marker survives.

Sabotage, on the committed tree with only the source reverted (`git checkout upstream/main -- hermes_cli/profiles.py`):

```
[100% | 23/~23 | ✓23 | ✗ 1] ✗ tests/hermes_cli/test_deleted_profile_tombstone.py (23✓ 1✗)
E       AssertionError: assert False
FAILED ...::TestImportClearsDeletedTombstone::test_import_over_a_deleted_name_lands_live
```

With the fix: `1 files, 24 tests passed, 0 failed`.

Adjacent suites (they drive the moved module and the profile publish paths):

* `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` — 108 passed, 3 skipped
* `tests/hermes_cli/test_profile_distribution.py`, `test_profile_pm_portability.py`, `test_kanban_transfer.py` — 84 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped
* `python scripts/check --base upstream/main` — `14 checks, ok` (code health: 3 files, 0 blocking)

## Scope

This is the import path only. `install_distribution()` is covered by #97587 (still open) and `create_profile()` already handled it, so I left both alone rather than duplicating that change — the two PRs touch different call sites and should merge in either order.

Not addressed: a tombstone left behind by an *interrupted* delete, and the `--force` question for importing over a tombstoned name (the import now simply clears it, which is what a restore means). Say the word if you would rather the import refuse while a marker exists and name the file.

Closes #149831

prs.title: fix(mattermost): keep thread follow-ups going without an @mention (#4221)
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes the remaining half of #4221. With `MATTERMOST_REPLY_MODE=thread` the bot answers inside a thread, but any reply there without an `@mention` is dropped by the channel mention gate, so a conversation stops after one turn. Thread-local delivery, the other half of the issue, is already on main.

Rewritten from the original patch onto `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`, following the review.

## Fix
- Track joined threads with the shared `ThreadParticipationTracker`, as the Discord and Matrix adapters do. It is capped at 500 entries, the oldest age out, and it survives restarts.
- A thread is joined only in thread mode, once a post has passed the gate. `reply_mode: off` keeps its current behaviour, and a reply in a thread the bot never joined stays gated.
- `allowed_channels` is still checked first and the user allowlist still applies.
- Add `MATTERMOST_THREAD_REQUIRE_MENTION` (`thread_require_mention`, default `false`), matching Matrix, to keep the gate inside joined threads. The docs now describe the `MATTERMOST_REQUIRE_MENTION` exception.

Mattermost threads are one level deep and `root_id` on an inbound post is always the root, so nested replies resolve to the same tracked id.

Peer bots are not told apart here: a bot replying unmentioned in a joined thread passes the gate, as any post does with `require_mention: false`. Dropping bot posts belongs at ingress, which #136958 covers.

## Tests
Added to `TestMattermostMentionBehavior`: a follow-up in a joined thread, a reply in an unjoined thread, flat reply mode, `MATTERMOST_THREAD_REQUIRE_MENTION`, and eviction from the bounded tracker. The follow-up test fails on main.

prs.title: Rollback no longer reverts files your git config ignores (port gemini-cli#30034)
prs.body:
If you tell git to ignore a file in a way only your own machine knows about (the project's `.git/info/exclude`, or your global ignore file), Hermes' checkpoints still copied that file, and `/rollback --all` then put the old copy back over your later edits. Now checkpoints follow those same ignore rules, so rollback leaves those files exactly as you left them.

Ported from google-gemini/gemini-cli#30034, which fixed the same hole in their shadow-repo checkpoints.

**Outcome:** checkpoint snapshots, `/rollback` diffs and safe-restore plans skip every file the user's own git configuration ignores, not only `.gitignore` matches.

## What changes

Live A/B, real classic CLI in tmux (probe model: gemini-3.8-flash on Nous, picked for cost), checkpoints enabled. The repo has `notes.local` in `.git/info/exclude` and `*.secret` in the user's global `core.excludesFile`. The agent edits `app.py`; the user then hand-edits `notes.local` and `keys.secret`; then `/rollback 1 --all`.

| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| files in the checkpoint | `app.py keys.secret notes.local` | `app.py` |
| `app.py` after rollback | `v1` (restored) | `v1` (restored) |
| `notes.local` after rollback | `old` (**user edit lost**) | `user-edit` (kept) |
| `keys.secret` after rollback | `old` (**user edit lost**) | `user-edit` (kept) |

**Live repro:** before: user's edits to both excluded files reverted to `old`; after: both kept, `app.py` still restored.

## Root cause

The store runs `git add -A` with `GIT_DIR` set to the shared shadow store and the user's global config hidden (deliberately, to keep gpg signing and credential helpers out), so git only saw the working tree's `.gitignore` files.

## Changes

- New `tools/checkpoint_excludes.py`: reads the user's `core.excludesFile` (falling back to git's XDG default `~/.config/git/ignore`) and the repo's `info/exclude` with the user's real git config, merges them into `<store>/excludes/<project hash>`, and returns `-c core.excludesFile=<that file>` for the shadow-store `git add`. Hermes' own `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` (the store's `info/exclude`) still applies on top.
- `tools/checkpoint_manager.py`: the three staging sites (snapshot, `/rollback diff`, safe-restore plan) pass those args, so all three agree on the file set.
- One invariant test (`tests/tools/test_checkpoint_user_excludes.py`), red on `origin/main`, green here. Checkpoint suites: 145 passed.

Not covered: Windows (path read through `git config --path`, no shell; only CI's Windows lane).

prs.title: fix(desktop): each delegate card shows only its own subagents
prs.body:
## ELI5

When the agent asked for helpers and that request was turned down, then tried again with the same tasks, the chat showed every helper twice: once under the request that failed and once under the one that worked. The turned-down request now shows as a plain error, and each helper card only shows helpers that really belong to it, even when two requests use the same wording.

## What does this PR do?

It fixes two ways the Desktop `delegate_task` card picks up the wrong live subagents. Both come from `mergeDelegateRows` matching live children to rows by normalized goal text.

- **A rejected batch followed by a retry.** `delegate_task` can reject a whole batch (an unavailable model option, a template marker it didn't expand, a pre-tool guard). It reports this inside `result` as `{"error": ...}`, so `isError` stays false. The card still listed one row per requested goal, and those rows matched the retry's children by goal text. With N children, the chat showed 2N cards with identical live activity. The card now asks `toolCallFailed` (which reads the result body, as the failure path next to it already does), so a rejected batch renders as the generic error row.
- **Two real dispatches with the same goals (#136532).** The settled combined result now carries `delegation_id`, the same id native `subagent.*` events stamp on every child. The background dispatch handle already carried it. Rows join live children on delegation id plus task index first, among children with the row's goal, and unit ids such as `<id>-1` count as the same call. The goal condition matters because `subagent.list` rows carry no task index, so every child loaded from the roster after a reload, a reconnect or on a second client reads as task 0. A live child stamped with a *different* delegation id is never matched to a row, by any join.
- **Unstamped children keep their live state.** When a batch has no live-transcript id, its children carry no delegation id, but the dispatch handle still names a generated unit id. Goal and task-order matching still applies to those children, so their cards keep showing live progress.

| Case | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Rejected batch, then a retry with the same goals | Both cards show the retry's children | Rejected call shows an error row; the retry shows its children once |
| Two dispatches with a shared goal | The older card picks up the newer call's children | Each card keeps its own children |
| Dispatched batch, or a settled batch where a child failed | Card with children | Unchanged |
| Older transcripts without a `delegation_id` | Goal or task-order matching | Unchanged |
| Background batch reloaded from the roster (children read as task 0) | Goal matching | Each child on its own goal's row |
| One call repeating a goal | Goal matching, children can swap rows | Task index keeps them apart |

## Related Issue

Part of #136532 (the background-dispatch half; see Known gap)

Salvages #149538 (@ErtzFiend) and #136573 (@liuhao1024).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

| Commit | Author | What |
|---|---|---|
| `c3f21c24` | @ErtzFiend (#149538) | `DelegateToolPart` routes a call whose result body reports failure to the generic row; tests pin the three delegate result shapes for `toolCallFailed`. Our only change to the cherry-pick is the `eslint --fix` import order and blank lines. |
| `af00a482` | @liuhao1024 (#136573) | `delegation_id` added to the settled combined result (`tools/delegate_tool_dispatch.py`); `DelegateRow.delegationId`; exact delegation-id join ahead of the goal and task-order matches, with unit-suffix handling. |
| `f62adc9a` | ours | A card that knows its delegation id refuses only children stamped with another id, rather than turning off goal and order matching for every child. |
| `657e236a` | ours | Maps @ErtzFiend's commit email for the attribution check. |
| `5be32e20` | @BearHuddleston | The delegation-id join only uses the task index between same-goal children, so a card loaded from the roster doesn't put children on the wrong rows. Patch from his review. |
| `5aab8d3c` | ours, co-authored by @BearHuddleston | His two tests: one call repeating a goal, and a running call whose children are stamped before its result arrives. Together with the roster test, they fail if any of the new matching rules is removed. |
| `c7a5dde2` | ours, co-authored by @BearHuddleston | Comment names the foreground case the goal join still serves. |

#136573's second commit (a separate `rejectedDelegateSpawn` check) is not carried: `c3f21c24` covers the same rejected-call case through the existing `toolCallFailed` helper, so the two would have been two checks for one condition. Thanks to @danieljustus for the rejected-then-retried repro on #136573, which is the case this PR fixes.

### Known gap (out of scope)

- **Foreground calls (the rest of #136532).** A sync `delegate_task` card has no result, so no delegation id, until its children finish. It still matches live children by goal, so it can take an earlier call's finished child with the same goal, the same as on `main`.
- **Split-unit failure labels.** `failed_delegations_for_session` (`tools/async_delegation.py`) pairs a split unit's task indexes with the call-wide goal list, so a failed task in a later unit gets an earlier task's goal. This is pre-existing and is fixed separately in #149862.

Thanks to @BearHuddleston for the review: the roster finding, the patch, and the mutation-checked tests.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project ui src/components/assistant-ui/tool/ src/components/assistant-ui/thread/ src/store/` → 289 files, 2,733 tests passed (head `c7a5dde2`).
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_delegate_combined_delegation_id.py` → 2 passed.
3. Each new test fails on the code it fixes:
   - `sealed-tool-parts.test.tsx` with `main`'s `message-parts.tsx`: the rejected-batch test fails.
   - `delegate-model.test.ts` with `main`'s `delegate-model.ts`: 4 fail.
   - Our unstamped-child test with `af00a482`'s `delegate-model.ts`: 1 fails.
   - The cold-roster test with `657e236a`'s `delegate-model.ts`: 1 fails.
   - Removing the delegation-id join, its task-index condition, or the rule that a row with no id still takes stamped children: each removal fails at least one test.
   - `test_delegate_combined_delegation_id.py` with `main`'s `delegate_tool_dispatch.py`: 1 fails.
4. An independent review also checked every result shape `delegate_task` can return (dispatched, settled with child errors or timeouts, sync fallback note, `process_notes`, `inline_results`, `refused`). `toolCallFailed` returns false for all of them, so no real delegation loses its card.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Only the related suites above ran.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (Node 26). Desktop typecheck and ESLint on the changed files are clean.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

prs.title: read_file names the missing folder instead of a bare "File not found" (port opencode#60688)
prs.body:
When `read_file` misses because a whole folder is gone (a deleted worktree, a renamed directory, a relative path resolved from the wrong place), the model used to get a bare "File not found" and start guessing paths. Now the error names the missing folder and the nearest folder that does exist, and suggests similar entries there.

Port from [anomalyco/opencode#60688](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60688). They counted 1,588 missing-file reads in a week of their own sessions, and in about two thirds the folder itself was gone. In Teknium's last 14 days of sessions, 20 of 25 `read_file` misses had the same shape: paths under removed `.worktrees/` and scratch dirs.

## What changes

| Read | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `proj/src/ap.ts` (typo, folder exists) | `File not found: …` + `similar_files: [proj/src/app.ts]` | unchanged |
| `proj/src-gone/deep/app.ts` | `File not found: …/proj/src-gone/deep/app.ts` | `… The folder …/proj/src-gone does not exist. The nearest folder that does is …/proj.` + `similar_files: [proj/src]` |
| `rel-missing/dir/f.py` | `File not found: rel-missing/dir/f.py` | `… The folder rel-missing does not exist. The nearest folder that does is ..` |
| `proj/src/app.ts/inner` | `File not found: …` | `… …/proj/src/app.ts is a file, not a folder.` |
| `we ird'dir/x/y.txt` (quote + space) | `File not found: …` | `… The folder …/we ird'dir/x does not exist. …` (quoting holds) |

- `ShellFileOperations._suggest_similar_files`: the ancestor walk goes into the same shell command as the existing directory listing (`ls … ; if [ ! -d ]; walk up with dirname; print marker + nearest; ls nearest`). Remote backends (docker/ssh/modal) get it with **no extra round trip**.
- The scoring loop moves as-is into `file_operations_common.similar_names` so both listings share it (`file_operations.py` is at ~1,700 lines; this keeps it from growing).
- 1 invariant test (`test_missing_folder_names_nearest_existing_one`) on a real `LocalEnvironment`, red on main.

**How it differs from upstream:** OpenCode walks up with repeated listings through its environment layer. Ours does the whole walk in one shell call, because each Hermes file op on a remote backend is a round trip. We also report "is a file, not a folder" when a path component is a regular file; upstream does not.

## Live repro

Real `hermes chat -q -t file` in isolated probe homes (Nous Portal, `google/gemini-3.8-flash`, N=1 per leg). The prompt asks for `MAGIC` in `proj-old/src/config.ts`, but the file actually lives at `proj/src/config.ts`. Counts come from each run's own `state.db`:

| | tool calls until the file was found | tool calls total |
|---|---|---|
| **main** (`origin/main`) | **46**, and on the way it read `/etc/passwd`, `~/.bash_history` and `~/.hermes/config.yaml` while guessing | 69 (interrupted) |
| **this PR** | **6** | 24, then a correct answer: "proj-old/src/config.ts does not exist. In proj/src/config.ts, MAGIC is zebra-41" |

With a NOTFOUND escape hatch in the prompt, main made 3 blind retries and tripped the tool-loop warning. The PR made 1 call and stopped.

## Tests

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over `tests/tools/test_file_ops_single_roundtrip.py test_file_operations.py test_file_operations_edge_cases.py test_file_tools.py test_read_unicode_filename_retry.py test_file_ops_env_not_ready.py`: 201 passed, 0 failed. The new test fails with main's `file_operations.py`.
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking. ruff, the no-tmp check and windows-footguns: clean.

Not covered: Windows-native local file ops. They go through the same POSIX shell (Git Bash) path, but this was not run on a Windows runner.

prs.title: Add pinpoint to the plugin catalog
prs.body:
### Summary
Adds the `pinpoint` plugin to the Hermes plugin catalog.

Pinpoint is Audit mode plus Design mode for the live page in Hermes Desktop's Browser pane. Audit mode measures the page with deterministic in-page checks (WCAG contrast, tap targets, form labels, image alt, heading order, small text, horizontal overflow), pins numbered findings on the offending elements, and verifies a fix with a same-element re-audit, an honest fixed-vs-gone split, a score delta and a pasteable receipt. Design mode lets you point at any element to see its live box model, typography, layout and contrast, navigate the DOM by keyboard, and send an instruction to the agent (the agent can also call `pinpoint_audit(inspect_selector=...)`).

- **Repository**: https://github.com/stupidburgers/pinpoint
- **Version**: `0.1.0`
- **Pinned SHA**: `cb0bbd8f8ca688f11d1cfba2a32c3f878f448c5b`
- **README at SHA**: https://github.com/stupidburgers/pinpoint/blob/cb0bbd8f8ca688f11d1cfba2a32c3f878f448c5b/README.md

### Validation Output
```
$ hermes plugins validate /path/to/pinpoint --install-deps
Validation passed.
```

### Disclosure
Pinpoint's desktop half runs its own audit script inside the web page open in Hermes Desktop's Browser pane, only after you allow it for that site (Desktop's per-origin consent dialog; revocable under Capabilities > Plugins); the script reads computed styles, layout and attribute names (not form values or cookies) and draws an overlay. Findings (CSS selectors, short element labels, measured values) are stored in a local SQLite file under the plugin-data folder (`pinpoint/data.db`, 20 pages max) and are sent to the model only when the agent calls `pinpoint_audit`/`pinpoint_pins` or when you click Fix on a pin; element labels originate from the page. The desktop half polls the page every 0.5-1 s while pins are shown (via `executeJavaScript`) and re-audits automatically after page changes (switch off in the pane). `pinpoint_audit` blocks up to 90 s waiting for the Desktop (configurable) and returns `desktop_unavailable` when no Desktop window answers, including under cron. No network calls, no subprocesses, no shell, no credentials, no telemetry, no files written outside plugin-data; it never edits your source (the agent does, under normal approvals).



### What is not verified
See the README "Not verified yet" list at the pinned SHA: no run against a live provider (the end-to-end suite in a real Desktop rig uses a scripted model), macOS/Linux untested, the desktop-only e2e scenario fails on this Desktop build, multi-window claim race is unit-tested only.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep bounded control reads off the serial queue
prs.body:
## Problem and behavior

`session.control.read` can miss the client's 30-second deadline while it waits behind a slow request on the same WebSocket. Switching from native Desktop to the gateway-hosted Webapp does not remove that transport queue. The ordinary dispatcher still awaits each serial request before taking the next frame; even existing concurrent reads were admitted into that queue before they could start.

Start the two allowlisted read projections at admission instead: `session.context_breakdown` and the pure `session.control.read` snapshot. Existing bounds remain **2 running + 8 waiting**; a flood still parks the reader. Mutations retain their arrival order.

## Ordering and profile boundaries

These snapshots are deliberately unordered relative to queued mutations. A client needing read-after-write consistency must await the mutation's reply. Desktop/Webapp `session.control` already awaits and consumes the returned snapshot; Ink's explicit control read hydrates the session once and receives later updates as events.

A read naming a hot-starting profile waits within the existing 20-second profile-start budget before taking a running read slot. It still counts against admission, cannot starve ready profiles' running slots, and is dropped when its viewer disconnects. Profile-bound grants naming another profile still fail immediately through the unchanged authority checks. The serial mutation hold lane is preserved.

Completed slow dispatches now log peer, request ID, method and elapsed time at a fixed 5-second threshold. IDs and methods use escaped repr; no request parameters or response bodies are logged. Cancellation and dispatch-crash paths keep their existing diagnostics. A handler that hands work to a pool is timed only through that handoff, not until its eventual reply. No new environment setting is added.

## Verification

Refreshed against upstream snapshot `8112254f8a934626032579cae967b25b7795836d` on 4 November 2026, preserving the published branch's history with a normal merge. Final head: `f41ee761ab98f1e0ab9c245d182a8aa0e59e9838`.

- **80/80 tests passed** across the concurrent-read, real ticketed profile-start, session-control, orphan-race and socket-send-deadline suites, using `scripts/run_tests.sh` with pinned Python 3.14 and two workers.
- The control-read regression fails on unmodified upstream: the read starts only after the gated mutation finishes. With the patch it replies while that mutation remains blocked, while a later mutation stays ordered. Both `prompt.submit` and `session.control` are exercised.
- `scripts/check --base origin/main`: **14 checks passed**, code health 0 blocking / 0 advisory. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Claude code/security/concurrency review: no remaining blocker or major for PR publication, conditional on passing the revised tests. The 80-test run above is that revised run. An earlier Gemini review raised the same profile-wait and ordering questions; the follow-up Gemini call hit quota and is not reported as a pass.

The first broader worktree run hit the repository's real-home I/O guard when bootstrap inspected its Git metadata under the live install. Verification was moved to an isolated clone outside the live home; the guard remained enabled.

## Limits

This proves the serial-queue regression, not the exact blocker on every naturally timed-out socket. Later independent-socket controls answered in 26–1685 ms while the user's original 30-second failure remained valid evidence. GIL pauses, database waits, read-lane saturation and full `session.resume` cost remain separate possible limits. See the new cross-surface evidence comment on this PR.

No live installation has been patched or restarted by this refresh. Installed activation and sustained real-use validation are outstanding. GitHub reported no configured CI checks; local test success is not a claim that GitHub CI ran.
