issues.title: [bug] slack-auto.test.ts fails when NANOCLAW_CHANNELS_REMOTE is set in the host environment
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

7be8d7f6 (upstream main). Also present in v2026.10.0.

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

The test `module absent: fetches the channels branch and materializes the one file, engine-style` in `setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts:200` fails when `NANOCLAW_CHANNELS_REMOTE` is set in the shell that runs the tests. This shows up during the validate step of `/update-nanoclaw` on an install that uses the override.

`resolveChannelsRemote()` in `setup/channels/slack-auto.ts:174` returns the override before it runs `git remote` or `git ls-remote`:

```ts
const override = process.env.NANOCLAW_CHANNELS_REMOTE;
if (override) return override;
```

The test never clears the variable. At `setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts:212` it asserts the exact exec sequence (`git remote`, `git ls-remote --heads origin channels`, `git fetch 'origin' ...`, `git show 'refs/remotes/origin/channels:...'`). With the override set, the first two calls are skipped and the fetch uses the override remote, so the assertion fails.

The file-level `afterEach` at `setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts:158-159` already calls `vi.unstubAllEnvs()`, but nothing in the `provisioning-core bootstrap` suite stubs this variable.

The same leak in `scripts/update-skills.test.ts` was fixed in #4081. That PR changed only that file, so the slack-auto test still has the problem.

### What did you expect?

The test suite should pass whatever the operator has set for `NANOCLAW_CHANNELS_REMOTE`. Tests that check the remote resolution order should isolate the variable, as `scripts/update-skills.test.ts` now does.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Check out upstream main (7be8d7f6) and run `pnpm install`.
2. Run `NANOCLAW_CHANNELS_REMOTE=nonexistent pnpm exec vitest run setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts`.
3. The test at `setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts:200` fails on the exec-sequence assertion at line 212.
4. Run `pnpm exec vitest run setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts` without the variable. It passes.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Debian 13, x86_64

### Install or update path

Development checkout

### Channel or interface

Slack

### Agent provider

Not provider-specific

### Relevant redacted logs

```shell
FAIL  setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts > provisioning-core bootstrap > module absent: fetches the channels branch and materializes the one file, engine-style
```

The `toEqual` at line 212 fails because the recorded calls start with the `git fetch` for the override remote rather than `git remote`.

### Suggested fix

This is a test-only change that follows the pattern from #4081. Stub the variable in the suite's `beforeEach`. The existing file-level `afterEach` already restores it.

```diff
--- a/setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts
+++ b/setup/channels/slack-auto.test.ts
@@ -163,4 +163,6 @@
 describe('provisioning-core bootstrap', () => {
   beforeEach(() => {
     state.warns.length = 0;
+    // A channels-remote override in the caller's environment would bypass remote resolution.
+    vi.stubEnv('NANOCLAW_CHANNELS_REMOTE', undefined);
   });
```

One alternative is to delete `NANOCLAW_CHANNELS_REMOTE` and `NANOCLAW_REGISTRY_REMOTE` globally in `src/test-setup.ts`. `vitest.config.ts` loads that file for `src/`, `setup/` and `scripts/` tests. This works, but it also hides the variables from any future test that wants to exercise the override on purpose, so the per-suite stub seems the better choice.

Happy to open a PR if wanted.

issues.title: [capability] Record how a task was solved and distill it into a reusable method skill
issues.body:
Related: #3089 (agent-driven skill learning), #2843 (`/learn`)

### What problem are you trying to solve?

After a long piece of work with my agent produces a good result, such as a multi-day research task, the *way* we got there is lost. That way includes the order of the steps, the checks that caught errors, the dead ends, and the corrections I had to make. The next similar task starts from scratch, and I repeat the same corrections.

`/learn` (#2843) captures **procedures**: exact commands, files and gotchas for repeating the same task. It does not capture **methods**, meaning how to approach a *class* of problems when the content differs. Two things make this hard today:

1. Long sessions get compacted or reset, so by the end the agent no longer sees the early steps and corrections.
2. A skill written straight from one case tends to be overfitted. It is full of that case's numbers and names, or so generic that it adds nothing a capable model would not do anyway.

### What should be possible?

- **Record while working.** `/record start <topic>` makes the agent silently append one line per method event to a file in the group workspace: GOAL, FRAME (scope or constraint), STEP (+ purpose), CORRECTION (the user redirects it), DECISION (+ criterion), DEADEND, CHECK, INSIGHT, RESULT (pointer only). Domain findings stay out of the log. Because the log lives in a file, it survives compaction and session resets. `/record stop` back-fills missed events from the session history and offers to distill.
- **Distill, also retrospectively.** `/distill` turns a record log, or a past stretch of chat history, into a method skill:
  1. separate method from content;
  2. name the problem class and abstract each step to it;
  3. ask the user at most three questions;
  4. draft the skill into `skills-staging/`;
  5. run a **transfer test**: a fresh subagent plans a *different* case with the skill, and a second fresh subagent plans the same case without it. If the skill adds nothing over the baseline, it goes back to step 2.
  6. promote only after the user's explicit OK.
- **Refine.** After the method has been applied again, the differences that would change the next run are merged into it.

The outputs are plain, reviewable SKILL.md files, opt-in, and nothing runs unless the user starts it. This is a concrete, user-triggered take on the loop proposed in #3089.

### What kind of skill is this?

Container skill

### Who benefits?

Users who run long, multi-step work through their agent (research, analysis, investigations) and want later tasks of the same kind to start from what worked, with the user's own working rules.

### What have you tried?

I have run two container skills, `method-record` and `method-distill`, on my own install since mid-October 2026, next to `/learn`. `/learn` alone was not enough for this purpose. Its result was a procedure tied to the one case, not an approach I could reuse on a different case.

The one part that needed host work in my setup is a small systemd timer that exports the chat history into the group folder (last 7 days), so the agent can read the history after compaction. Upstream could probably drop this: `ncl sessions history` already gives the pull layer for this.

### What would this change?

- Adds `container/skills/method-record/SKILL.md` and `container/skills/method-distill/SKILL.md` (+ `references/method-template.md`). Instruction-only: no code, no dependencies.
- Uses existing tools only: file read/write in the group workspace, the Agent tool for the two transfer-test subagents, and `ncl sessions history` for back-fill and retrospective distillation.
- Writes only to the group workspace (`methods/_records/`, `skills-staging/`) until the user approves. Removal means deleting the two skill folders.

### How could we test it?

1. On a fresh clone with the two skills: `/record start test`, do a 5–10 turn task that includes one explicit correction ("too detailed, summarize first"), then `/record stop`. Expected result: the log exists, the correction is recorded as CORRECTION with the rule it implies, and the log contains no domain numbers.
2. `/distill`. Expected result: the agent asks at most three questions, a draft appears in `skills-staging/`, and the transfer-test report shows A (with the skill) vs B (without it) on a case from another domain.
3. Nothing is promoted without an explicit "OK". The correction from step 1 appears as a working rule.

### Can you help maintain it?

- [x] I can help maintain this skill.

issues.title: nanoclaw.sh appears to hang on "Installing the basics…" when sudo needs a password

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
**Summary**                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                      
  On a fresh Debian 13 host where node isn't installed and sudo requires a password (i.e. the user is in sudo group but has no        
  NOPASSWD), bash nanoclaw.sh shows the "Installing the basics…" spinner indefinitely from the user's perspective, then exits with    
  node_missing after sudo gives up. The sudo password prompt is never visible to the user, so the failure looks like a hang.          
                                                                                                                                      
  **Repro**                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                      
  1. Fresh Debian 13 install, user in sudo group, no NOPASSWD.                                                                        
  2. git clone nanoclaw, no Node on PATH.
  3. bash nanoclaw.sh.                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                      
  Result: spinner runs ~60s, then fails with "Couldn't install the basics". The user never sees a password prompt.                    
                                                                                                                                      
  **Root cause**                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                    
  nanoclaw.sh (around line 199–208) launches setup.sh in a backgrounded subshell with stdout+stderr redirected to a log file:         
   
  (                                                                                                                                   
    if bash setup.sh > "$BOOTSTRAP_RAW" 2>&1; then                                                                                    
      ...
  ) &                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                    
  Inside that, setup/install-node.sh runs curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | sudo -E bash -. Sudo's password prompt   
  has no usable surface:
                                                                                                                                      
  - stderr is redirected to the log file → "sudo: a password is required" lands there silently.                                       
  - sudo's /dev/tty fallback gets painted over by the spinner that the parent shell is drawing on the same TTY.
  - Because the subshell is backgrounded (( ... ) &), sudo isn't in the foreground process group; in some configs it just refuses to  
  prompt at all.                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                      
  So the user sees a spinner, never a prompt, and the script eventually reports a generic failure.                                    
                  
  **Evidence from logs/setup-steps/01-bootstrap.log:**                                                                                    
                  
  === NANOCLAW SETUP: INSTALL_NODE ===                                                                                                
  STEP: nodesource-setup                                                                                                              
  === NANOCLAW SETUP: BOOTSTRAP ===                                                                                                   
  ...                                                                                                                                 
  STATUS: node_missing                                                                                                                
  strap] install-node.sh failed
                                                                                                                                      
  (Note: no "sudo: a password is required" line either — it got swallowed.)                                                           
                                                                                                                                      
  **Suggested fixes** (any of these would work, in order of preference)                                                                   
                  
  1. Pre-check sudo before the spinner starts. If command -v node is missing, run sudo -v (or sudo -n true and prompt explicitly if it
   fails) before spinner_start, so the user sees a clean password prompt up front. The spinner can then run uninterrupted.
  2. Run install-node.sh in the foreground (no background subshell, no spinner) when Node is missing, since it's the one step that    
  legitimately needs interactive input.                                                                                               
  3. Detect the sudo failure mode and surface a clear message like "sudo password required — re-run after sudo -v" instead of generic
  "Couldn't install the basics".                                                                                                      
                  
  **Environment**                                                                                                                         
                  
  - OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)                                                                                                  
  - Shell: bash   
  - nanoclaw commit: 0bc082a (main)                                                                                                   
  - User: in sudo group, password required (no NOPASSWD)                                                                              
                                                                                                                                      
  **Workaround for other users hitting this**                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                      
  Run sudo -v first to cache credentials, then bash nanoclaw.sh. Or install Node manually before running the script.

prs.title: fix(onecli): isolate payload tests from the caller's ONECLI_* / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL env
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the `/add-onecli` payload tests pass regardless of the environment they run in.

- **Problem**: `onecli.ts` reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and the `ONECLI_*` keys from `process.env` ahead of `.env`, at import time. The test mocks only the `.env` read, so a shell that exports one of them leaks into the fixtures. With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `ONECLI_GATEWAY_CONTAINER` set, 2 of 13 tests fail (for example `owns endpoint configuration and returns a typed session contribution`). Agent hosts routinely export `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, so the suite fails whenever an agent runs it.
- **Fix**: a `vi.hoisted` block clears the seven keys `onecli.ts` reads before the static import, and `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` restores them after the file.
- **Scope**: test-only, one file. No runtime change.

## Related work

None found (`gh pr list` / `gh issue list` for onecli test env).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, a faithful fake IMAP server for them (`src/test-utils/fake-imap.ts`), the barrel import, and six exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, no Proton DMARC verdict, and a From domain that is Proton's own (`proton.me`, `protonmail.com`, `protonmail.ch`, `pm.me`, or a subdomain), the Bridge account's own, or one listed in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS` (for Proton custom domains). The `From:` must be one plain address on one `From:` line. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread; internal mail from a domain not trusted is also flagged `$NanoClawFailed`, since it is almost always a real Proton user on an unlisted custom domain.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail, with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed, or no longer holds, refuses later replies with core's reason when it gave one. Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused rather than pushing one out. Answers to an open card are not held by the hourly sender limit (a held answer would let a gateway approval time out); mail on a card's thread that turns out not to be an answer is counted.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`): core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received".
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required; certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until core's `onHostStart` has run (the host releases inbound first), so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing. The callback only sets a flag; an adapter set up after host start reads at once, and one still waiting after 5 minutes logs an error (mail stays unread on the server). The inbound id is the adapter's (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts get just the answer. Failures inside the adapter are retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`; routing failures inside the host are not retried (the mail is already handed over). Mail over 40 MB is flagged without being fetched. State is written atomically with a backup (`state.json.bak`); with both unreadable the adapter does not start, so no mail is skipped.
- **Reading mail**: parsing and HTML conversion run in worker threads with timeouts and a heap ceiling, so crafted mail cannot stall the host. When a mail has both bodies the HTML is read. html-to-text runs with no word wrap and no upper-casing. HTML hidden from a mail-client reader (`display:none`, `hidden`, zero-size, transparent text, `<template>`, …) is kept but marked `[hidden CODE: … /hidden CODE]` with a per-mail random code, and invisible or direction characters are marked too (a lone direction mark beside Hebrew/Arabic letters, or a zero-width space between Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar letters, is ordinary text and left alone); when the body the agent gets carries any mark, a note tells it to treat marked text as suspect. Quoted history and signatures are cut; a forward keeps the forwarded mail (a forward's subject prefix, or a "Forwarded message" / "Begin forwarded message:" line before any quoted history). A forward sent as an attachment (`message/rfc822`) is read into the body. Attachment names are cleaned, made unique per mail and given extensions from their MIME type. A non-ASCII sender domain is shown with its punycode beside it. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300.
- **Limits**: attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. Bounces, auto-replies (`Auto-Submitted`, `X-Loop`, no-reply senders, …) and mailing-list mail (`List-Id`, `List-Post`, `Precedence: list`) are skipped before the router. `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Hourly limits and the hold queue**: at most 20 mails an hour from one sender reach the host; beyond that, mail waits unread (in the state's retry list) and is handed over as the hour frees up. **This is a throttle, not a loop breaker**: two agents mailing each other are slowed to about 20 mails an hour each, not stopped. Bridge drops every loop marker on outgoing mail (below), and core has no loop handling for any channel yet, so that risk stays open project-wide. New addresses not yet approved are limited to 10 an hour, 200 in any 7 days, and 20 per domain in the same 7 days, freed early when core settles (approves or denies) an address; a new address over its domain's share waits, re-checked hourly. Held mail is capped at 200, of which new senders may use 100 and any one domain 20, so approved senders' over-limit mail always has room. Past a cap, mail is left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. The own-address check, the inbound auto-reply filter and the hourly throttle are what remain.
- **Message kinds**: a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743, a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call); loop handling in core; laying out HTML tables row by row (html-to-text's default runs cells together; a small follow-up).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted, and why only for some domains (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values. Since a Proton account can also send as an address outside Proton's domains (a custom domain, or a connected external address), and nothing Proton adds says which, `internal` is trusted only for the domains above. On a real inbox, every internal mail without a verdict came from a Proton domain or a subdomain (`notify.proton.me`).
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, six deps.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

CI does not run tests on PRs into `channels`, so these were run locally on this head (57d4a78e) after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from this branch's own lockfile:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/proton-mail.test.ts src/channels/proton-mail-adapter.test.ts \
    src/channels/proton-mail-registration.test.ts src/test-utils/fake-imap.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  241 passed (241)
$ pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
(no output, exit 0)
```

- `eslint`: 0 errors on the new files.
- The whole suite on the same install: no failures in these files (16 elsewhere, in setup scripts and other channels' registration tests, unchanged by this PR).
- `proton-mail.test.ts`, the helpers: sender check (DMARC, `X-Pm-Origin`, trusted domains), plain-address and display-name checks, card matching and distinct commands, quote, signature and forward handling, hidden-text and invisible-character marks, attachment names, header caps, poll bounds, TLS options, skip and mailing-list rules.
- `proton-mail-adapter.test.ts`, the adapter against the fake IMAP server, faked SMTP and real mailparser: sender identity; approval cards (late answers, restarts, closed cards, ceilings, gateway confirmations, answers past the hourly limit); startup on `onHostStart`; the cursor across restarts and UIDVALIDITY changes; retries and giving up; worker timeouts; the hourly limits, the hold queue's caps and per-domain shares, settled addresses freeing their slots; forwards, hidden text and attached forwards.
- Each fix from the third review has a test that failed on the head before it (fc9ecaec, then each fix commit in turn).
- A read-only replay of the old head's and this head's rules over a real inbox (638 mails, counts only): no change to any sender decision; the text changes are no word wrap, heading case, horizontal rules drawn 40 dashes long instead of 80, forwards kept whole, and the hidden-text note now added in the mails whose hidden HTML held block elements.
- Adapter tests run against a scratch working directory and refuse to run otherwise, so they never touch a real install's `store/`.
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5 (Debian 13, Docker): the install's own build of this adapter has been live since 24 Oct with Bridge 3.27.0 (pinned certificate, required STARTTLS, card answers from Outlook).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New channel: Proton Mail via a local Proton Mail Bridge (`/add-proton-mail`). Native IMAP/SMTP adapter; mail counts as from its sender only on Proton's DMARC pass (or Proton-internal mail from a trusted domain), and approval cards are answered by replying to the card email itself. Proton custom domains other than the Bridge account's own go in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, trusted only for the domains above; anyone with a free Proton account is verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card.
- Hidden HTML and invisible characters are marked for the agent, not removed, with a code the sender cannot predict, so a mark without the code was written by the sender.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, and new addresses are limited per hour, per 7 days and per domain, so strangers cannot fill `pending_channel_approvals` or the cards the owner's approvals need.
- Loops: throttled, not stopped (see Hourly limits); stated here and in SKILL.md (#3726).
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `html-to-text@10.0.1`, `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

On Linux, a new local OneCLI gateway now publishes its admin API and Postgres on `127.0.0.1`; only the gateway proxy stays on the Docker bridge.

- **Before**: on bare-metal Linux the OneCLI installer publishes the gateway, admin API and Postgres on the `docker0` address. Agent containers only need the gateway (`host.docker.internal:10255`).
- **Fresh install**: when the installer picked `docker0`, setup edits the stock admin, Postgres and `APP_URL` lines in `~/.onecli/docker-compose.yml` to `127.0.0.1`, and points `ONECLI_URL` and the CLI `api-host` at `http://127.0.0.1:10254`. A bind the user chose (`ONECLI_BIND_HOST` exported, or anything but `docker0`), a compose file without the stock lines, and non-Linux installs are left as installed.
- **Existing install**: binds are left alone; one `docker port` check reports `ADMIN_NOT_LOOPBACK`, and the upgrade guide gives the manual steps.

## Related work

Supersedes #2434 (closes #2433), which targeted `setup/onecli.ts` before OneCLI setup moved into `/add-onecli` (d5c7cccc). Related: #3302 (thanks @wakqasahmed) saves the bridge bind for the gateway (#2903); main already does that, and this keeps it for `:10255`.

prs.title: fix(setup): install jq so channel setup works on stock Linux and WSL
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now installs jq, so Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup work on a stock Ubuntu or WSL install. It builds on #4200's sudo pre-flight, now merged.

- **Problem**: these skills pipe `curl` into `jq`, and nothing installs it. On WSL, Slack setup died at "Resolve your DM channel" with `jq: command not found`. The filters also let a bad reply through: `"slack:" + null` prints `slack:` and exits 0, so a revoked token or a missing `im:write` saved an empty id.
- **Fix**:
  - `setup.sh` installs jq with the system package manager (apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman, apk; Homebrew on macOS). #4200's one up-front sudo prompt now covers it ("Setup needs to install Node and jq"). The install itself only runs `sudo -n`.
  - The Slack and Discord id filters use `jq -er '.x // error(...)'`, so a reply without the id fails the step.
  - An older install without jq: a step that fails because the shell can't find jq now says how to install it, instead of a bare exit 127.
- **macOS**: macOS 26 ships `/usr/bin/jq` (checked on 26.6.1); reports say 15 does too. The repo states no macOS minimum, so a Mac without jq gets it from Homebrew, which `nanoclaw.sh` already requires.

## Related work

Replaces this PR's first version (jq-free Node one-liners), per review. Builds on #4200 (merged).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests: the three id filters on good and bad replies, plus the Dial pin's file mode (4); the jq install on each package manager, as root, on macOS, and with no sudo or a password sudo (15); jq in the sudo pre-flight (11); the missing-jq message, with other failures keeping their own reason (9). Full vitest on 4112407f (main merged in): 4340 passed, 15 skipped; one unrelated update e2e test timed out under full load (that file passes alone, 29/29).
- Live, fresh exe.dev Ubuntu VM, password-sudo user, no Node, Docker or jq, real installer in a PTY: one sudo prompt, jq installed, agent replied. With Node from uvx: one prompt, for jq alone. On that VM a real Telegram `getMe` works; Slack and Discord with a bad token now exit 5 with no output, where main printed `slack:` and `discord:@me:`. With jq removed, a jq step through the real engine says to install jq.
- Not run: the Slack and Discord success paths against real APIs, a Mac without jq, non-apt distros (tests only).
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Setup now installs jq when it's missing, so Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup work on stock Ubuntu and WSL. Slack and Discord setup now stop when the API reply has no id, instead of saving an empty one.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

jq comes from the system package manager, through `sudo -n` only: no prompt behind the spinner. If the user refuses sudo and only jq needed it, setup goes on and says to install jq. API replies are only parsed, never run. The Dial pin writes its temp file as 0600.

prs.title: fix(setup): ask for the sudo password up front on Linux, and give WSL the right docker-group hint
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

On Linux and WSL, setup now asks for the sudo password once, in the open, before the progress spinner hides it.

- **Problem**: `nanoclaw.sh` runs the Node bootstrap under a spinner, and the container step installs or starts Docker inside a windowed step. sudo's prompt lands under that output, the user never sees it, and it times out (#2025).
- **Fix**: a pre-flight in `nanoclaw.sh` (`setup/lib/sudo-preflight.sh`) says it will install Node, then runs `sudo -v` in the foreground, before the bootstrap spinner. It asks only when the bootstrap will really use sudo: it follows `setup/lib/node-version.sh` (the #4183 minimums, uvx, version-manager Node), so an unpatched apt Node 22 asks and a patched or nvm-managed one doesn't. The container step asks the same way right before it installs or starts Docker or adds the user to the docker group; a password still cached from the Node ask skips that prompt. When Docker runs but the socket refuses the user, the reason reads "add you to the docker group". On WSL, the docker-group hint says to run `wsl --shutdown`, since logging out doesn't refresh groups there.
- **Out of scope**: the service-side docker-group fix (separate PR).

## Related work

Closes #2025
Refs #2006

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/lib/sudo-preflight-shell.test.ts setup/lib/sudo-preflight.test.ts setup/auto.container-sudo.test.ts setup/lib/node-version.test.ts`: 68 pass. They cover Node missing or below the minimum (apt vs a version manager), patched Node off PATH, uvx, Docker missing (left to the container step), root, passwordless sudo, no TTY, and refused sudo. A scripted run of setup.sh's real path with a fake `sudo` agreed with the pre-flight on 19 machine shapes.
- Live, with a user whose sudo needs a password and no Node or Docker:
  - exe.dev Ubuntu 24.04 at this head, Node from NodeSource: exactly one prompt, before the spinner, for Node; the container step installed Docker without asking again. With #4201 on top, the install finished and the agent replied. With the image's `uvx` (Node without sudo), the one prompt came right before the container step, for Docker.
  - Windows 11 WSL 3.0.3 / Ubuntu 24.04 with Docker Engine, before the Docker ask moved to the container step: exactly one prompt, before the spinner.
  - The same WSL run on main showed the prompt after "Installing the basics…".

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Mattermost now gets the host's setup retry when its server, or a proxy in front of it, is briefly down at boot.

- **Problem**: the registry retries `adapter.setup` only for errors named `NetworkError`. The adapter threw `MattermostApiError` for any non-2xx and a bare `TypeError` when `fetch` failed. On a live install, a proxy's 502 at boot left the channel dead until a manual restart.
- **Fix**: 5xx/408/429 replies, requests with no full reply (refused, reset, DNS, cut-off body, timeout) and WebSocket failures before the token is accepted are now named `NetworkError`. Other 4xx and a rejected token still fail fast. Core is unchanged.
- **Out of scope**: the inline retry covers about 17 s (2 + 5 + 10 s). A longer outage needs a background re-arm: open #4055, `NetworkError`-only, which this change makes cover Mattermost.

## Related work

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Turns on Dependabot version updates for every manifest it can read, behind a release-age cooldown, and removes the Renovate config that never ran.

- **Problem**: main has no `dependabot.yml`. Alerts are on but security-update PRs are off, so a fixed version reaches us only when someone bumps it by hand, as with this week's Node.js base image. On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped a credential stealer to PyPI and Docker Hub for about two hours ([incident](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-incident-oct-21-2026)); a cooldown keeps a release like that out.
- **Fix**: weekly entries for GitHub Actions, the root pnpm project, `container/agent-runner` (bun), the `container/Dockerfile` base image, and the skill pins. Cooldown is 7 days, 14 for majors and agent-runner minors (its 0.x SDKs break on a minor), 3 for the base image; never below pnpm's 3-day gate. Minor/patch bumps are grouped, except root production and agent-runner runtime deps (one PR each, per CLAUDE.md), so the agent SDK and `claude-code` (skill pins) move in separate PRs. Majors come alone; nothing merges itself. `chat` moves only with its `@chat-adapter/*` pins; Node and `@types/node` majors wait for a deliberate Node move.
- **Out of scope**: turning on security-update PRs (a repo setting); the Dockerfile's `BUN_VERSION`, `PNPM_VERSION` and `NPM_VERSION` args and `# syntax` line; skill Dockerfiles and `go.mod` (listed in `not-covered.json`).

## Related work

No issue. Follows https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3968 (actions pinned by SHA) and https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4007 (skill-pins manifest, merged).

- Renovate: no PRs, `renovate/*` branches or dashboard issue since the file landed 2026-07-29.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): compact preset sessions against their selected context window
prs.body:
## Problem

A user reported that in a 快速 (`yd-fast`) chat, after pasting a ~400k-token document with "请只回复：收到。" and then asking about the weather, the context ring stayed at 100%, usage kept growing past the 400k limit, and auto-compaction never ran.

The session selects a 400k window, but the real model behind it (e.g. `deepseek-flash`) accepts 1M, so every request succeeds and overflow recovery never starts. In embedded runs the session's own threshold compaction is disabled (`getCompactionSettings().enabled === false`), so preflight compaction (`runSessionCompactionIfNeeded`) is the only automatic trigger. It resolved the window from provider/model only and used the native 1M window, so it compacted at 980k while the run, the session row and the UI used 400k.

The same mismatch affects:
- the `model_context_bytes` trigger added in #2988: it watched 6.4 MB while a 400k run hydrates at most 3.2 MB;
- 8 server models that declare no native window (kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, qwen3.6-plus, qwen3.5-plus, MiniMax-M2.7, glm-5.1, glm-5, doubao-seed-2-0-mini). The run used 400k, but preflight fell back to the 200k default and compacted early, at about 45%.

## Change

One version-scoped OpenClaw patch, `openclaw-session-window-preflight-compaction.patch`. No LobsterAI runtime code changes.

- `resolveMemoryFlushContextWindowTokens` takes the session's `SessionEntry.contextWindow` selection and resolves it from the configured model's `contextWindows` with the run's rule: never exceed a known native window, and use the selection when the model declares none. An unknown option keeps the native value.
- Both preflight callers (`runSessionCompactionIfNeeded`, `runMemoryFlushIfNeeded`) pass the selection.
- Preflight compaction uses the manual planner, which already falls back to the smallest valid tail. A single oversized turn is therefore summarized instead of being skipped as "too small".
- Also adds a strong validator in `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, registers the patch in `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`, and documents it in the patch README.

## Verification

- New OpenClaw tests: preflight uses the selected window, keeps the native window for unknown or larger options, and uses the selection when no native window is declared. The new preflight integration case fails on the old code.
- The full 89-patch series applies to a clean v2026.8.1 checkout with strong validation passing. `memory-flush.test.ts` 19/19 and `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` 107/107 pass, and LobsterAI patch tests 106/106 pass. Core typecheck shows only the existing `managed-image-replay.ts` errors; oxfmt, oxlint and ESLint are clean.
- All 37 server models from a real local config × `yd-fast` / `yd-ultra` / no selection (111 cases): preflight window equals the embedded run budget.
- Isolated gateway with a mock 1M-window model, three turns (≈410k-token paste, then two short questions):

| Runtime / model class | Turn 1 | Turn 2 | Turn 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (11-05 runtime) | 110% | 110%, no compaction | 110% |
| After, native 1M | 110% | **8%**, compacted | 8% |
| After, no native window | 110% | **8%**, compacted | 8% |
| After, native 262k | 167% | **11%**, compacted | 11% |

Turn 1 still ends above 100%, because nothing older exists to compact before a single oversized prompt is sent. Compaction runs at the next preflight.

Not covered: real-model in-app runs (needs account credentials and credits), and the overflow-error path for a native window below the paste size (the mock never returns context overflow).

## Behavior notes

OpenClaw runtime change only. 快速/旗舰 sessions now compact around 380k instead of 980k. Models without a declared native window compact at 380k instead of 180k. Ordinary model sessions (no `contextWindow` selection) are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(memory): stop memory search from launching a second app instance
prs.body:
## Summary

On Windows, every `memory_search` with vector memory on attached `memory-search-knn.child.js` to the prompt and pulled the window forward. Vector recall also failed every time.

OpenClaw spawns its vector KNN child through `process.execPath` with an allowlisted env that drops `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`. In LobsterAI that binary is `LobsterAI.exe`, so the child booted a second app instance instead of Node:

1. It reached `second-instance`.
2. The Open With handler queued the `.js` path as a file to attach.
3. The KNN query got no JSON back: `memory vector KNN child returned malformed JSON`.

While reproducing this, a second problem showed up: picking an embedding provider in Settings never loaded the OpenClaw plugin behind it. OpenClaw treats a non-empty `plugins.allow` as strict, so OpenAI, Gemini and Ollama embeddings silently fell back to keyword search.

## Related Issue

User report: "Agent那边好像一调用记忆就会跳这个文件" (from a user's logs, 2026-11-05)

## Changes Made

- **OpenClaw patch** `openclaw-memory-knn-child-electron-node-env.patch` (v2026.8.1): sets `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` for the KNN child under Electron. The env allowlist stays; the patch includes OpenClaw tests and is registered in the patch validators and the reviewed patch set.
  - Upstream main and v2026.11.1 still have the same bug. Upstream fixed the similar code-mode case (#121927 / #122037) by turning code mode off under Electron, but KNN has no such fallback.
- **Second-instance guard:** `second-instance` now ignores launches whose arguments point inside the app's resources or the OpenClaw runtime, so a stray child can't attach bundled files or take focus.
- **Embedding plugins:** config sync allows and enables the plugin that serves the selected embedding provider (openai, google, ollama), but only when the runtime has it, either bundled or preinstalled.
  - Voyage and Mistral are separate npm plugins in OpenClaw v2026.8.1 and are not shipped, so selecting them logs a warning and nothing is added to the allowlist.
  - One `EmbeddingProvider` constant is now shared by main, config sync and Settings.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

Unit tests, lint and compile:

- The 8 affected test files pass (265 tests). The new tests fail without the fixes.
- Patched OpenClaw KNN tests pass 9/9.
- ESLint is clean on all changed files.
- `compile:electron` and the renderer `tsc` both pass.

End to end on Windows:

- **Runtime:** with a runtime rebuilt from source with the patch, `openclaw memory search` under Electron Node mode returns vector hits (3/3 runs). The unpatched runtime hangs: its KNN child started Chromium GPU and network processes.
- **Real app, real model:** dev LobsterAI from this branch, signed in, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, local OpenAI-compatible embeddings.
  - The agent called `memory_search`, embeddings ran, and the answer came from the seeded memory.
  - The KNN child had no subprocesses.
  - No `second-instance` event fired and the composer stayed empty.
  - `openai` was allowed with no manual config.
  - Selecting Voyage logged the new warning.
- **Guard in the real app:**
  - Second instances pointing at a bundled KNN script or an Electron resources file were ignored.
  - "Open with" on a user file still attached it and focused the window.

Not covered: no packaged installer build. Gemini and Ollama embeddings are covered by unit tests only.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)

## Additional Notes

- The full `npm test` run on Windows shows 15 failing files that this branch doesn't touch: git snapshots with tab characters in file names, POSIX file modes, temp-dir EPERM, Word build artifacts, and similar. They fail the same way when run on their own.
- The OpenClaw patch must move to `src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.ts` when the runtime is upgraded past upstream's 2026-10-16 refactor, unless upstream fixes it first.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): apply sign-out config shrink without a gateway restart
prs.body:
## Problem

When a user signs out, LobsterAI re-renders `openclaw.json` without the `lobsterai-server` plan catalog (`models`), which is most of the file (e.g. 48 KB → 19 KB). OpenClaw treats a >50% shrink as a clobber:

1. `config.apply` is rejected (`size-drop:` in `io.write-safety.ts`) and LobsterAI retries.
2. LobsterAI falls back to a deferred gateway restart (`config-delivery-fallback:media-entitlement-changed`).
3. The restarted gateway "restores" the same bytes from `.bak` (`size-drop-vs-last-good:`).

Each sign-out costs a 12–60 s gateway restart on Windows. On the reporting machine one cost 58.5 s, with `.rejected.*` / `.clobbered.*` files on 10-30, 11-04 and 11-05.

`config.apply` has no way to pass the size-drop allowance. Keeping a stale plan catalog after sign-out would also have to keep the agent model allowlist, model-compat and thinking profiles consistent, so it was rejected as a contorted workaround. Per the patch policy, this adds a small version-scoped OpenClaw patch.

## Changes

**OpenClaw patch** `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/openclaw-config-apply-size-drop-allowance.patch` (documented in the patch README):
- `config.apply` accepts an optional boolean `allowConfigSizeDrop`, mapped to the existing `ConfigWriteOptions.allowConfigSizeDrop`. It waives only the size check: `gateway-mode-removed` and unreadable-baseline writes are still rejected. Writers that omit it (Control UI, CLI, doctor, agents) keep the full guard.
- Read-time recovery skips a `.bak` that is byte-identical to the current file. Restoring it only rewrote the same bytes and recorded a false clobber. Clobbers by other writers still restore, because OpenClaw's own writes rotate the previous file into `.bak`. This covers sign-outs persisted while the gateway is stopped.

**LobsterAI** (`src/main/libs/openclawConfigSizeDrop.ts`, `openclawConfigDelivery.ts`):
- Claims the waiver only when the shrink would trip the guard and everything outside `models` still passes it. Large drops elsewhere, including from LobsterAI bugs, keep OpenClaw's protection.
- Measures the gateway's current config from `config.get` `raw`, or from `parsed` when the gateway withholds `raw`. It does that whenever text redaction is unsafe, which LobsterAI's `${ENV}` refs always trigger.
- A gateway without the patch rejects the unknown param. LobsterAI detects that and falls back to the previous restart path instead of treating the config as invalid.

## Verification

- `npm test -- openclawConfig`: 368 passed. CI eslint on touched files clean. `npm run compile:electron` OK.
- OpenClaw: the full 89-patch series applies cleanly. `config.test.ts`, `io.observe-recovery.test.ts` and the gateway-protocol suites pass with 713 tests. 4 `config.openFile` cases fail on Windows with or without this patch (POSIX path expectations). tsgo core reports no errors in touched files.
- Runtime rebuilt from the patched source. End-to-end against real gateway processes, a temp OpenClaw home and a real LobsterAI-rendered config (44.8 KB → 15.3 KB): **23/23**.
  - Live sign-out: waiver claimed, applied, no restart, no `.rejected` file.
  - Restart after sign-out: no auto-restore.
  - Sign-in works.
  - Stopped-gateway sign-out: no restore or clobber; one observe warning, then clean.
  - An unpatched-runtime control reproduces the old auto-restore and exercises the compat fallback.
  - The first E2E run is what caught the `raw: null` case (commit 2).
- Manual desktop test: sign-out at 01:46:19 logged `claiming the size-drop waiver ... 39826->17250 bytes` and `mode=applied` in 826 ms. No `Config write rejected`, no fallback restart, no new `.rejected`/`.clobbered` files.

## Notes

- After the accepted write, OpenClaw still logs one `Config observe anomaly (size-drop-vs-last-good)` line before it promotes the new last-known-good. It restores nothing.
- A `HARD RESTART reason=server-models-updated` during sign-in, in the same manual session, is the existing sign-in path and is unrelated to this change.
- The runtime build fingerprint includes the new patch, so `npm run electron:dev:openclaw` and packaging rebuild the runtime.

prs.title: fix(dsh): stop the runtime on quit and reclaim leftovers on restart
prs.body:
## Problem

On macOS, after a normal quit the built-in DeepSeek Harness (dsh) process stays alive and keeps listening on its port. After a restart, Settings shows "not running" and the leftover is never reclaimed.

## Root cause

- The quit path (`before-quit` → `runAppCleanup` → `app.exit()`) never emits `will-quit`, and `DshEngineManager` only killed its child from a `will-quit` hook. `runAppCleanup` never stopped dsh.
- The child is Electron in Node mode, so when main exits it is reparented to launchd (ppid 1) and keeps running.
- The `~/.dsh` writer lock records the **main** pid, so after a restart the lock looks stale. A second dsh writer could then start next to the orphan, which risks corrupting the shared session log.

## Changes

- `main.ts`: `runAppCleanup` calls `stopDshFeatureRuntimes()` at the start, so it overlaps the other steps, and awaits it before the store closes (step `dsh-runtime`).
- `dshEngineManager.ts`: `doStart` bails before spawning if a stop landed during its awaits, for example a quit while a start was in flight.
- New `dshOrphanReaper.ts`:
  - Scans `ps -axww -o pid=,ppid=,command=` for `<same execPath> --expose-internals … web --port N --no-open` whose parent is not a main process of the same install.
  - Sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 6s.
  - Because it matches the same executable path, a dev build and a packaged app never reap each other's runtimes. It also matches the generated launcher entry from #3007.
- `handlers.ts`: reaps before every `ensureDshEngineReady`, ahead of the shared-home decision, and at launch when dsh is enabled.
- POSIX only. Windows has no `ps`, so there it relies on the quit-time stop.

## Verification

Tested in an isolated dev instance (`LOBSTERAI_DEV_USER_DATA_DIR`, `LOBSTERAI_DSH_AUTOSTART=1`) that ran next to a packaged app. Each quit used SIGTERM, which goes through the same `runAppCleanupAndExit` path as Cmd+Q.

- **Unfixed build:** after quit, the dsh child stayed alive with ppid 1, still listening on its port. Reproduced.
- **Fixed build, launch:** logged `[DSH] Stopping 1 runtime(s) left by an earlier run: pid=… ppid=1` and freed the port.
- **Fixed build, quit:** dsh exited together with main. Cleanup took 298ms.
- **Packaged app:** its dsh runtime was untouched throughout.
- `npm test` (775 files), `npm run compile:electron`, and changed-file eslint all pass.

Not yet tested: a real Cmd+Q from a packaged build, and Windows.

## Electron-specific behavior

- Quit cleanup now waits for dsh to exit, up to the existing 5s+1s stop grace, overlapped with the other steps.
- At launch, when dsh is enabled, the app spawns one `ps` (macOS/Linux only).

prs.title: perf(openclaw): ship build-info.json beside the gateway bundle
prs.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw's startup-migration checkpoint keys on `build-info.json` `builtAt`. It looks for `./build-info.json`, `../build-info.json` and `../../dist/build-info.json` relative to its own module. Those paths fit the `dist/` chunk layout, but LobsterAI runs the gateway from `gateway-bundle.mjs` at the runtime root, and only `dist/build-info.json` exists there.

As a result the build identity is `null`, the checkpoint is never recorded, and every gateway start reruns the full doctor preflight: legacy state migrations, plugin convergence, and 4–5 config snapshot reads.

Evidence:
- Installed and dev profiles have only the `primary` row in `state/openclaw.sqlite` `schema_meta`. There is no `startup-migrations` or `state-migrations` row.
- The host logs `startup summary: ... checkpoint=unknown` on every start.

## Change

- Add `dist/build-info.json` → `build-info.json` to `OPENCLAW_BUNDLE_ASSET_TARGETS`. This is the same mechanism `web-tree-sitter.wasm` already uses.
- The electron-builder hook, `finalize-openclaw-runtime` and the payload verification all read that list, so a runtime without the file now fails packaging instead of silently losing the checkpoint.
- The installer resource-recovery checks are unchanged. A missing `build-info.json` only costs startup time; the bundle still works.
- Version, commit and bundled model-catalog stamp lookups in the bundle read the same file. They now resolve as they do in the unbundled runtime.

## Measurements

Windows, dev app on the production renderer, run on a copy of a real profile with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`:

| | `gateway-run-bootstrap` | spawn → `loading configuration` |
|---|---|---|
| Before (checkpoint never hits) | ~5 s (9–12 s under load) | 6.4–13.8 s |
| After, first start (records checkpoint) | 12.1 s | 14.4 s |
| After, later starts (`checkpoint=hit`) | 1.25–2.2 s | 2.6–3.5 s |

Part of the plugin module-graph load moves from plugin convergence into plugin loading, so the net saving is about 2.5–3.5 s per warm start. In the cleanest interleaved A/B pair, launch-to-gateway-handshake was 11.8 s with the fix and 16.0 s without.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run tests/openclawBundleAssets.test.ts tests/openclawWindowsPayload.test.ts tests/windowsInstallerContract.test.ts`: all pass.
- CI ESLint on the touched test files: clean.
- `node scripts/bundle-openclaw-gateway.cjs` on an existing runtime places the file. Three app starts on a profile copy logged `checkpoint=miss` and then `hit` twice, and the `schema_meta` rows appeared.
- Not checked in a packaged installer build.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): re-render install paths in the no-model config sync
prs.body:
## Problem

LobsterAI installs can share one profile (`%APPDATA%\LobsterAI`) and so one `openclaw.json`. This happens with the installed app plus `npm run electron:dev`, after a reinstall to another directory, or when a macOS app is moved. The config sync that runs while no API model is resolved (`writeMinimalConfig`: app startup before server models load, and logout) copied `plugins` and `mcp` from the existing file unchanged. As a result:

- `plugins.load.paths` kept pointing at the other install's `resources/cfmind/third-party-extensions`, so the gateway loaded that install's third-party plugins.
- MCP stdio servers kept launching the other install's `LobsterAI.exe` / `app.asar/node_modules/...`.
- Sync still reported `changed=false`.

The full sync was not affected, because it already re-renders `plugins.load` and owns `mcp`. The gateway, however, is first started from the minimal config. On a machine with a DLP agent, the dev gateway made about 17.5k sync fs calls into the installed app's folder per start (about 15 s). With corrected paths, plugin loading took about 2.3 s.

## Change

- `openclawPluginRepairPaths.ts`: adds `isRuntimeThirdPartyExtensionsDir()` (the matcher Quick Repair already used) and `rebaseRuntimeExtensionLoadPaths()`. Entries naming a LobsterAI runtime's extensions dir (`resources/cfmind` or `vendor/openclaw-runtime/<name>`) are rebased onto this install's `findBundledExtensionsDir()`, or dropped when it returns null. User-linked plugin paths are kept.
- `writeMinimalConfig`: runs the preserved `plugins` through that rebase. It also renders and owns `mcp` through `buildMcpConfig()`, which is now shared with the full sync.
- `openclawRepairPreflight.ts`: uses the shared matcher. Its behaviour is unchanged.

Behaviour note: with no model configured, `mcp` now follows LobsterAI's MCP state instead of the last file contents, the same as the full sync.

## Verification

- `npm test -- openclawConfigSync openclawPluginRepairPaths openclawRepairPreflight`: 214 passed, 6 skipped.
- New runtime tests cover a profile written by another install, in both no-model and full sync. The two no-model tests fail without the fix.

prs.title: fix(dsh): install plugins with bundled pnpm and bump dsh to 0.2.2-rc.1
prs.body:
## Summary

Plugin installs in the built-in DeepSeek Harness (dsh) workbench failed for most users with `pnpm was not found`. `dsh web` started directly hands pnpm operations to `pnpm` on PATH, and a Dock- or Start-menu-launched app has none (macOS gives GUI apps only `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`). It only worked on machines where the app inherited a terminal PATH with pnpm.

- **Bundled pnpm**: `scripts/build-dsh-runtime.cjs` unpacks the pnpm pinned in `package.json` `dsh.pnpm` (11.28.5, the version upstream pins in its `packageManager`) to `package-manager/pnpm` inside the runtime, outside dsh's `node_modules`, and starts it once during the build.
- **Launcher**: `DshEngineManager` writes `userData/dsh-launcher/launch.mjs`, which statically imports the runtime's `lib/bin.js` and calls `runCli({ packageManager })`. pnpm runs on Electron in Node mode with the cowork node/npm/npx shims first on PATH. A runtime without bundled pnpm, or any failure writing the launcher, falls back to the direct entry.
- **dsh 0.2.2-rc.1**: version bump, expose-internals patch carried forward (still needed), mac-arm64 archive rebuilt and recorded.
- **Scripts**: `dsh:runtime:verify` and `dsh:e2e` now check the bundled pnpm with no pnpm or node on PATH; e2e boots through the generated launcher; the pack manifest records `pnpmVersion`.

## Not done yet

- **mac-x64 and win-x64 archives are not rebuilt.** `dsh.runtimes` holds only mac-arm64, so builds from this branch cannot install dsh on Intel macs or Windows until those two targets are built on matching machines, uploaded, and recorded with `npm run dsh:runtime:url`.
- Windows plugins installed from `github:` specs still need git on PATH; the bundled MinGit is not passed to pnpm.

## Electron-specific behavior

- dsh is now spawned with a generated launcher under `userData/dsh-launcher/` instead of the runtime's `lib/bin.js`.
- Existing users re-download the runtime once (new version and digest).
- No IPC, storage schema, or OpenClaw config changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run dsh` (137 tests), including one that runs the generated launcher against a stand-in entry
- [x] ESLint on touched TS files, `npm run compile:electron`
- [x] `npm run dsh:e2e` on mac-arm64: HTTP install with digest check, provider/model RPC, external plugin load, boot through the launcher, bundled pnpm reached with no pnpm on PATH
- [x] Bare-PATH repro (`env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`): before, `pnpm was not found`; after, `dsh-claude-design-system` installs with `pnpm v11.28.5`
- [x] `npm run dsh:runtime:verify-urls mac-arm64`: uploaded archive matches
- [ ] Install a plugin from the workbench in a packaged build launched from the Dock
- [ ] Rebuild, upload, and verify mac-x64 and win-x64

prs.title: fix(cowork): keep images when copying a user message
prs.body: ## 问题 用户反馈：任务（用户消息）中带有图片时，点击消息下方的复制按钮，再粘贴到输入框，只有文字没有图片。 原因：复制按钮只把 `message.content` 作为纯文本写入剪贴板，图片存放在消息元数据（`imageAttachmentPreviews` / `imageAttachments`）中，从未被复制。 ## 修复 - **复制**（`UserMessageItem.tsx`、新增 `services/messageClipboard.ts`）：消息带图片时，剪贴板除纯文本外还写入一份 HTML，以 data URL `` 携带图片，并带有 LobsterAI 专用标记。图片优先读取原始文件，原文件缺失时回退到消息中保存的图片数据。无图片的消息仍只复制纯文本。 - **粘贴**（`CoworkPromptInput.tsx` `handlePaste`、`clipboardAttachments.ts`）：识别到该标记时，把图片像粘贴截图一样加为附件；文字仍走原有粘贴流程（长文本照常变成粘贴文本卡片）。没有标记的剪贴板内容处理方式不变。 - **IPC**：新增 `clipboard:writeTextAndHtml`（`ClipboardIpc.WriteTextAndHtml`），在一次剪贴板操作中同时写入文字和 HTML；失败时退回只复制文字。 浏览器批注的传输截图不会被复制，与消息中展示的内容一致。 ## Electron 相关变更 - 新增 IPC 通道 `clipboard:writeTextAndHtml`（main + preload + 类型声明）。无存储、运行时或 OpenClaw 配置变更。 ## 验证 - `npm test -- clipboard UserMessage CoworkPromptInput imageAttachments`：9 个测试文件、84 个用例通过（新增 `messageClipboard.test.ts`，扩充 `clipboardAttachments.test.ts`）。 - 改动文件 ESLint（`--max-warnings 0`）、`tsc --noEmit`、`npm run compile:electron` 均通过。 - macOS 开发版端到端验证：在含两张图片的用户消息上点击复制，系统剪贴板中同时有文字和带两张图片的 HTML；在输入框按 Cmd+V 后，文字贴入，两张图片作为附件出现并保存到工作目录；普通文本粘贴行为不变。 - 未覆盖：Windows 上的实际粘贴（CF_HTML 包裹格式有单元测试覆盖）。

prs.title: feat(desktop-companion): continue selection requests after sign-in
prs.body:
## Summary
Selection users (mostly bundled with the dictionary) translate without signing in, but very few of them sign in. When they reach a signed-in feature (explain, summarize, follow-up, read aloud), three things get in the way:

- The prompt looked like an error and gave no reason to sign in.
- Clicking it opened the browser, and the unpinned card closed.
- The login itself reset the translation/read-aloud card and restarted the gateway, which closed the selection card too.

Either way the user's request was lost, and none of this could be measured. This PR keeps the request alive through the sign-in, makes the prompt say what signing in unlocks, and adds funnel events.

Design doc: `specs/features/desktop-companion/2026-11-05-selection-login-conversion-design.md`

## Related Issue
None.

## Changes Made
- **Sign-in prompt**: a compact row instead of the error style. It names the blocked feature, shows the new-user benefit (reuses `loginIntroductionPromo`) and has one pill button. A blocked follow-up gets its prompt under the question, where the answer would go. The waiting and failed states stay in the same row.
- **Continue after sign-in**: a new `desktop-companion:login-start` IPC pins the card before the browser opens.
  - Selection card: the renderer reruns its request when it sees the new session.
  - Translation/read-aloud card: the main process remembers the tool, the text and the blocked question. After the auth exchange (`handleLoginSucceeded()` in `main.ts`), it reopens the card pinned and in place with `showInactive`, reruns the tool under the new account, and sends the blocked follow-up once.
  - Closing the card or starting a new request drops the continuation.
- **Pinned answer cards survive gateway restarts** (and snooze). They still close when the toolbar or the companion is turned off, or when a screenshot starts. Every first sign-in restarts the gateway, which used to close the card and abort its answer.
- **Analytics**: `login_shown`, `login_click` and `login_success` on `lobsterai_desktop_companion_action`, for `selection` and `language_tools`, joined by `journeyId`. A success carries `durationMs` and is credited to the newest click within 30 minutes. Documented in the usage-analytics design.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
  - `companionLogin.test.ts`: request normalization and click-to-success attribution.
  - `desktopCompanionManager.test.ts`: hold → login reset → resume; drop on close, new request or stale sign-in; sender checks.
  - `companionSelection.test.ts`: answer cards held for sign-in; pinned cards kept through a restart; closed when the toolbar or companion is off or a screenshot starts.
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed: end to end in the real Electron app (isolated profile, production services, a real account). Analytics were checked against the rlog requests the app actually sent.
  - Translation card: a blocked follow-up → sign in → the card reopens pinned, re-translates, and the follow-up gets answered. Reloading its renderer afterwards does not resend the follow-up.
  - Selection card: a blocked summarize → sign in → the summary appears and survives the two gateway restarts that followed the login.
  - Funnel: `login_shown → login_click → login_success` share one `journeyId` and have no duplicate impressions.
- Desktop companion suites: 33 files and 494 tests pass. `tsc` for Electron and renderer is clean, and ESLint is clean on all changed files.
- The full `npm test` on Windows has 22 failing files, all outside the desktop companion (POSIX file-mode and `/tmp` assertions, a Vite prebundle check).

## Screenshots (if applicable)
| Follow-up blocked | Signing in | Dark, English |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Follow-up blocked](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/raw/6bc2b7a2248061105e04fcae12c2bdc95aa4a267/specs/features/desktop-companion/assets/selection-login-conversion/prompt-follow-up.png) | ![Signing in](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/raw/6bc2b7a2248061105e04fcae12c2bdc95aa4a267/specs/features/desktop-companion/assets/selection-login-conversion/prompt-waiting.png) | ![Dark, English](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/raw/6bc2b7a2248061105e04fcae12c2bdc95aa4a267/specs/features/desktop-companion/assets/selection-login-conversion/prompt-dark-en.png) |

After signing in (real app):

| Translation card: re-translated, follow-up answered | Selection card: summary appears |
| --- | --- |
| ![Translation card after sign-in](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/raw/6bc2b7a2248061105e04fcae12c2bdc95aa4a267/specs/features/desktop-companion/assets/selection-login-conversion/after-login-follow-up.png) | ![Selection card after sign-in](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/raw/6bc2b7a2248061105e04fcae12c2bdc95aa4a267/specs/features/desktop-companion/assets/selection-login-conversion/after-login-summary.png) |

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (desktop companion suites pass; see Testing for the Windows-only failures elsewhere)

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication: new `desktop-companion:login-start`; `login_shown` is now accepted from the selection and language tools windows through the existing analytics IPC.
- [x] Changes to window management: cards are pinned while the sign-in runs; the language tools window reopens with `showInactive` after login; pinned selection answers are no longer hidden while the gateway restarts.
- [ ] None

## Additional Notes
- Translation stays free without signing in. The sign-in requirements and quotas of the other tools are unchanged.
- `handleLoginSucceeded()` runs inside the auth exchange handler and catches its own errors, so a companion failure can't turn a successful login into an error.
- The base is `release/2026.11.2`, where recent PRs land; `main` is 77 commits behind it.

prs.title: docs(openclaw): record stacked post-ready measurement for registry/code page patch
prs.body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #3002, documentation only. This commit was pushed to the #3002 branch after that PR had already merged, so it never reached `release/2026.11.2`.

It adds the measurement on the merged runtime to the patch README section "Native Windows registry reads and console code page". The merged runtime has both `openclaw-windows-registry-codepage-native.patch` and `zz-openclaw-dreaming-cleanup-only-when-enabled.patch` (#3001).
- "Before" was produced from the same runtime by making only the `RegGetValueW`/`GetConsoleOutputCP` koffi bindings fail, so the unchanged `reg.exe`/`chcp` fallback runs. It reproduces a separately built runtime without the patch: the same 8 child processes and 435–485 ms of synchronous time after `ready`.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): read Windows registry roots and code page natively
prs.body:
## Summary
- Right after `[gateway] ready` on Windows, OpenClaw resolved its trusted install roots by running `reg.exe query` four times (`SystemRoot`, `ProgramFilesDir`, `ProgramFilesDir (x86)`, `ProgramW6432Dir`), then ran `cmd.exe /d /s /c chcp` for the console code page. All five calls were synchronous on the event loop (~470 ms), and non-Microsoft processes starting `reg.exe`/`cmd.exe` are a common EDR heuristic.
- New patch `openclaw-windows-registry-codepage-native.patch` (`src/infra/windows-install-roots.ts`, `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts`):
  - **Registry values** are read through koffi (already shipped on Windows) and `advapi32!RegGetValueW`, still from HKLM. Environment variables stay untrusted for these roots, as upstream intends. The read keeps reg.exe's view order (64-bit, then default) and its output form: unexpanded strings, `REG_DWORD` as `0x` hex, `null` when missing in both views.
  - **Console code page**: `chcp` printed the code page of the console it ran in. That is `GetConsoleOutputCP` when the gateway has a console. Otherwise it is the new console Windows creates, which starts on a valid `HKCU\Console` `CodePage` override, else `GetOEMCP`. The gateway runs under Electron, a GUI-subsystem binary with no console, so the second case is the normal one.
  - **Fallback**: `reg.exe` and `chcp` still run whenever koffi can't load or the native read is inconclusive (unsupported root or type, access denied).
- Upstream `main` still uses `reg.exe` and `chcp` (checked 2026-11). This is a LobsterAI patch, documented in the patch README with its removal condition.
- `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs` adds a strong validator (presence and order sentinels in both files). `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts` registers the patch and checks its content.

## Test plan
- [x] OpenClaw touched tests (infra project): 74/74 pass. New cases cover native reads without spawning, missing values, fallback when the reader is undecided or throws, reg.exe text form, and the native code page plus chcp fallback. Windows-only cases compare against real `reg.exe` output (four roots, `OEMCP`, a `REG_DWORD`) and the real `chcp` probe, with no child process started. `detect-binary.test.ts` now disables the native reader explicitly, because hiding `reg.exe` no longer turns off registry lookups.
- [x] OpenClaw process project: 65 passed. The 1 failure (`child.test.ts` service relay) also fails on the baseline.
- [x] Wider OpenClaw sweep: 167 test files touching install roots, encodings, exec or `SystemRoot`. Failure sets match the baseline. The only differences were git-timeout tests under CPU load, and they flip in both directions. Rerun on an idle machine, `update-runner.test.ts` fails the same 22 tests with and without the patch.
- [x] Native vs real tools on this Windows 11 machine, from both a console-attached Node and a console-less Electron process: 12 registry queries identical to `reg.exe`, including REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_DWORD and missing key/value. Code page identical to `chcp` (936/gbk; 0 from `GetConsoleOutputCP` under Electron).
- [x] All 87 v2026.8.1 patches apply from a clean reset with the new validator. LobsterAI `src/main/libs/openclawPatches/`: 29 files pass. ESLint is clean on the touched TS file.
- [x] Runtime rebuilt with `npm run openclaw:runtime:host`. The built `dist` and `gateway-bundle.mjs` contain the native readers, and koffi ships.
- [x] Warm gateway starts on the same machine and state, comparing release runtimes with and without the patch (4 interleaved runs each after a warm-up; harness spawns the gateway like LobsterAI with CPU profile and child-process tracing):
  - child processes per start: 8 → 3. Only the two SQLite read-only workers and an async `git rev-parse` remain.
  - `reg.exe`/`cmd.exe` spawns: 5 → **0**
  - synchronous child-process time after `ready`: median 466 ms → **0**
  - shipped dist chunks timed in a console-less Electron process: first `getWindowsInstallRoots()` 197–291 ms → 1.2–2.3 ms (9–17 ms when koffi is not loaded yet); first `resolveWindowsConsoleEncoding()` 69–129 ms → <1 ms; identical results
  - Without the dreaming-scrub patch, the main thread stays saturated for the first 3 s after `ready` in both variants, so the freed ~0.47 s only lets the remaining startup work run sooner.
- [x] Merged with `release/2026.11.2` (#3000, #3001). The runtime was rebuilt from the branch with all 88 patches, and its recorded patch hash equals the branch's. Stacked check: the same runtime with only the `RegGetValueW`/`GetConsoleOutputCP` koffi bindings forced to fail reproduces the old behavior: the same 8 children, 5 `reg.exe`/`cmd.exe`, and 435–485 ms sync, matching the separately built runtime without the patch. 10 interleaved rounds:
  - `reg.exe`/`cmd.exe` 5 → 0 and children 8 → 3 in every run; median sync child-process time after `ready` 448 ms → 0
  - idle in the first 1.8 s after `ready`: median 277 ms → 490 ms, over runs whose startup was not swamped by outside load (n=6/4). Another session's dev app was running on the machine, so the spread is large: 33–532 vs 29–961 ms. All 10 runs: 114 → 186 ms.

## Summary

prs.title: fix: credential log redaction, preview-server symlink containment, and OpenClaw proxy auth
prs.body:
Fixes #2795, Fixes #2796, Fixes #2797.

Three independent findings reviewed together, one commit per finding:

## #2795: OAuth tokens logged to diagnostic files

`api:fetch` logged raw request/response bodies verbatim. Added `redactBodyForLog` (parses JSON/form-encoded bodies and applies the existing key-based redaction) and wired it into both logging call sites. Also added `verifier` to `SENSITIVE_LOG_KEY_PATTERN`, which didn't cover PKCE `code_verifier` fields.

## #2796: HTML preview server follows symlinks

The preview server's containment check was lexical only (`resolvedPath.startsWith(rootDir)`), and `fs.stat`/`fs.createReadStream` follow symlinks. Added `streamFileWithinRoot`, which resolves both the requested path and the root via `fs.realpath` and rejects if the canonical target escapes the canonical root.

## #2797: OpenClaw token proxy missing authentication

The proxy forwarded every request upstream with the signed-in user's bearer token, without checking any credential on the incoming request. It now generates its own token on start and requires it (via `timingSafeEqual`) on every request, mirroring the pattern the neighboring Cowork compat proxy already uses. Also fixed `${LOBSTER_PROXY_TOKEN}`'s resolution, which previously always pointed at the Cowork proxy's token (meaningless to this proxy) regardless of which proxy was actually the active target.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --project electron-tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- New test files: `openclawTokenProxyAuth.test.ts` (real server, real HTTP requests), `htmlPreviewServerSymlink.test.ts` (real server, real HTTP requests, real symlink), plus new cases in `sanitizeForLog.test.ts`.
- `npx vitest run` (full suite): all passing, no regressions, including `openclawConfigSync.test.ts`/`openclawSecretEnv.test.ts` which specifically cover the shared `LOBSTER_PROXY_TOKEN` resolution.
