prs.title: feat(chats): add keyword and agentic conversation search
prs.body:
## Description

Automatically generated titles do not reliably contain the words users remember from a conversation. With a large history, a title-only filter can miss the exact discussion even when its messages contain the requested information.

This PR adds content search and agentic search to the existing conversation-history sidebar. For example, searching `PostgreSQL` now finds a conversation titled “A technical discussion” when its messages describe a PostgreSQL migration. Users who remember the intent instead of the wording can select **AI search** and describe the conversation in natural language.

Related: #1578.

### User experience

| Mode | Interaction | Retrieval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keyword | Type in the existing sidebar field; results update after a 275 ms debounce | Case-insensitive literal matching across titles and saved user/assistant messages, with pagination |
| AI search | Enter a description and explicitly submit with Enter or the search button | The current agent's configured model refines queries, pages through candidates, reads matching conversations, and selects relevant results |

Results show the conversation title and a highlighted excerpt. Clicking opens the existing conversation; clearing the field restores the normal grouped history. The compact mode switch and results use the existing sidebar styling and theme variables. Loading, empty results, retry, and partial results have dedicated states. Switching agents or editing the query cancels the client request and prevents stale results from entering the current view.

### Screenshots

Captured from commit `aa9b3f2f` in a local Console connected to the real backend, using three synthetic conversations.

**Search message contents, even when the title does not contain the keyword.** Searching `PostgreSQL` returns two conversations with highlighted matching excerpts; the unrelated reading conversation is excluded.

![Keyword search finds body-only matches and highlights the matching text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hehuang139/QwenPaw/f2787b8022e2d2ff6ba021b24c3a93d77b333e0c/docs/pr-evidence/8367/keyword-search.jpg)

**Open the original conversation from a search result.** Selecting “A technical discussion” opens its saved transcript while keeping the search results available in the sidebar.

![Opening a search result displays the original conversation transcript](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hehuang139/QwenPaw/f2787b8022e2d2ff6ba021b24c3a93d77b333e0c/docs/pr-evidence/8367/open-conversation.jpg)

### Design and implementation

- Add agent-scoped `POST /chats/search` with `query`, `mode`, `limit`, and `offset`. Both modes search the selected agent's unarchived conversations and exclude app-owned dialogues.
- Read current and legacy session snapshots plus the configured Scroll history database, including imported history and older messages removed from live context by compaction. Extract user/assistant text while filtering reasoning, tool results, and tagged runtime messages. Restore original attachment input when snapshot metadata is available, and prefer snapshot message IDs over duplicate durable representations. Older durable attachment turns without original-content metadata can retain generated file-upload descriptions in search results.
- Keep keyword search independent of model configuration. Use existing persistence and SQLite support, with no new dependency, embedding service, index migration, or vector database.
- Implement an ephemeral model-driven search loop with only `search`, `read`, and `finish` actions. It can reformulate terms and inspect older pages. Final results are resolved from retrieved server-side candidates, so invented IDs cannot become links. The search does not instantiate the general-purpose agent or write conversation history.
- Bound each corpus scan to 64 MiB and five seconds; cap individual snapshots/history rows at 16 MiB. AI search allows six model responses in 45 seconds, 60 candidates, and bounded transcript/output sizes. Preserve retrieved results and mark them partial when a budget is exhausted. Missing models, invalid responses, and provider failures return explicit errors.
- Preserve canonical result IDs through sidebar navigation, including results discovered before the next session-list refresh. Add English/Chinese UI strings and Console documentation.

**Security considerations:** reuse the existing agent-scoped request dependencies; constrain transcript files to the session directory; open history SQLite connections read-only and filter by exact agent/session identity. Historical text is treated as data and the model has no filesystem, command, or network tools.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console
- [x] Documentation

prs.title: fix(channels): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in rendered Markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model bolds CJK text it often leaves a sentence-ending punctuation mark inside the closing emphasis delimiter, e.g.:

```
**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。
```

CommonMark's "flanking" rules classify CJK sentence punctuation as Unicode punctuation, and CJK text has no inter-word spaces. The closing `**` therefore sits between punctuation and CJK text, is judged "not a valid closer", and the raw markers leak into the rendered output: the reader literally sees `**没有改动任何设置。**`.

This affects QwenPaw's own surfaces (TUI, web console) and every Markdown-rendering channel (QQ, Telegram, Slack, ...). Example (real QQ output):

```
主人，**重点**。后面的**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。
```

## Fix

Add `normalize_cjk_emphasis` in `qwenpaw.utils.markdown_cjk`, which moves the trailing CJK punctuation run outside the delimiter (`**中文。**后` becomes `**中文**。后`), and apply it where QwenPaw renders Markdown itself:

- `MessageRenderer.message_to_parts` — when the channel's `RenderStyle.supports_markdown` is set, repair the assistant text before the part is created. Covers QQ / Telegram / Slack / ...
- TUI `AssistantMessage` — repair once the answer is finalized (`finalize()`), so streaming deltas stay untouched and the live view does not flicker.

The repair is deliberately conservative and display-oriented:

- only `*`, `_`, `**`, `__`, `***`, `___` are considered;
- only `。！？；：，、…` plus full-width trailing closers (`”’」』】》〉）〕］`) are moved;
- only when the delimiter is immediately followed by Han / Hiragana / Katakana / Hangul;
- fenced, indented and inline code, escaped delimiters, CRLF endings and unrelated unfinished Markdown are preserved verbatim.

## Evidence

- `pytest tests/unit/utils/test_markdown_cjk.py tests/unit/app/channels/test_renderer.py -q` -> **60 passed**
- `pytest tests/unit/utils tests/unit/app/channels -q` -> **930 passed, 7 skipped**
- Direct behaviour checks:
  - `normalize_cjk_emphasis("**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。")` -> `"**没有改动任何设置**。所有内容保持不变。"`
  - `normalize_cjk_emphasis("**重点**后接中文")` -> unchanged
  - `MessageRenderer().message_to_parts(<TextContent "**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容">)[0].text` -> repaired
  - `RenderStyle(supports_markdown=False)` -> text left untouched
  - fenced code block containing `**代码。**后` -> left untouched
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` -> all 17 hooks pass.

## Notes

- This is a targeted, display-oriented repair, not a general Markdown parser: ASCII punctuation and non-CJK followers are out of scope by design.
- Related: CommonMark discussion `commonmark/commonmark-spec#650` on CJK-friendly emphasis.

prs.title: fix(providers): reject out-of-range model config values on the write path
prs.body:
Fixes #8549

## What Problem This Solves

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the write path never enforced those bounds: `Provider.update_model_config` assigned `int(...)` results directly (Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment), and `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` was the only numeric field in its model without a bound. An invalid value was accepted and persisted, then failed re-validation on every read — after a restart `load_provider` returned `None` and the provider silently disappeared.

## What changed

- `app/routers/providers.py`: add `ge=1` to `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget`, matching the existing `ge=1000` on `max_input_length`.
- `providers/provider.py`: `update_model_config` now raises `ValueError` for `thinking_budget < 1` and `max_input_length < 1000` before assigning, consistent with the existing `model_type` / `supports_*` validation in the same method.
- `providers/model_info.py`: `thinking_budget_range` gains a model validator requiring a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair (mirroring `ThinkingControl` in `providers/thinking.py`); previously `[8000]` constructed fine and `thinking_control()` crashed unpacking it.

## Evidence

New regression tests (10):

- `tests/unit/providers/test_provider_config_validation.py` — `thinking_budget` of -5 / 0 and `max_input_length` of 500 are rejected and not stored; valid values round-trip and clearing with `None` still works; `thinking_budget_range` of length 1 / 3 or `low > high` is rejected, an ordered pair still drives `thinking_control`.
- `tests/unit/app/routers/test_provider_config_request_validation.py` — `ModelConfigRequest(thinking_budget=-5 / 0)` fails request validation, `1` is accepted.

Red/green: with the fix reverted, the 8 rejection tests fail (the 2 valid-value guards pass both ways); with the fix, all 10 pass. The reproduction script that previously showed `update_model_config(..., -5)` returning `True` and poisoning reads now raises `ValueError: thinking_budget must be at least 1` at write time.

Broader subset `tests/unit/providers/` + the provider router tests: 1008 passed; the single failure (`test_typesafe_evaluation.py::test_as_model_injects_same_instance_and_preserves_host_headers`) fails identically on the unmodified baseline in this environment because the optional `reme` package is not installed.

prs.title: fix(skills): stage skill copies inside the target workspace
prs.body:
## Description

Windows Hub Local runtimes could not install their default skills. `staged_skill_dir()` used `tempfile.mkdtemp()` under the runtime process temp directory (`working/tmp`). Inside an AppContainer, directories created there receive a protected DACL that only grants `OWNER RIGHTS`, `SYSTEM`, and `Administrators`; the AppContainer SID is absent, so creating the nested skill directory (`QA_source_index`) fails with `WinError 5`. On Python builds where `TMP_MAX` is `2147483647`, `tempfile.mkdtemp()` also spins in its `PermissionError` retry loop instead of raising, which makes the runtime look hung.

This change lets `staged_skill_dir()` accept an explicit `root_dir` and makes `SkillPoolService.download_to_workspace()` stage inside the destination workspace's `skills/` directory. That directory is part of the existing writable AppContainer mount and its children remain writable. Callers that do not pass `root_dir` keep the previous temp-directory behaviour.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8565

**Security Considerations:** No trust-boundary change. The staging directory still uses the fixed `qwenpaw_skill_stage_` prefix and `safe_skill_dir()` for path-injection hardening, and staging stays inside the per-runtime workspace mount instead of the shared system temp directory.

prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8516

The `/api/console/chat` SSE responses (the stream itself and the empty reconnect response) did not send `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, unlike every other SSE endpoint (`backup.py`, `portability_imports.py`, `project_directory.py`, `skills_stream.py`, `workspace.py`). ## Description

After `/clear`, reopening a chat or refreshing the Console restored the cached command as a user bubble even though the backend history was empty. That synthetic bubble hid the empty-state greeting. A successful `/new` could leave the same stale cache.

When an idle chat has empty history and its pending input is `/clear` or `/new`, discard the pending entry instead of synthesizing a user card. This uses the existing history reconciliation shared by direct submissions and background queues, and cleans up both canonical Chat IDs and local draft aliases, including legacy sessionStorage entries. Running commands, nonempty histories, ordinary pending messages, and other chats keep their existing behavior.

prs.title: fix(tools): decode GBK/CP936 in read/edit/grep instead of dropping bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read_file_safe` (used by `read_file` / `edit_file`) and `grep_search` decoded files as UTF-8 with `errors="ignore"`. On Chinese Windows, Notepad/legacy `.txt` / `.csv` / `.md` notes are often GBK/CP936. Every non-UTF-8 byte was deleted with no log line, so:

- `read_file` returned ASCII leftovers (e.g. `姓名: 张三` → `: `)
- `grep_search` for Chinese terms missed the file
- `edit_file` could still report success and persist the damaged snapshot as UTF-8

Markdown/skill loaders already use `decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback` (utf-8 → gbk/cp936 → …). This PR routes the tool read path through the same helper.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/utils.py`: `_read_file_safe_sync` uses the shared encoding fallback
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/file_search.py`: `_walk_and_grep` reads bytes and decodes with the same fallback (files already capped at 2MB)
- Regression tests for GBK read, GBK `edit_file`, and GBK grep

## How to reproduce (before)

```python
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("note.txt")
path.write_bytes("姓名: 张三\n".encode("gbk"))
# read_file_safe previously returned ": \n"
```

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_search.py::test_walk_and_grep_matches_gbk_file -q
# 43 passed
```

Also re-ran the new GBK cases alone after rebase: 4 passed.

## Notes

- After a successful GBK decode, `edit_file` still writes with the existing suffix-based encoding (`.txt` → `utf-8-sig`). Chinese text is preserved; only the on-disk encoding may change to UTF-8, which matches the project’s Windows Excel/Notepad write path.
- CRLF whole-file rewrite and Ollama `num_ctx` sizing are separate follow-ups and are not in this PR.

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer preserving the original GBK bytes on write as well.

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show` or `/api/ps`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

`OllamaProvider.fetch_models` lists models with `/v1/models`, then sets `max_input_length_auto_detected` from native Ollama signals. Precedence:

1. `GET /api/ps` served `context_length` when the model is loaded (reflects `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` and the load-time window). A hit skips `/api/show`.
2. Modelfile `num_ctx` from a successful `POST /api/show`.
3. A conservative **4096** estimate only after a **successful** `/api/show` that has no `num_ctx`. **4096 is a conservative estimate, not a value Ollama reports.** It matches Ollama's smallest documented default so first-session compaction does not assume 128k.

GGUF `*.context_length` is **not** used. That field is the model's maximum supported context, not the window Ollama is serving.

Failed native probes (`None`, 401, 403, timeout, or an invalid payload) leave the model **unchanged**. The 128k default remains until a later successful probe. A failed `/api/show` does not apply 4096.

`check_model_connection` uses the lightweight `/v1/models` list (`super().fetch_models`). It only checks that the model id exists and does not call `/api/show` per model.

Native `/api/ps` and `/api/show` probes reuse `_build_default_headers()` and add `Authorization: Bearer` when an API key is set and Authorization is not already configured. Explicit user `max_input_length` still wins over auto-detection, and the cloud catalog stays disabled for Ollama. `ModelInfo.max_input_length_auto_detected` allows `ge=1` so a small explicit `num_ctx` (for example 512) is kept.

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py -q
# 87 passed
```

`black --line-length=79` is clean on the touched files.

Coverage includes precedence (served `/api/ps` → Modelfile `num_ctx` → conservative 4096 only after a successful show with no `num_ctx`), GGUF `*.context_length` ignored, 401/403 and timeout on `/api/show` leaving `max_input_length_auto_detected` unset, `check_model_connection` not calling `/api/show`, authenticated native probes, the catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

prs.title: fix(plugins): isolate synchronous hooks and add event loop lag watchdog (#7840)
prs.body:
## Description

When an installed backend plugin performs synchronous blocking operations inside an `async def` route handler or lifecycle hook (e.g. `time.sleep`, `select.select`, `os.read`, `subprocess.run`, or synchronous HTTP/socket calls), it freezes the host's single-threaded `asyncio` event loop. Consequently, all agent turns, messaging channels, and HTTP/SSE requests stall silently with zero logs or traceback until clients hit timeouts (typically 30s).

This PR addresses this structural gap from three complementary angles:

1. **Live Lag Watchdog & Real-Time Stack Capture (`EventLoopWatchdog`)**:
   - Introduces an independent background daemon thread that monitors event loop responsiveness via a `call_soon_threadsafe` heartbeat.
   - When loop lag exceeds the threshold (default 2.0s, configurable via `QWENPAW_EVENT_LOOP_LAG_WARN_SECONDS`), it instantly captures the live stack frames of the loop thread using `sys._current_frames()`.
   - Analyzes frames to identify culprit plugins (via regex matching against plugin directory and module naming conventions), immediately logging the culprit plugin ID, offending file, line number, and full stack trace at WARNING level.
   - Logs recovery duration once the stall resolves and exposes loop lag stats for health checks.
   - Safely releases locks before capturing frames and stack formatting to avoid blocking loop heartbeats.

2. **Safe Lifecycle Hook Execution & Timeout Isolation (`_app.py`)**:
   - Offloads synchronous startup and shutdown hook callbacks to background threads via `asyncio.to_thread` instead of executing them synchronously on the main thread.
   - Wraps hook execution in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=10.0)` to ensure a slow or hanging hook cannot block application startup or graceful shutdown.

3. **API Non-Blocking Contract & Helper (`PluginApi`)**:
   - Updates `PluginApi.register_http_router` docstring to document the non-blocking contract for `async def` vs `def` routes.
   - Adds `api.run_sync(func, *args, **kwargs)` helper method so plugin authors can safely offload synchronous blocking tasks to thread pools without ad-hoc workarounds.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7840

**Security Considerations:** None. Watchdog runs read-only thread-frame inspection on an internal daemon thread; no external network exposure or elevated permissions.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

1. Run unit tests covering watchdog lifecycle, stall detection, live stack capture, culprit plugin attribution, and hook safety timeouts:
   ```bash
   pytest tests/unit/utils/test_event_loop_watchdog.py tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_hook_safety.py tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_api_extensions.py -v
   ```
2. Run end-to-end verification against a plugin triggering synchronous blocking I/O:
   - Verify that the watchdog detects the stall at the configured threshold and logs the culprit plugin ID with the exact blocking line number (`plugin.py:11 in block: time.sleep(duration)`).
   - Verify that when the plugin uses `await api.run_sync(...)`, the event loop remains responsive (sub-2ms response for concurrent `/api/version` requests).

## Evidence

Here is the local validation evidence and live behavior transcripts demonstrating the fix:

**1. Test Suite Verification (28 tests passed)**
```text

platform darwin -- Python 3.11.13, pytest-9.1.0, pluggy-1.6.0
rootdir: /Users/nowcoder/Desktop/auto-code-work/agent-frameworks/QwenPaw
configfile: pyproject.toml
collected 28 items

tests/unit/utils/test_event_loop_watchdog.py ...                         [ 10%]
tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_hook_safety.py ..                         [ 17%]
tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_api_extensions.py ....................... [100%]

======================== 28 passed, 1 warning in 3.32s =========================
```

**2. Live Runtime Stall Detection & Attribution (After Evidence)**
When a synchronous blocking call is executed inside a plugin endpoint, the watchdog captures the live stack on the loop thread and identifies the culprit:
```text
WARNING src/qwenpaw/utils/event_loop_watchdog.py:218 | ⚠ [EventLoopWatchdog] Event loop stalled (current lag: 1.54s)!
Culprit identified inside plugin: 'repro-blocking-plugin'
Live stack trace on loop thread 8389959040:
  File ".../fastapi/routing.py", line 337, in run_endpoint_function
    return await dependant.call(**values)
  File ".../plugins/repro-blocking-plugin/plugin.py", line 11, in block

INFO src/qwenpaw/utils/event_loop_watchdog.py:188 | ✓ [EventLoopWatchdog] Event loop recovered after 4.07s stall.
```

**3. Concurrent Request Isolation with api.run_sync**
When offloading via `await api.run_sync(time.sleep, 3.5)`, concurrent normal endpoints respond in milliseconds without being starved:

- Thread frames are inspected outside the watchdog lock to avoid blocking the event loop's heartbeat callbacks.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

Long conversations previously depended on mutable session snapshots and loading large history windows. That made historical Turn forks, runtime recovery, and reconnect behavior difficult to keep consistent. This branch introduces durable per-session SQLite history with append-only facts and rebuildable projections, and bounds the Console's history and replay work.

This draft covers the complete branch, including:

- Store message/content facts and immutable context revisions separately from current message/runtime projections. Rebuild projections without rewriting historical facts; reuse state component references for usage-only revisions and avoid redundant block events.
- Migrate legacy JSON sessions and history databases, preserve available historical messages, reconstruct legacy runtime where possible, and retain provider session/Turn mappings.
- Fork completed Turns with their historical runtime boundary. Codex/Qoder branches use native provider interfaces and stored Turn mappings rather than rebuilding third-party context. Failed native restoration/reset must not silently create a fresh context.
- Add stable history pagination, bounded rendering, message-directory navigation, streaming/reconnect replay, and safe session switching/deletion.
- Integrate storage with clear/new, compact, dump/load, Scroll/Recall, cloning, backup, checkpoints, statistics, and PawApp/SDK session access. Preserve reset and checkpoint restoration semantics; roll back failed/cancelled compaction.

## Issues addressed

- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3915 — measured virtual rendering, incremental history loading, scroll anchoring, and bottom-follow behavior.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3923 — bounded Console history reads and windowed rendering address the full-history/full-DOM paths. This does not claim a measured memory result for the reporter's exact dataset or include all optional bundle-size suggestions.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8134 — durable display history is independent of the model's compacted context.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/6542 — completed turns persist their final messages and session state. This covers the real-time archival proposal, not zero loss of uncommitted output after a forced process termination or external notebook synchronization.

## PRs superseded after merge

prs.title: fix(matrix): recover cached sessions and missing device keys
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8365. Password-authenticated Matrix channels log in again on restart. If a homeserver loses a device's encryption keys while the local crypto store marks them as shared, startup does not restore the keys and the channel can appear healthy while decryption fails.

Adapt session recovery to main's native Matrix plugin and per-instance `channel_state/matrix` ownership. Reuse a session only for the same homeserver, login identity, device and password, then verify its canonical user/device pair with `whoami`. Fall back to password login only for `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`; preserve explicit tokens and main's atomic state writes and ownership checks.

Reconcile E2EE device keys at startup and re-upload a missing identity from the existing SQLite crypto store, preserving sessions. Refuse conflicting remote keys and distinguish query failure from deletion. Retry transient startup key-query failures up to three times, with a ten-second limit per query and a one-second interruptible delay. Permanent authorization failures and conflicting remote keys fail without retry. Run ongoing health probes in a separate background task once per minute, report failed key health to the plugin host, and keep routine sync/send maintenance independent of that result. Log the first undecryptable event at error level.

## Security considerations

Use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and the session token as salt for the password fingerprint, with an explicit format version. Legacy fast-hash fingerprints cannot authorize cache reuse and require a fresh password login. Passwords are not persisted. Conflicting remote identities are never overwritten.

## Evidence

Validated on Linux/Python 3.11 against main `c26d31c0`, using real matrix-nio HTTP calls, local aiohttp homeserver fixtures, python-olm and persisted SQLite crypto stores:

```text
pytest tests/unit/channels/test_matrix_recovery.py tests/unit/channels/test_matrix.py -q
With matrix-e2ee:    41 passed
Without matrix-e2ee: 27 passed, 14 skipped
```

The two runs explicitly checked `nio.crypto.ENCRYPTION_ENABLED=True` and `False`. E2EE-only tests skip when the optional backend is absent.

Cases cover transient HTTP errors, partial key-query failures, query timeouts, retry exhaustion without account mutation, permanent authorization rejection, cancellation during retry, background health failure/recovery, continued delivery of pending device messages after a failed health query, and repeated routine maintenance without extra health queries. Existing cases cover restart reuse, expired-token fallback, temporary authentication failure, changed credentials/server/device, localpart names, old unversioned fingerprints, explicit tokens, key loss, upload retry, conflicting identities, bounded health checks and the host's failed-state notification. Missing keys are restored using the original identity.

All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: fix: use shared root profile workspace for ACL store, not per-task workspace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multica starts a new task via ACP protocol, the channel's current workspace points to a fresh **per-task** directory whose `access_control.json` is empty. This causes the Telegram channel to reject all previously approved users, breaking access control for every new task.

## Evidence

**Root Cause:** `_get_acl_store()` in `BaseChannel` used the (possibly per-task) `workspace_dir` to resolve the ACL store path:

```
def _get_acl_store(self):
    workspace_dir = None
    if self._workspace is not None:
        workspace_dir = Path(self._workspace.workspace_dir)
    return get_access_control_store(workspace_dir)
```

But the channel config (`access_control_dm`) is read from the **shared root profile** `agent.json`. So config says access control is on, but the ACL data lives in a fresh per-task workspace with an empty whitelist.

**Fix:** `_get_acl_store()` now resolves the ACL store path from the agent's **root profile** `workspace_dir` (via `load_agent_config`), which is shared across all task instances. Falls back to the current workspace dir if config lookup fails.

**Tests:** Added `tests/unit/app/channels/test_channel_acl_workspace.py`:
- ACL store resolves to root profile workspace, not per-task
- Falls back to current workspace when config lookup fails
- Multiple task workspaces share the same ACL store (approval visible across tasks)

Fixes #6786

prs.title: fix(providers): filter unrecognized kwargs before OpenAI completions.create()
prs.body:
## Description

Middleware or proxy layers may inject custom kwargs (e.g. `streamIdleTimeoutMs`) that the upstream OpenAI SDK rejects with:

```
TypeError: AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'streamIdleTimeoutMs'
```

### Root cause

`OpenAIChatModelCompat._call_api()` forwards **all** kwargs (merged from `extra_generate_kwargs` + caller-provided `generate_kwargs`) directly into the agentscope base class, which in turn passes them to `openai.AsyncClient.chat.completions.create()`. The OpenAI SDK does not tolerate unknown kwargs and raises `TypeError`.

### Fix

Whitelist all known parameters for `openai.AsyncOpenAI().chat.completions.create()` (verified against OpenAI SDK v2.33) and drop unrecognized keys with a warning log before forwarding to the base class. This is analogous to the approach in unmerged PR #5607 but simpler and non-destructive (keeps `extra_body` passthrough intact).

### Related

- Related open issue: #7026 (auto-injected `chat_template_kwargs` not wrapped in `extra_body`)
- Related unmerged PR: #5607 (restore non-standard kwargs routing into `extra_body`)

## Test plan

1. Unit test: call `_sanitize_openai_kwargs()` with `streamIdleTimeoutMs` and other unknown keys; verify they are dropped.
2. Integration: run a model call through an agent whose provider config includes `streamIdleTimeoutMs` in `extra_generate_kwargs`; verify the call succeeds and a warning is logged.
3. Existing tests: run `pytest tests/unit/providers/test_openai_provider.py tests/unit/providers/test_openai_stream_toolcall_compat.py`

Fixes #7026 (related)

prs.title: refactor(runtime): unify session configuration for ACP and native execution
prs.body:
ACP and native execution now use the same session configuration snapshot. Two sessions of one agent can select different settings without changing saved defaults or other processes.

- Define session settings once in `SessionConfig`, inherited by `AgentProfileConfig`. Core `RuntimeParameters` merges global defaults, agent settings, startup defaults, and session overrides, preserving omitted fields and explicit `false`, `null`, and empty lists. ACP inherits the constructor and translates protocol inputs; new session fields require no ACP mapping.
- Support workspace/project directories, models, permissions, coding mode, goal, mission, and loop gates. Keep existing ACP flags, metadata, model/permission setters, and load/resume behavior. Resetting `qwenpaw.config` clears that layer without confusing it with retained legacy metadata.
- Let registered modes declare configuration or entry commands. Resolve saved mode state and Mission's pinned directories before constructing the execution snapshot. Remove duplicated Builder precedence, ACP-specific runtime hooks, the global stop-handler bridge, and obsolete state-loading entry points.
- Keep gate state and resource ownership session-local. Workspace replacements are prepared before publication; failed service or MCP preparation preserves the previous owner. Switching modes replaces derived defaults rather than accumulating them.
- Use one effective iteration limit throughout QwenPaw. Positive limits may exceed 500; disabling the iteration gate removes the fallback limit while cancellation and other enabled stopping conditions remain effective.

Validation: concurrent session and separate-process isolation, legacy restore semantics, no override persistence, failed resource replacement, restored mode switching, Mission directory consistency, ACP stdio lifecycle, and real execution beyond 100 iterations with cancellation. Existing regressions were extended and obsolete helper/forwarding tests removed. English and Chinese documentation matches the final behavior.

Results: 4,031 regression tests passed and 14 were skipped. The three frozen-worker tests needed the ignored official-channel bundle generated by the existing build hook, then passed on rerun. After the final parameter API cleanup, all 32 affected configuration/ACP tests passed again. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix(matrix): simplify legacy state migration and device locking
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #8187.

The previous legacy-state checks could prevent a valid Matrix account from starting when unrelated legacy files were present. Persistent device ownership could also block another workspace after the original workspace had stopped, while the host only reported `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`.

This PR simplifies the migration flow:

- Matching identities are migrated automatically by copying state into the current workspace.
- Mismatched identities start with independent workspace state instead of failing.
- Device exclusion is based on runtime locks rather than permanent workspace ownership.

## Changes

- Prefer existing state in the current workspace, including A → B → A account switches.
- Copy legacy sync tokens and crypto stores only when `user_id` and `device_id` match the authenticated identity.
- Preserve all legacy files during migration; fresh credentials are not overwritten by legacy auth data.
- Skip unrelated legacy state without blocking a valid account.
- Replace persistent device-owner enforcement with runtime device locks released when the Channel stops.
- Ignore stale owner/capture records without deleting user files.
- Preserve concurrent-use protection for the same Matrix device while allowing different device IDs.
- Fall back to initial catch-up when a non-E2EE sync-token copy fails.
- Fail explicitly on E2EE copy failures instead of creating a new identity for the same device.
- Propagate Matrix reason codes through the plugin host instead of returning only `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`.
- Remove the obsolete Matrix legacy-capture authorization module.
- Add migration, locking, failure-path, and host-error propagation tests.
- Update Matrix documentation in English and Chinese.

## Security and compatibility

- Legacy files remain read-only.
- Crypto state is never adopted across different user/device identities.
- Corrupt current workspace state still fails explicitly rather than being silently replaced.
- Concurrent use of the same account/device remains blocked.
- No access tokens, passwords, or key material are added to diagnostics.
- Other Channel implementations are unchanged.

## Tests

- Matrix migration and Channel tests: **18 passed**
- Channel unit suite: **159 passed, 1 environment-related failure**
- Plugin process suite: **56 passed, 1 skipped**
- `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`, and `git diff --check`: passed

prs.title: feat(memory): add reranker model center with service test, multi-query precision history and auto-verify
prs.body:
## Description

**What this PR does:** Adds a reranker model center to the reranker settings (Runtime Config → Memory & Retrieval), mirroring the existing Embedding model center, and upgrades the ranking-precision verification from a single binary smoke test into a multi-query, persisted, and optionally scheduled metric.

**Why:** A misconfigured reranker is currently invisible until retrieval quality degrades. The new center surfaces configuration status, current model, service verification (connectivity + latency) and a meaningful ranking-precision figure (`correct/total`, 10-run rolling average, sparkline) so a bad model is visible at a glance and its trend can be tracked across restarts.

The overview shows four slots: configuration status, current model, service verification and ranking precision.

### Changes

- **Reranker model center**: `RerankerModelCenter` overview on the same 4-column grid and status styles as the embedding card; session-scoped `rerankerVerificationStore` keyed by agent + service fingerprint, invalidated when the service config changes or the agent switches.
- **Service verification**: `POST /workspace/reranker/test` sends a real rerank request with sample documents (one clearly relevant plus two distractors) and returns latency, relevance scores mapped back to request order, and whether the expected most-relevant document ranked first. The outbound call runs under a hard `asyncio.wait_for` deadline, upstream HTML error pages are stripped to plain text, and the API key is masked in returned messages.
- **Multi-query precision**: runs a 5-case multi-domain suite (password / checkout / unit conversion / planet / subscription) and reports `total`, `correct_count`, `precision` and per-case `scores`/`correct`, instead of a single boolean.
- **Persistent history**: new `reranker_history.py` appends each verification to `WORKING_DIR/reranker_history.json`, keyed by a service fingerprint; new endpoint `GET /workspace/reranker/history?fingerprint=`.
- **Trend UI**: the precision slot shows `correct/total = NN%`, a 10-run rolling average and a mini SVG sparkline; history survives restarts and refreshes.
- **Scheduled auto-verification**: `RerankerConfig.auto_verify_interval_hours` (0 = off) plus a background sweep task in the app lifespan that probes due services.
- **i18n**: strings for the overview, verification and precision slots across all 7 locales.

prs.title: feat(memory): allow a separate model for ReMeLight memory writing
prs.body:
## Description

`ReMeLightMemoryManager` currently injects the agent's main model into ReMe's `as_llm` component before every memory-writing job (`auto_memory` / `auto_dream` / `daily_paper` / `auto_fin`), so memory writing always consumes the same (often expensive) model used for chatting.

This PR adds an optional `memory_model` slot to `reme_light_memory_config`, so memory writing can run on an independent, lighter model:

- Uses `{"provider_id": "...", "model": "..."}` as the canonical format; a string is treated as a bare model name that inherits the main model's provider, including version-tagged names such as `qwen2.5:7b`.
- When unset, behavior is unchanged (main model is used).
- If dedicated-model construction fails (including non-`ProviderError` SDK exceptions), the manager logs a warning and injects the usable main model. Runtime failures before output can also fall back to that model. Main-model failures still propagate. Image jobs exclude the main-model fallback unless it has confirmed image support.
- The injected model is refreshed before every LLM job, so config changes take effect without a restart.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7664

**Security Considerations:** `memory_model` stores only a provider/model reference; no credentials are written to `agent.json` (API keys stay in the provider store).

prs.body: ## Description Follow-up to #7613. This PR applies the plugin-local cleanups suggested during review, adapts automatic-recall budgeting to the host's current `HintBlock` format, and addresses the shutdown edge case accepted as a non-blocking follow-up in #7613. All changes are confined to `plugins/memory/openviking/`. **Related Issue:** Relates to #7613 **Security Considerations:** [If applicable, e.g. channel auth, env/config handling] ### Automatic-recall budgeting - Account for the actual `HintBlock.hint` content when reserving space for the host-generated recall wrapper. - Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and bound the full injected recall text, rather than only the retrieved body. - Update budget tests to measure the actual hint content instead of fields from the previous message format. - Remove the hard-coded request-budget expectation derived from the old host prompt. Existing boundary tests verify the complete-message budget. - Update the toolkit-builder test's mock configuration to include `coding_mode.enabled`. ### Shutdown lifecycle - Store and reuse a single HTTP cleanup task across repeated and concurrent `close()` calls, rather than treating a cleared client reference as proof that cleanup completed. - Use `asyncio.shield()` so cancelling a caller's wait does not cancel the underlying cleanup. Cancellation still propagates to the caller. - Preserve the actual cleanup result. If HTTP cleanup fails, subsequent `close()` calls continue to return `False` instead of incorrectly reporting success. - Add regression coverage for repeated close after failure, caller cancellation followed by successful or failed cleanup, concurrent close calls, and repeated close after success. Preserve credential redaction in failure logs. ### Review follow-up **Item 1 — Reuse the base automatic-recall flow** The session-aware `auto_memory_search()` override is retained in this PR. I agree that the base flow could serve the current default configuration with query expansion disabled. The retained override passes the current QwenPaw session ID to OpenViking, allowing session-based query expansion when `query_expansion="auto"` is enabled through the documented source change. The READMEs now clarify that query expansion remains disabled by default, requires editing source and redeploying, and depends on available session history or an archive overview. No Console or Agent configuration switch is introduced. **Item 3 — Use one UTF-8 clipping implementation** Reuse `_clip_utf8()` for both automatic recall and explicit search. When truncation cannot retain meaningful text, return an empty string rather than a marker-only result. Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and multibyte character boundaries. **Item 4 — Flatten persistence filtering** Combine role, persisted-ID, and pending-ID filtering into one pass, and calculate the `every_turn` condition once. Preserve the existing separation between successful append and successful commit progress. **Item 5 — Reduce test coupling** Move shared fixtures into `conftest.py` and centralize manager cleanup. prs.title: fix(scroll): accept Windows extended-length paths in history SQLite URIs
prs.body:
## Description

`recall_history` fails on every Windows host whose workspace path reaches the
history store in extended-length form (`\\?\C:\...`). `Path.as_uri()` renders
that spelling as `file://%3F/C%3A/...`, and SQLite refuses the URI:

```
OperationalError: invalid uri authority: %3F
```

Because only the URI-building read path is affected, writes to `history.db`
keep succeeding while every read through `HistoryStore`, the schema
validation and the backup source fails. Plain-path connections to the very
same file work, which is what makes the failure look like "the database is
corrupt" rather than "the URL is malformed".

The fix strips the prefix before the URI is built, and restores
`\\?\UNC\server\share` to `\\server\share` so network workspaces keep
working. Plain paths are untouched on every platform. Three call sites are
covered:

| Site | Mode |
| --- | --- |
| `validate_history_database()` | `ro` |
| `backup_history_database()` | `ro` |
| `HistoryStore._open()` | `rwc` / `rw` |

Fixes #8585

## Evidence

Before / after on Windows, upstream `main` @ `275fd26e`, against a real
`history.db` created by `HistoryStore`:

| Call | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `validate_history_database(<extended path>)` | `OperationalError: invalid uri authority: %3F` | returns `PRAGMA user_version` |
| `HistoryStore(<extended path>)` | same error | opens; append + read round-trip OK |
| `backup_history_database(<extended path>, snapshot)` | same error | snapshot written and re-validates |

The mechanism reproduces without any project code:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3

p = Path(r"\\?\C:\tmp\history.db")
p.as_uri()                        # 'file://%3F/C%3A/tmp/history.db'
sqlite3.connect(p.as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True)
# OperationalError: invalid uri authority: %3F
sqlite3.connect(str(p))           # non-URI path to the same file
# works -- this is why writes never failed
```

Regression tests in `tests/unit/agents/context/test_history_store.py`:

1. prefix stripping for drive-letter and UNC spellings (runs everywhere);
2. `HistoryStore` open on an extended-length path, append + read;
3. `validate_history_database` agrees on both spellings of one file;
4. `backup_history_database` reads an extended-length source.

The three behavioural cases `skip` on hosts that cannot spell an
extended-length path.

- Target: `tests/unit/agents/context/test_history_store.py` — 63 passed
- Neighbouring: `tests/unit/agents/context/`, `tests/unit/backup/test_history_sqlite.py`, `tests/unit/app/test_scroll_startup_io.py` — 687 passed
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — all hooks passed

prs.title: fix(matrix): use scoped crypto store filenames on Windows
prs.body:
## Summary
Fix Matrix E2EE crypto-store initialization tests on Windows by using
cross-platform, identity-scoped filenames for the database and device trust
state.
## Root Cause
matrix-nio derives its default database filename from:
```text
{user_id}_{device_id}.db
```
A Matrix user ID such as `@bot:example.com` contains a colon. Linux and macOS
treat this as a regular filename character, but Windows interprets it as an
NTFS alternate data stream separator.
As a result, SQLite can initialize and use the store, but directory enumeration
does not expose a regular `*.db` file. Assertions and state checks based on
`glob("*.db")` therefore fail on Windows.
## Changes
- Derive crypto-store filenames from the existing SHA-256 scope of
  `homeserver`, `user_id`, and `device_id`.
- Use the scoped basename for:
  - The SQLite database.
  - Trusted devices.
  - Blacklisted devices.
  - Ignored devices.
- Preserve matrix-nio's existing `DefaultStore` trust behavior.
- Migrate legacy identity-based filenames before matrix-nio opens the store.
- Support both workspace-scoped state and the legacy shared crypto directory.
- Migrate Windows alternate data streams through a temporary file followed by
  an atomic target replacement.
- Reject startup with `MATRIX_CRYPTO_STORE_CONFLICT` when both legacy and new
  files exist, instead of overwriting either one.
- Replace `*.db` discovery in affected conflict checks so Windows alternate
  data streams cannot bypass them.
## Compatibility
- Different accounts, devices, and homeservers retain distinct database names.
- Existing crypto databases and trust files are migrated without resetting
  the Matrix encryption identity.
- No fixed shared filename such as `matrix.db` is introduced.
## Tests
Added regression coverage for:
- Regular database creation on Windows.
- Account identity reuse after restart.
- Device trust persistence after restart.
- Legacy filename migration in workspace and legacy shared directories.
- Unique filenames for different identities.
- Legacy/new filename conflict detection.
Validated on Windows with matrix-nio 0.26.0 and vodozemac 0.10.0:
```text
pytest tests/unit/channels/test_matrix.py -q
14 passed
```
Black, Flake8, Mypy, and `git diff --check` passed. Pylint reported no E/F

issues.body:
### Documentation location

docs/book/src/channels/email.md, "Tools-only: enable it, don't bind it"

### Documentation issue type

missing documentation

### Problem

The tools-only section says that enabling an email alias registers `email_search` and `email_read`, and that binding it to an agent is what starts the IMAP listener. So it tells you to leave the alias out of every agent's `channels` list, and it covers the legacy fallback when no agent declares any bindings.

It doesn't mention approval routes, which also start the listener. `ActiveChannelAliases::contains` in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs` also accepts any channel named by an approval route:

- a `request_route` or `escalation_route` in `[sop.approval.policies.*]`
- the `approval_route.approver_channel` of an enabled agent's risk profile

A route can name a bare channel type such as `email`. When exactly one email alias is enabled, the route resolves to that alias. An operator who follows the section but routes approvals through email still gets the IMAP listener for that alias. Outbound behavior is unaffected; this is about unwanted inbound listener activity.

### Expected documentation

Add approval routes to the exclusions in the tools-only section. To keep an alias tools-only, leave it out of:

- every agent's `channels` list
- SOP approval `request_route` and `escalation_route`
- the risk-profile `approver_channel` of every enabled agent, including a bare `email` route when only one email alias is enabled

Optionally, add a sentence on what the listener does for an alias that only an approval route names: it stays live to deliver approval replies, but it isn't assigned to an agent for ordinary traffic.

### Related issue, PR, RFC, or discussion

Follow-up to #12003 (merged as 71e68a0d63), from @Audacity88's review suggestion: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12003#pullrequestreview-5703250355

issues.body:
### Affected component

runtime/daemon

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

The daemon holds RPC sessions in a live session map capped at 64 entries:

- `SessionStore::new(64, …)` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/daemon/mod.rs:967`.
- At the cap, every new session is refused with `-32001 Session limit reached` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/session.rs:553`, and again at 613 and 634). That applies to every client: zerocode over the socket, remote zerocode over WSS, and the gateway.

Nothing removes an idle session from that map:

- When a client disconnects, the transports only unregister its TUI identity and log "TUI disconnected; sessions retained (persistent)" (`rpc/local.rs:801–815`; `rpc/wss.rs:1264` does the same).
- `RpcSession.last_active` is updated on use (`session.rs:753` and `:1239`) but never read to evict anything.
- The daemon's 60-second reaper (`daemon/mod.rs:969–977`) evicts idle **queue actors** (`SessionActorQueue::evict_idle`), not sessions.
- A live session leaves the map only on `session/close`, `session/delete` or `session/kill`, through same-mode sibling eviction on the same TUI, or when the daemon reloads or restarts.

**Remote callers make this worse.** A non-local caller can resume a session only while it is live and owned by its own TUI identity (`capture_session_access`, `rpc/dispatch.rs:2818`). A client that reconnects under a new identity can't reach, or close, the sessions it left behind, so they hold their places until the daemon restarts.

### Expected behavior

Idle sessions of clients that are gone eventually give up their place in the live map, while their transcripts stay on disk. For example: close a remote client's session that has no running turn, no pending approval and no live connection for its identity after an idle timeout, leaving local-socket sessions alone.

A full map should also be visible to the operator, in a log line and in `status`, not only as a refusal.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Against a running daemon:
# 1. Start the daemon with a WSS listener and remote auth configured.
# 2. From a remote client, 64 times: connect, initialize without re-presenting
#    tui_id/tui_sig (a new identity each time), call session/new, disconnect.
# 3. From any client, call session/new: it is refused with "Session limit reached".
#
# As a test in rpc/dispatch.rs's test module, driving the dispatcher the way the
# WSS transport does:
# 1. Open a context on SessionStore::new(64, SessionActorQueue::new(32, 30, 600)),
#    the daemon's values.
# 2. 64 times: make a RemoteSessionOwner dispatcher with a new TUI identity, call
#    session/new (chat_mode: chat), then shutdown(), as the transport does when
#    its peer leaves.
# 3. Run the daemon's reaper step (SessionActorQueue::evict_idle).
# 4. From a dispatcher with yet another identity, call session/close on one of
#    the leftovers.
# 5. Call session/new from a new remote dispatcher and from a local one.
```

### Impact

Affected users: every client of a long-running daemon. After enough remote reconnects, or any client that opens sessions without closing them, new sessions fail for everyone until a restart.
Frequency: always, once 64 sessions are stranded; it builds up slowly with ordinary use, since a remote zerocode that relaunches under a new identity strands its previous sessions.
Consequence: shared or hosted daemons reach the cap fastest. Clients can work around it by closing their own sessions, but the core shouldn't depend on every client doing so.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
live sessions after 64 connect/open/disconnect cycles: 64
queue reaper evicted 0 queue actors; live sessions now 64
returning client's session/close on a leftover: Err(JsonRpcError { code: -32003, message: "Caller does not own this session", data: None })
65th session/new (remote): Err(JsonRpcError { code: -32001, message: "Session limit reached", data: None })
65th session/new (local): Err(JsonRpcError { code: -32001, message: "Session limit reached", data: None })
```

### ZeroClaw version

master 89bd18484b

### Rust version

rustc 1.98.0

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (not OS-specific: daemon session store)

### Regression?

Unknown

### Pre-flight checks

- [X] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.body:
### Task

Fence both of `session/close`'s later effects against the session's **current** TUI, not only the TUI checked before cancellation:
1. unregistering the RPC channel;
2. removing the session.

`session/run_once` uses the same cleanup path, so it gets the fix too.

### Context

- **Where this comes from:** Audacity88's review of #12239 (🟡 "inherited close still has a later TUI-transfer window"). The omission is inherited: #12239 neither introduces nor broadens it, and it isn't a condition for #12239.
- **The window:** `handle_session_close_bound` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs`) checks the TUI before cancellation, then waits again before unregistering the RPC channel and removing the session. Those later effects check principal authority and generation, but not the current TUI.
- **The consequence:** a trusted-local reconnect can transfer the same live generation during that wait, and the displaced remote close then removes the newly rebound live session. The durable transcript isn't deleted, and no cross-principal bypass has been shown.

### Acceptance criteria

- Both later close effects re-check the current TUI owner under the same boundary that performs them, and refuse (or leave the session in place) when it changed.
- A regression transfers the session to another TUI after the initial cancellation check and before the effects. It asserts that the displaced close leaves the rebound live session and its RPC channel in place.
- The same check covers `session/run_once`'s cleanup.
- Same-TUI reconnect and trusted-local behaviour are unchanged; the existing close tests still pass.

### Likely files or areas

- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs`: `handle_session_close_bound`, `handle_session_run_once` and their shared cleanup.

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

Audacity88 (raised it in the #12239 review); the #12239 reviewers.

### Risk notes

This is a session-lifecycle and authority path, so it needs two Core reviews. Land it after #12239, which adds the commit-time TUI fence for `session/configure` that this would mirror.

issues.body:
### Task

Tell the dashboard whether the signed-in account may read config, and hide the config pages from accounts that can't. The pages are reached from the sidebar, the command palette and the route guard.

### Context

- **The symptom:** a signed-in account without a `config` grant sees the config and agent-configuration entries in the sidebar. Both open a red *Couldn't load sections: API 403: {"error":"Principal lacks the config grant required for this method"}*. The gateway's refusal is right, but the dashboard shouldn't offer the page. Seen while testing the scoped dashboard chat (#12244), and the same on master.
- **What the session tells the dashboard:** `GET /api/auth/session` (`handle_auth_session` in `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs`) returns `admin` and `features { chat, core_sessions, operator_pages }`. Nothing in it says whether the account may read config.
- **The current rule:** `pathAccess` in `web/src/lib/navAccess.ts`, from #11965, allows `/config` and `/setup` for every signed-in account, because the gateway checks each config path. The sidebar, `CommandPalette.tsx` and the route guard in `Layout.tsx` all filter through it.

### Acceptance criteria

- **The session response carries `features.config`:**
  - true for an administrator, and for a profile whose grants allow reading config;
  - false otherwise;
  - decided by the same rule the config routes use, so the two can't drift.
- **The web reads the flag:**
  - an absent flag means false;
  - `pathAccess` allows the config paths only with it.
- **The home page:**
  - `/agents` for an account with chat;
  - `/config` for an account with config only;
  - the not-available page for an account with neither.
- **Tests:**
  - Gateway tests cover an administrator, a profile with config read and one without.
  - Web tests cover the parsing and the navigation rule.
  - Reverting either side fails a test.

### Likely files or areas

- `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/principal_gate.rs` (a helper built on the config routes' method floor)
- `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs` (`handle_auth_session`)
- `web/src/lib/auth.ts`, `web/src/lib/authSession.ts`, `web/src/lib/navAccess.ts` and their tests

@JordanTheJet

- **A grant changed mid-session** shows on the next session read.

issues.title: [Bug]: RPC cron/add and cron/patch treat the request as an operator approval for the shell command

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Affected component

runtime (RPC cron methods)

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

`cron/add` over the RPC socket passes `approved = true` to `add_shell_job_with_approval` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs:9765` on master 50e01f55e4, commented "RPC calls are pre-approved"). `cron/patch` validates a replacement command with `approved = true` as well (`dispatch.rs:9833`). #12232 left both in place.

Under `autonomy = "supervised"`, a command that needs approval (a medium-risk command with `require_approval_for_medium_risk`, or a high-risk one) is therefore accepted and stored, as if an operator had approved it. The CLI (`zeroclaw cron add`) and the gateway (`POST /api/cron`, `PATCH /api/cron/{id}`, `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api.rs:590` and `:842`) both pass `approved = false` and refuse the same command.

The stored command does not run unapproved: every scheduled run, and `cron/trigger`, re-validate it with `approved = false` and refuse it. The job then fails on every tick.

### Expected behavior

An RPC request is not an approval. `cron/add` and `cron/patch` should apply the same supervised-autonomy gate as the CLI and the gateway, and refuse a command that needs approval with the policy reason instead of storing it.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Configure an agent with autonomy = "supervised", require_approval_for_medium_risk = true,
   and `touch` in its allowed commands (allowlisted, medium risk).
2. Over the RPC socket (zerocode, or any client after `initialize`), call
   cron/add {"agent": "<agent>", "schedule": "*/5 * * * *", "command": "touch marker"}.
3. The job is stored. `zeroclaw cron add` and POST /api/cron refuse the same command
   with "Command requires explicit approval".
4. Each scheduled run then fails with the same policy reason.
Source-traced on master 50e01f55e4; the PR's regression tests reproduce it through the RPC handlers.
```

### Impact

Moderate. No command runs without approval, but RPC clients can store jobs the policy refuses, which fail on every tick, and the RPC surface disagrees with the CLI and the dashboard about what needs approval. The same `true` is in v0.8.5's `handle_cron_add` (introduced in #6848); the `cron/patch` half is master-only.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

master 50e01f55e4 (v0.8.7)

### Rust version

n/a (source review); CI pins 1.98.0

### Operating system

Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04); the code path is platform-independent

Unknown

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`03b29bcc68`). **Depends on #11320** and **#11186** (`zeroclaw-rpc-client` and the gateway's core RPC seam). The branch merges #11320 at its current head `864b58d76e` (with #11319 `c352574198`, #11339 and #11165 `19e41b09fa` beneath it) and #11186 at its current head `ed92285a87` (restacked 2026-10-23 and refreshed 2026-10-29, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land. Review this PR's own commits: `d15729ebff` (the forwarder), `5926ddde14` (docs), `c02e5c0bac` (the in-process seam tests get a TUI signing key), `7702fe138c` (the forwarder's failure records keep the webhook path out) `c02417bfac` (change filter path restored after the restack) and `6d8ed835a8` (the forwarder ends a connection the daemon has stopped recognising, so the link dials again; from Greptile's review); `de5cd570ab` (the connector fix) is superseded by #11186's `535b43829a`.
- **Refresh of 2026-10-29 (`fee8af1cb8`):** merges #11320's new head, which brings master `5a51398dd5` (the one `rpc/types.rs` conflict against it was master editing a doc comment inside the block #11165 moved into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`; the moved-out file stays and the doc line now lives on the proto copy) and #11320's admission re-check: the daemon re-resolves the forwarder's live grants at admission instead of trusting the binding its dispatch task copied, so a revoked or narrowed caller is refused and the forwarder answers 503 for it, as for any core refusal. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Second refresh of 2026-10-29 (`6d8ed835a8`):** merges #11320's `864b58d76e` (`2f1fa249a4`: a rename or delete over the socket now refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; the forwarder connects as the shared operator and is not affected) and adds `6d8ed835a8`, from Greptile's review of this PR: when a policy change removes or revokes the gateway's identity while its connection is open, the daemon keeps the socket and answers `AUTH_REQUIRED`, and the link redialed only after a close, so webhooks stayed 503 after the operator restored access. The forwarder now ends the connection at the first such answer (record `plugin_webhook_core_identity_lost`) and the redial is accepted once access is back, or refused into the slow backoff while it is not; `FORBIDDEN` stays on the connection. Two tests: the close seen from both sides, and the whole sequence over a local socket ending with a webhook served on the new connection.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (`9138333811`):** merges master `03b29bcc68`, which carries the Wasmtime 48.0.8 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 (#12129) and so clears the `Security` job for this branch. ### What this does, simply

You can run the web gateway on its own with `zeroclaw gateway`. Until now, webhooks meant for channel plugins did not work there, because the plugin routes live in the daemon. Now that gateway passes each plugin webhook to the daemon over the local socket and returns the daemon's answer, exactly as the built-in gateway would. If the daemon is down, senders get 503 so they retry, and nothing is forwarded to a socket owned by another user.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: under the default policy (`security.trust_daemon_uid = true`) the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials as the shared operator, which holds every grant. Only the `/plugin/{path}` route uses that connection; it is separate from the core RPC extension other routes can reach.
- New external network calls? No (local socket only)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes: webhook headers, including vendor signature headers, now cross the local socket to the daemon. Mitigation: on Unix the gateway verifies the socket's peer uid equals its own before sending anything; on Windows forwarding is off until the pipe server can be verified.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: messages reach the same plugin channel listener as before.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a publicly bound standalone gateway now exposes the daemon's plugin routes on that listener (same exposure as the supervised gateway on that address). The connection appears as a TUI client (`/api/tuis`) and keeps an `--ephemeral` daemon alive. A refused redial writes a daemon audit record, backed off from 30 seconds to 5 minutes. `zeroclaw gateway restart` first POSTs `/admin/shutdown` to the configured address, which stops a supervised gateway listening there (unchanged, now documented).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the supervised gateway. Standalone gateway: `/plugin/{path}` changes from 404 for every path to forwarding (Unix); 503 for every path while the daemon is unreachable or the socket belongs to another user; 503 `plugin_webhook_core_unsupported` against an older daemon without the method. New error keys: `plugin_webhook_core_{unavailable,refused,identity_lost,unsupported,unexpected,timeout}`, `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused,untrusted_peer}`, `plugin_webhook_forwarding_disabled` (Windows). Rust API: `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)`; `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` is an optional gateway dependency behind `plugins-wasm`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The standalone gateway resolves the daemon socket like other local clients (`ZEROCLAW_SOCKET` or `<data_dir>/daemon.sock`); next to a running daemon it runs on its own config dir, so it needs `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the standalone gateway returns to answering 404 for plugin routes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** stop the daemon, or build without `plugins-wasm`; `security.trust_daemon_uid = false` without a `[users]` entry for the gateway's uid makes the daemon refuse the connection (webhooks then answer 503).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_core_*` and `core_rpc_*` error keys in the gateway log; 503 bursts on `/plugin/*` from a standalone gateway; `RPC authorization denied` records for the gateway's connection in the daemon log.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(parser): recognize LFM <|tool_call_start|> function-style tool calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #12235.

When a provider emits chat-template special-token tool calls such as:

```text
<|tool_call_start|>[file_read(path='/root/zc-repro/data/estado.txt')]<|tool_call_end|>
```

(typical of LFM2.5 when the request has no native `tools` array), the text-fallback parser did not recognize the envelope. The raw tokens were returned to the caller as the agent reply instead of being executed.

This change:

- Parses `<|tool_call_start|>…<|tool_call_end|>` envelopes in `parse_tool_calls`.
- Accepts function-style kwargs with single quotes (`path='…'`) as well as double quotes / bare values.
- Strips the envelopes from visible text so the special tokens do not leak into the user-facing reply.

Note: the issue also suspects the delegate loop may omit the native `tools` array. This PR fixes the text-fallback path so the observed LFM format is executed even when tools were only described in the prompt; a separate follow-up can ensure `tools_count > 0` on delegated requests if traces still show that gap.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser --lib parse_tool_calls_handles` — **33 passed** (includes new `parse_tool_calls_handles_lfm_special_token_function_style`)
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser --lib function_style` — **4 passed** (includes `parse_function_style_kwargs_accepts_single_and_double_quotes`)
- [x] `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser`
