prs.title: feat(rpc): stable denial reason identifiers and localized selector denials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every RPC authorization denial now carries an `RpcDenialReason`, a stable identifier set by the typed constructor that builds it. The constructor also derives the JSON-RPC code from the reason and renders the message from the reason's Fluent key. `AuthDenied`'s `reason` field is private, so a denial cannot be built without one; the free-text `auth_required(message)` and `forbidden(message)` constructors are gone.
  - The denial audit record (`RPC authorization denied`) emits the identifier as `reason` and the localized text as a separate `denial_message` attribute, so operators can group and alert on refusals without depending on wording or the daemon's locale. The attribute is not named `message` because log exporters copy attributes out flat and log backends reserve that name.
  - The coarse grant denial and every selector refusal (config path, agent, cron, session workspace, `fs/list_dir`, attachment source, session environment, global streams, SOP) resolve through 12 new `rpc-auth-*` Fluent keys with arguments instead of inline English literals. Request values are quoted and escaped exactly as the old `{:?}` literals quoted them, so the English text is byte-identical. The one exception is the global-stream refusal, whose key carries the wording #11326 gives it, naming the persisted log.
  - A denial after failed revalidation now records the principal id and auth provider of the binding it drops. Before, the dispatcher cleared the binding first and the record carried nulls. The same change removes a production `expect()`.
  - The branch merges current master, so the denial sites #11171 added (the authority lease, the expiry helper, and the chunked-upload recheck) use the typed constructors too. The upload recheck's session-ownership refusal gets its own `session_not_owned` reason. The later merge converts #11132's sites the same way: `require_additional_grant` refuses with `grant_missing`, and steering admission records its ownership refusal as `session_not_owned` and its remote local-capability refusal as a new `session_local_capabilities` reason instead of rebuilding denials from message text, while the binding checks it calls record their own refusals once rather than twice. The latest merge converts #12232's two sites the same way: the admin-only procedure execution refusal becomes `sop_principal_ceiling_required` and the agent cron-job trigger refusal becomes `cron_agent_principal_required`, each rendering the Fluent key #12232 introduced; the `sop_tool_selector_constrained` reason, which #12232's rework left without a site, is removed before it ships.
- **Scope boundary:** The JSON-RPC wire shape is unchanged: codes and English message bytes are identical (apart from the global-stream refusal's #11326 wording), and the identifier is not sent to clients. Gateway HTTP denial bodies, handshake (`initialize`) auditing, the refusals that bypass `AuthDenied` (session ownership outside chunked uploads, shared memory plane, SOP decision authorization, TUI signature, remote-WSS SOP methods), and translated catalogues are unchanged. The cron refusal's client text ("Cron job not found: ...") stays an inline English literal on purpose: it must match the genuinely-missing-job answer, which comes from the cron store, so the refusal does not confirm that a job exists. The `cron/patch` writer-transaction rechecks that #12232 added keep their plain `rpc_err` refusals, which master does not audit; only their unbound-dispatcher literal moves to the shared first-call key.
- **Blast radius:** The audit record's `reason` attribute changes from prose to an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`. The record merged in #10259 on 2026-09-24 and shipped in v0.8.6 and v0.8.7 with the prose in `reason`, so a consumer written against those releases must display `denial_message` and group or alert on the identifier, as the docs section says. Open PRs that build denials with `AuthDenied::auth_required`/`forbidden` or struct literals will stop compiling at rebase; the fix is a variant, a key, and a typed constructor per new site.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11005. Depends on #12062, the holding-crate exception row for this change, which must be recorded before this merges. Related #11326 (merged; this PR's denial-records docs and the global-stream refusal describe the `logs/query` and `logs/get` scoping it implements), #8289, #10259.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

### What this does, simply

When the daemon refuses an RPC request because the caller lacks permission, it writes a warning to its log. Until now the "reason" in that warning was the English sentence the client saw, so it changed whenever the wording changed and would change with the daemon's language, which makes it a poor thing to alert on. It is now a short fixed code such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, and the sentence moves to its own field. Several refusal sentences were written directly in the code instead of in the translation catalogue; they now live in the catalogue like the rest. Finally, one kind of refusal, when a policy change invalidates an existing connection, forgot who the connection belonged to before logging; it now records that. Clients see the same error codes and English messages as before, apart from the refusal for daemon-wide logs, which now also names the persisted log.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the changed output is a structured log record, and the new tests drive real refused requests through the dispatcher and assert the record each one writes.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` and `Parallel Runtime Test` run the new unit and dispatcher tests; `Lint` covers the Rust changes; `Docs Style` and the links gate cover the documentation section.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Head 23703b20b0** (merges master 50e01f55e4, which includes #12232): the merge's one conflict was the SOP execution refusal, which #12232 made admin-only under a new Fluent key and this PR builds with a typed constructor; it now records `sop_principal_ceiling_required`, and #12232's agent cron-job trigger refusal records `cron_agent_principal_required`. `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`: `6121 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`, #12232's tests included; `-- rpc::`: `908 passed; 0 failed`. `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, clippy (no findings in changed files), the comment hygiene scanner on the touched files and the docs quality gate on `authentication.md` pass. Earlier heads: 3ab104bdac merged #11326 (the `GLOBAL_STREAM_SCOPED_DENIAL` deletion stands; the Fluent string carries its text), 0a386d6cce converted #11132's two denial sites, da62caf7e1 dropped c94abbf93e's configure-race synchronization in favor of #11330's fence.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.97.1, head 2e3f2e5101, which merges master a0f70b7925, unless noted):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`: `5455 passed; 2 failed; 8 ignored`. The two failures are `rpc::dispatch::tests::configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock` and `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`. Master a0f70b7925 itself fails the same way under the same command (the configure test in 2 of 2 runs, the cost test in 1 of 2), each passes alone 3 of 3 times on this branch, and neither touches code this PR changes. Before merging master (2d96dfa52d, on 2443af29ea) the same command passed clean: `5313 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`: `637 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `ws::tests::websocket_handler_projects_anthropic_empty_terminal_stream_as_user_error` hitting its response deadline under load; it passes alone 3 of 3 times, and `ws.rs` changes only in master's commits.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`: no findings in changed files. Under `-D warnings` it stops on four findings in files this PR does not touch, byte-identical to master: `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`, macOS test builds) and three `clippy::drop_non_drop` in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, which appear only when `-p zeroclaw-gateway` builds channels without `channel-telegram`.
  - `cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps`: 0 warnings.
  - `cargo fluent check`: all FTL files ok. `cargo fluent scan`: no `rpc-auth-*` key reported stale.
  - `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`, `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (markdownlint 0 errors), `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each restored afterwards:
  - Emitting the message text as `reason` again fails all six dispatcher capture tests.
  - Auditing after the binding is cleared (the old order) fails `denial_after_failed_revalidation_keeps_the_principal_it_dropped` with a null principal.
  - Renaming one identifier fails the identifier-pinning test and the matching dispatcher test.
  - Deleting one new key from `cli.ftl` fails three tests that render the `{rpc-auth-agent-not-entitled}` missing-key marker.
  - Not verified: a live daemon under a translated locale; Windows.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface changes; the changed output is a log record whose attributes the tests assert.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No `--no-default-features` check: nothing in `rpc/` is feature-gated, so no constructor can lose its only caller in that build.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The record carries the principal id and provider label it already carried, never bearer material; the attribution fix stops dropping data the dispatcher already held.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test principals are synthetic roster names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. Request values that appear in denial messages (agent aliases, paths, job ids, procedure names) are quoted and escaped, so control characters cannot break a message or its log line.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for clients: codes and English messages are unchanged, apart from the global-stream refusal's wording. The audit record's `reason` attribute now holds an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`; the prose form shipped in v0.8.6 and v0.8.7, so log consumers written against those releases need that one-field change.

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None

### Notes for reviewers

- **Refusal cost:** argumented Fluent lookups parse the catalogue on each call. On an Apple Silicon Mac that measured about 180 µs per refusal for an English daemon and about 530 µs for a translated locale that lacks the new keys (every translated locale until a translation pass). This affects only refused requests. Caching parsed bundles would remove it, but it changes every argumented call site, so it is left for a separate PR. The same cost makes a cron refusal for another agent's job slightly slower than one for a missing job; the answers themselves are identical.
- **Unbound selectors:** the five selector helpers that refused an unbound dispatcher with a bare literal now use the existing first-call key and write a record. They are unreachable once the gate has run.

- Audit handshake denials and the refusals listed as unrecorded in the new docs section.
- Translation fill for the `rpc-auth-*` keys, and parse each Fluent catalogue once.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.body:
> Maintainer note: I integrated @IftekharUddin's documentation update and corrected the scope and validation account below. The original contributor's work and history are preserved.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** Documents the shared OpenAI-compatible chat-completions `native_tools` override and its family defaults. Explicit `true` enables native tools and `false` selects text fallback; unset keeps the family default. Custom and Groq chat-completions aliases default to text fallback, Responses keeps native support independently, and Hailo-Ollama rejects `true`. The runtime-profile `tool_dispatcher` comment explains the difference between provider capability and dispatcher selection, and the Custom Providers page includes an opt-in example.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. No code, config parsing, or runtime behavior changes. The reworded comments flow into the generated config reference (`docs/book/src/reference/config.md`, gitignored) and rustdoc on the next generation run; no committed generated artifact changes.
- **Blast radius:** Anyone reading the config schema, the generated config reference, the Custom Providers page, or the Provider Configuration field list. No runtime consumer reads these comments.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

An operator pointing ZeroClaw at a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway via the `custom` provider slot may find that the agent never uses real tool calls. The gateway supports the OpenAI `tools` protocol, but ZeroClaw sends the tools as text in the system prompt and expects the model to answer with `<tool_call>` XML. Nothing in the `custom` slot docs said native tool calling is off by default, so the only clue was a schema comment that pointed at Groq. This PR documents the shared override and family defaults, documents the `tool_dispatcher` strategies (including what happens if you force `"native"` on a provider that was built without native tool calling), and adds a "Native tool calling" section to the Custom Providers page with a `native_tools = true` example. prs.title: fix(rpc): hold current authority through session effects
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** #11234 made queued session operations recheck the caller's authority after they wait. Several session effects still committed after another await, or never rechecked at all, so a revocation, demotion or ownership change that landed in between still let them through. This finishes those effects:
  - `session/configure` commits its overrides and provider in one step, under the caller's authority lease, rather than in two awaited writes after the recheck.
  - `session/append` and `session/rename` decide under the store's write lock, by the row's current owner and the caller's current authority. Append seeds the live Agent and sends its event inside the same commit.
  - For a remote client, configure, append, rename, abort and steering also check that the caller's TUI still owns the session when they commit. A same-generation resume by another TUI used to leave the old TUI able to reconfigure, write, cancel and steer. Steering it had already queued is now revoked when the session changes hands.
  - `session/abort` decides under the incarnation and cancellation locks with the caller's authority lease.
  - `session/run-once` looks up its id under current authority and requires `sessions:update`, since it closes the session it creates. If the close is refused after the turn, the call returns that error instead of reporting success. A remote caller can now name its own id, and the call keeps the generation it published even if that session is removed before it returns.
- **Scope boundary:** No new RPC method, config key or persisted schema. The SOP read repairs from #11411 are a separate follow-up after #12232 (which replaced #11220). Principal-owned Chat restore after a restart is #11737. Prompt admission, `session/new` resume and the destructive operations #11234 already covers are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** RPC session handlers in `zeroclaw-runtime` (`rpc/dispatch.rs`, `rpc/session.rs`, the run-once doc in `rpc/types.rs`) and two new default methods on `SessionBackend` in `zeroclaw-infra`, implemented for SQLite and for JSONL append. Gateway and channel sessions are not touched, since append still refuses any session that RPC does not write.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11126. Related #11234, #11408, #11411.

### What this does, simply

When an RPC client asks to change a session, the daemon checks the caller is allowed and then makes the change. Between those two steps it often has to wait: for the session's queue, a lock or the database. #11234 added a second check after those waits. A few changes still did more waiting after that second check, or skipped it. So a caller whose access was taken away at the wrong moment could still add a message, rename a session, change its model, cancel its turn or steer it.

This PR moves the final check to the moment the change is written, and holds it there until the write is done. It also covers a remote case: the TUI that loses a session to another TUI can no longer act on it, and any steering it had already queued is dropped.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: each case is a timing window that the focused tests open with test pauses. A manual run cannot hit them reliably.

### How I tested

On Linux x86_64 (Rust 1.98.0), at ffcfe904b3 (tree 3650786e3e), on master 72167d12e2:

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust lint and test jobs build and run `zeroclaw-infra` and `zeroclaw-runtime`, where all the changes are.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for this change; the windows are covered by the focused tests below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fetch --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, the comment-hygiene gate and `git diff --check` against master: clean.
  - `cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib`: `test result: ok. 329 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `test result: ok. 6084 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`.
  - The ported tests three runs in a row at 4ad6aebb42: runtime `12 passed; 0 failed` and infra `2 passed; 0 failed`, each time. At ffcfe904b3, the configure and remote session tests three runs in a row: `165 passed; 0 failed` each time.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I undid one functional line at a time (19 changes) and ran the session tests for each. Fifteen failed the tests written for them:
  - the configure commit without its authority check;
  - the SQLite append, SQLite rename or JSONL append without theirs;
  - configure, append, rename or abort without the TUI fence;
  - abort without its authority lease;
  - a create-only `session/new` capturing access, or re-reading its generation;
  - steering ignoring a revoked TUI binding, or a rebind that keeps the old binding;
  - run-once without the `sessions:update` check, or hiding a refused close.

  Four fail nothing, and I couldn't make them observable:
  - **Configure leaving automatic routing on after an explicit model choice:** the flag has no accessor outside the agent, the same gap master has.
  - **Run-once looking up its id by the connection's stamped scope:** the ownership check and the create-only `session/new` that follow refuse the same cases.
  - **Steering's TUI fence at enqueue:** steering admission fences the same TUI just before, and the revoked binding drops the steer when the turn consumes it.
  - **Steering resolving its grants without holding the lease:** only a publication racing that one read would show it.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** ffcfe904b3, RPC handlers through their unit-test dispatchers.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No live daemon, macOS or Windows run, and no full workspace test suite. The infra and runtime libraries cover the changed code.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. `session/run-once` now requires `sessions:update` as well, which only narrows who can call it.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Steering that a TUI queued before it lost the session is now dropped before the model sees it.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No, in three narrow cases:
  - A principal granted `sessions:create` and `sessions:execute` but not `sessions:update` can no longer use `session/run-once`.
  - On a JSONL session backend, `session/rename` now returns an error instead of succeeding without storing the name. Guarded appends work on both backends.
  - A remote TUI that lost a session to another TUI now gets `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` for append, rename, abort and steer on that session.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: grant `sessions:update` to any permission profile that uses `session/run-once`. Nothing else needs to change.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the merge commit. The guarded writes add no state, so nothing needs migrating back.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** RPC clients getting `FORBIDDEN`, `AUTH_REQUIRED` or `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` on append, rename, abort, steer or configure without any policy or ownership change; run-once returning "Turn completed, but could not close transient session".

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

Not used. #11408 and #11411 stay open for their SOP parts. The session-effect commits here are Aarlington's work, kept as cherry-picks where they applied and otherwise ported with a `Co-authored-by` trailer:

- **Configure:**
  - f455ba115b and aaa681d085 (#11411), cherry-picked.
  - A follow-up keeps master's explicit-model routing step from #11516 in the atomic commit and removes the setter it replaced.
  - 3a833e4cdd and 561ece3f0e, ported onto master's version of their test.
- **Run-once lookup:** 85567e108c, cherry-picked.
- **Operator abort test:** 75a72e84a4, cherry-picked.
- **Append and rename:** the guarded writes from #11408's master merge 90a5978dbb, with the tests from 874b4e43bc and f00fe86148.
- **Remote ownership:** b86d4536bb, ported. Abort now uses `signal_cancellation_authorized`, and `abort_session_for_generation` is removed because nothing calls it anymore.
- **Steering:** 9c7cfd9823, and the steering part of 874b4e43bc.
- **Create-only generation:** the rest of 874b4e43bc.
- **Run-once cleanup:** 569e6fc11d, with the test changes from 08033c25a4 and 2e6c2b7835.
- **Abort test:** one new test of my own. Abort no longer rechecks before cancelling, so nothing else covered the handler passing its authority lease into `signal_cancellation_authorized`.
- **Not carried:**
  - 70a39b766f and ebfa6a1874: master's tests already publish config through the commit API.
  - The `sop_principal.rs` part of 70a39b766f goes with the SOP-reads follow-up.

IftekharUddin found that configure still committed without checking the current TUI owner and wrote the fix and its test: 66a93d5446, cherry-picked as ffcfe904b3 with IftekharUddin as author.

prs.title: fix(oidc): bind enrollment callbacks to the initiating browser
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, true-rebased onto `6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Bind gateway OIDC enrollment to the browser that started it. A copied callback URL can no longer reveal a token in a different browser.
  - Generate a separate 32-byte random secret for each flow. Keep only its hash in the existing `PendingPkce` record. Check the cookie before code exchange; refuse and consume mismatched flows.
  - Preserve concurrent tabs, one-time consumption, issuer/provider checks, and the original deadline for a valid capacity retry. The cookie grants no session or API access.
  - Add four endpoint regressions, update existing callback tests to carry their actual issued cookie, and document cookie scope and recovery.
- **Scope boundary:** Enrollment start/callback and their documentation. Dashboard sign-in remains in #11965. Configured origin (#12048), same-host HTTP ports (#12088), broader availability (#12049), and response zeroization (#12090) remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Clients that complete `/oidc/login/<alias>` through `/oidc/callback` must keep the issued browser cookie. Device flow and bearer-authenticated API routes retain their current behavior. The existing gateway `rand` dependency moves from dev to normal dependencies; no new package or lockfile change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12050. Related #11965 and #8289.

### What this does, simply

The browser login page returns a token that a user can copy into a client. Before this change, someone could start a login under their own account, then send its final URL to another person. That person could receive and use the wrong account's token.

The gateway now gives the starting browser a short-lived cookie. The final page requires that cookie. A different browser gets the existing refusal page, and no code is exchanged. Start a new login in the intended browser after a refusal; do not forward callback URLs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: independent review of the callback boundary and an A/B browser check are useful for this security change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, gateway enrollment HTTP routes and the callback page. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a test OIDC alias and two isolated browser profiles. Use dedicated test accounts. Keep the gateway scheme/host consistent. The captured mock-provider recipe and source hashes are in [the evidence bundle](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/README.md).
- **Steps to run:** Start a login in browser A. Capture the final callback URL before following it. Open that URL in browser B. Then retry it in A. Start two fresh flows in separate tabs of A and finish both normally.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** B receives `Sign-in not completed`, with no token exchange. A cannot replay that consumed flow. Both fresh tab flows succeed, each once. A normal same-browser return succeeds and clears only its flow cookie.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The callback lacks this browser check. The guard-removal negative control reproduces acceptance of a missing-cookie callback (200 instead of 400). A live provider or a full unpatched-daemon A/B run was not performed.

### How I tested

### Current integration after #12200 - 2026-11-02

Current head: a0b660c198c9a8aef8f00b3a2c2096af671ce127. Both original commits were true-rebased onto master 6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e, which includes merged #12200 and #11174. Both range-diff entries are unchanged; no manual conflict resolution or extra feature work was added. Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml and deny.toml match this master, including pulldown-cmark 0.13.6. The own scope remains 5 files.

The enrollment source, gateway manifest, locale loader and enrollment client are byte-identical to the previous head. The new master catalog keys are retained alongside the single enrollment error key, with no duplicate message keys. Focused rustfmt and whitespace checks pass. The callbacks, cookie parsing, consume-before-refusal and original-TTL capacity retry were traced again. Local Rust execution remains unavailable under Windows Application Control; the current-head upstream compilation and test results are recorded below. Earlier mock-provider/browser evidence remains historical and is not live-provider or combined dashboard evidence.

Two adversarial self-review passes and a final source review found no new supported defect. These are not independent Core approvals. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125581473661) passes on this exact head, including Security, Lint and Test. The [Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125571496498) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four browser-binding regressions. Parallel Runtime Test also passes. No new private workflow or live-provider run was used.

### Earlier Fluent follow-up — 2026-11-02

Earlier head: `1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a`. Both new enrollment-start errors now use `get_required_cli_string("cli-oidc-browser-start-failed")`. The canonical English catalog keeps the exact existing text, `could not start sign-in`. Other locales inherit that English fallback until translated. This uses the existing runtime locale; it does not add per-request language negotiation.

Local `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs` and `git diff --check` pass. An exact inverse source comparison confirms that only the import, these two lookups and one English catalog entry changed. Status 500, the generic JSON error shape and early-return behavior remain. I traced the existing helper, catalog fallback and immediate JSON serialization; this was source validation, not a fresh gateway execution.

Historical CI on 1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a failed Security on inherited pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0433), with the aggregate gate also red. The merged #12200 repair is now inherited by the current head above. Historical results do not replace new-head checks.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical evidence: a bounded Ubuntu 24.04 job applied the exact patch to base `1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29`, checked all four source hashes, and ran Rust 1.98.0 tests, strict Clippy and the native browser fixture. Fresh upstream CI on the rebased head is recorded below. Independent Core/CODEOWNER security approvals remain required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The native browser check uses production enrollment routes, prefix and security headers over loopback HTTP, with a mock IdP. It is not the complete daemon, native TLS, dashboard popup integration, or real-provider acceptance. HTTPS cookie attributes and rejection of an unprefixed cookie have router assertions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
git diff --check
exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_oidc::tests:: -- --nocapture
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.95s
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0

# Temporary guard removal; require the selected regression to fail:
enrollment_binding_refuses_other_browsers_before_exchange_and_consumes_the_flow ... FAILED
left: 200
right: 400
# Exact bytes restored; repeat the OIDC suite:
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.89s

# Native browser fixture, then exact restoration and final suite:
5 browser assertions passed; same browser, isolated context, consumed replay and concurrent tabs
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 6.96s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes checked missing/wrong/duplicate cookies, consume-before-refusal, cookie-only API denial, concurrent flows, provider changes, issuer checks, original TTL and capacity retry. Source and dependency hashes were checked again. Both changed Markdown files passed pinned lint. No added documentation links need a new link target check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the existing success and refusal pages after the changed browser interaction; no layout redesign.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Historical source head `759ae4a5f1e4dffaa5d995503b222fc863e863d8`, exact four-file patch hash `945c228cff4dd8bf0a046630f7df1a22d3a14b34e6981eb64290d1e3fc9d55a9`; native Chrome `Chrome/156.0.8078.47`, Ubuntu 24.04, gateway `localhost`, mock IdP `127.0.0.1`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Same-browser success](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-same-context.png), [other-browser refusal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-other-context.png), and [machine receipt](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/receipt.json). All data is synthetic.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Follow the mock IdP page's link back to the prefixed callback: success with one exchange. Open a copied callback in another browser context: refusal with zero extra exchanges. Replay in the original context: refusal. Complete two fresh tab flows: both succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Windows Rust execution was blocked by Application Control, so this source was validated on Linux. No full workspace suite or live IdP run is claimed. The first Linux attempt passed the Rust checks but failed because the mock page had a plain-text MIME type. That fixture was corrected; the complete successful run above uses the corrected harness. No browser assertion was relaxed.

### Earlier rebase and dashboard integration — 2026-11-02

Earlier rebased head: `4ef9abef542eb90153587669f2650cefc1abcb1d`. This is a true rebase onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, which includes #12129. All four enrollment files and the exact patch are byte-for-byte unchanged from the historical tested revision above; range-diff reports the same single commit. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125043937233) passes, including Security, Lint and Test. The [hosted Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125040616464) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four new browser-binding regressions. Its checkout `0b80216b67e102089eebff5e2f6b7ff598a1e2bb` was verified to include this exact head. The earlier browser captures retain their named revision; no new native-TLS or real-provider acceptance run is claimed.

I also compared #11965 at `13486a064d2be1c05086e4ceaf6b08e94f2bc8b5`. At that historical snapshot, its delayed-start browser-family finding was open. It is now repaired at 02314854b32eb45a55d9d9c004f0bd73bb7b51e8, as recorded in [the repair review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11965#pullrequestreview-5731811340). That dashboard repair is separate from this per-flow enrollment binding. The branches overlap in `api_oidc.rs`; integration must keep one canonical binding in `PendingPkce`, checked before either exchange mode, with shared cookie parsing/cleanup and the original retry deadline. Preserve the dashboard's required ID token, provider pin, return/popup behavior and separate session-family/sign-out repair. Binding cleanup must coexist with the dashboard session cookie. This PR does not contain or validate that combined integration.

@IftekharUddin's [dependency and native-TLS proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12157#issuecomment-6553383007) remains useful, separately attributed candidate evidence. The dependency repair is now inherited from master; no proposal commit was cherry-picked and no contributor source was replaced.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the existing discovery and token endpoints remain the only provider calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A new per-flow secret is sent only in an HttpOnly binding cookie; its hash is stored with the pending flow and compared in constant time. Cookies use SameSite=Lax and root Path with no Domain; HTTPS adds Secure and the __Host- prefix. A terminal consumed-flow response clears its cookie. The recorded transport scope preserves the cookie attributes chosen at issuance. A valid 503 retry keeps its original expiry. Remote deployments should use HTTPS; plain HTTP does not isolate applications on different ports of the same host.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for callers that complete an enrollment callback without the starting browser's cookie; this is the intentional security correction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Finish enrollment in the same browser that starts it and permit its cookie. If a callback was copied, the gateway restarted, or the cookie expired/was blocked, start a new login. Existing bearer clients and the device flow require no migration. The new field creates the browser-binding fact in the existing pending-flow store; it does not copy live policy.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the resulting squash commit through a reviewed PR, then restart the gateway. This restores the login-CSRF exposure, so use only as an incident response with an explicit exposure decision.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Device flow is the alternative if browser cookies cannot be used.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A fresh same-browser login reaches `Sign-in not completed`; investigate cookie blocking, scheme/host changes and callback provenance. Do not log cookie secrets or token-bearing callback URLs.

The refreshed head now passes its required upstream CI; earlier results remain attached to their named revisions. This remains open for independent Core/CODEOWNER security review, with Jordan for the manifest and Audacity for the gateway and documentation. I have not approved my own change. After adoption, #11965 should use one binding fact in `PendingPkce` for both modes while preserving its dashboard-specific return, popup and ID-token behavior.

prs.title: fix(security): enforce cron approval and authority at the write across RPC, tools and token revocation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Merged with master 50e01f55e4, which includes #12232. Head c3d12f2026.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The approval fix.** `cron/add` passed `approved = true` ("RPC calls are pre-approved") into `add_shell_job_with_approval`. That skipped the supervised-autonomy gate that the CLI (`cron::add_shell_job`) and the gateway (`POST /api/cron`, `approved = false`) both apply. An RPC request is not an operator approval, so `cron/add` now passes `false`. `cron/patch` validated a replacement command with `approved = true` for the same reason, and now also passes `false`. Two regression tests show that a medium-risk command is refused by `cron/add` and `cron/patch` and never stored, and that a low-risk command still succeeds. The test command is `touch`: allowlisted, but medium-risk under a supervised profile with `require_approval_for_medium_risk`.
  - **Authority is rechecked at the write.** The cron store writes synchronously and can wait out SQLite's five-second busy timeout, so a revocation published during that wait used to be ignored. After the agent selector passes:
    - `cron/add` takes the agent lifecycle reservation first, then the config writer gate (`lock_config_writer()`, the mutex every config commit takes), and rechecks the caller against the current policy. This is the order `config/set` uses. It holds both through the insert, so neither a lifecycle delete or rename of the alias nor a grant publication can land between the recheck and the row.
    - `cron/patch` takes the writer gate, rechecks the caller, and runs #12232's agent-job check (`authorize_cron_agent_execution`) under it. It then runs #12232's checks of the row and the caller's authority under the store's writer, and validates a replacement command there without an approval. The gate is held through the store's writer wait, so a grant change published meanwhile waits behind the patch. If the store stays busy, the patch gives up with nothing written and the change publishes after it.
  - **Wrappers no longer carry approval.** The runtime writes a tool's `approved` argument only on the call it dispatched, under that call's own name. A `pipeline` step and a skill alias each call their child tool directly, and the model supplied that child's `approved: true`. Both wrappers now clear `approved` on a child that takes runtime approval, so a nested medium-risk command meets the supervised gate. The list of such tools moved to `zeroclaw_api::tool::takes_runtime_approval`, so the runtime's own sanitizer and the wrappers share it.
  - **Token revocation is ordered against these writes.** The gateway's device revoke, token rotation, admin single-device revoke and revoke-all used to remove the token from the live set first. They took the config write lock only to persist, so a cron write that had checked the token could commit after the token was gone. They now go through `PairingGuard::revoke_under_config_write_lock`, passing `begin_config_commit()`. Nothing changes until that commit holds the writer mutex. Under it, one synchronous closure removes the device row (or clears the registry) and the live token together, and the token set is then persisted under the same commit. As a result:
    - a write that checked the token first commits before the revocation lands, and one that checks after sees the token gone;
    - a request dropped while it waits has changed nothing and can be retried, and a commit refused because the daemon generation is closing changes nothing at all (503);
    - the boundary rechecks the requesting caller under the lock, before deleting anything, so a device revoked while its own request was queued is refused;
    - rotation keeps the commit until its new pairing code is issued.

    The three per-device paths share `revoke_device_credential`.
  - **Docs.** `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md` describes the approval rule for RPC cron writes, the recheck at the write, and wrappers never carrying an approval.
- **What #12232 now covers:**
  - This PR used to mark `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_run`, `schedule` and `send_message_to_peer` as tools a principal-bound session must not keep. It also refused agent-job patch and trigger to every principal but the shared operator.
  - #12232 marks the same tools and withholds them from every non-admin principal, through one posture function for prompts, rehydration and steering. It also refuses non-admin agent-job patch and trigger.
  - This PR now keeps #12232's rule: administrators keep the tools, and a non-admin with wildcard tools and agents keeps a bound `delegate`.
  - Dropped here: the markers, the shared-operator posture, the steering rule and their tests. The `cron_update` and peer-agent tests stay, worded for non-admin principals.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Scheduled and manual execution are unchanged; they already re-validate with `approved = false`.
  - Agent-job support in `cron/add` is unchanged.
  - The gateway's cron routes and the CLI are unchanged; only the gateway's token revocation paths change.
  - **Not changed here, and needs a design decision:** a job keeps running after whoever installed it loses their grants. Two cases remain: shell jobs a non-admin adds through RPC `cron/add` with its cron grant, and jobs installed before this change. Closing it means storing the submitter's authority with the job and re-resolving it on every run. That is the cron site of the authority-recheck work, not a guard this PR can add.
- **Blast radius:**
  - RPC clients (zerocode/TUI, and a future external gateway) that add or patch shell cron jobs.
  - Under `autonomy = supervised`, a medium-risk (when `require_approval_for_medium_risk`) or high-risk command is now refused at creation with `requires explicit approval`, instead of being stored.
  - Full-autonomy profiles are unaffected.
  - `cron/add` and `cron/patch` now queue on the config writer gate, as config writes and `session/new` already do. The store write runs while the gate is held, so a busy `jobs.db` delays config publications and revocations for up to the busy timeout.
  - Under supervised autonomy, a medium- or high-risk command inside a `pipeline` step or a skill alias is refused unless it is called directly, where the runtime's approval applies.
  - Gateway device revoke, rotation and revoke-all wait for any in-flight config write before deleting the device or removing the token. A request dropped while it waits leaves both in place. A device revoke or rotation whose caller was revoked while it waited is refused with 401 and changes nothing.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12260. Related #12232, #7432, #12046, #11225, #11176, #11182, #11286.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `agent`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tool`, `tool:cron`, `security:pairing`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `release:v0.9.0`.

### What this does, simply

A cron job scheduled over the RPC socket (zerocode/TUI) was treated as though a human had already approved its shell command. The CLI and the web dashboard both ask for approval under supervised autonomy. With this change the RPC path follows the same rule.

Related gaps are also closed:
- A permission removed, or a device revoked, while a cron write was waiting on the database now stops that write or waits for it to finish.
- A tool run inside a `pipeline` or a skill alias can no longer claim an approval nobody gave.

In practice the old behavior did not let the command *run*: every scheduled run re-checks the command without approval and refuses it. What it did was store a job the policy would not accept, which then failed on every tick. After this change the job is refused up front with the policy reason.

### Present in v0.8.5?

Partly.
- `git show v0.8.5:crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs` has the same `true, // RPC calls are pre-approved` in `handle_cron_add` (line 3143). It was introduced in #6848.
- v0.8.5 has no command validation in `handle_cron_patch` (no `validate_shell_command` call), so the patch half is master-only.

Because execution re-validates with `approved = false` in both v0.8.5 and master (`cron/scheduler.rs`, `execute_and_persist_job`), I do not think this alone justifies a v0.8.5 security patch. It is an approval-gate inconsistency that stores unrunnable jobs; it does not bypass execution.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The RPC tests drive the real handlers or `process_line`, and the tool tests go through the production tool dispatch. The revocation and lock-order tests use deterministic pauses rather than sleeps: they hold a competing SQLite writer or the config writer gate, and poll the waiting future once, before the change they race.

### How I tested

- **Tested revision:** the head's tree, 6d31e4bca4. Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0, with CI's own commands from `ci.yml` at master 50e01f55e4.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the lib tests of every changed crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```
# tree 6d31e4bca4 (head c3d12f2026, merging master 50e01f55e4); Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0
$ cargo fetch --locked                                  # exit 0
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                            # exit 0
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh && bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh   # exit 0
$ git diff --check 50e01f55e4 HEAD                      # no output
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets   # exit 0
$ bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace --summary-title "Lint diagnostics" \
    --log-name cargo-clippy.log                         # exit 0 (workspace, --all-targets, --features ci-all)
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway \
    -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings   # exit 0
$ cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
     Summary 20107 tests run: 20101 passed, 6 failed, 43 skipped
# the 6 are outside this change; see "skipped" below
$ cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools \
    -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --features tools-compat \
    --lib --test integration -E 'not binary(integration) or test(/^report_template_tool_test::/)'
     Summary 13367 tests run: 13367 passed, 169 skipped
$ cargo deny check                                      # cargo-deny 0.19.9, fresh advisory DB
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
$ cargo audit                                           # cargo-audit 0.22.2: exit 0, 8 allowed warnings

# this branch's tests, with #12232's agent-job and delegate tests that it touches;
# three runs in a row, every run:
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::dispatch::tests::cron_ \
    rpc::dispatch::tests::a_token_revocation rpc::dispatch::tests::a_cron_write_queued \
    rpc::dispatch::tests::constrained_session_cannot rpc::dispatch::tests::a_non_admin_principal \
    rpc::dispatch::tests::principal_headless:: rpc::dispatch::tests::principal_delegation_bounded \
    tools::cron_update tools::skill_tool
test result: ok. 84 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- api::tests::device_ api::tests::revoke \
    api::tests::rotate api::tests::a_device_request tests::admin_paircode
test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- pipeline
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- pairing
test result: ok. 109 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Revert checks on that tree:** each change below touches one functional line, or moves one line. The named tests fail, and the branch's other tests in that crate pass.

  - `cron/add` back to `approved = true`: `cron_add_does_not_pre_approve_a_medium_risk_shell_job`.
  - `cron/patch` validation back to `true`: `cron_patch_does_not_pre_approve_a_medium_risk_command`.
  - The write-time recheck reads the connection's stamped grants instead of current authority:
    - fails `cron_add_revoked_while_queued_is_refused`, `a_cron_write_queued_behind_a_token_revocation_is_refused`, `a_token_revocation_waits_for_a_cron_write_blocked_on_a_busy_store` and `cron_add_holds_the_publication_lock_while_the_store_is_busy`;
    - `cron/patch`'s revocation test still passes, because the check under the store's writer refuses that patch too.
  - `cron/patch` skips the agent-job check under the gate: `cron_patch_refuses_an_agent_job_change_before_waiting_on_the_store`.
  - `cron/patch` releases the gate before the store write: `cron_patch_rechecks_authority_and_row_after_sqlite_writer_wait`.
  - `cron/add` releases the gate before the insert: `cron_add_holds_the_publication_lock_while_the_store_is_busy`, `a_token_revocation_waits_for_a_cron_write_blocked_on_a_busy_store` and `cron_add_reserves_the_alias_before_the_writer_gate_and_holds_both_through_the_insert`.
  - `cron/add` takes the gate before the reservation, or releases the reservation before the insert: `cron_add_reserves_the_alias_before_the_writer_gate_and_holds_both_through_the_insert`.
  - **Wrapper approval clears:**
    - either pipeline clear removed (sequential or parallel): `steps_never_carry_approval_to_tools_that_take_runtime_approval`;
    - the skill-alias clear removed: `skill_builtin_tool_never_forwards_approval_to_its_target`.
  - The revocation runs before the gate is held: `device_revoke_and_rotate_remove_the_live_token_only_under_the_config_write_lock`, `device_revoke_and_rotate_dropped_while_waiting_can_be_retried`, `admin_paircode_rotate_dropped_while_waiting_can_be_retried` and `a_device_request_queued_behind_its_callers_revocation_is_refused`.
  - The caller's recheck under the gate ignored: `a_device_request_queued_behind_its_callers_revocation_is_refused`.
  - **Not pinned by any test:** a rotation keeping the commit until its new pairing code is issued. Dropping it right after the persist fails nothing.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Scheduled runs (`execute_and_persist_job`) and `cron/trigger` (`run_manual_job_with_selection`) already validate with `approved = false`, so no execution path changes.
  - In the daemon, the RPC context and the gateway admit config commits through the same live-config authority, whose writer mutex is the process-wide `shared_config_write_lock()`. A gateway revocation holding a commit is therefore ordered against an RPC cron write holding `lock_config_writer()`.
  - **Lock order:** the cron handlers take the config writer gate first, then the store's writer, and no production path takes them the other way round.
    - Every cron store write is a synchronous SQLite call. The only callback inside it, `cron/patch`'s recheck, takes the config read lock and the authority lease, never the writer gate.
    - The config commit's publish does not touch the cron store.
  - The gateway's `reauthorize` closures (`require_auth`, `require_gateway_admin_token`) are synchronous and take no config lock, so rechecking under the commit cannot deadlock.
  - I did not run a live daemon.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Nothing was skipped. My test machine has no `mold`, `clang` or `expect` and runs Node 18, so CI's linker settings were left out, and six workspace tests failed for reasons outside this change:
  - four `zerorelay` front-door page tests need Node's global `crypto` (Node 19 and later), and `daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` needs `expect`. These five fail the same way on master 50e01f55e4 on the same machine, every run.
  - `zeroclaw-infra`'s `concurrent_first_openers_of_a_fresh_store_all_succeed` hit `database is locked` once under the full parallel run, then passed 3/3 alone on the head and 4/4 on master.

  None of these crates is touched here, and master's own CI Test job passed all six at 50e01f55e4.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. This narrows them.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Paired-token revocation (device revoke, rotation, admin revoke and revoke-all) now waits for the config writer gate and removes the device row and the live token in one step under it. What a revocation removes is unchanged; only its ordering against in-flight writes changes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - The revocation change only orders an existing removal against in-flight cron writes. A request dropped or refused before it holds the gate changes nothing.
  - The rest tightens an approval gate to match the CLI and gateway, rechecks authority at the cron write, and removes a model-controlled approval path through wrappers.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for full-autonomy and low-risk commands. The following changes:
  - Under supervised autonomy, RPC `cron/add` and `cron/patch` now refuse medium- and high-risk commands that were previously stored and then failed at run time.
  - Wrappers no longer pass `approved` to a child.
  - A device request whose caller was revoked while it waited is refused.
- **Jobs already stored:** there is no migration.
  - Under supervised autonomy, a medium- or high-risk shell job added over RPC before this change is still in the store and keeps failing on every tick with `requires explicit approval`.
  - `cron list` and the run history show which ones. Remove or patch them, or approve a `cron_run` call for one.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. `zeroclaw_api::tool` gains `takes_runtime_approval` and `clear_runtime_approval`, and `PairingGuard` gains `revoke_under_config_write_lock` and `revoke_token_hash_ordered`; nothing existing is removed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - RPC `cron/add` returns `Cron add failed: blocked by security policy: Command requires explicit approval` for a command a client expects to schedule.
  - A nested medium-risk command in a pipeline or skill alias fails with `requires explicit approval`.
  - A device revoke or rotation during a daemon reload returns 503 with `Revocation refused without any change`.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(tools): per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search
prs.body:
## Summary

### What this does, simply

Each agent can only list, read, and write its own conversations, and only search the Discord archive rows its own Discord bots recorded. Which conversations are "its own" comes from trusted facts (who the runtime is, which channels the live config assigns to it, and what the storage layer recorded when the conversation was created), never from what the model asks for. Conversations recorded before this release had no owner stamp; the one agent that could have written them adopts them on the next message, and an install with several agents is told how to assign them instead of losing messages.

- **Base branch:** `master`; this head includes `master` through `3c18211b9f` (#11811).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Binds `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send`, and `discord_search` to trusted per-agent ownership. Ownership is checked inside the storage critical section of each read and write, so a check/use race cannot admit a foreign session, and Discord namespace predicates run inside SQLite before ranking and limits.
  - Routing a message to an agent is not permission to take over a transcript. The inbound path *claims* a session: an absent key is created, an explicitly or channel-owned key is admitted only for its owner, and a foreign key refuses the turn before any hydration or append.
  - Authority is resolved at effect time, not captured ahead of storage. `ChannelAuthority` and `NamespaceAuthority` are callbacks the backend invokes after acquiring its connection or mutation guard; the policy read guard is held through the read or commit, so a channel reassigned or an agent disabled during a wait stops being admitted on the same turn.
  - Transcripts written before ownership attribution existed (master stamped nothing on the channel path, so every existing channel conversation is one) are handled by the claim itself. The live policy reader hands the backend a `SessionClaimGrant`: the channels the agent owns plus `adopt_unattributed`, which is true only when the caller is the sole enabled agent (`Config::is_sole_enabled_agent`, the same rule the Discord archive already applied to legacy rows). A sole agent adopts such a transcript and continues the conversation with its history. With several enabled agents the claim refuses, nothing is read or written, and the refusal is logged as `session_owner_unattributed` with the enabled-agent count and the operator remedy. The adoption bit never widens an explicit agent or a channel the caller does not own.
  - Makes typed live config the single agent/channel ownership source. Disabled aliases grant nothing; ambiguous duplicate enabled owners fail closed. The alias view is a typed walk of the channel maps (`map_alias_entries()` from the `Configurable` derive), so resolving ownership never serializes config on a caller's stack.
  - Preserves trusted session attribution across SQLite and JSONL restart, migration, retention, purge, and empty-transcript cases. Startup hydration touches only channel-marked sessions, so gateway and RPC sessions keep their owners.
  - Enforces Discord alias/channel provenance on search and on every archive write; a row already claimed by another alias or channel is never moved.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change `sessions_current`, `send_via`, peer-group semantics, the knowledge graph, or dormant session-tool registration. It adds no CLI; the explicit adoption step for multi-agent installs is a documented manual edit until a migration command lands (see Compatibility and Merge order).
- **Blast radius:** Per-agent tool registration, channel routing/collection, both session backends and hygiene, Discord archive/search/mutation paths, SQLite memory mutations, the `Configurable` derive's generated surface, and affected Fluent tool descriptions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #9646. Related #9647. Related #8290.

The authorization inputs remain trusted runtime/config identity plus persisted provenance. Model-supplied session IDs and Discord channel IDs are selectors, never grants. A single-agent install, legacy or not, stays deterministic: it owns everything it wrote before and after the upgrade. Duplicate enabled owners are configuration ambiguity and are rejected.

### Review history on this head

- @JordanTheJet's 2026-09-30 blockers (F1 foreign claim of a channel-owned legacy transcript, F3 disabled caller inheriting the legacy Discord archive, F5 grants resolved before storage admission) were fixed in `040046750`, `344b610be`, `a6557147a`, and `0119cfe64` (now `e593ce5b7a`, `27063a7749`, `ba0d69c848`, and `5677f53b3e` after the history rewrite below); @tidux confirmed each on 2026-10-01.
- @tidux's 2026-10-01 blocker (pre-upgrade transcripts without attribution permanently drop their next inbound message) is fixed by the legacy adoption described above, with upgrade regressions on both backends.
- @tidux's `try_read` contention warning no longer applies after the master merge: the live config is now a `LiveConfigHandle` whose publish path holds its write lock only for the pair install and never across storage, so the authority callbacks take a short blocking `read()` instead of dropping the turn when a writer is queued. There is no longer an "authority unavailable" path on the inbound claim.
- The `.gitignore` entry @tidux flagged has been removed from this branch's diff.
- History was force-pushed once on 2026-10-23 to replace the merge commit `a6744b2b56`, which was authored as Claude with an attribution trailer and a session URL (AGENTS.md working rule 9), with the tree-identical `679755cf88` under my identity. Every descendant was re-created with its tree, message, author, and dates unchanged and only its parent re-pointed, so every SHA from that merge on moved; `git diff 6f0fdccc3b d1d9d03d27` is empty. The reviewed head `0119cfe64f` is now `5677f53b3e`, and the three commits on top are `9cc1a14780` (drift-only master merge), `fbbac6880e` (the fix), and `d1d9d03d27` (`.gitignore` chore).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; the deterministic regressions exercise the security, retention, and upgrade boundaries without credentials.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` tool registration and `channel` persistence/search.
- **Setup / preconditions:** None for automated tests. A manual Discord A/B needs two neutral agents with distinct enabled, archive-enabled Discord aliases that both watch one channel. A manual upgrade check needs a `data/sessions` directory written by a pre-ownership release (any channel transcript without `agent_alias`).
- **Steps to run:** Run the session ownership, retention, and upgrade tests. For the upgrade path by hand: start a build of this branch with one enabled agent over an old sessions directory and send a message on an existing conversation (the reply uses the old history and `agent_alias` is now set); then enable a second agent and send a message on a different old conversation (no reply, one `session_owner_unattributed` error with the remedy, transcript unchanged). For Discord: let the first alias archive a message and a reaction from the shared channel, let the second alias observe the same two events, and run scoped `discord_search` as each agent.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign sessions and Discord rows remain inaccessible; a sole enabled agent continues pre-upgrade conversations and adopts them; a multi-agent install refuses them with a logged remedy instead of silently dropping them; the owned Discord row stays in the first alias's namespace; archived JSONL sessions cannot reappear through metadata; ambiguous duplicate channel owners expose no scoped grant.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Session tools and the shared Discord archive lacked a complete per-agent boundary, JSONL ownership metadata could outlive retention, and the second observer's archive write took over the first alias's row.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted CI covers the repository matrix (strict lint, workspace tests, Landlock, security, supported targets, MSRV, and the parallel runtime/channel gate). The previous head `0119cfe64f` had `CI Required Gate` green but was reviewed as 7 commits behind master and later became CONFLICTING; this head merges current master (`3c18211b9f`) so the PR runs against the base it would land on. Hosted CI on this head: `Quality Gate` run [40047833401](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40047833401) started on the push of `640f1c3c47` and was in progress when this body was written. The previous run 40042714043 on `d1d9d03d27` failed on two things: master's `every_inventoried_tool_registers_under_a_maximal_config` (the maximal config inserted its archiving Discord alias with `enabled` off, so under the ownership-gated registration the sole agent owned nothing and `discord_search` never registered; fixed in `640f1c3c47` by enabling the alias), and the `Security` job, which is the repo-wide RUSTSEC-2026-0385/0386 advisory affecting every PR until the dependency bump lands on master. GitHub reports the PR as mergeable again. The four commits on top of `5677f53b3e` (formerly `0119cfe64f`) are the drift-only master merge `9cc1a14780` (checked standalone: `cargo check --locked` on the five touched crates with all targets, 0 errors, 0 warnings), the fix `fbbac6880e`, `d1d9d03d27`, which drops the `.gitignore` patterns, and the test fix `640f1c3c47`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live two-bot Discord deployment and no real pre-upgrade data directory; both are covered deterministically (the upgrade regressions seed exactly what master writes: a SQLite metadata row with NULL agent and channel, and a JSONL transcript with no sidecar). `cargo fluent check` and `cargo deny` were not run locally.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 macOS, `rustc 1.97.1`, at `d1d9d03d27` (tree-identical to the pre-rewrite `6f0fdccc3b` the commands ran on) plus the inventory test re-run at `640f1c3c47`, dedicated target dir, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`):

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all --check
    -> clean

  cargo check -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime \
      -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets
    -> Finished `dev` profile; 0 errors, 0 warnings

  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime \
      -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings
    -> Finished `dev` profile in 2m 04s; 0 errors, 0 warnings

  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    -> Finished `dev` profile in 2m 03s (cold target dir); 0 errors, 0 warnings

  RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> Finished `dev` profile in 1m 37s (cold target dir)

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
    -> test result: ok. 330 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- is_sole_enabled_agent channel_refs_owned_by_agent
    -> test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 1821 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib
    -> test result: FAILED. 1376 passed; 10 failed; 3 ignored
       The 9 content_search::tests failures are this machine's broken Homebrew ripgrep
       (dyld: libpcre2-8.0.dylib not loaded) and are unrelated to this diff.
       sessions::tests::send_tool_name_and_schema failed on a duplicated Fluent key the
       automatic merge had produced; the merge commit resolves the catalogue and the
       module passes:
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- sessions::
    -> test result: ok. 81 passed; 0 failed; 1308 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- \
      tools::tests::retained_session_and_archive_tools_follow_live_channel_reassignment \
      tools::tests::session_tools tools::tests::discord
    -> test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 5829 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- \
      tools::tests::every_inventoried_tool_registers_under_a_maximal_config \
      tools::tests::discord_search_registers_only_for_agent_owning_archiving_alias \
      tools::tests::retained_session_and_archive_tools_follow_live_channel_reassignment
    -> test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 5829 filtered out (at the test-fix commit)

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- orchestrator::tests::upgrade_keeps_legacy \
      orchestrator::tests::inbound_legacy_collision orchestrator::tests::existing_unattributed \
      orchestrator::tests::a_routed_agent_cannot orchestrator::tests::stamp_session_routing \
      orchestrator::tests::restart_hydration orchestrator::tests::passive_context
    -> test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 2018 filtered out

  python3 scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.py <NUL list of changed .rs files>
    -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```
