  ```text
      DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/architecture/runtime-state-and-persistence.md \
      bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
    -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files. Summary: 0 error(s)

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> Collected 0 added link(s) from 4 docs file(s).
  ```

  Focused regressions for the reviewed findings:

  ```text
  zeroclaw-infra    session_backend::tests::claim_decision_adopts_unattributed_only_with_the_grant
  zeroclaw-infra    session_sqlite::tests::claim_adopts_master_shaped_unattributed_row_only_for_the_sole_agent
  zeroclaw-infra    session_store::tests::claim_adopts_sidecar_less_transcript_only_for_the_sole_agent
  zeroclaw-channels orchestrator::tests::upgrade_keeps_legacy_unattributed_conversations_for_the_sole_enabled_agent
    -> new this revision. The backend tests seed exactly what master writes (a `(NULL, NULL)`
       session_metadata row; a `.jsonl` with no sidecar). The orchestrator test drives
       `process_channel_message` on both backends: the sole agent answers with the legacy
       history and the row gains `agent_alias`; a disabled second agent changes nothing; two
       enabled agents refuse both the live and the passive turn, append nothing, and log
       `session_owner_unattributed` with the remedy; a disabled caller never adopts.
       Mutation check: with the adoption arm of `decide_session_claim` removed (the previous
       head's behaviour), all four fail: the three backend tests on `Foreign(Unattributed)`
       where `Claimed` is expected, and the orchestrator test on the sole agent's turn never
       reaching the model (0 provider calls, 1 expected).
  zeroclaw-config   schema::tests::is_sole_enabled_agent_requires_exactly_one_enabled_agent_that_is_the_caller
    -> new this revision
  zeroclaw-channels orchestrator::tests::inbound_legacy_collision_preserves_owner_before_model_and_passive_append
  zeroclaw-channels orchestrator::tests::existing_unattributed_channel_session_refuses_claim_without_mutation
  zeroclaw-runtime  tools::tests::retained_session_and_archive_tools_follow_live_channel_reassignment
    -> unchanged in intent; the first and third now publish config revisions through
       `LiveConfig` instead of writing through a lock, and all three still pass
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Re-read every ownership predicate at its storage linearization point after the master merge, including the three `try_read` sites that became blocking handle reads. Confirmed that `LiveConfig::publish` holds its lock only for the pair install (the deadlock the `try_read` guarded against needs a writer that holds the config lock while waiting on storage, which the handle's publish path cannot do). Confirmed `Config::is_sole_enabled_agent` returns the same answer as the inline count it replaces in the Discord archive grant, including for an empty agent map. I did not exercise a real Discord account or a real pre-upgrade install.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; no rendered interface changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./dev/ci.sh all`, `cargo fluent check`, and live Discord were not run locally. The changed Fluent catalogues are unchanged since the previously green exact-head run, and the remaining external gap would require credentials.

**Historical evidence (previous heads).** Exact-head `CI Required Gate` was green at `0119cfe64f` (run on 2026-09-30) and at `c1c14d91f9` (run 34549879212). Exact-head [run 34189025680](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34189025680) covered `6cef56af45` and exact-head [Quality Gate run 33805478225](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/33805478225) was fully green at `a6744b2b56`. None of those runs covers the master merge or the legacy adoption on the current head. Those SHAs predate the 2026-10-23 history rewrite; their trees are unchanged under the new SHAs listed in Review history.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; access is narrowed. The only widening is the legacy adoption, and it is available to exactly one principal: the single enabled agent of a single-agent install, for transcripts that agent is the only possible author of.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**; the channel alias view no longer serializes any config section at all, so the transient copy it used to make of decrypted channel values is gone.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Static tool descriptions are model-visible Fluent strings. The ownership denial messages (`denial_message` in `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/sessions.rs`) are `format!` literals, following master's existing tool-error convention; the earlier claim that Fluent owns them was wrong. Denials name the owning agent or channel, matching the shipped reset/delete tools. Authorization comes only from trusted runtime identity, live config, and persisted provenance, never model arguments. The new `session_owner_unattributed` log line and its remedy are operator-facing log text, not model-visible.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; vulnerable cross-agent access and ambiguous ownership are intentionally denied.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`:
  - Existing attributed SQLite and JSONL sessions need no action.
  - **Pre-upgrade channel transcripts (no `agent_alias`, no `channel_id`; every channel conversation master wrote):** in an install with exactly one enabled agent, nothing to do; the agent adopts each conversation on its next inbound message and continues with the history. In an install with several enabled agents, those conversations are refused until attributed, and each refused message logs `session_owner_unattributed` with the remedy. To attribute one, with the daemon stopped: SQLite, `UPDATE session_metadata SET agent_alias = '<alias>' WHERE session_key = '<key>';` in `data/sessions/sessions.db`; JSONL, write `{"agent_alias": "<alias>"}` to the transcript's `.metadata.json` sidecar in `data/sessions/`. Archiving or deleting the transcript is the other option; the next message then starts a fresh, attributed conversation. The docs page `runtime-state-and-persistence.md` has the same steps under "Legacy session attribution".
  - Ambiguously owned data (two enabled agents bound to one channel) stays fail-closed; restore a unique enabled channel binding.
  - Scoped `sessions_send` no longer creates an unknown session key; establish the session through its owning runtime first. `sessions_list` and `discord_search` enforce the profile's `Read` operation, so restrictive profiles must permit it.
  - Where two enabled Discord aliases watch the same channel, the alias that archives an event first keeps the row and the later observer no longer replaces it.

## Merge order with the overlapping session-backend PRs (proposed)

Several open PRs add authority contracts to `SessionBackend`. Proposed order, so the backend ends up with one claim contract and one effect-time authority shape:

1. **This PR first.** It defines `SessionClaimGrant` / `SessionClaimAuthority` for the inbound claim and `ChannelAuthority` / `NamespaceAuthority` for effect-time reads and writes.
2. **#10412 (@REL-mame)** rebases its `claim_session_agent_alias` / `adopt_session_agent_alias` onto this PR's `SessionOwnerClaim` and `SessionClaimGrant`; its `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` adopt operation then becomes the command this PR's `session_owner_unattributed` remedy points operators at, replacing the manual edit above.
3. **#11230 (mine)** rebases onto this PR and updates its guard test to the `SessionsListTool::for_agent(backend, security, scope)` constructor; principal scoping and agent/channel scoping compose.
4. **#11234 (mine)** adopts the effect-time callback shape from this PR instead of a parallel `SessionEffectGuard` contract.
5. **#11301 (mine)** and **#10407 (@vrurg)** resolve their `session_sqlite.rs` (and, for #10407, `sessions.rs` / `tools/mod.rs`) textual overlaps at rebase; neither changes the ownership contract.

#11205 is closed. If maintainers prefer #10412's contract to land first, this PR will rebase onto it instead; the adoption rule and the regressions here transfer either way.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual PR landing commit from current `master`; no schema down-migration is required. Transcripts adopted by a sole agent keep their `agent_alias`, which the previous release ignores.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Disabling the affected channel/tool is the immediate containment option.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected ownership-denial errors, a missing scoped tool for a uniquely configured owner, empty owned Discord results, channel startup errors reporting ambiguous enabled owners, repeated `session_owner_unattributed` errors in a multi-agent install (expected until the legacy transcripts are attributed), or `discord archive row belongs to another alias or channel; not overwritten` debug events for rows an operator expects a given alias to own.

**Earlier validation head:** `640f1c3c47`

prs.title: fix(runtime): don't ask for approval of a tool call that can't run
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - In supervised mode, `prepare_tool_calls` ran the approval gate before anything checked that the call's tool exists. A made-up name, or a tool the session doesn't hold, got an approval prompt. Approving it ran nothing and answered `Unknown tool: <name>`, and an unanswered prompt held the turn until it timed out.
  - A call that would prompt is now looked up first, with the executor's own lookup (`resolve_dispatch_tool`: registry, activated tools, the turn's exclusions, and an active SOP step's scope, as sequential execution re-derives it per call).
    - A name that can't be dispatched gets the executor's own answer, `Unknown tool: <name>` or `Tool not available in this turn: <name>`, with the observer events execution records for it.
    - Nobody is asked to approve it.
    - Its hook context is abandoned once, and the ToolCall/ToolResult pair is emitted as for a denied call.
  - The executor's unknown-tool arm moves into `unknown_tool_outcome`, beside `unavailable_tool_outcome`, so both paths build the same answer. The caller in `turn/mod.rs` now passes the excluded tools it already holds.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Calls that wouldn't prompt keep today's path, so autonomous and auto-approved calls are unchanged.
  - Approval policy (`ApprovalManager`) is unchanged.
  - A call after a `tool_search` in the same batch keeps today's order. `tool_search` can activate a deferred tool before that call runs, so its name can be unknown at the gate and known at execution.
  - This changes existing preparation and execution code in `zeroclaw-runtime`. It adds no subsystem, config or retained state, so I don't think it needs an ADR-016 row.
- **Blast radius:** supervised approvals on every surface (CLI, channels, the dashboard and other RPC clients), and only for calls whose tool can't run.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12248

### What this does, simply

When an agent runs in supervised mode, each tool call waits for someone to approve it. The approval step came before the check that the tool exists in this session. When the model asked for a tool it doesn't have (an invented name, or one the user isn't allowed), the user still got an approval card. Approving it did nothing except return "Unknown tool", and ignoring it stalled the conversation until the card timed out. Now that call gets the "Unknown tool" answer straight away, with no card. Tools the session does have are approved exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the case depends on a model naming a tool it wasn't offered, which a live model doesn't do on demand. The RPC test below drives it with a scripted model through the same path the dashboard uses.

### How I tested

New tests:
- **`call_prep.rs`:** each test prepares the calls with a supervised manager, an approval channel that counts requests, hooks, and both event streams.
  - `a_prompted_call_for_an_unregistered_tool_is_answered_without_asking`:
    - no approval request is sent, and the answer is `Unknown tool: cron_list`;
    - the hook context is abandoned once, with no after hook;
    - the observer events equal what `execute_one_tool` records for the same call;
    - the stream carries one ToolCall/ToolResult pair.
  - `a_prompted_call_for_an_excluded_tool_is_answered_without_asking`: the same for `Tool not available in this turn: cron_list`.
  - `a_prompted_call_for_a_registered_tool_still_asks`: the control. The same call, once the turn holds the tool, is put to the operator.
  - `a_call_after_tool_search_in_the_same_batch_still_goes_through_the_gate`: in `[cron_list, tool_search, cron_list]`, the first call is answered at once and the third still goes to the gate.
- **`rpc/dispatch.rs`:** `a_supervised_principal_session_is_not_asked_to_approve_a_tool_it_does_not_hold`.
  - A non-administrator's supervised session with a scripted model asks for `cron_list`, which the session doesn't hold. The session can reach its client with an approval prompt (`ask_user` is selected).
  - No `approval_request` notification is sent, and the model's next request carries `Unknown tool: cron_list`.
  - Once #12232 lands, `cron_list` is also one of the tools a non-administrator's session never holds.
- **Existing approval tests:** the ones that passed an empty registry and expected prompts now register stub tools under the names they call. They are `approval_cancellation_abandons_retained_and_waiting_calls_once`, `approval_denied_call_is_abandoned`, `approval_replaced_call_is_abandoned` and `repeated_prompt_preparation_failure_abandons_retained_batch`. Their assertions are unchanged.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - `Test` runs the workspace suite, and `Test (opt-in tools)` covers the tool-feature build.
  - Lint covers fmt and clippy.
  - I also ran both test commands locally, below, because the point is to show nothing else depends on the old order.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none that I know of.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64, on `cf9cbd00ab`):

```text
cargo fetch --locked                                              exit 0
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                        exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
                                                                  exit 0, 0 warnings
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
  test result: ok. 6081 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  the 5 new tests, 3 runs each: 15/15 ok
  agent::turn::call_prep:: 15 passed; agent::tool_execution:: 38 passed
git diff --check 65f8eb3c92 HEAD                                  exit 0

# CI "Test (opt-in tools)" command, verbatim
cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --features tools-compat \
  --lib --test integration -E 'not binary(integration) or test(/^report_template_tool_test::/)'
  Summary [  42.814s] 13320 tests run: 13320 passed (1 leaky), 169 skipped

# CI "Test" command, plus --no-fail-fast
cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
  Summary [  56.150s] 20060 tests run: 20055 passed (2 leaky), 5 failed, 43 skipped
```

  The 5 failures come from my machine, not this change:
  - **`daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions`** panics with "expect must be installed for the PTY regression test". CI installs `expect`; my machine doesn't have it.
  - **Four `zerorelay` `frontdoor_assets` page tests** fail running the page script under the local node (v18.19.1). `zerorelay` doesn't depend on `zeroclaw-runtime`, the only crate this PR touches.
  - **CI's exact command** (fail-fast) stopped at the first of these, after 739 passes.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Revert check:** I changed only the condition of the new lookup to `if false` and rebuilt.
    - These fail:
      - `a_prompted_call_for_an_unregistered_tool_is_answered_without_asking` (1 approval request, not 0);
      - `a_prompted_call_for_an_excluded_tool_is_answered_without_asking` (the same);
      - `a_call_after_tool_search_in_the_same_batch_still_goes_through_the_gate` (the first call was denied by the operator instead of answered `Unknown tool`);
      - the RPC test, on the `approval_request` notification itself.
    - The control and the 10 existing approval and execution tests above still pass.
  - **Not verified:** a live dashboard or channel session with a real model; Windows and macOS.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The visible change is that an approval card no longer appears for a call that can't run, which the RPC test checks at the notification level.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cf9cbd00ab`; runtime turn preparation, plus the RPC `session/update` notifications.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** a supervised call to a tool the session doesn't hold sends no approval request, and the model gets `Unknown tool: <name>`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - The firmware protocol gate, the hardware-feature tests and the golden-frame replay weren't run locally; CI runs them, and this PR touches none of their crates.
  - CI's mold/clang linker settings weren't used locally.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The model now gets, without a prompt, the same `Unknown tool` / `Tool not available in this turn` text it got after an approval.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. A call that can't run never reaches the operator, and every call that can run still goes through the gate unchanged.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - A supervised call to a tool the session holds gets no approval prompt and answers `Unknown tool`. That would mean the lookup disagrees with execution.
  - A call after `tool_search` in the same batch fails as unknown.

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Rust XMPP with optional legacy OMEMO
prs.body:
## Summary

Base branch: `master`.

Implement feature-gated native Rust XMPP with optional Linux legacy OMEMO. Related #9814. Depends on #12015.

### What this does, simply

The native channel owns encrypted receipts independently of the socket. Reconnect reuses the exclusive store; completed runtime and control receipts can be recorded while offline. First-contact key publication explicitly requests readable public nodes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

Run the `xmpp` and `native_ingress_` channel-library filters with `--no-default-features --features channel-xmpp`; then run `crates/zeroclaw-channels/tests/xmpp_native/managed_server.py` using the documented disposable loopback-only fixture.

### How I tested

Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 47f16954424bcc3787379e5e1d2c21df52daf100, including every source-image build. The inherited master root-fixture packaging fix is confirmed across the current Dockerfile/Containerfile source matrix. Integrated validation passed 69 XMPP tests (4 separately marked ignored), 5 shared-ingress tests, all four real encrypted interoperability scenarios and strict channel/test and root binary Clippy. Fresh-account scenarios remove pre-created bot nodes and verify public key discovery without roster subscription. Offline receipt completion, explicit publication policy/refusal, live admission filtering, queue overflow and deferred authorized ping ordering are covered. Human changes-requested review has not been dismissed; re-review is requested.

Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

Native encrypted state stays protected by the existing vault and exclusive ownership. Uncertain admitted work remains unreleasable. Public device lists and bundles request open access; these contain public keys, while live peer allowlists and fingerprint pins still gate message admission. Server publication refusal fails explicitly. No private deployment information, real identities, credentials, or messages are included.

- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: Yes — the optional channel owns its private encrypted state and existing-vault access.
- New external network calls: Yes — configured XMPP service and bounded protocol exchanges.
- Secrets/credentials handling changed: Yes — native encrypted state and fingerprint-pinned sessions use the existing vault.
- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.
- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No — protocol content remains inside the existing shared dispatch/policy boundary.

## Compatibility (required)

Feature-gated XMPP; encrypted operation is Linux-only. Legacy OMEMO remains distinct from OMEMO v2. The existing migration and replay-protection boundaries remain documented. prs.title: fix(gateway/web): offer config pages only to accounts that can read config
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `GET /api/auth/session` now reports `features.config`: whether the signed-in account may read config. Until now the session said nothing about config, so the dashboard offered the config pages to every signed-in account. An account without a `config` grant opened them and got *Couldn't load sections: API 403: {"error":"Principal lacks the config grant required for this method"}*.
  - The flag comes from the config routes' own rule. `may_read_config` in `principal_gate.rs` applies the route layer's floor for a `GET` (`method_floor`) through the same check `config_route_auth` uses (now one helper, `clears_floor`), so the flag and the routes can't disagree. An administrator's grants permit everything (`ResolvedGrants::permits` short-circuits on `admin`), so the flag is true for them without a separate rule.
  - The web reads the flag. An absent or non-`true` value means no, and `pathAccess` allows `/config` and `/setup` only with it. The sidebar, the command palette and the route guard all filter through `pathAccess`, so all three stop offering the pages.
  - `homePathFor` sends an account with chat to `/agents`, one with config only to `/config`, and returns `null` for an account with neither. In that case the route guard shows the existing not-available page at `/` instead of redirecting.
  - The command palette now sends its config sections and entries through `pathAccess` too, not only its page destinations (`paletteItemsFor`). The config search caches what it loaded for the page's lifetime, so without this, results loaded while an account could read config stayed in the palette after the session stopped reporting config.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - What the gateway enforces doesn't change: the config routes refuse an account without the grant exactly as before.
  - No other feature flag changes, and nothing changes for a paired browser or an open gateway (full access, as before).
  - The flag reflects grants at session read time. A grant changed mid-session shows on the next session read, like the existing flags.
- **Blast radius:** the dashboard session response (one new boolean) and the web navigation rule. The config route layer's two floor checks now go through a shared helper with the same logic.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12249. Related #11965, which introduced `pathAccess`'s config rule.

### What this does, simply

When someone signs in to the dashboard with their organisation's identity provider, they only get what their permission profile grants. The dashboard asks the gateway what the account can do and hides what it can't. Config was the exception: the gateway never said whether the account could read config, so the dashboard always showed the config pages. Accounts without that permission saw the entries and got a red "API 403" error. Now the gateway says whether the account can read config, using the same rule it applies when the page loads, and the dashboard shows the config pages only when it can. The gateway still refuses config requests from accounts without the permission, as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a gateway with dashboard sign-in through an OIDC provider (`gateway.dashboard_sign_in.oidc`). In the provider's `profile_map`, map one group to a profile that grants something other than config (for example `grants = { memory = ["read"] }`) and another to a profile with `grants = { config = ["read"] }`.
- **Steps to run:** sign in as a member of the first group and open the dashboard. Open the sidebar and the command palette, then go to `/config` and `/` directly. Repeat with a member of the second group.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - First account: no config or agent-configuration entry in the sidebar or the palette. `/config` and `/` show "not available".
  - Second account: the config pages open, and `/` leads to `/config`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** both accounts see the config entries. For the first, each opens the red *API 403* error.

### How I tested

On a Linux x86_64 host, in an isolated `target/`, with tests in a private network namespace and a throwaway HOME. Run at head `f7584065d2`:

```text
cargo fetch --locked                                        ok, Cargo.lock unchanged
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  ok
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
                                                            ok, 0 diagnostics
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --no-fail-fast the_session_reports_config_access_as_the_config_routes_decide
                                                            1 passed (x3)
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --no-fail-fast
     Summary [  16.687s] 772 tests run: 772 passed, 0 skipped
cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
     Summary [  79.826s] 20056 tests run: 20055 passed (2 leaky), 1 failed, 43 skipped
        FAIL component::daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions
             "expect must be installed for the PTY regression test" (the host has no `expect`;
             CI's Test job installs it). The same test fails the same way on master 65f8eb3c92.
cargo nextest run ... --run-ignored only -E 'package(zeroclaw-gateway) & binary(golden_frames)'
     Summary [   0.233s] 7 tests run: 7 passed, 5 skipped
web: npm ci                                                 ok
cargo web check                                             ok (gen-api, tsc -b)
npm run test:auth                                           162 passed, 0 failed (13 files)
npm run test:navigation                                     9 passed, 0 failed
npm test                                                    110 passed, 0 failed
npm run test:permissions                                    32 passed, 0 failed
npm run test:contexts                                       95 passed, 0 failed
npm run test:sops                                           5 passed, 0 failed
npm run test:sop-editor                                     10 passed, 0 failed
npm run build                                               ok (built in 469ms)
```

The workspace run used a clean web tree, as CI's Test job does: no generated TS client, and a placeholder `web/dist`. It ran with the default linker; CI's uses clang with mold.

Revert checks, one line each, on this head:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `"config": true` in `handle_auth_session` | `dashboard_session::tests::the_session_reports_config_access_as_the_config_routes_decide` fails (the account with only a memory grant gets `true`) |
| `pathAccess` allows the config paths without `access.config` | 3 of 7 `navAccess.test.ts` tests fail: the chat-without-config account, the account with neither, and the missing-flags case |
| `parseOidcSession` reads an absent flag as allowed (`!== false`) | `authSession.test.ts` "parseOidcSession requires the credential fields and denies missing features" fails |
| The palette appends config results without `pathAccess` | `CommandPalette.access.test.ts` "config results loaded for a config reader drop out once the session loses config" fails (the cached `/config/providers` and `/config/agents/main` come back) |

With the changes restored, `navAccess.test.ts` passes 7/7 and `authSession.test.ts` 28/28.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - `Test` runs the workspace nextest, including the new gateway session test.
  - `Web Permission Tests` runs `test:auth` (the parsing and navigation tests) and `test:permissions` (the sidebar navigation tests), plus `cargo web check`.
  - `Lint` runs clippy.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test renders the sidebar or the palette for a signed-in session. Both filter through `pathAccess`, which is what the navigation tests cover. The palette test checks `paletteItemsFor`, the function the component renders from, not a rendered palette.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Revert checks, one line each:** forcing `"config": true` in the session response fails the gateway test for the account without a config grant. Dropping the `access.config` condition in `pathAccess` fails the navigation tests. Reading an absent flag as allowed fails the parsing test.
  - **Not verified:** a browser click-through on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot`: a Keycloak sign-in run on `f7584065d2` and on master `65f8eb3c92`, in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12251#issuecomment-6655268911).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f7584065d2`, plus `a7d67ec53d` for the palette (web suites, `cargo web check` and `npm run build`), `web`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [eight screenshots and the `features` each account gets](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12251#issuecomment-6655268911): the account without a config grant sees no config entries and a "Not available" card instead of the API 403, and the config reader and the administrator keep the config pages.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see "Expected on this branch".
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None skipped. The one workspace failure is environmental and is explained above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The flag only decides what the dashboard offers; the config routes still enforce the grant. It tells the browser no more than it already learns from a 403 on the config page.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The session response gains one field. The web ships inside the gateway, so the two always match, and the web reads an absent flag as no.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: revert the squash commit. Revert the gateway and web parts together: with only the gateway part reverted, the web reads the missing flag as no and hides the config pages from config readers who aren't operators.

N/A

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show message times in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The ZeroCode transcript never showed when anything happened. When an automated prompt, a refused queued message and a long tool call overlap in one session, there was no way to tell the order or the durations from the screen. A time on every message proved to be too much (an earlier revision of this PR did that). The transcript now shows time context in two places only:
    - a dim, centered divider (`── Today 01:00 ──`, `── Yesterday 22:20 ──`, or a date) before a prompt that starts the transcript, comes 15 minutes or more after the previous activity, or starts a new day. A quick back-and-forth gets no dividers.
    - a dim footer (`─── 01:00 → 01:31 · 31m 40s`) under a turn that ran for a minute or more. Short turns get none.
  - `session/messages` entries gain an optional `created_at` (RFC 3339) wherever the store has one: ACP full loads, ACP cursor pages, and the Chat backend via `load_with_timestamps`. It is skipped when absent and `#[serde(default)]` on the client, so either side can be older.
  - **Store fix underneath.** Checkpointed ACP turns write all their visible rows at finalization with one timestamp, so a turn's prompt read as the time the turn **ended**. A divider or footer built on that would be wrong by the whole length of the turn. The checkpoint row now records `started_at` (a nullable column, added on upgrade), and finalization and crash recovery stamp the turn's prompt row with it. The other rows of the turn keep the finalization time, which is the turn's end: exactly what the footer needs.
  - Live turns: entries are stamped on receipt, and the footer is placed when the turn settles. A later terminal frame for the same turn does not move it. A history load taken mid-turn hands the footer to the live settle.
  - A reloaded turn that ends in a recovery marker gets no footer, because recovery stamps its rows when it runs, which can be hours after the turn stopped.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Individual tool calls and replies in ACP history still share the turn's finish time. Giving each its own time would need a time on every checkpoint journal event; it isn't needed for dividers and footers.
  - No toggle. The only existing display toggle is thoughts; a timestamp toggle would need a new action, keybinding and help text.
  - The Chat-backend path (gateway SQLite) is affected by #11420, which rewrites every row's `created_at` on each turn. This PR passes through what that store holds.
- **Blast radius:** the ACP store's write path for checkpointed turns (only the prompt row's `created_at`) and one additive column on `acp_turn_checkpoints`; the `session/messages` wire shape (additive, optional); ZeroCode transcript layout (divider and footer rows drawn outside each entry's line range, with the tail re-render accounting for them).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11620. Related #11420.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the `zeroclaw-runtime` part (`created_at` on `session/messages`, confined to `handle_session_messages` and the entry builder) is covered by the row added in #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode now shows a small grey date-and-time line when you come back to a conversation after a break or on a new day, and a small grey line under any turn that took more than a minute, saying when it started, when it finished and how long it took. Quick exchanges look exactly as before. Under the hood, the daemon's database used to record every message of a turn as happening when the turn finished; this PR records when the prompt was sent, so those lines are right after a reload too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode over the daemon socket)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon and ZeroCode built from this branch; any agent.
- **Steps to run:** send a prompt that runs a tool and takes over a minute. Then send a quick follow-up. Wait 15 minutes (or reload a session from yesterday) and send another. Switch away from the session and back to force a `session/messages` reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a `── Today HH:MM ──` divider above the first prompt; a `─── start → end · duration` footer under the long turn; nothing around the quick follow-up; a new divider after the gap. The same marks after the reload. A session from an older daemon shows no marks rather than wrong ones.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no times anywhere.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran through `scripts/zc-cargo` on the remote build host.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files: clean.
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
Results below are for head `c57119d62da9` (rebased on `master` 2026-10-17) unless marked.

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode`: `test result: FAILED. 1537 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra acp_session_store`: `test result: ok. 88 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::`: `test result: ok. 850 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `5627 passed; 4 failed` at the earlier head. The 4 (`relay::local_dial_tests` x2, `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`) fail the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host. The runtime diff is unchanged since.

Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it restored:

- Store: `finalized_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time_and_reply_keeps_finalization_time`, `recovered_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time` (fail when the prompt keeps the finalization time); `turn_checkpoint_start_column_is_added_to_an_existing_database` (fails without the migration).
- RPC: `conversation_message_entries_carry_each_source_message_time` (fails when the projection drops times).
- Rules (`chat::entry_time`): `dividers_mark_the_first_prompt_gaps_and_day_changes_only` (fails when every prompt divides), `a_day_change_divides_even_after_a_short_gap` (fails without the day check), `footers_follow_finished_turns_of_a_minute_or_more` (fails without the one-minute floor), plus label and parsing tests.
- Transcript: `transcript_shows_gap_dividers_and_long_turn_footers_not_message_times` and `a_live_turn_gets_its_footer_when_it_settles` (fail when the layout drops the footer row, when a settle doesn't invalidate the tail, or when a later frame may move the end); `a_history_load_taken_mid_turn_hands_the_footer_to_the_live_settle` (fails when a moved footer doesn't force a full rebuild); `a_footer_on_a_divided_entry_keeps_one_divider` (fails when the tail re-render ignores the divider row); `a_recovered_turn_gets_no_footer_from_its_recovery_time`.

`rpc::dispatch::tests::cursor_pages_equal_legacy_projection_for_valid_tool_groups` was updated: cursor pages now carry times, so its full-load reference uses the timed projection.

- **CI checks relied on:** the Rust lanes for the three crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** no end-to-end daemon+TUI run in CI for this.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The divider and footer rows were checked in a live ZeroCode pane against a scratch daemon (seeded history plus a live turn), by reading the terminal's text.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11622#issuecomment-6232571932 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending. Daemon/store verification is also pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11622#issuecomment-6232571932 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Times are display-only and never reach the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The new wire field is optional both ways. The new column is nullable and added on open; an older binary ignores it (its inserts name their columns). A checkpoint begun by an older binary has no start time, and its prompt keeps the finalization time as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits. The added `acp_turn_checkpoints.started_at` column is harmless to the reverted code and needs no down-migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** no dividers or footers (old daemon or missing `created_at`), or a footer whose start is later than expected (start time not recorded).

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Added `sessions_prompt` tool: agents can prompt other agents' live RPC sessions, run a full turn there, and receive the final content

prs.title: feat(providers): honor runtime-profile thinking for OpenAI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Carry the existing opted-in runtime-profile thinking level with each request, independently of native token budgets, so two profiles sharing an OpenAI alias can select different reasoning efforts.
  - Resolve the neutral level against the actual selected OpenAI model, API, tool mode and public/subscription capability set, including fallback attempts and lazy streams.
  - Preserve the selected level across existing runtime adapters and disable response-cache reuse for explicit native-thinking overrides; document precedence, capability fallbacks and Rust source migration.
- **Scope boundary:** OpenAI Responses, native Chat Completions and the existing Codex subscription path. No new configuration key, global `runtime.reasoning_effort` values, authentication path, compatibility retry, provider family or runtime subsystem. Other providers keep their existing native budgets and wire behavior. Approval and dispatch authority, receipt/observer-event formats, history handling and cancellation semantics are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust request construction, runtime CLI/channel/Agent/RPC/delegate request propagation, routing and recovery, streaming/tool rounds, and response-cache eligibility. This requires cross-owner review and the separate runtime exception before merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12054. Depends on #12057. Related #10705 concerns accepting literal global `max`, which this PR does not implement.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10705

### What this does, simply

A profile could change thinking prompts or temperature while OpenAI's native reasoning effort still came from global provider options. The native Chat Completions path also lacked profile-derived effort. With `native_thinking = true`, a turn now carries the selected level to the actual OpenAI model making that request. Inline override takes precedence over session override, then the profile default; direct Agent/RPC sessions use their profile default.

`off` becomes `none` when supported, otherwise the lowest supported effort. `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high` use the matching effort, or the next higher supported effort capped at the maximum. `max` selects the model's highest supported effort. Public API and subscription capabilities stay separate. Unknown models and API/tool combinations absent from the capability table retain existing global/default behavior and emit an explanatory diagnostic. The GPT-5.x Chat Completions-with-tools entries are inferred from separately documented capabilities rather than verified by a live request; the remaining rejection risk is described under Testing.

The level survives tool rounds, max-iteration summaries, request rebuilding, recovery, fallback model changes and deferred streams. Independent delegates use their own profiles; bounded delegates inherit their caller's level. Legacy auxiliary one-shot requests keep their existing behavior. Explicit raw-body overrides retain their precedence.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: automated mock HTTP regressions exercise the real CLI/channel/Agent/delegate paths and assert outgoing efforts; judging model answers manually would not verify the wire setting. The real CLI regression is reproducible with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::loop_::tests::native_thinking_cli_profiles_override_global_effort_on_the_shared_endpoint -- --exact`.

### How I tested

Candidate `bd6de2fbf034debe604d00eab6445dbf201ba16a` integrates upstream `master` at `65f8eb3c9284e396d9de7872c3df6dba993b7093`. The conflict resolution keeps the daemon turn's native-thinking scope around the SOP call and preserves the upstream memory owner taken from the same accepted memory handle. GitHub reports the candidate is mergeable with master.

Core Team approval of the bounded runtime exception is recorded on PR #12057 and was formally confirmed at its current head. The exception record still needs to land on master before this implementation can merge. Owning human review of this implementation remains required.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057#pullrequestreview-5763468208

These jobs passed. Across all 58 checks on the commit, 46 succeeded, 10 were conditionally skipped and two failed. The skipped jobs do not supply executed coverage.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The required gate is red. [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/42048403224/job/127317561143) failed at `cargo deny check` on [RUSTSEC-2026-0441](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0441), which marks `pin-utils 0.1.0` unmaintained. Wire assertions are in `openai_reasoning_tests.rs` and the owning runtime/channel test modules.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Literal validation output above and outgoing-body assertions in those tests.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Opted-in profiles on one endpoint send their own efforts, model fallbacks remap the level, opt-out retains global/default behavior, and explicit native overrides bypass response-cache reuse. Single-call delegates retain their runtime prompt/temperature inputs; mapped non-`none` OpenAI efforts omit `temperature` on the wire for compatibility, as described below.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Desktop/UI and live/paid-provider checks are outside this change. Optional HTTP link validation was skipped because `lychee` is unavailable. No deployment or live account testing was performed.

</details>

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes: bypassing response-cache reuse for an explicit native-thinking override can issue an existing model request where a cached result was previously returned. Requests use the same configured endpoints and authentication; tests use local mock servers.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No: existing thinking-prompt selection is preserved.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Explicit overrides can increase model calls, latency and token cost. The existing `native_thinking` opt-in and rollback path control this behavior. Diagnostics include requested/effective effort, provider alias, model and mapping outcome; they exclude credentials, prompts, endpoint URLs and response bodies.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust source constructing or exhaustively destructuring affected public structs. Existing TOML values, schema enum values, provider defaults and serialized configuration remain compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new key, environment variable or CLI option. Existing opted-in profile levels now affect supported OpenAI native requests.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: No configuration migration. Downstream `ChatRequest` literals must initialize `thinking_level` (`None` for unrelated requests); rebuilders copy the original level, and exhaustive patterns add the field or `..`. `ThinkingLevel` remains available from its old configuration paths through a re-export. Callers of `default_budget_tokens()` through that path must import `zeroclaw_config::scattered_types::ThinkingLevelBudget`. Public runtime `ThinkingParams` literals need `native_level`; use the existing resolution helper where applicable. Recreate/reconnect Agent/RPC sessions after changing their profile defaults.

A successfully mapped non-`none` public OpenAI reasoning request omits optional `temperature`, as the verified models require. Existing runtime prompt/temperature policy, unmapped/global requests and other providers retain their behavior. Effort changes may affect latency and token usage; subscription model access still depends on the account's existing entitlements. Public API capabilities were checked against [official OpenAI model pages](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27; subscription sets come from list-visible entries in the [Codex catalog at commit `126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json). Client delegation modes such as `ultra` are excluded and never sent as wire efforts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `native_thinking = false` on affected runtime profiles and apply it through the existing runtime reload or restart lifecycle, including recreating/reconnecting Agent/RPC sessions, to return OpenAI requests to the existing global/default effort path. For a full rollback, revert this PR's merge/squash commit; if merged as separate commits, revert the complete feature commit range, including its API, config, provider and runtime changes together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `native_thinking` only. Disabling it on a mixed-provider profile also disables its existing native token budgets; revert the complete feature when those budgets must stay enabled.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Upstream request rejection, unexpected latency/token use, an unmapped-level diagnostic, or an effort substitution inconsistent with the serving model. Inspect `requested_level`, `effective_effort`, provider/model and mapping outcome diagnostics without logging request bodies or credentials.

prs.title: feat(security): bind gateway pairing tokens to roster users
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A gateway pairing token can now be bound to a `[users.<name>]` roster entry when its code is minted. A device paired with such a code authenticates as `user:<id>` with that user's permission profiles instead of as the shared operator. This was the one credential path in the #8289 principal model that always collapsed to the shared operator, so households and small teams could not give a remote person scoped access without deploying an identity provider.
  - The operator chooses the binding, not the client. `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user <name>` calls `POST /admin/paircode/new?user=<name>`, which already requires a loopback peer and the gateway's owner-only admin token. The subject travels with the pending code into its reservation and the committed token, and a failed issuance restores the code still bound. `/pair` and `/api/pair` take no user parameter; they now report the `principal_id` the new token authenticates as.
  - Bound tokens are persisted only in a new, gateway-managed `gateway.paired_token_users` map (token SHA-256 hash to durable roster principal id), never also in `gateway.paired_tokens`. Both fields are written in the same `save_dirty`, so a binding cannot be persisted apart from its token and revocation is durable for bound tokens too. `PairingGuard::from_gateway_config` loads both. A malformed or conflicting binding is skipped with a warning, and the token it names fails closed even if `paired_tokens` also lists it.
  - The `native` auth provider resolves a bound token to `IdentitySubject::Roster`, and provenance now admits `(Native, Roster)`. Connection revalidation rebuilds native identities from the token's live subject, so a bound connection survives policy generation changes, and a removed roster entry denies it (`NotEntitled`) instead of widening it.
  - The operator-authority gateway checks (`PairingGuard::is_authenticated` and `authenticate_and_hash`) accept only shared-operator tokens. They sit behind `require_auth`, `/ws/chat`, SSE, ACP, nodes, canvas, plugins, the webhook, and remote reload and SOP approval, so a bound token gets `401` there. Loopback callers of the admin routes stay trusted without a token, as before. A bound token works where principals are resolved: the RPC handshake (local socket, WSS, relay) and the gateway's configuration route group.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to OIDC, per-token grants, channel identity, or the daemon-uid path. Unbound tokens, which is every existing token, behave as before. Roster entries still need a `uid`; uid-less remote-only users are the issue's separate follow-up. No dashboard UI for binding, and the other gateway routes are not made principal-aware.
- **Blast radius:** `PairingGuard` (every surface that authenticates a paired token), pairing persistence in `[gateway]`, the RPC handshake and revalidation path, the admin pairing-code routes and `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode`, device rotation on the admin route and the dashboard, and the device list (`GET /api/devices`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10573, Related #8289

### What this does, simply

Today every device paired with the gateway is the same all-powerful operator. If two people share one agent, the only way to give the second person narrower access over the network is to run an OIDC identity provider. With this PR the operator can bind a pairing code to a person listed in `[users]` when minting it. The device that redeems that code signs in as that person and gets only their permissions. Codes minted without `--user`, and every existing token, keep working as before. A bound token is accepted only where ZeroClaw checks per-person permissions: zerocode's connection to the daemon and the gateway's config routes. Everything else, the web dashboard included, refuses it rather than treat it as the operator.

### Design decisions that differ from the issue text

- **The operator binds at mint time.** The issue proposed `pair --user` and a `user` parameter on `/pair`. `/pair` is unauthenticated (the code is the only credential), so a client-chosen user would not be a boundary: whoever holds a code could name any user, or leave the parameter out and pair as the operator. The binding is chosen on the loopback plus admin-token route instead.
- **Bound tokens live only in the binding map.** The issue suggested a map alongside `paired_tokens`. Keeping bound hashes out of `paired_tokens` means an older binary, or a lost map, makes a bound token stop working instead of turning it into an operator token.
- **Operator-authority routes refuse bound tokens.** Those routes act with full operator authority, so letting a bound token through would widen it.

### Other behavior changes

- Device rotation (`--rotate-device`, and the dashboard's rotate) mints the replacement with the revoked token's own subject. It issues no code when that user's roster entry is gone, or when the device's token was already revoked (a stale registry row), unbound devices included, because the binding cannot be determined. When a code is already pending, the dashboard offers it only if it pairs as the rotated device did; otherwise it names the gateway-host command that mints the right one.
- The CLI shows a code requested with `--user` only if the gateway confirms the binding by echoing the user and reporting a `user:` principal. A gateway older than the CLI ignores the parameter and mints an ordinary code, which is withheld with an explanation. Every shown code now says who it pairs as.
- The certificate enrollment endpoint refuses a user-bound code with `409` without consuming it. After #11940, enrollment shares the canonical pairing guard, so this check now protects the live shared authority. Enrollment codes stay in a separate purpose slot and issue certificates without creating bearer tokens.
- The gateway's startup banner names who a pending bound code pairs as.
- `GET /api/devices` reports each device's `principal_id`, read from the pairing guard when the list is built, or `null` once the device's token is no longer paired. An operator retiring a user can find that user's devices and revoke them. The registry stores nothing new.

### Settled in review

- `gateway.paired_token_users` stays in plain text and visible to principals granted `Config:Read`, as documented. It holds hashes, not tokens, and a hash cannot be presented as a credential, so encrypting it would be optional hardening, not a requirement.
- Known edge, not changed here and to follow separately: webhook channel readiness reports authenticated when the only paired tokens are roster-bound, although none of them can call the webhook.

### Merge-order notes

Current integration: `e9e261b3247f4b463541364f577dcaa57e2e40aa` additively merges `master` at `65f8eb3c9284e396d9de7872c3df6dba993b7093`, including #12213’s live pairing limits. The standalone gateway and daemon load roster bindings with `from_gateway_config` and retain the canonical live limit resolver. Dropped reservations keep their original subject and mint time, and the current lifetime is resolved before taking pairing locks. A shortened lifetime expires pending and reserved bound codes; extending it later cannot revive a code already discarded. Both the roster-token route restrictions and the dashboard sign-in pairing checks remain documented.

Previous integration: `6ce9e75a272de6671f168799fbb0c78b7a6cb204` additively merges `master` at `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, after #11940 landed. It preserves the roster subject and code-purpose slot through reservations and restoration, and keeps enrollment consume-only. `EnrollmentReservation::subject()` borrows the existing subject rather than duplicating authority state. The secure-transport documentation now distinguishes unbound gateway codes from roster-bound codes.

Earlier integration merges include the following two updates. The first merge (`aab2ffb427`) followed #11171. The token map keeps each token's subject behind the `RwLock` #11171 added, and `HeldPairedTokens` gains `subject_of_hash`. Revalidation looks up the token's subject instead of testing membership, so a bound connection revalidates as its roster principal both directly and under an `AuthorityLease`; the lease keeps its membership check for liveness. The second merge (`23893ad3c7`) followed #10911. `persist_pairing_tokens` now saves through an admitted config commit and publishes the result, and inside that commit it still writes both fields from `PairingGuard::persisted_tokens()`.

These open PRs conflict with this branch or change the pairing paths it depends on (checked with `git merge-tree` against each head on 2026-10-12):

- #11182, draft (`pairing.rs`; it also conflicts with `master` alone in the gateway and RPC files): it adds a revocation guard parameter and moves token persistence, code minting and the device list into `zeroclaw-runtime/src/devices.rs` for its RPC `pairing/*` methods. Whichever lands second carries this PR's rules into that module:
  - `persist_pairing_tokens_held` writes both fields from `PairingGuard::persisted_tokens()` and marks both dirty. Writing `tokens()` into `gateway.paired_tokens` alone would store bound hashes as operator tokens, and would leave a revoked binding on disk to authenticate again after a restart; the same holds for its revoke-all path.
  - Single-device rotation keeps the device's binding, or withholds the code, as `rotation_replacement_subject` does here.
  - `list_devices_body` reports each device's `principal_id`, as `GET /api/devices` does here.
  - `pairing/new-code` stays operator-only, because it mints unbound codes.
- #11149, draft, and #11176, draft and stacked on it: both conflict with `master` alone in `api_pairing.rs`, gateway `lib.rs` and `rpc/dispatch.rs`, and the conflict with this branch is about behavior. They move device revocation behind `PairingGuard::revoke_under_config_write_lock` (`revoke_device_credential`, `revoke_token_hash_ordered`) and token persistence into `persist_pairing_tokens_under`. Whichever lands second applies the rules listed for #11182: the locked revoke step uses `revoke_token_hash_subject`, so rotation keeps the device's binding, and `persist_pairing_tokens_under` writes both fields from `PairingGuard::persisted_tokens()`, because writing `pairing.tokens()` into `gateway.paired_tokens` alone would store bound hashes as operator tokens. Under #11149's `is_shared_operator` gating, sessions from bound tokens lose the cron, nested and peer tools, which is the intended result for a scoped user.
- #11264 and #11265 (`schema.rs`, `authentication.md`): they relax the roster's `uid` requirement and add a `UserConfig` field. The `uid` wording here (the validation message, the field docs, the new docs section) describes the current rule, and the new tests spell out `UserConfig` literals, so whichever lands second updates both: after #11264 the literals need `password_hash: None`, and the advice to pick an unused `uid` applies only to entries without a password.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw gateway get-paircode`), `web` (gateway HTTP routes), `tui` (zerocode over WSS)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon with the gateway and `gateway.require_pairing = true`, `[wss]` enabled for step 5, and a roster user whose uid no account on the host holds:

  ```toml
  [permission_profiles.reader.grants]
  sessions = ["read"]
  config = ["read"]

  [users.alice]
  uid = 59999
  permission_profiles = ["reader"]
  ```

- **Steps to run:**
  1. On the gateway host, as the gateway's user: `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user alice`
  2. `curl -s -X POST -H "X-Pairing-Code: <code>" http://127.0.0.1:42617/pair`
  3. `grep -n -A2 paired_token_users <config.toml>`
  4. With the returned token, request `GET /api/devices`, `GET /api/config`, and a `PATCH /api/config`.
  5. Connect zerocode over WSS with `ZEROCLAW_AUTH_TOKEN=<token>` and read the daemon's `RPC principal bound` log event.
  6. Restart the daemon and repeat steps 4 and 5.
  7. With an unbound operator token, list devices (`GET /api/devices`), run `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --rotate-device <id>` for alice's device, then repeat after removing `[users.alice]`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  1. A code, followed by "This code pairs as user:alice".
  2. A token and `"principal_id": "user:alice"`.
  3. The token's hash maps to `"alice"` under `[gateway.paired_token_users]` and is absent from `paired_tokens`.
  4. `401` from `/api/devices`, `200` from `GET /api/config`, `403` from the `PATCH`.
  5. `principal_id` is `user:alice`, and a method outside the profile is refused.
  6. Same results after the restart.
  7. The replacement code pairs as `user:alice` and the old token is refused. With the roster entry removed, the rotation revokes and issues no code.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `--user` is an unknown argument, and every paired token authenticates as the shared operator with full access on every route.

### How I tested

#### Current integration validation (2026-11-04)

#### End-to-end run

- **Revision:** `eaea62766b`. The locally built debug binary reports `zeroclaw 0.8.5 (v0.8.5-535-geaea62766b)`.
- **Environment:** macOS arm64. One isolated daemon, with `HOME`, `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` and the RPC socket in a scratch directory, and nothing read from or written to the real `~/.zeroclaw`. - **Client:** the WSS client certificate was enrolled with `zerocode --enroll`, after checking the client's SAS against the one on the daemon console. A small JSON-RPC client then connected over mTLS with that certificate and presented the token in `initialize`. Codes and tokens are omitted below.
- **Observed:**
  1. `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user alice` printed a code and "This code pairs as user:alice: the device that redeems it gets that roster user's permissions, not the operator's."
  2. `POST /pair` returned `200` with `"principal_id": "user:alice"`.
  3. `config.toml` holds the token's hash once, under `[gateway.paired_token_users]` mapped to `"alice"`, and `gateway.paired_tokens` is absent.
  4. With the bound token, `GET /api/devices` returned `401`, `GET /api/config` returned `200`, and `PATCH /api/config` returned `403` ("Principal lacks the config grant required for this method").
  5. Over WSS, `initialize` returned `principal_id: user:alice`, and the daemon logged `RPC principal bound` with `auth_provider: native` and `principal_id: user:alice`. `session/list` and `config/get` succeeded. `config/set` was refused with `-32012` ("Principal is not granted config:update (required by config/set)").
  6. After a daemon restart, steps 4 and 5 gave the same results with the same token.
  7. With an unbound operator token (its code printed "This code pairs as the shared operator, with the operator's full access."), `GET /api/devices` listed alice's device as `user:alice` and the operator's as `shared-operator`. `--rotate-device` on alice's device printed "the device again authenticates as user:alice", and its replacement code paired as `user:alice`. The old token got `401` and `-32010` ("Credential rejected"). After `[users.alice]` was removed and the daemon reloaded, the replacement token was refused at `initialize` with `-32012` ("Authenticated, but no permission profile grants this identity anything"). Rotating that device then revoked the token and issued no code, with the remedy text below.

<summary>Transcript (codes and tokens redacted, hashes shortened)</summary>

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The end-to-end run above.
  - Mutation checks. For each guard below, I broke the guard, confirmed the named boundary test failed, and restored it:
    - a dropped reservation restoring the pending code still bound;
    - operator-authority membership refusing bound tokens;
    - a valid binding winning over `paired_tokens` for the same hash;
    - a damaged, conflicting or whitespace-padded binding failing closed;
    - provenance admitting `(Native, Roster)`;
    - revalidation rebuilding a bound identity;
    - after the first merge: revalidation of an unbound token, directly and under an `AuthorityLease`, each path broken on its own;
    - both fields marked dirty in one save, checked on disk;
    - rotation keeping the subject, and withholding a code for a stale row or a removed user;
    - dashboard rotation not offering a differently bound pending code;
    - the CLI withholding an unconfirmed binding and trimming `--user`;
    - the device list reporting each device's principal;
    - the architecture gate flagging a production `PairingGuard::new` fed from `paired_tokens`, including `cfg(not(test))` items and aliases.
  - Not verified: Windows. The named-pipe transport itself is unchanged.
- **Visual interface evidence:** exact plain-text output from the end-to-end run above. The new CLI lines come from English-only Fluent keys, and other locales fall back to English: `cli-pairing-bound-user`, `cli-pairing-shared-operator`, `cli-pairing-bound-unconfirmed`, `cli-pairing-bound-no-code`, `cli-pairing-rotate-device-no-code` and `cli-pairing-rotate-device-unbound`.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `eaea62766b`; the unit, handler, router and architecture tests above, and the end-to-end run against a live daemon over the CLI, HTTP and WSS.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the transcript above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see "Observed" above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the no-default-features check was not run locally; CI runs it on Linux.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a roster user can now hold a pairing token, a second credential next to their peer uid. Only the operator can mint one (a loopback peer plus the owner-only admin token), the redeeming client cannot choose or strip the binding, the token carries only the user's permission profiles through the shared resolver, and every operator-authority route refuses it. The new persisted map holds token hashes and principal ids, written in the same atomic save as the token list, and a damaged entry makes its token fail closed at load. The map is stored in plain text; see "Settled in review" above.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing tokens are unbound and behave as before; the new field defaults empty.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes:
  - the gateway-managed `gateway.paired_token_users`;
  - `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user <name>`;
  - a `user` query parameter on `POST /admin/paircode/new`;
  - `principal_id` in the `/pair`, `/api/pair`, `/admin/paircode*` and dashboard rotation responses, on each device in `GET /api/devices`, and in the CLI's `--json` output.

  No schema version change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. An operator opts in by minting a code with `--user`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the merge. An older binary ignores `gateway.paired_token_users`, so bound tokens stop authenticating there instead of turning into operator tokens, and the affected users re-pair. Entries left in the file work again after a later upgrade, so delete the table when downgrading if the bound devices should stay revoked.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none. The feature is inert until a code is minted with `--user`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `RPC principal bound` events with `auth_provider = native` and a `user:` principal id;
  - `RPC authorization denied` events for bound principals;
  - the load-time warning `gateway.paired_token_users has entries that are not a token hash mapped to one valid roster principal id`;
  - `401` for a bound token on the dashboard and other operator routes.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
